prs.title: fix(settings): preserve disk edits when changing authentication
prs.body:
## Summary

Draft pending a clean full-suite run on unrestricted CI; the local environment
failures are recorded below rather than reported as passing checks.

Prevent `/auth signin` from overwriting unrelated settings edited after Gemini
CLI started. Confirming an auth method currently saves the entire startup
snapshot: a newly added MCP server can disappear, an edited theme can revert,
and a deleted model preference can return.

## Details

Persist only the property explicitly changed by `LoadedSettings.setValue`,
against the current on-disk JSON. Preserve unrelated additions, changes,
deletions, comments, arrays, and raw environment placeholders. Explicit object
assignment still replaces that subtree, and direct `saveSettings` calls retain
their existing whole-file replacement semantics. Invalid JSON stays intact and
reports a parsing error. This does not add cross-process locking.

Document the distinction between `/quit`, `/auth signin`, and `/auth signout`.
Add real-file regressions for stale snapshots and assertions that opening the
auth dialog or quitting does not save settings. No breaking changes.

## Related Issues

Related to #23138. The stale `originalSettings` snapshot described there also
reproduces when changing authentication on upstream `06d329873`.

## How to Validate

Run these checks from the PR checkout with Node 20.19:

1. Run `npm run preflight` for clean installation, formatting, build, lint,
   typechecks, and the workspace/script/SEA test suites.
2. Run the focused regression tests:

   ```sh
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- \
     src/config/settings.persistence.test.ts \
     src/config/settings.test.ts \
     src/utils/commentJson.test.ts \
     src/ui/commands/authCommand.test.ts \
     src/ui/commands/quitCommand.test.ts
   ```

   Verify external additions, edits, and deletions survive selecting Google
   authentication; sign-out removes only the selected auth property; malformed
   JSON remains unchanged. Comments, placeholders, unrelated arrays, indexed
   paths, and explicit replacement semantics are covered too.

3. Run `npm start -- --version` and `npx --no-install gemini --version`.
   Both must print the version built from this checkout and exit successfully.
4. Optional interactive reproduction: use a temporary `GEMINI_CLI_HOME`, start
   Gemini CLI, and edit an unrelated setting in that home's settings file from
   another terminal. Confirm `/auth signin`: the auth selection is saved while
   the unrelated edit remains. `/quit` keeps saved preferences and credentials.

Local results on Node 20.19 / Linux:

- Clean installation, formatting, build, full lint suite, and all typechecks
  passed. The five changed auth/settings test suites passed all 165 cases.
- The full preflight remains **failed**: workspace suites reported 15,880
  passing tests, 110 failures, and 68 skips. All 22 CLI failures reproduce with
  unmodified upstream runtime files. The other 88 occur in unchanged core code.
  Failure groups are restricted home writes, home-path fixture mismatches,
  headless trust checks, DNS/private-IP validation, inherited npm PATH, ancestor
  `.git` markers, and Bubblewrap UID-map setup in this environment.
- Linux `npm start` and local `npx` version checks passed. The installed-settings
  probe fails on current upstream and passes with this fix.
- Script tests passed all 202 cases; SEA launch tests passed all 17 cases, run separately
  because the workspace failures short-circuited those final preflight commands.

prs.title: fix(cli): support 'keys' array in keybindings.json
prs.body:
## Summary

Supports defining multiple key combinations via a `"keys"` array in `keybindings.json` entries in addition to the existing single `"key"` string property. This resolves an issue where keybinding overrides containing an array of keys (such as unbinding multiple defaults) failed schema validation, causing the entire custom configuration to be discarded.

## Details

- **Schema Update (`packages/cli/src/ui/key/keyBindings.ts`):** Updated `keybindingsSchema` to accept either `"key": z.string()` or `"keys": z.array(z.string())` (or both) per entry, with refinement verifying that at least one is specified.
- **Flattening:** During parsing, entries with `"keys"` are normalized and flattened into individual `{ commandEntry, key }` objects. This allows subsequent unbinding (`-`) and binding loops to process each key individually without altering the downstream keybinding engine.
- **Backward Compatibility:** Single `"key"` strings continue to work exactly as before with zero breaking changes.
- **Unit Testing:** Added comprehensive tests in `packages/cli/src/ui/key/keyBindings.test.ts` for multiple key addition, multiple key unbinding with negation, combining `key` and `keys`, and validation failure modes.

## Related Issues

Fixes #22813

prs.title: fix(cli): verify active binary update to prevent PATH shadowing false success
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes an issue where `handleAutoUpdate` reported a successful update even when the active executing binary was shadowed in `$PATH` or targeted by a non-matching package manager prefix, leaving the user running the outdated binary.

## Details

- **Problem:** When multiple installations exist on a system (e.g., `/usr/local/bin` preceding `/usr/bin` in `$PATH`, or switched npm/pnpm global prefixes), running the global update command installs the new version into the package manager's prefix directory while the active binary executing Gemini CLI remains untouched. `handleAutoUpdate` previously relied solely on the update process exiting with code `0`, falsely emitting `update-success` ("Update successful! The new version will be used on your next run.") and causing an infinite update prompt loop on subsequent runs.
- **Solution:** Added post-update verification in `handleAutoUpdate`. When the child process exits with code `0`, `handleAutoUpdate` inspects the active running binary via `process.argv[1]` and checks its `package.json` version using `getPackageJson`.
  - If the active binary's version is verified to still be older than `info.update.latest`, `handleAutoUpdate` emits `update-failed` with a descriptive message explaining that the active binary was not updated and may be shadowed by another installation in `$PATH`.
  - Employs a fail-safe fallback: if `package.json` cannot be determined or if an error occurs during verification, it does not block legitimate updates.
  - Added optional `getPackageJsonFn` injection to `handleAutoUpdate` for robust, deterministic unit testing.

## Related Issues

Fixes #21553

## How to Validate

1. **Automated Unit Tests:**
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/utils/handleAutoUpdate.test.ts
   ```
   All tests pass, including new coverage for PATH shadowing detection and graceful fallback handling.

2. **Full Workspace Build & Tests:**
   ```bash
   npm run build
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli
   npm run lint
   npm run typecheck
   ```

prs.title: fix(core): harden SKILL.md frontmatter parsing for single-line descriptions
prs.body:
Skill discovery in `loadSkillFromFile()` could fail to load `SKILL.md` files when the YAML frontmatter used a single-line `description` or was saved with common platform-specific formatting (such as a UTF-8 or UTF-16 BOM on Windows PowerShell, trailing spaces after the `---` fence markers, or YAML-sensitive punctuation in single-line descriptions that triggered the fallback parser). Switching to a multi-line `>` block scalar avoided some of these failures because `js-yaml` treats block scalars as literal text without falling back to `parseSimpleFrontmatter()`. This change decodes `SKILL.md` files with `readFileWithEncoding()`, relaxes `FRONTMATTER_REGEX` for BOMs and trailing fence whitespace, and hardens `parseSimpleFrontmatter()` so single-line and wrapped descriptions parse reliably.

## Details

- **`loadSkillFromFile` (`packages/core/src/skills/skillLoader.ts`)**:
  - Uses `readFileWithEncoding()` instead of `fs.readFile(..., 'utf-8')` so `SKILL.md` files saved with UTF-8, UTF-16 LE/BE, or UTF-32 BOMs (such as default PowerShell `Out-File` / redirection encodings on Windows) are decoded and stripped of their BOM before matching frontmatter.
- **`FRONTMATTER_REGEX` (`packages/core/src/skills/skillLoader.ts`)**:
  - Allows an optional leading UTF-8 BOM (`\uFEFF?`) and optional horizontal whitespace (`[ \t]*`) after the opening and closing `---` lines.
  - Anchors the pattern at the end (`$`) so trailing spaces on the closing `---` line do not cause the optional Markdown body group to be skipped, and lines starting with `---` inside frontmatter do not close the frontmatter block early.
- **`parseSimpleFrontmatter` (`packages/core/src/skills/skillLoader.ts`)**:
  - Matches `name` and `description` case-insensitively and allows optional horizontal whitespace before `:` using linear-time prefix matching (`^[ \t]*name[ \t]*:` and `^([ \t]*)description[ \t]*:`).
  - Strips matching outer single or double quotes (`"..."` or `'...'`) from `name` and `description` via `stripOuterQuotes()` so quoted names do not keep literal quotes that `loadSkillFromFile()` would sanitize into `-`.
  - Stops the `description` continuation loop before `name:` or `description:` keys at any indentation and before sibling keys (`key:`) at or above the `description:` indentation level, preventing single-line descriptions that trigger the fallback parser from swallowing a following `name:` field.
  - Supports unindented wrapped continuation lines and ignores standalone YAML block scalar indicators (`>`, `|`, `>-`, `|-`, `>+`, `|+`) on the `description:` line when the fallback parser is used.
- **Tests (`packages/core/src/skills/skillLoader.test.ts`)**:
  - Added coverage for UTF-8 BOM, UTF-16 LE BOM, trailing spaces after `---` markers (preserving the skill body), single-line descriptions with colons before indented keys, outer quote stripping in the fallback parser, case-insensitive keys with spaces before `:`, `Note:` lines inside multi-line descriptions, unindented wrapped description lines, and block scalar indicators in the fallback parser.
  - On the previous code, 6 of the 7 new tests fail.

## Related Issues

Fixes [#25693](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/25693)

## How to Validate

1. Run the targeted unit tests:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/skills/skillLoader.test.ts
   ```
2. Run the full preflight:
   ```bash
   npm run preflight
   ```
3. Manual check with a throwaway workspace and home directory (nothing in your real settings or workspace is touched):
   1. Build the CLI and create a temporary workspace containing `.agents/skills/` with single-line, BOM-prefixed, and fallback-parsed `SKILL.md` files:
      ```bash
      npm run build
      dir="$(mktemp -d)"
      mkdir -p "$dir/.gemini" "$dir/workspace/.agents/skills/test-single" "$dir/workspace/.agents/skills/test-colon"
      printf '{\n  "%s": "TRUST_FOLDER"\n}\n' "$dir/workspace" > "$dir/.gemini/trustedFolders.json"
      printf '\xef\xbb\xbf---  \r\nname: test-single\r\ndescription: A single line description that is relatively long and contains some punctuation.\r\n--- \r\n# Test Skill\r\nContent here.\r\n' > "$dir/workspace/.agents/skills/test-single/SKILL.md"
      printf -- '---\n  description: A single line description: with an unquoted colon.\n  name: "test-colon"\n---\n# Test Colon Skill\nContent here.\n' > "$dir/workspace/.agents/skills/test-colon/SKILL.md"
      ```
   2. List the discovered skills from the temporary workspace:
      ```bash
      (cd "$dir/workspace" && GEMINI_CLI_HOME="$dir" node "$OLDPWD/packages/cli/dist/index.js" skills list)
      ```
      - Expected: both `test-colon [Enabled]` and `test-single [Enabled]` are listed with their descriptions.
      - Before this change: neither skill was discovered (`No skills discovered.`).
   3. Clean up:
      ```bash
      rm -rf "$dir"
      unset dir
      ```

prs.title: fix(ci): remove unsupported members permission in unassign-inactive-assignees workflow
prs.body:
## Summary

Remove `permission-members: 'read'` from the `Generate GitHub App Token` (`actions/create-github-app-token`) step in `.github/workflows/unassign-inactive-assignees.yml` so the daily scheduled workflow can generate an installation token without failing with HTTP 422 (`The permissions requested are not granted to this installation`).

## Details

In PR #29609, `permission-issues: 'write'`, `permission-pull-requests: 'read'`, and `permission-members: 'read'` were added to the `actions/create-github-app-token` step to satisfy `zizmor` permission scoping checks. However, the GitHub App (`secrets.APP_ID`) installed on `google-gemini/gemini-cli` is not granted the organization-level `members: read` permission, causing `actions/create-github-app-token` to fail at runtime with HTTP 422 before the `Unassign inactive assignees` step can run.

Removing `permission-members: 'read'` while retaining `permission-issues: 'write'` and `permission-pull-requests: 'read'` keeps explicit token permission scoping for `zizmor` while requesting only permissions granted to the App installation. The script already wraps org/team membership checks in `try / catch` blocks and falls back to repository collaborator permission checks (`github.rest.repos.getCollaboratorPermissionLevel`).

## Related Issues

Fixes #29298

## How to Validate

1. Verify that the `zizmor` check passes on `.github/workflows/unassign-inactive-assignees.yml` in PR CI.
2. Trigger the `Unassign Inactive Issue Assignees` workflow via `workflow_dispatch` with `dry_run: true` and confirm that both the `Generate GitHub App Token` step and the `Unassign inactive assignees` step complete without error.

prs.title: fix(core): let /ide enable reconnect after the IDE server restarts
prs.body:
## Summary

After VS Code's **Developer: Reload Window** (or an extension update/disable), the CLI running in the surviving integrated terminal reported `🔴 Disconnected: IDE connection error…`, and `/ide enable` kept failing with `Failed to connect to IDE companion extension…` until VS Code was fully closed and reopened.

#29674 fixed the server side of #28785 (`IdeServer.stop()` hanging and leaking its port file). This PR fixes the **client side**, which could not survive an IDE-server restart even with a fixed extension — and still cannot with the Marketplace extension (v0.20.0), which predates #29674 and leaks a port file on every reload.

Two defects in `IdeClient`:

1. **Discovery tried a single port file.** The reloaded extension host starts a new server (new port, new token, new port file), but the terminal's `GEMINI_CLI_IDE_SERVER_PORT` / `GEMINI_CLI_IDE_AUTH_TOKEN` stay frozen at the old values. `getConnectionConfigFromFile()` used that frozen port as the tie-breaker, so a leaked old file was selected deterministically, `connect()` never fell through to the live file, and the env fallback pointed at the same dead port.
2. **A superseded client kept driving the state.** `onerror`/`onclose` were bound to the `IdeClient`, not to the client that registered them, and `establish*Connection()` never closed the previous client. After a successful `/ide enable`, the old transport's SSE reconnection attempts against the dead port (1 s, 2.5 s) flipped the state back to `Disconnected` while the new connection was healthy.

Two source files in `packages/core`, no public API change, no new `eslint-disable`.

## Details

### `ide-connection-utils.ts`

- New `getConnectionConfigsFromFile(pid)` returns **every** workspace-valid candidate, best first: the file whose port matches `GEMINI_CLI_IDE_SERVER_PORT` (the window the terminal belongs to), then the rest in the existing `sortConnectionFiles()` order. When no file matches the workspace it still returns the single best-sorted entry so the detailed "Directory mismatch" error is preserved.
- `getConnectionConfigFromFile()` is now `candidates[0]` — the ranking of the preferred file is **unchanged** (all 46 pre-existing tests pass untouched). The three inline config types were replaced by an exported `IdeConnectionConfig` alias. The module is not re-exported from core's index.

### `ide-client.ts`

- `connect()` iterates the candidates, each with **its own** auth token, before the env fallbacks. Behaviour is identical whenever the first candidate answers — the only case that worked before.
- `registerClientHandlers()` captures the client it is registering for; `onerror`/`onclose` no-op once `this.client` has moved on.
- New `retireClient()`, called by both `establishHttpConnection()` and `establishStdioConnection()` before creating a new `Client`: detaches the handlers and `close()`s the superseded client (aborting its socket and retry timers); a rejected `close()` is debug-logged.
- A failed attempt no longer leaves `this.client` pointing at a `Client` that never connected (`dropFailedClient()`, scoped to that attempt's client), so `openDiff`/`closeDiff` fail fast on `!this.client`; failed attempts are debug-logged. (Review feedback.)

### Deliberately out of scope

- Deleting stale files from the client (unsafe when the CLI runs in a sandbox/remote where a port is legitimately unreachable); an extension-side GC of dead sibling files is a natural follow-up.
- Auto-reconnect on disconnect (policy change). Users still see one `IDE connection error… run /ide enable` line after a reload; this PR makes that documented recovery actually work.
- Carried over: a stale file whose port was reused by an unrelated process that accepts TCP but never answers would wait for the SDK's `initialize` timeout (same exposure as before, now per candidate).

## Related Issues

Related to #28785 — client-side follow-up to #29674 (which fixed `IdeServer.stop()`; the issue was closed by it, but the reload symptom it mentions remained).

## How to Validate

**Unit / integration tests**

```bash
npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/ide/
# 7 files, 185 passed | 1 skipped
```

- `ide-connection-utils.test.ts` — +9 cases for `getConnectionConfigsFromFile` (legacy file, empty/error paths, workspace filtering and order, env-port promotion with fallbacks retained, no env match, mismatch → single entry, malformed files, singular returns the first candidate).
- `ide-client.test.ts` — +13 cases: candidate iteration (next candidate on failure with its own token, stop at first success, http → stdio candidate, env fallback after all candidates, disconnected when nothing answers), reconnecting (superseded client closed and detached, its late error/close ignored, errors from the current client still reported, rejected `close()` tolerated) and failed attempts (HTTP and stdio failures leave no client behind, `openDiff`/`closeDiff` fail fast, a later successful candidate's client is kept). Also fixes the latent singleton reset in that file (`instancePromise`, not `instance`) so its tests are actually isolated.
- `ide-client.server-restart.test.ts` (new) — real `node:http` MCP servers and real port files in a private `TMPDIR`, no SDK mocks: (1) leaked file matching the frozen env port, (2) late errors from the superseded transport after a clean restart, (3) several leaked files with no env hint, (4) the env-matching window still wins when several servers are alive. (1) and (2) fail on `main` with exactly the user-facing messages above and pass with this change.

**End-to-end with the real `/ide` commands** (harness kept out of the tree): the real `ideCommand()` actions from `packages/cli`, the real `IdeClient`, and the real companion `IDEServer` (vscode API mocked), executed as stash-fix → rebuild → run → restore → rebuild → run:

| Step | `main` | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/ide status` | `🟢 Connected` | `🟢 Connected` |
| Reload Window (A: v0.20.0 leaks file · B: fixed extension) | — | — |
| `/ide status` ≈1 s later | `🔴 Disconnected: IDE connection error…` | same (by design, one notification) |
| `/ide enable` | A: `🔴 Disconnected: Failed to connect to IDE companion extension…`  | `🟢 Connected` |
| `/ide status` 4.5 s later | B: `🔴 Disconnected: IDE connection error…` | `🟢 Connected`, `isDiffingEnabled() === true` |

**Manually in VS Code**

1. `rm -f /tmp/gemini/ide/gemini-ide-server-*.json` (macOS: `$TMPDIR/gemini/ide/`), open the repo, run `gemini` in the integrated terminal, `/ide status` → `🟢 Connected to VS Code`.
2. **Developer: Reload Window**; keep the terminal. Within ~1–2 s the CLI prints `IDE connection error… run /ide enable`.
3. `/ide enable` → **before:** `🔴 Disconnected: Failed to connect to IDE companion extension in VS Code…` (with the Marketplace extension; `ls /tmp/gemini/ide/` shows the leaked old file next to the new one) — **after:** `🟢 Connected to VS Code`, and `/ide status` stays connected; diffs work.

**CI parity (Linux, Node 20.20.2):** all `ci.yml` Lint-job steps (lockfile, eslint, actionlint, shellcheck, yamllint, build, typecheck, prettier, settings docs `--check`, sensitive keywords, actions pinning) and both Test (Linux) shards + `test:scripts` + bundle + bundle/npx smoke tests ran locally and passed; `npm run preflight` passed (cli 7327, core 8341, a2a 177, companion 62, scripts 202 tests).

## Pre-Merge Checklist

- [x] Updated relevant documentation and README (if needed) — not needed: docs already tell users to run `/ide enable` to reconnect and tell plugin authors to delete their discovery file on deactivation; this change makes that recovery work.
- [x] Added/updated tests (if needed)
- [x] Noted breaking changes (if any) — none
- [ ] Validated on required platforms/methods:
  - [ ] MacOS
    - [ ] npm run
    - [ ] npx
    - [ ] Docker
    - [ ] Podman
    - [ ] Seatbelt
  - [ ] Windows
    - [ ] npm run
    - [ ] npx
    - [ ] Docker
  - [x] Linux
    - [x] npm run
    - [x] npx
    - [ ] Docker

prs.title: fix(cli): resolve settings placeholders after loading .env files
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes a load-order defect in `loadSettings()`: settings files were parsed,
expanded against `process.env`, and validated **before** `loadEnvironment()`
injected the variables from `.env` files. Any placeholder whose variable was
defined only in a `.env` file (for example
`"Authorization": "Bearer $GITHUB_MCP_PAT"`) stayed unexpanded, and the literal
string was sent to MCP servers (`400 Bad Format Authorization Header`).

Settings are now read once and resolved **after** `.env` files have been loaded,
so `.env` can be used to keep secrets out of version-controlled `settings.json`,
as the documentation already describes.

## Details

`.env` discovery cannot simply be moved earlier because it depends on settings
itself (`security.folderTrust.enabled`, `advanced.ignoreLocalEnv`,
`advanced.excludedEnvVars`, `tools.sandbox`, `security.auth.selectedType`).
The fix therefore keeps a single read of each file and performs two resolution
passes over the raw data inside `_doLoadSettings` (`packages/cli/src/config/settings.ts`):

1. **Read:** `load()` now only reads and parses JSON (fatal parse errors are
   still recorded here).
2. **Preliminary pass:** `resolve()` expands placeholders against the *shell*
   environment and validates/coerces. These settings feed the workspace trust
   check and `loadEnvironment()` exactly as before, so no security-relevant
   decision changes (this addresses the concern raised by the review bot on the
   earlier community attempt, #28597, which passed raw unexpanded settings into
   those checks).
3. **`loadEnvironment()`** populates `process.env` from the `.env` file.
4. **Final pass:** `resolve()` runs again with `.env` variables available. Only
   this pass records Zod validation warnings, so a `"$VAR"` that becomes valid
   after `.env` loading no longer produces a spurious "expected number, received
   string" warning, and nothing is reported twice.

Other notes:

- `originalSettings` (what gets persisted on save) still holds the unexpanded
  placeholders, so secrets are never written back to disk.
- `GEMINI_CLI_AUTH_OVERRIDE` is now applied once to the raw user settings
  (before cloning into `originalSettings`) instead of separately to both
  objects; observable behaviour is unchanged and it remains visible to
  `loadEnvironment()` for the Cloud Shell / Vertex AI case.
- The legacy theme-name mapping moved after the final pass; it doesn't influence
  trust or `.env` loading.
- Startup cost: each settings file is expanded and validated twice. Files are
  small and `loadSettings()` is cached, so this is negligible.
- Known, inherent limitation (now documented in code and docs): settings that
  control `.env` loading can only reference shell variables, never `.env` ones.
- One existing `eslint-disable` comment became unnecessary and was removed; no
  new ones were added.

## Related Issues

Fixes #28684

## How to Validate

### Automated Unit Tests

Unit tests (exercise the real `_doLoadSettings` pipeline with only `fs`
mocked; `dotenv` parsing is real):

```bash
npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/config/settings.test.ts
```

The new `describe('resolving settings placeholders from .env files')` block
contains 7 tests. Before this fix, the resolution tests fail with the exact
symptom from the issue:

```diff
- "Authorization": "Bearer ghp_secretTokenHere"
+ "Authorization": "Bearer $GITHUB_MCP_PAT"
```

The remaining tests are regression guards: placeholders stay unexpanded in
`originalSettings`, shell variables win over `.env`, a `.env` in an untrusted
workspace is still ignored, the trust check still receives settings that were
resolved and coerced from the shell environment, and no duplicate Zod validation
warnings are emitted across the two passes.

### Manual End-to-End Verification

1. **Create `.env` in the repository root** (ensure `GITHUB_MCP_PAT` is **not** exported in your shell: `unset GITHUB_MCP_PAT`):
   ```env
   GITHUB_MCP_PAT=some-token
   ```
   *(If connecting directly to `https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/`, use a valid GitHub PAT here.)*

2. **Add `mcpServers` to `.gemini/settings.json` in the repository root:**
   ```json
   {
     "mcpServers": {
       "github": {
         "httpUrl": "https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/",
         "headers": {
           "Authorization": "Bearer $GITHUB_MCP_PAT"
         }
       }
     }
   }
   ```
   > **Tip (testing with dummy `some-token` without a real GitHub PAT):** Set `"httpUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:8787/mcp/"` and run `nc -l 8787` in a second terminal to inspect the raw incoming HTTP headers.

3. **Build and start Gemini CLI from the repository root:**
   ```bash
   npm i
   npm run build
   npm run start
   ```
   *(If prompted to trust the workspace folder on startup, select **Trust folder**.)*

4. **Verify:**
   - **With `https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/` and a valid PAT:** Run `/mcp` inside Gemini CLI. `github` connects (`🟢 github - Ready`) instead of failing with `401 Unauthorized` / `400 Bad Format Authorization Header`.
   - **With `nc -l 8787` and dummy `some-token`:** Observe the raw HTTP request in the `nc` terminal:
     ```http
     POST /mcp/ HTTP/1.1
     ...
     authorization: Bearer some-token
     ```
     confirming `Bearer some-token` is sent instead of the literal `Bearer $GITHUB_MCP_PAT`.

5. **Clean up local test files:**
   ```bash
   rm .env
   git checkout -- .gemini/settings.json
   ```

`npm run preflight` passes locally.

- [x] Added/updated tests (if needed)

prs.title: feat(core): make API request headers and body timeouts configurable
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds two settings, `general.requestHeadersTimeoutMs` and `general.requestBodyTimeoutMs`, so users can raise the model API request timeouts under **every auth type**. Today long-thinking turns that stream nothing for more than 5 minutes are aborted with `UND_ERR_BODY_TIMEOUT` and replayed from scratch (billed again), up to `maxAttempts` times. API-key users have no way to change this.

## Details

**Root cause:** `packages/core/src/utils/fetch.ts` hardcoded `defaultBodyTimeout = 300000` and `defaultHeadersTimeout = 60000`. The only override was `updateGlobalFetchTimeouts()`, driven by the `DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT` experiment flag. API-key auth never receives that flag, and even when it is present it only changed the headers timeout.

**Changes:**

- **`fetch.ts`**
  - `defaultBodyTimeout` is now mutable.
  - `updateGlobalFetchTimeouts(headersTimeoutMs, bodyTimeoutMs?)` accepts an optional body timeout and validates both values. It applies them to the global dispatcher, the proxy dispatcher (`setGlobalProxy`) and the safe agent.
  - Adds a small `getGlobalFetchTimeouts()` getter.
  - Existing callers are unaffected.
- **`Config` (core)**
  - New `requestHeadersTimeoutMs` / `requestBodyTimeoutMs` params. Non-positive or non-finite values are ignored with a `debugLogger.warn`.
  - `getRequestTimeoutMs()` now prefers the user setting over the experiment flag.
  - New `getRequestBodyTimeoutMs()`.
  - `refreshAuth()` applies whichever timeouts are configured. If only the body timeout is set, the current headers timeout is kept.
- **Settings schema (CLI):** two new `general.*` number settings (`requiresRestart: true`, not shown in the dialog), wired through `loadCliConfig`.
- **Small related fix:** a `DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT` flag value of `0` was accepted by `getRequestTimeoutMs()` and then made `updateGlobalFetchTimeouts()` throw a `RangeError` during `refreshAuth()`. It is now ignored.
- **Generated files:** regenerated `schemas/settings.schema.json` and `docs/reference/configuration.md` with `npm run schema:settings` and `npm run docs:settings`.

Behavior is unchanged when neither setting is configured.

Example `settings.json` (15 min, per the Gemini latest-model migration checklist):

```json
{
  "general": {
    "requestHeadersTimeoutMs": 900000,
    "requestBodyTimeoutMs": 900000
  }
}
```

Since `settings.json` already supports `${VAR}` expansion, containerized and headless users can drive these from environment variables without a separate env var.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29747
Related to #29693 (the headers-timeout half of the same problem)

## How to Validate

1. Unit tests:
   ```bash
   npm run build --workspace @google/gemini-cli-core
   cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/utils/fetch.test.ts src/config/config.test.ts
   cd ../cli && npx vitest run src/config/settingsSchema.test.ts src/config/config.test.ts src/config/settings.test.ts
   ```
   New tests cover:
   - setting precedence over the experiment flag
   - invalid value handling
   - applying timeouts on `refreshAuth` with API-key auth
   - body-only configuration
   - propagation to the proxy dispatcher and safe agent
   - the flag value `0` edge case
2. Manual check: set `general.requestBodyTimeoutMs` to a small value (e.g. `5000`), run `gemini -p` with a prompt that makes the model think for a long time, and confirm the request is aborted after ~5 s instead of 300 s. Then set a large value and confirm a long silent turn is no longer aborted at 5 minutes.
3. `npm run schema:settings` and `npm run docs:settings` produce no further diff.

## Pre-Merge Checklist

- [x] Updated relevant documentation and README (if needed)
- [x] Added/updated tests (if needed)
- [x] Noted breaking changes (if any): none, both settings are opt-in
- [ ] Validated on required platforms/methods:
  - [ ] MacOS
    - [ ] npm run
    - [ ] npx
    - [ ] Docker
    - [ ] Podman
    - [ ] Seatbelt
  - [ ] Windows
    - [x] npm run (unit tests, typecheck, lint)

prs.title: fix(cli): only auto-nudge genuinely empty continuations and await the nudge
prs.body:
## Summary

When a tool-loop continuation came back with no visible text, `useGeminiStream` automatically sent a nudge (`[System: You successfully executed a tool but returned an empty response...]`). It did this as a fire-and-forget promise from inside the stream loop, and it only checked that the text buffer was empty. As a result the nudge also fired when the stream ended for reasons that are **not** an empty model response, including **after the user pressed Esc**. In that case it silently undid the cancellation and started a new request. This PR only nudges genuinely empty continuations and sequences the nudge properly.

## Details

**Before** (`processGeminiStreamEvents`):

- The nudge condition was just `isContinuation && buffer is empty && attempts < 2`. That is also true when the stream ended with:
  - `UserCancelled`, or a signal aborted by Esc. `submitQuery` then resets `turnCancelledRef` and creates a new `AbortController`, so **the cancel is undone and the model is called again**.
  - `Error`: the error is shown, then another request is sent anyway.
  - `AgentExecutionStopped` / `AgentExecutionBlocked`: a hook asked the agent to stop and the nudge overrode it.
  - `MaxSessionTurns`, `ContextWindowWillOverflow`, `LoopDetected`.
  - `InvalidStream`, e.g. `NO_RESPONSE_TEXT`. Since #28934 the core already retries empty responses with its own nudge (`NO_RESPONSE_TEXT_NUDGE_MESSAGE`) before reporting this, so the CLI nudge was a second, stacked retry.
- The nudge was a floating `submitQueryRef.current?.(...)` call, started before the outer `submitQuery` had flushed its pending history item.

**After:**

- `processGeminiStreamEvents` records when the stream ended abnormally (the events above). It returns a new `StreamProcessingStatus.EmptyContinuation` only for a continuation that ended normally, was not aborted, and produced no text or tool calls.
- `submitQuery` handles that status after flushing the pending history item. It sends the nudge only if:
  - the turn was not cancelled (`turnCancelledRef`),
  - no newer query has started (`activeQueryIdRef`),
  - and the attempt limit is not reached.
- The nudge is **awaited**, so the request stays `Responding` until the nudge has finished.
- The nudge text is unchanged, moved to a module constant. The now-unused `prompt_id` parameter of `processGeminiStreamEvents` is removed.

**Not changed:** the issue also suggests skipping `geminiClient.addHistory` for completed tools in the cancelled path of `handleCompletedTools`. I left that alone. Those responses pair the model's `functionCall` turn that is already in history, and dropping them would leave an unanswered `functionCall`, which is the corruption the surrounding code works to avoid (see the comment in the `modelSwitchedFromQuotaError` branch). Happy to look at it separately if maintainers see a concrete repro.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29071

## How to Validate

```bash
npm run build --workspace @google/gemini-cli-core
cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/ui/hooks/useGeminiStream.test.tsx -t "nudge"
```

New `auto-nudge on empty continuation responses` tests:

- an always-empty continuation is nudged exactly twice, all sends share the prompt id, and everything has finished by the time the continuation's own promise resolves
- no nudge when the stream ended with: an error, an invalid stream, a hook stopping the agent, a hook blocking the agent, a user cancellation, or the session turn limit
- no nudge when the user cancels (`cancelOngoingRequest`) while the continuation is still streaming

7 of these fail on `main` and pass with this change. The existing auto-nudge test (via `handleCompletedTools`) still passes. All CLI hook and `AppContainer` tests pass (68 files, 1278 tests), and typecheck and lint are clean.

prs.title: fix(core): disable interactive credential and SSH prompts in getSafeGitEnv
prs.body:
## Summary

Prevent background Git extension update checks from spawning interactive credential helpers or SSH passphrase/host-key prompts on `/dev/tty`, which previously hijacked `stdin` from Ink's raw-mode TUI and froze the terminal when checking updates for private extensions.

## Details

While `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` was previously set in `getSafeGitEnv()`, several Git authentication pathways still bypass `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT` and open `/dev/tty` or launch interactive prompts directly:
    
    1. **Askpass helpers (`GIT_ASKPASS` / `core.askPass`):** In Git's `git_prompt()` (`prompt.c`), `git_askpass()` is evaluated *before* `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT`.
  If `GIT_ASKPASS` or `SSH_ASKPASS` is set in the environment, Git executes the helper regardless of `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`.

    2. **OpenSSH (`ssh`):** When fetching from a private `git@github.com:...` repository or when `url."git@github.com:".insteadOf` rewrites HTTPS URLs to SSH, `git` spawns `ssh`. OpenSSH does not inspect `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT` and directly opens `/dev/tty` via `read_passphrase()` for encrypted SSH keys or host-key confirmation unless `BatchMode=yes` is enabled.

    3. **GitHub CLI (`gh auth git-credential`) & Git Credential Manager (GCM):** Credential helpers configured in `~/.gitconfig` can trigger interactive prompts unless explicitly disabled via environment variables.
    
    This change hardens `getSafeGitEnv()` in `packages/core/src/utils/gitUtils.ts` by setting:
    - `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT: '0'`
    - `GIT_ASKPASS: ''`
    - `SSH_ASKPASS: ''`
    - `GIT_SSH_COMMAND: 'ssh -o BatchMode=yes'`
    - `GH_PROMPT_DISABLED: '1'`
    - `GCM_INTERACTIVE: 'never'`
    
    Any unauthenticated background fetch now fails fast and silently instead of competing with Ink for `/dev/tty`.

## Related Issues

Fixes #23480

## How to Validate

    1. Run the unit tests for `gitUtils` and `github` extension updates:
       ```bash
       npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/utils/gitUtils.test.ts
       npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/config/extensions/github.test.ts
       ```
    2. Manual reproduction check with a private repository extension:
       - Install an extension from a private GitHub repository.
       - Configure SSH or an unauthenticated credential helper so `git fetch` would normally prompt for credentials/passphrase.
       - Start `gemini -i "hello"` and wait for the background `checkForAllExtensionUpdates` fetch to run.
       - Verify that the background check fails fast without freezing the terminal or swallowing keyboard input on subsequent prompts.

prs.title: fix(core): make file credential store writes atomic and serialized
prs.body:
## Summary

The file-based credential store (`FileKeychain`, used when no native keychain is available) could **silently lose saved credentials** when two processes wrote at the same time. It could also **lock the user out of all saved credentials** if a write was interrupted. This PR makes writes atomic and serializes read-modify-write cycles across processes.

## Details

**Before:**

- `setPassword()` / `deletePassword()` did an unlocked whole-file read-modify-write. With two concurrent writers (e.g. an OAuth token refresh in one terminal and a login in another), both read the same snapshot and the second write erased the first's entry.
- `saveData()` used `fs.writeFile` directly on the live file. A crash or full disk mid-write left a truncated ciphertext. AES-GCM decryption of that always fails, so every later operation threw `Corrupted credentials file detected ...` until the user deleted the file by hand.

**After:**

- **Atomic writes:** `saveData()` writes to a unique `gemini-credentials.json.<uuid>.tmp` (mode `0600`) and `rename`s it over the credentials file. The live file is therefore always a complete old or new version.
  - Transient `EBUSY`/`EPERM` rename failures (Windows, file briefly open elsewhere) are retried with backoff, the same approach as `ProjectRegistry.save()`.
  - The temp file is removed if writing or renaming fails.
- **Cross-process serialization:** `setPassword()` and `deletePassword()` run under an exclusive `proper-lockfile` lock and re-read the file inside the lock.
  - `proper-lockfile` is already a dependency, used by `ProjectRegistry` and trusted folders.
  - `realpath: false` lets the lock be taken before the credentials file exists, so no empty (undecryptable) placeholder file is created.
  - Retries wait up to ~5 s. Stale locks from crashed processes are recovered by `proper-lockfile`'s default stale detection.
- **Reads** (`getPassword`, `findCredentials`) stay lock-free. With atomic renames they always see a complete file.

No change to the file format, encryption, or location.

I did not add a `.bak` self-heal generation, which the issue mentions as optional. With atomic writes, a truncated file can no longer be produced by this code. Happy to add it if maintainers want recovery for files corrupted by older versions.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29054

## How to Validate

```bash
cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/services/fileKeychain.test.ts src/services/gcmTruncationReproduction.test.ts
```

`FileKeychain` had no unit tests. This adds 10, using a real temp directory:

- basic set/get/find/delete, file removal on last delete, encryption at rest, no leftover temp or lock files
- **8 concurrent writers** (separate instances, standing in for separate processes): no entries lost
- **interleaved concurrent set/delete**: no entries dropped or resurrected
- **interrupted write** (partial temp write + `ENOSPC`): the existing file is byte-for-byte unchanged and still decrypts
- the lock is released after a failed write
- transient `EPERM`/`EBUSY` rename is retried; a permanent rename failure cleans up the temp file

The 5 tests covering the bug (both concurrency tests, the interrupted write, and both rename tests) **fail on `main` and pass with this change**.

Note: `keychainService.test.ts` has 5 failures on Windows both on `main` and on this branch. They come from WSL detection in that test's environment, and that test mocks `FileKeychain` entirely, so they are unrelated to this change.

prs.title: fix(cli): round before selecting units in formatDuration
prs.body:
## Summary

Adjusts the duration unit selection logic in
`packages/cli/src/ui/utils/formatters.ts` so that `formatDuration` evaluates
unit threshold boundaries after rounding to display precision.

This prevents durations immediately below a threshold from rendering as the
ceiling value of the lower unit, such as `1000ms` instead of `1.0s`, or `60.0s`
instead of `1m`. These values appear in `/stats` and its `model` and `tools`
subcommands, where latencies are fractional averages.

## Details

Previously, `formatDuration` compared the raw duration against each threshold
(`< 1000` ms, `< 60` s) and applied `Math.round` / `toFixed(1)` afterwards. Each
unit is now selected using the value rounded to that unit's display precision:

- **Milliseconds:** `Math.round(ms)`. Values that round to `1000` or more are
  displayed in seconds.
- **Seconds:** `toFixed(1)`. Values that display as `60.0` or more are displayed
  in minutes.
- **Minutes and hours:** `Math.round(ms / 1000)` whole seconds, followed by the
  existing hour/minute/second breakdown.

Additional notes:

- The seconds branch continues to format with `toFixed(1)`, so output below one
  minute is unchanged except for the boundary values described above.
- Durations of one minute or longer now round to the nearest whole second
  instead of truncating (for example, `60500` ms is displayed as `1m 1s` and
  `3599500` ms as `1h`). This keeps the minute and hour boundaries consistent
  with the rounding used for the smaller units.
- Existing formatting rules are unchanged: non-positive input returns `0s`, zero
  units are omitted, and multi-unit values are composed as `Xh Ym Zs`.

<!-- Concisely describe what this PR changes and why. Focus on impact and
urgency. -->

prs.title: fix(vscode-ide-companion): preserve terminal focus when closing diff tabs
prs.body:
## Summary

When using the VS Code companion extension, approving a file edit in the
Gemini CLI closes the background diff preview and steals keyboard focus from
the integrated terminal. The user then has to click back into the terminal
before every subsequent edit. This change keeps focus in the terminal by
passing VS Code's `preserveFocus` flag when the diff tab is closed.

## Details

The companion opens the diff preview as a background tab (`vscode.diff` with
`preserveFocus: true`) while the user works in the terminal where the Gemini
CLI runs. On `closeDiff`, `DiffManager.closeDiffEditor` in
`packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/diff-manager.ts` closes that tab with
`vscode.window.tabGroups.close(tab)`. VS Code's default behavior when a tab is
closed is to move focus into the editor area. Passing the second positional
argument to `TabGroups.close(tabs, preserveFocus?)` as `true` keeps focus in
its current position (the terminal):

```ts
await vscode.window.tabGroups.close(tab, true);
```

This is a one-line behavioral fix plus a focused regression test.

It resurrects the one-line fix that was reviewed and **approved by @kschaab**
in #23215, which was auto-closed by the 30-day inactivity bot rather than on
merits (the alternative #22331 is closed). #23215 shipped without a test; this
PR adds the missing regression coverage in `src/diff-manager.test.ts`,
asserting `tabGroups.close` is invoked with `preserveFocus = true` when a diff
tab is closed (the test fails on the old `close(tab)` call and passes with the
fix).

## Related Issues

prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes an unhandled promise rejection in `packages/a2a-server/src/agent/task.ts` caused by invoking `this.scheduler.schedule()` with `void`. When tool calls are queued and a task is aborted or cancelled, `CoreToolScheduler` legitimately rejects the promise, triggering an unhandled rejection that terminates the entire `a2a-server` process in Node.js 15+.

## Details

- Attached a targeted `.catch()` handler to `this.scheduler.schedule()` in `scheduleToolCalls`.
- Safely swallows expected abort and cancellation errors (`abortSignal.aborted`, `isAbortError`, and cancellation messages) so that aborting one task does not crash the server or affect other tasks.
- Logs unexpected scheduler errors via `logger.error`.
- Added regression tests in `packages/a2a-server/src/agent/task.test.ts` to ensure cancellation does not emit `unhandledRejection` and unexpected errors are appropriately logged.

## Related Issues

prs.title: fix(core): stop $ patterns corrupting prompt templates and {{args}}
prs.body:
## Summary

Prompt templates in core were filled with `String.prototype.replace(string, string)`. As a result, `$&`, `` $` ``, `$'` and `$$` in model, tool or user text were treated as replacement patterns instead of being inserted as-is. That silently corrupted:

- edit instructions and file contents sent to the LLM edit fixer
- tool output sent to the summarizer
- conversation text sent to the session summarizer

The same problem affected `{{args}}` substitution in custom commands, including inside `!{...}` shell commands. This PR fixes all of these call sites by reusing the existing safe helpers. It adds no new utilities.

## Details

**1. `$` replacement patterns (the reported bug).** For example, `'$&'` in an edit's `old_string` was replaced by the placeholder token itself (`{old_string}`), so the model received a different search string from the one that failed.

**2. Placeholder injection in `llm-edit-fixer` (found while fixing #1).** The five placeholders were filled one after another. Any input that contained a *later* placeholder got substituted into instead of the template. Example: an instruction that mentions `{old_string}`, or code containing `{error}`. That moved user/file content into the wrong section of the prompt.

**Changes:**

- `packages/core/src/utils/llm-edit-fixer.ts`, `packages/core/src/utils/summarizer.ts`, `packages/core/src/services/sessionSummaryService.ts`:
  - Use the existing single-pass `safeTemplateReplace()` from `textUtils.ts`. It is already used by the Conseca policy prompts and already tested for `$&` and double-interpolation.
  - The templates switch from `{key}` to that helper's `{{key}}` placeholder syntax. Each placeholder appears exactly once, so the generated prompts are unchanged for normal input.
- `packages/cli/src/services/prompt-processors/shellProcessor.ts`:
  - All five `replaceAll(SHORTHAND_ARGS_PLACEHOLDER, …)` calls now use the existing `safeLiteralReplace()`.
  - Custom command arguments containing `$` patterns now reach the prompt and the shell command unchanged.
  - The policy check still runs on the final resolved command.

`bugCommand.ts` also uses `.replace('{…}', …)`, but its values go through `encodeURIComponent`, which encodes `$`, so it is not affected and is left as-is.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29044

## How to Validate

```bash
npm run build --workspace @google/gemini-cli-core
cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/utils/llm-edit-fixer.test.ts src/utils/summarizer.test.ts src/services/sessionSummaryService.test.ts src/utils/textUtils.test.ts
cd ../cli && npx vitest run src/services/prompt-processors/shellProcessor.test.ts
```

There are 6 new regression tests: $-patterns in all five edit-fixer inputs, placeholder injection in the edit fixer, $-patterns in summarizer and session-summary input, and $-patterns in raw and shell-escaped `{{args}}`. **All 6 fail on `main` and pass with this change.** The existing prompt-construction tests (including the exact-match summarizer prompt test) pass unchanged.

Manual check: create a custom command with `prompt = "Echo: {{args}}"` and run `/<command> cost is $& or $'`. On `main` the prompt shows `cost is {{args}} or …`. With this change it shows the input exactly.

## Pre-Merge Checklist

- [x] Added/updated tests (if needed)

Agency in Autopilot mode has a tendency to take any question as a go-ahead to start and perform actions.  I told it not to, recorded rules to ensure that it only *answers* questions without performing any long-running action.  Now it is asking me each question five times in a row.  For example:

Waiting.
Waiting.

When told to stop doing that, it does this:

.

.
.

Which is basically the same thing.  The harness rules and the command to not go off on its own but instead just answer questions, conflict with each other.

Add the following copilot instruction: Ask a confirmation question exactly once. Reply with a single short sentence at most, and only if the user is not the sender; otherwise stay silent.

Then start an operation and interrupt it in the middle, and ask it about something.

The model asks once about continuing and stops repeating the question in various ways.

issues.title: Regression: skill tool cannot find valid skills in ~/.agents/skills

labels.name: area:platform-windows
labels.description: Windows-specific: PowerShell, cmd, Git Bash, WSL, Windows Terminal

labels.name: area:tools
labels.description: Built-in tools: file editing, shell, search, LSP, git, and tool call behavior

issues.body:
## Description

The `skill` tool cannot find or invoke a valid skill installed under `~/.agents/skills`, even though the skill directory and `SKILL.md` are present.

This appears to be a regression or an incomplete fix related to #2230, which is closed.

## Environment

- Copilot CLI: `1.0.78`
- OS: Windows
- Skill path: `C:\Users\omzig\.agents\skills\setup-matt-pocock-skills\SKILL.md`

## Reproduction

1. Create or install a skill at `~/.agents/skills/setup-matt-pocock-skills/SKILL.md`.
2. Ensure its frontmatter includes:

   ```yaml
   ---
   name: setup-matt-pocock-skills
   description: Configure this repo for the engineering skills.
   disable-model-invocation: true
   ---
   ```

3. Invoke the skill tool with `setup-matt-pocock-skills`.

## Actual result

The tool returns:

```text
Skill not found: setup-matt-pocock-skills
```

The skill is also absent from the tool's available-skill registry, despite the file being present and having valid frontmatter.

## Expected result

Skills in `~/.agents/skills` should either be discovered by the CLI automatically or produce a clear configuration/status indication explaining that the directory is unsupported.

## Workaround

Copying or linking the skill into a directory that the CLI does discover appears to be required.

## Additional validation: minimal test skill

To rule out a problem specific to the original skill, I created a minimal skill with valid frontmatter at:

`C:\Users\omzig\.agents\skills\test-skill\SKILL.md`

Its contents were:

```markdown
---
name: test-skill
description: A simple test skill that confirms whether skills installed in ~/.agents/skills are discovered and invoked.
---

# Test Skill

When this skill is invoked, respond with exactly:

`test-skill loaded successfully`
```

Invoking `skill(test-skill)` produced the same result:

```text
Skill not found: test-skill
```

This validates that the failure is with out-of-box discovery of `~/.agents/skills`, not with the original skill's complexity or frontmatter.

## Follow-up validation: supported path works

I moved the same minimal `test-skill` directory from:

`C:\Users\omzig\.agents\skills\test-skill`

to:

`C:\Users\omzig\.copilot\skills\test-skill`

After moving it, invoking `skill(test-skill)` succeeded and the skill returned:

```text
test-skill loaded successfully
```

This confirms that the skill content and frontmatter are valid. The failure is specifically that `~/.agents/skills` is not included in the CLI's out-of-box discovery paths, while `~/.copilot/skills` is.

issues.title: [Bug] gemini-4-argon: unexplained full cache miss on unchanged prefix, cacheReadTokens > inputTokens, and no cache-write reporting
issues.body:
**TL;DR:** In a 58-call `gemini-4-argon` session, prompt-cache telemetry shows one unexplained full miss on an unchanged prefix, one impossible accounting value, and no cache-write reporting. Looking for confirmation of whether these are expected.

Version: Copilot CLI 1.0.98, macOS, `gemini-4-argon` via `/chat/completions`, reasoning effort `high`.

## Observations (from `session.usage_record` / `session.usage_checkpoint` in `events.jsonl`)

**1. Full cache miss with no client-side prefix change (call 6)**

| Call | inputTokens | cacheReadTokens | TTFT (ms) | tools |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 5 | 96,311 | 82,077 | 4,290 | 76 (35,356 tok) |
| 6 | 104,892 | **0** | 5,820 | 76 (35,356 tok) |
| 7 | 107,317 | 104,893 | 4,032 | 76 (35,356 tok) |

Calls were about 10s apart, same tool set, no compaction. Call 7 read back the entire call 6 prompt. I cannot tell from client telemetry whether this is a backend routing or eviction effect. Call 6 was the first call over 100k input tokens, but calls 7 onwards (107k+) hit the cache, so it is not a persistent threshold.

**2. `cacheReadTokens` greater than `inputTokens` (call 36)**

`inputTokens: 197,564`, `cacheReadTokens: 225,900`. A cache read larger than the prompt looks like an accounting error, and it affects the billed `cache_read` token count.

**3. No cache-write reporting for Argon**

All 58 Argon calls report `cacheWriteTokens: 0`. In my other local sessions, Claude and GPT models report `cacheWriteTokens > 0` on every call. `cache_config` shows `marks_system_prompt: false` and `marks_conversation: false` for Argon, but also for Claude, so that flag alone does not explain the difference.

**4. Partial hits**

Reads are often slightly below the previous call's input (for example call 11: 106,615 read vs 108,664 prior input), so hits are prefix-granular, not whole-prompt. Probably expected, noted for completeness.

## Not claimed

Idle-gap misses (calls 10, 16, 48, 54) look like normal expiry or a tool-set change. A 382s gap hit and a 1,439s gap missed, so the TTL is somewhere in between and I have not measured it.

## Questions

1. Is the call 6 miss expected for implicit caching on this endpoint?
2. Is call 36 (`cacheRead` > `input`) a known accounting issue?
3. Is cache-write reporting intentionally absent for Gemini on `/chat/completions`?

## Evidence

- `providerCallId` for call 6: `E8D4:25658D:1770EE5:18C49E5:6ACFEF83`
- `providerCallId` for call 36: `E265:32FBDA:229ECFA:26A5860:6ACFFA46`
- The full per-call table can be attached if useful.

### Describe the bug

In assisted approval mode, when steering the conversation or asking a question during plan mode, the CLI's response may briefly appear and then disappear from the screen. The agent continues with a follow-up that refers to the missing explanation, but the explanation is no longer available in the conversation, even after expanding the `Thought for` line. N/A — not provided.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Start a session in assisted approval mode and enter plan mode.
2. While the plan is in progress, send a steering message or ask a question.
3. Observe whether the CLI's response appears briefly, then disappears as the agent continues.
4. Expand the associated `Thought for` line and check whether the response is available there.

issues.title: Allow unlimited (or higher) prompt history via `commandHistoryMaxSize`
issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

Copilot CLI keeps only the last 50 prompts for Ctrl+R and Up/Down history by default. The `commandHistoryMaxSize` setting can raise this, but only to 1,000 ([docs](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-cli-reference/cli-config-dir-reference#configuration-file-settings)). Once the limit is reached, older prompts are permanently dropped. For heavy users, 1,000 prompts only covers a short period.

### Proposed solution

Raise the maximum allowed value for `commandHistoryMaxSize`, or support an unlimited option (for example, `0`), so users can retain their full prompt history.

### Example prompts or workflows

- Set `"commandHistoryMaxSize": 0` in `~/.copilot/config.json` to keep all prompts indefinitely.
- Use Ctrl+R to find a prompt written weeks or months ago.
- Recall long, carefully crafted prompts without rewriting them.

### Additional context

Requested by an enterprise customer. Other agentic CLIs (e.g. Claude Code) don't impose a comparable cap on prompt history.

issues.title: Allow users to cancel or remove enqueued messages before they are executed

labels.name: area:input-keyboard
labels.description: Keyboard shortcuts, keybindings, copy/paste, clipboard, mouse, and text input

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

There is no way to cancel or remove a message or slash command that has been queued (via `Ctrl+Q` / `Ctrl+Enter`) while the agent is busy or during `/compact`. Once enqueued, messages are automatically processed in order when the agent finishes — even if the user has changed their mind or made a mistake.

### Proposed solution

Add a mechanism to view and selectively cancel queued messages before they are executed. This could take the form of:
- A `/queue` command to list pending messages, with `/queue cancel <n>` to remove a specific entry.
- An interactive UI overlay (e.g., triggered by a keybinding) showing the queue with the ability to navigate and delete items.
- A keybinding (e.g., `Ctrl+Shift+Q`) to clear the entire queue at once.

This would benefit Copilot CLI users by:
- Preventing accidental or unwanted actions from queued messages the user no longer intends to send.
- Complementing existing cancellation behavior (`Ctrl+C` for active operations, `Escape` for specific commands like `/compact`) with control over *pending* operations.
- Improving confidence in the queueing workflow, encouraging users to queue more freely knowing they can course-correct.

### Example prompts or workflows

1. **Accidental queue during compaction** — User sends a message during `/compact` (auto-queued per v0.0.389), then realizes it was wrong. They want to remove it before compaction finishes and the message is sent to the model.
2. **Multiple queued commands** — User queues several slash commands with `Ctrl+Q` while the agent is working, then decides the third one is no longer needed. They run `/queue` to see the list and `/queue cancel 3` to drop it.
3. **Clear entire queue** — User has queued several messages but the agent's response changes their plan entirely. They press `Ctrl+Shift+Q` (or run `/queue clear`) to discard all pending messages and start fresh.
4. **Review before execution** — User wants to double-check what's queued before the agent finishes. They press a keybinding to see a transient overlay of queued items, then dismiss it or remove specific entries.

### Additional context

- Current queueing was introduced in v0.0.394 (`Ctrl+D`) and the keybinding was later changed to `Ctrl+Q` / `Ctrl+Enter` in v0.0.407.
- Auto-queueing during `/compact` was added in v0.0.389.
- Existing cancel mechanisms (`Ctrl+C`, `Escape`) only affect the *currently running* operation, not messages waiting in the queue.

- bubblewrap: 0.11.1
- `kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns`: 1
- `kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone`: 1
- `user.max_user_namespaces`: 13625
- `user.max_net_namespaces`: 13625

## Diagnostics

Bubblewrap test succeeds:

```sh
bwrap --unshare-user --unshare-net \\
  --ro-bind / / \\
  --proc /proc --dev /dev \\
  /usr/bin/true
# exit 0
```

The `/etc/apparmor.d/bwrap-userns-restrict` profile is loaded, along with `unpriv_bwrap`.

A plain `unshare` test fails while writing `uid_map`:

```sh
unshare --user --map-root-user /usr/bin/true
# write to /proc/self/uid_map: Operation not permitted
```

At the time of Copilot tool-call failures, the kernel audit log showed:

```text
apparmor="AUDIT" operation="userns_create" profile="unconfined"
comm="unshare" requested="userns_create" target="unprivileged_userns"
apparmor="DENIED" operation="capable" profile="unprivileged_userns"
comm="unshare" capability=21 capname="sys_admin"
```

The same `userns_create` transition followed by `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` denial appeared for both observed attempts.

## Expected behavior

Copilot CLI should successfully initialize its tool sandbox on this Ubuntu/AppArmor setup, or report a precise actionable cause if the sandbox preflight relies on an `unshare` path that is blocked while bubblewrap itself can create the required namespaces.

Is this a known compatibility issue with Ubuntu's restricted unprivileged user namespaces, or is there a supported configuration/workaround that does not require weakening AppArmor restrictions globally?

issues.title: Copilot App: session name keeps reverting to a linked (merged) PR's title after an explicit rename
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

In the Copilot app, once a session has a pull request linked to it because the agent opened that PR from the session, the app replaces the session's name with the PR title. If the session is renamed afterwards, the new name doesn't stick: some time later it is reset to the PR title again. This keeps happening after the PR has been merged, with no new activity on the PR.

There is no way to unlink a merged PR from a session, so a long-running session that once opened a small side PR keeps losing its name.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a local (branch) session in a repository and give it a name, e.g. "My topic".
2. In that session, have the agent open a small pull request with the app's built-in create-pull-request tool. The session name changes to the PR title.
3. Merge the PR.
4. Rename the session back to "My topic" (via the agent's rename-session tool with `force`, which reports success).
5. Keep working in the session. Some time later, the session name is the merged PR's title again.

Observed twice in one session: the explicit rename reverted to the PR title within about 30 minutes the first time and within about 4.5 hours the second time. Nothing happened on the PR in between; it had been merged for hours.

### Expected behavior

An explicit rename, by the user or by the agent on the user's request, persists. The linked PR's title should at most be the default name for a session that was never named. Alternatively, it should be possible to unlink a PR from a session.

### Actual behavior

The linked PR's title periodically overwrites the explicit session name, even for a merged PR.

### Additional context

PRs opened from the same session with the `gh` CLI instead of the app's PR tool don't link to the session and don't affect its name.

issues.title: Cloud agent: "Registry only" MCP policy blocks all repo-configured MCP servers — proxy-bridged configs can't be fingerprinted ("unable to compute fingerprint from local configuration")
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

## Describe the bug

With the org MCP policy set to **Registry only**, the Copilot **cloud agent** silently drops every repo-configured MCP server, even when the server is present in the configured registry with a matching package identity. Only the platform defaults (`github-mcp-server`, `playwright`) reach the session.

The CLI log inside the session (`~/.copilot/logs/process-*.log`) shows:

```
[DEBUG] Registry <org-registry>: servers will be verified against this registry
[ERROR] MCP server "mcp-server-A" filtered: Could not verify server "mcp-server-A" against registry <org-registry>: unable to compute fingerprint from local configuration
[ERROR] MCP server "mcp-server-B" filtered: Could not verify server "mcp-server-B" against registry <org-registry>: unable to compute fingerprint from local configuration
```

With the policy switched to **Allow all**, the same servers mount and their tools work.

## Root cause (from reading the shipped runtime)

In the cloud agent, the CLI never sees the repo's MCP config. cca-engine (`dist-cca-v3/index.js`) replaces every proxy-discovered server with a bridge config:

```js
// ~line 80361
discoveredServers[name] = toBridgedMcpServerConfig(name, void 0, mcpProxyUrl);
```

```js
// ~line 79716
function toBridgedMcpServerConfig(serverName, serverConfig, mcpProxyUrl, customAgentName, customAgentVersion) {
  const args = [BRIDGE_SCRIPT_PATH, `--proxy-url=${mcpProxyUrl}`, `--server-name=${serverName}`];
  if (serverConfig) {
    args.push(`--config=${Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(serverConfig)).toString("base64")}`);
  }
  ...
  return { type: "local", command: process.execPath, args, ..., tools: ["*"] };
}
```

So for every third-party server the CLI receives `node <bridge-script> --proxy-url=… --server-name=…`. The CLI derives a stdio server's identity from its command (`npx`→npm, `uvx`→pypi, `dotnet`→nuget, `docker`, `mcpb`; see the explanation in mindovermachine-dev/product-cli#20). `node` maps to nothing, so no fingerprint can be computed and the server is filtered.

- At line 80361 `serverConfig` is `void 0`, so even the base64 `--config` arg is omitted. The original config is not available to the CLI at all.
- Built-in servers pass only because they are marked runtime-authored (`markRuntimeAuthoredServer`, gated by `copilot_swe_agent_mcp_builtin_provenance`) and are exempt from third-party policy.
- From code reading (not tested end-to-end): remote/HTTP configs are bridged the same way when `mcpProxyUrl` is set (`toSdkMcpServerConfig`, ~line 79741), so switching to an `http` server does not avoid this in the cloud agent.

**Net effect:** under "Registry only", no repo-configured (or custom-agent) MCP server can ever pass verification in the cloud agent.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Org settings → Copilot → Policies: **MCP servers in Copilot** = Enabled; **MCP registry URL** = a spec-compliant registry; registry access = **Registry only**.
2. Registry entry named `mcp-server-A`:
```json
   {
     "name": "mcp-server-A",
     "version": "0.0.2",
     "packages": [{
       "registryType": "oci",
       "identifier": "<registry-host>/<path>/mcp-server-A",
       "version": "0.0.2",
       "transport": { "type": "stdio" }
     }]
   }
```
   Verified: `GET <org-registry>/v0.1/servers/mcp-server-A/versions/latest` returns 200 with `server.name == "mcp-server-A"`.
3. Repo → Settings → Copilot → coding agent → MCP configuration:
```json
   {
     "mcpServers": {
       "mcp-server-A": {
         "type": "local",
         "command": "docker",
         "args": ["run", "-i", "--rm", "<registry-host>/<path>/mcp-server-A:0.0.2"],
         "tools": ["*"]
       }
     }
   }
```
4. Assign a task to the cloud agent.
5. Observe:
   - cca-engine logs `Discovered MCP server: mcp-server-A` and `MCP servers configured for session: …, mcp-server-A, …`.
   - No `MCP server 'mcp-server-A': pending` / `connected` lifecycle events appear.
   - The CLI log shows the `unable to compute fingerprint` error above.

## What we ruled out

- **Registry reachability/auth:** Cloud Run access logs show 200s for the CLI's requests during the session.
- **Name lookup:** before aliasing, the error was `Not found in registry`. After making the registry resolve the config key, the error moved to the fingerprint stage.
- **Local config shape:** `type: local` vs `stdio`, `-e VAR` vs `--env=VAR`, and minimal args all gave the identical error.
- **Package type:** `registryType` `oci` vs `docker` gave the identical error.
- **Policy fetch:** succeeds (`servers will be verified against this registry`). This is not the fail-closed family in #4378 / #2498 / #4346.

## Expected behavior

Repo-configured servers that match a registry entry should be verified against their **original** configuration. Options include passing `serverConfig` into the bridge and fingerprinting from it, or running the registry check in cca-engine/the MCP proxy before bridging. Registry-matching servers should then mount under "Registry only".

## Affected version

- Surface: Copilot cloud agent (Copilot Business, `api.business.githubcopilot.com`)
- Runtime: `runtime-cca-vendored-06412f43e9f392ebb48daa02136895268f688937` (also seen on `47b2e066…`)
- Feature flags present: `copilot_swe_agent_new_out_proc_mcp`, `copilot_swe_agent_mcp_builtin_provenance`
- Date observed: 2026-10-15

## Related

- mindovermachine-dev/product-cli#20: same error in the local CLI; documents the command→identity mapping.
- #4378: cloud agent silently dropping user-configured MCP servers (different trigger: policy fetch 401/403).
- Separate but adjacent: the registry lookup uses the config key as the server name, but config keys can't contain `.`. Spec-style reverse-DNS registry names (e.g. `io.example/server`) are therefore unmatchable from repo config without registry-side aliasing. Happy to file this separately.

issues.title: Command hooks always hit timeoutSec after the first JS-side child spawn (hook exits in ~20 ms but stays a zombie until timeout)
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

In a long-running interactive session, every command hook starts hitting the full `timeoutSec` (5 s), even though the hook process exits in about 20 ms. Each tool call runs up to three hooks (`preToolUse`, `permissionRequest`, `postToolUse`), so every tool call can take up to 15 s longer. On one machine this added 4 to 8 hours of waiting per day across sessions.

From inside an affected process, it looks like the CLI stops noticing when hook child processes exit:

- **The hook process exits immediately but isn't reaped.** I sampled `ps --ppid <copilot pid>` every 200 ms. Each hook's `bash` child went `<defunct>` (zombie) within milliseconds and stayed that way for 4.6 to 4.9 s, until the 5 s timeout fired:
  ```
  2484229 zombie_for=4.6s
  2494373 zombie_for=4.9s
  2497495 zombie_for=4.9s
  ```
- **The hook script itself finishes fast.** I timestamped the hook script at start, at stdin EOF, and at the end. In the affected process, stdin reached EOF about 7 ms after start and the script finished about 13 ms later, yet the CLI still logged `HookTimeoutError: Hook command timed out after 5 seconds` for those calls.
- **Nothing else holds the pipe open.** I scanned `/proc/*/fd` 0.5 s after each hook started for any other holder of the hook's stdout pipe. Across 22 timed-out hooks, none was found.
- **Fresh processes are fine.** The same hook config runs normally (around 20 ms) in a new interactive session and in `copilot -p`.

**What seems to trigger it:** in 6 of the 7 affected processes, the first timeout came shortly (13 s to 7 min) after the first clipboard write, which spawns a child process from the JS side:
```
07:53:38 [WARNING] writeToClipboard: clip.exe failed; relied on OSC 52: Error: clip.exe exited with code 1
07:54:45 [WARNING] [rust:hooks] Hook from ".../hooks/orca.json" timed out; allowing processing to proceed: HookTimeoutError: Hook command timed out after 5 seconds
```
The 7th was a resumed session that started an MCP server and a native extension at launch, then timed out on its first hook. After the first timeout, the process never recovered: one process logged 2,960 timeouts over about 6 hours. Processes without hooks configured were unaffected even after clipboard writes.

One possible cause, which I haven't verified: the JS runtime (libuv) installs its own `SIGCHLD` handler when it first spawns a child. If that handler replaces the Rust hook runner's handler instead of chaining to it, the runner would never be told its hook children have exited. It would then only find out when its timeout fires and it cleans up. That matches both the zombies lasting until the timeout and the state starting at the first JS-side spawn.

This started on October 13, when 1.0.96 was installed. From October 7 to 12 the same hook config ran about 2,000 to 4,000 hooks a day with zero timeouts. Since then, 16%, 40% and 61% of hooks per day have timed out (1.0.96 to 1.0.98).

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.98 (also seen on 1.0.96 and 1.0.97)

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Put any fast command hook in `~/.copilot/hooks/` for `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse` and `PermissionRequest`, for example a script that prints `{}` and reads stdin. My setup is the [Orca](https://github.com/stablyai/orca) agent hook with `"timeoutSec": 5`.
2. Start an interactive `copilot` session and run a few tool calls. The hooks finish in about 20 ms.
3. Do something that spawns a child process from the JS side, such as copying a response to the clipboard. On WSL this runs `clip.exe`.
4. Run more tool calls. Every hook now takes the full `timeoutSec` and logs `HookTimeoutError`, and `ps --ppid <copilot pid>` shows the hook's shell as `<defunct>` for about `timeoutSec`.

### Expected behavior

The CLI should reap a hook as soon as its process exits and continue right away. A hook that finishes in 20 ms shouldn't block a tool call for 5 s.

### Additional context

- OS: Ubuntu on WSL2 (kernel 6.18.54.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2), x86_64
- Shell: bash. Installed via npm (`@github/copilot`), Node v24
- Started with `--yolo`
- Workaround: lower `timeoutSec` or remove the hook config.

issues.title: /restart fails when the CLI was launched with --new-session-id

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

issues.body:
### What happened

Launching the CLI with `--new-session-id <uuid>` and then running `/restart` fails every time:

```
error: the argument '--new-session-id <id>' cannot be used with '--session-id <id>'

Usage: copilot --log-dir <directory> --plugin-dir <directory> --add-dir <directory> --additional-mcp-config <json> --yolo

For more information, try '--help'.
```

By the time this surfaces the foreground session has already been shut down, so the restart is not recoverable.

### Repro

1. `copilot --new-session-id 11111111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555` (any fresh UUID)
2. Run `/restart`

This matters for embedding hosts, which pass `--new-session-id` on every session launch, so `/restart` is permanently unusable there rather than occasionally.

### Cause

`/restart` rebuilds the child argv from `process.argv.slice(2)`, strips the session-selection flags, then appends `--session-id <current session id>`.

In `cli-main.js` (1.0.98) the strip helper removes `-r`, `--resume`, `--resume=`, `--session-id`, `--session-id=`, `--continue`, `--cloud`, `-i`, `--interactive`, `--interactive=`, `--experimental`, `--no-experimental`, `--fleet` and `-C`. `--new-session-id` is absent from that list, so it survives into the restart argv next to the freshly appended `--session-id`, and the parser declares the two mutually exclusive.

The same rebuilt argv is persisted for the supervised restart path, so both the supervised and unsupervised paths fail identically.

### Expected

The strip helper should drop `--new-session-id` and `--new-session-id=<uuid>`, consuming the following value in the bare form, exactly as it already does for `--session-id`. The session exists by restart time, so re-asserting a creation ID is both wrong and rejected.

### Workaround

Patching the strip helper locally to treat `--new-session-id` like `--session-id` resolves it, but the file lives in the extracted package folder and the fix is lost on every CLI update.

### Version

1.0.98 on Windows, win32-x64.
