issues.title: Regression: sandboxed git has no way to use a credential that differs from the Copilot/gh sign-in identity

labels.name: area:permissions
labels.description: Tool approval, security boundaries, sandbox mode, and directory restrictions

labels.name: area:tools
labels.description: Built-in tools: file editing, shell, search, LSP, git, and tool call behavior

issues.body:
### Summary

`sandbox.auth.git` authenticates sandboxed git using only the Copilot/gh sign-in identity. There's no way to supply a different credential (e.g. fine-grained PAT). The sandbox injects an empty, highest-precedence `credential.helper` override into every sandboxed git subprocess, discarding any helper configured in `.git/config`. This is independent of `auth.git`/`auth.gh` settings.

Related tickets #4804 #1460 

### Regression marker

 v1.0.92  (2026-10-05) changelog: "Sandboxed scripts that run Git now authenticate with masked credentials and SSH remote rewrites."  v1.0.91  does not exhibit this.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.92

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

```bash
mkdir repo && cd repo && git init
cat > /tmp/fake-helper.sh << 'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
echo "username=alice"
echo "password=hunter2"
EOF
chmod +x /tmp/fake-helper.sh
git config --local credential.helper '!/tmp/fake-helper.sh'

# Works on the host:
printf 'protocol=https\nhost=example.com\n\n' | git credential fill
# -> username=alice / password=hunter2

# Fails identically inside the sandbox:
copilot --sandbox --add-dir . -p "printf 'protocol=https\nhost=example.com\n\n' | git credential fill"
```

Host: helper fills the fake credential correctly.
Sandboxed: `bash
git config --show-origin --show-scope --get-all credential.helper
` shows the local helper present, but a trailing  command line: scope entry with an empty value overrides it ( env | grep GIT_CONFIG  shows  GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=6 ,  GIT_CONFIG_KEY_5=credential.helper ,  GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_5=  empty).  git credential fill  returns nothing; real-world  git clone / pull  against a credential-helper-only remote fails with  `fatal: unable to get password from user` .

### Expected behavior

Sandboxed git should have a supported way to authenticate as an identity other than whichever account Copilot itself is signed in as :

- Let the masking process accept a user-supplied credential.
Extend `sandbox.auth.git` (or `sandbox.credentials.envVars`) to accept a PAT/token supplied by the user (e.g. via a settings field or an env var name to mask), and have the masking proxy substitute that credential into git's HTTPS requests instead of always deriving it from the Copilot/gh sign-in session. This would let native masking work for repos/orgs the signed-in identity can't access, without exposing the raw token to the sandboxed process.

- Don't force out a user-configured `credential.helper` when native masking isn't handling that credential.
Today, the sandbox always injects an empty, highest-precedence `credential.helper` override into every sandboxed git subprocess, regardless of `auth.git`/`auth.gh`. This unconditionally discards any helper a user configured in `.git/config`, even when `auth.git` is off and no native masking is in play for that request. Could be opt-in/configurable, e.g. a sandbox policy flag (`sandbox.auth.gitCredentialHelper` or similar) that leaves a user-configured helper intact when native git masking isn't being used for that repo/host, so a custom helper can still supply credentials for identities the built-in masking doesn't cover.

issues.title: Regression: default-context Sol models rejected before first prompt after tool definitions grow from 15K to ~260K tokens
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Beginning around 2026-10-14, `gpt-5.6-sol` and `gpt-6.1-sol` at the default context tier fail before accepting a prompt:

```
compaction_static_context_blocked: Static system messages and tool definitions exceed the model's usable context budget. Reduce static context or switch to a larger-context model.
```

Selecting `long_context` immediately makes the same model, session, MCP configuration, and prompt work. Usage telemetry then reports `maxPromptTokens: 922000` and approximately 258K-260K tool-definition tokens.

This did not occur previously with the same broad tool configuration. A successful October 9 session on CLI 1.0.92 used `gpt-5.6-sol` with the default tier and reported 615 tools / 15,457 tool-definition tokens. The current configuration reports 676 tools / approximately 260,000 tool-definition tokens: roughly 10% more tools but a 17x increase in tool tokens.

The local standalone MCP configuration was unchanged during this period. A historical default-tier session that worked before the rollout also failed with the same warning when resumed on October 14.

### Affected versions

- GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.93, 1.0.97, and 1.0.98
- macOS 26.7.1, Apple Silicon
- Models: `gpt-5.6-sol` and `gpt-6.1-sol`
- Agency versions observed during the rollout window: 2026.10.13.x and 2026.10.14.3

Because 1.0.93 also began failing after the rollout window, this may involve remotely supplied tool catalogs, Agency integration, or context-budget metadata rather than only a 1.0.97 client change.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start Copilot CLI with a broad enterprise MCP/tool configuration.
2. Select `gpt-6.1-sol` with the default context tier.
3. Submit a short prompt.
4. Observe `compaction_static_context_blocked`, followed by `No response was returned`.
5. Switch only the context tier to `long_context`.
6. Resubmit the prompt; it succeeds.
7. Repeat with `gpt-5.6-sol`; default context fails and `long_context` succeeds.

### Expected behavior

The default tier should continue working with a tool configuration that worked previously. At minimum, the CLI should:

- avoid offering a model/tier combination that cannot fit its own static context;
- lazy-load or defer tool schemas instead of eagerly injecting hundreds of definitions;
- identify the largest static-context contributors;
- clearly report the effective default-tier prompt budget.

### Additional evidence

- October 9, CLI 1.0.92: 615 tools, 15,457 tool tokens, default-tier `gpt-5.6-sol` worked.
- October 14-15: approximately 258K-260K tool tokens; default-tier Sol models fail before a model request.
- `long_context` reports a 922K prompt allowance and succeeds without changing the tool setup.
- Related issues: #5042 and #3542.

Please investigate whether tool schemas or descriptions changed around October 13-14, whether more definitions are now eagerly materialized, or whether static-context token accounting/default-tier reserves changed. I can provide redacted event excerpts or confidential debug logs privately.

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Gradle cannot execute even an offline `help` task inside the Copilot CLI macOS sandbox when outbound and local networking are configured as allowed.

The Gradle daemon starts successfully and listens on localhost, but the Gradle client cannot connect to it:

```text
java.net.SocketException: Operation not permitted
```

The identical command succeeds with the Copilot sandbox disabled. Restarting Copilot with the sandbox enabled does not resolve the failure.

### Affected version

Copilot CLI `1.0.95`; also observed on `1.0.93`.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. On macOS, enable the Copilot CLI sandbox and allow both outbound and local networking. The configured network settings are:

   ```json
   {
     "allowOutbound": true,
     "allowLocalNetwork": true,
     "allowedHosts": [],
     "blockedHosts": []
   }
   ```

   `/sandbox policy` reports outbound and local networking as allowed.

2. In a Gradle 9.1.0 wrapper project with Java 21 selected, ask Copilot to execute:

   ```bash
   ./gradlew --offline --no-daemon --console=plain --stacktrace help
   ```

3. Gradle launches a single-use daemon to honor the project's JVM settings. The daemon binds a localhost port, but the client connection fails with `Operation not permitted`, before any task executes.

4. Disable the Copilot sandbox and repeat the identical command. It succeeds, executing only `help`.

### Expected behavior

When local networking is explicitly allowed, Gradle should be able to connect to its localhost daemon.

If that setting intentionally excludes host-loopback connections, the policy display should make this distinction clear and document a supported way to permit the required connection without disabling the entire sandbox.

### Additional context

**Environment:** macOS `26.6.2`, ARM64; Gradle wrapper `9.1.0`; Java Amazon Corretto `21.0.6.7.1`.

The command uses offline mode, so dependency downloads are not involved. `--no-daemon` still launches a single-use daemon in this project.

**Kernel-confirmed denial**

In one sandbox-enabled run, the daemon listened on `127.0.0.1:53774`. The macOS kernel log recorded:

```text
Sandbox: java(5913) deny(1) network-outbound remote:*:53774
```

**Effective policy from a separate failing run**

Copilot's debug log identified the generated policy used for the command. Its network section was:

```json
{
  "network": {
    "egress": {
      "default": "deny"
    },
    "ingress": {
      "default": "allow",
      "hostLoopback": "deny"
    },
    "runtimeConfig": {
      "networkProxy": "http://127.0.0.1:55437"
    }
  }
}
```

In that run, the Gradle daemon listened on `127.0.0.1:55438`, not the proxy port `55437`.

This appears consistent with the client being denied a direct host-loopback connection despite `allowLocalNetwork: true`. Gradle's daemon protocol uses raw TCP, so the HTTP proxy cannot carry that connection.

Please investigate whether `allowLocalNetwork` is being mapped correctly to the effective macOS policy, or whether a separate supported host-loopback permission is required.

**Related reports**

- [github/copilot-cli#4854](https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/4854): a Windows `/sandbox policy` display issue. Unlike that report, the display here says networking is allowed, while the generated policy and kernel denial demonstrate an actual blocked connection.
- [github/copilot-cli#4516](https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/4516): JVM filesystem-grant failures on macOS, with a recent comment also describing remote-repository/proxy problems. This report concerns the local Gradle daemon connection, without dependency downloads.

Only sanitized excerpts are included here; no project source, credentials, or full conversation/debug logs are attached.

issues.title: Copilot CLI exposes both MCP `content` and `structuredContent`

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

labels.name: area:tools
labels.description: Built-in tools: file editing, shell, search, LSP, git, and tool call behavior

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

## Summary

When an MCP tool result contains both `content` and `structuredContent`,
Copilot CLI appears to add both fields to the conversation context.

When `structuredContent` is present, the client should use it as the
structured tool result instead of exposing an equivalent or unrelated
`content` representation to the model.

For backward compatibility MCP tools which return structured content, should also set the unstructured `content`
> For backwards compatibility, a tool that returns structured content SHOULD also return the serialized JSON in a TextContent block.
see: [MCP spec about structured content](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools#structured-content)

## Example

### `server.py`

Here is a simple MCP server (based on the [MCP Python SDK](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk)) to demonstrate the issue:
```python
from pydantic import BaseModel

from mcp.server.mcpserver import MCPServer


class HelloOutput(BaseModel):
    message: str


server = MCPServer(name="hello", version="0.1.0")


@server.tool(structured_output=True)
def hello() -> HelloOutput:
    """Return a simple JSON hello object."""
    return HelloOutput(message="Hello World")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    server.run("stdio")
```

This is what the MCP server returns for the `hello` tool call.
```json
{
  "_meta": null,
  "content": [
    {
      "type": "text",
      "text": "{\n  \"message\": \"Hello World\"\n}",
      "annotations": null,
      "_meta": null
    }
  ],
  "structuredContent": {
    "message": "Hello World"
  },
  "isError": false,
  "resultType": "complete"
}
```

## Actual Copilot CLI context

Copilot CLI exposes both representations:

```text
{
  "message": "Hello World"
}

{"message":"Hello World"}
```

## Expected result

Only the structured result should be provided to the model:

```json
{"message":"Hello World"}
```

The `content` field may remain available for UI rendering or backwards
compatibility, but it should not be concatenated into the model context when it
duplicates `structuredContent`.

## Impact

The behavior unnecessarily increases context size and may cause the model to
interpret one tool result as two JSON objects.

## Related issue

The reporter of issue #3258 expects the opposite behavior.
Anyway, this contradicts the intention of the MCP spec:

> Tool results may contain structured **or** unstructured content.

>  For backwards compatibility, a tool that returns structured content SHOULD also return the serialized JSON in a TextContent block.

That means:
* a MCP tool must either return structured **or** unstructured content (but not both)
* but they should return a serialized representation in the unstructured content block for backward compatibility (i.e. for legacy clients which don't support structured content)

Clients which support structured content **must** therefore silently ignore the unstructured content if there is structured content.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.80.

issues.title: ACP: the autopilot task_complete summary is sent only as a tool call, not as an agent message
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

In ACP mode (`copilot --acp --stdio`), when an autopilot turn ends with the `task_complete` tool, the final answer of the turn reaches the client only as a `tool_call` / `tool_call_update` with `kind: "other"`. No `agent_message_chunk` carries the summary. Then `session/prompt` returns `stopReason: "end_turn"`.

Per ACP, `agent_message_chunk` is the response of the agent, and `tool_call` reports the execution of a tool ([prompt turn](https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/prompt-turn)). So ACP clients show the answer as a collapsed tool call, and the user must expand it to read the result. JetBrains Air (IntelliJ IDEA) is affected.

The Copilot TUI renders the `task_complete` summary as the final markdown answer (changelog 1.0.6). The ACP server does not. `task_complete` is an internal control tool of autopilot, so a client has no generic way to know that this tool call is the answer.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.96 (`agentInfo.version` "1.0.96"), started as `copilot --acp --stdio`. The same binary ships in `@github/copilot-language-server` 1.554.0 (`@github/copilot-win32-x64`). Windows 11, x64.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Start `copilot --acp --stdio` and send `initialize`, then `session/new`.
2. Switch the session to autopilot: `session/set_config_option` with `configId: "mode"` and value `https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/session-modes#autopilot`.
3. Send `session/prompt` with the text `Create a file hello.txt with the text "hello", then finish the task.`

The `session/update` notifications of that turn, in order:

```
config_option_update
config_option_update
session_info_update
usage_update
tool_call            "Creating ...\hello.txt"   pending
agent_message_chunk  "Info: ...\hello.txt"
tool_call_update     completed
usage_update
tool_call            "task_complete"            pending
tool_call_update     completed
```

The `task_complete` notifications:

```json
{"sessionUpdate":"tool_call","toolCallId":"toolu_014obvFRV78u2US8vcmwXq8p","title":"task_complete","kind":"other","status":"pending","rawInput":{"summary":"Created hello.txt containing \"hello\"."}}
{"sessionUpdate":"tool_call_update","toolCallId":"toolu_014obvFRV78u2US8vcmwXq8p","status":"completed","content":[{"type":"content","content":{"type":"text","text":"Created hello.txt containing \"hello\"."}}],"rawOutput":{"content":"Created hello.txt containing \"hello\".","detailedContent":"✓ Task completed: Created hello.txt containing \"hello\"."}}
```

Then `session/prompt` returns `{"stopReason":"end_turn", ...}`. The only `agent_message_chunk` of the turn is the `Info:` line of the file tool.

### Expected behavior

The ACP server sends the `task_complete` summary as an `agent_message_chunk`, as the TUI renders it. It can also keep the tool call, or not expose `task_complete` as a client-visible tool call at all.

### Additional context

The same class of output loss is reported for other channels: #2482 (`-p` output) and #1324 (subagent result).

issues.title: MCP: Cloudflare connection fails with "Subscription limit reached" after successful OAuth, then reports authentication required

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Cloudflare's remote MCP server fails to become available in Copilot CLI after successful OAuth authentication and protocol initialization. The runtime records:

```text
MCP error -32603: Subscription limit reached
```

The MCP UI subsequently reports that the server requires authentication. Reauthenticating succeeds but leads to the same connection failure.

Evidence suggests an interoperability problem with notification subscriptions: Cloudflare intentionally rejects `subscriptions/listen`, and Copilot appears to treat this rejection as a fatal startup error rather than continuing without notifications. The actual outgoing RPC method was not captured, so this is a diagnosis supported by the server implementation and matching error, not a confirmed client-side call trace.

### Affected version

```text
GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.89.
```

Environment: Windows, x64 distribution, PowerShell.
Observed on September 28, 2026.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Configure the Cloudflare server in a workspace `.mcp.json`:

   ```json
   {
     "mcpServers": {
       "cloudflare": {
         "type": "http",
         "url": "https://mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp",
         "tools": ["search", "execute"]
       }
     }
   }
   ```

2. Start Copilot CLI and authenticate with Cloudflare through the MCP UI.
3. Observe successful authentication and protocol initialization in the logs.
4. Observe `MCP error -32603: Subscription limit reached` immediately afterward. Cloudflare tools do not become available.
5. Open the server's tool listing. It reports:

   ```text
   MCP server "cloudflare" requires authentication. Run `/mcp auth cloudflare` to authenticate.
   ```

6. Reauthenticate. The same sequence occurs.

The failure was observed repeatedly in two runtime logs, including immediately after successful reauthentication. This was not separately reproduced with a clean profile or a standalone authenticated RPC harness.

### Expected behavior

If notification subscriptions are unavailable, the client should continue with ordinary tool discovery and calls where supported, without live tool-list updates.

If a subscription failure must be fatal, preserve the actual error rather than reporting an authentication requirement after successful authentication.

### Additional context

#### Sanitized diagnostic excerpts

These are selected events from one connection attempt; unrelated events and the verbose initialization payload are omitted.

```text
2026-09-28T22:47:42.601Z [ERROR] Successfully authenticated with cloudflare
2026-09-28T22:47:42.846Z [INFO] [rust:rmcp::service] Service initialized as client
2026-09-28T22:47:42.874Z [DEBUG] [rust:rt_mcp::native_host] Recorded failure for server cloudflare: MCP error -32603: Subscription limit reached {"server_name":"cloudflare"}
2026-09-28T22:47:42.874Z [WARNING] [rust:copilot_runtime::session::mcp::agent_host] MCP error -32603: Subscription limit reached {"server":"cloudflare"}
2026-09-28T22:47:54.185Z [WARNING] PluginsScreenDetail listMcpTools(cloudflare) failed: Error: MCP server "cloudflare" requires authentication. Run `/mcp auth cloudflare` to authenticate.
```

The successful initialization payload reports:

- Protocol version: `2026-07-28`
- Server: `cloudflare-api`, version `0.1.0`
- Tools capability: `list_changed: Some(true)`

The success event really is logged at ERROR severity; that is not a transcription mistake.

#### Relevant upstream implementation

Pinned to Cloudflare commit `259b2afc5aa84ce34461848d4fc36d817d49815e`:

- [MCP handler](https://github.com/cloudflare/mcp/blob/259b2afc5aa84ce34461848d4fc36d817d49815e/src/mcp-handler.ts): passes `{ maxSubscriptions: 0 }` to `createMcpHandler`. Its comment explicitly says the server publishes no change notifications and rejects `subscriptions/listen` to avoid long-lived streams.
- [Modern MCP tests](https://github.com/cloudflare/mcp/blob/259b2afc5aa84ce34461848d4fc36d817d49815e/tests/mcp-modern.test.ts): the test named `rejects subscriptions instead of opening a long-lived stream` expects error code `-32603` and message `Subscription limit reached`. Separate tests cover successful ordinary `tools/list` and `tools/call` requests.

This suggests the error is an intentional rejection of notification subscriptions, not an exhausted billing quota or evidence of invalid OAuth credentials. The advertised tool-list-change capability may also contribute to the interoperability problem.

Potential regression coverage: a server that initializes successfully, advertises tool-list changes, rejects `subscriptions/listen` with this error, but still supports `tools/list` and `tools/call`. Check that tools remain usable and authentication state is not incorrectly reported.

No credentials, account identifiers, or full logs are included.

issues.title: Claude Opus 5.5: 32k maxOutputTokens makes --reasoning-effort max/xhigh return empty turns on long tasks; auto-continue bills each empty turn

labels.name: area:non-interactive
labels.description: Non-interactive mode (-p), CI/CD, ACP protocol, and headless automation

labels.name: area:models
labels.description: Model selection, availability, switching, rate limits, and model-specific behavior

issues.body:
## Summary

With `claude-opus-5.5`, every reply is capped at **32,000 output tokens** (`maxOutputTokens: 32000` in `session.usage_record`), and hidden reasoning counts against that cap. At `--reasoning-effort max` (and often `xhigh`), Opus spends the whole 32k on reasoning for any non-trivial task. The turn then ends with **no assistant content**. The CLI auto-continues, hits the same wall again, and bills every turn. In headless mode you pay for roughly three full 32k reasoning turns and get an empty answer.

Anthropic documents 128k max output for Opus 5.5, so the effort levels the CLI offers (`max`, `xhigh`) are effectively unusable for long-form work inside Copilot.

## Environment

- Copilot CLI 1.0.98, Windows 11, usage-based billing
- Model `claude-opus-5.5` (Copilot provider, not BYOK)

## Repro

Pipe a ~20k-token prompt asking for a ~2,000-word structured document (a planning doc) on stdin:

```
copilot --model claude-opus-5.5 --reasoning-effort max --no-ask-user --no-custom-instructions --available-tools=view --output-format json
```

## Observed (from `~/.copilot/session-state/<id>/events.jsonl`)

- Each turn records `session.usage_record` with `outputTokens: 32000`, `reasoningTokens: 32000`, `maxOutputTokens: 32000`.
- `assistant.turn_end` arrives with no `assistant.message` content.
- The CLI starts another turn (`initiator: "agent"`) and the same thing happens. After 3 turns the session ends with `assistant.message` `content: ""`.
- Billed: about 200 AI credits for zero output. `--reasoning-effort xhigh` behaved the same on 4 of 5 long tasks. `high` completed the same tasks normally.
- Across ~65,000 Opus 5.5 calls logged locally this month, `outputTokens` never exceeded 32,000, and `maxOutputTokens` was always 32000.

Short tasks (e.g. a ~300-word reply) usually complete at `xhigh`, but can still stall at `max`.

## Expected (any of these would fix it)

1. Allow Opus 5.5's documented 128k output, at least when `xhigh`/`max` is selected.
2. Or reserve part of `maxOutputTokens` for visible output, so reasoning cannot consume all of it.
3. Or, when a turn ends with reasoning = max output and no content, fail fast with a clear error instead of auto-continuing and billing repeated identical turns.
4. Document per-model output caps, and which reasoning efforts are practical under them.

## Impact

Headless/agent workflows that pin Opus at `max` silently burn credits and return nothing. We now detect the stalled turn ourselves, kill the process and step down to a lower effort. That workaround shouldn't be needed.

issues.title: Bug: Idle CLI sessions pin one CPU core at 100% (`notify-rs debouncer loop` busy-spins)
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

**Environment:** Copilot CLI 1.0.98, macOS 26.6.1 (Apple Silicon arm64, 14 cores).

**What happened:** Four concurrent CLI sessions each used about 100% of one core. Three of them stayed pegged from startup: about 52–54 minutes of CPU time over a similar wall-clock time. The sessions were started with `--allow-all`, or with `--allow-all --autopilot --fleet`. Three shared one git worktree (Maven project) as their working directory; the fourth used a sibling worktree.

**Evidence that this is internal to the CLI, not agent work:**

- The main Node thread is idle (parked in `kevent` under `uv_run`).
- Logs only show periodic OTel and telemetry POSTs. The log files didn't grow over a 5-second window.
- Child processes (jdtls, MCP servers, background shells) were at 0% CPU.
- `sample <pid> 3` shows the thread `notify-rs debouncer loop` on-CPU in every sample (2478/2478) and never blocked. The `notify-rs fsevents loop` threads are idle.
- The hot frames are the same in two separate processes: `runtime.node +0x3dd8278` (and nearby offsets), called from `+0x3ddb8b4` under `+0x25c8c0c`, plus `_platform_memcmp`. It appears to be iterating or comparing over debouncer state already in memory rather than handling new filesystem events.

**Expected:** When no filesystem events are arriving, the debouncer thread should block (on a condvar or timeout) and use about 0% CPU.

**Possible trigger (unconfirmed):** Several sessions watched the same high-churn worktree (Maven `target/` output, Docker/acceptance builds). A large event backlog, or a zero or expired debounce timeout, could leave the loop spinning.

**Workaround:** Exit and run `copilot --resume <session-id>`, or kill the process.

**Request:** Please check the debouncer loop for a busy-wait or zero-timeout path. Please also consider excluding ignored or build directories (e.g. `.gitignore`d `target/`) from the watch.


### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.98

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

Not sure but the description `what happened` section may provide clues

### Expected behavior

No idle loop 100% cpu

### Additional context

macOS 26.6.1

issues.title: 400 `reasoning_text` in thinking mode must be passed back — triggered by runtime-synthesized assistant turn after a background shell exits

labels.name: area:models
labels.description: Model selection, availability, switching, rate limits, and model-specific behavior

labels.name: area:tools
labels.description: Built-in tools: file editing, shell, search, LSP, git, and tool call behavior

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

A session using a **custom OpenAI-compatible provider with `wireApi: "responses"`** (DeepSeek, model `deepseek-flash`) is killed by an HTTP 400 on the model call that immediately follows a **runtime-synthesized, model-less assistant turn**.

The trigger is the background-shell-completion flow:

1. A command is backgrounded (short `initial_wait`).
2. When it exits, the runtime emits a `<system_notification>` (`kind.type = "shell_completed"`).
3. The runtime then injects a **synthetic `assistant.message`** to read the shell output. That message has `model: undefined`, empty `content`, and — critically — **no `reasoningBlocks`**.
4. The next request to the provider is rejected because thinking mode requires the previous assistant turn's reasoning to be passed back.

Result: `session.error`, the session ends (`was_interrupted: true`, `interruption_reason: "error"`).

The provider and credentials are fine — the same provider/model served 160+ successful model calls in the same session. It is specifically the model-less synthetic turn that breaks the reasoning passback invariant.

### Affected version

- `copilot --version`: **1.0.95-3** (dist: `pkg/win32-arm64/1.0.95-3`)
- Host: Copilot app (`copilot-desktop-gh-2.98.0`)
- OS: Windows, ARM64

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Configure a custom provider:
   - `type`: `custom`
   - `baseUrl`: `https://api.deepseek.com`
   - `wireApi`: `responses`
   - `authKind`: `api_key`
   - model `deepseek-flash` (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash; **thinking mode is enabled by default**)
2. In a session, start a long-running command so it moves to the background, e.g. a `powershell` call with a short `initial_wait`:
   `dotnet test --project <integration test project> --filter-class "*SelectiveOperationScaleTests"`
3. Continue working while the shell runs. When it exits, observe the injected turn and the failure:
   - `system.notification` → `<system_notification>Shell command "…" (shellId: 68) has exited with exit code 2.</system_notification>`
   - `assistant.message` with `model: undefined`, `content: ""`, one `read_powershell` tool call, **no `reasoningBlocks`**
   - `tool.execution_complete` for `read_powershell`
   - HTTP **400** on the next model call → `session.error`
4. See error: session terminates.

Exact sequence from `events.jsonl`:

```
22:24:02.368Z  assistant.message           "Let me start the heaviest scale test in the background while I update the documentation."
22:24:02.380Z  tool.execution_start        powershell  { initial_wait: 12 }   → backgrounded as shell 68
22:24:45.826Z  system.notification         kind.type="shell_completed", shellId=68, exitCode=2
22:24:45.827Z  assistant.message           messageId=2414e771-…, model=undefined, content="",
                                           toolRequests=[read_powershell {shellId:"68", delay:0}],
                                           reasoningBlocks=<absent>
22:24:45.833Z  tool.execution_complete
22:24:48.944Z  (model call fails)
22:24:48.976Z  session.error               400 The `reasoning_text` in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API.
```

Raw error envelope and error context:

```json
{"type":"hook.start","data":{"hookType":"errorOccurred","input":{
  "error":{"name":"Error","message":"{\"message\":\"The `reasoning_text` in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API. (request_id: 3821e7d3-e76b-4688-8be6-4461e1d1e46b)\",\"type\":\"invalid_request_error\",\"param\":null,\"code\":\"invalid_request_error\"}"},
  "errorContext":"model_call",
  "recoverable":true}}}

{"type":"session.error","data":{
  "errorType":"query",
  "message":"400 The `reasoning_text` in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API. (request_id: 3821e7d3-e76b-4688-8be6-4461e1d1e46b)",
  "statusCode":400}}
```

The synthetic assistant turn (note the UUID-style `toolCallId`, versus the model's `call_00_…` style):

```json
{"messageId":"2414e771-73dc-4bb2-be5b-8b1e537e8982","content":"",
 "toolRequests":[{"toolCallId":"0666f48c-0b07-413f-ae92-aaf94b4ca60f","name":"read_powershell",
                  "arguments":{"shellId":"68","delay":0},"toolTitle":"Read shell output"}]}
```

### Expected behavior

The session should continue. Thinking-mode providers require the reasoning payload on assistant turns; the runtime should satisfy that invariant for **every** assistant turn it sends, including turns it synthesizes itself (or must otherwise exclude those turns from the reasoning-required history).

### Additional context

**Provider configuration (valid, working):**

```
type: custom, authKind: api_key, baseUrl: https://api.deepseek.com, wireApi: responses, headers: {}
model: deepseek-flash  (max_prompt_tokens 840000, max_output_tokens 128000)
reasoning efforts: none | low | high | max
```

DeepSeek documents both a Responses API and thinking mode (on by default) for `deepseek-flash`.

**Why this points at the client, not the provider:**

- 142 of 162 `assistant.message` events in the session carried correct reasoning blocks: `reasoningBlocks.provider = "openai-responses"`, block `type: "reasoning"`, content `[{type:"reasoning_text", …}]`, plus `encrypted_content`.
- 20 assistant turns had no reasoning block. 18 were ordinary model turns; **1 was the model-less synthetic turn above** — and the failure landed on the very next model call.
- Same provider/model serviced 160+ other calls in this session and all other sessions without this error.
- Across 44 local sessions with this provider, there is exactly **one** `session.error` of this kind. It was also the session's only `system.notification`. Correlation is 1:1.

- The injected turn is not a model output, so it cannot carry model reasoning; sending it as a plain assistant turn breaks the API contract for thinking mode.

**Impact:** the entire session is terminated mid-task, losing in-flight work. In this case the session was implementing changes across many files.

**Workarounds used:** avoid backgrounding commands (run them in the foreground) in thinking-mode sessions; set the model's reasoning effort to `none` to sidestep the passback requirement.

**Suggested direction:** when the runtime injects a synthetic assistant turn (e.g. `read_powershell` after `shell_completed`), either attach whatever reasoning payload the provider requires, or mark it so it is not presented to thinking-mode providers as a reasoning-bearing assistant turn (e.g. keep it out of the reasoning-required history, or fold the shell output into the following user/tool message).

**Related observation (possibly a separate issue):** the same provider also produced two genuine context-length 400s in an earlier session — `you requested 1049487 tokens (921487 in the messages, 128000 in the completion)` against a 1,048,576-token context — while `max_prompt_tokens` was configured as 840000. That suggests the app-side prompt budget does not reserve enough headroom for its own token estimation error. Happy to file separately if useful.

### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

Subagents constantly and repeatedly request permissions in interactive mode

If your operation generates subagents to do some work, and those subagents require permissions, then the subagents will constantly request permissions at a high rate.  

If the operations generates 15 subagents, you get 15 sets of requests, each with possibly half a dozen requests (which adds up very quickly).  That is completely unworkable in Interactive mode and requires the user to switch to Autopilot mode.

### Proposed solution
Have the subagents inherit permissions of the main agent.  Then have the main agent figure out what permissions the subagents require, and ask for permissions once. issues.title: CLI: follow-up to an idle background agent is delayed by minutes to hours while its status shows "running"

labels.name: area:agents
labels.description: Sub-agents, fleet, autopilot, plan mode, background agents, and custom agents

issues.body:
> _Filed with the help of GitHub Copilot CLI (model: Claude Opus 5.5). Root-cause analysis and any proposed fix were AI-assisted and human-reviewed before filing._

---

### Summary

`write_agent` behaves very differently depending on the background agent's state:

- **Steering a running agent works.** The steer took effect 12 s after `write_agent` returned
  (23 s after the call; the agent was finishing a 15 s sleep).
- **A follow-up to an idle agent** (its turn has finished) is reported as delivered, but the new
  turn starts minutes to hours later: 6.5 and 9.2 min for two trivial repro agents, about 8.5 h
  in a long, busy session. Meanwhile `read_agent` reports `status: running` with no new turn.
- **There is no cancel/stop operation** for background agents; a stalled one stays `running`.

### Impact

- Coordinator workflows that give an idle agent its next step stall for minutes to hours, with no
  error and no timeout.
- A queued agent looks exactly like a busy one: `status: running`, with no tool-call count or a
  stale one from the previous turn. Even a "stop" sent with `write_agent` waits behind the delay.
- Workaround: never send follow-ups to idle agents; start a fresh one-shot agent with full context.

### Root cause (observed/suspected)

`read_agent` shows the idle state and the final answer in real time. Follow-up dispatch instead
appears to follow the session event stream, which trails real time for background agents:

1. **Observed:** an agent's events (messages, tool calls, `subagent.completed`) are recorded
   minutes to hours late: 5-10 min in the repro, 6-9 h in the long session. The lag differs per
   agent: during the repro, the long-session agent in the same session was still hours behind.
2. **Observed:** in all three cases, the queued follow-up's `user.message` was recorded 0.4-3 s
   after the previous turn's late `subagent.completed`.
3. **Observed:** `read_agent`'s `tool_calls_completed` equalled the number of the previous turn's
   tool calls recorded in the lagging stream at that moment (9 of 13).
4. **Suspected:** a queued follow-up is dispatched only once the previous turn's completion drains
   through that stream, not when the agent goes idle. Steering bypasses this path.

### Log signature / evidence

Local times. Event times are as recorded in `events.jsonl`; first actions (file writes, `Get-Date`) are ground truth.

| | Agent A (steered, then follow-up) | Agent B (follow-up only) |
|---|---|---|
| Previous turn | 13 tool calls; last write 04:27:26 | text-only reply, 0 tool calls |
| `read_agent` shows `idle` | 04:30:31 | 04:23:07 |
| Follow-up sent (`write_agent`: "Message delivered") | 04:30:44 | 04:23:30 |
| `read_agent` while waiting | `status: running, ... total_turns: 1, tool_calls_completed: 9` | `status: running, ... total_turns: 1` (timed out at 04:26 and 04:29) |
| Previous turn's `subagent.completed` recorded | 04:36:52.1 | 04:32:33.7 |
| Follow-up `user.message` / `assistant.turn_start` | 04:36:52.5 / 04:36:55.8 | 04:32:35.5 / 04:32:36.9 |
| First follow-up action | 04:37:13 (**+6.5 min**) | 04:32:43 (**+9.2 min**) |

Also from the repro: the steer took effect at 04:23:05, but its `user.message` was recorded at
04:28:30; A's first tool call (it wrote at 04:21:33) was recorded at 04:26:30. B's turn reports
`durationMs: 624022` in `subagent.completed`, yet `read_agent` showed it done within 170 s of launch.

Long, busy session (one general-purpose background agent):

- It finished a 183-tool-call turn (last file change 21:48; `read_agent` showed `idle` at 22:07).
  A follow-up asking for more work was sent at 22:08.
- `read_agent` at 22:13 and 22:15: `status: running, ... total_turns: 1, tool_calls_completed: 22`.
- At 22:37 a second `write_agent` told it to stop and reply with one word; it returned `delivered, task_status=running`.
- At 06:41 the next day the previous turn's `subagent.completed` was recorded. The follow-up
  started 3 s later and the stop message 11 s after that, so the agent replied "stopped" and did
  no work. The follow-up had waited about 8.5 h.

### Steps to reproduce (ISOLATED)

Everything writes only to a throwaway folder, shown as `<scratch>`.

1. In an interactive session, have the main agent start two general-purpose background agents:
   - **A:** "Make 12 separate shell calls. Each runs `Start-Sleep 15`, then appends
     `<HH:mm:ss> step <n>` to `<scratch>\steer.txt`. Then reply `steer done`."
   - **B:** any trivial task that ends with a text-only reply.
2. While A is still looping, steer it with `write_agent`: "Append `<HH:mm:ss> ack` to
   `<scratch>\ack.txt`, then continue." `ack.txt` appears about 12 s after `write_agent` returns.
3. Once `read_agent` shows B `idle`, send it a follow-up: "Make three separate shell calls running
   `Get-Date -Format 'HH:mm:ss'`, then reply `turn1 done` plus the times."
4. Once A is `idle`, send it a follow-up: "Make two separate shell calls, each appending
   `<HH:mm:ss> turn1 call <n>` to `<scratch>\turn1.txt`, then reply `turn1 done`."
5. Poll `read_agent` and note when each follow-up's first action happens.
   - **Expected:** both follow-ups start within seconds, like the steer.
   - **Actual:** both show `running` with no new turn, then start after 9.2 min (B) and 6.5 min
     (A), each right after its previous turn's `subagent.completed` is recorded.

**Conditions:** the tasks were isolated, but the session was not idle. It was long-running, with
28 idle background agents and five others `running`: three actively working, and two that had
shown `running` for hours (one is the long-session agent above). The hooks listed under
Environment were active. Not yet confirmed in a fresh, otherwise idle session.

### Proposed fix (optional)

1. **Deliver a queued follow-up as soon as the agent is idle** (the state `read_agent` already
   reports), and emit `subagent.completed` when the turn actually ends.
2. **Report the real state:** "queued, not started" (with its age) instead of `running`, without
   the previous turn's tool-call count.
3. **Add a cancel/stop operation for background agents** that does not depend on message delivery.

### Related

- github/copilot-cli#3350: background agents stay `running` with no completion notice. The late
  `subagent.completed` described here may be the same mechanism.
- github/copilot-cli#4101: `write_agent` to an idle agent blocks the caller. Here it returns at
  once, but the agent's next turn starts late.

### Environment

- Copilot CLI `1.0.96-2`
- Windows, x64
- Model: Claude Opus 5.5 for the main session; background agents were `general-purpose`, with no
  model override
- `preToolUse`/`postToolUse` hooks configured; they also fire for background-agent tool calls

### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

Selecting the default agent using the /agent command directly, without opening the interactive agent list

### Proposed solution

While custom agents can be selected by typing `/agent agent-name` *\<enter\>*, the default agent can only be selected by typing `/agent` *\<enter\>* (the interactive agent list pops) *\<enter\>*.

In general, this behavior is acceptable one you get used to it, even if represents different treatment for the default agent. However, but this can become an annoyance if one wants to **enqueue** (*\<ctrl\>+q*) the selection of the default agent, because that would enqueue the popping of the agent list, not the default agent itself.

A possible solution could be a syntax like `/agent .` (dot) or `/agent -` (dash) or `/agent default` (if we assume that `default` is not a custom agent name).

### Example prompts or workflows

1. Stuff is running in a custom agent
2. `/agent .` *\<ctrl\>+q*
3. `Paint my dragon with rainbow colors using unicorn brush` *\<ctrl\>+q*
4. After custom agent has finished, default agent is selected and executes queued prompt

issues.title: Headless mode exits 0 mid-task when a model response has `finish_reason: "tool_calls"` but no tool calls

labels.name: area:non-interactive
labels.description: Non-interactive mode (-p), CI/CD, ACP protocol, and headless automation

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

In non-interactive mode (`-p` / `--prompt-file`, `--no-ask-user`), the CLI ended a long-running agentic session after one model response that came back empty: `finish_reason` was `"tool_calls"` and the API billed 193 completion tokens, but `message.tool_calls` was missing and `content` was `null`. The CLI treated this as a normal end of the task and logged `runHeadlessMode: succeeded=true` and `exiting with code 0`, even though the agent was in the middle of driving an Android emulator and had not finished.

Because the exit was clean, our wrapper's retry logic never ran. The session's final outputs were never produced. In our case this was a GitHub Agentic Workflows (gh-aw) run, which ended with no safe outputs. We only found out after the fact.

Turn 63 response (request ID `00000-8dd40ac2-8861-4961-b4dd-12408dad56f5`), quoted from the `--log-level all` log:

```json
{
  "id": "msg_011Cg27ptWDQ938VwzsJAMAn",
  "object": "chat.completion",
  "created": 1791980400,
  "model": "claude-sonnet-5-5",
  "choices": [
    {
      "index": 0,
      "message": { "role": "assistant", "content": null, "refusal": null },
      "finish_reason": "tool_calls",
      "logprobs": null
    }
  ],
  "usage": {
    "prompt_tokens": 136561,
    "completion_tokens": 193,
    "total_tokens": 136754,
    "completion_tokens_details": { "reasoning_tokens": 0 }
  }
}
```

The previous 62 turns all had a populated `tool_calls` array and usually `reasoning_text`. Their tool calls were bash commands about the same size as the 193 tokens here. This suggests the tool call was generated but dropped somewhere between the model and the CLI. That part may belong to the Copilot API team, but the CLI is where the silent success happens.

Right after that response, the log shows:

```
executeHeadlessDirectly completing: operation=prompt, hasError=false, taskBlocked=false, blockedExit=false, ... will return true
runHeadlessMode: operation=prompt, succeeded=true
runHeadlessMode: exiting with code 0
```

Related, but not the same: #3239 is about text-only turns ending the session. Here the response has no content at all, and its `finish_reason` contradicts its body.

### Affected version

1.0.90

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

This is not deterministic, since it depends on the API returning the malformed response. It happened once, after about 30 minutes and 62 successful turns:

1. Run `copilot --prompt-file <prompt> --no-ask-user --log-level all --log-dir <dir> --allow-tool ...` with a long multi-step task that uses `bash` and MCP tools heavily. Model: `claude-sonnet-5.5`.
2. Let a model response arrive with `finish_reason: "tool_calls"`, no `tool_calls` and `content: null`.
3. The CLI exits 0 straight away, with no error and no retry.

### Expected behavior

A response whose `finish_reason` is `"tool_calls"` but which has no tool calls, or an empty response with completion tokens > 0, is malformed. The CLI should treat it as a transient error: retry the request, or at least nudge the model to continue. If retries run out, headless mode should exit non-zero so automation can tell that the task stopped early.

### Additional context

- Linux x86_64 (GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-latest` runner), non-interactive. No terminal emulator; the CLI was spawned by the gh-aw harness.
- Session ran 30m 23s and 63 turns: 8.9M input tokens (8.7M cached), 31K output tokens.
- Session ID: `1b556a30-bfaa-48f8-a7ab-274d386b0762`
- Request ID of the malformed response: `00000-8dd40ac2-8861-4961-b4dd-12408dad56f5`, at 2026-10-14T12:20:00Z

issues.title: plugin: package spec with an export subpath (pkg/subpath) fails to install with "An unknown git error occurred"
issues.body:
## Summary

An entry in the `plugins` array whose `package` contains an export subpath (for
example `opencode-pty/v2`) can never be installed or loaded. OpenCode passes the
string to npm unchanged, npm parses `name/subpath` as a GitHub shorthand, and the
load fails with an opaque `NpmInstallFailedError (cause: Error: An unknown git
error occurred)`. Since the plugin entry schema has no separate entrypoint field,
there is no way to reference a package subpath export at all.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.0.30
- OS: Windows_NT 10.0.26200 (win32 x64)
- Terminal: Unavailable: desktop app, no terminal environment variables set
- Shell: `C:\WINDOWS\system32\cmd.exe`
- Install/channel: latest (desktop app, `@opencodedesktop`)
- Active plugins:
  - `@tarquinen/opencode-dcp` (loads fine)
  - `opencode-mem` (loads fine)
  - `./plugins/opencode-pty-v2` (local wrapper, workaround for this issue)
- Config file: `C:\Users\Administrator\.config\opencode\opencode.json`

## Reproduction

1. Use opencode v2.0.30 with a global config at `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`.
2. Add a plugin entry that points at an export subpath of an npm package:
   ```json
   { "plugins": ["opencode-pty/v2"] }
   ```
   Object form fails identically:
   ```json
   { "plugins": [{ "package": "opencode-pty/v2", "options": { "autostart": false } }] }
   ```
   `opencode-pty@0.4.0` really does declare that export:
   ```json
   { "exports": { ".": "./dist/index.js", "./v2": "./dist/src/v2/index.js" } }
   ```
3. Restart the service (`opencode service restart`) or launch opencode.
4. The plugin never loads; `opencode plugin list` shows `-  -  opencode-pty/v2`.

## Expected Behavior

OpenCode should resolve the package name `opencode-pty` from npm, install it, and
load its `./v2` export (as the plugin's README instructs authors to configure it),
or at minimum report that subpath specs are unsupported instead of a git error.

## Actual Behavior

```
level=WARN message="failed to load plugin" target=opencode-pty/v2 cause="Cause([Fail(NpmInstallFailedError (cause: Error: An unknown git error occurred))])"
level=WARN message="failed to check plugin update" target=opencode-pty/v2 cause="Cause([Fail(NpmInstallFailedError (cause: Error: Package is not installed: opencode-pty/v2))])"
```

The npm spec `opencode-pty/v2` is not a valid npm specifier: npm interprets
`name/subpath` as the GitHub shorthand `github:opencode-pty/v2`, which does not
exist. A stray cache directory is created:
`~/.cache/opencode/npm/git-v2-355e8b55fd00`.

`opencode plugin add opencode-pty/v2` fails the same way.

## Additional Context

- The V2 entry schema `Config.Plugin.EntryEncoded` only allows `package` and
  `options` (`additionalProperties: false`), so the subpath has to go inside
  `package` 鈥?the one place npm cannot parse it. There is no way to declare an
  entrypoint or export subpath for an installed package.
- Plugin authors do document this shape. `shekohex/opencode-pty` README tells
  users to configure exactly `{ "package": "opencode-pty/v2", "options": {...} }`.
- Workaround in use: a local wrapper plugin that re-exports the subpath, with its
  own `node_modules` copy:
  ```js
  // ~/.config/opencode/plugins/opencode-pty-v2/index.js
  export { default } from "opencode-pty/v2";
  ```
  registered as `"./plugins/opencode-pty-v2"`. This loads correctly, confirming
  the package subpath itself is fine and only resolution/installation is broken.
- Suggested fix directions: split an optional subpath off `package` before
  resolving from the registry (and use it as the module entry), or add an
  explicit entry/export field to the plugin entry, and surface a clear
  "unsupported package spec" error instead of `An unknown git error occurred`.
- Reproducible consistently on every restart.

issues.title: ECONNRESET when using Custom Provider: socket connection closed unexpectedly and custom server not detected correctly
issues.body:
### Description

Description
I am encountering repeated ECONNRESET errors when using a Custom Provider to connect to an OpenAI-compatible AI server. The error occurs during chat with the selected AI model and causes the response stream to terminate unexpectedly.

The app also seems unable to correctly detect or handle the custom provider endpoint. This does not appear to be a transient network issue because official providers (e.g., OpenAI, Anthropic) work fine under the same network conditions.

Steps to Reproduce
Start an OpenAI-compatible server at http://<host>:<port>/v1 (e.g., vLLM, SGLang, Ollama, etc.).

Add a Custom Provider in the app with the server URL and model name.

Start a new chat session using this custom provider.

Send a chat request or upload files (without exceeding the model context limit).

After a few interactions, the response stops and the ECONNRESET error appears.

Repeat the same steps with an official provider to confirm the issue is specific to the custom provider.

Environment
OS: <e.g., Windows 11 / macOS 15 / Ubuntu 22.04>

App Version: <e.g., 1.18.25 or latest>

Terminal: <e.g., PowerShell / CMD / Bash / Zsh>

Custom Provider Type: <e.g., SGLang / vLLM / Ollama / OpenAI-compatible>

Model: <e.g., Qwen3.5-27B-FP8>

Endpoint: http://<host>:<port>/v1 (no proxy or load balancer)

Error Logs
text
[ERROR] service=llm providerID=custom
error={"error":{"code":"ECONNRESET","path":"http://<host>:<port>/v1/chat/completions","errno":0}}
stream error
[ERROR] service=session.processor
error=The socket connection was closed unexpectedly.
For more information, pass `verbose: true` in the second argument to fetch()
In some cases, the app enters an endless retry loop:

text
Connection reset by server, retrying in 25s - attempt #21
Expected Behavior
The app should correctly detect and manage the Custom Provider.

When the socket connection is closed unexpectedly, it should show a clear user-friendly error instead of a raw fetch() error.

It should use a proper retry mechanism with backoff, not an infinite retry loop.

Timeout and retry behavior should be configurable.

Additional Context
The issue only occurs with custom providers; official providers work normally.

Disabling reasoning-parser or reasoning features on the server side avoids the error, but this is not suitable for agentic use cases.

issues.title: `opencode run` (v2) exits 1 after a transient provider error that the runner retried and recovered from
issues.body:
## Description

We run `opencode run` non-interactively in automation with `--format json`. When the upstream model provider is flaky and a step fails mid-stream, opencode reports a `provider.transport` error (for example `ECONNRESET: The socket connection was closed unexpectedly`, with HTTP status 200 because the response headers had already arrived), the runner retries the step, and the session completes normally with finish reason `stop`. The process still exits with code 1. stderr is empty; the only trace is the earlier `error` event in the JSON stream.

Cause in the v2 runner, `packages/cli/src/run/noninteractive.ts`:

- The `session.step.failed` handler sets `emittedError = true` and `process.exitCode = 1`, then `continue`s:
  https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v2.0.10/packages/cli/src/run/noninteractive.ts#L470-L481
  (permalink: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/b8cedc1a7a5e2916bbb65dc1d4b620729c261638/packages/cli/src/run/noninteractive.ts#L470-L481)
- `session.execution.succeeded` just returns, so a later success never clears the code:
  https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v2.0.10/packages/cli/src/run/noninteractive.ts#L504

The file is identical from v2.0.0 through v2.0.10. In v1.18.31 the exit code is set only on startup errors, and a retried step does not affect it.

**Observed:** any non-interactive run in which one step failed transiently and was retried exits 1, even when the run finishes with reason `stop` and a complete answer.

**Expected:** exit 0 when the session completes successfully. The exit code should report the outcome of the run, not whether a recoverable fault happened along the way. Comparable tools (`curl --retry`, `wget`, `pip`, `rsync`) exit 0 when a retry succeeds and keep the fault in their logs.

**Why it matters:** anything scripting `opencode run` trusts the exit code. With this behavior a caller must either treat 1 as "maybe fine, parse the event stream" or discard good output.

**Suggested fix:** do not set `process.exitCode = 1` on `session.step.failed` when the step is going to be retried, or clear it on `session.execution.succeeded`. If "completed, but errors were emitted" is worth surfacing, use a distinct documented exit code or an opt-in strict flag rather than 1.

## Plugins

None.

## OpenCode version

v2.0.10 (git tag; the v2 line is on the `@opencode-ai/cli` beta channel, `0.0.0-beta-*`). Also v2.0.8. Not reproducible on v1.18.31 (`opencode-ai@latest`).

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run `opencode run --format json "<any multi-step prompt>"` against a provider that drops one streaming response mid-body (a proxy that closes the socket after the headers and a few SSE events reproduces it; #39573 mentions a test-LLM harness that can inject a failure followed by successful replies).
2. Observe in the JSON stream: an `error` event with `error.type == "provider.transport"`, followed by further steps and a final `step_finish` with reason `stop`.
3. `echo $?` prints `1`.

## Screenshot and/or share link

Not applicable (non-interactive; JSON event stream shows the `error` event followed by a normal finish).

## Operating System

Linux (x86_64).

## Terminal

Not applicable (headless).

Related: #39573 reports the same symptom class on the v1 runner (exit 1 after a recovered provider 413 during auto-compaction) through a different code path.

issues.title: Zen free models: publish the current free-usage limit and return it in 429 responses
issues.body:
### What I'm asking for

Please be transparent about the Zen free-model limits. Today a client cannot tell how much free usage it has, when it resets, or why a request was refused, so a "free" model behaves like an unannounced trial.

In #28055 a maintainer said free usage is dynamic and shifts with capacity. That is reasonable, but the current value should still be visible. Concretely:

1. **Publish the current rule** in the Zen docs: the unit (requests or tokens), the window (per hour, per 5 hours, per day, rolling or fixed), and the scope (account, API key or IP). If it changes with capacity, say so there and show the current value.
2. **Say why a request was refused in the 429 response** with standard headers, e.g. `Retry-After` and `x-ratelimit-limit` / `x-ratelimit-remaining` / `x-ratelimit-reset`, so clients can back off precisely instead of polling.
3. **Use one error type, or document the difference.** Others report `FreeUsageLimitError` (#33318, #42977). We get `type: "rate_limit_error"` with the same message. Is this a separate short-term limit or the same free-usage cap?

### What we observed (2026-10-15, America/Toronto)

- Model: `opencode-zen/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free`, via the OpenAI-compatible completions endpoint, from a third-party agent harness.
- First refusal at 14:23:55, then every retry about once a minute was refused, still at 14:57:
  ```
  429: {"code":null,"message":"OpenCode Zen: Rate limit exceeded. Please try again later.","param":null,"type":"rate_limit_error"}
  ```
- No `Retry-After` or reset information was available to the client.
- Our own count before the first refusal: about 966 requests on this model since 08:00, about 500 of them between 13:00 and 14:24. We can live with any limit; we just need to know what it is.

### Related

#52894 and #53252 (show reset time), #54338 (reset time not exposed via API), #33318, #28055, #42977.

issues.title: reasoning: repetition loop on deepseek-v4.1-flash, plus a paired `reasoning_text must be passed back` 400
issues.body:
# Reasoning repetition loop on `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, plus a paired `reasoning_text must be passed back` 400

## Summary

I hit two failure modes on `deepseek-v4.1-flash` in thinking mode, and I believe they are **two different bugs** that happen to co-occur on long sessions.

1. **The repetition loop** already tracked in #44962 / #50634 / #51503. This report adds measured data across three abandoned sessions: where it starts, how big the context was, and what actually breaks it.
2. **A paired HTTP 400** that I could not find documented anywhere in this repo:

   ```
   The `reasoning_text` in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API.
   ```

   It fires in sessions as small as ~75k packed tokens, so it is not a context-length problem, and it looks like OpenCode building a request where a reasoning item and its text are out of sync. That is why I am filing it rather than treating it as another symptom of (1).

## Environment

| item | value |
| --- | --- |
| opencode | `2.0.28` when observed, re-checked on `2.0.29` |
| OS | Linux x86_64 |
| Client | third-party desktop client driving the OpenCode server, **and** the `opencode` CLI against the same session (both reproduce) |
| Model | `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, thinking on, variant `medium` |
| Provider | OpenCode Zen |
| Proxy | a local OpenAI-compatible passthrough in front of Zen. It does not touch reasoning items (no `reasoning_text` handling in its source), so the request body Zen receives is the body OpenCode assembled |

## Observation 1 — repetition loop, with measurements

The reasoning stream collapses into one short filler phrase repeated thousands of times inside a single turn. No assistant message is ever emitted, the session is effectively hung, and it has to be abandoned.

The repeated segment is consistently a 1–4 character Chinese filler. The top segment is always `好。` ("okay."), followed by `执行。` ("execute."). That matches the `好。` reports in #51503.

Measured by parsing the persisted session store, three abandoned sessions:

| session | assistant msgs | peak packed tokens | peak @ seq | max repeats of one phrase | turn outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | 357 | 531,938 | 3221 | 5,867 | aborted by user |
| B | 381 | 517,473 | 4094 | 6,604 | aborted by user |
| C | 289 | 348,184 | 1940 | 6,699 | aborted by user |

Packed tokens = `input + output + reasoning + cache.read + cache.write`.

Three things worth noting:

- **Context size alone is not a clean trigger.** The first time a single phrase crossed 50 repeats, packed context was 200k, 342k and 362k in the three sessions respectively. The sessions that got furthest also grew largest, but small-by-comparison sessions still looped.
- **It clusters around long sessions with heavy tool use**, which is consistent with #44962 and #51503.
- **It does not self-correct.** Once it starts, the only thing that reliably broke it was **injecting a new user message**. Manually stopping the turn and resuming produced the loop again immediately.

## Observation 2 — the `reasoning_text` 400

Full upstream payload, verbatim (id redacted):

```json
{
  "model": "deepseek-v4.1-flash",
  "error": {
    "message": "The `reasoning_text` in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API. (request_id: <redacted>)",
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "param": null,
    "code": "invalid_request_error"
  }
}
```

Persisted shape: `finish: "error"`, `error.type: "provider.invalid-request"`, HTTP 400.

Counted over the whole local session store: **66 occurrences across 9 distinct sessions**. Two of them are small, early, unrelated sessions:

| session | total messages | max packed tokens in session |
| --- | --- | --- |
| small session X | 26 | ~87k |
| small session Y | 28 | ~112k |

So this 400 fires in sessions that are nowhere near any window limit.

Two things separate it from a context overflow:

1. **It is not `context_length_exceeded`.** On the same provider, requests above roughly 530k packed tokens were rejected with a normal overflow error. This 400 fires well below that, and in sessions under 120k.
2. **It clusters right after compaction or a long-session resume**, which points at the assistant reasoning item being reconstructed and then replayed in a shape the upstream rejects. Most likely a reasoning item sent without its text, or text sent without the matching item id, so the two halves of one item get split apart.

## Why file this separately

#44962 / #50634 / #51503 cover the loop. What I could not find documented anywhere is:

- the paired `reasoning_text must be passed back` 400 on the same long sessions, and
- that **a single new user message reliably breaks the loop**, while the 400 keeps recurring after the loop is broken.

#53489 is directly related: it reported that server-side `finish_details` (such as `repetition_loop`) is not surfaced. Surfacing it, or aborting on it, would turn an unbounded token burn into a clean, catchable error instead of a stream that never ends.

## Ask

1. On the Responses path, when a prior assistant turn contains a reasoning item, is it expected to be echoed back verbatim? If so, the 400 suggests OpenCode can assemble a request where the reasoning text and its item envelope get out of sync. Is that a known issue, and is there a known input shape that triggers it?
2. Is there any server-side repetition guard today? If the upstream already reports `repetition_loop` in `finish_details`, could OpenCode surface it, or abort the turn, instead of streaming the loop to completion?

I can provide the raw session rows (assistant, tool and compaction records, with model and token fields) if that helps. I will redact anything else needed.

### Description

# Free models fail when `shell` or `read` permissions are denied

## Description

Using **OpenCode v2.0.16** with OpenCode free models such as `opencode/big-pickle`.

If either the `shell` or `read` permission is set to `deny`, requests to free models fail with:

```text
Error: OpenCode's free tier can only be used from within OpenCode
```

For example:

```json
{
  "action": "shell",
  "resource": "*",
  "effect": "deny"
},
{
  "action": "read",
  "resource": "*",
  "effect": "deny"
}
```

Changing both permissions to `allow` immediately makes the error disappear:

```json
{
  "action": "shell",
  "resource": "*",
  "effect": "allow"
},
{
  "action": "read",
  "resource": "*",
  "effect": "allow"
}
```

The behavior can be reproduced without restarting OpenCode: changing these permissions while OpenCode is running changes whether the next request succeeds or fails.

## Expected behavior

Tool permissions should control whether the model can use those tools.

Denying `shell` or `read` should not cause a request made from the official OpenCode CLI to be identified as coming from outside OpenCode.

## Actual behavior

Disabling these tools causes OpenCode free-tier requests to be rejected as if the request were not originating from OpenCode.

## Environment

* OpenCode: `v2.0.16`


### Plugins

Reproduced with the official CLI. The behavior is permission-dependent.

### OpenCode version

2.0.16

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run OpenCode v2.0.16.
2. Select a free OpenCode model, for example `opencode/big-pickle`.
3. Set `shell` or `read` to `deny`.
4. Start a new session or send a simple prompt such as `Hello`.
5. The request fails with:

```text
Error: OpenCode's free tier can only be used from within OpenCode
```

6. Change both `shell` and `read` to `allow`.
7. Send the same prompt again.
8. The request succeeds.
