issues.title: [Research] Cache-Aware LLM Request Optimization Middleware for Reducing Agent API Costs
issues.body:
## Executive summary

Investigate a conservative, provider-aware cache optimization pass for session requests. The goal is lower **expected cost per successful task**, not simply fewer prompt tokens. The proposed first phase should observe and measure the existing request path, make only deterministic transformations with a protocol-level correctness argument, and forward the original request whenever safety is uncertain. This issue is research/design only; it does not authorize production changes.

**Recommendation:** proceed with an instrumentation and compatibility spike, then evaluate a small deterministic MVP only if measured cache misses are attributable to avoidable request instability. Do not begin with lossy prompt compression or generic “reordering” middleware. OpenCode already has stable tool sorting, history reconstruction, compaction/pruning, provider transforms, plugin hooks, cache key support, and cached-token accounting. The opportunity is to quantify those behaviors and address specific gaps, not duplicate them in a generic proxy layer.

## Current architecture and repository findings

| Component | File / symbol | Current behavior | Potential opportunity |
|---|---|---|---|
| Session request loop | `packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts`, `SessionPrompt.run` | Reloads projected session messages each loop; filters compacted content; reconstructs `ModelMessage[]`; carries tool calls/results forward; adds a max-steps assistant instruction on the last step. | Record stable segment fingerprints and explain prefix changes per turn; preserve append-only history where valid. |
| System/project instructions | `session/prompt.ts`; `session/instruction.ts`, `Instruction.system`; `session/system.ts` | Assembles environment, project/global/config instructions (including discovered `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`), remote instructions, MCP instructions, skills, structured-output text, and model/agent prompts. Instruction files are re-read per request. | Attribute prefix divergence to source and detect content changes. Re-read is correct for fresh instructions; caching content in-process needs invalidation. |
| Request preparation | `session/llm/request.ts`, `LLMRequestPrep.prepare` | Joins agent/built-in and user/session system text; gives plugins a system transform hook; merges provider/model/agent/variant options; applies `chat.params` and `chat.headers` hooks; filters tools by permissions/user settings; adds session headers. | Best common interception seam for segment analysis before choosing runtime; keep provider-specific policies downstream. |
| Tool building | `session/tools.ts`, `SessionTools.resolve`; `request.ts` | Resolves current registry, model/agent/permission-specific tools and schemas. Request prep sorts tool entries by name. Tool set/schema can legitimately change with permissions, agent, MCP, structured output, or configuration. | Fingerprint names and schemas and report whether changes are justified; do not keep unavailable tools enabled just to preserve a cache. |
| Message projection | `session/message-v2.ts`, `MessageV2.toModelMessagesEffect` | Projects persisted user/assistant/tool parts into AI SDK model messages; retains tool call/result relationships and provider metadata when compatible; may represent files/media and handle provider-specific replay constraints. | Use projected messages as the optimizer input; preserve exact relationships, order, and provider metadata. |
| Provider adaptation | `provider/transform.ts`, `ProviderTransform.message/providerOptions`; `session/llm.ts` | Filters unsupported content, normalizes/sanitizes message parts, applies provider-specific transforms, remaps options, and strips some Responses item IDs. The default path passes prepared content to AI SDK `streamText`; the opt-in native adapter lowers it to `LLMRequest`. | Shared deterministic analysis before runtime selection, plus provider capability policy in transforms/adapters. Avoid independently transforming only one runtime. |
| Context management | `session/compaction.ts`; `session/message-v2.ts` | Estimates tokens from serialized projected messages; overflow compaction summarizes selected history and retains a recent tail; optional pruning replaces older tool output with a compacted marker; tool output truncation is also supported. | Existing lossy controls need evaluation against cache economics and task quality. Preserve the durable event log; only change model projection under explicit policy. |
| Provider serialization/runtime | `provider/provider.ts`; `session/llm.ts`; `session/llm/native-request.ts`; `session/llm/native-runtime.ts` | Provider selection resolves AI SDK models. OpenAI uses Responses API in the first-party provider loader. AI SDK is default; native LLM runtime is experimental/opt-in and supported only for selected providers. | Capability-aware adapter layer is required; do not claim a provider-agnostic body layout or direct access to provider tokenization/KV cache. |
| Cache configuration | `provider/transform.ts`, `ProviderTransform.options/providerOptions/message` | OpenAI-family option generation assigns a `promptCacheKey` from the session ID unless `setCacheKey: false`; selected other APIs receive provider-specific cache markers. The `applyCaching` path does not add markers for first-party `@ai-sdk/openai`. | Verify current SDK wire mapping and model/API support. The current OpenAI docs say GPT-5.6+ routes automatically and does not need a key for cache routing; keys can still separate accounting. |
| Usage/cost | `session/llm/ai-sdk.ts`; `session/session.ts`, `Session.getUsage`; session persistence | Normalizes cache-read/write token reports from AI SDK/provider metadata, stores them, and computes cost using model pricing metadata. | Add aggregate diagnostic metrics (prefix divergence, actual cache ratio, cost/task) without logging prompt contents. Validate telemetry completeness provider by provider. |
| Extension hooks | `request.ts`; `session/prompt.ts`; `session/compaction.ts` | Existing hooks can transform system text, params, headers, projected messages, and compaction behavior. | Prefer existing seams over a second independent middleware stack; document hook ordering and determinism. |

### Request outline

`SessionPrompt.run` projects history and context; `LLMRequestPrep.prepare` produces the system text, messages, tools, parameters, and headers. In the normal API-key case the composed system instruction is represented before the prior/current conversation messages. Tool definitions are a separate request field, not appended chat turns. The AI SDK path passes those fields to `streamText`, then a wrapped model applies `ProviderTransform.message`; the native path runs its own request lowering and transport. The final provider body and tokenization are SDK/provider-controlled.

Relevant sources: [`prompt.ts`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts), [`instruction.ts`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/opencode/src/session/instruction.ts), [`request.ts`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/opencode/src/session/llm/request.ts), [`message-v2.ts`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/opencode/src/session/message-v2.ts), [`tools.ts`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/opencode/src/session/tools.ts), [`transform.ts`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/opencode/src/provider/transform.ts), [`llm.ts`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/opencode/src/session/llm.ts), [`native-runtime.ts`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/opencode/src/session/llm/native-runtime.ts), [`native-request.ts`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/opencode/src/session/llm/native-request.ts), [`compaction.ts`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/opencode/src/session/compaction.ts), [`session.ts`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/opencode/src/session/session.ts).

## Problem statement and evidence to collect

The code already preserves and replays conversation history, alphabetically sorts the resolved tools, exposes request hooks, applies provider-specific compatibility changes, supports compaction/pruning, and records cached token usage. Therefore a blanket “canonicalize everything” layer could duplicate behavior or invalidate protocol-specific metadata.

Potential avoidable divergence remains unmeasured: prompt hooks may be nondeterministic; system/environment/project/MCP/skill content may change; tool availability and schemas may vary; model options and structured-output modes may change; compaction rewrites history; provider transforms can alter serialized messages; separate session cache keys may affect grouping/accounting. Some changes are necessary. The first deliverable should classify and measure them without retaining raw prompt text.

No savings or hit-rate improvement is established by this source inspection. The cost example in the proposal is illustrative only. We need real per-provider/model usage data and controlled task-quality comparisons.

## Research findings

These papers motivate techniques, but they do not establish that transparent prompt rewriting is safe in this harness.

- [Cache-Aware Prompt Compression (CAPC), arXiv:2607.15516](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.15516) (2026 preprint): proposes a two-tier cost model, query-independent compression for reusable context, and a ratio bound intended to avoid crossing cache tiers. The abstract reports API experiments and benchmarks; methods and assumptions must be independently checked before adopting its reported results. Useful hypothesis: a stable compressed shared prefix can retain reuse, while query-dependent compression may change that prefix on every request. Not evidence that OpenCode should compress instructions automatically.
- [Don't Break the Cache, arXiv:2601.06007](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.06007) (2026 preprint): compares full-context, system-only, and dynamic-tool-result strategies on multi-turn agent tasks across providers; reports cost/TTFT reductions and sensitivity to cache-block layout. It supports benchmarking realistic trajectories and varying tools/results, not assuming all providers share one cache model.
- [ACON, arXiv:2510.00615](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.00615): compresses observations and interaction histories, updating natural-language compression guidance using failure analysis; evaluated on long-horizon agent benchmarks. This is a lossy, quality-sensitive context management strategy, best treated as a later optional phase with its own inference/latency cost.
- [SGLang / RadixAttention, arXiv:2312.07104](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.07104): radix-tree longest-prefix matching and KV reuse are server/inference-runtime techniques. OpenCode does not own provider KV caches. Prefix fingerprints/divergence diagnostics are inspired by this idea, but cannot predict provider placement, tokenization, or cache availability.
- [LongLLMLingua, arXiv:2310.06839](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.06839): query-aware context selection/compression can reduce long-context tokens and improve some benchmark outcomes, but output depends on the query and may rewrite the reusable prefix. Test only on dynamic retrieved/tool content and compare quality and cache effects.
- [FrugalGPT, arXiv:2305.05176](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.05176): studies prompt adaptation, model approximation, and cascaded model routing. Routing changes model quality/latency and is a separate optimization, not a prerequisite for cache-safe request normalization.

### Current official provider behavior (verify at implementation time)

- [OpenAI prompt caching](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching): caching is prefix-based and covers rendered instructions, tools, and conversation. A minimum cacheable prefix applies. The current docs distinguish GPT-5.6+ (automatic routing, implicit or explicit cache breakpoints, 1,024 visible-token minimum; `prompt_cache_key` is not needed for routing but can separate accounting) from earlier models where a stable key helps route related requests. Keys do not guarantee a hit. The docs advise preserving history, stable tool definitions/order, and stable prefixes; compaction, changed tools/settings, or edited earlier messages can cause divergence. Cached usage is reported. GPT-5.6+ has explicit vs implicit modes and cache-write charges; exact pricing/retention are model-specific and can change.
- [OpenAI cache diagnostics](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching/diagnostics): Responses API diagnostics for supported newer models can classify some cache comparison outcomes without recording raw prompt/output. Availability is model/API/version limited; baseline/retry requests have normal cost.
- [Anthropic prompt caching](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching): explicit `cache_control` breakpoints are placed on supported prompt blocks; exact matching is required through the marked block, cache lifetime and minimum length vary by model/provider, and usage exposes cache creation/read tokens. The current docs specify a bounded lookback for prior cache points; a growing conversation may need a nearer breakpoint if it grows beyond the lookup window. Tool definitions can be cached by marking the final tool. Breakpoint placement and TTL can affect write/read cost.
- [Anthropic tool caching guidance](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-use-with-prompt-caching): specifically addresses stable tool definitions and invalidation. This differs from OpenAI's automatic/explicit breakpoint model.

Pricing, token minimums, supported fields, TTLs, and SDK option names are unstable. At implementation time, check official docs and the exact pinned SDK version. Provider API claims above are documentation facts; any predicted cost savings are hypotheses until measured.

## Proposed architecture

Do not start with a proxy that parses serialized HTTP bodies. Place a typed, read-only analysis pass at the normalized request seam, then let provider adapters own valid cache controls and serialization:

```text
Session projection / context management
  -> LLMRequestPrep.prepare (typed segments + existing hooks)
  -> cache diagnostics: segment fingerprints, volatility, prefix divergence
  -> provider capability policy (OpenAI / Anthropic / other)
  -> existing AI SDK or opt-in native adapter
  -> normalized usage + cost + diagnostics
```

Represent components as typed segments with `kind`, stable content digest, source/version, and observed change rate—not raw content in metrics. Candidate kinds: model/system instructions, project instructions, skills/MCP context, tool definitions/schemas, durable conversation prefix, tool outputs, current user turn, dynamic metadata, generation settings. Fingerprints diagnose exact harness-visible equality only; they are not provider token hashes and must not be labeled a cache hit.

The shared analysis should run once before the runtime fork. Transformations requiring protocol fields belong in provider adapters. Keep durable session history unchanged. The default should be observe-only with a feature flag and sampled local diagnostics; allow opt-in policies after evaluation. Avoid a new external LLM call in Phase 1.

### Safe, conditional, and unsafe operations

**Safe candidates (still verify provider behavior):** deterministic sorting of equivalent unordered tool maps (already done in request prep); stable serialization/fingerprints of harness-owned schemas; removing nonsemantic serialization jitter only where the typed protocol confirms equivalence; tracking exact unchanged message prefixes; reporting volatile components without content; using documented provider cache controls when supported; no-op fallback if the adapter cannot prove support.

**Conditional / empirical:** moving timestamps or volatile metadata later; changing instruction assembly/layout; retaining a superset tool list and disabling tools via choice/allowed-tool controls; context omission, truncation, or summarization; changing cache-key scope; explicit cache breakpoints; query-independent compression. These can change priority, semantics, accounting, cache economics, or task outcome and require provider/model benchmarks.

**Unsafe by default:** reordering turns, system/developer/user instructions across priority boundaries, tool calls/results, or dependent context; rewriting user text/arguments; dropping paths, code, errors, constraints, signed reasoning/provider metadata, or unresolved tasks; cross-tenant shared request/cache identity; rewriting durable history in place; assuming hashes match provider tokenization.

## Provider compatibility and cost model

Define capabilities per resolved API/model, not a single `cache: true` flag: cache mode (automatic/explicit), eligible component types, minimum length, breakpoints, key semantics, retention, cache write/read prices, usage fields, and SDK support/version. Unknown capability means pass through unchanged. First-party OpenAI Responses, Azure/OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic Messages, Bedrock, Vertex Anthropic, and gateways must not be conflated; gateways may hide upstream behavior.

Estimate an expected request cost as:

`E[C] = E[N_uncached] * P_input + E[N_read] * P_read + E[N_write] * P_write + N_output * P_output + C_preprocess + E[C_retries/additional calls]`.

For task-level decisions use `E[cost per successful task]`, with success probability and expected retries/calls included. Obtain actual rates from resolved model metadata/official pricing where possible. Estimate cache probabilities only from observed telemetry grouped by compatible provider/model/workspace/key/prefix signature and time window; start with descriptive rates and confidence intervals, not a learned policy. If no cache-read/write report exists, mark cost split unknown instead of imputing a hit. Include latency and task success as constraints. Cost values and provider terms must be versioned by date/model.

## Evaluation plan

Use replayable, representative OpenCode sessions with deterministic tool fixtures and a holdout set. Run cold/warm repeats and realistic inter-request delays; vary tool availability, instruction files, project changes, and compaction. Where provider caches are opaque, record reported cache usage and official diagnostics where supported; do not infer cache hits from matching hashes alone.

| Configuration | Hypothesis | Measurement | Success gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline current behavior | Establish actual divergence, usage, cost, latency, and task success. | Existing harness, repeated identical task/session patterns. | Valid, reproducible baseline with provider/model dimensions. |
| Observe-only diagnostics | Fingerprints explain avoidable prefix changes at low overhead. | Segment digests, LCP token estimate where a matching tokenizer is available, CPU/memory, cache usage. | No prompt-content logging; negligible overhead target set before experiment; useful attribution coverage. |
| Deterministic normalization | Stable harness-owned serialization improves reuse without semantic change. | Same workloads, compare provider-reported cache reads/writes and costs. | No protocol failures; no statistically meaningful quality regression; cost improvement on eligible workloads. |
| Cache policy | Provider-specific key/breakpoint settings improve cost without write-cost or routing regressions. | OpenAI and Anthropic separately, supported models only. | Net total cost/task decreases with cache telemetry and unchanged task success. |
| Context optimization | Pruning/compaction changes can trade cache reuse for token reduction. | Existing compaction/prune vs candidate policy. | Lower cost per successful task, quality noninferiority margin pre-registered, no increased critical omissions. |
| Adaptive policy | Historical telemetry improves candidate selection. | Train/validation/holdout split by tasks and time. | Beats simpler policy on holdout including preprocessing, retries, output, and latency. |

Required metrics: input/cached-read/cache-write/output tokens; API cost/request and per successful task; cache ratio; TTFT and end-to-end latency; call/retry/tool counts; task completion and correctness; preprocessing CPU/memory. Include short requests where overhead dominates, long-running coding sessions, large stable toolsets, large tool outputs, repeated project instructions, changing tools/files, compaction, and multi-provider requests. Define statistical power and quality noninferiority thresholds before running.

## Phased plan

### Phase 0 — Instrument and characterize (recommended first)
- Inventory current requests by provider/model/runtime and hook configuration.
- Add no-content diagnostics in a development branch or opt-in instrumentation prototype: fingerprints, segment lengths, prefix divergence, schema/order changes, actual cache usage, cost.
- Confirm telemetry parity and provider API/SDK capabilities with fixtures and official docs.
- Produce a baseline report and a short decision memo.

### Phase 1 — Deterministic cache-safe MVP (conditional on Phase 0)
- Typed request segmentation and versioned fingerprints.
- Retain existing deterministic tool sorting; add schema-diff diagnostics and serialization stability checks.
- Provider capability interface for documented cache options and their versioned constraints.
- Apply only transformations with an equivalence argument; keep original request fallback.
- Add opt-in flags and request/usage correlation without prompt content logging.
- No compression, extra LLM calls, user-message rewriting, or persistent history rewrite.

### Phase 2 — Context reduction (separately gated)
- Evaluate existing pruning/truncation/compaction policies against cache usage and task quality.
- Consider duplicate/obsolete output removal and compression only for eligible dynamic context, preserving complete durable event history.
- Account for compression inference and cache re-write costs.

### Phase 3 — Adaptive optimization (evidence required)
- Use historical hit rates and costs for thresholds/breakpoint decisions.
- Consider model routing only as a separate product/quality decision.
- Reject complexity that does not beat Phase 1 on a holdout workload.

## Answers to investigation questions

1. **Safest insertion point?** Read-only analysis after `LLMRequestPrep.prepare` has assembled messages/tools/params and before AI SDK/native branching. Provider-specific mutation belongs in adapter transforms.
2. **Avoid public API changes?** Likely yes; internal typed request additions/options should suffice, subject to adapter boundaries.
3. **Stable components?** Built-in/agent instructions, sorted tool names/schemas when the same agent/permissions/registry apply, and prior persisted messages when not transformed/compacted. Actual stability must be measured.
4. **Divergence causes?** New user/assistant/tool turns; system/project instruction changes; environment/MCP/skills; dynamic tool registry/permissions; plugin hooks; model/variant/structured output settings; provider-specific compatibility transforms; compaction/pruning.
5. **Unnecessary tool changes?** Tool sorting is deterministic already; available tool set/schema may vary for valid reasons. Need fingerprints to tell which.
6. **Can normalization help?** Possibly for accidental nondeterministic harness-owned data. No evidence yet that current stable serialization is a material source of misses.
7. **Move dynamic metadata later?** Only if it is semantically independent and provider API permits it; not a generic safe rewrite. Measure first.
8. **Prefix fingerprint accuracy?** Exact bytes/typed tree are measurable; provider token prefix is not exact without the provider's renderer/tokenizer. AI SDK final serialization can differ. Diagnostics must distinguish these.
9. **Telemetry?** AI SDK usage normalization captures cache read/write fields where providers report them; support and precision vary. OpenAI and Anthropic have provider-side cache usage; OpenAI newer Responses models also expose diagnostics. Validate exact SDK mapping and native path.
10. **No-extra-inference savings?** Stable serialization, cache key/breakpoint configuration, accurate usage accounting, and avoiding avoidable schema/instruction churn are candidates. Savings unproven.
11. **When compression is worthwhile?** When avoided uncached/read/write charges plus future token savings exceed compressor costs, cache misses/writes, retries, and expected quality loss; evaluate over successful task trajectories.
12. **Never remove casually?** User constraints, system/developer instructions, paths/code/errors/test output needed for task, tool call/result pairing, signatures/provider metadata, unresolved state, and safety/permission context.
13. **Hit probability?** Estimate empirically per provider/model/config/prefix family/time window, with confidence bounds and cache TTL/traffic controls; never treat a hash match as a hit guarantee.
14. **Multi-provider representation?** Common typed segments plus capability adapters; avoid assuming same ordering, cache thresholds, breakpoints, pricing, or usage semantics.
15. **Overhead?** Fingerprinting is linear in serialized request size; measure CPU, memory, and latency. No target value should be claimed before profiling.
16. **Reliability?** Replay benchmarks, paired task runs, regression suite, quality noninferiority criteria, exact transformation audits, and original-request fallback.
17. **Smallest MVP?** Observe-only segment/prefix diagnostics plus provider-usage aggregation; then a narrowly scoped, deterministic transformation only if attributable churn exists.
18. **Reusable code?** `LLMRequestPrep`, provider transform/capability metadata, sorted tool construction, `Token.estimate`, compaction/prune, usage normalization and session cost tracking, and existing plugin seams.
19. **Paper findings vs hypotheses?** Paper benchmark results are their own empirical claims and workload-specific; proposed fingerprinting, middleware placement, expected savings, and transfer to OpenCode are engineering hypotheses.
20. **Evidence to implement?** Enough to justify a measurement spike. Not enough to justify broad rewrite/compression middleware or claim savings today.

## Risks and mitigations

- **Semantic change:** allowlist only transformations with equivalence reasoning; opt-in, compare original/candidate, keep fallback.
- **Cache misses/writes increase:** provider/model-specific experiments; include writes and retention costs; no generic breakpoint policy.
- **Existing useful cache invalidated by compaction:** measure compaction cost and task-level effect; do not disable useful context management solely to preserve a cache.
- **Tool correctness/security:** never retain disallowed tools to stabilize schema; preserve permission and tool-call semantics.
- **Cross-user leakage/probing:** isolate fingerprint telemetry and keys by tenant/workspace; do not share raw prompt data; respect provider key/accounting isolation.
- **Privacy:** store digests and aggregate counts only; keyed/HMAC digests if stable cross-process comparison is needed; no raw prompt/tool outputs in telemetry.
- **Provider/version drift:** explicit capability/version matrix and contract tests; unknown behavior falls back unchanged.
- **Tokenization mismatch:** label local estimates; compare with provider usage, avoid claimed exact LCP in tokens unless exact tokenizer+serialization is known.
- **Added latency/complexity:** profile and require holdout benefit; no extra LLM call in MVP.
- **Plugin nondeterminism:** instrument hook outputs without logging contents; surface hook-contributed divergence and preserve existing plugin order.

## Open questions

- Which model/provider combinations dominate real request cost and expose reliable cache telemetry?
- Does session-scoped OpenAI `promptCacheKey` still improve routing on older models in the supported catalog, and how does the current AI SDK map the option? On newer models it is not required for routing per current docs; should it remain for accounting isolation?
- Are `system` message and tool ordering at the final SDK wire layer stable across supported SDK versions?
- Which plugin transforms are nondeterministic, and are they intended to vary each call?
- Does existing compaction/pruning save total task cost after accounting for a cold rewritten prefix and extra summary call?
- Are explicit cache breakpoints supported by pinned AI SDKs and useful for actual OpenAI/Anthropic models in this repo?
- Can OpenAI diagnostics be wired safely without adding a second billed request or exposing sensitive prompt data?
- What noninferiority margin, test corpus, and overhead budget should gate lossy Phase 2 work?

## Acceptance criteria

### Investigation / Phase 0
- [ ] Existing request assembly, projections, providers, hooks, context management, and usage tracking are documented (see table above).
- [ ] Official model-specific OpenAI and Anthropic cache behavior is re-checked at implementation time and mapped to supported SDK versions.
- [ ] A privacy-preserving report measures request component stability, prefix divergence, cache telemetry availability, and cost by provider/model.
- [ ] Candidate causes of divergence are separated into necessary behavior and avoidable harness churn.
- [ ] Baseline benchmark includes cold/warm cache, realistic delays, multiple task types, quality, latency, and task-level cost.
- [ ] A decision record recommends proceed/no-go based on measured opportunity; no unmeasured savings claim.

### Any later implementation
- [ ] No change to durable user/assistant history or tool-call meaning from Phase 1 transformations.
- [ ] Provider/model capability is checked; unsupported/unknown cases forward original request.
- [ ] No raw prompt content is logged or used in cross-tenant metrics.
- [ ] Cache read/write token accounting and total cost are validated against provider responses.
- [ ] Paired holdout benchmarks show lower expected cost per successful task with task quality within a pre-registered noninferiority margin.
- [ ] Overhead, latency, retries, provider errors, and rollback behavior are documented.
- [ ] Any lossy pruning/compression is an explicit separately gated policy with durable original history retained.

## References

- CAPC: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.15516
- Don't Break the Cache: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.06007
- ACON: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.00615
- SGLang / RadixAttention: https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.07104
- LongLLMLingua: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.06839
- FrugalGPT: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.05176
- OpenAI prompt caching: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching
- OpenAI prompt cache diagnostics: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching/diagnostics
- Anthropic prompt caching: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching
- Anthropic tool caching: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-use-with-prompt-caching

issues.title: Top-level `permission: {"read": "deny"}` makes every headless `opencode run` fail with a misleading free-tier 403
issues.body:
opencode 1.19.0, macOS (darwin). The repro is a single config key.

Supplying an inline config merge that denies top-level `read` causes every headless
`opencode run` to fail:

```
{"permission":{"read":"deny"}}
```

```
$ OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT='{"permission":{"read":"deny"}}' \
    opencode run "Reply with exactly: PROBE_OK" --model opencode/space-bunny-free --format json

{"type":"error", ... "error":{"name":"APIError","data":{
  "message":"OpenCode's free tier can only be used from within OpenCode. Download it at https://opencode.ai and keep building.",
  "statusCode":403, "isRetryable":false, ...}}}
```

## Minimal matrix

| Config | Result |
|---|---|
| `{"permission":{"read":"deny"}}` | **403** |
| `{"permission":{"read":"allow"}}` | OK |
| `{"permission":{"read":"ask"}}` | OK |
| `{"permission":{}}` | OK |
| no config at all | OK |
| `{"agent":{"x":{"mode":"subagent","permission":{"read":"deny"}}}}` | OK |

Characteristics:

- **Deterministic** — reproduced 2/2.
- **Order-independent** — interleaved A/B/C over 3 rounds, identical results each round. Not rate limiting.
- **Narrow** — sweeping all eleven documented permission keys individually, `read` is the *only* one that triggers it. `bash`, `edit`, `glob`, `grep`, `list`, `task`, `webfetch`, `websearch`, `lsp`, `skill` all pass.
- **Nesting matters** — the identical denial scoped inside an agent definition works.

## Why this reads as a bug rather than a tier gate

All six probes above ran on the same account, same free tier, same model. Four succeeded. A billing check fails consistently; this one flips on config shape alone.

The practical cost is that the error text is **misleading**: it points users at upgrading to a paid plan for behaviour that payment does not change. If this is deliberate free-tier policy, the boundary seems arbitrary — `read: "deny"` behaves differently from `read: "ask"`, which is not a distinction a user would guess at. Either way the error message seems worth revising.

## Workaround

Scope the denial to an agent instead of top level:

```
{"agent":{"my-agent":{"mode":"subagent","permission":{"read":"deny", ...}}}}
```

That's what I ended up doing, but it required a 3×3 probe matrix to find, which suggests the failure isn't where the message says it is.

Happy to provide logs or a fuller repro script if useful.

issues.title: policy: deny shell * on custom agent breaks free tier with "can only be used from within OpenCode"
issues.body:
## Summary

Enabling `permissions: [{action: shell, resource: "*", effect: deny}]` on a custom primary agent makes every request fail on all free-tier models with `OpenCode's free tier can only be used from within OpenCode`, even though the request originates from inside OpenCode TUI.

## Environment

- opencode version: v2.0.13
- OS: Linux saka 7.2.5-3-omarchy #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Mon, 14 Sep 2026 19:55:01 +0000 x86_64 GNU/Linux
- Terminal: TERM=xterm-256color, TERM_PROGRAM=ghostty, COLORTERM=truecolor
- Shell: /usr/bin/bash
- Install/channel: latest
- Active plugins: none found

## Reproduction

1. Use TUI with custom primary agent at `~/.config/opencode/agents/search.md` with frontmatter:
```yaml
permissions:
  - action: edit
    resource: "*"
    effect: deny
  - action: shell
    resource: "*"
    effect: deny
  - action: subagent
    resource: "*"
    effect: deny
  - action: subagent
    resource: "explore"
    effect: allow
  - action: subagent
    resource: "general"
    effect: allow
  - action: websearch
    resource: "*"
    effect: allow
  - action: webfetch
    resource: "*"
    effect: allow
  - action: read
    resource: "*"
    effect: allow
  - action: glob
    resource: "*"
    effect: allow
  - action: grep
    resource: "*"
    effect: allow
```
2. Send any message to that agent on any Console free-tier model via TUI.
3. Observe `Error: Error from provider (Console): OpenCode's free tier can only be used from within OpenCode`.
4. Comment out the `shell: "*"` deny lines -> works again.

## Expected Behavior

Shell deny should only block shell tool calls; the LLM request itself should still authenticate as in-OpenCode free-tier use.

## Actual Behavior

Entire session fails with free-tier origin error on every message, before any tool use. Always reproducible; removal fixes. Affects all free models. Error is single line only.

## Additional Context

- Interface: TUI. Agent `mode: primary`.
- Related same-error cluster, different triggers: #50081 (custom agents), #50516 (subagents, duplicate), #49966 (Muse Spark Free inside OpenCode), #50366, #49756 (User-Agent not forwarded).
- No exact match for `permission deny shell` + free-tier trigger — appears to be a new trigger for the same validation bug.

issues.title: tui: messages_copy with nothing selected writes an empty clipboard (wipes the previous content)
issues.body:
### What happens

In the TUI, `<leader>y` (`messages_copy`) with nothing selected writes an **empty string** to the system clipboard. It does not leave the clipboard as it was: whatever was there before is gone.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Copy some text in another app, so the clipboard has content.
2. In the opencode TUI, with the composer focused and no selection active, press `ctrl+x` then `y`.
3. Paste anywhere: the clipboard is empty (same on both sides of the clipboard bridge I checked).

Reproduced twice on v2.0.30. The key presses were injected with `herdr pane send-keys`, so nothing else touched the terminal, and the clipboard was read back before and after.

### Expected

Either copy the focused or the last message, or do nothing and leave the clipboard untouched.

### Environment

- opencode v2.0.30 (TUI), Linux (Ubuntu 26.04), x86_64
- Plain terminal over SSH inside `herdr` 0.9.3, which reports `TERM_PROGRAM=herdr` and has mouse capture on, so the TUI may never see a selection
- X11 present on the host (`DISPLAY` set) and `xclip` installed and on PATH
- `terminal.copy` left at its default

### Notes

- The [troubleshooting page](https://opencode.ai/docs/troubleshooting/) asks for `xclip`/`xsel` (or `wl-clipboard`) on the machine running opencode. Here `xclip` is installed and on PATH and the copy is still empty, so this is not a missing-tool problem.
- Copying with a mouse selection inside the multiplexer does work (the multiplexer does that copy itself), so the bug is specific to the TUI's own copy action.
- Related, but not the same: #50208 ("Copied to clipboard" does not update the local clipboard over SSH and tmux) — there the clipboard is left alone; here it is overwritten with nothing.

issues.title: Windows CLI: WSL2 镜像网络预留范围内的 45278 导致服务启动失败，端口查询无占用记录
issues.body:
### Description

Windows 原生 CLI 启动失败，提示 `127.0.0.1:45278` 被其他进程占用，但 Windows 和 WSL 均查不到该端口的连接/监听记录。实测该端口位于正在运行的 WSL2 镜像网络的临时端口范围 `44620–48715` 内。

```text
Starting background server...
Error: Server process exited with code 1
Error: Managed service port 45278 on 127.0.0.1 is already in use by another process.
Configure another port with `opencode service set port <port>` and start the service again.
```

### OpenCode version

2.0.30，Windows 原生 npm 包 `@opencode/cli`。`opencode service get` 返回 `{}`，`opencode service status` 返回 `stopped`。

### Operating System

Windows 11，build 26200.9711；WSL 2.7.3.0，Ubuntu 正在运行。

相关 `.wslconfig` 配置：

```ini
[wsl2]
networkingMode=Mirrored
[experimental]
hostAddressLoopback=true
```

### Terminal

PowerShell

### Steps to reproduce

1. 在启用了 WSL2 镜像网络的 Windows 上运行 Ubuntu。
2. 查询 WSL 临时端口范围：
   `wsl -d Ubuntu -- cat /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range`
   本机结果为 `44620 48715`。
3. 在 Windows PowerShell 执行 `opencode`，服务尝试监听 45278，报上述错误。

排查结果：

- `Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort 45278` 无匹配记录。
- `netstat -anoq` 无 45278 记录；WSL 的 `ss -tanp` 也无该端口记录。
- IPv4/IPv6 的 `netsh interface ... show excludedportrange protocol=tcp` 仅列出 3336 和 50000–50059，均不包含 45278。
- 独立于 OpenCode 的 .NET TCP 监听测试也失败，返回 SocketException **10048 / AddressAlreadyInUse**。
- 对照测试：45279、45000、46000、47000 同样失败；43000、44000、49374、18080 均可监听。

最小端口测试（Windows PowerShell）：

```powershell
$listener = [System.Net.Sockets.TcpListener]::new(
    [System.Net.IPAddress]::Loopback, 45278
)
try { $listener.Start(); 'bind succeeded' }
finally { $listener.Stop() }
```

### Expected behavior

端口不可绑定时，提示应涵盖系统/WSL 预留的可能性，而不直接断言存在占用进程。对于未显式配置的服务端口，建议尝试可用端口并保存发现信息，避免一直重试不可用端口。

### Additional context

上述证据与 WSL 镜像模式的 HNS 临时端口预留行为一致：microsoft/WSL#40169。未通过关闭 WSL 做对照实验，因此这是根据端口范围和独立绑定测试得出的判断。

可尝试 `opencode service set port 18080` 绕过。本报告只验证了 18080 能正常绑定，尚未修改服务配置或验证 OpenCode 在该端口完整启动。

关联 #53351（显式 excluded TCP range）和 #55907（进程竞争）。此处补充的区别是：端口不在 netsh 排除列表内，且没有服务进程时独立绑定测试仍失败。

issues.title: invalid opencode.json is silently ignored
issues.body:

Set a theme whose panel background token has alpha 0 (e.g. a transparent theme where `background.raised.base` is fully transparent). 2. Start `opencode` (v2.0.26) in WezTerm — the session pane and input area show the host terminal background through. 3. Open the embedded terminal panel ## Expected Behavior The embedded terminal panel's default background composites via SGR 49 so the host terminal's background shows through, matching the rest of the transparent TUI. ## Actual Behavior The panel is a solid block filled with the theme's panel background RGB. `terminalPalette()` (`packages/tui/src/component/terminal-pane.tsx:338`, used at `:159`) writes the background as an opaque 6-digit hex via OSC 11, and the embedded terminal renderable's `transparentBackground` option is never set anywhere in the tree (`git grep transparentBackground v2.0.26` → no matches), so it stays `false`. ## Additional Context - opentui side is already solved: anomalyco/opentui#1502 adds `transparentBackground` to `EmbeddedTerminalRenderable`; rationale and rendering-chain analysis in anomalyco/opentui#1501. - v2.0.26 pins `@opentui/core@0.5.17`, so the native capability is already in the dependency tree; only the consumer opt-in is missing. - Suggested change in `packages/tui/src/component/terminal-pane.tsx`: pass `transparentBackground={panelBackground.a === 0}` (using the same `background.raised.base` token already consumed at `:159`/`:287`) to the `` renderable. issues.title: Agent steps limit does not stop opencode run on 1.19.1: tools still sent with tool_choice auto after the cap (2.0.30 stops)
V2: summary compaction still reads almost nothing from the prompt cache, even right after a warm request
issues.body:
## Description

This is the new report requested in the closing comment of #43249 ("If you're seeing repeated cold compactions on
current V2, please open a new report with the exact version, provider/model, and input/cache-read counts").

On V2, summary compactions read almost nothing from the prompt cache. This also happens when the
previous model call in the same session ran less than a minute earlier and read more than 80% of its input from the
cache. On Anthropic Messages routes, about 96% of each compaction's input is billed as a new cache write.

Selection: compactions in the local `opencode.db` that completed on 2.0.12 or later (version estimated from the
sessions created just before), with at least 50k input tokens.
In each case, the previous model call in the session ran at most 5 minutes earlier and read at least 80% of its input
from the cache. Only 1 of these 132 compactions read at least 50% of its input from the cache.

| Route | Compactions | Versions | Median input | Median cache read | Read share | Write share | Median gap since previous call |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Built-in `openai` provider (`gpt-6-luna`, `gpt-6-sol`, `gpt-6-astra`), auto | 113 | 2.0.16–2.0.21 | 253,321 | 20,992 | 7.4% | 0.0% | 0.68 min |
| Anthropic Messages (Anthropic API, Vertex AI, Azure AI Foundry; Claude models), mostly manual | 12 | 2.0.14–2.0.21 | 407,080 | 8,051 | 4.2% | 95.8% | 0.76 min |

Example rows (previous call input / previous call cache read → compaction input / cache read / cache write):

```text
2.0.21 openai gpt-6-luna auto    gap 0.54 min: 784,645 / 776,704 → 487,401 / 4,608 / 0
2.0.19 anthropic claude-sonnet-5-5 auto gap 0.31 min: 903,250 / 883,134 → 641,900 / 8,051 / 633,845
2.0.16 google-vertex claude-opus-5-5 manual gap 1.27 min: 837,966 / 836,224 → 672,165 / 0 / 672,161
2.0.22 google-vertex gemini-3.8-flash auto gap 0.57 min: 951,296 / 899,938 → 421,711 / 0 / 0
```

The constant read of about 21k tokens on OpenAI and about 8k tokens on Anthropic looks like the system prompt and tool
definitions only. The cache match appears to stop at the first conversation message.

## Possible cause

In 2.0.22, `summarize` sends only the older part of the history, `split.older`, and keeps the recent part as text
outside the request:

- <https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v2.0.22/packages/core/src/session/compaction.ts#L263-L270>
- <https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v2.0.22/packages/core/src/session/compaction.ts#L690-L701>

For Anthropic, this would explain the result. The request's cache breakpoints sit at the end of the older part. The
cache entries that the main loop keeps fresh end at the end of the full history, so no live entry matches the shorter
prefix. For OpenAI, I would expect the shorter prefix to still match, so I could not explain the miss there. The
request may differ from the main-loop request in the first conversation message, or in transport or cache-key
routing. I did not confirm either of these.

The closing comment on #43249 cites a `/compact` test on 2.0.12 that read about 99% from the cache. The one hit in
our data (`github-copilot`, 2.0.20) read 113,792 of 114,744 input tokens. Its input was about the same size as the
previous call's input (113,815), which suggests that the older part covered almost the full history there.

## Possible direction

One option is to send the main loop's full current request with the summary instruction appended, as
`session.generate` does, and apply the older/recent split to the stored result instead of to the request. #46369
proposes something in this direction as an opt-in. Related: #48542 (Anthropic compaction cache writes never read).

## Plugins

A local plugin rewrites the `cache_control` TTL from 5m to 1h on Anthropic Messages requests. It does not change
OpenAI requests, so the OpenAI rows are unaffected by it.

## OpenCode version

2.0.22 (data from 2.0.12 to 2.0.22)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run a long session on the built-in `openai` provider until auto compaction triggers, or run `/compact` on a
   session with an Anthropic Messages model after more than one exchange.
2. Compare `tokens.cache.read` of the compaction message (`session_message.type = 'compaction'`) with the previous
   assistant message in the same session.

## Operating System

Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS

## Terminal

Not applicable (OpenCode server)

issues.title: [BUG] Web UI: New session button does nothing when no session/project is open (2.0.30); shortcut hardcoded to browser-reserved Ctrl+T
issues.body:
### Description

On a fresh web UI state (no project / no session open), clicking the "+" / "New session" button does **nothing** — no draft is created and **no network request is issued**. It works only after a session is already open.

### Environment

- OpenCode **2.0.30**, Windows x64
- Web UI paired via `opencode pair` (`http://127.0.0.1:45278`)
- Browser: Chrome and Edge (shortcut collision applies to Firefox/Safari too)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run `opencode pair` and open the link in a browser (fresh state, no project added).
2. On the start screen (`/`), click the "+" / "New session" button.
3. Nothing happens.

**Expected:** a new session draft opens (same as when a session is already open).
**Actual:** nothing happens; zero requests are made.

### Evidence

- The button exists and is not disabled: `aria-label="Nova sessão"`, `disabled=false`.
- Clicking it — via the UI **and** via a programmatic `element.click()` — fires **no request at all** (no `POST /api/session`).
- Console shows **no JS errors** (only asset `preload` warnings).
- **Control:** with any session already open (URL `/server/<enc>/session/<id>`), the *same* button works — it navigates to `/new-session?draftId=...` and issues `POST /api/worktree/refresh` (204).
- The server is healthy: `opencode api post /api/session` creates a session successfully. This is a client-side-only bug.

### Root cause (matches #37606)

`packages/app/src/components/titlebar.tsx` → `openNewTab()` returns early when no project is known, exactly as diagnosed in #37606:

```ts
const fallback = global.servers.list().flatMap((conn) => {
  const project = global.ensureServerCtx(conn).projects.list()[0]
  return project ? [{ server: ServerConnection.key(conn), project }] : []
})[0]
if (!fallback) return   // <- fresh state lands here and nothing happens
```

#37606 was auto-closed by the inactivity bot (`NOT_PLANNED`). The bug still reproduces on 2.0.30.

### Additional: the new-session shortcut is a browser-reserved key

The button tooltip advertises **Ctrl+T**. `Ctrl+T` is reserved by every major browser (new tab), so the key never reaches the web UI.

- Verified the handler itself is fine: dispatching a **synthetic** `Ctrl+T` keydown to the page *does* open `/new-session?draftId=...`. The default key choice is simply unreachable in a browser.
- Verified the web UI does **not** read `cli.json`: setting `keybinds.session.new = "alt+n"` had **no effect** in the browser (Alt+N did nothing) while Ctrl+T kept working. So users cannot remap it.

### Impact

On the start screen there is **no way** to create a session from the web UI: the button is a silent no-op and the advertised shortcut is unreachable in any browser.

### Suggested fixes

1. Fall back to the server/location directory (as proposed in #37606) so the button always creates a draft.
2. Use a browser-safe default shortcut (e.g. `Ctrl+Shift+N` / `Alt+N`) and/or make web UI keybinds user-configurable.

### Workarounds

- Open any existing session first, then use the "New session" button.
- Create the session in the terminal TUI (`leader`+`n`, default `Ctrl+X` then `N`); sessions are shared with the web client.

issues.title: server: restart that interrupts a tool call fails the next Anthropic request with "tool_use.input: Input should be an object"
issues.body:
## Summary

A server restart that interrupts a running `shell` tool call breaks the next request in that session. Anthropic rejects it with `400 tool_use.input: Input should be an object`. One restart did this to all 3 sessions that had a tool call running at the time. This may be a reliable way to trigger #53865.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.0.30 (server) after the restart. Unknown before it.
- OS: Linux 7.0.0-1014-aws x86_64
- Terminal: none. Sessions run headless through the server API.
- Shell: /bin/bash
- Install/channel: latest
- Active plugins: `compound-engineering` (git plugin); local plugins `goal`, `session-id.js`, `skill-commands.ts` in `.opencode/plugins/`
- Provider/model: built-in `anthropic` provider, direct (no relay), `claude-opus-5-5`, variant `high`

## Reproduction

1. Start background subagent sessions on the Anthropic provider that run long `shell` calls.
2. Restart the opencode server while a `shell` call is running.
3. The session gets the "server restarted" message. The interrupted call is stored with `status: "error"`, `error.type: "aborted"` ("Tool execution interrupted: shell") and `executed: false`.
4. The session sends its next request.

## Expected Behavior

The interrupted call is replayed as a `tool_use` with object input and an error `tool_result`, and the session continues.

## Actual Behavior

The request fails in about 0.3 s:

```
{"type":"error","error":{"type":"invalid_request_error","message":"messages.142.content.1.tool_use.input: Input should be an object"}}
```

opencode saves an empty assistant message (`content: []`, `finish: "error"`, `error.type: "provider.invalid-request"`) and ends the turn with `outcome: "failed"`. A later turn in the same session succeeded, but the parent agent had already received `state="error"` and treated the subagent as crashed.

All 3 sessions, times in UTC:

| Session | Interrupted call's message | Restart | Failed request | Error path |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | `[reasoning, shell]` | 22:16:00 | 22:16:05 | `messages.142.content.1` |
| B | `[reasoning, reasoning, shell]` | 22:16:00 | 22:18:01 | `messages.147.content.2` |
| C | `[reasoning, shell]` | 22:16:00 | 22:18:34 | `messages.164.content.0` |

In A and B, the error's `content` index is the interrupted `shell` call's position in its message. In C it is one lower, perhaps because a reasoning block was dropped on replay.

## Additional Context

- **Stored inputs are clean.** `opencode session export` shows every tool input as an object, including the 3 interrupted calls. So, as in #53865, the bad input probably exists only in the outgoing request. I did not capture that request.
- **This is a different case from #53685.** That fix (2.0.25) closes out calls whose arguments never finished. These calls had complete arguments and had started running (`time.ran` is set) when the restart aborted them.
- **Each session had one interrupted call.** No other tool call in the 3 sessions was interrupted.
- **Not reproduced on purpose.** All 3 cases come from one unplanned restart.
- **Related:** #53865, closed as not planned. On 2026-10-14 a user reported it still happens on 2.0.29 in background subagent sessions.

issues.title: [BUG] zsh completion: top-level flags (--continue, --session, --fork) never suggested by tab completion
issues.body: ## Summary Top-level (root) flags of the `opencode` command are never suggested by shell tab completion. Completing `opencode ` lists subcommands but no `--option` flags. ## Expected behavior Typing `opencode --` (or `opencode ` showing both commands and flags) should suggest all valid top-level flags, including `--continue`, `--session`, and `--fork`. ## Actual behavior `opencode --get-yargs-completions opencode --co` (and `--cont`) returns only: ``` --help --version --print-logs --log-level --pure ``` Flags like `--continue`, `--session`, and `--fork` are valid (confirmed via `opencode --help`: `-c, --continue`, `-s, --session`, `--fork`), but are never surfaced by the completion script. ## Reproduction ```sh # Install completion opencode completion > /usr/share/zsh/site-functions/_opencode # In zsh: opencode --co # suggests --help, --version, --print-logs, --log-level, --pure opencode # lists subcommands only, no flags ``` The completion script is a thin wrapper that calls `opencode --get-yargs-completions` at runtime, so this is a bug in the yargs completion generation (`--get-yargs-completions`), not in the installed completion file. The installed file is byte-identical to the current `opencode completion` output. ## Environment - opencode binary: `/usr/bin/opencode` - shell: zsh - completion installed via `opencode completion` to `/usr/share/zsh/site-functions/_opencode`

prs.title: feat(desktop): install Windows updates in about a second
prs.body:
Restarting into a Windows update took 12 s on a fast NVMe machine and about 30 s on slower ones. It now takes about 1.4 s: the running app unpacks the update in the background, so the restart only renames a directory.

![Where the installer spends its time](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4480dbc2-8dd1-431b-b4e0-238871f102e6)

## Results

Real 236 MB beta payload, rebuilt under a throwaway app id with a timestamp at each NSIS step. Windows 11, NVMe, Defender on. Update runs start with the app already closed.

| Scenario | `dev` | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Update | 12.0 s | **1.4 s** |
| Update, first one after this ships (old app, old uninstaller) | 12.0 s | 7.3 s |
| Update, if the background unpack is skipped | 12.0 s | 5.4 s |
| Fresh install | 6.9 s | 3.9 s |
| Uninstall | 2.6 s | 0.8 s |
| Background unpack, while the app runs | – | 3.4 s |

## Where the time went

| Step | `dev` | This PR | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Is the app running? (installer and old uninstaller) | 4.8 s | 0.3 s | In-process Toolhelp walk instead of 3 Windows PowerShell launches each |
| Start installer | 2.1 s | 0.1 s | `CRCCheck off`; Defender already scanned the exe during `--stage` |
| Decompress 741 MB (single-threaded LZMA2) | 3.0 s | 0 s | Done earlier by `--stage`; the restart renames the directory |
| Copy temp → install dir | 0.7 s | 0 s | Extracts straight into the empty install directory |
| Copy installer into updater cache | 0.1–1.7 s | 0 s | Hard link when the update runs from the updater's own download |

## How a staged update works

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant App as Running app
  participant New as New installer
  participant Disk as Programs folder
  App->>App: downloadUpdate()
  App->>New: --stage (hidden, app keeps running)
  New->>Disk: extract to "OpenCode.staging"
  New->>Disk: rename to "OpenCode.update-<payload hash>"
  Note over App: Restart to update
  App->>New: --updated (electron-updater)
  New->>Disk: old uninstaller empties "OpenCode"
  New->>Disk: rename "OpenCode.update-<hash>" → "OpenCode"
  New->>App: relaunch
```

- The app side is one call after the download, in `packages/gui-extensions/src/updater/platform.ts`:

  ```ts
  execFileAsync(installer, ["--stage"], { windowsHide: true, timeout: unpackTimeout })
  ```

- `--stage` runs in `preInit`, before the single-instance mutex, and exits 0 only when it staged. The installer stores the payload once: both `File` commands point at the same stored 7z, so NSIS deduplicates it (+1 KB).
- The swap (`customInstallStagedApp` in `packages/desktop/resources/windows/installer.nsh`) only takes a directory whose name carries this payload's hash, and only into an emptied install directory. Anything else falls back to normal extraction. Install, `--stage` and uninstall remove leftover staged directories.

## app-builder-lib patch

`patches/app-builder-lib@26.15.7.patch` changes two NSIS templates:

- `extractEmbeddedAppPackage` calls the `customInstallStagedApp` hook first and skips extraction when it reports `installed`.
- `extractUsing7za` extracts straight into an empty `$OUTDIR`. A non-empty one still goes through temp with the stock retry loop.
- The updater-cache copy becomes a hard link when `$EXEPATH` is inside the updater cache directory, and falls back to the copy.

## Notes

- **App check:** an update gives the quitting app 10 s to exit before it is terminated (stock: about 5 s, spent mostly starting PowerShell). A manual install still asks first.
- **Disk:** a staged update uses about 740 MB until the restart. Staging is skipped when free space is under twice that.
- **First update after this ships** still runs the previous uninstaller, so its PowerShell check costs 2.4 s once more.
- **CRC check:** off. The updater verifies the download's SHA-512 before it runs the installer; a corrupt manual download is no longer caught by NSIS.

prs.title: fix(core): escape quoted env config values
prs.body:
Refs #42856. Previously reported on V1 in #20640, #32695, #35536 and #43691, none of which were fixed.

`{env:VAR}` values were pasted raw into the config text before it was parsed as JSON. If a value used inside a JSON string contained a backslash or a quote, such as a Windows path, the whole config file was rejected, with only a warning in the log.

References inside JSON strings now get the same escaping that `{file:}` already uses. Unquoted references are still substituted raw, as before.

Verified with an extended substitution test and `bun run check`.

prs.title: feat(core): model-independent agent effort override
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #54430

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Adds an optional `effort` setting to agents, allowing their reasoning effort to be configured independently of the model.

Currently, using a different reasoning level for subagents can require pinning a specific model and variant. This is inconvenient when the selected model is already the best option for both quality and price.

For example, I use Muse Spark 1.3 at medium effort for my primary agent, but I want delegated tasks to use the same model at low effort. Tasks like code exploration, straightforward implementation, and verification often don't need as much reasoning.

This can reduce reasoning-token usage, latency, and potentially cost, without switching to a weaker or different model.

Example:

```json
{
  "agents": {
    "general": {
      "mode": "subagent",
      "effort": "low"
    },
    "explore": {
      "mode": "subagent",
      "effort": "low"
    }
  }
}
```

The subagents inherit the selected model while overriding only the reasoning effort. If the primary model changes, the subagents continue inheriting it without requiring configuration updates.

The implementation passes the configured effort into model request preparation after normal model selection. Existing model/variant behavior remains unchanged when `effort` is omitted.

Kept the implementation minimal, with no additional dependencies or changes to model selection.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Schema and core TypeScript checks passed.
- 83 existing targeted tests passed, with no failures.
- Reviewed configuration propagation and delegated-agent request handling.
- Full test suite and live provider behavior have not been verified.

prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #55777

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Serving the web UI over plain HTTP on a LAN IP means `isSecureContext` is false, so `crypto.randomUUID` is `undefined` even though `crypto` itself exists. `ask()` in `packages/gui-extensions/src/btw/model.ts` called `crypto.randomUUID()` directly and threw `TypeError: crypto.randomUUID is not a function` before anything else ran, surfacing as the generic "Failed to send command" toast. The naive fix location (`packages/app/src/runtime/persistence/uuid.ts`) already had an insecure-context fallback — this call site was the unguarded one.

Fix: `const id = crypto.randomUUID?.() ?? Math.random().toString(16).slice(2)` — mirrors the existing app-side fallback, no new strings.

Test-env side fix only: `model.ts` statically imported `@opencode/ui/toast` (solid-sonner), which throws at import time under bun's server-side test runtime, where `mock.module` cannot intercept the package specifier. The toast import is now lazy, in the empty-question branch only (per this repo's dynamic-import pattern in AGENTS.md). No production behavior change.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New regression test `packages/gui-extensions/src/btw/model.test.ts` (2 tests): the insecure-context test fails pre-fix with the issue's exact `TypeError`, passes post-fix; secure-context control passes both ways. 2/2 green.
- `bun run lint`: 0 errors. `tsgo -b` on `@opencode/gui-extensions`, `@opencode/core`, and `@opencode/cli`: 0 errors. (The repo's pre-push hook runs a full-monorepo turbo typecheck which SIGKILLs the tsgo binary on this machine, so I verified package-by-package instead.)

### What does this PR do?

Adds multi-language support to the V2 docs (`services/www`) using the same 18 locales and codes as opencode.ai, and translates all 62 pages into the 17 non-English locales.

- **Routing:** English stays at `/v2/docs/...`; other locales live at `/v2/docs/<code>/...` (e.g. `/v2/docs/zh/`). Translations mirror the English path under `content/<code>/`. Internal links, the header, the sidebar, and cards keep the reader's locale.

- **UI strings:** per-locale `.ts` dictionaries following `packages/console/app/src/i18n`.
- **RTL:** Arabic renders right-to-left (logical CSS properties). Code stays LTR and monospace, and Arabic prose uses the system font because OpenTUI Mono breaks letter joining.

### Issue for this PR

### Type of change

### What does this PR do?

`session import` currently dies with HTTP 500 (empty body) when the payload's message IDs already exist in `session_message` — reachable by re-importing an export under a new session ID, or when orphaned message rows survive their session (#50260).

prs.title: chore(ci): speed up the beta desktop publish
prs.body:
Beta publishes the desktop app to the team on every push. Today a beta run takes **24–34 min**, and a push that lands during a run waits for that whole run first (8 min in [38829647049](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/actions/runs/38829647049)). This PR rebuilds the beta path around what beta actually ships and is expected to take **~6–8 min** from push to the update being live, with notarization on Apple's side as the remaining floor.

Every change is gated on `github.ref_name == 'beta'` or the beta electron-builder channel. Dev and release publishes run the same jobs and steps as before (checked by evaluating every job and step condition for `dev` releases, `dev` pushes and other push branches against the old file).

## Where the time goes today

Beta run [38829647049](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/actions/runs/38829647049), measured:

```mermaid
gantt
  title Beta today (run 38829647049, 34.6 min)
  dateFormat X
  axisFormat %M:%S
  section Queue
  Behind the previous push        : 0, 477
  section Setup
  version                         : 477, 513
  build-cli (12 targets, 1.4 GB)  : 519, 692
  section Desktop
  macOS x64 on Intel              : 696, 1956
  Linux arm64                     : 709, 1790
  macOS arm64                     : 699, 1195
  Windows arm64 (GitHub-hosted)   : 695, 1066
  Windows x64                     : 737, 985
  Linux x64                       : 699, 1042
  section Publish
  publish                         : 1963, 2078
```

| Cost | Where |
| --- | --- |
| 8 min queue | a newer push waits for the running publish |
| 173–233 s | `build-cli` compiles all 12 CLI targets and uploads them as one 1.4 GB artifact, though beta bundles 6 |
| 128–148 s | each desktop job downloads that whole artifact for one binary |
| 1027–1260 s | macOS x64 packages on `macos-26-intel` |
| 721 s | Linux arm64 `Package`: fpm compresses deb (`xz -3`, one thread) and rpm (`xz -9`) |
| ~72 s | macOS zip (7z deflate `-mx=7`) and DMG (UDZO zlib level 9) after notarization |
| 53–110 s + 42 s | desktop jobs upload installers as artifacts, then `publish` downloads them again to upload to R2 |

## After

```mermaid
gantt
  title Beta after (expected, ~6.5 min)
  dateFormat X
  axisFormat %M:%S
  section Setup
  version (no checkout)                 : 0, 8
  6 CLI jobs in parallel                : 15, 75
  section macOS x64 (Apple Silicon)
  install + app build while CLI builds  : 15, 100
  sign + notarize + zip/DMG             : 108, 320
  upload to R2                          : 320, 345
  section Other desktop jobs
  Linux arm64                           : 15, 300
  Windows arm64 (Blacksmith)            : 15, 270
  macOS arm64                           : 15, 340
  section Publish
  record the release                    : 350, 385
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  push[push to beta] --> version[version: computed, no checkout]
  version --> cli[build-cli-beta: 6 jobs, one target each]
  version --> desktop[build-electron x6: install, app build]
  cli -. artifact per target .-> wait[wait for own CLI]
  desktop --> wait --> package[Prepare, Package]
  package --> r2[upload installers to R2]
  r2 --> publish[publish: post update metadata]
```

## Pipeline shape

- **Newer push cancels the running beta publish:** `concurrency.cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref_name == 'beta' }}`. Beta only ships the newest commit. A cancelled run can leave files under `/files/bin/0.0.0-beta-N/` in R2, but nothing references them: only `publish` records a release, in one request.
- **`version` without a checkout:** a beta version is `0.0.0-beta-<run number>[.<attempt>]` (the same rule as `packages/script`), so beta computes it in one shell step. About 40 s → under 10 s.
- **CLI as a matrix, only what beta bundles:** `build-cli` is skipped on beta. `build-cli-beta` builds the 6 targets the desktop bundles, one per job, each uploaded as its own artifact. Each job takes about a minute instead of one 3–4 min job building 12 targets.
- **Desktop jobs start right after `version`:** `build-electron` keeps `needs: [version, build-cli]` and uses `!cancelled() && !failure()`, so on beta it starts as soon as `version` finishes. It installs dependencies and builds the app while its CLI builds, then `script/wait-for-artifact.ts` polls this run's artifacts for its own CLI and fails as soon as the producing job ends without it.

  ```yaml
  - name: Build (beta)
    run: bun run electron-vite build # not `bun run build`: its prebuild hook copies the CLI
  - name: Wait for the CLI (beta)
    run: bun ./script/wait-for-artifact.ts opencode-cli-unsigned-cli-${{ matrix.settings.cli }} "build-cli-beta (${{ matrix.settings.cli }})"
  ```

  The workflow gains `permissions: actions: read` for that polling.

## Packaging

- **macOS x64 on Apple Silicon:** the x64 entry runs on `macos-26` with `--os=darwin --cpu=*` (arm64 build tools, x64 node-pty for the app). electron-builder's `afterPack` already rejects a bundle whose CLI or node-pty has the wrong CPU (`script/native-arch.ts`). The Intel job took 1027–1260 s; the arm64 job took 496–659 s.
- **Windows arm64 on Blacksmith:** GitHub-hosted `windows-2025` was kept from the Tauri build, which needed an ARM64 MSVC toolchain. Electron packaging compiles nothing (`@electron/rebuild` runs with `buildFromSource=false`), and the same `afterPack` check applies.
- **Linux deb and rpm at `xz -1`, multithreaded:** the beta channel passes `--deb-compression-level 1` and `--rpm-compression-level 1` to fpm, and the job sets `XZ_DEFAULTS=-T0` (fpm overwrites `XZ_OPT`; xz still reads `XZ_DEFAULTS`). On the real 2.0.23 Linux arm64 payload (596 MB, 2 vCPU):

  | Level | Time | Size |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `-6` | 100 s | 166 MB |
  | `-3` (deb default) | 52 s | 181 MB |
  | **`-1` (beta)** | **18 s** | **189 MB** |

- **macOS zip and DMG at level 1:** `ELECTRON_BUILDER_COMPRESSION_LEVEL=1` makes electron-builder use 7z deflate `-mx=1` for the zip and zlib level 1 for the UDZO DMG. It is written to `GITHUB_ENV` on beta macOS only, because electron-builder throws on an empty value.
- **No `.app.tar.gz`:** only the retired Tauri updater feed read it.
- **Windows CLI signed once:** `prepareCli()` skips its Azure signing on beta; electron-builder signs `resources\opencode-cli.exe` in `Package`, and "Verify signed Windows Electron artifacts" still checks it.

## Transfers

- **One CLI artifact per target, at deflate level 1:** each desktop job downloads ~120 MB instead of 1.4 GB. Level 1 compresses a 190 MB CLI binary in 3.8 s instead of 7.9 s, for 7% more bytes.
- **Installers go to R2 from the job that built them:** `packages/desktop/scripts/upload.ts` uploads one platform's files with `UpdateArtifact.upload` and writes the returned file list. `publish` downloads only those lists and the `latest*.yml` files, and `packages/desktop/scripts/publish.ts` reads them through `OPENCODE_DESKTOP_UPLOADED` instead of uploading everything itself. Without that variable, `publish.ts` behaves exactly as before.

  ```ts
  const uploaded = uploadedDirectory ? await uploadedByBuildJobs(uploadedDirectory) : await uploadFiles()
  ```

- **`publish` skips Docker, git committer and AUR setup** on beta; beta's `script/publish.ts` only records the desktop release.

## Build inputs

- **Web UI brotli at quality 6 on beta:** since #53644, every CLI build compresses the embedded web UI at quality 11; `build-cli` spent ~50 s on it in recent dev runs. Beta keeps quality 6 (a few seconds); the beta desktop only bundles this CLI.
- **Bun cache fallback on beta:** every dev merge changes beta's `bun.lock`. On a cache miss, beta now restores the newest cache for the same OS, arch and Bun version (`restore-keys`) instead of installing everything from npm.
- **Authenticated Bun release lookup:** `packages/cli/script/build.ts` sends the existing `GH_TOKEN` with its `api.github.com` release lookup, so 6 parallel CLI jobs on shared runners do not hit the unauthenticated per-IP limit.

## Not included

| Technique | Why not |
| --- | --- |
| `bun install --filter @opencode/desktop` in desktop jobs | Install now overlaps the CLI build, so it saves ~20 s; electron-builder's dependency collection on a filtered install is untested on macOS and Windows |
| Cache Electron and electron-builder downloads | Electron downloads in ~3 s on `macos-26`; restoring a GitHub cache there runs at ~17 MB/s, which is slower |
| Upload Sentry sourcemaps from one job | The Sentry plugin injects debug IDs; skipping it on 5 jobs changes their bundles and loses symbolication |
| Windows Dev Drive | Windows jobs are no longer on the critical path |
| Skipping builds for pushes that change nothing beta ships | Beta pushes are dev merges and app features; they always ship |

## First beta run after merge

- `build-electron` jobs start right after `version`, and "Wait for the CLI (beta)" logs a short or zero wait.
- `afterPack` passes for macOS x64 on `macos-26` and Windows arm64 on Blacksmith (it fails the run on a CPU mismatch instead of shipping).
- Notarization succeeds, and the beta update feed lists every platform: `https://opencode.ai/update/api/beta/desktop/opencode/latest-mac.yml`, `latest.yml`, `latest-linux.yml`, `latest-linux-arm64.yml`.
- An installed beta app updates to the new version on macOS, Windows and Linux.
- **Rollback:** revert this commit; nothing outside the beta path changes.

Enable the embedded terminal's `transparentBackground` option when the theme's `background.raised.base` token is fully transparent, so the terminal panel composites its default background via SGR 49 and matches the rest of a transparent theme. prs.title: fix(core): wait for plugin activation before each runner step
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #51128

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

The runner waited for plugin activation once per drain, but every step and retry prepares its context again (`prepareContext` → `context.select` → `resolveModel`). If a plugin reloads mid-turn, a retry could read the half-rebuilt catalog, so the turn failed and the session was told its skills had been removed.

This waits for `plugins.awaitActivation` at the start of `prepareContext` and in manual compaction's `resolveContext`. When nothing is reloading the wait is immediate; during a reload the step waits for it to settle.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New runner test: a transient stream failure followed by a successful retry must wait for activation before each step's context (3 waits; 1 without the fix).
- `bun test test/session-runner.test.ts` (211 pass) and `bun run typecheck` in `packages/core`.
- Reproduced the issue end to end with `opencode serve`, a local stub provider and a slow local plugin; with the fix the retry waits for the reload and reaches the provider.

prs.title: fix(core): honor the selected agent's configured model for new sessions
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #55727

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

A new session ignores the `model` configured for the agent it runs with. Passing `-m` on the command line works, but setting `model` under `agents.<id>` in the config (or in agent frontmatter) does not — the session starts on the catalog default instead.

`session.create({ location, agent })` deliberately takes no model, so a session row can legitimately be model-less. `SessionContext.load` then resolved the model from `selection.session` alone, and resolution fell through to the catalog default in `packages/core/src/model-resolver.ts`. The agent's own configuration was never consulted there, although the title and compaction paths already pass the agent's model.

The fallback now lives in one place — the `SessionContext.resolveModel` helper — and reads: the session's own model wins when it has one (an explicit `-m` or a picker selection is written to the session row, so it stays authoritative), otherwise `selection.agent.info.model` stands in before resolution reaches the catalog default.

Because the fallback sits in the shared helper rather than in `load`, it also closes the same gap at the two other call sites that passed a raw session and discarded the agent:

- `session/generate.ts` — transient generation
- `session/runner/llm.ts` — the manual compaction preview

`selectTitle` keeps the raw session-level resolution: it deliberately resolves overridden refs, and it already reads the title agent's own `model` itself.

### How did you verify your code works?

One case in the existing session-context harness, `packages/core/test/session-generate.test.ts`, which drives the real `SessionContext` and asserts on the model actually sent: the session has no model of its own, the agent's configured `model` is what resolution receives, and the request carries that model. The mock in that harness now mirrors the route it is asked to resolve, so the assertion can follow the model through to the request.

- `bun run script/test.ts test/session-generate.test.ts` → 4 pass, 0 fail.
- Removing the source change and re-running → that case fails and the other three still pass, so it measures the fix rather than the fixture.
- `bun run typecheck` in `packages/core` → clean. It failed on the previous head; the test that caused it is gone.
- Related suites (`session-title`, `session-compaction`, `session-compact`, `session-model-request`) → 44 pass, 0 fail; `session-runner` + `session-execution` + `location-layer` → 288 pass, 0 fail.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR
