prs.title: chore(ci): speed up and stabilize the test workflow
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #51951. Addresses the AppProcess half of #37321 (its Windows `ProjectCopy` flake is not covered here).

`test` on dev was slow and flaky; this combines the stack that fixed it (#55689 → #55855, now closed) into one change. Each closed PR has the detailed evidence for its part.

**Before merging:** a repo admin needs to add `build (linux)` (and `build (windows)`) to the required status checks of the dev and v2 rulesets. The compiled-service smoke tests and the library build check now run in that job instead of `unit`.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [x] Refactor / code improvement
- [x] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

**Result** (full runs, all suites):

| Check | dev before | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `e2e (windows)`, slowest check on app PRs | 20-27 min, and red on most runs (component tests hit the 15 min step timeout) | ~8.3 min (slowest leg: app shard 1) |
| `unit (windows)`, slowest check on other PRs | 9.6-10.8 min | ~7.8 min |
| Windows "Setup Bun" per job | 91-122s | 35-38s |
| Component suites on Windows | one leg, ~8.8 min | two legs, ~5-5.5 min each |

**Workflow (`.github/workflows/test.yml`, `turbo.json`, `setup-bun`)**
- App e2e runs as two Playwright shards per OS; the session UI and app component suites each get their own leg. `e2e (linux)`/`e2e (windows)` are now small aggregator jobs over those legs, so the required check names stay the same; they fail if any leg or the `affected` job failed.
- A parallel `build` job runs the compiled-service and Node build smoke tests and builds the affected libraries (Linux). Unit tests no longer wait for library builds: every package exports its sources, so no test reads a dependency's `dist`.
- Test tasks depend on a no-op `transit` task, so each test hash covers its whole workspace closure, and the root `package.json` (which pins Bun) is a global dependency. Before, the Blacksmith remote cache on Linux replayed `cli:test` passes for commits that changed core (e.g. dev runs 38691743520, 38692392415).
- The 11 packages whose tests never ran in CI (no turbo task) are registered: client, gui-extensions, http-recorder, merman, plugin, plugin-browser, script, sdk, simulation, theme, util (119 test files).
- Storybook-only changes now trigger e2e (no app package depends on Storybook, so those PRs got a vacuous green). PRs check out two commits instead of full history. The Turbo `actions/cache` steps cached a path Turbo 2 never writes and are gone. Windows skips the bun cache (extracting it with tar was slower than a cold install) and installs with the isolated linker; oven-sh/bun#28147, which the hoisted workaround was for, is fixed.

**Test harness**
- Built e2e is served by a small Bun static server (`e2e/utils/serve.ts`) that keeps vite preview's fallback rules. vite preview synchronously reads the ~3,100-file `_assets` directory for every asset request on case-insensitive file systems, which serialized every worker's page loads on Windows.
- Service workers are blocked suite-wide (70% of tests precached ~1,600 files during the test), video is recorded only on the first retry in CI, and `mobile-timeline-scroll` runs in its own trailing parallel project instead of one serial tail.
- Storybook pre-bundles its dependencies at startup (based on the approach in #55632 by @Hona, plus `preview.tsx` and the preview runtime), so component tests no longer hit optimizer reloads mid-test; `@tanstack/solid-query` is deduped instead of aliased into `app/node_modules` (that path didn't exist under the hoisted install, which broke every app component story on Windows). Component mounts skip axe, whose results nothing read.
- core: 30s default timeout like cli/tui, real-clock AppProcess tests, an injected clock for browser-idle, and fixture repos with one config write instead of a `git config` per setting. The AppProcess interruption tests' child now registers its SIGTERM handler before it announces readiness and publishes its pid with a rename; with a 300ms gap forced between the two, the old order hangs until the timeout and the new one passes.

**Product bugs the tests found**
- Dialogs that had started closing kept blocking every shortcut for 100ms (`packages/ui/src/context/dialog.tsx`).
- Web search didn't wait for plugin activation, so the first query on a cold Location failed for plugin providers.
- The timeline virtualizer restored a stale scroll offset when a scroll settled, undoing its own anchoring.
- A video double-click also entered native fullscreen over the in-window theatre (click-to-play kept).
- `@corvu/drawer` 0.2.4 left mobile drawers stuck when dismissed while opening (patched).
- merman's label search runs the cheap distance check before the clearance check: identical output on all 321 audit runs, half the CPU.

**Flaky and rotted tests**, each with a root cause, mostly from a census of 165 `test` runs: What's New, subagent title anchor, session-summary tooltip, tab preview clock, code font status (a Chromium font-face cache rebuild), video theatre, timeline paging, composer overflow, TUI frame waits, Windows-only `client` service tests (uncatchable SIGTERM; the port check now asserts nothing is listening instead of re-binding an ephemeral port), util (tests compiled into `dist` and run twice, TEMP vs TMPDIR, socket reset race), http-recorder (`CI=true` forced replay), sdk and client tests stale after intended API changes, merman layout ceilings. Also `core/test/provider.test.ts` (recently added on dev): `Bun.Glob` returns `\` on Windows, which ended up in the import specifiers; this PR's full Windows run was the first to execute it there.

**Skills:** `.opencode/skills/{unit-tests,tui-tests,app-e2e-tests,component-tests}` describe what made tests slow or flaky here and the patterns that fixed it; `AGENTS.md` points to them.

**Measured and left out**
- 4 component-test workers instead of 2: slower on Windows (one Vite server plus browsers saturate 4 vCPUs).
- A Windows Turbo cache: with no builds left in `unit`, it could never hit.
- `bun test --parallel=2 --no-isolate` for core: 6 Windows runs, no crashes, about 40s (~12%) faster, but `core`, `tui` and `cli` already share 4 vCPUs. Not included; giving core its own Windows unit leg is the more promising follow-up.

Overlaps with #55559: compatible (that PR scopes 30s timeouts on the npm Git tests; here core's runner default is 30s).

### How did you verify your code works?

- Every part ran through CI on Linux and Windows in the stacked PRs; the top of the stack was green.
- On this branch (rebased onto current dev): `bun run check` (35/35), `bun run lint:changed origin/dev` (0 problems), actionlint, `bun install --frozen-lockfile`, `turbo run test --dry` (24 test tasks, 0 builds).
- This PR's own run exercises every suite on both OSes (it changes `test.yml` and `turbo.json`).

### Screenshots / recordings

N/A

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: feat(app): add generative UI to the GUI
prs.body:
Agents can now show interactive UI in the timeline. They write a small GenUI program in a `genui_render` call; the app draws it with OpenCode's own components while the call streams, and every call is checked so the agent knows whether its UI rendered. It is on by default, and **Settings > Experimental > Generated UI** turns it off.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/042070ac-986d-46ca-af60-49b4a134f6d0

<sub>The demo telemetry is synthetic.</sub>

## How it works

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant A as App
  participant C as Core
  participant P as GenUI plugin
  participant M as Model
  A->>C: prompt with metadata.genui = true
  C->>P: prompt hook notes the user is in the app
  C->>P: context hook keeps genui_render and adds a one-time reminder
  M->>C: genui_render argument chunks
  C-->>A: session.tool.input.delta, batched every 100 ms
  A->>A: parse new statements, render, reconcile by statement ID
  C->>P: complete call, checked against the catalog
  P-->>M: rendered, or each problem by statement
  A->>A: buttons run set and reset in place
  A->>C: reply actions and forms send the user's next message
```

- **Core streams tool input.** `publish-llm-event.ts` publishes `session.tool.input.delta` through the same batching as text and reasoning, and flushes held tool input before the next block starts. The event, the client reducer, the TUI and the CLI already handled it. Schema and the rest of Core are unchanged.
- **Offered only in the app, and only when on.** The app marks its prompts with `metadata.genui`, from the Generated UI setting. The plugin removes `genui_render` from requests whose latest prompt did not say `true`, such as a terminal, a subagent or the setting turned off, and adds a short reminder when that changes, the way Plan mode reminds. No RPC, polling or permission writes.
- **Checked on every call.** The tool returns each problem by statement and line. Blocks that fail are left out; everything else still renders.
- **Streams without flicker.** Each finished statement parses once. While the call streams, a block that does not render yet, such as a chart whose last data point is half written, keeps its previous version.

## The language

```
root = Surface([counts, status, actions])
$approved = 0
$total = 4
counts = Metrics([done, left])
done = Metric("Approved", $approved + " of " + $total)
left = Metric("Remaining", $total - $approved)
status = $approved == $total ? ready : review
ready = Notice("All changes approved", "Apply them when you are ready.", "success")
review = Progress("Review", $approved / $total * 100)
actions = Actions([approve, undo, apply])
approve = Button("Approve next", set($approved, $approved < $total ? $approved + 1 : $total), "primary")
undo = Button("Undo", set($approved, $approved > 0 ? $approved - 1 : 0), "ghost")
apply = Button("Apply approved", reply("Apply the " + $approved + " approved changes"), "secondary")
```

- One statement per line, components with positional arguments, and text, numbers, booleans, `null`, lists and objects.
- `$name` state lives in the app. Expressions (`+ - * / %`, comparisons, `&& || !`, `? :`) read it; `set`, `reset`, `reply` and `open` run when the user presses a button. There are no loops, functions or host access.
- The component catalog is one Effect schema per component. Its props order is the argument order, its types check programs, and the `genui` skill prints typed signatures from it, e.g. `Metric(label: string, value: string | number, detail?: string, delta?: number, trend?: number[], inverse?: boolean)`.
- The plugin ships the `genui` skill whenever it is enabled. Besides the syntax, components and examples, it keeps generated UI rare: text is the default, a surface must clearly beat text, a list names what never gets one, and an answer gets at most one. It also tells the agent to gather data before rendering, to end the turn after a surface that asks for a choice, and what a reply looks like. Its description says to load it before the first `genui_render` call. The skill description, the tool description and the in-app reminder also say that text is the default, so the agent knows before it loads the skill.

What the agent gets back for a broken program:

```
count (line 3): Metric needs value: Metric(label: string, value: string | number, detail?: string, ...)
chart (line 4): BarChartt is not a component. Did you mean BarChart?
root (line 1): Surface.children takes Block | Columns | Section, not Row; Row goes in Group
spare (line 6): spare is defined but nothing under root uses it, so it does not render
```

### Why our own language

The syntax follows OpenUI Lang, but we dropped `@openuidev/lang-core`:

| | `@openuidev/lang-core` 0.4.1 | Ours |
|---|---|---|
| Source | 7,679 lines; about 1,200 do work we use | ~1,000 lines, plus the catalog |
| Install script | Posts telemetry to PostHog by default; npm runs it for users of `@opencode/core` and `@opencode/sdk` | None |
| Runtime telemetry | Opt-in, but the code ships | None |
| Schemas | Zod only, so every component was defined twice | One Effect schema per component |
| Model-facing prompt | Third-party prose | Generated from our catalog |
| State and actions | Separate React-oriented runtime | Part of the language and its checks |

## Changes

- **`core`:** tool input deltas, as above, with tests for batching and ordering.
- **`@opencode/plugin-genui`:**
  - `lang/`: lexer, incremental parser, evaluator and checks, generic over a catalog.
  - `catalog.ts`: components and examples.
  - `guide.ts`: the `genui` skill.
  - `tools.ts`: `genui_render`.
  - `session.ts`: app-only offering and the reminder.
  - `./genui`, `./lang` and `./catalog` are browser-safe entry points.
- **`@opencode/plugin-browser`:** a built-in `browser` skill: explicit tab IDs, snapshots and refs, showing results to the user, recipes for debugging, performance and memory, recovery after failures, and every operation from `Browser.Operations`. It is gated like the browser tools: hidden until a desktop browser attaches to the session.
- **`session-ui`:**
  - `genui/` renders surfaces, charts, state and actions.
  - Only `genui_render` reads arguments while they stream; every other tool still waits for complete input.
  - `DataProvider` gains `onPrompt` for replies.
- **`app`:**
  - **Settings > Experimental > Generated UI**, on by default. The Experimental page shows again now that it has a setting.
  - Prompts and surface replies carry `metadata.genui` from that setting.
  - Wires `onPrompt`.

| Experimental settings |
|---|
| ![Generated UI setting](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6b81cf81-308e-4a26-a8b2-296d31f6808d) |

## Components

| Group | Components |
|---|---|
| Layout | `Surface`, `Section`, `Columns` |
| Content | `Text`, `Markdown`, `Code`, `Divider`, `Notice`, `Status` |
| Data | `Metrics`/`Metric` (sparkline, delta), `Progress`, `BarList`, `Table`, `Steps`, `Group`/`Row` |
| Charts | `BarChart` (grouped or stacked), `LineChart`, `AreaChart` (stacked), `ComboChart` (two axes), `ProjectionChart` (target line), `DonutChart`, `ShareBar`, `RadarChart`, `ScatterChart`, `Heatmap` |
| Meters | `Meter`, `Gauge`, `Pips`, `StatusStrip`, `Comparison` |
| Actions and forms | `Actions`, `Button`, `Link`, `Form`, `Input`, `TextArea`, `Select`, `Choice`, `Segmented`, `Toggle` |

- Everything draws with `@opencode/ui` and `--v2-*` tokens. One series uses the text color; several use `--genui-series-1..6` from v2 hue steps; state colors mean outcomes only.

## Follow-ups

- Open a surface in the side panel as a tab. The earlier side-panel prototype is removed.
- Chart number formatting still uses `en-US`; it should follow the app locale.

prs.title: fix(cli): deliver large stdout writes past one pipe buffer
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #55525

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

`opencode --completions fish` (~68 KiB) lost everything past 65536 bytes when piped. I traced it to stdout/stderr being left nonblocking once `@opentui/*` is imported: a single write larger than one pipe buffer is silently truncated (I confirmed the `EAGAIN` on the 5th 16 KiB chunk with a bare `@opentui/core` import, and that the tail is dropped at write time, so no exit-flush can recover it).

Since the TUI shares this binary, the fix guards the writes instead of the imports: at CLI startup, oversized `process.stdout`/`stderr` writes are split into blocking 16 KiB chunks with a bounded EAGAIN retry (5 s, then give up quietly so a broken pipe still exits with the real code), and the line-oriented `console` methods go through the same path (Bun's console does not route through the stream wrappers). Small writes delegate to the original behavior, so token streaming and friends are untouched.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New `packages/cli/src/stdout-drain.test.ts`: asserts piped completions are byte-identical to file output across 3 piped runs. It shells out through real OS pipes (`/bin/sh`), because Bun's own spawn pipes use larger buffers and mask the bug. Fails on `dev`, passes with the fix. Skipped on Windows (no `/bin/sh`).
- Manual: `bun run src/index.ts --completions fish | wc -c` gives 69533 (was 65536), identical to `> file`; `| head -c 100` still exits cleanly; `--version`, `--help`, and error paths unchanged (exit codes match `dev`).

prs.title: fix(opencode): keep OpenCode 1 updates on 1.x using npm discovery
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

This keeps OpenCode 1 clients on 1.x once OpenCode 2 is published as GitHub Releases.

**This PR no longer uses the update service.** Every install method gets its version from the `opencode-ai` npm package, which only ever contains OpenCode 1; OpenCode 2 ships as `@opencode/cli`. Nothing in OpenCode 1 reads GitHub's `releases/latest` any more. #54903 is now only needed to publish 2.0 GitHub Releases. Its `v1` update-service channel and the seeding step in `docs/release/v1-v2-isolation.md` don't apply to OpenCode 1.

**Version discovery (`Installation.latest()`):**
- Fetches `${registry}/opencode-ai/latest` using the user's npm registry (registry.npmjs.org by default). Preview builds use their own dist-tag. The lookup times out after 10s.
- Anything that isn't a newer version in the same major reports the installed version, so the existing OpenCode 2.0 offer shows instead.
- A failed check stays silent in the background. `/update` now shows "Couldn't check for updates." and `opencode upgrade` reports the same instead of crashing.

**Installing a 1.x update, per method:**
- **npm / pnpm / bun / yarn:** install `opencode-ai@<version>`. Yarn upgrades previously failed with "Unknown installation method"; they now work.
- **curl:** runs `opencode.ai/install` with `VERSION=<version>`.
- **Homebrew Core:** its `opencode` formula is already 2.x, so `brew upgrade opencode` would install OpenCode 2.
  - No 1.x update is offered, and no request is made; the OpenCode 2.0 offer shows instead.
  - An explicit `upgrade` refuses and points to `--major` or to reinstalling from the tap.
- **Homebrew tap (`anomalyco/tap/opencode`):** this formula is only written by the OpenCode 1 publish; OpenCode 2 uses `opencode-v2` and `opencode-beta`. The tap is updated a few minutes after npm.
  - Before running `brew upgrade`, it pulls the tap and checks the formula version.
  - If the tap isn't yet at the target version (or isn't 1.x), it asks the user to try again in a few minutes and runs nothing.
- **Chocolatey:** `choco upgrade --version` can only install versions the moderated community feed has published. The npm version is only advertised once the feed lists that exact version.
- **Scoop:** `scoop install opencode@<version>` generates the manifest from the bucket's autoupdate URLs, which point at our GitHub release files. Any published 1.x release can be installed.
  - Limitation: in the first few minutes after npm publishes, before the GitHub release is out, an install fails (the curl upgrade path has the same window).
- **Every method:** `upgrade` refuses 2.x targets and points to `opencode upgrade --major`.

**`install` script:**
- Gets the default version from `registry.npmjs.org/opencode-ai/latest` (grep/sed, no jq), and checks the release file for this platform exists.
- If npm fails or returns something other than 1.x, or the release is still publishing, it falls back to the newest `v1.*` in GitHub's release list. It never uses `releases/latest`.
- Downloads from `releases/download/v$version/`.
- Still refuses `VERSION`/`--version` 2.x or later.
- An explicit version is now checked against the release file rather than the tag page, so a release that's still publishing fails with a clear message.

**Release tooling:**
- Removed the ported `script/update-artifact.ts` and the publish-to-service step.
- Kept `--latest` on the V1 GitHub release and the `v1.*` filter in `raw-changelog.ts`.

The OpenCode 2.0 offer UI and the semver-aware comparisons in `cli/upgrade.ts` / `dialog-update.tsx` are unchanged from the first revision.

**Note:** merging changes `opencode.ai/install` immediately, because it redirects to the `install` file on `v1`. Clients only pick up the CLI changes in the next V1 release.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `bun run typecheck` (30/30).
- `packages/opencode`: `bun test test/installation test/cli test/server` (708 pass).
- `packages/tui`: `bun test test/component` (12 pass).
- `bun test ./script/install.test.ts ./script/raw-changelog.test.ts` (10 pass).
- Discovery tests cover:
  - npm used for each method (curl, yarn, unknown, npm, bun, pnpm, scoop, choco, brew tap);
  - 2.x ignored for each method;
  - Homebrew Core making no request and offering nothing;
  - Chocolatey not advertising a version its feed lacks;
  - registry 503, missing version and timeout, with no GitHub calls.
- Upgrade tests cover:
  - `opencode-ai@<v>` for npm, pnpm, bun and yarn;
  - 2.x refused for every method;
  - Homebrew Core refusing;
  - the tap at the target version, behind it, and at 2.x.
- Install script tests use a stand-in `curl` and cover:
  - npm success;
  - falling back to the GitHub `v1.*` list when npm fails or the release is still publishing;
  - a 2.x npm response being ignored;
  - `VERSION` 2.x refused;
  - a missing explicit release.
- Mutation checks confirmed the timeout test and the still-publishing fallback test catch regressions.

### Screenshots / recordings

N/A

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: fix(session-ui): slide the tool group count when it changes
prs.body: Fixes #54653 Fixes #43643 The "Used N" tool group count jumped to its new value. It rolls again with `AnimatedNumber`, including when it gains or loses a digit. The number now reads correctly to screen readers, keeps numeric order in RTL, and settles on the pixel it rolled to. **Before** (9 → 10 → 9) https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/543e1340-741b-49f0-b711-13350c1a7665 **After** https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/00172e1c-3ace-4623-a3a1-9546cee72026 | `AnimatedNumber` | Before (`dev`) | After | | --- | --- | --- | | Accessibility tree, `37` | `7`, `3`; while rolling also `0123456789` ×3 per digit | `37`, once, in every state | | Text content / copy, `37` | reversed digits plus strip cells | `37` | | `aria-label` on a roleless `span` | yes (prohibited ARIA) | removed | | RTL document, `37` | shows as `73` | `37` | | 9 → 10 / 10 → 9 | the `1` pops in / vanishes and leaves a gap | the `1` rolls in from `0` / rolls out to `0` | | Font swap or zoom after mount | the width animates | no animation | | 12 changes while the timeline is detached | blank digit when it returns | correct digit, no roll | | 10 → 11 while the tens digit is rolling | the tens digit jumps to rest | it finishes its roll | ```tsx {label()} {(place) => } ``` - The value is the only text: one `.sr-only` node in reading order. The visual layer is `aria-hidden` and draws every digit with `content: attr(data-digit)`, so screen readers, copy and `textContent` all get the number once. - Digits render in reading order, keyed by place value, and the row is pinned to `direction: ltr`. `row-reverse` is gone. - A spare leading zero waits outside the clipped width, so a new digit rolls in from `0` as the width grows. A departing digit stays until the width transition ends, so it rolls to `0` as it is clipped away. Digits no longer shrink while the width eases. - The strip rolls with `top` on a relatively positioned strip, so the rolling and resting digit are drawn by the same text renderer. A composited `transform` roll ended 0.1–0.5px off the text pixel grid and snapped as it settled. Below: 5 → 4 on a 150% display, frame by frame. Mounting at a new value does not animate; reduced motion skips the roll. ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/641b1514-8d3b-442a-be6c-727129fb00f4) - Only a change in digit count eases the width, so a late web font swap or a zoom change never animates it. - A change while the number is detached settles at once. The session cache keeps up to 16 timelines alive off-page; before, each change there pushed the strip further along its 30 cells until a background tab came back with a blank digit. An unchanged digit keeps its in-flight roll instead of jumping to rest. - `tool-group.spec.ts` covers a two-digit count in LTR and RTL, one accessibility snapshot mid-roll, both digits rolling across 9 → 10 → 9, no animation on mount or font change, changes while detached, and a second change mid-roll. The last three fail on the previous commit. - #54977 fixes the screen-reader half with the same `sr-only` / `aria-hidden` split; this also keeps the text content to one value and fixes RTL.

prs.title: feat(tui): add prompt.history_scope to recall only the session's own prompts
prs.body:
Note: I'm aware v1 is now the maintenance branch and new features go to v2 only. This PR is here for others to use, and I'll submit the v2 version once I've migrated my whole plugin system to it.

### Issue for this PR

Refs #52154

The v2 counterpart is #55261 by @asamarts, against `dev`. This PR uses the same key and values (`prompt.history_scope`: `"global"` | `"session"`), so a `tui.json` written for one works with the other.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [x] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

<kbd>up</kbd> and <kbd>down</kbd> in the prompt walk one history file shared by every session and every OpenCode window on the machine, so a session recalls prompts written for unrelated work in another terminal.

- `prompt.history_scope` in tui.json: `"global"` (default, today's behavior) or `"session"`, where a session walks only the prompts submitted in it.
- Each `prompt-history.jsonl` entry records its `sessionID`. The first prompt sent from the home screen is recorded with the session it creates. Recall filters at read time (`promptHistoryView`), so switching the setting needs no migration.
- The home screen has no session yet, so it keeps walking every session's prompts in both scopes. Entries written by older versions have no session: only the home screen and `global` recall them.
- Shell-mode (`!`) entries, paste placeholders and cleared drafts come back exactly as before; that is why history stays in the file rather than being derived from the session's user messages, which lose all three.
- Retention follows the scope. `global` keeps the newest 50 entries, as before. `session` keeps the newest 50 of each of the 50 most recently used sessions, so a busy session cannot push a quiet one's history out.
- A trim rereads the file before rewriting it, so a TUI that has been open for hours does not drop entries other TUIs appended since it loaded.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `bun typecheck` in packages/tui; `bun test test/prompt test/config.test.tsx` pass. `history.test.ts` covers both scopes' views and retention, the home-screen fallback and shell mode.
- A real TUI in tmux with isolated XDG dirs, two processes, shell-mode prompts. `session`: session B recalls only `echo beta-1`; reopened session A recalls `echo alpha-2`, then `echo alpha-1`, in shell mode, and nothing from B. `global`: session B recalls `echo beta-1`, `echo alpha-2`, `echo alpha-1`.

### Screenshots / recordings

prs.title: fix(core): keep interrupted tool calls replayable for Anthropic
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #55886

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

A server restart during a running tool call can replay an assistant message whose `error.type` is `aborted`. For a `streaming` or `running` non-hosted tool call, `to-llm-message.ts` can emit a `tool-call` without a matching result, and streaming JSON input can remain unparsed. Anthropic then rejects the next request as `tool_use.input: Input should be an object`.

This patch hardens the provider-history lowering boundary only: parses streaming tool input and keeps only object values; otherwise uses `{}`. When the assistant error is `aborted`, it synthesizes the same `{ type: "aborted", message: "Tool execution interrupted" }` error result that the runner already uses for interrupted tools. No execution, persistence, migration, API, or schema change is included.

The tests are deterministic, credential-free, and validate provider-safe `tool-call`/`tool-result` pairing, provider metadata preservation, and a non-aborted error control case.

prs.title: fix(app): keep the file view in place when a link rereads it
prs.body:
Clicking a timeline link to a file that is already open and scrolled shows line 1 for one frame, then jumps back.

| | Consecutive frames of the code view across the link click |
| --- | --- |
| Before | ![Frame 2 shows line 1 between two frames at line 223](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8bfaab17-6918-49bc-9f9d-137f7c04b868) |
| After | ![The code view stays at line 223](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2edbfa6e-ae8f-43bb-af91-0a09b3465ce1) |

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[link click] --> B["files.sync(path, { force: true })"]
  B --> C[new content object, same text]
  C --> D["Show re-runs its tracked fallback"]
  D --> E["new ScrollView at scrollTop 0"]
  E --> F[stored scroll restored a frame later]
```

- Every link click rereads the file ([`renderer.tsx`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/beta/packages/gui-extensions/src/file/renderer.tsx#L577-L579)). The reread stores a new content object even when the text is unchanged.
- Solid's `Show` reads `props.fallback` inside its memo. Passing `value().content` there made each new object rebuild the `ScrollView` and the Pierre viewer.
- `codeView()` now reads `contents()`, a string memo:
  - **Same text:** nothing re-renders.
  - **Changed text** (agent edits, watcher reloads): the viewer updates in place and keeps its scroll.

```tsx
// Before: value() is tracked through the fallback getter
<Show when={artifact()} fallback={codeView(value().content)}>

// After: the code view reads contents() itself
<Show when={artifact()} fallback={codeView()}>
```

- The `review.spec.ts` keeper case "rereads a file each time an artifact link opens it" now rereads an open, scrolled file and checks that the code view keeps its node and scroll offset.

prs.title: feat(desktop): ship GUI plugins through ./gui exports
prs.body:
A plugin in `opencode.json` can now ship a GUI part: one `./gui` export beside its server and `./tui` entries. There is no separate extension concept. The desktop app's built-in features are built-in plugins, and **Settings > Plugins** lists them with plugins from your config. The unshipped `.ocdx` archive installer is gone.

Docs preview: https://docs.vcybm3xt4hhu.opentunnel.xyz/v2/docs/build/plugins/gui/package/

## Authoring

One npm package, one `@opencode/plugin` dependency, any combination of entries:

```jsonc title="package.json"
{
  "exports": {
    ".": "./dist/server.js",   // import { Plugin } from "@opencode/plugin"
    "./tui": "./src/tui.tsx",  // import { Plugin } from "@opencode/plugin/tui"
    "./gui": "./dist/gui.cjs"  // import { Plugin } from "@opencode/plugin/gui"
  },
  "dependencies": { "@opencode/plugin": "latest" }
}
```

The GUI half has the same shape as the server and TUI halves: one default export.

```tsx title="src/gui.tsx"
export default Plugin.define({
  id: "acme", // must equal the server plugin's id
  provides: { acme: Acme },
  setup(ctx) {
    // every app window
    ctx.add(Command, { id: "open", title: ctx.t("open"), run: () => void ctx.client?.rpc(AcmeRpc).open({}) })
    return () => {} // optional cleanup, as server and TUI plugins return
  },
  main(ctx) {
    // optional: once in the desktop main process
    ctx.provide(Acme, { ping: () => `pong for ${ctx.options.team}` })
  },
})
```

```ts title="vite.config.ts"
export default defineConfig({ plugins: [gui()] }) // import { gui } from "@opencode/plugin/gui/vite"
```

| Server / TUI plugin | GUI plugin |
| --- | --- |
| default export `{ id, server }` / `{ id, tui }` | default export `Plugin.define({ id, setup, main })` |
| plugin options | `ctx.options` (window and main) |
| `context.client` | `ctx.client`: the client of the server that runs the plugin |
| `ctx.app` | `ctx.app` (was `ctx.build`) |
| returned cleanup | returned cleanup (window setup stays synchronous) |

- **Id check:** a GUI whose id differs from the server plugin's id fails with a clear error. Built-in ids, ids nested under one with `.`, and the `opencode` namespace are reserved.
- **Vite preset:** `gui()` compiles Solid JSX and writes one CommonJS file with every dynamic `import()` inlined. It keeps exactly the modules the app provides external, plus Electron and Node built-ins. Any other `effect/*`, `solid-js/*` or `@opencode/*` import fails the build. A test builds a real fixture and reads the hosts' module lists, so the preset and the hosts cannot drift apart.
- **Inert placeholders:** bundlers hoist `require` calls, and Solid hoists templates to module scope, so each process gets inert placeholders for the other process's modules. Main skips `uses`/`requires`, so a window-only token never breaks main.
- **Built-ins** declare with the same `Plugin.define`, as TUI built-ins do. "Built-in" is only the host's flag for what `packages/gui-plugins` lists; the lists attach lazy entries and earlier ids through the host-only `compose`.

## Load path

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant S as Desktop's own server
  participant W as App window
  participant M as Desktop main
  W->>S: plugin.list() (features.gui)
  W->>S: GET /api/plugin/gui?id=acme
  S-->>W: { code, revision, options }
  W->>W: evaluatePluginBundle(code, { id, process: "window" })
  S-->>M: plugin.updated (main follows the server itself)
  M->>S: plugin.list() + GET /api/plugin/gui?id=acme (sidecar credential)
  M->>W: PluginGuisChanged { plugins, reserved }
  M->>M: evaluatePluginBundle(code, { id, process: "main" })
```

- **Trust:** GUI code loads only from the desktop's own server, which already runs the plugin's server entry. The web app (its CSP forbids evaluating code) and remote SSH/WSL/HTTP servers load no plugin GUIs yet. Remote TUI and GUI slots will follow together.
- **Main owns the plugin list:** main follows its own server's `plugin.updated` (as the TUI does), lists the plugins, evaluates each bundle once per revision, and sends windows the set. Windows never list plugins, so every window, main and Settings see one list; a listing or read that fails keeps what main runs.
- **Hot reload, as for the server and TUI:** `vite build --watch` rewrites the local `gui.cjs`. Only the GUI revision changes, so the GUI reloads in every window and in main without restarting the server entry. Editing the server entry, its options, or running `opencode plugin update` reloads both.
- **Options:** the server decodes the plugin's options as JSON and serves them with the bundle; non-JSON options fail the plugin load with a clear error.
- **Isolation:** the definition is checked at the boundary (tokens, stores, inline catalog), so a malformed or version-skewed bundle fails only its own plugin. A plugin's `legacy` ids are dropped.

## Changes
- **Server:**
  - `Host.resolve` finds `./gui` (`gui.cjs`/`gui.js` locally; `.ts`/ESM are never served).
  - New `Plugin.Features.gui` and `Plugin.GuiBundle { code, revision, options }`. The revision is an opaque hash of the plugin operation and the bundle.
  - `GET /api/plugin/gui` returns `PluginNotFoundError` (404). `Plugin.ID` gains its schema identifier.
- **App:**
  - `runtime/plugin/plugins.tsx` loads bundles and keeps the last good list on transient failures. The host receives each plugin's options and its server's client.
  - The host accepts definitions that join, are replaced (hot reload), and leave. Plugins never hold the startup gate. A returned window cleanup runs when the plugin goes away.
  - **Settings > Plugins** reports a plugin GUI that cannot load because a built-in claims its id.
  - **Settings > Plugins** (was the dev-only **Extensions** page, which collided with each server's **Extensions** tab) ships, with a **Built-in** label.
  - A disabled plugin stays disabled at startup.
  - Built-in plugins always run: `pluginEnabled` ignores a setting saved under a built-in's id in both hosts and the preload snapshot, main rejects enabling or disabling one (`builtin` error), and Settings > Plugins shows no switch for it. Rows show a status only for Loading, Blocked and Failed; the switch shows on and off.
  - **Settings > Plugins** tags each plugin from the config with its other parts (**Server**, and **TUI** when it exports `./tui`), and one note under the list says how to turn them off: `-<id>` in the global `opencode.json` or in `cli.json`. The row's switch turns off only the desktop UI. No switch changes what it does.

    ![Settings > Plugins listing each part of a plugin and its switch](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eaf83865-6184-445a-8ae1-f2b72870bc38)
- **Desktop:**
  - Plugin `main` setups run in the main-process host with `ctx.options` and a sidecar `ctx.client`. A returned cleanup becomes a scope finalizer. They get the same main context as built-ins, `ctx.serverEndpoints` credentials included: `main` already runs with full Node access, so this is not a new boundary.
  - Main lists plugin GUIs from its own server, filters them with the same `runsOn` OS rule as built-ins, and pushes them to windows.
  - Removes the archive install/remove/source RPCs, the `oc://extensions` asset protocol and the manifest.
  - Migration `20261013231314_drop-extension-files` drops `extension_file`. `extension.manifest`/`revision` stay so 2.0.24ΓÇô2.0.27 can still open the database after a downgrade.
- **SDK:**
  - The SDK lives in `packages/plugin/src/gui` and publishes with the same `tsc` step as `./tui`: `@opencode/plugin/gui`, `/gui/main`, `/gui/{file,review,browser,updater}` and `/gui/vite`. The hosts' internal `/gui/host` is workspace-only: the build leaves it out and the published package exports it as `null`. No copy script.
  - `packages/gui-extensions` is now `packages/gui-plugins` and holds only the 13 built-ins, which import `@opencode/plugin/gui` like any plugin.
  - Plugin names everywhere: the SDK (`usePlugin`, `bindPlugin`, `PluginContext`) and the hosts (`runtime/plugin`, `main/plugin`, `usePluginHost`, `Plugin*` IPC). Persisted names move too; see **Stored data**.
  - Every declaration field is declared once, in `Plugin.Declarations`; `Plugin.Definition` adds setups, and the host-only `Entry` (with `compose` and its error types, in `/gui/host`) adds `windowEntry`/`mainEntry`.
  - `IconName` is generated from the app's icon catalog (`bun run generate` in `packages/plugin`); `gui-plugins` fails its typecheck when they drift.
  - `solid-js`, `electron`, `vite` and `vite-plugin-solid` are optional peers.
  - The server and TUI runtime never load `gui/`, so the CLI bundle does not grow.
  - `Build`/`ctx.build` is renamed `App`/`ctx.app`, which gains `name` as in server plugins.
- **Stored data:** plugin data lives at `plugin.<id>.<key>` (window) and `plugin.<id>` (main), and the enable table is `plugin`. Each store imports its pre-rename `extension.*` value once, copying rather than moving, and the migration leaves a read-only `extension` view so 2.0.24 to 2.0.28 still read their settings after a downgrade.
- **Docs naming:** the sidebar lists Server, TUI and GUI plugins as parallel groups, and the TUI half is called TUI plugins throughout. The GUI pages use the server docs' layout (examples, then a TypeScript `#### Reference` block) instead of field tables, and describe only what works today.
- **Tooling:** `lint:changed` lints in chunks (a renamed package lists hundreds of files) and skips files moved without edits.
- **Docs:** adds a **Desktop** section (plugins, review, files, terminal, browser, session, SSH, WSL, pairing) and **Build > GUI Plugins** (overview, package and build, window SDK, main process and IPC), and a GUI example in **RPC**.

## Verification
- A packed `@opencode/plugin` tarball installed into a sample npm plugin: `vite build` with the preset emits one 1 kB `gui.cjs` (lazy page inlined); `tsc` passes against the published types. Both hosts load the bundle: the window renders the lazy settings page with `ctx.options`, and main provides its Ipc.
- Component stories cover plugin GUIs joining, hot-reloading in place, running their returned cleanup and leaving.

prs.title: fix(core): keep interrupted tool calls replayable for Anthropic
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #55886

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

A server restart during a running tool call can replay an assistant message whose `error.type` is `aborted`. For a `streaming` or `running` non-hosted tool call, `to-llm-message.ts` can emit a `tool-call` without a matching result, and streaming JSON input can remain unparsed. Anthropic then rejects the next request as `tool_use.input: Input should be an object`.

This patch hardens the provider-history lowering boundary only: parses streaming tool input and keeps only object values; otherwise uses `{}`. When the assistant error is `aborted`, it synthesizes the same `{ type: "aborted", message: "Tool execution interrupted" }` error result that the runner already uses for interrupted tools. No execution, persistence, migration, API, or schema change is included.

The tests are deterministic, credential-free, and validate provider-safe `tool-call`/`tool-result` pairing, provider metadata preservation, and a non-aborted error control case.

prs.title: feat(app): add commentary timeline category
prs.body:
Adds a **Commentary** row to **Settings → Timeline detail → Advanced**. Commentary is the text an agent writes between tool calls, such as "I'll check the config first." Users can show it (current behavior), group it into the activity group, or hide it. The final answer of each turn always stays visible.

| Separate (current) | Grouped | Grouped, expanded |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b7fc21dc-ac7b-4053-8ecf-29a53922adf8) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3f3806fe-0b79-426e-ba7c-4f2583dbe634) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/65cabd2c-f315-4e6b-8b2b-39881cd9a302) |

![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aaa50a27-7bcf-47ae-9635-f1789c8bc861)

## Classification

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  T[text part] --> P{state.phase}
  P -- commentary --> C[Commentary]
  P -- final_answer --> F[Answer]
  P -- none --> Q{tool call later in the turn?}
  Q -- yes --> C
  Q -- no --> F
  C --> S{settled turn without an answer?}
  S -- "yes: last text" --> F
```

- **OpenAI Responses models** (gpt-5.3-codex and later) tag each message with `phase`. Core already stores it on `text.state`, so that tag wins.
- **Every other provider:** text followed by a tool call in the same turn is commentary. Text after the last tool call is the answer. This also covers hosted tools inside the final step and output-limit continuations.
- **Settled turns without an answer** (for example, interrupted turns) keep their last text.
- **Client projection only:** no schema, event, or server changes.

```ts
// packages/session-ui/src/timeline/projection.ts
const commentary = contents.filter(
  (content, index) =>
    content.type === "text" &&
    (content.state?.phase === "commentary" || (content.state?.phase !== "final_answer" && index < lastTool)),
)
```

## Notes

- Every preset keeps `commentary: separate`, so nothing changes until a user opts in. Open question: should **Compact** group commentary?
- While a non-OpenAI model streams, trailing text shows as the answer until a tool call starts. Then it folds into the group.
- Grouped commentary uses the group's 8px item spacing instead of the timeline's 24px text margin.
- Adds the `OpenCode/Conversation/Commentary` story with a placement control.

prs.title: feat(tui): add paged transcript output experiment
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #51203 

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

When I use AI tools, whether it's opencode or other, I get dizzy from trying to read the output. I'm reading one line, and as new text is being generated, the line I'm reading jolts up and gives me a small vertigo sensation. Throughout the workday, I get hundreds of these sensations, and I leave my computer feeling like I just ended a VR session, nauseous and exhausted.

The goal of this PR was to try a different flow inspired by e-readers. The idea is the page generates once initially, and then page-up and page-down flips back and forth pages rather than scrolling up a number of lines. When you skim something interesting, and you want to read it more in detail, you can use page-up to find the page, and all the text is in the same location as when the page was generated the first time. There is no jolt of text infinitely scrolling upwards, so hopefully no dizziness.

--
AI description:

This adds an experiment, `experimental.paged_output`, that pins the transcript to page boundaries instead: text fills the current page without moving, then the view advances one page when the page is full. Each page repeats a few lines from the previous page so you don't lose your place, and page up/down snap to the same boundaries the page was generated on, so revisiting a page looks the way it did while streaming. Scrolling away pauses follow and returning to the page bottom resumes it; the transcript and history are untouched.

Native sticky-follow can't do this by itself. It reacts to the content height on the frame it grows, before the bottom padding that creates the flip room is applied, so it moves one line and bounces back on every streamed line. The paging controller therefore owns the viewport from the frame loop against a dynamic bottom pad, and native sticky is disabled while paging.

Opt in with `{ "experimental": { "paged_output": true } }` or the Experiments dialog (Ctrl+P).

### How did you verify your code works?

I tested with `bun run dev` locally, and there is an included test file.

`packages/tui/test/component/paged-scroll.test.tsx` drives the real OpenTUI renderer and checks that per-frame scroll movement is only ever a full page step (the bounce above), that follow pauses on scroll-up and resumes at the page bottom, that enabling it mid-session does not yank a scrolled-away reader down, and that page navigation lands back on the exact generated page tops.

Ran `bun run lint`, `bun typecheck`, and `bun test` in `packages/tui`. There is also a storybook fixture (`OPENCODE_STORY=paged-output`) that streams output and shows live movement/jitter counters, overlap cycling, and page navigation.

### Screenshots / recordings

[![asciicast](https://asciinema.org/a/MsIfn4LpEfcGdRnH.svg)](https://asciinema.org/a/MsIfn4LpEfcGdRnH)

### Checklist

- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: fix(app): keep the review pane steady when the side terminal toggles
prs.body:
Toggling the side terminal disturbed the Review pane in two ways. Both are fixed.

## 1. The Review header jumped 3px

When a terminal was stacked under it, the Review header grew from 48px to 51px to match the terminal's 51px header. All side-panel headers now have the same height, so nothing in the top row moves.

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aa64737c-e562-4b67-bfe2-2b87e7873022) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/46ac4013-546b-4e3f-94e7-314cfbc48225) |

| Header height (+1px divider) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Review, terminal closed | 48px | 48px |
| Review, terminal stacked below | 51px | 48px |
| Terminal (side, bottom, mobile) | 51px | 48px |
| Review toggle row | 48px or 51px | 48px |

## 2. Closing the terminal left a line over the Review

The Review's rounded bottom corners were hidden under a dark band and a flat line for about 240ms after the terminal closed. Slowed 5x; the lower half of each frame is the bottom-right corner, zoomed.

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8c1ac45d-874d-4d61-846f-e31688a90d97) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3546d827-d5a0-4ed9-a9d4-733f42d276b4) |

- **Restored panels never animated their heights.** Height motion turned on only when the side panel's entrance animation ended. A panel restored after a reload has no entrance animation, so the regions snapped while the gap's delayed collapse and the terminal's 240ms exit still ran over the expanded Review.
- **The gap covered the Review mid-motion.** The 8px gap collapsed on its own timing (200ms delay, then 40ms), so the growing Review slid under it. The gap now moves with both regions, so Review, gap and terminal always fill the column exactly.
- **A collapsing frame ended as a hairline.** At near-zero height, a frame's elevation still drew a line. The terminal and Review frames now drop their shadow as they collapse.

```diff
  // screen.tsx
+ if (sideVisible() && !sidePresence.animate()) setStore("sideHeightMotion", true)
- "transition-[height] duration-[40ms] …", "delay-[200ms]": closing, "transition-none": !regionAnimating()
+ "transition-[height] duration-[240ms] …", "transition-none": screen.size.active() || !store.sideHeightMotion || !regionAnimating()
```

## Tests

- `side-panels.spec.ts`: closing and reopening the terminal under the Review must not move the Review header or the toggle.
- `side-panels.spec.ts`: after a reload, hiding the terminal must still animate both regions, and the Review must never run under the gap (also checked while the Review closes).
- The file's unchecked type assertions are replaced, because `lint:changed` checks the whole file.

prs.title: fix(tui): roll the compact form over to M at the rounding boundary
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #55256

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

`Locale.number` picks its unit before it rounds, so a value that the K branch rounds up to four digits prints as four digits. `number(999_950)` is `"1000.0K"` where `"1.0M"` is meant, and the status bar's context counter shows the same thing through `formatContextUsage`.

The K branch is `(num / 1000).toFixed(1)`, so its result first reaches `"1000.0"` at `999_950` (999_949 gives `"999.9"`). That is the whole fix:

```ts
export function number(num: number): string {
  // One decimal place means the K branch reaches "1000.0K" at 999950, so that range belongs to M.
  if (num >= 999950) {
    return (num / 1000000).toFixed(1) + "M"
  } else if (num >= 1000) {
    return (num / 1000).toFixed(1) + "K"
  }
  return num.toString()
}
```

Everything below the boundary is unchanged: `999_949` still reads `999.9K`, `1000` still reads `1.0K`, and `1_000_000` still reads `1.0M`, which it already did.

`number` has two callers, both fixed by the same line: the token line in `routes/session/index.tsx` (`N in · N out`) and `formatContextUsage` in `util/session.ts`, which is what the reporter and the bot's reproduction script saw in the footer (`mini/footer.view.tsx` and `feature-plugins/prompt/footer.tsx` both render it through that helper).

Not in this PR: the same shape at the top of the scale. There is no unit above `M`, so `number(999_999_999)` still prints `1000.0M`. That is the end of the scale rather than a missing rollover — adding a `B` unit is a formatting decision the issue does not ask for, and this PR stays on the reported boundary.

The two earlier attempts at this, #48969 and #47523, were both closed by the periodic automated stale-PR sweep rather than on their merits, and `dev` still carries the bug, so this is not a resurrection of a rejected fix.

### How did you verify your code works?

Two tests, both of which fail on the unmodified source with exactly the reported string:

- `packages/tui/test/util/locale.test.ts` — `rolls the compact form over at the rounding boundary` pins `999`, `1000`, `999949`, `999950`, `999999`, `1000000`, `2500000`. Without the change it fails at `999949 → 999.9K` being fine but `999950` coming back as `"1000.0K"`.
- `packages/tui/test/util/session.test.ts` — `reports the context counter a million tokens in as 1.0M` covers the path the reporter actually sees, through `formatContextUsage`. Without the change it returns `"1000.0K (101%)"` instead of `"1.0M (101%)"`.

Both directions were measured by reverting only `locale.ts` and re-running: 2 fail on the old source, 5 pass on the new one. `tsgo -b` in `packages/tui` exits 0, and is a real gate here (it was confirmed to reject a deliberate type error first). `oxlint` reports 0 warnings and 0 errors on the three files — note that `packages/tui` is not in the anti-slop override list in `.oxlintrc.json`, so the only rule reaching these files is the global `no-restricted-globals`, which was shown to fire before being trusted.

Full `packages/tui` suite: **1487 tests, 7 failures**, all in the plugin/watcher family (`a component layer ends …`, `failed setup reports batched layer errors …`, `Node reloads the local ESM graph …`, `setup layers before and after await …`). A pristine `upstream/dev` checkout of the same tree fails **8**, including every one of those, plus `real watchers observe atomic saves to nested, outside-root, and symlinked helpers` — so the failures are pre-existing and environment-dependent, this branch's set is a strict subset of the pristine one, and nothing in `util/locale.ts` is reachable from those files.

### Screenshots / recordings

_Not a layout change — this changes the text a counter renders, and the exact string is pinned by the tests above (`1000.0K` → `1.0M` at the reported boundary). The reproduction the bot posted on the issue shows the same counter._

### Checklist

prs.title: fix(core): evaluate permissions for commands the scanner cannot decompose
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #49948

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

A command the shell scanner finds no commands in currently skips the permission check and runs unchecked:

```ts
if (parsed.commands.length > 0)
  yield* permission.assert({ … })
```

A bare redirect is the clearest way in. `> file` is valid POSIX, truncates or creates the file, and parses to zero commands — so with `permission.shell "*": "deny"` it still empties the file, with no prompt and no denial.

Checked against `ShellParse.scan` directly, which is what `prepare` calls:

| command | legacy | portable |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `> victim.txt` | 0 commands | 0 commands |
| `>> victim.txt` | 0 commands | 0 commands |
| `echo hi > out.txt` | 1 | 1 |
| `rm -rf x` | 1 | 1 |

Command substitutions are already handled — `FOO=$(whoami)` yields 1 — so this is specific to a redirect with no command word.

The destructive part is easy to confirm:

```sh
printf 'important data\n' > victim.txt   # 15 bytes
/bin/sh -c '> victim.txt'
wc -c < victim.txt                       # 0
```

This PR drops the guard and falls back to the raw invocation when the scan yields nothing, so a deny rule applies and an explicit allow can still permit it. Commands the scanner does decompose are unaffected — same resources, same save patterns as before.

Worth flagging why the guard is load-bearing: with an empty `resources` list, `evaluateInput` in `packages/core/src/permission.ts` returns `allow`, because neither `effects.includes("deny")` nor `effects.includes("ask")` is true for `[]`. So the empty case doesn't fall through to "ask" — it falls through to "allow". I left that code alone here since nothing reaches it once `resources` is always populated, but it may be worth hardening separately.

### How did you verify your code works?

Added four cases to `packages/core/test/permission.test.ts` (both redirect forms × both scanners) asserting that the scan really does yield zero commands, that the raw-invocation fallback evaluates to `deny` under a deny-all ruleset, and that an empty resource list evaluates to `allow` — the fail-open this guards against. That last assertion passes against the current implementation, so the behaviour is documented rather than assumed.

108/108 pass in that file, `bun run lint` is clean, and `packages/core` typechecks.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: fix(app): paste into unfocused composer and guard terminal Command chords
prs.body:
## Why

Pressing `⌘V` on macOS could fail to paste and instead insert a literal `"v"` in both the session screen and the embedded terminal:

1. **Session composer (`packages/app/src/session/composer/region.tsx`)**: When the composer editor is unfocused (after switching tabs, clicking in the timeline, or closing a dialog), pressing `⌘V` dispatches `paste` on `document.body`, which was ignored because `region.tsx` only listened for `keydown`.
2. **Embedded terminal (`packages/gui-extensions/src/terminal/`)**: `ghostty-web`'s `InputHandler` only exempts physical `event.code === "KeyV"` and `event.code === "KeyC"` from `KeyEncoder.encode`, and passes ASCII `utf8` for printable keys when `event.metaKey` (`Mods.SUPER`) is held. In standard VT100 mode, `KeyEncoder.encode` ignores `Mods.SUPER` and writes the raw ASCII character (`"v"`, `"k"`, `"a"`, etc.) to the PTY while calling `event.preventDefault()`—so `⌘V` on non-QWERTY layouts (such as Dvorak or Colemak where `event.key === "v"` is not on `KeyV`) sent a literal `"v"` to the shell and blocked the paste.

## What Changes

| Surface | Interaction | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Session screen (composer unfocused) | `⌘V` (`paste` on `document`) | Dropped (`paste` ignored while unfocused) | Focuses the composer, restores the cursor, and passes the `ClipboardEvent` to `composer.onPaste` |
| Embedded terminal | `⌘V` / `⌘C` across QWERTY and non-QWERTY layouts | Non-`KeyV` `⌘V` encodes `"v"` to the PTY and prevents paste | Triggers `paste` / `copy` across layouts without falling through to `KeyEncoder.encode` |
| Embedded terminal | Printable `⌘+<key>` chords (`⌘K`, `⌘A`, etc.) | `KeyEncoder.encode` emits raw ASCII letters to the PTY | Consumed before `KeyEncoder.encode` so raw letters never leak to the shell |

## Demo

Left: `origin/dev` (`b4a57f6849`). Right: this branch (`paste-focus-guard`).

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f35ebd8e-917d-4d58-a46b-584d72c0646a

## Scope

Owns unfocused session-screen paste handling in `createActiveSessionRegion` and `event.metaKey` chord handling in the terminal extension.

## Verification

```bash
bun test --cwd packages/gui-extensions src/terminal/terminal-key-event.test.ts
bun run --cwd packages/app test:e2e e2e/regression/terminal-input.spec.ts e2e/regression/composer.spec.ts
bun run lint:changed
bun run check
```

- `terminal-input.spec.ts` & `composer.spec.ts`: 21 passed in Chromium (verifies unfocused session `paste` and terminal `Meta` chord suppression).
- `bun run lint:changed`: 0 problems in 5 changed files.

prs.title: fix: include attached images in btw side questions
prs.body:
## Why

Attaching an image and asking `/btw` sent only the question text. Side questions could use images already in session history, but could not see a freshly attached image in Desktop or the TUI.

## What Changes

**Before:** `/btw Describe this attachment` drops the fresh image from the generation request.

**After:** the request includes the image alongside existing session context, without adding messages to the conversation.

- `session.generate` accepts optional files and reuses prompt attachment materialization and model-message conversion. The client API is regenerated.
- Client slash commands opt into images. Other commands keep attached images in the composer.
- Desktop keeps image files in memory for retries while the extension is mounted, avoiding the browser storage quota. Only questions and answers are persisted. Reload restores those, but not images.
- The TUI clears the submitted draft immediately and remains available while generation runs. Failure restores an untouched draft, including images, without overwriting a follow-up.
- Command plumbing contains only the attachment-related changes; the unrelated refactors have been removed.

## Demo

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c7c2a45b-2a7c-4e5f-9d41-22a279cbf7d7

Real production TUI driven by the same OpenCode Drive fixture at 100×32. Left: base `e31136bdbd`. Right: initial image-delivery implementation `82ae3c1cbc`. The simulated provider reports whether the actual request contains the pasted PNG. Both runs assert unchanged durable session messages. Final frames are held for three seconds. The subsequent immediate-clearing correction is covered by the held-response TUI regression below.

## Scope

Shared generation API, Desktop `/btw` retry state and composer delivery, and TUI slash-command delivery. Verification ran on Linux, including the production browser build; native macOS Desktop was not exercised.

## Verification

```sh
# Repository root
bun run lint:changed e31136bdbd
bun run check

# packages/core
```

## Why

The browser toolbar's Inspect button (`[data-action="browser-inspect"]`) advertised `⇧⌘C` (`Ctrl+Shift+C` on Windows/Linux) in its tooltip, but `browser.inspect` was registered without a default `bind`. As a result, the shortcut only worked when OS focus was already inside the child `WebContentsView`. Pressing `⇧⌘C` while focus was in the composer, the browser address bar, the toolbar, or while hovering the Inspect button itself did nothing.

## What Changes

- **Before**: `browser.inspect` had no default keybind (`bind` was omitted), and the Inspect button tooltip displayed a second `"While the page has focus ⇧⌘C"` line. Pressing `Mod+Shift+C` outside the embedded page did not start or stop element inspection.

| Focus Location | Shortcut | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Browser address bar, toolbar, or session composer | `Mod+Shift+C` | Toggles `browser.inspect` when the browser pane is visible and inspectable |
| Embedded browser page (`WebContentsView`) | `Mod+Shift+C` | Handled by the page's input listener (`chromium.ts`), toggling the same picker |

prs.title: test(app): fix races in the mobile timeline scroll e2e tests
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

No issue. Follow-up to #55866: the remaining flaky e2e tests, in `mobile-timeline-scroll.spec.ts`, from a census of recent `test` runs.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Fixes the remaining flaky tests in `packages/app/e2e/regression/mobile-timeline-scroll.spec.ts`. Each was a test-side race; none is a product bug. No timeout, retry or assertion changed.

| Test | Where it flaked | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| :79 keeps the reading anchor when 2 earlier images load (both devices) | Linux, ~5-6% of jobs | Release fling | Stamp the drag 100 ms early |
| :639 returns Home after scrolling the touch target out of view (touchEnd) | Linux, 3 in the census | Release fling | Stamp the drag 100 ms early |
| :227 nested output owns the gesture or chains at its boundary (500) | Linux, ~35% of sharded jobs; Windows rarely | Control+Home dropped at the end of Control+End's animation | Wait for `scrollend` at the end |
| :153 reaches the start without a gap or release jump | Windows, 7-17% | Screencast frames arrive out of order | Sort frames by capture timestamp |

#### Root causes

**Release fling (:79, :639 touchEnd).**
- The drags sent unstamped `Input.dispatchTouchEvent` calls, so CDP stamped each event when it arrived.
- Chromium's velocity tracker (ui/events/velocity_tracker) flings when two things hold:
  - the last two moves are less than 40 ms apart;
  - the touchEnd comes less than 80 ms after the last move.
- When the check before the release passed on its first try, both held, and the drag carried momentum:
  - **:79:** the anchor ended 108-717 px past 704.
  - **:639:** without a fling, the delayed image's row ends 5 px above the viewport. A fling moves the viewport ~158 px further toward the start, which brings that row into view. Its 300 px growth then correctly pushes the anchor down, by exactly the +300 px seen in CI. Every census failure of this test was a touchEnd variant; touchCancel never flings.
- Both drags now stamp touchStart and touchMoves 100 ms early (`restingTimestamp()`) and stamp the release from the same clock, so the release always lands at least 100 ms after the last move, and no fling starts.

**Dropped Control+Home (:227 (500)).**
- Control+End on the nested output is a native 150 ms compositor keyboard scroll. It reaches its end offset about one frame before it finishes.
- Chromium drops a keyboard scroll that arrives in that gap: the retargeted animation is reset when the old one's finish notice arrives.
- The old poll checked only the offset, so it could press Control+Home inside the gap, and `scrollTop` stayed at 2229.
- The test now registers a `scrollend` listener that marks the scroller once a scroll ends at its bottom. It waits for that mark before pressing Control+Home.

**Out-of-order screencast frames (:153).**
- Chromium stamps each screencast frame at capture. It then JPEG-encodes up to three frames at once on unsequenced thread-pool tasks and emits each frame when its encode finishes.
- On Windows runners, a slow encode arrived after newer frames. In the painted-motion check that read as `reversed` or `missing`.
- `capturePromptMotion` now orders frames by `metadata.timestamp` before reading motion.

### How did you verify your code works?

All runs were on macOS in built mode, chromium-touch-scroll project, `--workers=5 --retries=0` unless noted. The before/after probes add `--disable-blink-features=MacDisableCtrlHomeEnd`, because macOS ignores Ctrl+Home/End.

**Forced CI timing, before vs after the fix:**

| Test | Forced timing | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| :79 | Back-to-back release | 10/10 failed (Received 687-1558) | 0/10 |
| :639 touchEnd | Immediate release | 4/16 failed; all 4 natural flings in 32 runs landed here and failed | 0/16, no flings |
| :227 (500) | Control+Home in the frame Control+End reaches its end | 19/20 failed with Received 2229 | 0/20 |
| :153 | Every 5th frame delivered 2 frames late | 10/10 failed | 0/10 |

**Whole file, with the fix:**
- 222/222 passed with `--repeat-each=6`.
- The changed tests passed 140/140 at `--workers=10 --repeat-each=10`, load ~19.

**Checks:**
- `bun run lint:changed`: clean.
- `bun typecheck` in packages/app: passes.
- `typecheck:e2e`: only the 4 known errors.

## Notes

- **:153 cannot be reproduced on macOS.** The frame reorder only shows on Windows CI, so it was validated by injecting late frames.
- **macOS-only overscroll on :153.** Under heavy local load, :153 can fail from elastic-overscroll spring-back (116 → 110). Windows CI frames never go past 110.
- **:431 (held) is not touched.** Its Windows flakes were navigation and mount stalls from before the Bun static server.

### Screenshots / recordings

N/A

- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: fix(client): start the service at once when its registration names a dead process
prs.body:
A restart or crash leaves the background service's registration file (`service.json`) behind. `Service.ensure()` gives any registration that doesn't answer a 5 s `spawnDelay` before it starts a replacement. So the first desktop launch after every reboot waits for a process that no longer exists.

The delay now applies only while the registered process is still running:

```ts
// packages/client/src/service-contender.ts
shouldRecruit(owner: number | undefined) {
  if (lastSpawn === 0 && owner !== undefined && running(owner)) lastSpawn = Date.now()
  ...
}

// Only ESRCH means the process is gone; EPERM is a live process this user cannot signal.
function running(pid: number) { ... process.kill(pid, 0) ... }
```

- **Both clients:** the Promise client (used by the desktop) and the Effect client (used by the CLI) both pass `info?.pid` to the shared contender pool.
- **Permission errors:** a process the client can't signal (`EPERM`, for example a service started as Administrator) still counts as running and keeps the delay.
- **Reused PIDs:** if Windows has given the old PID to another program, the client waits 5 s, the same as before.

### Impact: first desktop launch after a reboot

Desktop 2.0.29 with this change, registration left by a killed service (`bench:startup --service stale`), 4 alternating launches each.

| | Server spawn starts | App shell visible |
|---|---|---|
| Before | 5.66 s | 6.21 s |
| After | 0.73 s | 1.47 s |

On one Windows machine, 8 of the last 16 desktop launches were in this state, each waiting 5.2–7.3 s before it spawned the server.

issues.title: pi-durable: permanently delete a conversation from storage

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Add a way to permanently delete a conversation from pi-durable storage, e.g. `harness.deleteConversation(id, ctx)`: it refuses (or aborts first) while a run is active, then removes the conversation's entries, docs, inbox items and scheduler state from the store.

### Why?

We host pi-durable for end users (SQLite storage, one harness per process). When a user deletes a conversation we can drop our own index row and files, but the message history stays in the durable store forever: in 1.2.0 the store is append-only and the only removal I could find is for inbox items (`removeInboxItem`). So "delete" only means "nobody can look it up any more", which is a weaker privacy guarantee than users expect, and the store only ever grows.

Deleting rows from the SQLite file ourselves would depend on the internal schema and break on upgrades.

### How? (optional)

A storage-level `deleteConversation` implemented by each backend, plus a harness method that checks the live run state, evicts the conversation from memory (rooms/subscriptions get a terminal "deleted" signal), and calls it. Tombstoning the id so a later `submit`/`entries` fails with a clear "not found" error would keep callers honest.

issues.title: Compaction can overflow by including thinking messages omitted from earlier model requests

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### What happened?

During a long session with local Qwen3.8 exposed through llama.cpp, four responses reached the 16,384-token output limit (as per limit set here: [index.ts:22](https://github.com/huggingface/pi-llama/blob/8a876fca45c7824a50cd74f01ea11e0bab7964a2/index.ts#L22)) while still thinking (Qwen 3.8 has this habbit of long thinking). They contained no answer or tool call. Pi saved these messages in the session but skipped them when sending later llm requests to the model.

When Pi later tried to compact the session, it sent a separate model request asking for a summary of the conversation. That request included saved thinking messages that earlier model requests had omitted. The server rejected the summary request because its input exceeded the context limit, so compaction could not complete.

Configuration: Pi 0.84.2, llama.cpp, Qwen3.8-27B, effective context 86,016, Pi response limit 16,384, and reserve tokens 16,384.

## Sequence observed in the original run

1. Four assistant responses each stopped at the 16,384-token response limit while still thinking. They had no visible answer or tool call. Their reported total usages were 51,051, 51,698, 51,822, and 51,946 tokens, below Pi's compaction threshold of `86,016 - 16,384 = 69,632`. The threshold check is in [packages/coding-agent/src/core/compaction/compaction.ts:237](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v0.84.2/packages/coding-agent/src/core/compaction/compaction.ts#L237).

2. Pi kept these thinking-only messages in the saved session. However, when preparing subsequent requests through the OpenAI-compatible provider, Pi omitted assistant messages with no visible answer or tool call. The server's reported token usage therefore did not include those earlier thinking blocks. The message-skipping condition is in [packages/ai/src/api/openai-completions.ts:1240](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v0.84.2/packages/ai/src/api/openai-completions.ts#L1240).

3. Later, a response stopped at 16,360 tokens. Pi treated it as recoverable context pressure and began compaction (`reason: "overflow"`). The recovery check is in [packages/coding-agent/src/core/agent-session.ts:1993](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v0.84.2/packages/coding-agent/src/core/agent-session.ts#L1993).

4. To prepare the summary request, `serializeConversation()` converted the saved conversation into text, including thinking blocks under `[Assistant thinking]`. This brought the four earlier thinking-only responses back into the input, even though they had been omitted from subsequent model requests. Thinking text is included at [packages/coding-agent/src/core/compaction/utils.ts:133](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v0.84.2/packages/coding-agent/src/core/compaction/utils.ts#L133); summary preparation calls this serializer at [packages/coding-agent/src/core/compaction/compaction.ts:651](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v0.84.2/packages/coding-agent/src/core/compaction/compaction.ts#L651).

5. llama.cpp counted 90,609 input tokens in this summary request, exceeding its 86,016-token context by 4,593 tokens, before generating any summary


### Steps to reproduce

This may also reproduce with other models that generate long reasoning. It depends on Pi saving thinking-only responses but omitting them from subsequent model requests, as in the OpenAI-compatible provider path described above.

1. Start Pi with a reasoning model and a response limit that allows generation to stop before its thinking finishes. Leave auto-compaction enabled.
2. Give it a substantial coding task. Whenever a response stops at the output limit with only thinking and no answer or tool call, ask it to continue in the same session.
3. After several such responses, continue until automatic compaction occurs, or use `/compact` to test summarization manually.
4. Check whether the server rejects the summary request for exceeding its context limit even though the preceding model requests fit.


### Expected behavior

Pi should be able to summarize the session without sending a request that exceeds the model's context limit. Here, the saved session contained thinking text that was absent from earlier requests, so their reported token usaage did not account for all the text later sent for summarization.

Could the summary request also omit those thinking-only messages, or could Pi check and reduce the completed summary input before sending it? The idea is that compaction shoudl be able to recover instead of sending oversized requests.

### Version

0.84.2
