issues.title: openai-responses: legacy response.reasoning.delta events are dropped, no thinking_delta streamed
issues.body:
### What happened?

`openai-responses` drops `response.reasoning.delta` events, so reasoning from some OpenAI-compatible Responses endpoints is not streamed.

Example: Vercel AI Gateway (`https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/responses`) with `moonshotai/kimi-k3` and `reasoning: { effort: "high", summary: "auto" }` streams:

```
event: response.reasoning.delta
data: {"type":"response.reasoning.delta","item_id":"rs_...","output_index":0,"content_index":0,"delta":"We"}
... (35 deltas)
event: response.reasoning.done
event: response.output_item.done
data: {..."item":{"type":"reasoning","summary":[],"content":[{"type":"reasoning_text","text":"..."}]}}
```

pi emits `thinking_start`, no `thinking_delta`, then `thinking_end` with the full text (backfilled from `output_item.done`). Streaming UIs show an empty thinking block until the item ends; delta-only consumers get nothing.

`processResponsesStream` in `packages/ai/src/api/openai-responses-shared.ts` handles `response.reasoning_summary_text.delta` and `response.reasoning_text.delta`, but not `response.reasoning.delta`. That was the official OpenAI event name between openai-node v4.101.0 (2025-05) and its removal in v5.10.2 (2025-07); `response.reasoning_text.delta` replaced it. Bedrock and Vercel AI Gateway still emit the old name.

Same issue elsewhere:
- TanStack/ai#1207, fixed by TanStack/ai#1211 (treat `response.reasoning.delta` as an alias of `response.reasoning_text.delta`)
- strands-agents/harness-sdk#4598 (Kimi K3 on Bedrock)

### Steps to reproduce

```sh
curl -sN https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/responses \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"moonshotai/kimi-k3","stream":true,"input":"Hi","reasoning":{"effort":"high","summary":"auto"}}'
```

The stream contains `response.reasoning.delta` and no `response.reasoning_text.delta`. Using the same model through pi with `openai-responses` yields no `thinking_delta` events.

### Expected behavior

Treat `response.reasoning.delta` the same as `response.reasoning_text.delta` (string `delta` appended to the current thinking block). This is a small change in the stream loop plus a unit test. I would like to implement it and can open a PR if this gets an `lgtm`.

### Version

@earendil-works/pi-ai 1.2.0 (also current main)

---

This issue was drafted by an AI agent (Claude Code) on behalf of @LiyanChen-X; the repro and stream trace were captured against the live endpoint.

issues.title: [fullscreen] Large transcripts re-render every frame; every resize re-emits the whole transcript (1 core saturated)
issues.body:
> 🤖 Drafted by the reporter's local pi agent from measurements we collected together; the reporter verified the repro with `pi -ne` (no extensions). Disclosed per CONTRIBUTING.md.

## What happened?

On Windows 11 / Windows Terminal / **2 logical cores**, working in a session with a large transcript
(current session file ~1.6–2.4 MB) makes the TUI stutter badly on window resize and when scrolling.

Measured inside the pi process (wrapping `process.stdout.write` + sampling `process.cpuUsage()` deltas over 5 s windows):

| Scenario | pi process CPU | stdout written |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `regular`, each resize 120×30 ↔ 209×51 | **5.2–5.8 s CPU per 5 s window** | **3.9–5.2 MB per resize** |
| `regular`, scrolling | 3–5 % of one core | ~10–120 KB / 5 s |
| `fullscreen`, scrolling a large transcript | **66–101 % of one core** | ~30–360 KB / 5 s |

On a 2-core machine, 66–101 % of one core is 25–50 % of the whole machine spent on the render path, which is what
shows up as stutter. Switching `tuiMode` from `fullscreen` to `regular` removes most of it.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Windows Terminal, `tuiMode: "regular"` (default), resume a session with a large transcript
   (a few thousand entries / ~1.5–2.5 MB `.jsonl`).
2. Maximise → restore → maximise the window a few times (each resize with a large transcript).
3. Observe the stutter; confirm by measuring bytes passed to `process.stdout.write` and `process.cpuUsage()` deltas.
   With `tuiMode: "fullscreen"`, scrolling the same session saturates one core continuously.

## Expected behavior

Render and emit work should scale with the **visible viewport**, not with the total transcript size — both for
per-frame rendering and for resize.

## Version

pi 0.85.1, node 22.23.2, Windows 11 26100, Windows Terminal, 2 logical cores.
Only difference between the rows above is `tuiMode`.

## Additional context

- `createChatViewport()` places the transcript document inside `new ScrollView(document, { follow: "end", ... })`,
  and on resize the whole transcript appears to be re-emitted at the new width (3.9–5.2 MB per resize).
- The numbers were collected with one locally loaded panel extension that wraps `process.stdout.write` and samples
  `process.cpuUsage()`; that extension's own components render in **0.1–0.2 ms/frame** (instrumented), and the CPU burn
  also appears in windows where it renders nothing.
- Re-validated with **`pi -ne`** (no extensions): resizing with a large transcript still stutters → not extension-caused.

issues.title: [Windows] [sink-thread] How do you use Pi on windows? What issues are you seeing?
issues.body:
## Motivation

There are gazzilion developers on windows. Some use pi. Many could use pi. There are however too many ways pi can be run on windows and as such it is hard to know where to focus energy (fixing bugs, having best docs, having out of box) vs what ways can be delegated out of core to extensions. 

## Ways to run pi on WIndows:

- Pi runs on windows, uses git bash (default)
- Pi runs on windows, uses wsl bash (?semi-automatic fallback)
- Pi runs fully on windows with pwsh.exe/powershell.exe bash replacement (only plugins?)
- Pi runs fully in wsl2

## Issues seen:

All of these have some papercuts. Windows/wsl bash suffers from https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/7064, Windows/*  suffers from https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/7427, Windows/git-bash suffers from git bash being iffy and e.g. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/6817 (among some closed). Full wsl2 has least amount of problems but might not be feasible due to compliance + still pi uses wrong keybidnings for copy/paste images with WT/allactitty. Running fully natively on windows/powershell isn't easy even with plugins as bash tool cannot be easily replaced (just shadowed; ie same name) and not all shell invocations can be hooked (RPC, ...).

## Call to action:
As such, I'd like to ask: how do you use pi on windows? Why this particular way and not any of other of the abovementioned ones? If you use some plugins, why and which ones? What's missing? What's challenging? What UX gaps are you seeing? 

Feel free to also link your other more specific issues.

issues.title: Emit session_compact_end event to extensions after clearing compaction state
issues.body:
`session_compact` is currently emitted to extensions *before* `this._clearManualCompactionState()` runs in `agent-session.ts`. 

Because `this._compactionAbortController` is still active when `session_compact` fires, any extension trying to inspect `ctx.isIdle()` or dispatch a follow-up message (`sendUserMessage`) throws:
`"Cannot submit a prompt while compaction is in progress. Wait for compaction to finish and retry."`

Could we emit a `session_compact_end` event on `_extensionRunner` right after clearing the controller in `AgentSession.prototype.compact` (around line 1565)?

```typescript
this._clearManualCompactionState();
await this._extensionRunner?.emit({
  type: "session_compact_end",
  compactionEntry: savedCompactionEntry,
  reason: "manual",
  willRetry: false,
});
```

This would let extensions coordinate post-compaction workflows directly, with zero timers, zero deferral hacks, and 100% native engine alignment.

labels.name: bug

issues.body:
### What happened?

Mouse wheel in fullscreen mode scrolls through the editor's prompt history instead of the conversation transcript when running inside Zellij on native Windows (Windows → Alacritty → Zellij → Pi).

Direct terminal (no multiplexer) works correctly. Linux with tmux also works correctly.

**Root cause:** `TuiAltScreen.beforeTerminalStart()` writes mouse DECSET sequences (`?1000h`, `?1002h`, `?1006h`) before `ProcessTerminal.start()` calls `process.stdin.setRawMode(true)`. Zellij then falls back to emitting `ESC[A`/`ESC[B` arrow keys for wheel events on alternate-screen panes, which the editor interprets as history navigation. I made a PR #9655 already, please review.

**Fix:** Move the alt-screen entry and mouse DECSET writes from `beforeTerminalStart()` to `afterTerminalStart()`, after raw mode is active. I'd like to submit a PR for this.

**Environment:** Pi 0.85.1, Zellij 0.45.1, Alacritty 0.17.0, Windows 11 25H2 (build 26200), Node 22.

_No response_

issues.title: --print exits 0 with empty output when the model exhausts its output budget
issues.body:
## Summary

`pi --print --mode text` exits **0** with **0 bytes on stdout and 0 bytes on stderr** when the assistant turn is truncated by the output token limit before any text is produced. A caller cannot distinguish "the model produced nothing" from "the model ran out of budget": the failure looks like a clean success.

## Environment

- pi 0.85.1 (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`), Node 24, WSL.
- Provider `nan`, model `deepseek-v4-flash` (max output **32.8K tokens**), `defaultThinkingLevel: high`.
- argv used by the caller:

```text
pi --print --mode text --no-session --no-tools --no-extensions --no-skills \
   --no-prompt-templates --no-themes --no-context-files --no-approve
```

## Observed

Three consecutive runs with the same prompt on stdin: `exit_code: 0`, `timed_out: false`, **0 bytes stdout**, **0 bytes stderr**, elapsed 59.9 s / 59.3 s / 60.8 s.

## Root cause (evidence from `--mode json` on the same prompt)

- 13 951 `thinking_delta` events and only 3 `text` events.
- The final assistant message carries `"stopReason":"length"`, `"rawStopReason":"length"`, `"willRetry":false`, and no text content.

The model spends the entire output budget on reasoning, the turn is truncated, and there is no text to print. Truncation itself is expected behaviour; presenting it as a silent success is what costs a caller the diagnosis.

## Reproduction

Any prompt that triggers a long reasoning chain. Measured on this machine with the same prompt and model, varying only the thinking level:

| Thinking level | Wall time | `stopReason` | stdout |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `high` (one run) | 5.8 s | `stop` | text produced |
| `medium` | 62.9 s | `length` | **no text** |
| `low` | 39.4 s | `stop` | text produced |
| settings default (`high`) | 59.3-60.8 s, three times | `length` | **no text** |

It is not monotonic in prompt size: a 300-line diff failed, a 400-line diff succeeded and a 540-line diff failed, because what matters is how much the model decides to reason before answering.

Minimal command (the prompt below is written to stdin):

```bash
printf 'Responde SOLO con un objeto JSON: {"findings":[...]}.\n\n```diff\n%s\n```\n' \
  "$(git show HEAD | head -300)" \
  | pi --print --mode text --no-session --no-tools --no-extensions --no-skills \
       --no-prompt-templates --no-themes --no-context-files --no-approve
```

## Requested behaviour

1. When a turn ends with `stopReason: "length"` and no text was produced, `--print` should not look like a clean success: either exit non-zero, or write a diagnostic line to stderr (for example "response truncated by the output token limit; no text produced").
2. Make that state detectable from `--mode text`, or document how a caller is expected to detect it. Today the only usable signal a wrapper has is wall time: ~0.4 s means an empty prompt, ~60 s means a truncated model.

## Impact

A host relay in `gentle-pi` (the review host relay) spawns exactly this argv and treats empty stdout as a transport failure. The operator then sees an undiagnosable `pi-empty-output` and the review of the candidate cannot complete. Empty/whitespace stdin reproduces the same zero-byte output but in ~0.4 s instead of ~60 s, which is how the two causes were told apart.

issues.title: parseChunkUsage drops provider usage fields that aren't on its known list
issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Let `parseChunkUsage` in `packages/ai/src/api/openai-completions.ts` carry provider-specific usage fields through to `AssistantMessage.usage` instead of dropping them.

Right now it builds a fresh object from a fixed set of named OpenAI keys (`prompt_tokens`, `prompt_tokens_details.*`, `prompt_cache_hit_tokens`, `cached_tokens`, `completion_tokens`, `completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens`) and returns it. Anything else the provider put in `usage` is gone by the time a caller sees the message. `openai-responses` has the same shape.

### Why?

Some OpenAI-compatible endpoints report more than token totals. The one I'm on returns a `usage.attribution` object breaking the prompt down per request field and per message id, so you can see how many tokens went to the system prompt versus tool schemas versus conversation history. That's the difference between knowing a run cost 150k tokens and knowing which part of the prompt to fix.

There's no way to get at it today. The data arrives, gets parsed, and the parser throws it away. I can't tap the raw chunk either without reimplementing the SSE loop, so my only option was patching the built package locally, which I'd rather not keep doing across version bumps.

This isn't specific to my provider. Any endpoint adding a usage field that isn't on the list hits the same wall.

### How? (optional)

The narrow version is a couple of lines: after the six mappings, copy across any key of `rawUsage` that isn't one of the recognised ones and isn't already set on the result. That's what I'm running locally and it hasn't disturbed anything.

The part I'd want a maintainer's call on is where it lands in the type. `AssistantMessage["usage"]` is a closed interface, so either it grows an index signature or the extras go somewhere explicit like `usage.providerMetadata`. I'd lean toward the explicit field since it keeps the typed surface honest about what's ours and what's the provider's, but that's a core API decision and I'm not going to guess at it.

Happy to implement whichever you'd prefer, including the matching change to `openai-responses`.

Version: 0.82.0 (also checked against current `main`)

issues.title: Sign in with ChatGPT through a credential-injecting proxy: GPT-6 requests fail with configuration_update (sign-in detection depends on baseUrl)

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

We run Pi in sandboxed environments (containers/VMs) that hold no credentials. The `openai` provider's `baseUrl` points at a central proxy on the host, which holds the Sign in with ChatGPT login, swaps in its access token (`pi auth print-bearer-token --provider openai`) and forwards the request unchanged to `https://api.openai.com/v1`.

Since 1.3.0, every request to `gpt-6-sol`, `gpt-6.1-sol`, `gpt-6-luna` and `gpt-6-astra` fails in this setup:

```
400 subscription_sharing_unsupported_capability
User subscription sharing currently supports only text, image, and file messages, ... Remove unsupported input items or use an API key instead.
```

`isChatGPTSignIn()` in `openai-responses` only matches `baseUrl === "https://api.openai.com/v1"`. Behind the proxy it returns false, so Pi sends `configuration_update` items for models with `supportsMidConvoEffort` (#10853), and also keeps `max_output_tokens`, `temperature` and `prompt_cache_*`, which the code itself notes sign-in rejects.

Workaround: `modelOverrides.<id>.compat.supportsMidConvoEffort: false` (and `supportsMaxOutputTokens: false`) per model.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On the host, sign in with ChatGPT for the `openai` provider.
2. Run a pass-through proxy that sets `Authorization` to that access token and forwards the body to `https://api.openai.com/v1`.
3. In the sandbox's `models.json`, set `providers.openai.baseUrl` to the proxy.
4. `pi -ne --provider openai --model gpt-6-sol --thinking low --print "Reply with exactly OK."` → 400 above. Same on 0.99.1 → OK. `gpt-daybreak-blue-latest` on 1.3.0 → OK.

### Expected behavior

A way to declare a provider's credentials as Sign in with ChatGPT independent of `baseUrl` (e.g. an option in `models.json`), so the sign-in field omissions also apply behind a proxy instead of each new one surfacing as a 400.

### Version

1.3.0

issues.title: Cancellation gaps after de2de549b: between-turn compaction and pending input
issues.body:
## What happened?

After [de2de549b](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/commit/de2de549bcc369726b2e1a50d1626c39806ccc09), the auth fix and original #9340 post-error case work, but stopping between turns still leaves gaps:

- Escape during automatic compaction calls `abortCompaction()`, not `session.abort()`.
- Explicit abort during between-turn preparation still invokes the provider again. Already-drained steering input can enter the transcript even after `clearQueue()`.
- Input held in an interceptor can start a new request when released after abort/settlement.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Queue steering input after a tool response; hold `prepareNextTurn` before the next request.
2. Call `abort()` and clear the queue, then release preparation. The queued message still reaches the transcript.
3. Separately, hold an `input` handler for a streaming submission, abort and settle the current prompt, then release the handler: another provider invocation starts.

Reproduced offline with the actual Agent/AgentSession and faux provider. The queue-owner reproduction loads no extensions; Escape verification is headless, not a live `pi -ne` session.

## Expected behavior

Stop prevents further continuation; unaccepted input stays queued unless explicitly cleared. SDK attempt cancellation, extension vetoes and manual compaction remain unchanged.

issues.title: Aborting during tool execution leaves unanswered tool calls in the session
issues.body:
### What happened?

When I abort while a batch of tools is running, the tool calls after the abort point never get a result. The ones that already started are answered (real results or "Operation aborted"), the tail just disappears from history. No error is shown.

Both executeToolCallsSequential and executeToolCallsParallel in packages/agent/src/agent-loop.ts break out of their loop on abort and skip the remaining calls.

Requests built afterwards are padded by closePendingToolCalls (packages/ai/src/api/transform-messages.ts) with a "No result provided" error, so the model never learns the tools were aborted, it just sees a generic error for calls it did make. The gap in the session file is permanent, and anything reading session entries directly (compaction, external tooling) has to cope with it.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `pi -ne`, any model with tools
2. ask for a batch of slow calls, e.g. run `sleep 10` three times
3. press Esc while the first one runs
4. quit and check the session jsonl: `tool_use` with no `tool_result` after it

### Expected behavior

The skipped calls should get an error `tool_result` ("Operation aborted") recorded in history, same as the started ones.

I have a fix with tests ready and would like to send a PR once this is approved.

Related: #9124 is the same symptom on the dispose/exit path (fix pending in #9126), this is the mid-session abort path. #8378 asked for resuming interrupted turns, a different thing.

### Version

0.87.1

---

Drafted with AI assistance (Claude Code); the abort path was verified against the 0.87.1 sources and a real session file.

```text
openai    gpt-6.1-sol  272K     128K     yes       yes
```

issues.title: OpenRouter compaction/summary requests drop x-session-id when cacheRetention is none
issues.body:
### What happened?

Compaction and branch-summary requests to OpenRouter are sent without `x-session-id`, so OpenRouter logs them as `session_id: null`. They don't show up under the session in Logs/Analytics/Sessions, and they get no sticky routing.

Cause: these calls set `cacheRetention: "none"` (#6618). `openai-completions.ts` and `anthropic-messages.ts` then drop the session ID completely:

```ts
const cacheSessionId = cacheRetention === "none" ? undefined : options?.sessionId;
```

`x-session-id` is OpenRouter's routing/observability key and does not write to the cache. The `uuidv7()` that `createSummaryRequestOptions()` generates for these calls never reaches the provider.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use an OpenRouter model and trigger compaction (`/compact`).
2. Look up the compaction generation: `GET /api/v1/generation?id=<id>` returns `session_id: null`. Normal turns in the same session have a session ID.

### Expected behavior

OpenRouter summary calls keep `x-session-id`. `prompt_cache_key` and `cache_control` stay omitted under `cacheRetention: "none"`.

I'd like to submit the fix. It's OpenRouter-only, so other session-affinity formats are unchanged: https://github.com/Shoshkin/pi/compare/main...fix/openai-completions-session-affinity-cache-none

This reverses the cache-disabled part of bbb61e34a (#9102) for OpenRouter. Happy to adjust if that was intentional.

### Version

0.85.1, still present on main (0.87.1)

issues.title: Don't send another model's thinking as plain text after a model switch

labels.name: pkg:ai
labels.description: LLM API package

issues.body:
When you switch models mid-session, `transformMessages()` turns the earlier model's thinking blocks into plain assistant text. The new model copies that pattern and writes its own reasoning into the visible reply.

Example: a user ran several turns with GLM-5.3, then switched to Kimi K3. Kimi received GLM's reasoning as part of earlier replies and started putting its own thinking in the output. Kimi K3 asks callers not to do this.

**Proposal:** Drop thinking blocks that came from a different model instead of turning them into text. Frontier models only give summaries or encrypted thinking, so little is lost. Full reasoning from DeepSeek, GLM, and similar models is long and makes the output worse.

**Maybe later:** add a compat flag so related models can keep each other's thinking as real thinking blocks, for example Sonnet to Opus.

issues.title: Anthropic tool calls: corrupted non-ASCII edit arguments are silently accepted (dropped `u` in `\uXXXX` → `\b`/`\f` control chars)
issues.body:
### What happened?

With Claude models, `edit` calls on files containing Korean text fail very often, and occasionally corrupt a file. I have been tracking this for about three weeks. It keeps coming back and costs a lot of retries.

There are two symptoms, usually in the same sessions:

1. **Control characters instead of Korean.** The arguments contain C0 control characters where Korean characters were intended.
2. **Garbage calls.** An `edit` whose `oldText` is a few meaningless characters that exist nowhere in the file. Several in a row can occur.

Both usually fail safely as "Could not find ... oldText". Once, a corrupted `newText` was written to a file and had to be repaired by hand.

### The pattern behind symptom 1

It points to a `\uXXXX` escape whose `u` is missing in the tool-input JSON. When the next hex digit happens to be `b` or `f`, the result is still **valid JSON**: `\b` / `\f` followed by the remaining three hex digits. `JSON.parse` accepts it, so the tool runs with wrong strings instead of returning an error.

Illustration (synthetic): intended `\ub0b4` → emitted `\b0b4` → parsed as U+0008 + `0b4`.

### Evidence

Automated scan of my local session logs (edit arguments only, no file contents):

| Model | edit calls | errors | error rate | args with C0 control chars |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| openai-codex/gpt-6-astra | 398 | 9 | 2.3% | 0 |
| openai-codex/gpt-6-sol | 82 | 5 | 6.1% | 0 |
| xai/grok-4.7 | 27 | 3 | 11% | 0 |
| anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 | 212 | 86 | 40.6% | 15 |
| anthropic/claude-opus-5 | 34 | 20 | 58.8% | 8 |
| anthropic/claude-fable-5-1 | 20 | 8 | 40% | 2 |

- All control characters found in Claude edit arguments are U+0008 (`\b`) or U+000C (`\f`). 848 of 873 are followed by exactly three hex digits.
- An earlier manual classification over 20 days: 52 of 68 failed Opus 5.5 edits had lost their Korean text. GPT, Grok and DeepSeek had none.
- I found no case where `repairJson` turned an invalid escape into a literal backslash, so I don't think the repair path causes this. The corrupted cases are already valid JSON before any repair.

### What I ruled out

- **`eager_input_streaming`:** on vs off, 21 attempts each. One corrupted call in each group.
- **Session length:** I forked an affected session and ran four edits each with the default `edit`, a hash-anchored edit extension, and all extensions loaded. All 12 succeeded. On the same day, the original window failed 3 of 4.
- **Edit tool format:** the hash-anchored edit tool made no difference.
- **Encoding in general:** in the same failing window, shell edits, `write`, and a Node script inside the shell all wrote Korean correctly.

### A context effect

The failures cluster after corrupted strings have been visible in the context. In the original window, the broken calls closely resembled an example string that had just been displayed during analysis. Later, a fresh session reproduced it twice in a row right after reading notes that contained such an example. I also hit the garbage-call symptom about six times today in a long session, after the raw examples had already been removed from those notes, so removing them does not prevent it.

So this looks like a model-side tendency that feeds on its own output. I can't prove where the `u` goes missing from the client side.

### Why report it here

Even if the root cause is the model, the pi-side problem is that corruption is silent. A cheap guard would make it a normal retryable validation error:

- For `edit` / `write` (or any string tool args), reject C0 control characters other than `\t`, `\n`, `\r`, with a message like "argument contains control character U+0008; possible malformed \u escape".
- Or, in the Anthropic provider, flag `\b`/`\f` followed by hex digits in the raw `partialJson` before parsing.

If the context effect is real, the error should not echo the corrupted string back to the model. Naming the code point is probably enough.

I can write this guard as a local extension (a `tool_call` handler returning `{ block, reason }`). It seems worth handling in core, though, because every non-ASCII user on Claude is exposed to silent file corruption.

Related: #6278 (Claude tool-call schema errors, closed as model behavior). This case is narrower: non-ASCII content only, and it can corrupt files without any validation error.

### Steps to reproduce

Not deterministic. Using a Claude model, ask for several `edit` calls that replace Korean text in a UTF-8 file. It is much more likely once a corrupted string has appeared in the conversation. Failures show up as oldText mismatches whose arguments contain U+0008/U+000C, or as very short oldText values.

I can share the log-scanning script (counts only) if helpful.

### Version / environment

- pi 0.87.1 (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`), Windows, PowerShell 7
- Provider `anthropic`, Claude subscription login through the third-party `@gotgenes/pi-anthropic-auth` 3.3.2 extension. It only handles authentication, but I have not tested with an API key.

issues.title: Chinese **bold** renders literally when the closing ** sits between 。/：/， and a CJK character (still broken in 0.87.1, was #3353)
issues.body:
## What happened?

In Chinese assistant messages, most `**bold**` spans render as literal `**…**` in the TUI transcript. A span fails **if and only if** its closing `**` is immediately preceded by CJK/fullwidth punctuation (`。：，！？`) and immediately followed by a CJK character or digit. `**X**：` renders; `**X。**Y` shows literal asterisks. Since Chinese prose has no space after sentence-ending punctuation, this is the default shape of mid-paragraph bold in LLM output — long Chinese replies visibly render "half markdown".

Verified under `pi -ne` (no extensions): in the same rendered frame, `**摘要**：这一行正常加粗` renders bold (markers consumed) while `**…核心结论。**后续句子…` stays literal.

Root cause: the bundled marked 18.0.11 implements CommonMark 0.30 delimiter flanking; its gfm closing rule classifies `。**字` as a run that cannot close, so no `strong` token is emitted. This is spec-compliant (long-standing commonmark/commonmark-spec#650), and marked explicitly delegates the fix to integrators (markedjs/marked#3838). The markdown-it and remark ecosystems already ship CJK-friendly emphasis fixes (`markdown-it-cjk-friendly`, `remark-cjk-friendly` — Vercel's streamdown bundles the latter as `@streamdown/cjk`, motivated by exactly pi's case: AI-generated content).

Fix path: `hooks.emStrongMask` (already available in the bundled marked) makes those closers closeable without changing rendered text or ASCII/spec behavior. Prototyped and verified on a 32-line Chinese message: 7/13 → 13/13 bold spans; all ASCII regression cases unchanged. Happy to open a PR.

## Steps to reproduce

1. `pi -ne`
2. Send a message asking the model to output exactly (or paste as user text):

```
**摘要**：这一行正常加粗
**这一段是整份说明的核心结论。**后续句子原样显示星号
```

3. Transcript renders line 1 as bold, line 2 with literal `**…。**`. (Reproduced this way on 0.87.1; #3353 reports the same for TUI and exported HTML on 0.67.6.)

## Expected behavior

Both lines bold. Ideally CJK-friendly emphasis by default (or opt-in), the way streamdown / markdown-it-cjk-friendly handle it.

## Version

0.87.1 (macOS, TUI). Root cause verified directly against the bundled marked 18.0.11; same bug previously reported as #3353 (0.67.6).

issues.title: openai-responses: support configuration_update for cache-preserving reasoning changes

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
## Summary
Support `configuration_update` to change reasoning effort without busting prompt cache (GPT-6)

## Evidence
- GPT-6 guidance: `Add a configuration_update input item to increase/decrease reasoning effort ... without rewriting the original prompt prefix`.
- Pi `0.85.1` changes request-level `reasoning.effort` on thinking-level switch (verified: `xhigh` → `{"effort":"xhigh"}` in `openai-responses:buildParams`), which rewrites prefix and misses cache.
- Pi bundle: zero hits for `configuration_update`.

## Why
Tuning effort mid-session (e.g. xhigh for hard work, low for follow-ups) currently invalidates the entire prefix. Codex preserves cache via `configuration_update`.

## Proposal
- When effort changes mid-conversation on supporting models, keep request-level `reasoning.effort` stable and append `configuration_update` input item instead.
- Gate by model capability; fall back to current behavior where unsupported.
- Include it in WebSocket incremental-request comparison (immutable or forces full request on change).

issues.title: Interactive mode silently drops settings save failures (read-only settings.json)
issues.body:
### What happened?

If the global `settings.json` cannot be written (read-only file, read-only mount, e.g. a Nix/home-manager-managed symlink), changing a setting in interactive mode looks successful (`Thinking blocks: visible`) but nothing is persisted and no error is shown.

`SettingsManager.enqueueWrite` catches the write error (`EROFS`/`EACCES` from `writeFileSync`) and only pushes it onto `errors` for `drainErrors()`. Interactive mode only drains at startup (`main.ts` → `collectSettingsDiagnostics`), so runtime save failures are never reported. On the next start the setting is back to its old value, still with no message.

### Steps to reproduce

```sh
mkdir -p /tmp/pi-ro/agent
echo '{"hideThinkingBlock": true}' > /tmp/pi-ro/agent/settings.json
chmod 444 /tmp/pi-ro/agent/settings.json
PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR=/tmp/pi-ro/agent pi -ne --no-session
# press Ctrl+T -> "Thinking blocks: visible", no error
# quit; settings.json still has "hideThinkingBlock": true; restart shows no warning
```

The recorded but never displayed error, from the same code path:

```
{"scope":"global","path":".../settings.json","code":"EROFS","message":"EROFS: read-only file system, open '.../settings.json'"}
```

### Expected behavior

A failed save is reported in the TUI (for example `Error: Failed to save global settings to <path>: EROFS ... The change applies to this session only.`). A minimal approach that works for me: a `SettingsManager.onWriteError(listener)` hook, which interactive mode subscribes to in `rebindCurrentSession`. Errors still go to `drainErrors()` when no listener is registered.

### Version

0.87.1 (main @ 2b0a123); code path unchanged on main @ 5257d0d

issues.title: 0.99.x: terminal color query replies leak into the prompt and BEL opens the external editor (mintty on Windows, ConPTY)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### What happened?

On startup pi opens the external editor. The prompt contains `;0;rgb:0000/0000/0000;1;rgb:d4d4/2c2c/3a3a;…`.
The query runs regardless of theme.

**Versions:** 0.99.x are affected. 0.87.1 is fine. Windows Terminal is fine.
**Terminal:** mintty on Windows, native node.exe, `TERM=xterm`, `EDITOR=vim` (I am using GitBash for Windows environment)

## Cause

0.87.1 sent a single `ESC]11;?BEL` query. 0.99.x sends OSC 10, OSC 11, OSC 4 for indices 0–15, and DA1 (`ESC[c`) as the end marker (`TERMINAL_COLOR_QUERY` in `packages/tui/src/tui.ts`). In this terminal:

1. The DA1 reply arrives first, before any color reply. `consumeTerminalColorResponse` then drops the pending query, so later replies are no longer consumed.
2. The OSC replies arrive without their `ESC]4` prefix, in fragments (`;0`, `;rgb:0000/0000/0000`, `BEL`, `;1`, …). The reply regex cannot match them anyway.
3. `StdinBuffer` splits non-escape input into single characters, so they land in the editor as text. Each stray BEL is Ctrl+G and opens the external editor.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run pi under GitBash (Windows).
2. The prompt contains `;0;rgb:0000/0000/0000;1;rgb:d4d4/2c2c/3a3a;…`.

issues.title: stdin `read EIO` is recorded as a crash — `process.stdin` has no `error` guard while stdout/stderr do
issues.body:
### Summary

When the controlling terminal disappears while pi holds the tty in raw mode (window/tab closed, ssh or tmux session dropped, parent shell exiting, sleep/wake), Node raises `read EIO` on the stdin read stream. pi has no `'error'` listener on `process.stdin`, so the error reaches `uncaughtException`, and `uncaughtCrash()` persists it to `crashes.json` and exits 1. On the next interactive start, `takeUnnotifiedCrash()` replays it as:

```
Warning: pi crashed on 9/30/2026, 8:16:48 PM (read EIO). Run /bug to report it;
the crash details are attached automatically.
```

An environmental hangup is reported to the user as a pi crash, and lands in crash telemetry. Note this is the stdin half of the same class as #4144 (stdout had no EIO guard) — stdout/stderr are now guarded, stdin was not.

### Evidence

`~/.pi/agent/crashes.json` is a 5-entry ring buffer, and all 5 slots are this error, spanning two releases:

```json
{
  "timestamp": "2026-09-30T18:54:15.878Z",
  "version": "0.99.1",
  "kind": "uncaught_exception",
  "message": "read EIO",
  "stack": "Error: read EIO\n    at TTY.onStreamRead (node:internal/stream_base_commons:216:20)",
  "sessionFile": "~/.pi/agent/sessions/--<cwd-slug>--/<timestamp>_<uuid>.jsonl",
  "cwd": "~",
  "notified": true
}
```

(The other 4 records are identical in message and stack, on 0.99.1 and 0.99.2.)

`~/.pi/agent/crashes.json.bak` holds 5 byte-identical records from 2026-09-23 on `0.87.1` — so this is long-standing, not a 0.99.x regression.

Environment: macOS 26 (Apple Silicon), Ghostty, Node v25.4.0 (`pi` declares `engines.node >= 22.19.0`), `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` 0.99.2 / `@earendil-works/pi-tui` 0.99.2.

### Root cause

`packages/tui/src/terminal.ts` — `ProcessTerminal.start()` arms raw-mode stdin but never attaches an error listener (dist line numbers for 0.99.2):

```ts
this.wasRaw = process.stdin.isRaw || false;
if (process.stdin.setRawMode) {
    process.stdin.setRawMode(true);            // 113-115
}
process.stdin.setEncoding("utf8");
process.stdin.resume();                        // 118
...
process.stdin.on("data", this.stdinDataHandler);   // 183
```

`stop()` (dist line 338+) removes the `data` handler, but there is no `error` handler to remove. A repo-wide grep for `process.stdin.on("error"` (and `once`/`addListener`) in both `pi-tui` and `pi-coding-agent` returns nothing for the process-level stdin handle.

Meanwhile `packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts` already owns exactly the right policy for a dead terminal — it is just not applied to stdin:

```ts
const DEAD_TERMINAL_ERROR_CODES = new Set(["EIO", "EPIPE", "ENOTCONN"]);   // 118
function isDeadTerminalError(error) { ... }                                // 119

const terminalErrorHandler = (error) => {                                  // 3491
    if (isDeadTerminalError(error)) {
        this.emergencyTerminalExit();   // exits 129, does NOT write a crash record
    }
    throw error;
};
process.stdout.on("error", terminalErrorHandler);                          // 3497
process.stderr.on("error", terminalErrorHandler);                          // 3498
this.signalCleanupHandlers.push(() => process.stdout.off("error", terminalErrorHandler));
this.signalCleanupHandlers.push(() => process.stderr.off("error", terminalErrorHandler));
```

So an EIO on stdout/stderr is treated as an environmental hangup and exits cleanly with code 129 (`emergencyTerminalExit`), while the identical EIO on stdin is logged as a pi crash and exits 1. The `SIGHUP` path is already covered by the stdout guard; the unguarded stdin read is what survives it.

There is no deterministic local reproduction — the trigger is environmental. The claim above is derived from the code path plus the persisted crash records, not from a scripted repro.

### Suggested fix

Cheapest fix: reuse the existing helper and cleanup list in `interactive-mode.ts::registerSignalHandlers()`:

```diff
     process.stdout.on("error", terminalErrorHandler);
     process.stderr.on("error", terminalErrorHandler);
+    process.stdin.on("error", terminalErrorHandler);
     this.signalCleanupHandlers.push(() => process.stdout.off("error", terminalErrorHandler));
     this.signalCleanupHandlers.push(() => process.stderr.off("error", terminalErrorHandler));
+    this.signalCleanupHandlers.push(() => process.stdin.off("error", terminalErrorHandler));
```

Non-dead-terminal stdin errors still `throw`, so they keep reaching `uncaughtCrash()` exactly as today — only EIO/EPIPE/ENOTCONN change from "crash" to "exit 129".

Architectural alternative, if the stdin raw-mode lifecycle should own its own guard: attach and detach the listener in `packages/tui/src/terminal.ts` `start()`/`stop()` alongside `stdinDataHandler`. That is tidier ownership-wise, but pi-tui would need an exit-policy hook to reproduce the "exit 129, no crash record" behaviour, since `isDeadTerminalError` and `emergencyTerminalExit` live in coding-agent.

### Optional, same area

`DEAD_TERMINAL_ERROR_CODES` omits `ENXIO`, which other CLIs treat as a terminal hangup alongside `EIO` — for example gemini-cli #15369 and react-doctor's `guard-stdin.ts`, which uses `{ EIO, ENXIO }` with exit code 129 for precisely this case.

### Expected behaviour

A vanished terminal should exit like an interrupted run (129) without writing a crash record, so the next launch does not tell the user "pi crashed" for something that is not a pi bug.

I am happy to open a PR for the `interactive-mode.ts` variant if that is the preferred placement.

issues.title: Transcript OSC 133 prompt markers invalidate OSC 7501 program status

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

Pi uses OSC 133;A as a transcript-navigation marker, but OSC 7501 interprets it as a new shell prompt and expires program status. iTerm2 3.7.5 now supports OSC 7501, making this conflict relevant to Pi's native status integration (#10607).

`UserMessageComponent.render()` and `AssistantMessageComponent.render()` prepend this marker to transcript messages, including on repaint. An unchanged working/blocked state can therefore lose its terminal status without a corresponding agent lifecycle event.

Related: #9683 reported the same marker conflict with iTerm2's older Session Status protocol. This report concerns OSC 7501, whose [lifetime rules](https://www.superlogical.com/rex/docs/build/program-status#states) explicitly require clearing working/blocked records at OSC 133;A. [iTerm2 3.7.5 also clears idle](https://github.com/gnachman/iTerm2/blob/5964ff23177814d752e95a6e57931863842131d4/sources/VT100/iTermProgramStatus.swift#L617-L625).

### Steps to reproduce

Minimal protocol reproduction in iTerm2 3.7.5:

```sh
printf '\033]7501;state=working:app=pi\007'
sleep 2
printf '\033]133;A\007'
sleep 5
```

The second write invalidates the working record while the script is still running. Pi emits that same marker from its [user](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/user-message.ts) and [assistant](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/assistant-message.ts) render methods.

This is a source-level report with a protocol reproduction, not a verified extension-free end-to-end Pi reproduction. Our extension currently compensates by observing stdout and reasserting status after rendering.

### Expected behavior

Transcript navigation and repaint should not announce a new shell prompt or invalidate program status.

### Version

Pi 1.3.0; iTerm2 3.7.5. Marker emission also verified in current Pi source.

prs.title: fix(ai): coerce JSON-encoded object and array tool arguments
prs.body:
## Summary

`validateToolArguments` recovers a tool argument the model delivered as a JSON-encoded string, for `object` and `array` parameters.

`arguments` already travels as a JSON string, so a model that mixes up the two encoding levels quotes a nested value one time too many: the outer parse succeeds and the inner value stays a string. `coercePrimitiveByType` already recovers that for every scalar type, but not for structures, so a tool whose parameter is an object or an array cannot be called at all by such a model — validation fails before the tool runs, once per `oneOf` branch:

```
Validation failed for tool "configure":
  - target: must be object
  - target: must be object
  - target: must match exactly one schema in oneOf

Received arguments:
{
  "action": "inspect",
  "target": "{\"kind\": \"agent\", \"name\": \"researcher\"}"
}
```

Reproduced on openrouter with `qwen/qwen3.8-flash`, 3/3 on two different object parameters. The scalars beside it arrive natively.

`parseStructuredString` sits next to the structural coercion rather than in `coercePrimitiveByType` — it reshapes a value instead of converting a primitive — and runs before the per-property descent so the parsed structure still gets the existing item/property coercion. It takes a string only when the schema asks for `object` or `array`, the string parses, and the result matches a type the schema accepts; otherwise the value is returned untouched and the original type error is still reported. A schema that also accepts `string` is left alone, so a caller's literal JSON-looking text is never rewritten. For example, with `type: ["string", "object"]` a JSON-encoded object stays a string, because it already matches the `string` arm; this is deliberate, so a model that sends serialized objects there keeps the string.

JSON-encoded strings on plain `properties`/`items` are decoded while optional nulls are normalized, before `Value.Convert`. The decoded structure gets the same optional-null handling as a native one, and a native TypeBox `Type.Array` does not wrap the encoded string into a one-element array. Strings decoded later inside `anyOf`/`oneOf` branches are normalized against the branch schema before descending.

Refs #5697, #8757.

## Testing

- `npx vitest --run test/validation.test.ts` in `packages/ai` — 14 passed; the coercion, TypeBox array/object, and native-vs-encoded optional-null tests fail without the change
- `npm run check` — passes, rebased on current `main`
- `npx vitest --run` in `packages/ai` — same pass/fail set as `main`, plus the 5 new tests
- `npx biome check` on both changed files
- `npx tsgo --noEmit` — no new errors

prs.title: fix(env): include stderr in pi-env startup errors
prs.body:
When the daemon exits before `hello`, the error has only the exit code. For example, with `loginShell: true` and a profile that aborts on a missing file:

```
pi-env exited with code 3 before it was ready
```

`sshConnection`'s probe and deploy steps already report ssh's stderr, so this is about the launch itself: a login profile, a daemon that can't execute, or a `Connection` created with its own command, which has no probe or deploy step, so auth and network errors also end up here.

This keeps a short stderr tail until `hello` and adds it to startup errors:

```
pi-env exited with code 3 before it was ready
remote stderr:
profile: /opt/toolchain/env.sh: No such file or directory
```

The tail is capped at 20 lines / 2000 chars, with terminal escapes and control characters stripped. Ready sessions are unchanged.

I hit it while testing `loginShell` against an sshd in Docker. Tests are in `test/connection.test.ts`, and `npm run check` and `./test.sh` pass.

## Problem

With `contextWindow <= 400k`, the fixed reserve-based compaction trigger fires too early: a session barely past the (small) context limit gets compacted immediately, losing working state that would still fit. Real-world impact observed on self-hosted deployments running 200k-400k models with long tool-heavy sessions.

## Fix

For small windows (`contextWindow <= 400k`), scale the compaction trigger to **90% of the context window** instead of the fixed reserve computation. Larger windows keep the existing behavior.

## Tests

Compaction suite: 5 files / 48 tests passed, 10 skipped (existing suite green with the change).

prs.title: fix(ai): throttle streaming partial-json re-parse (O(n^2) wedged event loop)
prs.body:
## Problem

On the Anthropic stream path, every `input_json_delta` re-parsed the **entire accumulated** tool-use `partialJson` (`JSON.parse` + repair + partial-parse). A multi-MB tool-use argument pinned the event loop for minutes and wedged the whole server (observed in production on a self-hosted pi-web instance, 2026-09-07). Total parse work across a stream is O(n^2) in the final argument size.

## Fix

Re-parse on **geometric growth** only, via a new `shouldReparsePartial(len, lastParsedLen)` helper in `utils/json-parse.ts`:

- re-parse when the buffer grew **>= 4KB** and **>= 25%** since the last parse
- `content_block_stop` always performs the exact final parse, so throttling never loses correctness
- total parse work per block drops to O(n)

## Tests

`test/json-parse-throttle.test.ts` (5 cases): throttle schedule boundaries, exact final parse at `content_block_stop`, and parse-count bounding that demonstrates the O(n) bound.

## Notes

- The same per-delta full-reparse pattern may exist on other provider stream paths; this PR scopes to the Anthropic path where the incident was reproduced.
- Understand & verified against current `main` (imports unioned with the newer `parseToolCallArguments` export; vitest run: throttle tests 5/5 green; the provider E2E failures in this environment are pre-existing on `main` without API credentials).

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): close own custom UI overlay
prs.body:
I ran into this with two extensions open at once, [pi-interactive-shell](https://github.com/nicobailon/pi-interactive-shell) and [pi-ask-user](https://github.com/edlsh/pi-ask-user). After tracking it down, it looks like a pi bug in how `ctx.ui.custom()` closes overlays.

`done()` from `ctx.ui.custom({ overlay: true })` closes the overlay with `ui.hideOverlay()`, which removes the topmost overlay as opposed to the one that called `done()`. That works when only one overlay is open, but with two it can remove the wrong one. In my case, the agent opened a shell overlay with pi-interactive-shell and then asked me a question with pi-ask-user in a second overlay. When the shell process exited, its `done()` removed the ask_user dialog. The finished shell overlay stayed on screen ignoring all input, and the dialog's promise never resolved, so the turn hung until I restarted pi.

This fix keeps the handle returned by `showOverlay()` so `done()` hides its own overlay. I added a regression test that opens two overlays and closes the bottom one. It runs with both a normal and a non-capturing bottom overlay, since pi-interactive-shell opens its overlay as non-capturing.

#10648 describes the same bug, so I didn't open a duplicate issue. It was auto-closed, but this should fix it.

closes #10648

prs.title: fix(ai): avoid thinkingBudget and MINIMAL on unmapped Gemini 4 models
prs.body:
**Urgent (P0 incomplete fix for #10890):** Unblocks Gemini 4 (`gemini-4-argon`, `gemini-4-argon-cyber-permissive`) requests before the next release so custom `models.json` definitions (including the exact repro in #10890) and `pi-ai` callers without `thinkingLevelMap` do not fail with HTTP 400 on `off` or `minimal`.

### Problem

After #10890 (`1692bba63`), `usesGoogleThinkingLevel` matches `gemini-4-*`, but two paths in `packages/ai/src/api/google-shared.ts` still emit invalid `thinkingConfig` payloads when `thinkingLevelMap` is not populated (such as custom `models.json` definitions like the repro in #10890, `gemini-4-argon-cyber-permissive`, or direct `pi-ai` `Model` objects):

1. When reasoning is omitted or `"off"`, `getDisabledGoogleThinkingConfig(model)` calls `clampThinkingLevel(model, "off")`. Without `thinkingLevelMap.off: null`, `clampThinkingLevel` returns `"off"`, hitting `if (fallback === "off") return { thinkingBudget: 0 }` even though `usesGoogleThinkingLevel(model)` is `true`. Vertex AI rejects this with HTTP 400 (`Thinking budget is not supported for this model. Use thinking level instead.`).
2. Per the [Gemini 4 Argon developer guide](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/guides/gemini-4-argon), both `thinking_budget` and `thinking_level="MINIMAL"` return HTTP 400 (`LOW`, `MEDIUM`, and `HIGH` are the only valid levels, same as Gemini 3 Pro). Without `thinkingLevelMap.minimal: null`, `resolveGoogleThinkingLevel(model, "minimal")` resolves to `"minimal"` (`"MINIMAL"`).

### Solution

- Clamp disabled thinking from `"minimal"` instead of `"off"` in `getDisabledGoogleThinkingConfig(model)` so `usesGoogleThinkingLevel(model)` models never fall back to `{ thinkingBudget: 0 }` when `thinkingLevelMap.off` is not `null`.
- Map unmapped `"minimal"` to `"low"` in `resolveGoogleThinkingLevel(model, level)` for Gemini 3 Pro (`/gemini-3(?:\.\d+)?-pro/`) and Gemini 4+ (`/gemini-(?:[4-9]|[1-9]\d)/`) models.
- Add regression tests in `packages/ai/test/google-thinking-level-map.test.ts` covering both omitted reasoning (`{ thinkingLevel: "LOW" }`) and `minimal` reasoning (`{ includeThoughts: true, thinkingLevel: "LOW" }`) on unmapped `gemini-4-argon`.

fixes #11003

prs.title: fix(ai,coding-agent): base context recovery on declared model metadata
prs.body:
## What this is

A turn that exhausts its context window now recovers instead of ending in an empty response. Pi decides recovery from declared model metadata: the configured context window and an optional list of response model aliases. Recovery means one compaction followed by a continuation of the same turn.

## What this changes for the user

Pi users get a continued turn when the context window is exhausted. The turn compacts once and continues, and it reuses the tool result it already produced. The old path sent the request with `max_tokens: 1`, and the provider returned an empty `length` stop.

The cost is one extra provider request for the compaction summary. A route whose provider renames the model also needs a declared alias. Without that declaration, a truncated turn from that route stops recovering.

## Requirements

- A request whose configured window cannot hold the answer fails before network I/O with a recognizable context-overflow error.
- Ordinary requests keep their output caps and thinking configuration.
- A context-overflow error or a short `length` stop compacts and continues the same turn at most once.
- A completed tool call runs once, and recovery reuses its result.
- Only the selected model or a declared alias is eligible; a genuine fallback is not.
- A failed recovery settles with an actionable incomplete response.

## The architecture

Pi now decides context recovery from the model's declared context window and declared response aliases.

The old request builder floored an exhausted budget at one token. The request still reached the provider with `max_tokens: 1`. The provider returned an empty `length` stop that ended the turn. Recovery also required the provider's echoed model id to match the selected id exactly.

The request builder now exposes the unfloored budget. The provider fails before network I/O when the budget cannot hold 1,024 output tokens. That error enters the existing compaction path. For a `length` stop, Pi matches the response through the route's declared `responseModelAliases`.

Before:

```mermaid
graph TD
  Request[next request] --> Clamp[max_tokens clamped to 1]
  Clamp --> Provider[provider request]
  Provider --> Empty[empty length stop]
  Empty --> Exact{echoed id equals selected id?}
  Exact -->|no| Stop[turn ends incomplete]
```

After:

```mermaid
graph TD
  Request[next request] --> Budget{output budget usable?}
  Budget -->|no| Overflow[context-overflow error]
  Budget -->|yes| Provider[provider request]
  Provider --> Length{short length stop?}
  Overflow --> Trust{selected model or declared alias?}
  Length --> Trust
  Trust -->|yes| Retry[compact and retry once]
  Trust -->|no| Stop[turn ends incomplete]
```

Three decisions shaped the design. Declared aliases replace name normalization, because normalization cannot separate a gateway rename from a genuine fallback. The budget check lives in every built-in `streamSimple` provider, because all of them clamp through the same helper. Context-overflow errors are not retryable. Their token counts can contain digit sequences such as `500` that the transient-error patterns match.

The compaction and retry machinery is untouched, and the existing bounded-retry tests stay green. Healthy requests use the same request-building path, covered by the existing provider payload tests.

## Decision review

- **An undeclared rename stops recovering.** Merging accepts that catalog authors must add `responseModelAliases` to a renamed route. Without the declaration, a truncated turn from that route stops recovering.
- **A configured window below 5,120 tokens now fails before the request.** The limit is the 4,096-token safety margin plus the 1,024-token answer floor. Merging accepts that a custom model with such a window errors instead of sending `max_tokens: 1`. Raising the configured window fixes it.

## Interface changes

models.json model entries accept an optional `responseModelAliases` list:

```json
{
  "id": "claude-opus-5-5@default",
  "responseModelAliases": ["claude-opus-5-5"]
}
```

## Data and contract model

`responseModelAliases` names the provider-reported model ids that this route is trusted to produce. Pi accepts a response when both the requested and reported ids are the model id or an alias. A missing list trusts only the exact model id.

## Testing

**Automated coverage.** The `ai` suite covers the budget helper, the pre-fetch failure, and the preserved caps. It also covers the model-switch protection and the alias and fallback identity. The `coding-agent` suite drives the incident shape through the real agent loop. It uses a scripted Anthropic transport. The over-window follow-up never reaches HTTP, and the tool runs once. One compact-and-retry runs, and the same turn resumes. `npm run check` and the `ai`, `agent`, and `coding-agent` suites pass. Two tests that need a built `dist/` were not run in this worktree.

**How to test manually.** Not exercised by hand; the incident shape is driven end-to-end by the new suite test.

prs.title: chore(rebase): fence と ratchet を入れて pi engine の vendoring 方針を決める
prs.body:
## 何をしたか

pi を fork した msa を typescript-template ベースに再構築する作業の 1 つ目。着手前に「どの設定がどのパスを支配するか」（fence）を決め、house の strict 設定を vendored engine にそのまま当てた場合のコストを実測して、ratchet として保存した。

この 1 本はコードを書き換えない。後続の slice が機械的作業になるか、全体をやり直す必要があるかを最初に確定させるためのもの。

## なぜ fence が要るのか

`packages/**` は pi の engine（src 174,587 LOC）で、fork した理由はここに手を入れるため。house の規約をそのまま当てると、実測で:

| house のルール | コスト |
| --- | --- |
| `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` | 1,081 errors |
| `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` | 1,713 errors |
| `noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature` | 2,217 errors |
| oxlint の house categories | 55,665 errors |
| `no-comments` | コメント 25,595 行 |
| 再整形 | vendored ファイル全件 |

しかも整形すると、msa が手を入れるファイルほど以降の upstream 変更が必ず衝突する。そこで、msa が書くコードには house の規約を full で適用し、engine は pi の整形・lint のまま、strict フラグとの差だけを数値で監視する。

## 入れたもの

- `UPSTREAM.md` — 固定 base commit（`4a5d3729`）と、`packages/**` だけを取り込む手順・衝突の解決規則
- `docs/toolchain-fence.md` — fence の表、ratchet の規則、実測値、house テンプレートから意図的に採らないものと理由
- `tools/fence-counts.mjs` + `baseline.json` — strict フラグごとの error 数を測定。`npm run fence:counts` で保存、`npm run fence:check` で回帰検出
- `specs/msa/` — 再構築全体の slice ladder（Phase A 8 本 + Phase B/C の概要）と決定・未確定事項

## どう確認したか

```
npm ci --ignore-scripts
tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json         # 0 errors
npm run fence:counts                  # 11 フラグを測定して baseline を書き込み
npm run fence:check                   # 同じ測定で「no regression」
git merge-base main upstream/main     # == main（msa の patch はまだ無い）
```

## 次の slice

`02-delete-npm-machinery` — pi の publish / release / nix / コミュニティ機構を削除して、workflow を 13 本から減らす。

prs.title: feat(durable): support namespaced SQLite storage
prs.body:
## Summary

Some use cases may require Pi Durable to share a single SQLite database, e.g. Cloudflare Durable Object could store additional data, unrelated to the harness in other tables. To isolate Pi Durable storage from the rest, this PR introduces the option to provide a table prefix. A prefix `pi_` results in table names like `pi_conversations` instead of `conversations` for instance, same for index names.

- add optional SQLite table and index prefixes rendered from one portable schema map
- expose prefixing through `SqliteStorage.open()`, `openNodeSqliteStorage()`, and `openDurableObjectSqliteStorage()` helper
- keep adapters prefix-agnostic by rendering names in storage SQL; split Node database options from combined Node storage options
- validate Node prefixes before creating or configuring the database
- simplify the Cloudflare adapter by removing SQL rewriting while improving cursor reads and cross-adapter transaction ordering
- document prefix behaviour and cover host-table coexistence plus multiple isolated namespaces

Changing a prefix does not migrate existing data.

## Testing

- `npm run check`
- `vitest --run test/sqlite-cloudflare.test.ts test/sqlite-migrations.test.ts test/sqlite-facade.test.ts test/sqlite-storage.test.ts` (111 tests)

prs.title: fix(ai): inline $ref tool schemas for NVIDIA NIM models
prs.body:
Fixes #10270.

`nemotron-3.5-super-vl-preview` and `qwen3.8-flash-next` return an object described only by a local `$ref` as a JSON string. `validateToolArguments` rejects that:

```
schema:  "settings": { "$ref": "#/$defs/Settings" }
model:   "settings": "{\"notifications\":false}"
```

With the definition inlined, both work. Kimi K2.6 on the same route works either way. Thanks @itayzit for the report, the reproduction, and the [first patch](https://github.com/itayzit/pi/tree/schema-ref-compat).

### Changes

- New `OpenAICompletionsCompat.inlineSchemaRefs`, wired like `supportsStrictMode`:
  - `detectCompat()` and `NVIDIA_OPENAI_COMPAT` default it to true for NVIDIA NIM; it is false everywhere else.
  - `models.json` can enable it for other endpoints, for example Qwen on vLLM.
  - When it is on, `convertTools` sends the inlined schema.
- Other providers are unchanged.
- New `packages/ai/src/utils/json-schema-refs.ts` does the inlining:
  - Expands local `#` and `#/...` references only.
  - Leaves recursive, external, and unresolved refs in place, along with refs that have non-annotation siblings, and keeps the root `$defs` they point into.
  - Sends the schema unchanged if a nested `$id` or anchor is present, or if inlining would add more than 1,000 nodes.
  - Never mutates the input, and caches the result per schema object.
- Argument coercion and optional-null cleanup in `validateToolArguments` now run against the inlined schema. Before, `{"notifications": "false"}` was coerced to `false` in an inline schema but rejected behind a `$ref`. `Check` still runs against the original schema. This applies to all providers and changes nothing that is sent.

Not included:

- Repairing stringified objects during validation, which was declined in #3336.
- Keeping `$defs` in Anthropic non-strict schemas, which is #9557.

This PR was prepared with AI assistance.

releases.name: v1.3.0
releases.body:
### New Features

- **Choose where `/share` uploads**: `sessionShareDestination` selects `auto`, `gist`, or `radius`. See [Sessions and context](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.3.0/packages/coding-agent/docs/settings.md#sessions-and-context) and [Export or share a session](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.3.0/packages/coding-agent/docs/sessions.md#export-or-share-a-session).
- **Cache-preserving thinking level changes on OpenAI GPT-6**: changing the thinking level mid-session with an API key keeps the prompt cache.
- **Kimi Code over Chat Completions**: tools added mid-conversation no longer invalidate the prompt cache. `models.json` base URL overrides must now include `/v1`. See [Providers](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.3.0/packages/coding-agent/docs/providers.md).
- **Clean model switching**: thinking from a previous model is dropped instead of being shown to the new model as text.
- **Resumed sessions keep their active tools**: `--tools +name`/`-name` applies on top of them. See [Tools](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.3.0/packages/coding-agent/docs/settings.md#tools).

### Added

- Changing the thinking level mid-session on OpenAI GPT-6 models (API key) now keeps the prompt cache ([#10853](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10853))
- Added the `sessionShareDestination` setting to choose automatic, GitHub gist, or Radius uploads for `/share` ([#10870](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10870) by [@vegarsti](https://github.com/vegarsti))

### Changed

- Changed the `kimi-coding` provider to use OpenAI Chat Completions at `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1`, the protocol used by the official Kimi Code client. K3, K3-256K, and Kimi For Coding now accept tools added mid-conversation without invalidating the prompt cache. `models.json` overrides of the `kimi-coding` base URL must now include `/v1` ([#10720](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10720))
- Changed model switching to drop thinking blocks from earlier assistant messages produced by a different model, instead of sending them as plain text. The new model previously saw the old model's reasoning as part of its replies and could start writing its own reasoning into the visible answer ([#10995](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10995))

### Fixed

- Pinned internal Pi dependencies to exact release versions to prevent fresh installs from mixing incompatible packages ([#10865](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10865))
- Fixed resumed sessions dropping tools activated during the session. Resume now restores the session's active tools, with `--tools +name`/`-name` entries applied to them, unless `--tools` with tool names, `--no-tools`, or `--no-builtin-tools` selects tools explicitly ([#10785](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10785))
- Fixed stopping a codemode script or reaching its deadline waiting for a non-interruptible built-in to return on Bun ([#10748](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10748))
- Fixed repeated codemode timeouts or aborts accumulating surviving workers; admission now limits live workers to two across sessions, counting cancelled workers until actual exit ([#10748](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10748))
- Fixed `--model` choosing a provider by catalog order when several providers offer the match; Pi now prefers the provider with credentials and otherwise reports the ambiguity. `--models` and `enabledModels` add a model for each provider that offers it and warn about the ambiguity ([#10160](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10160))
- Fixed `read` line-range labels for numeric-string or null arguments in the TUI, session tree, HTML exports, and examples ([#9887](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9887))
- Fixed the Nix flake build failing when a provider switched APIs: the model catalog pin is now refreshed from the newest published catalog when its model API groups differ, and releases pin the newest catalog and build with it before tagging ([#10985](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10985))
- Fixed the Nix package putting its Node.js first on `PATH`, which made bash tool shells use Pi's Node instead of the user's `node`/`npm`. Pi's Node is now only a fallback ([#10519](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10519))
- Fixed prompt templates dropping empty quoted arguments (`""` or `''`), which shifted later positional arguments and prevented positional defaults from applying ([#10867](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10867))
- Fixed the Nix package build failing in its install check because it still expected chord and esbuild, which Pi no longer depends on
- Fixed tool-call argument parsing dropping fields when a string contains an invalid `\u` escape such as `\usepackage` ([#10868](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10868))
- Fixed Anthropic and Bedrock Claude requests failing with a 400 when an error tool result contains images; the images are now sent after the tool results of the turn, so the model still sees them ([#10794](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10794))
- Fixed OpenCode Go Gemini models failing with a 404 by moving OpenCode Zen and OpenCode Go to the `opencode.ai/inference` endpoints, and added Google Generative AI support to the OpenCode Go provider
- Fixed OpenCode Go MiniMax M2.7 failing with "Model does not support this protocol" by using the Anthropic Messages API
- Fixed automatic retry not triggering for gateway `Unable to forward upstream stream` errors ([#10920](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10920))
- Fixed automatic retry not triggering for `The service is temporarily unavailable` errors, which also made compaction fail on the first attempt ([#10965](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10965))
- Fixed OpenAI-compatible responses showing thinking after the answer when a proxy such as LiteLLM sends reasoning and content in the same stream chunk ([#10926](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10926))
- Fixed Gemini 4 Argon requests on Google Vertex failing with "Thinking budget is not supported", and its thinking level being ignored on the Gemini API ([#10890](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10890))
- Fixed Xiaomi MiMo models failing with a 400 at the `minimal` thinking level; they now expose only the `off` and `high` levels ([#10818](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10818))
- Fixed `openai-codex/gpt-6.1-sol` using a 272K context window instead of the 500K window Codex now provides ([#10840](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10840))
- Fixed tool calls whose final arguments are malformed JSON silently running with only the fields parsed before the error; they now fail validation and show the model the raw arguments it sent ([#10897](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10897))
- Fixed Claude Haiku 5.5 and Claude Opus 5 not supporting the `off` thinking level ([#10753](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10753))
- Fixed `done()` of an extension's `ctx.ui.custom({ overlay: true })` closing the topmost overlay instead of its own, which left the finished overlay on screen and another extension's dialog unresolved ([#10648](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10648), [#10999](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10999) by [@masonc15](https://github.com/masonc15))

## Problem

A command whose reply never arrives gets its answer from `sessionCommandEvidenceText` ([hosted-session-command-session.ts L85-L105](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/643bcaa07e4f01100e51e4778e03851d0451f9fe/packages/cli/src/serve/hosted-session-command-session.ts#L85-L105), decision 14). The text depends only on the delivery state, not on the command kind. The `accepting` and `unknown` texts were written for board writes:

> `accepting`: The command reached the leader, but its reply did not arrive in time; a write may have taken effect. End your turn and say so in your result; **read the board again before repeating the write.**
>
> `unknown`: The command's outcome is unknown; the leader may have run it and a write may have taken effect. **Read the board again before repeating the write.**

Since #13955, `member_message` (a member's `send_message` to another member or `"*"`) rides the same channel and gets the same text. For a message this advice is wrong twice over:

1. **The board can't tell a member whether a message arrived.** `task_list` returns the board and the roster with each member's run state, not messages. A member who follows the advice learns nothing.
2. **Repeating the send duplicates it.** The command id is derived from the sender session, the prompt and the call id ([L5566](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/643bcaa07e4f01100e51e4778e03851d0451f9fe/packages/cli/src/serve/hosted-workspace-tool-turn.ts#L5566)). Each `msgc_` id is `sha256(lead \0 commandId \0 position)` ([hosted-member-chain.ts L103](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/643bcaa07e4f01100e51e4778e03851d0451f9fe/packages/cli/src/serve/hosted-member-chain.ts#L103)). So a send repeated in a later Turn gets new ids, and the lead's idempotency check, which is keyed on the `msgc_` id, does not catch it. Meanwhile the `msgc_` entries the lead already committed are still delivered once the lead recovers. Recipients then get the message twice, and as #14054 FG9 puts it, *"a duplicated member message is user-visible and cannot be retracted."*

## Evidence (real stack, #13955 verification)

The stack was the Spring managed-agent-server on MySQL 8.4.7, the embedded Runtime Broker and the bundled Hosted Harness; only the model was scripted. Full report: https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13955#issuecomment-6139614564. These runs used #13955 head `ce9306ed4c` and its trial merge with main.

- **P3 (no restart).** A MySQL trigger refused the lead's `session_command` receipt INSERT while member `alice` sent to `"*"`, with `bob` and `carol` running.
  - The lead's later writes all answered `503 session log writes stopped after an earlier failure` (#13413). The relay gave the command up as `unknown`.
  - The two `msgc_` already committed stayed `planned`.
  - After the 2-minute bound, alice's model was told, verbatim: *"The command reached the leader, but its reply did not arrive in time; a write may have taken effect. End your turn and say so in your result; read the board again before repeating the write."*
- **P7 (same trigger, then the Harness is killed and restarted).** The re-run delivers those same two `msgc_` ids: `bob` and `carol` each receive exactly one input. So committed messages do arrive after recovery, and a re-send would arrive as a second copy.

![P3 / P7 evidence](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/3b6260d57de34867d4cf496d1cc75e5ab3aa2b82/pr13955/05-rerun-and-latch.png)

The duplicate in point 2 follows from the id derivation above. I did not run it end to end: no probe had alice re-send and then let the lead recover.

## Expected

A `member_message` timeout should not point to the board, and should tell the model not to re-send. For example:

- `accepting`: *"The message reached the leader, but its reply did not arrive in time; some recipients may already have it or get it later. Do not send it again; end your turn and say so in your result."*
- `unknown`: *"The message's outcome is unknown; some recipients may already have it or get it later. Do not send it again."*

`planned`, `rejected` and `cancelled` already read correctly for a message.

## Notes for a fix (not tested)

- **The kind is available at every call site.** The live wait computes `kind` right before minting the command id ([L5557-L5564](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/643bcaa07e4f01100e51e4778e03851d0451f9fe/packages/cli/src/serve/hosted-workspace-tool-turn.ts#L5557-L5564)) and answers at [L5772](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/643bcaa07e4f01100e51e4778e03851d0451f9fe/packages/cli/src/serve/hosted-workspace-tool-turn.ts#L5772). The recovery settle at [hosted-runtime-recovery.ts L1068](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/643bcaa07e4f01100e51e4778e03851d0451f9fe/packages/cli/src/serve/hosted-runtime-recovery.ts#L1068) has `run.toolName`.
- **Keep the three answers identical.** The docstring requires the live wait, the resumed wait and the interrupted-turn settle to say the same words. A kind-aware text has to keep that across all three.
- **Check `plan_submit` too.** #13974 (b3d) added `plan_submit` to the same channel, and it gets the same board wording. Whether that fits a plan submission was not checked here.

## Related

- #13955: finding 3 of its verification.
- #13413: the store-failure latch that produced the stall in P3.
- #14054: FG9 covers delivery and duplicate member messages.

<details>
<summary>中文版</summary>

## 问题

命令一直等不到回复时，返回给模型的文案来自 `sessionCommandEvidenceText`（[hosted-session-command-session.ts L85-L105](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/643bcaa07e4f01100e51e4778e03851d0451f9fe/packages/cli/src/serve/hosted-session-command-session.ts#L85-L105)，decision 14）。文案只看投递状态，不看命令类型。其中 `accepting` 和 `unknown` 两条是为看板写入写的：

> `accepting`：The command reached the leader, but its reply did not arrive in time; a write may have taken effect. End your turn and say so in your result; **read the board again before repeating the write.**
>
> `unknown`：The command's outcome is unknown; the leader may have run it and a write may have taken effect. **Read the board again before repeating the write.**

#13955 之后，`member_message`（成员用 `send_message` 发给另一成员或 `"*"`）走同一通道，拿到的也是这两条文案。对消息来说，这个建议有两处错误：

1. **看板无法告诉成员消息是否已送达。** `task_list` 返回的是看板和成员名单（含各成员 run 的状态），不包含消息。成员照着做也查不到任何东西。
2. **重发会导致重复。** 命令 id 由发送方 session、prompt 和 call id 派生（[L5566](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/643bcaa07e4f01100e51e4778e03851d0451f9fe/packages/cli/src/serve/hosted-workspace-tool-turn.ts#L5566)）；每个 `msgc_` id 是 `sha256(lead \0 commandId \0 position)`（[hosted-member-chain.ts L103](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/643bcaa07e4f01100e51e4778e03851d0451f9fe/packages/cli/src/serve/hosted-member-chain.ts#L103)）。所以在之后的 Turn 里重发会得到新的 id，lead 按 `msgc_` id 做的幂等检查拦不住。与此同时，lead 已提交的 `msgc_` 在 lead 恢复后仍会被投递。于是收件人会收到两份；正如 #14054 FG9 所说，*「重复的成员消息用户可见，且无法撤回」*。

## 证据（真实栈，#13955 验证）

环境是 Spring managed-agent-server（MySQL 8.4.7）、内嵌 Runtime Broker 和打包后的 Hosted Harness，只有模型是脚本模拟的。完整报告：https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13955#issuecomment-6139614564 。以下运行用的是 #13955 head `ce9306ed4c` 及其与 main 的试合并。

- **P3（不重启）。** 成员 `alice` 在 `bob`、`carol` 运行中发给 `"*"`，同时用 MySQL 触发器拒绝 lead 的 `session_command` 回执 INSERT。
  - lead 之后的写入全部返回 `503 session log writes stopped after an earlier failure`（#13413），relay 最终把命令判为 `unknown`。
  - 已提交的两条 `msgc_` 一直停在 `planned`。
  - 等满 2 分钟后，alice 的模型收到的原文是：*"The command reached the leader, but its reply did not arrive in time; a write may have taken effect. End your turn and say so in your result; read the board again before repeating the write."*
- **P7（同一触发器，之后杀掉并重启 Harness）。** 重跑时投递的就是这两个 `msgc_` id：`bob` 和 `carol` 各收到恰好一条。也就是说，已提交的消息在恢复后确实会送达，重发的那份会成为第二份。

第 2 点的重复是由上面的 id 派生方式推出来的，我没有端到端跑过：没有探针让 alice 先重发、再让 lead 恢复。

## 期望

`member_message` 超时后的文案不应该指向看板，并且应该让模型不要重发。例如：

- `accepting`：*"The message reached the leader, but its reply did not arrive in time; some recipients may already have it or get it later. Do not send it again; end your turn and say so in your result."*
- `unknown`：*"The message's outcome is unknown; some recipients may already have it or get it later. Do not send it again."*

`planned`、`rejected`、`cancelled` 三条用在消息上已经是对的。

## 修复提示（未验证）

- **每个调用点都拿得到命令类型。** 实时等待在生成命令 id 之前就算出了 `kind`（[L5557-L5564](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/643bcaa07e4f01100e51e4778e03851d0451f9fe/packages/cli/src/serve/hosted-workspace-tool-turn.ts#L5557-L5564)），并在 [L5772](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/643bcaa07e4f01100e51e4778e03851d0451f9fe/packages/cli/src/serve/hosted-workspace-tool-turn.ts#L5772) 返回文案；恢复路径的结算（[hosted-runtime-recovery.ts L1068](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/643bcaa07e4f01100e51e4778e03851d0451f9fe/packages/cli/src/serve/hosted-runtime-recovery.ts#L1068)）手里有 `run.toolName`。
- **三处文案要保持一致。** docstring 要求实时等待、恢复后的等待和被中断 Turn 的结算三处逐字相同，按类型区分后也要保持这一点。
- **`plan_submit` 也要看一下。** #13974（b3d）把 `plan_submit` 也加到了同一通道，它拿到的同样是看板措辞。这对计划提交是否合适，这里没有检查。

## 相关

- #13955：验证报告中的第 3 条发现。
- #13413：P3 中造成停滞的写库失败锁存问题。
- #14054：FG9 覆盖投递和成员消息重复。

</details>
