prs.title: fix(ci): distinguish missing logs from missing test results
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Makes main-branch CI failure reports distinguish unavailable evidence from a failure before tests ran. Reports show supplied log-file counts against recorded failed jobs and flag either direction of mismatch. Test-keyed recurrences refresh only marked machine coverage lines, preserving human notes that quote the visible text.

## Why it's needed

A missing log download, or output without a recognized failure identifier, cannot establish that tests never ran. The current assertion can send maintainers and the autofix worker toward an unsupported diagnosis. This addresses the log-availability finding in #11115 without changing issue matching or the workflow's job selection.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

With one failed job and no logs, expect `0 of 1` incomplete coverage, job/step names and the run link, without claiming that tests never ran. With an available log containing no recognized failure, expect diagnostic uncertainty to remain. With more logs than recorded jobs, expect a mismatch warning as well.

Record repeated test-keyed recurrences with an investigation note starting `- Job logs analyzed:`. Expect that note and adjacent prose to survive, one marked machine coverage line to remain, and all run records to be retained. Matching counts do not certify complete log contents or a complete failing-test list. Existing per-commit reports retain their original bodies.

An empty readable jobs file and a missing file both retain uncertainty: the report says the entries are empty or unavailable. A readable empty TSV can also result from a failed projection, so file readability alone is not treated as proof of zero failed jobs. A supplied zero-byte log still counts as one input file.

### Evidence (Before & After)

- Initial five regression checks failed before the original patch and passed afterward.
- The first two review regressions failed before their fix. The follow-up wording checks failed before their update; all nine related checks now pass. One explicitly marked case retains real analyze/plan subprocesses; the others reuse the existing in-process CLI helper. No mocks were added. Temporary mutations that ignore blank logs or disable the CLI entry both fail their respective regression checks.
- Workflow contract tests: 17 passed. Focused lint and formatting checks passed.
- Full build, typecheck and bundle passed at `0599d2e`; the subsequent follow-up changes reporting text, tests and documentation only, with focused tests, lint and formatting rerun.
- Complete helper suite on Windows: 56 passed, 4 failed, 4 skipped. Re-running the original HEAD gave 53 passed, 4 failed, 4 skipped, with the same four Flyway Windows path-encoding failures.
- Full monorepo preflight is not green: the earlier run reported workspace failures, including Windows symlink permissions and an IPC rejection. Those failures were not all baseline-verified. The previous hosted Linux unit-test run was cancelled at its one-hour limit, so it is not reported as passing.

### Tested on

Windows, Node.js 24.15.0 and pinned pnpm 11.24.0. Linux and macOS were not locally tested. Verification exercised the reporting helper, not a live failed download or a GitHub-hosted reporting run.

## AI assistance

Codex assisted with investigation, implementation and validation. Separate Codex agents reproduced and verified the review regressions and reviewed the update.

## Related Issue

Addresses the log-availability finding in #11115; the separate latency finding remains outside this PR.

## What this PR does

Adds the stage-F fault-gate letters FG8a (lost replies), FG8b (store failures), and FG8d (cancellation and routine/drain release split) to the managed-agent fault-gate suite, following the FG8e/FG8f slice in #14120. All of the work lives in the integration-test driver and the `HostedMonitorRunFaultGatesIT` letters; no production code changes. The gate makes "one physical process per dispatch, zero OS effects on rejected commits, and honest settlement for cancellation and drain" provable against a packaged Harness, a real MySQL/MariaDB instance, and JDBC ground truth.

## Why it's needed

 #13889 enabled `monitor_run` plus the `child_run` `shell` kind without a fault round. Issue #14163 keeps the remaining bucket: fault injection that must resolve through the original identity (never a second process), a rejected commit that must leave nothing behind (no dead rows, no ghost capture chain), and a cancellation model where routine release refuses while a drain actually stops the world. The design doc records the gate ledger, the assertion precedence chosen (physical/OS/store truth over wording bets), and one environmental discovery: on macOS the monitored Shell actor and the background monitor both reject any supervised spawn with `HookCommandIsolationUnavailableError`, because they need a delegated Linux cgroup v2 root on the runtime (`packages/cli/src/serve/managed-runtime-tool-executor.ts:1105/1331`). Ten of the fourteen cases are therefore only verifiable on Linux; the local runs cover every case whose settle point precedes physical start.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Build the packaged CLI first: `npm run build && npm run bundle` (the gate drives the packaged harness via `qwen serve --profile hosted-harness` on the bundled entrypoint).
2. Start a throw-away MariaDB (`--skip-grant-tables`) and run one cgroup-free case on macOS: `cd packages/sdk-java/managed-agent-server && JAVA_HOME=<jdk21> mvn -Phosted-monitor-run-gates failsafe:integration-test failsafe:verify -Dmysql.url=jdbc:mysql://127.0.0.1:11444/fg8abd -Dmysql.user=root -Dnode.executable="$(which node)" -Dqwen.fg8a.case=dispatch-reply`.
3. Expected vs observed: `Tests run: 1, Failures: 0`. The four cgroup-free cases were run one at a time and all went green locally: `dispatch-reply` (14.5 s), `invocation-commit` (14.5 s), `process-ledger-commit` (15.1 s), `cancel-before-start` (34.7 s). On Linux (`hosted-harness-mysql` lane), all fourteen cases should run with cgroup v2 enabled.
4. Also reproducible from logs: `/tmp/fg8a-seed4.log`, `/tmp/fg8b-inv-n3.log`, `/tmp/fg8b-process-ledger.log`, `/tmp/fg8d-cbs-2.log` each contain the `FG8_*_OK` terminal sentinel plus JDBC evidence (one physical process per dispatch; zero rows when the admission commit was rejected; `SETTLED/not_started` and zero OS effects when a spawn gets refused by cgroup).

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — test-only slice, no UI change.

- Before: `HostedMonitorRunFaultGatesIT` contained exactly the two letters from #14120 (`fg8e...`, `fg8f...`).
- After: the same class contains five letters (`fg8e`/`fg8f` plus new `fg8a`, `fg8b`, `fg8d`), and the driver gains lose-once / hold arms, broker identity capture, broker control-kind logs, store arms, child-cancel, and the routine/drain release maintenance routes.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ✅ tested |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested |
|  🐧 Linux  | ⚠️ not tested (expected CI lane) |

### Environment (optional)

Local: JDK 21 (`~/Install/jdk21`), Maven 3.9.11, Node from `~/.local/lib/qwen-code/node/bin/node`, bundled `dist/cli.js` from `npm run build && npm run bundle`.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: on non-Linux hosts the gate uses honest `start_failed/not_started` settlement wherever a physical spawn is refused by cgroup isolation. The letter asserts identity and OS-truth invariants that stay valid regardless of which one the runtime actually goes through; commentary on the class and in the design doc explains this.
- Not validated / out of scope: FG8c stays out pending the restart-behavior rewrite in #13986 (per the issue's sequencing constraint). The remaining ten cgroup-bound cases can only produce evidence on Linux.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none; driver/IT change only.
- The two-stage design document is linked in both English and Chinese below and is kept synchronized.
- A physical stop before physical start stays `start_failed`/`not_started_proven` and never manufactures an `exited` outcome — the IT documents this in both Settle projections, and the cgroup wall is documented in the English and Chinese versions of the design doc.

## Linked Issues

- See #14163 (FG8a/FG8b/FG8d slice)
- See #14054 (Stage F fault-gate umbrella)
- Preceding slice: #14120 (FG8e/FG8f)

prs.title: feat(serve): auto-remove completed sub-sessions after a configurable TTL
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds TTL-based auto-removal of completed sub-sessions in `qwen serve` (daemon mode). A new `serve.subSessionCompletionTtlHours` setting (integer, hours; default `24`; `0` keeps completed sub-sessions forever, i.e. today's behavior) controls how long a finished sub-session stays in the workspace session roster before the daemon removes it.

After a sub-session's turn reaches a terminal state (any stop reason except `timeout`, `incomplete`, `shutdown`), the sub-session launcher starts a per-session completion clock. A 5-minute sweep (unref'd, serialized, so it never keeps the process alive or re-enters) then removes expired sub-sessions the same way the existing launch-rollback cleanup does: `closeSession` (tolerating entries the bridge reaper already closed) plus `SessionService.removeSession` for the persisted transcript, so an expired sub-session is no longer continuable — consistent with how closed sessions are treated elsewhere (#7420). A revived sub-session (a new prompt after completion) restarts the clock from its latest activity instead of being removed, and running sub-sessions (`hasActivePrompt`) are never removed. Out-of-range or non-integer values produce a one-time warning and fall back to the built-in default, mirroring the existing `serve.maxConcurrentSubSessions*` handling.

## Why it's needed

Finished sub-sessions (`create_sub_session`, daemon/serve only) currently accumulate in the session roster for the lifetime of the daemon. The bridge reaper closes the live entry of an idle completed sub-session, but the persisted transcript keeps the thread listed in the Web Shell sidebar until the daemon is restarted or the parent session is closed. On long-running daemons this turns into dozens of dead threads under a single parent session with no way to prune them except a restart. This is the request from #14289: auto-removal of completed sub-sessions, terminal-state only, with revival resetting the timer.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Unit level: `cd packages/cli && pnpm vitest run src/serve/create-sub-session.test.ts src/serve/run-qwen-serve.test.ts src/config/settingsSchema.test.ts` — the new `sub-session completion TTL` block (7 fake-timer lifecycle tests: removal at exactly the TTL moment, `0` keeps forever, active prompt never removed, revival extends the clock, unobserved-then-reaped fallback, terminal dispatch failure, `stop()` clears the sweeper) plus `subSessionCompletionTtlMsFromSettings` (4 config-reader tests) and the schema pin test (default === runtime default, minimum 0).

Live: run `qwen serve` from this branch with `"serve": { "subSessionCompletionTtlHours": 1 }` in user settings, create a session and let its model spawn one trivial sub-session (`create_sub_session`, `completion: "sent"`). After the sub-session's turn finishes, wait ~65 minutes: the daemon logs `qwen serve: removed completed sub-session <id> from the roster (completion TTL 60min expired)`, the transcript `.jsonl` is gone from `~/.qwen/projects/<slug>/chats/`, and `GET /workspace/<id>/sessions` no longer lists the thread.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before (0.25.1, no such setting exists — the roster only shrinks on daemon restart or parent close):

- Live daemon (0.25.1) with 10 completed sub-sessions under one parent session; transcripts on disk, last activity spread over ~19 hours, all still listed:
  ```
  10-14 17:39  b71c0254-… (410 KB)   10-14 17:51  f728b509-… (727 KB)
  10-14 18:24  c19070d1-… (462 KB)   10-14 20:37  a1fa001e-… (3335 KB)
  10-15 00:55  040484ea-… (1403 KB)  10-15 00:55  27d92160-… (735 KB)
  10-15 00:55  48fa030b-… (1927 KB)  10-15 02:40  56aefda8-… (3133 KB)
  10-15 12:12  bbe2dda6-… (969 KB)   10-15 12:35  ba085532-… (1785 KB)
  ```
  (each file's first record: `type: system, subtype: parent_session` → sub-session of the parent; daemon uptime 14h51m at capture)

After (this branch) — the new `sub-session completion TTL` suite drives the real completion sweeper through a fake-bridge daemon and asserts exactly the behavior this diff adds: a terminal sub-session is removed from the roster and its persisted transcript deleted at precisely the TTL moment; `0` keeps it forever; an active prompt is never removed; a revival restarts the clock from the latest activity; an already-reaped entry is tolerated. This is the same `closeSession` + `SessionService.removeSession` path a live `qwen serve` run exercises (repro steps above).

Machine evidence — the 3 touched test files, per platform:

```
🐧 Linux   — Docker node:22-bookworm, fresh container, pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
  ✓ settingsSchema.test.ts (63)   ✓ create-sub-session.test.ts (62)   ✓ run-qwen-serve.test.ts (503)
  Tests  628 passed (628)          tsc --noEmit  clean

🍏 macOS   — host, Apple Silicon, node 26.5.0, pnpm 12.10.1
  ✓ settingsSchema.test.ts (63)   ✓ create-sub-session.test.ts (62)   run-qwen-serve.test.ts (503, 5 failed)
  Tests  623 passed | 5 failed (628)   tsc --noEmit  clean
  the 5 = pre-existing provider-HTTP-installer/voice cluster, reproduced identically on base 476f624b53 (outside this diff)

🪟 Windows — UTM Win11 ARM, WinOnArm x64, node 22.23.3, pnpm 11.24.0
  ✓ settingsSchema.test.ts (63)   ✓ create-sub-session.test.ts (62)   run-qwen-serve.test.ts (503, 5 failed)
  Tests  623 passed | 5 failed (628)   tsc --noEmit  clean
  the 5 = same pre-existing provider-HTTP-installer cluster (chat/image/voice, "expected 500 to be 200"), outside this diff

All 7 sub-session completion TTL lifecycle tests and all 4 subSessionCompletionTtlMsFromSettings config-reader tests pass on all 3 platforms; every failure above is in the provider-HTTP-installer cluster, none in the touched TTL code.
```

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ✅ |
| 🪟 Windows | ✅ |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ |

### Environment

macOS 26 (Apple Silicon), node 26.5.0 (homebrew), `pnpm 12.10.1`; Linux: Docker `node:22-bookworm` (fresh container, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`); Windows: UTM Win11 ARM (WinOnArm x64 emulation), node 22.23.3 + `pnpm 11.24.0`. On the macOS and Windows hosts, `run-qwen-serve.test.ts` shows the same 5 failures in the provider-HTTP-installer/voice cluster (chat/image/voice, "expected 500 to be 200") — reproduced identically on base `476f624b53` in the same environments (pre-existing, outside this diff; Linux, which lacks the host's provider/voice environment, is fully green).

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: default behavior change — completed sub-sessions are now removed 24h after completion by default; set `serve.subSessionCompletionTtlHours: 0` to restore the previous keep-forever behavior. Removal is destructive by design (the issue asks for the sub-session to become "not continuable"); it reuses the exact cleanup path already run on launch rollback, so the failure modes are identical to the existing one (transcript removal is best-effort and non-fatal; a `SessionNotFoundError` from `closeSession` on an already-reaped entry is expected and tolerated).
- Not validated / out of scope: no live Windows e2e daemon run (unit/typecheck only on the UTM VM); the standalone session path shares the terminal-marking code, but removal for ids without a bridge entry is a harmless no-op (covered by unit tests).
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. New setting with a safe default; `0` is an explicit opt-out to current behavior.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #14289

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做什么

为 `qwen serve`（守护进程模式）中的已完成子会话添加基于 TTL 的自动移除。新增 `serve.subSessionCompletionTtlHours` 设置（整数，单位小时；默认 `24`；`0` 表示永久保留已完成的子会话，即当前行为），控制一个已完成的子会话在被守护进程移除前在工作区会话名册中保留多久。

当子会话的一轮达到终态（除 `timeout`、`incomplete`、`shutdown` 以外的任何停止原因）时，子会话启动器为该会话启动一个完成计时器。一个 5 分钟一次的扫描（unref、串行化，既不会阻止进程退出也不会重入）随后移除过期的子会话，方式与现有的启动回滚清理完全一致：`closeSession`（容忍桥接收割器已关闭的条目）加上 `SessionService.removeSession` 删除持久化转录，使过期的子会话不再可继续——与其他地方对已关闭会话的处理一致（#7420）。被唤醒的子会话（完成后又收到新提示）会从最近一次活动重新开始计时而不是被移除；正在运行的子会话（`hasActivePrompt`）永不被移除。越界或非整数的值会产生一次性警告并回退到内置默认值，与现有 `serve.maxConcurrentSubSessions*` 的处理方式一致。

## 为什么需要

已完成的子会话（`create_sub_session`，仅守护进程/serve 模式）目前会在守护进程存活期间不断堆积在会话名册中。桥接收割器会关闭空闲已完成子会话的实时条目，但持久化的转录会让该线程一直显示在 Web Shell 侧边栏中，直到守护进程重启或父会话关闭。在长期运行的守护进程中，单个父会话下会堆积几十个死线程，除了重启没有任何清理手段。这正是 #14289 的需求：自动移除已完成的子会话，仅限终态，唤醒时重置计时器。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

单元测试：`cd packages/cli && pnpm vitest run src/serve/create-sub-session.test.ts src/serve/run-qwen-serve.test.ts src/config/settingsSchema.test.ts`——新增的 `sub-session completion TTL` 测试块（7 个 fake-timer 生命周期测试：恰好 TTL 时刻移除、`0` 永久保留、活动提示永不移除、唤醒延长计时、未观察到后被收割的兜底、终态派发失败、`stop()` 清理扫描器）加上 `subSessionCompletionTtlMsFromSettings`（4 个配置读取测试）和模式固定测试（默认值 === 运行时默认值，最小值 0）。

实测：用本分支运行 `qwen serve`，用户配置中设置 `"serve": { "subSessionCompletionTtlHours": 1 }`，创建一个会话并让其模型生成一个平凡子会话（`create_sub_session`，`completion: "sent"`）。子会话一轮结束后等待约 65 分钟：守护进程输出 `qwen serve: removed completed sub-session <id> from the roster (completion TTL 60min expired)`，转录 `.jsonl` 从 `~/.qwen/projects/<slug>/chats/` 消失，`GET /workspace/<id>/sessions` 不再列出该线程。

### 证据（之前与之后）

之前（0.25.1，不存在该设置——名册只在守护进程重启或父会话关闭时缩小）：

- 实时守护进程（0.25.1）中单个父会话下有 10 个已完成子会话；转录在磁盘上，最后活动时间跨越约 19 小时，全部仍在名册中：
  ```
  10-14 17:39  b71c0254-… (410 KB)   10-14 17:51  f728b509-… (727 KB)
  10-14 18:24  c19070d1-… (462 KB)   10-14 20:37  a1fa001e-… (3335 KB)
  10-15 00:55  040484ea-… (1403 KB)  10-15 00:55  27d92160-… (735 KB)
  10-15 00:55  48fa030b-… (1927 KB)  10-15 02:40  56aefda8-… (3133 KB)
  10-15 12:12  bbe2dda6-… (969 KB)   10-15 12:35  ba085532-… (1785 KB)
  ```
  （每个文件的首条记录：`type: system, subtype: parent_session` → 父会话的子会话；采集时守护进程已运行 14 小时 51 分）

之后（本分支）——新增的 `sub-session completion TTL` 测试套件通过一个假桥接守护进程驱动真实的完成清扫器，并精确断言本 diff 新增的行为：终态子会话在 TTL 精确时刻从名册中移除、其持久化转录被删除；`0` 永久保留；活动提示永不被移除；唤醒后计时从最近一次活动重新开始；已被收割的条目被容忍。这与实时 `qwen serve` 运行所执行的同一条 `closeSession` + `SessionService.removeSession` 路径一致（复现步骤见上）。

机器证据——所触及的 3 个测试文件，按平台：

```

  ✓ settingsSchema.test.ts (63)   ✓ create-sub-session.test.ts (62)   ✓ run-qwen-serve.test.ts (503)
  Tests  628 passed (628)          tsc --noEmit  干净

🍏 macOS   — 主机，Apple Silicon，node 26.5.0，pnpm 12.10.1
  ✓ settingsSchema.test.ts (63)   ✓ create-sub-session.test.ts (62)   run-qwen-serve.test.ts (503，5 个失败)
  Tests  623 passed | 5 failed (628)   tsc --noEmit  干净
  这 5 个 = provider-HTTP-installer/voice 测试簇的既有问题，在基线 476f624b53 上完全复现（不在本 diff 范围内）

🪟 Windows — UTM Win11 ARM，WinOnArm x64 模拟，node 22.23.3，pnpm 11.24.0
  ✓ settingsSchema.test.ts (63)   ✓ create-sub-session.test.ts (62)   run-qwen-serve.test.ts (503，5 个失败)
  Tests  623 passed | 5 failed (628)   tsc --noEmit  干净
  这 5 个 = 同一 provider-HTTP-installer 簇的既有问题（chat/image/voice，"expected 500 to be 200"），不在本 diff 范围内

7 个 sub-session completion TTL 生命周期测试和 4 个 subSessionCompletionTtlMsFromSettings 配置读取测试在全部 3 个平台均通过；上述所有失败都在 provider-HTTP-installer 测试簇中，没有一个触及本 diff 的 TTL 代码。
```

### 测试平台

|     系统     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ✅ |
| 🪟 Windows | ✅ |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ |

### 环境

macOS 26（Apple Silicon），node 26.5.0（homebrew），`pnpm 12.10.1`；Linux：Docker `node:22-bookworm`（全新容器，`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`）；Windows：UTM Win11 ARM（WinOnArm x64 模拟），node 22.23.3 + `pnpm 11.24.0`。macOS 和 Windows 主机上 `run-qwen-serve.test.ts` 在 provider-HTTP-installer/voice 测试簇（chat/image/voice，"expected 500 to be 200"）有相同的 5 个失败——在各自同一环境中于基线 `476f624b53` 上完全复现（既有问题，不在本 diff 范围内；Linux 没有宿主的 provider/voice 环境，全绿）。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或权衡：默认行为变更——已完成的子会话默认在完成 24 小时后被移除；设置 `serve.subSessionCompletionTtlHours: 0` 可恢复此前的永久保留行为。移除是破坏性的，这是设计如此（issue 要求子会话变为「不可继续」）；它复用在启动回滚时已经运行的确切清理路径，因此失效模式与现有一致（转录删除是尽力而为且非致命的；`closeSession` 对已被收割条目返回的 `SessionNotFoundError` 是预期且被容忍的）。
- 未验证/范围外：无 Windows 实测守护进程 e2e（在 UTM VM 上仅单元/类型检查）；standalone 会话路径共享终态标记代码，但对没有桥接条目的 id，移除是无害的空操作（有单元测试覆盖）。
- 破坏性变更/迁移说明：无。新增带安全默认值的设置；`0` 是显式选择当前行为的开关。

## 关联 Issue

Fixes #14289

</details>

prs.title: feat(web-shell): add file creation and confirmed folder deletion
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds **New file** and **New folder** to the Files toolbar and folder menus. Toolbar actions create at the selected workspace root; folder menus create inside that folder. The name dialog shows the destination, prevents accidental replacement, and keeps failures available for correction or retry.

Adds **Delete** to folder menus with a second confirmation that names the folder and warns that it and all its contents will be permanently deleted. Cancel is initially focused. Successful deletion removes the subtree and its active descendant preview while preserving unrelated expansion and filtering. Regular-file deletion remains in #14158.

Uses `sticky-note-plus` for New file and `rotate-cw` for Refresh, and horizontally centers the initial Files loading label. Creation and folder deletion are authenticated and limited to the selected trusted local workspace, with no primary-workspace fallback.

The review follow-up also keeps workspace mutations out of the read-only transcript bundle without raising its size ceiling, restores visible focus after deletion, revalidates new folders on first expansion, discards stale state after same-path folder recreation, and aligns directory error/audit metadata and protocol documentation.

## Why it's needed

Files already supports browsing, previews and uploads, but creating empty files and folders and removing an unwanted folder currently requires another tool. These actions keep routine workspace file management in the tree and make destructive operations explicit.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Open Files in a trusted local workspace. Use the toolbar to create an empty file and folder; both should appear at the workspace root even when another entry is selected. The icons should match the choices above.
2. Hover a folder and open its trailing menu, or right-click it. New file and New folder should show that folder as the destination and create there. Invalid names and existing entries must not overwrite data. Cancel must send no mutation; failures should remain retryable.
3. Choose Delete on a nonempty folder. Expect the relative path, a warning covering all contents and irreversible deletion, and initial focus on Cancel. Cancel or Escape must leave the directory intact. Confirming should remove the entire subtree and close its active descendant preview while preserving other expanded folders. Pending actions must prevent cancellation and duplicate submissions; failures must remain visible for retry. While a file-tree upload is active, deletion confirmation must wait for it to finish. New drops must be rejected while deletion is pending.
4. Verify creation and folder deletion in a secondary workspace preserve same-named primary entries. Roots, escaping paths and final symlinks must be rejected; links within a deleted subtree must not remove their outside targets. SSH workspaces and missing capabilities must not expose unsupported actions.
5. On a cold first opening, the loading label should be horizontally centered. Refresh should still reload the listing. A late listing must not resurrect a deleted subtree or hide a newly created entry. A newly created folder should read its contents on first expansion; successfully recreating an externally removed folder at the same path should clear its old subtree and descendant preview. Successful deletion should restore focus to a surviving file row. With no directory capabilities, hovering a folder should not expose an inert Options button.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before, the Files toolbar offered Refresh and folder menus did not offer these management actions. After, the toolbar and folder menus support creation, and folders have confirmed recursive deletion. No unmodified latest-main browser baseline was captured; the installed global CLI 0.22.0 lacks Files.

These are actual browser E2E captures using a **simulated daemon**, visually inspected after implementation. They establish UI states, not actual disk or Git operations. Creation and recursive deletion were verified separately against a real bundled daemon with isolated temporary workspaces.

| Root creation actions and completed tree | Create inside a folder |
| --- | --- |
| ![Toolbar and new entries](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ytahdn/qwen-code/c7ff6e1eb134ea0e7041a3d7f6dc21b90a0f15e9/web-shell-file-create/toolbar.png) | ![Folder creation dialog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ytahdn/qwen-code/c7ff6e1eb134ea0e7041a3d7f6dc21b90a0f15e9/web-shell-file-create/create-dialog.png) |

| Irreversible folder-deletion confirmation | Horizontally centered initial loading |
| --- | --- |
| ![Folder deletion confirmation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ytahdn/qwen-code/c7ff6e1eb134ea0e7041a3d7f6dc21b90a0f15e9/web-shell-file-create/folder-delete-confirmation.png) | ![Centered loading](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ytahdn/qwen-code/c7ff6e1eb134ea0e7041a3d7f6dc21b90a0f15e9/web-shell-file-create/loading-centered.png) |

Creation and deletion coexist with main's existing uploads. Deletion confirmation waits for uploads to finish; new drops are rejected during deletion. The capture below uses a simulated daemon.

![Create/upload/delete coordination](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ytahdn/qwen-code/c7ff6e1eb134ea0e7041a3d7f6dc21b90a0f15e9/web-shell-file-create/create-upload-delete.png)

Images are pinned to an immutable commit on a separate fork assets branch and are not part of the implementation branch.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :---: | :---: |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ tested |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ not tested |

### Environment (optional)

Node.js 22.14.0, Playwright Chromium with a simulated daemon for browser tests, and a real bundled daemon with isolated primary, secondary and untrusted fixture workspaces for disk assertions. Build, typecheck, bundle, lint/format, 395 CLI tests, 138 artifact-panel tests, 3 file-browser unit tests, 34 build-artifact tests, 18 reference-contract tests, 5 SDK tests, 43 Files browser tests, 23 real-daemon creation cases and 20 real-daemon folder-deletion cases passed. A separate comment contains the E2E report.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: folder deletion is permanent and recursive failures may leave partial deletion. Portable path-based filesystem mutations retain the existing limitation around an external process replacing a parent directory concurrently.
- Not validated / out of scope: SSH creation/deletion, Windows/Linux execution, injected concurrent external filesystem replacement, regular-file deletion in this change, and a latest-main browser baseline.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. Actions require the advertised capabilities and an exact trusted local workspace owner; older or unsupported daemons retain browsing behavior.
- Synchronized design: [English](docs/design/web-shell-file-create.md) · [简体中文](docs/design/web-shell-file-create.zh-CN.md).

## Linked Issues

Related: #14158 provides regular-file deletion; this change adds folder deletion separately.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 的改动

在 Files 顶部和文件夹菜单中添加**新建文件**、**新建文件夹**。顶部操作始终作用于选定工作区的根目录；文件夹菜单作用于该文件夹。名称弹窗显示创建位置，禁止意外覆盖，并保留失败提示供修改或重试。

在文件夹菜单中添加**删除**，二次确认显示目标文件夹，并明确提示文件夹及全部内容将永久删除且不可恢复，默认聚焦取消。成功后移除子树及其中的当前预览，保留其他目录的展开和筛选。普通文件删除仍由 #14158 提供。

新建文件使用 `sticky-note-plus`，刷新使用 `rotate-cw`，首次打开 Files 的加载提示水平居中。新建和文件夹删除经过鉴权，仅作用于选定的可信本地工作区，禁止回退主工作区。

Review 后续修复还在不提高体积上限的前提下从只读 transcript 包移除工作区变更动作，恢复删除后的可见行焦点，新建文件夹首次展开时重新读取，同路径重建时清理旧状态，并补齐目录错误/审计元数据及协议文档。

## 为什么需要

Files 已支持浏览、预览和上传，但创建空文件和文件夹、删除不需要的文件夹仍需借助其他工具。本次将常用文件管理操作放入目录树，并让破坏性操作有明确确认。

## 评审者验证计划

### 如何验证

1. 在可信本地工作区打开 Files，通过顶部按钮创建空文件和文件夹。即使已选中其他条目，也应创建在工作区根目录。图标应与上述选择一致。
2. 悬停文件夹打开行尾菜单，或右键该文件夹。新建文件和新建文件夹应显示该目录为创建位置，并创建在其中。非法名称和已有条目不能覆盖数据；取消不发送变更，失败应能重试。
3. 对非空文件夹选择删除。应显示相对路径、全部内容不可恢复的警告，并默认聚焦取消。取消或 Escape 应保留目录；确认后删除整棵子树并关闭其中当前预览，其他展开目录保持展开。请求中禁止取消和重复提交，失败提示保留供重试。文件树上传进行中时，删除确认应等待上传完成；删除处理中拒绝新的文件拖放。
4. 在次工作区创建及删除文件夹时，主工作区同名条目应保持完整。根目录、越界路径、末级符号链接必须拒绝；被删除子树中的链接不能删除其外部目标。SSH 工作区和缺少必要能力的 daemon 不应显示不支持的操作。
5. 冷启动首次打开时，加载提示应水平居中，刷新仍能重载列表。迟到的列表不能使已删除子树重现，也不能隐藏新建条目。新建文件夹首次展开应读取实际内容；外部删除后同路径重建成功应清理旧子树和后代预览。成功删除后焦点应恢复到仍存在的文件行。没有目录能力时，悬停文件夹不应显示无效的 Options 按钮。

### 证据（改动前后）

改动前，Files 顶部只有刷新，文件夹菜单没有这些管理操作。改动后，顶部和文件夹菜单支持创建，文件夹支持二次确认递归删除。未捕获未修改的最新 main 浏览器基线；全局安装的 CLI 0.22.0 没有 Files。

以下为使用**模拟 daemon** 的实际浏览器 E2E 截图，已在实现后目视检查。截图仅证明 UI 状态，不证明实际磁盘或 Git 操作。创建及递归删除另由真实打包 daemon 和隔离临时工作区验证。

| 根目录创建操作及完成后的文件树 | 在文件夹内创建 |
| --- | --- |
| ![顶部操作与新建条目](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ytahdn/qwen-code/c7ff6e1eb134ea0e7041a3d7f6dc21b90a0f15e9/web-shell-file-create/toolbar.png) | ![文件夹内创建弹窗](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ytahdn/qwen-code/c7ff6e1eb134ea0e7041a3d7f6dc21b90a0f15e9/web-shell-file-create/create-dialog.png) |

| 文件夹删除不可恢复确认 | 首次加载提示水平居中 |
| --- | --- |
| ![文件夹删除确认](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ytahdn/qwen-code/c7ff6e1eb134ea0e7041a3d7f6dc21b90a0f15e9/web-shell-file-create/folder-delete-confirmation.png) | ![加载提示居中](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ytahdn/qwen-code/c7ff6e1eb134ea0e7041a3d7f6dc21b90a0f15e9/web-shell-file-create/loading-centered.png) |

新建和删除与 main 已有上传共存：删除确认等待上传完成，删除处理中拒绝新拖放。下图使用模拟 daemon。

![新建/上传/删除协调](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ytahdn/qwen-code/c7ff6e1eb134ea0e7041a3d7f6dc21b90a0f15e9/web-shell-file-create/create-upload-delete.png)

图片固定到 fork 独立素材分支的不可变 commit，不进入实现分支。

### 测试平台

| 系统 | 状态 |
| :---: | :---: |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ 已测试 |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ 未测试 |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ 未测试 |

### 环境

Node.js 22.14.0；浏览器测试使用 Playwright Chromium 和模拟 daemon；磁盘断言使用真实打包 daemon，主、次及不可信工作区均为隔离测试目录。构建、类型检查、打包、lint/格式、395 项 CLI 测试、138 项 artifact 面板测试、3 项文件树单元测试、34 项构建产物测试、18 项文档契约测试、5 项 SDK 测试、43 项 Files 浏览器测试、23 项真实 daemon 创建用例和 20 项真实 daemon 文件夹删除用例均通过。E2E 报告另附评论。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：文件夹永久删除，递归删除失败可能已经移除部分内容。可移植路径变更沿用外部进程并发替换父目录的既有局限。
- 未验证或范围外：SSH 创建/删除、Windows/Linux 运行、注入外部并发文件系统替换、本次变更中的普通文件删除，以及最新 main 浏览器基线。
- 兼容性与迁移：无破坏性变更。操作要求已公布能力和准确的可信本地工作区所有者，旧版或不支持的 daemon 仍保留浏览行为。
- 同步设计：[English](docs/design/web-shell-file-create.md) · [简体中文](docs/design/web-shell-file-create.zh-CN.md)。

相关：#14158 提供普通文件删除，本次单独添加文件夹删除。

prs.title: feat(hooks): add FileChanged notifications for local sessions
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds `FileChanged` notifications for local, non-managed sessions. Hooks can register literal cwd filenames or absolute files and recursive directories through successful synchronous `SessionStart` and `FileChanged` output. Notifications identify the listening session, absolute path and `add`, `change` or `unlink`, including changes made by external processes.

Subscriptions follow session rotation, skill hook registration/removal and cwd changes. Static registrations exclude regex fragments and directories; initially absent sibling files and deeply missing roots are discovered without traversing unrelated subdirectories, and deleted/recreated roots recover. Reconfiguration retains already queued events for retained roots, and watcher errors permit subsequent registration retries. ACP bootstrap and MCP reconnect temporary configs do not start host subscriptions. Managed execution engines, remote environments and shell sandbox workers remain excluded. Late reload/skill registration after session rotation rebinds the current owner, while ended sessions and stale asynchronous results remain disarmed.

CI repairs retain behavior assertions and bundle-size limits, correct native-storage fixtures and allow the Hosted suite's shared JVM to finish all test classes. The shared fork now has 2,400 seconds, its wrapped step 50 minutes and its job 295 minutes to cover main's additional capped gates; individual test deadlines and completeness guards remain enforced. Main's current CI policy and lint gate are incorporated. The extension commit-boundary test now awaits its actual durable-commit signal and completes in-flight work before fixture cleanup; a controlled 1,500 ms disk delay reproduces the old failure and passes after the repair.

## Why it's needed

Memory integrations need notifications from editors, shells and other writers, including directories outside cwd and multiple accessible workspaces. This provides a general filesystem event instead of a memory-specific API. Integrators register their actual directories and route by absolute path; initial reconciliation and offline synchronization remain their responsibility.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- Configure `.env|.envrc` when both files are absent. Create either first, atomically replace one and delete it; expect corresponding notifications. Unrelated cwd subdirectories must remain silent.
- Register absolute files or a directory outside cwd during SessionStart. Expect nested future additions, changes and deletions, including initially missing sibling files and deeply missing roots. Delete a registered root, wait briefly and recreate it; expect later child additions. Replacing or clearing the dynamic list retains static registrations.
- Change cwd: static registrations move to the new directory, old static paths stop notifying and explicit absolute dynamic roots remain active.
- Reconfigure while a hook runs: previously queued events under retained roots are delivered, removed-root events are discarded. A subsequent refresh after a watcher error can retry the same paths. Shutdown cancels intake and pending work, including registration still awaiting readiness.
- Rotate without a SessionStart hook, then reload or register a skill hook; expect current-session notifications. Initialize ACP bootstrap or MCP reconnect; expect no host watcher. Managed, remote and sandbox configurations must not observe the host.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Current repair validation: on `1989259fe6`, full build, workspace/integration typecheck, full CI lint and bundle passed. Core 2,234, CLI/ACP/MCP 1,542, WebShell artifact/i18n 41 and workflow consumers 368 tests passed: **4,185 total**, plus 10 existing platform skips. Both Server and Broker Checkstyle passed with zero violations on Java 21 / Maven 3.9.11; seven related Java files passed syntax parsing. Full Maven compilation/verify, MySQL and full Hosted acceptance were not executed locally. The committed tree exactly matches the tested tree after commit hooks.

Fresh Darwin integration runs the compiled modules with real filesystem writes and actual hook commands: a deeply missing root discovers its first file without a reload; deletion and recreation after a 250 ms gap restores notifications; unrelated ancestor siblings stay silent; late registration after empty-hook SessionEnd/rotation runs under the replacement session; bootstrap opt-out remains silent. MCP reconnect is verified through all 38 actual-handler caller-contract tests, not a full real-server reconnect E2E. Earlier native and CI failure history remains historical in the [validation report](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13969#issuecomment-6184202393).

CI: the preceding `66f72e1be6` product checks all passed. `1989259fe6` incorporates main `8bd79c9192`, including Server/Broker consolidation, and fixes all four new R2 Critical findings. Current remote status is reported in the follow-up comment; pending or skipped checks are not passes. SDK Java runs daily or manually, so fresh full Hosted acceptance remains outstanding. Formal review remains `CHANGES_REQUESTED` pending reassessment; source fixes do not resolve reviewer threads or constitute approval.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :--: | :-- |
| 🍏 macOS | Build, typecheck, bundle, scoped tests and compiled-module native command integration |
| 🪟 Windows | Not tested locally |
| 🐧 Linux | New remote CI reported separately; full Hosted suite not rerun locally |

### Environment

macOS, Node 24.19.0, pinned pnpm and an isolated worktree. Java style checks use an isolated Linux container with Java 21 and the workflow-pinned Maven 3.9.11.

## Risk & Scope

- Notifications are best effort and may be coalesced, duplicated or missed during downtime and reconfiguration. Handlers must avoid self-trigger loops.
- Remote/hosted event producers, durable synchronization, symlink traversal and memory toggles are outside this change. Discovery can enumerate entries in the nearest existing ancestor directory. Deferred review Suggestions, including remaining ancestor-scan cost, are recorded separately in the PR thread.
- The event is additive. Dynamic registrations use the last valid explicit list and are reset with session ownership.

Design: [English](https://github.com/samuelhsin/qwen-code/blob/codex/file-changed-hook/docs/design/file-changed-hooks.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/samuelhsin/qwen-code/blob/codex/file-changed-hook/docs/design/file-changed-hooks.zh-CN.md).

## Linked Issues

Refs #12558. Supersedes #12561 without closing the separate memory-toggle requirement.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

为本地非托管会话添加 `FileChanged` 通知。Hook 可通过 cwd 字面文件名，或成功的同步 `SessionStart`／`FileChanged` 输出注册绝对文件及递归目录。通知包含监听会话、绝对路径和 `add/change/unlink`，覆盖外部进程的修改。

订阅跟随会话轮换、skill hook 注册／移除及 cwd 迁移。静态注册排除正则片段和目录，在不遍历无关子目录的前提下发现多个初始缺失文件及多层缺失根，根删除重建后可恢复。重配置保留仍订阅路径的已入队事件；watcher 报错后可由后续注册重试。ACP bootstrap 和 MCP reconnect 临时配置不创建宿主订阅；managed engine、远程环境和 shell sandbox worker 继续排除。会话轮换后的延迟重载／skill 注册绑定到当前会话，已结束会话和过期异步结果仍被隔离。

CI 修复保留行为断言和包大小限制，修正原生存储测试 fixture，并让 Hosted 共享 JVM 完成所有测试类。共享 fork 为 2400 秒，封装步骤 50 分钟，job 295 分钟，以覆盖主干新增的有界 gate；单项超时和完整性检查仍执行。已同步主干现行 CI 策略及 lint gate。扩展提交边界测试改为等待真实持久提交信号，并在清理 fixture 前结束在途提交；受控 1500 毫秒磁盘延迟可复现旧失败，修复后通过。

Memory 业务需要来自编辑器、shell 等写入者的通知，包括 cwd 外及多个可访问 workspace 的目录。本变更提供通用文件系统事件，业务注册实际目录并按绝对路径分发，启动对账和离线同步仍由业务负责。

审查验证：两文件均不存在时配置 `.env|.envrc`，分别创建、原子替换及删除，应收到对应通知，无关子目录保持静默；通过 SessionStart 注册 cwd 外的绝对文件或目录，未来嵌套文件、多个缺失文件和多层缺失根应生效；删除根并稍候重建后仍可收到新增事件，替换／清空动态列表仍保留静态注册；迁移 cwd 后静态路径迁移、旧路径停止通知、绝对动态根保留；hook 运行期间重配置，保留根的已入队事件继续投递、移除根的事件丢弃，watcher 错误后可重试相同路径，关闭可取消仍在等待 ready 的注册；会话轮换、skill 注册／移除及 ACP bootstrap 应保持正确所有权和订阅边界，managed／远程／sandbox 不监听宿主。

本轮验证：`1989259fe6` 的完整构建、workspace／integration 类型检查、完整 CI lint 和 bundle 均通过。Core 2234、CLI／ACP／MCP 1542、WebShell 41、工作流消费者 368 项通过，合计 **4185 项**；另有 10 项现有平台条件跳过。Java 21／Maven 3.9.11 的 Server 和 Broker Checkstyle 均零违规，七个相关 Java 文件通过语法解析。完整 Maven 编译／verify、MySQL 和完整 Hosted 验收未在本地执行。提交 hook 后的代码树与测试时完全一致。

本轮 Darwin 编译模块集成验证使用真实文件写入和真实 hook 命令：多层缺失根无需重载即可发现首个文件，根删除 250 毫秒后重建仍可通知，无关祖先同级文件保持静默，空 hook 的 SessionEnd／轮换后延迟注册由新会话执行，bootstrap 禁用监听保持静默。MCP reconnect 通过全部 38 项真实 handler 调用契约测试，未声称完成真实服务重连 E2E。[既有验证报告](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13969#issuecomment-6184202393)保留历史证据。

CI：上一提交 `66f72e1be6` 的产品检查全部通过。`1989259fe6` 已同步主干 `8bd79c9192`（含 Server／Broker 目录合并）并修复新增四项 R2 Critical。新检查状态见后续报告，待运行和跳过项不计为通过。SDK Java 为每日／手动策略，完整 Hosted 验收仍待验证。正式 review 仍为 `CHANGES_REQUESTED`，源码修复不等于解决审查线程或获得批准。

本地环境为 macOS／Node 24.19.0／固定 pnpm，使用隔离 worktree；Java 风格检查使用独立 Linux 容器、Java 21 和工作流固定的 Maven 3.9.11。macOS 本轮已验证构建、类型、bundle 及针对性测试；包含本轮编译模块的真实 hook 命令验证；MCP 重连为调用契约验证；Windows 未本地验证，Linux 新 CI 单列，完整 Hosted 未在本地重跑。

通知为尽力投递，停机和重配置期间可能合并、重复或遗漏；处理器须避免自触发。远程／托管事件生产、持久同步、符号链接遍历及 memory 开关不在本次范围。发现过程可能枚举最近已存在祖先目录的条目；其剩余扫描成本等延期 Suggestions 已在 PR 线程逐项记录。事件为增量能力，动态注册采用最后一个有效显式列表，并随会话所有权重置。中英文设计链接如上。

Refs #12558；替代 #12561，不关闭独立 memory 开关需求。

</details>

<!-- qwen-release-notes:v1 -->

## Highlights

_See the complete change list below._

## Breaking Changes

No known breaking changes.

## Complete Change List

### Features

- feat(managed-agent): H4e-b2 the lead's mailbox over Session messages ([#13892](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13892)) by @wenshao
- A new private extension imports Vitest 3.2 JSON reports and exposes failures, errors, counts, and diagnostics through MCP tools with search and pagination. ([#13854](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13854)) by @qqqys
- Opt-in headless Mods now support TypeScript authoring, relative imports, typed non-secret configuration, and dependency validation before startup. ([#13890](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13890)) by @qqqys
- Adds a default-off option allowing authorized public REST and WebShell sessions to use foreground Shell with mandatory approval. ([#13674](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13674)) by @doudouOUC
- feat(managed-agent): Introduce the EventTransport seam behind the after-commit publisher ([#13909](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13909)) by @wenshao
- feat(managed-agent): Stop Hosted team members with request_shutdown (H4e-b3a) ([#13923](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13923)) by @wenshao
- Opt-in headless Mod runtime gains ordered middleware dispatch, command interception, and bounded failure recovery without resetting module state. ([#13915](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13915)) by @qqqys
- Adds a Test Failure Explorer app that lets users browse, search, page through, and copy analysis requests for up to 20 selected test failures. ([#13916](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13916)) by @qqqys
- Enables H3 Monitor and background Shell capabilities, allowing background runs to outlive their turn and output artifacts. ([#13889](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13889)) by @wenshao
- Adds a Java mirror of the managed-event-envelope contract with derivation, validation, deduplication, and fixture tests, without changing runtime behavior. ([#13940](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13940)) by @wenshao
- Adds a selection menu to completed Web Shell assistant replies with Copy plain text and Copy Markdown actions while preserving selected formatting. ([#13833](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13833)) by @ytahdn
- Adds Web Shell task reminders for tool approval or AskUserQuestion answers, with notification controls, authorization prompts, and in-panel help. ([#13832](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13832)) by @ytahdn
- Enables opt-in Mods in trusted headless main sessions to intercept tool calls, rewrite arguments, refuse calls, return synthetic results, and check permissions. ([#13950](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13950)) by @qqqys

## Highlights

The bundled CLI 0.23.0 includes two fixes requested in #11022:

- Managed memory availability now respects the `memory.enableManagedAutoMemory` setting (#6941). Hosts that disable managed auto memory no longer see remember/dream requests admitted or managed-memory instructions in the system prompt; local patches can be removed.
- Size-triggered microcompaction now clears old tool results toward a low watermark (#8464), so it no longer rewrites another part of the conversation prefix on every subsequent turn. Provider prompt-cache reuse is preserved across long tool-heavy sessions, reducing cached-input cost.

issues.title: ACP regression in 0.10.1: config sandbox_mode/ask ignored — Paseo ACP sessions run sandboxed and approval-gated

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: New external report awaiting maintainer triage; repro, logs and version output help

issues.body:
# ACP regression in 0.10.1: `sandbox_mode` / `ask` from config ignored again — Paseo ACP sessions run sandboxed and approval-gated

## Summary

The ACP posture bug from #6310 (fixed in the 0.10.0 nightlies and verified in Paseo) is back in stable **0.10.1**: sessions launched via `codewhale serve --acp` ignore `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"` and `ask = "never"` from `~/.codewhale/config.toml`, and run with the OS sandbox on, network off, and approval gates firing on every shell call.

## Environment

- codewhale **0.10.1** (build `fead51eeea0f`), macOS (Apple Silicon)
- Launched as an ACP provider for the Paseo app (verified: multiple `codewhale serve --acp` processes owned by Paseo)
- `~/.codewhale/config.toml`:
  ```toml
  approval_policy = "suggest"
  sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"
  ask = "never"
  ```

## Observed (live session, 2026-10-15)

- `CODEWHALE_SANDBOX=seatbelt` is set in the session environment → the OS sandbox is applied despite `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"`.
- `python3 -c 'import socket; s=socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX); s.bind("/tmp/x.sock")'` → `PermissionError: [Errno 1] Operation not permitted` — the exact #6310 signature; this breaks Node test runners and Playwright webServer.
- `ps` → `operation not permitted` (can't even list processes).
- Network is blocked: `curl -sI https://example.com` returns nothing (`000`).
- Every shell call still hits the typed-ask gate and requires a manual approval in the client UI, even though `ask = "never"`. (`gh` could not even read its own config at `~/.config/gh/hosts.yml` — EPERM — until the shell was escalated.)
- The policy engine itself agrees these should be skipped: `codewhale sandbox check --ask never 'ls -la /tmp'` → `{"allow": true, "requires_approval": false}`. So the disconnect is between the policy engine and the posture actually applied to live ACP sessions.

## Difference vs the original #6310 report

- Writes to `/tmp` now succeed (in 0.9.13 they were EPERM), but AF_UNIX socket creation is still blocked — the one thing Playwright/Node runners need.
- Approval prompts now reach the Paseo UI and can be approved manually (in 0.9.13 they were auto-denied). Still: `ask = "never"` should not gate at all.

## Suspected relation

#6473 (Full Access now requires per-session confirmation) combined with #6310's fix ("makes Full Access discoverable **without letting a client select it**") leaves the ACP path with no way to enter Full Access at all. `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"` is effectively dead config for Paseo users, and every real workflow — network, sockets, process listing, CLI tools like `gh` — breaks. If per-session confirmation is the intended mechanism, the ACP client needs a way to request/confirm it. Until then this is a regression from the verified-working 0.10.0 nightly.

## Ask

1. Restore config-derived posture for ACP sessions when the client does not pin one, or
2. Expose a Full Access selection/confirmation path to ACP clients (Paseo), or
3. At minimum, honor `ask = "never"` so gated commands skip instead of prompting.

Happy to provide full transcripts or run a nightly/repro build. Greetings from Colombia 🇨🇴

issues.title: OHOS cross-build fails on Windows (aws-lc-sys CMake uses the Visual Studio generator) and codewhale-cli then fails E0433
issues.body:
## Environment

- Host: Windows, Visual Studio 17 2022 BuildTools (MSVC 19.44.35215.0), CMake 3.31.5, ninja on PATH
- DevEco OpenHarmony native SDK 26.0.0 via `OHOS_NATIVE_SDK`
- Target: `aarch64-unknown-linux-ohos` (rustup target installed)
- Reproduced with the documented flow from `docs/HarmonyOS.md`: set `OHOS_NATIVE_SDK`, dot-source `scripts/ohos-env.ps1`, then
  `cargo build --release --target aarch64-unknown-linux-ohos -p codewhale-cli`

## Failure 1 - `aws-lc-sys v0.45.0` build script panics

```
error: failed to run custom build script for `aws-lc-sys v0.45.0`
-- Building for: Visual Studio 17 2022
-- The C compiler identification is MSVC 19.44.35215.0
-- Check for working C compiler: .../cl.exe - broken
cl : command line error D8021: invalid numeric argument '/Wa,--noexecstack'
```

`aws-lc-sys` builds through the `cmake` crate, which passes no `-G`. On Windows, CMake then
defaults to the Visual Studio generator. That generator ignores the clang compiler that
`ohos.toolchain.cmake` sets via `CMAKE_C_COMPILER`, uses `cl.exe` instead, and still applies the
toolchain's clang-only flags (`-Wa,--noexecstack`, `--target=...`, `--sysroot=...`), which
`cl.exe` rejects. `scripts/ohos-env.ps1` exports `CMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE_aarch64_unknown_linux_ohos`
but no generator. On Linux/macOS the default generator is Unix Makefiles, which honours the
toolchain, so non-Windows CI never hit this.

## Failure 2 - `codewhale-cli` no longer compiles for OHOS once failure 1 is fixed

```
error[E0433]: cannot find `update` in the crate root
  --> crates/cli/src/cloud/work.rs:236:33
note: found an item that was configured out
  --> crates/cli/src/lib.rs:9:5
```

`mod update` is `#[cfg(not(target_env = "ohos")]`, but three call sites reference
`crate::update::sha256_hex` without the same gate:

- `crates/cli/src/cloud.rs:1501` - SHA-256 verification of a downloaded account file
- `crates/cli/src/cloud.rs:1962` - dispatch stamp seed digest
- `crates/cli/src/cloud/work.rs:236` - Work task-context digest verification

The first and third are content-integrity checks, so they must stay compiled on OHOS and cannot
simply be cfg'd out. CI compile-checks `codewhale-tui` for the OHOS target but not
`codewhale-cli`, which is why this regressed unnoticed.

## Proposed fix

1. `scripts/ohos-env.ps1`: export `CMAKE_GENERATOR=Ninja`, falling back to the SDK-bundled
   `build-tools/cmake/bin/ninja.exe` and failing loudly when neither exists.
2. Move `sha256_hex`/`hex_bytes` out of the cfged `update` module into an ungated `crate::hashing`
   module in `codewhale-cli` (same implementation the TUI already shares through
   `codewhale_runtime::hashing`) and point the three call sites at it.

Verified on Windows with the SDK above: `aws-lc-sys` builds in about 43 s and
`cargo build --release --target aarch64-unknown-linux-ohos -p codewhale-cli` exits 0, producing
an ELF64 AArch64 PIE that needs only `libc.so` and `libtime_service_ndk.so`. Host-target
`cargo check -p codewhale-cli` and `cargo check -p codewhale-cli --tests` both exit 0, and
`cargo fmt --all -- --check` exits 0.

A fix PR follows this issue (#6989).

---

## 中文说明

**环境**：Windows + Visual Studio 17 2022 BuildTools(MSVC 19.44.35215.0)、CMake 3.31.5、PATH 中有 ninja;DevEco OpenHarmony native SDK 26.0.0(通过 `OHOS_NATIVE_SDK` 指定)；目标 `aarch64-unknown-linux-ohos`。按 `docs/HarmonyOS.md` 文档流程复现：设置 `OHOS_NATIVE_SDK`、dot-source `scripts/ohos-env.ps1`,然后执行 `cargo build --release --target aarch64-unknown-linux-ohos -p codewhale-cli`。

**问题一:`aws-lc-sys v0.45.0` 构建脚本直接 panic。** 它通过 `cmake` crate 构建,而该 crate 不传 `-G` 参数;Windows 上 CMake 于是默认选中 Visual Studio 生成器——这个生成器会无视 `ohos.toolchain.cmake` 里通过 `CMAKE_C_COMPILER` 指定的 clang,强行使用 `cl.exe`,同时又应用工具链里那些只属于 clang 的参数(`-Wa,--noexecstack`、`--target=...`、`--sysroot=...`),`cl.exe` 无法解析,报 `D8021`。`scripts/ohos-env.ps1` 只导出了 `CMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE_aarch64_unknown_linux_ohos`,没有指定生成器。Linux/macOS 上默认生成器是 Unix Makefiles,会遵循工具链,所以非 Windows 的 CI 从来没有暴露过这个问题。

**问题二:问题一修好后,`codewhale-cli` 在 OHOS 目标上编译不过(E0433)。** `mod update` 带有 `#[cfg(not(target_env = "ohos"))]`,但有三处调用没有加同样的门控就直接引用 `crate::update::sha256_hex`:

- `crates/cli/src/cloud.rs:1501` —— 校验下载的账户文件 SHA-256
- `crates/cli/src/cloud.rs:1962` —— dispatch stamp 种子摘要
- `crates/cli/src/cloud/work.rs:236` —— Work 任务上下文摘要校验

第一处和第三处是内容完整性校验,在 OHOS 上必须保留,不能简单 cfg 掉。CI 对 OHOS 目标只检查 `codewhale-tui`、不检查 `codewhale-cli`,所以这个回退一直没被发现。

**修复方案**:

1. `scripts/ohos-env.ps1` 导出 `CMAKE_GENERATOR=Ninja`;PATH 里没有 ninja 时回退到 SDK 自带的 `build-tools/cmake/bin/ninja.exe`,两者都没有则明确报错退出。
2. 把 `sha256_hex`/`hex_bytes` 从被门控的 `update` 模块移到 `codewhale-cli` 中未门控的 `crate::hashing` 模块(与 TUI 已在使用的 `codewhale_runtime::hashing` 实现一致),三处调用改指新位置。

**已验证**(Windows + 上述 SDK):`aws-lc-sys` 约 43 秒构建成功;`cargo build --release --target aarch64-unknown-linux-ohos -p codewhale-cli` 退出码 0,产物为 ELF64 AArch64 PIE,只依赖 `libc.so` 和 `libtime_service_ndk.so`;宿主目标 `cargo check -p codewhale-cli` 与 `--tests` 均退出码 0;`cargo fmt --all -- --check` 通过。修复 PR 见 #6989。

issues.title: Turn snapshots fail with "git commit-tree failed: fatal: <sha> is not a valid object" since 2026-10-12 (0.10.0 after rollback from 0.10.1); old user turns are re-delivered

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: New external report awaiting maintainer triage; repro, logs and version output help

issues.body:
Hello,

I would like to report a defect in CodeWhale 0.10.0. We run it on Windows 11 in daily work, and the instance
in question holds a long-running session (about 99 MB) that we would very much like to keep. The problem has
been with us since 12 October 2026.

**Environment**

- CodeWhale **0.10.0** (npm package installed globally). Binary: `%APPDATA%\npm\node_modules\codewhale\bin\downloads\codewhale.exe`,
  100 331 520 bytes, last written **2026-10-12 15:48**.
- Current version in npm: **0.10.1**.
- Windows 11 IoT Enterprise LTSC 10.0.26100, git 2.55.0.windows.5.
- Data dir `%USERPROFILE%\.codewhale`; workspace `C:\Users\Public\CodeWhale`.
- Session journal `sessions\fd452c83-….json`: **98 989 231 bytes** (it was ~72 MB on 2026-10-12 and grows).

**Symptom 1 — every turn snapshot fails**

```
WARN snapshot: snapshot 'pre-turn:2: <first words of a user message>' failed:
     git commit-tree failed: fatal: 6a55c90c6ada7206170f178fd20032f813a3b3d9 is not a valid object
```

**Symptom 2 — old user turns are re-delivered as new input**

Because snapshots never complete, past turns are never marked done and are fed back. The order is stable and
reproducible: in the most recent run the app re-delivered turns 2, 3 and 4 — the same three messages, in the
same order, as in every previous run (logs `tui-2026-10-14-20628`, `-14004`, `-23528`). The user sees his own
old messages answered again.

**Symptom 3 — shell operations frequently fail**

```
WARN codewhale_tui::tools::shell: shell work-graph registration skipped;
     running without a bound operation shell_id=shell_<hex>
     error=To-do state is busy; operation was not registered

WARN codewhale_tui::tools::shell: failed to reconcile shell lifecycle shell_id=shell_<hex>
     error=operation binding shell:shell_<hex> is not registered
```

273 such lines in the logs; on the user's side roughly every 3rd–4th shell call fails. Possibly the same root
cause as the snapshot failure.

**Symptom 4 — at startup the store looks empty**

```
WARN snapshot: boot prune failed: git log failed: fatal: bad object HEAD
```

**When it started**

- first occurrence: **2026-10-12T16:00:16Z** — `snapshot prune failed: commit-tree failed: fatal: c6d19349dd4298bf49945c1e64e4e7b35c4b334c is not a valid object`;
- 458 lines containing “is not a valid object” in total, over four runs;
- only two lost objects in total: `6a55c90c6ada7206170f178fd20032f813a3b3d9` and `c6d19349dd4298bf49945c1e64e4e7b35c4b334c`.

**What correlates with the date**

On the same day the user updated to **0.10.1** and then **rolled back to 0.10.0**. The package directory is
stamped **2026-10-12 15:48** (the rollback), and the first snapshot failure is at **19:00** local time.
Hypothesis: a snapshot store was begun by 0.10.1, and after the rollback 0.10.0 cannot complete that chain.

**What we tried**

- Reinstalled the same version (`npm install -g codewhale@0.10.0`) — **no effect**. The store is not part of
  the program files; `boot prune failed: bad object HEAD` still appears and snapshots still fail with the same SHA.

**Where we looked for the store (found nothing)**

Workspace `C:\Users\Public\CodeWhale` (not a git repo; only `.codewhale\state` with subagent state);
`%USERPROFILE%\.codewhale` (no `work-graph`, `objects`, `refs`, `.git` — only `sessions\.work-graph-import-archive`);
`%LOCALAPPDATA%` and `%APPDATA%` (depth 4); `%TEMP%`; the app package dir (only `bin`, `scripts`, `test`,
`package.json`, `README.md`); the app's `state.db` is empty and stale (2026-10-04).

**Questions**

1. Where are the snapshot store and the work-graph kept, and how can a corrupted chain be repaired on the
   user's side?
2. How can the **turn queue / parent-commit pointer** be reset so that snapshots work again and old turns stop
   being re-delivered **without discarding the session**? The session is 99 MB and losing it would be costly.
3. Is the `To-do state is busy` shell failure the same root cause as the snapshot failure? Both began in the
   same period.

**Related: cannot move to 0.10.1 with a long session**

On 2026-10-12 we also tried 0.10.1: it installs cleanly, but resuming our session fails:

```
error: selected saved history could not be captured
caused by: session exceeds full-history transport bound; source retained
```

The session file was ~72 MB then and is **98 989 231 bytes** now, so this bound will trigger even more readily.
We cannot test 0.10.1 — and therefore cannot check whether it fixes the snapshot store — while it stands.
Is there a way to raise or bypass it?

**Materials available on request**

Full log excerpts (458 snapshot lines, 273 work-graph lines), the environment dump, and our extended Russian
report. Happy to attach or translate anything you need.

Thank you for the tool, and for taking the time to look at this. I will gladly provide any further logs,
dumps or reproductions you need.

Best regards,
Sergej Malevich

issues.body:
### Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate. 我已搜索过现有 issue。

### What problem does this solve? 要解决什么问题？

Significantly reduce context overhead

### What should Codewhale do? 希望 Codewhale 怎么做？

https://github.com/yc-duan/fastctx

A significant reduction in token consumption through FastCtx, rather than through model compression or conversation summarization. The actual amount of token savings depends on how the Agent is used and the type of tasks.

Core principles:

**1. Batch reading:** Read multiple files or code ranges in a single call, reducing the number of tool invocations and repeated reads.
**2. Limit output length:** Set output budgets for file reading, searching, and command execution to avoid irrelevant content consuming context.
**3. Reduce redundant operations:** Simplify command execution through structured tools, minimizing syntax errors, failed retries, and redundant work.
**4. Optimize truncation handling:** Clearly indicate omitted content and allow on-demand log retrieval, avoiding repeated execution of already completed commands.
**5. Simplify tool descriptions:** Shorten MCP tool descriptions to reduce token consumption from the tool definition itself.
**6. Background task execution:** Run time-consuming tasks such as building and testing in the background, and retrieve results only when needed, reducing repeated polling and output.

## Rules (applied to every sub-EPIC)

1. Behavior-preserving — extraction only, no command/UX behavior changes.
2. Trait-first — define the boundary interface before moving code (pattern: EPIC-006 `CommandContext`).
3. Compiles at every step — bottom-up extraction, workspace stays green at each commit.
4. CI gate — extracted crate must never depend on `codewhale-tui` (e.g. `cargo check -p codewhale-commands` pulls no TUI).
5. Deliver one independently verified PR per completed FEAT against current upstream main; keep parent EPICs open until their remaining work and acceptance criteria are complete.
6. Sequencing — EPIC-006 first, then 007/008, then 009, then 010.

The whole point of this decomposition: once a sub-EPIC's crate exists (EPIC-006 Feature 3 and later), day-to-day development happens **entirely outside the TUI monolith** (\~700k lines). The TUI is only compiled when you explicitly need it — TUI integration tests, `cargo test --workspace`, or the final pre-PR validation.

```bash
cargo check -p codewhale-commands          # production change check — seconds, not minutes
cargo test -p codewhale-commands           # test loop — compiles only the commands crate + thin test binaries, never the TUI
cargo watch -x "check -p codewhale-commands"  # continuous check while editing (cargo-watch)
cargo nextest run -p codewhale-commands    # optional: parallel test runner, faster startup
```

Why this stays fast:

* `cargo build` / `cargo check` never compiles `#[cfg(test)]` code, so production iteration is bounded to the small crate.
* `cargo test` compiles each `tests/` file as its **own small binary crate** depending only on the public API — a production change recompiles/relinks only those thin binaries, in parallel.
* The Gherkin acceptance harnesses live in separate test binaries (or a dedicated acceptance crate), so thousands of acceptance-test lines are **never part of the production crate compile**.
* Small white-box unit tests that need private access stay inline — they are cheap and cannot live outside the crate.

**Acceptance criterion for every extracted crate:** `cargo test -p <crate>` must compile only that crate and its test binaries — if it pulls in `codewhale-tui`, the boundary was cut wrong.

The numbers and impact motivating this are documented in [#4991](<https://github.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale/issues/4991>) (Discussion: Compilation times and the TUI crate monolith): 476k lines / 82% of the workspace in one crate, 8–16 min release builds, 30+ min test suite, 2–3 iterations per hour.

issues.title: Android (Termux): every confined file operation fails with EACCES — `open_confined` opens `/` with `O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY`, which SELinux denies to apps

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: New external report awaiting maintainer triage; repro, logs and version output help

issues.body:
## Summary

Since v0.10.1, on Android/Termux every engine feature that goes through the confined file opener (`WorkspaceFile::open_confined` in `crates/tui/src/fleet/files.rs`) fails with `Permission denied (os error 13)`:

- `workflow journal unreadable (~/.codewhale/workflow-runs.jsonl): Permission denied` on every session start
- `context compaction failed ... error=Permission denied (os error 13)` — and the turn is then settled as **Failed**, which is the most visible symptom
- `spillover: could not save full tool output before cutting it for model context err=... PermissionDenied`
- skill loading via `fs_confined::read_to_string` fails (`read cannot expose...` style errors aside, direct SKILL.md loads return EACCES)

Everything that does *not* go through `open_confined` (plain `std::fs` paths such as `save_checkpoint`, shell tool output, bash subprocesses) works fine, which makes the failure look random.

Logs from v0.9.x sessions on the same device show **zero** occurrences of these warnings; they start exactly at the 0.10.1 install and now appear in every session.

## Root cause

`open_confined` anchors its `openat` walk at the filesystem root:

```rust
let fd = unsafe {
    libc::open(
        c"/".as_ptr(),
        libc::O_RDONLY | libc::O_DIRECTORY | libc::O_NOFOLLOW | libc::O_CLOEXEC,
    )
};
```

On Android, app processes run in the `untrusted_app` SELinux domain. That domain has **search** (traverse) permission on `/` and on mount-point directories such as `/data` and `/data/data`, but **not read**, so `open("/", O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY)` returns `EACCES` even though the DAC bits are `drwxr-xr-x`. Every `WorkspaceFile` operation therefore fails before it even reaches the workspace, and `com.termux` (uid `u0_a435`) is affected as `untrusted_app` (domain confirmed via `/proc/self/attr/current` = `u:r:untrusted_app_27:s0:c179,c257,c512,c768`).

Verified with strace on a live session — the only non-environment `EACCES` calls in the entire process lifetime are:

```
openat(AT_FDCWD, "/", O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC|O_DIRECTORY) = -1 EACCES (Permission denied)
```

(52 occurrences in one session, interleaved with the failing journal/compaction/spillover warnings.)

DAC permissions, ownership, fcntl record locks (EAGAIN, not EACCES, when contended), disk/inode headroom, `TMPDIR`, and multi-process concurrent appends were all checked and are not factors. `realpath`/`opendir` on the same paths succeed — the failure is specific to opening `/` as a readable directory.

## Minimal reproducer

Run inside Termux (`python3 android-repro.py`, attached):

```
workspace: /data/data/com.termux/files/home
open('/', O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY)  [current open_confined anchor]: FAIL errno=13 (Permission denied)
open('/', O_PATH|O_DIRECTORY)    [proposed fix anchor]:        OK
confined walk (fix):             OK
confined write/read through fix: OK
```

## Proposed fix (patch attached, against main as of 2026-10-14)

Open the anchor and every intermediate component with `O_PATH` instead of `O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY`, and re-materialize the file's immediate parent as a real directory fd after the walk:

- `O_PATH|O_DIRECTORY` still fails with `ENOTDIR` on non-directories, so the per-component type check and the symlink refusal are unchanged.
- `O_PATH` requires no read permission, so SELinux `search`-only domains (Android apps, hardened sandboxes) work.
- The final parent is reopened with real flags (`openat(pinned_parent, ".")`) because O_PATH fds cannot be `fsync`ed (`EBADF`) or read, and `WorkspaceFile` uses the directory fd for `sync_all`, `renameat`, `unlinkat` afterwards. This reopen cannot escape the walk: it resolves `.` inside the pinned parent.
- Final file opens (`open_with_flags`, `atomic_write`, `mkdirat`) are untouched.

Verified on-device that with the fix the full `WorkspaceFile` semantics work end-to-end: journal read, `O_CREAT|O_EXCL` leaf creation, `mkdirat` branch, atomic tmp+rename, `fsync` on the materialized parent, `fstat`/`dup` on the directory fd.

## Environment

- codewhale 0.10.1 (fead51eeea0f), GitHub Releases aarch64 build
- Android 16 (Termux app, `untrusted_app_27` SELinux domain, targetSdk profile c179/c257/c512/c768)
- Workload: multiple parallel TUI sessions; failure rate 100% for compaction once context passes the auto-compact threshold

Happy to test a patched build on the device.

issues.title: Brief the model when MCP boot servers fail — and when they recover (design discussion)

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: context
labels.description: Context management / context

labels.name: reliability
labels.description: Reliability, flaky behavior, retries, fallbacks, and robustness

labels.name: mcp
labels.description: MCP servers, tools, OAuth and the mcp CLI

milestone.title: Backlog
milestone.description: Kept ideas without a release commitment: platform requests, integrations and speculative features. Say why when you pick one up or close it; nothing here blocks a release.

issues.body:
**Title:** `Brief the model when MCP boot servers fail — and when they recover (design discussion)`

**Body:**

## Problem

When MCP servers fail during session boot, the model gets no signal. Its tools simply don't appear: it names a tool it was told exists, gets `unknown tool`, and cannot distinguish "server failed to connect this session" (retryable, maybe transient) from "never configured" (permanent). Recovery is equally invisible — a server that reconnects mid-session makes its tools reappear without the model learning it can retry the earlier failure.

Upstream already carries the host-facing half: `Event::McpSessionBoot` receipts reach the UI (`engine.rs` ~:7103) and reconnect reporting exists for users. But nothing reaches the *model*, and the model is the party that has to adapt its next tool call.

## Proposal

Model-facing runtime-handoff briefings for boot failure and recovery, rendered as internal briefings on the session timeline:

- New runtime-handoff event kinds (e.g. `mcp_boot_failed` / `mcp_boot_recovered`) carried through the existing handoff machinery, so SyncSession reconciliation re-briefs consistently on session reload.
- The failure briefing distinguishes *failed* from *not configured* and names the affected server(s) with the connect error.
- The recovery briefing names the server and tells the model previously-missing tools are callable again (with the deferred-tool activation path, since the tools won't be in the first-round catalog).
- Hardening that has to ride along, because server-reported strings would now reach the model: control-character flattening on briefing reasons, and no echoing of raw server-authored envelope fields (anti-injection surface).

Scale: the fork-side implementation is ~400 lines including tests (`crates/tui/src/runtime_handoff.rs` briefing constants + engine bookkeeping + reconcile + tests).

## Why an issue first

This is model-facing prompt content — the contribution guide's trust-boundary surface — so I'm looking for a design sign-off (and any naming/placement preferences) before opening a PR. The reference implementation exists and is tested on the fork side: Pinvou/CodeWhale `6f780290f` (with the hardening above); happy to re-derive it onto current main's handoff architecture whatever way reviewers prefer.

## Coordination

Checked against current main: no `mcp_boot_failed`/`mcp_boot_recovered` kinds exist in the runtime-handoff kind list yet, and lazy boot (#6033) plus connection supervision (#6187) changed the failure semantics since the fork implementation — the recovery briefing in particular needs to key off the supervisor's reconnect results rather than boot-time state.

issues.title: Saved DeepSeek key reads back as missing while DeepSeek is not the active provider (root vs [providers.deepseek] auth_mode marker mismatch)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate. 我已搜索过现有 issue。

### What happened? 发生了什么？

After saving a DeepSeek API key, an engine restart keeps reporting DeepSeek's credential as missing as long as another provider is active (e.g. zai). The key is present in the durable secret store but is never read for a non-active DeepSeek route.

Root cause: DeepSeek's save path writes the api-key marker at the ROOT of config.toml only, while the non-active-provider read gate only probes the durable secret store when that provider's own [providers.<name>] table carries auth_mode = 'api_key'. The marker the save writes is not the marker the read checks.

Observed home (macOS):
- ~/.codewhale/secrets/secrets.json holds the deepseek slot.
- ~/.codewhale/config.toml has root auth_mode = 'api_key' and [providers.deepseek] model = '...', but no [providers.deepseek] auth_mode.
- the active provider is zai.
Result: the provider picker / GET /v1/providers reports DeepSeek as missing on every restart.

Code pointers:
- crates/tui/src/config.rs save_api_key_for_identity: for Deepseek returns save_api_key() (~L12062).
- save_api_key() -> save_root_api_key_for_secret_slot(key, 'deepseek', 'deepseek') (~L11443).
- save_root_api_key_metadata_without_plaintext writes only root auth_mode, never [providers.deepseek] auth_mode (~L11546-L11566).
- Every other provider goes through codewhale_config::credentials::prepare_provider_api_key_metadata (crates/config/src/credentials.rs), which sets the per-table auth_mode.
- Non-active read gate: secret_slot_save_marker_on_shared_slot (crates/tui/src/config.rs ~L12572) checks provider_config_for(..).auth_mode, consumed by crates/tui/src/config/credential_resolve.rs (~L262-L292). A test already pins this asymmetry: crates/tui/src/config/tests.rs picker_and_request_path_disagree_when_the_secret_slot_marker_is_missing (~L15618).

Workaround: add auth_mode = 'api_key' under [providers.deepseek], or re-save the key while DeepSeek is the active provider.

Suggested fix: in save_root_api_key_metadata_without_plaintext also set ['providers', table, 'auth_mode'] = 'api_key', so DeepSeek writes the same marker prepare_provider_api_key_metadata writes for every other provider.

### Steps to reproduce 复现步骤

1. Make a non-DeepSeek provider active (e.g. zai) and leave DEEPSEEK_API_KEY unset.
2. Save a DeepSeek key via the provider picker / onboarding (path: save_api_key() -> save_root_api_key_for_secret_slot(.., 'deepseek', ..)).
3. Inspect ~/.codewhale/config.toml: root auth_mode = 'api_key' is set and the deepseek slot is present in ~/.codewhale/secrets/secrets.json, but [providers.deepseek] has no auth_mode.
4. Restart the engine (or the host app) and open the provider picker, or call GET /v1/providers.
5. DeepSeek is reported as missing key, even though making DeepSeek active resolves the saved slot fine.

prs.title: fix(ohos): build CMake crates with Ninja and ungate the cli sha256 helper
prs.body:
Fixes #6988.

Two fixes for the OpenHarmony cross-build.

## 1. `scripts/ohos-env.ps1` exports `CMAKE_GENERATOR=Ninja`

`aws-lc-sys` builds through the `cmake` crate, which passes no `-G`. On Windows CMake then
defaults to the Visual Studio generator, which ignores the clang compiler that
`ohos.toolchain.cmake` sets and feeds its clang-only flags to `cl.exe`
(`D8021: invalid numeric argument '/Wa,--noexecstack'`). When `ninja` is not on `PATH` the
script falls back to the SDK-bundled `build-tools/cmake/bin/ninja.exe` and fails loudly when
neither exists.

## 2. `sha256_hex`/`hex_bytes` move to an ungated `crate::hashing` module in `codewhale-cli`

With the generator fixed, the OHOS build reached `codewhale-cli` and failed E0433: `mod update`
is `#[cfg(not(target_env = "ohos"))]`, but `cloud.rs` (two sites) and `cloud/work.rs` (one site)
called `crate::update::sha256_hex` without the same gate. Those sites verify downloaded-content
integrity and Work task-context digests, so they stay compiled on OHOS; the helper now lives in
an ungated module, matching the shared `codewhale_runtime::hashing` implementation the TUI
already uses.

## Verification (Windows, DevEco OpenHarmony native SDK 26.0.0, current main)

- `aws-lc-sys` v0.45.0 builds in about 43 s, producing `libaws_lc_0_45_0_crypto.a` (5.9 MB)
- `cargo build --release --target aarch64-unknown-linux-ohos -p codewhale-cli` exits 0 in
  28 m 32 s; the binary is an ELF64 AArch64 PIE (116,462,208 bytes) needing only `libc.so` and
  `libtime_service_ndk.so`
- `cargo check -p codewhale-cli` on the host target exits 0
- `cargo check -p codewhale-cli --tests` exits 0
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` exits 0

---

## 中文说明

本 PR 修复 Issue #6988,包含两处改动:

1. **`scripts/ohos-env.ps1` 导出 `CMAKE_GENERATOR=Ninja`。** `aws-lc-sys` 通过 `cmake` crate 构建,该 crate 不传 `-G`;Windows 上 CMake 因此默认选中 Visual Studio 生成器,无视 `ohos.toolchain.cmake` 指定的 clang,把只属于 clang 的参数喂给 `cl.exe`(`D8021`)。PATH 中无 `ninja` 时回退 SDK 自带版本,两者皆无则明确失败。

2. **`sha256_hex`/`hex_bytes` 移至 `codewhale-cli` 未门控的 `crate::hashing` 模块。** 生成器修好后 OHOS 构建走到 `codewhale-cli` 触发 E0433:`mod update` 带有 `#[cfg(not(target_env = "ohos"))]`,而 `cloud.rs`(两处)与 `cloud/work.rs`(一处)未加门控地调用了 `crate::update::sha256_hex`。这些调用承担下载内容完整性与任务上下文摘要校验,OHOS 上必须保留,因此把助手函数搬到未门控模块,与 TUI 已共享的 `codewhale_runtime::hashing` 实现保持一致。

**验证**(Windows,DevEco OHOS native SDK 26.0.0,当前最新 main):`aws-lc-sys` 约 43 秒构建成功并产出 `libaws_lc_0_45_0_crypto.a`(5.9 MB);`cargo build --release --target aarch64-unknown-linux-ohos -p codewhale-cli` 退出码 0(28 分 32 秒),产物为 116,462,208 字节的 ELF64 AArch64 PIE,仅依赖 `libc.so` 与 `libtime_service_ndk.so`;宿主目标 `cargo check -p codewhale-cli` 与 `--tests` 退出码 0;`cargo fmt --all -- --check` 通过。


### Maintainer qualification (2026-10-15)

Current head: **[deb491c44b](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/deb491c44bb4bcf9b4dbfb0b9c5b3cde601a17ef)**, tree `13d1be6be2d58c66a161870a79c30e8d75cb3db7`. It preserves @shenjackyuanjie's original commit `5c6a61ab7f74c466bb65be71addfc8897783bff9`, the six original source files and all maintainer follow-ups. The preceding `39ceb861` update carried the shared main repair; this merge additionally carries [#6985](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/pull/6985)'s exact `9f5ed8eb` source so CI can qualify the eventual combined tree before the first PR lands. Only five shared changelog/credit/generated-document conflicts required resolution; both implementations and every contributor's history remain intact.

**Merge #6985 as its own PR first, then this original OHOS PR.** This source update merges neither PR. Admission requires #6985's exact reviewed head to be merged into live main, this head's fresh native/web/budget checks to pass, and the actual resulting merge tree to match the qualified tree. The source branch remains retained.

The Windows/SDK26 linked build above remains contributor-reported validation. Maintainer Linux-hosted SDK checking of TUI and CLI passed on prior head `c59004af`, along with its Ubuntu native, web and actual Runtime/persistence gates. Linux cross-compile checking does not establish Windows-host SDK or OHOS-device acceptance.

That head's [Windows native job](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/actions/runs/38794829670/job/116629008631) recorded **18,355 passed (1 leaky), 1 failed, 27 skipped**. Its sole failure was the inherited tool-metric fixture: both samples used `bash`, but optional `code_execution` appeared only in the second full catalog (51→52 tools). The exact interpreter and reason for the differing probe outcomes were not captured. Windows doctests and containment receipt export were skipped after the failure; the original receipt is retained.

The preceding main repair changed only `crates/tui/src/dependencies.rs`, the existing tool-metric fixture and `scripts/mobile-smoke.sh`; every other blob from that preceding PR head was preserved. The metric fixture now uses the existing test-only host-capability pin on all test platforms, and the smoke assertions avoid an upstream broken pipe under `pipefail`. Production probe behavior, catalog budgets and the complete equality assertion remain unchanged.

The three-file repair was validated locally on macOS before committing `51c00f23`: **2 existing focused Rust tests passed**, the complete extracted tool catalog equals the existing budget with no identity/cap changes, the production CLI binary built, **9 mobile HTTP smoke assertions passed**, and `npm test && npm run check:web` passed **1,312 tests with 0 failures and 7 skipped** (540 Node + 772 Vitest). The first isolated smoke launch exceeded macOS's socket-path limit before HTTP assertions; correcting only the artifact launcher then passed all 9 assertions with the same compiled binary. Both attempts are retained. These are focused local results on the main repair, not full native qualification of this PR head.

**Current head remains blocked.** Its [Windows job](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/actions/runs/38810132099/job/116681656721) timed out waiting for Windows Terminal composer readiness before the native suite began. The retained artifact proves PowerShell entered the script; it contains no later stage, readiness, paste or provider-request evidence. The exact blocking statement and cause are unknown. The same clipboard scripts and CI workflow are byte-identical to successful main51 and #6985 checks; no interactive-startup change was found in this OHOS diff.

One bounded retry of that Windows job at unchanged `deb491c4` is planned. GitHub rejected the request while the rest of [this workflow](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/actions/runs/38810132099) is still running, so no retry has started and the other legs are left running. The original failure is retained. A repeated failure requires further diagnostics, not a presumed pass or timeout increase. Fresh Linux-SDK TUI+CLI checking, Web Frontend, Safety and the Linux npm smoke have passed; remaining native and actual budget gates still govern admission. Earlier receipts retain their source identities. The contribution and source branch remain preserved; 0.10.2 has not shipped.
