issues.body:
### Request type

Config exposure for an existing internal option (plus one behavioral consideration).

### Problem

The durable channel-ingress drain dead-letters any claim that is not adopted within `DEFAULT_INGRESS_ADOPTION_STALL_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000` (`src/channels/message/ingress-drain.ts`, ~L33). The watchdog deliberately stays armed through deferral ("Timer is not cleared by deferral", `armStallWatchdog`; also documented in `extensions/telegram/AGENTS.md`: "stays armed through deferral; dead-letter reason `handler-timeout`").

On the claude-cli runtime, `queue.mode: "steer"` degrades to followup (no mid-turn injection point), so a follow-up message arriving during an active turn sits **pre-adoption** for the remainder of that turn. Any agent whose turns can exceed 5 minutes — routine for claude-cli with high thinking budgets — therefore silently loses every mid-turn follow-up:

```
17:27:21  turn starts (claude-cli, ran 466s)
17:27:52  follow-up claimed on the same lane → deferred behind the running turn
17:32:52  "Channel ingress claim→adoption stalled for event Ev… on lane team:…:conversation:…
           after 300001ms; marking failed (handler-timeout)."
          → the user's message is dead-lettered: never answered, never retried, no user-visible signal
```

(Observed 2026-07-30 UTC, OpenClaw 2026.7.2-beta.5 `ee929db`, `@openclaw/slack@2026.7.2-beta.5`, socket mode. The stall's abort also interacts badly with the running turn's delivery — receipts in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/116546 / #111969 — but this request stands on the dead-letter alone.)

### Current state of configurability

- The Slack monitor's ingress module already accepts the option — `extensions/slack/src/monitor/ingress.ts` (~L99) declares `adoptionStallTimeoutMs?: number` and forwards it to the drain (~L308–317) — **but no caller passes it and no config-schema key exposes it** (`extensions/slack/src/config-schema.ts` has no ingress timing keys). The Slack drain therefore always runs the 5-minute core default.
- Precedent for a longer, channel-appropriate value exists in-tree: the Telegram webhook spool wires a 25-minute stall ("Pre-migration product default: 25m claim→adoption stall for webhook", `extensions/telegram/src/webhook.ts` ~L405).

### Ask

1. Expose `adoptionStallTimeoutMs` in Slack channel config (provider-level, per-account override), wired through the existing option — a pure plumbing change.
2. Optionally: consider making the pre-adoption watchdog lane-activity-aware for deferred claims — a claim parked behind a *live, progressing* turn on the same lane is not a wedged handler, and dead-lettering it guarantees user-visible message loss. Even a simple "extend the stall deadline while the lane owner shows run activity" would remove the hard turn-length cliff without weakening the wedged-handler protection the watchdog exists for.

issues.body:
### Summary
Provide a supported way to opt claude-cli backend runs into readable thinking text (Claude Code's thinking display mode), now that the `agents.defaults.cliBackends` args DSL is retired and the bundled backend's argv is plugin-owned.

### Problem to solve
On current Anthropic models, thinking display defaults to `omitted`: headless Claude Code runs persist thinking blocks signature-only (empty `thinking` text, signature present). Claude Code opts in automatically only for interactive sessions; its print mode exposes a `--thinking-display <mode>` flag instead (undocumented but present and working at 2.1.209 — same family as the hidden print-mode flag your `claude-live-session.ts` already relies on for `--resume-session-at`).

Before 2026.7.2, deployments could carry that flag via `agents.defaults.cliBackends.claude-cli.args` (raw backend args). That DSL was retired in favor of plugin registrations (deprecation record `2026-07-21`, removal after `2026-09-22`), and the bundled anthropic plugin now owns the full argv: `resolveClaudeCliExecutionArgs` in `extensions/anthropic/cli-shared.ts` only manages `--effort`, and the plugin's `configSchema` exposes no argv or thinking-display surface. Result: there is no supported way to make claude-cli agent transcripts carry readable reasoning — operators auditing agent fleets lose the agent's thinking entirely (signature-only blocks), with no config recourse.

### Proposed solution
A config-surfaced thinking-display option for the claude-cli backend — e.g. alongside the existing thinking-level handling (which already maps to `--effort`), accepting Claude Code's modes (`summarized`, `omitted`; default unchanged) — applied by the plugin as either:

- `--thinking-display <mode>` on the launch argv in `resolveClaudeCliExecutionArgs`, and/or
- the `thinking_display` session control on the existing `claude-stdio` control channel: Claude Code accepts it in the same control request that sets `max_thinking_tokens`, and it "sets the thinking display mode for the rest of the session" — request-scoped, no argv change, and `claude-live-session.ts` already speaks this channel (today it only answers `can_use_tool` requests).

Per Anthropic's docs the thinking block is billed identically either way, so the option is cost-neutral; it changes persistence/visibility only.

### Alternatives considered
- **Claude Code settings key** — none exists: no settings.json key or env var feeds print-mode thinking display as of Claude Code 2.1.209 (verified against docs and by probing; `showThinkingSummaries` affects interactive display only). If Anthropic adds one later it would compose nicely with the `--setting-sources user` you already pin, but nothing exists today.
- **PATH wrapper injecting the flag** — defeated by design: `runtimeArtifact: bundled-package-tree` verification fails closed for launchers outside the declared package on auth-binding runs, and a wrapper is invisible to OpenClaw's arg normalization.
- **Out-of-tree plugin re-registering the backend** — forks security-sensitive adapter code (credential FD transport, restricted-args enforcement) that operators shouldn't own.

### Impact
- Affected: any deployment running agents on the claude-cli backend that needs auditable transcripts (compliance/oversight of autonomous agents).
- Severity: capability loss with no workaround — agent reasoning is unrecoverable after the fact (signature-only blocks cannot be expanded later; the text must be requested at run time).
- Frequency: every claude-cli turn.
- Consequence: fleet audit tooling can show *what* an agent did but no longer *why*; we previously restored this via `cliBackends.claude-cli.args` and lost it again with the DSL retirement.

### Evidence/examples
Headless probes, Claude Code 2.1.209, identical agentic task (`-p --output-format stream-json --verbose --effort high`, one Read-tool task), inspecting the persisted session transcript:

| invocation | thinking block in transcript |
| --- | --- |
| baseline | `text` empty, signature-only |
| `--thinking-display summarized` | readable summarized text + signature |
| `--settings '{"showThinkingSummaries":true}'` | `text` empty, signature-only |

Interactive sessions on the same host and account persist thinking with text — confirming the interactive-only auto-opt-in.

References: `extensions/anthropic/cli-shared.ts` (`resolveClaudeCliExecutionArgs`, effort mapping), `extensions/anthropic/cli-backend.ts` (static argv), `src/agents/cli-runner/claude-live-session.ts` (control-channel handling, hidden-flag precedent), Anthropic model-config docs on thinking display defaulting to omitted for non-interactive use.

### Additional information
The retired DSL also carried per-deployment watchdog overrides (`reliability.watchdog.noOutputTimeoutMs`); we're currently fine on the new built-in defaults, so this request is deliberately scoped to thinking display only.

issues.body:
## Summary

With OpenClaw.app running, the gateway service restarts continuously at irregular intervals (measured: 32s to 727s, degrading to ~60s). Sessions die mid-task with WebSocket 1005/1006 closures. Quitting the app stops it completely — 14h44m of uninterrupted uptime with the app closed, versus restarts every few minutes with it open.

## Environment

- **Version:** 2026.7.1-2 (0790d9f), macOS
- **LaunchAgent:** `gui/501/ai.openclaw.gateway`
- **Two installs of the same version coexist:**
  - `/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/openclaw` (what `which openclaw` resolves to; `doctor` runs from here)
  - `~/.openclaw/tools/node-v24.15.0/lib/node_modules/openclaw` (app-managed runtime)
- Both `package.json` files report `2026.7.1-2` — this is **not** a version skew.

## Mechanism (verified)

1. `openclaw doctor` reports *"Gateway service entrypoint does not match the current install"* and offers to repair it.
2. Accepting the repair writes a plist that still contains the **old entrypoint** — it fixes `PATH` only. The stale-entrypoint warning therefore recurs.
3. Editing the plist manually to the homebrew path **does work**: the gateway starts clean from it, health `{"ok":true,"status":"live"}`, no module errors.
4. **On launch, the app rewrites the LaunchAgent back to its own path and boots the service to apply it:**

```
09:29:44  app launched
09:30:10  plist rewritten (manual edit reverted)
09:30:11  [gateway] signal SIGTERM received
```

Manual fix survived **26 seconds**.

## Process chain (captured by 1s process sampling)

The invocations are too short-lived for a plain `ps` snapshot:

```
launchctl bootout gui/501 .../ai.openclaw.gateway.plist
  ← openclaw-gateway
    ← openclaw
      ← /Applications/OpenClaw.app/Contents/MacOS/OpenClaw
        ← launchd
```

## Excluded with evidence

- **No `StartInterval`** in the plist; `RunAtLoad` + `KeepAlive` only
- **ProcessType Interactive** — not macOS resource throttling
- **No crashes** — every stop is a clean `"[gateway] signal SIGTERM received"`
- **No health-monitor failure** logged; it only ever logs at startup
- **Cron:** 6 enabled jobs, 0 overdue, none on a matching interval
- **Not a version skew:** both `package.json` report `2026.7.1-2`

## Additional observations

- `~/.openclaw/logs/gateway-restart.log` stopped recording on 2026-07-22; none of these restarts appear there. The live log is `~/Library/Logs/openclaw/gateway.log`.
- `openclaw doctor` reports cron at `~/.openclaw/cron/jobs.json`, which was migrated away on 2026-06-05 and no longer exists; live cron is in `~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite` (`cron_jobs`, `cron_run_logs`).

## Expected behavior

Either the app tolerates a separately-installed CLI without rewriting the service definition, or `doctor` recognises the app-managed entrypoint as legitimate instead of flagging it and offering a repair that cannot hold.

## Practical impact

Sessions are interrupted mid-task, subagents can be pruned during recovery, and long-running orchestration is unreliable while the app is open. The browser UI at `http://127.0.0.1:18789/` works normally — everything gateway-side is unaffected by quitting the app, which is the stable workaround.

## Description

Closing a Codex app-server client does not abort an in-flight inbound server-request handler, so local tool/auth/approval work can continue after its transport and response path are gone.

## Expected behavior

The client close transition should abort every active inbound server-request controller and clear the registry, in addition to rejecting outbound requests and notifying observers.

## Root cause and evidence

Abort controllers were scoped only to the request-timeout helper and were not tracked by the client close lifecycle. The fix registers active controllers, removes them on settlement, and aborts/clears them during the single close transition. The fail-before regression observed `signal.aborted === false`; it now passes as part of the 112-test client/shared-client/router group.

Pinned reproduction: `c66ca2fbb2b038f4796abfa76bd52dcc3b675b02`. No public Plugin SDK or protocol boundary changes. Found and fixed during an AI-assisted QA campaign.

## Problem

Currently, the model is fixed at session level. There's no way to automatically route messages to different models based on content type (text, image, audio, TTS).

## Use Case

Users with multiple specialized models (e.g. Xiaomi MiMo V2.5 series) want automatic routing:

| Message Type | Target Model |
|---|---|
| Plain text | mimo-v2.5-pro |
| Text + image | mimo-v2.5 |
| Audio/voice | mimo-v2.5-asr |
| TTS request | mimo-v2.5-tts |

## Proposed Solution

Add a `routing` config under `models`:

```json
{
  "models": {
    "routing": {
      "text": "xiaomi-token-plan/mimo-v2.5-pro",
      "multimodal": "xiaomi-token-plan/mimo-v2.5",
      "audio": "xiaomi-token-plan/mimo-v2.5-asr",
      "tts": "xiaomi-token-plan/mimo-v2.5-tts"
    }
  }
}
```

The agent should auto-detect message type and switch model accordingly, instead of requiring manual `session_status` model override per request.

## Context

- Provider: xiaomi-token-plan (MiMo V2.5 series)
- Models available: mimo-v2.5-pro, mimo-v2.5, mimo-v2.5-asr, mimo-v2.5-tts-voiceclone, mimo-v2.5-tts-voicedesign, mimo-v2.5-tts
- Current workaround: manually switch via `session_status` with model override

issues.body:
# Bug: Matrix room agents can loop on visible no-reply output, replay stale session state after restart, and ignore reply-gating expectations

## Summary

Matrix room agents can enter a self-sustaining loop where "no reply" reasoning, STOP handling, restart recovery notices, and stale room/session context become visible Matrix messages. Once one agent emits visible meta-output, other agents treat that text as fresh inbound room input and continue the cycle.

This is not just prompt failure. The failure crosses:

- Matrix ingress
- session persistence and replay
- restart recovery
- outbound delivery
- reply-gating semantics

During the latest incident on July 27, 2026, containment required archiving Bethany's active Ops session state, restoring runtime files from backups, forcing `requireMention: true` for the Ops room, and restarting gateways one at a time while watching the room.

## Expected behavior

1. If an agent decides no visible reply is needed, no Matrix message should be sent.
2. STOP/no-reply decisions should never appear as visible room output.
3. Restart recovery should not post stale "please resend" notices into active group rooms unless explicitly user-triggered.
4. Restarting or resetting a Matrix room session should not cause older room content to be processed as fresh inbound work.
5. `requireMention`, `autoReply`, `allowBots`, and bot-to-bot visibility should behave predictably and be clearly documented.
6. Gateway health should not be considered sufficient if Matrix provider startup, replay, or recovery is still pending.

## Actual behavior

Agents visibly posted messages like:

- "No response needed..."
- "I will stay silent..."
- "Final answer: NO_REPLY"
- "STOP command acknowledged. NO_REPLY"
- "I was interrupted by a gateway restart and couldn't safely resume..."

Those visible messages were then consumed by other agents as new room input, causing more replies. In the latest incident, Bethany repeatedly processed messages from roughly 10 to 20 minutes earlier after restarts and recovery.

## Impact

- Ops room floods with self-generated agent noise.
- STOP handling becomes self-defeating because agents narrate silence instead of staying silent.
- Restarting gateways can worsen the incident by replaying stale state.
- Health checks can report "live" while Matrix delivery behavior is still unsafe.
- A single asymmetric node can restart the loop fleet-wide.

## Minimal reproduction shape

1. Configure two or more Matrix room agents in a shared room.
2. Enable room participation with settings equivalent to `autoReply: true` and bot visibility such as `allowBots: "mentions"` or similar.
3. Allow visible model output for no-reply reasoning, STOP handling, or "not for me" classification.
4. Send a room-wide status prompt.
5. Have one agent emit visible meta-text about why it should not reply.
6. Restart one or more gateways during the active conversation.
7. Observe stale room/session content being replayed as fresh work and restart/no-reply messages retriggering other agents.

## Evidence timeline

### May 15, 2026: contributing background context - Bethany workspace split-brain increased loop risk

Evidence: `/home/pi/agent-ops/notes/morning-session-discoveries-2026-05-15.md`

- `workspace-chat` was created as a lean Matrix/WhatsApp context on May 8, 2026.
- It was not kept in sync after Bethany gained direct tools on May 11, 2026.
- Recorded effect: Bethany read stale instructions, delegated unnecessarily, then looped between "can't do it" and "builder broken."
- This is useful background on agent fragility, but not presented here as the direct cause of the July 27 replay incident.

### May 19-22, 2026: Matrix tool leak, version skew, stale processes

Evidence: `/home/pi/agent-ops/bug-report-2026-05-22-rollback-crisis.md`

Recorded failures included:

- `toolProgressDetail` default behavior change made internal tool progress visible in Matrix.
- Plugin/core version skew caused Matrix channel instability.
- Stale gateway processes held the port while health checks still passed against the wrong process.
- Mention-gating was used as an emergency containment step.

### May 21-22, 2026: room noise and manual session clearing were already required

Evidence: `/home/pi/.codex/history.jsonl`

History records:

- reports of hundreds of loop/noise messages in Ops and Cron
- reports of tool/thought output bleeding into chat
- reports of Bethany looping visibly
- explicit request to clear all Matrix sessions

Related archives:

- `/home/pi/.openclaw/session-archive/ops-room-clear-20260613T133500Z/`
- `/home/pi/.openclaw/session-archive/matrix-room-clear-20260614T085628Z/`
- `/home/pi/.openclaw/session-archive/matrix-room-clear-20260614T093052Z/`
- `/home/pi/.openclaw/session-archive/ops-bethany-clear-20260727T011855/`

### June 1-13, 2026: historical reply-gating and history handling bugs were real, but not the sole July 27 replay cause

Evidence: `/home/pi/agent-ops/workspace-maya/memory/MEMORY.md`

Documented lessons included:

- `autoReply: false` could silently force `requireMention: true`
- `historyLimit: 0` caused agents to wake without useful room context
- room session resets did not backfill history cleanly
- `historyLimit` placement was easy to misconfigure
- mention-gating asymmetry could create self-sustaining loops
- "NO_REPLY deprecated - simply don't reply. Describing silence in chat triggers response spirals."

These bugs matter historically, but `historyLimit` had already been corrected fleet-wide before July 27. The latest incident looked more like stale session/restart replay plus visible meta-output than a simple `historyLimit: 0` regression.

### June 13, 2026: major loop incident showed severity before the July 27 failure

Evidence: `/home/pi/agent-ops/workspace-chris/memory/archive/2026-06/2026-06-13-runtime-event-status.md`

- Ops ran into a 400+ message loop over roughly 130+ minutes.
- STOP/silence instructions were ineffective once the loop became self-sustaining.
- Admin intervention was required to contain the room.

This is a strong severity datapoint because it shows the same class of failure at room scale well before the July 27 incident.

### June 13, 2026: deterministic no-reply guard was attempted

Evidence: `/home/pi/agent-ops/plugins/matrix-no-reply-guard/`

A local plugin was created to suppress visible no-reply narration before Matrix delivery. This helped only as a workaround and did not reliably cover every outbound path, recovery path, or restart notice.

### July 7, 2026: same Bethany loop pattern documented again

Evidence: `/home/pi/agent-ops/workspace-maya/MEMORY.md`

Recorded incident:

- Bethany emitted repeated "NOT_FOR_ME" style replies to every Ops message.
- STOP_LOOP was ignored.
- Human workaround was to force Bethany and Lilly to mention-only in Ops.

### July 27, 2026: latest live incident

Evidence: Matrix Ops room readback on July 27, 2026

Observed pattern:

- Room-wide status prompt triggered multiple agent replies.
- Bethany began visibly classifying other agents' messages as not directed at her.
- Older Chris/Lilly/Maya messages were replayed after restart and treated as fresh work.
- A restart recovery notice was posted visibly into the room.
- Full containment required stopping gateways, restoring runtime files from backups, archiving Bethany's active Ops session state, and reintroducing mention-gating.

Containment artifacts created during the latest incident:

- `/home/pi/.openclaw/openclaw.json.bak-bethany-ops-requiremention-true-20260727-0119`
- `/home/pi/.openclaw/session-archive/ops-bethany-clear-20260727T011855/`
- `/home/pi/.local/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/monitor-C124lfVF.js.bak-fleet-agent-mention-gate-20260727-0045`
- `/home/pi/.local/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/main-session-restart-recovery-Ce8fihTV.js.bak-suppress-restart-notice-20260727-0020`

## Why current workarounds are insufficient

- Prompt instructions are not enough because model-generated silence reasoning can still leak into visible Matrix output.
- Outbound no-reply guards do not help if not every send path, recovery path, and restart notice passes through the same deterministic filter.
- Restarting gateways can worsen the incident because stale room/session state can be replayed.
- Fleet-wide config changes are brittle because one asymmetric node can retrigger the whole loop.
- Health/live checks do not prove Matrix safety.

## Requested product fixes / questions

1. Can no-reply decisions be enforced in core as a deterministic drop before Matrix outbound delivery?
2. Can restart recovery notices be disabled or made opt-in for group Matrix rooms?
3. Can Matrix session reset clear active room bindings and pending recovery/replay state atomically?
4. Can `requireMention`, `autoReply`, `allowBots`, and bot-to-bot handling be documented with a tested state table?
5. Can gateway health expose Matrix provider readiness, replay/recovery state, and last outbound Matrix event time?
6. Can replay logic distinguish historical context from new inbound user work after restart?
7. Can the product expose a supported "clear this Matrix room session safely" operation?
8. Can plugin/core version skew be detected before a gateway reports healthy?

## Current safe local workaround

For Bethany on Europa:

- Ops room set to `requireMention: true`
- active Ops session entries archived instead of deleted
- runtime files restored from pre-experiment backups
- gateway restarted and verified live

This stopped the latest loop from resuming, but it is only a containment workaround and reduces spontaneous room participation.

## Maintainer framing

This is not just bad prompt behavior. It is a systemic failure where:

- model-generated silence decisions are delivered visibly
- restart/session recovery can reintroduce stale room messages
- bot-to-bot room traffic is not consistently treated as passive context
- health checks do not reflect Matrix delivery safety

The fix likely needs deterministic controls at Matrix ingress, session recovery, and outbound delivery layers.

issues.body:
## Summary

When the Codex harness resumes a persisted thread whose `thread/resume` response contains an already-active native turn, it waits for that turn but does not adopt it into the wrapper run's liveness instrumentation. The native Codex turn can continue to execute tools and produce useful work, while OpenClaw diagnostics retain an old `turn:start` as the last progress event and eventually invoke `abort_embedded_run`.

This is distinct from a genuinely stalled Codex turn: the native transcript shows continuing activity after the wrapper has considered the session stale.

## Environment

- OpenClaw `2026.7.1` (`2d2ddc4`)
- Codex app-server / embedded Discord agent
- Reproduced on a long-running issue-work session with a persisted Codex thread

## Observed sequence

1. The pipeline redrives an existing Discord/Sima session.
2. `thread/resume` returns the persisted Codex thread with `activeTurnIds`.
3. The harness logs:

   ```text
   codex app-server resumed thread has active native turn; waiting before turn/start
   ```

4. After 30 seconds it logs:

   ```text
   codex app-server active native turn did not complete before turn/start wait timed out
   ```

5. The original native turn is still alive. Its Codex rollout records tool calls, waits, GitHub CI readback, and assistant progress messages.
6. However, core diagnostics report stale progress from the wrapper (the old `codex_app_server:turn:start`), and after approximately 360 seconds recover with:

   ```text
   stuck session recovery: ... action=abort_embedded_run aborted=true drained=true
   ```

7. The caller receives `runtime_unavailable`; a downstream orchestrator may redrive the same session. Subsequent attempts again find the still-active native turn, producing duplicate working cues / prompts without duplicate commits.

A related symptom then appears:

```text
nativeHook.invoke ... errorMessage=native hook relay not found
```

## Root cause in current source

`extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-turn-request.ts` detects `thread.lifecycle.action === "resumed"` plus `activeTurnIds` and calls `waitForActiveNativeTurnCompletion()`. It does not adopt the existing turn into the wrapper attempt.

Normal `turn/start` flow in `run-attempt-active-turn.ts` does all of the following:

- sets `turnIdRef`;
- creates `CodexAppServerEventProjector`;
- arms/touches `turnWatches` and emits progress;
- binds the turn route;
- installs the dynamic-tool / notification lifecycle bridge.

The resume-with-active-turn branch does none of those. In particular, `noteNotificationReceived()` returns immediately when `projectorRef.current` or `turnIdRef.current` is absent. Existing native-turn notifications and dynamic-tool activity therefore cannot refresh the wrapper's progress.

Separately, wrapper cleanup unregisters the native-hook relay although the original native turn can still retain its hook configuration. This accounts for the `native hook relay not found` failures, but the primary false-stale cause is the missing active-turn adoption/liveness binding.

## Expected behavior

When `thread/resume` reports a live turn, OpenClaw should either:

1. adopt it as the current embedded run without submitting a second prompt: bind route, turn id, event projector, notification/dynamic-tool bridge, watches, and relay ownership; or
2. explicitly retain a bounded, observable wait that emits liveness progress and prevents diagnostic active-abort while the app-server proves the existing turn is alive.

It must not treat an active native turn as stale merely because it was created by a preceding wrapper attempt.

## Regression coverage requested

Add an integration test where:

1. `thread/resume` returns `activeTurnIds: [existing]`;
2. that existing turn emits notifications and/or `item/tool/call` activity for longer than `stuckSessionAbortMs`;
3. no duplicate `turn/start` is submitted;
4. diagnostics continue receiving fresh progress and never call `abort_embedded_run`;
5. a parent-wrapper cleanup/recovery safely rebinds the native-hook relay, or reports a controlled terminal failure rather than leaving a live turn with a missing relay.

## Related but not duplicate

- #85532 tracks diagnostic recovery aborting active embedded runs after terminal-looking app-server progress. This report is a distinct source of stale progress: the active turn is never bound to the resumed wrapper.
- #110702 tracks an app-server no-terminal-completion stall shape.
- #112705 improves detached native-worker supervision and relay lifecycle across parent turns, but does not appear to adopt a top-level resumed embedded turn with `activeTurnIds`.

## Impact

Long-running automated sessions are falsely aborted despite real Codex activity. Pipeline/orchestrator retries then amplify tool/token use and produce misleading repeated "agent started" cues.

## Problem

Agents stamp their first reply in a thread with a runtime "run-badge" — custom emoji encoding the session's model + delivering harness (e.g. `:m_opus::h_cc:` = Opus via Claude Code). The badge is derived purely from runtime facts the gateway already knows (resolved session `model=` and the delivering harness).

Today the only way to append it is a prompt instruction, which is unreliable across sessions — it competes with other reply-formatting rules for the last line and gets dropped intermittently. There's no mechanical way to guarantee it:

- No config field for a reply footer/signature.
- The plugin system exposes no outbound / before-send transform event.
- The runtime ships compiled in `dist/`; patching it isn't durable across upgrades.

## Proposal

Add a supported extension point for deterministic outbound reply post-processing. Either (or both):

1. **Declarative** — a per-agent `replySuffix` config with runtime template vars:
```jsonc
"agents": { "liv": { "replySuffix": {
  "template": ":m_{model}::h_{harness}:",
  "once": "per-thread",       // per-thread | per-reply | on-change
  "surfaces": ["slack"]
} } }
```
with `{model}` / `{harness}` resolved from the session's runtime values.

2. **Programmatic** — a `beforeReply(ctx) => text` plugin hook receiving the assembled reply plus session runtime metadata (model, harness, surface, thread state), returning the final text. This covers first-reply-only / re-emit-on-model-change logic a static template can't express.

## Why the gateway, not the model

The badge is a runtime fact, not a content decision. The model shouldn't have to remember an operational convention the gateway can stamp deterministically — and can't reliably, since it doesn't observe the harness tile consistently. Moving it to the harness makes it 100% and frees prompt space.

issues.body:
# BUG: Workboard cannot spawn ACP workers (opencode / Codex / Claude Code)

## Context

Workboard is an agent-owned kanban plugin that can dispatch cards to workers for
execution. OpenClaw ships ACP (Agent Client Protocol) support, where multiple external
agents can be launched as **ACP backends** in standalone processes. The control-plane
registry (`AGENT_REGISTRY` in `dist/runtime-DXAKhVSX.js`) explicitly includes:
- `opencode`: `npx -y opencode-ai acp`
- `codex`: `npx -y @agentclientprotocol/codex-acp@^0.0.44`
- `claude` (Claude Code): `npx -y @agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp@^0.37.0`

In other words, OpenClaw already has the ACP capability to spawn opencode / Codex /
Claude Code as independent worker processes.

But after inspecting the source, the Workboard dispatch mechanism **cannot spawn any ACP
worker process at all (opencode / Codex / Claude Code alike)**. It only runs through
OpenClaw's embedded LLM harness and never uses the registered ACP backends.

## Environment

- OpenClaw version: 2026.7.1 (2d2ddc4)
- Entry points: `workboard_dispatch` / `dispatchAndStartWorkboardCards`
- Relevant modules:
  - `dist/extensions/workboard/index.js`
  - `dist/runtime-api-BWc6b9BO.js`
  - `dist/acp-spawn-CtlOotd2.js` (ACP spawn path, independent)
  - `dist/runtime-DXAKhVSX.js` (`AGENT_REGISTRY` contains the opencode/codex/claude ACP launch commands)

## Investigation (code facts)

1. **Dispatch does not go through ACP**: `workboard_dispatch` -> `dispatchAndStartWorkboardCards()`
   calls for each startable card:
   ```js
   const run = await params.subagent.run({
     sessionKey,
     message: buildWorkerPrompt(...),
     ...(params.options?.provider ? { provider: params.options.provider } : {}),
     ...(params.options?.model ? { model: params.options.model } : {}),
     lane: `workboard:...`,
     lightContext: true,
     deliver: false,
     ...(materialized.cwd ? { cwd: materialized.cwd } : {})
   });
   ```
   `params.subagent.run` resolves to `runEmbeddedAgent` (OpenClaw's **embedded LLM harness**),
   **not** the ACP spawn entry point.

2. **Limited passthrough**: `dispatchAndStartWorkboardCards` only consumes these options:
   `boardId / maxStarts / model / ownerId / allowManagedWorktrees / provider`.
   There is **no `runtime` or `acpBackend` field**, and the tool schema does not accept them.
   So there is no way to specify "which ACP backend should run the worker".

3. **ACP spawning is a separate code path**: actually launching the opencode / Codex /
   Claude Code process goes through `spawnAcpDirect` (`dist/acp-spawn-CtlOotd2.js`), which
   runs the corresponding `npx ... acp` command from `AGENT_REGISTRY` via the ACP control
   plane. The Workboard dispatch logic never calls it.

4. **No Workboard -> ACP linkage**: a full grep of `workboard` finds no references to
   `acp`, and the dispatch logic never calls `spawnAcpDirect`.

## Result (the bug)

- ❌ Workboard **cannot spawn any ACP worker process** (none of opencode / Codex / Claude
  Code). Even though OpenClaw has these ACP backends registered, Workboard never spawns them.
- ⚠️ The only available setting is `provider: "opencode"` — but this merely makes the
  embedded harness send **model requests** to opencode's API (as an LLM vendor). It does
  **not** have the opencode / Codex / Claude Code ACP process host the card's work. Codex
  and Claude Code do not even have an "LLM provider" entry point (they are only ACP
  backends), so Workboard is **completely unable** to use them.

## Expected behavior

Workboard should be able to route card work to an ACP worker, e.g.:
- `dispatchAndStartWorkboardCards` (and the `workboard_dispatch` tool) should accept a
  `runtime` / `acpBackend` option;
- When `runtime: "acp"` is set (optionally with `acpBackend: "opencode" | "codex" | "claude"`),
  spawn the corresponding process as the worker via `spawnAcpDirect`, instead of only using
  the embedded harness.

## Current workarounds (not officially supported)

To have a card executed by an opencode / Codex / Claude Code process today, one must modify
the Workboard dispatch code to route `subagent.run` through `spawnAcpDirect` and pass
`runtime`/`acpBackend`; or have an upstream step convert the card into an ACP session first
and then let Workboard track it. Both require source changes — not available out of the box.

## Suggestion

Please fix the missing ACP worker support in Workboard: expose `runtime`/`acpBackend` on
`workboard_dispatch` and reuse the existing `spawnAcpDirect`, so that registered ACP backends
such as opencode / Codex / Claude Code can actually be spawned as worker processes.

issues.body:
## Summary

Allow a plugin-owned agent tool to return a supported result that asks OpenClaw to end the current turn cleanly after the tool has successfully started an external interaction.

## Problem to solve

Plugin tools can deliver an approval prompt, form card, or another asynchronous interaction to an external channel, but they can currently return only a normal tool result. The agent loop may therefore continue in the same turn before the external callback arrives, producing an unnecessary final reply or racing the pending interaction.

OpenClaw already has the model-facing `sessions_yield` tool and the embedded runner already knows how to convert that signal into a clean `end_turn`. A plugin tool, however, cannot atomically reuse that behavior:

- `OpenClawPluginToolContext` does not expose a yield/end-turn control.
- Asking the model to call `sessions_yield` after the plugin tool is a second, model-dependent tool call and may be blocked by tool policy.
- Aborting or stopping the active run from the channel side is not semantically equivalent to a clean handoff and can target the wrong run.
- Keeping the original run blocked on generic next-message input does not fit externally correlated interactions: an unrelated user message can be mistaken for the answer, while the plugin already has a platform callback carrying its own correlation id.

The missing primitive is a narrow plugin-to-runtime handoff after the external side effect succeeds.

## Proposed solution

Add an optional runtime-control request to `AgentToolResult` and expose a public Plugin SDK helper such as:

```ts
return yieldToolResult({
  message: "Waiting for the external interaction to complete.",
});
```

When OpenClaw receives that result, it should:

1. Persist the successful tool result normally.
2. Route the control request through the existing `sessions_yield` runner path.
3. End the current turn cleanly, with the existing yielded/paused lifecycle metadata.
4. Allow a later inbound event to start the next turn in the same session.

The plugin remains responsible for external delivery, correlation ids, authorization, persistence, expiry, supersession, and callback reinjection. This proposal does not add a core question manager or channel-specific UI.

Existing tools remain unchanged when no control field is returned. Unsupported runtimes should fail explicitly rather than silently pretending that the turn yielded.

An implementation candidate already exists in #101665.

## Alternatives considered

### Ask the model to call `sessions_yield`

This requires a second model-selected tool call after the external prompt is delivered. It is not atomic and depends on prompting and the effective tool allowlist.

### Keep the current run open until the next user message

This is appropriate for runtimes with a native `request_user_input` protocol, but not for plugin-owned form callbacks. It keeps a run alive and may consume an unrelated chat message as the answer instead of requiring the external correlation id.

### Abort or stop the current run from the channel plugin

This models a successful handoff as an interruption, can emit interruption semantics, and requires the channel to identify the exact active run safely.

### Add a question-specific API to core

That is a broader product surface. #102260 tracks a first-party structured question pipeline. This request is deliberately narrower: it provides a generic turn-handoff primitive so third-party plugins can own their interaction UX and state.

## Impact

- **Affected:** Authors and users of channel/integration plugins that start asynchronous approvals, forms, or native platform interactions.
- **Severity:** Medium; it blocks a reliable, race-free implementation of these workflows through the public Plugin SDK.
- **Frequency:** Every time such a plugin tool must wait for a later platform callback.
- **Consequence:** The model can continue before the callback, send conflicting output, or force plugins to rely on model prompting or unsafe run cancellation.

## Evidence/examples

- Existing runtime primitive: `sessions_yield` already cleanly ends a turn and records yielded/paused lifecycle state.
- Current Plugin SDK tool context exposes session and delivery metadata but no yield/end-turn control.
- Implementation candidate: #101665 adds `yieldToolResult(...)`, normalizes a result-level control request, and reuses the existing `sessions_yield` runner path.
- Adjacent but broader roadmap: #102260 covers first-party structured questions, plan mode, and goal mode; it does not replace the need for a low-level plugin-owned external-interaction handoff.

## Additional information

This Issue is being filed retroactively for #101665 so the public SDK contract can be discussed independently from the implementation diff.

Non-goals:

- No new channel-specific card or callback protocol.
- No core persistence for pending plugin interactions.
- No requirement to resume the same provider run; a later inbound callback starts the next turn in the same OpenClaw session.
- No behavior change for existing plugin tool results.

issues.body:
### Summary

Extend OpenClaw's existing shared exec primitive — which already supports
timeout, idle timeout, output caps, process-tree kill, cancellation, and
structured termination — with optional OS-level caps for memory/RSS, swap, CPU,
and subprocess count. Enforcement is capability-reported by a host adapter and
never mandatory.

### Problem to solve

OpenClaw already bounds several execution dimensions for processes it spawns via
`src/process/exec.ts` / `src/process/exec-runner.ts` (used by node-host
system-run, ffmpeg, skills install/extract, media-understanding):

- wall-clock timeout (`timeoutMs`) and idle timeout (`noOutputTimeoutMs`);
- per-stream output byte caps (`maxOutputBytes`, `outputCapture`);
- process-tree kill via detached process group (`killProcessTree`,
  `exec-runner.ts:145`);
- AbortSignal cancellation;
- structured termination:
  `"exit" | "timeout" | "signal" | "output-limit" | "error"`.

The remaining gap is host-resource pressure: a policy-approved job can still
consume unbounded memory, swap, CPU, or process count. The only memory-adjacent
control today is the OOM-score nudge (`src/process/linux-oom-score.ts`), which
biases kill order under pressure but does not cap a job. There is no
`setrlimit`/cgroup/`systemd-run` enforcement anywhere in core or extensions, no
capability report of what the current host could enforce, and no structured
outcome for a requested-but-unenforceable cap.

### Proposed solution

Build on `RunExecOptions` and the existing termination outcome surface — no
parallel subsystem:

- add optional fields such as `maxMemoryBytes`, `maxSwapBytes`, `maxProcesses`,
  and a CPU limit/share;
- absent fields preserve current behavior for every existing caller;
- add a host enforcement adapter with reported capabilities;
- extend the existing `termination` union with `memory-capped`, `process-limit`,
  `declined-unsupported-budget`, and `adapter-unavailable` — requested caps the
  host cannot enforce produce an explicit decline, never a silent no-op;
- use platform adapters where available, e.g. transient user
  `systemd-run --scope` / cgroups on Linux, without requiring them anywhere.

### Alternatives considered

- **A parallel "budget" options/result type.** Rejected: the primitive already
  carries budget options and a structured `termination` union; a second system
  duplicates the surface and forces callers to reconcile two result shapes.
- **Mandatory sandbox/container per job.** Rejected: heavy, platform-locking,
  and sandboxing already exists as a separate layer; this bounds an
  already-approved local job.
- **Relying on the OOM-score nudge for memory.** Insufficient: biases kernel
  kill order; caps nothing.

### Impact

- **Affected:** operators and plugins running heavy local work through
  OpenClaw-spawned paths — node-host system-run, media processing, package
  builds, scientific scripts, tests, delegated node commands.
- **Severity:** medium-to-high for automation reliability. Time and output are
  bounded today, but CPU/memory pressure can still degrade the gateway or host.
- **Frequency:** occasional in ordinary chat; common for developer/scientific/
  power-user workflows.
- **Consequence:** host memory pressure, CPU starvation of the gateway, manual
  cleanup of resource-unbounded but policy-approved jobs.

### Evidence/examples

- Existing enforced budgets: `src/process/exec.ts:117-137`,
  `src/process/exec-runner.ts:44-63`.
- Process-tree kill via detached group: `src/process/exec-runner.ts:145,178`.
- node-host caller already using tree-kill + head capture:
  `src/node-host/invoke.ts:337-343`.
- Cancellation wrapper: `src/node-host/with-timeout.ts`.
- OOM-score nudge (observe/bias only): `src/process/linux-oom-score.ts`.
- No `setrlimit`/cgroup/`systemd-run` enforcement exists in `src`/`extensions`
  (verified by search).
- Linux adapter viability verified live on a real host: transient
  `systemd-run --user --scope` with `MemoryMax`, `CPUQuota`, and `TasksMax`
  succeeded for `/bin/true` without elevated privileges.

### Additional information

**Scope boundary.** These caps apply only to processes OpenClaw spawns through
its own exec primitive. Agent harnesses (Codex / Claude CLI) execute their own
tools in processes OpenClaw does not spawn-control; whether those runtimes
expose comparable controls is their owners' question and is not assumed here.

**Non-goals:** no mandatory systemd/cgroup/Docker dependency; no parallel
execution subsystem; no batch scheduler; no promise of identical enforcement
across OSes; no replacement for tool policies, sandboxing, approvals, or
diagnostics.

**Acceptance criteria** (wall-clock, output caps, and tree cancellation already
ship and are not restated):

- the exec primitive accepts optional memory/swap/CPU/process caps; omitting
  them preserves current behavior;
- adapters report which caps are enforceable on the current host;
- unsupported requested caps produce an explicit structured decline, never a
  silent ignore;
- at least one common Linux path enforces memory and process-count caps;
- new outcomes extend the existing `termination` union rather than a new type;
- tests cover success within cap, cap hit, unsupported-cap decline, and
  adapter capability differences.

AI-assisted: drafted with Claude and reviewed against current source; file
references verified at authoring time.

issues.body:
## Version / environment

- openclaw `2026.6.11`, Linux, gateway running as a systemd **user** service.
- Agent on an `openai-completions` provider.
- `tools.exec.security: "full"`, `approvals.exec.enabled: false`, no sandbox, `exec.host` unset (auto → gateway).

## Reproduction

```
openclaw agent --agent myagent --session-id $(uuidgen) --json --timeout 480 \
  --message "Run exec: echo exec-alive-test"
```

The model emits the exec call correctly (`stopReason=toolUse`), `tool:exec:started` is logged, but the completion **never** arrives.

Diagnostics observed:

```
stalled session … reason=blocked_tool_call … activeTool=exec
stuck session recovery: action=abort_embedded_run aborted=true drained=true   # after ~390s
[session-write-lock] releasing lock held for ~322000ms (max=300000ms)
```

## Key facts

1. The command is trivial (`echo`) — this cannot be slow command execution.
2. Reproducible as the **first** exec after a fresh gateway restart → rules out the abort-wedge from #102006 (no prior aborted exec is required).
3. The same run type with `read` instead of `exec` completes normally → the embedded spawn path itself is healthy.
4. Model-independent — the model emitted the call and no fallback was involved.
5. 30 days of diagnostics history: every exec stall is on the embedded / isolated path; interactive channel sessions show none.
6. Observed repeatedly on scheduled weekly runs (2026-07-05, 2026-07-12) and reproduced manually 2026-07-15.

## Cross-references

Adjacent but not identical: #25209, #83474, #73581, #102006.

## Ask

Where does exec completion get lost on the embedded path — is the completion event never emitted, is the executor slot not released, or is there a deadlock against the session write-lock?

issues.body:
### Summary

When the `openclaw agent` gateway path loses the CLI↔gateway WebSocket **after the gateway has already accepted (and detached) the run**, the CLI's current reflex is to re-execute the turn locally (embedded fallback). I'd like a maintainer decision on whether to **flip that reflex**: first *reattach* to the already-running gateway run and return its real result, and re-run locally only as a last resort. This changes user-visible disconnect behavior, so I'm filing for direction **before** building it.

### Problem to solve

Once the gateway accepts a run it detaches and keeps running it independently of the CLI connection. If that connection then closes non-transiently before the final frame (proxy/LB idle timeout, `1006` abnormal close, `1012` restart — anything other than a clean transient `1000`), the CLI falls back to an embedded run.

Today that fallback is **"recook-first"**: the CLI's first and only reflex is to re-run the turn locally. Consequences:

- **The turn executes twice** — the detached gateway run *and* the local embedded run each run it once: two model calls, tool side effects on both, and under `--deliver` a possible second delivery.
- **The locally re-run result may not equal the authoritative one** — model nondeterminism plus side effects the gateway run already performed mean the user can get a *different* answer than the run the gateway actually executed.
- **The already-computed result is simply ignored.** The gateway has the primitives to hand back the real result of the detached run, but this CLI path never asks for them.

Scope note: the **narrow correctness bug** on this path — the embedded fallback reusing the *original* session and producing duplicate transcript turns in one session (`impact:session-state`) — is already fixed on current main: the fallback now routes to a fresh `gateway-fallback-<uuid>` session, matching the existing gateway-timeout fallback. That fix intentionally did **not** address the deeper question here ("should we re-run at all, or retrieve the real result first?"); fully suppressing the second run remains out of scope there. This issue is that deeper product question.

### Proposed solution

A **layered recovery** in the CLI fallback decision (`src/commands/agent-via-gateway.ts`): on *accepted + non-transient close*, reattach before re-running.

```
accepted + non-transient close
  → reconnect, agent.wait(acceptedRunId, timeoutMs)
      ├─ ok              → readLatestAssistantReply(acceptedSessionKey) → print → done   (single run, authoritative result)
      ├─ error           → surface the real failure
      └─ timeout/pending → fresh-session embedded fallback  (current main fallback, demoted to last resort)
```

The notable part is that **the primitives for this already exist and are used elsewhere** (e.g. the QA lab does `startAgentRun` → `waitForAgentRun`):

- Detached runs survive the connection drop (run lifecycle is owned server-side, not by the CLI socket).
- `agent.wait { runId, timeoutMs }` lets any/fresh connection await a run's terminal state by id — see `src/gateway/server-methods/agent-wait.ts` (`agentWaitHandler`).
- Terminal outcomes are cached server-side for ~10 min so a reconnecting client can still observe a completion after the live event stream moved on — see `src/gateway/server-methods/agent-job.ts` (`AGENT_RUN_CACHE_TTL_MS`).
- The reply text is recoverable from the transcript via `chat.history { sessionKey }` → `readLatestAssistantReply` in `src/agents/run-wait.ts`.
- Transport-drop errors (`1006`, `transport close`, `ECONNRESET`, …) are already classified recoverable by `isRecoverableAgentWaitError` in `src/agents/run-wait.ts`.

So this is a **CLI fallback redesign reusing existing gateway primitives**, not a new protocol. The same shape could also unify the gateway-*timeout* fallback (try reattach before re-running).

The one genuine gap: there is no "give me runId X's result payloads" RPC — the answer is reconstructed from the **session transcript tail** (latest assistant message for the sessionKey), which is a heuristic rather than a precise per-runId fetch. The layered version can ship on the existing transcript recovery; a clean `result-by-runId` RPC would be a nice follow-up but isn't required.

### Alternatives considered

1. **Keep recook-first (current main behavior).** Simplest. Guarantees the user always gets *a* result, and preserves live streaming/progress in the terminal. Cost: rare duplicate execution. For an interactive CLI on a rare disconnect, this may genuinely be the right product call.
2. **`in_flight` / no-local-result** (just report "already in flight" and return nothing). Achieves single execution but the user can get **no answer at all** on stdout when `--deliver` is not set — a regression for the primary use case. Weaker than both other options.
3. **Hybrid by mode.** `--deliver` runs do not stream to stdout (results go out through a channel), so for them "lose live streaming" basically doesn't apply → reattach-first is close to a pure win. Interactive stdout runs are where streaming loss hurts. A maintainer might pick **reattach-first for `--deliver`, recook-first for interactive**.

### Impact

- **Affected:** `openclaw agent` users on the gateway path (not `--local`), most likely on remote gateway deployments behind a proxy/load balancer on long-running turns, where the socket can drop between acceptance and the final frame.
- **Severity:** Medium — correctness (possibly divergent answer) + wasted cost (double model/tool execution) + possible double `--deliver`.
- **Frequency:** Edge case. The common gateway-loss modes don't trigger it (killing the gateway also kills its in-process run; a clean `1000` close is retried as transient).
- **Consequence:** Duplicate transcript turns (already fixed on main by the fresh-session fallback), duplicated model calls and tool side effects, and possible double delivery.

### Evidence/examples

Tradeoff summary:

| | Recook-first (current main) | Reattach-first (this proposal) |
|---|---|---|
| Executions | up to 2 | 1 in the common case |
| Result returned | locally re-run (may differ) | the authoritative gateway run |
| Live streaming/progress | yes (local run streams) | no (blocks until the detached run finishes) |
| Result retrieval | n/a | sessionKey transcript-tail heuristic |
| `--deliver` | possible double send | single send |
| Complexity | low | medium (wait/timeout/errored/tool-only/raw cases) |

Code references (`5ca5c5c1e0`):
- Current fresh-session recook fallback + accepted-disconnect routing: `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.ts`
- `in_flight` reply carries no result: `src/gateway/server-methods/agent-request-preflight.ts` (~`status: "in_flight"`)
- `agent.wait` handler: `src/gateway/server-methods/agent-wait.ts` (`agentWaitHandler`)
- Terminal-snapshot cache (~10 min): `src/gateway/server-methods/agent-job.ts`
- Transcript-based reply recovery + recoverable-error classification: `src/agents/run-wait.ts`

Related (closed, similar "lost final reply on disconnect" theme, not duplicates): #87808, #58569.

### Additional information

- This is **compatibility-sensitive**: it changes what `openclaw agent` shows on a disconnect (what stdout returns, streaming vs. blocking). Per the repo's contribution rules that's an owner/product decision, which is why this is an issue rather than a direct PR.
- **Relationship to the fresh-session fallback fix on main:** that fix is correct regardless of the decision here — even under reattach-first, its fresh-session path stays as the **last-resort layer**, so it is never wasted.
- Happy to implement whichever direction is chosen.

issues.body:
## Summary

Please add a small on/off option to make the TUI status line recording-friendly by disabling the live elapsed-seconds counter and animated spinner/shimmer while a request is running.

## Why this matters

This is useful for recording OpenClaw demos with asciinema/asciinema.org.

Asciinema and related tooling often rely on terminal inactivity / silence detection, or at least produce much cleaner casts when the terminal is not constantly repainting. Today the OpenClaw TUI status line keeps changing during waits/runs because of:

- the elapsed seconds counter (`0s`, `1s`, `2s`, ...),
- the loader/spinner,
- the animated waiting shimmer.

That means an otherwise idle screen is still constantly changing, which makes promotional/demo recordings noisier and interferes with clean pause/silence handling. For short marketing/demo casts, this is a surprising papercut: the actual assistant output may be still, but the footer keeps moving.

## Proposed UX

A simple boolean is enough, for example one of:

```jsonc
{
  "tui": {
    "quietStatus": true
  }
}
```

or, if the project prefers explicit naming:

```jsonc
{
  "tui": {
    "animateStatus": false,
    "showStatusElapsedSeconds": false
  }
}
```

A slash command would also be handy for temporary recording sessions:

```text
/tui-status quiet on
/tui-status quiet off
```

But config-only would already solve the core problem.

## Suggested implementation

The current behavior appears to live in `src/tui/tui.ts` / built output around the busy status rendering:

- `formatElapsed(startMs)` formats seconds/minutes,
- `ensureStatusLoader()` creates a `Loader`,
- `startStatusTimer()` updates every second,
- `startWaitingTimer()` updates shimmer every ~120ms,
- `buildWaitingStatusMessage(...)` includes `elapsed`.

A minimal implementation could:

1. Add a TUI config boolean, e.g. `tui.quietStatus` default `false`.
2. When enabled:
   - render busy status with plain `Text` instead of `Loader`, or make loader spinner text empty/static,
   - omit elapsed seconds from the message,
   - skip the fast waiting shimmer timer,
   - only update status on state changes, not every second/tick.
3. Keep existing behavior as the default.

Example quiet messages:

```text
waiting | connected
streaming | connected
running | connected
```

No elapsed counter, no spinner, no animated shimmer, no repaint loop while nothing meaningful changes.

## Benefit

This keeps normal TUI users unchanged, while giving demo/recording workflows a clean, stable terminal surface for asciinema casts and marketing videos.

issues.body:
### Version

`openclaw 2026.4.20 (115f05d)`, also matches behavior described in the `2026.5.4` CHANGELOG.

### Problem

Different `--json` subcommands return different envelope shapes for "list things":

| Command | Shape |
|---|---|
| `openclaw agents list --json` | bare array `[ {...}, ... ]` |
| `openclaw sessions --json` | `{ "path": "...", "count": N, "activeMinutes": null, "sessions": [...] }` |
| `openclaw models list --json` | `{ "count": N, "models": [ {...} ] }` |
| `openclaw cron list --json` (per downstream consumers) | array OR `{jobs: [...]}` OR `{cron: [...]}` |
| `openclaw nodes list --json` | array OR `{nodes: [...]}` |
| `openclaw skills list --json` | array OR `{skills: [...]}` |

(The bottom three are inferred from defensive duck-typing in our consumer code; the top three I just verified live on `2026.4.20`.)

This forces every JSON consumer to write something like:

```ts
const items = Array.isArray(data) ? data : (data.items ?? data.agents ?? data.sessions ?? data.jobs ?? data.cron ?? []);
```

which both ages poorly and silently swallows real errors.

### Proposal

Standardize `--json` list output on a versioned envelope, e.g.:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://openclaw.ai/schemas/list-v1.json",
  "version": "1",
  "kind": "agents",
  "count": 42,
  "items": [ {} ],
  "meta": { "//": "command-specific extras like sessions.path, sessions.activeMinutes" }
}
```

Migration path:

- One release ships both shapes; new shape is opt-in via `--json-envelope=v1`.
- One release flips the default; old shape stays available via `--json-envelope=legacy`.
- One release removes legacy.

### Why this matters

We ship a desktop frontend (Crystal: https://github.com/jvpflum/Crystal) on top of OpenClaw with ~30 views that consume these subcommands. We currently maintain ~12 different defensive shape-coercion blocks. This is a paper-cut for every frontend / CI / SDK author that wraps the CLI.

Happy to draft the schema + back-compat flag if the design lands.

### Related

Closed #73077 ("parent CLI commands exit 1 when invoked without a subcommand") and the ongoing CLI-stabilization theme suggest this is in scope.

issues.body:
## Problem

When OpenClaw runs as a headless gateway (gateway.mode set), `memorySearch.sync.watch` defaults to `true`, which creates a chokidar file watcher for every memory file and extra path. On a multi-agent gateway this leaks file descriptors — we observed 1,292 chokidar watchers on a single instance.

Interactive desktop use benefits from near-real-time reindexing on file change. A headless gateway with many agents does not — files rarely change externally, and the FD cost is disproportionate.

## Proposed Change

Default `sync.watch` to `false` when the process detects it is running in gateway mode (i.e., when `gateway.mode` is set to any non-CLI value).

Falling back:
- `agents.defaults.memorySearch.sync.watch` → `false` when gateway mode
- Explicit `sync.watch: true` in config still wins (user override)
- No change to CLI/desktop behavior (watch remains `true` by default)

### Alternative considered
Replace chokidar `awaitWriteFinish` polling with native FSEvents on macOS to avoid per-file FD allocation. This would help on macOS but not on Linux gateways, and does not address the fundamental problem of O(n) watchers per agent.

## Impact

- Reduces FD consumption on gateway deployments from O(agents × files) to near-zero for the watch subsystem
- No behavior change for desktop/CLI users
- Users who want watch in gateway mode can opt in explicitly

## Workaround

Set `sync.watch: false` in `openclaw.json` under `agents.defaults.memorySearch.sync`. This is already documented in the schema help text but should be the default for gateway mode.

Related: #64549 (watch does not auto-index new files — separate bug, but same subsystem)

issues.body:
## Summary
On Linux, broad file-system search commands run via the OpenClaw `exec` tool are repeatedly terminated with `SIGKILL` / `terminated`, even though normal narrow commands and file `read`/`edit` flows continue to work.

This does **not** currently look like a kernel OOM kill on the host. `journalctl -k` did not show matching OOM / killed-process evidence during the failures.

## Impact
This makes the agent unreliable for repo/workspace discovery tasks unless it avoids broad `find` / `grep -R` style commands and falls back to narrow path reads.

## Observed behavior
The failures are most common with commands like:
- broad `find` over large trees
- `grep -R` over large trees
- searches spanning `/home/.../work` or other large directory roots

What still works reliably:
- `read` on already-known file paths
- `edit` / `write`
- narrow `exec` commands in small directories
- direct one-shot `python3 runner/...` commands against known files

Example symptoms seen in chat/system messages:
- `Exec failed (..., signal SIGKILL)`
- `terminated`

## Important negative finding
I checked kernel logs during the session:
- `journalctl -k --since '2026-04-20 00:00:00' | grep -Ei 'killed process|out of memory|oom|sigkill'`
- no relevant OOM / kill evidence appeared

So this currently looks more like an OpenClaw exec/supervisor-layer termination than a host OOM killer event.

## Environment
- OpenClaw version: `2026.4.19-beta.2`
- Host OS: Linux (`Linux 6.17.0-20-generic (x64)`)
- Shell: bash
- Session type: main agent session via Telegram surface

## Reproduction pattern
Not every command fails. The pattern is:
1. Run one or more broad search-style exec commands over a large directory tree
2. Some of them get terminated with `SIGKILL` / `terminated`
3. Narrower commands still work afterwards

Representative commands that were problematic:
```bash
find /home/.../work -maxdepth 6 \( -type d -iname '*bundle*' -o -type d -iname '*backtest*' -o -type d -iname '*strategy*' -o -type d -iname '*kis*' -o -type d -iname '*codex*' \)
grep -R "..." -n /large/tree
```

Representative commands that remained okay:
```bash
python3 runner/reflection_writer.py ...
python3 runner/healthcheck_runner.py
```

## Expected behavior
- Broad search commands should either complete normally or fail with a clear resource/timeout explanation
- They should not be silently or abruptly killed with `SIGKILL` / `terminated` while the host shows no OOM evidence

## Actual behavior
- Broad search exec commands are intermittently killed
- This creates noisy system messages and forces workflow changes inside the agent

## Workaround
Current safe workaround is:
1. avoid broad `find` / `grep -R`
2. prefer direct `read` on known paths
3. split discovery into much smaller directory scopes

## Notes
This may be related to the broader family of exec/SIGKILL issues, but this Linux case seems specifically tied to broad search/discovery commands rather than OpenClaw CLI subcommands themselves.

issues.body:
## Summary

Background `exec` runs launched with `pty: true` appear to rely on in-memory-only ownership. If the gateway restarts or otherwise loses run state, the PTY-backed worker tree can remain alive while OpenClaw no longer knows about it. In practice this looks like orphaned Codex/OMX/MCP helper trees continuing to consume memory even when `process list` reports no running sessions.

## Observed behavior

On a live macOS install, I observed repeated helper-process families rooted under a long-lived Codex worker, including:

- repeated `npm exec mcp-remote https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/...`
- repeated `npm exec mcp-remote https://mcp.exa.ai/mcp`
- repeated `npm exec mcp-remote https://api.ref.tools/mcp`
- repeated OMX sidecars such as:
  - `oh-my-codex/dist/mcp/code-intel-server.js`
  - `trace-server.js`
  - `state-server.js`
  - `memory-server.js`
  - `team-server.js`

At one point the repeated remote MCP fingerprints showed 12 copies each for Firecrawl / Exa / Ref, all under a Codex-rooted worker tree, while OpenClaw runtime state did **not** show a corresponding tracked run:

- `~/.openclaw/subagents/runs.json` was empty (`{"version":2,"runs":{}}`)
- `process(action="list")` returned `No running or recent sessions.`

That combination strongly suggests a live worker tree can outlive tracked ownership.

## Why this looks like an OpenClaw lifecycle bug

The supervisor implementation currently documents orphan reconciliation as a deliberate no-op:

- `src/process/supervisor/supervisor.ts`
  - `reconcileOrphans(): Promise<void>`
  - comment: `Deliberate no-op: this supervisor uses in-memory ownership only. Active runs are not recovered after process restart in the current model.`

Relevant launch-path differences:

### Generic exec PTY path

- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-runtime.ts`
  - `runExecProcess(...)`
  - when `usePty` is true, this spawns with `mode: "pty"`
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec.ts`
  - background runs can end up with `effectiveTimeout = null` when `backgroundTimeoutBypass` applies
- I do not see the same explicit scope-replacement semantics here that the CLI-runner path uses

### CLI-runner path

- `src/agents/cli-runner/execute.ts`
  - uses `mode: "child"`
  - passes `scopeKey`
  - passes `replaceExistingScope: Boolean(useResume && scopeKey)`
  - passes `noOutputTimeoutMs`

### Process visibility path

- `src/agents/bash-tools.process.ts`
  - `process list` is driven from in-memory session/registry state
- `src/agents/bash-process-registry.ts`
  - running/finished sessions are also in-memory maps

So if the gateway restarts, reloads, or otherwise loses that state, OpenClaw can truthfully report no running sessions while the actual PTY child tree is still alive.

## Why this matters

This can produce a bad failure mode for long-lived Codex/OMX workers launched through generic background PTY exec:

1. worker is launched and tracked only in memory
2. gateway restarts or loses run state
3. worker tree survives
4. OpenClaw forgets it
5. Codex/OMX inside that still-living worker can reopen/reconnect MCP helpers over time
6. helper processes accumulate and total memory climbs

Even if Codex/OMX has its own cleanup bug, OpenClaw currently appears to make that failure mode much worse by allowing PTY-backed background workers to become unowned.

## Proposed fix direction

### Minimum viable fix

1. Persist active background exec metadata for PTY-backed runs
   - run id
   - pid
   - scope key
   - session id
   - backend id
   - started at
2. Implement real `reconcileOrphans()` on startup
3. On startup, kill or re-register stale PTY-backed runs from a previous gateway epoch
4. Remove persisted records on normal finalize

### Additional hardening

1. Add explicit scope replacement for long-lived PTY background runs where a stable scope exists
2. Add a default `noOutputTimeoutMs` / watchdog for background PTY runs instead of letting them drift forever when no explicit timeout is set
3. Add lifecycle logging around:
   - PTY spawn
   - scope replacement / cancellation
   - finalize
   - orphan sweep results

## Files / code points inspected

- `src/process/supervisor/supervisor.ts`
- `src/process/supervisor/adapters/pty.ts`
- `src/process/supervisor/adapters/child.ts`
- `src/process/supervisor/registry.ts`
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-runtime.ts`
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec.ts`
- `src/agents/bash-tools.process.ts`
- `src/agents/cli-runner/execute.ts`
- `src/agents/bash-process-registry.ts`

## Important note

I am **not** claiming the entire leak is only OpenClaw. It is possible Codex/OMX is also failing to clean up helper bundles inside a still-running worker. But OpenClaw currently appears to have a real ownership / cleanup gap for background PTY exec runs that can leave those workers alive but untracked after restart or session-state loss.

If helpful, I can open a follow-up PR once there is agreement on whether the preferred behavior is:

- kill stale PTY exec orphans on startup, or
- attempt to reattach / re-register them.

issues.body:
## Feature request

Allow context engine plugins to contribute status information to the TUI footer bar.

### Current state

The TUI footer displays: agent name, session, model, token count. There's no way for plugins (especially context engine plugins) to add their own status indicators.

Currently, the only way to show context engine stats (like "17.9M tokens saved ($53.74)") in the TUI is to monkeypatch `tui-Dl-T6b_3.js`, which breaks on every update.

### Proposed API

Add a `registerStatusProvider` method to the plugin API:

```ts
// In plugin setup
runtime.registerStatusProvider('contextclaw', () => ({
  label: 'ContextClaw',
  text: '17.9M tokens saved ($53.74)',
  // optional: urgency/color for alerts
  level: 'info' // 'info' | 'warn' | 'error'
}));
```

The TUI would poll registered status providers and append their output to the footer bar.

### Use cases

- Context engine stats (tokens saved, compression ratio)
- Provider health indicators (ties into #64085)
- Plugin-specific status (MCP server health, memory stats, etc.)
- Any plugin that wants to surface a small status indicator

### Why this matters

Context engines are a first-class plugin type in OpenClaw, but they're invisible to the user during normal operation. A status footer contribution lets users see that their context engine is working and what value it's providing — without needing to run `/status` or check logs.

### Additional context

I maintain [ContextClaw](https://github.com/dodge1218/contextclaw) and currently monkeypatch the TUI to show savings stats. Happy to help implement this if there's appetite for it.

issues.body:
## Problem

The `.github/workflows/ci.yml` file has grown to 800+ lines with complex conditional matrices and scattered job dependencies. The preflight job alone outputs 20+ different conditions that downstream jobs consume using brittle `if: always() && needs.x.outputs.y == 'true'` chains.

## Current Pain Points

1. **Hard to reason about** — Adding a new platform or check requires touching multiple sections
2. **Duplicated boilerplate** — Node setup + artifact download pattern repeated in ~10 jobs
3. **Fragile dependencies** — The matrix output pattern creates tight coupling between jobs
4. **Review difficulty** — Changes to CI logic require understanding the entire file context

## Specific Examples

From `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:

```yaml
# Lines 30-50: Preflight outputs 20+ conditions
outputs:
  docs_only: ${{ steps.manifest.outputs.docs_only }}
  docs_changed: ${{ steps.manifest.outputs.docs_changed }}
  run_node: ${{ steps.manifest.outputs.run_node }}
  run_macos: ${{ steps.manifest.outputs.run_macos }}
  # ... 17 more outputs

# Lines 200-250: Downstream jobs check these conditions
if: always() && needs.preflight.outputs.run_checks == 'true' && needs.build-artifacts.result == 'success'
```

## Proposed Solution

### Phase 1: Extract Matrix Definitions

Create `.github/matrices/` directory with JSON configs:

```json
// .github/matrices/node-tests.json
{
  "include": [
    { "check_name": "test (shard 1/3)", "task": "test", "shard_count": 3, "shard_index": 1 },
    { "check_name": "test (shard 2/3)", "task": "test", "shard_count": 3, "shard_index": 2 },
    { "check_name": "test (shard 3/3)", "task": "test", "shard_count": 3, "shard_index": 3 },
    { "check_name": "channels", "task": "channels" }
  ]
}
```

Reference in workflow:
```yaml
strategy:
  matrix: ${{ fromJson(needs.preflight.outputs.checks_matrix) }}
```

### Phase 2: Create Reusable Workflows

Extract common patterns to `.github/workflows/_setup-node.yml`:

```yaml
# .github/workflows/_setup-node.yml
name: Setup Node Environment
on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      node-version:
        type: string
        default: '24.x'
      install-bun:
        type: string
        default: 'false'
    outputs:
      cache-hit:
        value: ${{ steps.cache.outputs.cache-hit }}

jobs:
  setup:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup-node-env
        with:
          node-version: ${{ inputs.node-version }}
          install-bun: ${{ inputs.install-bun }}
```

### Phase 3: Simplify Main Workflow

Target structure:
```yaml
jobs:
  preflight:
    uses: ./.github/workflows/_preflight.yml
  
  checks-fast:
    needs: preflight
    if: needs.preflight.outputs.run_checks_fast
    uses: ./.github/workflows/_checks-fast.yml
    with:
      matrix: ${{ needs.preflight.outputs.checks_fast_matrix }}
  
  checks:
    needs: [preflight, build-artifacts]
    if: needs.preflight.outputs.run_checks
    uses: ./.github/workflows/_checks.yml
    with:
      matrix: ${{ needs.preflight.outputs.checks_matrix }}
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `.github/workflows/ci.yml` reduced to <300 lines
- [ ] Matrix definitions extracted to JSON files
- [ ] At least 3 reusable workflow patterns extracted
- [ ] No functional changes to CI behavior (verify with test PR)
- [ ] Documentation added in `.github/workflows/README.md`

## References

- Current CI: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
- Related: Composite actions in `.github/actions/`

---

### Bug type

No

### Summary

Signing in with OpenAI through the Control UI's Model Setup enables the bundled Codex plugin ("codex agent runtime configured, enabled automatically") on an install that has no managed `@openclaw/codex`, and the gateway's session observer then logs `Managed Codex app-server binary was not found for @openai/codex. Reinstall or update OpenClaw…` even though the turns run fine.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Fresh install (2026.9.1, official image), no `@openclaw/codex` installed.
2. Control UI → Model Setup → sign in with OpenAI (the ChatGPT-subscription OAuth) and complete it in the browser.
3. Send a message; watch the gateway log.

### Expected behavior

The panel's OpenAI sign-in either performs the same on-demand Codex install that the CLI's OpenAI onboarding does (the package's own QA scenario `codex-plugin-cold-install`), or does not enable the plugin; and the observer's message says whether the turn is affected.

### Actual behavior

The plugin is enabled without its runtime; the observer logs the "not found … Reinstall or update OpenClaw" line once; the turns themselves run on the embedded runtime's `openai-chatgpt-responses` route without error.

### OpenClaw version

`2026.9.1` (commit `ad6fe23`), the official Docker image `ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw:2026.9.1-browser`

### Operating system

the image's Debian, in Docker on an Ubuntu 24.04 host

### Install method

Docker Compose; onboarding by `openclaw onboard --non-interactive`

### Model

`openai/gpt-5.6-sol` through the ChatGPT-subscription sign-in.

### Provider / routing chain

OpenAI (ChatGPT OAuth via the Control UI) → `gpt-5.6-sol`; an OpenRouter route configured beside it, not in the chain.

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell
`codex agent runtime configured, enabled automatically` at sign-in; `Managed Codex app-server binary was not found for @openai/codex. Reinstall or update OpenClaw…` from the session observer at the first turn.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

Every owner who connects a ChatGPT subscription through the panel rather than the CLI. Nothing fails, but the log tells them to reinstall OpenClaw for a problem that does not affect them, and a plugin is enabled that has nothing to run. Related: #139527 and #124137 concern the managed Codex binary's presence on other paths.

### Additional information

Observed on `2026.9.1`, official `-browser` image, Docker Compose on Ubuntu 24.04.

issues.body:
## Summary

When a `message` tool call **fails** (e.g. `Network request for 'sendMessage' failed`) and is then **retried** in the same turn, both the retry tool call AND the text reply are delivered to the user. This produces duplicate messages.

## Root cause (traced in source)

In `shouldSuppressMessagingToolReplies` (pi-embedded, `reply-payloads-dedupe.ts`):

```js
// Only records target when tool SUCCEEDS
if (!isToolError) {
  ctx.state.messagingToolSentTargets.push(pendingTarget);
}
```

Because the first (failed) tool call is never recorded into `messagingToolSentTargets`, when the retry fires, `shouldSuppressMessagingToolReplies` returns `false`, so the text reply is **not suppressed** — even though the retry message tool call is also in the same turn.

## Repro sequence (from session logs 2026-03-26)

```
[19:59:04] ASS → message tool call (1st attempt)
[19:59:14] TOOL → { "status": "error", "error": "Network request for sendMessage failed" }
[19:59:23] ASS → message tool call (retry, same turn)
[19:59:24] ASS → text reply auto-delivered (suppress did not fire — no entry in sentTargets yet)
[19:59:24] TOOL → { "ok": true, "messageId": "22864" }
```

User receives **two** messages with the same content within 2 seconds.

## Proposed fix

Record the **pending** target into `messagingToolSentTargets` (or a parallel pending set) **when the tool call starts**, not only when it succeeds. This way, if the same turn contains a retry + text reply, the suppress mechanism will correctly fire even if the first attempt failed.

Alternatively, record a `pendingMessagingTarget` immediately on tool call start and check it in the suppress logic regardless of success/failure.

## Impact

- Causes duplicate messages when Telegram API has transient failures (common with proxy setups).
- Forces users to remove retry rules from AGENTS.md to avoid duplicates, at the cost of losing genuine failure recovery.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.3.24 (cff6dc9)
- Telegram channel
- Observed consistently with `message` tool action=send
