issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

An empty legacy `auth_profile_store` table in the per-agent SQLite makes every agent request fail with AUTH_PROFILE_MIGRATION_REQUIRED, while dropping that same table makes startup migrations fail and the gateway refuse to become ready, so no database state satisfies both checks.

### Steps to reproduce

Starting state (observed on our install): `agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite` has table `auth_profile_store` with one row `('primary', '{"version":1,"profiles":{}}')` — an empty profile set. `state/openclaw.sqlite` has four `auth-profile-v2:*` rows in `migration_runs` marked `completed`, whose `report_json.targetTable` is `auth_profile_stores`, but that table does not exist in the database.
1. Send any message to the agent. Every request fails with AUTH_PROFILE_MIGRATION_REQUIRED.
2. Run `openclaw doctor --fix`, and separately `openclaw doctor --fix --force` (offline, container stopped). Both report `Failed relocating the shared auth store: shared auth credential rows conflict with the relocation target` and only archive the legacy JSON again. Requests still fail.
3. Delete the single row from `auth_profile_store`, leaving the table. Requests still fail with the same error, so the block is triggered by the table existing, not by its content.
4. Drop the `auth_profile_store` table. `openclaw models auth list` now works for the first time, but the gateway refuses to start: `OpenClaw startup migrations did not complete cleanly; refusing to report the gateway ready.` / `Skipped historical transcript directive migration ... SQLite schema is incomplete or noncanonical ... missing table auth_profile_store` / `OpenClaw exited with code 1`.
5. Recreate `auth_profile_store` empty and create `auth_profile_stores` in the state DB with one row `('shared', '{"version":1,"profiles":{}}')`. The gateway boots and reports ready, but requests fail again with AUTH_PROFILE_MIGRATION_REQUIRED.
6. Delete the four `auth-profile-v2:*` rows from `migration_runs`, plus the orphaned `migration_sources` rows. `doctor --fix` now performs a real migration (`Migrated auth profile JSON for ...`) but ends with `Failed relocating the shared auth store: shared auth state rows conflict with the relocation target`. Requests still fail.

### Expected behavior

A legacy store holding an empty profile set (`"profiles":{}`) should be treated as having nothing to migrate and retired, letting requests proceed. When a `migration_runs` receipt is marked `completed` but its `targetTable` does not exist, `doctor --fix` should be able to reconcile that state rather than reporting a relocation conflict on every run. Before the legacy store entered this state, this same install answered Telegram messages normally on the same config and credentials.

### Actual behavior

100% of agent requests fail. The gateway reports ready and Telegram polling runs normally, but each inbound message produces, in the gateway log: `lane task error: lane=main ... error="Couldn't sign in to deepseek. Your saved login looks expired or no longer works. ... (Auth profile store ~/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite requires legacy credential migration; run openclaw doctor --fix.) | AUTH_PROFILE_MIGRATION_REQUIRED"`, then `Embedded agent failed before reply`, and the user receives only the generic fallback "Something went wrong while processing your request. Please try again, or use /new to start a fresh session." The fallback model is attempted and fails identically, so the failure is independent of the provider. `openclaw models auth list --agent main` fails with the same error, so there is no CLI path to inspect or repair the profiles. Docker reports the container as `healthy` throughout. This has been ongoing for over two weeks; each `doctor --fix` run buys a shorter working window than the last (from ~30-90 minutes down to a single message) and leaves another `auth-profiles.json.migrated-*` archive behind (14 accumulated so far).

### OpenClaw version

2026.8.2 (0965053)

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04 (container), host Ubuntu 24.04 LTS on a KVM VPS

### Install method

docker (image ghcr.io/hostinger/hvps-openclaw:latest, docker compose)

### Model

deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash, fallback openrouter/google/gemma-4-31b-it:free

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> deepseek (direct), fallback openclaw -> openrouter

### Additional provider/model setup details

Four agents are configured (main, claude, gpt, gemini); the failing one is main. Both providers are custom OpenAI-completions-compatible entries under `models.providers` in openclaw.json with inline API keys, so the working credentials never lived in the auth profile store that is blocking them — the store being migrated is empty. The `migration_runs` receipts reference archive paths such as `/data/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/auth-profiles.json.migrated-<timestamp>-<uuid>`. The `auth_profile_state` table in the same per-agent DB holds only provider usage stats (a DeepSeek billing cooldown), and it is that table which produces the "shared auth state rows conflict" in step 6.

### Logs

```shell
Per-message failure (gateway log, timestamps local -04:00):
[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=main durationMs=32 error="Couldn't sign in to deepseek. Your saved login looks expired or no longer works. Run `openclaw models auth login --provider deepseek` or `openclaw configure`. (Auth profile store ~/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite requires legacy credential migration; run openclaw doctor --fix.) | AUTH_PROFILE_MIGRATION_REQUIRED"
[model-fallback/decision] model fallback decision: decision=candidate_failed requested=deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash candidate=openrouter/google/gemma-4-31b-it:free reason=auth next=none detail=Couldn't sign in to openrouter ... | AUTH_PROFILE_MIGRATION_REQUIRED
Embedded agent failed before reply: Auth profile store ~/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite requires legacy credential migration; run openclaw doctor --fix.
[diagnostic] message dispatch completed: channel=telegram ... outcome=error

doctor --fix / --fix --force (steps 2 and 5):
[state-migrations] Legacy state migration warnings:
- Failed relocating the shared auth store: Error: shared auth credential rows conflict with the relocation target
Doctor changes: Archived a previously migrated legacy auth source without replaying credentials (~/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/auth-profiles.json.migrated-...).

Gateway refusing to start with the table dropped (step 4):
OpenClaw startup migrations did not complete cleanly; refusing to report the gateway ready.
- Skipped historical transcript directive migration for /data/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite: Error: SQLite schema is incomplete or noncanonical for /data/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite: missing table auth_profile_store
Run "openclaw doctor --fix" against the same state/config, then restart the gateway.
WARN: OpenClaw exited with code 1

doctor --fix after clearing the receipts (step 6):
[state-migrations] Auto-migrated legacy state:
[state-migrations] Legacy state migration warnings:
```

_No response_

issues.body:
## Summary

When using `google/gemini-2.5-pro` via the `google-generative-ai` API, three issues combine to cause rapid session context bloat, aborted runs, and silent Telegram delivery failures.

## Issue 1: textSignature Session Bloat (High Severity)

Gemini assistant responses include a `textSignature` field containing ~15KB of base64 data per response turn. OpenClaw stores these signatures verbatim in the session JSONL history. After 10+ turns, the accumulated signatures alone consume 150KB+, causing:

1. Context window bloat (observed: 416K tokens in one session)
2. Gemini API timeouts on re-submission of full context
3. Compaction failures (session too large to compact)
4. Silent message delivery failures (run aborts before reply is sent to Telegram)

**Expected:** `textSignature` should either not be stored in session history, be stored separately, or not be re-sent to the model on subsequent turns.

## Issue 2: Embedded `<think>` Tags in Text

Gemini 2.5 Pro embeds `<think>...</think>` tags directly in the `text` content field (not as separate `thinking` type blocks). If OpenClaw treats `<think>`-prefixed text as internal/thinking content, the reply is suppressed and never delivered to Telegram.

**Expected:** OpenClaw should either strip `<think>` tags from the delivered text, or not suppress messages that contain them.

## Issue 3: Mixed Text + ToolCall in Same Response

Gemini 2.5 Pro consistently emits text + toolCall in the same response turn. OpenClaw processes the toolCall, gets the result, then emits an empty `content: []` as the final stop. The original text from the first part of the response is never delivered to the user.

**Expected:** Text content from a mixed text+toolCall response should be delivered to the user, not silently dropped.

## Reproduction

1. Configure an agent with `google/gemini-2.5-pro` as primary model
2. Send 5-10 interactive messages via Telegram group topic
3. Check session JSONL — each assistant message contains `textSignature` (~15KB base64)
4. After ~10 exchanges, session reaches 150K+ tokens
5. Subsequent runs timeout or abort; replies never reach Telegram

## Workaround

Switched affected agent to Claude Sonnet 4.6, which does not exhibit these behaviors.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.3.13 (61d171a)
- macOS Darwin 24.6.0 (arm64)
- Gemini API key auth (google-generative-ai provider)
- Telegram channel with group topics

issues.body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
When using certain models, the generation can occasionally get stuck in an infinite loop, spamming the exact same phrase (e.g., "Done, I will output it") endlessly. This floods chat channels with identical lines of text and wastes tokens.

### Describe the solution you'd like
Implement a stream-level repetition safeguard in the core daemon's streaming handler. 
1. Maintain a sliding window/buffer of recent stream chunks.
2. Count the number of sequential identical responses/phrases.
3. If the count exceeds a threshold (e.g., 20 repetitions), **halt the LLM stream immediately**.
4. Pause execution and send an alert to the user instead of the spammed text (e.g., "⚠️ Output paused: Detected 20 repeating sequences.").
5. Require manual confirmation from the user (e.g., `/approve` to resume or `/cancel` to abort) before continuing.

### Describe alternatives you've considered
- Relying solely on `frequency_penalty` or `presence_penalty` (not always supported by every provider or fully reliable).
- Hard `max_tokens` limits (doesn't stop the loop immediately, just caps the total spam).

### Additional context
This would act as a circuit breaker for LLM hallucination loops. By monitoring the output stream directly, we save tokens and prevent endless spam in the chat channel before the generation finishes.

issues.body:
### Summary

Startup got materially **slower** after upgrading from 2026.9.9 to 2026.10.1 on the same Windows host: `gateway ready` went from a ~410 s baseline mean (489 s measured T0→ready) to **~1030 s**, reproducible across two consecutive hot boots. A previously invisible phase, `sidecars.control-ui-assets`, now spans **~477 s** per boot.

The release notes say startup with installed plugins was improved ("large plugins start without multi-minute stalls"), so this may be a local interaction or a regression — either way the numbers below are from a clean, disk-uncontended run.

### Environment

- Windows 11, Node v24.18.0 (nvm), `npm i -g openclaw@latest` → 2026.10.1 (e178c39)
- Gateway: scheduled task, loopback+token, heartbeat off, 13 non-bundled+bundled plugins enabled (acpx ~655 MB capture, tavily, tencent-weixin, ollama, memory-wiki, workboard, cua-computer, browser …)
- `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_STARTUP_TRACE=1` in the launcher; T0 = `schtasks /Run`; ready = first `gateway ready` log line after T0
- After the upgrade: install unified with `gateway install --force`, plugin generations refreshed (tavily 2026.10.1, weixin 2.4.10), asset cache rebuilt once on boot 1

### Measurements (same host, same config)

| # | scenario | port listen | T0 → ready | top phases (duration / total) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | first boot after upgrade | 432 s | **914 s** | runtime.post-attach 453 s, plugins.runtime-post-bind 421 s, config.snapshot.auto-enable 299 s, secret-preflight 73 s |
| 2 | hot reboot | 504 s | **1028 s** | sidecars.control-ui-assets 480 s, plugins.runtime-post-bind 458 s, auto-enable 335 s, secret-preflight 70 s |
| 3 | hot reboot, disk uncontended | 528 s | **1039 s** | sidecars.control-ui-assets 477 s, plugins.runtime-post-bind 456 s, auto-enable 374 s, secret-preflight 69 s |

For comparison, the same trace on **2026.9.9** (same host/config, 2026-10-08) had `ready` at ~308–410 s of phases and `sidecars.control-ui-assets` did not appear in the top-12 phases at all (<1.1 s).

### What control-ui-assets is doing

- `eventLoopMax=0.0ms` for the whole 477 s — pure wait, no CPU.
- The state-side asset cache (`~/.openclaw/cache/control-ui-assets`, 67 MB / 1039 files) was fully rebuilt on boot 1 (files stamped at ready time), but boots 2 and 3 did **not** rewrite it — yet still spent ~477 s in this sidecar.
- Both installs ship `dist/control-ui` (~53 MB), so the assets are present; something in verification/copy is waiting.
- `sidecars.total` reports only ~20 s of actual work while `sidecars.control-ui-assets` reports a 477 s span — suggesting the phase duration includes waiting on dependencies rather than doing work.

### Exclusions measured on this host (so these are NOT the time)

- Disk uncontended on boot 3: 97 GB free; the old 252 GB `plugin-captures` accumulation is gone (now 2 dirs / 3.3 GB).
- Capture reuse is working: boot 3 created exactly **one** new capture dir, 32 s — so `plugins.runtime-post-bind` at 456 s is not raw copying.
- Provider endpoints, file enumeration, and reindex locks were measured earlier and are seconds-scale (see #160959 comments by me on 2026-10-08).
- `config.snapshot.auto-enable` remains unpatched (was 237 s on 2026.9.9, now 374 s) — tracked under this issue.

### Health after boot 3

models.list 19 entries (incl. custom `opencode-go/muse-spark-1.3-contributor`), primary model unchanged, 13/13 plugins loaded, zero ERROR lines during boot. The gateway works — it is just ~2.5x slower to become usable.

### Ask

1. Is `sidecars.control-ui-assets` expected to block `ready` for ~8 minutes? What is it waiting on (the 20 s of work inside a 477 s span)?
2. Please capture a startup trace on 2026.10.1 with installed plugins on Windows to confirm/reject the regression vs 2026.9.9.
3. Happy to run `OPENCLAW_DIAGNOSTICS_EVENT_LOOP=1` + timeline, `NODE_DEBUG_NATIVE=COMPILE_CACHE`, or any env-gated probe you provide and post the output.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

The Feishu channel receives incoming DMs but fails to send replies, while token acquisition returns business error 21001 (“Access denied by access control policy”) and no token.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use the affected Docker deployment running OpenClaw 2026.6.10 (aa69b12), with the @openclaw/feishu plugin and existing Feishu credentials.
2. Send a direct message to the configured Feishu bot.
3. Check the gateway log: the message is received and dispatched to the agent, but the final reply fails with Feishu error 99991661.
4. Request a token separately using the currently configured credentials: the diagnostic result shows HTTP 200, business code 21001, and no token.

Reproduction from a clean installation has not been verified.

### Expected behavior

The official Feishu documentation describes support for bot direct messages and replies:
https://docs.openclaw.ai/channels/feishu

For an application permitted to obtain an access token, incoming DMs should receive replies. Whether this application's access control policy permits token issuance has not yet been established.

### Actual behavior

The gateway receives Feishu DMs and dispatches them to the agent, but replies fail.

Logs repeatedly show:
- failed to obtain token
- Token error: Access denied by access control policy. Contact the administrator for assistance.
- Final reply failure with Feishu code 99991661: Missing access token for authorization.

A separate token request using the current credentials returns HTTP 200 with business code 21001 and no token.

### OpenClaw version

2026.6.10 (aa69b12)

### Operating system

Linux inside Docker; exact distribution/version not yet collected.

### Install method

Docker deployment. OpenClaw is installed under /usr/local/lib/node_modules/openclaw; @openclaw/feishu is loaded from a workspace-local npm installation.

### Model

kimi/kimi-2.7

### Provider / routing chain

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Additional provider/model setup details

The observed failure is in the Feishu API authentication path. A separate token request also fails outside the agent reply flow.

### Logs

```shell
Observed on 2026-10-15, timezone UTC+08:00.

17:29:47 — feishu[default]: received message from <redacted> in <redacted> (p2p)
17:29:47 — feishu[default]: dispatching to agent
17:29:53 — feishu[default]: streaming start failed; using non-streaming card fallback for 60s:
Error: Token error: Access denied by access control policy. Contact the administrator for assistance.

17:33:19 — feishu[default]: received message from <redacted> in <redacted> (p2p)
17:33:28 — feishu[default] final reply failed:
http_status: 400
feishu_code: 99991661
feishu_msg: Missing access token for authorization. Please make a request with token attached.

Repeated warnings:
failed to obtain token
feishu[default]: bot open_id resolved: unknown

The bot identity request also fails with HTTP 400:
POST https://open.feishu.cn/open-apis/bot/v1/openclaw_bot/ping

Sanitized diagnostic output from a separate token request
(this is a diagnostic summary, not the raw HTTP response):

{
  "accountId": "default",
  "appId": "<redacted>",
  "httpStatus": 200,
  "code": 21001,
  "msg": "Access denied by access control policy. Contact the administrator for assistance.",
  "tokenPresent": false,
  "expire": null
}
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

The Logs section contains excerpts from /tmp/openclaw/openclaw-2026-10-15.log and the sanitized result of a separate token request.

Official Feishu setup documentation:
https://docs.openclaw.ai/channels/feishu/setup

### Impact and severity

Affected: The observed Feishu default account in one Docker deployment.
Severity: Blocks bot replies in the affected conversations.
Frequency: Repeated failures in the supplied log, including incoming messages at 17:29 and 17:33 on 2026-10-15 (UTC+08:00). Behavior outside the observed period is not established.
Consequence: Incoming DMs reach the agent, but outgoing replies fail.

### Additional information

Feishu domain: feishu.cn.
Connection mode: WebSocket.
Node.js version recorded in logs: 24.18.0.
The exact independently installed @openclaw/feishu package version has not yet been collected.

Our platform launches the Feishu setup command through a PTY automation wrapper. We have not reproduced the issue with a clean configuration and direct interactive CLI setup.

The gateway detected changes to channels.feishu.appId, appSecret, and allowFrom at approximately 17:29 and 17:32 on 2026-10-15 (UTC+08:00). The logs do not identify the actor responsible for each change.

We have not established whether error 21001 is caused by a Feishu application/tenant/network policy or plugin behavior. No known-good version or regression boundary has been established.

Could you advise whether QR-created Feishu bots have special token acquisition requirements, and which sanitized diagnostics would help identify the policy rejecting token issuance?

issues.body:
## Summary

Allow plugin-contributed Control UI tabs to participate in the same customizable pinned sidebar zone as built-in routes and sessions.

## Problem to solve

Plugin tabs are always placed in **More** and cannot be added through **Customize sidebar**. Frequently used plugin surfaces therefore cannot be promoted into the visible navigation area, even though built-in routes and sessions can be customized there.

This is a distinct but related limitation to #110379: that issue concerns the discoverability of **More** itself, while this request concerns plugin tabs being excluded from the existing pin/customize model.

The restriction is explicit in current source: `sidebarPluginTabs()` keeps dynamic plugin tabs in **More**, and the persisted sidebar entry model accepts routes and sessions but not plugin tabs.

## Proposed solution

Extend the existing sidebar entry model with a stable plugin-tab entry based on the tab descriptor's composite identity, for example `plugin:<pluginId>/<tabId>`.

Expected behavior:

- List currently available plugin tabs in **Customize sidebar**.
- Render pinned plugin tabs as normal sidebar links in the user's chosen order.
- Remove pinned plugin tabs from **More** so they do not appear twice.
- Preserve a well-formed plugin pin while its plugin is temporarily unavailable, omitting the link until the descriptor returns.
- Keep **More** highlighted for an active unpinned plugin tab, but not for an active pinned plugin tab.
- Continue rejecting malformed or duplicate persisted entries and remain backward-compatible with existing route/session preferences.

A prototype using this behavior was implemented and live-tested against OpenClaw `2026.7.2` (`c63bc343`). Pinning, navigation, persistence, unpinning, and restoration after reload all worked as expected. The prototype also passed 179 focused Control UI tests, UI type-checking and linting, a production UI build, compressed-asset verification, and performance budgets.

Current `main` (`8365383391472831f5a425a35de13b56adabc839`) has since generalized the pinned zone to serialized route/session entries; the same solution can fit that model by adding a plugin entry variant rather than reviving the older route-only representation.

## Alternatives considered

- **Leave plugin tabs in More:** This preserves the current implementation but prevents users from promoting frequently used plugin surfaces.
- **Have each plugin add its own navigation workaround:** Plugins do not own the core sidebar persistence/rendering model, would produce inconsistent UX, and could duplicate entries.
- **Persist only a display label or URL:** Labels can change and URLs are presentation details; the existing `pluginId` + tab `id` identity is the stable descriptor key.

## Impact

- **Affected:** Users with plugin-contributed Control UI tabs.
- **Severity:** UX friction rather than data loss or a blocked gateway.
- **Frequency:** Always; every plugin tab is excluded from sidebar customization.
- **Consequence:** Common plugin surfaces require repeated navigation through **More** and remain second-class relative to built-in destinations.

## Evidence/examples

Reproduction on `2026.7.2` and current `main`:

1. Install or enable a plugin that contributes a Control UI tab.
2. Open **More** and confirm the plugin tab is present.
3. Open **Customize sidebar**.
4. Observe that built-in destinations are available, but the plugin tab is not.

The live-tested prototype confirms the proposed persistence and rendering behavior is viable without changing the plugin tab registration contract.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, I do not plan to open a PR for this.

## Additional information

The implementation should build on the current serialized sidebar entry model and preserve unavailable plugin pins so temporary disconnects or disabled plugins do not silently erase user preferences.

| Plugins | 13 enabled: browser, cua-computer, discord, discord-voice, lobster, lossless-claw, memory-core, memory-wiki, ollama, openai, telegram, tool-preflight, workboard |

## Symptoms

- Gateway `[gateway] ready` at **~85 s after boot** (cold), **~72 s on warm restart**. Consistent across every restart: 64–91 s over a full day of restarts (measured 2026-10-05 → 2026-10-06).
- The span `"listening (...; 85.3 s)"` counts from **before** any plugin work; with `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_STARTUP_TRACE=1` enabled the attribution is exact (see below).
- Older version comparison: with OpenClaw 2026.5.x (5 plugins, before the npm plugin generation sandbox) the same log line read `listening (...; 1.8 s)`.

## Reproduction

Any `openclaw daemon restart` reproduces on this machine (3/3 boots traced). The cost reproduces on a **warm** restart, minutes after the previous boot, with **zero files modified between boots** — it is not a cold-cache artifact.

Repro + attribution:

```sh
launchctl setenv OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_STARTUP_TRACE 1
openclaw daemon restart
grep "startup trace:" ~/Library/Logs/openclaw/gateway.log
```

## Instrumentation data

### Startup trace (warm restart, boot of 2026-10-06 09:37)

```
process.bootstrap (cli bootstrap, config, db admission)      8 780.7 ms
plugins.runtime-post-bind                                   59 488.7 ms   ← dominant
runtime.post-attach                                         60 602.9 ms
sidecars.control-ui-assets                                  61 089.9 ms   (first publish of
                                                                            generation after asset
                                                                            update; fast path after)
sidecars.total (everything else: channels, plugin services)  1 074.2 ms
total                                                        71 611.9 ms
```

The other trace steps (config snapshots, secrets, channels, sidecars) are all < 1 s.

### Per-plugin load times (`plugins.gateway-load.plugin.<id>` metrics, 3 boots, consistent)

| Plugin | node_modules | files walked | `loadMs` | ~µs/file |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| discord-voice (local extension) | 1.4 GB | 47 186 | 29 416–30 840 ms | ~640 |
| lossless-claw (`@martian-engineering/lossless-claw` 0.11.2) | 536 MB | 26 694 | 21 918–22 195 ms | ~820 |
| discord (`@openclaw/discord`) | 69 MB | 6 082 | 5 043–5 316 ms | ~870 |
| lobster (`@openclaw/lobster`) | 13 MB | — | 1 347–1 439 ms | — |
| workboard | 2.1 MB | — | 199–205 ms | — |
| memory-core / memory-wiki / browser / ollama / telegram / openai / tool-preflight / cua-computer | ≤ 0.1 MB | — | 9–27 ms each | — |

`loadMs` (module **import**, not `registerMs`) scales **linearly with file count of the plugin's source tree**, at ~0.6–0.9 ms per file. Disabling the two heaviest plugins would cut ~52 of the 59 s.

### CPU profile (node `--cpu-prof` on a manual gateway boot during the slow window)

Main event loop stays responsive (`eventLoopMax ≈ 14 ms` in trace) but one dedicated loader thread pegs ~100 % CPU. Aggregated non-idle self time across the hot window:

```
17.0 %  structuredClone              deep-copying prior fact members
10.4 %  lstat (fs)                   per-file stat of source tree
 8.4 %  open (fs)
 6.4 %  copyFile
 3.9 %  realpath
 3.0 %  isCapturedPathInside         plugin-generation-artifact
 2.0 %  finishPluginNativeNamespace  plugin-generation-artifact
 2.0 %  nativeMemberForSource        plugin-generation-artifact
 1.8 %  innerDeepEqual/comparisons   identity map comparison
 1.5 %  update [hash]
 1.4 %  readdir / realpathSync / relative (path)
```

No copy took place in these boots (0 files under `~/.openclaw/npm/projects/**` touched after 09:20; the generation directories retain 2026-09-29/2026-10-03 mtimes) — **100 % of the time is pure re-validation**.

## Root cause analysis

The plugin generation mechanism (`src/plugins/plugin-generation-artifact.ts`, `plugin-generation-file-capture.ts`, `plugin-generation-receipt.ts`, `plugin-native-namespace.ts`) persists per-plugin "facts" capturing file identities for native-namespace safety. On **every gateway start**, the reuse check

```ts
// src/plugins/plugin-native-namespace.ts
function pluginNativeNamespaceIsCurrent(fact, boundary, outputRoot) {
    const source  = inspectDirectory(fact.sourceDirectory, boundary, outputRoot);
    const captured = inspectDirectory(pluginNativeNamespaceDirectory(fact), ...);
    return source.size === Object.keys(fact.members).length &&
           [...source].every(([relative, member]) =>
               prior?.source === member.source &&
               prior.sourceIdentity === member.identity &&     // dev:ino:mode:size:mtimeNs:ctimeNs
               prior.capturedIdentity === captured.get(relative)?.identity);
}
```

walks the **entire plugin source root (including `node_modules`, tens of thousands of files)** with `inspectDirectory`, then compares each entry's `dev:ino:mode:size:mtimeNs:ctimeNs` identity against the persisted fact via deep map comparison (`structuredClone` + `keyCheck`/`innerDeepEqual` dominate the profile).

Key properties:

1. **No stat-level cache** — the previous identity table is only used as the *comparison target*; the source side is re-walked from scratch each boot.
2. **No fs-event invalidation** — a cheap pre-check (root dir stat, or recursive dir mtime/size aggregate, or a watcher) would let an unchanged tree skip the walk entirely.
3. **Content-hash receipts already exist** (`plugin-generation-receipt.ts`) for tamper detection — per-boot full identity re-verification of *every* JS/text file adds nothing for those; what actually needs tamper checking is the **native namespace** (native binaries), which is a tiny subset of the tree.

## Security framing (why this exists, and what a fix can keep)

The full re-inspection is presumably there so a boot can always detect external modification of plugin payloads. The proposal below keeps that guarantee with a cheaper invalidation scheme:

1. **Cheap fast-path, correct-by-construction**: persist a rolling digest over the source tree's *directory metadata* (e.g. recursive (mtime,size) aggregates with directory-count), and skip the full `inspectDirectory` walk when it matches the value recorded at the last verified capture. Any file edit forces a directory mtime change, so edits are never missed; deletions of the last entry of a directory change `(count, mtime)` too. Fall back to the existing full walk on mismatch — the invariant "boot never trusts an unverified tree" is preserved.
2. **Narrow the verified set**: per-boot content verification is only meaningful for **native members** (binaries with content hashes in the receipt); JS/text files are re-hashable at first use.
3. **Short-term stop-gap**: parallelize `inspectDirectory` across a worker pool / do it per-plugin concurrently (today it appears serialized into sequential `loadMs` per plugin).

Expected effect on this machine: plugin revalidation 59.5 s → < 1 s per boot (files unchanged, fast path hit).

## Related observations (same boot path, smaller)

- ~22 s cold-start import of the gateway bundle itself — `dist/package-update-activation-recovery.mjs` is a single 63 MB / >1.2 M-line module; splitting lazy-loading it would shave the cold-boot tail.
- `cli.bootstrap.admission.database-readiness` ≈ 1.0 s (160 MB state DB, `agentCount=11`, canonical-validation workers each ~0.7–1.4 s during startup reclamation) — acceptable, but visible.
- `sidecars.control-ui-assets` takes ~61 s **once** after a Control UI asset update (first retained-generation publish of 35–53 MB), then hits the fast utimes path on subsequent boots — fine, worth documenting that the one-off cost lands inside gateway startup.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Intermittent network/transport stall (gateway process stays up and serves localhost, but provider/model HTTPS requests hang until timeout).

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

The Telegram and WhatsApp transports already enable **TCP-level keepalive** on their sockets specifically to survive idle-flow drops by home/NAT and WSL2 Hyper-V NAT (see #49460 and #72735). The **provider/model HTTP request path does not appear to get the same treatment**, and the undici pool idle timeouts (`keepAliveTimeout` / `keepAliveMaxTimeout`) are not configurable.

On a long-running gateway under WSL2 NAT, after hours of uptime we repeatedly hit a state where:

- provider/model `fetch` calls fail with 120s `UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT` / `"no response from model"` several times in a row,
- but the process is otherwise healthy: the local HTTP probe answers, and an **independent `curl` to the exact same provider endpoint keeps returning HTTP 200/401 from the same machine at the same time**.

Only restarting the gateway process clears it; restarting returns model traffic to 200 within tens of seconds. This fingerprint (process-internal egress wedged while OS-level egress and localhost stay healthy) is consistent with connections/connection state being silently invalidated by NAT rather than a provider or machine outage.

### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.10.3 (`59cb447`)
- Node v24.21.0 (built-in undici/global `fetch`)
- WSL2, Ubuntu 24.04, Windows 11 (build 26200)
- Observed in both WSL2 `networkingMode=NAT` and, previously, `mirrored` mode
- Provider endpoint: a Volcengine Ark HTTPS endpoint (`https://ark.cn-beijing.volces.com`); also seen on other long-lived provider transports

### Evidence

**1. Provider/model HTTP dispatcher sets no TCP keepalive and exposes no pool idle-timeout knob.**

In the shipped bundle, the global/provider dispatcher is built by `src/infra/net/undici-runtime.ts` / `src/infra/net/undici-global-dispatcher.ts` (`createHttp1Agent` / `createHttp1EnvHttpProxyAgent`). Its `connect` options only carry the auto-select-family policy (WSL2 is forced to IPv4); no `keepAlive`, `keepAliveInitialDelay`, `keepAliveTimeout`, or `keepAliveMaxTimeout` is set, and there is no config/env override:

```ts
// connect options for the HTTP/1 Agent used by provider/model requests
{ autoSelectFamily, autoSelectFamilyAttemptTimeout: 300 }
// no keepAlive / keepAliveInitialDelay; pool keepAliveTimeout left at undici default
```

**2. A socket on this stack does not have SO_KEEPALIVE enabled.**

A minimal probe using Node's built-in global `fetch` against the provider endpoint shows the underlying TLS socket has keepalive disabled (HTTP 401 confirms a real connection was established):

```js
const tls = require('node:tls');
const orig = tls.connect;
tls.connect = (...a) => {
  const s = orig(...a);
  s.on('secureConnect', () => {
    console.log('SO_KEEPALIVE=', s.keepAlive);              // undefined
    console.log('initialDelayMs=', s.keepAliveInitialDelay); // undefined
  });
  return s;
};
fetch('https://ark.cn-beijing.volces.com/');
// -> SO_KEEPALIVE= undefined, HTTP 401
```

Since the OpenClaw provider dispatcher adds no `connect.keepAlive`, its sockets behave the same way: the OS never sends TCP keepalive probes, so a NAT-silenced flow is not detected/recut and the request waits for the full connect/body timeout instead of recovering quickly.

**3. This is the exact failure the existing transport fixes were created for.**

- #49460 (Telegram): *"Home/office NAT devices typically expire idle TCP entries after 60–1800 s ... When the NAT entry is silently dropped the socket hangs instead of returning an error"* → fixed by setting undici `connect.keepAlive` + `keepAliveInitialDelay`.
- #72735 (WhatsApp): *"Windows Hyper-V NAT drops idle TCP connections after ~60 seconds"* → fixed with `socket.setKeepAlive(true, 15000)`.

The model/provider HTTP path makes many short, bursty TLS requests that sit idle between turns — the same NAT exposure — but has no equivalent protection.

### Why both layers matter

These are two different mechanisms; it would help to control both:

1. **TCP `SO_KEEPALIVE`** on the provider socket (`connect.keepAlive: true`, `connect.keepAliveInitialDelay` < the ~60s WSL2/NAT expiry, e.g. 30s) — keeps NAT mappings fresh and makes dead peers fail fast. This mirrors the accepted Telegram/WhatsApp fixes and is the primary ask.
2. **undici pool idle timeouts** (`keepAliveTimeout` / `keepAliveMaxTimeout`) as an advanced option — bounds reuse of aged idle connections in more aggressive NAT environments (cf. nodejs/node#47130, nodejs/undici#3492, nodejs/undici#3133).

### Expected behavior

Provider/model HTTPS sockets receive the same NAT-resistant TCP keepalive already applied to Telegram/WhatsApp transports, ideally with a configurable initial delay; and, if feasible, the undici pool `keepAliveTimeout` is exposed under advanced network config. Long-running gateways behind WSL2/NAT should recover from silently-dropped flows quickly instead of stacking 120s timeouts that look like a frozen agent.

### Actual behavior

After hours of uptime, provider/model requests inside the gateway process hang to `UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT` (120s) while independent `curl` from the same host succeeds and localhost stays up; recovery requires a gateway restart.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run the gateway for several hours under WSL2 NAT with normal, bursty provider traffic (idle gaps between turns).
2. Let the host/NAT cycle or expire idle flows (sleep/wake, network change, or NAT idle timeout).
3. Observe in-gateway model `fetch` calls timing out at ~120s while `curl https://ark.cn-beijing.volces.com` from the same WSL instance returns immediately and the local gateway probe answers.
4. Restart the gateway → model requests return to 200 within tens of seconds.

### Workarounds tried

- Switching WSL2 `networkingMode` between `NAT` and `mirrored` (both have shown outbound black-hole behavior on this host).
- Forcing IPv4 / Happy-Eyeballs handling (already present in `undici-runtime.ts`).
- An external process watchdog that restarts the gateway on repeated model timeouts (recovers, but reactive; the underlying transport still stalls).
- OS-level `net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_*` tuning — ineffective for this path because the provider sockets do not enable `SO_KEEPALIVE`.

### Related

- PR #49460 — Telegram TCP keepalive for NAT stalls (same root mechanism)
- PR #72735 — WhatsApp TCP keepalive on WSL2 Hyper-V NAT
- #87407 — intermittent provider `UND_ERR_SOCKET` mid-turn (closed as not reproduced; possibly related transport behavior)
- nodejs/undici#3492, nodejs/undici#3133, nodejs/node#47130 — undici/Node keep-alive connections being silently closed by peers/NAT

issues.body:
### Summary

Add full Korean (ko) locale support to the OpenClaw Control UI and enforce
Korean language consistency in the AI agent's response behavior.

### Problem to solve

Korean-speaking operators currently have no localized UI experience in the
OpenClaw Control panel. All interface labels, navigation elements, and status
messages are rendered in English only, forcing Korean users to work in a
non-native language. Separately, the AI agent does not persistently respond in
Korean across multi-step tool outputs and technical explanations, causing
language inconsistency mid-conversation and degrading user trust.

### Proposed solution

1. **Control UI i18n**
   - Implement `ui/src/i18n/locales/ko.ts` with complete translations for all
     UI components.
   - Register the Korean locale in `ui/src/i18n/lib/registry.ts` and update
     `ui/src/i18n/lib/types.ts`.
   - Add Korean display names (`한국어`) to all existing locale files
     (`en.ts`, `zh-CN.ts`, etc.).

2. **AI Agent Language Consistency**
   - Update `src/agents/system-prompt.ts` to include an explicit instruction
     block requiring the agent to respond in the user's detected primary
     language (e.g., Korean) for all outputs, including tool call results and
     technical explanations.
   - Add a `Final Instruction` section to the system prompt reinforcing
     language persistence across the full conversation turn.
   - Enable `search_lang: 'ko'` in localized search parameters to improve
     retrieval quality for Korean queries.

3. **Test Coverage**
   - Add unit tests in `ui/src/i18n/test/translate.test.ts` covering Korean
     locale completeness and missing-key fallback behavior.
   - Update `src/i18n/registry.test.ts` to verify Korean locale registration
     and navigation fallbacks.

### Alternatives considered

- **Manual language hints in per-user prompts**: Inconsistent across operator
  configurations and cannot be enforced at the platform level.
- **Browser `Accept-Language` header detection only**: Does not cover agent
  response behavior and is unreliable in proxied or API-driven deployments.

### Impact

| Dimension        | Detail                                                      |
|------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
| Affected users   | All Korean-speaking operators and end-users of OpenClaw     |
| Affected systems | Control UI, AI agent response pipeline, i18n registry       |
| Severity         | Medium — usability blocker for Korean locale deployments    |
| Frequency        | Every session for Korean users (100% of their interactions) |
| Consequence      | Reduced adoption in Korean-speaking teams; agent responses switching mid-conversation to English cause confusion and require manual correction |


### Evidence/examples

- Current behavior: UI renders entirely in English regardless of browser
  locale; agent reverts to English in tool-use steps even when the user writes
  in Korean.
- Comparable prior art: `zh-CN.ts` locale implementation in the same codebase
  serves as the direct template for this feature.
- Internal reports from Korean-speaking operators indicate frequent complaints
  about mid-conversation language switching.

### Additional information

- Implementation must remain fully backward-compatible with all existing locale
  keys and configuration structure.
- No sensitive credentials or private configuration data will be introduced.
- This issue is tracked by the corresponding PR:
  `feat: add Korean language support to Control UI and AI agent`.

issues.body:
### Summary

When a command that takes an argument (registered with `acceptsArgs: true` or an `args:[{captureRemaining:true}]` spec, e.g. the built-in `/btw` and `/steer`) is tapped from the Telegram "/" command menu, Telegram sends the bare command immediately with no argument. The command handler then returns its usage string (`Usage: /btw [side question]` / `Usage: /steer <message>`). The user has to notice the hint, then re-type the command plus the argument.

### Proposal

On external channels that support it (Telegram in particular), when an args-requiring command is received with an empty/missing argument, reply with a Telegram **ForceReply** keyboard:

```json
{ "reply_markup": { "force_reply": true, "input_field_placeholder": "e.g. what changed in the last run?" } }
```

ForceReply opens the compose box pre-focused (and, in a group, replying to the bot), so the user just types the argument and sends. This turns a menu tap into a single guided flow instead of a usage hint followed by a manual re-type.

### Notes

- `force_reply` / `ForceReply` does not currently appear anywhere in the Telegram send path, so this is a net-new capability rather than a tweak.
- Ideally opt-in per command (a flag on the command definition, e.g. `promptForMissingArgs: true`) so commands that are meaningful with no argument keep their current behavior.
- TUI/other surfaces are unaffected; this is a Telegram-surface enhancement gated on the channel supporting ForceReply.
- Tested against openclaw 2026.6.10.

issues.title: [6.1] Cron run "failed" notifications fire during hot reload and during retries, causing alert fatigue

labels.name: clawsweeper:not-repro-on-main
labels.description: ClawSweeper found high-confidence evidence that this issue no longer reproduces on main.

labels.name: issue-rating: 🦪 silver shellfish
labels.description: Thin issue quality; more reproduction proof or environment detail is needed.

issues.body:
## 1. Environment

- OpenClaw version: 2026.6.1 (latest stable on npm dist-tag `latest`)
- Upgraded from: 2026.5.12 (5.12) where this issue did not exist
- Provider: an anthropic-messages-compatible LLM endpoint (M2.7 + M3 model endpoints, both via `minimax` provider alias)
- Channel: Feishu (1 bot account)
- Cron workload: ~30 cron jobs (5-minute to daily schedules), 2 isolated lane worker pool

## 2. Summary

After upgrading from OpenClaw 5.12 to 6.1, cron run failure notifications became noisy. Investigation shows that **most "failed" notifications are false positives** — the actual isolated session is still running and completes minutes later, posting a second "completed" notification in the same scheduling window.

The pattern is consistent with **three 5.26-introduced mechanisms that did not exist in 5.12**:

1. **`cron.retry`** — default `maxAttempts: 3`, `backoffMs: [30000, 60000, 300000]`, `retryOn: [rate_limit, overloaded, network, timeout, server_error]`. In 5.12 there was no retry, a single fail was final.
2. **`auth.cooldowns`** — default `authPermanentBackoffMinutes: 10` after a transient failure. 5.12 had no cooldown concept.
3. **Config hot reload on mtime change** — 5.26 watches `openclaw.json` mtime and applies a hot reload within seconds. If a cron run is in flight when mtime changes, the run is reported as `failed` via Feishu, then the Gateway restarts, then a new isolated session resumes the same work and posts a `completed` notification minutes later. In 5.12 there was no hot reload; mtime changes only mattered on next manual restart.

The triple combination is the regression: 5.12 cron failures were terminal and unambiguous. 6.1 cron failures are now ambiguous, with a transient fail → retry → cooldown → possible hot-reload-interrupt all triggering their own notifications.

## 3. Reproduction (minimal)

1. Configure a cron job calling the provider on a 3-5 minute schedule.
2. Wait until a run is in flight.
3. Touch `openclaw.json` (any whitespace edit — it just has to bump mtime).
4. Watch Feishu within ~1s — you will receive a `Cron job X failed: cron: job interrupted by gateway restart` notification.
5. Wait — the same cron job will complete successfully a few minutes later, posting a second `completed` notification for the same job in the same scheduling window.

User experience: two contradicting notifications for the same job. A user filtering "failed" alerts cannot tell whether the work was lost or whether the notification is a false positive.

## 4. Sample Gateway log (sanitized)

```
[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=cron-nested durationMs=134613
  error="FailoverError: The AI service is temporarily overloaded. Please try again in a moment."
[reload] config change detected; evaluating reload (cron)
[reload] config hot reload applied (cron)
[diagnostic] message processed: channel=cron chatId=unknown outcome=error duration=134666ms
  error="FallbackSummaryError: All models failed (2): minimax/MiniMax-M2.7: overloaded |
         minimax/MiniMax-M3: minimax is overloaded right now. ... (overloaded)"
```

## 5. Expected behavior

For an interrupted-by-reload run, we would expect the cron delivery notification to describe the **current state of the work** (e.g. `interrupted`, `resuming`, or suppressed while a new run is in flight) rather than `failed`. The user should not have to grep the Gateway log to determine whether a real failure occurred.

## 6. Suggested fixes

a. **Distinguish `interrupted` from `failed`** in cron delivery notifications. Surface a new outcome type so Feishu (and other channels) can render it differently from a real fail.
b. **Optionally resume in-place on hot reload** rather than restart in a new isolated session, to avoid duplicate-notification noise and lost partial work.
c. **Document the new `cron.retry` and `auth.cooldowns` defaults prominently** in the 5.26 → 6.x upgrade notes so users upgrading from 5.12 are not surprised by the new retry traffic and cooldown behavior.
d. **Add a setting to opt out of config hot reload** (e.g. `gateway.hotReload: false`) for users who prefer the 5.12 "manual restart only" model.

## 7. Workarounds in the meantime

- Avoid touching `openclaw.json` while cron runs are in flight.
- Consider `openclaw cron set <job> --retry-disabled` or similar to opt out of the new retry behavior.
- Live with the noisy false-positive notifications and verify the actual work state via the `cron run list` CLI.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

With sandboxing on, the system prompt's Documentation section gives the gateway host's package docs path (`Docs: /opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/openclaw/docs`, "docs first via `read`"), which the sandboxed `read`, `ls` and `exec` tools cannot access, so every local docs lookup fails.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install OpenClaw globally with npm and configure an agent with `sandbox: { mode: "all", backend: "podman", workspaceAccess: "rw" }` (Docker should behave the same).
2. Ask the agent a question about OpenClaw configuration.
3. The agent follows the Documentation section and calls `read` or `ls` on the docs path.

### Expected behavior

A sandboxed agent is given a docs location it can read. For example, the docs mounted read-only in the sandbox, as skills already are, or, when they aren't available, the prompt pointing sandboxed runs to the docs.openclaw.ai mirror instead of a host path.

### Actual behavior

- `read` returns "Sandbox path is container-only: /opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/openclaw/docs/gateway/sandboxing.md. Use exec to access this mount…".
- `exec ls` returns "No such file or directory".
- The agent then answers OpenClaw questions from memory.

One agent made six such failed attempts over three days. The same agent read these docs without trouble before it was sandboxed.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.3 (59cb447). The cause is unchanged on `main` at e0c858e5 (2026-10-16): `resolveOpenClawReferencePaths` (`src/agents/docs-path.ts`) and its caller in `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-system-prompt-prepare.ts` don't take sandboxing into account.

### Operating system

macOS 27.0.1 (arm64)

### Install method

npm global

### Model

Not model-specific (seen with a local model)

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw → managed llama-cpp provider

### Additional information

This is the same class of problem as #172430, where sandboxed `web_fetch` advertised an unreadable host path.

issues.body:
## Problem

An agent that knows the section it needs in a Markdown memory file still has to discover line numbers or repeatedly read bounded windows. A search hit for a refund rule can omit the exception in a child section.

## Proposed small feature

Add an optional `heading` argument to the existing memory-core `memory_get` tool, rather than adding a tool or changing indexing. It selects one unique ATX heading by exact text, includes child sections, and stops before the next heading of equal or higher level. Preserve absolute source lines and existing line/character limits; continuation remains inside that section. Missing or duplicate headings return an explicit error with a line-read fallback.

Initial scope is memory-file reads only (omitted corpus or `corpus=memory`). No wiki adapter contract, filesystem permission, persistence, indexing, embedding, or dependency changes. Unsupported heading styles retain the existing line-based read path.

## Example

Synthetic `memory/store-policy.md`:

```markdown
# Store policy
## Refunds
Refunds are available within 30 days.
### Exceptions
Custom items are excluded.
## Shipping
Orders ship within five days.
```

`memory_get({"path":"memory/store-policy.md","heading":"Refunds"})` returns the Refunds section and its Exceptions child, without Shipping, subject to existing budgets.

## Alternatives and prior art

Existing `from`/`lines` remains fully supported. Search chunking is complementary: this request concerns an explicit section read after the agent knows the file and heading. Prior section-aware chunking PR #28071 addressed index construction, not this read operation.

The idea comes from heading-aware retrieval in Orca, adapted to OpenClaw's existing safe reader. The proposed implementation and all fixtures contain only general logic and synthetic documents, not private Orca data.

Implementation: #173708 (same author; includes focused tests and independent review). Feedback on this additive existing-owner scope is welcome. This is a feature proposal, not a claim that current line-based reading is broken.

issues.body:
Follow-up to #87291 / #87909.

`resolveInlineReplyQuote` (`src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-meta.ts:345-346`):

```ts
function resolveInlineReplyQuote(ctx: TemplateContext): string | undefined {
  return sanitizeTranscriptBody(ctx.ReplyToQuoteText) ?? sanitizeTranscriptBody(ctx.ReplyToBody);
}
```

When a Telegram user reply-quotes a bot message **and selects a specific span** (Telegram's "quote selection" UX, supported in recent clients), `ReplyToQuoteText` contains the selected span only — possibly a single sentence from anywhere in the original. The `??` short-circuits, so `ReplyToBody` (the full replied-to message) is never rendered.

If the selected quote happens to be the actionable tail, this is fine. If the user selected the *question* and is asking the bot to revisit its *recommendation*, the recommendation is now invisible to the next turn.

## Why this is subtle

The selection is a real semantic signal — Telegram is letting the user point at a span. We shouldn't override it with the full body unconditionally, but we also shouldn't drop the rest of the message when the selected span doesn't carry the actionable content.

## Proposed shape

Keep `ReplyToQuoteText` precedence and primacy, but make the framing explicit and add a body excerpt when the quote is a strict substring of the body:

- `ReplyToQuoteText` absent → `[Replying to: "<sanitized body>"]` (current behavior with the new head+tail sanitizer).
- `ReplyToQuoteText` present and effectively equal to `ReplyToBody` (modulo whitespace) → `[Replying to: "<sanitized quote>"]` (current behavior).
- `ReplyToQuoteText` is a strict substring of `ReplyToBody` → `[Replying to (user-selected): "<quote>"]` + `[Full replied-to message excerpt: "<head+tail of body>"]`. Per-block budget split, not 2× budget.
- `ReplyToQuoteText` diverges materially from `ReplyToBody` (Telegram's edit-quote feature, translations, etc.) → emit both with the labels above; let the model decide which signal dominates.

## Why not "always render both"

Telegram quote selection is a meaningful user signal. If we always emit both at full size we (a) double the worst-case inline reply budget and (b) confuse the model about which span the user is pointing at.

## Suggested tests

- `resolveInlineReplyQuote_emitsBothLabelsWhenQuoteIsStrictSubstring`
- `resolveInlineReplyQuote_emitsOnlyQuoteWhenItEqualsBody`
- `resolveInlineReplyQuote_emitsBothLabelsWhenQuoteDivergesFromBody`
- `resolveInlineReplyQuote_doesNotDiscardFullBodyWhenQuoteIsShortSnippet` — regression specifically for the short-snippet case.

Linking #87291 / #87909.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Duplicate `chrome-devtools-mcp` subprocess sets accumulate under the OpenClaw desktop/gateway process tree and are never reaped; 13 identical leaked sets were observed on 2026.10.5-beta.2, the same lifecycle pattern that #92569 described and that the fix PR #93559 (merged 2026-07-17) was supposed to close.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install OpenClaw 2026.10.5-beta.2 via npm global; configure `chrome-devtools-mcp` as an MCP server (`--browser-url=http://127.0.0.1:9222 --no-usage-statistics`).
2. Use OpenClaw normally across multiple sessions/reconnects over several days (exact trigger per set not identified — see Additional information).
3. List processes: `pgrep -fl "chrome-devtools-mcp" | grep -v grep`.
4. Observe accumulated duplicate sets (one `npm exec` wrapper + one `chrome-devtools-mcp` server process per set), all with `INIT_CWD=~/.openclaw`, parented under `openclaw/dist/proc*` node processes.

Observed inventory at cleanup time (all INIT_CWD=~/.openclaw):

```
npm exec wrappers:   4374 9763 24452 27356 28077 29153 37965 40104 59927 60819 72458 91294 92374  (13)
chrome-devtools-mcp: 4385 9798 24462 27370 28100 29166 37986 40118 59939 60830 72468 91306 92385  (13)
```

All 26 PIDs exited cleanly on a single SIGTERM round; OpenClaw itself kept running without any visible impact, confirming these sets were not in active use.

### Expected behavior

When a session (or the process tree owning it) ends, its MCP server subprocesses are terminated by the gateway — the post-#93559 behavior promised by the canonical issue #92569 (merged fix PR #93559, closed as completed 2026-07-17).

### Actual behavior

13 duplicate `chrome-devtools-mcp` sets coexisted on 2026-10-16, spanning a wide PID range (4374–92385) that indicates accumulation over multiple gateway/session lifecycles since install. Each set is: `npm exec chrome-devtools-mcp@latest --no-usage-statistics --browser-url=http://127.0.0.1:9222` whose parent chain runs into `openclaw/dist/proc*` node processes. None of them were reaped automatically; manual `kill` was required.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.5-beta.2

### Model

custom local model (GLM) via OpenAI-compatible endpoint — model identity is very likely unrelated to this process-lifecycle bug

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> self-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoint

### Additional provider/model setup details

MCP server config: `chrome-devtools-mcp@latest` stdio server, installed via npm global OpenClaw on macOS (Apple Silicon, macOS 15.x, zsh).

### Logs

Process listing evidence (abridged, one of the 13 sets shown; all others structurally identical):

```
$ ps -p 4374 -o pid,ppid,command
  PID  PPID COMMAND
 4374  4373 npm exec chrome-devtools-mcp@latest --no-usage-statistics --browser-url=http://127.0.0.1:9222 INIT_CWD=/Users/<user>/.openclaw

$ ps -p 4385 -o pid,ppid,command
  PID  PPID COMMAND
 4385  4374 chrome-devtools-mcp NODE=/usr/local/lib/node-v26.5.0/bin/node INIT_CWD=/Users/<user>/.openclaw

# 4373's parent chain: node openclaw/dist/proc* (OpenClaw runtime)
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO (terminal-only evidence, captured in the Logs section)

### Impact and severity

- Affected: macOS npm-global desktop users of 2026.10.5-beta.2 with `chrome-devtools-mcp` configured (likely any stdio MCP server that does not self-exit on stdin close).
- Severity: Medium — resource leak; each leaked set pins a node process (~tens of MB RSS each, 26 processes in total here); left unattended it grows without bound across gateway/session cycles.
- Frequency: cumulative / always present at cleanup time; per-set trigger not isolated.
- Consequence: manual periodic cleanup required; on machines with tight resources the leaked node processes add up. In the #92569 scenario the same pattern additionally caused file-lock contention for MCP servers that use exclusive locks.

### Additional information

- This looks like the same defect class as canonical #92569 ("MCP server processes leaked across sessions — stale PID holds file lock on next reconnect"), which was closed as completed on 2026-07-17 via PR #93559 ("fix(gateway): reap stale MCP processes on session reset regardless of …"). The leak is still observable on 2026.10.5-beta.2, roughly 3 months after that fix merged — so either the reset-timeout path fixed by #93559 is only one of several leak paths, or a later change reintroduced it.
- Also related: #142826 (open, `mcp doctor --probe` leaks stdio server children under a live gateway) and #101645 (closed as not_planned, consolidated into #92569) — suggesting the leak surface is broader than the one path #93559 covered.
- Honest scope caveat: I did not capture the per-set creation moment, so I cannot pin the exact trigger (session end vs. reconnect vs. gateway restart) for each of the 13 sets — only the accumulated end state and the wide PID-range timeline. Happy to run instrumented repro on request.
- Workaround: periodic manual cleanup, e.g. `pgrep -f "chrome-devtools-mcp" | xargs kill`.

issues.body:
## Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect state transition that can cause a process outage)

## Beta release blocker

No

## Summary

Main-session restart recovery can automatically resume a mutating channel turn almost 11 hours after interruption, overwrite newer operator remediation, and restart the Gateway without any fresh user input.

## Steps to reproduce

This sequence was observed once end to end on a shipped installation:

1. Start an owner-authorized channel turn that updates Gateway configuration and calls `openclaw gateway restart`.
2. Let the restart interrupt the turn while the restart command is still in flight.
3. Keep the affected main session pending while the Gateway remains unavailable for several hours.
4. Repair the Gateway out of band, including changing the affected configuration back to a known-good value.
5. Start the Gateway without sending another channel message.
6. Observe `main-session-restart-recovery` inject its synthetic interruption prompt and resume the old turn.
7. Observe the recovered turn read the current, corrected value, write the stale requested value back, and restart the Gateway again.

No owner message was admitted between the original interrupted turn and the automatic recovery. The synthetic `internal_system` recovery prompt was the only new transcript input.

## Expected behavior

Automatic main-session recovery should have a bounded staleness window. Once an interrupted turn is older than that window, OpenClaw should terminalize or quarantine it and notify the user to resend or explicitly confirm the work; it should not dispatch the model or permit new state-changing tools automatically.

Recent interrupted turns should continue to recover automatically. The existing two-hour stale-run cutoff documented for subagents is a reasonable default and precedent for main-session recovery.

## Actual behavior

The main session resumed automatically 10 hours, 48 minutes, and 47 seconds after the original interruption. The recovered turn:

1. Read the current Gateway configuration and observed the corrected value.
2. Executed a new config write that restored the stale value from the old task.
3. Executed another Gateway restart.
4. Reintroduced a known startup failure, causing a systemd restart loop and taking the messaging channel offline.
5. After later operator recovery, resumed again and sent the user an obsolete activation instruction that no longer matched the corrected configuration.

The main-session recovery attempt budget limits repeated dispatches, but it does not limit how old a turn may be when the first automatic dispatch occurs.

## OpenClaw version

`2026.8.1 (ea80657)`

## Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04 LTS x86-64, systemd user service

## Install method

npm global installation

## Model

`openai/gpt-5.6-sol` through the bundled Codex harness

## Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw Gateway -> bundled Codex harness -> OpenAI

## Additional provider/model setup details

The provider and model are not believed to own recovery eligibility. OpenClaw persisted the interrupted main-session state, injected the synthetic recovery prompt, selected the session for automatic dispatch, and exposed the tools for the recovered turn.

Codex app-server dynamic tools are client-supplied function specifications and calls are returned to the client for execution; the host owns which tools are exposed and how they execute:

- https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/8d32abcd017d06511b46050cff9dbba8738fc2fa/codex-rs/protocol/src/dynamic_tools.rs#L10-L63
- https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/8d32abcd017d06511b46050cff9dbba8738fc2fa/codex-rs/app-server/src/bespoke_event_handling.rs#L1094-L1122

## Logs

```text
01:05:07 assistant tool.call  bash: openclaw gateway restart
01:05:20 tool result          interrupted; session ended with error

# No owner/user input during this interval.

11:54:07 user input           [System] previous turn was interrupted by a gateway restart...
                              provenance.sourceTool=main_session_restart_recovery
11:54:15 recovery             inspected current state before continuing
11:55:13 recovery tool.call   read current Gateway config; affected mode was off
11:55:33 recovery tool.call   openclaw config set gateway.tailscale.mode serve
11:55:40 config watcher       detected gateway.tailscale.mode change; restart required
11:55:43 recovery tool.call   openclaw gateway restart
11:55:47 recovered turn       interrupted again by the restart
11:57:11 gateway startup      optional ingress setup failed; process exited
11:57:16 systemd              scheduled restart job
# The startup failure/restart sequence repeated until operator remediation.
12:06:59 recovery             the same main session resumed again
12:07:57 recovery             sent the user a now-obsolete activation instruction
```

Session trajectory and config-backup ordering independently showed the corrected value before the recovery write and the stale value after it. Session IDs, run IDs, tool-call IDs, hostnames, account identifiers, phone numbers, user names, and activation URLs are omitted.

## Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Current `main` has retry-count and startup-scan cutoffs, but no maximum interruption age before automatic main-session dispatch:

- Startup captures `Date.now()` only to avoid selecting rows updated after the current scan began; it is not a stale-work expiration: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b4a972ae7fb8fdc189fca29671adc812faa88e85/src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-restart-recovery-runtime.ts#L270-L312
- Startup marking rejects rows newer than that scan boundary but does not reject old rows: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b4a972ae7fb8fdc189fca29671adc812faa88e85/src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-restart-recovery-marking.ts#L197-L267
- Recovery dispatch evaluates transcript shape and retry state, then resumes without an age gate: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b4a972ae7fb8fdc189fca29671adc812faa88e85/src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-restart-recovery-store.ts#L533-L652
- The retry budget is three attempts, but no max-age constant exists beside it: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b4a972ae7fb8fdc189fca29671adc812faa88e85/src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-restart-recovery-shared.ts#L1-L24
- Documentation explicitly finalizes subagent runs older than two hours, while the main-session section documents unconditional automatic resume: https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/restart-recovery#automatic-resume

### Concentrated implementation handoff

The lifecycle owner is `src/agents/main-session-recovery/`, before model dispatch.

Recommended fix:

1. Define one main-session recovery maximum age, preferably aligned with the existing two-hour subagent cutoff unless product policy chooses another value.
2. Compare that limit against the persisted interruption/recovery-cycle timestamp, not a bookkeeping timestamp that retries or unrelated metadata writes may refresh.
3. When expired, terminalize/tombstone the recovery cycle before `resumeMainSession` and deliver one bounded notice asking the user to resend or start a replacement turn.
4. Do not dispatch the model or expose tools for an expired cycle.
5. Preserve current automatic recovery, durable attempt budgeting, idempotency, pending-final settlement, and recent agent-requested restart continuation behavior inside the valid window.

Regression coverage should prove:

- A recent interrupted main-session turn still resumes.
- An interrupted main-session turn older than the cutoff is terminalized without an agent/tool dispatch.
- A stale turn cannot overwrite a newer operator config write.
- Repeated restarts emit at most one stale-recovery notice and never re-arm the expired cycle.
- Pending final delivery settlement remains independent from stale unfinished work and does not resend an already-delivered reply.

## Impact and severity

- **Affected:** Gateway operators with an interrupted main-session turn and a long outage or delayed repair.
- **Severity:** High. Stale work can mutate current configuration or repeat other external effects without fresh user intent.
- **Frequency:** 1/1 observed long-gap recovery; broader prevalence is `NOT_ENOUGH_INFO`.
- **Consequence:** A successful operator repair can be silently undone, the Gateway can restart or crash again, channels can go offline, and users can receive obsolete instructions hours later.

## Additional information

This is distinct from the Tailscale failure itself:

- #133827 / #133885 cover optional Tailscale exposure failure becoming fatal to an otherwise-ready Gateway. That fix would prevent this incident's particular crash loop, but it would not prevent stale recovery from overwriting current state or repeating a different side effect.
- #121570 concerns external orchestrators opting sessions out of OpenClaw-owned recovery. No external orchestrator owned this session; this was an ordinary owner-authorized channel turn.
- #124941 concerns unbounded repeated recovery attempts. A single stale automatic recovery is sufficient to cause this bug even with the current three-attempt budget.

Temporary operator workaround: before starting a Gateway that has been offline for a long interval, inspect pending main-session recovery state and replace or reset stale work rather than allowing it to resume automatically.

---

issues.body:
### Summary

On OpenClaw `v2026.5.18`, a scheduled background agent turn using the Codex harness failed during app-server startup with:

```text
Error: codex app-server client is closed
```

The local logs showed repeated startup-close handling in the same shape:

```text
codex app-server connection closed during startup; restarting app-server and retrying
```

After the retry budget was exhausted, a later turn succeeded shortly afterward, which suggests the replacement app-server may still have been warming up when the immediate retries ran.

### Impact

A scheduled/background turn can fail before reaching user work, even though the Codex route becomes viable moments later. This is especially noisy for cron-style automation because it reports a job failure even when there is no task-level or repository-level problem.

### Expected behavior

When the app-server connection closes during startup, OpenClaw should tolerate a short replacement-server warm-up window before declaring the Codex harness failed.

Useful behavior would be:

- retry with a small backoff instead of immediately reusing the same failing window
- use a retry budget large enough for the replacement app-server to bind and become ready
- preserve the hard failure if the app-server remains unavailable after that bounded window
- make the terminal error distinguish startup lifecycle exhaustion from task/model failure

### Local mitigation tested

A local mitigation increased the startup-close retry budget and added a short bounded backoff between startup retry attempts. After restarting the gateway, a trivial Codex agent smoke test completed successfully and no new startup-close exhaustion was observed.

### Related

Possibly related to #79495, which covers shared Codex app-server client eviction across agents. This issue is narrower: even when restarting the app-server is the intended recovery path, the startup retry loop can exhaust before the replacement process is ready.

## Summary

A turn whose model call fails with a connection error keeps retrying the provider `baseUrl` it resolved when the turn started. If `models.providers.<id>` is hot-reloaded during those retries (for example a local llama.cpp server restarting on a new endpoint), the in-flight turn never uses the new configuration and fails once the retry budget runs out, even though a turn sent a second later succeeds.

## Reproduction (Gateway 2026.10.3, WSL)

1. Configure a custom OpenAI-compatible provider, e.g. `models.providers.llamacpp` with `baseUrl: http://127.0.0.1:62632/v1`, as the primary model, and confirm a turn succeeds.
2. `openclaw config set models.providers.llamacpp.baseUrl http://127.0.0.1:0/v1` (nothing can answer there).
3. Start a turn: `openclaw agent --session-id retry-test -m "Reply with exactly: OK" --json`.
4. 12 s later, restore the working URL: `openclaw config set models.providers.llamacpp.baseUrl http://127.0.0.1:62632/v1`. The hot reload is applied.
5. The turn keeps failing against the old URL (`[model-fetch] error provider=llamacpp ... causeCode=ETIMEDOUT message=fetch failed`, about 137 s per attempt) and never reaches the restored endpoint. A new turn sent after step 4 succeeds immediately.

## Why it matters

The OpenClaw Windows companion restarts its managed llama.cpp server on app start (about 33 s while the model is verified). Today it withdraws the provider during that window, so turns fail with `Unknown model` (openclaw/openclaw-windows-node#1445). The companion would rather keep the provider configured and let the Gateway's existing connection-error retries wait for the server, but that only works if a retry picks up the provider configuration that is current at retry time. Without that, the companion has to hold chat sends on its side (openclaw/openclaw-windows-node#1738).

## Request

When a same-model retry follows a connection-class failure (`fetch failed`, `ECONNREFUSED`, timeouts), re-resolve the provider configuration (at least `baseUrl`/headers) if it changed through a hot reload since the turn started.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Since 2 October 2026 23:45 BST, images attached in the dashboard chat are stored in the inbound media folder but never copied into the sandbox, and the run fails with "Sandbox media reference is not staged".

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run OpenClaw 2026.9.7 with the native rootless Podman sandbox (workspaceAccess rw) and runtime codex.
2. Open a brand new dashboard chat session.
3. Attach one small PNG (about 2.3 MB) as the first message, or as a file upload.
4. The run fails with run_failed ("Sandbox media reference is not staged" or "failed to hydrate 1 structured image attachment(s)").

### Expected behavior

Earlier attachments on this install were staged: 60 staged folders (openclaw staged followed by a UUID, under the workspace media inbound folder) exist dated 9 September to 2 October 23:45. I expect the attachment to be copied into the sandbox workspace and the model to receive it.

### Actual behavior

Observed on 4 October 2026, 5 uploads, all failed:
1. Each upload is stored intact under ~/.openclaw/media/inbound.
2. No staged folder was created. None exists after 2 October 23:45.
3. The run fails with the errors above after a silent gap of about 14 seconds.
4. With logging.level set to debug for a test (since restored), the gateway log contains no "Failed to stage inbound media" line.
5. It fails as the first message of a new session, as a file upload, and with GPT 6 Sol selected.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.7

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04 (VPS)

### Install method

npm global, gateway as a systemd user service

### Model

openai/gpt-5.6-sol (default) and openai/gpt-6-sol (picker); both fail the same way

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw to openai (ChatGPT OAuth) with the Codex runtime

### Additional provider/model setup details

Native Podman sandbox, workspaceAccess rw. No media configuration in openclaw.json. The file transfer extension is disabled.

### Logs

```shell
Errors seen: "Sandbox media reference is not staged" and "failed to hydrate 1 structured image attachment(s)". No staging error line at debug level (capture 4 October 11:15 to 11:17 BST). I can attach a redacted capture if useful.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

Affected: dashboard chat image attachments on this install (main agent; other agents and channels not tested).
Severity: blocks image attachments; workaround is describing the image in words.
Frequency: 5 of 5 attempts on 4 October.
Consequence: the agent never receives the image and the run fails with no hint of the cause.

### Additional information

Last known good: staged folders were still being created up to 2 October 23:45. No OpenClaw version change since 2026.9.7 was installed on 30 September. I could not find a config change that explains it.
In the installed 2026.9.7 code (stage sandbox media chunk), the staging function returns without logging in several cases (no path entries or session key, a registered prepareTurnAttachments handler, no effective workspace, an unresolvable or disallowed source path). A failed copy is logged only through logVerbose. The only registrant of prepareTurnAttachments I found is the file transfer extension, which is disabled here.
Questions: (1) Which of these exits does staging take for a stored upload? (2) Can each exit log its reason at the default level?
Related but different: #51656 and #51857 (closed, 2026.3.13) describe a primary model without vision not being routed to the image model.
