prs.title: feat(nextcloud-talk): support inbound attachments
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Let authorized, opted-in Nextcloud Talk senders provide verified files and native voice through durable ingress, without leaking rejected staged media or rejecting valid recipient shares. No outbound upload capability is added.

## Current correction

**Published head:** `de3c954557d29104f9b71e8f7f189477b4bf9a8e`. This preserves @lordratner’s implementation and adds these corrections:

- Retire owned staged media after voice canonicalization, final authorization or context failure; retain attachments handed to core dispatch, including downstream rejection.
- Accept canonical `/index.php/s/<token>` URLs under the configured server path while retaining origin/token guards.
- Accept recipient collision-renamed mounts while preserving exact message, actor, room, MIME, size and WebDAV file-ID checks. Metadata mismatch tests now vary one condition at a time.
- Preserve caption mention placeholders through durable ingress and use the actual host matcher; file/actor metadata does not grant mention activation.
- Correct named-account media-allowlist inheritance hints and regenerate config metadata. Root omission/empty denies media; named-account omission inherits root and explicit empty denies.

## Verification and remaining gates

Focused media/security/behavior/authorization/spool/account/channel suites pass with isolated state and temporary files. Physical-file regressions cover cleanup and retention; actual core inbound dispatch and durable caption/host-matcher tests pass. Formatting, the configured content guard, config generators and relevant structural ratchets pass. Fresh independent API-only full-candidate review returned no actionable P0–P2 findings. Full touched test files, helpers and teardown were audited; no skips, retries or timeout loosening were used.

Native signed baseline refresh integrated 4e90d155d8abdd7191076b6bac2b0828a2dc5c30, regenerated the three affected metadata outputs and preserved the previous published source ancestry. Four refreshed focused Vitest shards passed. Nextcloud and targeted host typechecks passed; host type-aware lint passed. Extension lint found only duplicate type imports, now consolidated; corrected-file type-aware lint and all four durable-caption cases passed. Independent API-only substantive-candidate review was scoped-clean; the final type-only import delta was separately inspected. Metadata/environment checks pass (452/452). The packaged-declaration guard remained enabled: a minimal task-private compiler/declaration closure enabled proof, then was deleted and shared links restored.

**Investigated local failure, not waived:** the max-lines ratchet rejects an existing suppression in ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message.test.tsx. Its source, checker and baseline blobs are unchanged from the integrated baseline. Running the original checker against an alternate Git index populated from that baseline and against the final candidate produced the same sole failure. Native review retains tests.result: fail with exact-head investigated-local-failure evidence; its documented READY route permits publication, not a CI pass. Required exact-head GitHub CI and applicable dependency/security approvals remain mandatory. No merge or full-CI-green claim is made.

## Coordinated release requirement

The narrow public cleanup method and media policy remain in this feature. Source merge is not registry publication. Existing official release sync must assign the actual matching host/plugin release identity and raise `compat.pluginApi`/build metadata accordingly; no release H is invented here, and historical minHost/API metadata is not proof of compatibility with stock hosts lacking `deleteMediaBuffer`. A focused test runs existing sync against the actual Nextcloud manifest with synthetic versions and proves old-host installation/discovery rejection with config preservation.

Release owners must qualify immutable paired artifacts, complete existing SDK acknowledgement/evidence gates and the new/old host-plugin matrix, then perform required registry/dist-tag/ClawHub readbacks. The release-aligned API floor protects the plugin-first publication gap. No release, live Nextcloud run, live Gateway change or new shipped-artifact qualification was performed for this correction. Historical proof below retains its original bindings and limitations.

<details>
<summary>Retained contributor qualification and earlier revision history</summary>

All current-head and merge-gate statements below describe their historical revisions, not the correction above.

## What Problem This Solves

Allow otherwise-authorized Nextcloud Talk users to provide files and native voice through existing durable ingress, with guarded retrieval, staged-media cleanup and final authorization.

## User Impact

Authorized opted-in senders can attach media. Media remains denied when its narrowing allowlist is absent or empty; ordinary text, sender policy and conversation continuity remain intact. This adds no outbound upload capability.

## Current revision and review follow-up

**Current head:** `412fb31d86cab77ff8fd711d80ddbf5ca2dc6a6e`. Since reviewed `328ac2397f204cd8b049ad8a955ab8bade580e55`, the only product delta is **52 deleted test lines**: two mocked complete staging-argument echoes and their unused import. No production implementation, dependency or configuration schema changed. Thirty PR product files; QA files remain fork-only.

- [Exact candidate package and focused cleanup checks](https://github.com/lordratner/openclaw/actions/runs/38826014761): canonical installable matching host/Talk package, **29/29 retained media tests**, exact-file format/lint passed. The focused command took49.91s including its transform/setup; this is not CPU/billing time.
- [Configured fresh-install proof](https://github.com/lordratner/openclaw/actions/runs/38835244988): install actual package; enable its matching bundled Talk owner; validate authored config; start actual Gateway; signed webhook -> provider -> signed Talk reply. Closed image caused **zero downloads/zero provider images**; explicit opt-in delivered **one authenticated PNG download and provider image**. Existing account/sender settings were preserved. Inspection requires the exact admitted packaged plugin root, not a stale external override.
- [Current-stable data-survival proof](https://github.com/lordratner/openclaw/actions/runs/38835618787): actual published **2026.10.4** creates the Talk conversation; after isolated external package replacement into this paired source candidate, the same public session ID, prior conversation marker at the provider, authored Talk settings and workspace sentinel survive. The absent media key remains absent/closed; explicit opt-in works without broadening sender settings.
- **Version limitation:** current main/candidate still identifies itself as **2026.10.3**. The preceding result proves data survival in an **unpublished source-build replacement**, not a released semantic-version upgrade or a successful in-process updater. The canonical transition receipt explicitly records both versions and `selfUpdatePassed: false`. No future release identity, released compatibility floor or old-host fallback was invented.
- [Immutable current packet, source binding, costs and limitations](https://github.com/lordratner/openclaw/tree/72442c0cfdf403992c66a74da3c0436eed8e2068/.qa/evidence/nextcloud-readiness-20261015). The earlier complete source/worker/transport proof remains applicable to unchanged inputs; after removing two echo cases, **237 Talk cases +5 Matrix controls** are covered by composite receipts, with29 media cases freshly rerun. This is not a fresh237-case global run. Earlier exact-release backport/canary evidence is separate and is not relabelled as this package's live proof.

## Maintainer decisions and remaining merge gates

Please decide whether to accept the narrow public `runtime.channel.media.deleteMediaBuffer` contract and the separate deny-by-default Talk media allowlist, and select their **coordinated first-party host/plugin publication contract**. First-party current-host-only ownership is preserved; there are no older-host capability probes/adapters. The installation/data-survival evidence above does **not** assign the first released cleanup-capable host or make a plugin-only installation on stock2026.10.3/10.4 safe. Existing version-only metadata cannot distinguish an unreleased cleanup addition from an unmodified host sharing main's placeholder version; release owners must align the actual release identities/floor.

The earlier review found no actionable code findings and rated proof5/6, patchquality4/6 and overall readiness3/6. This revision addresses its two mock-only cases and supplies the missing configured installed-path/data-survival evidence; it does not override the maintainer decision or request a rating-label change. Broader upstream CI remains independent, including the previously documented Gateway terminal-reason assertion and aggregate gate; no baseline replay, waiver, full-CI-green or merge-ready claim is made. No production files/config/service were changed for this follow-up.

<details>
<summary>Previous full-scope qualification and retained transport/canary history — earlier head</summary>

The following is retained unchanged for provenance. Its “current head” and conflict/CI statements describe the earlier revision, not a new current-head/global pass.

## What Problem This Solves

Allow otherwise-authorized Nextcloud Talk senders to deliver attachments and native voice messages through the existing durable ingress owner, with verified retrieval, bounded media handling, cancellation cleanup, and final authorization.

## User Impact

Authorized configured senders can attach files rather than having file-share activities silently ignored. Denied attachment-only messages create no agent turn; captions remain subject to ordinary authorization. This does not add outbound uploads or unrelated channel features.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep Nextcloud verification and media semantics in the Talk plugin and reuse the shared media-store and ingress owners. The refresh preserves current upstream spool validation/lifecycle ownership instead of restoring redundant checks.

## Evidence

**Current head:** `328ac2397f204cd8b049ad8a955ab8bade580e55`. Thirty product files; QA workflow/payload/evidence files are fork-only and absent from this PR.

- Refreshed once for seven actual conflicts against `27721b8fec4bd5593bb0ba609b4ab1257f9613c1`. The final exact-Git-blob check against `e5b5a35a3ba68dd5d857dc9fe2042f579fc5abfd` found no intervening changes to PR paths; GitHub reports conflict-free. This is not freshness-only main churn.
- [Shared-source qualification](https://github.com/lordratner/openclaw/actions/runs/38801908491): canonical build, generators, affected formatting, core/extension/test types, focused lint and entrypoint profile passed; 197 messaging tests and 5 Matrix controls passed.
- [Required worker-profile supplement](https://github.com/lordratner/openclaw/actions/runs/38805415585): 42 additional PR tests across the four registered database-worker files passed. Combined Talk coverage: **239 tests in 30 files**, plus 5 Matrix controls. Source-byte guards bind the supplemental proof to the retained passing source; it did not rerun the green type/lint/profile suites.
- [Exact 2026.10.3 artifact qualification](https://github.com/lordratner/openclaw/actions/runs/38802811817): canonical stock/additive-seam builds, plugin build, types/lint/profile and 270 messaging tests plus 6 Matrix controls passed. The supplement adds 26 registered worker-profile tests: **296 Talk tests in 32 files**, plus 6 Matrix controls. Complete export contains all 15 expected files, including six hidden setup chunks, byte-identical to the initial qualified artifact.
- [Immutable proof summary and source/artifact manifests](https://github.com/lordratner/openclaw/tree/07df35c4fd3a6c40a2ac9d4e9503fea59d94dff5/.qa/evidence/nextcloud-attachments-20261015). All 30 final product-source hashes match the executed shared-source proof. The release adaptation shares the feature owners and changes only release-host adapters; it is not whole-source equivalence to current main.
- Aggregate job wall cost for these four successful jobs: **2,259 seconds including setup/build/checks**, not CPU or billing time. Actual messaging commands took 66.87 seconds (shared source) and 42.48 seconds (release); worker-profile JSON reports are retained by the supplemental run. The setup-only supplemental run superseded for the artifact-export correction is not claimed as passing proof.

Fresh independent review found no actionable P0–P2 issue in the narrow conflict repair. It is source review, not execution proof. The SDK mock reuses the current upstream owner; the obsolete split media-mock module was removed. Four metadata/catalog outputs were restored from upstream and regenerated canonically, not hand-merged.

## Compatibility and remaining maintainer gates

- The feature requires the matching host `runtime.channel.media.deleteMediaBuffer` addition. A plugin-only installation on stock 2026.10.3 is **not** claimed safe. The separately qualified production artifact pairs the exact-release plugin/schema with its additive host seam; installed package identity/dependencies stay unchanged and XML parser dependencies are bundled.
- Maintainer acceptance of the public cleanup method and deny-by-default media allowlist remains required. The modified-release artifact does **not** establish fresh-install/upgrade compatibility on an unmodified supported host or settle the permanent compatibility floor.
- Full upstream merge CI is separate and was still running when this body was updated. This is not a full-CI-green, merge-ready, released, or live-installation claim.
- No new end-user media sample was requested for this refresh. Retained real transport/authority/cancellation and release media observations below remain historical evidence, with their original limitations (including captionless-audio command projection and video comprehension).

## Current upstream CI disposition

The broader merge run is not green: [checks-node-changed-compact-large-9](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38806330854/job/116669030492) fails `src/gateway/server.agent-late-admission.test.ts` because the terminal frame reports `stopReason: restart` where the test expects `rpc`. Its provider-not-started check passes. The test, admission phase/service, close owner, session admission owner, and Gateway test helper have identical Git blobs between CI base `e5b5a35a3ba68dd5d857dc9fe2042f579fc5abfd` and test merge `19032d72`; these files are not modified by this PR. The immutable proof packet records those comparisons. This is source attribution, **not baseline execution or a waiver**; the assertion remains unresolved before merge. It is outside the exact-release canary delta, which changes no Gateway admission/shutdown code.

<details>
<summary>Historical qualification packet — earlier heads, not fresh current-head CI</summary>

The following packet is retained for provenance. Its references to an earlier “current head,” earlier CI, and older release installation describe that historical revision and must not be read as fresh proof for the head above.

## What Problem This Solves

Nextcloud Talk users cannot send files or native microphone voice notes into an agent turn with verified, authorized local media and reliable cleanup after cancellation or revocation.

## User Impact

Authorized media senders can provide attachments and native voice to the agent; disallowed senders cannot stage or dispatch media. A compatible host exposing the generic cleanup API is required; publication against an unmodified shipped host remains a maintainer gate.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add guarded Talk metadata/download/staging and media context through the existing authorization, async preparation and durable queue owners. Keep this PR focused on attachments and their necessary cleanup contract.

## Evidence

Historical real production-owner authority/cancellation probes and six owner-originated media controls are retained below with exact source continuity and explicit limits. Fresh pinned-head Talk/Matrix tests, canonical build/generation/format and standalone single-worker cost are recorded below. Broader PR CI is terminal with an unresolved X-publication failure; no globally green or merge-ready claim is made.

## Talk attachments — scope cleanup

**Current head:** `1f0550a66086ac61965359cfa6931903d11b30c5`, integrated against upstream `390fcec17863174dda480f563f87927738b9ee24` to resolve actual conflicts. Adds authorized inbound Talk files/native voice, guarded metadata/download and bounded staging, mediaAllowFrom narrowing, cancellation/revocation cleanup, and media context. Includes only necessary generic media.deleteMediaBuffer runtime/type/test-mock seams, Talk parser dependency, generated channel/schema/catalog/docs and controls. The Matrix delta is a three-line test-runtime mock for that required runtime contract, not Matrix production behavior.

### Unrelated work removed

- Gateway public-session history repair preserved in a separate **draft**: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/166416. It is not part of this PR's main-relative diff.
- MCP dependency/issuer-fixture follow-up is already merged and superseded by [#166217](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/166217). No duplicate draft. This head preserves upstream's patched dependencies, production credential-retention guard and stronger issuer tests unchanged.

The main-relative PR is **31 files (+4,856/-87)** instead of 38. Root/browser/QA/UI manifests, OAuth implementation/tests and both Gateway paths have no PR-owned changes. Root lockfile differs only by the 3-line Talk saxes importer.

### Proof continuity, not a blanket new-head pass

Prior exact proof head: `fd74a2e849af5f8f65b14361b1368e7eb76c7173`. All **13 production-owner files** in the recorded authority/cancellation manifest match this head byte-for-byte, including Talk handler/media/spool, async envelope/session preparation, fetch guard and ingress queue/drain. Of the 31 changed-scope files, 28 match the historical proof head; `types.ts` retains identical attachment fields but adopts upstream removal of three stale comments, the lockfile retains main plus the Talk importer, and the installation paragraph removes an unsupported host-version claim. No attachment-behavior change was made by this cleanup.

The historical observations below remain tied to their original execution/artifact. Source continuity supports reuse for these boundaries, not a fresh current-head run or transitive dependency/host equivalence. Fresh focused GitHub qualification and terminal PR CI are recorded below; old CI/review verdicts do not automatically attach to this head. No live canary/runtime/config/restart change was made during splitting.

### Retained isolated authority/cancellation observations


Archived exact-head source hashes verified; frozen dependency restore with scripts disabled, manifests/lockfile unchanged. Real production handler, public async envelope/session owners, guarded fetch and durable ingress queue were used. Observation wrappers forward unchanged; dispatch is intercepted before agent generation/outbound delivery.

- **Actual loopback TCP:** retire a real durable claim after authenticated metadata I/O; original abort propagates and prevents subsequent history/media requests, staging, context and dispatch. No async-envelope/history/fetch/spool/queue doubles; zero staged files.
- **Real Nextcloud allowed fixture:** canonical-user lookup + exact-message history + WebDAV file-ID metadata/download; one real staged file reaches canonical structured-media context and one dispatch-boundary observation, preserving elapsed envelope timestamp.
- **Forbidden sender:** after the room check, zero user/history/WebDAV/download requests, staging/context/dispatch or unavailable-marker turns.
- **Revoked after staging:** actual saved-ID deletion removes the staged file; no context or dispatch.
- **Cancelled after staging:** actual deletion, original abort identity, no context/dispatch, held claim released and exactly one durable retry row retained.
- All four real-server cases observed **zero caller-thread session-data SQL executions** through unchanged async preparation owners. Unexpected requests and unavailable markers were zero; both cleanup cases removed their actual staged files.

**Limits:** isolated state/config/queue; synthetic event constructed from authenticated real metadata, not the installed signed-webhook boundary. Revocation changes isolated config only. Dispatch ends at a counter, not final agent/outbound delivery. Fresh spool recovery untested. Earlier harness credential-context/obsolete-field observation failures were retained and corrected without product changes or weakened assertions. This is historical exact-head production-owner evidence retained by the source continuity check below, not fresh execution or a deployment claim.

### Real user-originated media on the release-compatible canary

Base **2026.9.8**, `fc23bc864e4553c2d215e479eeec47b67a0bf943`. Official-path plugin compiled/generated-schema overlay plus **one additive runtime file exposing existing `media.deleteMediaBuffer`**. Stock package identity/version, install record, trust, dependencies, ownership/modes and all 42 core import names/dependency hashes preserved. No full-core update or state/schema migration.

**Backport-only adaptations, explicitly not PR equivalence:** stock public preparation is synchronous; read its session timestamp before media/revalidation and pass the captured value to the stock envelope (explicit null prevents a late reread). Envelope/history owners stay stock and tests exercise that synchronous boundary, not async-worker/zero-caller-SQL equivalence. Preserve release SDK/schema facade compatibility; canonically generate Talk channel metadata and approved config-doc baseline. Bundle already locked `saxes`/`xmlchars` through runner-only resolution without host dependency/lock changes. Add the stock deletion runtime/type seam and typed release test mocks (including the approved three-line Matrix fixture, no Matrix production change). Restore compiled hashed imports to stock names with closure verification. Preserve official package/assets; install only compiled plugin/schema and the one core file, and configure only narrowing `mediaAllowFrom`. Generated CI docs, diagnostic whole-core trees and profiler-only clean-source/root-host links are not extra installed surfaces. The PR's MCP/Gateway changes are not backported.

Observed controlled cases, one at a time:

1. Ordinary text received and handled after restart.
2. Native microphone voice: authenticated `voice-message`; declared MP3/audio-mpeg but real audio-only MP4/AAC; correctly staged M4A and transcribed as voice.
3. Ordinary captioned audio: authenticated `comment`, audio-only MP4/AAC staged M4A; caption remains user text, transcript separately marked audio content.
4. Exact same audio bytes without caption: `comment`/audio/M4A retained, not native voice. Final internal command projection **not captured**; transcription wording varied despite identical bytes.
5. Captioned genuine video: H264 video + AAC audio, MP4/video and staged-to-agent byte identity verified, caption retained, no visible audio transcript.
6. Exact same video bytes without caption: `comment`/MP4/video retained and delivered bytes match; no visible audio transcript.

Five media ingress rows completed without recorded errors: **8.550 / 4.819 / 3.539 / 2.551 / 1.953 seconds**, respectively. These are individual receipt-to-ingress-completion observations, not steady-state assistant latency or single-worker test cost. Completed queue rows erase raw payload; exact authenticated Chat records plus trusted ingress context are retained privately, not falsely described as archived raw signed webhooks. Read/notification markers unchanged; configured credentials resolved in memory through an anonymous pipe, never persisted.

**Final state:** detached safe-restart verification and independent manual owner continuation passed; candidate stays enabled/loaded, Gateway and Talk healthy/connected/ready, exact installed hashes/config rechecked after uploads. Task verifier/notice units collected. Explicit operator direction disabled automatic rollback/deadman; preserved stock archives, duplicate-path/stub restoration drills and reset-safe manual recovery remain inactive. Production rollback was not run.

**Outside Talk scope:** unchanged shared core has a transcript-to-command fallback when original user text is absent (it also considers transport Body). Actual branch execution/final commandText was not captured; no command execution or full command-trust pass is claimed. This is a separate documented core question, **not a Talk-canary gate or repair included here**. Video comprehension is untested because no model is configured. Only supplied client/samples were observed. Isolated denial/cancellation above is not relabelled as a live production-room race.

### Source/artifact binding and qualification

[CI7](https://github.com/lordratner/openclaw/actions/runs/37551148253) passed **281 Talk tests/30 files**, **six Matrix controls/two files**, types and 39 canonical selected checks before a 55-minute timeout. [CI8](https://github.com/lordratner/openclaw/actions/runs/37557414361) supplied the remaining two canonical pairing guards. Subsequent profile retries changed runner provenance/host layout only. [Final canonical profile](https://github.com/lordratner/openclaw/actions/runs/37558331483) passed in 2m25s; complete 7,032 stock + 7,032 seam-core + 16 plugin-overlay inventories, metadata/docs/source and installed staging reconciled. **41/41 checks are covered by exact-source composite receipts, not one globally green run or replacement for PR CI.** Fresh single-worker Talk suite cost and current-head integration receipts are recorded in the following section.

prs.title: perf(logbook): batch frame claims and replacement writes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Logbook assigns frames and replaces observations/timeline cards with one write statement per row. A normal 30-frame analysis batch therefore executes 30 frame UPDATEs inside one existing worker request.

## User Impact

Logbook analysis uses fewer SQLite statements while preserving frame ownership, replacement ordering, and atomic rollback. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use bounded, dialect-neutral Kysely batches of 64 rows: UPDATE ... WHERE id IN (...) RETURNING id for frame claims, and multi-row INSERT for observations and cards. The existing worker and transaction own each operation. Remove the three superseded per-row prepared commands. At most 768 parameters are bound in a card batch, and the existing per-connection statement cache handles repeated full/tail SQL shapes.

Frame claims still reject missing, already-owned, and duplicate IDs in input order, rolling back the complete operation. Observation and card replacements preserve order, duplicate content, empty replacement, and rollback after a later batch fails. No schema, SDK, ownership, cache invalidation, or worker-routing change.

## Evidence

- Logbook Gateway-main T1 calls: **0 → 0**; SQL remains in `store.worker.ts`.
- Three alternating shared-harness v3 pairs and owner-specific statement/request/prepare measurements: running; results will be added before closeout. The standard chat workload does not enable Logbook, so no warmed-chat savings are claimed.
- Formatting, type-aware lint and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Independent Codex review: passed, no actionable findings. Focused owner regression tests: 13/13 passed, including cross-batch rollback, ordering, and immediate-read cases.
- Required CI gate: passed. PR CI passed production/test types, type-aware lint, source contracts, architecture guards, owner tests, and database ratchets. Global T1: 222 → 222; Logbook: 0 → 0. Changed-file dialect counts: 0 → 0.
- No update cell or SDK API diff: this change does not touch their triggering surfaces.

## Checks and size

No authority checks were removed. The frame ownership predicate protects real user data against assigning a frame twice and remains in the one UPDATE that performs the effect. There are no newly accepted stale-authority edge cases or replacement handshakes.

Production: +52 / -55 lines (net -3). Tests: +77 / -15. New coverage exercises more than one batch, including late failure rollback and immediate reads after replacement.

prs.title: fix(agents): sandboxed agents are pointed at docs mirror instead of unreadable host docs path
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #173657

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where users running an agent with sandboxing enabled (`sandbox.mode: "all"`) would get failing documentation lookups: the system prompt's Documentation section advertised the gateway host's package docs path (e.g. `/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/openclaw/docs`), which sandboxed `read`/`exec` tools cannot access, so every local docs lookup failed and the agent answered OpenClaw questions from memory.
- **Related:** #172430 (same class of problem: sandboxed tool advertised an unreadable host path); clawsweeper review confirms the fix belongs in shared documentation prompt rendering.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** Sandboxed runs keep local docs/source reference lines only when the resolved path lives inside the sandbox-accessible host workspace (`sandboxInfo.workspaceDir`, which is always mounted into the container); otherwise they fall back to the existing public mirrors (`Docs: https://docs.openclaw.ai` / `Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw`), which already carry "docs mirror first when web exists" guidance. Non-sandboxed prompts are byte-identical to before.
- **Out of scope:** No sandbox mount changes — the package docs are not auto-mounted read-only (that would expand scope unnecessarily per the issue review); no changes to docs path resolution itself.
- **Highest-risk area:** Single rendering point in `buildAgentSystemPrompt` (`src/agents/system-prompt.ts`), which serves both normal attempts and compaction, so both paths are covered by one change.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** Workspace-local docs (e.g. `<workspace>/docs`) still keep local read guidance; regression tests cover host-only fallback, workspace-local keep, and unchanged non-sandboxed output.

## User Impact

- **Success criteria:** A sandboxed agent whose only docs source is the gateway host's package install is no longer told to read an inaccessible host path; it is pointed at the public docs mirror instead, eliminating the repeated failed `read`/`exec ls` attempts described in the issue.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `src/agents/system-prompt.ts` (Documentation section gating) and `src/agents/system-prompt.test.ts` ("falls back to public mirrors for sandboxed runs with host-only docs paths", "keeps local docs guidance for sandboxed runs with workspace-local docs paths").

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** Worktree `aispace/worktrees/issue-173657` on branch `feat/issue-173657-sandbox-docs-path`; zero-mock rendering of the real `buildAgentSystemPrompt` output before (origin/main) and after (patched) via `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs`, plus the full `src/agents/system-prompt.test.ts` suite.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  skills/fix-pr/scripts/validate.sh src/agents/system-prompt.ts src/agents/system-prompt.test.ts  # oxfmt + oxlint + suite + tsgo:core: all green
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/system-prompt.test.ts                               # 58/58 passed
  node scripts/run-tsgo.mts -b test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-root.json --builders 1    # targeted test-type shard
  node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs <render script>                                                # zero-mock before/after prompt rendering
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:** rendered Documentation section for the issue's repro scenario (sandbox enabled, host-only package docs path), patched head:
  ```text
  Docs: https://docs.openclaw.ai
  Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw
  OpenClaw behavior questions: docs mirror first when web exists. ...
  If docs are silent/stale, say so and inspect GitHub source.
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** Sandboxed runs with host-only docs paths now advertise the public mirror and no longer contain the unreadable host path or "docs first via `read`" local-read guidance; sandboxed runs with workspace-local docs keep `Docs: <workspace>/docs` local guidance; non-sandboxed prompts are unchanged (byte-identical lines). Regression test was RED on origin/main (advertised `/opt/homebrew/...` host path) and GREEN after the patch; full suite 58/58.
- **Before evidence:** same scenario on origin/main rendered `Docs: /opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/openclaw/docs` + "docs first via `read`/local search", which sandboxed tools cannot read (`read` → "Sandbox path is container-only", `exec ls` → "No such file or directory" per the issue report).
- **What was not tested:** No live podman/docker sandboxed gateway session was launched locally; sandbox mount semantics (host workspace always mounted, package roots never mounted) were verified from `src/agents/sandbox/workspace-mounts.ts` and exercised through `sandboxInfo` in the prompt builder. Explicit user bind-mounts of the package docs cannot be detected from `EmbeddedSandboxInfo`; such setups fall back to the mirror. CI lanes pending on GitHub Actions.
- **Proof tier:** L2
- **Proof limitations:** Live sandbox container run not performed; the fallback output is deterministic real-builder output, and the accessibility rule follows the sandbox mount selection source.
- **Review state:** Awaiting CI + maintainer review

prs.title: refactor: avoid redundant session bookkeeping reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session replacement, restart recovery, and reset repeat reads of state already owned by the writer. Ordinary actor admission also checks twice that its own callback did not mutate the database.

## User Impact

Session bookkeeping does less redundant work. Durable settlement, approval and disclosure boundaries, destructive-cleanup revocation, and the final reset identity/lifecycle guard remain intact. No schema or public API changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the normalized entry returned by `writeSessionEntry` to publish replacement identities, preserving untouched case-sensitive lookup siblings. Reuse reset's post-drain entry until its final guarded mutation. Remove the actor admission mutation-revision sandwich and its synthetic direct-SQL test.

Removed-check ledger and accepted edges:

| Removed check | Accepted edge |
| --- | --- |
| Entry replacement's post-write identity snapshot | Trust the normalized writer result inside the same synchronous transaction; an unsupported direct write outside the owner is not rediscovered. |
| Branched-transcript replacement's post-write identity snapshot | Same owner contract; transcript authority checks remain. |
| Restart recovery's two post-write identity reads | Trust both writer results; required membership/full projection hydration remains. |
| Actor admission's before/after native mutation revision comparison | Unsupported admission callbacks that directly mutate the database are no longer separately diagnosed. Actual authority admission remains. |
| Reset's extra pre-boundary reload and session-ID comparison | An intervening replacement reaches the final no-op guard, preserving the newer entry, instead of raising the preliminary error. |

The sweep retained write-receipt invalidation shared with sibling writers, nested transcript rewrite publication ordering, settled-turn and delivery custody, approval/credential authority, cross-user disclosure checks, and destructive cleanup's lease-loss abort. Those protect supported writers or real effects. Deferred candidates include creation's readback, message-cut/parent-fork postimages, duplicate receipt filtering, and canonical-row validation cleanup; they need separate caller cutover or overlap coordination.

## Evidence

Format, changed-file oxlint, and `git diff --check` pass. Codex autoreview: two rounds, no actionable P0–P2 findings. CI and three alternating baseline/candidate SQL harness v3 pairs pending. Local host is loaded; no latency claim.

Focused regression coverage includes successive same-ID and different-ID replacement publication with case-sensitive siblings; same-ID and different-ID replacement during reset cleanup; existing atomic restart-recovery publication, actor rollback/settlement, and transcript branching tests.

T1: the changed worker operations introduce no main-thread SQLite calls. The touched mixed transcript module retains **3 → 3** inventory calls in the synchronous native transcript-lock callback API (`replaceEvents`, `appendMessage`, `appendMessageWithMessageSequence`). Moving that API requires a separate owner/public synchronous contract redesign; this PR does not disguise it as worker-only. Measured MAIN counts will be reported below.

| Harness phase | Base SQL / requests / MAIN | Candidate SQL / requests / MAIN |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Warmed turn | pending | pending |
| First turn | pending | pending |
| Restart boot / connect / first turn | pending | pending |
| Spawn | pending | pending |
| Compaction | pending | pending |

Production LOC: +20/−19; tests: +119/−78 (mostly parameterizing the existing reset regression). Per-operation attribution will be filled from the exact reviewed head before closeout. The shared harness does not exercise `sessions.reset`; the dedicated reset regression covers that boundary.

prs.title: feat(sessions): allow same-channel thread recall without agent-wide visibility
prs.body:
Closes #163256

## What Problem This Solves

Let an agent recall sibling threads in one verified channel without exposing every session owned by that agent.

## User Impact

Opt-in `tools.sessions.visibility: "channel"` enables same-channel retrieval while excluding other agents, channels, accounts and workspaces. Existing defaults and other visibility modes are unchanged. Sibling send, status/model changes and session mutations remain denied.

In channel mode, cross-session list, history, search and transcript-backed memory recall require a Gateway-hosted agent; standalone RPC-only readers fail closed. Self-only reads and ordinary memory/wiki retrieval retain their existing behavior. Cross-session history anchors must name the target's current admitted session ID; retained older incarnations do not inherit its current channel authorization.

This is not a complete multi-tenant sandbox: shared memory/filesystem access, direct channel-history tools, integrations and already-mixed transcripts need independent boundaries. No production deployment or live Slack traffic is included.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Require matching stored provider, explicit account, opaque channel destination, chat kind and workspace/space under the same agent. Missing or inconsistent facts deny access; main/DM, lineage, A2A and scoped grants cannot widen the channel ceiling.
- Recheck route, incarnation and physical owner at final disclosure, rather than trusting an earlier asynchronous admission. List/search already use a synchronous Gateway-owner read; history now serializes its buffered response inside that same boundary.
- Reject cross-session history anchors for a different or unverifiable incarnation before `chat.history` reads an old transcript.
- Carry query-local transcript-owner bindings through memory/wiki aggregation, then synchronously filter transcript results, citations and recall reservations before serialization. Ordinary memory/wiki results remain outside this transcript-only filter. The bridge uses the existing private-local memory SDK subpath, not a new supported public SDK contract.
- Keep archived transcript-backed memory excluded and preserve explicitly requested archived metadata-only session inventories.

## Verification

Exact head: `0fd1876bc7c8a8c9e1d55b997dd4844854b61b67`. Ordinary merge of upstream main `9a7d4d1b6802f463ce43666a44ff19177d559d0e`; no force push.

- Reproduced and repaired three disclosure defects: route withdrawal during awaited history, withdrawal before memory/wiki aggregation completes, and old-generation cross-session history anchors. The follow-up comment contains actual synthetic red/green stdout, not only contributor assertions.
- Final focused regression: **7 files / 88 tests passed after all guard and adapter changes; four supported wrapper shards completed in 34.49s**. Memory consumer coverage includes route withdrawal, incarnation replacement and a new forbidden alias while retaining permitted transcript/memory/wiki results.
- core production, owning memory production, agents-tool/SDK test types and the focused memory test-type probe passed; standard touched-file oxlint, formatting, config docs and diff checks passed. Full build and broad checks remain for exact-head canonical PR CI; no local full-build success is claimed.
- Independent manual source review found no further actionable P0-P2 in the repaired scope. This is distinct from the new upstream re-review.
- CI follow-up: the original Linux Control UI cleanup/admission race is retained as unresolved cause. Its selected case plus immediate neighbors passed locally (3 passed / 74 skipped, wrapper 20.37s); this is not proof of flakiness or repair. New-head hosted CI is pending.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Preserve stable-written session history and permit verified same-channel retrieval while excluding other channels/accounts/workspaces/providers/agents and denying sibling mutations. Separate consumer regressions cover withdrawal during outstanding history/wiki work.

Real environment tested: macOS, Node 24.19.0; isolated published OpenClaw 2026.10.3 Doctor/Gateway with real SQLite, then this exact candidate offline Doctor migration and actual source Gateway. Memory is explicitly disabled in this product fixture.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 OPENCLAW_CHANNEL_VISIBILITY_STABLE_CLI=/path/to/isolated/openclaw@2026.10.3/openclaw.mjs node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.sessions-channel-visibility-upgrade.product-proof.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` on Node 24.19.0, after an isolated exact-version baseline install

Evidence after fix: ```json
{
  "proof": "channel-visibility-stable-upgrade",
  "scope": "core-session-with-memory-disabled",
  "baselineVersion": "2026.10.3",
  "candidateOfflineDoctorMigration": true,
  "persistedHistoryRetained": true,
  "channelBoundary": true,
  "siblingMutationsDenied": true,
  "reassignedRouteDenied": true,
  "externalApisUsed": false,
  "memoryWorkerVerified": false,
  "limitation": "Memory worker not exercised; the explicit full scope requires built candidate SDK artifacts."
}
```

```text
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 44.82s
```

Observed result after fix: Stable-written history retained; sibling history/list/search allowed only within the verified channel; other channel/account/workspace/provider/agent fixtures excluded; sibling send/model changes denied without transcript/model mutation; subsequent route reassignment blocks recall.

What was not tested: Real native memory-worker engine, full public packaged updater/install path, live Slack/customer traffic, external model calls, cross-OS and broad benchmarks were not tested

## Evidence boundaries and remaining work

The memory aggregation regressions use real SQLite writers, the real in-process Gateway row owner and production tool consumption, with the search backend and recall-persistence sink stubbed. They are not a native memory-engine product proof. The fresh core fixture uses real Gateway processes and stable persisted state, but is not the public packaged updater as a whole.

The older 55.090s/64.30s Gateway proof belongs to published tree `db48b36f072113af3ec7881617a2aba23bf962a0`, not a later head relabel; see the [original report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163267#issuecomment-6185324019). The current-head rerun is recorded above.

Native-memory/full-updater proof gaps, new-head CI and re-review remain author follow-up; maintainer acceptance of the config/SDK product contract is separate. The remaining work is not maintainer-only. No production runtime or account configuration was changed.

prs.title: fix(state): refuse cached plugin reads after database quarantine
prs.body:
Related: #168635, #168999, #173534

## What Problem This Solves

Plugin-state reads can return cached values after shared-state database acquisition has refused a persisted quarantine.

## User Impact

Quarantined plugin state remains unavailable through the keyed-store cache. The existing repair owner, reader-pool routing and ordinary cache performance are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

The terminal-refusal owner invalidated cached handles without retiring physical schema facts that acquisition could publish before discovering quarantine. Those facts could still authorize the plugin-state row cache. Revoke them at that existing owner; introduce no new latch, cache, schema, dependency or hot-path SQL.

The lookup/lookupMany cache shortcut was added in `841272e230d0` (#168999), before the latest hourly's 22-commit window. Its failure-latch/schema-admission guards intended to preserve quarantine refusals. Earlier #168635 explicitly accepted that "A cached observation may retain its last committed value after a terminal database refusal is recorded" as a follow-up; the later lookup guard and existing quarantine test require fail-closed reads. This repair completes canonical revocation without removing the cache or weakening that contract. The suggested extension cleanup and ambient UI memory-type commits do not change these owners.

The existing quarantine test forces the unsafe acquisition shape with a real read-only schema inspection followed by canonical refusal. It retains lookup, lookupMany and register rejection assertions and adds entries/count checks. The final change is only these two quarantine files (+22/−1 lines).

## Evidence

- Main hourly 38836157770 reported a fail-open bulk read. Current main `161bd95c1d22` reproduced it: 22 passed / 1 failed, resolving `[{ ok: true, value: true }]` instead of rejecting.
- The forced regression fails at keyed lookup returning `true` when only the new revocation is omitted (64.73 s wrapper). With revocation restored, all 23 cases pass: `pnpm test src/plugin-state/plugin-state-store.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (115.57 s wrapper-reported wall, including artifact-lock cleanup wait).
- Reader/retention/quarantine-cleanup siblings pass: plugin-state-worker 20 cases (130.56 s), database-cache retention 1 (75.14 s), quarantine cleanup 8 (122.56 s). **52 tests pass across 4 files**, each run with one worker.
- Core production types, the owning state test typegraph, targeted type-aware lint, boundary lint, formatting and diff checks pass. Full `pnpm check:architecture` passes, including zero runtime/Madge cycles, SQL generation and Kysely/legacy-store guards. Independent P0–P2 review is scoped-clean.
- Main `bd5f760aecae` (#170534) already fixes the separately reported Gateway retention-sampling fixture. Its diff and body (five borrowing cases passed) were verified; that covered hunk is omitted here. Dropping it resolves the differing-comment merge conflict without rebasing unrelated main changes. The two retained files are byte-identical to the proven/reviewed candidate; their proof is reused.

Exact-head PR CI supplies broad proof. The first run belongs to prior head `00874bc3ae59`; it is not claimed as CI for the conflict-repair head. No CI rerun, timeout increase, skip or assertion removal. The follow-up push changes source solely to remove the landed peer fix and resolve a real merge conflict.

prs.title: fix(node-host): log original node worker supervisor failures
prs.body:
Closes #173351

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when a node worker supervisor command fails for an ordinary reason, the node log has no record of what went wrong.

## User Impact

User impact: operators debugging a failed node worker supervisor command (launch, status, cancel, and similar) can now find the original failure in the node log. Before, the only trace was a generic `UNAVAILABLE` response. The caller-facing response is unchanged, so there is no API or protocol change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ordinary supervisor failures were collapsed into a generic `UNAVAILABLE` / "node worker supervisor command failed" response, and the original diagnostic was never written anywhere. The fix logs the original error at the `UNAVAILABLE` branch in `invokeNodeWorkerSupervisorCommand`. It reuses the existing bounded, redacted worker-error formatting (`boundedWorkerErrorWithCode`, already used for workspace failures). The generic caller-facing message is preserved, so internal details still do not leak to callers.

A regression test covers both sides: the log contains the command name and the original failure text, and a `Bearer` secret in the error is redacted from the log.

## Evidence

- Focused regression (`logs the original supervisor failure while returning only the generic error`): passed
- Negative control against the old implementation: failed as expected
- Format: passed
- Lint: passed
- Production typecheck: passed
- Test typecheck: passed
- Autoreview: 0 actionable findings through P2

Known unrelated failure: the broader `src/node-host/invoke-worker-supervisor.test.ts` file has one pre-existing Windows/Git Bash path assertion failure. I reproduced it on a clean baseline at the same base commit, so it is not caused by this change. I am not claiming the whole test file passes.

prs.title: fix(webchat): make voice transcript echo visible in WebChat/Control UI history
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing recognized speech in saved user-message history when transcript echo is enabled for a voice note sent from WebChat/Control UI or a native chat client.

## User Impact

The approved transcript stays with the original user message after reopening history. The existing `tools.media.audio.echoTranscript` setting remains opt-in, with no new configuration or default change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway prepares the transcript through the existing selected-agent media runner, then passes the display text through the ordinary approval and canonical user-turn writer. The agent-facing speech remains machine-generated/untrusted, and synthesized speech is not promoted to slash-command input. Completed audio selections, including empty/failed/dropped outcomes, are reused by later enrichment without repeating that selection. Telegram's first-note mention preflight and outbound echo remain separate.

Transcription can precede the durable input acknowledgment. Declared `audio/*` client requests therefore wait on the captured connection by default; cancellation, disconnect, and explicit native deadlines remain available. This is not an unlimited agent-run timeout or a promise to terminate an already-running provider request/process immediately.

## Durable State

- Successful, approved speech becomes ordinary content on the existing canonical user message. Existing pending-input custody can hold the same enriched message while it waits for transcript commit.
- Embedded dispatch may capture the separate model-facing rendering in the existing optional `__openclaw.modelPromptProjection` metadata. This adds no new field contract, table, column, schema version, or persistence owner.
- Audio files and `media://inbound/…` references keep their existing format and lifecycle. Selection decisions and already-transcribed flags are request-local reuse state, not a new durable STT cache or job queue.
- No historical backfill or re-transcription is performed. Disabling the setting or rolling back does not erase already saved speech. Incognito retains its existing memory-actor behavior; attachment/CLI file lifecycles remain separate.

## Current Main Integration

Prepared head `4586a494ef440647693692e44c878c77e5c4dfa4` incorporates main `8ee1d36ae28960b475f8984a3849942f3cb77327` with contributor ancestry preserved, without a rebase or squash.

- Resolve the Android request-handler conflict while keeping both default audio ACK lifetime and current main's bounded Talk-catalog warming retry.
- Address the independent review's zero-deadline finding: disabling an outer RPC deadline must not defeat the catalog's own ten-second warm-up budget. Extend the existing public `requestDetailed` WebSocket test with `timeoutMs = 0`, retaining its negative controls.
- Reuse the existing input-admission assertion during audio preflight so routing/source/creator authority is checked before external effects, not only before the later write. Add a negative-control regression proving changed input authority starts no transcription command.
- Preserve main's WebChat wording and the feature's documented audio-acknowledgment behavior. The feature scope is 26 files: the prior 24 plus the existing Android regression and the Gateway input owner's assertion handoff.

## Evidence

- Exact prepared head: `4586a494ef440647693692e44c878c77e5c4dfa4`; reviewed tree: `f1f72a6a17a75962539e376d0692353a9628cac0`. Full 26-file independent review completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings. The signed integration preserves the contributor head and incorporated main as ancestors.
- Fresh exact-head [CI run 38844643874](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38844643874), attempt 1, completed successfully: 96 jobs, 76 successful and 20 skipped, with no failures. Required `openclaw/ci-gate` checks are successful. Current-head ClawSweeper follow-through is in progress; the prior-head verdict is not counted as this repair's review.
- All three affected Kotlin files passed the repository-pinned ktlint 1.8.0 with the repository configuration in a credential-free, network-isolated tool container; those exact bytes match this head. Git diff/whitespace, signature, ancestry and reviewed-tree equality checks passed.
- Added regressions cover the zero-deadline catalog warm-up and rejection of changed input routing before transcription process I/O. Exact-head CI passed the changed Node test lanes, all three Android test variants, Android ktlint, UI checks, production/test typechecks, lint and security-fast. No local execution of contributor tests is claimed.
- The macOS Swift regression job was skipped. CI's iPhone/iPad screenshot fixtures and evidence reduction passed, but are not a voice-send or real-device acceptance run. The existing native deadline regressions remain present; historical proof is not fresh-head native voice acceptance. No new recognition-accuracy or in-flight Stop claim is made.

### Accepted Historical Behavior Evidence

These artifacts remain bound to their stated source/integration heads, not a new device or external-provider run of the prepared head.

- [Immutable Android/WebGUI acceptance](https://github.com/dankarization/openclaw/blob/669a7dfd1ec8576cc97f4e35fe579cccf7d73c72/proofs/voice-user-transcript-20261005/README.md): the screenshots below show recognized speech in the original user message; the operator separately confirmed refresh/reopen persistence. Serving integration was OpenClaw 2026.9.8 at `b2f11f84d189125752c32d45ad0d306853ee7d7c`.
- [Immutable selected-agent transport and revocation proof](https://github.com/dankarization/openclaw/blob/dc281ca5d57c936ac2c338d530671b40325a4fa1/proofs/voice-authority-20261006/README.md), source `911e0f238e86451c0d2d24b9efe2b391398305e1`: actual multipart HTTP used the selected support agent's synthetic credential, not main's; actual ffmpeg/CLI positive controls ran. Preparation-time revocation produced zero uploads, conversions, or CLI starts. This is routing/effect proof, not external recognition accuracy or in-flight Stop proof.
- [Operator-reported mobile/macOS/WebGUI acceptance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163557#issuecomment-6022733558) is separate from those transport receipts.

![Android voice transcript in the user message](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dankarization/openclaw/669a7dfd1ec8576cc97f4e35fe579cccf7d73c72/proofs/voice-user-transcript-20261005/android-user-transcript.png)

![Same transcript in WebGUI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dankarization/openclaw/669a7dfd1ec8576cc97f4e35fe579cccf7d73c72/proofs/voice-user-transcript-20261005/web-user-transcript-redacted-v2.png)

Private identities and attachment identifiers are redacted; original audio remains attached. These captures do not establish fresh iOS acceptance or final-reply delivery.

Original feature and accepted proof by [dankarization](https://github.com/dankarization). This PR remains open and unmerged; auto-merge is not armed.

prs.title: test(ui): give cold source-mode e2e boots the 30s readiness budget
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: local `pnpm test:ui:e2e` runs of source-mode files (the `ui-e2e-serial-standalone` lane, e.g. `child-session-load-errors` and `session-management.promotion`) fail with "Control UI initial roster did not finish loading and rendering … waitForFunction: Timeout 10000ms exceeded" on roomy but busy hosts, while the same command passes with `CI=true`.

## User Impact

No product change. Developers get reliable local source-mode Control UI e2e runs without setting `CI=true`. Bundled shared-preview lanes keep their 10s fail-fast budget on roomy hosts, and CI and hosts with 4 or fewer CPUs keep 30s as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The readiness budget was 30s only on CI or small hosts. Files that start a private Vite dev server transform the source graph on first page load, and the lazily imported routes behind the first roster render routinely exceed 10s on a busy machine. The dev-server path in `startControlUiE2eServer` now raises the process's wait budget to the existing loaded 30s value. Each ui-e2e file runs in its own isolated fork, so the larger budget never reaches bundled files. Consumers read the live binding at call time, so the ~20 existing callers needed no changes.

Pre-warming the dev server was measured and rejected. Warming the static graph from `/src/main.ts` cost about 2s in setup and cut `goto` from 5.4s to 1.1s, but only shortened the failing roster wait from about 6.8s to 5.2s. That wait is dominated by dynamically imported route modules, which Vite's static pre-transform crawl doesn't reach.

## Evidence

Local runs on a 32-core Mac Studio at load average 70–90. `taskpolicy` slows the test tree while `availableParallelism()` still reports 32, so the 10s branch stays selected. Each run started with a cold `.artifacts/control-ui-e2e-vite` optimizer cache.

- Before, `taskpolicy -c utility`: red with the exact reported `Timeout 10000ms exceeded` (the cold first file failed). The harsher `taskpolicy -b` also failed both files.
- After, same `utility` clamp: green twice, at 19.0s/16.6s and 19.9s/31.2s per test.
- After, plain `pnpm test:ui:e2e ui/src/e2e/child-session-load-errors.e2e.test.ts ui/src/e2e/session-management.promotion.e2e.test.ts`: green, at 7.6s/7.5s per test.
- Budget split, from temporary instrumentation in one invocation: the bundled `tooltip-first-activation` process saw 10000ms, and the source-mode `child-session-load-errors` process saw 30000ms.
- `oxfmt --check`, `run-oxlint` on both files, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `git diff --check`: pass.

Gap: today's unthrottled runs of the reported SHA `ce7439db00d9` and current main both passed. Main had only about 3s of headroom (a 7.1s roster wait), so the red proof uses the QoS clamp to emulate the contended host.

prs.title: feat(memory): read sections by heading
prs.body:
Related: #173706

## What Problem This Solves

Agents that know a Markdown memory section by name currently need to discover its source line range before reading it, which can leave nearby conditions or exceptions out of a bounded excerpt.

## User Impact

Users can ask for a named section such as "Refunds" and receive its child "Exceptions" section too, within the existing excerpt budgets and with accurate source line numbers. No configuration or migration is required, and reads without `heading` are unchanged.

First version: unique, exact ATX heading text (`#` through `######`); memory corpus only. Missing/duplicate headings fail explicitly instead of guessing. Other heading styles and wiki/all reads remain available through the existing line-based interface.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds optional `heading` to the existing memory-core tool and selects the section in the existing authorized memory reader. It preserves child sections, ignores fenced examples and leading YAML frontmatter, and ends before the next same-or-higher-level heading. Keep `heading` with an absolute `from: nextFrom` for bounded continuation; offsets outside the section are rejected.

No new tool, index, database schema, permission, dependency, or configuration switch. The heading-aware retrieval idea is adapted from Orca, not a transfer of its application data or runtime.

## Evidence

- Focused production-path and reader tests: **51 passed across 3 files**, plus **28 existing tool-contract tests passed** (79 total). Includes real `memory_get` execution, nested sections, Chinese/CRLF, code fences, frontmatter, line/character budgets, continuation boundaries, missing/ambiguous headings, unsupported corpora, and unchanged path authorization.
- Test wall time: result-shaping file 0.269s; authorized-reader file 1.77s; existing real-manager suite 57.74s including worker preparation (new feature case 41ms). Combined wrapper wall time 64.94s. Existing tool-contract suite 20.09s including worker preparation (wrapper 22.39s). CI timing is pending.
- Core and extension production typechecks and targeted lint passed. Formatting, assertion-safety and line-cap ratchets, documentation configuration examples, and documentation links passed (zero broken internal links). Full test typecheck matrices and broad suites are left to PR CI.
- Independent Codex autoreview: **scoped-clean at P0-P2**. No accepted/actionable findings. Review did not independently verify unchanged remote transport; source inspection confirms the client spreads remaining read parameters and the same-version worker forwards them to the authorized reader.
- Scope simplification: reuse the existing read and truncation owners rather than introducing a reader, tool, cache, or persistent state. Production delta +94/-4 lines, tests +130/-0, docs +21/-1 (before any mechanical formatting changes).
- All document fixtures are synthetic. No provider calls, credentials, private notes, user logs, or operator Gateway state were used. No authenticated full-agent UX claim; proof is the real tool boundary and safe reader.

This proposes a new optional capability; maintainer product acceptance remains required.

Maintainer edits are disabled because workflow/secrets access on the fork has not been authorized. Follow-up commits can be supplied by the author; this does not request access to any repository Secrets.

The Solid migration needs one documented controller replacement recipe and a guard against bringing the old lifecycle back after retirement. Shared event bindings also repeat native listener teardown.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Avatar loading/error behavior, native overlay events, routes, tags, selectors, and lazy loading remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a worked controller-to-Solid example to the existing playbook, expose the small `lib/reactive/listener.ts` teardown helper for explicit effect/settle lifetimes, and use it for overlay event forwarding. Avatar load/error listeners use the same explicit teardown, including retained detached images; the Gateway page effect no longer wraps its already-untracked apply phase in `untrack`.

The existing syntax-aware Lit inventory now counts lifecycle identifiers and controller classes. Growth remains advisory while production callers exist; once the production baseline has no controller patterns, the same guard rejects reintroductions. Comments, strings, and test fixtures do not hold enforcement open.

Remaining shared controller adapters still have production callers in the assistant panel, command palette, session widgets, and custodian setup. Their removal belongs with those callers' cutovers; this PR does not introduce another implementation or change domain ownership.

| `pnpm tsgo:ui` | Passed |

prs.title: fix(codex): first Codex turn fails on a busy host while the app-server starts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the first message to a Codex-runtime agent after a Gateway start fails with "Your request couldn't be completed: LLM request timed out." when the host is busy, even though no model request was made.

## User Impact

User impact: the first Codex turn after a restart now waits for the local Codex app-server to finish starting instead of failing after 10 seconds. If startup genuinely exceeds its budget, the error says so ("Codex app-server startup exceeded its wait budget. Retry this request; if it persists, check the Gateway logs.") instead of blaming the LLM.

## Why This Change Was Made

Native model discovery runs before turn admission with a 10-second budget. On a cold Gateway it is the first caller of the shared app-server, so that budget paid for spawning and initializing the shared client. When discovery's budget expired, the shared startup was aborted and the client closed, and the turn that needed it failed. Shared startup now has its own deadline, derived from the existing startup calculation (10× the configured request timeout, 600 s by default). A caller whose own budget expires abandons only its wait, and short request budgets start after the client is ready. Startup timeouts use the existing preflight error instead of the generic timeout classifier.

## Evidence

- Live, before (stock main, fresh state, host load ~40–97 on 32 cores): first Codex turn failed in ~13 s with `codex app-server scope timed out phase=acquire-client timeoutMs=10000 … acquireStartup=created-shared … initialize pending`. The second (warm) turn succeeded.
- Live, after (this change on the same base, fresh state, cold Gateway, host load ~112): the first Codex turn completed (`pong`). The Gateway log has zero scope timeouts and no "LLM request timed out".
- Regression: two fake-clock tests in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/shared-client.test.ts` abandon the only discovery waiter, leave a gap, delay initialize/catalog observation past a later short budget, then complete `turn/start` on the same physical client. With only the production changes reverted, both fail (`stdinDestroyed` expected false).
- `shared-client.test.ts` + `request.test.ts`: 202 passed. `attempt-timeouts.test.ts` and `model-catalog.test.ts` also pass. Extension typecheck, madge cycles (0), oxfmt, and `git diff --check` passed. Codex autoreview scoped-clean at P0–P2.
- Known gap: local scoped oxlint for the extension graph timed out during SDK declaration preparation under host load; CI runs lint.
- Size: production +108/−108, tests +117/−90, docs +9 (timeouts reference).

prs.title: fix(gateway): incognito turns send clients a stream error instead of their start event
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: every incognito turn sends clients a stream error ("seq gap") instead of its start event, and logs dispatch failures at the end of the turn.

## User Impact

User impact: incognito sessions on both the OpenClaw and Codex runtimes emit normal lifecycle start/end events again, so clients no longer receive a spurious error or a gap in the event stream for every incognito turn. Incognito privacy guarantees are unchanged: nothing on disk, excluded from search and rosters, gone after restart.

## Why This Change Was Made

Incognito sessions became memory-only (#170712), but two paths were not cut over. Lifecycle admission treated the memory owner's identity as a filesystem path and stat'ed a nonexistent incognito SQLite file, so the start event failed to dispatch and clients saw a sequence gap. Three row-projection readers treated a released turn handle as a closed session, so end-of-turn dispatch read a released actor. Admission now selects the memory owner directly, and the row readers acquire their own existing-session handle while keeping session-close and disclosure checks.

## Evidence

- Live, before (stock main, fresh state): `sessions.create { incognito: true }` on both runtimes answered correctly, but clients received `{"stream":"error","data":{"reason":"seq gap","expected":3,"received":4}}` and no lifecycle start. The log showed `Agent event dispatch failed … ENOENT … stat '…/incognito-openclaw-agent.sqlite'` and `Lifecycle event dispatch failed … Session actor is released`.
- Live, after (this change, fresh state): incognito turns on both runtimes emit lifecycle start=1, end=1, zero error events, and a normal final. The log has zero incognito dispatch failures.
- Regressions (fail with only production reverted): `server-chat.lifecycle-read.test.ts` (ENOENT on the nonexistent database), `session-row-projection.memory.test.ts` and `session-row-projection.incognito.test.ts` (released actor). The shared lifecycle test checks queued/start/reply/end sequences 1, 2, 3, 4.
- 47 tests across 10 incognito, session, and actor suites passed (one Windows-only skip). Existing privacy, no-disk, search-exclusion, and lifetime tests pass. Codex autoreview scoped-clean.
- Size: production +12/−16, tests +143/−1, docs +1/−1.
