prs.title: fix(agents): restore saved history for fresh Claude CLI sessions on a native login
prs.body:
Related: #154716

Supersedes #156600 (builds on its account-fingerprint approach; its author is credited as co-author on the commits)

Note: #154716 carries the `clawsweeper:needs-product-decision` and `clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr` labels and this PR does not fix the existing-session gap described under Gaps, so it uses `Related:` and should not auto-close the issue.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Claude CLI conversation on a native Claude login loses its saved history whenever its Claude session is replaced or lost, because OpenClaw cannot name the login's owner and so refuses to replay it.

With the `claude-cli` backend on a native Claude CLI login and no OpenClaw-managed credential, the history boundary cannot build an owner fingerprint. `prepareCliHistoryBoundary` writes no `cliHistoryBoundary`, `prepare.ts` turns the missing writer into `rawTranscriptReseedReason: "auth-unknown"`, and `loadCliSessionPromptContext` refuses to seed saved history into any fresh CLI session (replacement session, cleared binding, lost native transcript). On the base commit every native turn logs `cli session history refused across auth boundary: reason=auth-unknown` (scenario 1 below). On the author's own install (a file-backed native login) all 301 session entries carry an empty boundary.

The guard exists so saved history never crosses to a different account. This change keeps that property and adds the native login as an accepted owner only when the operator opts in (`plugins.entries.anthropic.config.historyRecovery.attestNativeLogin: true`), only when Anthropic attests which account its credential belongs to, and only for the environment the Claude process is actually started with. Without the opt-in, nothing changes: the native login has no owner and saved history stays refused, as on main.

## User Impact

Nothing changes for an install that does not opt in. With `plugins.entries.anthropic.config.historyRecovery.attestNativeLogin: true` on a Gateway host whose Claude CLI login is a readable credential, a fresh Claude session for a conversation that started after the opt-in gets its saved history reseeded again, with or without the `anthropic:claude-cli` profile. If the login changes, is revoked, is selected differently by the child environment, or Anthropic does not attest it, saved history is refused, as the contract table below lists.

What an operator who opts in sees differently (without the opt-in, OpenClaw never reads the native token for history recovery and makes no profile request: row 35 below, 0 requests, the same prompt as current main):

- The Gateway makes one `GET https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/profile` per access token it has not attested yet, with the token Claude CLI itself would send there (834 ms measured once on a real login). Later turns on the same token make no request. `openclaw agent --local` starts a new process per turn, so it makes one request per turn.
- A turn prepared within ten minutes of its access token's expiry runs without saved history, because Claude CLI rotates the token before it accepts the prompt (measured below). The next turn is offered history again.
- A turn whose writer may replay saved history fails with `CLI history authority changed before execution` if its login changes, or cannot be attested, between preparation and the prompt reaching Claude, instead of sending that history to another account. That is every turn of a conversation the native login owns, fresh or resumed, except a turn prepared within ten minutes of token expiry, which runs without saved history. Conversations the native login does not own are never refused because of it.

One new plugin config key, `historyRecovery.attestNativeLogin` in the Anthropic plugin's config schema, default `false`. No schema migration. Conversations that already have history and no recorded boundary stay fenced, including conversations written before the opt-in (see Gaps).

## Why This Change Was Made

Main documents opaque CLI logins as unable to authorize replay (`docs/gateway/cli-backends.md`, "History account boundaries"). That is right when the login is only a profile name or a local record. It is wrong when the Gateway host holds a readable credential and Anthropic can say which account it belongs to. An acceptable owner has to cover the no-profile install (the bundled backend sets `autoSelectAuthProfile: false`), must be bound to the credential rather than to the `.claude.json` account record beside it, must be rechecked wherever saved history is sent to Claude or a turn becomes the owner's history, must survive Claude CLI's own token rotation, and must not put a network request or a subprocess on every transcript write.

## The change in one sentence

Once the operator opts in, the native Claude login's owner is the account uuid Anthropic's OAuth profile endpoint returns for the exact access token the child Claude would use, attested asynchronously at preparation and after the run, and rechecked synchronously at every spawn, prompt send, prompt hook answer that carries the turn's private context, and coverage commit against an in-process attestation cache keyed by a per-process HMAC of the token.

Shape of the whole PR against base `012bb1ccaf0` (five commits, all signed): 22 production files +910/-145 (21 TypeScript files and the Anthropic plugin manifest), 14 test files +2301/-241, and three docs files (the contract paragraphs and the config baseline counts and hash); 39 files, +3217/-390 in total. The attestation lives in `provider-auth-claude-compat.ts` (credential read, profile request, cache), `cli-credentials.ts` (the resolver seam), `history-boundary.ts` (async attestation, synchronous rechecks, background re-attestation, refresh window), `execute.ts` (one post-run settle call) and `prepare.ts`. The owner confirmation inside worker transactions is in the turn commit and transcript report paths in `src/config/sessions` and in the SessionManager metadata worker in `src/agents/sessions`. The check on the prompt hook answer is in `extensions/anthropic/cli.runtime.ts`. The opt-in is declared in `extensions/anthropic/openclaw.plugin.json` and read by `isNativeCliLoginAttestationEnabled` in `cli-credentials.ts`.

Design:

- The attestation runs only when the operator opts in: `plugins.entries.anthropic.config.historyRecovery.attestNativeLogin: true`, declared in the Anthropic plugin's config schema with default `false` and a UI hint that names the endpoint the token goes to. `prepareCliHistoryBoundary` checks `isNativeCliLoginAttestationEnabled(provider, params.config)` before it resolves the native owner, so without the opt-in no credential is read for history recovery, no request is made and the turn is prepared exactly as on main (`auth-unknown`). The rechecks below exist only on writers whose owner was attested at preparation. The run's config is read per turn, so turning the opt-in off takes effect on the next turn.
- `attestClaudeNativeLoginOwner({ env })` (`src/plugin-sdk/provider-auth-claude-compat.ts`) reads the access token the CLI would use under `env` with the CLI's own precedence (Keychain first on macOS, bounded non-interactive lookups, tri-state so only `security`'s item-not-found exit 44 lets `.credentials.json` stand; then the file). It sends that token, and nothing else, to `https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/profile` (`Authorization: Bearer`, `redirect: "error"`, 3 s `AbortSignal.timeout`, the process global fetch, so the env-proxy dispatcher OpenClaw installs at startup applies). Claude CLI 2.1.283 calls the same URL with the same header (bundle excerpt below). The owner is `uuid:<account.uuid>` from the response. No owner on any failure: network error, timeout, non-2xx, a body without `account.uuid`, no credential, or an access token already expired. The error is dropped, not logged. The `.claude.json` account record is no longer read.
- The cache maps `HMAC-SHA256(key, token)` to the attested owner, with `key` from `randomBytes(32)` per process, at most 64 entries, only in memory. A token belongs to one account for its whole life, so an entry can stop matching (rotation, logout) but never start naming someone else. Only successes are cached. Nothing about the token is persisted; the stored boundary keeps only the existing `cli-history-v1` fingerprint over `["native-login", "uuid:<account>"]`.
- `readClaudeNativeLoginOwner({ env })` is the synchronous recheck: it rereads the credential and returns the cached owner for that exact token, or nothing. It never touches the network. The seam stays `resolveNativeCliLoginOwner(backendId, env)` (now asynchronous, returning `{ owner?, refreshDueAt? }`) plus `readAttestedNativeCliLoginOwner(backendId, env)` for the synchronous checks; both return nothing for backends other than `claude-cli`.
- Preparation awaits the attestation for the environment the child will start from (`resolveCliChildEnv`, under the run's skill env snapshot, as before). Spawn, prompt send and coverage commits call the synchronous recheck, so the per-turn Keychain budget stays at 10 lookups for a readable item.
- Claude CLI rotates its access token itself, before it answers `initialize` and so before the prompt is sent, once the token is within 5 minutes of expiry (bundle: `now + 300000 >= expiresAt`; probe below). Two rules follow:
  - A turn prepared with a token that expires within 10 minutes runs without saved history (`writer.replaysHistory === false`; `prepare.ts` treats it like `auth-unknown`), and still covers its rows.
  - A boundary check on a turn without saved history that sees a token this process has not attested starts a background attestation of it. Coverage waits until it settles and stops for good if it names another account. A turn carrying saved history refuses an unattested token outright.
- After the child exits and before the turn's rows commit, `writer.settleNativeLogin()` awaits any background attestation and, if the prepared token had entered the refresh window, attests whatever token the child left behind.
- Worker coverage confirms the owner from inside the worker's write transaction. The host no longer decides before it dispatches the command. When coverage is about to advance, the worker puts a probe (a `SharedArrayBuffer` cell) on a transaction admission request (turn commits) or on the commit admission of the write (transcript reports). The host answers the cell with the live owner check, synchronously, right before it grants that admission, and the worker reads the answer after the grant. A missing answer, a missing owner check or a check that throws means the owner does not hold. On a mismatch the rows commit and coverage is not advanced. The check runs once per coverage commit, so the Keychain budget is unchanged. The in-process path checks inside its transaction as before.
- A resumed Claude session also receives saved data: durable reference context from the transcript and the conversation's interrupted inputs. So any native turn whose writer replays history counts as carrying saved history at spawn and prompt send, fresh or resumed, including a conversation's first turn. A turn prepared inside the refresh window runs without saved history and receives no interrupted inputs either.

- Claude asks for the turn's private context (interrupted inputs, durable reference context) through its `UserPromptSubmit` hook after it has received the prompt, so the hook answer is the last place that saved data leaves OpenClaw. The stdio transport writes each answer through a closure the Claude runtime returns, called synchronously at the final write. The host passes the bundled Claude runtime a host-internal `assertPrivateInputCurrent` (set only for a native-login writer, like the forwarded auth credential: it is not part of the plugin SDK `CliBackendExecuteContext` type, `ClaudeCliExecuteContext` in `cli.runtime.ts` declares it), which runs the turn's full `assertCurrent` (on a native login: reread the credential and require this process's attestation of that exact token for the same owner). The runtime calls it before it sends the prompt and again when it answers a `UserPromptSubmit` hook with `additionalContext`. If the second check fails, Claude receives an empty hook answer and the saved context is withheld. The public execution context is unchanged from main.

- SessionManager appends committed by the metadata worker take the same host owner check. The probe rides on the command's one transaction admission and the host answers it before it grants. Coverage facts that ask for the check advance coverage only on a confirmed answer, so a write path that cannot ask keeps its rows and leaves coverage where it is. Writers whose owner cannot change during the run (a static credential or a named OAuth account) carry no owner check.
- What a mismatch does depends on what is at stake, as before: a turn that may carry saved history is refused before Claude receives it; a change after the prompt was sent withholds the turn's private context from the prompt hook answer; that change, or one on a turn prepared inside the refresh window, lets the turn run, and its rows are kept but not covered, so coverage stops and the next turn is refused that history until `/new` or an empty reset.

`docs/gateway/cli-backends.md` states the contract: what is attested, the request and its timeout, fail-closed cases, what is held in memory and what is persisted, the synchronous rechecks, the refresh window, and the restart limitation.

## What this PR decides, and why

The question is what may authorize native replay: the local account record beside a readable credential, or an identity bound to the credential itself. This PR binds the owner to the credential with Anthropic's own account lookup (option C below), and only for an operator who opts in. Every other install keeps D, main's behavior.

| | A: local account record | B: `claude auth status` | C: authenticated profile request (this PR) | D: keep native replay fenced |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Owner source | `.claude.json` `oauthAccount.accountUuid`, read from the child's environment while a credential exists | the same record, as the CLI reports it | the `account.uuid` Anthropic returns for the exact access token the child would use | none |
| Credential for account B beside a record for account A | owned by A: history replayed to B's credential | owned by A | owned by B: A's history refused | refused |
| Bound to the executing environment | yes | yes, if run with the child env | yes: attested for the child env at preparation, rechecked at spawn, send and every coverage commit | not applicable |
| Cost per turn | 10 Keychain lookups (readable item) | one subprocess per check, 135 to 1673 ms measured | the same 10 lookups; one request per new access token (834 ms measured), none for a token already attested | none |
| Token rotation by Claude CLI | owner unchanged | owner unchanged | the rotated token is attested before the turn's rows are covered; a turn prepared inside the refresh window runs without saved history | not applicable |
| What it sends where | nothing | nothing | the access token, to the Anthropic endpoint Claude CLI itself sends it to | nothing |

Why C:

- A and B cannot detect the mismatch. Run against synthetic files with the real Claude CLI 2.1.283, `claude auth status --json` reports a fake token as logged in and returns whatever account the record holds; editing the record moves the same credential from account A to account B ([identity/claude-auth-status-probe.txt](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/1e6c130ad78e23be6b323b15eaaafa1e9ee6f438/final/identity/claude-auth-status-probe.txt)). The CLI's own refresh path never rewrites `accountUuid` or `emailAddress` ([identity/cli-bundle-excerpt.txt](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/1e6c130ad78e23be6b323b15eaaafa1e9ee6f438/final/identity/cli-bundle-excerpt.txt)).
- Anything keyed on token material alone changes owner on every refresh: one real refresh rotated both the access and the refresh token while the account stayed the same ([identity/refresh-rotation.txt](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/1e6c130ad78e23be6b323b15eaaafa1e9ee6f438/final/identity/refresh-rotation.txt)). C keys the cache on the token but takes the owner from Anthropic, so a rotation needs one new attestation, not a new owner.
- The profile request is the one Claude CLI makes itself. The bundle's `AFe(e)` is ``gt.get(`${BASE_API_URL}/api/oauth/profile`, {headers: {Authorization: `Bearer ${e}`, ...}, timeout: 1e4})``, validated against `{account: {uuid, email}, organization: {uuid}}`. OpenClaw already sends Claude OAuth tokens to the same host for usage (`src/infra/provider-usage.fetch.claude.ts`, `GET /api/oauth/usage`).
- D keeps native conversations losing history when their Claude session is replaced. It stays the default: C sends the token to Anthropic, so it runs only for an operator who sets `historyRecovery.attestNativeLogin`.

### Real built binary

The real `openclaw agent --local` (built `dist`), a real SQLite session and worker threads, synthetic login files on disk, the real Anthropic Claude runtime and stream-json transport. The `claude` executable is a synthetic child (`harness/bin/claude`) that speaks the control protocol and records every record that reaches it, with the account named by the login's `.claude.json` record (`loginAccount`) and by its credential (`credentialAccount`) at that instant. It can rewrite the login at chosen moments: `FAKE_ON_INIT` after it initializes and before the prompt is sent, `FAKE_ON_USER` after it receives the prompt. By default it writes no Claude project transcript, so every later turn enters the fresh-session reseed branch; with `FAKE_WRITE_TRANSCRIPT=1` (scenarios 23 to 26) it writes one under the session id OpenClaw passed, so later turns resume. **The Anthropic profile endpoint is a local STUB** (`harness/profile-stub.mjs`), reached through a preload that redirects only that one URL (`harness/shim/profile-fetch-shim.mjs`). ## Gaps

- **The access token leaves the process, for an operator who opts in.** Only with `historyRecovery.attestNativeLogin: true` (default `false`, row 35: no request without it). It goes only to `https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/profile`, once per token not yet attested in the process, with redirects refused, a 3 s timeout and errors dropped unread. The token is never logged, stored, refreshed or written back. A proxy was not exercised. The opt-in's UI hint names the endpoint.
- **An idle, expired token after a Gateway restart has no owner.** An access token that expired while the Gateway was down cannot be attested until Claude refreshes it. The first turn on it has no owner, and that conversation's history stays refused until `/new` or an empty reset. Persisting attestations across restarts would mean persisting a token-derived value, which this PR does not do.
- **A refresh-due turn runs without saved history.** A turn prepared within 10 minutes of token expiry runs without saved history, because Claude rotates the token before the prompt and the send check could not prove the new one. The next turn is offered history again (scenario 20).
- **A rotation outside the CLI's refresh window stops coverage.** If the CLI rotates the token outside that window (for example after a server-side revocation and a 401 recovery), the new token is not attested before the turn's rows commit, so coverage stops and later turns are refused history (scenario 21). Detecting this would cost a Keychain read after every turn; the settle reads only when a rotation is expected.
- **Transient failures fence the conversation.** A profile request that fails at preparation, and a Keychain lookup that fails at a coverage commit, stop coverage until `/new` or an empty reset. The reply is kept. Only successes are cached, so a failed attestation retries on the next turn.
- **A login without the `user:profile` scope has no owner.** A long-lived `claude setup-token` credential carries only `user:inference`; the real profile endpoint answers it with HTTP 403 (`OAuth token does not meet scope requirement any_of(user:profile, user:office)`). Run against a login like that, the branch refuses saved history exactly as BEFORE does (`reason=auth-unknown`, `historyPrompt=none`, reply `UNKNOWN`), so those installs get no recovery. That is the fail-closed outcome; the run is in the evidence folder, `mini-setup-token`.
- **Some endpoint behaviors were not exercised.** A real successful token refresh, a revoked token and an HTTPS proxy were not run against the real endpoint; the harness endpoint is a stub.
- **Sessions that already have history and no recorded boundary stay unknown.** Only conversations that start empty after the opt-in benefit (row 37); `/new` or an empty reset establishes the boundary. History written by v2026.10.2 is kept and not adopted (scenario 27).
- **Plugin-defined backends wrapping Claude** (`id` other than `claude-cli`) are not covered.
- **A last-instant window remains in worker coverage.** The worker asks the host for the owner check from inside its write transaction and the host answers right before it grants. A credential replaced between that answer and the end of the same SQLite transaction (microseconds on the worker) is not seen for that write, and is caught at the next boundary. The worker cannot read the Keychain or the attestation cache itself, so a fully atomic check is not possible. A reassignment while the command is queued, or during any awaited preparation, is seen (scenario 22 and the queued tests).
- **Saved notes are not shown reaching a resumed session.** A note reaches a Claude CLI turn only when its row is covered, and no shipped path reachable from `openclaw agent` writes a covered note into a claude-cli conversation (the plugin-SDK append in row 32 is uncovered, as on main). The resumed-session context that is shown is the interrupted input (rows 28 to 31). The refusal does not depend on which saved data is present (rows 24, 25, 30, 31, 33, 34; RED3, RED4).
- **The metadata-worker path is shown by a test, not by the built binary.** The CLI runner never posts `session.metadata.append` or `session.transcript.appendMessage` (row 32), so no shipped CLI flow reaches it. `history-boundary.native-login-metadata.test.ts` runs it on the real worker thread and SQLite (RED1, RED2).
- **The real Claude recovery run was not repeated at the pushed head.** It ran at `69861729ddf` on base `0816aa1b57dc`; at the pushed head the same paths are shown by the harness scenarios above with a synthetic child and the stub endpoint.
- **Three failures are present without this change.** The `src/config/sessions` archive-read timeout reproduces on pristine main (Tests). `check:changed` fails the env-var count budget (452 below 453) and the dead export scan (`classifyFsSafeReadError`, `TranscriptTestHost`) on files this diff does not touch.
- **Incognito sessions on a native login may stop coverage.** The in-memory incognito actor confirms the owner only through the running turn's writer when that writer is in scope; otherwise it keeps the rows and stops coverage. No test covers a native login on an incognito session.
- **One new plugin config key.** `plugins.entries.anthropic.config.historyRecovery.attestNativeLogin` grows the plugin config surface by two entries, so `docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json` raises the plugin budget from 4623 to 4625 and `config-baseline.sha256` is regenerated with `pnpm config:docs:gen`.
- **Unrelated suites were not run.** The full suite, the e2e and live lanes, and the Docker lanes were not run. `check:changed` selects `core`, `coreTests`, `extensions`, `extensionTests` and `docs` for this diff, all of which ran above together with the owning-directory lanes. One `src/config/sessions` test is red on main as well (see Tests), and the AGENTS.md files do not require unrelated suites.

prs.title: fix(agents): treat empty .git directories as non-Git workspaces
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An otherwise non-Git agent workspace with an empty `.git` directory is classified as a damaged checkout. Repository discovery then emits “Git metadata is unavailable … checkout preserved” instead of treating Git features as unavailable.

## User Impact

Ordinary child sessions can use the workspace without Git features, and its empty `.git` directory stays untouched. Explicit worktree requests report “agent workspace is not a git checkout.” Linked-worktree pointers with missing targets and partial metadata still fail closed with checkout-preservation guidance.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared checkout-discovery owner now skips readable empty `.git` directories while retaining ancestor discovery. Nonempty directories, pointer files, and unreadable metadata keep the existing preservation behavior. No caller-specific fallback, cache, migration, or workspace mutation was added.

History: the preservation error was introduced by 8e4eb78fa20b (#132706, August 29), moved into the repository-path owner by f0fafba02efd (#146273, September 12), and discovery moved into the shared workspace helper in 3ac0c058fe16 (#170467, October 13). The October 15 display-cache refactor retained the same existence-only detector.

## Evidence

- Before: the new empty-directory regression failed with the exact preservation error through the real repository resolver. Both damaged child-worktree cases passed (1 failed, 2 passed; 92.98 s including cold worker preparation).
- After: all three focused Gateway regressions pass (115.96 s including cold worker preparation; 14.70 s test time). Workspace display-cache regression passes (14.79 s wall; 0.37 s test time). Both focused checkout-discovery tests pass (20.84 s wall; 0.19 s test time). Total: 6 focused tests passed across 3 existing files. Changed-file oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): clean at P0–P2. Autoreview refused the provider/config mismatch before starting; operator configuration was not changed.
- Simplification pass: one existing detection owner, no duplicate fallback. Production delta: +12/-4 lines (net +8), required to distinguish empty directories from metadata that must remain protected. Tests: +64/-2 lines. Documentation: +5 lines.
- Correctness repair; no throughput or latency claim and no performance benchmark. No Testbox/Crabbox lease, repository-wide local build/typecheck/lint, or suite run. Broad validation belongs to PR CI. Live workspace data was not modified.

Focused command (remaining cases belong to PR CI):

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/workspace-git.test.ts src/agents/worktrees/git.test.ts src/gateway/server.sessions.create-worktree-spawn.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'workspace Git presentation|returns the nearest checkout root|returns null outside|child sessions use an empty|child worktree sessions preserve'
```

prs.title: feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage
prs.body:
feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can emit skill-usage diagnostics while an agent reads or invokes a skill, but that observed runtime signal is not available through the durable audit surface. Operators therefore cannot inspect which skills were actually used during a run from the audit CLI/API.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first revision inferred skill selection from prompt text after attempt completion. Review correctly called that out as the wrong boundary: prompt inference is not proof of skill use and it also risked perturbing the embedded attempt-result contract.

This revision records only observed runtime skill usage from the existing `before_tool_call` skill-usage boundary:

- Skill read/command activation is detected where `recordRunSkillUsage()` already emits runtime diagnostics.
- A metadata-only `skill_selection` audit event is emitted with `selectionSource: "observed_runtime"` and `selectionConfidence: "observed"`.
- No prompt text, tool arguments, tool output, or skill file contents are persisted.
- `skill_selection` is persisted outside run-start deduplication so it is not dropped after `agent.run.started`.
- Legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only; the versioned `audit.activity.list` surface exposes skill-selection records.
- `completeEmbeddedAttemptResult()` is restored to the production calling contract, preserving the existing truncated-stream/tool recovery behavior.

## User Impact

- `openclaw audit --kind skill_selection` can show observed skill usage for a run through the activity-list API.
- Existing `audit.list` clients keep their shipped run/tool event shape and do not receive the new record kind.
- Operators get a durable metadata trail for actual skill usage without sensitive prompt or file-content capture.

## Evidence

Current-head validation after merging `upstream/main` and removing the unrelated `USER.md` bootstrap policy change:

```bash
pnpm tsgo:core
pnpm protocol:check:swift
pnpm db:kysely:check
pnpm lint:kysely
pnpm check:architecture
pnpm test src/agents/workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts src/audit/audit-events.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.test.ts
```

Results:

- `pnpm tsgo:core` passed.
- `pnpm protocol:check:swift` passed after regenerating `GatewayModels.swift`.
- `pnpm db:kysely:check` passed after regenerating `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts`.
- `pnpm lint:kysely` passed after moving ordinary companion-table insert/read/prune queries to the sync Kysely owner.
- `pnpm check:architecture` passed, including generated Kysely verification, Kysely guardrails, and database-first legacy-store guard.
- Targeted Vitest run passed 4 shards in 22.13s.
- `audit-events.test.ts`: 54 tests passed, including companion-table storage, bounded retention, and observed runtime projection.
- `server-methods/audit.test.ts`: 34 tests passed, including explicit `skill_selection`/`observed` activity access and V1-compatible unfiltered activity.
- `audit.test.ts`: 7 protocol schema tests passed, including activity schema discrimination.
- `workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts`: 9 tests passed; shared sessions now drop only root `MEMORY.md`, leaving `USER.md` behavior unchanged.
- `pnpm exec oxlint src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` passed. A full local `pnpm lint:core` was started but manually stopped after 6+ minutes with no diagnostic output; CI remains the authoritative full core-lint signal.

Published-release upgrade, older-reader, and candidate-reopen proof:

- the published `v2026.9.4` tag at `3a9d69db3` created a fresh state database and wrote legacy `agent_run` sequence `1`.
- candidate head `7d74807a5` opened that exact database, preserved the legacy row, created the additive `audit_skill_selection_events` table, and wrote observed `debug-toolkit` sequence `2`.
- `v2026.9.4` then reopened the candidate-used database without migration or schema errors, ignored the additive table, and wrote a second legacy `agent_run` at shared sequence `3`.
- the candidate reopened the same database and returned sequences `[3, 2, 1]`, including both legacy rows and the retained skill-selection row.
- physical SQLite readback reported `integrity_check: ok`, `user_version: 17`, `audit_events: 2`, and `audit_skill_selection_events: 1`.
- this proves published release → candidate upgrade → published older-reader open/use → candidate reopen while preserving the legacy table, additive companion, and shared sequence allocation.

## Changed Files

- `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.ts` — observed-only metadata marker.
- `src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.wrapper.ts` — emits `skill_selection` from the existing observed skill-usage boundary.
- `src/audit/agent-event-audit.ts` — projects observed-only skill-selection records and routes them outside run-start deduplication.
- `src/audit/audit-event-store.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-types.ts` — durable store/types for observed skill-selection metadata, with ordinary companion-table access through Kysely.
- `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` — generated Kysely declarations for the companion table.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.ts` — exposes skill-selection through `audit.activity.list` while preserving legacy `audit.list`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit-activity.ts` — versioned activity schema includes `skill_selection`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.ts` — legacy audit schema stays run/tool-only.
- `src/commands/audit.ts` — CLI uses the activity surface and renders selected skill metadata.
- `docs/gateway/audit.md` / `docs/gateway/config-observability.md` / `docs/cli/audit.md` — document the approved metadata fields, default-on collection, 30-day retention, separate 100,000-row cap, compatibility behavior, and explicit CLI filters.

## Test Plan

1. Verify observed skill reads/commands emit `skill_selection` audit events.
2. Verify `skill_selection` persists between run start and terminal events.
3. Verify `audit.activity.list` and CLI expose skill-selection records.
4. Verify legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only.
5. Verify attempt-result recovery tests still pass.
6. Verify existing SQLite state opens, creates the companion table, preserves old activity rows, and reopens with skill-selection rows intact.


## Review findings addressed (2026-10-10)

All five ClawSweeper code findings are fixed on this head:

- **Distinguishable skill identities** — the lossy hyphen sanitizer is replaced by an injective dash-escape encoding (`-` doubles to `--`, other unsafe bytes become `-hh-` hex), so `Daily Brief` persists as `Daily-20-Brief`, distinct from `Daily-Brief` → `Daily--Brief` (and `_helper` stays distinct from `helper`). The audit projector accepts the encoding. Boundary coverage in `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.test.ts`.
- **Admission-owned schema setup** — the canonical schema admission owns `audit_skill_selection_events` (`src/state/openclaw-state-schema.sql`); additive DDL now runs at most once per connection and only for pre-admission databases, instead of on every insert and prune tick.
- **Bounded write overhead** — per-connection row-count cache mirrors the canonical ledger pattern: one `COUNT(*)` per connection lifetime, advanced by inserts and maintenance deletes, invalidated on rollback.
- **Restart guidance** — `docs/gateway/audit.md` now states the recorder re-reads `logging.audit.enabled` on every event, so disabling stops new rows immediately.
- **Protocol type ownership** — `AuditActivitySkillSelectionV1` is derived from the canonical schema properties via `SchemaContract` (same pattern as adjacent variants), restoring wire-required attribution to typed consumers.

## Production-path proof

Throwaway script (not committed) driving production code on a temp state DB — marker encoder → recorder projector → production SQLite writer → `audit.activity.list` Gateway handler:

```
encoded identities: Daily-20-Brief vs Daily--Brief
projected inputs: 1 kind: skill_selection
writer stored: skill_selection Daily-20-Brief
gateway response: {"events":[{"schemaVersion":1,"sequence":1,"eventId":"<uuid>","sourceSequence":1,"occurredAt":<ts>,"redaction":"metadata_only","kind":"skill_selection","agentId":"main","sessionKey":"agent:main:<session>","sessionId":"session-<id>","runId":"run-proof-1","action":"skill.selection.observed","status":"observed","eventType":"skill_selection","actor":{"type":"agent","id":"main"},"selectedSkill":"Daily-20-Brief"}]}
worker rows: 1 first toolName: Daily-20-Brief
PROOF OK: gateway output matches the observed skill invocation
```

Tool-invocation → emission coverage lives in `src/agents/agent-tools.skill-selection-audit.e2e.test.ts`; recorder → DB → filtered readback in `src/audit/audit-events.skill-selection-hidden.test.ts`; handler shaping in `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts`.


## Round 2 (rev.199 follow-up)

Three further findings from review rev.199 are fixed on this head:

- **Token-built identities** — the encoder appends complete encoding tokens only while they fit the 128-char bound (reserving the `x-` flag prefix up front), so truncation can never cut inside an escape and valid suffixes survive (`skill-a` vs `skill-b` regression covered).
- **Single-owner expiry accounting** — the deleter returns the removed count without touching the warm cache; insert-prune and maintenance ticks each adjust exactly once, with a warm-cache expiry-to-overflow regression test (exact cap trim to 99,976 rows).
- **Tool-boundary assertion** — the wrapper e2e expects the encoded `demo--skill` identity while the run-usage receipt keeps the original `demo-skill` name.

prs.title: fix(ui): retire the live terminal copy once its run clears
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

WebChat can render a final assistant reply twice — the stored transcript holds one clean copy (`thinking` + `text`, no `textSignature`), while the screen shows two identical stacked copies that survive until a reload. The live terminal projection and the persisted row are supposed to converge through the authoritative-terminal dedup, but the record that owns that dedup is only armed when the persisted final arrives with `hasActiveRun !== true`. When the final row lands while its run still reads active — long turns with tool calls interleaved make that ordering more likely — no record is armed, and nothing arms it later, so `reconcileAuthoritativeTerminalHistory` never retires the live copy and both renders stay.

## Why This Fix

`rememberAuthoritativeTerminal` now keeps such a terminal **pending** instead of dropping it, and the run-clear reconcile (`finishSessionMessageRunReconcile`, right before the history reload it already triggers) promotes the pending record via `armPendingAuthoritativeTerminal`. The existing history reconciliation then removes the live copy for that run, so the turn converges to the single persisted reply. A pending terminal for a different run is left untouched, and a terminal that already armed stays armed.

## User Impact

A completed turn no longer shows the same reply twice, and it recovers automatically at run completion instead of waiting for a page reload — the duplicate disappears as soon as the run clears and history applies.

## Evidence

- New `ui/src/pages/chat/terminal-message-identity.test.ts` pins the sequence: a final persisted with `hasActiveRun: true` keeps the live copy (the pre-fix state), the run-clear arming retires it, a pending terminal for another run is preserved for its owning run, and the already-clear path still arms immediately. These fail against the old guard because the record was never kept.
- `ui` typecheck (`tsconfig.ui.json`) clean, boundary-guard lint and formatting clean; the neighboring `chat-gateway` and `stream-reconciliation` suites show no new failures (the six locale-dependent "Retrying…" expectations fail identically before and after this change on a zh-CN host).


## Update (c34c8b750b9) — promotion moved onto the history owner

The previous revision armed the deferred terminal inside the run-clear reconcile, which the review correctly flagged: `chat.final` clears the run first and the reloads it triggers never promoted the record, and an already-cleared run skipped the hook. Promotion now lives in the single history-apply owner (`chat-history-hydration`), so every reload path — `chat.final`, session reconciliation, manual reload — arms the pending terminal and retires the live copy.

## Browser reproduction status (open work)

A deterministic Control UI E2E reproduction (mocked Gateway, not committed) puts the reporter's ordering through the real app: a run goes active, the persisted final lands while `hasActiveRun: true`, then `chat.final` completes. Against this branch it still renders two copies, and the instrumented trace pinpoints the second one: an **identity-less live projection** (materialized stream message with no `__openclaw` identity) survives beside the persisted final. The promotion fix works on that trace — the armed terminal retires the live-terminal copy — but retiring the identity-less projection needs a change in the stream-materialization/publish path rather than the dedup helper, so this revision does not yet close the reported duplication. Keeping the PR as work in progress rather than claiming the fix.


## Update (fdfd6791b83) — review findings on eligibility and per-run pendings

- **P1 eligibility:** the deferred record now requires the saved row to own the run's final reply (`ownsFinalReply`): stream-segment-keyed rows and text blocks tagged `phase: "commentary"` no longer arm it, so a commentary-only refresh can't set the run-wide suppression flag and hide the actual final.
- **Per-run pendings:** pending records are keyed by run id (`Map` per host) instead of a single slot, so a second run persisting while active no longer drops the first run's terminal; each run keeps its own retirement path (raises from the reviewer's notes).
- Tests: five cases now cover the happy paths plus the commentary-refusal and two-active-runs sequences.

**Still open:** the reported identity-less duplicate (the app-level reproduction still shows two copies after the fix — the surviving copy is a live projection with no run identity, so retiring it needs a stream-materialization/publish change, not the dedup helper), and the cursor-delta history path (promotion currently runs on page responses only).


## Update (61ffd8e733d) — commentary phase via its canonical owner

The eligibility check now asks `resolveAssistantMessagePhase` (the shared phase owner) instead of parsing `textSignature` itself. The direct read also drifted from the contract — signatures are serialized JSON, so an object-shaped fixture never matched — and the canonical owner is the only place that decides commentary vs answer. The commentary-refusal test now pins the serialized form.

**Still open from Revision 3:** retaining every promoted run until its own live copy reconciles (my armed record is still a single slot), the cursor-delta history path, and the identity-less duplicate from the browser reproduction.

prs.title: feat(ui): create and review Claws from agents and sessions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Users cannot turn an agent or one of its sessions into a private, reviewable Claw through the Control UI.

## User Impact

Create Claw starts a normal agent session to author a private proposal. The creator can edit it, inspect the scope and exact packaged files, and explicitly Publish under their personal account. Pending scanning remains visible as pending.

## Why This Change Was Made

```text
agent settings or session menu
  → agent authors a private draft
  → creator edits and reviews exact files
  → creator explicitly publishes
```

Draft edits invalidate publication review. Responses from an old draft cannot overwrite the selected draft, and navigating to the generation session preserves its accepted first turn. Session-based generation forks the selected conversation through the existing private session API. The draft page stays mounted across unrelated shell layout updates. Uses the draft API in the preceding stack layer.

## Evidence

- **Before:** agent settings and session actions offered no creation flow.
- **After:** creation, editing, review invalidation, personal publisher display, and pending publication are covered by the focused UI tests.
- Current rebased stack: 252 UI tests and 7 browser scenarios pass. Coverage includes source-session context, shell-layout updates that previously remounted the page, session actions without draft capability, and conflict recovery. UI/Gateway method typechecks, formatting, targeted lint, runtime build and protocol checks pass.
- Real local integration on combined stack commit `16029c078424`: agent-page Create → normal agent write tool → creator edit/review → explicit personal publication → credential-free consumer discovery → acknowledged Add → ordinary-agent chat. Session-menu Create then copied all four completed parent messages into the new private child; real chat history confirms byte-identical role/content and the context marker. The child was stopped without a second publication.
- The downloaded archive contains exactly the reviewed `CLAW.md` and `package.json` bytes (847 bytes, SHA-256 `6d91eff0ed17172d05a522947986b111ed99f07565c15657c5cf662696bd1432`); all four synthetic private markers and private source files are absent. The model needed a creator-side format-only Python-literal-to-JSON edit after correction attempts; every authored value was preserved.
- The earlier full-flow proof was followed by inspected desktop/mobile captures on `ab69a4c31103`: the editor is 340px tall with scoped card spacing. The current revision also fixes capability admission and conflict recovery, and preserves main’s direct Solid catalog renderer; focused tests and new conflict screenshots cover those changes.
- Real Gateway/ClawHub auth, storage, publication, finalization, discovery, download and Add; simulated external scanner receipts. Pending scanning and the consumer warning remain enforced. [Companion final-effect rejection proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173345) covers publisher mismatch and missing consent before installation writes. No production publication or deployment.

### Review repairs: session actions and conflict recovery

- **Session menu:** the draft entry checked configuration before admitting the Gateway capability, crashing menus in contexts without draft support. The capability guard now runs first. The affected suites fail 50 tests before the fix and pass afterward, with 211 passing tests including the draft page suite.
- **Save conflict:** a stale revision previously left both Review and Reload disabled. Reload now offers a discard confirmation; cancelling preserves local edits, while accepting loads the latest revision, clears the conflict and restores Review. The browser regression fails before the fix and passes afterward.

| Before: conflict has no recovery | After: latest draft loaded and review available |
|---|---|
| ![Conflict with disabled Reload](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bfe69098-472e-47d6-8894-168f12aa8a34) | ![Recovered draft with Review available](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e8f0035a-efc0-4db2-9fce-48f5753b448b) |

These conflict screenshots use the real Control UI with a controlled Gateway stale-revision response. The test also verifies that cancelling discard does not read or replace the local draft.

Author simplification pass: reused the existing capability guard, draft load operation, and native discard confirmation. No recovery-state owner or parallel catalog renderer was added. Whole-PR delta: production +799/−18, tests/support +332/−0, docs +22/−1. The UI is the final coherent stage above the draft API; its state tracks private editing, exact review and explicit publication.

### Agent settings: before and after

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| ![Before: agent settings](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/96f228f6-bf80-44f8-a54c-0e9be410a4b0) | ![After: Create a Claw](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/719422e0-677d-44b8-ba8c-80180fdd82b6) |
| ![Before: mobile agent settings](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/74c273d5-91f7-4112-b946-ce1e5ead24ec) | ![After: mobile Create a Claw](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f3cb5ebe-ca8a-4169-82bc-788be65db8b1) |

Captured from real running Gateways, desktop 1440×900 and mobile 390×844, light theme. Private workspace/model/identity/build fields are masked. The read-only baseline uses an earlier build and differs in fixture agent name and selected skills; no baseline state was modified.

### Creator review and session entry

| Desktop review | Mobile review |
|---|---|
| ![Review exact files and personal publisher](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a5301ed3-8930-44f2-813a-30af3b2965e7) | ![Mobile publication review](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/394680b2-b1c0-4233-b64e-33a3aac5c7c1) |

![Create from the selected session](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4ed9064e-b184-4c2a-8eca-5e160be06783)
![Explicit publication reports pending scanning](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ad3dcc8c-b403-4595-b6a5-1ce4708b01f3)

The attached 30-second recording shows real consumer discovery, preview, acknowledgement, Add, and chat opening at normal speed. The [companion proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173345) includes the completed chat reply. Private fields are masked; the recording was trimmed, not sped up.

### Current-build publication authority proof

Run on `853e003fb4988d4759e36027874d396533bf9a69`, build `2026.10.4-853e003fb498-2026-10-16T03-21-06.275Z`. The publication, caller-admission, device revocation, paired-device cache, dispatcher and HTTP-client sources match API head `2f5e81e5097b`. This rerun includes main’s updated device-authority cache behavior.

| Actual Gateway caller | Actual package POSTs |
|---|---:|
| Authorized administrator (positive control) | 1 |
| Connected operator without admin scope | 0 |
| Production plugin synthetic caller | 0 |
| Administrator disconnected in flight | 0 |
| Operator device-role credential revoked in flight | 0 |

The test uses real signed WebSocket requests to the built Gateway and a real local HTTP counter server. For disconnect and revocation, publication first reaches a held `/api/v1/whoami` response. It then closes the actual socket or successfully calls `device.token.revoke(role=operator)`, releases the HTTP response, waits for terminal Gateway dispatch, and checks zero `/api/v1/packages` POSTs. The revoked connection closes with code 4001. The synthetic case calls production `api.runtime.gateway.request`; it does not fabricate a GatewayClient. The positive control sends the reviewed 935-byte artifact once and reports pending publication.

Limits: the counter server is a controlled publication-transport fixture; real ClawHub storage and discovery are covered by the separate end-to-end proof above. Revocation here removes the device’s operator credential; it does not claim named-user policy-demotion coverage. Driver exit 0, all five assertions pass, both listeners are verified closed, and personal/OCM state is unchanged.

### Current revision validation

On combined stack head `853e003fb498`: 59 focused source/disclosure/draft/filesystem tests, 252 UI unit tests, and 7 browser scenarios pass. UI and Gateway-method typechecks, formatting and targeted lint, the runtime build, and the protocol gate pass. The stack is rebased onto main `49ecf70827307`, after its Add prerequisites merged.

Broad `check:changed` checkpoint: inherited failures in unchanged files: a max-lines suppression in `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message.test.tsx`, and TS2540 (assignment to readonly `text`) in `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/model-request-body.test.ts:69`. Both files and the suppression baseline have identical Git blobs at base and head. Targeted checks above pass.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way for UI; Publish is an explicit public action. **Blast radius:** administrator Claws UI behind the existing Labs flag. No migration or deployment is included.

prs.title: feat: schedule weekly mobile store releases with Discord results
prs.body:
Closes #173722

## What Problem This Solves

Store releases need a weekly unattended run and a concise Discord result without notifying on manual or daily test distributions.

## User Impact

Both store workflows run every Monday at 11 AM Pacific, including daylight saving time, through their existing qualification and upload paths. Only completed weekly attempts post PASS/FAIL and a run link. Manual store releases, daily TestFlight/internal distributions, and screenshot-only runs stay silent. App Review submission and Google Play production promotion remain manual.

The first Monday occurrence after merge is enabled automatically. `DISCORD_MOBILE_RELEASE_WEBHOOK_URL` is installed in both store-release environments, and neither currently requires approval. GitHub scheduling is best-effort; this does not add a missed-run watchdog.

## Why This Change Was Made

Separate the weekly store event from the existing daily test-distribution event, preserving the platform concurrency queues and daily enable switches. The shared release command now admits scheduled store uploads while retaining canonical repository, exact-main-source, clean-checkout, and first-attempt checks. The completion notifier runs trusted default-branch code on GitHub-hosted Ubuntu, uses the matching environment webhook, and checks attempt-specific upload-job/step results before reporting PASS. Bounded delivery retries never rerun releases; ambiguous network delivery can duplicate a message. A failure inside the combined preparation/upload command leaves store acceptance explicitly unconfirmed.

The narrowly scoped `workflow_run` audit exception covers trusted default-branch code and read-only job metadata; it never executes triggering source or artifacts. This rollout also includes the previously validated iOS fix for an editable App Store version with no selected build, allowing normal build selection instead of Fastlane's `No data` failure.

## Evidence

- 91 focused tests passed across routing, notifications, existing release CI tools, Fastlane gates, and Android qualification admission. Wrapper wall time: 18.38s. New routing tests: 0.09s; notification tests: 0.77s. The existing CI-tools file took 14.97s, primarily its unchanged emulator-diagnostic and process-lifecycle probes. CI timing is pending.
- The actual shared release-command tests first reproduced the two scheduled-store rejections, then passed all 14 cases after the admission fix (14.31s tests / 15.35s wrapper). Both platforms exercise real orchestration with publishing stubbed; detached source pinning and invalid CI admission remain covered.
- After binding notification jobs to environment secrets, all 38 notification tests passed again (0.80s tests / 2.11s wrapper), including both environment selections, silent manual/daily runs, all terminal results, pagination, retries, missing credentials, and credential-safe errors.
- Targeted typecheck/lint/format, workflow actionlint/zizmor checks, line-cap ratchet, Ruby syntax, and diff whitespace checks passed. Independent P0-P2 review of the complete candidate and the subsequent shared-command fix found no actionable defects.
- Read-only live GitHub checks confirmed workflow/run metadata semantics, both webhook secret names, and unattended environment eligibility. Secret values were never retrieved.
- The included iOS selected-build fix was previously proven against pinned Fastlane 2.240.1 and a successful stage-only recovery of an already-uploaded build.
- No builds were published and no Discord messages were sent for this scheduling change. Live webhook delivery remains to be verified after deployment.

prs.title: test(gateway): stop visitor lease test flaking when the startup catalog refresh settles mid-run
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Gateway shard intermittently fails `published Gateway plugin services > cold start` with `expected 1 to be greater than 1` when the startup provider catalog refresh finishes while the test's agent-run lease is open. Seen twice on #173550 (heads 958f92e5 and 3ae37519) in the `agentic-control-plane-http-plugin-ws` shard, although that PR does not touch this path.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. The test now proves the run-lease contract deterministically instead of depending on how fast a background worker thread runs.

## Why This Change Was Made

Startup publication (`publishConfiguredModelRuntimeSnapshots`) commits a replacement that kicks off a background full provider catalog refresh. That refresh runs in the catalog worker thread and holds `retainPreparedPluginGeneration` for its whole duration, so it retains work on the same borrowed Gateway instance the test measures. The test sampled `retainedWorkCount` as a baseline while that refresh was usually still running (baseline 1). When the refresh settled inside the lease window, the lease's +1 and the refresh's −1 cancelled out and the assertion saw 1 > 1.

This retention is intentional product behavior: it keeps provider plugins from being replaced mid-discovery. The test was sampling an unrelated owner's work, so the product is fine. The test now waits on the instance's own observation API (`waitForRetainedWork`, the same one the reload drain uses) before acquiring the lease, then asserts that the lease raises the count above zero and disposal returns it to zero. The `hot enable` mode had the same latent race and is covered by the same change.

## Evidence

- An instrumented local run (temporary logging in `PluginInstance.retainWork`) traced the baseline hold to `refreshCommittedProviderCatalogs → loadFullModelCatalog → retainPreparedPluginGeneration`, released about 3 s after it started and after the lease had already been acquired.
- Failing before the fix: a temporary 6 s pause before the post-execute assertion forces CI's ordering, where the catalog settles inside the lease window. Both `cold start` and `hot enable` failed with the exact CI error, `AssertionError: expected 1 to be greater than 1`.
- Passing after the fix: the same pause on the fixed test passes in both modes.
- Normal run: `pnpm test src/gateway/server-plugin-reload.prepared-borrow.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passes 5/5. On this busy Mac, `cold start` took 10.6 s before and 10.3 s after; the added wait is bounded by whatever remains of the startup catalog refresh.
- `oxfmt --check`, type-aware `oxlint`, the targeted core-test typecheck for the file, and `git diff --check` are clean.

Gap: the flake was not reproduced naturally outside CI. Before this change the file passed 3/3 on an AWS c7a.4xlarge box and in 1- and 8-worker local replays. The forced ordering above is the CI interleaving, and the instrumented trace names the owner.

Diff delta: production 0 lines, test +5/−3.

prs.title: perf(sessions): bound full-detail list pages under load
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Large full-detail `sessions.list` requests monopolize the Gateway main thread and delay unrelated clients. A 10,000-row request observed during load spent 245 ms selecting and 940 ms presenting rows, followed by a 1,184 ms main-thread stall; sampled ELU reached 0.999.

## User Impact

Full-detail lists now cap the shared page at 200 rows before preparation. The default remains 100. Clients requesting larger full-detail inventories must follow `hasMore` / `nextOffset`; `limitApplied` reports the effective limit. Owner-first additions retain their existing bounded behavior. The same policy applies to subscription snapshots.

Compact/sidebar/dashboard limits remain unchanged. Metadata-only ACP, MCP, CLI tail, Workboard, Android group, and macOS voice-routing readers use compact rows so their existing inventory limits remain intact. Workboard uses the explicit completeness flag, preventing a short partial page from marking an omitted prepared launch as failed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing list owner applies the cap once, before selection, exact row preparation, cache-key construction, and synchronous presentation. It preserves current authorization through response publication and reuses existing pagination; no worker, cache, schema, or configuration option is added. Whole-roster counts/facets still require metadata work.

Production grows by 16 lines across the cap and required caller cutover. That growth preserves bulk metadata readers and native routing contracts while removing unbounded full-detail pages. The former Workboard row-count completeness inference is deleted.

## Evidence

Real WebSocket RPC replay against two fresh synthetic fixtures: 5,000 sessions (1,000 archived), 6,000 retained runs, 200 approval recovery records, 100 disabled cron jobs, and 12 projects with real worktrees. Before/after runtime builds used the same source revision except for the list cap. Benchmark execution was isolated on Linux with 64 CPUs / 64 GiB limits; no Testbox lease or live Gateway load test was used.

| Replay measurement | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Cold full request | 795 ms / 5,000 rows | 80 ms / 200 rows |
| Cold maximum main-loop delay | 405 ms | 33 ms |
| Cold maximum sampled ELU | 0.994 | 0.615 |
| Cold synchronous row presentation | 354 ms | 20 ms |
| Warm request mean, 12 reads | 154 ms | 9.6 ms |
| Warm maximum main-loop delay | 143 ms | 16 ms |
| List mean after 30 concurrent label patches, five rounds | 184 ms | 20.6 ms |
| Mutation-phase maximum main-loop delay | 172 ms | 26 ms |
| Mutation-phase maximum sampled ELU | 0.855 | 0.737 |
| Warm complete inventory | 162 ms / one page | 647 ms / 25 pages |

The throughput tradeoff is intentional: a complete full-detail scan takes more RPCs and about four times longer, while each response yields to other clients between pages. Pagination returned all 5,000 distinct rows, including all archived rows. Continuous pagination still reached sampled ELU 0.918; its maximum loop delay was 36 ms. These are observed maxima from 250 ms ELU windows and 10 ms delay sampling, not p99 estimates. The replay uses synthetic label churn, not provider-backed session creation/archive stress, and its 236 MB agent database preserves metadata shape rather than production byte size. Both isolated Gateways stopped cleanly.

Focused proof:

- `sessions-list-archived.test.ts`: regression failed before the cap (205 rows, no continuation); all five tests passed after. 148.22 s command wall time, dominated by worker compilation; new regression 7.7 s.
- `session-utils.perf.test.ts`: all eight behavioral tests passed; 161.37 s command wall time, dominated by worker compilation.
- `translator.lifecycle.test.ts`: nine tests passed in 18.55 s command wall time.

prs.title: perf(sessions): skip disk-budget checks after unchanged patches
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Unchanged session-entry patches can schedule physical disk-budget maintenance and start a worker even though they committed no entry change.

## User Impact

Session background updates that leave the entry unchanged avoid unnecessary maintenance work. Committed changes still schedule disk-budget enforcement; explicit cleanup and its existing throttles remain unchanged. No configuration or stored-format changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The patch owner already records whether an entry mutation committed. Use that existing `wrote` fact for physical disk-budget maintenance, alongside entry maintenance. The ACP sibling uses its existing committed-entry publication; metadata-only clears still commit in the separate shared-state database. This removes the no-op execution path without adding a cache, timer, state, or validation. Production LOC delta: 12 added / 12 removed (net zero); both existing calls move inside existing committed-write boundaries.

## Evidence

- Regression fails on the old code because an unchanged patch queues `enforceSqliteSessionHistoryDiskBudget`. With the fix, null and identical-postimage updates perform no physical measurement; a subsequent changed entry performs one.
- Focused `session-history-budget-owner.test.ts`: 10/10 passed (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/sessions/session-history-budget-owner.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`). Changed-file oxfmt, targeted oxlint, and `git diff --check` passed. Broad validation belongs to PR CI; no Testbox lease used.
- independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): no actionable findings. The requested autoreview provider route was refused because it did not match operator configuration; configuration was left unchanged.
- ACP sibling regression failed on the old code after a metadata-only clear; the amended `session-meta-write.worker.test.ts` passes 11/11 with the fix. It proves metadata deletion persists without a budget kick and retains positive coverage for actual entry writes. An existing clone-error assertion now checks `DataCloneError` instead of runtime-specific Node/Bun wording; the absent-entry assertion remains. This addition received a fresh clean independent review.
- Isolated Linux measurements use a synthetic fixture generated with 5,000 sessions, 6,000 retained runs, 200 approvals, 100 disabled cron jobs, and 12 projects (~225 MiB session DB). Fresh processes patch one unchanged entry; fixture is preconditioned and shared sequentially. Three alternating pairs: A/B, B/A, A/B.

| Unchanged patch, median of three runs | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Cross-thread messages | 75 | 70 |
| Disk-budget workers started | 1 | 0 |
| Main-thread CPU | 33.069 ms | 25.761 ms |
| Wall time, including cold worker startup and maintenance settlement | 7,794.9 ms | 5,845.0 ms |

Message counts include necessary patch traffic, not just maintenance. This is an avoided-work measurement on a fresh process, not a steady-state throughput claim. Existing maintenance throttles limit how often the avoided sweep occurs.

Steady-idle measurements used three further alternating pairs, each with a 60-second warmup after readiness and a 120-second quiet window. No client polling or attribution instrumentation ran inside those windows. All owned Gateways shut down successfully.

| Steady idle, median of three runs | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Worker messages/s | 0.97418 | 0.97471 |
| Main-thread CPU, percent of one core | 0.17223% | 0.17409% |

Idle is neutral within noise: CPU ranges overlap (before 0.1650–0.1755%, after 0.1696–0.1816%). Per-pair before/after CPU percentages were 0.1722/0.1816, 0.1650/0.1741, and 0.1755/0.1696. This change removes work when unchanged patches occur; it does not claim a steady-idle speedup.

A separate diagnostic window attributed most remaining messages to worker memory sampling (~0.8 messages/s), with occasional skills refresh and cron registry reads. The fixture disables channels, plugins, heartbeats, and cron execution; production traffic rates are not treated as idle because concurrent RPC clients were active. Measurements compare `18044d5bb00b` with the generic-patch fix at `86eb80edfd08`; the subsequent ACP sibling fix has direct functional regression coverage, not a separate performance claim.

The initial head passed all PR CI in [run 38844453308](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38844453308). Final-head CI runs in [run 38845985368](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38845985368).

## What Problem This Solves

Claws published by personal accounts cannot be discovered or opened through the official-only catalog.

## User Impact

Users can find, inspect, and Add community Claws as ordinary agents. Publisher identity is shown separately from the current Official badge; existing artifact verification and trust prompts still apply.

## Why This Change Was Made

```text
public Claw → verify publisher + artifact → inspect contents → Add → ordinary agent chat
```

Package links carry the full publisher/name identity. Official status comes from the publisher's current status, including after revocation. The Claw Add prerequisites have merged into main; registry discovery is provided by https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/pull/3963.

Creation/review UI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173377. Private draft/publication API: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173346.

## Evidence

- **Before:** opening a personal publisher's card threw an official-only route error; badge revocation still displayed Official.
- **After:** the personal-publisher browser flow reaches Add and sends the first chat message. Catalog tests cover current publisher status and verified community artifacts.
- A real fresh-user run found a remaining official-only manifest-disclosure guard. The regression failed for personal and unscoped packages before the fix; all 52 disclosure/Add/source tests now pass. The guard uses the shared canonical name validator and retains artifact identity, version, and checksum checks.
- Current rebased stack: 252 UI tests and 7 browser scenarios pass, including all 6 catalog/Add scenarios across mobile, tablet, laptop, and desktop layouts. UI and Gateway method typechecks, formatting and targeted lint pass. The runtime build and protocol checks pass.
- Real integration on combined stack commit `16029c078424`: an agent authored the proposal through its normal file tool; the creator reviewed and explicitly published `@cli-user/public-source-brief@0.1.0`. A fresh consumer without publisher credentials discovered it without an Official badge, explicitly acknowledged the warning, and completed Add (`status: complete`, `readiness.ready: true`). - The real `claws.add.apply` owner rejected both a mismatched publisher and missing risk acknowledgement before installation: configured agents stayed `[main]`, the config hash was unchanged, and all workspace roots/file hashes were unchanged. The allowed Add then created `workspace-public-source-brief`, confirming the snapshot covered the allocation parent. The publisher case uses an explicit read-only fault proxy changing only `owner.handle` from `cli-user` to `other`; the genuine registry/package are unchanged. Missing consent returns `CLAWHUB_RISK_ACKNOWLEDGEMENT_REQUIRED` through the real UI.

This experiment investigates a signed-in reload of a dashboard deep link when connects overlap concurrent writes. Returning an unchanged device token currently joins the pairing lock and a writer transaction. Verification also waits for a transaction that records last use.

The candidate reads existing tokens from the pairing owner's committed process publication, keeps one shared verification/reuse policy, and retains guarded worker transactions for issuance and rotation. Last-use bookkeeping is conditional on the current token and runs through a coalesced, lifecycle-tracked background writer. Remote ingress continues to receive no reusable credential.

Performance results are pending. This draft is the source anchor for the campaign's remote-clone benchmark route; do not merge. The comparison will use seven interleaved pairs on one quiet AWS c7a.4xlarge, signed WebSocket handshakes, concurrent session creation and pairing writes, focused auth/pairing suites, and the synthetic renderer control. No private captures or live state are included.

prs.title: refactor: consolidate repeated runtime family ownership
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Several runtime families still repeat shared mechanics at their consumers: retained work phases, Gateway request validation, migration source verification, recovery evidence normalization, setup credential environment policy, admission finish observers, accepted-delivery receipts, and prepared navigation targets. The copies make the common contract harder to follow without giving the callers meaningful independence.

## User Impact

Class-based session-binding adapters keep their prototype methods and original receiver, including private fields. The remaining changes consolidate existing behavior without changing UI layout, configuration, protocols, persistence, or channel features.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move each common responsibility into its existing owner and migrate its consumers together. Keep channel transport, credentials, authority, persistence, settlement, and rendering decisions with their current owners. Reuse the canonical Markdown and memory-probe types rather than maintaining mirrors. Reuse existing script argument, schema-generation, and Docker inspection owners, and let the Channels controller consume the existing Gateway binding.

The family census uses declared names, structural comparisons, mirrored types, forwarding modules, and native/UI reads. Its coverage log distinguishes implemented cuts, genuinely different owners, other-lane assignments, rejected abstractions, and parked native work. Corrected filename and exact-member indexing exposed additional production paths. All 49,810 raw supplemental references now have member-qualified decisions or owner routes; this accounts for that inventory, not every possible semantic similarity missed by the discovery methods. Further existing-owner adoptions remain isolated from this cut.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- No security or authorization boundary is removed. This cut consolidates duplicate mechanics and omits empty transaction hooks; normal durability, FIFO, realistic concurrency, and write-capable shutdown settlement stay intact.
- Binding snapshot consumption calls the same owner-currentness assertion once instead of twice in one synchronous callback (both came from [#168483](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168483)). The record-identity comparison and effect-time authority check remain; no new stale-selection scenario is accepted.
- Validation remains at the existing request boundary; migration verification performs the same safe read/comparison; finish observers retain synchronous `finally` ordering and error precedence. The shared observer adds a callback invocation; no performance improvement is claimed.
- Navigation retains its effect-time scope check, and partial sends retain accepted receipts before later failures. No speculative timing scenario is newly accepted to obtain the line reduction.

## Evidence

Current production delta against the pinned merge base: **659 net lines removed across 116 production files**. Tests, fixtures, generated files, declarations, docs, and shrink-only baselines are excluded. Final committed proof head: **08bcea37b281d5add4e1cb6353e593e2f652ecd5**.

The integrated independent review completed all seven passes and final source verification. Its sole finding was declined after verifying the cited SDK subpath already exists in both base and candidate; no accepted/actionable finding remains. The real public-SDK class/receiver regression passed, including the wrapper's final generation verification and cleanup. Its pre-fix control was interrupted before assertions, so no failing baseline run is claimed. Whole-diff formatting and runtime cycles passed (zero cycles).

All nine structural gates passed against the frozen candidate bytes: changed-source line caps, runtime cycles (zero), Madge cycles (zero), SDK exports, unchanged SDK surface (155 entrypoints / 3761 names / 2196 callables), and core production, UI, extension production, and script types. Targeted core, root-test, and script lint, seven-file UI Stylelint, and script erasability (880 TypeScript implementation files) passed. Local extension lint did not start because SDK declaration preparation exhausted its unchanged 300000ms deadline. Core graph-boundary inventory was interrupted on the loaded host and remains incomplete. Broad build/declarations, API report, extension lint, packaged imports, and remaining consumer coverage are deferred to exact-head PR CI, not claimed as local passes. Consumer gaps include nonempty snapshots from the three real channel managers and positive Gateway plugin patch/tools handlers.

Qualified focused results include six status-summary cases, the SDK account-status case, two accepted-delivery owner cases, and three LINE receipt/failure cases. The receipt command was interrupted after LINE completed and before a qualified Teams result; the aggregate is incomplete. One actual local failure remains investigated, not attributed: Zalo `keeps startAccount pending until abort` expected the startup mocks once but observed zero. Its only production change passes the original account context directly to the unchanged synchronous status-sink factory instead of constructing the equivalent two-field projection. No causal fix is claimed; the original assertion and uncertainty are retained for CI attribution. No assertion, timeout, retry, or skip was altered.

The additional retained-work/setup-credential/recovery owner selection was stopped during cold compiler preparation on the saturated host, before assertions. Those suites remain unpassed locally. An earlier `nodes.read.test.ts:180` timeout is also unresolved, not silently attributed to load or relabeled green.

The required pre-push suppression suite ran: the companion-rule and explicit production-suppression allowlist assertions passed; the unchanged Git-based production-file enumeration assertion exceeded its existing 120-second limit (143.6 seconds observed). The command failed. This is an unresolved local timing failure, not proven inherited or PR-caused; no retry or limit change was made. Final frozen-head/source verification completed without drift.

Native changes are excluded on parked branches pending native integration proof. Manifest metadata projection and shared sent-hook dispatch were also removed from this candidate because their new SDK names exceeded the unchanged surface budget. Existing SDK names/subpaths remain; no configuration keys, schemas, protocol shapes, dependencies, generated artifacts, or changelog entries change.

The configured Testbox queued and was stopped without executing the payload; its workflow completed/cancelled and blocking native cleanup reconciled successfully. No remote test result is claimed. The local `ciArtifacts` build completed runtime compilation, 97 plugin distributions, CLI import guard, assets, and runtime postbuild checks, then was intentionally stopped during SDK declarations on the saturated host. The whole build is incomplete. Shell syntax passed for all three changed materializers. No full-build or API-report pass is claimed from those substeps.

The V2 binding-factory parameter cutover updates all bundled callers. Its implementation file is absent from the current stable source tag, v2026.10.4 (current GitHub release refreshed after recovery). This is source/contract evidence, not full release-artifact verification.
