prs.title: chore(deps): refresh dependencies with a seven-day cutoff
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Refreshes OpenClaw's dependencies across every tracked ecosystem while keeping newly selected releases at least seven days old.

## User Impact

User impact: users receive compatible provider, Codex, mail, media, and native dependency updates; development and release tooling receive matching refreshed pins. There are no intentional configuration, database, runtime-floor, or permission changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fixed cutoff is **2026-10-09 02:37:10 UTC**, seven days before this audit began. Existing pins newer than the cutoff are preserved rather than downgraded. Package managers generated their own lockfiles; no new dependency patches or compatibility shims were added.

This covers npm/pnpm, all three npm-format tool locks, Rust, Go, Ruby/Bundler, Android/Gradle, Swift, GitHub Actions, Python/tool pins, and container images. Eligible changes include Codex 0.162.0, OpenAI 7.30.1, AWS SDK 3.1148.0, Claude ACP 0.88.0, Copilot SDK 1.0.18, Vite 8.3.4, Tauri 2.12.2, x/net 0.60.0, CodeQL Action 4.38.3 and JavaScript libraries 2.10.3, Vercel 63.1.0, and Sandbox 4.7.1.

The Codex integration is aligned with the actual 0.162.0 protocol and model catalog. Vercel's materializer retains its exact lock hash and registry-integrity checks. Existing ownership and security policies remain unchanged; the CodeQL changes require independent SecOps review.

Compatibility holds are intentional:

- The October 8 TypeScript candidate removes the unstable filesystem API consumed by the compiler wrappers. Its core typecheck failed; the existing compiler pin is retained rather than folding a filesystem-contract migration into a dependency refresh. The classic TypeScript compiler remains for JS compiler-API consumers.
- MXC 1.0 removes the root container API consumed here and changes its sandbox/network contract; 0.9.0 remains.
- Gradle 9.8.1 still conflicts with AGP 9.4.1 under strict deprecation handling; 9.7.1 remains.
- The Tauri updater fork remains because upstream still performs cleanup before successful Windows installer launch.
- Codex Action 1.13 is used on the three qualified hosted Ubuntu workflows. The maturity workflow retains 1.12 because its supported custom runner group has not been qualified for the new ACL prerequisites.
- Native ABI/owner constraints and releases younger than the cutoff remain unchanged.

Simplification: the only non-pin production change removes an obsolete, unused Codex response field. No new machinery or test cases were added; existing tests still protect package ownership, the managed-version fallback, audited desktop pruning, and pinned release-tool/container contracts. Source/test changes total +15/-16 lines; the remaining changes are manifests, generated locks, workflow pins, and version documentation.

## Evidence

- Audited 203 JavaScript manifests / 748 direct specs; verified every one of the 59 new npm lock resolutions against the fixed cutoff and registry integrity. Frozen install and dependency-pin guard pass.
- Audited all three Rust locks, Ruby/Bundler, 40 Android catalog versions / 60 libraries, 30 Swift repositories, and 34 Actions repositories / 1,146 references. Cargo locked/offline metadata and Go tidy/module verification pass; generated checksum deltas are limited to the selected updates.
- Checksum-verified Codex 0.162.0 completes real isolated unauthenticated `initialize` and `model/list`. The integration's upstream protocol changes were inspected directly.
- Focused `pnpm test <six files> --maxWorkers=1 -t <changed contracts>` passes: **9 cases**, 169 excluded, **162.42 seconds** wall time. No broad local suite or pressure workload was repeated. CI timing will come from the PR run.
- Workflow validation (including actionlint and zizmor), targeted lint/format, shell syntax, and whitespace checks pass.
- Independent isolated autoreview is complete with no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- CodeQL CLI 2.27.2 was downloaded from its official release and SHA-256 verified; it generated the 13-entry library lock. Both custom queries pass `query compile --check-only --threads=1`, without building a database or running broad analysis. All 13 library packages match the October 7 release's source revision.

PR CI owns broad tests and native builds. No release, deployment, live Gateway mutation, VM lease, or publication was performed. Failed candidate qualification is not represented as final-head failure or passing proof.

prs.title: experiment(control-ui): early WebSocket open [do not merge]
prs.body:
Parked experiment; no ready PR or landing. The reviewed, default-off prototype remains on this branch for inspection.

## What Problem This Solves

A signed-in dashboard deep-link reload starts its Gateway socket after the app modules evaluate. Campaign evidence originally measured 14 visual states across roughly 15 seconds; this experiment tested whether moving socket creation into the existing document bootstrap removes a meaningful part of that waterfall.

## User Impact

No shipped behavior change. Early opening improved hello conditionally, but did not give a clear Team-scale transcript/FCP win across 80 ms and 200 ms delays. Keeping the additional lifecycle is not justified by these measurements.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing CSP-hashed head script opens one socket behind a default-off local experiment flag. The normal adapter adopts it only for an exact URL match and retains all sending, signing, and protocol ownership. Buffered challenges replay after adapter assignment. Expiry, early error/close, target/query mismatch, stop, and reconnect preserve the normal fresh-socket path. No Gateway schema, server state, protocol, config option, or authentication model changes.

Production delta: **66 additions, 1 deletion, net +65 lines**, in `ui/index.html` and `ui/src/api/gateway-browser-socket.ts`; coverage in `ui/src/api/gateway-browser-socket.test.ts`. Bounded buffering/expiry/handoff is new lifecycle rather than replacement machinery; the measured gain does not justify retaining it.

## Evidence

Head: `dc6e42fe207ff4cd10c60ec988f092bbae0e3093`. Quiet AWS Crabbox `cbx_71ae8c8dceaf`, fixed `c7a.4xlarge`, observed 16 CPUs and 31,378 MiB RAM. Production UI Team-scale bench, repository Playwright Chromium, campaign LoAF/mutation and RPC probes, untraced, seven interleaved off/on pairs at each delay. A confirmation pass retained first-socket timestamps so later reconnects could not overwrite them. All confirmation samples are included. Values: milliseconds, median [Q1, Q3], inclusive quartiles.

| Upgrade/RPC delay | Metric | Flag off | Flag on |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 80 ms | Socket open | 242.3 [231.8, 248.3] | 147.6 [146.5, 159.1] |
| 80 ms | Connect sent | 788.7 [761.1, 800.5] | 162.5 [157.3, 173.3] |
| 80 ms | First hello | 893.3 [866.1, 910.5] | 798.9 [788.8, 808.5] |
| 80 ms | First transcript row | 683.6 [669.7, 696.3] | 679.7 [677.2, 690.2] |
| 80 ms | FCP | 800.0 [790.0, 816.0] | 796.0 [796.0, 812.0] |
| 200 ms | Socket open | 763.2 [752.2, 774.6] | 744.1 [737.8, 755.5] |
| 200 ms | Connect sent | 789.2 [774.8, 800.3] | 769.2 [761.2, 782.5] |
| 200 ms | First hello | 992.2 [980.0, 1005.2] | 971.1 [962.6, 985.1] |
| 200 ms | First transcript row | 663.3 [652.4, 677.3] | 650.6 [644.5, 659.3] |
| 200 ms | FCP | 780.0 [772.0, 798.0] | 764.0 [764.0, 772.0] |

Attribution: pre-hello longest-frame medians were 520→524 ms (80 ms) and 519→507 ms (200 ms); scripts attributed to `IDBTransaction.oncomplete` consumed 415→413 ms and 410→406 ms. That interval includes cache restoration/rendering and layout, not just storage work. Early opening leaves the dominant renderer work intact. The initial complete pass likewise found hello 866.6→779.3 ms at 80 ms and 992.8→986.1 ms at 200 ms, with no consistent transcript/FCP improvement.

Boundary: the Team-scale fixture retains browser-owned synthetic responses, with a real native WebSocket relay delaying upgrade and request echoes; extra fixture response latency is zero and frame spacing is 4 ms. This models upgrade/RPC delays, not remote HTTP assets, TCP/TLS, Cloudflare, or real Gateway admission. CDP handshake notifications do not independently establish network-process arrival time; overlapping renderer work is an attribution inference.

A separate temporary native E2E case used one isolated real Gateway and a same-origin proxy injecting synthetic trusted identity headers. Three unmeasured warm reloads, then seven interleaved pairs per RTT, with half-RTT forwarding each way. All 28 loads used one socket, retained device signing, and received hello; the case passed with clean shutdown. It used an empty chat rather than the Team-scale transcript fixture. prs.title: fix(agents): keep the skills catalog when toolsAllow is not a narrow grant
prs.body:
## Severity: high — silent, fleet-wide, and invisible in telemetry

Every cron `agentTurn` job that carries a `toolsAllow` runs **without `<available_skills>` in its system prompt**. The model is never told which skills exist or where their `SKILL.md` files are, so it cannot deliberately use one — it can only rediscover a skill by searching the filesystem, or answer from priors. There is no error, no warning, and no log line.

Three things make this worth prioritising:

1. **On the 2026.7.2 line it hits every box.** Since #112483, `applyDefaultCronToolsAllow` stamps `toolsAllow = ["*"]` on **every** tool-using cron job, to record "unrestricted" as an explicit fact. `["*"].length` is truthy, so on that line *every cron job everywhere* loses its skills catalog.
2. **The failure is silent and plausible.** In our measurements an affected run did not say "I could not check" — one fabricated a confident, well-formatted answer for a capability it never queried.
3. **Telemetry reports the opposite.** `buildSystemPromptReport` is handed the **un-gated** `skillsPrompt` while the prompt is built from the gated one, so `systemPromptReport` shows the catalog as present in exactly the runs where the model never received it — identical hash and char count in a failing cron run and a passing chat run. Anyone diagnosing this from telemetry gets a confident false negative. (Not fixed here; flagged so it does not mislead the next person.)

## The bug

`prepareEmbeddedAttemptSystemPrompt`:

```ts
const effectiveSkillsPrompt = attempt.toolsAllow?.length ? undefined : params.skillsPrompt;
```

A non-empty `toolsAllow` is treated as proof of a narrow run. It is not.

`toolsAllow` is three-valued in this codebase — `undefined` unrestricted, a short array restricted, `["*"]` **explicitly** unrestricted — and the rest of the code honours that:

- `hasWildcardToolAllowlist` in `attempt-tool-construction-plan.ts` (sibling file, same directory);
- `cli-runner/prepare.ts` normalising a wildcard back to `undefined`, covered by `does not restrict CLI-backed announce runs when toolsAllow contains a wildcard`.

Only this gate uses a bare `.length` check. It also cannot consult `toolsAllowIsDefault`, because `EmbeddedRunAttemptParams` does not carry it.

**Timeline** — the gate is not wrong for the callers it was written for. It predates cron's stamping by about a day, when every non-empty `toolsAllow` came from a genuinely narrow helper turn (realtime-voice consult, system-agent `["openclaw"]` / `[]`). Those still behave exactly as before after this change. Cron later walked into a gate built for something else.

## Evidence

Controlled harness, 20 runs per cell. Same agent, same five-section prompt, same model, same tool set, same skill; the **only** difference is whether the cron job carried an explicit tool list:

| cell | correct | skill body read | attempts at the capability |
|---|---|---|---|
| cron, tool list set | 8/20 | 5/20 | `{0:12, 1:2, 2:6}` |
| cron, no tool list | 20/20 | 20/20 | `{1:20}` |

Fisher exact: **p = 4.5e-05** on outcome, **p = 7.7e-07** on whether the skill body was read. Twelve of twenty affected runs made **zero** attempts at the capability.

## The fix

Rather than special-casing the wildcard, the predicate asks what the gate was approximating: *can this run open a skill body?* A skill is loaded by calling the read tool on the catalog's `<location>`, so the catalog is kept when `toolsAllow` grants `read` or is explicitly unrestricted, and still dropped otherwise.

A wildcard-only check would **not** be sufficient: agent-created jobs persist a mirror of the creating turn's own tools, which is a long, fully-privileged list with no wildcard in it. That is the shape that hit us in production.

`promptMode` is deliberately left untouched — this change is scoped to the skills catalog.

## Tests

`attempt-system-prompt-prepare.skills-catalog.test.ts` covers seven cases: unset, empty, explicit wildcard, wildcard needing normalization, a creator-cap list carrying `read`, and two genuinely narrow lists that must still skip the catalog.

Negative-controlled: with the predicate reverted to the current behaviour, exactly the three cases this PR fixes go red and the four that must not change stay green.

I could not find any existing test asserting the current coupling, nor a doc or CHANGELOG entry describing it — `docs/concepts/system-prompt.md` says Skills "stay available" under `minimal` mode, which is what this restores.

prs.title: fix: background completion is dropped when the config changes mid-turn
prs.body:
Closes #169054

## What Problem This Solves

A background completion that an active turn already accepted (`tools.exec.notifyOnExit`, restart continuations, hook wakes, ACP/CLI notices) is silently dropped when a config publication (`config.apply`/`config.patch`, hot reload, `auth.order` rotation) lands before it starts. The queued follow-up run holds the config captured at enqueue, the session-event owner rejects it with `Session event configuration changed; retry under the current policy`, and no producer retries — so the assistant never runs its follow-up turn. Regression from #167113 in the 2026.10.5 line.

## User Impact

Accepted background completions now still run after a mid-turn config change, under the **newly published** policy (e.g. a just-added `tools.deny` applies). Stop, abort, queue abandonment, and producer retirement still settle terminally; a publication storm is bounded (2 re-admissions) and then settles as failed with an error log instead of looping or leaking into a later ordinary turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

`session-event-handoff.ts` is the single owner. The stale-config guard stays (running under a superseded policy would be wrong). Instead, when that guard rejects an occurrence that **never started, never attempted delivery, was not aborted and was not abandoned**, `finish()` releases custody and re-dispatches the same occurrence through `enqueueSessionEventForHost`, which re-reads current config and re-runs every destination/authority check. The producer contract carries over: captured target (store, tool ceiling, settings, delivery opt-out), `assertCurrent`, `abortSignal`, `onAdopted`, and — if never accepted — the submitting `assertAcceptanceCurrent`. The original receipt's `cancel()`/`settled` forward to the live attempt.

### Maintainer update (merge with main after #173452)

#173452 moved the config check from admission/adoption into `assertEffectCurrent`, which is still fed to execution-start `assertSourceCurrent`, so the drop still reproduced on main (now at execution start instead of `onAdopted`). The branch now:

- merges current `main` and ports the re-admission onto `assertEffectCurrent`;
- gives each re-admission its own `MessageSid` (`<occurrence>:readmission-<n>`): inbound dedupe is retained once a turn is adopted, so reusing the occurrence id made the re-dispatch a silent duplicate drop (the previous mocked-dispatch tests could not observe this);
- keeps passive-notice preservation (`preserveOccurrenceOnRejection`) only until some attempt has adopted the occurrence (autoreview P2);
- replaces the old mocked-adoption cases (incompatible with main's slimmed handoff test harness, which forbids synthetic adoption) with a real queue/dispatcher regression.

Production: one file, `src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-handoff.ts` (+102/-9). No config, protocol, storage, or migration surface.

## Evidence

New `src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-config-readmission.test.ts` drives the real dispatcher, followup queue, admission and session store (only `runEmbeddedAgent` is mocked): turn 1 is held in the model, an `exec` completion is accepted as a deferred follow-up, `tools.deny: ["write"]` is published, turn 1 is released.

- **RED on main** (`origin/main` production file, same test): `storm: false` fails — completion settles `{ status: "failed", executionStarted: false }`. Control with no publication completes, isolating the publication as the cause.
- **GREEN on this head**: completion settles `completed, executionStarted: true`; the second model run binds `config.tools.deny === ["write"]`; no system events remain.
- **Storm** (`storm: true`): every liveness check publishes a distinct policy; the completion settles `failed`, never runs, and nothing is left for a later turn (terminal bound).
- Adjacent suites on the merged head: `session-event-handoff`, `session-event-permissions`, `followup-turn-admission`, `agent-runner-execution-session-events`, `queue/lifecycle` + new file — 76/76 passed. `pnpm tsgo:core` clean; oxlint/oxfmt clean.
- `pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-config-readmission.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: ~70–130s wall on a loaded host (2 cases, ~8–20s each, dominated by real reply-runtime prewarm like sibling `session-event-permissions` cases). Lives in its own file because `session-event-permissions.test.ts` is at the line-cap ratchet; registered in the database-worker core paths (needs the host SQLite broker).
- CI: the earlier `checks-node-changed-1` red was `src/agents/bash-tools.process.e2e.test.ts` (`keeps post-exit finalizer failure truthful…`), outside this PR's files.

The contributor's earlier packaged-Gateway RED/GREEN traces (hook wake + `tools.deny` rewrite, retained producer ceiling, destination replacement) were captured on the pre-#173452 shape; they remain in the collapsed section below for history.

Credit: original fix, design, and Gateway proof by @wangmiao0668000666.

<details>
<summary>Original PR description (pre-#173452 shape)</summary>

Closes #169054

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a background completion that an active turn already accepted is silently destroyed when a configuration change lands before that event starts, so the assistant never runs its follow-up turn.

An automatic `exec` completion (`tools.exec.notifyOnExit`), a restart continuation, an ACP parent-stream notice, a CLI stall notice, or a hook event that defers to the running turn is *accepted* by that turn. Any config publication in between — `config.apply`, `config.patch`, a hot reload, an `auth.order` rotation — made the session-event owner treat the occurrence as failed (`Session event configuration changed; retry under the current policy`) and its settlement path then cancelled the queued occurrence. No producer retries, so the event was lost without a trace.

## User Impact

An event that an active turn already accepted is no longer discarded when a configuration change lands mid-turn. The occurrence stays under the session-event owner's custody and is re-admitted through a fresh dispatch that binds the current policy, so the follow-up turn still runs — with the operator's latest tool restrictions, not the stale ones.

Terminal settlements consume the occurrence exactly as before, and this now holds across the re-admission chain too: Stop, abort, queue-owner abandonment (queue-capacity drops, lifecycle cleanup), and producer cancellation of a pending re-admission all consume the occurrence — canceled work never leaks into the next ordinary turn. When the bounded re-admission budget (two attempts) is exhausted, or the re-dispatch itself rejects synchronously (retired producer, moved destination, revoked ingress), the occurrence settles as failed with an explicit error log instead of being parked in the passive queue, where a later ordinary turn would have drained it as contract-less prompt text under its own authority.

An event that never reached an accepted turn keeps its current behavior, and a real destination change (store replacement, agent deletion, unresolvable agent) still fails. Events that already started or attempted delivery still fail as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

`assertOwnerCurrent` in `src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-handoff.ts` compared the captured config object identity plus the runtime-config publication metadata and threw for any change. That guard must stay: the queued follow-up run captured its execution config at dispatch time, so letting adoption proceed after a publication would run the event under the *stale* policy — including a `tools.deny` the operator just added.

So instead of relaxing the guard, settlement now converts exactly one failure mode into a fresh re-admission: when a policy publication rejects an occurrence that never started and never attempted delivery — whether the publication races admission before acceptance or lands at adoption while deferred — `finish()` releases custody back to the occurrence and calls `enqueueSessionEventForHost` again with the same occurrence. The new dispatch re-reads the runtime config, re-captures and re-validates the destination, and re-runs every destination check — execution authority is therefore always the current policy by construction.

The re-admission carries the full producer contract forward: the captured `expectedTarget` (physical session identity, permission ceiling, settings, delivery opt-out), the producer's live `assertCurrent` revocation callback, the explicit `abortSignal`, the durable producer's `onAdopted` commit hook, and — while the original attempt never reached acceptance — the submitting invocation's live `assertAcceptanceCurrent`, so revoked ingress still rejects the retry before any session preparation or turn admission. A retired producer, moved store, or reset destination still rejects at re-admission; nothing re-mints a producer binding. The original receipt's `cancel()` forwards to the live re-admission attempt, and its `settled` promise chains to the re-admitted receipt, so exec-completion acknowledgement and exactly-once semantics are preserved.

Two terminal-path invariants pin the retry chain to the original contract:

- Re-admissions never opt into `preserveOccurrenceOnRejection` — that flag is reserved for occurrences that already existed as passive notices before a failed promotion. A producer-owned occurrence whose retry is canceled, stopped, abandoned, or admission-refused is consumed terminally, never released into the passive queue.
- When the bounded budget is exhausted, or the re-dispatch itself throws synchronously, settlement consumes the occurrence and logs an explicit error. The generic system-event queue carries no captured target, permission ceiling, delivery opt-out, or producer assertion, so leaving the occurrence there would silently drop the producer contract; the failed settlement is observable instead.

No producer retry loops, validator, option, config value, or persistence policy are added.

Production LOC is `+137/-8` across one file.

Classification: `behavior-completing`

## Evidence

### Real shipped-Gateway proof (RED → GREEN)

Driver: `proof-169529.mjs` (linked below) runs the packaged Gateway from this PR's `dist/` with a stateful mock OpenAI Responses provider. Flow: an ordinary turn is held open by the provider gate → a `POST /hooks/wake` event (`mode: "now"`, explicit sessionKey) is accepted and deferred behind it (`{"ok":true,"mode":"now","eventOutcome":"queued"}`) → `tools.deny: ["write"]` is published by rewriting the config file → turn 1 is released. When the completion turn reaches the model it attempts a `write` tool call, so the tool result shows exactly which policy the executing turn bound.

**GREEN (dist rebuilt from the exact head; the current head `9cf97d1f275` adds only test-file changes on top of `2bfb02d057a`, production code is byte-identical):**

```text
POST /hooks/wake -> 200 {"ok":true,"mode":"now","eventOutcome":"queued"}
publishing tools.deny=[write] via config file rewrite
releasing turn 1
provider #1: COMPLETION TURN arrived (marker visible); calling write
provider #2: completion-turn write result back; final text
write tool result seen by model: Tool write not found
write denial visible to model: true
forbidden file exists: false
SCENARIO_A_RESULT=PROOF_OK
```

The stale-policy adoption was rejected, the occurrence was re-admitted through a fresh dispatch, and the completion turn executed under the **published** policy: `write` was gone from the toolset (`Tool write not found`) and no filesystem I/O happened.

**RED (same tree with `session-event-handoff.ts` at the PR-base version, dist rebuilt):**

```text
POST /hooks/wake -> 200 {"ok":true,"mode":"now","eventOutcome":"queued"}
publishing tools.deny=[write] via config file rewrite
releasing turn 1
completion turn never arrived (occurrence silently consumed)
SCENARIO_A_RESULT=PROOF_INCOMPLETE
```

and the base Gateway log shows the silent loss verbatim:

```text
[session-events] session event execution failed source=hook agentId=main sessionKey=agent:main:pr169529proof eventId=3cc6dde6-… error="Error: Session event configuration changed; retry under the current policy"
[hooks] hook wake failed status=failed error="Error: Session event configuration changed; retry under the current policy"
```

**Control (this PR's head, no config publication, turn 1 aborted via `chat.send` `/stop`):** the deferred occurrence is adopted after the abort and executes under the unchanged policy — the write succeeds and the file is created:

```text
chat.send /stop -> {"ok":true,"payload":{"ok":true,"aborted":true,"runIds":["8c96dafc-…"]}}
provider #1: COMPLETION TURN arrived (marker visible); calling write
control: write result returned: true; file exists: true
SCENARIO_B_RESULT=PROOF_OK
```

A vs control differ only in the config publication, which isolates the GREEN write denial to the freshly bound policy. The control also confirms the deferred-event machinery itself is exercised end-to-end.

**Double-publication collapse (this PR's head):** two publications land while the occurrence is deferred (`tools.deny: ["write"]`, then `["write", "message"]`); settlement must re-admit exactly once under the *latest* policy — one completion turn, no per-publication retry storm, no duplicate execution:

```text
publishing tools.deny=["write"] via config file rewrite
publishing tools.deny=["write","message"] via config file rewrite
releasing turn 1
provider #1: COMPLETION TURN arrived (marker visible); calling write
write tool result seen by model: Tool write not found
write denied under the latest policy: true
completion turn count (must be 1): 1
forbidden file exists: false
SCENARIO_C_RESULT=PROOF_OK
```

Driver script: `proof-169529.mjs` at the PR-head tree root is intentionally **not** part of the diff; full run logs are available on request.

### Retained-authority final effects (shipped Gateway, exact head)

Two further shipped-Gateway scenarios close the retained-authority gap with final-effect evidence, using deterministic state the config watcher cannot stage on demand.

**Scenario D — retained producer tool ceiling beats the current policy.** Turn 1 is admitted under `tools.deny: ["write"]`, so the background exec completion it produces captures a tool ceiling that excludes write. While the completion defers behind the held turn, the driver publishes a config that **removes** the denial — the current policy now allows write. The re-admitted completion turn still cannot write:

```text
provider #0: launching background exec
provider #1: background exec started; holding turn 1
publishing config with write ALLOWED (deny removed)
releasing turn 1
provider #2: COMPLETION TURN arrived (marker visible); calling write
provider #3: completion-turn write result back; final text
write tool result seen by model: Tool write not found
write denied under retained producer ceiling: true
forbidden file exists: false
SCENARIO_D_RESULT=PROOF_OK
```

The current policy permitted write at execution time, so only the retained producer ceiling (`expectedTarget.toolsAllow`, captured from the producing turn's admitted tool set) explains the rejection — enforced before filesystem I/O. A lost ceiling would have created the file.

**Scenario E — destination replacement settles before I/O, with no drain.** A deferred wake occurrence faces a publication that also moves `session.store`. On a real Gateway the store move tears the queue down at reload, so the occurrence settles as queue-owner abandonment (the re-dispatch never runs); the synchronous re-dispatch rejection for a captured-destination mismatch is the other terminal shape, pinned by the `producer retires before re-admission` unit. Either way the occurrence is consumed before any I/O, and a later ordinary turn does not inherit it:

```text
POST /hooks/wake -> 200 {"ok":true,"mode":"now","eventOutcome":"queued"}
publishing config with a REPLACED session store
releasing turn 1
completion turn arrived (must be false): false
gateway log: readmission rejected=false abandoned=true
wake text drained into a later ordinary turn (must be false): false
forbidden file exists: false
SCENARIO_E_RESULT=PROOF_OK
```

with the Gateway log showing the terminal settlement verbatim:

```text
[reload] config change detected; evaluating reload (tools.deny, session.store)
[hooks] hook wake failed status=cancelled error="Session event was abandoned before execution"
[reload] config hot reload applied (tools.deny, session.store)
```

The delivery opt-out boundary is the same owner code on every attempt: `deliver()` checks `options.deliver === false || target?.deliver === false` before any transport send, the re-admission carries the captured target forward unchanged, and the capture-side invariant is pinned by `captures the original store, route and producer restrictions across asynchronous lookup` (`deliver: false` retained on the target).

### Terminal-path coverage (exact-head unit, driving the real queue boundary)

The three terminal findings concern internal custody transitions with no external trigger surface — instrumenting the shipped Gateway showed the deferred occurrence's adoption is only attempted once the reply queue drains to it, so successive rejections cannot be staged deterministically through the watcher (~1s publication latency vs a sub-second re-dispatch window). These paths are pinned by exact-head unit tests that drive the real claim/consume APIs and the real queue-lifecycle callback pair (`onAbandoned` → `onSettled`), and every one fails against the previous reviewed head `1438fbb02e3`:

- `consumes a canceled re-admission instead of preserving it for a later turn` — cancels the original receipt while the retry is deferred; the retried occurrence settles `cancelled` and nothing survives for a later turn. On `1438fbb02e3` the canceled occurrence leaked into the passive queue (`expected [ { …(5) } ] to deeply equal []`).
- `settles terminally after the bounded re-admission budget is exhausted` — three consecutive publications reject the occurrence and both retries; the third settles `failed` with the explicit `readmission attempts exhausted` error and consumes the occurrence. On `1438fbb02e3` it leaked into passive custody (same assertion diff).
- `settles terminally when the producer retires before re-admission` — the producer's `assertCurrent` starts throwing between the policy rejection and settlement; the synchronous re-dispatch rejection consumes the occurrence and logs `readmission rejected`. On `1438fbb02e3` it was retained passively (same assertion diff).
- `carries submitting authority into a pre-acceptance re-admission and settles on revocation` — the hook's `assertAcceptanceCurrent` is invoked again by the re-dispatch and, once revoked, rejects it before any new turn admission; the occurrence settles `failed` and consumed. On `1438fbb02e3` the retry proceeded without the ingress assertion, so the expected terminal revocation settlement never happened (test timed out).

### Exact-head unit proof receipt

- Product head SHA: `9cf97d1f275` (full SHA in the commit list above)
- Pre-change RED baselines: `8f8a68d434a62d5977a8e7d8e51d368448a780c6^` (PR base; the silent-loss scenario) and the previous reviewed head `1438fbb02e322f4cc8bc1cfd38653b3f4ecd6391` (the four terminal-path regressions)
- Production entry: `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.config.ts src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-handoff.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`
- Canonical owner exercised: `enqueueSessionEventForHost` in `src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-handoff.ts`
- Decision surface: occurrence custody (`ownership.release()` vs `ownership.cancel()`), the policy snapshot the re-admitted dispatch binds, and the ingress assertion carried across the pre-acceptance retry
- Recorder/readback boundary: `receipt.settled` status, dispatch invocation count and its captured `cfg`, the `session-events` error log, plus `peekSystemEventEntries(sessionKey)`
- Acceptance RED (base): with the production file at the pre-PR version, `re-admits an accepted deferred occurrence under the current policy after a config publication` fails — the receipt settles with `executionStarted: false` and no second dispatch happens, i.e. the occurrence was consumed, which is the silent loss
- Acceptance RED (round-2 head `1438fbb02e3`): the four terminal-path cases above fail — the canceled, exhausted, and producer-retired occurrences each leaked into the passive queue, and the revoked-ingress case proceeded without the submitting assertion
- Acceptance GREEN: on the exact head, `Tests 29 passed (29)`, including all seven re-admission cases
- Terminal control: `consumes a deferred occurrence the queue owner abandons, even after a config publication` still drives the real `onAbandoned` → `onSettled` pair after a publication and asserts no re-admission and a consumed occurrence — abandoned work cannot be resurrected by a publication
- Cleanup: every case runs under `withOpenClawTestState` isolated state/config; no production Gateway, session, token, or configuration was touched

### Inspectable RED -> GREEN (unit)

RED (production file at round-2 head `1438fbb02e3`, final test text, no timers or sleeps):

```text
× session event target custody > consumes a canceled re-admission instead of preserving it for a later turn
× session event target custody > settles terminally after the bounded re-admission budget is exhausted
× session event target custody > settles terminally when the producer retires before re-admission
× session event target custody > carries submitting authority into a pre-acceptance re-admission and settles on revocation

```

GREEN (exact head, whole file):

```text

 ✓ session event target custody > re-admits an accepted deferred occurrence under the current policy after a config publication
 ✓ session event target custody > consumes a deferred occurrence the queue owner abandons, even after a config publication
 ✓ session event target custody > consumes a canceled re-admission instead of preserving it for a later turn
 ✓ session event target custody > settles terminally after the bounded re-admission budget is exhausted
 ✓ session event target custody > settles terminally when the producer retires before re-admission

 Test Files  1 passed (1)

```

### Verification

- `session-event-handoff.test.ts` — 29 passed (22 existing + 7 re-admission cases); the cancellation and exhaustion cases await an owned dispatch gate resolved by the collecting mock, no polling
- `session-event-permissions.test.ts`, `agent-runner-execution-session-events.test.ts`, `followup-turn-admission.test.ts`, `queue/lifecycle.test.ts`, `queue/cleanup.session-authority.test.ts` — 80 passed across the five adjacent suites (109 total with the owner file)
- Scoped `tsgo` typecheck on the changed production file and the test file: clean (the dispatch mock is now typed with the real async dispatch contract, so Vitest 5 `mockImplementationOnce` signature checking passes)
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint -c .oxlintrc.json` on the two changed files: clean (0 warnings, 0 errors)
- Shipped-Gateway GREEN: single publication (A), `/stop` control (B), double-publication collapse (C), retained producer ceiling after the denial is lifted (D), destination replacement with no drain (E) — plus base RED — all on `dist/` rebuilt from the exact head

<details>
<summary>Review responses (fourth pass)</summary>

- **[P3] Replace retry-count polling with an owned completion signal:** fixed. The collecting dispatch now resolves an owned gate when it observes the Nth call (`collectDeferredAdoptions` returns `whenDispatchCalled(count)`); the cancellation case awaits the retry's own dispatch before cancel, and the exhaustion loop awaits each re-admission's dispatch before the next publication. No `vi.waitFor` remains in the file.
- **[medium] Retained authority forwarded without final-effect evidence:** addressed with shipped-Gateway final effects. Scenario D proves the retained producer tool ceiling is enforced at execution: the completion turn runs while the *current* policy allows write, yet the write is rejected (`Tool write not found`) with no filesystem I/O, because the occurrence re-admitted with the producing turn's captured ceiling. Scenario E proves a replaced destination never reaches I/O — the occurrence settles terminally (queue-owner abandonment at reload on a real Gateway; the synchronous re-dispatch rejection is unit-pinned), nothing drains into a later ordinary turn (verified by driving one), and no file is created. The delivery opt-out rides the same owner boundary: `deliver()` consults the retained target on every attempt before any transport send.
- **[merge risk] Final-effect enforcement of producer ceiling / opt-out / destination:** covered by D (ceiling), the owner-level opt-out boundary (above), and E (destination) respectively; forwarding plus enforcement is now demonstrated, not just forwarding.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Review responses (third pass)</summary>

- **[P1] Consume canceled readmissions instead of preserving them:** fixed by removing `preserveOccurrenceOnRejection` from the re-admission. That flag is reserved for occurrences that already existed as passive notices before a failed promotion (the restart/coalesce producers); a producer-owned retry that is canceled, stopped, abandoned, or admission-refused now settles through the normal consume path. The original receipt's `cancel()` still forwards to the live attempt, and the canceled retry settles `cancelled` with the occurrence consumed (unit: `consumes a canceled re-admission…`, RED on `1438fbb02e3`).
- **[P1] Retain producer authority when bounded readmission falls back:** fixed by settling terminally instead of falling back to passive custody. Retry exhaustion and synchronous re-dispatch rejection (retired producer, moved destination, revoked ingress) consume the occurrence and log an explicit error; the generic system-event queue never receives the producer-owned occurrence, so no later ordinary turn can drain it as contract-less prompt text under its own authority (units: `…budget is exhausted`, `…producer retires before re-admission`, both RED on `1438fbb02e3`).
- **[P1] Carry submitting authority until the first acceptance:** fixed. If the original attempt never reached acceptance, the still-live `assertAcceptanceCurrent` is captured before settlement clears it and passed to the re-dispatch, whose synchronous assertion call then rejects revoked ingress before any session preparation or turn admission (unit: `carries submitting authority…`, RED on `1438fbb02e3` — the retry previously proceeded without the assertion).
- **[P2] Type the dispatch mock with its asynchronous call contract:** fixed. The mock is declared as `vi.fn<typeof dispatchInboundMessageWithRoutedChannelDispatcher>` with the throwing default retained; implementations use the real parameter type and return a well-formed `DispatchFromConfigResult` via a tiny `dispatchResult()` helper. Scoped `tsgo` over the production file and the test file is clean.
- **[security, high] Passive fallback removes the producer's security ceiling:** eliminated — the passive fallback no longer exists for producer-owned occurrences; terminal settlements consume, and the only custody-transfer path is the fresh dispatch that re-runs every destination and authority check under the current policy.
- **[security, high] Pre-acceptance retry drops ingress authority:** eliminated — the retry carries the submitting invocation's live assertion until its first acceptance, so revoked ingress rejects the re-dispatch synchronously (see the revocation unit).
- **[provenance] Producer-owned occurrence settlement:** preserved — fresh producer-owned occurrences still settle terminally on every terminal signal; `preserveOccurrenceOnRejection` remains exclusive to pre-existing passive notices (the existing `releases an occurrence when Gateway restart admission refuses the producer` and cold-preparation custody cases still pass unchanged).

</details>

<details>
<summary>Scope, alternatives, and land-ready notes</summary>

**Scope:** one owner (`session-event-handoff.ts`) and its regression file. The state that changes is exactly "not started AND no delivery attempted AND settled by a policy publication".

**States that still fail by design** (unchanged, and asserted by existing tests): a queued occurrence that was never accepted; an occurrence that already started or attempted delivery; a store replacement; agent deletion; an unresolvable agent; lost reply-run ownership; an already-settled occurrence.

**Alternative considered and rejected:** keeping a passive-custody fallback after budget exhaustion (this PR's second cut). Review found the generic queue carries no producer contract, so a later ordinary turn would drain the occurrence as prompt text under its own authority — and exec completions would be stranded entirely. Terminal settlement with an explicit error keeps the failure observable and the authority contract intact.

**Alternative considered and rejected:** pushing retry into the five producers. That spreads the same rule across 5-6 files and leaves the accepted-but-unstarted window open in the owner itself; central re-admission keeps the rule in one place.

**Land-ready reasoning:** the change is behavior-completing in one owner, reuses the existing dispatch and destination checks rather than adding new ones, adds no config/protocol/storage/migration surface, and ships deterministic regressions that fail on current main and on the previous reviewed head, plus a shipped-Gateway RED/GREEN proof.

</details>

</details>

prs.title: fix: updates fail after transient Git download errors
prs.body:
Related: #169667

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes source updates aborting after a settled transient Git download failure, including incomplete ref advertisements during dry runs.

## User Impact

The installed updater retries an eligible fetch or remote-ref probe once. An explicit `--timeout` remains one total budget; omitted work deadlines remain unbounded. Authentication failures, expired deadlines, and cancelled commands are not replayed. A requester revoked during backoff cannot start the second network request.

This fixes the updater already installed; an older updater cannot acquire the repair from a candidate before its first failing fetch.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing Git retry owner for update commands and read-only dry-run probes, forwarding inherited cancellation and rechecking live requester authority immediately before network attempts. Local cleanup stays available after revocation. No new retry policy, state, permission, or cancellation owner is added.

This branch now incorporates the distinct dry-run/incomplete-advertisement repair from #169667 together with the newer optional-deadline and requester-authority repair. It is the consolidated implementation; the older overlapping PR should not land independently. Upstream `3971bf53e7b0` is integrated without replacing the original PR ancestry.

## Evidence

- Two new regressions failed before the follow-up: incomplete dry-run ref advertisements did not recover, and inherited cancellation did not settle retry backoff immediately. The repaired four-suite scope passes **27 tests**. The last dry-run-only verification passes **3/3**, 23.34 s wrapper wall; combined test bodies are under one second. The initial combined run took 107.44 s, mostly worker compilation. CI seconds for this revision are pending.
- Canonical core typing, a changed-test type graph, targeted lint/format, whitespace checks, and the supported runtime build pass. The clean pinned runtime build took **3m33.1s**. Independent P0–P2 autoreview is scoped-clean with no actionable findings; a subsequent test-only assertion adjustment preserved the same contract and passed typing/tests/lint.
- Original transport implementation build: `2026.10.3-5ebd48d0f9b8-2026-10-16T02-08-10.382Z`, commit `5ebd48d0f9b822fc3bc61b53b659944fb09222e3`. The native CLI cases below ran in disposable Docker state with networking disabled except their container-local Git server. Git subprocesses and `git http-backend` were real.
- A separate authority-chain experiment entered real `updateGitInstall` through `createManagedUpdateRequesterAuthority`, `createUpdateCommandAuthority`, and a native update executor. The server cut a real 2 MiB upload-pack response. The allowed requester recovered on attempt two. Editing the actual isolated `commands.ownerAllowFrom` during backoff revoked the requester: one fetch/pack response, no second HTTP request, `requester-revoked`, unchanged installed HEAD, and no remaining private Git inspection directory in either case. No Boolean-backed authority or subprocess-result mock was used.

<details>
<summary>Inspectable current-implementation terminal results</summary>

```text
Native installed CLI:
  node openclaw.mjs update --channel dev --no-restart --yes --json
  --timeout omitted

Real Git: transfer closed with 353 bytes remaining to read
[git/network] Git fetch hit a transient failure; retrying once
actual Git fetch starts=2; HTTP requests=2; injected faults=1
git-target-inspection-fetch: exitCode=0, termination=exit
CLI exitCode=0; durable run=finished/skipped, reason=already-current
remaining updater/Git processes=0
wall=29.203 s

Fresh installation, SIGTERM after the production retry warning:
actual Git fetch starts=1; HTTP requests=1; no second request
CLI exitCode=143; durable run=finished/failed, reason=interrupted
remaining updater/Git processes=0
wall=30.329 s

Native read-only CLI:
  node openclaw.mjs update --dry-run --channel dev --no-restart --yes --json --timeout 120
first real ref advertisement: advertised=631 bytes, sent=315
Real Git: transfer closed with 316 bytes remaining to read
[git/network] Git ls-remote hit a transient failure; retrying once
actual ls-remote starts=2; second advertisement=631/631 bytes
CLI exitCode=0; dryRun=true; no preflight failures
refs unchanged=true; object-file SHA-256 manifest unchanged=true
tracked worktree clean=true
wall=10.830 s

Real policy owner + native executor + updateGitInstall + real Git:
allowed requester:
  upload-pack responses=2; actual fetch starts=2; first response truncated
  target fetch exitCode=0; policyCurrent=true
revoked during backoff by changing commands.ownerAllowFrom:
  upload-pack responses=1; actual fetch starts=1; no second GET or POST
  UpdateRequesterRevokedError, code=requester-revoked; policyCurrent=false
both cases:
  installed HEAD unchanged; private inspection directories remaining=0
```

The native CLI uses the canonical absent-service fixture and an already-current target; it proves transport recovery, CLI continuation, read-only behavior, and cancellation, not a version-changing activation. The root-run container's account-home ownership prevented optional original capture, so no data-preservation claim is made from that case. The separate real-policy experiment deliberately uses a minimal synthetic package with no build script: its allowed fetch proceeds to the later build refusal, which is not counted as successful activation.

Reproduction harness SHA-256:
- Native transport: `403a68e575dbc24d6a3597bd20e5c9ba470a30a79259df9b0c42da80090160e8`
- Native dry run: `46a999765605f9eb52df434b4229392214f8259ba93dbedcdfa81e35b5819b9b`
- Real-policy HTTP fixture: `29bbf259f6f327f835e311c2b0232e87bb8d160300b97585374997e01dee2b11`
- Real-policy driver: `a7dd1c5baa05cd636807aefe54d186fbf772ff538a555e740a2d9543a04db96f`

</details>

The current revision does not have latest-stable published-driver-to-candidate activation proof. The historical published-driver trace on #169667 remains evidence for that older implementation. The later partial managed-install experiment below did not complete activation. Broad CI must attach to the final head.

## Preview Signal Follow-up

Latest head: `55ec6ca678fcbef853d051f683da56667aa9d6b3`.

Fixed [the P2 preview-shutdown finding](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173569#discussion_r4290274501). The existing preview owner now synchronously stops its inherited command scope before draining SIGINT/SIGTERM. A real bare-profile CLI experiment then exposed the separate initialization preview entry point, which bypassed that owner; it now uses the same owner around the complete preview and Git probe.

A no-run preview cancels only its local work and never creates or adopts ledger custody. Foreign/inherited run-object delegation, unchanged-row checks, cleanup joining, and accepted signal exit remain intact. There is no new signal, retry, or authority policy.

- Four added native signal cases failed before their respective repairs with an unaborted command signal. The complete selected lifecycle scope passes **16 tests**, including fresh, no-run, foreign, inherited, changed, pending, missing-state, handoff, and repeated-signal controls. **2 existing fresh-preview caller tests** also pass.
- Final scoped CLI-update typing, targeted lint/format, and fresh canonical P0–P2 review pass. The final clean `pnpm build:runtime` passes in **2m22.1s**.
- The actual CLI ran under Node.js 24.21.0 with build `2026.10.3-55ec6ca678fc-2026-10-16T03-10-01.099Z`. The container-local HTTP server truncated a real ref advertisement; SIGTERM was sent only after the production retry warning. Both entry points now stop before attempt two.

```text
Native dry-run CLI: SIGTERM during real ls-remote retry backoff

Before, 5ebd48d / bare profile:
  accepted signal exit=143, but actual ls-remote/HTTP requests=2
Intermediate f6738be / bare profile:
  actual ls-remote/HTTP requests=2 (separate initialization path)
Final 55ec6ca / bare profile:
  actual ls-remote/HTTP requests=1; CLI exit=143
  config unchanged=true; SQLite absent before and after
  refs unchanged=true; object manifest unchanged=true; worktree clean=true
  remaining updater/Git processes=0; wall=4.599s
Final 55ec6ca / Doctor-initialized profile:
  actual ls-remote/HTTP requests=1; CLI exit=143
  config unchanged=true; existing SQLite retained
  refs unchanged=true; object manifest unchanged=true; worktree clean=true
  remaining updater/Git processes=0; wall=14.329s
```

<details>
<summary>Additional real installed-update continuation and its explicit limit</summary>

Real installed CLI transport, retention, and installation proof (partial)

Driver candidate: `5ebd48d0f9b822fc3bc61b53b659944fb09222e3`. Synthetic upstream child: `7972a77871d950333bd335748db2ee467f88da76`; its only difference is a 4 MiB random transport marker, with identical production source. Candidate source and host caches were read-only; state and dependency-store copies were private synthetic fixtures.

Invoked the installed `openclaw update --channel dev --no-restart --yes --json`, without a fixed CLI timeout, against loopback smart HTTP backed by real `git http-backend`. The first pack advertised 4,198,419 bytes and sent 2,099,209; Git reported curl 18 and early EOF. The production updater waited one second and retried once. The second real fetch received all 4,198,939 advertised bytes. Exactly two fetch attempts occurred.

Real runtime retention passed (688.812 seconds; 170,138 entries, 147,997 copied files). Real candidate `pnpm install` passed in 26.36 seconds across 194 workspace projects, reusing all 1,596 registry packages. No skip-scripts flag or lifecycle override was introduced; the repository's normal lifecycle policy ran unchanged. Matrix crypto 0.6.6 used its supported `MATRIX_SDK_CRYPTO_DOWNLOADS_BASE_URL` override to download 24,788,544 qualified cached native-library bytes from loopback; the recorded SHA-256 is `aeb21029ac6bb29cd06493f67b19a5a75b3d0371a1ab452fe59f78249350f0f7`. No production code or GitHub state was changed by this proof lane.

prs.title: feat(telegram): add per-message context control with /ignore
prs.body:
Related: #123937

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw agents in Telegram groups currently ingest every authorized message,
even when two humans are talking only to each other. That side conversation can
later surface in an unrelated reply, waste prompt context, or steer the agent's
future behavior.

The existing mention and activation controls are chat-wide and decide whether a
message triggers the bot; they do not selectively remove one update from rolling
group history. `/ignore <message>` adds that message-level context boundary.

```text
Alex: /ignore Dinner at 7? The reservation is under "banana."
Sam: Summarize the deployment decisions from today.

Without /ignore: the side conversation can enter the agent's rolling context.
With /ignore: that update never enters ambient agent context.
```

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a Telegram-native `/ignore` command that drops one authorized inbound
update before reply-chain recording, media processing, history compilation, or
agent dispatch. An authorized `/ignore <message>` is intentionally silent; bare
`/ignore` returns usage help. Exact command matching supports commands addressed
to this bot, leaves foreign-bot and forwarded commands alone, and lets an
account-scoped custom `/ignore` retain ownership when configured.

Media albums are ignored as a unit at the existing flush boundary. Durable,
account/chat-scoped message and album tombstones prevent an ignored update from
returning after an edit, replay, process restart, command-policy change, or bot
rename. Privacy tombstones use their own bounded persistence namespace, separate
from the ordinary message-cache LRU, and override cache hydration regardless of
hydration order.

A deliberate direct reply may reintroduce Telegram's replied-to quote for that
turn. Same-chat cached ancestry is detached from the ignored message and its
descendants; unrelated cross-chat messages with the same numeric message ID are
not affected.

`/btw` remains complementary: it keeps a message in context without requiring a
normal reply, while `/ignore` keeps a message out of context.

## User Impact

- Human participants can have one-off side conversations without distracting or
  unintentionally steering the agent.
- Agents retain useful ambient group context without treating every authorized
  message as relevant memory.
- Operators avoid toggling chat-wide mention or activation behavior for a
  message-level need.
- Ignored text and albums skip media work, prompt tokens, and agent dispatch.

This is context hygiene, not deletion, secrecy, encryption, or message
redaction. Telegram retains the original chat message normally.

## Evidence

Validated on exact head
`836dd8b3540018e1eea670b8f5f62d19e10e3206`, based on frozen `main`
`5e5f9c27559776303d962aa37f8c09f676e640d4`:

- Focused Telegram matrix: 350/350 tests.
- Full Telegram bot owner: 186/186 tests.
- Final album-ordering/cache/privacy corrective matrix: 66/66 tests, including
  deterministic record/remove interleaving across durable tombstones.
- Canonical no-fetch pre-PR wrapper: all selected gates pass, including core and
  extension source/test types, dead exports, format, core/extension/scripts
  lint, boundary and dependency guards, database-first storage, runtime cycles,
  and repository ratchets.
- Independent exact-head Sol review: no actionable P0-P2 finding remains.

Independent review found and fixed three final P2s before publication:

1. Cross-chat external reply IDs could be persisted as local reply identities.
2. A later message could overtake an album before its members entered prompt
   context.
3. A recorder could resume after `/ignore` removal and reinsert an embedded
   ignored reply snapshot.

The final implementation preserves cross-chat payload/media without borrowing a
local reply identity, records album members before delayed flush, and serializes
record/remove mutation per account and chat while installing privacy tombstones
before removal waits.

Exact-head Telegram Test Server proof remains `blocked_external`: it requires
maintainer TDLib/Test Server credentials and the official QA route. No live
Telegram claim is made from deterministic local evidence.

AI-assisted implementation and review; I inspected the final diff and understand
the behavior and scope.

prs.title: refactor: trust prepared command and runtime facts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The commands/CLI/runtime lane repeats work after its owners have already admitted or materialized the data: config and manifest rereads, whole-tree copies before serialization, redundant typed shape checks, and parallel terminal-wizard/control adapters. These costs and competing paths obscure the actual security and durability boundaries.

## User Impact

This is maintainer-requested internal cleanup, with no public surface change. Doctor also preserves and reports the original quarantine-read failure instead of silently replacing that observation with a retry. Accepted best-effort diagnostic/preview edge cases are listed below; no operator migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Share terminal Gateway wizard-step projection while keeping each command's presentation, input, cancellation, and secret handling.
- Consolidate MCP controls, Workshop archive/restore registration, hook config lookup, cron agent ownership, and status-row preparation onto their existing owners.
- Carry the first admitted config/quarantine/transcript observation through Doctor and channel-status reporting rather than rereading it. Keep failures visible.
- Replace redundant deep copies with existing owned values or copy-on-write; retain mutable provider/SDK snapshots, shared-cache protection, live authorization, FIFO ordering, and write settlement.
- Remove verification of just-created Claw artifacts and redundant staging-manifest rereads, retaining input validation, publication verification, backups, hashing, and atomic/durable writes.

No public config keys, CLI flags, Gateway/SDK protocol contracts, persisted shapes, dependencies, schema, retention, or permission changes. The internal cron worker snapshot drops its version field as described below. The standalone Phase E session-memory backend and its associated machinery/tests are untouched. Two stale max-lines baseline entries are removed and five assertion baseline entries shrink to match removed assertions; no budget or suppression is added.

The trajectory partial-skill guards and their regressions are retained: the original human report in #71185 describes actual Gateway agent-turn failures with before/after runtime logs (landed through #84797).

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Overlapping cron commands can briefly install an older coherent config snapshot in arrival order. Internal snapshot ordering came with #169766 and is pinned by a synthetic reversed-version fixture, not a cited human config-ordering incident. The next tick/refresh supplies current facts; live effect authority, FIFO ordering, and settlement remain.
- A schedule edit during read-only Doctor pagination can yield a transient mixed diagnostic inventory. The revision/total fence was introduced by #102427 with mocked snapshots, not a cited human incident; rerun Doctor after the edit. Cursor bounds and page validation remain.
- Retired/replacement progress callbacks can briefly perturb preview deduplication. #143621 supplied synthetic overlapping fixtures, not a cited actual-use human report. Final delivery, retirement, and settlement are unchanged.
- Mutating a registry without publishing through its owner can leave lookup results unchanged until proper publication. The removed grow-in-place fixture bypassed that publication contract; ordinary registry replacement remains covered.
- A stale local bundled manifest must be rebuilt rather than repaired by guessing a peer source directory. #165492's fixture manufactured stale dist metadata; canonical bundled manifest artifacts remain the alias owner.
- Unsupported callers that mutate internal prepared requests, returned facts, or config descriptors during consumption no longer receive extra deep-copy/freeze isolation. Actual mutable provider-stream and public SDK boundaries retain their snapshots; traced internal producers do not perform these writes.
- Unsupported malformed internal media decisions fail at typed consumption rather than receiving partial fallback summaries. The restored guards in #65096 were requested to satisfy cast-malformed fixtures; external attachment normalization and real provider-failure reporting remain.
- Our own freshly written/exported/packed data is not immediately re-read/extracted to assert that the writer worked. Writer errors still surface; input, publication, manifest/hash/DB validation, backup, and recovery responsibilities remain with their existing owners.
- Offline Doctor reports one quarantine observation instead of retrying the same read for its UI. A transient observation failure is now reported consistently in both structured and interactive output, with its original error.
- A plugin that replaces a contribution's callback or metadata during its own repair is best effort. Stable adapter receiver binding remains where an overlay actually needs it; contribution findings are otherwise borrowed read-only.

## Size and coverage

Net production LOC: **534 removed**, excluding tests/support/fixtures/generated/declarations and including the new 53-line wizard helper. Tracked production +754/-1341, plus the new helper. This is within the campaign's authoritative 500–1,500 net-production-line band; test deletions do not count toward it.

Coverage and exact provenance are recorded in the task-owned z07 ledger and per-owner supplements: **10,181/10,181 original inventory occurrences across 54 directories, zero missing keys**, independently reconciled after correcting misplaced protocol/typed-field family deferrals. This is exact-hit coverage, not an assertion that every possible semantic cleanup has been found. Family-owned SQLite wiring, directive/config normalization, and generic helpers remain assigned to z14–z16; unrelated work is not claimed as completed by this lane.

## Evidence

PR CI on the exact pushed head is the broad gate. The original 151-file Node selection finished with compiled-generation verification: **147 files passed / 4 failed; 1,933 tests passed / 72 failed / 3 existing skips**, across 18 configurations. Only unit and infra configurations failed. The tooling reporter's duplicated summary is counted once. The diagnosed socket-path recovery and additional owning-boundary checks are still pending.

Completed local evidence: final changed-file formatting and type-aware lint; core production types; all seven selected core test type graphs (Gateway, commands, config/CLI, other runtime, Plugin SDK consumers, Doctor, and cron services); runtime import cycles (0); Madge (0 cycles); assertion-safety ratchet (2,680 files / 6,215 assertions); UI session-goal tests (4 passed); unchanged Doctor canonical-key ownership/retention tests (15 passed). Graph-boundary admission was reused after import/root/membership-neutral mechanical repairs; all seven selected type graphs were executed on final source. Mandatory lint-suppressions and PR wrapper source-closure tests passed in the completed Node selection. An earlier supported `qaRuntime` build and built-package import smoke passed before later mechanical repairs/base-guard restorations; these are not a final-head full build. The interrupted full build and whole check-changed invocation are not passes.

The focused status-model case `prepares bounded usage off-thread and sees a later committed transcript` exceeded its existing 120-second timeout on both Bun (121,111ms) and the documented Node route (125,253ms). Cause remains unresolved, not attributed as inherited or established as load-only. No deadline, retry, skip, or assertion changed. Its only direct status-text change is an equivalent numeric-completeness predicate for this fixture's missing-or-number inputs.

The Node run also timed out `renders current discovered limits without reusing a stale cache or estimate` at 120,645ms. Later adjacent status cases passed with decreasing execution times; that is diagnostic evidence, not a repair or inherited-failure attribution. Both exact failures remain under investigation.

Independent review completed with two P2 findings, both declined after full owner/caller inspection: receipt normalization starts with an empty record map (there is no retained pre-normalization object alias), and channel env lookup consumes fresh locally normalized string buckets rather than raw plugin metadata. This is an explained finding disposition, not a claim that the reviewer returned clean. Earlier review's valid mutable-provider/SDK snapshot concerns were repaired.

The current MCP CLI probe case failed with `exit 1` after 5,413ms in the normal-server add at test line 269, after its expected hung-server rejection. Its cause is unresolved; it is not attributed as inherited or load-only. Earlier local runs also had a 10-second test timeout and state-lease/config-owner errors; an earlier replay failed source-graph identity verification and is not passing proof or inheritance evidence. The final 151-file invocation did verify its source/output generation.

Two node-worker supervisor cases failed: blocked cancellation exceeded its existing 15-second limit (16,101ms actual), and restart/re-arm replay reached its existing 10-second launch deadline with an additional unexpected-cancellation cleanup error in the same case. The supervisor and capacity production modules are unchanged. Changed dependencies only drop private terminal-outcome freezes, a model copy, and an installer-result copy; no causal repair or baseline attribution is claimed.

The remaining 67 failures were worker-runtime fixture setup failures: the task wrapper's canonical macOS socket path was 116 bytes. A native bind control reproduced `EINVAL` at 116 bytes and succeeded at 42 bytes. Only the task-owned isolation wrapper was corrected to a short mode-0700 temp root; production/tests, deadlines, retries, skips, assertions, and authority guards are unchanged. Full worker-runtime replay is running, not a claimed pass. The additional TTS status-config file reports 7 passing cases, including per-agent persona selection; its invocation's final generation verification remains pending.

Local gaps at publication: the separately filtered eager-wrapper inventory check and original-base Doctor negative control have not yet run. Existing PR wrapper source-closure tests passed; hosted inventory/import-closure checks remain unweakened gates. The original-base control is regression qualification only, never current-main/inherited-CI proof. No green check or complete build is claimed for an unfinished invocation.

prs.title: feat(plugins): default package installs to ClawHub
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Installing a ClawHub plugin currently requires a registry prefix even though ClawHub is the default plugin catalog.

## User Impact

Users can install ClawHub packages directly:

```diff
-openclaw plugins install clawhub:@composio/composio
+openclaw plugins install @composio/composio
```

Unprefixed package names, versions, and tags now resolve through ClawHub. Use `npm:package` for npm installs; existing `clawhub:`, Git, local path/archive, and canonical built-in plugin shortcuts remain supported. A missing ClawHub package does not silently fall back to npm.

## Why This Change Was Made

Companion website change: https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/pull/3965. It retains a clearly labeled command for stable releases through 2026.10.4 alongside the shorter command for updated builds.

A shared source planner applies the same default to CLI, chat, and system-agent installs. CLI help, search commands, repair hints, and public docs follow that behavior; persisted provenance stays explicit for updates. Unscoped search results include `@latest` to avoid collisions with built-in shortcuts.

This removes the superseded npm-to-bundled fallback and duplicate source classifier. Most documentation changes are regenerated plugin inventory examples. This intentionally changes the registry used by unprefixed third-party installs, so npm-specific automation must add `npm:`.

## Evidence

- Before: six new CLI regression cases failed because unprefixed packages selected npm. After: focused source-selection, CLI, repair, and agent tests pass, including explicit npm, version/tag parsing, local paths, built-in collisions, and update provenance.
- CI exposed two stale fixtures and a recovery ownership gap. Six new regression cases reproduced cross-registry/canonical-ID recovery failures; the fix now passes 61 focused tests, preserving explicit npm and canonical-ID recovery while denying npm catalog recovery authority to ClawHub specs.
- Saved npm and ClawHub records now round-trip through SQLite into the updater: legacy npm specs retain npm and disabled/custom settings; legacy ClawHub pins retain ClawHub in update and dry-run paths. All 86 update tests pass, and the corrected search E2E assertion passes.
- The CLI pre-action recovery table now covers explicit npm and canonical IDs separately from ClawHub denials. All 48 touched/adjacent tests pass; the first-party mock preserves real exports and its obsolete baseline allowance is removed.
- Five compiled CLI end-to-end tests pass against a fixture registry with isolated state, including prefix-free installation and repeated explicit updates.
- Final standard build, scoped lint/format, core and affected test-graph typechecks pass. Documentation links, MDX, glossary, and generated inventory checks pass.
- Optional private-QA build hit its SDK declaration-size guard: 5,353,620 bytes against 5,340,536 allowed. Baseline attribution is unverified; the standard build passes. Hosted checks below are the landing gates.

Two hosted runs timed out in an npm-pack lifecycle test and reported a database teardown error. A focused npm/npm-pack replay passed locally, but that does not prove the failure is inherited. CI classifies it as unknown because there is no matching scheduled-main job; the actual merge-ref inputs are under investigation. No timeout or fixture changes have been made to hide it, and landing remains gated on resolution.
