prs.title: fix(discord): honor discord:user:<id> command owners in voice access and exec approvals
prs.body:
## Summary

When `commands.ownerAllowFrom` holds a Discord owner in the canonical direct-user form `discord:user:<id>`, the Discord plugin treats the owner list as empty:

- `/vc join|leave|status` replies "You are not authorized to use this command." to everyone, including the configured owner, and voice transcript turns lose owner status and admission.
- Owner-derived Discord exec approvers resolve to none, so `channels.discord.execApprovals.enabled: "auto"` stays disabled and the owner cannot approve exec requests from Discord.

Doctor writes and preserves this form since #167059, and `docs/tools/slash-commands.md` documents `ownerAllowFrom: ["discord:user:123456789012345678"]` as the example config. Text and native slash command authorization already accept it through core `src/auto-reply/command-auth.ts`; only the Discord-local owner selector disagrees.

## Root cause

`extensions/discord/src/command-owners.ts` still drops every `discord:user:` entry, a filter added in #137780 when that form was a retired envelope that Doctor rewrote away:

```ts
// before
return entries.length > 0 ? entries.filter((entry) => !/^discord:user:/i.test(entry)) : undefined;
```

For `["discord:user:<id>"]` this returns `[]`, not `undefined`. Every Discord owner consumer routes through this selector:

- `voice/owner-access.ts`: `admissionAllowFrom = commandOwnerAllowFrom ?? accountAllowFrom ?? ...`. `[]` is not nullish, so the account `allowFrom` fallback is skipped and voice admission is an empty allowlist. `ownerAllowFrom` is also `[]`, so speakers are never the owner.
- `exec-approvals.ts`: the owner fallback passes `[]` as the explicit approver list, so there are zero approvers and `isDiscordExecApprovalClientEnabled` is false for `enabled: "auto"`.
- `monitor/native-command-auth.ts`: the native command owner gate sees a configured but empty owner list.

#167059 made `discord:user:<id>` canonical (`docs/gateway/doctor/config-migrations.md`, "Command-owner target kinds"). ClawSweeper's review of #167059 flagged this exact gap as P1 before merge ("Update Discord owner consumers for the preserved target kind", https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/167059#issuecomment-6056057751): "`resolveDiscordCommandOwnerEntries()` still filters out every `discord:user:` entry at `extensions/discord/src/command-owners.ts:10`. Consequently, Doctor's recovery changes a working bare owner into an empty voice admission list and removes owner-derived exec approvers." That PR merged without the selector change, and current main still has the filter.

## Fix

Keep `discord:user:` entries in the selector:

```ts
// after
return entries.length > 0 ? entries : undefined;
```

No new parsing is needed. `resolveDiscordCommandOwnerAllowFrom` already strips `discord:`, which yields `user:<id>`, and `normalizeDiscordAllowList` already resolves that to the native sender id. That is the same path the existing `user:<id>` owner cases use. On the approval side, `normalizeDiscordApproverId` already parses `discord:user:<id>` through `parseDiscordTarget`, which is how explicit `execApprovals.approvers: ["discord:user:456"]` already works. Wildcards keep their current behavior: `discord:user:*` becomes `user:*`, which the allowlist and the approver parser both still reject. The stale comment describing the retired envelope is removed.

## Why this is the right boundary

The selector is the single Discord-owned place that turns `commands.ownerAllowFrom` into Discord owner entries, and all of its consumers (voice admission, voice speaker owner status, the native command owner gate, exec approvers) now agree with core command authorization and with the form Doctor preserves. Bare ids, `discord:<id>`, `user:<id>`, `pk:<id>`, and mention forms are unchanged, and so are foreign-channel entries.

Slack sibling, out of scope: `extensions/slack/src/exec-approvals.ts` passes raw `commands.ownerAllowFrom` entries to `parseSlackTarget`, which has no `slack:` channel-prefix handling. That gap predates #167059, is not this filter, and would need its own Slack-specific change.

Possible rebase overlap: open #157298 edits `extensions/discord/src/exec-approvals.ts` and its test for linked-requester approval discovery. It does not touch the owner selector, so the two changes are independent.

## Verification

- Local gates (vitest, oxlint, oxfmt, tsgo) are left to CI per contributor workflow on this machine.
- Updated colocated regression cases that fail on main and pass with this patch:
  - `extensions/discord/src/voice/command.test.ts`: `discord:user:100000000000000001` owner is now authorized for `/vc status`.
  - `extensions/discord/src/voice/speaker-context.test.ts`: `discord:user:123456789012345678` owner now yields `senderIsOwner: true`.
  - `extensions/discord/src/exec-approvals.test.ts`: `commands.ownerAllowFrom: ["discord:user:123"]` now resolves approver `123` and enables the client with `enabled: "auto"`. Explicit approver targets are unchanged.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: A Discord owner configured as `commands.ownerAllowFrom: ["discord:user:<id>"]` is refused on `/vc` and gets no exec approval delivery or approve rights on Discord.
Real environment tested: The shipped Discord provider interaction surface (`createDiscordProviderInteractionSurface` from `extensions/discord/src/monitor/provider.interactions.ts`, the same builder `monitor/provider.ts` uses at boot) registered on the real internal Discord `Client`, with a real `DiscordVoiceManager` on a real `GatewayScheduler`. A raw Discord APPLICATION_COMMAND payload for `/vc status` from the owner goes through `Client.handleInteraction`, and the reply is read from the REST call the client sends back to Discord. The only replaced seam is the Discord HTTP fetch (`requestOptions.fetch`), which records outgoing REST calls and answers guild/channel GETs. Exec approval state comes from the shipped `discordPlugin.approvalCapability` from `extensions/discord/src/channel.ts`. Runs used pristine main 512cc70 (no changes to `extensions/discord/src`, `src/plugin-sdk`, or `src/auto-reply/command-auth.ts` between it and current main 49563b5) and this branch at 09ef7b5, with identical inputs. Config: `commands.ownerAllowFrom: ["discord:user:100000000000000001"]`, `channels.discord.allowFrom: ["*"]`, `channels.discord.execApprovals.enabled: "auto"`, `groupPolicy: "open"`.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `ROOT=$PWD node --import tsx drive.mts` from the repository root, once on pristine main and once on this branch. The driver builds the provider interaction surface and Client as above, calls `client.handleInteraction(<raw /vc status interaction from user 100000000000000001 in a guild text channel>)`, prints the content of the outgoing interaction response, then prints `approvalCapability.getExecInitiatingSurfaceState`, `delivery.hasConfiguredDmRoute`, and `authorizeActorAction({ senderId: owner, approvalKind: "exec" }).authorized`.
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine main 512cc70)
ownerAllowFrom=["discord:user:100000000000000001"]
/vc status from owner 100000000000000001: PATCH /webhooks/400000000000000001/itok/messages/%40original -> "You are not authorized to use this command."
exec approval surface: {"kind":"disabled"}
exec approval DM route configured: false
owner 100000000000000001 may approve exec: false
# AFTER (this branch 09ef7b5, identical inputs)
ownerAllowFrom=["discord:user:100000000000000001"]
/vc status from owner 100000000000000001: PATCH /webhooks/400000000000000001/itok/messages/%40original -> "No active voice sessions."
exec approval surface: {"kind":"enabled"}
exec approval DM route configured: true
owner 100000000000000001 may approve exec: true
```
Observed result after fix: The configured `discord:user:` owner now gets the real `/vc status` answer instead of the authorization refusal, and Discord native exec approvals become enabled with that owner as an authorized approver. Nothing else in the run changed.
What was not tested: No live Discord bot token or real Discord API. Voice audio capture and an actual approval DM delivery were not exercised, and the full gateway process was not booted.


## Maintainer proof (release lane 2026.10.5)

Added `extensions/discord/src/approval-native.test.ts` › "lets only the current typed Discord owner approve owner-derived exec requests". It drives the shipped `getDiscordApprovalCapability()`, the same capability Gateway approval custody (`src/gateway/approval-channel-custody.ts`) calls through `authorizeActorAction` before it settles a decision. With `commands.ownerAllowFrom: ["discord:user:555555555"]` and `execApprovals.enabled: "auto"`:

- approver DM targets resolve to `[{ to: "555555555" }]` (the owner receives the approval);
- the owner is authorized; an unlisted sender (`666666666`) is rejected;
- on a sibling account with explicit `execApprovals.approvers`, the global owner is rejected (account binding unchanged);
- after the owner list is replaced (`discord:user:888888888`), the former owner is rejected. Authority is evaluated against the current config at decision time; custody additionally refuses a decision prepared under a superseded config (`configCurrent`, unchanged core).

Fail-before/pass-after on current main `01cf74e6469` + this PR (`pnpm test <4 files> --maxWorkers=1`):

- main selector restored: 4 failed / 38 passed — new authority test (`expected [] to deeply equal [{ to: '555555555' }]`), exec-approvals typed owner, `/vc` command typed owner, voice speaker typed owner.
- this PR: 42/42 passed (`approval-native`, `exec-approvals`, `voice/command`, `voice/speaker-context`); shard wall ~99s including worker compile. New test adds no timers or I/O.


### Gateway settlement proof (production-path authority harness)

Uncommitted maintainer harness (core tests may not import bundled plugins, so it is not part of this diff). It loads the shipped `discordPlugin` and `slackPlugin` into the active plugin registry and drives the real `approval.resolve` Gateway handler (`createApprovalHandlers`) with real durable exec approval managers and the real, unmocked `prepareApprovalChannelCustody`. Each decision carries a channel reviewer `{ channel, accountId, senderId }`; the runtime config is read through `context.getRuntimeConfig()` at decision time. Config: `commands.ownerAllowFrom: ["<channel>:user:<owner>"]`, `execApprovals.enabled: "auto"`, plus an `ops` account with explicit `execApprovals.approvers`. Command: `pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/zz-typed-owner-custody.proof.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` on main `01cf74e6469` with both fixes applied, then with both selectors restored to main.

```
# AFTER (main 01cf74e6469 + #172385 + #172424)
[discord] unlisted 666666666: ok=false status=pending
[discord] owner on ops-bound request (ops explicit approvers): ok=false; via default account: ok=false status=pending
[discord] typed owner discord:user:555555555: ok=true status=allowed
[discord] former owner after reassignment to discord:user:666666666: ok=false status=pending
[slack] unlisted U0666NOPE: ok=false status=pending
[slack] owner on ops-bound request (ops explicit approvers): ok=false; via default account: ok=false status=pending
[slack] typed owner slack:user:U0123ABCD: ok=true status=allowed
[slack] former owner after reassignment to slack:user:U0666NOPE: ok=false status=pending
# BEFORE (same harness, owner selectors from main)
[discord] typed owner discord:user:555555555: ok=false status=pending
[slack] typed owner slack:user:U0123ABCD: ok=false status=pending
(negative controls identical: all ok=false, status=pending)
```

The typed owner settles a pending exec approval to `allowed` (the waiter resolves `allow-once`). An unlisted sender, the owner on a request bound to the `ops` account (whether reviewing via `ops` or via `default`), and the former owner after the owner list is reassigned while the approval is pending are all refused before settlement; their records stay `pending`. Voice: `voice/command.test.ts` drives `/vc` through the command handler and asserts the voice manager is invoked for the typed owner (fails on main), and rejects wildcard/foreign owners.


### Voice privileged-effect proof

Added `extensions/discord/src/voice/command.test.ts` › "runs vc leave only for the current typed owner". It drives the shipped `/vc leave` subcommand with the real `createDiscordLivePolicyReader` reading a mutable runtime config (the same live-policy owner the provider wires at boot). With `commands.ownerAllowFrom: ["discord:user:<owner>"]`: an unlisted member is refused and `manager.leave` is never called; the typed owner's `/vc leave` reaches `manager.leave` once; after the owner list is reassigned in config, the former owner is refused on the next interaction and `manager.leave` is not called again. On main's selector the owner case fails (`expected { content: "You are not authorized…" } to match { content: "Left voice." }`).

Branch integration: merged current `origin/main` because this test's import was adjacent to a main-side import removal in the same file (textual conflict). Result on main `cf7311c1048` + this PR: `approval-native`, `exec-approvals`, `voice/command`, `voice/speaker-context` 43/43 passed (`pnpm test <4 files> --maxWorkers=1`, ~121s shard wall including worker compile).

Not run: a live Discord bot/voice session and a real approval DM click; the remaining live-surface proof is limited to the contributor's real-`Client` interaction trace above plus the Gateway custody harness.

prs.title: fix: preserve recall dates and honor worktree configuration
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes recall-repair and worktree-configuration defects, plus runtime and host assumptions in the updater and Docker helper tests found during the Node/Bun census.

## User Impact

Memory repair preserves existing recall dates, and session worktrees honor their supplied configuration. The updater retains its existing Linux-only systemd maintenance behavior; its tests now distinguish Linux from macOS and Windows. The Docker startup-failure test is isolated from unrelated local listeners.

## Why This Change Was Made

| Test | Classification and root cause | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming-repair-recall.test.ts` | Bucket 1: repair appended the UTC date to existing local-date evidence, changing valid history and breaking idempotence. Bucket 2: assertions assumed store-row ordering. | Backfill only missing dates, pin the fixture timezone, and compare complete retained entries without ordering assumptions. |
| `src/gateway/server.chat-worktree-readiness.product.test.ts` | Bucket 1: the per-operation worktree service did not receive the supplied configuration. On APFS, acceleration could bypass the configured early-prompt path. | Pass the operation configuration into the existing service. Reuse an environment binding and remove a redundant promise temporary so this over-cap file does not grow. |
| `src/cli/update-cli.already-current.test.ts` | Bucket 2: the changed-owner case expected the Linux-only systemd policy refresh on every host. | Pin Linux in that case's existing test support. Preserve the production guard introduced by #153636. Extend the existing no-op boundary test with macOS and Windows cases that require no systemd maintenance. |
| `test/scripts/docker-build-helper.test.ts` | Bucket 2: an unrelated listener on port 18789 could satisfy readiness in the intentional startup-failure scenario. | Make that scenario's HTTP probe return false and assert the expected startup-failure diagnostic. |

Production delta: **+6 / −7 (net −1)**. Test delta: **+30 / −13 (net +17)**. Documentation: **+3 / −0**. `session-worktree-preparation.ts` has **zero net line growth** (+3 / −3) from the PR base. No production updater or update-documentation changes remain in the final diff. No new runtime skips, dependencies, or fork workarounds.

## Evidence

The new macOS and Windows no-op cases both fail if the Linux guard is removed: the systemd maintenance boundary is invoked unexpectedly. The retained Linux cases still require refresh for native admission.

Earlier focused proof passed all four census files on Node v26.11.1 and the pinned Bun fork 1.4.3-canary.1+65d94e715: 166 passed, 2 pre-existing Docker skips per runtime. The final memory assertion correction was rerun separately on both runtimes (3/3 each). The existing missing-day backfill regression also passed on both runtimes.

The coordinator revision reruns the changed updater and Gateway paths, plus the expanded no-op boundary test:

```sh
export TMPDIR=/private/tmp/oc-mainreds
export PATH=/private/tmp/oc-bun-fork/bin:$PATH
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test \
  src/cli/update-cli.already-current.test.ts \
  src/cli/update-cli/update-command-noop.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server.chat-worktree-readiness.product.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun pnpm test \
  src/cli/update-cli.already-current.test.ts \
  src/cli/update-cli/update-command-noop.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server.chat-worktree-readiness.product.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

The coordinator revision passes all 24 selected tests on both runtimes: Node 250.53s, Bun 165.19s. Per-file durations (Node / Bun): Gateway 24.49s / 21.10s, updater 184.67s / 121.67s, no-op boundary 6.76s / 12.21s. The existing Gateway test exercises prompt delivery and revoked workspace effects through a real Gateway; the existing Docker suite exercises shell process lifecycle behavior. Neither was expanded with additional slow cases.

Formatting, core and CLI-update test typechecks, and the local max-lines ratchet passed. The focused lint run reports only the inherited 725-line Gateway file (limit 700), unchanged from the base. Independent Codex review of the final staged candidate passed through P2 with no actionable findings.

On head `28147ef1639f4f5a0a5035a10c59c96b423e4bcf`, [checks-fast-baseline-ratchets passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38839582247/job/116776786434). The bounded [CI watch](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38839582247) ended with 64 of 66 jobs complete and no failed jobs; `PostgreSQL conformance` and `checks-node-changed-2` remained running. No CI reruns were requested. The PR remains ready and unmerged.

prs.title: perf(sessions): skip redundant worktree creation target lookup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Parallel worktree session creation performs an unnecessary storage lookup before entering the creation service.

## User Impact

Worktree session creation does less preflight work. Routing, workspace ownership, authorization, and lifecycle behavior remain unchanged. No configuration or schema changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The handler already obtains a validated agent ID from `resolveSessionCreateAgentId`. Its subsequent worktree target lookup reads storage only to recover that same ID. Remove this lookup; the creation service remains responsible for resolving the physical target and checking it under lifecycle custody.

Production delta: 3 added / 12 removed lines (net -9). No cache, parallel fast path, or new owner. Existing tests cover selected agents, parent inheritance, workspace authorization, and rollback.

## Evidence

Measured the real WebSocket `sessions.create` RPC on an isolated Linux sandbox: 30 concurrent creates with `projectId`, `worktree: true`, unique names, display names, and initial messages. One signed synthetic operator, a local synthetic model, and a real synthetic Git project with a local bare origin. Fixture: 5,000 seeded sessions, 6,000 retained runs, and a 4,641,595,392-byte initial agent database (`team-shape-fixture.ts --transcript-mib 1500`). Each revision gets one 30-create warmup and three measured 30-create rounds; every turn must subsequently complete successfully.

| Revision | Measured creates | Create p50 | Create p90 | Successful creates + turns, including warmup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Baseline `49ecf7082730` | 90 | 824 ms | 1,024 ms | 120/120 |
| Patch `55032fc03a78` | 90 | 738 ms | 934 ms | 120/120 |
| Baseline replay | 90 | 791 ms | 954 ms | 120/120 |

The result is directionally favorable, but round-to-round variation is too large to claim a robust total-latency speedup. There is no meaningful regression, and the change removes work and code. Observed target-preparation p50/p90: 24/53 → 7/20 → 18/26 ms.

Measurement limits: the same fixture is reused across the baseline–patch–baseline sequence, starting with 5,030 / 5,150 / 5,270 sessions and adding 120 each time. Thirty failed setup sessions precede every valid comparison: the initial fixture lacked a remote, repaired with a local synthetic bare origin. Those timings are excluded. This small Git repository and synthetic model do not establish large-repository checkout or live-provider performance.

Validation:

- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): no actionable P1/P2 findings. Reviewed agent aliases, fixed/global stores, explicit fleets, reset-in-place, spawn inheritance, and retained lifecycle/authority checks.
- `server.sessions.create.worktree-selection.test.ts`: 6/6 passed locally with one worker.
- `server.sessions.create-worktree-spawn.test.ts`: initial file run had 18 passes and one fixture teardown failure (`expected 1 to be 0`, active Gateway root work). The isolated failing case passed on unchanged baseline and patched head. This is unresolved timing/order evidence, not a claimed test fix.
- Formatting and focused boundary lint passed. Full syntax lint reports only the existing file-length limit; this patch reduces the file by nine lines. The local type-aware preparation was stopped to honor the compute limit.
- [PR CI run 38844846667](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38844846667): all 64 jobs completed successfully on this PR head. Broad validation ran in CI; no Testbox/Crabbox lease was allocated.

prs.title: fix(ui): Recent chats timestamps wrap and misalign in narrow panes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Recent chats timestamps on the welcome / New Session screen wrap onto two lines ("32m / ago") and drift off the shared right edge when the pane is narrow and a row has a long title plus a checkout subtitle.

## User Impact

User impact: every Recent chats timestamp stays on one line, flush right, in every row; long chat titles and checkout subtitles truncate first to make room.

## Why This Change Was Made

The timestamp was an ordinary shrinkable flex item, so its one-line rendering depended only on `white-space: nowrap` surviving the cascade. Once anything allowed that text to wrap, the row squeezed the timestamp to its narrowest word. The timestamp now opts out of shrinking (`flex: none`), right-aligns, and uses tabular numerals, so the name and subtitle are the only parts that give up width.

## Evidence

Before (narrow 320px Recent chats column, inherited text wrapping allowed):

![Before: Recent chats timestamps wrap onto two lines](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bc654c86-6c49-44a6-b22a-a8ec908b877d)

After (same state):

![After: Recent chats timestamps stay on one right-aligned line](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3c6e9cad-2fd4-4037-8741-e7ad84c80e0d)

- New E2E `keeps recent-chat timestamps on one right-aligned line in a narrow column` (`ui/src/e2e/new-session-page.responsive-welcome.e2e.test.ts`): asserts every timestamp is one line, unclipped, and shares one right edge, and that the long title truncates instead. It fails on `main` (`"just now"` renders 37px tall, two lines) and passes with this change; the whole file passes (6/6).
- `oxfmt --check`, `stylelint` on the touched files: clean.

prs.title: refactor(sqlite): remove redundant worker and snapshot checks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

SQLite infrastructure repeats owner checks and file reads without strengthening the final native-effect boundary.

## User Impact

This removes CPU and filesystem work without changing the SQL command sequence, schema, or public API. Native grants still check live database access, accepted writes still settle, and snapshot integrity and physical identity checks remain. A completed checkpoint observation or warning can now be reported during shutdown.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway is the database owner. Check authority when granting native work, trust completed maintenance results, and read a pinned header once. Repeating the same two atomics cannot fence revocation after the final load.

Removed-check ledger (line numbers at base `0169c8acfbff`):

| Site | Redundant check | Accepted edge case |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/infra/sqlite-worker-request-custody.ts:21` | Second slot/request atomic-load pair | Revocation can occur immediately after observation, as it could after the former fourth load; native-effect admission remains. |
| `src/infra/sqlite-worker-operation-admission.ts:483` | Access assertion before domain preparation, repeated inside `grant()` | Preparation can run before revoked access is refused; no native grant is issued. |
| `src/infra/sqlite-wal-write-admission.ts:91` | Post-await preparation before observing an already-completed checkpoint | One completed observation can publish while shutdown starts. |
| `src/infra/sqlite-wal-write-admission.ts:114` | Preparation before reporting a failed maintenance operation | One final warning can publish during shutdown. |
| `src/infra/sqlite-readonly-location.ts:127` | Second synchronous header read and byte comparison | A concurrent journal-mode transition may select a stale strategy for one attempt; native refusal/coherent-copy recovery still handles it. |
| `src/infra/sqlite-readonly-location-cleanup.ts:362` | Reader-set assertion immediately repeated by `prepareSnapshotRetirement()` | No new edge: the same check remains before retirement, with no intervening callback or await. |
| `src/infra/sqlite-page-cache.worker.ts:245,250` | Second `/proc/self/io` sample and progress copy within one warming step | Progress uses the sample already used for its byte-budget decision, taken immediately before that comparison. |

The audit also considered removing the idle-worker checkpoint probe. Existing coverage in `sqlite-wal-checkpoint.test.ts` shows that a row-decoding failure can leave a native reader pinned after JavaScript reader accounting is empty. That probe stays: removing it risks unbounded WAL retention. Broker transport, group commit, schema admission, and agent-database cutover findings remain with their current owners.

## Evidence

- Production LOC: +5 / -29 (net -24). Tests: +0 / -5. Seven files changed.
- T1 inventory in the touched area: **0 → 0**. No SQL call, worker route, or synchronous fallback is added. CI ratchets pending.
- Formatting, scoped type-aware lint, and `git diff --check`: pass. Two independent Codex review rounds: clean through P2 (initial patch and incremental deletions).
- Focused owner coverage is delegated to PR CI: worker request custody, operation admission/timeout, WAL checkpoint/tick, readonly snapshot/copy/cleanup suites, and the Linux page-cache worker suite. Static type/lint/export/Knip/Madge/T1/dialect gates must complete before merge.
- No SDK surface, update, Doctor, schema, plugin-loading, or service-lifecycle change; those extra proof cells do not apply.

Performance evidence is pending three alternating harness-v3 base/candidate pairs. This PR claims no SQL/request reduction and no latency improvement. Fixture state is isolated on the internal disk; the shared harness is unchanged.

| Phase | Base statements / requests / MAIN | Candidate statements / requests / MAIN |
| --- | --- | --- |
| First turn | Pending | Pending |
| Warmed turn, median [min–max] | Pending | Pending |
| Restart boot / connect / first turn | Pending | Pending |

Two test assertions that pinned suppression/exact counts of preparatory callbacks are removed. Existing refusal, custody, retirement, schema-lease, snapshot correctness, and byte-budget assertions remain.

Per-operation work removed: successful custody predicate 4 → 2 atomic loads; journal-mode classification 2 → 1 header reads; one pre-grant access assertion and two post-effect maintenance preparation sites removed; one duplicate reader-set assertion removed; nonterminal page-cache warming steps take one I/O sample instead of two. An uncontended microprobe of the actual custody predicates (three alternating pairs, 2 million successful checks each) used **582.506 ms [570.267–607.592] → 289.334 ms [285.506–294.781] process CPU** (median [min–max], −50.3%). This isolates the predicate and is not a Gateway latency claim.

prs.title: fix(x): failed requests are posted as public X replies
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the bundled X channel publicly posts failure replies (for example "session creation failed: 'X runtime not initialized'... please resend") when an X mention's request could not be completed.

## User Impact

User impact: X now receives only replies the agent declares successful. Failed, untagged, and error replies are withheld from X. With `channels.x.failureRoute` set, OpenClaw sends a notice with the post URL, the author's handle, and a redacted summary to that channel; without a route the reply is dropped and logged. Maintainer mentions that open public work sessions no longer fail with "X runtime not initialized".

**Behavior change:** a reply without `[[x_success]]` is withheld instead of posted. If a model forgets the tag, that answer is withheld too, but it stays visible in the log or the failure route. To send failures to a Discord channel:

```json5
{
  channels: {
    x: {
      failureRoute: { channel: "discord", to: "channel:1456744319972282449" },
    },
  },
}
```

## Why This Change Was Made

The deleted tweets were ordinary model prose, not `isError` payloads, so an error-flag filter alone would not have stopped them. The X channel's delivery rules (`agentPrompt.inboundFormattingHints`) now ask the agent to start every reply to a mention with `[[x_success]]` or `[[x_failure]]`. The monitor's `preparePayload` already decides automatic X delivery, so it now reads and strips the tag and posts only declared successes. It is fail-closed because the public post is the risky effect. I chose a tag over a report-failure tool because it adds no model round trip, works with every harness, and is decided at the single point where the post happens. A failure tag is sticky for the rest of the turn. `isError` finals are withheld and routed. `NO_REPLY` and empty finals are dropped.

`failureRoute` (`{ channel, to, accountId? }`, rejected if it targets `x`) is delivered through core `sendDurableMessageBatch` on a best-effort basis, and the result is logged. The summary is passed through `redactSensitiveText`, capped at 500 characters, and `@` is defused so model text cannot ping the channel. Message-tool sends, which are the manual posts from work sessions, refuse `[[x_failure]]` and strip `[[x_success]]`. Untagged manual posts still go out.

<details>
<summary>Root cause of "X runtime not initialized"</summary>

`createPluginRuntimeStore` (`src/plugin-sdk/runtime-store.ts`) resolves its slot from the **calling** plugin-instance invocation frame (`getPluginInstanceRuntimeSlot`). The loader calls `setXRuntime` inside X's instance, so the runtime exists only in X's instance slot. X gives the host closures for public work-session publication: `childSessionPublication.prepare`/`assertCurrent`, plus the guard returned by `prepare`. These called `getXRuntime()` through `resolveXIngress`, `resolveXSenderTier`, and the monitor's runtime-replacement check. The host runs them from the agent run, at run admission, in `sessions_spawn` (`sessions-spawn-visible.ts`), and in the `sessions.create` claim. When that frame is not X's, either another plugin's or none, the lookup hits an empty slot and throws, so session creation fails. A probe with `PluginInstance("x").run(() => setXRuntime(rt))` reproduces it. `getXRuntime()` returns the runtime inside X's frame. Outside the frame, inside another plugin's frame, and from an X-created closure called outside, it throws "X runtime not initialized". The existing composition e2e passes only because its deterministic model runs inline in the monitor's frame. It is not a second module instance and not a restart window.

Fix: the publication preparation and the ingress guard use the monitor's captured runtime. Host-facing guards rely on the account abort signal, the allowlist snapshot, and the config identity. In-frame monitor checks keep the runtime-replacement check.

</details>

## Evidence

- `pnpm test extensions/x --maxWorkers=1`: 21 files, 242 tests passed. The new `monitor-outcome.test.ts` runs the real monitor delivery adapter. The fixture now follows core's `preparePayload` → null-suppression contract.
  - Negative control: with `monitor.ts`/`ingress.ts`/`guest-policy.ts`/`channel.ts` restored from `origin/main`, the verbatim deleted tweet is posted (`api.reply` called once), a declared failure is posted, and a success is posted with the literal tag. With this change, the failure is withheld and logged `reason=unclassified route=none`, the declared failure is routed to `discord channel:1456744319972282449` with the redacted summary, and the success posts without its tag.
- `pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/channel-run-admission.x-recovery.test.ts`: 8 passed. The new case sets X's runtime inside a real `PluginInstance("x")` and runs the real reply runner, host ingress, and `ChildSessionPublication` outside X's frame. On `origin/main` sources it is rejected because preparation throws; with this change it settles `ok` and the spawn-time `assertCurrent()` passes.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src`, oxlint on the touched files, `oxfmt --check`, `pnpm config:channels:gen`, and `git diff --check` are clean. `autoreview` (local, P1) reported no actionable findings.
- Gaps: I did not post anything live to X or Discord. The dedicated `x-publication-owner-composition.e2e.test.ts` tier is outside default CI and refused to prepare on this Team host because a managed Gateway runs there. I updated its expectations so denied work-session replies are withheld, but I have not run it.

Requested by @Patrick-Erichsen and @joshavant.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @Patrick-Erichsen](https://discord.com/channels/1456350064065904867/1456744319972282449/1560479414075260949)
- [Original discussion with @joshavant](https://discord.com/channels/1456350064065904867/1456744319972282449/1560479458652196985)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/445b87e6-ded5-4524-b809-f04fa2383980)

prs.title: refactor(channels): consolidate shared plumbing owners
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repeated channel plumbing creates competing owners for the same lifecycle work and duplicated maintenance.

## User Impact

This is an internal cleanup with no new configuration or setup steps. Security policy, transport contracts and ordinary shutdown settlement remain intact. Failed preview deletion is explicitly best effort and may leave a stale preview; Slack route-conflict diagnostics now come from the core route owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

Slack stores HTTP routes twice; several channels rebuild receipts, queues and credential status; progress and status paths repeatedly copy trusted values; Doctor importers query their own committed writes again before archiving.

Reuse the existing core HTTP route owner for Slack's running account and remove the static forwarding registry and facades. Keep signature verification, exact request paths, bounded bodies, first-account ownership and account cleanup. Reuse existing secret inspection, keyed queues and receipt bridges while leaving transport policy, ClickClack media receipts and unknown-send reconciliation local.

Trust committed Doctor insertion receipts, typed status rows and immutable handed-off progress/disconnect facts. Keep external validation, refusal/source retention, revocations, archive-after-commit, Matrix SDK-facing snapshots and normal shutdown settlement. Synology GET/POST now share one bounded native request lifecycle, retaining their distinct response acceptance and retry policies. SMS validates the exact loaded media bytes before persistence instead of publishing, rereading and compensating.

Production delta: **462 added / 968 removed: 506 net production lines removed**. Tests, fixtures, generated files, docs and baseline-only shrink are excluded. The separate cache/webhook helper proposal is not in this PR: it exceeds the unchanged SDK surface budget. A2A's explicit receipt adapter stays because the generic bridge would imply unsupported reply/thread placement. A2A and Discord retain their status projections because their provider-specific fields are not part of the shared snapshot type.

Test delta: **412 added / 579 removed: 167 net test lines removed**, primarily retired Slack registry/wrapper suites and tests of the explicitly removed best-effort machinery. Native route-owner and signed-receiver coverage remains; path normalization moved intact, and migration refusal/source-retention coverage was expanded. Synology's client is imported once during collection instead of repeatedly assigning cached exports in hooks; the new lookup regression preserves its transport warning. Baseline changes are exact shrink-only maintenance.

## Coverage log

At the initial base (`4d50e81f6c9`), the corrected census covers 28 channel manifests and 3,277 production files, with decisions for all 264 repeated-name families and 42 cross-file structural groups found during inventory. Every exact repeated-name member pointer and structural-group identity has a recorded decision. The local campaign ledger records member files, provenance, measured family/member deltas, rejected pilots, and retained contracts. Remaining allowlist, account, media, formatting, pairing, retry and status differences retain their channel-specific security and transport policies. Generic credential and recursive streaming pilots were rejected after implementation because they grew code or changed behavior. Configuration/schema changes and additional SDK exports are not part of this PR.

<details>
<summary>Family coverage and retained boundaries</summary>

| Family | Consolidation or retained contract |
| --- | --- |
| Webhook HTTP ownership | Slack uses the core route owner; exact paths, signature verification, body bounds, first ownership, and cleanup remain channel-owned. |
| Accounts and credentials | Discord/Slack reuse secret inspection; WhatsApp shares directory enumeration. Account defaults, credential precedence, unavailable SecretRef authority, and inheritance remain intact. |
| Access policy | Matrix reuses the existing allowlist matcher; DM/group defaults, mention policy, sender grammar, and authorization boundaries remain channel-owned. |
| Hosted media | SMS validates loaded bytes before persistence; Zalo uses canonical metadata expiry. SSRF, MIME/size checks, tokens, quotas, consumption, and physical retention remain intact. |
| Text and Markdown | Existing chunking owners retained. Transport length/encoding differences and code-delimiter semantics ruled out speculative generic renderers. |
| Receipts and outbound adapters | LINE/Teams reuse accepted receipts; ClickClack's text bridge shares the existing adapter while keeping its media and unknown-send behavior local. A2A's specialized adapter stays. |
| Typing, reactions, and previews | Reuse existing queue/effect owners; remove preview-delete retry custody and redundant trusted-value copying. Holds, admitted-send settlement, and final-message safety remain. |
| Retry and rate limiting | Keyed tails share the existing queue. Provider retry/resource policies and Synology's distinct failure-only limiter stay unchanged. |
| Pairing and setup | Mattermost reuses its account configured predicate; Synology reuses its raw-account accessor. Prompt/account policy and third-party setup compatibility stay. |
| Status and probes | Base/probe summaries share one lightweight owner; typed WhatsApp/Zalo/ZaloUser rows avoid repeat projection. A2A/Discord provider-field projections and real provider probes stay. |
| Doctor and migration | Importers trust committed insertion receipts, retaining refused-write/source preservation, conflicts, revocation, offline custody, and commit-before-archive. |
| Config/schema fragments | Inventoried but unchanged; structural schema/config changes and SDK-budget expansion are outside this cleanup. |

</details>

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Failed preview DELETE is attempted once and warned; a stale preview may remain. Cleanup-retry custody originated in synthetic failure/interleaving work in #104865 and #155641, not a cited human actual-use incident. Accepted finals are never resent or revoked.
- WhatsApp, Zalo and ZaloUser consume their already-typed status rows without another defensive field projection. A2A and Discord keep their existing projections for provider-specific fields; no public status type is widened.
- A caller mutating an immutable progress fact after handoff is unsupported rather than defended by repeated deep copies. #152517's retained-card behavior stays; only its synthetic post-handoff mutation fixture lines are retired.
- Offline Doctor trusts the state owner's committed true insertion receipt. A refused insertion retains the source and warns rather than rereading a competing insert to see if it coincidentally matches. #109380 supplied generic migration hardening and synthetic proof, not a human report requiring that redundant readback; exclusive offline custody, commits, conflicts, revocation and archival remain.
- Legacy Matrix sync-cache migration uses its first validated file snapshot instead of chasing a replacement between two reads. #163740 introduced the duplicate read without a cited actual-use report; another legitimate writer is excluded during this migration. Commit-before-archive stays.
- Matrix's persistence-only clone immediately before synchronous serialization is removed; SDK-facing input/output snapshots remain because the real SDK shares and mutates nested events. #156777's extra serialization-adjacent clone adds no ownership boundary.
- Draft-loop promise identity revalidation is removed because the owner admits only one in-flight send. #82713's real error containment remains; no production caller can replace a live promise through this API.
- A resolved progress-start promise stays until reset rather than being retired immediately. Failed-start retry, joining startup and cancellation from #88749 stay unchanged; retention is one void promise per existing gate.
- The queue's second activity check covered only synchronous reentrant deactivation from its status callback, not waiting behind older work. The first queued check, lifecycle signal, effect authorization and finally settlement stay. Introducing refactor `364c67bcb5b` cites no human actual-use incident; such an unsupported callback may let its already-admitted task begin.
- Hosted media's private close helper from #119941 has exactly one finally/early-exit owner, so its double-close flag is redundant. Its synthetic read/delete-race provenance does not establish a second close caller. Reader accounting, revocation, physical grace and retention remain unchanged.
- Synology's request/error/end callbacks use native Promise single-settlement rather than duplicate `settled` flags from `eeb5f12293c` and #110520. A late callback cannot change the outcome; absolute deadlines, bounded bodies, response draining, and acceptance distinctions remain. This delegates the safeguard rather than accepting an unbounded or double-completion path.
- Zalo trusts the existing metadata/expiry owner and the process clock rather than synthetic invalid-`Date.now()` protection from `08ae0e6d299`. Eager expiration cleanup and physical retention stay unchanged.
- Slack has no placeholder route before an HTTP receiver starts or after it stops, just the same normal Gateway fallback formerly reached through its empty inner registry. Duplicate diagnostics now come from the core owner and the troubleshooting guide follows that cutover.

## Evidence

Retained core/SDK proof passed 174 tests in 20 files for unchanged contracts; the public status-helper cases (14 tests) and lint-suppression guard (3 tests) also passed. These selections overlap and are not summed. Madge and runtime-value cycle checks each passed with zero cycles. The unchanged SDK surface/export gates passed: 155 public entrypoints, 3,761 exports, 2,196 callables. Independent whole-candidate and Synology delta reviews found no actionable findings through P2.

Synology's added lookup regression failed for the intended warning-suffix difference before the repair. The repaired full client/suppression selection passed 29 tests across two shards (613.65s). The fixture imports its subject once during collection rather than repeatedly assigning the same cached exports in timed hooks; no deadline or assertion changed. Targeted messaging, plugin-SDK and plugins/platform test-type graphs passed. Extension production types exposed a missing explicit return in Slack's exact-path callback; returning the existing handler promise preserves its undefined result and rejection propagation. Extension production types passed after that repair (71.2s), and extension-test types passed (80.1s). The exact one-line Slack patch received an independent scoped-clean P2 review (0.99 confidence), with complete-file and binary-patch identity verified against the task branch. Its fresh suppression guard passed three tests; the two-file signed-ingress/lifecycle rerun was interrupted by host/session termination after worker preparation, without a final Slack result. The prior six-file Slack selection passed 27 tests, including signed loopback ingress, exact-path aliases, first-owner/duplicate cleanup, bounded bodies, and socket/relay startup. No final-head local Slack pass is claimed; exact-head CI remains required.

The broad committed-ref SDK renderer was stopped after 3h33m without a report; this is incomplete proof, not an API pass. The unchanged export/surface gates and focused contract checks passed; the dedicated exact-head hosted API-diff check remains required before merge.

The public ClawHub consumer query for `sdk-export:openclaw/plugin-sdk/channel-outbound#createFinalizableDraftLifecycle` returned HTTP 404 (2026-10-16 UTC). External usage impact is unknown, not zero. Its signatures and accepted-final safety are preserved; the explicitly accepted retry-to-best-effort preview cleanup change is documented above and in the SDK guide.

The first full build exposed four owned type errors in the proposed A2A/Discord status projection removal. Both whole proposals were dropped, restoring those production/test files exactly to the base. The repaired full build passed at `81a273664a1a9442894897082989fe64347c79d5`, including unified declarations, all public SDK exports, plugin distributions, runtime postbuild, and UI guards (2h23m12s on the saturated local host). Core production types and graph-boundary checks also passed. This was an isolated private-QA build, not release/publication validation; no allowance was changed. Slack's isolated cold-import profile is qualified with no gaps (100.08 MiB max RSS); no comparable performance baseline or improvement claim.

The 61-file extension selection finished with 643 passing and 12 failing tests (59 passing files, two failing files; 8,783.29s). All failures are existing WhatsApp callback-polling assertions expecting one dispatch but seeing zero at their 5,000ms deadline, in socket lifecycle and duplicate durable-delivery tests. The changed delivery code only extracts the identical verbose logger. Investigation found the harness's existing event-driven final-state drain, but a blanket substitution would be invalid for intentionally held read-receipt work. No timeout, retry, skip, assertion, or delivery policy was weakened. These failures remain unresolved local fixture/load uncertainty, not proven inherited CI failures; exact-head CI must still pass or receive independent causal attribution.

An earlier local Gateway ownership test stage hit the existing 900-second no-output limit during cold worker preparation, before any assertions; the wrapper exited 143. Ordinary-wrapper follow-through after build passed all four selected files: Gateway ownership (8 tests, 467.45s), HTTP registry (37 tests, 132.95s), and Discord voice E2Es (31 tests, two files, 616.55s). The complete wrapper passed three shards in 1,796.86s and verified its compiled generation normally. No timeout/retry/skip was changed. Exact-head hosted CI is still required.

Targeted core lint passed all 15 changed files. Extension lint could not start: its native SDK package-boundary declaration prerequisite hit the existing 300,000ms managed-command deadline. This remains incomplete infrastructure proof, not a lint pass, product defect, or inherited-CI attribution. No prerequisite bypass or deadline increase was used; exact-head hosted extension lint/types must cover it.

No Telegram live harness, operator Gateway/state, dependency, config/schema/protocol or SDK budget changes. No live-provider claim.

prs.title: refactor(ui): own chat CI disclosure state with Solid
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The chat CI monitor and automation controls still use controller inheritance, manual property-diff maps, and render-revision counters after their Solid migration.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible change. CI details still refresh only while visible, preserve manual job expansion, respect rate-limit delays, and retire work when the session or connection changes. Automation keeps independent toggles, reconciles uncertain acknowledgements, and leaves durable settings with the Gateway/Cron owners.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace both controllers and their shared base class with component-owned factories, Solid stores, and scoped effects/subscriptions. Remove the manual property diff and revision publication paths. Keep synchronous request tokens and write admission separate from deferred presentation writes so stale requests and same-turn duplicate actions remain fenced.

This is an internal behavior-preserving refactor: rendered JSX, host tags, selectors, CSS, and lazy import boundaries are unchanged. No startup module was touched; local UI builds and visual capture were omitted under the campaign's lighter proof rule. Startup bytes were not remeasured.

prs.title: perf(state): reuse committed receipts and current plugin contracts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Background image mutations reread the image metadata and preference immediately after committing them. Workboard similarly reloads a complete card before dependency promotion after link/reclaim writes have already returned that card. Return or reuse the owner's committed values instead.

Beam and MSTeams use the current host's V2 keyed-store contract directly, removing runtime probes for atomic methods and tests for unsupported older hosts. Their CAS retries and publisher authorization remain.

## Removed checks and accepted edges

| Removed work | Accepted edge / retained boundary |
| --- | --- |
| Background post-write metadata and preference reads | The response describes this mutation's state; a later edit is visible on the next read. Profile ownership, expected-value conflict checks, quotas and commit authority remain. |
| Workboard post-link card reload | An unsupported independent writer can produce a visible CAS conflict instead of being incorporated by the reload. Parent-state checks and final CAS remain. |
| Workboard post-reclaim card reload | Same boundary; promotion uses the committed claim-free card. Initial reads at claim/start/dispatch entry points remain. |
| Beam atomic-method capability probe | Bundled plugins require the current host; older-host method absence is unsupported. Publisher authorization and CAS remain. |
| MSTeams atomic-method capability probe | Bundled plugins require the current host; older-host method absence is unsupported. CAS preserves concurrent learnings. |

No schema, retention, SDK surface, or worker-routing changes. Image payloads stay out of metadata reads.

## SQL and main-thread impact

Pending measured results. Source-derived savings are two SELECTs per background mutation and thirteen SELECTs plus one worker request per Workboard link/reclaim. These are operation savings, not warmed-turn savings. The touched owners have zero T1 calls before and after.

The shared harness v3 comparison covers three alternating base/candidate pairs, including first turn, warmed turns and restart. No latency claim is made from a loaded host.

## Evidence

Both Codex review rounds completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings. Changed-file formatting, core type-aware lint, plugin lint and `git diff --check` passed. The initial default lint wrapper timed out generating unrelated SDK declarations; the source-backed core configuration passed.

Focused owner tests and the six shared-harness runs are pending local proof capacity. Required static and broad test evidence will come from this PR's CI. Measurements will be added before merge. No update/Doctor/migration/plugin-loading/service-lifecycle or SDK surface changed, so the update cell and SDK API diff do not apply.

LOC against the base: production +25/−16 (net +9), tests/support +69/−70 (net −1), docs +4. The production growth is the explicit background receipt replacing a database read; the plugin changes reduce code.

## Audit finding retained

The plugin journal's existence-before-write probe cannot be replaced with a simple insert-if-absent without changing supported shared cursor/journal namespace retention behavior. At capacity one, insertion order can determine whether the journal entry or cursor survives. That path is unchanged.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI repeats parsing, copying, and forwarding work after its owners have already established the facts.

## User Impact

No intended rendering, text, feature, configuration, or protocol changes. Lit and Solid keep their existing implementations. Rare overlapping catalog edits now settle best effort until refresh or reconnect.

## Why This Change Was Made

Maintainer-requested wave-6 cleanup: consume canonical environment/node/identity types, reuse parsed session events, copy config trees at their mutation boundary, share immutable recovery/library facts, and consolidate markdown navigation and settings-select rendering onto existing owners. Internal forwarding modules are removed with callers migrated; boot/offline entry facades remain. External/plugin validation, authorization, durable recovery, connection identity, and ordinary concurrent-session behavior remain.

Net production reduction: **546 lines** across the complete diff (+595/-1141), including the supporting CI-owner inventory path migration; **549 lines** within `ui/src` (+581/-1130). Counts exclude tests, fixtures, support, generated files, declarations and baseline metadata. The complete local coverage ledger is `.local/z01-ledger.md`: 4,724 original unique references, 4,724 classified, zero missing, plus inherited-main decisions. This is the campaign's permitted 500–999-line packet.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- A same-connection catalog read can finish after a rename or invalidation and briefly replace presentation state; the next refresh/reconnect repairs it. Removed publication/successor choreography came from #170074's synthetic delayed-response reproduction, not a cited human production incident. Connection identity and the effect-boundary check before legacy group import remain.
- An already-unsubscribed callback from the same source, reattached before delivery, can cause a redundant current-source invalidation. #102745 / #102423 were a maintainer modernization proposal, not a human incident report for this interleaving. Source identity, connection status, unsubscribe, and frame cancellation remain.
- Internal immutable config, library, placement and composer facts now share references; a caller mutating them outside the existing replacement/copy-on-write owners could affect another reader. No such production mutator was found. Library clones originated in #168758 and placement clones in #152370; those contracts concern retained drafts/recovery, not independent mutable ownership. Actual edit boundaries and externally mutable plugin snapshots still copy.
- Internal typed numbers/arrays/strings and producer-owned discovery/node/identity facts are no longer revalidated at each consumer. Impossible malformed internal values may now fail visibly instead of being silently discarded; the external producer/network/storage/plugin boundaries remain. No version-skew compatibility contract is introduced or removed.
- Outbox recovery no longer repeats normalized reads/comparisons of writes the storage owner has just verified. Persisted-byte verification, including no-op/quota failures, remains at `writeStoredOutboxStore`; no durability tradeoff is accepted here. A later writer cannot be prevented by another immediate read of the same write.
- Tool inputs already transported as JSON no longer fall back for BigInt/cyclic/non-JSON objects. Such impossible internal input now throws instead of rendering a fabricated object label; valid JSON/string output remains unchanged.
- A private virtualizer row-key array is no longer frozen; no consumer mutates it. Shared borrowed-fact freezes remain.

prs.title: feat(agents): open agent databases through the selected engine
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agent-shaped databases always opened native SQLite, even when boot selected PostgreSQL. This includes explicit agent/session directories and shared-main auth profiles.

## User Impact

Operators selecting PostgreSQL can create and use fresh agent and session stores through the existing workers. PostgreSQL transcript search reports that the capability is unavailable until its search backend ships.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing agent database owner and actor worker transport now consume the immutable engine selection for open, admission, reads, identity, and close. Generic reader workers receive that same set-once selection through their existing task context, including workers prewarmed before boot selection. PostgreSQL uses the generated agent DDL with exact-drift admission and a bootstrap-only migration path at schema version 27. The pending-preparation promise still gates first-chat discovery and sessions.create; the existing recoverable cancellation and multi-candidate edges are unchanged.

Agent appends use plain event_json on PostgreSQL and skip unavailable FTS indexing. Search callers consume P3-5a's admitted capabilities and throw DatabaseSearchCapabilityUnavailableError (DATABASE_SEARCH_CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE), including missing-index memory searches. P3-5a search implementations and SQL are unchanged. This adds no second executor, compatibility reader, main-thread application SQL, schema-version change, port provider, or backup provider.

## Evidence

Rebased onto 56c315156f4542f197a2b7f727681ba3f41c21b5, including P3-5a and the firstbirth pending-preparation contract. Final conflict resolution only combines wrapper entries and preserves the new transcript-index expression parameter type with EngineConnection; it changes no runtime or SQL logic.

- PostgreSQL 17: all six owner cases pass through the canonical conformance wrapper: default/explicit open and retained identity/close; cold explicit-owner discovery; plain-JSON append/hydration and real-worker FIFO; auth reads and cold shared-main bootstrap; wrong-owner rejection; exact drift rejection.
- FIFO: interleaved enqueues with sequences [1, 2, 3], close/reopen, and reversed timestamps drain as z-first → a-second → m-third through the real agent worker, then leave an empty outbox.
- SQLite: pinned 56c315 and final candidate execute 145 raw byte-identical statements (73,144 bytes), including clean close; SHA-256: 5c1cea18092d804a63485ff7f810327b084feaf514d1d269a612d22feb85c845. An initial autonomous-checkpoint ordering difference is preserved in the evidence; a replay with the unchanged harness matched without filtering. The earlier cedc5aeb comparison also matched all 146 statements (73,178 bytes). P3-5a adds no statements to these flows.
- Native: new ordinary/retained prewarmed-worker selection tests and the missing-PG-memory-index refusal test pass. Full owner suite: 282 passed, one skipped, one inherited ownership-race failure; attribution below. After the final type-only base integration, the three focused worker/index/FTS owner suites pass all 24 cases.
- Static: formatting, Madge (zero cycles), Kysely, PostgreSQL generation (19 tests plus artifact verification), wrapper inventory/closure, and ratchets pass. Worker SQL remains 222 → 222; compatibility calls 12 → 12. Wrapper inventory is 2,516 files; dynamic closures 160 / 204 / 747; zero missing/stale paths. Knip files/dependencies pass cleanly.
- Independent Codex delta review completed: one P2 finding, an empty-session search predicate, verified byte-identical to pinned main and excluded from this caller-only cutover. No introduced P0–P2 finding; inherited search fix remains with its owner.
- Full build and typed lint pass. Formatting passes all 317 applicable changed files; the transport fixture type correction also passes both real-worker cases.
- Typecheck: all 38 execution graphs pass (35 canonical CI graphs), including final extension, infra, extension-test, and root-partition refreshes. After the final base integration, core, infra, and agent-session graphs also pass.
- The earlier CI auth-profile-removal failure is inherited: the exact case fails on both the candidate and an independently built, clean cedc5aeb baseline. Both show successful logout, metadata-cache retirement, and an unpublished reply-dispatch owner instead of bounded missing-login recovery (1 failed / 1 skipped on each). This is outside the database cutover; the existing runtime path is unchanged.

The native ownership-race case observed both independent schema openers succeeding where one must refuse the other owner. Its exact candidate replay passed (1 passed, 57 skipped), as did the ordinary pinned-main replay. A deterministic two-child barrier against pinned main then reproduced both successful owners through the real `ensureOpenClawAgentDatabaseSchema` API, establishing that the defect predates R4: both openers capture empty-store/owner facts before the final transaction. R4 preserves that schema algorithm. The original failure remains recorded as a pre-existing race; the passing replay does not erase it. This cutover does not repair that separate concurrency defect.

The first final-head CI run exposed two unintended public SDK exports used only by bundled memory-core. They now live on the existing private memory host facade, preserving the same singleton and error-class identity. The public SDK surface is unchanged at 3,772 exports / 2,197 callables. The repair passes focused SDK and missing-PG-index tests, typed lint, extension typecheck, wrapper closure checks, and a separate narrow Codex review with no actionable findings.

## Scope and Size

Against the pinned base: 318 files, +1,111 net production lines, +1,039 net test lines, and +6 other lines (+2,156 total). Production growth includes the complete selected-engine owner cutover, generic worker selection transport, and P3-5a caller integration; fixture widening accounts for much of the file count.

This is one complete cutover: engine ownership must agree across the existing actor, read, identity, auth, and close paths. Most existing-file edits widen DatabaseSync handles to EngineConnection; the native-only path is replaced. The fixture follow-up makes existing SQLite-only tests explicit without changing their SQL or expected behavior.

The final rebase resolution in `src/config/sessions/session-transcript-index.ts` preserves `Expression<string>` in the two existing selector parameter types and combines type imports; it adds no runtime or SQL change beyond the already-reviewed R4 delta.

The following live-lane production changes are type-only handle/parameter widening plus type-import changes, with no runtime or SQL change:

- src/infra/session-cost-usage-worker.ts
- src/infra/session-cost-usage-cache.kernel.ts
- src/infra/session-cost-usage-partitions.worker.ts

The final base integration also uses the existing native-handle helper for three arguments in `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-schema-probes.test.ts`; this only satisfies the new native-only fixture parameter type.

The coordinator-cleared fixture addition in src/infra/sqlite-database-admission.retention.test.ts adds mutationRevision: 0 to its existing mock. The following released test files contain approved native-handle guards for their existing counters/migration fixtures:

- src/cron/delivery-preview.current-origin.test.ts

## Integration Blocker

R6's PostgreSQL search implementation landed as #173625 after the validated R4 base. The attempted integration onto `18044d5bb00baa7a4cbc12236095a5524b98ee27` exposes a caller-contract overlap that exceeds this order's search-file and no-agent-schema-change boundaries. Current-main adapters, search implementations, contracts, and PostgreSQL search DDL must remain unchanged.

Required follow-up is concrete:

- Retire R4's obsolete 31-line `src/infra/database-engine/search-capabilities.ts` addition, whose global PostgreSQL-null table conflicts with R6's installed capabilities. This path is explicitly reserved for the search owner.
- Remove path-only, empty-schema `admitStoreSearch` probes from the session search gates and memory guard. R6 binds an admitted worker connection and the store's matching search schema.
- PG transcript search needs an active-text projection and `agentEngineSchema.search`, causing derived PostgreSQL DDL, plus query/identity adaptations. R4's append/delete no-ops and SQLite allocation semantics cannot simply be enabled against R6.

No R6 implementation change is proposed. The published R4 head stays `421c3bae09b8534a8c9d997025e00f6179cb0da5`; the integration requires coordinator sequencing before another push. No merge has been performed.

prs.title: fix(agents,gateway): page terminal reads with a cumulative output cursor
prs.body:
Closes #173169

Related: #125312

## What Problem This Solves

An agent watching a long-running command had to re-read the terminal's whole scrollback on every poll. `terminal({ action: "read" })` now returns a bounded page of output with cursors, and passing the returned `cursor` back reads only what arrived since.

- Problem: `read` returned the entire retained buffer (up to 256K UTF-16 code units) on every call. With no cursor, offset, or page-size parameter, a long session re-paid the full scrollback in tokens on each poll to find what had just happened (#173169). #125312 asks for the same cursor-paged contract.
- Solution: The terminal output ring counts every accepted write, so offsets are cumulative UTF-16 units that stay valid after eviction, and it serves a page from a cursor. `read` accepts optional `cursor`/`maxChars` and returns `startCursor`/`cursor`/`endCursor` with `truncated`/`hasMore`.
- What changed: the output ring (cumulative counter, page read), `session-limits.ts` (page bounds), `session-manager.ts` (`readAgentPage` behind the existing owner check), `terminal-tool.ts` (parameters, result fields, description), the operator-terminal protocol doc, and the ring/tool tests.
- What did NOT change: conversation scoping, the 256K retained buffer, `terminal.attach` replay, terminal writes and approvals. A cursorless read now returns the newest 32K code units instead of everything, and `startCursor` is an absolute offset in the stream rather than proof that older output survives — paging back works only while that output is retained, and a stale cursor comes back `truncated` with the evicted text unrecoverable.

## Why This Change Was Made

Cursors must survive eviction to be useful, and eviction is the normal state of a busy terminal. Counting writes makes each offset meaningful for the session's lifetime, while an index into retained text would silently re-point after every eviction.

- Best fix: keep the terminal manager as the owner of buffered output and add paging to it, rather than streaming events or adding a second buffer.
- Alternative: scoping buffers per conversation (the issue's second complaint) was rejected as unnecessary — ownership already requires the exact `agentSessionKey`/`agentSessionId`/`agentId`, so a new conversation cannot read a previous one's terminal.
- Risk / non-goals: pages are rendered per page, so a page that starts mid-ANSI-escape or splits a carriage-return overwrite line renders approximately — the renderer's documented approximation for evicted output.

## User Impact

Tailing a long-running command now costs a bounded amount of tokens per poll, and a read after a cursor returns only the new output. Cursorless callers get the cursors that let them follow forward or page back.

## Evidence

Real behavior trace: an operator-opened PTY (real `/bin/bash` via node-pty, default 256K ring) driven by the shipped `TerminalSessionManager` and the real agent tool handler, read with `terminal({ action: "read" })`. Numbers are the result fields the model receives:

```text
1 initial page (cursorless)  len=   518 startCursor=0     cursor=557   endCursor=557   truncated=false hasMore=false
2 read(cursor=1.cursor)      len=    25 startCursor=557   cursor=584   endCursor=584   truncated=false hasMore=false
   2.text="printf 'alpha\n'\nalpha\n> "
3 poll unchanged             len=     0 startCursor=584   cursor=584   endCursor=584   truncated=false hasMore=false
4 maxChars=64                len=    61 startCursor=584   cursor=648   endCursor=982   truncated=false hasMore=true
   4.text="for i in $(seq 1 40); do echo line-$i; done\nline-1\nline-2\nlin"
5 next page maxChars=4096    len=   296 startCursor=648   cursor=982   endCursor=982   truncated=false hasMore=false
6 cursorless default cap     len= 32768 startCursor=8255  cursor=41023 endCursor=41023 truncated=false hasMore=false
7 read(evicted cursor)       len= 32768 startCursor=101475 cursor=134243 endCursor=361065 truncated=true hasMore=true
   7.keepsAlpha=false
```

Follow-up reads return only new output, an unchanged poll returns empty text with an unchanged cursor, `maxChars` bounds a page (61 rendered units here because the 64-unit raw page held carriage returns), and the cursorless default stops at 32768 raw units. Step 7 is the P3 case: after ~361K units, cursor 557 returns `truncated=true` with `startCursor=101475 > 0` and the old text gone, so the tool description and protocol doc now call `startCursor` an absolute offset and tie availability to the retained window.

The same contract through the tool (real manager and real tool handler) is pinned by tests that fail on unmodified main:

```text
pnpm test src/gateway/terminal --maxWorkers=1              -> 8 files | 114 tests
vitest output-ring.test.ts                                 -> 7 passed (7 failed before the change)
vitest terminal-tool.read-paging.test.ts                   -> 6 passed (6 failed before the change)
oxfmt --check / oxlint / git diff --check                  -> clean
```

What was not tested: no live operator UI session (the unit tests use a fake PTY and the trace above spawns a real PTY in-process), no upgrade from stable with settings intact, and no Telegram lane here, so the changed default and cross-transport behavior are unverified beyond this checkout. The subprocess-worker harness cannot build here (unrelated `Symbol.dispose` failure) and the leaf typecheck reports only pre-existing errors outside the changed files; `terminal-tool.test.ts` passes 21/22, the sandbox failure reproducing identically on unmodified main.

## AI Assistance 🤖

This PR is AI-assisted. Used `grep`, `git diff` and `pnpm test` to confirm the read contract in `terminal-tool.ts`, the retention bounds in `session-limits.ts` and the owner check in `session-manager.ts`, then implemented cursor paging in the output ring. The implementer understands the code: offsets count raw UTF-16 units of every accepted write, pages are served only through the existing agent-owner check, and page bounds never split a surrogate pair. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

prs.title: fix(cli): keep source commands on Node instead of switching to Bun
prs.body:
Closes #173365

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: source CLI commands unexpectedly run on an automatically downloaded Bun fork, with a different SQLite build, even though the package launcher and build use Node.

## User Impact

`pnpm openclaw` and `pnpm dev` keep the launcher's Node executable and no longer stage Bun or interpret `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME`. Local tests still default to the pinned Bun fork.

This intentionally changes the CLI portion of #172625. Users relying on its test setting to select the application runtime should build, then explicitly run `bun --no-install openclaw.mjs ...`. Managed-service and desktop runtime selection, the Bun pin, database schemas, and dependencies are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The source launcher reused the Vitest runtime selector, coupling ordinary application execution to test preferences, cache availability, and CI detection. Retain the existing Node child-launch path instead, including build ordering, diagnostics, environment, and signal cleanup. Update source/install/testing guidance and the existing launcher fixtures together.

The linked issue records verified Node 26.12.0 / SQLite 3.54.0 versus pinned Bun 1.4.3 / SQLite 3.53.4. The reported Unicode incompatibility was not independently reproduced; this PR does not assert or attempt to fix a Unicode root cause or make the engines semantically identical.

## Evidence

- **Real launcher boundary:** an isolated synthetic CLI printing runtime metadata ran on Bun/SQLite 3.53.4 before the fix and Node/SQLite 3.54.0 afterward. Unset, `bun`, and invalid test-runtime settings all retain Node; no Bun cache is created, even with a nonexistent Bun override. The synthetic CLI never contacts a Gateway or real database.
- **Explicit Bun unchanged:** `bun --no-install openclaw.mjs` still runs the synthetic CLI on Bun/SQLite 3.53.4.
- **Regression baseline:** the new launcher contract fails before the production change for unset/Bun settings (wrong executable) and invalid settings (test-selector exception); the explicit Node case already passes.
- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test src/infra/run-node.test.ts test/scripts/run-node-cancellation.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **44 passed**, 76.47 seconds wrapper wall time. The changed launcher file has 41 passing cases, 20.85 seconds Vitest duration; the existing real lifecycle file has 3 passing cases, 44.38 seconds duration.
- The unchanged runtime/cache owner suites also passed: **29 tests** in `test-runtime.test.ts` and `pinned-bun.test.ts`, preserving local Bun defaults and explicit/CI behavior. Total focused proof: **73 passing tests** across the commands.
- Targeted script/core lint, changed-file formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Documentation audit: **15,534 internal links checked, zero broken**.
- Independent Codex autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 issues in the implementation. A subsequent mechanical cancellation-fixture executable expectation correction is covered by the final passing launcher tests.

Validation caveat: an earlier cold run of the unchanged SIGINT cancellation case hit its 120-second timeout while subprocess preparation took 91 seconds. The isolated replay passed, but that does not establish a repair for the original timing failure. No timeouts, assertions, retries, or skips were weakened. An initial borrowed dependency layout was replaced with an independently owned frozen-lockfile install before final validation.

Targeted `tsgo` typechecking passed with no diagnostics, using a program extending `tsconfig.scripts.json` and rooted at the changed launcher, launcher test, and shared fixture plus repository declarations. Full script/core typechecks and the wider suite are left to PR CI; CI timings are not yet available. No full local suite was run.
