prs.title: fix(matrix): read fails with a bare homeserver error when before/after is an event id
prs.body:
Closes #173252

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Matrix `message read` fails with a bare homeserver error when `before`/`after` is given an event id, which is what the CLI help suggests.

## User Impact

User impact: Matrix agents and CLI users are told that `before`/`after` take the `nextBatch`/`prevBatch` token from a previous read, and a rejected cursor now says what to pass instead. Passing `before` and `after` together fails with a clear error instead of reading forward from the `before` token. Other channels are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Matrix forwards `before`/`after` verbatim as the homeserver `from` pagination token, but the CLI help described them as ids, the message tool schema had no description for them, and the homeserver error carried no next step.

- Matrix-owned guidance: when Matrix exposes `read`, its message-tool discovery describes the shared `before`/`after` fields as a pagination token from a previous read. Only Matrix sessions see this text; the shared core schema is not modified. The contribution lists no actions, so cross-channel discovery is unchanged (same metadata-only shape as the Telegram emoji guidance; the shared-field description follows the Slack `messageId` pattern).
- Error guidance: when the homeserver rejects a caller-supplied cursor with HTTP 400 or 500, the read error keeps the server message (the original error stays on `cause`) and names the next step. Both statuses are matched because homeservers disagree: Synapse answers 400 (`'from' parameter is invalid`), while the tuwunel image pinned by the Matrix QA harness answers 500 `M_UNKNOWN` "invalid digit found in string" for both room history and thread relations. Reads without a caller cursor and other statuses are rethrown unchanged.
- `before` + `after`: the direction followed `after` while the token preferred `before`, so passing both read forward from the `before` token. Matrix now rejects the combination, as Mattermost already does.
- CLI help and `docs/cli/message.md` note the Matrix cursor semantics.

Token handling is unchanged: no event-id conversion, cursors (including the synthetic thread-start cursor) are still forwarded verbatim. Accepted edge case: a valid cursor that hits an unrelated 400/500 also gets the hint appended; the server message is kept, so the real cause stays visible.

## Evidence

Real CLI path: `openclaw message read --channel matrix --json` (bundled Matrix plugin, isolated state) against the Matrix QA harness's pinned homeserver image `ghcr.io/matrix-construct/tuwunel:v1.8.3@sha256:699fa997...` in local Docker, in a room with main-timeline messages and a thread. Before = clean checkout of current base `5d85ad57d12`; after = this branch at `1002a4d436f` (current `main` merged in). `read` abbreviates `openclaw message read --channel matrix --target room:<roomId>`; JSON output is condensed to message bodies and cursors; room and event ids are redacted (tuwunel tokens are numeric).

Before (base `5d85ad57d12`):

```text
$ openclaw message read --help
  --after <id>         Read/search after id
  --before <id>        Read/search before id

$ read --limit 2 --json
ok: messages=["main 3","main 2"] nextBatch="121" prevBatch="9223372036854775807"

$ read --after <roomEventId> --limit 2 --json
error: invalid digit found in string
exit=1

$ read --thread-id <threadRootEventId> --after <replyEventId> --limit 25 --json
error: MatrixError: [500] invalid digit found in string (<homeserver>/_matrix/client/v1/rooms/<roomId>/relations/<threadRootEventId>/m.thread?dir=f&from=<replyEventId>&limit=25)
exit=1

$ read --before 121 --after 121 --limit 2 --json
ok: messages=["main 3"] nextBatch="124" prevBatch="121"
exit=0   (read forward from the before token)
```

After (this branch, `1002a4d436f`):

```text
$ openclaw message read --help
  --after <id>         Read/search after id (Matrix: nextBatch/prevBatch token
                       from a previous read)
  --before <id>        Read/search before id (Matrix: nextBatch/prevBatch token
                       from a previous read)

$ read --after <roomEventId> --limit 2 --json
error: invalid digit found in string. Matrix read before/after take a pagination token from a previous read's nextBatch or prevBatch, not an event id; use messageId to read one event.
exit=1

$ read --thread-id <threadRootEventId> --after <replyEventId> --limit 25 --json
error: MatrixError: [500] invalid digit found in string (<homeserver>/_matrix/client/v1/rooms/<roomId>/relations/<threadRootEventId>/m.thread?dir=f&from=<replyEventId>&limit=25). Matrix read before/after take a pagination token from a previous read's nextBatch or prevBatch, not an event id; use messageId to read one event.
exit=1

$ read --before 121 --limit 2 --json                                    (nextBatch of the first room page)
ok: messages=["main 1"] nextBatch="115" prevBatch="121"

$ read --thread-id <threadRootEventId> --before 115 --limit 2 --json    (nextBatch of the first thread page)
ok: messages=["thread reply 2","thread reply 1"] nextBatch="109" prevBatch="112"

$ read --before 121 --after 121 --limit 2 --json
error: Matrix read accepts either before or after, not both.
exit=1
```

Model-visible schema, built by the production `createMessageTool` with the real bundled Matrix plugin loaded and Matrix as the current channel:

```text
base 5d85ad57d12   before: (no description)   after: (no description)
this branch        before: "Matrix read: pagination token from a previous read's nextBatch/prevBatch, not an event id; pages toward older messages."
                   after:  "Matrix read: pagination token from a previous read's nextBatch/prevBatch, not an event id; pages toward newer messages."
Matrix action list, identical on both: channel-info, delete, edit, emoji-list, list-pins, member-info, pin, poll, poll-vote, react, reactions, read, send, unpin
```

Tests (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <file> --maxWorkers=1`, on this branch after merging current `main`):

- `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/actions/messages.test.ts`: 25 passed. New: cursor hint for room history (500, plugin HTTP client error) and thread relations (400, `MatrixError`), original error kept on `cause`; first-page and 403 failures unchanged; `before` + `after` rejected before any request.
- `extensions/matrix/src/actions.test.ts`: 4 passed. New: metadata-only read-cursor guidance, absent when `read` is disabled.
- Unchanged and passing: `extensions/matrix/src/tool-actions.test.ts` (26), `src/agents/tools/message-tool-schema.test.ts` (6), `src/cli/program/message/register.read-edit-delete.test.ts` (4).
- The four new behavior tests fail on current base `5d85ad57d12` (hint missing, combined cursors resolve, contribution missing).
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs`: touched-surface lanes pass (typecheck core, core tests, extensions, extension tests; lint for changed core and extension files; format; assertion and line-cap ratchets; runtime import cycles; plugin boundaries). Two lanes fail identically on a clean checkout of base `5d85ad57d12` and are unrelated to this diff: the max-lines ratchet lane (its env-var count budget check reports `OPENCLAW_* count 452 is below budget 453`) and the dead-export scan (exports in untouched Discord, gateway, commands, claws, skills, UI and script files).

Not tested: a live Synapse homeserver (the 400 path is covered by the `MatrixError` unit case and Synapse's source), and an agent-driven read through a model.

prs.title: feat(prometheus): expose provider usage windows
prs.body:
Closes #139188

## What Problem This Solves

Operators can monitor OpenClaw request and tool behavior through the authenticated Prometheus exporter, but cannot monitor provider subscription allowance windows or refresh health without maintaining a separate Gateway RPC collector.

## Why This Change Was Made

This extends the existing provider-usage cache with a sanitized, selection-bound metrics snapshot and gives only the official Prometheus exporter a lifecycle-scoped observer capability. The cache owns periodic refreshes and last-good retention; Prometheus scrapes remain synchronous, render-only, and network-free.

Credential-backed provider polling is explicit opt-in through `providerUsage.enabled`, which defaults to `false`. The selection contract follows the same default/legacy-agent credential selection as unscoped `usage.status`. Selection changes withdraw prior allowance series until the new selection produces an observation. Exported labels are bounded to provider, window, and refresh outcome; account emails, profile IDs, credential fingerprints, prompts, responses, and other identifiers are excluded.

## User Impact

When operators explicitly enable provider-usage polling, they can graph and alert on:

- provider allowance used ratios;
- allowance-window reset timestamps;
- last refresh attempt and success timestamps;
- refresh success and bounded failure outcomes.

Upgrades and fresh installs do not begin credential-backed provider polling unless `providerUsage.enabled` is explicitly set to `true`. No provider API call is triggered by a Prometheus scrape.

## Review Fixes

- Makes provider-usage polling explicit opt-in and default-off for upgrades and fresh installations.
- Supports lifecycle-safe hot enable/disable without changing ordinary diagnostics or Prometheus metrics.
- Releases the observer and withdraws provider metrics when diagnostics are disabled, and reacquires exactly once when re-enabled.
- Rejects callbacks from retired exporter generations and revoked service leases.
- Cancels future provider refresh scheduling after observer release.
- Reads lifecycle-managed runtime configuration instead of ambient configuration.
- Preserves bounded Z.AI window identities so allowance and reset series cannot overwrite one another.
- Integrates the restricted observer with current plugin-service ownership, reload, rollback, cleanup, retirement, pending-owner, and current-claim lifecycle fencing.
- Preserves explicit runtime-config overrides in capable-client cache tests after the latest upstream rebase.
- Updates the generated plugin config baseline for the intentional two-entry surface increase (`4623` to `4625`).

## Evidence

The exact published head `5bcdf1a3d62bf82e2badcef3919a07eab3628295` passed both the isolated Portainer candidate validator and the published-release upgrade proof before the PR branch was updated.

### Candidate validation

- Validation ref: `validate/pr-141276-5bcdf1a3d6`
- Verified target: `5bcdf1a3d62bf82e2badcef3919a07eab3628295`
- Validation base: `3150853d9dee8ad161011682c130ea5731faa365`
- Merge base: `2f228582f354803021c3d217d3a2fd79b54b0305`
- Candidate runtime handoff SHA-256: `924213e6e6d7dae92d5f038666360275f31423173fa3e87363b0a11db1235dee`
- Runtime build cache: rebuilt

Passed gates: locked dependency installation; changed-file diff hygiene, formatting, line-cap ratchet, and type-aware lint; core, extension, owning test-graph, and extension-test types; plugin contracts; focused provider-usage tests; exact-SHA runtime build; isolated managed-install lifecycle proof including auth-suspended revocation; and the final temporary-ref identity fence.

Managed-install evidence recorded an authenticated scrape, one initial provider request after explicit enablement, provider metrics observed, and zero requests caused by scraping, disabled startup, hot-disable release, plugin revocation, or authority revocation during authentication. The restricted observer capability remained unavailable to a non-official plugin.

### Published-release upgrade compatibility

- Integrity-pinned baseline: `openclaw@2026.9.4` and `@openclaw/diagnostics-prometheus@2026.9.4`
- Baseline/default-off provider requests: `0` / `0` over 65-second observations
- Database schema migration: `19` to `27`
- Operator intent and runtime invariants preserved: `true`
- Diagnostics, provider-plugin, Gateway configuration, and managed exporter installation preserved: `true`
- Initial/scheduled requests after explicit opt-in: `1` / `1`
- Observed cadence: `59852 ms`
- Scrape-triggered requests: `0`
- Requests after exporter disable: `0`
- Candidate exporter tarball SHA-256: `7fcd9712b575c84b346b6a50834f31a4f7e77a91948ec524d847b87bfbe58587`
- Final temporary-ref identity fence: passed

### Current upstream conflict check

Canonical `main` was refreshed to `2f2c09d1c12d93408692e950a82d01fd04fa5af1` after validation. An isolated real merge completed with zero conflicts.
## Maintainer Gate Still Required

The compatibility concern is addressed by making credential-backed polling explicit opt-in. The security-sensitive capability boundary still requires authorized maintainer review and approval for the exact published head.

prs.title: fix(slack): honor slack:user:<id> command owners as exec approval approvers
prs.body:
## Summary

When `commands.ownerAllowFrom` holds a Slack owner in the canonical direct-user form `slack:user:<id>`, Slack exec approvals treat the owner list as empty. With `channels.slack.execApprovals.enabled: "auto"` and no explicit `execApprovals.approvers`, native Slack exec approvals stay disabled, no approval DM is planned for the owner, and the owner is not an authorized exec approver.

`docs/tools/exec-approvals-advanced.md` says Slack approvers can be inferred from `commands.ownerAllowFrom`, `docs/tools/slash-commands.md` tells users to write the channel's direct-user target, Slack declares `directTargetStyle: "user-prefixed"`, and Doctor keeps `slack:user:U123` as canonical (`src/commands/doctor-config-flow.workspace-persistence.test.ts`). Core command authorization in `src/auto-reply/command-auth.ts` already accepts this form; only the Slack exec approver normalizer disagrees.

This is the Slack sibling of #172385 (Discord), whose body noted this Slack gap as out of scope.

## Root cause

`extensions/slack/src/exec-approvals.ts` passes the raw entry to `parseSlackTarget`:

```ts
// before
const target = parseSlackTarget(trimmed, { defaultKind: "user" });
```

`parseSlackTarget` treats `slack:` as a user prefix and keeps the remainder as the id, so `slack:user:U0123ABCD` becomes a user target with id `user:U0123ABCD`. That fails the `^[UW][A-Z0-9]+$` check, so the entry is dropped. Every Slack exec approval consumer reads approvers through `getSlackExecApprovalApprovers` (capability `hasApprovers`, `approval-native-gates.ts` DM targets and gating, the exec approval profile), so all of them see zero approvers.

## Fix

Strip the `slack:` channel prefix before parsing:

```ts
// after
const target = parseSlackTarget(trimmed.replace(/^slack:/i, ""), { defaultKind: "user" });
```

`slack:user:<id>` now resolves exactly like `user:<id>`, and `slack:<id>` keeps resolving like `<id>`. Channel targets (`slack:channel:C...`) and foreign-channel entries stay rejected.

Workspace-qualified owners (`slack:team:T...:user:U...`) intentionally stay excluded from exec approvers. They now parse to the same qualified target as `team:T...:user:U...`, which `normalizeSlackApproverId` already rejects for exec approvals because that path has no workspace filter; stripping the team would allow cross-workspace rebinding (the boundary set in eebf68d5b6a for #133932). This matches how explicit team-qualified exec approvers already behave.

## Why this is the right boundary

`normalizeSlackApproverTarget` is the single Slack-owned normalizer behind exec approvers, exec sender checks, forwarding target matching, and plugin approval approvers, so the fix lands once for every caller. Bare ids, `user:`, `slack:<id>`, and mention forms are unchanged. Sender ids from Slack events are bare user ids and are unaffected.

## Verification

- Local gates (vitest, oxlint, oxfmt, tsgo) are left to CI per contributor workflow on this machine.
- Added colocated regression cases in `extensions/slack/src/exec-approvals.test.ts` that fail on main and pass with this patch:
  - `commands.ownerAllowFrom: ["slack:user:U0123ABCD", "slack:team:T0123:user:U0999ZZZZ", "telegram:user:1"]` with `enabled: "auto"` resolves approvers `["U0123ABCD"]`, enables the client, authorizes `U0123ABCD`, and does not authorize the workspace-qualified user.
  - `normalizeSlackApproverId("slack:user:u123owner")` returns `U123OWNER`; `slack:team:...:user:...` and `slack:channel:...` stay undefined.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: A Slack owner configured as `commands.ownerAllowFrom: ["slack:user:<id>"]` gets no native Slack exec approvals: the surface is disabled, no approver DM is planned, and the owner cannot approve.
Real environment tested: The shipped `slackPlugin.approvalCapability` from `extensions/slack/src/channel.ts`, plus the core native delivery planner `resolveChannelNativeApprovalDeliveryPlan` from `src/infra/approval-native-delivery.ts` (the planner the gateway uses for native approval routing) fed the plugin's real native adapter and an exec approval request whose turn source is a Slack channel. Nothing is replaced: no Slack network call is made on this path. Runs used pristine main 512cc70 (no changes to `extensions/slack`, `src/plugin-sdk`, or the two core approval modules between it and current main 0160a3e) and this branch at 48dd345, with identical inputs. Config: `commands.ownerAllowFrom: ["slack:user:U0123ABCD"]`, `channels.slack.execApprovals.enabled: "auto"`, no explicit approvers.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `ROOT=$PWD node --import tsx drive.mts` from the repository root, once on pristine main and once on this branch. The driver prints the capability's exec initiating surface state, the core native delivery plan targets for the exec request, and `authorizeActorAction({ senderId: "U0123ABCD", action: "approve", approvalKind: "exec" }).authorized`.
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine main 512cc70)
ownerAllowFrom=["slack:user:U0123ABCD"]
exec approval surface: {"kind":"disabled"}
native delivery plan targets: []
owner U0123ABCD may approve exec: false
# AFTER (this branch 48dd345, identical inputs)
ownerAllowFrom=["slack:user:U0123ABCD"]
exec approval surface: {"kind":"enabled"}
native delivery plan targets: [{"surface":"approver-dm","target":{"to":"user:U0123ABCD"},"reason":"preferred"}]
owner U0123ABCD may approve exec: true
```
Observed result after fix: The configured `slack:user:` owner now enables native Slack exec approvals, receives a planned approver DM, and is authorized to approve, matching what the bare `user:U0123ABCD` owner already produced on main. A workspace-qualified owner (`slack:team:T0123TEAM:user:U0123ABCD`) still yields a disabled surface, no targets, and no approval rights.
What was not tested: No live Slack workspace or bot token; the actual DM post to the Slack Web API and a real button click were not exercised, and the full gateway process was not booted.

### Control run
On pristine main 512cc70 the same driver with `ownerAllowFrom: ["user:U0123ABCD"]` prints `{"kind":"enabled"}`, the same single `approver-dm` target `user:U0123ABCD`, and `may approve exec: true`, so the only thing that moves in the run above is the `slack:` prefix handling.


## Maintainer proof (release lane 2026.10.5)

Added `extensions/slack/src/approval-native.test.ts` › "lets only the current typed Slack owner approve owner-derived exec requests". It drives the shipped `slackApprovalCapability`, the same capability Gateway approval custody (`src/gateway/approval-channel-custody.ts`) calls through `authorizeActorActionAsync` before it settles a decision. With `commands.ownerAllowFrom: ["slack:user:U0123ABCD"]` and `execApprovals.enabled: "auto"`:

- approver DM targets resolve to `[{ to: "user:U0123ABCD" }]` (the owner receives the approval);
- the owner is authorized; an unlisted sender (`U0666NOPE`) is rejected;
- on a sibling account (`ops`) with explicit `execApprovals.approvers`, the global owner is rejected (account binding unchanged);
- after the owner list is replaced (`slack:user:U0888NEXT`), the former owner is rejected. Authority is evaluated against the current config at decision time; custody additionally refuses a decision prepared under a superseded config (`configCurrent`, unchanged core).

Fail-before/pass-after on current main `01cf74e6469` + this PR (`pnpm test <files> --maxWorkers=1`):

- main normalizer restored: 3 failed / 36 passed — new authority test (`expected [] to deeply equal [{ to: 'user:U0123ABCD' }]`), typed owner approvers, wrapped sender normalization.
- this PR: 39/39 passed (`approval-native`, `exec-approvals`); sibling consumers of the shared normalizer also pass: `approval-auth`, `approval-actions`, `approval-native.policy-routing`, `approval-handler.runtime` (37/37). New test adds no timers or I/O.


### Gateway settlement proof (production-path authority harness)

Uncommitted maintainer harness (core tests may not import bundled plugins, so it is not part of this diff). It loads the shipped `discordPlugin` and `slackPlugin` into the active plugin registry and drives the real `approval.resolve` Gateway handler (`createApprovalHandlers`) with real durable exec approval managers and the real, unmocked `prepareApprovalChannelCustody`. Each decision carries a channel reviewer `{ channel, accountId, senderId }`; the runtime config is read through `context.getRuntimeConfig()` at decision time. Config: `commands.ownerAllowFrom: ["<channel>:user:<owner>"]`, `execApprovals.enabled: "auto"`, plus an `ops` account with explicit `execApprovals.approvers`. Command: `pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/zz-typed-owner-custody.proof.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` on main `01cf74e6469` with both fixes applied, then with both selectors restored to main.

```
# AFTER (main 01cf74e6469 + #172385 + #172424)
[discord] unlisted 666666666: ok=false status=pending
[discord] owner on ops-bound request (ops explicit approvers): ok=false; via default account: ok=false status=pending
[discord] typed owner discord:user:555555555: ok=true status=allowed
[discord] former owner after reassignment to discord:user:666666666: ok=false status=pending
[slack] unlisted U0666NOPE: ok=false status=pending
[slack] owner on ops-bound request (ops explicit approvers): ok=false; via default account: ok=false status=pending
[slack] typed owner slack:user:U0123ABCD: ok=true status=allowed
[slack] former owner after reassignment to slack:user:U0666NOPE: ok=false status=pending
# BEFORE (same harness, owner selectors from main)
[discord] typed owner discord:user:555555555: ok=false status=pending
[slack] typed owner slack:user:U0123ABCD: ok=false status=pending
(negative controls identical: all ok=false, status=pending)
```

The typed owner settles a pending exec approval to `allowed` (the waiter resolves `allow-once`). An unlisted sender, the owner on a request bound to the `ops` account (whether reviewing via `ops` or via `default`), and the former owner after the owner list is reassigned while the approval is pending are all refused before settlement; their records stay `pending`. Voice: `voice/command.test.ts` drives `/vc` through the command handler and asserts the voice manager is invoked for the typed owner (fails on main), and rejects wildcard/foreign owners.

prs.title: fix: preserve automation management for queued owner messages
prs.body:
Related: #168823 (this fixes fresh channel-owner messages queued for followup/collect execution, not every parent-resumption path).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an authenticated channel owner sees only the current conversation's automations when their message waits in the followup queue.

## User Impact

Owners retain their existing ability to manage gateway-wide automations after a queued message starts; revoked ownership and non-owner or internal messages remain restricted. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The original ingress capability expires before queued execution starts with a new run identity. Preserve a source-bound capability factory through queue collection and overflow, then enter a fresh scope for that queued run. The original sender, transport identity, current-owner check, and run-settlement/abort revocation remain authoritative; presentation defaults cannot supply another turn's capability.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the loss through real ingress preparation, queue draining, followup execution, and the native cron tool before the fix, then verified gateway scope after it. External model execution and gateway transport are isolated fixtures; the capability and grant checks are real.
- 130 focused tests pass on the current main base: 112 prepared-reply tests, 3 queued-callback tests, and 15 queue-authority tests. The 36 new cases cover both queue modes, batching, overflow, mixed sources, current-owner revocation, sender aliases, and internal/replayed/spawned/non-owner inputs.
- Targeted typed lint, formatting, whitespace checks, and the repository-required autoreview pass. CI exposed that a whole-object queue type annotation rejects existing private ingress metadata; the factory is now captured before object construction so the existing inferred shape is preserved. All 130 focused tests pass again after this adjustment. The changed 112-test file also passes after narrowing the native tool result and preserving all real typing-module exports; two obsolete mock allowances were removed, and the mock-export ratchet passes.
- The complete [PR CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38639828076) passes on e5691d669a93ada9b8dd75099d76a12292510b9c, including production/test declarations, lint, extension-package boundaries, and baseline ratchets. Local declaration checks could not use the borrowed dependency installation; CI provides that verification. No local full core build. The packaged-Gateway negative controls below use synthetic external services; the additional real Telegram check uses the normal channel and model provider.

- Additional packaged-Gateway proof: with exact-original negative control, a queued owner returns `caller/1` before and `gateway/6` after; fixed output IDs exactly match the global inventory, including foreign-agent jobs. Native ingress, queue, tool, grants, Gateway transport and handlers are real; only external Telegram/model endpoints are fixtures.
- Nearest forbidden paths: non-owner tool surface excludes automations; a different local agent-RPC source without channel-owner/Control UI management entitlement returns `caller/1` and no foreign jobs; authenticated `/stop` after queued tool binding prevents automation execution or result. Config-only owner removal was deferred by channel reload and is not counted as applied-revocation proof. No mutation-race claim. [The evidence comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/172539#issuecomment-6179957120) contains the redacted native trace and boundaries.


- Real Telegram owner-channel check (October 15): B arrived while A was executing a bounded command and ran afterward with its own run identity using a per-message followup directive. Its actual native `automations` list result was `scope=gateway`, `total=73`, 73 returned, `hasMore=false`, with every job ID matching the operator inventory. The reply was delivered to Telegram; persistent queue mode stayed unchanged. This proves the production read path, not a new revocation or mutation-commit race.

prs.title: feat(provider): add Databricks Unity Gateway
prs.body:
Closes #155633

## Problem and user impact

Organizations routing inference through Databricks Unity Gateway currently hand-author workspace routes, credentials, transport and model metadata. This adds provider-specific onboarding and model resolution through an externally distributed plugin.

Operators install `@openclaw/databricks-provider`, supply `DATABRICKS_HOST` and `DATABRICKS_TOKEN`, and run `openclaw onboard --auth-choice databricks-token`. Models use `databricks/<catalog>.<schema>.<model-service>`.

Same-workspace onboarding preserves existing routes, APIs, model entries, aliases and primary selections. Fresh setup uses `/ai-gateway/mlflow/v1` with `system.ai.claude-sonnet-4-5`. Non-interactive onboarding refuses reuse of a saved profile when `DATABRICKS_HOST` selects a different workspace, and rejects invalid explicit hosts before persistence. Trusted manual provider-config edits remain operator-controlled routing changes; this does not introduce immutable workspace identity in the credential format.

## Implementation and distribution

- Databricks host validation, auth, onboarding and model resolution stay in `extensions/databricks`.
- Reuses the existing OpenAI-compatible streaming transport and credential store.
- Follows the in-repo-source / external npm and ClawHub package pattern used by official providers such as Cerebras and Radius; excluded from the core npm tarball.
- Adds `DATABRICKS_HOST` to untrusted workspace `.env` filtering, with a regression. Credential environment filtering comes from the manifest.
- No new external runtime dependencies, generic transport, credential owner, schema or migration. The lockfile adds only the workspace importer and existing `@openclaw/plugin-sdk` workspace devDependency.

## Current candidate

Head `edda4d7bf4c717a627015024ab7c61ed9ef27a43`, rebased onto main `9828e28906f50d674625bb1474814bd5c4b4681e` on October 13, 2026. Conflicts were confined to generated config baseline artifacts and resolved through their generator. Package version/build compatibility is aligned to `2026.10.2`; minimum host remains `>=2026.9.6`. Plugin inventory was regenerated.

Databricks production code and its tests are byte-identical to previously reviewed head `ad52f68faf19ccdf8ca0315201561927739f7e72`. Prior-head CI is historical evidence, not current-head CI.

## Live installed-package proof — October 13

Executed against a real Databricks workspace using the current candidate. The token existed only in the child process environment; onboarding used `--secret-input-mode ref`. Workspace and token are redacted.

| Boundary | Observed |
| --- | --- |
| Core runtime build | Completed successfully, 83.3 seconds |
| Release-pipeline plugin pack | `openclaw-databricks-provider-2026.10.2.tgz`, 8 files, 3 runtime JS modules, manifest, package metadata, README and 2 assets; no runtime dependencies |
| Managed install | `plugins install npm-pack:<tarball> --force --accept-capabilities`, exit 0 |
| Runtime identity | `plugins inspect databricks --runtime --json`: loaded, global origin, installed `node_modules/@openclaw/databricks-provider/dist/index.js`, provider `databricks`, no diagnostics |
| Source exclusion | Both bundled discovery and bundled source overlays disabled throughout install, onboarding and agent turns |
| Onboarding | Exit 0, primary `databricks/system.ai.claude-sonnet-4-5`, `openai-completions`, environment SecretRef; token absent from `openclaw.json` |
| Streaming and real tool round trip | `agent exec` exited 0; two HTTP 200 `text/event-stream` responses; exactly one successful `read` call; final reply exactly matched random file nonce `DBX-baf85764f87acf9d` |
| Non-catalog model | `databricks/system.ai.claude-sonnet-4-6` resolved dynamically; real streamed agent turn exited 0 and replied `DYNAMIC_OK` |
| Invalid explicit workspace | Browser URL containing `?o=1234` rejected with exit 1 before inference; active `openclaw.json` SHA-256 unchanged |

This proves local package installation and real inference through the installed runtime. It does not claim that the package is published or that catalog-linked official publisher trust has been established.

## Installed-runtime authority and stable-upgrade proof

Using the same packed plugin with bundled discovery and source overlays disabled:

- Started with published latest stable `openclaw@2026.10.2` (`b8952d4`), created an existing Databricks Serving route and saved synthetic workspace-A credential through its published SDK, then installed the candidate and ran candidate onboarding. Exit 0; deep comparisons confirmed provider route/API/model metadata, primary selection, aliases/model entries and saved credential including workspace metadata were unchanged.
- Positive control: saved workspace-A credential was reused successfully without a token environment variable.
- Workspace-B selection without a fresh token exited 1 before network access; active configuration hash was unchanged.
- Hostile cwd `.env` supplied an attacker workspace and token. A benign dotenv witness was loaded, proving the actual cwd loader ran, while `DATABRICKS_HOST` stayed absent. Onboarding exited 1 for missing trusted workspace; configuration hash was unchanged.
- A Node preload denied and recorded fetch, HTTP(S) and socket connection attempts. Both negative cases recorded `attempts: []`; it did not modify provider auth/config logic. Synthetic credentials were used for these boundary probes.
- The real-token live run above was separately scanned across 23 isolated state files: zero occurrences of the supplied token.

## Validation

- Focused provider, real-transport loopback and workspace `.env` suites: 28 tests passed across 3 files. Combined wall time 80.44 seconds on a heavily loaded macOS arm64 host, Node 26.5. Provider files: 19 tests, 28.32 seconds wall, individual transport scenario 416 ms. No new tests were added in the rebase.
- Extension package-boundary production typecheck, targeted type-aware lint, and changed-source formatting passed.
- Config baseline, plugin inventory and version-sync checks passed.
- Full docs checks passed: formatting, Markdown/MDX, glossary, links, config examples and changelog checks.
- `git diff --check` passed.

Fresh independent review was completed. Findings were checked against owning paths:

- The proposed interactive SecretRef failure did not reproduce through the registered auth method with source overlays disabled and an explicit plugin load path. The reviewer retracted it.
- The proposed dynamic API override failure is prevented by core's `applyConfiguredProviderOverrides`; the final resolution probe retained `anthropic-messages` and the configured route. No duplicate override was added to the plugin.
- The proposed immutable credential/workspace binding would change the trusted manual-config contract and credential semantics. The implemented guard covers onboarding workspace selection, not arbitrary operator edits; that scope is explicit above.

Current-head [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38397087861) completed with 167 successful jobs, 22 skipped jobs and 6 failed jobs (5 shards plus the aggregate gate). The Databricks shard, production/test types, lint, package boundaries, docs, source contracts and npm-lock checks passed. The failing shards were OpenAI realtime auth fixtures (missing admitted database worker), Codex dynamic-tool host instructions, node-worker launch wire timeout, Telegram emoji gateway timeout, and QA POSIX SIGTERM lifecycle timeout. These are outside the Databricks diff; only the OpenAI failure was independently reproduced and repaired in separate #171064 (18 unchanged tests pass). Other failures are attributed by hosted logs and unchanged source scope, not claimed baseline reproductions. Dependency approval remains separate from the failed CI gate.

## Limits and maintainer decision

This is Unity Gateway support. Existing workspace Serving configuration is preserved, but broader Serving compatibility belongs to dependent #163202, which still requires its own repair, restack and validation. OAuth token minting/refresh, automatic live model discovery and per-workspace pricing are outside this change; unknown model services use fallback metadata.

The remaining product decision is whether Databricks receives official provider catalog sponsorship and in-repository maintenance. Maintainer edits are enabled. If accepted, the final head requires the existing maintainer dependency-change approval path; publishing/release is a separate action.

prs.title: fix: updates fail when a channel is unavailable
prs.body:
Related: #172494, #173358

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes successfully installed updates being reported as failed when a disconnected channel leaves `/readyz` at HTTP 503.

## User Impact

Updates can complete with a named channel warning when the expected Gateway is running and its core is ready. Database failures, incomplete startup, plugin replacement, wrong versions/builds, and changed process ownership still prevent successful verification. Ordinary service restarts keep their existing full-readiness requirement.

The installed updater controls the first upgrade: an already-running older updater can still require HTTP 200 until the patched updater is installed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The earlier channel-warning change relaxed the RPC health check, but final HTTP verification still required all channels to be ready. The existing Gateway readiness owner now reports `coreReady` separately. Update verification accepts channel-only HTTP 503 only with explicit core-ready evidence and valid failing-channel details; legacy or malformed 503 responses remain unverified. Receipts preserve the actual HTTP and channel facts across normal verification, repair, interruption recovery, and immutable activation.

## Evidence

- Real isolated Linux Gateway and systemd service: the bundled Telegram plugin received HTTP 401 from a local API fixture using a synthetic token. `/readyz` stayed HTTP 503 with `coreReady: true`. The compiled production update verifier observed real service/PID, listener, RPC version/build, and HTTP facts, accepted the running Gateway, and retained named Telegram warnings with `readyz: false` and `channelsReady: false`.
- Real core negative control: the public `gateway suspend` CLI made `/readyz` return `coreReady: false` with `gateway-draining`; the production verifier rejected that same service PID/build with verification exit code 1.
- Released-data compatibility: the official SHA-512-verified v2026.10.4 CLI generated settings, shared SQLite state, and an actual update-history row. The patched `update status --json` read that history. Settings/workspace bytes, SQL table definitions, schema version 20, and original update-history columns remained unchanged.
- Runtime reuse is explicit: production source files were byte-identical to the original implementation head `491de657`, while the reused implementation build retains its recorded `885bd760863b` build identity. This was not a fresh clean build with the PR SHA.
- The original implementation passed its red/green readiness-owner regression, focused lifecycle/verification/recovery/immutable/ledger tests, typechecks, lint, formatting, and scoped P0–P2 autoreview. Follow-up validation is recorded below.

## CI Fixture Follow-up

The initial [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38836705036) exposed missing `coreReady` facts in sibling fixtures and eight obsolete mock-factory baseline entries. The follow-up updates six test/support files and prunes those eight entries using the canonical baseline tool. That fixture-only commit (`9618a99d`) left production code unchanged; success and failure assertions retain their intended outcomes.

- 142 focused tests have passing evidence: 133 in unchanged files, plus all 9 native-recovery tests after strengthening its exact ledger expectation.
- The targeted CLI-update type project, scoped lint/format, baseline prune, and diff checks pass. Fresh canonical P0–P2 review is scoped-clean.
- These local checks use the existing `885bd760` implementation checkout. They do not claim that every newer test on the CI merge ref ran locally; CI on the new head is pending.
- The runtime and released-data trace below records the original `491de657` head. That fixture-only commit changes no production code.

## HTTP Diagnostic Follow-up

Head `a2ade6c27a0584e3fc47d52723b09d65da1b3c01` also fixes [the P2 diagnostic finding](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173593#discussion_r4290084407). When `/healthz` fails but `/readyz` returns 200, terminal output, ledger details, and public failure reports now preserve both actual observations:

```text
Gateway HTTP readiness unverified: healthz=503; readyz=200.
Gateway HTTP readiness unverified: healthz=unavailable; readyz=200.
```

Two real loopback HTTP regressions failed against the original implementation and pass with this repair. The verification/channel sibling suites and support-redaction suite pass **110 tests**. Scoped production/test typing, targeted lint, formatting, and fresh P0–P2 autoreview pass. The public redactor accepts only this closed status format and retains stored-format compatibility; arbitrary private suffixes remain redacted. This adds no state fields and changes no readiness acceptance condition.

Final combination check: the isolated checkout matches the full `a2ade6c` tree byte for byte. The verification-report suite passes **3/3** after the fixture and diagnostic changes are combined, and the scoped CLI-update type project passes. CI on that diagnostic head was pending when checked.

A separate real integrated installation also completed the shipped managed update with all three repairs present; see [the backup PR's final-effect trace](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173616). Every channel was healthy in that run, so it is complementary update-completion evidence, not a reproduction of the channel-outage case.

## Public Protocol Follow-up

Latest head `c7bcfe0e034075ca1743a82921869ca8643be814` fixes [the P1 public-schema finding](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173593#discussion_r4290329546). The canonical ledger already stores and projects optional `coreReady`; the existing closed wire schema now declares that optional boolean too. No readiness rule, method, protocol version, stored schema, or projection changed.

Actual canonical records pass through `toPublicUpdateRun` and the record/get/list/status validators:

| Verification input | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `coreReady=true`, `readyz=false` | rejected by all four | accepted by all four |
| `coreReady=false`, `readyz=false` | rejected by all four | accepted by all four |
| Legacy record without `coreReady` | accepted | accepted |
| String `coreReady` or unknown verification field | rejected | rejected |

The existing parity fixture and real validator suite pass **5 tests**. Targeted typing/lint/format and canonical `protocol:check` pass, including generated JSON, Swift/Kotlin contract and determinism, and the since check with zero new methods. Generated verification remains closed. No generated artifact was hand-edited. Fresh P0–P2 autoreview is scoped-clean with no actionable findings. Production +1 line; tests +51 lines in the existing suite.

## Limits and Maintainer Decision

The runtime experiment invoked the built production verifier, and the health/channel/suspension operations used the normal CLI. A complete package update from v2026.10.4 through patched activation has not been demonstrated. The extracted stable package correctly skipped updating an unmanaged installation; a public repair attempt deferred Doctor while the live Gateway retained database ownership. These are not counted as successful update completion. Broad CI and non-Linux service environments remain unverified locally.

Owner direction is still needed for accepting explicit core readiness across update activation, retained-service certification, and recovery completion while retaining channel-only HTTP 503. This PR does not claim maintainer approval.


<details>
<summary>Inspectable runtime and released-data trace</summary>

Additional runtime and released-data evidence for `491de6578f0bb955e9f1ad13e9bf432674ebf318`:

The update verifier now has a real Gateway/service positive control and a real core-readiness negative control. This is stronger than the earlier in-process HTTP fixture, but it is **not a completed end-to-end package update**.

**Runtime setup and build identity**

- Linux, Node.js `v26.11.1`; isolated state/config, an ephemeral loopback port, and a dedicated temporary systemd user service. No existing Gateway or user data was changed.
- The real bundled Telegram plugin received HTTP 401 from a local Bot API fixture through its documented `apiRoot` setting, using a synthetic token. Its actual lifecycle became `blocked`, `terminalDisconnect: true`, `configured: true`, `running: false`. No Telegram account or external Telegram server was used.
- Reused the previously compiled runtime from the implementation checkout. Every tracked file under `src/`, `packages/`, and `scripts/`, plus `package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml`, was compared byte for byte with this PR head: **zero differences**. Its recorded build identity remains `2026.10.3-885bd760863b-2026-10-16T00-10-44.971Z`; this was a dirty implementation build, not a new clean build labeled with the PR SHA.
- Gateway startup, HTTP, WebSocket hello/health, systemd inspection, listener ownership, PID, version, and build observations were real. No service, RPC, readiness-owner, or verifier mocks were used. The driver invoked the compiled production `verifyUpdatedGateway` with `purpose: "recovery"`, `requireRunningService: true`, and `waitForStartup: false`.

**Observed behavior**

The normal CLI entry point was used for `gateway run`, `gateway health --json`, `channels status --probe --json`, and `gateway suspend --json --wait 1 --request-id readiness-proof-core-negative`.

```text
Telegram local API fixture: HTTP 401, Unauthorized (local synthetic fixture)
Gateway: Telegram channel exited; auto-restart skipped, terminal disconnect
GET /readyz: HTTP 503
{"ready":false,"coreReady":true,"failing":["telegram"]}

gateway health --json: exit 0, plugins.errors=[], telegram.running=false
channels status --probe --json: exit 0, telegram.probe.ok=false, status=401

Production update verifier, channel outage:
  validation.ok=true
  serviceRunning=true, pid=542112, versionMatch=true
  pluginErrors=[], settled=true, coreReady=true
  readyz=false, channelsReady=false
  verification step exitCode=0
  warning: Channel health warning (telegram: channel readiness unavailable).
           Run openclaw channels status --probe or openclaw health --json to inspect it.

gateway suspend --json: exit 0, status=ready, activeCount=0
GET /readyz: HTTP 503
{"ready":false,"coreReady":false,"failing":["gateway-draining"]}

Production update verifier, core draining, same service PID/build:
  validation.ok=false
  serviceRunning=true, pid=542112, versionMatch=true
  settled=false, coreReady=false, readyz=false, channelsReady=false
  verification step exitCode=1
  failure: restart-unhealthy; health unavailable during gateway suspension
```

**Released v2026.10.4 data**

Downloaded the official `openclaw@2026.10.4` npm tarball and verified its published SHA-512 integrity:

```text
sha512-+FH0StZF1tlTazM7JJGY6JePeJmhFNSRByi2Q3jXPRiLO7o4dJh2xa9Vy4Dk8Cd2ic8B7Zkf5NfEaCCWUkgqnQ==

Official openclaw --version: OpenClaw 2026.10.4 (383c124)
Official openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive: exit 0
Official openclaw update --json --yes --no-restart --timeout 15:
  exit 0, status=skipped, reason=unmanaged-package-install
Patched openclaw update status --json --timeout 1:
  exit 0, lastRun.runId=ea1d006e-692d-494e-9014-41ac37ec5e9f
  lastRun.status=skipped, before.version=2026.10.4
```

The released CLI generated the settings and shared SQLite database, including an update-history row, heartbeat job, device identity, and migration records. The patched CLI read that actual stored update history. Before/after comparison found the settings and workspace bytes, table SQL, `PRAGMA user_version` (`20`), and every original update-history column unchanged. For the canonical sorted JSON of all original `update_runs` rows, SHA-256 stayed `55db426dc94aa720fa1fa5e628a2892e97be1d1cddd34799adec0c2a4a474fb8`.

**Remaining gaps and decision**

This proves real service/Gateway acceptance with factual channel warnings, rejection during core draining, and reading released stored data. It does not prove a full v2026.10.4-to-patched installation/activation. The extracted official package correctly skipped a managed update; its optional native capture helper was unavailable. A public `update repair` attempt against the running temporary service deferred Doctor with exit 2 because the live Gateway still owned its state database. Neither result is counted as successful update completion. A released verifier also correctly refused the newer schema of the separate current-runtime test state; that attempt is not a red/green reproduction of this change.

No source changes were needed for these experiments; the existing scoped autoreview applies to the unchanged patch. The temporary service and Gateway were stopped afterward.

The maintainer decision remains open: should explicit core readiness permit activation, retained-service certification, and recovery completion while channel-only failures keep `/readyz` at HTTP 503? This evidence does not claim that decision has been approved.

</details>


## Final-head CI Status

The main CI suite passes. The separate security-sensitive review is awaiting maintainer approval; it is not a passing gate. The Swift static-scan failure below remains unresolved and is not waived.

| Check at `c7bcfe0e034075ca1743a82921869ca8643be814` | Result | Classification |

| [Main CI 38842558253](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38842558253) | Passed | Passing |

The tested merge is `f183beb384e4b7e91b29bc1aabf53f2d78fb78f1`, with main parent `5462f7f146436a50a56354dd39f8405eaeb5b60f`. Both have the identical entire `apps` tree `29412570ec1181ffe3f35c2411e0174d40bcb246`, generator/tooling `scripts` tree `43e0d5baf4df43a4805b1f34a59ccfc5a419aee8`, and `.github` tree `e6c2dfc1d926cf9e620ad844cccded2ed157c8a8`.

A separate in-memory check of the candidate's canonical Swift generator, with the optional `coreReady` field present and absent, emitted identical 1,101,963-byte models: SHA-256 `634e9055a02d2d0027291b8d0bffad9e949a5e0baeeb363d23f24ae8259047d6`. This supports an inference that the field does not introduce these Swift findings; it is not a base/merge Periphery comparison or a Mac execution.

No matching baseline execution was found. This workflow has no main push/schedule runs, and no run for exact base `5462f7f...`. prs.title: feat(database): shared-state port and backup on PostgreSQL
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Registers shared state with R12's existing database port and matched-backup provider. Existing `state/openclaw.sqlite` stores can be ported to PostgreSQL without introducing another copy or schema owner.

## User Impact

Discovery includes the selected state root, retained Voice Call roots, and explicitly configured stores even when the plugin is disabled or removed. Matrix account/token roots remain excluded for R18. Older SQLite schemas must run Doctor with a compatible binary before porting. No canonical schema or schema-version change.

PostgreSQL-to-SQLite and exact/user backup-restore conformance remain explicitly pending R14a PostgreSQL maintenance custody. Their code paths use the shared provider lifecycle; this PR does not bypass custody or claim those recovery flows have passed.

## Implementation

The port metadata contains copy order, identity allocation policy, PostgreSQL DDL offsets and SQLite source offsets. It references the existing bundled `statePostgresRuntime` DDL/catalog, canonical SQLite schema and feature-schema owners. Fragment dependencies also come from the runtime owner. Loading remains lazy through the R12 registry, once per operation.

`state-port.json` shrank from **457,460 bytes / 14,386 lines to 26,959 bytes / 1,905 lines** (94.1% smaller). It contains no inline SQL or duplicate column/constraint facts, and the generator enforces a 60 KB ceiling.

The provider preserves all 134 canonical tables and optional fragments, including absent Doctor-owned deletion history. Exact captures retain secrets and transient rows; exports retain the existing sanitizer. Normal restore admission keeps PostgreSQL drift checks. Keyless join-code rows, duplicate/null values, integer precision and allocation high-watermarks remain covered. Equivalent generated DDL is re-admitted only after exact catalog comparison.

## Validation

- PostgreSQL 17: **14 passed (2 state + 12 admission), 1 todo**. Reverse/backup conformance remains explicitly pending R14a.
- `pnpm db:postgres:gen` and `pnpm db:postgres:check`: passed, including 20 generator tests. Root discovery and provider import guard passed.
- SQLite before/after capture: all 10 sanitizer statements and four backup/export owner source hashes are identical.
- Scoped core/scripts lint, core typecheck, formatting, wrapper inventory and dialect ratchet passed.
- One completed independent autoreview of the compacting delta: **scoped-clean, P0–P2**. The initial launcher attempt stopped before model review because Python selected shared temporary storage; the completed run uses the macOS private temporary directory.
- The state suite now preloads compiled subprocess declarations at collection, following the repository fixture contract. The initial cold run exposed compilation inside the test deadline; no timeout was increased.

## Existing Local Gate Failures

Classification against current main `0169c8acfbff959e3009c2550e5a0ca2bd708371`:

- Max-lines still reports `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message.test.tsx` on main. The test file, baseline and guard are byte-identical to this branch. This is inherited.
- The prior Knip finding, `ui/src/components/loading-skeleton.ts`, is inherited from the branch base but the file has since been removed on newer main. It is not a current-main Knip failure. The separate current-main Knip check passed with no unused files or dependencies (exit 0, 16m28s).

Neither UI path is changed by this PR. The PR is ready for CI; these local baseline findings are not described as passing checks.

Related: #172677. Concurrent generator work in #173617 must be integrated and regenerated by whichever lane lands second.

The final conformance wrapper took 756.09 seconds on the loaded local host, including 423.12 seconds of collection-time worker preparation. The state cases took 117.66 seconds; the full 134-table copy and real R2 admission/drift rejection are required boundary proof, not replaceable by a helper-only test. CI timing will be reported separately.

Whole-PR delta: **+237 handwritten production lines**, +278 test lines, +1,924 generated lines, +10 documentation lines. The compacting revision itself removes 12,481 generated lines.

## CI

Ready-for-review CI is running on head `704ecc245c7df9e7d770072652551a591a48a815`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38845000336 . No merge is requested.

prs.title: fix(infra): align Windows renderer CR/LF checks with analyzer policy
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Proposes an independent CR/LF check in `windowsEscapeArg`, matching the policy already applied by the Windows shell analyzer. This is renderer policy alignment, not a demonstrated shipped execution bug or security exploit.

The earlier description and argv-to-renderer test overstated production reachability. `analyzeArgvCommand` is not the source of the segments used by the shipped Gateway renderer caller; that synthetic composition test has been removed.

## User Impact

No user-visible execution change has been demonstrated. The production caller in `processGatewayAllowlist` obtains segments from `evaluateShellAllowlistWithAuthorization`; its Windows analyzer already rejects LF/CR, including inside quoted arguments. Direct calls to the renderer would now reject those characters instead of quoting them.

## Why This Change Was Made

The renderer previously omitted LF/CR from its own rejection expression while the analyzer rejects them. This patch aligns those local policies and retains only a direct renderer unit test. It does not establish that quoted LF/CR causes command injection or invalid PowerShell syntax.

**Exec-owner decision remains pending:** the current production caller already validates these characters. This PR does not establish a new reachable failure or claim owner acceptance of additional validation. If an execution-permission security guard requires approval, that approval must come from an upstream maintainer with the required role.

## Evidence

- Actual repository workspace and dependencies, Node 26.1.0, pnpm 12.10.1, Vitest 5.0.3; no dependency shims.
- `pnpm test src/infra/exec-approvals-analysis.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **17 passed** (Vitest duration 44.00s).
- Targeted repository Oxlint, formatting, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Infra-test typecheck (`node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.infra.json --incremental`): passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`: fails at unchanged `src/tui/tui-session-actions-test-support.ts:91` (`setProgramStatus` is not a property of `Terminal`). The file is byte-identical to this PR base; no TUI fix is included. Production typecheck is not claimed as passing.
- Canonical autoreview P0–P3: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Reviewer explicitly distinguished local renderer correctness from the still-pending exec-owner acceptance and missing shipped Windows reproduction.

No Windows CLI/Gateway execution, reachable production failure, full workspace test suite, or merge approval is claimed. Passing helper tests cannot replace the outstanding exec-owner decision or requested real behavior proof.

AI assistance was used in investigation, implementation, verification, and review.

Remote CI on merge commit `970c3198` fails `check-test-types-core-3` at `test/scripts/apple-build-cache.test.ts:232:73` (TS2345: fixture outcome inferred as string). The failing test and its workflow-context type contract have identical blob SHAs in the tested merge and its upstream parent `13bf1f2d9e4983df6b6012bf8192c93a3e927a90`; this failure is inherited from upstream, outside this PR’s infra-only diff. No unrelated test/CI repair or rerun was added.

prs.title: perf(boards): reuse captured session routing scope
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Board reads and writes resolve the same session routing scope twice before selecting durable storage. This repeats config, canonical-session, and store-path resolution on the dashboard data-read path.

## User Impact

No behavior or protocol change. This is a small hot-path simplification; it does not claim to fix the multi-second tail latency seen under load.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the scope already captured by the board store to resolve the physical database owner, and remove the duplicate resolver wrapper. Shared databases retain their physical owner and logical session key; incognito retains its memory owner. Current-authority checks remain unchanged. No cache, schema change, or new configuration.

Production delta: +5 / -26 lines (net -21). Existing boundary tests cover owner separation, shared-store reopen, and rejection after routing changes; no implementation-count test added.

## Evidence

- Focused `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/board-store.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 4/4 passed; 172.48 seconds including cold worker preparation on a constrained host.
- Changed-file format, diff checks, and `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/gateway/board-store.ts` passed. 
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): no P2-or-higher findings. The configured autoreview helper refused the requested provider route; no operator configuration was changed.
- Source attribution: widget-authored `openclaw.data.read` calls dispatch one-for-one. The Control UI does not globally poll this endpoint, and inactive widgets are already blocked before dispatch. Existing usage and GitHub bindings already coalesce their own refresh work.
- Broad validation belongs to PR CI; no Testbox/Crabbox lease. Exact-head CI run 38843882614 passed, including changed-node lanes, type checks, lint, and UI end-to-end checks. Hosted code review also completed without findings. A traced 33,185 ms data read spent 27,540 ms and 5,627 ms waiting for two database admissions; each admitted operation took 8 ms. The first wait named `session.actor.appendTranscriptEvent` as its blocker. This PR does not remove those live-grant reads or claim to solve their queueing delay. Binding identity is not present in the retained RPC trace.

### Before/after measurement

Synthetic Linux sandbox, 5,000 sessions and 24 stored/granted HTML widgets reading the real `cron.status` binding. Real `board.get` minted the tickets; direct `board.data.read` handler calls exercised the board store and CronService. Two blocks of three alternating pairs (AB/BA/AB, then AB/BA/AB to investigate the outlier), 96 warmups and 720 measured calls per run: 8,640 measured calls total. Each process seeded fresh synthetic state; no production state or service was touched.

| Median across six runs per revision | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Handler mean | 1.476 ms | 1.510 ms |
| Handler p50 | 1.346 ms | 1.373 ms |
| Handler p95 | 2.066 ms | 2.138 ms |
| Handler p99 | 3.013 ms | 3.136 ms |
| Saturated sequential throughput | 40,644 calls/min | 39,731 calls/min |
| Board-target resolution diagnostic | 9.292 µs | 5.834 µs |

Routing cost fell 37.2%, consistently across all six pairs. Complete-handler latency is neutral within shared-host spread; no handler speedup is claimed. The third candidate run was an outlier and remains included. Individual run means (ms):

| Pair | Order | Before | After |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | before/after | 1.561 | 1.523 |
| 2 | after/before | 1.470 | 1.477 |
| 3 | before/after | 1.510 | 2.227 |
| 4 | before/after | 1.479 | 1.496 |
| 5 | after/before | 1.469 | 1.551 |
| 6 | before/after | 1.473 | 1.442 |

This is a net-deletion simplification with a smaller routing cost, not a fix for the traced admission-queue tail. Throughput is a saturated synthetic measurement, not dashboard polling frequency. This fixture excludes WebSocket transport, transcript payloads, retained runs, and concurrent transcript writes; it cannot reproduce the production contention. No cache or reduced grant-check frequency was introduced.

prs.title: fix(docker): repeated container restarts each take a full Doctor pre-repair capture
prs.body:
Fixes #173564

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: every start of the official Docker image takes a new full pre-repair copy of local state, even on a plain `docker stop`/`docker start` with the same image. On large state this adds minutes to Gateway startup (about 7.5 of 10 minutes in the report) and leaves one more multi-GB copy under `<state-dir>.update-captures/` per restart, retained for 30 days.

## User Impact

User impact: restarting the same container no longer re-copies the whole state. The first activation in a container (a new image, or a recreated container) still takes the full pre-repair copy before Doctor changes anything; later starts of that container still run the `doctor --fix` repair pass, skip only the repeated full copy, and log that they did. Repair-specific backups (schema migrations, rewritten databases, config backups, legacy archives) are unchanged. Manual `openclaw doctor --fix` and update-time Doctor are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The image entrypoint (#151025) runs `doctor --fix` before every Gateway start, and standalone Doctor (#161044, retention in #162364) takes a full capture before every repair pass, so the two combined capture on every restart. Doctor cannot know up front whether a pass will mutate state, and the shared database's writer stamp is not refreshed on version changes without a schema change, so neither works as a "nothing changed" signal.

A container keeps its image, environment, and mounts across stop/start, and its writable layer survives them. After Doctor exits successfully, the entrypoint records a marker in the container's temp directory, keyed to the install root and the selected root options. On later starts, it passes `OPENCLAW_IMAGE_ACTIVATION_REPEAT=1` to that Doctor child only, and Doctor skips the standalone capture. An inherited value of that variable is stripped, so only the container's own record counts. If Doctor fails, no marker is written, so the next start captures again. When `/tmp` does not persist, the marker is never found and behavior stays as it is today.

No schema, retention, persisted state, or config change. Update behavior: update continuations return before the new check and keep reusing the updater's capture. Existing captures are left as they are.

## Evidence

- Real entrypoint, built CLI (`pnpm build:docker`), isolated state, three starts each, Gateway reaching `http server listening`:
  - `origin/main` entrypoint: 1, 2, 3 `doctor-*` captures. Every start printed `Pre-repair state retained for manual recovery at …`.
  - This branch: 1, 1, 1 captures. The first start captured. The second and third printed `This container already completed image activation; Doctor skipped a repeated full pre-repair capture. Repair-specific backups still apply.`
- New regression tests, failing before the fix and passing after:
  - `src/commands/doctor-original-capture.test.ts`: with the repeat flag, no capture root is created and the skip message is logged. On unfixed code, a capture was written and the test failed. With the fix: 3/3 passed, about 61 s wall for the file (the existing refusal cases dominate; the new case takes 5 ms).
  - `test/docker-entrypoint.test.ts`: a failed Doctor writes no marker, an inherited flag is stripped, the flag is set only on the start after a successful activation, and a different root option selection does not reuse the marker. 22/23 passed; the new case takes about 0.4 s.
  - The one failing case, `[ 'openclaw', 'gateway' ]` (the installed-symlink case), fails the same way on unmodified `origin/main` on this host (`env: node: No such file or directory`, a local PATH/node-wrapper fixture issue). It is unrelated to this change.
- Codex autoreview (P2, branch mode against `origin/main`): scoped-clean.

prs.title: fix(wizard): report a failed gateway restart instead of success
prs.body:
Closes #173348

## What Problem This Solves

The `action === "restart"` branch of `ensureGatewayServiceForOnboarding` wrapped the restart in a bare `try/finally`. When `service.restart()` rejected, the progress line still stopped with the success label ("Gateway service restarted.") and the error then propagated out of the function, so the wizard reported success *and* threw, instead of degrading like the sibling branches.

## User Impact

A failed service restart now reports failure: the branch returns `{ status: "failed", error }`, the progress line stops with the neutral service label rather than the success copy, and the caller — which already renders `gateway.error` in its failure note — shows the real reason. The success paths (`restarted`, `restart-scheduled`) are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Every other service outcome in this function degrades through a `catch` that returns `{ status: "failed", error: formatErrorMessage(error) }`; the restart branch simply lacked one, which is why a rejection escaped instead of being reported. The fix adds that catch and keeps the existing `finally` that stops the progress line.

## Evidence

- Regression in `src/wizard/setup.finalize.test.ts` ("reports a failed restart instead of a success label"): `service.restart` rejects with `launchctl restart failed`; asserts the result is `{ status: "failed", error: "launchctl restart failed" }` and that the progress stop is **not** called with "Gateway service restarted.". Red before the change (the rejection propagated), green after.
- `pnpm test src/wizard/setup.finalize.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → 52 passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` clean; `oxlint --deny-warnings` → 0 warnings / 0 errors; `oxfmt --check` clean; `git diff --check` clean.

prs.title: fix(ui): Settings Prefs shows an unlabeled empty Locale text box
prs.body:
Closes #172817

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Settings → Appearance → UI → Prefs shows an unlabeled, empty "Locale" text box that people mistake for a region or timezone setting.

## User Impact

User impact: the UI language is set in one place, the Appearance → Language picker. The generic Prefs form no longer offers a free-text box for it, which could save an invalid locale string. Existing `ui.prefs.locale` values are kept and still apply. `openclaw config schema` and the config docs now describe the field as the Control UI language, unrelated to `agents.defaults.userTimezone`. No migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Appearance → Language already owns `ui.prefs.locale`, so the generic form now leaves that one field out. This uses the same pattern as the `wizard` section, which the generic form leaves out because Setup owns it. The schema keeps `string`, max 20, rather than adding an enum, so configs that already hold a locale stay valid. The field gets a title and description (`Interface Language`) for every schema-driven surface. The UI labels move into `schema.labels.ui.ts`, because `schema.labels.ts` is already over the line cap.

## Evidence

Before and after: Control UI Settings → Appearance → UI, rendered in Chromium by the repo's mocked-Gateway e2e harness. The mocked `config.schema` is the real `ui` schema and hints from `computeBaseConfigSchemaResponse()`, on `upstream/main` 55147a0e6 for "before" and on this branch for "after".

**Before (main):** the Prefs group has an empty "Locale" text box between Chat Show Tool Calls and Theme.

![Before: Prefs form with empty Locale text box](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ae93a684-6c09-4fe5-9a3f-9dcdc232482b)

**After:** the Prefs group no longer shows Locale. Every other pref is unchanged.

![After: Prefs form without Locale](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7d2f9dbf-fc51-4a57-a9ed-a9d3e08e389c)

**After:** the owned Language picker on Appearance is unchanged.

![After: Appearance Language picker](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2816983a-bbe7-466b-a3e3-601a53ca2336)

Schema output for `ui.prefs.locale`:
- Before: `{"type":"string","maxLength":20}`
- After: `{"type":"string","maxLength":20,"title":"Interface Language","description":"Language for the Control UI, as a supported locale id such as en, de or zh-CN. Leave it unset to follow the browser or system language. Set it from Settings → Appearance → Language. Not related to the assistant's timezone (agents.defaults.userTimezone)."}`

Checks run locally (ClawSweeper's acceptance list):
- `pnpm --dir ui test src/pages/config/view.browser.test.tsx src/pages/config/view-appearance.browser.test.tsx`: 37 passed. The new regression test covers both an unset locale and a set one (`de`). It fails on main, where the form still renders "Locale", and passes here.
- `pnpm test:ui:e2e ui/src/e2e/config-form-guidance.e2e.test.ts ui/src/e2e/appearance-settings-defaults.e2e.test.ts`: 10 passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm config:schema:check`, `pnpm config:docs:check`: pass.
- `pnpm check:changed --base upstream/main`: the line-cap, format, schema, docs-baseline, typecheck and plugin-boundary checks pass for this change. The remaining failures happen the same way on `upstream/main` 55147a0e6 and involve none of the files changed here: the `OPENCLAW_*` env-var budget (455 > 454), knip unused exports in `chat-picker-overlay.ts` and other files, and `max-lines` lint errors in 43 existing files. The SQLite worker ratchet needs `rg`, which is not installed on this machine, and this change has no SQLite code.

Merge danger: **two-way door**. Reverting brings the text box back. The change touches no persisted state, schema validation or Gateway behavior. Blast radius: the generic UI Prefs form and the schema metadata for one field.

prs.title: refactor: consolidate secret and provider configuration normalization
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Completes the configuration/secret-normalization family split from #173394, removing duplicate parsing and assignment plumbing without proposing the already-landed speech directive and Voice Call changes again.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible change, configuration migration, or credential-policy relaxation. Existing provider overrides, account activation/ownership, meeting defaults and video-duration policies remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing channel secret collector for snapshot-bound assignments, a shared undefined-only omission primitive for fresh normalized speech records, and a private meeting-config owner for the duplicated browser/realtime fields and audio-command defaults. Reuse the video-duration owner and remove redundant internal type/absence checks in reply, CLI and TTS configuration paths.

Google Meet retains its format aliases, custom-command G.711 default, 20-second in-call wait and provider-specific transcription fallback; generic meetings keep their 60-second wait. Speech normalization retains meaningful zero/false values and provider-specific URL, model and key precedence. SDK surface validation reports no unauthorized shipped removals; bundled consumers share the registered production-private meeting-config entrypoint and speech omission helper.

Conservative production delta, including required registration-checker and SDK/package/path metadata: +465/-798, **333 net lines removed**. Tests, docs, fixtures, generated declarations, and ratchets are excluded. The 500-line floor is waived for completion of this already-landed family.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Unexpected audio-command-builder defects now propagate instead of being silently retried with a BlackHole fallback. The catch came from the Linux audio feature work in #118451, not a reported failure requiring catch-all recovery. Config-only unsupported hosts still materialize Darwin defaults; actual execution retains platform validation.
- Typed internal config records are no longer repeatedly checked as unknown objects, and unused fallback owner projections are no longer constructed. Existing external object/leaf validation stays at its boundary; malformed values injected by untyped internal callers can fail at use rather than receiving another silent empty fallback. Provenance: shared collector refactors #162827/#168496, compatible speech factory #138483, Fish coercion #121366, CLI config split #113248.
- Absent optional directive fields are omitted rather than eagerly created with `undefined` (#166685). The real consumer still projects the complete outward shape; no public own-property-enumeration contract is removed.
- TTS performs one sanitizing/detaching merge and skips additional merges for absent overrides. Scope precedence and prototype-key filtering remain; redundant copies were implementation work, not a user-visible durability or security guarantee.

## Evidence

Serial Linux diagnosis used the same isolated Testbox, workers=1, pinned main `2a1151addfbf7d48508367cc3a6a3271aa131f0d`, and verified raw candidate tree `ef83d2cf03dccc16a5efe6935acce85fca100c5f` before the fixture repair:

| Probe | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Candidate scheduler-state cron case | Fails at `cron.add`: no route-compatible OpenAI auth, 4.955s |
| Pinned-main identical cron case | Same error, 4.979s |
| Candidate acknowledged Control UI first-turn recovery, worktree=true | Pass, 8.326s; cleanup passed |

The observed cron failure is inherited fixture setup, not a dropped provider field: stored inference-account admission from #172590/#172794 requires an account that this older scheduler-state test did not seed. The existing fixture now pins `openai/gpt-4.1` and writes one synthetic account through its canonical isolated state owner before startup. Scheduler handoff/state assertions and production auth stay unchanged. The earlier first-turn timeout did not reproduce serially; exact-head PR CI remains the broad gate.

The repaired candidate scheduler-state case passes (32.409s), exercising the unchanged handoff/state assertions. Final proof independently verified the fixture and helper hashes, completed the full runtime build and CLI bootstrap guard, and passed canonical SDK registration. Fresh independent review of the final candidate, including the fixture repair and generated SDK mapping, completed clean through P2.

All 34 selected focused suites pass: 346 assertions across 12 serial shards. Selected type checks pass: core production, UI, all 29 core-test shards, extension projects, scripts and all four root-test shards. The changed-file run also passed formatting, SQLite boundary/dialect and assertion ratchets, doctor closure checks, config-doc baselines, SDK registration/surface compatibility, plugin boundaries, coercion declarations and deprecated-API checks.

The final Testbox workflow was cancelled after approximately an hour, before final lint/cycle receipts; that aggregate is incomplete, not a pass. Earlier unchanged-input targeted core/package lint and zero runtime/static cycle checks passed. Exact-head PR CI remains the broad gate. Both diagnostic Linux runtime builds and CLI bootstrap guards also passed.

Known baseline-only local reds were independently replayed on pinned main: the environment-variable budget is 453 while the actual count is 452; the lint-suppression test reports 96 rows against 94, including two existing rules in the unchanged Control UI streaming test helper. No allowlist or budget is expanded here. Exact-head PR CI will determine the final merge-ref result.

The final dead-export scan also named unchanged Codex, memory-wiki, Voice Call and UI files. Clean-main replay of those findings is pending; they are not claimed as attributed or green.

No timeouts, retries, skips, lint suppressions, retained-behavior assertions, public contracts, schema, dependencies, or changelog entries are changed to obtain green.
