prs.title: fix(doctor): PostgreSQL maintenance custody
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Doctor cannot acquire maintenance custody on PostgreSQL shared state because lease inspection takes a SQLite repair snapshot and rejects the PostgreSQL reader. Populated PostgreSQL leases also lose their camel-case column aliases, preventing owner identity decoding.

## User Impact

Doctor can acquire and release offline PostgreSQL custody and run data-only legacy state migrations. A live Gateway still blocks maintenance, including through another anchor for the same PostgreSQL store.

Schema migrations remain blocked with an actionable error until their state-family backup path is available. The remaining work is tracked separately: the PG schema-migration end-to-end proof follows R13 (state family registration).

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the admitted PostgreSQL state reader and existing owner-lease checks, with typed PostgreSQL lease selection. Keep SQLite's private snapshot and damaged-index-safe query byte-for-byte. Writes retain the existing PostgreSQL advisory transaction lock; no new lock protocol or shared-admission revision changes.

The schema runner is unchanged. Its backup dependency now reports the missing PostgreSQL state-family support and directs the operator to keep the database and retry with a supporting version.

## Evidence

- PostgreSQL 17 conformance: all four cases pass, using one in-process suite fixture. The actual `config-machine-state` no-op step runs through the migration runner, followed by a synthetic committed state write. Custody releases/reacquires; a real Gateway lease blocks a second anchor; schema backup refusal names the next step.
- SQLite maintenance inspection: the original implementation and patched implementation both pass the same eleven ordered raw-statement expectation, including writable-schema admission and the `NOT INDEXED` lease scan.
- Production delta: +27 net lines, below the 400-line limit.
- Existing SQLite custody/lock tests: 47 passed. SQLite migration-backup tests: 17 passed.
- Format, targeted lint, and all 29 core test-typecheck shards plus the final core production typecheck passed. Madge reports zero cycles. Worker ratchet: 222 → 222 live calls. Assertion, dialect, timeout, mock-export, and line-cap ratchets passed. One isolated Codex autoreview completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Inherited local gate failures at the base commit: max-lines still lists `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message.test.ts` while the unchanged file is now `.tsx`; Knip reports the unchanged, unused `ui/src/components/loading-skeleton.ts`. No UI files or baseline exceptions are changed here.

Conformance timing: 25.79 seconds in Vitest (about 2 seconds executing the four cases); 128 seconds for the wrapper including cold worker compilation. The initial live-lease test exposed PostgreSQL alias folding and passed after the typed-query fix. A first SQLite backup test attempt was rejected because source changed during worker compilation; the final frozen-source rerun passed.

Draft CI observation for `90c825a832ac5117536859cd217e971987198269`: all 12 checks that ran passed (including TypeScript contracts, Rust workspace, actionlint, PR context/evidence, and Socket). Full CI and `openclaw/ci-gate` were skipped while the PR was draft; this is not full-CI proof.

## Landing validation

Final-head CI: [run 38843454803, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38843454803), head `90c825a832ac5117536859cd217e971987198269`. PostgreSQL conformance passed, including all four maintenance-custody cases; all typechecks, baseline ratchets, and the other selected test jobs passed. No failed/cancelled-job rerun or fix push was needed.

The native admin exception is limited to this unrelated failure and its downstream aggregate:

| Failure | Classification and evidence |
| --- | --- |
| `checks-node-changed-compact-large-18-2`: `src/state/openclaw-agent-db.test.ts` / `serializes concurrent ownership claims for one unowned database` | Unrelated SQLite ownership race: both child openers returned success. The failing test and its owner, `src/state/openclaw-agent-db-schema.ts`, are unchanged; the case invokes `ensureOpenClawAgentDatabaseSchema` on SQLite and does not call the changed PostgreSQL maintenance-custody path. The failed job's executed test-file set is disjoint from this PR's changed files. |
| `openclaw/ci-gate` | Aggregate failure caused by the single test job above; `security-fast` passed independently. |

The earlier local UI gate failures are also present on main and remain outside this PR: Knip reports unused `ui/src/components/loading-skeleton.ts` in [scheduled main run 38841437948](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38841437948/job/116782472083); main `6ce4fb7f39ca751db358b0da9f50f7552b0e8ef3` retains `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message.test.ts` in `config/max-lines-baseline.txt` while the actual file is `.tsx`. Neither UI file nor the baseline is changed here. The final-head CI baseline-ratchet job passed.

prs.title: perf(channels): move ingress polling off the SQLite writer
prs.body:
## Decision

**Measurement says skip; do not merge.** The proposed read-worker migration reduced writer request counts but regressed elapsed time and CPU in a synthetic channel-traffic fixture. Two smaller follow-up experiments also failed to establish non-regression. Production behavior remains unchanged.

## Problem and experiment

Durable ingress polling uses the shared SQLite writer for stale-claim discovery, unsettled listings, and claim preparation. The proposed change moved those reads to the existing reader owner while retaining transactional claim/recovery checks and consolidating health-read routing (net −50 production lines).

Measurements used the real queue/drain API, 30 synthetic channels, fresh isolated state per run, warmup excluded, and three alternating pairs in B/H, H/B, B/H order. All messages completed and queues drained. Native worker diagnostics counted operations and summed queue wait; process CPU includes workers. No production data, Gateway, or channel account was used.

| Candidate / workload | Writer operations before → after | Median summed writer wait before → after | Median elapsed before → after | Median CPU before → after |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Read offload; 600 messages with bounded diagnostic polling | 6,000 → 1,800 | 74.319 → 50.772 s | 1,548 → 1,823 ms | 2,419 → 3,821 ms |
| Read offload; 600 messages, real drain only | 3,600 → 1,800 | 31.944 → 36.678 s | 1,117 → 1,322 ms | 1,667 → 2,641 ms |
| INSERT/UPDATE RETURNING; 3,000 messages, real drain only | 18,000 → 18,000 | 144.479 → 153.076 s | 5,028 → 5,328 ms | 7,551 → 7,762 ms |
| Remove unused audit progress post-insert projection; 3,000 events | 3,000 → 3,000 | 15.180 → 16.014 ms | 1,831 → 2,358 ms | 2,110 → 2,144 ms |

The read-offload drain-only result increased elapsed time **18.4%**, CPU **58.5%**, and writer queue wait **14.8%** despite halving writer request counts. It added 1,800 reader requests with another 24.7 ms of summed reader wait. This moves work between owners without reducing total work.

The initial 150-read burst also exceeded the reader pool's existing 128-task pending limit; the writer baseline accepted it. Normal monitor pumps serialize reads, so that burst is a capacity limit rather than a demonstrated ordinary-pump failure, but it remains relevant stress evidence.

The RETURNING follow-up had a longer warmup and measurement window; elapsed time rose 6.0% and CPU 2.8%, with mixed pair directions. The eight-line audit deletion was CPU-neutral (+1.6%) but wall time was highly variable and all three head/base wall comparisons were slower. Neither follow-up established non-regression, so neither is published in this PR.

## Validation and limits

Focused queue, claim-ownership, and health-cache tests passed (45 tests) for the proposed migration. The later kernel/audit candidate also passed its three focused files (45 tests). Changed-file formatting, repository core lint, and diff checks passed. Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable) found no P0–P2 correctness issues; no operator configuration changed.

These are source-API contention measurements, not a full Gateway/provider workload or a production-sized database reproduction. Queue-wait sums aggregate concurrent requests and are not elapsed time. The ingress fixture emitted no `stateLease.acquire` or `audit.writer.process`; the audit fixture measured the latter separately. Lease renewals already batch by database, and acquisition traffic needs caller/scope attribution before changing retry behavior.

Broad PR CI was not completed because performance rejected the draft. No Testbox/Crabbox lease was allocated. The task-owned synthetic benchmark sandbox was removed after verifying all owned processes had stopped. No schema, stored-format, durability, retention, configuration, or production-runtime change is landed.

prs.title: perf(control-ui): stop sidebar artwork churn during live updates
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated sidebar artwork replacement after a signed-in reload of a dashboard deep link, while live presence and session updates continue. Campaign evidence recorded 3,805–5,116 sidebar mutations after five seconds on a settled page.

## User Impact

Avatars, glyphs, and row actions stay mounted when their visible facts are unchanged. Closed picker options render when opened, with current choices and keyboard selection. Genuine identity, membership, run-state, and selection changes still appear. The existing image-cache and keyed facepile owners remain in place.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retain components instead of rebuilding JSX from whole-row snapshots; preserve settled image state for an unchanged URL; bind row style properties individually; leave closed picker options unmounted. The document overlay observer also stops repeatedly retiring menus that are already hidden and empty, while retaining root cleanup and open/closing invalidation.

Runtime production code is **net −2 lines across five files**. The requested `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD -- ':!*.test.ts' ':!*test-support*' ':!docs/*'` reports 24 files, +527/−203 (net +324), because its exclusions retain TSX tests, benchmark/fixture code, and test helpers; actual runtime is +84/−86. The larger proof diff updates tests that inspected hidden picker options to open the actual picker, adds mutation/lifecycle regressions, and extends the synthetic Team-scale fixture and benchmark probes. No server schema, durable shape, configuration, or compatibility path changes.

## Evidence

### Quiet AWS comparison

One AWS `c7a.4xlarge` lease (`cbx_62858257607f`), headless repository Chromium, production bundles, seven interleaved baseline/candidate pairs; smoke runs excluded. Values are medians with IQR widths in parentheses. The fixture has 300 sessions, 120 people, mixed successful/failed/slow avatar responses, and 125 live events over 20 seconds. One viewer and one run genuinely change through 14 seconds; 14–15 seconds settle; 15–20 seconds publish equivalent heartbeat/receipt facts.

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Sidebar mutation records, live 0–20 s | 12,828 (18) | 1,027 (0) |
| Sidebar mutation records, late 5–20 s | 8,384 (10) | 665 (0) |
| Sidebar mutation records, equivalent-only 15–20 s | 36 (18) | 0 (0) |
| LoAF duration, live window, ms | 4,861 (31) | 3,695 (220.5) |
| LoAF blocking duration, live window, ms | 1,172 (40) | 971 (28) |
| LoAF duration, late window, ms | 3,186 (35) | 2,378 (121) |

prs.title: refactor(ui): render chat composer content with Solid
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The chat composer still passes native Solid controls through Lit template adapters.

## User Impact

Composer menus, notices, attachment actions, and recovery controls keep their existing behavior and markup while rendering directly in Solid. No configuration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the composer content adapter with native children, render icons and existing notice components directly, and remove unused template helpers. Model, microphone, and recovery controls receive plain props at retained Solid owners so refreshes preserve their menus and local state. Pane-supplied component references keep chat-only implementations out of the shared composer's eager imports.

This is the first bounded chat content cutover. Production chat interop importers decrease from **81 to 71** (all chat importers: **124 to 110**); `lib/chat` has none. The remaining transcript, sidebar, and media boundaries follow in separate batches. Production LOC across changed files: **9,225 → 9,233 (+8)**; test LOC: **9,096 → 9,122 (+26)**.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Focused tests | 90 passed across composer content, session controls, copy payload lifetime, question takeover, model-control fixtures, plugin replacement identity, and skill notices |
| UI typecheck | Passed; coupled UI chat test type graph also passed |
| Import cycles | Madge: zero cycles after replacing the broad recovery host type with its consumed contract |
| Scoped lint | Passed after a type-only JSX namespace alias correction |
| Production Knip | Passed after integrating current main; the earlier inherited unused loading-skeleton file has been removed on main |
| Independent review | No actionable P0–P2 findings |
| Same-machine production builds and strict performance check | Pass on base `4cf3df6352cea0` and this change |
| Startup JS gzip | **347,318 B → 347,320 B (+2 B)**; below 374,285 B ceiling; raw bytes unchanged |
| Startup CSS | **1 request / 38,844 B gzip** on both sides |
| Total JS gzip | **10,218,987 B → 10,219,151 B (+164 B after manifest refresh)** |
| Synthetic browser capture | Idle and microphone picker inspected; hover shift remains 0 px |

The open picker capture waits for device discovery to settle; the initial 500 ms head capture still showed its loading state, and a focused follow-up confirmed the same blocked-microphone outcome as the base. Full chat/browser coverage runs in PR CI with `ci:full`.

### Composer

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Composer before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/67c5ce3c-9dac-47dd-8ac1-afe2c9ef52af) | ![Composer after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8f421a70-643d-4c3e-9a29-765ced6ee493) |

### Microphone picker

The generated boot manifest was refreshed after removing the composer adapter. The final production build and strict performance check pass at 347,320 B startup gzip, eight JS requests, and one 38,844 B CSS request. The manifest also catches up already-landed file moves; chat boot now accounts for 33 JS requests / 1,765,561 B, within the 35-request limit.

CI on the initial head exposed five test callers still sending the new component/props recipe to the old template renderer. Those fixtures now mount the retained native model control directly, preserving their permission, materialization, and refresh assertions. All 61 tests across those five files pass. The first isolated permissions retry used an earlier helper location captured during local setup; the final frozen-source run passes 20/20. A stale legacy cleanup call was removed from the catalog fixture. The production increase is ten lines of narrow recovery-host typing that remove a type-import cycle; runtime rendering itself remains smaller.

The repaired composer head `b399b6c93dbe209bfe038c568062988274b67ef8` passed the full CI run [38839789528](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38839789528), including all nine Control UI E2E shards and both real-Gateway shards. Native admission then found real conflicts with newer main. The integration preserves main's deleted copy-button facade and native plugin surface, plus the composer's native recovery and lightbulb icon. UI typecheck, five focused plugin-identity/skill-notice tests, targeted lint, production Knip, and independent review pass for that resolution. One local lint attempt selected the UI typecheck config and timed out generating unrelated plugin declarations; the standard repository core lint config passes. The final merged head `5a943f7e070471a6ef9903a23a074ed6a75ec628` passed [CI run 38842819314](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38842819314): 44 successful jobs, including every Control UI E2E shard and both real-Gateway shards.

prs.title: fix(ai): preserve multiline Google replies and report malformed streams
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing Google Interactions reply content and false success when streaming events span multiple data lines or contain malformed JSON.

## User Impact

Valid multiline streaming events preserve their content. Malformed events fail the request visibly with a content-free diagnostic instead of disappearing before a later successful completion.

## Why This Change Was Made

Assemble complete SSE events before lossless JSON decoding and reuse the canonical malformed-fragment error owner. Keep the existing event reducer, unsafe-integer handling, terminal tool validation, cancellation and pending-cleanup settlement.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- The original adapter (#149880) silently skipped malformed JSON; it cites no human requirement for that recovery. Selected streams now fail rather than omit a text or tool event and falsely report completion.
- Preserve the adapter's existing newline-terminated final-event tolerance at EOF. Completely undelimited final data remains discarded; this does not add stricter SDK EOF semantics or speculative recovery.

Net production LOC: **8 added**. This is a silent-failure bug fix, not a cleanup batch claimed to meet the deletion floor.

## Evidence

- Actual `streamGoogleInteractions` entry point with synthetic external fetch/SSE fixtures: baseline **5 intended failures / 19 passes**, then repaired owner **24/24 passes**. Existing unsafe-integer, immediate DONE, cancellation and terminal-tool cases remain intact.
- Baseline wrapper115.99s / Vitest82.17s; fixed owner Vitest40.03s on the loaded host. One earlier fixed attempt terminated137 before assertions and is not counted as proof. No timeout, retry or skip change.
- Targeted production/test graph typecheck and source-backed type-aware lint pass. Formatting, whitespace, changed-check dry-run and single-page MDX checks pass.
- Suppression inventory **2/3**: untouched `code-mode-node.watchdog.test-support.ts` adds one entry beyond the inherited allowlist (95 versus94). Neither that helper nor the allowlist changed; no suppression was added.
- Installed pinned Google SDK source independently confirms multiline SSE data is joined before JSON parsing. No live provider request or credential proof is claimed.
- Runtime import-cycle scan passes with **0 cycles**. Full static-SCC scan is a hosted-CI requirement, not a local passing claim. Fresh independent P0-P2 review is **scoped-clean** (confidence0.96). Exact-head hosted CI is the broad gate.

prs.title: fix(memory-wiki): preserve lint report notes on read errors
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Wiki lint can discard existing report notes when reading the report fails for a reason other than absence.

## User Impact

An unreadable lint report now produces a visible filesystem error and keeps its original bytes. Resolve the access or I/O error and run lint again. Missing reports still receive their normal template; no migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The report writer treated every failed read as a missing file and could atomically replace an existing report from a blank template. It now uses the existing page-read owner with a Node ENOENT-only fallback. Strict UTF-8 decoding, frontmatter admission, atomic publication, file modes and synchronization remain unchanged.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Persistent report-read failures are no longer successful lint runs. The broad catch predates the extraction in #165407 and persisted through #168583; neither inspected description establishes a partial-success contract. The real lint-boundary regression reaches an injected EACCES and demonstrates the existing silent success. No human-use incident is claimed as provenance.
- Earlier compile updates are not rolled back if the later lint report read fails. The report stays intact, and the next run can refresh derived output after the filesystem problem is resolved. Existing bounded read recovery is reused; no new retry loop, custody mechanism or public surface is added.

## Net LOC

Production: **3 net lines added** (+16/-13 in one file). Tests: +49. Documentation: +4. This is a reproduced silent-failure/data-preservation bug fix, not cleanup deletion credit. Phase E standalone session memory and its factory, registry, expiry, federation and tests are untouched.

## Evidence

- Baseline: the actual compiler runs, then the test arms a persistent EACCES at the lint writer's report read. Injection is confirmed, but lint resolves successfully instead of returning that error. Selected regression fails for the intended reason; canonical exit 1. Total wall about 1,012s, Vitest 852.50s (97% transform), test case 3.907s on the heavily loaded host. Existing cases excluded by baseline selection are not source skips.
- Regression test graph and fixed production graph typechecks pass; formatter and diff whitespace pass. Runtime import cycles: zero.
- Fresh independent review through P2: scoped-clean, patch correct (0.97), no accepted/actionable findings after final source verification.
- Fixed: **44 tests pass across five Wiki owner/sibling files**, plus **3 suppression tests**. This covers lint, existing-page read recovery, page writes, compile and apply. Canonical exit 0 after completed-generation verification, 1,342.71s total wall; Wiki shard 1,077.72s (86% transform). The new regression takes 1.404s. Existing missing-report creation, malformed UTF-8/frontmatter refusal, Notes preservation, authority/publication checks and atomic-write failure assertions stay intact. No new retries, timeouts, skips or suppressions.
- Runtime import cycles: 0; Madge import cycles: 0 (exit 0).
- Changed-check passes conflict markers, line-cap growth, max-lines suppression and assertion-safety ratchets. It also reports an unrelated local environment-name budget mismatch (452 names against 453), without any environment-name change in this diff or the preceding cleanup squash; no baseline edit or inherited-CI waiver is claimed. The broad run was deliberately stopped and its owned process tree drained after it entered the unrelated SQLite worker ratchet. No full changed-check pass is claimed.
- Targeted type-aware lint failed during SDK declaration preparation at its existing 300,000ms deadline, before lint executed. No lint pass, code-failure attribution or inherited-CI waiver is claimed. Exact-head PR CI remains the broad gate.

All runtime proof uses isolated task-owned HOME, OpenClaw state/config and XDG directories. No operator Gateway/state, remote runner, dependency, schema, durability, retention or permission change.

Related: #173512

## What Problem This Solves

Factory-backed Enterprise session reads need a current-person repository admission path and a cleanup-owned GitHub App reader before private previews can be enabled.

## User Impact

Explicit foreground session reads can obtain an App token for the selected repository while retaining the person's current account and session authority. OAuth, native GitHub, and public reads keep their existing behavior. App publication, background reads, and shell execution remain unsupported and refuse before token issuance.

## Why This Change Was Made

The verified configured-host handshake principal and current resident profile catalog bind a one-use proof to the session and item digest. The existing private broker RPC redeems that proof, and its receipt must match the exact actor, App, installation, repository, and session before token issuance. The reader retains that authority through private requests; its owner awaits revocation before returning content.

The base has no App reader, so the prerequisite includes issuer verification, App config/SecretRef resolution, child-secret scrubbing, and status labeling. The generated configuration budget grows by 30 paths for system and agent App selections. No worker, chat admission, background repository authority, or publication lifecycle port is included.

Depends on [#173652](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173652); the lower identity layer is [#173513](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173513). That parent retains known issuer-sensitive consumer P2 findings and unfinished live/upgrade qualification. This PR is not a stack-wide deployment/readiness claim.

## Evidence

CI repair completed the extracted schema wrapper inventory and generated App SecretRef matrix, moved the shared App selection type to its existing leaf owner, preserved lightweight mock exports, and corrected the new method’s introduction metadata. No exemption, baseline expansion, dependency change, or runtime workaround was added.

- Exact head `48916909635a212a6596a4fc1811be329dd10e48`: clean supported `pnpm build` passed in 3m 6.5s; both clean build stamps and build info match that head. Source archive SHA256: `881a6284196324c6644a6ff228a0fa8cbaba1376d41eba003e1b8e9c5ea74539`.
- Focused group: 111 tests passed. The retired-principal regression failed before repair; 25 authority/admission tests then passed. Final App/native/OAuth identity scope: 35 tests passed; OAuth lifecycle: 43 passed. Unchanged proof was reused after the parent update; published history is preserved with ordinary merges.
- Core/UI types, targeted lint/format, config docs, full protocol/native determinism checks, and UI i18n verification passed. CI repair verification passed: 18 wrapper-closure tests, 14 registered RPC/receipt tests, 9 App-reader tests, the SecretRef matrix sync test, mock-export ratchet, and both import-cycle guards. Independent whole-change and focused P0/P1 reviews found no actionable findings.
- Simplification retained only `session-item-read`; removed worker/dispatch/chat/publication purposes and unsupported App execution paths. Necessary production delta: +1234/-110 lines, including the absent App issuer/config/secret dependency. Tests: +975/-1.

The full local provisioning file passed 15 cases with one Linux-only skip; its final macOS APFS cold/warm/sparse case timed out at the existing 120-second budget. All three provisioning cases that failed on the old PR head passed. The APFS timeout remains a qualification gap; no timeout or assertion was weakened. The pane parent supplies its independently verified application-context fixture correction.

Proof uses isolated synthetic catalog/API/broker fixtures. It does not redeem live grants, exercise external authenticated APIs, deploy, restart a service, or qualify the original checkout.

prs.title: fix: files read through safe handles truncate on WSL/9p mounts
prs.body:
Related: #145589

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: media, Claw workspace sources, skill files, backup config captures, memory exports, systemd unit snapshots, and Canvas/browser-hosted files can be read truncated when they live on a WSL/9p (or similar) mount.

## User Impact

User impact: files that OpenClaw reads through its safe-open path come back complete on filesystems that return short reads, instead of silently losing their tail. No behavior change on ordinary local disks.

## Why This Change Was Made

`@openclaw/fs-safe` opens read handles with `O_NONBLOCK`. Node's `FileHandle.readFile()` treats a short read as EOF when the stat size is known, so on WSL/9p it returns a prefix of the file. fs-safe 0.26.5 (adopted in #172306, upstream openclaw/fs-safe#983) already replaced its own uncapped `readFile()` calls with `readFileHandleBounded`, a `handle.read()` loop that reads to EOF under a byte cap. OpenClaw still called `handle.readFile()` directly on handles it got from fs-safe opens; this PR moves every such production call to `readFileHandleBounded` so there is one read owner for these handles.

Core imports it from `@openclaw/fs-safe/advanced`; the browser and Canvas plugins use the documented `openclaw/plugin-sdk/file-access-runtime` export. Call sites with an existing byte cap pass it (media store `maxBytes`, managed-image thumbnail `maxBytes`, Claw `MAX_MANAGED_FILE_BYTES`, memory export `MAX_MEMORY_HOST_PUBLIC_EXPORT_BYTES`); the rest pass `Infinity`, matching the old uncapped read. Where the old code decoded utf8, the new code decodes the returned buffer.

<details>
<summary>Site list</summary>

Converted (handle from an fs-safe open, or opened with explicit `O_NONBLOCK`):

| Site | Handle origin | Cap |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `extensions/browser/src/browser/extension-native-host-file.ts` | `root().open` | `Infinity` |
| `extensions/canvas/src/host/a2ui-route.ts` (HTML utf8 + binary) | `root().open` via `resolveFileWithinRoot` | `Infinity` |
| `extensions/canvas/src/host/a2ui.ts` | `root().open` via `resolveFileWithinRoot` | `Infinity` |
| `src/claws/reader.ts` | `root().open` | `MAX_MANAGED_FILE_BYTES` |
| `src/daemon/systemd-definition-mutation.ts` | `fs.open(O_RDONLY \| O_NOFOLLOW \| O_NONBLOCK)` | `Infinity` |
| `src/gateway/managed-image-thumbnail-cache.ts` (was in `managed-image-attachments.ts`) | `openLocalFileSafely` | `maxBytes ?? Infinity` |
| `src/infra/backup-config-capture.ts` | `openLocalFileSafely` | `Infinity` |
| `src/media/store.ts` (`readMediaBuffer`) | `fileStore().open` | `maxBytes` |
| `src/plugin-sdk/memory-host-core.ts` (utf8) | `root().open` | `MAX_MEMORY_HOST_PUBLIC_EXPORT_BYTES` |
| `src/plugin-sdk/memory-host-event-export.ts` (two utf8 reads + one buffer) | `root().open` | `Infinity` |
| `src/skills/lifecycle/skill-change-hook.ts` | `root().open` | `Infinity` |

Intentionally unchanged (plain blocking `fs.open`, not fs-safe/nonblocking): `src/agents/worktrees/checkout-apfs.ts`, `src/agents/worktrees/snapshot-exact-state.ts`, `src/daemon/launchd-service-files.ts`.

After this change, `git grep -n -E '([Hh]andle|opened|fh)[A-Za-z_]*\.readFile\(' -- 'src/**/*.ts' 'extensions/**/*.ts' ':!*.test.ts' ':!*test-support*'` lists only those three.

</details>

Behavior notes:

- Claw workspace sources that exceed the per-file cap while being read still return the same `workspace_source_too_large` diagnostic; only `too-large` is caught, other read errors propagate as before.
- Media store and thumbnail reads drop their post-read size checks; the bounded read now enforces the cap and throws fs-safe's `too-large` error (same `FsSafeError` class and code for the media store). Their stat pre-checks are unchanged.
- Accepted edge: a memory export that grows past its 1 MiB cap between the stat pre-check and the read now throws `too-large` instead of reading the oversized file. This is rare, visible, and recoverable on the next pass.
- `skill-change-hook.test.ts` no longer spies on `handle.readFile`; that hook went dead with this change, and the existing `handle.read` spy now covers the content read.

## Evidence

- New regression in `src/media/store.test.ts` (`finishes short nonblocking media reads`): an fs-safe `afterOpen` test hook makes the first `handle.read` a real one-byte read, and `readMediaBuffer` returns the full content. It fails against the old `handle.readFile()` line (`expected false to be true`: Node's `readFile` never reaches `handle.read`) and passes with the fix.
- Focused tests, all green (`pnpm test ... --maxWorkers=1`, 208 tests in 7 lanes): `src/media/store.test.ts`, `src/skills/lifecycle/skill-change-hook.test.ts`, `src/claws/reader.test.ts`, `src/infra/backup-config-capture.test.ts`, `src/plugin-sdk/memory-host-core.test.ts`, `src/plugin-sdk/memory-host-event-export.test.ts`, `src/daemon/systemd-definition-mutation.test.ts`, `src/gateway/managed-image-attachments.test.ts`, `extensions/canvas/src/host/a2ui.test.ts`, `extensions/canvas/src/host/file-resolver.test.ts`, `extensions/browser/src/browser/extension-native-host.test.ts`.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, core oxlint on the touched core files, `oxfmt` on all touched files, and `git diff --check`: clean.
- Gap: extension lint/typecheck did not complete locally (the plugin-sdk boundary declaration step timed out on a heavily loaded host); PR CI covers it. No live WSL/9p run; the regression injects the short read directly at the `FileHandle.read` boundary.

Thanks @Hawk5150 for the original report.

prs.title: fix: background updates fail after installing a new version
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes managed source updates that activate a valid candidate and then roll back because the running updater first imports a backup chunk from its replaced runtime.

## User Impact

The retained backup child can take the required pre-migration capture after activation, including when the parent holds exclusive SQLite maintenance ownership. Retained PostgreSQL stores belonging to disabled plugins remain discoverable, and their existing custody checks remain in effect.

This repairs the installed updater. A candidate cannot change an older updater already executing; an affected installation may need the documented source-checkout bootstrap once.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move lazy engine discovery into the existing retained backup child. Prepare installed-plugin and bundled-discovery facts from a private SQLite snapshot through their existing owners, retaining original resource roots and the source environment. An operation cache owns those facts until asynchronous discovery settles.

Canonical inventory, rehearsal exclusions, disk admission, capture and restore checks remain with the same owners. There is no new worker, protocol, public API, persistent state, or authority mechanism.

## Evidence

- The original compiled owner fails with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` after its installed `dist` is physically relocated.
- The initial PR revision reproduces the subsequent maintenance refusal with a real physical maintenance owner held across that same replacement. The final compiled revision passes the identical experiment, preserves the payload and machine-state row, and leaves source bytes unchanged.
- Four focused final-source cases pass: cold SQLite capture; real maintenance capture with native `preserveSourceArtifacts` flags and persisted metadata; disabled-plugin PostgreSQL custody refusal using a persisted install record; original SQLite/WAL/SHM byte preservation.
- Core and changed-test typing, scoped lint/format, docs checks, and the full pinned build pass. Build time: 6m03.6s. Fresh independent full-owner review found no P0–P2 issues. The maintenance follow-up kept the repair in the existing owner (production +55/-11, tests +120, docs +8); the later path follow-up is recorded below.

Inspectable synthetic reproduction output:

```text
Before: State schema inspection failed (exit): ... during database backup ...
OpenClaw state at <synthetic-state>/state/openclaw.sqlite is undergoing offline maintenance
After: post-swap cold database snapshot preserved under real maintenance ownership
Exit code: 0
```

The regression is in `src/infra/update-database-backup.runtime.test.ts`. The focused command is:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/update-database-backup.runtime.test.ts src/infra/update-database-backup.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'keeps first-use|seals equivalent original bytes'
```

## Relative Plugin Discovery Follow-up

Latest head: `6f5d289c2e40743366e54253a05b5df54f9e9ac0`. The three published blobs match the frozen, checked source.

Fixed the P1 in [the relative plugin-path review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173616#discussion_r4290306943). The existing backup parent now resolves configured `plugins.load.paths` through `resolveUserPath` while the invocation-directory scope is still active, then sends those paths through the existing config field. The retained child's parked working directory and cold discovery boundary stay intact; this adds no protocol, state, or environment variable.

The regression uses the real retained child with `plugins.load.paths: ["./extensions/workboard"]`, the plugin disabled, bundled discovery disabled, and no persisted plugin install record. Its synthetic PostgreSQL anchor must reach the existing exclusive-custody refusal before any external export. The parent cold backup import is made unavailable by the existing runtime-replacement fixture; the child's code and plugin discovery run normally.

- Negative control on production blob `e61c2d28fe36d12cc3535510b16328c985547901` from `f587422858e00bc3e708e1f3d1f05a0a3b8ba12e`: the relative case fails because capture incorrectly succeeds with shared SQLite state only, instead of rejecting for PostgreSQL custody.
- Fixed production blob `0060354d6ce430f0702586d4885fceebc8afd4ec`: all four retained-child runtime cases pass, including relative and persisted PostgreSQL discovery, stopped SQLite capture, and maintenance-owned SQLite capture. Source database bytes remain unchanged. Runtime shard: 82.28 s including 55.00 s worker compilation; test execution: 12.75 s.
- Targeted typecheck, scoped lint, formatting, docs inventory, and patch whitespace checks pass. `pnpm build:runtime` passes in 2 min 47.2 s, including CLI bootstrap imports, built plugin closures, plugin assets, Control UI budgets, and startup metadata.
- Fresh canonical `autoreview`, scoped to the patch and P0–P2, reports `scoped-clean` with no actionable finding. Review is static; the executable evidence comes from the separate runtime checks above.

This follow-up uses isolated synthetic state and does not contact an external PostgreSQL service. The earlier real managed-update receipt remains evidence for its original `f587` source; it is not relabeled as a full live deployment of this follow-up. Final source identities and a compact red/green trace are provided separately for inspection.


## Managed-update Evidence at the Prior Maintenance Head

The following real cold managed source update ran with the `f5874228` backup-owner source, before the relative-path follow-up. It completed through the shipped entry point:

```text
gateway RPC: update.run, params {}
managed command: openclaw update --yes
database snapshot after activation: exit 0, 52.895 s, 8 nonempty SQLite captures
final updater exit: 0
handoff finalizer exit: 0
recorded run: status=succeeded, phase=finished
verification: booted=true, serviceRunning=true, versionMatch=true
verification: channelsReady=true, readyz=true, coreReady=true, settled=true
running version: 2026.10.3
```

This was an integrated installation with the separate Git retry and channel readiness fixes already present. There was no target-ref override or intervention during the managed run. The ordinary source update preserved all four local repair commits; the configuration was semantically unchanged. A fresh HTTP readiness request after the helper exited also returned ready/coreReady true.

The real run took about 26 minutes, including 12m23s of Gateway downtime. The old Gateway reached its existing stop deadline and systemd terminated it before activation continued; this was not a graceful stop. The updater also retained snapshots after detecting later database writes whose writer it could not attribute, so this run does not claim automatic database rollback eligibility. Neither advisory prevented verified activation.

External PostgreSQL export/restore remains outside this proof. The isolated disabled-plugin case verifies that the existing custody refusal remains enforced.

prs.title: feat(qa): compare recorded Decision answers offline
prs.body:
Related: #156341 (historical context; closed as not planned)

## What Problem This Solves

QA authors need to inspect how recorded Decision answers compare with explicit references without making another model call or dropping failed and unscored cases.

## User Impact

There is no change to normal agent behavior. The existing QA Lab confidence-report command gains an opt-in offline replay lane: JSON retains each identifiable case, its captured answer and provenance; Markdown summarizes agreement, disagreement, and unscored counts.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is a standalone QA contribution, not a dependency of the withdrawn task-routing proposal. It changes no core routing, model selection, provider execution, SDK export, runtime configuration, or dependency. It remains useful for reviewing recorded JEV, local Decision-model, or other compatible typed results without adopting a new routing contract.

The replay compares Choice acceptable sets, explicit Boolean thresholds/operators, and inclusive Score intervals against scorer-only reviewed references. It preserves original probabilities and optional confidence. Missing, unreviewed, disputed, or unscorable references remain unscored; malformed and failed executions fail pipeline integrity separately from semantic disagreement. A valid replay can pass while answers disagree with references.

This does not run a live benchmark, certify model quality, measure calibration, enable consumers, or settle the closed RFC's broader evaluation roadmap. Repeat/group metadata is retained without treating repeats as independent samples. The existing report remains the only file-reading/output owner.

## Evidence

### October 10 maintenance rebase

Current head `ec7b620198aefa13063d23ce3f42d8b8824c47fe`, tested main `0aee279a71af78b8914dced0507ddb94c0d1f5b0`. Existing contribution behavior is preserved; no dependency, configuration or migration change is added by this refresh.

Focused Decision evaluator, confidence-report and Markdown suites: 88/88 passed; changed-source formatting/lint and whitespace checks passed. All three contribution commits are patch-equivalent. The earlier actual offline CLI replay evidence is retained for unchanged contribution behavior; this is not a new CLI execution. QA-owner sponsorship/adoption remains a maintainer decision.

Fresh independent Astra source/integration review found no actionable source defect. Current-head hosted CI and completed ClawSweeper review are pending after publication; older-head CI/review below are historical, not certification of this head. Main advanced to `dd036a4b1d855c366c7b3148a1814c83da765e50`; none of this PR’s changed paths intersects that base drift. Rollback is the prior head `d6d8e6a8871ab2f163459201b90ab5b41bb7af66`.

<details>
<summary>Retained pre-rebase evidence and review history (not current-head CI)</summary>


### October 8 rebase — current local evidence

prs.title: perf(gateway): resolve session event targets once per recipient
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session event fan-out repeatedly resolves the same session target while deciding whether a named recipient may receive a suggestion or draft typing event.

## User Impact

Authorization decisions and live revocation behavior stay unchanged. The broadcaster does less synchronous work per recipient, without retaining authorization decisions across requests, recipients, or awaited work.

## Why This Change Was Made

Combine visibility and event-specific participation checks in one pass over the event's session keys. Remove the single-use sharing snapshot allocation and second target lookup. Missing rows, incognito sessions, draft ownership, role caps, suggestion authorship, and membership remain enforced by the existing policy owner. Production delta: 21 fewer lines; no new cache, configuration, or stored format.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/gateway/session-sharing.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 17/17 passed (76.89 s warm wrapper; expanded event test 2.53 s; initial cold run 252.75 s). Covers the existing decision matrix plus multi-key author/hidden-target cases and membership add/revocation between deliveries.
- Changed-file formatting, lint, and whitespace checks only; broad validation is delegated to PR CI. No Testbox/Crabbox lease used.
- Isolated Linux sandbox measurement: 5,000 synthetic session metadata rows, 24 profiles, 30 non-admin recipients, 3,334 memberships, real broadcaster/projection/membership owners, synthetic in-memory transports. Three alternating pairs, each 400 warmups + 2,000 measured broadcasts; identical per-recipient delivery vectors for every fixture event and measured sample. Median calling-thread CPU per broadcast:

  | Event | Before | After | Reduction |
  | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
  | Ordinary message | 57.17 µs | 54.73 µs | 4.3% |
  | Suggestion | 65.56 µs | 57.80 µs | 11.8% |
  | Draft typing | 57.87 µs | 47.50 µs | 17.9% |

  Suggestion target resolutions dropped from 51.418 to 30 per broadcast; draft typing from 50.75 to 30. The existing broadcaster and prepared policy checks remain in the timing. Benchmark-only runner: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/session-sharing.test.ts -t 'benchmarks repeated-policy' --maxWorkers=1` with a temporary harness (96.83 s including cold artifacts; measurement/fixture body 6.36 s). This measures synchronous fan-out, not network latency or end-to-end RPC CPU. No production data or Gateway used.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): clean at P0/P1/P2. The autoreview helper refused the requested provider because it did not match the operator configuration; no configuration was changed.

The initial lint command used the root TypeScript config and timed out preparing unrelated plugin declarations. Final changed-file lint passed using `config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json`; no broad local validation was rerun. The added tests were reduced to fit the existing 1,000-line limit.

prs.title: perf(sqlite): avoid scratch databases during schema admission
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway schema admission constructs temporary SQLite databases to rediscover the expected schema in each process. That repeats scratch DDL and PRAGMA work before inspecting the real database.

## User Impact

Startup and first-use schema admission do less SQLite work while retaining the existing compatibility and drift checks. There are no schema-version changes, migrations, or operator actions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing PostgreSQL schema generator now records exact SQLite catalogs for declared shared-state, agent, and daemon runtime-pin fragments, including supported upgrade-start definitions. Runtime admission compares a fingerprint of normalized sqlite_schema SQL and native table_xinfo, index_xinfo, and foreign_key_list facts. Full diagnostic facts live in per-store JSON and load only on mismatch, historical compatibility, or explicit repair. Normalization preserves expression text; DEFAULT, CHECK, partial-index predicate, and trigger-body drift remain rejected.

This removes scratch-template construction, cache capture/adoption, environment transfer, and empty-install template warmup. The generator accepts computed fragments and build-only extension setup so memory owners can use the same path. The explicit dynamic memory-migration builder remains until that owner's cutover; it is not a fallback for undeclared static schemas. PostgreSQL outputs and required minimum versions are unchanged.

Generated output is 56,482 bytes of TypeScript plus 595,692 bytes of lazy JSON. A build plugin emits the JSON as relocatable installed assets, and compiled test workers use the same plugin. The larger JSON remains outside executable chunks and TypeScript checking.

Removed redundant work and accepted edges:

- Runtime reconstruction of committed expected schemas: generated facts are authoritative; source changes require regeneration, enforced by db:postgres:check.
- Cross-process comparison-contract capture/adoption and prewarming: each process reads the same generated fingerprints; no mutable contract cache needs synchronization.
- Extra ordinary indexes and unrelated objects remain compatible; unexpected uniqueness and canonical-object drift still fail admission.

## Evidence

Focused proof passes: 109 catalog-equivalence cases, 20 generator tests, 41 runtime/index/snapshot/worker tests (one existing native-authorizer skip), and the relocated installed-asset test. The cold-worker regression observes zero scratch DDL and zero diagnostic JSON reads on canonical admission, then detects an in-process schema write and loads diagnostics once. The four drift probes are rejected.

Equivalence compares generated facts with native scratch catalogs for every distinct declared fragment and covers fresh stores plus every supported upgrade-start definition. It does not claim to replace historical data-migration suites.

Formatting, basic lint, and the final Codex review pass (two rounds; no actionable P0–P2 findings). The published-driver update cell passed from published 2026.10.4 to candidate: readiness, running version, durable/incognito session persistence, and service stop were verified. Post-integration CI at `d248ec660637` passed security, production/test types, lint, source contracts, architecture, and ratchets. It exposed an unregistered daemon runtime-pin schema introduced on main; this PR registers that unchanged DDL and tests existing-store reopening and restore. The three alternating harness-v3 pairs completed. Measurements use isolated synthetic state and make no wall-time claims. The remote check:changed run lost transport after type and boundary checks; scoped type-aware lint and export-collision checks passed separately; the local Knip scan has inherited findings undergoing exact-main attribution. A final-head update-cell allocation queued and was cancelled immediately, so the earlier update pass remains prior-head evidence.

Three alternating pairs compare `ffcb0a8cfa75` with `9e9fd87e3549` (the six-query collector). Phase values are median [min–max]. Requests count sends.

| Phase | Base SQL / requests / MAIN | Candidate SQL / requests / MAIN |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Boot | 478 [477–489] / 92 [92–95] / 193 [193–193] | 362 [359–363] / 95 [95–95] / 72 [71–72] |
| Connect | 341 [324–345] / 16 [16–19] / 0 | 73 [68–231] / 20 [16–20] / 0 |
| First turn | 1024 [1017–1026] / 164 [159–170] / 9 [5–9] | 1014 [872–1063] / 157 [154–171] / 9 [0–13] |
| Boot + connect + first | 1840 [1837–1844] / 275 [270–278] / 202 [198–202] | 1465 [1450–1490] / 272 [269–282] / 80 [72–85] |
| Warmed raw turn, pooled 30 | 75 [74–106] / 28 [27–34] / 0 [0–8] | 75.5 [74–101] / 28 [27–33] / 0 [0–9] |
| Warmed causal turn, pooled 30 | 75 [74–82] / 28 [27–31] / 0 | 75 [74–82] / 28 [27–31] / 0 |
| Restart boot + connect + first | 815 [792–822] / 239 [237–240] / 83 | 786 [784–833] / 240 [239–241] / 83 |
| Whole workload | 4639 [4592–4643] / 1159 [1154–1161] / 307 | 4219 [4217–4277] / 1160 [1160–1164] / 186 [185–186] |

Warmed causal totals are identical: 2,272 SQL / 850 requests / 0 MAIN. The median of per-run raw warmed medians is 75.5 on both sides, and pooled raw totals fall 2,348→2,342 SQL / 859→857 requests. All five required shared read families remain zero; separately classified entry-cache exact reads remain 1.2 SQL / 1.1 containing requests per turn. Every run has the same 13 background lease-expiry MAIN reads distributed between first and warmed windows; none is turn-caused.

The original candidate removes exactly 403 static scratch statements in every run, including 121 MAIN, but adds 14 catalog reads over 14 cold captures (net −389). The final repair fuses index-list and index-term reads: five catalog queries, matching the previous collector's count while retaining strict facts. All 109 equivalence cases and the five-query budget test pass. Final-head sanity pair: pending.

The whole-workload request median varies by +1 in the original pairs. Catalog operations use the same containing requests; no schema work occurs on warmed turns. A 48-SQL background transcript-index invocation appears in candidate1 and baseline2/3 with identical statements. The original candidate's real +2 first-turn causal catalog reads are removed by the final query fusion, not attributed to noise.

T1 remains **222 → 222** globally and **0 → 0** in changed files. T1-compat stays 12, T2 stays 397, T3 stays 341, and worker sites stay 1,306. Dialect counts: mechanical 4 → 4, design 22 → 22, maintenance 49 → 37. Madge reports zero cycles.

Diff against integrated main `7740cd562dcc`: 96 files, +4,189/-1,308 lines. Production/tooling: 50 files, +1,988/-904; tests/support: 38 files, +680/-401; documentation: +18/-3; generated output: seven files, +1,503 lines. The full diagnostic catalogs are data assets and do not enter TypeScript checking.


Pre-integration [CI run 38836198627](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38836198627) has three inherited failing leaf jobs and the aggregate gate. All failing files below are unchanged by this PR:

- Agent database `serializes concurrent ownership claims for one unowned database`: matching two-success assertion reproduced on untouched base `ffcb0a8cfa75f189abbbf425180907c797522767`. The owner reads metadata before the write transaction; this existing ownership issue is routed to its repair owner.
- UI test TS2304 at `chat-pane-model-catalog.test.ts:167`: exact message in [main job 116765909164](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38836157770/job/116765909164). Upstream fix `56c315156f4542f197a2b7f727681ba3f41c21b5` removes the stale Lit cleanup call.

The upstream UI fix is included. Post-integration head `d248ec660637` passed types, lint, source contracts, architecture, security, and ratchets. Its PostgreSQL conformance job was cancelled by the repair push and is not passing evidence. Repair head `5fed5ffb4b10` registers the daemon runtime-pin catalog and passes changed-file type-aware lint; CI, focused packaging/restore, SDK comparison, and the final sanity pair are pending. No failing test or static check is reported as passing.

prs.title: fix(update): reduce snapshot writes on copy-on-write filesystems
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Strict update/Doctor checks and recovery-generation inspection rewrote entire private SQLite snapshots, even when Btrfs could share their unchanged storage.

## User Impact

Artifact-preserving snapshots now use copy-on-write cloning when supported, including Btrfs NOCOW sources copied into ordinary staging directories. Unsupported filesystems retain the full-copy fallback. Source comparisons and generation hashes still run, so their read cost is unchanged.

A source replacement during guarded copy admission stops that snapshot rather than retrying: helper errors cannot safely distinguish source drift from simultaneous destination, I/O, or cleanup failure. Unambiguous source-only drift retains the existing bounded retry.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing guarded synchronous copier at the canonical snapshot owner instead of the forced streaming loop. Consume fs-safe 0.26.6, whose Linux copier matches the source NOCOW policy only on its newly created private target before attempting a clone. Source files and parent-directory policies remain unchanged.

Retain the original source pin, safe alias resolution, exclusive destination creation, fsync, source revalidation, WAL coherence, private-only checkpointing, and cleanup. No schema, configuration, protocol, staging-placement, or runtime changes are required.

Qualification also exposed three inherited CI failures. This branch declares the existing memory-core Kysely runtime imports at the same 0.29.6 version as core, corrects two Codex fixture expectations to preserve the actual validated terminal object without inventing `itemsView`, and incorporates the already-landed UI test cleanup through base `56c315156f4542f197a2b7f727681ba3f41c21b5`. Codex production behavior and exact-object/lifecycle assertions remain unchanged. The implementer personally checked the [Codex Turn contract](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/414782450952a196bbb64b1605a458c2531c47b6/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/thread_data.rs#L188-L219) and [terminal emitter](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/414782450952a196bbb64b1605a458c2531c47b6/codex-rs/app-server/src/bespoke_event_handling.rs#L1345-L1366).

## Evidence

- Fresh full-candidate independent review against the named baseline completed with zero P0, P1, P2, or P3 findings. Formatting and diff checks passed. The implementer and independent dependency reviewer inspected the exact dependency implementation; the isolated reviewer could not independently retrieve that release source and used the supplied contract evidence.
- Published fs-safe 0.26.6 is bound to the reviewed [dependency repair](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/pull/991); all 21 [release jobs](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/actions/runs/38771544319) passed, and integrity/provenance were verified for all 11 published packages. All 13 direct consumers and the generated lock are aligned. The subsequent Kysely lock generation changed only its memory-core importer; all other package, snapshot, and package-manager records were preserved.
- With that published native package and the existing Bun runtime, a 32 MiB synthetic Btrfs NOCOW source copied into the default destination policy reported `clone`: 18.492 ms through fsync, 32,768 physical bytes written, and zero physical bytes read. Initial digests matched; distinct inodes and a private-target edit proved source independence. Parent policies remained unchanged and owned cleanup completed. The previous dependency on the same route wrote 33,636,352 bytes via `copy-file-range`.
- Regression coverage includes native/fallback snapshots, source and sidecar identity, symlink retargeting, terminal copy/fsync failures, quota reporting, concurrent writers, and cleanup. [Current-head consumer CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38843724694) is running for `c4ce26f2e1e92590e27e05b97cecde6e3b35b75e`; its exact-head gates remain pending. The four snapshot implementation/test files are unchanged from the preceding reviewed candidate. No local dependency-backed test, deployment, or end-to-end UI latency result is claimed.
- The preceding candidate `e5154362502310ada799dd66df7b68fa24130ef7` passed the native [published-updater × candidate cell](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38837443818/job/116774595369) in 618 seconds, with joined cleanup and no cell failures; package integrity also passed. The aggregate Package Acceptance run **failed** its separate installed-tree budget: 47,517 entries against 47,500, below the shipped updater cap of 50,000. A fresh updater cell is required for the current head; the prior result is not relabeled as current-head proof.

Production delta: +21 lines; test delta: +140 lines; dependency metadata net delta: +4 lines. Production growth preserves source-alias admission and error ownership while removing the forced streaming-copy path.

Named follow-ups:

- **Acquisition-owned generation evidence:** reduce repeated full-family reads safely. Blindly halving hash passes weakens change detection: committed WAL-prefix snapshots and whole-WAL generation hashes cover different bytes, and normalized backup digests differ from committed-content digests.
- **Installed package entry-budget headroom:** the separate acceptance guard remains failed. Verified published fs-safe archives have identical file inventories across 0.26.5 and 0.26.6, with unchanged native-package topology. Of 343 entries added since the prior passing package candidate, 289 came from SDK upgrades already in the base. No exact base-package receipt establishes whether that base itself exceeded the budget. This PR neither raises the cap nor claims an inherited-only exemption for this failure.

prs.title: refactor: deslop auto-reply, provider and channel remainders (wave-6 bundle B)
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Auto-reply, providers, and channel adapters repeat parsing and lifecycle bookkeeping after their owning producers have already prepared the facts.

## User Impact

This is an internal simplification, with no new configuration or migration. Live effect authority, credential-use checks, persisted-input validation, FIFO ordering, durability, and ordinary shutdown settlement remain with their existing owners. Phase E session-memory owners are unchanged. No changelog changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bundle the pushed wave-6 remainders, credited to lanes z03, z11, and z09:

- z03: finalized auto-reply facts, one queue lifecycle-state owner, normalized payload outcomes, and existing runtime/typing/effect owners. Only `z03-2-typed-facts` is included; the superseded auto-reply branch is excluded.
- z11: admitted provider/model/startup facts, existing Tencent catalog family, shared transcript byte accounting, normalized deadlines, and shared schema slot inventories.
- z09: channel sibling facts, native Discord REST owner, Matrix verification/migration facts, and tail owner cleanup. z09-12 supersedes z09-10. z09-15 includes only cleanup `99bb445aff6` and test-only `b1d424cc82a`, not its already-landed component-registry parent. Parked Telegram work is excluded.

Combined delta against pinned base `5462f7f146436a50a56354dd39f8405eaeb5b60f`: **702 net production lines removed** (+939/-1641), **723 net lines removed overall** (+1615/-2338). Tests/support/config account for the remaining 21 net removals. Conflict integration keeps main's WebChat Resume recovery wording, type-only Vydra auth import, and newer Discord/Slack test helpers and assertions.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

Auto-reply trusts internal prepared facts rather than rereading diagnostic preferences, comparing a selected recovery database again, or deep-copying a private completion input twice. Unsupported reentrant actor acquisition/claim replacement gets no compensation; an installed transition may acknowledge while shutdown starts during old-resource release. Steering no longer treats an equal-valued fallback replacement or preparatory generation change as a separate protocol; its actual injection/effect owner still checks current authority. Stop selects currently pending same-session work at its effect, including arrivals during preparation, and never treats active work as pending.

A synthetic reset preserving both session ID and recovery cycle keeps recovery-notice suppression until bounded eviction/restart; real replacements permit a notice. Detached producers enqueueing after their owning run completes get no microtask grace; already accepted sends and transport finalization are awaited. Private injection callbacks remain synchronous one-consumer code, not a second concurrency protocol. Reentrant narrator visibility can leave a harmless retry timer whose entry still checks cancellation. A rolled-back restart with paused work waits for the next normal queue kick rather than an automatic reversible-fence wakeup; delivery can remain deferred without another kick/restart. Detached root/fresh async scope, restart retry suppression, FIFO, and ordinary-shutdown settlement remain.

Provider request callbacks retain their real lease until completion; unsupported retention of request options beyond that callback gets no synthetic closed bit. Passive overlapping model discoveries may return older metadata to their own request without replacing a newer readiness observation; last-observed picker metadata can persist until ordinary refresh/disposal. Picker readiness is not execution authorization. Held binding leases rely on their owner instead of detecting unsupported foreign mutation at every intermediate await. Captured startup policy is not reparsed during inventory discovery. Canonical config/timer/report/string producers own their admitted shapes; raw config/network/file/model/persisted inputs remain validated at ingress. Duplicate app-admission warnings are removed, not the contextual fail-closed error. Credential-migration revision checks remain unchanged.

Channel cleanup uses typed SDK and prepared conversation/verification facts rather than reparsing them internally. Matrix retired-file refusal precedence, no-empty-store creation, strict persisted recovery-key encoding, crypto-store exclusivity, corrupt-state rereads, and shutdown settlement remain. No message content is added to logs.

## Evidence

Pending exact bundled-head proof: focused owner/conflict tests and recorded source gaps; serial z09-8 four-case head/base comparison; touched type graphs and lint/format; suppression guard; runtime/Madge cycles; SDK exports, surface, and committed-ref API comparison; independent fresh review. PR CI on the exact pushed head is the broad proof. No CI reruns for green.

prs.title: fix(macos): DMG packaging leaks an attached disk image when hdiutil attach fails on a busy host
prs.body:
Related: #172903

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: macOS DMG packaging leaves disk images attached on the build host when `hdiutil attach` fails on a busy machine, and `create-dmg.sh` then deletes the image file out from under the still-attached devices.

## User Impact

Release and local DMG packaging no longer accumulate orphaned `/dev/diskN` attachments after a transient attach failure. If an image cannot be detached, packaging fails, keeps the files, and prints the exact `hdiutil detach /dev/diskN` command to run.

## Why This Change Was Made

On a busy host, `hdiutil attach ... -mountpoint M IMAGE` can fail with `Resource temporarily unavailable` after it has created the image's devices (for example `/dev/disk8` plus the synthesized APFS container `/dev/disk11`) but before mounting. Both scripts only detached when the attach had succeeded, so this state was never cleaned up:

- `scripts/create-dmg.sh` skipped detach and ran `rm -rf` on the temp root, deleting the RW image while it stayed attached.
- `scripts/package-mac-dist.sh` (`audit_retained_dmg_async_frames`, notarization resume) left the retained release DMG attached.

This is the same leak class #172903 fixes for the Peekaboo snapshot image. The new shared `scripts/lib/mac-disk-image.sh` uses that approach: find every attachment of the image in `hdiutil info -plist` by real path, detach its whole-disk device with `hdiutil detach -quiet` (never `-force`), re-query to confirm, and fail closed if it is still attached. `create-dmg.sh` checks before deleting its temp root on every exit and preserves it if the image stays attached; the DMG audit runs the device cleanup when its attach did not complete. `mac-swift-build.sh` can adopt the helper once #172903 lands.

Release-note context: macOS packaging (`scripts/create-dmg.sh`, `scripts/package-mac-dist.sh --resume-notarization`) detaches disk images by device after a failed attach instead of leaking them; maintainer/release tooling only, no app behavior change.

## Evidence

Real `hdiutil` on macOS 27 (`hdiutil` wrapped so `attach` runs `attach -nomount` and then fails with the EAGAIN message, reproducing the leaked state exactly; every other command is the real `/usr/bin/hdiutil`):

- `create-dmg.sh` on `main`: exit 35, temp root deleted, `hdiutil info` still lists the deleted `image-rw.dmg` attached as `/dev/disk8`, `/dev/disk8s1`, `/dev/disk11`, `/dev/disk11s1`.
- `create-dmg.sh` with this change: exit 35, temp root deleted, no attachment left.
- `audit_retained_dmg_async_frames` on `main`: exit 35, release DMG still attached as `/dev/disk8` + `/dev/disk11`. With this change: exit 35, nothing attached.
- The new helper also detached both leaked `main`-run images (one whose file was already deleted), so the host was left clean.

Focused tests (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`):

- `test/scripts/create-dmg.test.ts`: 16 passed. The new failed-attach cases (detach succeeds / detach fails) fail against `main`'s script.
- `test/scripts/package-mac-dist.test.ts`: 29 passed. The new failed-audit-attach cases (detach succeeds / detach fails) fail against `main`'s script.
- `test/scripts/build-and-run-mac.test.ts` macOS Bash selection: 137 passed (the helper is pinned to `/bin/bash` and scanned for Bash 3.2 compatibility).
- `node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs root`, `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the touched tests, and `/bin/bash -n` on the touched scripts all pass.

Test cost: the two new `create-dmg` cases run about 0.6 s each. The two new `package-mac-dist` cases run about 4–5 s each, measured on a heavily loaded host (load average around 200), because they go through the real `--resume-notarization` entry point with a built checkpoint; the existing checkpoint cases in that file have the same shape.

prs.title: fix(update): prevent missing backup modules after runtime replacement
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes source updates failing with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` after the updater replaces its own runtime files.

## User Impact

Gateway-managed source updates can capture the rollback database backup after runtime activation without trying to load removed modules from the previous build.

## Why This Change Was Made

The regression was introduced on October 13 by #170828 ([commit d0ea7eae7ead](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/d0ea7eae7eade7740fad79db1aa73a2ebd337bde)). PostgreSQL backup support added lazy imports of `backup-sqlite-snapshot` and `snapshot/database-backup` to `createUpdateDatabaseBackup`. These imports run on the shared backup path, including SQLite installations; they were absent from this function before that change.

The existing Git update flow activates the replacement runtime before capturing the rollback database backup. The still-running updater can therefore request a hashed module from its old build after that file has disappeared. Load and retain those module exports at the existing awaited, update-only preparation boundary, then reuse them during capture.

This also explains why a long-running `dev`/`main` installation can start failing only recently: the update that installs the regression can succeed under the previous updater, while a subsequent update runs the affected code. The failure can be masked when the backup path already loaded these dependencies before activation or when the replacement build retains the same hashed filenames. A successful retry alone does not establish that the loading-order defect is fixed.

## Evidence

- Reproduced through the actual Gateway-managed update path on macOS/Node 24.21.0, updating `a80c9757c3f1` toward `6574349e132d`: activation failed with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for `backup-sqlite-snapshot-5eszxg3P.mjs`, imported by the old `update-database-backup-CUaWNTFS.mjs`. The updater rolled back and verified the previous Gateway healthy.
- Added a process regression using the real preparation and backup functions: remove both old lazy-import files after preparation, capture a SQLite database, and verify its row in the snapshot. It fails before the fix and passes afterward.
- Separately reproduced the failure with an unpatched compiled build after replacing its dist tree; the patched compiled build completed the same replacement scenario and produced an intact database snapshot.
- All 25 focused tests pass across `update-database-backup.test.ts`, `update-execution.runtime.test.ts`, and the new process regression. Core typecheck, targeted lint/format, and the `qaRuntime` build pass. Fresh autoreview found no actionable issues.
- Added [matched actual Gateway update traces](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173587#issuecomment-6205990150) from disposable foreground installations using the same candidate target. The unpatched starting updater fails with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` after runtime activation. The patched starting updater captures two nonempty SQLite snapshots after activation, preserves the marker row/settings/workspace data, exits 0, and automatically restarts a Gateway that passes health and RPC checks. Snapshot hashes, timing, old/new chunk names, and the recovery limitations are included in the evidence. The live installation was unchanged; PostgreSQL and forced database restoration were not tested.

prs.title: fix(x): public X requests fail to start sessions with "X runtime not initialized"
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: public X requests that ask Roboclaw to start a session fail with "X runtime not initialized" when the agent's model provider runs through a plugin.

## User Impact

User impact: authorized X mentions can open visible child sessions again. Authorization is still rechecked live, and requests are still rejected when access is revoked or the X plugin is unloaded.

## Why This Change Was Made

Agent tools start while the provider's response stream is being consumed, so they run inside the provider plugin's instance scope. The X publication authorization callback, which ingress keeps for later, then looked up the X runtime in the provider plugin's slot and found nothing. Ingress now binds that callback to its owning plugin instance when it is created, using `wrapCurrentPluginInstance` like the other retained plugin callbacks. The authorization recheck itself is unchanged.

<details><summary>Production trace and regression origin</summary>

On 2026-10-16 at 01:58:54 and 02:00:23 UTC, two X front-door runs failed in `sessions_spawn` → `ChildSessionPublication.assertCurrent()` → X monitor authorization → `getXRuntime()`. The retained callback path came from #171384. The earlier end-to-end coverage ran `spawn.execute` outside any provider stream scope, so it never hit this ordering.

</details>

## Evidence

- `src/gateway/x-publication-owner-composition.e2e.test.ts` now registers a second (provider) plugin instance and runs the real `sessions_spawn` inside `runPluginStreamConsumer` for that provider, matching agent-core's production ordering.
  - Without the fix: fails with the exact production error `X runtime not initialized`.
  - With the fix: passes, including the revoked-access and unloaded-plugin cases.
- Related suites pass: `src/channels/message-access` (47 tests), `extensions/x/src/monitor-publication.test.ts`, and `src/auto-reply/reply/channel-run-admission.x-recovery.test.ts` (7 tests).
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs`: core typecheck, all 29 test-file typecheck groups, lint, format, import-cycle and boundary guards pass. The only failure is the dead-export scan on `ui/src/components/lazy-view-error.ts` (plus a UI test-support export), which comes from the base commit's #172149 and is untouched here.
- Autoreview (gpt-6.1-sol, P1): no actionable findings.

prs.title: fix(agents): use monotonic clock for ask_user question expiry
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an agent calls `ask_user`, the question expiry deadline was seeded and read with `Date.now()` (wall clock) at two layers — the tool-local budget in `ask-user-tool.ts` and the Gateway owner in `QuestionManager` — but consumed through `setTimeout` (monotonic), crossing clock domains. A wall-clock forward jump (NTP correction, sleep/resume) caused the question to expire before the user could answer, through both the direct `get()`/`list()` epoch comparison and the scheduled `expire()` wake.

- Problem: `expiresAtMs` was seeded/read with `Date.now()` but consumed by `setTimeout`; wall-clock jumps stretch or shrink the timeout at either layer.
- Solution: both layers now use monotonic clocks — the tool-local budget uses `performance.now()`, and `QuestionManager` retains a private `expiresAtMonotonicMs` seeded with `scheduler.monotonicNow()`. The scheduled wake re-checks the monotonic deadline and reschedules if it has not passed. The client-visible `expiresAtMs` remains an epoch timestamp.
- What changed: `ask-user-tool.ts` — 4 sites switched to `performance.now()`; `question-manager.ts` — private `expiresAtMonotonicMs` on `QuestionEntry`, used in `get()`, `runPendingContinuation()`, `resolveWithCommit`'s `assertCurrent()`, and the `expireScheduled()` wake; `gateway-scheduler.ts` — exposed `monotonicNow()`.
- What did NOT change: client-visible `expiresAtMs` (epoch), RPC `timeoutMs`, delivery state machine, any persistence.

## Why This Change Was Made

The maintainer (obviyus) reproduced the end-to-end flow: advancing only the Gateway's `Date.now()` by 120s caused a 30s question to expire early via `question.list` → `get()` (~0.7s). After that path was made monotonic, the scheduled `expire()` wake still terminated it at ~17s because `GatewayScheduler.remaining()` takes `min(wallDelay, monotonicDelay)` and a wall-clock jump makes `wallDelay` negative.

A follow-up review found a deeper race: when a wall-clock jump wakes the callback while `resolveWithCommit()` awaits its write, the committing guard ran before the rearm, so the scheduler deleted the one-shot wake with no replacement — a later rejected commit left the question pending with no expiry job. `expireScheduled()` now re-arms the remaining monotonic budget before the committing guard.

## User Impact

The `get()`/`list()` direct checks and the scheduled `expire()` wake are now monotonic, so a wall-clock forward jump no longer causes premature expiry. A wall-clock wake overlapping an in-flight commit no longer loses the expiry job: a failed commit still reaches automatic terminal expiry without a later read.

## Evidence

Native-timer proof through the production `QuestionManager` + `GatewayScheduler` (native `setTimeout`/`performance.now()`). A 30s question is seeded, `Date.now()` is forward-jumped 120s, then a short trigger trips the scheduler's wall-clock-due wake. The wake fires at ~1.8s (monotonic) but the question stays pending. A second scenario covers the commit-overlap race:

```console
$ node --import tsx/esm proof-scheduler-wake.ts
[proof-jump] PASS: scheduled wake re-checked the monotonic deadline and did not expire early
[proof-commit] PASS: wall-clock wake overlapping an in-flight commit re-armed expiry; failed commit reached terminal expiry
```

Running-Gateway E2E through a live WebSocket transport (not in-process). A Gateway started with `pnpm openclaw gateway run --auth token --port 19876 --dev`; a CLI client connected over WebSocket, completed the token-auth handshake, and called `question.request` → `question.get` through production RPC dispatch:

```console
$ node proof-gateway-e2e.cjs
[proof-e2e] WebSocket connected to running Gateway
[proof-e2e] Authenticated connect handshake complete
[proof-e2e] question status before jump: pending
[proof-e2e] wall clock jumped forward by 120s
[proof-e2e] question status after jump: pending
[proof-e2e] PASS: question stayed pending after +120s wall-clock jump
[proof-e2e] question status after ~3s: expired
[proof-e2e] PASS: question expired within 2s budget (monotonic)
```

Gateway-level regression tests (66 passed, 5.72s wall-clock):

```console
$ npx vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/question-manager.test.ts src/gateway/question-manager-monotonic-deadline.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  66 passed (66)
   Duration  5.72s
```

The wall-clock-jump regression now also advances past the remaining monotonic budget and asserts expiry, proving the re-armed job is not lost (per maintainer suggestion). Lifetime is **awake time**: a suspend that advances only the wall clock does not consume the window — the question stays pending past public `expiresAtMs` and expires on the monotonic budget.

Tool-local tests remain green: `ask-user-tool.test.ts` (29 passed) plus the wall-clock regressions split into a sibling `ask-user-tool.wall-clock.test.ts` (2 passed) so the original file stays under the lint line budget. The outbound delivery suite (`deliver.question-generation.test.ts`, 4 tests, 58s) also passes.
