prs.title: fix(codex): backoff startup connection-close retries and surface exhaustion (#83959) [AI-assisted]
prs.body:
> [AI-assisted] This PR was generated using Claude Code.

## Summary

- **Problem:** When the Codex app-server connection closes during startup, `startCodexAttemptThread` cleared the shared client and retried **immediately** — before the replacement app-server process had bound/become ready — under a tight 3-attempt budget. All retries landed in the same failing window and exhausted, so a scheduled/background turn failed even though the Codex route became viable moments later. Cron automation reported job failure with no task-level problem. (Issue #83959)
- **Why now:** P1 for background/cron Codex turns; the issue's own local mitigation confirmed the direction (raise the startup-close retry budget + add a bounded backoff).
- **Intended outcome:** Startup tolerates a short replacement-server warm-up window before declaring failure, and when it does give up it says so distinctly instead of surfacing a misleading "client is closed".
- **Out of scope:** The separate per-run replay retry gate in `embedded-agent-runner/run.ts` (already correct, untouched) and the shared-client eviction work tracked under #79495.
- **Success:** A transient startup connection-close no longer fails the turn when the server recovers within the bounded window; persistent closes fail with a distinguishable error.
- **Reviewer focus:** The retry-loop change in `attempt-startup.ts` (budget 3→5, added `computeBackoff`+`sleepWithAbort` backoff, new `CodexAppServerStartupExhaustedError`) and the two new regression tests.

## Linked context

Closes #83959

Related #79495 (shared Codex app-server client eviction across agents — broader, separate).

Was this requested by a maintainer or owner? No — external contributor fix for an open P1.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: Codex app-server startup connection-close retry loop exhausted before the replacement server was ready (#83959).
- Real environment tested: Windows 11, Node v22.22.3, OpenClaw checkout. The capture drives the REAL `startCodexAttemptThread` (the production function this PR changes) against a REAL local app-server subprocess spawned by the REAL `CodexAppServerClient.start` -> `createStdioTransport` -> `child_process.spawn`. The subprocess speaks the same newline-delimited JSON-RPC framing as the real Codex app-server; on the first N attempts it closes its connection during the `initialize` handshake (real child exit -> real `codex app-server exited:` error -> real `isCodexAppServerConnectionClosedError` -> the real startup retry loop), and completes the handshake on attempt N+1. It is a stand-in for the `codex` binary (no Codex account/backend is available on this host); it is NOT a reimplementation of the retry loop and does not stub `startCodexAttemptThread`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: `pnpm exec tsx .tmp/capture-83959-real.ts` with `CLOSES_BEFORE_SUCCESS=4` (recovery) and `CLOSES_BEFORE_SUCCESS=99` (persistent-close exhaustion), run on unpatched main and on this PR branch. Driver: `.tmp/capture-83959-real.ts`; stand-in app-server subprocess: `.tmp/fake-codex-app-server.mjs`.
- Evidence after fix (terminal capture):
```
$ CLOSES_BEFORE_SUCCESS=4 pnpm exec tsx .tmp/capture-83959-real.ts   # this PR (budget=5, bounded backoff)
codex app-server connection closed during startup; restarting app-server and retrying
codex app-server connection closed during startup; restarting app-server and retrying
codex app-server connection closed during startup; restarting app-server and retrying
codex app-server connection closed during startup; restarting app-server and retrying
{
  "outcome": "recovered",
  "closesBeforeSuccess": 4,
  "spawnAttempts": 5,
  "spawnModes": ["exit", "exit", "exit", "exit", "serve"],
  "observedWallClockGapsMs": [1962, 2531, 3399, 5340],
  "backoffPolicyComputedMs": [532, 1179, 2019, 4000],
  "elapsedMs": 14856
}

$ CLOSES_BEFORE_SUCCESS=99 pnpm exec tsx .tmp/capture-83959-real.ts  # this PR, persistent close
codex app-server connection closed during startup; restarting app-server and retrying
codex app-server connection closed during startup; restarting app-server and retrying
codex app-server connection closed during startup; restarting app-server and retrying
codex app-server connection closed during startup; restarting app-server and retrying
codex app-server connection closed during startup; retries exhausted
{
  "outcome": "exhausted",
  "closesBeforeSuccess": 99,
  "spawnAttempts": 5,
  "spawnModes": ["exit", "exit", "exit", "exit", "exit"],
  "observedWallClockGapsMs": [1836, 2417, 3459, 5278],
  "backoffPolicyComputedMs": [575, 1183, 2332, 4000],
  "elapsedMs": 14385,
  "error": {
    "message": "codex app-server startup exhausted after 5 connection-close retries",
    "name": "CodexAppServerStartupExhaustedError",
    "cause": "codex app-server exited: code=1 signal=null"
  }
}
```
- Observed result after fix: BEFORE (unpatched, budget 3) — startup exhausted at 3 attempts with 2 flat ~1.3s gaps (no backoff sleep; the gaps are spawn/cleanup overhead only) and the turn failed with the raw `codex app-server exited: code=1 signal=null` (plain `Error`, no distinct exhaustion type). AFTER (this PR, budget 5 + bounded abortable backoff) — the same 4 leading closes were survived: startup recovered on the 5th attempt with 4 monotonically increasing gaps [1962, 2531, 3399, 5340] ms that track the real `computeBackoff` policy [532, 1179, 2019, 4000] ms (policy value + spawn/cleanup overhead), and the turn succeeded. Persistent-close AFTER — exhausted at 5 with the distinct `CodexAppServerStartupExhaustedError` ("codex app-server startup exhausted after 5 connection-close retries"), the original `codex app-server exited:` preserved as `cause`, instead of the raw close error.
- What was not tested: A live `codex` app-server process backed by a real Codex/LLM account (no local Codex harness or API key on this Windows host). The stand-in subprocess reproduces the connection-close-during-startup condition and the JSON-RPC initialize/thread-start handshake but does not execute Codex model turns. macOS/Linux runtime not exercised locally.
- Proof limitations or environment constraints: The stand-in app-server subprocess is a real local process exercising the real production startup retry path (real spawn, real stdio JSON-RPC, real child-exit close detection, real `computeBackoff`+`sleepWithAbort` wall-clock delays, real `CodexAppServerStartupExhaustedError`); it is not the real `codex` binary because no Codex backend is available on this host.
- Before evidence (optional but encouraged):
```
$ pnpm exec tsx .tmp/capture-83959-real.ts        # unpatched main (budget=3, no backoff)
codex app-server connection closed during startup; restarting app-server and retrying
codex app-server connection closed during startup; restarting app-server and retrying
codex app-server connection closed during startup; retries exhausted
{
  "outcome": "exhausted",
  "closesBeforeSuccess": 4,
  "spawnAttempts": 3,
  "spawnModes": ["exit", "exit", "exit"],
  "observedWallClockGapsMs": [1329, 1231],
  "backoffPolicyComputedMs": [551, 1078, 2252, 4000],
  "elapsedMs": 3917,
  "error": { "message": "codex app-server exited: code=1 signal=null", "name": "Error" }
}
```

## Tests and validation

- Commands run: `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` (changed files, clean); `pnpm tsgo:extensions` (clean); `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` (clean); `pnpm exec oxlint --type-aware` (changed files, clean); `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-startup.test.ts -t "83959"` (2 passed).
- Regression coverage added: Two new tests in `attempt-startup.test.ts` covering the previously-**untested** startup connection-close retry loop — (1) survives N transient closes with bounded backoff and recovers, asserting `sleepWithAbort` is awaited between attempts with bounded delays; (2) persistent closes produce the distinct `CodexAppServerStartupExhaustedError` with the original error as `cause`, and the loop is bounded (no infinite retry).
- Failed before this fix: Both new tests fail on unpatched main (budget=3 exhausts before the 4th-close recovery; raw "client is closed" rethrown with no distinct exhaustion error).
- Note: `pnpm check:host-env-policy:swift` skipped on Windows (no Swift).

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? `Yes` — a Codex startup that previously failed after 3 immediate retries now retries up to 5 times with a bounded backoff (worst case a few extra seconds before a transient-close recovery or a cleaner failure).

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? `No`.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? `No` — the change only affects the Codex app-server startup retry timing/error shape; no auth, secret, network, or tool-execution surface touched. `extensions/codex/src/**` is not a CODEOWNERS secops path.

What is the highest-risk area? Added latency on a Codex startup that closes repeatedly during warm-up (bounded to ~8s worst case across 5 attempts).

How is that risk mitigated? Backoff only fires after a connection-close failure (never on the success path); `sleepWithAbort` is abortable so a cancelled/aborted run fails fast instead of stalling; the budget is still bounded (5) so a permanently-broken server fails rather than retrying forever; the distinct exhaustion error preserves the original cause for diagnostics.

## Current review state

What is the next action? Awaiting maintainer review. The real behavior proof was upgraded (see above) from a synthetic retry-loop model to a real local app-server subprocess driving the actual `startCodexAttemptThread`; `@clawsweeper re-review` requested.

What is still waiting on author, maintainer, CI, or external proof? External-fork heavy CI shards require maintainer workflow approval to run. A maintainer proof/latency override is also an acceptable path per ClawSweeper's option 2 if the stand-in-subprocess proof is deemed sufficient.

Which bot or reviewer comments were addressed? Upgraded the real behavior proof in response to ClawSweeper's `status: 📣 needs proof` ("supplies tests and a synthetic terminal model, but not after-fix live OpenClaw/Codex app-server startup proof").

prs.title: fix: custom endpoint setup fails auth-less servers outside loopback, leaving half-applied provider config
prs.body:
Closes #172150.

## What Problem This Solves

Custom model endpoints that do not require authentication can pass setup with a blank key but then fail on the first turn when their hostname is not classified as local.

## User Impact

Custom OpenAI Chat Completions providers can explicitly set `auth: "none"`, choose no-auth in the wizard, or pass `--custom-no-auth` during noninteractive setup. Requests omit Authorization even when inline, environment, stored/pinned, or activated SecretRef credentials remain configured. The optional value needs no Doctor migration.

The effective model adapter controls support. Responses, Azure OpenAI, and Anthropic adapters still require a key or placeholder; unsupported no-auth choices fail before reset or persistence. Hostname-locality rules are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

No-auth is terminal before core credential preparation, provider plugin exchange, and session-registry credential lookup. The shared header override also survives SDK header merging. Setup validates model-level API overrides and Azure URL rewriting, while an explicit replacement key can switch an existing no-auth provider back to keyed mode.

Builds on @rubencu's original contribution and preserves their commits ([original tailnet proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/172152#issuecomment-6172067062)). Config schema, generated help, CLI help, and docs describe the new option.

## Evidence

Evidence below records the tested source heads: the full build and live matrix ran on `9c63b3f47b673cc03a22c406831248111e31fcc0`. The final main integration leaves all authored production owners unchanged and narrows only erased types in one test fixture.

The 279 focused owner cases have passing evidence on the pre-merge candidate (14 files; full run 2,220.38 seconds, followed by a corrected 57-case reset-test rerun in 324.58 seconds). After merging main for a generated-config conflict, the SDK no-auth/keyed request cases and one-shot completion/profile-failover suite passed all 21 cases in 600.25 seconds. Feature-owner sources were unchanged by the merge. Long local durations are dominated by compilation/import preparation (95% transform in the SDK shard); the plugin credential-preparation regression exercises the real lazy runtime boundary, whose first import took 110.64 seconds on this shared Mac.

On `9c63b3f`, core, agents-root and agents-sessions type checks passed in 44.00, 29.57 and 28.76 seconds. Scoped type-aware lint passed in 57.34 seconds on the unchanged feature sources. All seven ratchets passed on that head (0.53–133.47 seconds each), including generated config docs. Codex autoreview on `656b3635b94c9e0b4f99f9c34e4e1358313c566b` is scoped-clean with no actionable P0–P2 findings; the only later change is the verified shrink-only baseline correction.

Full `pnpm build` passed on `9c63b3f47b673cc03a22c406831248111e31fcc0` in 922.70 seconds, including declarations and SDK export checks. Real macOS proof used `pnpm openclaw` with isolated profiles/state and a task-owned proxy at `auth-none.127.0.0.1.nip.io:18782`, a hostname outside the lexical local-provider classification. The isolated provider used the existing `request.allowPrivateNetwork` option for that deliberate private DNS result. Capture records only path and whether Authorization is absent.

| Real CLI proof | Wall time | Result |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Noninteractive `setup --custom-no-auth` | 19.95s | Persists no-auth, no key, despite an ambient synthetic key |
| Interactive setup with Ollama verification | 135.71s | Completes and persists no-auth; both requests omit Authorization |
| Inline/env, saved/pinned profile, activated SecretRef conflicts | 22.01–29.99s each | Successful fixture replies; Authorization absent |
| Normal keyed inference control | 25.05s | Authorization present |
| `infer model run --local`, Ollama `llama3.2:latest` | 32.98s | Real `AUTH_NONE_LIVE_OK` reply; Authorization absent |
| Same-session keyed → no-auth `agent --local` | 59.15s + 71.59s | Real `AUTH_NONE_AGENT_OK` reply; header present → absent, including retained profile, SecretRef and explicit Authorization header |
| Responses override / Azure rewrite with full reset | 37.41s / 12.63s | Reject before HTTP; Azure preserves exact config bytes and workspace marker |
| Responses provider with selected Completions override | 30.27s + 16.76s | Setup and turn pass through Chat Completions without Authorization |
| Real wizard receiving deliberate HTTP 400 | 142.17s | Unverified model/auth selection is not persisted |

The final agent proof disables Tool Search and Code Mode and completes one assistant turn with zero tools. An initial small-model attempt looped on malformed tool-discovery calls; all 19 requests still omitted Authorization. A separate existing-primary wizard case failed before HTTP with a runtime-config-preparation error and preserved its old selection; it is retained as an unclassified setup follow-up, not claimed as the HTTP-400 proof.

Before the fix, isolated macOS setup succeeded but `infer model run --local` failed with “No API key found” before any request reached the endpoint. The original PR also returned an activated SecretRef credential despite explicit no-auth. New regression assertions failed against the original owner: five failures, four passes (489.10 seconds including compiler preparation).

Production: +400/-156 lines (net +244). Tests: +723/-12 (net +711). Growth implements the new optional public contract and terminal request policy; nearby cleanup shares the header policy, removes a duplicate test shape, and extracts registry request auth from the oversized registry file. Docs: +35/-1; generated fingerprint: +2/-2; maintenance baselines: +1/-2 against the final base. The inherited environment-variable budget was narrowed from 453 to the source count of 452; the feature changes no counted environment names.

The initial CI run found broad generic types in the new auth test fixture. Its specific Completions model and profile-map annotations are now corrected; the affected `core-test-agents-other` graph passes (14.7 seconds compiler time, 67.13 seconds including lock wait), and scoped type-aware lint passes (70.73 seconds). Test behavior is unchanged.

Prior-head publication checks: all seven required ratchets had passing evidence; the corrected max-lines/environment-budget check passes in 100.31 seconds. Other refreshed ratchets took 0.79–62.12 seconds. Prior head: `715947e196e19cfa9ff1638f3a72c302be618bb1`.

CI run `38794345432` completed: build, UI E2E, test jobs, and the repaired auth type stripe passed. CI attribution: the sole code-check failure, `check-test-types-core-3`, is inherited from the newer CI merge base `d0d0f86547285fee3eb8d861510d1878b9740deb`. Its Apple build-cache test infers `record-ios-build-cache-metadata.outcome` as `string` instead of the required literal union. The exact-base test and matching helper/compiler inputs reproduce the same TS2345 at `test/scripts/apple-build-cache.test.ts:232` locally in 17.41 seconds. The candidate file was restored byte-for-byte; the auth fixture type stripe now passes.

Limits: local live proof is macOS/Apple silicon only. Security-sensitive approval remains pending.


## SDK merge follow-up

Merged main `19c8b47143194d97baabb80e337416d23524b7e3` into the contributor branch without rebasing. SDK validation head: `6e4676b6a6b7a2a665a9a2f8539cd72b0e8a85ef`. The sole content conflict was `src/agents/sessions/sdk.ts`. Resolution keeps main's extracted stream function and narrow captures, preserving its disposed-parent/fork-replay fix, and applies the existing no-auth policy after final header merging. Relative to main, the SDK change is one import and the header-policy call (+5/-1).

Fresh focused validation: all 30 cases across `sdk.no-auth.test.ts`, `sdk.test.ts`, and `model-registry.no-auth.test.ts` passed (799.98 seconds total, including fixture compilation and source verification). Main's disposed-parent collection/replay regression passed. Core types, session test types, and scoped SDK lint passed (53.31, 61.09, and 41.68 seconds). Fresh Codex autoreview of the resolved candidate is scoped-clean with no actionable P0–P2 findings.

Assertion-safety, environment budget, line-cap, timeout, mock-export, config-doc and inventory checks passed. Max-lines reports inherited UI baseline debt: main renamed `chat-message.test.ts` to `.tsx` while its baseline still names `.ts`. The source and baseline blobs are identical to the integrated main; no unrelated allowance or policy change was made. Prior live proof remains attributed to its original head. Fresh CI is requested for this merge; the lead will re-post security approval on the new revision.

Main advanced during publication, so the final head `9a9960d2ca52dc4510d97546eedea87b59f946d5` also merges `07afec7832b49097729956fecf38e42894cc9a5d`. Its only conflict was the generated config fingerprint, regenerated canonically. Config-doc validation passed in 48.47 seconds and plugin inventory in 3.41 seconds. SDK/auth sources remain identical to the validated head above; the clean review and focused proof are reused with that attribution.

prs.title: perf(sessions): reuse written transcript replacement snapshots
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Locked transcript replacement immediately reloads every event it just persisted to retain the snapshot used by the next mutation. This repeats SQL row materialization and payload decompression while holding the writer transaction.

## User Impact

No public behavior or stored-format change. Transcript replacements retain the same canonical bytes, duplicate filtering, conflict detection, and live authority checks.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing replacement owner records its final sequence numbers and canonical JSON in an optional transaction-local snapshot supplied by the two locked-write adapters. Those adapters no longer reload the transcript after replacement. Other replacement callers retain no additional payloads. There is no new cache, persisted state, schema change, or alternative writer.

The audit also inspected session-entry patches, normal transcript appends, cron receipts, usage rollups, plugin state, and subagent registry writes. Their hot paths already carry committed results; remaining reads serve current authority, existing backlog, or recovery.

## Evidence

- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable). The configured helper refused the requested route because it did not match the operator configuration. Review identified unnecessary payload retention for callers that discard snapshots; the revised collector is opt-in.
- Focused storage test: 31 passed (35.75 s Vitest duration; 203.58 s including wrapper preparation). The initial candidate passed all 5 cross-process concurrency tests (91.94 s); the final collector change passed the 2 relevant conflict checks again (46.12 s Vitest duration; 64.26 s including preparation).
- Changed-file `oxfmt`, repository-configured `oxlint`, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent review of the revised diff: no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- File-backed Linux measurement, 401 synthetic events (~0.65 MB), 10 warmups and 100 replacements per trial, alternating AB/BA/AB: snapshot-consuming means 64.22→60.32, 65.92→58.28, 67.71→61.18 ms (~9.1% average reduction). SELECTs 9→7 per replacement; writes unchanged at 2,412. Across those pairs: mean 65.948→59.925 ms (−9.13%), median 62.346→56.531 ms, CPU 7.115→6.520 s (−8.37%). Without snapshot capture, the initial 3×100 trials were noisy (+16.8% mean, including a 159 ms p95 outlier). A bounded 3×300 BA/AB/BA follow-up resolved this: mean 59.063→59.331 ms (+0.45%), median 57.026→57.265 ms (+0.42%), CPU 18.746→18.783 s (+0.20%): neutral within noise. Broader patch+append and chat+tool stress are not claimed by this narrowly scoped replacement change.
- Production delta: +13 lines; tests: +57. The additional lines carry the existing conflict-detection snapshot from the single writer without retaining serialized data for other replacement callers; both redundant replacement reloads are removed.
- Broad typecheck, suites, and build validation belong to PR CI. No Testbox/Crabbox lease was allocated.

prs.title: fix(auth): keep OAuth refresh fence timeout monotonic across clock skew
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A wall-clock rollback can make callers observing an OAuth refresh wait beyond their timeout. The refresh observer calculated its deadline with `Date.now()`, although its timers measure elapsed time. Forward clock changes can also reject a healthy settlement too early.

## Change

Measure the existing observation deadlines with `performance.now()`. Keep token expiration timestamps and credential validity checks on wall time. Refresh ownership, persistence, cancellation, timeout messages, and configured budgets remain unchanged.

Thanks @SunnyShu0925 for the report and fix; the contributor's commit is retained unchanged. The fix stays in the existing shared observer, with no new state or compatibility path. The original monotonic conversion is retained. Follow-up fixes round fractional observer timeouts and positive polling remainders upward so neither expires early nor busy-polls without yielding. Tests cover both wall-clock directions, exact boundaries, blocked reads, late settlement and cancellation.

## Evidence

Validation for current head `fe34335fe5c31fdabb5b0753244dcffa64cf0b5a` (same source tree as locally tested `139811d3e675c87abf48156c9d47dbd2a201406f`):

- Independently reproduced premature fractional expiry through both public observer APIs: at 99 ms, monotonic time 99.75 was still below deadline 100.25, but the incoming floor-rounded timer had already rejected. Both regression fixtures failed before the correction.
- Final focused asynchronous suite: **19 passed**.
- Qualified the final correction composed with main `5462f7f146436a50a56354dd39f8405eaeb5b60f`, merged tree `a0a623d39589a51a16b873a9ba7962f1542640ab`: **65 passed** across OAuth fence sync/async, abort-signal and backoff tests. Command: `pnpm test src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth-refresh-fence.test.ts src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth-refresh-fence.async.test.ts src/infra/abort-signal.test.ts src/infra/backoff.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.
- The prior composed candidate failed the fractional polling boundary; rounding positive polling remainders upward corrected it. Independent forward/backward wall-step polling cases also fail against the former Date-based implementation.
- Whole changed-file and caller audit retains epoch-based token validity, refresh ownership/CAS, account barriers, durable persistence and cancellation. Local lint is **not claimed**: the local wrapper rejects the shared pnpm compiler realpath; required GitHub lint/type/test gates must pass before merge.
- Fixtures use private synthetic auth state, never production credentials or stores. Original contributor runtime observations below are preserved and are not represented as this correction's own runtime proof.

## Original contributor validation (historical head)

Built current main `56c315156f4542f197a2b7f727681ba3f41c21b5` and this head `588022c34c35772d025eb7c73c4c0a8b26e9dd5c` in an isolated Node 24.16.0 Linux container. Synthetic pending refresh credentials were persisted in the real SQLite auth store. Only the process's `Date.now()` was stepped backward by 5,000 ms; the system clock was not changed. Elapsed durations were measured with `performance.now()`.

The compiled observer reading the real persisted store, with a 200 ms budget:

| Case | Current main | This head |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Rollback, first run | 5,213.5 ms | 200.4 ms |
| Rollback, second run | 5,240.2 ms | 200.2 ms |
| No rollback | 203.1 ms | 201.9 ms |

The shipped `openclaw/plugin-sdk/provider-auth` resolver, `resolveProviderAuthProfileApiKey`, also observed a pending refresh through the normal auth manager. This path keeps its production 120,000 ms budget. Total call durations include initialization:

| Case | Current main | This head |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Rollback, first run | 127,019.9 ms | 120,881.9 ms |
| Rollback, second run | 126,755.4 ms | 120,766.8 ms |
| No rollback | 120,927.1 ms | 120,893.2 ms |

All calls ended with the existing OAuth refresh timeout error; the pending owner was intentionally never settled. Current main requires its published asynchronous runtime-config initialization before the resolver call.

A separate public-SDK control checked the same unchanged token-expiry timestamp before expiry, after expiry, and after a wall-clock rollback. Both builds returned `[true, false, true]`, confirming that token validity still follows wall time.

Focused tests: `pnpm test src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth-refresh-fence.test.ts src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth-refresh-fence.async.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **33 passed**, 2 files; command elapsed 200.31 seconds. These also cover cancellation and durable success/failure settlement.

No real-provider gate is needed for this observation-deadline-only change. No live provider credentials were used. The runtime reproduction covers pending-generation observation; the existing focused tests cover the other settlement boundaries.

## Merge risk

Two-way door: reverting fully restores the previous behavior; there is no schema, stored-token, configuration, or public API migration. The affected surface is OAuth callers waiting for a refresh or refresh settlement. An incorrect deadline could return a timeout too early or let those callers wait too long; it does not change token expiry or cancel the durable refresh owner.

observeOAuthRefreshSettlementBeforeDeadline seeded its deadline with
Date.now() and fed deadline - Date.now() to setTimeout. Wall-clock
adjustments (NTP, container drift, sleep resume) warped the remaining
budget: a rewind let the fence hang past the configured timeout and a
forward jump tripped the timeout on a healthy refresh.

Seed the deadline from performance.now() and read remaining budget from
the same monotonic clock, flooring the value before handing it to
setTimeout/sleepWithAbort. Mirrors the canonical wall-clock fix in #155323.

prs.title: fix(ci): avoid repeated source scans before remote checks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Remote check preparation rereads every selected source file twice before dependency installation.

## User Impact

Remote checks perform one fewer full source scan while preserving source-integrity verification before and after installation. Import or canonical preinstall verification rejection preserves the prepared checkout’s previous Git HEAD and index; working-tree edits are not rolled back. Installation and postinstall rejection still retain the selected Git identity and block the payload.

## Why This Change Was Made

The canonical verifier already checks the source bytes, modes, symlinks, deleted paths, Git owner, index, comparison refs, and unexpected entries. Remove the older standalone scan and promote the imported Git directory only after canonical preinstall verification succeeds. Extend the existing rejection cases to check index preservation alongside HEAD preservation.

## Evidence

- The actual exported bootstrap, using a local Git bundle and dependency-installer fixture, performs three full file-hash passes before the change and two afterward. This measures file reads, not end-to-end duration or production spending.
- Bootstrap checks of the unchanged receiver: valid source runs the payload; preinstall tampering blocks the installer and payload while preserving previous HEAD/index; installer tampering blocks the payload.
- Existing transport/lifecycle suite on the earlier draft head found the premature Git promotion regression: three lifecycle cases passed and the transport case failed its previous-HEAD assertion. [Failed run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38832213384). Prior reviewed head `027f4fe35bf0ce4d3e2ff819b43b86fcf4c7ec31` passes the full wrapper file in PR CI: **287 passed, 1 skipped**, including all 11 transport scenarios and the previously failing Testbox transport plus all three lifecycle cases. The transport case exercises mode, bytes, and deletion rejection with preserved HEAD/index. [Passing job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38836094194/job/116765811620) for head `027f4fe35bf0ce4d3e2ff819b43b86fcf4c7ec31` (PR merge `e7566774f`). File test time: 268.44 seconds; native Git transport, tamper rejection, and recovery ordering require the real Git boundary.
- Two independent reviews of the receiver repair found no actionable issue. `node --check scripts/crabbox-source-receiver.mts` and `git diff --check` pass.
- Production delta: +6/-5 lines, including the comment explaining the recovery boundary. Tests: +7/-0 lines.

The branch was updated once to integrate main after the prior CI merge exposed an unrelated missing `render` name in the UI type stripe. Current head is `7a74d8815f40daa002c2451f56172b3af5075fdf`, merging reviewed `027f4fe35bf0ce4d3e2ff819b43b86fcf4c7ec31` with main `387ebd69dfd38220f99be9bd949782d752c6ae92`, which contains [the UI repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/56c315156f4542f197a2b7f727681ba3f41c21b5). The receiver blob and introduced two-file repair are unchanged. Independent integration review accepted the unchanged repair after checking the owner and caller paths. Current-head CI is successful: the full wrapper file passes **287 tests, 1 skipped**, including all 11 transport scenarios, the mode/bytes/deletion HEAD/index rejection assertions, and all three lifecycle paths. [Current-head job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38842060192/job/116784505392), PR merge `00427ba9b395c220384ee8deae0c1acb542f9402`; file test time 294.268 seconds. The UI type stripe and required CI gates also pass. [Exact-head ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173607#issuecomment-6205679115) has no findings or before-merge actions.

prs.title: perf(agents): avoid redundant subagent restore reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway startup reloads finished subagent task/result text even when its retained metadata is already current. During later activation it also opens child sessions whose restart recovery or cancellation already has a separate owner; an unavailable child store can abort activation of unrelated healthy runs.

## User Impact

Startup avoids unnecessary retained-payload reads, and healthy subagents can activate without waiting on child stores owned by recovery or cancellation. Retention settings, persisted text, cancellation authority, and startup admission ordering are preserved. No schema or configuration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Select metadata changes from resident records before entering the existing mutation owner. Only selected rows hydrate full payloads, and the mutation still recomputes the same metadata plan after FIFO predecessors settle. Skip separately owned recovery/cancellation rows before reading their child session, retaining the post-await ownership check for changes during an ordinary read.

The startup investigation confirmed that `sidecars.subagent-recovery` runs after readiness and includes transcript/maintenance prewarm, saved-message recovery, exec notifications, and registry activation. Registry hydration and metadata restoration instead run inside pre-ready `plugins.bootstrap`. Main-session orphan marking already overlaps other preparation and must retain its pre-channel join. Plugin services are unchanged.

## Evidence

- The new metadata regression fails on the original code because it reloads both unchanged and changed retained payloads. It also checks that retention correction preserves the full persisted task and result.
- Recovery/cancellation regressions cover healthy-sibling activation with unavailable child metadata for restart recovery, kill intent, and kill reconciliation.
- Both focused files passed: `subagent-registry.persistence.resume.test.ts` and `subagent-registry-queued-recovery.test.ts`, 35 tests, 232.43 s Vitest duration, 267.61 s including the wrapper (74% transform, 21% tests). The new payload regression took 2.1 s; the three recovery cases took 1.66 s / 53 ms / 83 ms. Changed-file syntax lint, formatting, and diff whitespace checks passed.
- Isolated Linux before/after startup measurements are below. Broad validation belongs to PR CI; no Testbox/Crabbox lease was used. One earlier local invocation was invalidated by a source edit during harness compilation; the frozen-source rerun above passed.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): no actionable P0–P2 findings. The configured autoreview preflight refused the requested provider route; no configuration was changed.

Production delta is +5 lines: selection and an early ownership check preserve the existing metadata-write and post-await authority contracts. No new module, queue, cache, or alternate recovery path.

## Measurement

Compared baseline `01cf74e64692` with this PR on an isolated Linux sandbox (Node 26.8.2; 64 CPUs allowed, 64 GiB memory cap, low scheduling/I/O priority). Separate freshly generated synthetic fixtures each contain 5,000 sessions and 6,000 retained runs, with exactly 4,641,595,392 bytes in the agent database and 262,762,496 bytes in shared state. Retained task/result text is 8/32 KiB per run. The normal retention owner computes canonical future archive deadlines with a 60-day retention setting; the default generator otherwise forces metadata writes on every retained row. No production data was used.

Both builds have identical temporary timing instrumentation. Plugins, channels, cron, discovery, and models are disabled. The driver polls the actual `/readyz` endpoint from process spawn, then waits for recovery activation. No competing fixture generation/build ran during the paired measurements; unrelated host load remains uncontrolled. Values are milliseconds unless labeled otherwise.

| Phase / metric | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Retained metadata restoration | 697.96 | 14.16 |
| First `/readyz` 200 from spawn | 10,663.84 | 9,170.13 |
| Process bootstrap (unchanged code) | 3,846.1 | 2,962.3 |
| Plugins bootstrap, including registry initialization | 1,334.8 | 659.2 |
| Config/auth | 246.0 | 261.6 |
| Sessions admission | 357.2 | 364.1 |
| Main-session recovery | 1,295.9 | 1,677.2 |
| Plugins runtime post-bind | 4.5 | 5.3 |
| Plugin services | 16.0 | 13.1 |
| Model runtime | 409.5 | 413.8 |
| Channels | 0.6 | 0.8 |
| Worker environments | 275.4 | 280.2 |
| Post-ready subagent recovery | 1,587.6 | 1,628.3 |
| Ready trace RSS, MiB | 1,823.1 | 1,303.1 |
| Ready trace used heap, MiB | 1,081.8 | 383.1 |

Metadata restoration is **49.3× faster, saving 683.8 ms (98%)**. Gross readiness improves 1.49 s, but unchanged bootstrap varies by 884 ms: the entire readiness improvement cannot be attributed to this patch. Memory values are single checkpoint observations, not peaks or steady-state allocation measurements. Post-ready recovery is neutral within this single-pair observation (+40.7 ms / 2.6%); the reported production 19.5-second tail was **not reproduced or established as fixed**.

The post-ready baseline phase breaks down into prewarm 452 ms, saved-message recovery 78 ms, exec recovery 24 ms, registry owner binding 479 ms, requester settlement 4 ms, restored-run resume 526 ms, and interrupted-run recovery 18 ms. Ordinary completed rows are skipped cheaply by interrupted recovery; the fixture does not exercise thousands of unfinished provider-backed executions. Recovery ownership skipping is therefore established by behavioral regressions, not a separate timing claim.

A limited head-only reconnect diagnostic starts four operator clients at readiness, each issuing 105 compact `sessions.list` requests (five warmups, 100 samples). All succeed and observe 5,000 sessions; per-client means are 20–28 ms and p99 62–93 ms. Recovery stretches to 2,518 ms, with saved-message recovery increasing from 101 to 853 ms. This supports contention with interactive reads but does not distinguish reader/writer queues or reproduce production load. The attempted baseline burst had repeated listen-admission failures and is excluded from comparison. The sandbox and owned processes were removed after preserving evidence.

## Readiness boundary

HTTP bind alone does not admit ordinary connections. Dispatch readiness and sidecar readiness gate connect; `/readyz` also checks draining, database and relevant plugin/channel health. Request/projection setup, early runtime and main-session orphan marking already overlap, with orphan marking joined before channels can admit foreground work. Moving that join would violate recovery ownership, so admission ordering is unchanged.

Subagent recovery is scheduled only after startup settles, followed by a 500 ms delay and an event-loop yield. It can compete with reconnect work, but its entire reported duration is not time-to-ready. The useful critical-path reduction here is avoiding full retained-payload reads during registry metadata initialization. No new parallel startup owner or unbounded background task was introduced.

prs.title: feat(ui): lift plugin theme backgrounds toward the shared cap above default visibility
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin theme backgrounds (#172627) are painted under a theme-colored scrim fixed at the palette-safe default upload strength. The viewer's **Image visibility** slider only scales a second surface layer, which is already at full opacity from 50% upward, so moving the slider above the default changes nothing. On a near-black palette the contrast ceiling is low, so a dark image is barely visible even at 100%. Ghost Claw's firehouse-at-night background shows at about 9% and the slider cannot lift it.

## Change

- Above the default visibility, the plugin-art scrim now thins linearly from the palette-safe default strength to the shared `BACKGROUND_IMAGE_OPACITY_CAP` (32%) that every background image already stops at, reaching the cap at 100%.
- At or below the default visibility nothing changes, so existing defaults and the text-contrast protection stay as they are.
- `syncThemeBackgroundArtwork` accepts the saved visibility and repaints the token on slider changes without refetching the image. `bootstrap-theme` passes it through.
- The cap moves from a literal in `backgroundImageOpacityLimit` to an exported constant shared by both owners.
- Docs: plugin manifest surfaces and Control UI settings describe the behavior above the default.

## Evidence

### Before / after

Control UI new-session page against a mock Gateway, Ghost Claw palette, **Full bleed**, Image visibility 100%. Same build, same image bytes.

| Before (`main`, 100%) | After (this branch, 100%) |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: plugin background at 100% visibility on main, image strength 8.7%](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5e6a3587-3df5-4ef2-9d7b-a4eb4e9b8c07) | ![After: plugin background at 100% visibility, image strength 32%](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9e6b82d4-d4c6-47d3-aceb-6bef0778ff10) |

Default 50% on this branch, unchanged from `main` (scrim 91.3% in both):

![After at the default 50% visibility, identical to main](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/84323442-b548-4afa-8161-b177571d7be6)

Measured `--app-background-image` scrim on the root token:

| Visibility | `main` | This branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 50% (default) | 91.3% | 91.3% |
| 100% | 91.3% | 68% |

### Validation

- `vitest` for `ui/src/app/theme-background-artwork.test.ts` (new case: lift above default without refetch) and `ui/src/components/session-background.test.ts`: 24 passed.
- `ui/src/e2e/theme-plugin-background.e2e.test.ts` (bundled Control UI, Chromium): passed; default-strength assertion unchanged.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm tsgo:test:ui`, `oxfmt --check`, `pnpm format:docs:check`: clean.
- `pnpm check:changed`: all lanes green except two inherited failures untouched by this branch: the `max-lines suppression ratchet` on `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message.test.tsx` (from #173575 on `main`), and the dead export scan reporting `SessionInputLifecycleAdmission`, `formatReturnedAgentErrors`, `renderLazyElementState`, and `renderLazyViewError` in files this PR does not modify. No export added here is flagged.

## Not in scope

Built-in theme artwork and custom uploads keep their existing strength rules. The palette ceiling still applies below the default and the cap still bounds the maximum.

prs.title: feat(tools): per-turn per-target send budget guard for message tools
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds a per-turn, per-target outbound send guard shared by the `message` and `conversations_send` tools to curb within-turn duplicate-answer storms.

The existing loop detector hashes full tool params, so a model that re-sends the same answer with slightly reworded text produces a distinct hash every time and stays invisible to it — a single healthy `200` run can emit six reworded variants of one reply. This adds a lightweight ledger, independent of the loop detector and its default-off switch, that counts *successful* deliveries per (turn, target).

Closes #119992

## What Problem This Solves

A model can emit many reworded copies of the same reply within one turn. The existing tool-loop detector hashes the full stable tool-parameter object, so each reworded body is a distinct call and evades it entirely — a single healthy run can fan out six variants of one answer to the same recipient. Nothing in the ordinary send path accounts for repeated deliveries per turn.

This change adds a shared per-agent-turn, per-destination ledger observed by both the `message` tool and `conversations_send`, giving the model a default-on nudge to finalize after the first repeat and an opt-in hard cap that blocks further sends before dispatch.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The loop detector cannot catch reworded duplicates (it is content-hash based and default-off), so the guard must be independent of it and count *successful* deliveries, not param hashes.
- The two send tools reach the same recipients, so the ledger has to be shared and keyed on one canonical destination identity, or alternating the tools would evade it.
- The ledger must run on the ordinary Gateway execution path (not just embedded/subagent paths), which requires the active run ID to reach the tools that gate on it.

Seven runtime-path defects surfaced in review are fixed here so the guard actually protects the claimed workflow:

- **Gateway path dropped the run ID.** `resolveGatewayScopedTools` forwarded `runId` to the mediated coding tools but not to `createOpenClawTools`, so the `message` tool and `conversations_send` received `runId=undefined` and their ledger contexts declined to activate — the nudge and cap were silently inert for every Gateway-scoped turn. `params.runId` is now forwarded to `createOpenClawTools`; it stays `undefined` on the single-shot HTTP `tools.invoke` path, which correctly leaves the ledger off there.
- **Current-source key split.** `resolveOutboundActionRoute` keyed current-source sends on a literal `<current-source>` sentinel, while `conversations_send` keys on the resolved concrete target. The two never matched, so alternating a no-target source reply with `conversations_send` to the same peer split the count across two ledger slots and bypassed both the nudge and the cap. The current source is now resolved to its concrete target (`currentMessagingTarget ?? currentChannelId`), failing open when it cannot be resolved (mirroring the existing multi-target bail), so both tools share one slot for the same recipient.
- **Routable target not threaded through the Gateway/CLI-loopback chain.** The fallback above resolves to the routable delivery target only if the Gateway scope actually carries `currentMessagingTarget`, but that field was dropped across the whole loopback chain (`GatewayScopedToolParams`, `McpLoopbackRequestContext`, `RunCliAgentParams`, the CLI MCP grant context, the loopback tool cache key, and the `createOpenClawTools` call), so on a gateway turn the key always fell back to the native `currentChannelId`. On channels whose native channel id differs from the routable target, the native/routable identity split was therefore incomplete. The trusted routable target is now threaded end to end and emitted by the CLI reply producer alongside the native id. The direct HTTP path already treats the `x-openclaw-message-to` header as the routable target, so it keeps its `agentTo` fallback. Security: the routable target is trusted only from the server-minted bound grant context — the grant-authenticated header branch fails closed and a spoofed `x-openclaw-current-messaging-target` header can never override the bound value.
- **Ledger key was not canonicalized before admission.** The key was built from the raw agent-typed target text, but the delivery path canonicalizes the recipient later, so equivalent spellings of one peer (case, provider prefix, phone formatting) produced different keys and separate ledger slots — alternating them evaded the guard, and the `message` tool and `conversations_send` did not truly share a slot. The target is now canonicalized through the same synchronous, idempotent, provider-bound normalizer the delivery path uses, inside the shared `buildTurnSendTargetKey`, so both tools converge on one slot. Async directory-alias resolution (`@username` -> id) stays out of scope by design and off the cap hot path.
- **Queued was counted as a delivery.** `conversations_send` recorded a ledger entry on a `queued` status, but `queued` is distinct from `sent` in the gateway protocol and means the intent was enqueued without confirmed delivery. With a cap of one, a queued acknowledgement suppressed the next real send and the nudge falsely reported the message had already been sent. It now counts only confirmed `sent` deliveries, matching the delivery owner and the `message` tool (which has no `queued` concept and already counted only confirmed deliveries).

- **Overlapping same-session runs evicted each other's counts.** The ledger stored one slot per session and reset it whenever a different run recorded on that session. Concurrent foreground turns can share one session key with distinct run ids (see `src/auto-reply/dispatch.freshness.test.ts`, which starts run A, completes run B on the same session, then resumes A), so an A -> B -> A interleave let run B evict run A's slot; when run A resumed, its per-target count read zero and both the nudge and the opt-in cap were silently bypassed — exactly under the concurrency the cap exists to protect. The ledger is now keyed by a composite `(sessionKey, runId)` so overlapping runs keep independent counts. Each slot stays authoritative for the whole run lifetime (no idle expiry) and is deleted by the run owner at its terminal boundary (`clearTurnSendLedgerForRun`, wired into the embedded runner's fallback-chain `finally`); terminal cleanup is the ledger's only delete path — there is deliberately no size-based eviction, because evicting a slot while its run is still live (an idle run while many turns execute concurrently) would silently zero that run's committed counts and release the opt-in cap mid-turn. Retained slots are bounded by the number of concurrently live runs.
- **An idempotent message replay was blocked by the cap.** The message tool evaluated the opt-in per-turn cap before deriving its stable idempotency key and recorded successes with the operation-blind counter, so a retried tool call with the same idempotency key (which the Gateway resolves to the already-completed send and returns the original receipt without re-delivering) was rejected with `turn_send_budget_exhausted` — the model was told a completed send had failed. The key is now derived before the cap, the cap is skipped when that key was already recorded this turn, and success is recorded via `recordTurnSendOnce` so a replay is counted at most once; a genuinely new or reworded send still counts and caps. This matches the `conversations_send` cap, which already admits idempotent replays.
## User Impact

- **Default-on, model-only nudge**: from the second same-target send within a turn, the tool result carries a one-line, model-visible reminder to finalize instead of re-sending. It never alters the outbound message and does not pollute a `message_tool_only` final reply. Opt out via `tools.message.turnSendNudge: false` (per-agent override inherits the global).
- **Opt-in hard cap (default off)**: `tools.message.maxMessagesPerTurnPerTarget` blocks a send before dispatch once the cap is reached, returning `turn_send_budget_exhausted`. Media (`sendAttachment` / `upload-file`) and broadcast fan-out are exempt from the cap but still counted.
- No hash normalization: legitimate distinct messages, multi-part replies, media, and fan-out remain fully allowed. Existing operators who take no action get only the model-visible nudge; nothing blocks delivery unless the opt-in cap is enabled.

## Design notes

- A "turn" is one agent run (`runId`). A slot is authoritative for the entire run lifetime — including long tool waits and provider-fallback candidates that reuse the `runId` — so the opted-in cap holds for the whole turn; the run owner deletes the slot at the terminal run boundary (`clearTurnSendLedgerForRun` from the embedded runner fallback-chain `finally`), and that terminal cleanup is the ledger's only delete path — retained slots are bounded by concurrently live runs, and no size-based eviction ever removes a live run's counts. Module-level, keyed by agent session, mirroring the reviewed `recentPollVoteBySession` precedent.
- Counting always runs regardless of the nudge toggle; only the reminder text is gated.
- The hard cap reserves a slot before dispatch and settles after delivery (reserve-then-settle), so concurrent same-target sends are counted synchronously; documented inline.

## Evidence

Real behavior verified at the two boundaries the guard depends on (redacted local run):

- **Gateway boundary — ledger activates only when the run ID flows through.** `resolveGatewayScopedTools({ runId, surface: "loopback" })` produces a `message` tool whose per-turn cap engages; reverting the `runId` forward makes this fail. Verbatim:
  ```
  gateway-core  src/gateway/tool-resolution.test.ts (11 tests)
    ✓ forwards runId so the message tool per-turn cap engages on the loopback surface
  Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  11 passed (11)
  ```
- **Mixed-tool shared slot — no-target `message` reply + `conversations_send` to the same peer now share one ledger slot.** With `maxMessagesPerTurnPerTarget: 1` the second tool is capped; reverting to the `<current-source>` sentinel makes it deliver (`status: "sent"`) instead of `suppressed`. Verbatim:
  ```
  agents-tools  src/agents/tools/conversation-tools.test.ts (15 tests)
  Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  15 passed (15)
  ```
- **Routable-target threading boundary — native id != routable target still share one ledger slot.** `resolveGatewayScopedTools` with `currentChannelId: "D123"` (native) and `currentMessagingTarget: "user:U123"` (routable) differing: a pre-seeded routable slot and a no-target source send resolve to the same key and hit the cap. Reverting the routable-param forward makes this fail (verified). The header fail-closed invariant is covered: a spoofed `x-openclaw-current-messaging-target` header leaves the bound routable target undefined. Verbatim:
  ```
  gateway-core  src/gateway/tool-resolution.test.ts / mcp-http.request.test.ts / mcp-grant-context.test.ts
  Tests  24 passed
  ```
- **Canonical shared-slot boundary — equivalent spellings collapse to one ledger slot.** `buildTurnSendTargetKey` now runs the target through the provider normalizer, so two spellings of one peer produce a byte-identical key (verified by a spelling-equivalence unit test). Because both tools flow through this one builder, `message` and `conversations_send` to the same peer share one slot.
- **Queued does not consume a slot.** A `queued` (unconfirmed) `conversations_send` result no longer records a delivery or emits the false nudge; a subsequent `sent` to the same conversation is admitted as the first counted delivery. Verified by a queued-then-sent regression under `maxMessagesPerTurnPerTarget: 1` plus a table over `suppressed`/`queued`/`unknown`. Verbatim:
  ```
  agents-tools  src/agents/tools/turn-send-ledger.test.ts / conversation-tools.test.ts
  Tests  27 passed
  ```
- **Overlapping-run isolation boundary — interleaved runs on one session keep independent counts.** With the ledger keyed by `(sessionKey, runId)`, an A -> B -> A interleave keeps run A's count climbing (`record(A)=1`, `record(B)=1`, `record(A)=2`, `peek(A)=2`, `peek(B)=1`) and per-run operation-id isolation holds; the A -> B -> A regression fails on the pre-fix single-slot code (the resumed run A reads a reset count of 1 instead of 2). The new tests are anchored to the concurrent-same-session behavior proven in `src/auto-reply/dispatch.freshness.test.ts`. Verbatim:
  ```
  agents-tools  src/agents/tools/turn-send-ledger.test.ts (16 tests)
  Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  16 passed (16)
  ```
- **Idempotent-replay-past-cap boundary — a retried send at the cap reaches delivery dedup.** With `maxMessagesPerTurnPerTarget: 1`, a first send is admitted and counted, a replay of the same tool call (same idempotency key) is not cap-blocked and returns the completed receipt without double-counting or a false nudge, and a genuinely different send is still capped. The regression fails on the pre-fix code (the replay came back `suppressed`/`turn_send_budget_exhausted`). Delivery-layer dedup here applies to Gateway-routed sends (the `conversations.send` `operationId` store); direct-mode channels do not yet dedup on the idempotency key at the delivery layer — tracked in #125824.
- Both regressions were confirmed to have teeth by reverting each production change and observing the corresponding test fail.
- Full suite for the feature: `turn-send-ledger.test.ts` + `message-tool.test.ts` + `conversation-tools.test.ts` pass; `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:core:test` exit 0; changed files pass `oxlint --type-aware`.
- Rebased onto latest `upstream/main`; clean.




- **Live-run budget retention boundary — the cap survives long idle waits and provider fallbacks.** The 10-minute idle TTL is deleted: a `(sessionKey, runId)` slot now lives for the whole run and is removed only at the run's terminal boundary. Regressions (fake timers): a capped run stays `exhausted` after an idle interval far past the old TTL (this fails on the pre-fix TTL code — verified by temporarily restoring the prune), a committed operation is still admitted as a `replay` across the same idle wait, and `clearTurnSendLedgerForRun` deletes only the exact `(session, run)` slot (siblings on the same session and same-runId slots on other sessions stay intact; missing scope/slot is a no-op). Run-entry tests prove the budget survives the fallback boundary and is cleared on both success and throw paths. Verbatim:
  ```
  agents-tools  src/agents/tools/turn-send-ledger.test.ts (28 tests)
  embedded-agent-runner  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run-entry.test.ts (22 tests)
  Test Files  passed   Tests  50 passed
  ```
- **Direct-mode replay cap guard — a duplicate model-emitted tool-call id is disambiguated into a distinct cap-blocked send, not admitted as a replay.** The discriminating regression drives the real streaming normalization (`wrapStreamFnTrimToolCallNames` -> `normalizeToolCallIdsInMessage`): a model response emitting the same `message` tool-call id twice with byte-identical arguments is rewritten to two distinct ids, so the copies derive different idempotency keys and the second is cap-blocked with a schema-valid `turn_send_budget_exhausted` result while the runner is invoked exactly once. This guards the exact mechanism that keeps the replay-admission branch unreachable from a real model turn on direct channels (the delivery-layer dedup gap for an admitted replay is tracked separately in #125824). Verbatim:
  ```
  agents-tools  src/agents/tools/message-tool.test.ts (253 tests)
  Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  253 passed (253)
  ```

- **Route-aware replay admission boundary — a replay is only admitted past the cap when the selected delivery route dedups it.** The message tool resolves the actual gateway-vs-direct delivery route BEFORE reserving and hands the operationId to the ledger only when delivery relays through the Gateway backend (whose completed-result store dedups the repeated operationId). On direct in-process routes a repeated operation is treated as an ordinary new send: cap-blocked when a cap is set, honestly counted otherwise — closing the hole where an admitted replay on a direct channel would re-deliver because the delivery layer does not dedup idempotency keys there (tracked in #125824). Route detection fails conservative: when unsure it withholds the operationId, which cap-blocks a replay rather than re-delivering it. Regressions drive the REAL delivery path (actual outbound adapter call counts): a direct-route replay is suppressed and delivers exactly once, and a Gateway-routed replay is admitted without re-delivering or double-counting. Both fail on the pre-fix unconditional replay admission. Verbatim:
  ```
  agents-tools  src/agents/tools/message-tool.test.ts (254 tests)
  Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  254 passed (254)
  ```
- **Run-terminal budget release boundary — a reused runId starts the next turn with a fresh budget, and fallback candidates never lose committed counts mid-chain.** `prepareCliRunContext` records the exact ledger slot (agent/session/run) the loopback grant mints; CLI settlement deletes only that slot, and only at the true terminal — success or the FINAL fallback attempt's failure. A non-final failure hands off to the next candidate, which must inherit the committed counts, so settlement defers; a dispatched CLI candidate (no `isFinalFallbackAttempt`) defers to the embedded runner's fallback-chain owner, keeping exactly one cleanup owner per terminal. The threw state is derived from real control flow (a `completedNormally` flag), not from `runError`, so a `settleCliAuthProfile` throw after a successful non-final candidate defers exactly like a non-final run failure instead of wiping the budget mid-chain (discriminating regression: the pre-fix `runError` proxy fails it). Cron's isolated-agent finally adds a bounded, idempotent safety net keyed identically to the loopback grant (same `canonicalizeMainSessionAlias` composition, durable session id as runId), so a chain that throws before any candidate settles still releases the slot. Verbatim:
  ```
  agents-support  src/agents/cli-runner/cli-run-settlement.test.ts (18 tests)
  cron            src/cron/isolated-agent/run.turn-send-ledger.test.ts (1 test)
  agents-tools    src/agents/tools/turn-send-ledger.test.ts (28 tests)
  Test Files  3 passed (3)   Tests  47 passed (47)
  ```

### Real delivery-boundary proof (mock provider + mock channel, ephemeral Gateway, in a container)

Added `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/per-turn-send-budget.e2e.test.ts`: a real-behavior proof that boots an ephemeral Gateway child with the mock-openai provider and the `qa-channel` synthetic transport, then exercises the shared per-turn send ledger at the real delivery boundary (Gateway + qa-channel outbound bus), not by stubbing `callGateway`. It was run inside a clean `node:24-bookworm` container with container-local Linux dependencies (not just a host unit run). All scenarios pass and the run emits a machine-readable verdict:

```
test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/per-turn-send-budget.e2e.test.ts (8 tests)
  ✓ sanity: a plain qa-channel DM turn delivers one outbound reply
  ✓ scenario 1: second confirmed message send in one turn nudges and both deliveries land
  ✓ scenario 2: hard cap returns a schema-valid suppressed conversations_send result
  ✓ scenario 3: a suppressed message send does not charge the per-turn budget
  ✓ scenario 4: idempotent conversations_send replay does not re-deliver or double count
  ✓ scenario 5: two concurrent distinct-op sends to one target admit exactly one under the cap
  ✓ scenario 6: a model-repeated direct message send under the cap is disambiguated and cap-blocked (exactly-once delivery) — proves the cap-block path, NOT idempotent admission
  ✓ scenario 7: a spoofed attach-grant principal is refused before any delivery I/O (authority chain)
Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  8 passed (8)
```

Verdict (`pass: true`), summarized per scenario:

- **Soft nudge counts confirmed deliveries** — two confirmed `message` sends to one target land on the qa-channel bus; the second tool result carries the model-visible "already sent 2 messages to this target this turn" nudge. `deliveriesRecorded: 2`, ledger `{ "qa-channel:qa-operator": 2 }`.
- **Hard cap returns a schema-valid suppressed result** — with `maxMessagesPerTurnPerTarget: 1`, only one delivery reaches the bus; the second `conversations_send` returns `status: "suppressed"` with details that pass `Value.Check(ConversationSendResultSchema, details)` (only `status`, `conversationRef`, `channel`; no `reason`/`message`) and the block explanation in the result text. `deliveriesRecorded: 1`.
- **Only visible deliveries charge the budget** — applying the production `deliveredNothing` predicate: `suppressed` and `failed` do not count (`0`), `partial_failed` counts (`1`, a visible partial reached the peer), plugin/gateway `undefined` counts (`1`), `sent` counts (`1`); no false "sent" nudge is emitted for a non-delivery.
- **Idempotent conversations_send replay** — replaying the same `operationId` returns the Gateway's completed `sent` receipt without a second bus delivery, is not cap-blocked, and does not double-count. `deliveriesRecorded: 1`, ledger stays at `1`.
- **Concurrent distinct-op sends under the cap (reserve-then-settle)** — two parallel `conversations_send` calls with distinct operationIds (NOT a replay) to the same conversation under `maxMessagesPerTurnPerTarget: 1`: the first in-flight reservation counts toward the cap synchronously, so the second call is exhausted before it reaches the Gateway — exactly one delivery lands on the bus and the ledger commits exactly one send. This is the core concurrency regression for #119992 (the old peek→await→record path let both peek 0 and both deliver).
- **Cap-blocked model-repeated direct send (cap-block proof, NOT idempotent admission)** — the mock provider emits the SAME direct `message` send twice in one model response (identical planned call id and byte-identical args). The runtime disambiguates the duplicate model-emitted ids into two distinct tool-call ids, so the copies derive different idempotency keys: the first delivers, and the second is cap-blocked before dispatch with a schema-valid `turn_send_budget_exhausted` result fed back to the model. Exactly-once delivery is asserted on the RECEIVE side — the qa-channel outbound bus carries exactly one copy of the marker, and a re-delivered copy would surface as a second. This proves end-to-end cap enforcement for the direct `message` tool at the real delivery boundary; it proves the cap-block path, not the idempotent-admission path (a duplicate model-emitted send is always disambiguated upstream and can never be presented as an idempotent replay).
- **Authority chain — an unauthorized principal is refused before any delivery I/O (scenario 7).** The harness's own `attach.grant` method mints a real non-owner grant; the test then drives the REAL MCP loopback HTTP entry with that grant plus spoofed delivery-authority headers (`x-session-key`, message channel, account id, current channel id, and `x-openclaw-current-messaging-target` pointed at a registered conversation) — every hop is the genuine defense, with no mocked resolver output: `validateMcpLoopbackRequest` → `resolveAttachGrant` → `resolveMcpRequestContext` (grant branch forces every spoofable header, including the routable target, to undefined) → owner-only tool deny. Asserted: `tools/list` does not advertise `conversations_send` for the grant principal; a `tools/call conversations_send` attempt is refused; and zero deliveries reach the qa-channel bus. Positive control on the same lane: the legitimate owner-bound path (real Gateway `conversations.send` → qa-channel bus, as scenarios 2/4/5) delivers exactly one — so the zero above is a real refusal, not a dead harness. Verdict entries carry no tokens.

Full unit suite for the feature (`turn-send-ledger.test.ts` + `message-tool.test.ts` + `conversation-tools.test.ts` + `cli-run-settlement.test.ts` + cron `run.turn-send-ledger.test.ts`) passes; `tsgo:core`/`tsgo:extensions`/`tsgo:test:root` exit 0; changed files pass `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check`. Rebased onto latest `upstream/main`; clean.

### Final-head validation (HEAD `782540cd69f`)

Second upstream catch-up: the published branch was brought up to current `upstream/main` via an ordinary merge commit that merged main `36537b21828`. No published commit was rewritten, so the branch stays a descendant of its published head `97eb46dc643` and an ordinary fast-forward push applies. This second merge only resolved the generated config-documentation baseline conflicts (`docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json` / `.sha256`, core option count settles at 2450) alongside the auto-merged code; the CHANGELOG Unreleased section is byte-identical to the merged upstream parent.

Re-verified on this final head `782540cd69f`:

- **Real qa-lab per-turn-send-budget E2E: 8/8 passing.** All eight stable scenario outcomes are pre-registered and fail-closed — the run asserts no missing, duplicate, unknown, or unsuccessful outcome; every registered scenario reports its expected result and the machine-readable verdict is `pass: true`.
- **Typecheck green:** `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, and `tsgo:test:root` all exit 0.
- **Focused tests: 759 passing** across the feature's unit and integration suites, plus proof 9/9.
- **Config docs / lint / format / diff check green:** config docs generation, `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` are all clean.
- **Autoreview (honest scope note):** the final PR-tree fresh autoreview was scoped-clean with 0 P0–P2 findings on the predecessor head `97eb46dc643`, run over the PR tree against that merge commit's second parent `8e1f02805f66` (exact `upstream/main`). This second catch-up merge (`782540cd69f`) only resolved the generated config-baseline conflicts and did **not** receive a new fresh autoreview on `782540cd69f`.

Note: the Telegram (D5) live-channel proof from earlier revisions was not rerun on this final head; the validation above covers the qa-lab delivery-boundary E2E, typecheck, focused tests, config/lint/format/diff, and the prior scoped-clean autoreview.



### CI line-cap ratchet remediation (HEAD `4bcae80db14`)

CI job `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` failed at `782540cd69f`: the send-budget work pushed eight grandfathered files past their `check:line-cap-ratchet` baseline (deterministic against the merge base `36537b21828`). No cap was raised, no rule disabled, and no coverage trimmed — each file drops back to or below its base counted-line count by relocating cohesive helpers and the new send-budget test group into focused sibling modules:

- `message-tool-execution.ts` → `message-tool-turn-send-budget.ts` (turn-send-budget resolve/reserve/settle/nudge orchestration).
- `message-tool.test.ts` → `message-tool.turn-send-budget.test.ts` for the per-turn-send-budget group; `createChannelPlugin` and the runner-input type shared via `message-tool.test-support.ts`. The tool-assembly wiring assertion stays where its `createOpenClawTools` mocks live.
- `command/attempt-execution.ts` → `attempt-execution-auth-profile.ts` (harness auth-profile selection).
- `cli-runner/prepare.ts` → `auth-profile-resolution.ts` (CLI auth-profile resolution).
- `config/schema.labels.ts` → `schema.labels.message-tool.ts` (the `tools.message.*` label block).
- `agent-runner-memory.test.ts` / `gateway/mcp-http.test.ts` → `*.test-support.ts` siblings (flush-plan fixtures / schema-builder helpers).
- qa-lab `mock-openai/server.ts` → `mock-openai-per-turn-send-budget.ts` (QA-PTSB fixtures) and `mock-openai-tool-call-input.ts` (tool-call input parsers).

Validation on this head (`4bcae80db14`):

- `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet --base 36537b21828` and `pnpm check:max-lines-ratchet --base 36537b21828` both green; `git diff --check` clean.
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:extensions:test` all exit 0.
- `oxlint` (core + extensions) and `oxfmt --check` clean on the changed files.
- Feature suites green: `message-tool.turn-send-budget.test.ts` + `turn-send-ledger.test.ts` (53), and the parent `message-tool.test.ts` + `agent-runner-memory.test.ts` + `mcp-http.test.ts` suites.
- Real qa-lab `per-turn-send-budget.e2e.test.ts`: **8/8** passing (re-run because the QA fixture organization changed).

The eight node-compact shard failures on the prior run were single integration tests timing out at exactly 120000ms; each reproduced green locally (`message-tool.scheduled-writes` 7/7, and feishu-mutations + channel/slack read-authority 124/124), so they were CI resource-contention flakes, not a regression — left for the fresh run to clear rather than triggering unrelated edits. prs.title: perf(sessions): trust internal transcript hydration frames
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Full transcript hydration repeats structural validation of every chunk and frame constructed by its paired local worker.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior or stored format changes. Full transcript and correction reads do less redundant work. Bounded model-context reads do not use this stream and are unaffected.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bundled producer constructs `SessionTranscriptHydrationChunk` under its admitted database snapshot. The receiver now consumes that shared internal contract without repeating object, array, byte-view, and boolean checks. JSON decoding, row-sequence requirements, complete-stream checks, database admission, identity, read fences, and cancellation remain in their existing owners.

Production delta: 4 added / 18 deleted, net **−14 lines**. Simplification pass removed the obsolete malformed-internal-view tests while retaining cross-realm decoding. Added focused coverage for malformed JSON, missing sequences, partial events, and event-count mismatch.

## Evidence

Synthetic receiver microbenchmark on an isolated Linux sandbox, restricted CPU set and memory, no production state. The unchanged production `readTranscript` method was extracted from base/head source and fed identical producer-shaped chunks (64 KiB slices, at most 128 frames or 1 MiB per chunk). Three alternating pairs per scenario (before/after, after/before, before/after), separate processes, 20 warmups each. CPU includes the receiver and synthetic callback driver; allocations use V8 heap sampling.

| Scenario | Before CPU ms/read | After CPU ms/read | Before allocated MiB/read | After allocated MiB/read |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 5,000 short events, 2.923 MiB, 100 reads/run | 4.2730 | 4.2622 | 7.4579 | 7.4644 |
| 128 large events, 16.012 MiB, 30 reads/run | 8.7992 | 8.7226 | 32.1278 | 32.0174 |

Medians are **neutral within noise**; this is a requested net-deletion simplification, not a claimed throughput win. This isolates receiver cost: it does not measure SQLite, worker transport, a full Gateway, production traffic, or stress throughput.

Focused checks: the reader and hydration-worker files passed (18 tests; 84.51 s Vitest wall time, about 3.2 s test execution). The final reader rerun after the review-suggested fixture correction passed all 14 tests (58.18 s Vitest wall time, about 7 ms test execution). Changed-file oxfmt, core-config oxlint, and git diff --check passed. The initial lint invocation selected the broad declaration-preparation route and was stopped; the core-config invocation completed successfully. Broad validation belongs to PR CI; no Testbox/Crabbox lease, local suite, build, or repo-wide typecheck was run.

Review: independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable). The configured helper refused provider-route preflight; operator configuration was not changed. Review is clean for P0–P2; the suggested test correction isolates unfinished-frame detection from event-count mismatch.

PR CI passed on `1277b7b5b5fc51b4e8b4a78ce84af3978cbf8513`: [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38842613509), including changed-code tests, broad lint/typechecks, build artifacts, UI E2E, and the aggregate CI gate. No retries or inherited-failure exception were needed.
