prs.title: fix(logging): preserve non-secret env references; add exemption list and redaction notification
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

OpenClaw's text redaction is always-on and runs over model-visible tool payloads and persisted transcripts. Four related DX problems bite agent-driven work:

1. **Non-secret references get masked.** A value like `process.env.FOO` after a secret-looking key is treated as a credential and masked, corrupting source/config content. Repro on `2026.9.6`: `const token = ***;` -> `const token = ***;`.
2. **No escape hatch for false positives.** `logging.redactPatterns` only *adds* patterns, so a deployment cannot exempt a benign value that keeps getting masked.
3. **Redaction is easy to miss.** `***` / `proces…OKEN` is indistinguishable from real content.
4. **No Control UI signal.** Redaction never reached the Control UI, so an operator watching a session could not see that a secret was masked.

## Why this change was made

**1. Preserve non-secret references.** `isNonSecretReferenceValue` recognizes `process.env.FOO`, `process.env["FOO"]`, `os.environ["FOO"]`, `os.environ.get("FOO")`, `os.getenv("FOO")`, `getenv("FOO")` and skips masking them. Anchored on the raw input from the capture start so bracket/quote forms truncated by the capturing pattern are still recognized; applies only to assignment-family patterns - vendor-token and header patterns keep masking.

**2. `logging.redactAllowPatterns`.** Regex strings (same `/…/flags` syntax as `redactPatterns`). A candidate secret value matching any exempt pattern is left unmasked. Default `[]` leaves behavior unchanged; registered exact secret values stay masked. Wired through value-pattern redaction, the sensitive-redaction bitmap, and structured-field redaction; plus config schema, help, labels, and docs.

**3. Obvious notification.** Model-visible redaction replaces masked spans with a self-describing marker (`⟦redacted⟧`) instead of the ambiguous `***`/hint, and appends a one-line notice to the tool content when redaction changed it. Diagnostic log surfaces keep the compact `***`.

**4. Control UI panel.** New `session.redaction` gateway event, scoped `SESSION_READ_SCOPE` and broadcast to session subscribers when a projected `session.message` carries a model-visible redaction marker/notice (`containsModelVisibleRedaction`). The Control UI handles it in `handleGatewayEvent` and raises a notification panel via `showToast`. The event carries only session scope plus a timestamp - no secret material.

## Evidence

### Unit tests (branch)

`src/logging/redact.test.ts` covers, with values assembled from parts (so the diff contains no credential-shaped literal):

- complete references (`process.env.<NAME>` assignments) are preserved on every sink;
- a capture that merely **starts** with a reference (the reference-prefixed credential case) is masked - regression for the prefix bypass;
- truncated reference captures (`os.environ["…"]`, `os.getenv("…")`) stay masked (safety boundary);
- synthetic secrets and vendor-shaped tokens are still masked.

### Sink-level trace (real redactor, synthetic values)

Produced with the production 2026.9.6 redaction bundle carrying this PR's guard changes, exercising the same registered sinks the gateway uses (log, diagnostic, model-visible). No private values involved - all inputs synthetic:

| Sink | Input (synthetic) | After redaction |
|---|---|---|
| log sink (redactSensitiveText) | `complete reference` | `token = process.env.GATEWAY_TOKEN;` |
| log sink (redactSensitiveText) | `reference-prefixed credential` | `token=proces…tial` |
| log sink (redactSensitiveText) | `synthetic secret` | `MY_TOKEN=aaaaaa…aaaa` |
| diagnostic sink (redactToolPayloadTextWithConfig) | `complete reference` | `token = process.env.GATEWAY_TOKEN;` |
| diagnostic sink (redactToolPayloadTextWithConfig) | `reference-prefixed credential` | `token=proces…tial` |
| diagnostic sink (redactToolPayloadTextWithConfig) | `synthetic secret` | `MY_TOKEN=aaaaaa…aaaa` |
| model-visible sink (redactModelVisibleToolPayloadText) | `complete reference` | `token = process.env.GATEWAY_TOKEN;` |
| model-visible sink (redactModelVisibleToolPayloadText) | `reference-prefixed credential` | `token=process.env.FOO-privateCredential` |
| model-visible sink (redactModelVisibleToolPayloadText) | `synthetic secret` | `MY_TOKEN=aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa` |

Legend: the complete reference stays intact on every sink; the reference-prefixed
credential and the synthetic secret are masked (diagnostic/log sinks keep a short
hint, the model-visible sink emits the self-describing marker and appends the notice).

Note: the model-visible sink intentionally keeps upstream's narrow assignment policy (assignment-family patterns are excluded from model-visible payloads), so the new exemption does not change what that sink masks; the fix targets the log and diagnostic sinks where the bypass was found.

## Review fixes in this revision

- **[P1] reference-prefix bypass - fixed.** `isNonSecretReferenceValue` now requires the **entire captured value** to be a complete reference (`$`-anchored alternation, evaluated on the delimiter-stripped capture). A capture like the review's reference-prefixed credential example no longer qualifies and is masked on log and diagnostic sinks (see sink trace). Regression test added; the bitmap path got the same boundary.
- **Input-safety hold - fixed.** The credential-shaped literal fixtures are gone; all fixtures are assembled programmatically from parts, so the diff no longer contains token-shaped strings.
- **Real behavior proof - added.** Sink-level trace above covers a real log sink, diagnostic sink, and model-visible sink, including a synthetic secret that must still be masked.
- **Line-cap ratchet - partially addressed.** The model-visible marker/notice presentation moved into the sibling module `src/logging/redact-model-visible.ts`. If `src/logging/redact.ts` still exceeds its baseline, I'll split the reference exemption and the allow-list feature into separate PRs - guidance welcome.
- **Maintainer security approval** - requested; the `session.redaction` payload carries only session scope and a timestamp.

prs.title: refactor: consolidate small helper owners across runtime and plugins
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Small helper responsibilities were implemented independently throughout core, bundled plugins, packages, UI and tooling. The implementations looked alike but had enough policy differences that blanket textual replacement would be unsafe.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible change, migration, or configuration action. External-input validation, security/effect authority, common-path durability, FIFO ordering, and write settlement remain at their existing boundaries.

## Why This Change Was Made

Consolidate the exact families onto their existing owners: record/string and numeric normalization, marker/UTF-8 truncation, literal text and HTML escaping, POSIX argument quoting, plain text-block extraction, SHA-256, filesystem discovery probes, optional lstat, nullable JSON-object reads, descriptor flush/hash and UTF-8 HTTP JSON serialization. Bundled plugins consume private SDK facades, including one small crypto-runtime facade so hash-only imports do not load filesystem/runtime owners. No public SDK budget is changed. Keep admission, cache-header, filesystem authority, durability and presentation policy at their existing boundaries.

The whole-tree inventory classifies 393 original exact helper-family hits (320 KEEP / 69 CONSOLIDATE / 4 DELETE), five supplemental native-language hits (KEEP), and 98 semantic duplicate clusters (62 KEEP / 36 CONSOLIDATE). There are no undecided hits. Distinct policies, external-input guards, native-language contracts, and frozen/bootstrap boundaries remain separate deliberately. The requested per-hit coverage/provenance ledger is retained at `.local/z16-ledger.md` in the campaign worktree. No CHANGELOG.md or restricted scripts/pr closure edits.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Remove LM Studio's read-only string-list shallow copy. Its introducing onboarding work (#114405, commit b6c3ff1aa1a) was not a mutation-isolation repair, and current consumers only read, filter or build Sets. A future mutating consumer must own its mutation rather than imposing copies on every read.
- Remove LM Studio's duplicate unconfigured-header record check: the canonical helper validates the external value once. Configured secret resolution retains its own boundary and is unchanged.
- Reuse the existing UTF-8 truncation owner instead of parallel byte-budget loops. The original truncation work (#139911, commit 071f606eae7; sibling ad861d4c9df) does not establish a contract for isolated malformed surrogates. Valid Unicode and byte limits remain preserved; malformed isolated surrogates follow the canonical encoder's replacement behavior.
- Plain text-block extraction no longer separately rejects exotic arrays carrying named type/text properties. The Ollama source (#164804, commit 07a870b2eaa) handles ordinary JSON provider responses, where that shape cannot be represented. Genuine external input shape checks remain.
- Filesystem discovery remains best effort: inaccessible optional candidates remain absent, exactly as before. ENOENT-only operations still propagate other errors; symlink, permission, atomic write and durability policies are not weakened.
- Keep filesystem operations on the existing private filesystem facade. Hash-only callers instead use the two-line crypto facade, and pure text callers use the lightweight string-normalization facade, so those consumers do not acquire the filesystem/runtime graph.

## Evidence

Net production-source reduction after conflict reconciliation, CI repairs, and the conservative workspace cut: **808 lines** (1,097 added, 1,905 removed across 333 production source files), excluding tests, fixtures, generated files, declarations, docs, and baseline text. This uses the campaign's explicit 500–999-line exception after the exhaustive family pass; no unrelated padding.

Local proof uses isolated HOME/OpenClaw/XDG roots; no operator state or Gateway is touched. Hosted CI on the exact PR head is the broad proof.

- Core/package, extension, UI and scripts typechecks passed. Formatting, changed-source boundary lint, assertion/max-lines ratchets, SDK registration and surface checks passed. Public SDK surface remains 3,761 exports / 2,196 callables; no budgets were widened.
- Runtime cycles and static/madge cycles both passed at zero on b718d0819e928e7bd0e522ae28eabb0d9fe838db. The subsequent four-file correction has scoped graph proof: three runtime bodies unchanged, original container body restored, one removed bootstrap edge, and the sole added crypto edge terminates in a four-file pure-library closure with no path back to a plugin.
- Completed focused proof includes owner contracts (9 files / 138 assertions), core consumer shards (51 / 630), DOM (11 / 220), chat/infra shards (5 / 66), Feishu/Memory Core (2 / 19), bootstrap guard (1 / 16), and container/bind paths (1 / 10 selected assertions). Interrupted broader commands are partial evidence, not complete-suite passes. Native Node source import, normalization package declarations, and real loopback HTTP JSON serialization also passed.
- Review accepted and repaired a heavy filesystem-facade dependency for scalar hashing. Type/build proof caught missing stat/hash imports and a package dependency entering CLI bootstrap; those were repaired rather than relaxing guards. The Node-only bootstrap probe is intentionally retained.

Local gaps: ordinary broad type-aware lint and the global SQLite audit were stopped without a passing result; exact-head CI owns that broad proof. The readiness-observer child test twice produced empty stdout at its unchanged 5,000ms child deadline, while the other 25 assertions passed. This is an unresolved local failure, **not proven inherited**. A browser annotation test could not collect because isolated HOME lacked pinned Chromium; DOM proof passed. No timeout, retry, skip, assertion, or kept-behavior baseline was weakened.

Fresh four-file correction review completed scoped-clean at P2 after source verification. The original pre-rebase suppression test passed all three assertions; the post-rebase result is recorded separately below. The corrected selected build was deliberately stopped before changing source for GitHub-reported conflicts; it is not a passing build. Two isolated canonical API comparisons ended without a result: the first was stopped after over an hour in declaration rendering, and the repaired-head attempt was interrupted during session recovery without producing either revision snapshot. Neither is compatibility proof. A supported remote route is being checked; the passing surface-budget check is separate. Current CI only reports that comparison on manual/release dispatches, so no hosted API-diff pass is claimed. Import profiles have not completed.

Conflict reconciliation against cb64c69beec4b04ecb63965b33b96b60996b88ee preserves main's removal of the Discord timeout helper and MCP adoption hook, plus main's centralized receipt parsing. Only the existing canonical string-array predicate is retained in the MCP/publication conflicts. Current main's pr-simplify pass found no additional repair architecture necessary. On rebased head6d4dabf0b979658e1c5132ffb7e4740cc479f435, runtime and static/Madge cycles passed at zero, extension production types and focused core-graph types passed, SDK registration/public surface passed unchanged, and conflict formatting/whitespace passed. Earlier proof retains its original head attribution.

Rebased local core typecheck found an installation mismatch in untouched `tui-session-actions-test-support.ts`: main's dependency refresh (#172883, 4097fd641f7) pins pi-tui 1.1.0 and adds `setProgramStatus`, but this lane's one-time install still has 1.0.4. Its declaration lacks that method. The fixture is identical to main and this PR has no dependency/lockfile change. No fixture/type suppression was added; clean exact-head CI must cover the current dependency set. Focused conflicted-graph and extension typechecks run separately.

Rebased suppression contracts passed two assertions and failed the allowlist equality: main's cache-worker repair (#173239, e60c548c368) added `typescript/unbound-method` in `src/infra/sqlite-worker-store.test-support.ts`, but the unchanged allowlist lacks that entry. Both owner and test blobs match main exactly; this lane adds no suppressions or allowlist entries. The tooling failure prevented the owned runtime selections in that command, so those suites are running separately. Temporary focused-type configuration errors (inferred `.local` root and missing ambient declarations) were corrected without production or compiler-strictness changes; those failed attempts are not passing proof.

Rebased publication-worker runtime proof: **26 passed / 1 failed**. `commits oversized expiry batches and retires binding coverage before replying` hit its unchanged 120,000ms timeout, followed by worker shutdown timeout. The case seeds 17 extremely long conversation keys to exercise oversized-receipt retirement; this PR does not alter that test, SQLite batching, or receipt limits. The publication delta is the equivalent string-array predicate, but this is **not proven inherited** and no passing result is claimed. A separate MCP run timed out in its first two ordinary config cases at their unchanged 120,000ms deadlines before the substituted sentinel predicate was reached, and was stopped/joined without a passing claim. Exact-head hosted runtime/build proof and the separate canonical API comparison remain required; no timeout or test weakening.

### Exact-head CI repairs

The first ready-head CI run (38800285205, head `6d4dabf0b979658e1c5132ffb7e4740cc479f435`) exposed owned defects: a host SDK import in standalone Diffs browser assets, import-first/duplicate-import errors, an incomplete optional-lstat cutover, and filesystem fixtures that did not cover the preloaded shared helper's Node filesystem instance. These are repaired, not classified as inherited failures. Diffs keeps its original inline external-JSON validation; curated and full-language builds and its config/render tests (2 files / 17 assertions) pass. Worktree callers now use the single optional-lstat owner with explicit ENOENT-only policy, retaining invalid-parent failures. Fixture fixes restore external I/O control without changing any assertion or production discovery behavior.

The complete repair review is scoped-clean at P2. Focused core-graph types pass; runtime and static/Madge cycle checks both pass at zero; import-first/duplicate-import checks pass across all 349 changed source/test files; formatting and diff whitespace pass. The repaired runtime selections assert 123 passes across five files, with one existing Windows-only skip: fs-safe, system-binary resolution, Gateway discovery, worktree Git, and browser discovery. The combined command exits nonzero because the unchanged suppression allowlist mismatch described above still fails (2 pass / 1 fail); no whole-command green is claimed. PR-wrapper inventory passes unchanged, as do the three selected real-service provisioning and file/directory replacement snapshot round-trips.

### Conservative workspace-flow cut

Signed repair `9eb718292dd97729e153b0261ecd39e6cf4fc58e` removes the helper substitutions in `extensions/file-transfer/src/node-host/file-write.ts` and `src/agents/workspace-state-publication.ts` from the PR. Both files now match reconciled base cb64c69beec4b04ecb63965b33b96b60996b88ee byte-for-byte. The workspace E2E timeout below remains unattributed: its qualified local replay never reached assertions, was stopped through native supervision during runtime preparation, and no base replay ran. Dropping these seven lines of cleanup is conservative scope reduction, not a claim that the timeout is fixed or inherited.

The rollback's independent review is scoped-clean at P2 (correctness 0.98); the file-write suite passes all 28 unchanged tests; its strict two-file production graph typecheck, formatting, targeted core lint, and runtime and static/Madge cycles (both zero) pass. Extension lint's declaration preparation hit its unchanged 300,000ms deadline and is not a pass. The mandatory suppression suite again reports the same untouched allowlist mismatch above (2 pass / 1 fail). No source or test suppressions, deadlines, assertions, retries, or skips changed.

### Prior-head CI attribution (not yet merge-ready)

[Run 38809701926](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38809701926) completed red on exact head `9e7b9f67ea9dec2bc2ed0f45e0fbbc8f38e656fb`. All check runs were enumerated. Five underlying failures now have independently matching baseline signatures; two failures remain unresolved. The cancelled stripe's missing proof passes locally on this exact head. No CI reruns or speculative pushes were used.

| Exact-head failing job | Failure | Baseline / remaining proof |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 116681401376 | UI private-server inventory 65 vs 64 | Scheduled main run 38810511907 job 116682662551 fails the same test with the same missing claws-catalog inventory entry. The guard is unchanged by this PR. |
| 116681406737 | Gateway stop/graceful recovery assertion | Main run 38810511907 job 116682662447 fails the same two cases. Main changed shutdown semantics in #173342; these owners/tests are unchanged here. |

| 116681406978 | Scheduler cron.add rejects missing OpenAI authentication | Unrelated PR run 38811857880, head d153e4446a2680d8e221429b8b0ba63b42628604, job 116687867604 reproduces the identical gateway.multi case and route-compatible-auth error. |

A prewarmed remote lease completed its idle window before local source packaging finished, so that attempt produced no remote payload proof. Profiles also remain unproven. ### Current head CI — attribution in progress

Run 38825262926 attempt 1 completed on signed head `9eb718292dd97729e153b0261ecd39e6cf4fc58e`. ### Completed manual Linux proof and API review

Provider `blacksmith-testbox`, lease `tbx_01m511bw20jjtybbh2t8ecw2sv`, backing run 38829036923 tested source head `9eb718292dd97729e153b0261ecd39e6cf4fc58e`, tree `fdf723ee44173d9bc83b978cac52727812ce5856` (synthetic transport commit `96bfe6cab7d8edbeb8bb5d77949a90e84d42fc41`). The retained artifact was subsequently reviewed and its digest verified through the API owner: `e91d4344e5d4d306e9327d463bfb7883cdb10b26393881f30a0d5ff69c3e63a5`, acknowledged as `e91d4344`. No entrypoint/export removals; 167 reachable declaration changes and one parameter-name-only signature change. prs.title: fix(backup): stage offsite scratch archive outside backup sources
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves
On macOS the Gateway service sets `TMPDIR=<stateDir>/tmp`. `openclaw backup create --to <location>` (and the scheduled job from `openclaw backup enable --to ...`) stages its scratch archive in `os.tmpdir()`, which is then inside a backed-up source, so every Gateway-run offsite backup fails with "Backup output must not be written inside a source path". Fixes #173583.

## User Impact
Scheduled offsite backups on macOS Gateways fail every run; only manual runs from a shell with an outside TMPDIR succeed.

## Why This Change Was Made
Local archives already avoid this via `chooseBackupTempRoot`; the offsite path lacked the same handling. This reuses it so the offsite scratch is never placed inside a source path, without weakening the containment check.

## Evidence
- Regression test `register.backup.offsite.test.ts` "creates, verifies, uploads and cleans scratch when TMPDIR is nested inside state": fails before (CLI exit 1), passes after.
- Focused suites 110/110 passed at `ad5d31279` (details below).
- Shipped-CLI repro on macOS with nested TMPDIR: before fails, after creates, verifies and uploads (output below).

---

Reuses `chooseBackupTempRoot` for the offsite scratch archive; when there is no output path, it falls back to the parent of the source that contains the temp dir.

Fixes #173583

## ClawSweeper follow-ups (head `fef80c6a4`)

### P1 — discover sources without validating unused local output
Offsite scratch planning no longer calls `createBackupArchive({ dryRun: true })`.
That dry-run resolved and containment-checked a default local archive path that offsite never uses, so home=workspace=cwd with a safe `TMPDIR` (e.g. `/tmp`) could fail before scratch allocation.
Scratch planning now uses `resolveBackupPlanFromDisk` for the source plan only; containment still applies to the real scratch/archive output.

### Proof — offsite CLI regression (in-process)
Replaced helper-only `src/infra/backup-temp-root.test.ts` with an offsite CLI regression in `src/cli/program/register.backup.offsite.test.ts`:
`creates, verifies, uploads and cleans scratch when TMPDIR is nested inside state`.

Boundary:
- **Before** (scratch = `os.tmpdir()` nested under state): test fails with `CLI exit 1` (archive output rejected as inside a source path).
- **After** (this head): create → verify → upload → list → `backup verify latest` succeed; no leftover `openclaw-backup-*` under the nested TMPDIR.

### Proof — shipped CLI (nested TMPDIR, macOS, 2026-10-16 KST)
Isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` with `TMPDIR=$STATE/tmp` (nested inside state) and filesystem storage `archive`.

**Before** — shipped release CLI `OpenClaw 2026.10.3 (59cb447)`:
```text
Storage location archive initialized: …/offsite
Backup output must not be written inside a source path:
  …/state/tmp/openclaw-backup-owned-K9RE2F/archive.tar.gz is inside …/state
```

**After** — worktree-built shipped CLI head `967a534245027d63861dd83740cae806e2ed88e4` (`node ./openclaw.mjs` → `dist/entry.js`):
```text
$ export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=…/state TMPDIR=…/state/tmp
$ node ./openclaw.mjs storage init archive
Storage location archive initialized: …/offsite

$ node ./openclaw.mjs backup create --to archive --namespace nested-tmp-host \
    --no-include-workspace --claim-namespace --json
# verified: true
# localArchiveRetained: false
# archivePath: storage://archive/backups/nested-tmp-host/20261016T011446Z-84dae7be.tar.gz
# location.key: 20261016T011446Z-84dae7be.tar.gz
create_exit=0

# nested TMPDIR after create: no openclaw-backup-* leftovers
# (only unrelated openclaw-501 dir from other tmp consumers)

$ node ./openclaw.mjs backup list --from archive --namespace nested-tmp-host
20261016T011446Z-84dae7be.tar.gz  26622 bytes (26766 stored)

$ node ./openclaw.mjs backup verify latest --from archive --namespace nested-tmp-host
Backup archive OK: …
Assets verified: 1
verify_exit=0
```

### P2 — reclaim abandoned scratch at the selected fallback root (`fef80c6a4`)
With `TMPDIR` nested inside state, offsite scratch falls back to the parent of the state source (e.g. `/Users/alice/openclaw-backup-owned-*`). Previously nothing maintained that root: `createBackupArchive` runs maintenance inside the new scratch directory (its output parent), and Doctor scans `TMPDIR` plus recorded absolute archive parents, while offsite results record `storage://` URLs. A hard-killed upload could therefore leave its plaintext archive there indefinitely.

`createOffsiteBackupArchive` now runs `maintainBackupScratch({ roots: [chosenTempRoot], repair: true })` through the existing scratch owner before `createBackupScratchDirectory(chosenTempRoot)`, and logs `Removed abandoned backup scratch: …` for each reclaimed directory (same as local `backup create`). Active scratch is still fenced by its lifetime token.

Regression in `src/cli/program/register.backup.offsite.test.ts`:
`reclaims abandoned fallback-root scratch on the next nested-TMPDIR run while preserving active scratch` — seeds an abandoned (token released) and an active (token held) `openclaw-backup-owned-*` directory with `archive.tar.gz` under the fallback root, then runs `backup create --to archive`.
- **Before** (`967a53424` source, new test): fails — `fs.stat(abandoned.directory)` resolves (abandoned scratch survives the next run).
- **After** (`fef80c6a4`): abandoned directory removed, active directory and payload preserved, the run's own scratch retired, nested TMPDIR has no `openclaw-backup-*`; after the active owner finishes, the fallback root has no `openclaw-backup-*` left.

### Tests run
```text
pnpm test src/cli/program/register.backup.offsite.test.ts \
  src/infra/backup-create.test.ts src/commands/backup.test.ts \
  src/infra/backup-scratch.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
# 96/96 passed at fef80c6a4
#   infra 81: register.backup.offsite 5 (incl. new P2 regression), backup-create 59, backup-scratch 17
#   commands 15: backup.test.ts
```


### P2 — surface fallback-root scratch maintenance warnings in the archive JSON (`ad5d31279`)
`createOffsiteBackupArchive` now keeps `maintenance.warnings` from the fallback-root `maintainBackupScratch` call and merges them into `result.warnings` after `createBackupArchive` (which otherwise replaces `warnings` with its own root's maintenance), so JSON consumers see preserved/uninspectable outer scratch.

Regression in `src/cli/program/register.backup.offsite.test.ts`:
`reports fallback-root scratch maintenance warnings in the offsite archive JSON` — places a scratch-named non-directory (`openclaw-backup-strayf`) at the fallback root and runs `backup create --to archive`.
- **Before** (`fef80c6a4` source, new test): fails — `warnings` lacks the `not a directory` warning.
- **After** (`ad5d31279`): warning present in JSON; the stray entry is preserved.

```text
vitest run register.backup.offsite register.backup.product-path register.backup \
  backup-scratch backup-create backup-create.publication --maxWorkers=1
# 6 files, 110/110 passed at ad5d31279
```

prs.title: perf(sessions): skip deep freezing worker publication receipts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session entry patches and transcript rewrites recursively inspect and freeze detached actor receipts immediately before serialization, although that transport does not preserve frozen object descriptors.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. The worker does less work while publishing session state; schemas, stored formats, authority checks, and rollback behavior stay unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the two worker-side deep-freeze passes. Keep the existing structured clones that detach receipts from mutable transaction state and the receiving replica's immutability policy. No new cache or alternate path. Production delta: +6/-11 lines (net -5).

## Evidence

- Focused local checks: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/sessions/session-actor-entry-residency.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-actor-message-rewrite.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 2 files, 14 tests passed; 205.30 s including cold import preparation. Covers consecutive publications, rollback, intervening writes, exact payload preservation, and stale rewrite rejection.
- Changed-file formatting and lint passed. [Full PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38842485307) and all required gates passed on exact head `f4b78b5b425696ac3d4ad531feecbe16bd49ba0e`; no CI retries or inherited-failure exception. No validation leases allocated.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings. The configured review helper refused the requested provider because it did not match the operator configuration; configuration was not changed.

Measured the actual resident entry-patch and correlation-metadata rewrite producers on isolated Linux / Node 26.8.2. Three alternating pairs (base→head, head→base, base→head), fresh synthetic state per process, 50 warmups and 300 measured operations per scenario. Fixture: one resident session, 160 skill metadata rows, 128 transcript messages. Both receipt paths are asserted exercised. Source hashes matched base `204ff97706173276407e022b02afb6437653cb56` and head `f4b78b5b425696ac3d4ad531feecbe16bd49ba0e`.

| Scenario | CPU ms/op, before → after | Sampled MiB/op, before → after | Wall ms/op, before → after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Entry patch | 3.389 → 3.168 (-6.5%) | 1.125 → 0.985 (-12.4%) | 2.987 → 2.813 (-5.8%) |
| Correlation-metadata rewrite | 1.709 → 1.387 (-18.8%) | 0.461 → 0.316 (-31.5%) | 1.510 → 1.154 (-23.6%) |

Values are medians of three runs. Every paired CPU, wall-time, and allocation result improved. Allocation sampling used V8's 4 KiB sampling interval with minor/major collected objects included; it is estimated allocation, not retained heap. CPU is producer-process CPU. The harness invokes the real worker owners and entry receipt transport in-process, not a full Gateway; these measurements do not establish sessions.list/chat.send latency or production-wide memory savings. No full-inventory Gateway stress run was performed. Clone capture, authority validation, and receiving-replica freezing remain intact.

prs.title: fix(crabbox): keep coordinator retry deadline monotonic across clock skew
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a laptop wakes from sleep or an NTP correction steps the system clock backward, `crabbox stop` commands hang far longer than their configured timeout, delaying cloud lease reclamation. The retry deadline is seeded with `Date.now()` and remaining budget is read with `Date.now()`, then passed to `runCommand` → `setTimeout` (monotonic). On wall-clock rewind, `remaining = deadline - Date.now()` is amplified by the rewind delta, so a lease stop configured for `CRABBOX_STOP_TIMEOUT_MS` (~16 min) can hang ~18× longer.

- **Solution**: Replace all five `Date.now()` calls with `performance.now()`, which is monotonic and immune to wall-clock skew.
- **What changed**: `crabbox-worker-command.ts` — 5 calls at L181/196/201 (retry loop) and L285/308 (stop + Azure recovery); `crabbox-worker-command.test.ts` — spy moves to `performance.now`, plus a new rewind regression test; `crabbox-worker-stop-lifetime.test.ts` — Azure recovery spy moves to `performance.now`, plus a new Azure recovery rewind regression test.
- **What did NOT change**: `resolveTimerTimeoutMs`, `CRABBOX_STOP_TIMEOUT_MS`, retry/backoff constants, error messages, coordinator-failure classification. No new imports (Node 16+ exposes `performance` globally). Sibling `Date.now()` deadline patterns in `crabbox-worker-provider.ts`, `crabbox-worker-warm-image.ts`, and `crabbox-worker-node-process.ts` are out of scope; separate budgets, tracked by #162813/#169908.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix puts the deadline seed and remaining-budget read on the same monotonic clock as the `setTimeout` consumer, so `remaining` is always bounded by the original budget.

- **Best fix**: `performance.now()` is the canonical monotonic clock in Node and matches the `setTimeout` consumer's clock domain. Mechanical, line-for-line replacement with no logic change.
- **Alternative**: `process.hrtime.bigint()` is also monotonic but returns nanoseconds and requires conversion.
- **Risk**: None. On systems with no clock skew, both clocks advance at the same rate.

## User Impact

After a laptop wakes from sleep or an NTP correction steps the clock back, Crabbox lease stop commands now respect the configured timeout and give up on time, so workers and cloud leases are reclaimed within their expected cleanup window.

## Evidence

### Dispatcher-triggered teardown (running Gateway, real client, shipped dispatcher)

The **real Gateway** is started via `startGatewayServer` (shipped server kernel + RPC dispatcher); a **real GatewayClient** completes the token-authenticated handshake. `client.request("environments.destroy")` is routed through the **running Gateway's shipped dispatcher** to the `environments.destroy` handler, which calls the **shipped `createCrabboxWorkerProvider` factory** → `provider.destroy(lease)` → `stopLease()` → `stopCrabboxLease()` → `runCrabboxCommandWithCoordinatorRetry()`. `performance.now()` is native (not mocked); `Date.now()` is rewound 90 s between the deadline seed and the budget read.

```console
$ node --import tsx proof-dispatcher-triggered.mts postfix
[gateway] REAL gateway listening on ws://127.0.0.1:18889
[gateway] REAL client authenticated & connected
[rpc] sending environments.destroy through REAL running Gateway (shipped dispatcher)...
[dispatch] environments.destroy handler invoked through shipped dispatcher!
[results] stop timeoutMs: [1005000, 1003830, 1001759]
VERDICT: PASS — bounded within CRABBOX_STOP_TIMEOUT_MS — max=1005000

$ node --import tsx proof-dispatcher-triggered.mts prefix
[gateway] REAL gateway listening on ws://127.0.0.1:18889
[gateway] REAL client authenticated & connected
[rpc] sending environments.destroy through REAL running Gateway (shipped dispatcher)...
[dispatch] environments.destroy handler invoked through shipped dispatcher!
[results] stop timeoutMs: [1005000, 1095000, 1095000]
VERDICT: BUG REPRODUCED — amplified beyond CRABBOX_STOP_TIMEOUT_MS — max=1095000
```

| | pre-fix (`Date.now()`) | post-fix (`performance.now()`) |
|---|---|---|
| running Gateway, `client.request("environments.destroy")` through shipped dispatcher, shipped `createCrabboxWorkerProvider` → `provider.destroy` → `stopCrabboxLease`, 90s rewind | max 1 095 000 ms — amplified +90 000 ms beyond `CRABBOX_STOP_TIMEOUT_MS` (FAIL) | max 1 005 000 ms — bounded within `CRABBOX_STOP_TIMEOUT_MS` (PASS) |

### Focused test suite (pre-fix fail / post-fix pass)

```console
$ npx vitest run extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-command.test.ts extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-stop-lifetime.test.ts
 Tests  62 passed (62)   Duration  28.14s
```

Includes `"keeps the coordinator retry deadline bounded when the wall clock rewinds"` (pre-fix fails `94000 > 5000`, post-fix passes) and `"keeps Azure recovery bounded when the wall clock rewinds"` (pre-fix fails with amplified `recoveryTimeoutMs`, post-fix passes).

## What was not tested

- Full integration with a real Crabbox coordinator endpoint (requires cloud credentials). The proof exercises the deadline math through the shipped provider factory and production `runCommandWithTimeout` with real child processes; only the Crabbox CLI binary is substituted.
- Actual NTP step-back in a live process (simulated via `Date.now` rewind). The proof confirms correct native monotonic behavior with the real Gateway dispatcher; the rewind confirms the bug's credible failure and fix.

prs.title: fix(agents): honor exact NO_REPLY and drop fabricated turn-ending replies
prs.body:
Fixes the source-chat forms of #170147 (fabricated and forced replies after deliberate silence); the Anthropic runtime-context form is handled by #170438. Related: #150539, #85714.

## Problem

OpenClaw conflated deliberate silence, missing output, and an undelivered answer. Canned assistant replies masked missing results, required turns overrode explicit `NO_REPLY`, and consumers used different silence heuristics.

## Fix and user impact

- A final is silent only when its trimmed raw text is exactly `NO_REPLY`. A leading `NO_REPLY` followed by a newline and text delivers that text. Punctuation, lowercase, quotes, JSON, reasoning wrappers, and prose remain visible.
- `prepareAgentRunTerminalReply` classifies once and publishes `meta.terminalReply`. Consumers use that fact; stored-row readers use one exact helper.
- External chats honor `NO_REPLY`, including required turns. Subagents, private completions, and WebChat/Control UI require a result by default. Trusted input handling can explicitly mark result consumption optional, avoiding a duplicate answer to a late peer result.
- When a result is owed, an empty final goes through recovery, then fallback, then one system notice: **"No answer was returned. Ask again if you still need one."** The notice is never an assistant row. External recovery permits an answer or `NO_REPLY`; result-required recovery requires an answer.
- A required, undelivered final in message-tool-only mode gets one hidden retry (send it or choose `NO_REPLY`), then the notice. Optional turns keep private finals quiet.
- Optional turns owe no result: an empty final ends quietly without recovery or notice. Native and CLI results retain the reply obligation through fallback; a clean empty result without an explicitly optional policy still remains fallback-eligible.
- A yielded CLI turn returns its paused continuation metadata even when a result is required. Merely spawning a child without yielding still requires a real private result.
- Canned stand-ins are removed. Authored acknowledgments, classified failure guidance, restart/session-recovery notices, tool warnings, uncertain-delivery notices, media no-ack behavior, and retention warnings remain.

This reverses #168571's suppression of punctuated reasoning placeholders. Replies rejected by narrowed permissions report failure rather than completion. Yields without an authored acknowledgment stay quiet.

Out of scope: run-wait full-result hydration, child-result retention and the `truncated` snapshot field, and the broader waiting-status redesign.

## Evidence

[Before/after Control UI screenshots and synthetic QA-channel receipts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/170534#issuecomment-6198030745).

The [published-driver upgrade proof from v2026.10.3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/170534#issuecomment-6198687389) remains applicable: this PR adds no schema or stored-row changes since that proof; its later repairs change runtime reply policy and test fixtures only.

| Check | Observed result |
|---|---|
| Fleet replay: 90 days, 4 production installs, 21,344 terminal finals, 29 provider/model pairs | 0 silent/visible classification differences; 0 newly visible control text |
| Mutation checks on 15 guarantees | All 15 regressions fail when their fix is removed |
| Live Telegram matrix: 352 turns, 6 models | 205 of 212 non-empty silent-scenario finals were exact `NO_REPLY`; no punctuated, wrapped, lowercase, or trailing near-misses; cross-chat sends 48/48; reactions 48/48; required answers 79/80 (one pre-existing steering overlap) |
| Targeted live re-check at `cc0a8c8` | Cross-chat 16/16 (was 3/8); yields 16/16 without canned status; empty-first recovery 20/20 real answers with no wrong `NO_REPLY`; Control UI 5/5 results |
| Forgotten message tool (#85714) | Scripted 6/6; real required turns: OpenAI 10/10, Anthropic 10/10 |
| Earlier integration at `068b53b8ca2` | 13/13 focused files, 833 tests pass; direct format/lint and diff checks pass |
| Main integration at `063436cbde5` | Merged `8d4e374169b`; conflict owners and terminal/retry/replay/CLI/followup boundaries: 12/12 focused files, 580 tests pass; direct format/lint and diff checks pass |
| Integration repairs at `16b7f78ef93` | 11 repaired files pass (236 tests); core and affected test type lanes, direct lint, and mock-export ratchet pass. The local trusted-obligation Gateway test stopped before startup on stale runtime-artifact publication; fresh-build CI covers that entry point. |
| Optional completion at `9041ced336c` | 11 focused assertions across 4 files pass: optional empty completion, no recovery/fallback, unchanged exact silence, and preserved genuine heartbeat failure; core types and direct lint pass. |
| Empty fallback repair at `3ccbec7ea0b` | 12 targeted files pass (709 tests, including focused reruns of corrected fixtures); required/default clean-empty fallback, optional no-fallback, native/CLI obligation metadata, Codex finalization, and dispatch boundaries covered. Direct format/lint and diff checks pass. |
| Conflict integration and collector proof at `4841cf797c5` | Integrated `20b5969cd83` only after GitHub reported a merge conflict. Collector lifecycle: 230 tests pass, checking captured text in the durable row rather than the lightweight runtime projection. Unchanged plugin-reload suite: 5 tests pass locally. Direct format/lint and diff checks pass. |
| CLI and final CI repairs at `0479f1981de` | CLI reliability 62/62, Gateway agent 394/394, announce fencing 9/9, targeted Slack progress 1/1, versions UI 1/1, and plugin borrowing 5/5 pass. ## What Problem This Solves

A link reader cannot bind a private preview or document to the chat pane that opened it when requests carry only an agent hint.

## User Impact

Plugins can opt into receiving the current pane session key on preview and detail reads. Switching panes retires the previous session's cached preview and in-flight results. Existing readers keep their request shape; a session key never grants repository access.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds optional `sessionScoped` reader metadata and carries the existing pane context through hover, transcript prefetch, and detail requests. The receiving Gateway method remains responsible for authorization. This layer reuses the existing card, cache, request cancellation, and session owners; it adds no authentication or worker lifecycle machinery.

Stack base: #173513 (Enterprise GitHub identity), exact published head mirrored as this PR base branch. The parent review reports a P2 issuer-loss finding in Visitor Access and Team Reports consumers; this layer does not repair it and the complete stack is not merge-ready. GitHub refuses fork PRs in native stacks, so #173513 remains the explicit parent link while the canonical upper layers form their own stack. A separate Factory repository-admission layer and authenticated Enterprise preview consumer follow above this PR.

- Exact head: `778b213fd7989c6d8e07fba579d81e0ced91687c`, based on identity head `7780f92024606c234e8fe0fd585bd0f151c99f2e`.

prs.title: fix(macos): save downloads instead of displaying archive bytes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes file downloads in the macOS dashboard and conversation window displaying ZIP bytes instead of saving a file.

## User Impact

Downloads open the native Save dialog and preserve the current page. Canceling or replacing the document discards the transfer; completed downloads use the existing staged file replacement behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Honor WebKit's download actions and attachment/unsupported-MIME responses, then hand them to the existing native download owner. Keep the document alive through WebKit's expected policy interruption and preserve Gateway certificate authentication.

```text
download link → WebKit download → native Save → staged file commit
```

The shared document host owns conversion and lifetime for both presenters. No second file-writing implementation was added. The change adds 171 production lines and removes 16; added tests cover download, cancellation, document, TLS, and browser-session boundaries. It is reversible and scoped to native macOS downloads; there are no migrations.

## Evidence

- **Before:** production DashboardWindowController at `3bfccdb9bd3` rendered raw ZIP bytes; the Save regression failed.
- **After:** the same fixture opened Save in a disposable macOS 26.6.1 Parallels VM. The OS dialog was confirmed through VM keyboard input, the saved ZIP matched every input byte, and the original page remained open. Attached video and screenshots show both states.
- **Native tests:** 28 tests across six affected suites passed in the VM, including Blob and `target=_blank` HTTP downloads, attachments, unsupported MIME, cancellation/document replacement, pinned self-signed HTTPS, file staging, and existing navigation/conversation behavior.
- **Checks:** Swift build, lint, format, localization verification, `check-changed`, and `git diff --check` passed.

The reproduction uses a synthetic ZIP through the real native controller, not a live authenticated chat. Localhost HTTP fixtures disable external Safe Browsing lookups to avoid dependence on the VM's stalled service; application security preferences are unchanged.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0d1309fb-7ed4-4d59-a19a-54402c8b51b8

![Before: downloading a ZIP replaces the page with raw bytes](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5b34593e-cfda-46fa-9818-ceed48fa76ad)

![After: downloading the same ZIP opens the native Save dialog](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/24957e06-3807-4bb9-aed7-5a11eb94c6ed)
## Download authority proof

The follow-up uses the same production document/transfer owners in the disposable Parallels VM, with synthetic loopback HTTPS and a real `DashboardBrowserSessionStore.Lease`. The application code is unchanged from `23470b66003f`.

| Scenario | Production path and observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Embedded-frame download, both dashboard and conversation | Real WebKit action reports `shouldPerformDownload=true` and `sourceFrame.isMainFrame=false`. An observer forwards it to the original presenter; production returns `.cancel`, with no download owner or Save sheet. Even the same-origin child cannot gain main-frame download authority. |
| Revoke while Save is pending, new file | Admit the transfer with a current lease, call `store.invalidate()` without closing/replacing the page, then accept the native Save using Parallels keyboard input. The transfer reports unavailable; the selected filename and canonical parent directory match the intended destination, and no destination file exists. |
| Revoke while Save is pending, existing file | Repeat with a sentinel file, accept Save and the OS Replace confirmation. The transfer reports unavailable and the sentinel bytes remain identical. Document generation and URL stay unchanged. |

The regular test run cancels the pending sheet after revocation and checks the rejected transfer. The external proof run sets `OPENCLAW_DOWNLOAD_AUTHORITY_PROOF=1` and actually accepts the OS dialogs; it verifies both destination effects. No auth credentials, production data, or production test hooks are involved.

Selected trace from the successful external run:

```text
DOWNLOAD_AUTHORITY_SUBFRAME_REJECTED conversation=false
DOWNLOAD_AUTHORITY_SUBFRAME_REJECTED conversation=true
DOWNLOAD_AUTHORITY_READY_CREATE
DOWNLOAD_AUTHORITY_VERIFIED_CREATE
DOWNLOAD_AUTHORITY_READY_REPLACE
DOWNLOAD_AUTHORITY_VERIFIED_REPLACE
Test run with 28 tests in 6 suites passed after 55.791 seconds.
```

The allowed-save control remains the attached red/green video: the ZIP bytes are saved exactly and the original page stays open.

prs.title: fix(gateway): return the stored compaction summary from chat.message.get
prs.body:
Closes #173158

## What Problem This Solves

After a compaction the agent keeps working from the summary the gateway wrote, but no client-facing RPC returned it, so a client could not show what the agent still remembers. The exact-message read now carries that summary for a visible compaction marker; history pages stay exactly as they were.

- Problem: `src/gateway/session-transcript-entry-message.ts` projects a stored compaction entry into a marker-only system message (`__openclaw.kind = "compaction"` with token counts), so `chat.message.get` returned the marker without the summary stored on the same entry.
- Solution: the exact-message read opts into the stored summary and exposes it as `__openclaw.summary`. Every page/window reader keeps the previous marker-only projection.
- Backend coverage: the option is now forwarded on all three transcript backends the exact-message read can select from — the SQLite projection, the incognito actor-memory projection, and the retained reset-archive reader. Before this revision only SQLite forwarded it, so an incognito or archived compaction still returned a bare `Compaction` label.
- What changed: `src/gateway/session-transcript-entry-message.ts`, the read-option plumbing (`session-transcript-read.types.ts`, `session-transcript-read-kernel.ts`, `session-transcript-archive-reader.ts`, `session-actor-memory-history-projection.ts`, `chat-history-pages.ts`, `cli-session-history.ts`, `session-history-types.ts`, `chat-message-get-handler.ts`), one doc sentence in `docs/gateway/protocol/rpc-session-control.md`, and regressions in `chat-message-get-handler.test.ts`, `session-transcript-readers.markers.test.ts`, `session-actor-memory-history.test.ts`, and `session-utils.fs.test.ts`.
- What did NOT change: `chat.history` / `sessions.get` payloads, the marker text `Compaction`, token fields, and the storage schema. `readFiles` / `modifiedFiles` are not included (the issue marks them optional); the summary is the part that answers "what does the agent still remember".

## Why This Change Was Made

The summary was already persisted; only the client projection dropped it. The narrowest fix is therefore an additive field on the existing exact-message RPC instead of a new endpoint or a wider history payload.

- Best fix: yes — additive field on the RPC that already owns transcript selection and disclosure authority, which is the shape this issue's triage asked for.
- Alternative: a new `sessions.compaction.get` RPC (duplicates authorization) or attaching the summary to every projection (enlarges every history page). Both rejected.
- Bounded read: a stored summary longer than the write-time cap (16,000 characters) is withheld rather than returned unbounded, matching how `parseCompactionDetails` drops an oversized `latestUnresolvedUserRequest`.
- Risk / non-goals: a client that renders `__openclaw` verbatim will now see one extra field on compaction markers; the field only appears on exact-message reads. Adding a second parameter to `sqliteMessageEventWithSeq` also required converting two `.map(sqliteMessageEventWithSeq)` call sites to explicit callbacks, because `map` passes the element index as the second argument; the type checker caught both.
- Load-bearing default: the option stays opt-in, so the archive reader's `readById` keeps its previous call shape for any reader that only wants a marker; only the exact-message path passes `includeCompactionSummary`.

## User Impact

A client can show the retained summary for a compaction marker it already renders, without reading the agent's SQLite store directly or decoding compressed transcript bytes. That now holds whether the selected message comes from the active SQLite projection, an incognito session held in memory, or a retained reset archive. History pages, token counts, and every other read are unchanged.

## Evidence

Live Gateway WebSocket capture. A real `openclaw gateway` process was started on loopback with an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, sessions were written into that store, and every call below is the shipped `openclaw gateway call <method>` CLI — an authenticated WebSocket `req`/`res` round trip against the running Gateway, not an in-process handler invocation.

```text
$ export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<proof-state-dir>/state
$ export OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=<proof-state-dir>/config.json
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway --port <port> --token <gateway-token> \
    call chat.message.get \
    --params '{"sessionKey":"agent:main:proof-sqlite","messageId":"sqlite-comp"}' --json
{
  "ok": true,
  "message": {
    "role": "system",
    "content": [
      {
        "type": "text",
        "text": "Compaction"
      }
    ],
    "timestamp": 1792116000000,
    "__openclaw": {
      "kind": "compaction",
      "id": "sqlite-comp",
      "tokensBefore": 400,
      "tokensAfter": 120,
      "summary": "Goal: keep the release plan for beta.4.",
      "transcriptPosition": { "source": "<display-source-hash>", "rawSeq": 2 },
      "seq": 2
    }
  }
}
```

The same Gateway, same capture session, across the three backends and the bound:

```text
# SQLite exact-message read -> summary present
chat.message.get agent:main:proof-sqlite / sqlite-comp
  {"ok":true,"message":{"role":"system","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Compaction"}],
   "__openclaw":{"kind":"compaction","id":"sqlite-comp","tokensBefore":400,"tokensAfter":120,
   "summary":"Goal: keep the release plan for beta.4.","seq":2}}}

# retained reset-archive exact-message read -> summary present
chat.message.get agent:main:proof-archive / archive-comp
  {"ok":true,"message":{"role":"system","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Compaction"}],
   "__openclaw":{"kind":"compaction","id":"archive-comp","tokensBefore":400,"tokensAfter":120,
   "summary":"Goal: keep the archived release plan.","seq":2}}}

# history page for the same session -> marker only, no summary anywhere in the payload
chat.history agent:main:proof-sqlite
  {"role":"user","content":"Original question","id":"sqlite-q","hasSummary":false}
  {"role":"system","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Compaction"}],"kind":"compaction","id":"sqlite-comp","hasSummary":false}
  {"role":"assistant","content":"Continued","id":"sqlite-a","hasSummary":false}

# bound: exactly the stored cap -> returned
chat.message.get agent:main:proof-bound-at / bound-at
  {"ok":true,"kind":"compaction","id":"bound-at","hasSummary":true,"summaryChars":16000}

# bound: one character over the stored cap -> withheld, marker still returned
chat.message.get agent:main:proof-bound-over / bound-over
  {"ok":true,"kind":"compaction","id":"bound-over","hasSummary":false,"summaryChars":null}
```

The `hasSummary`/`summaryChars` lines are a projection of the raw `__openclaw` object from the same responses, printed compactly because a 16,000-character field does not belong in a PR body. IPs, tokens, and local paths are redacted; the endpoint is loopback only.

Regression result for the six files this touches:

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
    src/gateway/server-methods/chat-message-get-handler.test.ts \
    src/gateway/server-methods/chat-read-scope.rpc.test.ts \
    src/gateway/session-transcript-readers.markers.test.ts \
    src/gateway/session-transcript-message.test.ts \
    src/config/sessions/session-actor-memory-history.test.ts \
    src/gateway/session-utils.fs.test.ts
Test Files  6 passed (6)
     Tests  87 passed (87)
```

The two backend regressions are real: with the projection change reverted they fail, and the live Gateway keeps returning only the label on the archive backend.

```text
$ (production change reverted) node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
    src/config/sessions/session-actor-memory-history.test.ts src/gateway/session-utils.fs.test.ts -t "compaction summary"
FAIL  session-actor-memory-history.test.ts > memory actor history > returns the stored compaction summary only to the exact-message read
      - "summary": "Retained compaction summary"
FAIL  session-utils.fs.test.ts > archive selection > returns the stored compaction summary only to an exact-message archive read
      - "summary": "retained archived summary"
```

Type check and formatting on the same tree:

```text
$ npm run tsgo:core
exit=0
$ npm run check:assertion-safety
assertion SAFETY ratchet OK: 2682 files, 6223 grandfathered assertions.
$ oxfmt --check <changed files>
All matched files use the correct format.
$ oxlint <changed files>
(clean)
```

Not tested: the incognito backend is covered by the in-process regression only. Incognito transcripts are memory-authoritative and never persisted (`createMemorySessionActorOwner`), so the scenario cannot be seeded into an external process and the live WebSocket capture above cannot produce it. The regression drives the same production memory store writer, the same projection, and the same option plumbing the Gateway uses.

## AI Assistance 🤖

This PR is AI-assisted. Used `grep`, `git diff`, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`, and a disposable loopback Gateway to trace the marker projection from `chat.message.get` down to `projectTranscriptEntryMessage` on each backend. The implementer understands the code: the summary is stored on the compaction entry, the projection dropped it, and the exact-message option is what restores it without changing any page reader. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution against the shipped entry points.

prs.title: feat: override agent exec configuration for one run
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Scripts using `openclaw agent exec` can inherit an operator's configuration or select a complete alternative file with `--config`. They cannot currently change a few settings for one invocation without constructing another configuration file. That makes a small tool or agent-setting change unnecessarily responsible for preserving provider definitions, credentials, and unrelated per-agent settings.

## User Impact

Adds repeatable `--config-override '<JSON object>'` to `agent exec`. Each object overlays the selected ordinary, pinned-file, or isolated base in argument order. Nested objects merge; arrays and scalar values replace their previous values, including empty arrays. Unspecified settings remain inherited, and saved configuration is unchanged.

The flag retains ordinary per-agent precedence and the command's explicit run options, workspace binding, and state ownership. `--config` continues to select an alternative file. `--auth-env-only` rejects configuration overrides, preserving its guarantee that configuration cannot introduce credentials. Overrides use JSON syntax and normal runtime normalization, including `~` paths; includes and shell imports retain the selected base loader's behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native command already owns configuration loading, agent selection, authentication, and the in-memory run snapshot. The new option uses its existing deep-merge, configuration-validation, and runtime-materialization owners before selecting the agent and credential store. Callers can therefore change the selected system agent without copying or redirecting its credentials into temporary run state.

Configuration environment values use the existing runtime environment owner and its restoration receipt. This makes an `env.vars` override effective for the invocation while preserving process-environment precedence and cleanup. Invalid overrides fail before agent execution, with malformed JSON diagnostics that do not echo the input.

## Evidence

The exact baseline rejects `--config-override` through the public Commander registration before execution. Focused coverage exercises ordered arguments, inherited and pinned configuration, isolated defaults, empty-array replacement, per-agent settings, explicit run-option precedence, saved-file preservation, native credential-owner selection, invalid inputs, and environment cleanup.

Changed-file formatting/lint and the native production/test compiler families passed. All 98 related tests across 12 files passed in a 60.60-second batch. The complete ordered validation command, including compiler preparation and tests, took 407.561 seconds; these are separate wall-time measurements, not summed worker durations.

The affected configuration/credential files were rerun after qualifying runtime path materialization: 41 tests passed in 48.97 seconds, with unchanged cases and compiler families retaining their prior proof. Normal file configuration and overrides resolve the same `~` path.

Two full public CLI invocations against a synthetic local HTTP provider passed. Both retained the configured non-main agent's model and credentials; the override removed workspace context and model-visible tools using the existing tool-policy settings, and the saved file remained byte-identical. No live provider credentials or paid model calls were used. Independent review is clean. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38839471553) passed: 36 successful jobs and 27 jobs skipped by the native plan. Observed CI job time totaled 6,824 seconds across concurrent jobs; this is not wall time.


<details>
<summary>Actual CLI request and saved-file evidence</summary>

The following is the recorded output from two full `corepack pnpm --silent openclaw agent exec` invocations on tree `6fda4ed1f00b5149f62f0067068d7431dd7c5385`, identical to published head `01667a8fd4a8468bc5265b8c8e1eae0d68f7c80d`. A local synthetic HTTP provider intercepted the requests. Its model and synthetic API key came from the selected base config, whose system agent was `worker`. These observations come from the requests and file readback, rather than only the in-memory configuration.

```json
{"scenario":"inherited","status":"ok","provider":"overlay-fixture","model":"proof-model","inheritedAuth":true,"workspaceContext":true,"toolsPresent":true,"savedConfigUnchanged":true}
{"scenario":"overridden","status":"ok","provider":"overlay-fixture","model":"proof-model","inheritedAuth":true,"workspaceContext":false,"toolsPresent":false,"savedConfigUnchanged":true}
```

Both invocations used `--cwd <fixture-workspace> --code-mode direct --json`, with `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` selecting the fixture file. The second invocation additionally passed these ordered overrides:

```sh
--config-override '{"tools":{"deny":["read"]}}' \
--config-override '{"tools":{"deny":["*"],"toolSearch":false},"agents":{"entries":{"worker":{"contextInjection":"never","skills":[]}}}}'
```

The fixture saved the initial file bytes before either invocation. Its request collector compared the authorization header against the synthetic fixture key and parsed the HTTP body. These assertions ran after each actual CLI process exited successfully:

```js
assert.equal(request.authenticated, true);
assert.equal(request.body.model, "proof-model");
assert.equal(JSON.stringify(request.body.messages).includes(marker), !overridden);
assert.equal((request.body.tools?.length ?? 0) > 0, !overridden);
assert.equal(await fs.readFile(configPath, "utf8"), original);
```

`marker` came from the fixture workspace's `AGENTS.md`. The explicit `toolSearch: false` removes the existing discovery controls as well as the ordinary tools denied by `"*"`.

</details>

prs.title: feat(mcp): per-request header provider for volatile turn attribution on OpenClaw-owned HTTP transports
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Per-turn MCP attribution currently has to enter declarative server headers or the connection resolver. Declarative header changes invalidate the catalog; the reported Reef production measurement was **221 re-catalogs across 222 runs**. The existing connection resolver caches requester credentials for five minutes, and changed resolved headers rotate the connection. Neither path can provide fresh turn attribution while retaining a transport and its catalog.

This adds a separate plugin request-header provider for OpenClaw-owned MCP HTTP transports. Upstream main was checked at `7aaef70932b30f4d7410ae00aa65b07089de2ce0`; no equivalent provider existed.

**Deployment consumer.** The Reef embedder plugin (the same production deployment behind the measurement above) adopts this provider on release adoption: it moves `traceparent` and signed per-turn context headers off declarative server configuration and onto this seam, which retires the measured per-run re-catalog. Requester authentication stays entirely on the existing connection-resolver contract — this consumer sends attribution and turn-scoped credentials only, and its stable credentials are unchanged.

## User Impact

Plugins can attach `traceparent`, signed turn credentials, and optional direct-request credentials to individual MCP requests without rebuilding the catalog or connection. Stable authentication remains in static server configuration or the existing connection resolver.

The SDK infrastructure documentation includes registration and embedded-runtime usage. This contract covers OpenClaw-owned HTTP transports; external harness-native MCP clients need OpenClaw materialized tools to use it.

## Design

- Add `api.registerMcpServerRequestHeaderProvider({ serverName, resolve })`, following connection-resolver registration conventions. Resolver and header-provider registrations share per-server plugin ownership, and the connection resolver is authoritative regardless of registration order: a foreign provider is rejected when the resolver already exists and displaced (removed, error diagnostic on the provider's plugin) when the resolver registers later. Registry state is identical in both orders, so a declared server with a resolver is never partitioned as static.
- Only the host binds run identity. The embedded backend binds MCP attribution to the admitted run's actual `sessionId`/`sessionKey`/`runId` (internal `bindMcpRequestRun`), and the binding is revoked when that run settles. A context the host did not issue (forged) or whose run has settled (stale/reassigned) is dropped: the provider is not called and no volatile headers are sent. The public export from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime` is `runWithMcpRequestMetadata(metadata, callback)` — caller tracing metadata only (e.g. `traceparent`), never identity.
- Capture only MCP attribution when materializing tools. Each retained tool/resource/prompt executor opens its own operation scope, preserving attribution under overlapping acquisitions and calls without capturing unrelated cancellation or runtime authority.
- Resolve volatile headers immediately before actual guarded HTTP fetches, including same-origin redirects and authentication/RPC retries. Streamable HTTP and SSE POST/EventSource paths share this boundary. Header values never enter server configuration, catalog identity, or the resolver rotation digest.
- Keep configured headers, authentication, and MCP protocol fields authoritative. Scope provider headers to the configured origin; register returned values and bare bearer tokens for secret redaction. Bound provider resolution to ten seconds and report provider failures without exposing plugin error contents.

## Correctness

Each operation owns an immutable context. Missing context explicitly clears inherited attribution and skips the provider. No transport stores a mutable latest-turn header map. Provider results are freshly merged into a new request header object and are not retained for redirect replay.

Initial SSE discovery can carry its discovery context. Shared streamable notification GETs and legacy SSE reconnects carry no volatile attribution. The streamable initialized-notification send has a short-lived scope so its shared stream parser and reconnect timers cannot retain the opening turn, including reconnects with `Last-Event-ID`. Resumable RPC streams retain their own still-active operation context. Completed scopes cannot supply headers to background callbacks.

Static authentication, requester credential revalidation/rotation, genuine configuration invalidation, `tools/list_changed`, and transport-close recovery retain their existing owners and behavior.

## Evidence

### Guarded caller-authority revalidation (Rev 24 P1, head `34a4b55ad`)

**Defect (ClawSweeper Rev 24).** `fetchWithSsrFGuard` asserts the captured guarded caller authority (`captureGuardedFetchRequestAuthority`, e.g. a live cron-root claim) *before* invoking the transport `fetchImpl`. The header wrapper is that `fetchImpl` and awaits `provider.resolve()`, so authority revoked during resolution was not re-checked before stable credentials and volatile headers reached the server.

**Fix.** `withMcpRequestHeaders` captures the guarded assertion on entry and re-asserts it immediately before dispatch, alongside the existing abort and run-context checks. A revoked caller gets the assertion's own error, and no request is sent.

**Final-effect proof.** The real-runtime e2e adds a call under `withGuardedFetchRequestAuthority` whose MCP run stays active. Caller authority is revoked while the provider is resolving. The call is rejected, and the recording loopback server's request count is unchanged (no request for `revoked_authority_operation`). **Regression-before-repair:** with the re-assertion removed, the same scenario fails with `promise resolved "{ content: [ ... ] }" instead of rejecting`, meaning the real server received and answered the revoked call. A matching unit case (`mcp-request-headers.test.ts`) fails without the fix and passes with it.

Redacted terminal capture (`OPENCLAW_E2E_SKIP_BUILD=1 OPENCLAW_E2E_VERBOSE=1 pnpm vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts test/pr154043-real-runtime-proof.e2e.test.ts`):

```text
[pr154043-proof] allowed: real tools/call arrived with volatile header present
[pr154043-proof] canceled: rejected before I/O, server request count unchanged; pending send settled
[pr154043-proof] shared transport: subsequent attributed tools/call succeeded
[pr154043-proof] foreign: forged and SDK-asserted identity reached the server unsigned; provider never saw victim-run
[pr154043-proof] reassigned: settled run's captured context reached the server unsigned; provider never saw it
[pr154043-proof] revoked authority: provider resolved, caller authority revoked mid-resolution; rejected before I/O, server request count unchanged
 ✓ test/pr154043-real-runtime-proof.e2e.test.ts > PR #154043 real runtime proof > dispatches attributed calls and rejects canceled calls before HTTP I/O
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```

At this head: focused suites 8 files / 156 tests passed; core `tsgo` passed; timeout-race ratchet clean for PR files; formatting and lint clean.

### Run-identity authority + final-I/O proof (Rev 22 security item, head `a6194b291`)

**Concern (ClawSweeper Rev 22).** The public `runWithMcpRequestContext` accepted caller-supplied `sessionId`/`runId`, and the documented provider signs those IDs, so a caller could assert a foreign run and obtain a signed header at final HTTP I/O. A captured context also stayed usable after its run settled.

**Fix — bind signed identity to admitted runs (the recommended option).**
- Identity is issued only by the host: `runEmbeddedAttemptWithBackend` calls the internal `bindMcpRequestRun` with the admitted run's identity, keeping enclosing caller metadata.
- Each issued context carries run authority that is revoked when the run settles. `getMcpRequestContext()` returns nothing for a revoked or never-issued context, so the provider is never invoked for it. A run that settles while headers resolve is refused before dispatch by the existing `MCP request context expired` check.
- The public SDK export narrows to `runWithMcpRequestMetadata` (metadata only). Plugins and embedded callers can no longer name a session or run.

**Final-effect proof.** `test/pr154043-real-runtime-proof.e2e.test.ts` now also drives, on the same real MCP SDK client + guarded streamable-HTTP transport + recording loopback server:
- **Foreign:** a forged frozen context `{ runId: "victim-run" }` and the public SDK helper each reach the server with **no** attribution header; the provider never sees `victim-run`.
- **Reassigned/settled:** a context captured inside a run that has since settled reaches the server with **no** attribution header; the provider never sees it.

**Regression-before-repair.** With the old trust semantics temporarily restored (any context accepted, no revocation), the proof fails at final I/O. The server received a signed header for the forged run:

```text
- Expected
+ Received
  {
-   "attribution": undefined,
+   "attribution": "synthetic-victim-run",
    "rpcMethod": "tools/call",
  }
 ❯ test/pr154043-real-runtime-proof.e2e.test.ts:193:75
```

Redacted terminal capture after the fix (`OPENCLAW_E2E_SKIP_BUILD=1 OPENCLAW_E2E_VERBOSE=1 pnpm vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts test/pr154043-real-runtime-proof.e2e.test.ts`):

```text

[pr154043-proof] canceled: rejected before I/O, server request count unchanged; pending send settled
[pr154043-proof] shared transport: subsequent attributed tools/call succeeded
[pr154043-proof] foreign: forged and SDK-asserted identity reached the server unsigned; provider never saw victim-run
[pr154043-proof] reassigned: settled run's captured context reached the server unsigned; provider never saw it
 ✓ test/pr154043-real-runtime-proof.e2e.test.ts > PR #154043 real runtime proof > dispatches attributed calls and rejects canceled calls before HTTP I/O 61ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```

Unit coverage (`src/agents/mcp-request-headers.test.ts`) adds: forged identity never resolves headers, captured context revoked after its run settles, and a run settling mid-resolution refuses dispatch. `agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.request-headers.test.ts` now holds each turn open across acquisition and execution, as a host run does, and asserts that a settled turn's executor sends no attribution. On the merged head (current main `3f7689e64`): focused suites (`mcp-request-headers`, `agent-bundle-mcp-runtime{,.request-headers}`, `mcp-transport`, `mcp-http-transport`, `mcp-http-fetch`, `backend`, requester-connect, `registry-registrars-network.mcp-request-headers`) 10 files / 159 tests passed; both PR e2e proofs passed; core `tsgo` passed; `plugin-sdk:surface:check` passed (budget pinned to exactly this PR's two exports); formatting and lint clean. The merge resolved main's `mcp-http-fetch.ts` redirect-policy refactor by applying the provider wrap inside the shared builder.

### Registration-order fix + authority-chain proof (head `2587f4f3`)

**Defect (ClawSweeper P1, Rev 8).** `hasMcpServerOwnerConflict` was first-registration-wins across both seams: a request-header provider registered first by plugin A caused plugin B's later `registerMcpServerConnectionResolver` for the same server to be rejected. `partitionMcpServersByConnectionScope` then found no resolver and classified the declared server as **static**, exposing its configured connection to requesters the resolver would have excluded. The PR's own registrar test pinned that behavior.

**Fix.** The connection resolver is authoritative regardless of order. `registerMcpServerConnectionResolver` still fails closed against a different plugin's resolver; against a different plugin's *provider* it now displaces it — the provider entry is removed and an error diagnostic is reported on the provider's plugin (`MCP server request header provider for "<name>" displaced: connection resolver registered by plugin "<resolver plugin>" owns requester admission`). `registerMcpServerRequestHeaderProvider` is unchanged (rejected when a different plugin owns either seam). Final registry state is identical in both registration orders. `docs/plugins/sdk-overview/infrastructure.md` states the rule.

**Regression proof, unit** (`src/plugins/registry-registrars-network.mcp-request-headers.test.ts`, `it.each(["provider","resolver"])`): with the registrar fix reverted, the provider-first case fails —

```text
AssertionError: expected [ { level: 'error', …(3) } ] to deep equally contain ObjectContaining{…}

- Expected:
ObjectContaining {
  "level": "error",
  "message": StringContaining "displaced",
  "pluginId": "plugin-a",
}

+ Received:
[
  {
    "level": "error",
    "message": "MCP server connection resolver for \"user-mail\" rejected: already registered by plugin \"plugin-a\"",
    "pluginId": "plugin-b",
    "source": "/plugins/plugin-b/index.ts",
  },
]
```

— and passes with the fix (5/5). Both orders additionally assert, under `withPluginRuntimeRegistryScope`, that `partitionMcpServersByConnectionScope` puts `user-mail` in `resolverRequesterServerNames` and `staticServers` is empty.

**Authority-chain proof, real transports** (`test/pr154043-registration-order-proof.e2e.test.ts`, no transport/SDK mocks). plugin-a registers a request-header provider for `user-mail`; plugin-b registers a requester-scoped connection resolver that returns `{ url: <loopback>, headers: { Authorization: "Bearer proof-token" } }` only for `allowed-requester` and `null` otherwise. The declared config is `url: "https://placeholder.invalid/mcp"`; the loopback (`startRequesterScopedMcpProofServer`) 404s without the bearer and records every request. Driven through `materializeRequesterScopedMcpToolsForHarnessRun` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`. In **both** orders: `user-mail` partitions as resolver-scoped, never static; the allowed requester materializes tools and executes `requester_probe`, and every loopback request carried the bearer and none carried plugin-a's header; an excluded requester and a run with no `requesterSenderId` get no tools and the loopback request count does not move; plugin-a's provider is never invoked.

With the registrar fix reverted, the provider-first case fails at the static-partition assertion (the exact exposure):

```text
AssertionError: expected { 'user-mail': { …(2) } } to deeply equal {}

- Expected
+ Received

- {}
+ {
+   "user-mail": {
+     "transport": "streamable-http",
+     "url": "https://placeholder.invalid/mcp",
+   },
+ }

 ❯ test/pr154043-registration-order-proof.e2e.test.ts:69
```

Redacted passing capture (`OPENCLAW_E2E_SKIP_BUILD=1 OPENCLAW_E2E_VERBOSE=1 pnpm vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts test/pr154043-registration-order-proof.e2e.test.ts test/pr154043-real-runtime-proof.e2e.test.ts`):

[pr154043-order-proof] provider-first: allowed requester executed requester_probe; loopback served 5 bearer-authorized requests
[pr154043-order-proof] provider-first: excluded + anonymous requesters got no tools; loopback request count unchanged (5); foreign provider never invoked
[pr154043-order-proof] resolver-first: user-mail partitioned as resolver-scoped

[pr154043-order-proof] resolver-first: allowed requester executed requester_probe; loopback served 5 bearer-authorized requests
