**Merge with main.** Branch merged `upstream/main` (`a08479ac`, plain merge commit). Conflicts: `backend.ts` (main dropped harness-finalization imports; the `runWithMcpRequestContext` wrapper around `runAgentHarnessAttempt` is re-grafted on main's shape) and `agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts` (main extracted `startRequesterScopedMcpProofServer` to a test-support module; the PR's `startRequestHeaderMcpProofServer` now lives in `agent-bundle-mcp-request-headers.test-support.ts`, and the per-request header runtime tests moved to the sibling `agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.request-headers.test.ts` to satisfy the line-cap ratchet, leaving `agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts` untouched). `scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mts` budget raised by this PR's two public exports (`runWithMcpRequestContext`, `McpServerRequestContext`).

Verification at this head: core `tsgo` 0 errors; unit batch (`agent-bundle-mcp-runtime`, `backend`, `mcp-http-transport`, `mcp-request-headers`, `mcp-transport`, `registry-registrars-network.mcp-request-headers`, `mcp-connection-resolver`) 7 files / 193 passed; `agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.request-headers` 2 passed; e2e proofs 2 files / 3 passed; `test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts` 16 passed; `pnpm config:docs:check` OK; full `pnpm lint` (core + extensions) passed; `pnpm check:changed` green through the SDK surface budget, plugin boundaries, wrapper shadowing and core typecheck (the only failure, `typecheck core tests`, is two `assertReliabilityForcedExit` import errors in `src/infra/package-update-activation-*.test.ts`, present on untouched upstream main).

### Cancellation lifecycle fix + real-runtime proof (head `15fdd821`)

The prior head had a defect at the dispatch boundary: an operation canceled while `provider.resolve()` was awaited settles its attribution scope, and the fallback then forwarded the request **without** volatile headers on the retained transport — final I/O after cancellation, under stable connection credentials. The dispatch point now rejects an expired attributed operation with a content-free error instead of falling back; the shared-transport abort check is unchanged. Regression-before-repair was verified both ways: the new unit case fails on the old expression (fetch dispatches), and temporarily restoring the old expression makes the runtime proof's server-request-count assertion fail (expected 5, received 6).

`test/pr154043-real-runtime-proof.e2e.test.ts` drives the real transport path — `resolveMcpTransport` + the real MCP SDK `Client` over streamable HTTP against a loopback server that records every request it receives, with synthetic attribution and no real credentials. It proves, on one retained transport: (1) an allowed `tools/call` arrives carrying its volatile attribution header; (2) an operation aborted mid-header-resolution is rejected and the server receives **no** request for it (the real pending `transport.send` is observed to settle rejected, so the zero-I/O assertion cannot race dispatch); (3) a subsequent attributed call on the same transport succeeds.

Redacted terminal capture (`OPENCLAW_E2E_SKIP_BUILD=1 OPENCLAW_E2E_VERBOSE=1 pnpm vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts test/pr154043-real-runtime-proof.e2e.test.ts`):

```text
[pr154043-proof] shared transport: subsequent attributed tools/call succeeded
```

At this head: focused suites `mcp-request-headers`, `mcp-http-transport`, `mcp-transport`, `registry-registrars-network.mcp-request-headers` — 4 files / 46 tests passed; core `tsgo` passed; formatting clean.

### Original evidence (unchanged)

- Real HTTP and SSE tests send two distinct contexts through **one retained runtime/transport**, overlap acquisitions and asynchronous header resolution, execute retained tools in reverse completion order, and invoke a contextless tool under an unrelated ambient context. Wire assertions cover discovery headers, distinct turn credentials, unchanged static authorization, unchanged fingerprint, and exactly one initialize/tools-list cycle.
- Registrar ownership tests cover same-plugin provider/resolver coexistence, foreign-provider rejection, and (at the current head) resolver displacement of a foreign provider in both registration orders.
- Transport tests cover per-hop header refresh, cross-origin stripping, initial SSE discovery, contextless EventSource reconnects, notification reconnects with `Last-Event-ID`, and attributed RPC resumptions.
- Provider/backend/registry tests cover copied immutable metadata, context expiration and clearing, secret registration, bounded failures, network error preservation, host identity binding, and registration ownership.

Validation on Node 24.18.0 with the pinned pnpm 12.4.0 toolchain:

- `pnpm build`: passed.
- Core `tsgo`: passed.
- Focused transport/provider/backend/registration tests: 73 passed across 7 files.
- Full `agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts`: 120 passed, 6 failed (all six reproduced on untouched upstream main); final source verification completed.
- Targeted lint: passed with no warnings. Affected test-graph typechecks (`agents-root`, `agents-other`, `plugins-platform`): passed.
- SDK export synchronization check: passed.

Both complete runtime runs had 120 passes and six failures. All six failures reproduced on untouched upstream main in an isolated archive using the same dependencies. They involve existing stdio cleanup exceeding test deadlines: concurrent catalog startup, catalog invalidation during connection, default hung tools/list timeout, reconnect after child exit, and private acquisition cancellation during initialize/tools-list. No deadlines, assertions, or production stdio behavior were changed. The final run used the settled source and completed artifact verification.

prs.title: fix(codex): next turn stalls after Stop during session handoff
prs.body:
Related: #167280

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the next Codex turn can stall for minutes when Stop interrupts startup while it is waiting for a retired predecessor app-server to exit.

## User Impact

User impact: a pre-write Stop now releases the interrupted attempt without retiring the healthy app-server needed by peers and the next turn. Startup deadlines, in-flight native requests, and post-`thread/start` handoffs keep the existing conservative retirement behavior. No migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The predecessor-exit wait now reports the narrow case where cancellation happened before the current client wrote thread state. Startup preserves its healthy client only for that case while leaving the predecessor writer fence in place, so a successor still waits for the old process to physically exit before `thread/resume`.

## Evidence

- Negative control: the new Stop regression fails against the original production files because the healthy client is retired, then passes with this change.
- Mutation check: removing the post-write exclusion makes the configured-MCP ownership regression fail.
- Focused Docker tests: 6 files, 56 tests passed.
- Static validation: extension production/test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Broader Docker lane: all 12 database-worker chunks passed. The app-server lane had one failure in `client-catalog-preview.test.ts`; the same test fails identically on the untouched base commit `f1d0c07dfa7`, so it is unrelated to this change.
- GitHub CI: 46 checks passed with no failures or pending checks.
- Native writer-fence behavior was checked against the pinned Codex `rust-v0.161.0` source.
- Automated local review was unavailable because the Codex CLI rejected authentication before producing a report; the final diff was reviewed manually.

### Native runtime proof

An isolated Docker proof exercised the production `startCodexAttemptThread` path with the shipped pinned Codex app-server binary, a local scripted provider, and no operator credentials. The binary identified itself as `0.161.0` with SHA-256 `9a820c17865fa825d04db416818679a9d63bd72e50835c396f496e5684626c9c`.

```text
predecessor turn persisted
pre-write predecessor-exit wait entered
Stop settled: predecessorAlive=true replacementHealthy=true resumeSent=false
successor reused replacement: appServerStarts=2
predecessor physical exit
replacement native RPC: thread/resume
successor resumed: sameReplacementClient=true
proof complete: writerFencePreserved=true
```

The proof passed as one native test in 11.3 seconds. The predecessor's physical-exit event was sequence 14 and the replacement's native `thread/resume` was sequence 15, demonstrating that Stop preserved the healthy client without weakening the writer fence. The proof harness was temporary and was removed after the run; the committed regression remains the deterministic synthetic-transport test.

prs.title: fix: discover Codex plugins in direct migrations
prs.body:
Related: #168735

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing plugin inventory when running `openclaw migrate codex` directly in a new process.

## User Impact

Users can preview installed curated Codex plugins and select them with `--plugin <name>` without first running onboarding. No configuration or data migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Explicit migrations load the public provider artifact without registering the full Codex harness. The Codex artifact now prepares its managed plugin root when constructing the provider, so inventory discovery can start the bundled app-server. Other providers retain the lightweight artifact path, and onboarding keeps its existing registration flow.

The change adds 8 production lines net and 12 test lines; it introduces no core special case or new public contract.

## Evidence

[Inspectable terminal capture, complete CLI logs, and stdio fixture](https://gist.github.com/obviyus/854a17787254373b0096ca518c05b919) cover baseline `fe92b8e0bd2` and this exact head `d99d6477a4d`.

- On current main (`fe92b8e0bd2`), two isolated invocations of the shipped CLI returned no plugin items and warned that the Codex plugin root was unavailable.
- On this change, the same CLI and stdio inventory fixture list `plugin:calendar` with no warnings. `--plugin calendar` resolves successfully.
- Fresh onboarding still previews the same plugin on both versions. The fixture intentionally does not implement target app activation; both onboarding controls retain the same incomplete-activation warning.
- The added public-provider startup regression fails with the missing-root error on main and passes with the fix. All 72 focused managed-binary and migration-provider tests pass; changed-file formatting and lint pass.
- The built candidate also completed a real OpenAI `gpt-5.4-mini` turn through the Codex harness, returning the requested `ROOT_OK` response. (`gpt-5-mini` was not in the runtime model catalog.)

This is a two-way door: reverting restores the old provider startup behavior without changing stored data. The blast radius is direct Codex migration discovery; it does not alter other migration providers or normal Codex harness registration.

prs.title: fix(lobster): require operator approval for workflow continuations
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Lobster currently returns approval credentials to the agent and accepts a model-supplied `approve: true`, allowing a workflow effect to proceed without an operator decision. Approved continuations also need to retain the host's live invocation authority across awaited runtime work.

Related upstream fix: https://github.com/openclaw/lobster/pull/200. Release preparation: https://github.com/openclaw/lobster/pull/203.

## User Impact

Approval checkpoints go through the Gateway's operator approval flow while the tool call waits. Approval credentials stay private; structured input remains resumable through the tool. Old approval tokens can be cancelled but cannot be approved through model-supplied arguments.

**Draft / do not merge:** the fixed upstream runtime is not published. The installed `@clawdbot/lobster@2026.9.16` drops the host callback, so this candidate deliberately refuses approved continuations. The [protected release run](https://github.com/openclaw/lobster/actions/runs/38520109310) is waiting for `npm-release` approval from an eligible human release approver. After publication, this PR still needs the exact published dependency/lockfile update and passing integration proof.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing Gateway approval owner and version 2 plugin tool context, then carry the host callback into Lobster's effect checks. Reject oversized approval previews rather than approve truncated material.

```diff
 approval checkpoint
- return token to agent; accept approve: true
+ keep token private; request operator allow-once or deny
+ recheck host authority before resuming and at runtime effects
```

This is standalone work and does not modify or gate the Claws stack. No pnpm patch, override, vendoring, or unpublished dependency is introduced. The manifest and lockfile remain unchanged until publication is verified. Do not bypass the release approval, remove the authority guard, or weaken the failing integration tests to make this draft green.

## Evidence

Production tool entry points, original base versus candidate, using isolated synthetic filesystem state and the same installed runtime:

| Scenario | Before | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Model supplies approval | Accepted; zero operator requests; state written | Rejected as operator-only; no state written |
| Operator denies | Not part of the old tool flow | One approval request; cancelled; no effect or approval token in the result |
| Operator allows once | Model could approve directly | Blocked by the old runtime's missing host callback; no effect |

- Version 2 registration regression: failed before the factory change, passed afterward; sandbox exclusion retained.
- Focused Lobster suite: **38 passed, 6 failed / 44** (31.93s wrapper wall time). All six fail at `Lobster runtime does not preserve host invocation authority`. Successful approved state/shell continuation and retirement during actual resume remain unproven until the dependency is published and pinned. No tests were skipped or weakened.
- Existing host-authority contract suite: **13 passed / 13** (18.93s wrapper wall time), including missing admission and owner/run/plugin closure before effects.
- Production and touched-test typechecks, targeted lint, seven-file formatting, two-file Markdown/MDX parsing, and `git diff --check` passed.
- npm registry rechecked before publication: `latest=2026.9.16`; `2026.9.17` absent. Full build, exact-head CI, and hosted review remain pending.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** Two-way code rollback; existing persisted Lobster checkpoint formats remain owned by the upstream runtime.

**Blast Radius:** Lobster. Approval-call behavior changes intentionally. Merging before the published runtime update would break successful approved continuations, so this draft must remain unmerged until that dependency and the required proof/review/CI are complete.

prs.title: refactor(ui): separate presentation contracts from Lit
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Solid surfaces and plain TypeScript consumers imported presentation events and types from a Lit directive module, retaining a rendering dependency for a plain contract. The last shell cutover also left an unused loading wrapper. Regenerating the boot manifest exposed a session-background re-export that made Chat preload the entire New Session chunk.

## User Impact

Presentation keeps the same event value, lifecycle behavior, host tags, classes, and lazy boundaries. Chat does not load New Session through the background renderer.

## Why This Change Was Made

Presentation events and types now live in one plain TypeScript owner. Solid and domain consumers import that contract directly; the three callers that still use Lit directives retain the adapter. Both background callers import the unchanged Solid implementation directly, and the unused loading wrapper is deleted. The boot manifest is regenerated through its canonical command. No new dependency, state owner, compatibility export, or chunking rule is introduced.

The branch incorporates main through `56c315156f4542f197a2b7f727681ba3f41c21b5` using ordinary merges. The authored delta is 41 files, +97/−106 lines. Affected-file LOC: 15,340 → 15,331 (production 7,317 → 7,298; tests 3,226 → 3,243).

## Evidence

Reviewed head: `971260ed52d989e89d02c1b5a09365607565628a`; tree: `c089ac843e3ca01dcadc3056047cf641739c77d0`.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Review | Isolated Codex P0–P2 review passed for the contract extraction. Fresh isolated review of the final five-file cleanup also found no actionable issues. The committed cleanup patch exactly matches the reviewed patch. |
| Generated output | Canonical `pnpm ui:boot-manifest:gen` passed; the manifest was not hand-edited. |
| Paired builds | Exact main `56c31515` and the final candidate built on the same host. Strict performance comparison passed without violations or warnings. |
| Scoped checks | Final UI types passed (4.279s). Scoped lint and formatting evidence are retained for unchanged extraction inputs. |
| Focused runtime proof | Both `chat-pane-sidebar-view.test.tsx` cases passed on the extraction candidate. No local runtime suite was repeated for import-only integration. Final-head full CI passed. The corrected conversation-versions E2E passed once (4.765s test / 31.864s process), with scoped types, lint, formatting and isolated P0–P2 review passing. |
| Final production Knip | Production-head `c15ca477e` `pnpm deadcode:knip` passed in 177.401s with no findings; production files and dependencies, no export scan. Reused unchanged: the final commit changes only an E2E test. |
| Current full CI | [38841234884](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38841234884) passed on the final reviewed head with `ci:full`: 54 successful jobs, 23 skipped, zero failures. All UI unit, Control UI E2E and both real-Gateway shards passed. |
| Prior full CI | Production-head `ci:full` run [38838967126](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38838967126): 52 successful jobs, 23 skipped; one E2E shard and its aggregate gate failed. All three UI unit and both real-Gateway shards passed. |

| Paired gzip metric | Base | Head | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Startup JavaScript | 347,311 B / 8 requests | 347,390 B / 8 requests | +79 B |
| Startup CSS | 38,844 B / 1 request | 38,844 B / 1 request | Unchanged |
| Chat JavaScript | 1,660,650 B / 31 requests | 1,661,162 B / 32 requests | +512 B |
| Chat CSS | 130,174 B / 8 requests | 130,174 B / 8 requests | Unchanged |
| New Session JavaScript | 1,351,083 B / 29 requests | 1,350,683 B / 29 requests | −400 B |

Startup remains below the original 374,285 B budget. No page, bridge registration, or third-party library enters startup. The generated preload closure contains no New Session asset for Chat. The contract extraction and import cleanup do not change rendered output, so no new screenshots were taken. No compute leases or broad local suites were used.

Earlier local scans found three unused Web Awesome files, since deleted on main; the exact package scan and broader export-aware baseline scan remain distinct evidence. The preceding head's package scan found the unused loading wrapper deleted here. Historical WebKit setup exit 137 and a broad SDK declaration-preflight timeout remain unresolved tooling observations; scoped passing checks do not claim to explain them.

An earlier full CI run, [38835388945](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38835388945), failed the UI-chat type leaf and two model-catalog cases because main had restored a call to removed Lit `render` in Solid test cleanup. The exact failure reproduced on main; [56c315156f45](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/56c315156f4542f197a2b7f727681ba3f41c21b5) removed the stale call. The type leaf and all seven affected tests passed, with independent review, lint, and formatting. This branch includes that repair. Earlier passing runs remain prior-head evidence; they do not stand in for final-head CI.

The prior run’s sole failing case was `chat-versions.e2e.test.ts > Conversation versions > explains versions on demand without switching, and preserves keyboard selection`: the selected-branch SVG returned a null bounding box at line 105 after the surface helper had observed it visible. The corresponding shard passed on latest scheduled main run `38836157770`; this failure is **not classified as inherited**. The unmodified focused reproduction also passed, so the original cause remains unconfirmed. Source shows that header updates can replace nested menu details between Playwright child-handle resolution and box reads. The final test-only correction reads all current menu geometry synchronously in one browser evaluation, preserving every non-null, headline, alignment, keyboard, help and navigation assertion, with no retries or deadline changes. Both passing local runs remain distinct from final-head CI; no CI rerun or merge exception was requested.

prs.title: refactor(ui): make Solid own application context
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Removes the Control UI's separate Lit application-context provider while preserving context for lazily upgraded native custom elements.

## User Impact

No intended visual or interaction change. Registered tags, properties, methods, attribute reflection, retained children, focus, layout providers, and connect/disconnect hooks keep their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

`defineSolidBridge` already uses `HTMLElement` and Solid rendering. The remaining context dependency was `@lit/context`: the root installed an additional provider and native bridges subscribed to it. `ApplicationProvider` now owns both the Solid context and its native host transport. The application context token and all remaining `@lit/context` consumers are native TypeScript/Solid. Subscription replacement, nearer-provider handoff, and disposal retain their existing contract.

CI caught an extra native responder on each bridge overriding descendant-specific HTML preview contexts. Native transport now remains at explicit provider hosts; bridge content still receives its Solid provider. The repair passes all nine HTML preview browser cases. Remaining native test handlers now declare their event type explicitly. Main integration retains its model-catalog cleanup removal and workspace-fixture fixes; all seven model-catalog tests and six shell tests pass.

The content migration is independent: the bridge's `LitContent`/`createLitContentRef` exports still have production callers owned by the content lanes, so they remain until those callers are ported. No lazy import boundary changes in this PR.

Production LOC in changed files: **1,185 → 1,266 (+81)**. This replaces the external context-provider implementation with the native host transport under the single Solid provider; the native bridge itself shrinks by 18 lines. Test/helper LOC: **3,084 → 3,118 (+34)**. The later removal of the still-used content adapters is intentionally not claimed here.

## Evidence

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Codemod dry run on both assigned modules | Inspected; retained native lifecycle is intentional |
| `pnpm tsgo:ui` | Pass |
| Bridge, application-context, and warm-boot tests | 28 contracts checked; repaired synchronous fixture publication and passed the targeted replacement rerun (6.34 s; initial run 41.78 s) |
| CI repair proof | All 9 HTML preview browser tests and all 7 model-catalog tests pass (combined wrapper 45.99 s); both failed core UI typecheck scopes pass; all 6 merged shell tests pass (29.06 s) |

| Strict performance comparison against merge base `7740cd562dcc0ae9a4d0713d0726953f41a32bdb`, same machine/toolchain | Startup **347,378 → 347,038 B gzip (−340 B)**; **1 → 1 startup CSS request**; below 374,285 B budget |

| Broad integration | `ci:full` requested for all UI unit/E2E, browser-extension, and real-Gateway shards |

prs.title: fix(openai): keep device-code deadline on the monotonic clock
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Signing in with ChatGPT via the device-code OAuth flow can hang past the configured 15-minute budget or fail spuriously when the system clock moves. The 15-minute device-code deadline was seeded and read with `Date.now()` (wall clock) but its remaining budget is consumed through `setTimeout` (monotonic), so a clock rollback enlarged the budget and a forward jump shrank it.

- Problem: `pollOpenAICodexDeviceCode` computed `deadline = Date.now() + OPENAI_CODEX_DEVICE_CODE_TIMEOUT_MS`, then `resolveNextDeviceCodePollDelayMs` and `resolveDeviceCodePollRequestTimeoutMs` derived the remaining budget with `deadline - Date.now()`. Those values feed `waitForDeviceCodePoll`'s `setTimeout` and `buildTimeoutAbortSignal`'s `setTimeout`, both monotonic. A wall-clock rollback (NTP correction, sleep/resume, manual change) made the remaining budget grow past 15 minutes, so the poll loop could hang well beyond the configured timeout; a forward jump shrank the budget and rejected healthy authorization polls as timed out.
- Solution: seed and read the deadline with `performance.now()` so the producer and consumers share the same monotonic clock domain. Wall-clock jumps can no longer stretch or shrink the 15-minute device-code budget.
- What changed: `extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-device-code.ts` — four `Date.now()` calls in the device-code poll deadline path switched to `performance.now()`. A comment documents the clock-domain rationale. `extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-device-code.test.ts` — a `beforeEach` aliases `performance.now` to `Date.now` so existing fake-timer assertions hold, plus a regression test that rewinds the wall clock mid-login.
- What did NOT change: the JWT-derived token `expires` fallback stays on `Date.now()` because it is an epoch timestamp consumed elsewhere as wall-clock. No new parameters, parser branches, or configuration surfaces.

## Why This Change Was Made

The deadline is a local variable that never crosses function boundaries, so a direct `Date.now()` → `performance.now()` replacement at the canonical owner aligns the clock domain without threading a monotonic seed through callers — matching the approach already shipped for the same bug pattern in #155801, #162779, and #162813.

The remaining budget flows to two monotonic consumers: `waitForDeviceCodePoll`'s bare `setTimeout`, and `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` → `resolveSafeTimeoutDelayMs` (which already floors to an integer). Because neither consumer uses `AbortSignal.timeout`, the sub-millisecond float returned by `performance.now()` does not trigger `ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE`.

## User Impact

Users signing in with ChatGPT for the first time via the device-code flow no longer risk a login that hangs beyond the 15-minute window when an NTP correction, sleep/resume, or manual clock change occurs mid-login, nor do healthy authorization polls get rejected as timed out after a forward clock jump. The configured 15-minute device-code budget is now honored regardless of wall-clock movement.

## Evidence

**Production-deadline exhaustion proof** — calls the real exported `loginOpenAICodexDeviceCode`. The production `pollOpenAICodexDeviceCode` runs its real code path (guarded fetch → `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` → `setTimeout`). The 15-min deadline constant is hardcoded, so `performance.now` and `setTimeout` are accelerated 300× uniformly (the 1:30 ratio between the 30s request timeout and 15min deadline is preserved; production code unchanged). `Date.now()` is rewound 1h backward independently mid-poll. The production poller exhausts its **own** monotonic deadline and throws its **own** timeout error — not a caller abort, not copied arithmetic:

```console
$ node --import tsx/esm production-deadline-proof.ts
usercode endpoint hits (real HTTP): 1
token endpoint hits (real HTTP, real polling): 407
onVerification fired (production poller entered): true
  +84ms   onVerification fired: user_code=PROOF-CODE
  +1509ms WALL CLOCK REWOUND 3600000ms backward; Date.now() jumped -3600000ms; performance.now()=460207 (monotonic, unaffected)
  +3153ms PRODUCTION POLLER REJECTED: Error: OpenAI device authorization timed out after 15 minutes.
PASS: production poller exhausted its own monotonic deadline and threw
"OpenAI device authorization timed out after 15 minutes." The wall clock was
rewound 1h backward mid-poll; the monotonic deadline was unaffected.
```

Pre-fix (same harness, deadline reverted to `Date.now()` per `origin/main`) — rollback enlarges the budget by 1h, loop never exhausts:

```console
$ node --import tsx/esm production-clock-skew-proof-prefix.ts
Budget before rewind: 2958ms | after: 3602958ms (grew by 3600000ms)
  +11070ms polled (HTTP 403) remaining_budget=3594927ms
FAIL (bug confirmed): after 12000ms the deadline had NOT exhausted.
```

Post-fix full suite (21 tests, incl. fake-timer regression). Single-worker wall time 9.6s; CI shard `checks-node-changed` ~2m54s:


prs.title: fix(workboard): guard specification with an optional caller revision
prs.body:
Closes #171083

## What Problem This Solves

A stale answer silently replaced a card someone else had just edited. `workboard_specify` — the call that turns a rough triage card into a `todo` card — had no way for a caller to say "I decided this from the revision I read", so the read-think-specify sequence overwrote newer title or notes instead of reporting a conflict.

- Problem: neither the `workboard_specify` tool nor the `workboard.cards.specify` RPC accepted a caller revision. The store only guarded its own write, not the caller's decision.
- Solution: accept an optional `expectedUpdatedAt` on the specification input, the tool schema, and the RPC, and enforce it through the existing conditional-write owner (`updateCard`), which already rejects a mismatched revision before touching the card.
- What changed: `extensions/workboard/src/store-workflow.ts`, `store-inputs.ts`, `tools-orchestration.ts`, `gateway.ts`, a `normalizeExpectedUpdatedAt` helper in `store-normalizers.ts`, the optional field in `docs/plugins/workboard.md`, and regressions in `store.test.ts`, `tools.test.ts`, `gateway.specify.test.ts`.
- What did NOT change: omitting the field keeps today's unguarded behaviour, and the claim/owner guard, the `triage`/`backlog`/`todo`-only guard, the `todo`-only target, and the dependency/status holds are untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

The conditional-write machinery for caller revisions already existed for `cards.update`, `cards.move`, `cards.archive`, and `cards.delete`; specification was the one guarded mutation that did not expose it, and it already funnels through `updateCard`.

- Best fix: reuse `WorkboardUpdateCardOptions.expectedUpdatedAt` rather than add a second conflict mechanism, so `workboard_conflict` / `workboard_card_conflict` keeps one shape.
- Alternative: a new store-level precondition in `specify()`. Rejected — it would duplicate the check that `updateCard` performs and skip the conditional persistence that protects cross-host races.
- Risk / non-goals: the conflict is reported before the specify-specific status policy, because policy checks still run ahead of `updateCard`. Nothing else in the specification contract is broadened.

## User Impact

Agents and operators can pass the `updatedAt` they read into `workboard_specify` (or `workboard.cards.specify`) and get an actionable conflict instead of losing a concurrent edit. Callers that pass nothing see no change. `docs/plugins/workboard.md` now lists `cards.specify` and the tool with the other guarded requests.

## Evidence

Observed result — real workboard SQLite store, real registered Gateway methods, real `workboard_specify` tool (isolated temp DB, non-production):

| Scenario | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workboard.cards.specify` with a revision read before a concurrent host edit | `ok: true` — title overwritten, `status: todo`, summary comment appended, `edited` → `specified` events | `ok: false`, `code: workboard_conflict`, `details.type: workboard_card_conflict`; card still `status: triage`, title `Edited by another host`, 1 comment, events unchanged |
| `workboard.cards.specify` with the current revision | `ok: true` | `ok: true`, `status: todo`, exactly 1 summary comment, last event `specified` |
| Two callers, same revision | `["ok","ok"]` — last write wins | `["ok","error:workboard_conflict"]` |
| `workboard_specify` tool with a stale revision | `isError: false`, title overwritten | throws `WorkboardCardConflictError`; card unchanged (`status: triage`, notes `tool host edit`) |

```
PROOF rpc ok: false
PROOF rpc error: {"code":"workboard_conflict","message":"Card changed while you were editing. Review the latest values and retry.","details":{"type":"workboard_card_conflict","card":{"title":"Edited by another host","status":"triage",...}}}
PROOF card after rpc: {"title":"Edited by another host","notes":"notes from the concurrent editor","status":"triage","commentCount":1,"lastEvents":["comment_added","edited"]}
PROOF caller outcomes: ["ok","error:workboard_conflict"]
PROOF tool threw: WorkboardCardConflictError: Card changed while you were editing. Review the latest values and retry.
PROOF card after tool: {"title":"Tool rough","notes":"tool host edit","status":"triage"}
```

```
Test Files  31 passed | 1 skipped (32)
     Tests  326 passed | 11 skipped (337)      # pnpm test extensions/workboard/src --maxWorkers=1
gateway.specify.test.ts: 3 passed
oxfmt --check: all 10 files formatted; oxlint: 0 errors
run-tsgo -p tsconfig.extensions.json / test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json: clean
```

What was not tested: the control-UI card dialog still calls `cards.update`, so no UI path exercises the new field; concurrent writers were simulated with two sequential callers against one store, not two processes.

## AI Assistance 🤖

This PR is AI-assisted. Used `grep`/`git log` to trace the guarded-mutation owners, `node --import tsx` and `vitest` against a temp SQLite workboard store to capture before/after behaviour, and implemented the fix. The implementer understands the code: `specify()` now forwards the caller's `updatedAt` into `updateCard`, whose existing revision check throws `WorkboardCardConflictError` before any field, comment, or event is persisted. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

prs.title: fix(gateway): keep cloud attachment transfer deadline on the monotonic clock
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cloud attachment transfers in `prepareWorkerTurnAttachments` seeded their deadline with `Date.now()` (wall clock) but the computed `timeoutMs` was consumed by `tunnel.runWorkspaceCommand` as a monotonic transport timeout. A wall-clock rewind inflated the remaining budget to the 60_000ms cap (letting transfers hang). Additionally, `performance.now()` returns fractional milliseconds, but the node-worker protocol requires `Number.isSafeInteger` for `timeoutMs` — without flooring, a fractional remaining budget would be rejected as `INVALID_REQUEST`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The deadline block at `worker-turn-attachments.ts:164-176` had three `Date.now()` calls: one to seed the deadline, one to compute remaining `timeoutMs`, and one to guard against expiry. All feed into `tunnel.runWorkspaceCommand({timeoutMs})`, whose transport consumes the value as a monotonic timeout. Seed and consumer were on different clock domains. Switching all three to `performance.now()` + `Math.floor` aligns seed, budget, and guard on the same monotonic clock (matching sibling PRs #155799, #155855, #162813, #164951) and keeps the dispatched value a safe integer across the protocol boundary.

## User Impact

Gateway worker turns that transfer file attachments (images, PDFs) to a remote workspace no longer risk hanging due to wall-clock adjustments (NTP correction, laptop sleep/resume, manual time change). Affects every cloud turn with attachments.

## Evidence

**Real-transport transfer proof** (head `c434bae2fcf`, `node --import tsx`): drives the PRODUCTION `prepareWorkerTurnAttachments` through the REAL workspace transport — `runCommandWithTimeout` spawns a real node child running the production `STAGE_ATTACHMENT_SCRIPT` — then verifies the transferred file on disk. A 90s wall-clock rewind is applied; the pre-fix source is checked out from `origin/main` so the before/after run the genuine integer `Date.now()` clock path.

```console
$ node --import tsx proof-real-transport.mts   # head c434bae2fcf
POST-FIX (this PR, real spawn transport):
  clock: fractional monotonic (seed 500, read 500.25) + 90s wall rewind
  workspace commands dispatched: 2
  captured timeoutMs values: [4999,4999]
  all timeoutMs are safe integers: true
  transferred file exists on disk: true
  transferred file content equals original bytes: true
PRE-FIX (origin/main source, real spawn transport):
  clock: same 90s wall rewind (real integer Date.now)
  workspace commands dispatched: 2
  captured timeoutMs values: [60000,60000]
  threw: null
POST-FIX: PASS — real transport transferred the file with bounded safe-integer timeouts
PRE-FIX: PASS — real integer Date.now() rewind inflated the budget to the 60s cap (the genuine bug)
VERDICT: PASS
```

**Before → after** (real spawn transport, same 90s wall rewind; the pre-fix is `origin/main` source):

| | pre-fix (main) | post-fix (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| dispatched `timeoutMs` | **60000** (inflated to cap) | **4999** (bounded, monotonic) |
| real file on disk | yes (but allowed to hang up to 60s) | yes (bounded to ~5s) |

The pre-fix file did transfer, but with an inflated 60_000ms allowance — exactly the bug. Post-fix bounds it to 4999ms under the same rewind.

**Regression test** — `worker-turn-attachments.test.ts`, 7/7 pass. The monotonic test uses a counter-model `performance.now()` (seed=500, read=500.25) and wall rewind (−90s), asserting `Number.isSafeInteger(timeoutMs) && timeoutMs === 4999`. Vitest `Duration 6.66s`. Net +33 test lines, no new test file or shard.

prs.title: fix(heartbeat): keep flood guard correct across backward clock steps
prs.body:
Replacement for closed-unmerged #156693, addressing the proof gaps from its ClawSweeper review.

## Problem

The flood buffer is insertion-ordered, but the guard reverse-scans it as though timestamps are sorted and stops at the first out-of-window value. A backward wall-clock step can place a stale timestamp between newer in-window starts, causing the guard to under-count a real burst.

## Fix

Count every in-window start, sort those timestamps newest-first, and derive the same threshold-oldest retry instant from the filtered set.

## Proof

This revision replaces the unreachable direct fixture from #156693 with scheduler-reachable state:

- the unit regression builds the buffer exclusively through `recordRunStart`, with `lastRunStartedAtMs` equal to the final recorded start;
- the scheduler regression drives six manual wakes through the registered handler/bookkeeping path across a backward clock step, then verifies a scheduled wake is skipped as `flood` with `retryAtMs: 1005001`;
- `runOnce` remains at six calls, proving the seventh wake was actually blocked.

The prior downstream proof run measured the focused cooldown test at ~0.3s single-worker and the scheduler harness at ~2.3s; fresh CI on this rebased head should provide the current-main result.

No stored-data or scheduling-contract changes outside the flood-counting assumption.

## What Problem This Solves

1. `printCronShow` dereferenced `job.state.*` and `job.payload.*` directly, so `openclaw cron show <id>` threw a `TypeError` for a row missing either object.
2. `createCronAmbiguousNameError` read `job.schedule.kind` unguarded, so `openclaw cron show <name>` matching two rows where one has no `schedule` threw a `TypeError` instead of the expected ambiguous-name error.

## User Impact

`cron show` prints malformed or version-skewed rows instead of throwing, and the ambiguous-name path keeps reporting its typed error. Rows with complete data render exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The writers share this module and the same `CronJob` shape, and `printCronList` already established the tolerance (`job.state ?? {}`, `job.payload?.kind`). The fix mirrors those guards rather than adding an abstraction; no valid-row behavior changes.

## Evidence

Entry-point regressions in `src/cli/cron-cli.test.ts`, both through the real CLI program:

- "renders a cron show row whose state and payload are missing" — `cron.list` returns a row with neither object; `cron show <id>` must print it and log no error. Red before (TypeError), green after.
- "keeps the ambiguous cron show name error when a matching row has no schedule" — two rows match the name, one malformed; the command must fail with the ambiguous-name error, not a TypeError. Red before, green after.

`src/cli/cron-cli/shared.test.ts` keeps the owning-boundary case: its existing malformed-row test now passes the same row to `printCronShow`, so `list` and `show` stay covered together.

- `pnpm test src/cli/cron-cli.test.ts src/cli/cron-cli/shared.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → 115 passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` reports no new errors from these files (only the pre-existing `src/tui/tui-session-actions-test-support.ts` drift, untouched here); `oxlint --deny-warnings` and `oxfmt --check` clean; `git diff --check` clean.

## Note On The Type Stripe

An earlier revision of this PR showed `check-test-types-core-3` red with `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-model-catalog.test.ts: TS2304: Cannot find name 'render'`. That file is untouched here and it is **already fixed on current `main`** (`7740cd562` no longer has that call); the stripe was running against an older base and clears on rebuild. Details in the CI note comment.

Closes #168200
Related: #167873 (native-thread recovery; separate runtime work)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unhelpful failure notices when conversation context disappears or workspace preparation is interrupted.

## User Impact

Users see what failed and what to do next without opening technical details. Refresh preserves drafts and does not resend work; workspace failures do not tell users to archive or abandon their conversation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Share curated startup-error presentation across live chat, saved failure notices, session summaries, and channel replies. Keep redacted diagnostics available in Details/copy and history metadata, including after reopening the conversation.

This is presentation only: no new retries, automatic replay, lease repair, thread rebinding, or error-code changes. Missing native-only context is not silently reconstructed.

## Current rebase validation (2026-10-15)

Its fixture initially lacked main's new runtime-config initialization; matching the neighboring fixtures fixes it. ## Pre-rebase evidence (head `ebd94db7589b`)

prs.title: fix(qa): Telegram live lane fails scenarios when the stale-update drain hits a transient Bot API error
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the QA Lab live Telegram lane fails a run of consecutive scenarios at transport setup with `Telegram Test Bot API getUpdates failed while draining stale updates.` when the Telegram Test Bot API briefly rejects the one-shot stale-update drain.

## User Impact

No product change. Release validation's live Telegram lane now waits out short Telegram flood control (429 `retry_after`), a releasing long poll (409), 5xx responses, network errors, and per-attempt timeouts during the per-scenario drain, instead of failing the scenario. Persistent failures still fail, with the last HTTP status and Telegram `error_code` in the error and in sanitized log lines.

## Why This Change Was Made

`drainTelegramTestUpdates` issued a single `getUpdates` (timeout 0, 15 s abort) and threw on any non-OK response, with no retry and no logged status, so 429, 409, and 5xx failures looked the same in logs.

- Retries 409/429/5xx and no-response failures inside a 120 s wall-clock budget (sized for slow runners; each attempt keeps its 15 s abort). It honors `parameters.retry_after` when the wait fits in the budget and otherwise uses 1 s to 10 s exponential backoff. Other statuses (for example 401) fail right away.
- Proxy teardown and lease revocation abort the in-flight attempt and cancel the pending retry wait (the timer is cleared, so the process isn't held open); each attempt's abort is capped by the remaining budget, so the drain settles within 120 s.
- Logs one `telegram_test_api_drain_failure` JSON line per failed attempt, with only integers and allowlisted atoms (`status`, `telegramErrorCode`, `retryAfterSeconds`, `retryable`, network `errorCode`). It shares the token-safe atom extraction with `reportProxyFailure`. Descriptions, URLs, and tokens are never logged.
- The sleep is injectable (`startTelegramTestApiProxy({ sleep })`), so the tests never use real timers.

The drain is the only one-shot Bot API call in the proxy and the QA Lab transport setup path. The userbot driver that runs next uses TDLib, and the SUT Gateway's own polling has its own retry, so nothing else needed this change.

## Evidence

Failure: 2026.10.4 FRV14, candidate `383c124cc32`, Release Checks run 38775999936, attempts 1–3 (Telegram QA child runs such as 38793849651). In each attempt, roughly scenarios 9–12 of 25, the ones right after the `telegram-long-final-*` scenarios, failed with `isolated scenario worker: failed to create QA transport live:telegram: Telegram Test Bot API getUpdates failed while draining stale updates.`. Attempt 1 surfaced it as `telegram account "sut" did not become ready ... reconnectAttempts 6`. Later scenarios recovered, and the same SHA passed this lane earlier that day. The old code logged no status, so the exact Telegram status is still unknown. This PR adds the log line that will identify it. The ~35 `telegram_test_api_proxy_failure` `upstream-fetch` `getUpdates` lines per run come from aborted long polls, appear in passing runs too, and are not this failure.

Tests (`.agents/skills/telegram-e2e-userbot/scripts/telegram-test-api-proxy.test.mjs`, upstream faked through the proxy's `fetchImpl`, injected sleep plus mocked `Date.now`):
- 429 with `retry_after: 7`, then success: one 7 s wait, offset kept, a single sanitized log line with no token, description, or "Too Many".
- 409, then success: one 1 s backoff.
- Persistent 502: fails after 15 attempts inside the 120 s budget. The error names `HTTP 502, error_code 502` and contains no token.
- 401: fails immediately with no retry.
- Proxy closes during a real 60 s `retry_after` wait (default sleep): the drain rejects right away and the timer is cleared. On the previous head the drain waited out the full minute.
- Stalled attempt at the deadline: after a 119 s `retry_after` leaves 1 ms of budget, a hung second attempt is abandoned and the drain fails with `no HTTP response (TIMEOUT) within the 120s retry budget`. On `55c8b525d3b` it hung for the full per-attempt timeout (the 5 s test timeout fired).
- On the old code, the four retry, budget, and status tests fail. The close and budget-cap tests fail on this PR's first head, `55c8b525d3b`: the close test timed out and the process stayed alive for 60 s, and the stalled-attempt test hung past the deadline.

Commands:
- `node --test .../telegram-test-api-proxy.test.mjs`: 20/20 pass, about 0.2 s.
- `pnpm test test/scripts/telegram-e2e-userbot-skill.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (the Vitest wrapper that owns these node tests; `pnpm test <the .mjs>` finds no Vitest file): about 15 s wall. The proxy suite passes. Two failures in other files, `telegram-run-composition.test.mjs` (EPERM `uv_cwd` under the local macOS sandbox) and `telegram-test-credential.test.mjs` (real uv/TDLib launcher), happen without this change too and do not import the proxy.
- `pnpm test extensions/qa-lab/src/live-transports/telegram/adapter.runtime.test.ts`: 18/18 pass.
- `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` are clean.

Not run: a live Telegram Test Server lane.

## Release note

This harness is candidate-owned during qualification (`trusted_harness_sha` = candidate). The fix applies to future candidates cut from `main`, not the 2026.10.4 FRV that is already running.

prs.title: chore(release): temporarily stop publishing the Windows companion app
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: every stable release ships an unplanned Windows Tauri companion installer when the Linux companion release runs. Since #169522, `.github/workflows/linux-app-release.yml` (triggered by `linux-app-release-request.yml`) builds and publishes `OpenClaw-<version>-windows-x86_64.exe`, `latest-windows.json`, and the `windows-stable` updater channel from every release tag, including tags whose source lacks Windows local Gateway support. 2026.10.3 and 2026.10.4 both shipped an unplanned Windows exe that had to be withdrawn by hand. For 2026.10.4 the publisher also created a `windows-stable` channel that had to be deleted (ledger RRI-133; 2026.10.3 retro 3.5/3.6). Windows companion publication should stay off until someone deliberately turns it back on.

## User Impact

Release operators: regular stable releases now publish only the Linux companion. That means the AppImage, `.deb`, `SHA256SUMS.linux-app.txt`, immutable `OpenClaw-<version>-linux.json`, `linux-stable`, and the legacy `latest.json` mirror. Releases no longer publish a Windows companion exe, `latest-windows.json`, or `windows-stable` channel, so nothing has to be withdrawn afterward. Linux publication works as before. The Windows Hub / Windows Node lane (`windows_node_tag`, `windows-node-release.yml`) is untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

A single, commented workflow-level switch, `WINDOWS_COMPANION_RELEASE: "false"`, now controls Windows companion publication. Its comment says the switch is temporary, explains why, and gives the re-enable step. The change reuses the existing `--windows` plumbing and adds no repository variables or new config.

- `validate_release` derives `windows_build`, which is true when the switch is on or when an opt-in desktop-test request needs the Windows test installer.
- `Build Windows installer`, `Authenticode-sign Windows installer`, and `Sign finalized desktop updater bundles` run only when `windows_build` is true. The two signing jobs already chain off `build_windows` success.
- `publish` no longer requires Windows jobs when `windows_build` is false. It skips downloading the desktop updater bundles. Assembly copies only Linux inputs, writes checksums over the 2 Linux bundles, and exits before reading Windows signatures or release metadata. `latest-windows.json` is written only when the switch is on.
- The publisher passes `--windows "$WINDOWS_COMPANION_RELEASE"`, which is `--windows false` today. `scripts/linux-app-channel.mjs` already supports a Linux-only, 3-asset publication proof and creates no `windows-stable` channel in that case. `scripts/linux-updater-manifest.mjs` status and `scripts/verify-stable-main-closeout.mjs` already accept a 3-asset proof, so no script changes were needed.
- Opt-in desktop-test requests (`desktop=true`, never used by release automation) still need the Windows installer for their fixed 6-asset inventory and `latest-desktop-test.json`. They still build it, but with the switch off they publish no `latest-windows.json` or `windows-stable` channel.
- `openclaw-release-publish.yml` / `scripts/lib/release-publish-children.sh` have no Windows Tauri companion dispatch. Their only Windows child, `publish_windows`, is the Windows Hub lane gated by `windows_node_tag`, so they are unchanged.
- The release maintainer platform-publication reference documents the temporary disable, what releases should expect meanwhile, and how to re-enable.

**How to re-enable:** in a reviewed `main` PR, set `WINDOWS_COMPANION_RELEASE: "true"` in `.github/workflows/linux-app-release.yml`, flip the `expect(linux.env.WINDOWS_COMPANION_RELEASE).toBe("false")` guard in `test/scripts/ci-workflow-guards.test.ts`, and remove the note in `.agents/skills/release-openclaw-maintainer/references/platform-publication.md`. The next `Linux App Release Request` dispatched from `main` then builds, signs, and publishes the Windows companion as it did before.

## Evidence

- New regression test `assembles a Linux-only release without Windows companion inputs` runs the real assembly step with only Linux inputs and a failing `gh` stub. It produces exactly the AppImage, `.deb`, and `SHA256SUMS.linux-app.txt`. It fails on `main`'s step, which hits `cp dist/input/windows/release/*`.
- Workflow guards now cover `build_windows` gating, `publish` admission for Linux-only and Windows-enabled runs, the switch defaulting to `"false"`, and the publisher passing `--windows false`.
- Local runs (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, wall time):
  - `test/scripts/ci-workflow-guards.test.ts`: 161 passed / 8 skipped, 144s
  - `test/scripts/linux-app-channel.test.ts`: 61 passed, 7s (existing Linux-only publication fixtures cover `--windows false`)
  - `test/scripts/linux-updater-manifest.test.ts`: 70 passed, 46s
  - `test/scripts/verify-stable-main-closeout.test.ts`: 78 passed, 15s
  - `test/scripts/tauri-workflow.test.ts`: 13 passed, 3s
- `actionlint .github/workflows/linux-app-release.yml`: clean. `oxfmt`: clean. `git diff --check`: clean.
- Not exercised live: this PR dispatches no workflow. The first real proof is the next stable `Linux App Release Request`, which should show `Build Windows installer`, `Authenticode-sign Windows installer`, and `Sign finalized desktop updater bundles` as skipped and a 3-asset Linux publication proof.

prs.title: fix(browser): distinguish changed-page reads from revoked access
prs.body:
Closes #173453

## What Problem This Solves

Chrome relay clients are told that tab access was revoked when an authorized navigation invalidates an in-flight document read, sending users toward the wrong recovery action.

## User Impact

Document-sensitive commands now report that the page changed and advise inspecting the current page before retrying. Stale results remain blocked, and real permission revocation or debugger detach still rejects the command. No configuration changes are needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The maintainer reopened #173453 after #173486 to retain this diagnostic correction. Choose the error only after the existing access check rejects the command, using the existing proven-tab authority check to distinguish document lifetime from revoked tab/group authority. Command scope, dispatch, and acceptance checks are unchanged.

## Evidence

- With the production fix reverted, the four Network/Fetch response-body diagnostic assertions fail in All tabs and Selected tabs modes; the other 11 cases pass.
- With the fix, 57 tests across four focused browser files pass, including the real background command handler, access policy, navigation wiring, real revocation after navigation, and debugger-detach controls. Native Chrome APIs are mocked at the I/O boundary. Vitest reports 4.56 s total duration for this selection; no new sleeps or polling were added.
- Production extension types (`node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.extensions.json --incremental`), extension test types (`-p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental`), targeted oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` pass.
- The combined max-lines command reports `max-lines ratchet OK: 527 grandfathered suppressions`, then fails its environment-variable budget companion: 452 existing `OPENCLAW_*` names versus budget 453. Checking the untouched HEAD index with `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-env-var-count.mts --staged` reproduces the identical mismatch. This patch changes no environment-variable names or budget files; that unrelated baseline issue is left intact.
- Independent Codex autoreview through P2: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. The reviewer inspected supplied source and evidence; it did not rerun tests.
- Follow-up for the initial CI failure ([browser shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38832264574/job/116753814062)): the existing `preserves ordered navigation events in selected mode` test still expected the old access-revocation message. The original head reproduces this locally (1 failed / 20 passed). Update only that expected diagnostic, retaining rejection, navigation ordering, and debugger-detach assertions. After repair, 78 tests across five focused browser files pass in 4.76 s; targeted oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` pass. Fresh independent Codex autoreview through P2 is scoped-clean. Initial-head CI's production/test types, lint, baseline ratchets, and docs gates passed; Repaired-head CI passed the browser shard; see the current CI attribution below.
- Native Chrome/Gateway behavior and the full test suite were not run locally. The requested native relay behavior trace remains unprovided; in-process tests use mocked Chrome I/O. This contribution used AI assistance.


### Current CI attribution (head `c5f8d4f9955101558913eaafe5057e9992eb583f`)

The repaired browser shard passes. Overall CI remains red because `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-model-catalog.test.ts:167` calls an undefined `render`: the [test-types stripe](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38836569401/job/116768128013) reports TS2304, and the [UI stripe](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38836569401/job/116767286821) reports the matching ReferenceError in two teardown cases. The affected file has identical blob `173c37c59ed9b07c2cb36429b81e27ea12ac829f` in CI's actual merge `7ad7190950d686097bc85d4bf4175d16de8a1ee1` and upstream parent `22b27470739bfb66b1d43aad7195e73e8add62ed`. This file is outside this PR's diff; no unrelated test-only repair or CI rerun was added.

## What Problem This Solves

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

Pass the existing verification context through the stale-receipt loop, matching the neighboring retained-source lookup. The cache remains local to one verification phase; the asynchronous source-index rebuild is unchanged. No configuration, schema, retention, or recovery-authority change is introduced.

## Evidence

- Reproduced before the production edit using real isolated Doctor imports, archive manifests, and a foreign receipt with exactly 2 or 32 absent primary transcripts. With two manifests, the stale verification owner performed **4/64 reads and JSON parses** before the fix and **2/2 afterward**. Full Doctor import performed **14/74 total manifest reads before** and **12/12 afterward**; fixed overhead remained ten reads. Stale-loop attribution was captured from the real reader stack.
- Fixed full-command proof kept the superseded-receipt diagnostic, emitted no unavailable-history refusal, and imported zero entries or transcript events.
- **19/19 canonical tests passed** across the stale-receipt and retained-source-verification files. The regression covers 2/32 sources, bounded reads, fresh subsequent passes, rejection after manifest/archive tampering, restored-content acceptance, and source-count-independent full-command reads. Existing canonical metadata, deletion, and no-replay checks remain green. Final wrapper wall time: **101.12 s**; new regression: **3.234 s**. CI timing is pending.
- Bounded Doctor typecheck, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Normal pre-commit hook passed without changing the reviewed tree.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Requester-settlement sweeps repeatedly rehydrate settled subagent task/result text just to count descendants, causing allocation bursts even without new work.

## User Impact

Background settlement and session-list projections do less allocation while preserving descendant status, delivery settlement, generation selection, and runtime ownership. Explicit payload reads continue to return full retained text. No configuration or stored-format changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing publication-maintained membership lookup and immutable row projections for status reads. Requester listing selects indexed candidates in registry order instead of scanning every retained run. Compact facts retain delivery disposition so delivered and permanently failed children remain settled. Runtime-owner views remain distinct from data-only projections.

The removed path selected and hydrated full rows, projected them again, and built a status index from those payloads. Production delta: 81 additions / 85 deletions (net -4); no additional cache or invalidation owner. Simplification pass completed.

## Evidence

An operator-supplied near-idle allocation sample recorded 399.53 MB / 5.2706 s (75.80 MB/s total), with at least 145.19 MB attributable to subagent stacks. Those stacks lead to requester-settlement checks, not `sessions.list`. A second sample recorded 24.29 MB/s and no subagent stacks, so this is an intermittent burst rather than a constant baseline.

The new regression fails against the original descendant reader: four reads of settled full payloads versus zero after the fix, with identical descendant/terminal-delivery results. It also covers requester ordering after a row replacement. Compact cache tests verify projection reuse and invalidation.

Focused local proof:
- Descendant settlement, scoped reads, and registry state: 31 tests passed in 37.59 s wall time (32.66 s Vitest duration, mostly compiler preparation).
- Liveness owner integration: all 11 tests passed, including old active runs, exact queued collector reservations, released claims, and successor ownership. Together with descendant tests: 20 passed in 50.75 s wall time.
- Changed-file formatting/lint and `git diff --check` passed. Broad typecheck/build/suites are delegated to PR CI; no Testbox lease used.
- independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): clean through P2. The helper refused the configured provider route; operator configuration was left unchanged.

## Before/after measurement

Isolated Linux sandbox, synthetic fixture with 5,000 sessions and 6,000 retained runs across 1,000 requester owners. Main-isolate V8 allocation sampling at 32 KiB includes collected objects; figures are estimates, not heap deltas. Base `70833f4c3c11`; head has the production patch in this PR.

| Workload | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Real descendant reader, median allocated bytes/read | 401,994 | 81,789 (−79.7%) |
| Same reader, median ms/read | 0.88479 | 0.06338 (14× faster) |
| `sessions.list` sidebar 200, median bytes/RPC | 3,203,091 | 3,197,582 (neutral) |
| Ordinary synthetic idle, weighted MB/s | 0.511 | 0.556 (overlapping windows) |

The real descendant reader selects six retained rows across four children from the full registry. Five captures of 100 reads per revision returned identical status results. Allocations beneath `restoreSubagentRunPayload` were 1.87–2.89 MB per 100 reads before and zero sampled bytes in all five after captures.

The real Gateway returned 500 validated `sessions.list` pages per revision. Two 65-second idle windows per revision overlapped: 0.450–0.572 MB/s before and 0.483–0.630 MB/s after. The default fixture has no requester-settlement wake backlog, so it does not reproduce the live allocation burst: no idle improvement or RPC speedup is claimed. Post-deployment idle confirmation remains a gap. All benchmark processes exited and the sandbox was removed.

## CI follow-up

Initial PR CI passed all typecheck lanes and identified two test updates for the compact read cutover: the prepared-read test expected redundant reprojection, and a lifecycle fixture omitted the new compact state-owner APIs. The former now checks projection identity reuse and publication invalidation; the latter retains the real compact owner in its mock boundary. The prepared-read file passed all 7 tests; the registry lifecycle file passed all 103 tests (21.31 s Vitest shard wall time). Both repairs passed changed-file formatting/lint and independent review. No production-code changes were needed for the CI fixes. Final CI run [38840870866](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38840870866) passed on `27b3b1865c8e6d3baece63c0086cc0485f558188`; the PR rollup has 64 successful checks with none pending or failed, including all broad typecheck lanes. No CI reruns or inherited-failure exception were needed.

Maintainers need published plugin consumer evidence when considering SDK deprecation, removal, or incompatible behavior changes.

## User Impact

Contributors can query canonical SDK identities, inspect distinct consumers and evidence, and distinguish complete empty results from missing or incomplete analysis. Usage counts inform the maintainer's decision; they never waive SDK compatibility or security approval rules.

## Why This Change Was Made

SDK and extension instructions route to a repository skill with a dependency-free, read-only CLI:

```text
canonical SDK key
  → all ClawHub usage pages + all coverage pages
  → distinct consumers, runtime/type counts, evidence and coverage gaps
```

Requires deployment of the public endpoints in [ClawHub #3957](https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/pull/3957). The helper fails explicitly when unavailable. prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`main` does not yet carry the shipped 2026.10.4 stable state (tag `v2026.10.4` @ `383c124cc32f`, npm `openclaw@2026.10.4` on `latest`, shasum `ac000cc196b31208b0108c171780a3312ea26e5e`).

## User Impact

No user-visible change. `main` records the shipped release so the stable main closeout can bind its evidence, and first-hop update lanes cover 2026.10.4.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Version:** `origin/main` was at `2026.10.3` (the 2026.10.10 beta train has not changed main's root version), so main moves to the shipped `2026.10.4`. No later train is downgraded, and no future/beta version or empty changelog section is added. `pnpm release:prep` aligned the root, package, and extension versions (it also fixes the pre-existing advisor/mcp-events/muse plugin-version drift on main), the matrix plugin changelog, and the official channel catalog. The macOS `Info.plist` base version is set by hand to `2026.10.4` / `2026100400`, matching what the preflight checks.
- **Changelog:** `CHANGELOG/2026.10.4.md` and `CHANGELOG/records/2026.10.4.md` are byte-identical to the tag. `loadReleaseChangelog` returns the same section and record from `v2026.10.4` and from this branch. The index is refreshed with `pnpm changelog:split`. Existing approved docs mirrors (2026.9.4–2026.10.3) are unchanged.
- **Update compatibility:** `scripts/lib/update-compat-inventory.json` was regenerated with `pnpm update:compat:gen` for the full recorded window (2026.9.1 … 2026.10.3, including 2026.10.1-beta.1/beta.2) plus 2026.10.4. Each tarball was downloaded, checked against npm `dist.integrity` before extraction, and checked against the integrity already recorded. The diff only adds entries. Regeneration `--check` passes.
- **CI timings:** `config/ci-test-timings.json` was refreshed by `scripts/ci-shard-timings-refresh.mts --run 38776000457`. That run is the normal-CI child (attempt 1, success, head `383c124c`) of Full Release Validation 38774938703 attempt 2. 108 hosted shard costs were updated, all generator-owned.
- **Forward-port audit:** every PR-numbered commit in `v2026.10.3..v2026.10.4` is already on `main`. The commits without a PR number are either backports of commits already on main (heap-flag `5ed6a305`, sqlite admission clock `39bd0a59`, qa-lab #172786 `59d6c69d`, OAuth sidecar seed `951dffef`, watch fixture `742012c9`, OpenCode Go lane), release-branch-only adaptations (Tailscale abort coercion, heap-flag fixture/dup-scan companions), or the release-only Kova calibration pins. Nothing needed forward-porting.
- **Shipped Plugin SDK surface:** `scripts/lib/plugin-sdk-shipped-surface.json` was regenerated with `pnpm plugin-sdk:shipped-surface:gen -- --release v2026.10.4`, per RELEASING.md. The export set is identical to the v2026.10.2 baseline; only the `release` and `commit` fields change. `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check` passes (no unauthorized removals).
- `appcast.xml` is not touched. The macOS publish has not happened yet; the appcast lands separately via its own `chore(release): update appcast for 2026.10.4` PR. Android did not ship (pinned at 2026.8.2). Linux and Windows companion assets are still building.

## Evidence

Release evidence:
- Full Release Validation [38774938703](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38774938703) attempt 2 (stable profile, all group). Normal-CI child [38776000457](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38776000457).
- Release Publish [38827593754](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38827593754) succeeded (resume of 38818061334; core npm publisher child 38824408033). npm, GHCR/Docker Hub, and the GitHub release `v2026.10.4` are published.

Local checks on this branch:
- `pnpm deps:npm-lock:check`: pass.
- `pnpm changelog:check`: pass.
- `pnpm update:compat:gen … --check`: pass.
- `pnpm release:generated:check`: fails only on `Control UI locale bundles` (`ui/src/i18n/.i18n/sv.tm.jsonl does not contain sv translations`). Clean `origin/main` @ `c921503c9d28` fails the same way, and also fails `plugin versions` there, which this PR fixes. This is pre-existing Control UI locale lag owned by the locale refresh workflow.
- `pnpm check:changed` (local; lanes=all): typecheck and 30 of 32 lanes pass. Two lanes fail, and both fail identically on clean `origin/main` @ `c921503c9d28`:
  - `lint`: the same 32 `max-lines` errors in files this PR does not touch (identical file list on clean main).
  - `max-lines suppression ratchet`: `OPENCLAW_* count 452 is below budget 453` in `config/env-var-count-budget.txt` (no env-var changes here).

PR CI on the first head (`a3be79bd`, merge ref against main @ `4cf3df6352ce`): 4 red jobs. None is caused by this PR; it touches no source or tests in these areas. Each reproduces locally on a clean detached checkout of main @ `4cf3df6352ce`:
- `checks-node-changed-3`: `extension-runtime-dependencies.contract.test.ts` reports that memory-core is missing a `kysely` dependency (`manager-search*.ts`, `manager-source-index-kernel.ts`). Introduced on main by #172681 (`20b5969cd83`). It passes on this branch's base `c921503c9d28` and fails on clean `4cf3df63`.
- `checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-5`: codex `turn-router.test.ts` and `turn-router-lifecycle.test.ts` fail. Clean `4cf3df63` gives the same 2 failures.
- `check-test-types-core-3` and `checks-ui (2/3)`: `chat-pane-model-catalog.test.ts` hits `render` not defined (TS2304 / ReferenceError). Introduced by #173275 and already fixed on main by `56c315156f4`.
- `openclaw/ci-gate`: aggregate of the jobs above.

Main's push CI for `4cf3df63` (run 38835446867) was green because it was scoped and did not select these shards.

PR CI on the current head (`0d74303b`, merge ref against main @ `44e80ff314a2`): the UI and test-types reds are gone because the main fix `56c315156f4` is now in the merge base. The remaining reds:
- `checks-node-changed-3`: the same memory-core `kysely` contract failure from #172681 (pre-existing on main).
- `checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-5`: the same codex turn-router failures (pre-existing on main).
- `checks-node-changed-26`: `package-openclaw-for-docker.e2e.test.ts` timed out on `npm pack --dry-run` after 20000ms on the runner. The same job passed on the first head, and the file passes locally on this head (54 passed, 3 skipped). Runner timeout, not caused by this PR.

prs.title: fix(codex): preserve continuity across races and paginated history
prs.body:
Closes #114302
Closes #114304
Closes #114305
Closes #114306
Closes #114308

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes five Codex continuity failures where users could lose a message during a request-input race, fail to continue or fork paginated threads, leave request handlers running after disconnect, or miss client-close cleanup when observers throw or subscribe late.

## Why This Change Was Made

The change honors the compare-and-resolve result before steering, adds one validated full-history reader for paginated and inline Codex threads, and makes the client close transition abort active inbound handlers while delivering terminal state to every observer exactly once. The implementation follows the currently checked-out official Codex app-server contracts and remains internal to the Codex extension.

## User Impact

Messages survive request-input resolution races, paginated threads can be continued/materialized/message-forked, and disconnect cleanup is deterministic across active, throwing, and late observers.

## Evidence

- Steering, fork boundary, catalog, and lifecycle group: 227/227 passed.
- Client, shared-client, and turn-router group: 112/112 passed.
- User-input bridge: 6/6 passed.
- Upstream session fork: 6/6 passed.
- Production extensions typecheck, targeted `oxfmt`, targeted `oxlint`, `git diff --check`, public Plugin SDK surface, protected-path, and secret scans passed.
- Fresh independent autoreview: no actionable findings, correctness 0.98.
- Official Codex source was inspected at `18f50c9e628af083a52d9240de09fc2db24d79ce` for paginated-history and request-resolution semantics.
- AI-assisted implementation and review; no public Plugin SDK or generated protocol boundary changed.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Shared Control UI components and plugin defaults still crossed the Lit template layer even though their implementations were already Solid.

## User Impact

Preserves the existing modal, tab, focus, retained-view, and plugin behavior while removing the non-chat production consumers of `solid-content.tsx`. Startup remains within the existing budget, growing by 6 B on the same machine.

## Why This Change Was Made

The presentation context now lives in a native Solid module, with the temporary legacy export sharing that same context. The shell renders its lazy modal directly. Plugin surfaces use their existing native mount callbacks for defaults and companions, and the link-reader panel owns its hosted action's DOM, listener, updates, and cleanup.

Seven obsolete shared render-wrapper files are removed. The remaining chat owners invoke their existing bridge directly until the chat lane completes; this PR does not delete `solid-content.tsx` while those callers remain. Hosted-tab icons now carry native content. No tags, routes, CSS classes, or lazy module boundaries are renamed.

This is 48 paths, including seven deletions and directly coupled import/type/test migrations. Production LOC across the touched files: **8,931 → 8,757 (−174)**. Test LOC: **4,867 → 4,860 (−7)**.

## Evidence

| Proof | Result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm tsgo:ui` | Passed |
| Targeted router, chat-router, and panel-placeholder suites | 36 tests passed across 3 files; 10.52 s wall time. The two CI-repair fixture files also pass: 41 tests in 9.22 s. |
| Original failing browser cases | Light and dark rail navigation/persistence passed, including all six 15×15 glyphs; 2 tests, 50.04 s |
| Production `pnpm deadcode:knip` | Passed; no new ignores |
| Targeted lint and formatting | Passed; existing advisory Solid warnings retained |
| Independent Codex review | No actionable P0–P2 findings |
| Same-machine baseline/head builds and strict performance | Passed; 347,050 → 347,056 B startup JS gzip; 8 JS requests unchanged; 38,844 B CSS gzip and 1 CSS request unchanged; zero violations |
| Synthetic browser proof | Both screenshot pairs are byte-identical; modal Close works; reader New tab disables offline, restores on the same DOM button after reconnect, and creates a second tab; no page errors |

The first full CI run found stale Lit icon fixtures, a disconnect fixture that incorrectly removed reader registrations, and a terminal icon whose cloned DocumentFragment accumulated SVGs during native updates. The fixtures now use the native contract and the terminal producer clones its SVG element, preserving replacement during repeated updates.

Related: #173509

## What Problem This Solves

#173509 records an old automation's account by the run's normal planner, and that planner moves accounts in a rate-limit cooldown to the end of the list. If the usual first account is rate-limited while Doctor runs during an update, Doctor records the next account permanently. Before the update that switch lasted only until the cooldown ended; now the job stays on the other account with no error.

Two texts were also wrong: the docs said the recorded account is "the account every unbound run used", which is true only with `auth.order` (without it, runs rotate between accounts of the same type by last use), and the creation error named only provider config, although environment keys are accepted too.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Doctor plans with a copy of the auth store that has the rate-limit cooldown fields (`cooldownUntil`, `cooldownReason`, `cooldownModel`) removed. Disabled and blocked accounts (`disabledUntil`, `blockedUntil`) stay excluded, and the stored state is not changed.
- `cron-jobs/payloads.md` now states the `auth.order` and last-use behavior. The code comment and the creation error text are corrected.

## User Impact

An update no longer moves an automation to a backup account because its usual account was briefly rate-limited at that moment.

## Evidence

- `inference-binding-migration.accounts.test.ts`: the ambiguous fixture now puts the first account (`openai:a`) in a rate-limit cooldown. On `main` Doctor records `openai:b` and the test fails ("expected … to contain 'Automation ambiguous (ambiguous): retain openai:a…'"); with this change it records `openai:a` and passes.
- `oxlint` passes on the changed files, and `oxfmt` was applied.
- **Final effect through the real embedded runner** (`isolated-agent.auth-continuity.integration.test.ts` > "records the usual account even while it is rate-limited during Doctor"): two shared OpenAI accounts with `auth.order = [platform, other]`, `platform` in a rate-limit cooldown while the real Doctor migration runs, then the cooldown ends and the real cron runner runs the job with only provider HTTP stubbed. On `main` this fails: Doctor records `openai:other-platform` ("expected … to contain 'retain openai:platform'"). With this change Doctor records `openai:platform`, the run returns `ok`, and the only provider request carries `Bearer synthetic-platform-key`.
- **Unchanged boundaries:** this change only alters which account Doctor picks before recording. Binding enforcement, personal-account exclusion, replacement and revocation refusal, and upgrade loading are the same code as #173509, whose live evidence (a `v2026.10.3` → candidate differential, replacement and logout refusal with zero provider requests, and the real-runner personal-account test) is in that PR. No stored shape changes, so existing data loads as before.
