prs.title: fix(memory-core): add memory_get recall tracking with correct workspace and range
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Memory dreaming promotion never receives recall signals from `memory_get` reads (#94769). Without this, deep-dreaming considers the wrong content for promotion, so important `memory_get` interactions never reach long-term memory.

The original submission also had three issues flagged by ClawSweeper, all addressed here:

- **P1:** Used `cfg.workspace` instead of the resolved agent workspace → multi-agent recall tracking could write to the wrong store
- **P2:** Reconstructed the read range from request params → `endLine` was off by one, and default reads recorded `0` lines instead of the actual returned range
- **P1:** Had lowered the deep dreaming threshold from `0.75 → 0.55` without calibration evidence

## Changes

- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts`: Add optional `workspaceDir` param to `executeMemoryReadResult`; queue recall tracking after successful reads using the **actual** returned range (`MemoryReadResult.from` / `MemoryReadResult.lines`)
- `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/runtime-files.ts`: Export `resolveMemoryHostAgentWorkspaceDir`
- `src/plugin-sdk/memory-core-host-runtime-files.ts`: Re-export through the SDK barrel
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.runtime.ts`: Re-export through tools runtime
- Keep the `0.75` deep dreaming threshold (current main has explicit calibration evidence supporting it) — no threshold change

## Evidence

- Rebased on current `main`: no merge conflicts (`mergeStateStatus` clean at time of submission)
- Recall tracking is **best-effort and non-blocking**: it only queues a read event after `executeMemoryReadResult` succeeds, so it cannot degrade existing `memory_get` behavior
- Range fix verified in code: reads now use the returned `from`/`lines` from `MemoryReadResult` (the authoritative value) instead of reconstructing from request params
- Workspace fix verified in code: uses `resolveMemoryHostAgentWorkspaceDir(cfg, agentId)` so multi-agent sessions write to the correct per-agent store
- Note: focused unit tests for `memory-core` recall tracking were not included in this PR scope; the change is an additive, guarded extension of the existing read path

## Verification

Builds on current `main` with no conflicts. Recall tracking is best-effort and non-blocking.

prs.title: perf(workers): reduce allocations while polling task ports
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repeated empty native task-port drains allocate a new decode callback on every poll. A captured allocation profile attributed 21,311,904 bytes to this routine service path, primarily through state-reader servicing; this was not retirement allocation.

## User Impact

Lower allocation and main-thread CPU overhead while servicing worker task ports. Message delivery, startup admission, failure handling, retirement, and stall diagnostics are unchanged. No configuration or stored-format change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the decode callback on its owning task port and reuse it for the port's lifetime. The callback still reads the same port synchronously inside `runWithMainThreadTask`. No cache, alternate transport, timer, or public API was added. Production delta: **+2/-3 lines (net -1)**; no test changes. Existing boundary tests already cover the preserved contracts.

## Evidence

An isolated Linux sandbox on Node 26.8.2 ran the actual source with 32 real MessageChannels and the production stall monitor enabled. Each round performed 500,000 empty drains. Both revisions used esbuild 0.28.2, matching the repository. V8 sampling interval was 4,096 bytes with collected objects included. Five measured rounds per process, executed base/head then head/base (10 rounds per revision):

| Median per 500,000 drains | Base | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Sampled allocated bytes | 147,784,284 | 100,515,460 |
| Main-thread CPU | 109.620 ms | 98.525 ms |
| Elapsed time | 111.763 ms | 99.822 ms |

**32.0% less sampled allocation and 10.1% less main-thread CPU in this focused workload.** These are drain-path measurements, not full-Gateway latency or heap-retention claims. No production state was used. No Testbox/Crabbox leases; broad validation is delegated to PR CI.

Local proof: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/worker-native-task-port.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed all four tests (33.56s Vitest duration; 39.18s wrapper wall time including a cold fixture compile). Changed-file `oxfmt --check`, repository oxlint for the changed file, and `git diff --check` passed. PR CI passed on `dc85bb5e5ea64dc07295c259b840defa03acb7f4`, including the production/test types, lint, changed-code tests, architecture guards, UI E2E, and required aggregate gate: [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38839528513). No CI reruns or inherited-failure exception were needed.

Review: **independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable)**, no actionable P0–P2 findings. The autoreview helper refused before inference because its selected provider did not match operator configuration; configuration was not changed. Simplification pass retained only the per-port callback reuse.

<details>
<summary>Worker-construction attribution and remaining gap</summary>

The same five-second CPU capture contained 216.716ms of sampled Worker-constructor self time. Of that, 116.072ms was definitely disk-budget maintenance starting on demand after idle expiry. The other 100.644ms had an async caller stack without pool identity; several counters advanced in the same scrape, so attribution is unresolved. These are sampled totals, not precise milliseconds per individual start.

Observed incremental starts in a 1,635-second window, normalized per hour: catalog-page 52.844; git-operation 17.615; session-transcript 11.009; image-processor, memory-search, and provider-prompt-state each 6.606; code-mode-node 4.404; disk-budget, state-read, identity-file, and fs-safe-copy each 2.202. Other pools had zero incremental starts. Disk-budget retirement was `idle_timeout`; no GC-storm retirement appeared in that window.

Constructor placement and start frequency are unchanged by this PR, and no before/after per-start improvement is claimed. Full admission-snapshot removal would affect SDK workers that can read inherited facts before task-relay installation; a disk-only retained transport migration adds separate lifecycle/shutdown obligations. This change addresses the independently proven recurring drain allocation without changing those contracts. Full-Gateway performance and construction mitigation remain unproven.
</details>

prs.title: fix(memory-wiki): reject malformed ChatGPT export encoding
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

A damaged ChatGPT export can contain invalid UTF-8 bytes while otherwise being valid JSON. Memory Wiki previously decoded those bytes as replacement characters and imported corrupted titles and content over existing pages.

## What changed

Validate the original export bytes in the existing conversation loader before decoding and parsing. Reject invalid UTF-8 with the affected path and instructions to download a fresh export. Load the export before initializing the vault, so rejection does not recreate missing scaffold files either. Valid Unicode, including a literal U+FFFD replacement character, remains supported.

Alix-007's original fix and recovery-message commits are retained. The additional change moves validation ahead of initialization and extends the existing regression to protect that ordering. No new helper is needed: this loader and source synchronization share Node's `isUtf8` primitive while retaining their own recovery messages.

## Evidence

Linux Docker, Node 24.16.0. Built baseline `efbe024a9aa3e42eb6a84af68a249081799c2d56` and candidate `e63b3168b21f00379b29b7305b2faec534a31629` once each with `pnpm build cliStartup`. Candidate source hashes match the committed files.

Both builds ran the shipped command against isolated local Memory Wiki vaults:

```sh
node openclaw.mjs --profile <isolated-profile> wiki chatgpt import --export <fixture.json> --json
```

Each vault first imported a valid conversation titled `Café 🤖 �`. Two subsequent exports (array and object-envelope forms) contained a raw `0xff` byte inside a title. Before each malformed import, the existing `inbox.md` scaffold was removed to detect initialization writes.

| Input | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Valid Unicode seed | Exit 0, one source page created | Exit 0, one source page created |
| Malformed array | Exit 0; title became `Café �AD_BYTE false`; vault changed; inbox recreated | Exit 1; all vault file hashes unchanged; inbox remained absent |
| Malformed object envelope | Exit 0; title became `Café �AD_BYTE true`; vault changed; inbox recreated | Exit 1; all vault file hashes unchanged; inbox remained absent |
| Valid Unicode refresh | Exit 0, existing page updated | Exit 0, existing page updated |

Captured candidate error:

```text
ChatGPT conversations export must be valid UTF-8: /work/evidence/head/invalid-array.json. Download a fresh ChatGPT export and retry the import.
```

Focused checks passed:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-wiki/src/cli.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **20 passed**.
- Formatting of the three changed files.
- Syntax lint of the two changed TypeScript files.

Simplification retained one byte-validation check at the existing owner, plus two table-driven regression cases for the supported export forms. Full change from the merge base: production **+9/-3**, tests **+33/-0**, documentation **+4/-0**. No new config, dependency, schema, migration, public API or retry path.

Not tested: real downloaded account exports or external search backends. The proof uses synthetic export data and the local search backend; no live user data was accessed. A live-provider gate is not applicable: this change does not affect providers, models, or agent-turn behavior, and ChatGPT export import makes no provider calls.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: reverting restores the old decoding and initialization order without a migration. The blast radius is Memory Wiki's ChatGPT import command; malformed exports now fail instead of silently replacing invalid bytes.

prs.title: refactor(state): simplify admitted database lifecycle
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Admitted database work repeats preliminary grants, close/release handshakes, warm schema polling, and duplicate queue bookkeeping. Those paths add work and obscure the actual owners of authority and completion.

## What Changed

Use cold worker preparation, one foreground FIFO grant, and actual task completion for reclamation. Keep one bounded maintenance preparation instead of UUID slots and a release RPC. Session mutations await their real completion through the existing abortable FIFO. Heartbeat workers keep independent renewal and committed lease checks without synchronous liveness acknowledgments. Shared-state reads retain consistent snapshots and await native/child settlement before releasing them. Projection maintenance keeps its bounded cursor and writer-receipt invalidation without traversal generations. Internal producers retain their owned values without defensive cloning and repeated typed guards.

No intentional schema, durability, retention, permission, public config/protocol, SDK, or dependency change. Phase E standalone session memory, security-effect revalidation, ordinary-shutdown settlement, and human-incident protections remain.

Net production LOC: 956 removed (+1008 / -1964). Tests, fixtures/support, declarations, generated files, and docs excluded. The older preserved cleanup branch overlaps this cut and is not additive credit.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Manual read continuations and redundant post-query scope checks (#160946, async-storage campaign #144592; synthetic interleavings, no cited human report): an accepted internal read can finish its selected snapshot during owner closure. Native close and accepted children still settle before snapshot release.
- Calls through an already-retired runtime context (#160946; synthetic retirement controls, no cited human report) fail visibly rather than guarantee late-query error ordering or unwind every inherited private-snapshot reference. Such a reference can remain until process/temp cleanup; accepted work still joins producer/native cleanup before releasing its snapshot. Starting preparation close earlier would not terminate pending work: the actual staging close itself waits for that request to settle.
- Warm schema/version/journal polling (#166253/#172371; performance/synthetic foreign-DDL cases): unsupported raw live edits can fail at the next statement until reopen or Doctor. Cold admission and explicitly invalidated memory facts still route preparation through the worker.
- Automatic schema-publication replay (#168612; synthetic publication revocation, no cited human report): pre-entry revocation fails visibly instead of closing/reopening and replaying. Entered writes are never retried.
- Projection schema/traversal generations (#165377 and synthetic churn controls): a bounded cursor and completion result replace cross-request traversal history. Dirty writer receipts, fair cursor progress, and late dirty sessions remain.
- Per-row lease rereads (#172373; internal same-process bookkeeping): one synchronous transaction checks live rows at the effect. If a live owner blocks drainage, stale-row cleanup can roll back and the next drain retries it.
- Reclamation RELEASE/nonce and mirrored close/custody flags (#161181, owner split #172357; synthetic close/termination interleavings): the native task closes before returning completion, and the parent awaits that completion under FIFO. Failed stop remains visible; exact crash cleanup still waits for native transport settlement.
- Repeated preliminary admission grants (#140897 and cold-admission refinements; synthetic revocation scenarios): existing lifecycle authority covers native startup, followed by one foreground writer grant. An unsupported owner change can fail at the actual effect; archive-before-delete and current authority remain.
- Maintenance preparation UUID map/capacity/release RPC (#158251; synthetic concurrent retirement): one planner owns one bounded preparation. A canceled pass may retain it until the next preparation or ordinary close; authoritative protection and row/transcript checks remain at commit.
- Duplicate mutation idle waiters, second run-lock phase, and manual cancellation race (#103618 and synthetic lifecycle work): the abortable FIFO owns queued cancellation; active accepted mutation completion includes finalization.
- Heartbeat ACK/progress/completed-request side channels (#157696/#164615/#168214; synthetic delayed delivery): async replies use the existing finite operation/committed-expiry bound. A delayed exit callback does not independently reject an effect while its exact persisted owner remains current. Human-reported independent renewal (#134880), slow Btrfs tolerance (#157160), and provisioning diagnostics (#170835) remain.
- Repeated journal-table/warm-schema/archive-result inspection: admitted handles and successful producer operations are trusted. Unsupported raw live DDL may fail at the next statement; cold validation, actual recovery reads, snapshots, archive-before-delete, and deletion-journal protection (#154002) remain.
- Defensive internal copies and typed guards: producers own their values. Unsupported mutation of queued internal inputs is best effort; external config/file validation, public shapes, borrowed shared facts, and security predicates remain. In particular, the background CAS clone introduced with #168301 is redundant for its request-owned production callers; later client requests cannot mutate an already-parsed server request. The actual database compares the full expected preference and asset at the write effect.

## Evidence

Current signed head: `e3d559cd3bd6d2e26a4adba49fcede9b701ef147`. Its production tree is identical to the conflict-graph proof head `c3a625ab39f3843ff7cda82468feb2789e018d01`; the final commit only corrects the reviewed storage wording. Exact-head hosted CI remains the broad gate.

Fresh combined review and focused repair proof are complete. Final formatting passed across 129 files, and the ordinary core type-aware lint invocation passed. Exact-head hosted CI is the broad gate.

Conflict-only rebase onto `4cf3df6352cea03d80bf0ff35758503089ba30db` preserves main's authored-source publication/policy invalidation fix (#173334), its value-fact caches and tests, and the newer shared GitHub read route. The removed preparation hash moved modules on main; its now-unused relocated definition is removed as part of the same cut. On rebased head `4d04f1f266c2749609a41cafa6f76681367c651c`, affected source/test type graphs, narrow type-aware lint, seven-file formatting, and runtime/static cycles (0/0) passed. All four affected owner suites passed: 17 GitHub publication/lifecycle cases and 59 runtime-config/value-fact cases, including the authored-policy invalidation controls. The wrapper completed generation verification/cleanup and exited 1 after 720.21 seconds, retaining the suppression failure below (78 total passing cases, one failing case); no aggregate-green claim.

The post-rebase suppression guard passed two cases and failed its allowlist comparison on two unchanged base entries: `scripts/lib/control-ui-warm-reload-probe.ts|typescript/unbound-method|1` (#173266) and `src/agents/code-mode-node.watchdog.test-support.ts|typescript/unbound-method|1` (#173574). Both files and the guard are byte-identical to the rebase base. No suppression or allowlist change is included; the subsequent exact baseline replay is recorded below.

GitHub reported another conflict on the verified pushed `4d04f1f266c...` head. The next conflict-only rebase onto `6b91e8cb63a67ae5dee6c1ddd4226ade6ad7d76d` preserves main's measured bounded reconciliation batching (#173620), its shared readiness predicate and new bounded-SQL regression. The sole conflicting overlap removes the already-retired traversal-counter increment while retaining the new batching. Code head `c3a625ab39f3843ff7cda82468feb2789e018d01` passes affected strict source/test types, ordinary type-aware lint, formatting and runtime/static cycles (0/0). All 14 projection-status/readiness cases pass, including the new bounded-SQL regression, rollback/savepoints, orphan bounds, receipt invalidation, contention and cursor progress. The wrapper completed generation verification/cleanup and exited 1 after 880.04 seconds, retaining only the suppression failure below (16 passing cases, one failing case). Prior unchanged-owner proof above remains valid; passing readiness cases do not establish a fix for the earlier unexplained timeout.

The original suppression guard was also replayed on clean exact main `6b91e8cb63a67ae5dee6c1ddd4226ade6ad7d76d`: two cases pass and line 190:72 fails with exactly the same two extra entries (96 received versus 94 expected). The original test and both implicated files have identical blobs on candidate and baseline. That establishes this specific baseline assertion only, not another CI failure or gate waiver. A fresh narrow P0-P2 documentation review is scoped-clean for the two-line storage-description correction: writer receipts request a new bounded scan after the current cursor completes, while local writes consume the pending queue. No schema or trigger change is included.

Exact prior head `8d6bd9e19794aab604631406df6b86d8903d476a`, CI run 38826267037 attempt 1, exposed security post-grant, explicit-invalid-proof worker routing, and replacement-cache integration regressions. Security checks and explicit-invalid-proof routing are restored; the incomplete watcher-removal proposal is excluded. All 17 failing root jobs were inspected individually; none is called inherited without current-main proof. Existing security/cancellation/FIFO/committed-data assertions remain unchanged.

The queue cancellation assertion in job 116734771814 independently reproduces on clean current main `6574349e132d11db684392cfd1ef8cb9f32598e6`: queue.authority.test.ts:285 expects `[false,true]`, receives `[true,true]`. The exact-case baseline wrapper exited 1 after generation verification. This attributes that assertion only, not the other failed jobs.

Combined production-graph types and a separate graph rooted in all 21 surviving changed test files passed; runtime and static import cycles are both zero. All three lint-suppression tests passed. Independent full-candidate review completed both passes and final source verification, returning one P2 about background CAS input mutation. Declined after tracing the actual request-owned callers and retained database CAS/effect authority, under the explicit queued-input best-effort tradeoff above; not a scoped-clean verdict. The final mechanical changes shrink one obsolete assertion allowance and drop an unrelated getter edit, restoring that file exactly to base.

The changed-check invocation passed conflict, max-lines suppression, and environment-count checks, then required the getter revert and one shrink-only assertion allowance. It was stopped after 26 minutes, with 11 minutes in SQLite-worker inventory without a result; no aggregate or inventory pass is claimed. Only its verified task-owned processes were stopped. Exact-head hosted CI owns broad proof. The completed focused repair batch passed 107 tests: 64 storage admission/reclamation/projection cases, 21 auth-profile SQLite cases, 19 infra cases and three suppression cases. The auth suite includes the prior schema-error classification failure; storage includes the prior off-thread integrity, cold admission, revocation and replacement failures. The batch also reproduces the matching baseline queue failure. Its MCP suite timed out in its unchanged 180-second setup hook, so none of its 17 cases ran; this is an unresolved local proof gap, not a passing security claim. Completed-generation verification and cleanup finished; wrapper exit 1 retains both failure observations.

Prior focused proof and its gaps are retained in the lane ledger. Two Doctor cases subsequently passed serially on both candidate and exact clean base at unchanged budgets; their original batch timeouts remain unexplained, not a claimed fix. Readiness comparison was inconclusive after the clean-base wrapper stopped before a result, not evidence of inheritance. No timeout increases, retries, skips, new suppressions, or hosted CI reruns.

The kept failed-native-retirement test was also replayed serially on the candidate and exact clean base `0001c2cd97518a456109caaba920de201ef726e0`. Both fail at the same initial one-second `vi.waitFor(retryEntered)` gate, before any native-close settlement assertions. Both wrappers completed generation verification and cleanup. prs.title: fix(ui): list sessions after a cold start restores a chat route
prs.body:
Closes #173095

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on a cold start that restores the last chat route, the Control UI never requested `sessions.list`. The sidebar then showed only the open chat until some other action, such as creating a chat, refreshed the list.

Since #146591, the connection bootstrap coordinator holds background work, including the sidebar's session list, until the foreground chat pane reports a ready transcript. The pane is accepted only when its key equals the foreground route key. Both keys come from `resolveChatSnapshotKey`, which prefixes the session key with the connection's account scope.

On a cold start, the restored route resolves while the Gateway is still connecting, so `subscribeForegroundChatBootstrap` registers it under the provisional `scope:unowned:<n>` prefix. The chat pane mounts after connect and registers under the connected `scope:["ws://…","<account>"]` prefix. Nothing re-keyed the route after connect, so the two keys never matched. The pane was rejected, and background bootstrap stayed held for the life of the connection.

## User Impact

User impact: reloading or reopening the Control UI on a chat now lists every accessible chat in the sidebar once the restored transcript is ready. The selected transcript still loads first: the background queue is held until the pane is ready, exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

`ui/src/app/bootstrap-location.ts`: `subscribeForegroundChatBootstrap` already subscribes to Gateway snapshots to synchronize the coordinator's client. It now also recomputes the foreground route key on each snapshot. A route restored before connect is therefore re-keyed with the connected account scope, which is the key the mounted pane uses.

The route rules are unchanged:

- non-session routes and pending creations still clear it;
- pending routes still hold it;
- catalog keys still bypass it.

The subscription moved below `synchronize` so the first snapshot can re-key the route.

## Evidence

**Real Control UI, Windows 11, headless Edge.**

- **Build:** the Gateway and Control UI were built from this checkout (`main` `c47f803` vs this branch), with a fresh state dir and a local mock model.
- **Setup:** three chats were created through the UI.
- **Cold start:** a fresh page in the same browser profile opens `/`, and the client restores the last chat route itself.
- **Measured:** the client's WebSocket RPCs and the sidebar's chat links, 20 s after load.

![restored chat sidebar](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/173095/restored-chat-sidebar-live-proof.png)

| Build | `sessions.list` sent in 20 s | Sidebar chats before reload → after cold start |
|---|---|---|
| `main` `c47f803` | **0** (38 other methods were sent, including `chat.startup` and `board.get`, as in the report) | 2 → **1** |
| this branch | **3** | 2 → **2** (the same chats) |

**Root-cause trace** on `main`, from temporary logging in `connection-bootstrap.ts` (not committed):

| Call | Key |
|---|---|
| `setForegroundRoute` | `scope:unowned:1\u0000agent:main:dashboard:<id>` |
| `setForegroundPane` (`ready: true`) | `scope:["ws://127.0.0.1:28795","<account>"]\u0000agent:main:dashboard:<id>` |

The pane was rejected, so `foregroundPending` stayed `true` and the background `sessions.list` task never started.

**Regression test** in `ui/src/app/bootstrap-location.test.ts`. It uses the real coordinator: the route resolves before connect, the Gateway then connects, the foreground key must equal the pane's connected key, and a queued background `sessions.list` task must run once the pane is ready.

| Test | `main` | This branch |
|---|---|---|
| re-keys a route restored before connect so the mounted pane releases background work | fails | passes |

**Gates:**

- `bootstrap-location.test.ts`, `connection-bootstrap.test.ts` and `bootstrap.test.ts` pass.
- oxfmt, oxlint, `pnpm tsgo:ui` and `pnpm tsgo:test:ui` pass.
- `pnpm check:changed` could not run locally. Its Crabbox route downloads from github.com, which this network resolves to a private address, so CI covers it.

prs.title: perf(sessions): reduce idle usage worker memory
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Usage-cost transcript workers unnecessarily retain the host configuration and plugin-loading graph after their first request.

## User Impact

Reduces worker memory overhead without changing usage totals, store selection, cache policy, or worker lifetimes. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Usage request preparation already resolves the configured store path before dispatch. The internal collector now requires that prepared path instead of importing the configuration resolver for an unused fallback. Native storage test helpers retain their optional path convenience. Production code: 3 added, 10 removed (net −7 lines).

## Evidence

- The extended import-boundary test fails on the original code with `session-cost-usage-worker → session-cost-usage-collection → session-store-path → config/io` and passes with this change.
- 30 tests passed across `session-history-read.imports.test.ts`, `session-cost-usage-worker-env.test.ts`, and `session-cost-usage.test.ts`, including custom stores, captured environments, and usage totals. Test-runner durations: 45.47 seconds for the two usage files and 6.48 seconds for the import file on a shared Mac.
- Changed-file formatting, repository lint, and `git diff --check` passed. Broad build/typecheck/suites are delegated to PR CI. No Testbox/Crabbox lease was used.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): no actionable findings through P2. The configured autoreview helper refused the requested provider route; operator configuration was not changed.

### Memory measurements

Measured on an isolated Linux sandbox with Node 26.8.2, restricted to CPUs 64–127 and 64 GiB. Each real transcript worker completed its request, idled for 2.5 seconds, and was sampled before and after `HeapProfiler.collectGarbage`; snapshots were taken after the reported sample. MB below means decimal MB.

| Worker / workload | Baseline heap (forced GC) | Candidate heap (forced GC) | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Bundled usage worker, empty inventory | 56.80 MB | 37.27 MB | −19.54 MB (−34.4%) |
| Source usage reader, 5,001-session inventory | 105.71 MB | 68.67 MB | −37.05 MB |
| Source usage refresh, same inventory | 107.32 MB | 69.90 MB | −37.42 MB |
| Source history after 35,000-event conversation | 79.19 MB | 79.19 MB | neutral |
| Source maintenance reader | 47.47 MB | 47.47 MB | neutral |

The four workload transcript workers total 339.69 → 265.23 MB (−74.46 MB). The bundled comparison uses the production tsdown configuration restricted to the transcript worker entrypoint, with normal external workspace packages built; it does not reproduce the full installed application's chunk layout. Bundled target, maintenance, and history controls stayed within 0.05 MB. Source measurements include loader overhead, so the bundled and source savings must not be combined.

Bundled usage external memory: 4.95 → 4.82 MB; ArrayBuffers: 0.64 → 0.57 MB (included in external). Workload usage external memory stayed around 5.7–6.0 MB, with 1.4–1.6 MB ArrayBuffers. Forced GC barely changed the source-worker idle samples; the dominant retained families are module/source strings, bytecode, module metadata, and configuration schema objects, not large decoded transcript buffers. The existing five-minute lane retirement and bounded data caches remain intact.

Workload: the repository's team-shaped fixture, 5,000 sessions, 6,000 retained runs, approvals/cron/projects, plus a new 35,000-message conversation; both revisions used independently generated synthetic state. Inventory returned 5,001 sessions and the long history returned 35,001 records including its header. Fixture agent database was about 322 MB after the added conversation; this was not a multi-GB production database or a reproduction of every production lane. No production state was accessed.

Single-pass timing observations: inventory 4.94 → 3.34 s, refresh 13.67 → 11.65 s, long history 3.31 → 3.33 s. These are context, not statistically established latency claims; the decision is based on the retained-heap reduction and unchanged behavior.

Baseline: `6b91e8cb63a6`; candidate: `e16d1a7c3aa0`. The experiment exercised `WorkerTaskPool` with the real transcript worker entrypoint, plus production `prepareUsageCostWorker`/`runUsageCostWorker`, `refreshCostUsageCacheForAgent`, and `loadTranscriptEvents` against the synthetic fixture. RSS during heap snapshots is deliberately excluded. The reported production pool's 473 MB was not reproduced as an exact total or remeasured on a live Gateway.

prs.title: perf(gateway): reduce session row allocation on plugin publications
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Background plugin-state writes scan every resident session row, even for pending and settled notifications that cannot change its presentation facts. Allocation profiling identified 30.8 MB in 5.27 seconds at this subscriber while session-list traffic was low.

## User Impact

Reduces session-projection allocation and unnecessary work during background plugin-state activity. Row contents, sharing, ownership, and stored formats are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Skip pending/settled notifications before scanning rows, visit Map values without per-row iterator results, and skip empty ownership dependency lists. Committed and unknown outcomes still use the existing dependency matcher and invalidate all affected facts before notifying observers. No new cache, index, or invalidation lifecycle.

Production delta: +4 lines (8 added, 4 removed); these small event filters remove execution work while preserving the existing two-phase facts/publication ordering. Test delta: +17 lines in the existing ownership integration test. No modules, exports, or test files added.

## Evidence

- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings. The helper refused the configured provider mismatch before inference; operator configuration was unchanged.
- Changed-file formatting and core lint passed. An initial lint command selected the general tsconfig and began artifact preparation; it was stopped and replaced with the core-scoped command.
- Focused ownership integration file: all 5 tests passed, 4.83 seconds of tests, 27.26 seconds Vitest duration (56.97 seconds wrapper wall time including worker preparation). Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/session-row-projection.runtime-ownership.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. PR CI owns broad validation. No Testbox/Crabbox lease used.

### Allocation measurement

Isolated Linux sandbox, Node 26.8.2, baseline `70833f4c3c11` versus `484d89650b93`; three interleaved baseline/head pairs. The driver imports the actual subscriber and creates 5,000 synthetic rows through `records.create`. It calls real publication begin/install/finish APIs with an unrelated keyed deletion receipt. Each case has 200 warmups, 2,000 unprofiled timing operations, and 1,000 sampled operations (V8 4 KiB interval, including objects collected by minor/major GC). One committed operation includes pending, commit, and settled publication; the pending/settled case omits the commit. No database or RPC costs are included.

Medians, decimal MB per operation:

| Fixture / operation | Subscriber MB/op before → after | Whole-operation MB/op before → after | Wall µs/op before → after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 500 native dependencies / 5,000 rows; unrelated commit | 1.136129 → 0.164177 (**−85.6%**) | 1.144848 → 0.173674 (**−84.8%**) | 280.05 → 121.38 |
| Same mixed rows; pending + settled | 0.484545 → 0.000095 | 0.486693 → 0.002281 | 90.79 → 1.03 |
| Empty dependencies / 5,000 rows; unrelated commit | 1.005549 → 0.000247 | 1.015087 → 0.010470 | 86.34 → 34.24 |

Mixed-row committed CPU: 284.12 → 124.61 µs/op. With all dependency lists empty, pending/settled total allocation was neutral within sampling noise (0.002869 → 0.002881 MB/op, a 12-byte difference), while CPU fell from 36.60 → 2.28 µs/op. All 24 case samples retained zero invalidations and zero dirty rows, as expected for unrelated publications. The existing integration test separately proves affected committed and unknown outcomes still refresh ownership. prs.title: feat: use oMLX for local chat and memory embeddings
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw cannot select oMLX for memory embeddings or discover a running oMLX server during setup.

Closes #74732. Thanks @mppyes-ai for reporting the missing integration.

## User Impact

Users can choose **oMLX** during setup, use `omlx/<model-id>` for chat, and set `memory.search.provider: "omlx"` with an explicit embedding model. The default endpoint is `http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1`; authentication is optional when the server permits it.

After changing the embedding provider or model, run `openclaw memory index --force`. The inference catalog has no model-type field, so select a chat model for conversations and configure the exact embedding ID separately. oMLX owns model installation and loading.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bundled plugin supplies identity, lazy setup/detection, `/v1/models` discovery, and an embedding adapter, reusing the existing OpenAI-compatible transports. There is no new core tool, manager, dependency, or management-API integration.

Authentication follows the selected endpoint. Setup clears obsolete endpoint credentials/request settings; header-only chat works without `apiKey`; custom-header auth suppresses generated bearer auth. Memory-specific header overrides apply before the adapter resolves provider header secrets, preserving the shared adapter's destination policy.

Live proof exposed two shared auth issues: dispatch/compaction suppressed headers using the source credential rather than the prepared key, and prepared direct auth rejected non-secret provider markers along with profile fallback. The existing auth owner now uses the prepared key and permits pure/already-captured markers without acquiring external credentials. Source credentials remain intact for profile ownership and attribution; explicit SecretRefs remain terminal.

Explicit custom authentication headers are excluded from embedding cache identity only when the configured provider owns the embedding endpoint. Rotating that credential no longer changes the vector-space identity; transport credentials and non-authentication routing headers are preserved.

Production TypeScript: **+755/-16**; tests: **+1382/-7**. Growth is the first-class plugin plus 31 net lines correcting shared authentication and embedding identity. Metadata/build/lockfile: +52/-0; docs: +215/-22; generated config/budget maintenance: +4/-4. The environment-name budget was stale on the merged base (453 budget, 452 actual) and is reduced to 452.

## Evidence

Live proof used isolated state on macOS/Apple Silicon, installed oMLX, `all-MiniLM-L6-v2-4bit` (384 dimensions), and `Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct-4bit`. Timings include startup/local I/O, not just inference.

- Before: the original CLI rejected `omlx` as an unknown memory provider (166.357 s). Generic OpenAI-compatible indexing/search worked against the same real server.
- Registered running-server detection/preparation passed (52.404 s), as did noninteractive onboarding with padded URL/model flags and a blank key (43.987 s). Discovery took 8.774 s.

- Three real header-only chat cases—loopback Authorization, non-local-classified Authorization, and custom-header auth—answered **“The sum is 42.”**, one assistant turn each, no fallback. Strict proxies verified intended credentials and no markers on the wire. Whole commands took 36.505–36.507 s during concurrent startup; embedded runs took 5.738–6.069 s. Chat proof is on `adbea7b6`, whose chat/core auth code is unchanged by the final memory-only fix. Previously, loopback lost Authorization (HTTP 401), while the other two failed auth admission. Endpoint switching with a retained old profile also passed strict authenticated/keyless controls.
- On final head `528b45417436803cfa0f5f25bb402460644160a7`, real credential rotation preserved the existing index without any reindex after the key change. Before the fix, the same sequence reported `mismatched/provider_settings` and returned no search results despite a successful embedding probe. After the fix, status stayed valid (6.116 s), two files/two chunks were retained, and semantic search returned the greenhouse note in **5.992 s** (vector 0.4343842864, text 0). Strict proxy evidence confirmed the new custom key and no Authorization header. Initial indexing took 135.693 s including a 120 s automatic rebuild; status before rotation took 7.173 s and the credential-only config change 3.623 s.
- **98/98 focused tests passed** (121.6 s): 49 plugin/setup tests and 49 generic embedding-owner tests. Header-only, public SDK direct-resolution, and memory-override regressions failed before their fixes; real-credential and unavailable-effective-secret controls remain passing.

Max-lines, line-cap, assertion-safety, timeout/race, mock-exports, config docs, and plugin inventory checks passed. Docs validation checked 1,370 MDX files and 15,535 links with zero broken links.

prs.title: fix(gateway): log slow plugin service startup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A signed-in reload of a dashboard deep link waits for Gateway startup. Deployment evidence recorded 7.09 seconds in `sidecars.plugin-services`, but the normal journal contained only the aggregate phase, so it could not identify the slow service. Per-service spans were visible only with full startup tracing enabled.

## User Impact

Operators can identify plugin services that take at least 250 ms during Gateway startup without enabling full startup tracing. Startup scheduling and admission behavior are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Log each top-level plugin-service start taking **at least 250 ms** through the existing Gateway startup trace/logger, regardless of `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_STARTUP_TRACE`. Each compact line includes the encoded plugin/service identity, duration, and `outcome=success|failure`. It contains no payload or error text. Full tracing emits the same line once; fast services and nested diagnostics remain opt-in. `docs/logging.md` documents the default.

Plugin startup scheduling remains **serial**, exactly as on main. `src/plugins/services.ts` and `src/plugins/services.test.ts` have no PR diff. Connect admission, `ready`, `readyz`, health reporting, and update acceptance retain their existing barriers. No concurrency change, new configuration, schema, or stored records is included.

Crabbox audit found no blocking startup work to detach: at deployed source revision `39ca16f1`, its only registered service has an empty `start()`, while remote worker maintenance is already backgrounded and drained during shutdown. No Crabbox lifecycle code changes are included.

## Evidence

Final head: `3ae375192760ca2875926f24c73c613e038073cb`.

Before: with full tracing disabled, a slow service produced no normal per-service startup line. After: services at or above 250 ms produce exactly one attributed line. The old trace owner fails three new assertions; all 13 trace tests pass with this change. Cases cover the unset/disabled flag, inclusive threshold, success/failure, payload exclusion, nested-span suppression, original-error propagation, and no duplicate line with full tracing. No startup speedup is claimed.

The prepared-borrow test and its retained-work assertions are unchanged. On AWS **c7a.4xlarge**, lease `cbx_6b9cc0806db1`, [run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_5f8519c78feafa57d78761b158a5704f), all three complete runs of `server-plugin-reload.prepared-borrow.test.ts` passed, including the cold-start retained-work assertion. The failure did not recur in those three isolated runs; the serial-head CI failure is recorded below. Focused tests also passed: **59 remote test executions** in total.

Each command ran serially with `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`. These wall times document test cost, not startup performance:

| File | Passed | Command wall time |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `src/gateway/server-plugin-reload.prepared-borrow.test.ts`, run 1 | 5 | 64.12 s |
| Same file, run 2 | 5 | 43.92 s |
| Same file, run 3 | 5 | 44.23 s |
| `src/plugins/services.test.ts` | 18 | 32.67 s |
| `src/plugins/services.reload.test.ts` | 13 | 27.53 s |
| `src/gateway/server-startup-trace.test.ts` | 13 | 3.98 s |

Core types passed. Changed-source lint passed with zero warnings/errors, and formatting passed. The proof archive was retrieved and verified; the lease is released.

**The same retained-work assertion still fails in [exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38838029833), without the concurrency change.** [Failed job `checks-node-changed-compact-small-3`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38838029833/job/116771905463) reports `server-plugin-reload.prepared-borrow.test.ts > published Gateway plugin services > cold start lets a published agent runtime use the visitor service`, line 832: `expected 1 to be greater than 1`. Only the shard name changed from the earlier run; the failing test, assertion, and signature are identical. Both service files match main exactly, including the serial scheduler (`services.ts` blob `07e6236d98de2ad2a14f7473bf1a9d57c3ea538d`). The prepared-borrow test is also unchanged. This is direct evidence of recurrence without the withdrawn scheduling change, despite the three passing isolated AWS runs. No assertions were weakened and no CI rerun was requested. CI completed on this exact head: **34 jobs passed, 26 skipped, the test job above failed, and the CI gate failed**. No other validation job failed. The corrected PR context/evidence check [passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38839304085/job/116775455735). This PR remains open and unmerged; the retained-work failure is reported as requested after removing concurrency.

Independent autoreview of the staged attribution-only candidate is clean through P2. The mechanical rebase preserved every remaining changed file and both restored service files byte-for-byte. Local focused tests passed: startup trace 13, serial services 18, and service reload 13.

## Scope

Three files: `src/gateway/server-startup-trace.ts`, its test, and `docs/logging.md`. Runtime delta: **+11 lines** (13 insertions / 2 deletions); tests +43, docs +4. The growth carries the required outcome and normal-log threshold through the existing owner; no additional timing, logging, or lifecycle owner is introduced. The withdrawn scheduling machinery and its tests are removed from the PR.

prs.title: refactor(gateway): collapse duplicate read and service lifecycles
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway display reads and service adapters repeat lifecycle preparation already owned by their worker, channel, scheduler, persistence, or provisioning owner. This removes those duplicate mechanisms while preserving security effects, bounded work, per-session FIFO, committed transcripts, and ordinary shutdown settlement.

## Changes

Prepare session-row prerequisites once; let the worker retain its database resources and keep one row-identity/facts-revision check at installation. Replace channel recovery's two-request handshake with one request after cleanup. Let the canonical cron service own start/pause/stop rather than duplicating its lifecycle in the lazy adapter. Reuse original event/reservation object identities for private chat handoffs. Carry decoded worker preparation into retention/refill and let the durable store own capacity. Remove observational approval fingerprints and the resource-free private inference drain reserve/accept shell. Preserve the shipped worker version methods and their original counter progression.

No config, schema, protocol, dependency, public SDK or persisted shape changes. The standalone Phase E session-memory implementation and its tests are untouched. Local-source validation remains before a new paid allocation; already-provisioning recovery still works after source loss.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Database display reads no longer retain an additional main-thread native continuation. #155388's held-worker/peer-commit tests do not establish a human incident requiring this second owner. The worker retains physical resources; the consuming row and sharing-facts revision must still match.
- Config/registry/topology changes during a display batch are prepared by the next publication rather than repeatedly re-admitting the current batch. The extra protocol has synthetic provenance; disposal, final physical admission and disclosure checks remain. Rare overlapping changes may temporarily display prior topology.
- Native ownership churn no longer gets two immediate attempts and a separate next-request retry registry (#171300); the dependency-currency veto from #168480 also disappears. Both cite synthetic interleavings, not human incidents. Descriptive fallback lasts until the next owner publication; real read errors still propagate.
- Catalog replacement settlements need not match the latest promise (#156339/#171519, synthetic). An older settlement may request a redundant refresh. An incomplete replacement retains the previous complete display catalog.
- Channel replacement no longer waits for a second start request (#88299, synthetic). A terminal diagnosis arriving only after replacement cannot cancel its successor. Health recovery uses the ordinary cooldown/hourly budget instead of #116089's synthetic continuation allowance. Human timeout recovery (#77651/#94008), cleanup refusal and current plugin selection remain.
- Stop/start while a canceled cron startup is pending joins that operation instead of recursively replaying a new generation (#103618/#126963, synthetic). Call start normally after its drain. A broad stream sweep overtaken by a direct mutation is skipped instead of re-listing five times (#112387); one destructive-effect revision check and exact mutation routing remain.
- Eager lifecycle persistence is reused by original private event identity rather than a serialized key with expiry flags. A cloned event is not a replay API. The actual write remains eager, ordered and joined at shutdown; human transcript-loss protections remain.
- Chat reservation identity is its existing payload object, not another random attempt UUID. Identically shaped replacement payloads remain distinct; strict external-abort identity and eviction fallback remain. Terminal persistence retains one hold and awaits its write rather than creating a child settlement capability (#166674's synthetic mechanism).
- Independent prepared-worker sources may progress even if another source fails; #143372's mocked cross-source generation test was not a human batch-atomicity incident. The existing store enforces capacity/expiry and provisioning rechecks repository authority before paid effects. Requested local reserves validate their pinned source before allocation; paid replays retain recovery.
- The private inference drain is acquired directly rather than wrapped in a resource-free reservation immediately accepted by its sole production caller. #157422 introduced the snapshot protocol; #168747 moved all acquisition into acceptance, leaving the shell with no resource or intervening await. No human incident supports that dead phase. Deferred cancellation, current effect authorization, provider/native settlement, ingress exclusion and ordinary shutdown joins remain.
- Approval replay can publish an identical terminal tombstone twice when it overlaps a held manager mutation (#154619's synthetic migration test). Durable expiry, authorization, waiter settlement and the owner effect remain once; the event neither edits transcripts nor wakes agents.

## Evidence

Base: `631b5e86299eb40fd04e25b7145d1d6c99d1d269`.
Current candidate including CI repairs: 727 added / 1255 deleted = **528 net lines removed** (37 production files; tests, fixtures, generated files and declarations excluded). Signed repair head `2794fb824e0d39a08de43b05bf6ba53a32b2f12f` is pushed; exact-head hosted CI is pending and is not claimed green.

Public-contract correction: machine-shape, disk-space, runtime-install and inventory version methods are transitively exposed through the stable Plugin SDK Gateway handler context. Their complete original implementations and counter assertions are restored, not replaced with constants or compatibility shims. The prior counter-removal snapshot is parked on `deslop/z02-parked-worker-counters-20261015`, with no PR for that contract change. The private inference drain was separately checked through the current/stable service, WeakMap registration and start/cancel-only RPC closure before simplification.

Independent initial review through P2 finished scoped-clean. Runtime cycles: zero. Changed-file formatting passed. Repair lint passed (401.22 s) and core types passed (913.40 s). The fresh complete-candidate P2 review completed with one finding about starting the same cron instance while its canceled startup still drains. This is the explicit accepted tradeoff above, not ordinary reload: the production reload drains the predecessor and starts a different nextState.cronState. The canonical owner still joins startup during shutdown. No generation/successor replay was restored for that unsupported interleaving. The review verdict is findings, not scoped-clean.

Two local focused attempts were intentionally interrupted and joined after long cold compilation to repair known types/lint. They produced no Gateway assertion outcome; the later attempt passed all 3 lint-suppression cases and completed worker preparation in 963.56 s before interruption (2465.04 s total). This is an explicit runtime-proof gap, not a pass or inherited-failure attribution. The loaded local host did not provide bounded Gateway proof; exact-head hosted CI must cover abort, node-dispatch, intent, cron-drain, channel, projection and native-ownership boundaries before landing. No timeout, retry, skip or suppression was added.

Scope marker occurrences against the pinned base: lifecycle terms 7463→7421, generation 1284→1267, epoch 283→279, lease 2961→2942, stale 322→319, tombstone 21→22 (an explanatory accepted-tradeoff comment). Other inventory marker counts are unchanged. These counts are coverage aids, not claims that every remaining mechanism is justified; the whole-scope causal audit continues.

Published-head CI run 38824809869 exposed eleven individual failing jobs. The repair addresses test-fixture typing (116730649664), cold topology/config/key publication (116730205058,116730204661), foreground materialization scheduling (116730205489), obsolete two-request channel recovery expectations (116730204955), direct Stop persistence (116730204840), obsolete main-thread continuation/native-retention expectations (116730204690), and exact assertion/mock-export ratchets (116730204390). Topology and foreground failures are real regressions: the replacement keeps one pending-publication identity check before installation and one foreground hold check at materialization, not a generation/admission protocol. Goal expiration mutates the actual pending payload; replacement uses a different payload identity. All behavioral refusal, no-dispatch and admission-settlement assertions remain.

Latest repair gates: Gateway-root and Gateway-other graphs pass after the private drain cut and restored public counter implementations; direct changed-file formatting/type-aware lint passes (48.08 s). Fresh recovery review is terminal scoped-clean through P2. The nine-file focused runtime proof completed successfully: all 112 Gateway cases and three lint-suppression cases passed (1845.13 s total wall). This covers inference caller/lifecycle/store, original provider/native failures, lost outcomes, retention bounds, public installer/disk/provider counters and actual agent deletion drains. No timeouts, retries, skips or suppressions changed.

Main-alias lookup (116730205278) plausibly shares the cold-publication regression but is not yet runtime-proven. Preview/aggregate timeout (116730205275) and native E2E capacity rejection (116730204849) remain unknown, not inherited. The native failure occurs before provider HTTP with capacity 1/wait 0; the occupied launch is not identified. All failed logs were fetched once. No CI rerun is requested.

Fresh repair review including the Goal fixture correction is terminal scoped-clean through P2. Gateway-root and gateway-other test graphs passed (399.7 s and 264.8 s; 1278.70 s total command). The nine-file repair proof passed lint-suppressions, then hit the existing no-output watchdog without Gateway assertion results (1221.59 s total, exit 143); that is not green or inherited evidence. The subsequent narrow Goal proof passed both expiration and replacement cases (1507.10 s wall). The four targeted real-regression cases also passed: pending config, cold-store publication, concurrent selection, and recovered in-process Stop (1217.46 s wall). All three lint-suppression tests passed again before this repair push (126.09 s wall). The startup loop now records its existing continuation condition after each batch, fixing the 702/700 max-lines failure without a suppression or limit change. A direct do/while attempt failed the lint rule that cannot model the async closure's writes; the explicit local continuation remains behavior-equivalent. Final repair lint is running. No timeouts, retries, skips or suppressions changed.

prs.title: refactor: simplify infra and plugin lifecycle bookkeeping
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Internal lifecycle paths repeat admission, copy producer-owned facts, and coordinate unsupported reentrant callers after their real owners already establish the required contract. These mechanisms obscure the actual security, FIFO, durability, and shutdown boundaries.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible feature or public SDK change. Rare, recoverable internal reentry and manually incomplete build scenarios follow the best-effort behavior named below; security effects, FIFO, user-data durability and ordinary shutdown settlement stay.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use one shared telemetry check, caller-local Git cancellation, per-registration cleanup settlement, first-settlement auth receipts, and straight-line private install batches. Remove redundant approval bookkeeping while preserving the live registered-context check before delivery starts. Consolidate official plugin-version candidate construction and service-stop preparation.

Plan transcript changes inside the existing immediate transaction and write prepared archive rows under the existing exclusive maintenance owner. Keep recovery journals, canonical hashes, publication receipts, authority checks and restart reconciliation. The state-directory latch cut was withdrawn after inconclusive changed-path proof; its producer, caller and test isolation are restored together.

Drop duplicate native removal acknowledgements, HTTP abort once flags, diagnostic drain generations and permanent profiler poisoning. Expose temporary ClawHub archive cleanup failures as warnings without replacing the installation result; its record-field normalization moves unchanged to the existing record owner.

Public SDK names/signatures, config/protocol/persisted shapes, security boundaries, normal user-data durability, ordinary shutdown settlement and Phase E standalone session memory remain unchanged.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Git read caches: viewer cancellation stops waiting instead of borrower-counting and aborting a shared bounded read. Owner shutdown still aborts and joins actual worker work. Producer-owned results are shared; the transport-mutated diff envelopes keep their targeted copies. Unsupported mutation after handoff is no longer hidden by generic cloning.
- Approval bootstrap: replace generations and repeated admission with one live exact-context check before external delivery starts, plus ordinary stop. Cleanup errors remain visible. A context replaced during preparation is not started. If an old in-flight start rejects after its successor starts, one retry timer may restart that healthy successor; no human incident was cited for this recoverable interleaving. The timer reads the current context, and no speculative generation protocol is retained.
- Question delivery and exec-approval bookkeeping: keep exact request identities, live recipient/effect authority and actual stop joins, not surrounding retired-generation or own-write readback machinery. Synthetic ID reuse must not transfer another request's answer.
- Telemetry: concurrent callers share one operation, including a cached result. Endpoint/state-root changes during that operation wait for a later check. #150824 explicitly used synthetic fixtures and injected HTTP, not an operator incident requiring recursive predecessor arbitration. Consent and request-boundary policy checks stay.
- Plugin auth and install batches: first settlement wins and ordinary orchestrators await their real preparation/compensation. Concurrent conflicting commit/rollback/close reentry by internal callers is unsupported. Credential rollback, source authority, locks, errors and physical cleanup joins remain.
- Registration disposal: settle each registration's own work rather than globally scheduling sibling scopes until all are idle. #144252 describes synthetic foundation scenarios, not a verified human cross-sibling-disposer incident. Cleanup that deliberately mutates a sibling's private resource must respect that owner's closure; actual registration and write settlement stay.
- Runtime contexts/adoption and diagnostics: remove second synchronous currency/map checks with no await between them. Initial abort/currency admission, actual callback authority, request identity and disposal tokens stay. Exotic reentrant getters or custom signal methods are not supported. #144424's real backoff deadline remains protected; it does not require self-mutating assertion callbacks.
- SDK aliases: a listed but manually incomplete dist graph may now fail with an ordinary missing-module error instead of scanning its relative imports and silently selecting source. f76b426e2bac introduced a synthetic missing-chunk fixture, not a verified human incident. Rebuild/restart repairs it; absent-dist fallback, public exports and native/plugin authority stay. Complete the cutover by deleting the orphan standalone scanner/facts/AST adapter and its fabricated old-scanner fixture; generic image admission, Doctor hashes, packaged assets and native resources stay.
- Plugin install facts: remove extra producer-owned copies, repeated parsing/compatibility checks and same-transaction own-write SELECTs. Introductions #167702/#140328 and the inspected planning extractions describe transport/record bookkeeping, not human post-handoff mutation incidents. Canonical boundary parsing, worker serialization, rollback receipts, source retention and effect authority stay. The cheap completed-cache-publication preference and retained-root target-mode branch stay; the latter cut was conservatively withdrawn after inconclusive timeout evidence.
- Transcript/archive repair: unsupported raw SQL mutation from an injected callback during exclusive maintenance is no longer detected by a second before-image/CAS owner. #124888 introduced the older drift path; #133563 later supplied exclusive maintenance. Remove only three synthetic in-custody writer tests. Real authority loss, rollback, cancellation, publication failure and between-invocation recovery tests remain unchanged.
- Logging: forced-exit rescue already sets processExiting before draining, making a second drain generation unnecessary (#114769). Keep FIFO, issued-write settlement and rescue of only the unissued tail. A diagnostic cleanup failure marks that capture unavailable instead of permanently poisoning all future captures; the #148004/#170932 failure controls are synthetic. Current capture authority and real cleanup errors remain.
- Native package work: remove an unused native-to-host removal acknowledgement left after its receiver's bookkeeping disappeared, not the real removal command or custody. Remove only package pending-I/O telemetry accounting, not deadlines, late close or hash ordering. HTTP abort uses its native once listener rather than another flag.

Net production LOC: **584 removed** across 40 production files, +415/−999 against `efbe024a9aa3e42eb6a84af68a249081799c2d56`, excluding tests, support, fixtures, generated files and declarations.

## Evidence

Conflict-only rebased signed head `5b07712ef799229e5fc9ae296ab09cfd31849eb9` completes the standalone scanner orphan removal, restores synchronous idle projection release ordering, and repairs fixture settlement observations. GitHub reported CONFLICTING at the preceding published head; the sole conflict was the Telegram fixture, whose identical readiness repair had already landed on main in `172aae503c5`. That file now equals the new base byte-for-byte. Production changes are patch-identical. Post-rebase runtime and madge cycles are both zero; all three held-operation cases pass (706.98s Vitest, predominantly cold transform). The suppression check reproduces the two already-verified clean-main unbound-method allowlist omissions; no suppression/allowlist was added. Broad local types are not qualified because the borrowed install contains pi-tui1.0.4 while the lock pins1.1.0; exact-head frozen-install CI owns that proof. Canonical SDK comparison remains pending, without acknowledgement waiver.

Earlier isolated proof: 3 lint-suppression tests, all5 Gateway borrowing/service cases, and all3 Telegram held-operation cases passed in1126.80s total wrapper time (Gateway666.27s, Telegram290.85s). The Telegram fixture observes the real mocked setWebhook notification rather than polling before account preparation finishes; accepted commit, rollback and introduction settlement assertions remain unchanged. Gateway retained-work assertions settle the existing shared startup catalog owner before comparing counts; missing and leaked run retention remain detectable. Fresh independent P0–P2 review was scoped-clean. Core fixture lint and formatting passed; extension lint did not reach linting because prerequisite SDK declarations exceeded the existing300000ms build bound. No timeout/retry/skip was changed, and no extension-lint pass is claimed.

Earlier isolated proof passed8 restored state-directory migration tests; runtime value cycles and madge cycles are both zero. Core/tooling repair lint, format and diff checks passed. Earlier focused repair proof passed53 tooling tests,46 infra tests and45 plugin tests; the existing Commander explicit-registration case timed out at its unchanged120-second bound. That timeout remains investigated but unattributed, not a claimed inherited failure or a proven repair. Production/test typecheck and regular build groups passed on the earlier head; canonical SDK API comparison remains pending. Corrected-head hosted CI is the broad gate; no SDK acknowledgement waiver is authorized. A serial replay of published head19e9 and clean main-parentf4 reproduces the same Telegram account-preparation abort before the held-operation scenario; the repaired fixture reaches and passes all three actual settlement scenarios. This is fixture-repair evidence, not a live Telegram claim or a blanket inherited-CI exception.

Independent full-candidate review completed. One earlier cache-consistency/security-consumer finding was fixed by restoring the completed-publication preference. The signal finding is disproved by the unchanged early abort boundary; partial-dist fallback is the explicit rebuild tradeoff above. A final skipped-migration finding is also disproved by the sole caller: a prior completed migration leaves no legacy path and returns before the reported condition; preparation is called once. A captured source disappearing during teardown remains a refusal, not a successful relocation.

Repair review: the disposal-ordering and complete standalone scanner cascade passed independent P0–P2 review. A subsequent withdrawal review identified the original process-global migration-latch limitation; all17 withdrawal paths are byte-identical to the actual PR base, so this is an existing follow-up, not a change-owned regression. The withdrawn multi-root/retry feature is not replaced with another cache or latch map.

The ClawHub cleanup regression uses real parsing/compatibility/archive installation with synthetic network I/O and preserves the original result while reporting temporary cleanup failure. Existing tests remain. Earlier interrupted/load-bound proof runs are incomplete, not passes or product-failure attribution. No new suppressions, retries, skips, budgets or raised timeouts.

prs.title: fix(cron): say an automation's account was removed instead of naming MCP
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the stored account an automation is bound to is removed or signed out (`openclaw models auth logout`), the run is correctly refused, but the error says "MCP authorization was disconnected or replaced" (`MCP_AUTHORIZATION_RETIRED`). The automation has nothing to do with MCP, so the message points the operator to the wrong place.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared authorization owner (`AuthProfileAuthorizationError`) keeps its MCP name and codes for its existing MCP callers. `acquireCronInferenceAuthorization`, the cron owner that reacquires a job's bound account, now translates a retired authorization into "Automation inference account <profileId> was removed or signed out. Explicitly select an authorized account again." It keeps the original error as `cause`. The flow is now one try block, and the "was replaced" case and disposal behave as before. The refusal and the no-fallback behavior are unchanged.

## User Impact

A job whose account was signed out now names that account and the next step, instead of an unrelated MCP message.

## Evidence

- `inference-binding.test.ts` > "rejects saved authorization after revocation…" now expects the new message: it fails on `main` (the run reports the MCP text) and passes with this change. The whole file passes (7 tests).
- In live evidence from #173509, `models auth logout` on the bound account gave `MCP_AUTHORIZATION_RETIRED` with 0 provider requests. That refusal path is unchanged; only its message is new.

prs.title: feat: discover models during custom provider setup
prs.body:
Related: #121584, #122042

## What Problem This Solves

Custom OpenAI-compatible setup requires users to find and enter a model ID even when the endpoint advertises its models.

## User Impact

The existing wizard offers advertised models alongside manual entry. Noninteractive setup can omit `--custom-model-id` to import the advertised list and use its first model as primary; an explicit ID skips discovery. Imported models are selectable. Empty, invalid, unauthorized, or unavailable model lists give a manual-ID recovery path.

Discovery runs during setup only. Anthropic-compatible setup still requires an explicit model ID. Endpoints may advertise embedding models alongside chat models, so use an explicit ID when their first model is unsuitable for chat.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both setup paths delegate to the existing guarded self-hosted discovery owner, retaining authentication, request deadlines, response-size limits, and network policy. Reset preflight carries its discovered IDs into setup so it does not rediscover after the reset. This adds no command, runtime catalog owner, dependency, or persistence schema.

Bulk imports preserve authored Azure model capabilities and compatibility fields. Explicit Azure model setup retains its established normalization, and an explicit input-mode option still takes precedence. This repairs the metadata-overwrite issue found during review.

Thanks @alexandre-leng for the reports and setup proposal.

## Evidence

- Original CLI against an authenticated local fixture: exit 1 with the mandatory model-ID error; zero requests reached the fixture. New wizard and noninteractive regressions also fail against the original implementation.
- 167 unique focused cases passed across the campaign. Final-head rerun: 57/57 custom config and noninteractive cases, 357.13s Vitest duration (518.56s wall including wrapper cleanup). The Azure regression fails in all three discovery cases on the pre-repair code; the explicit-model sibling passes before and after. Cases preserve a stored credential reference, Azure header, unrelated Gateway settings, authored capabilities, and model selections.
- Final-head core typecheck (63.47s), scoped type-aware lint (145.79s including artifact-lock wait), formatting, and diff checks passed. Final ratchets: max-lines, line-cap, assertion-safety, test-timeout-race, test-mock-exports, config docs, and plugin inventory all passed. Fresh independent Codex review through P2: scoped-clean, no accepted/actionable findings.
- Earlier full runtime/UI build passed on `8fcc7cdafcfd` (23m28s build phases; 29m23s wall including lock wait). The final follow-up changes only the Azure merge option and its regression coverage; the discovery and transport paths used in the live proof are unchanged.
- Real `pnpm openclaw ... onboard --non-interactive` runs omitted `--custom-model-id` and succeeded against an authenticated fixture (181.54s), Ollama `/v1` (181.64s, 9 IDs), and LM Studio `/v1` (181.64s, 2 IDs). The fixture received one authorized GET; duplicate/empty IDs were removed. All imported IDs are selectable in the written config.
- Real embedded OpenClaw turns on Node 26 used the imported providers without rerouting: LM Studio `google/gemma-4-e4b` returned `DISCOVERY_READY.` (147.14s wall), and Ollama `qwen2.5:7b` returned `DISCOVERY_READY` with tools disabled in an isolated config copy (187.63s wall). With the full tool surface, local Ollama models generated malformed or unwanted tool calls; catalog/auth/routing worked, but tool-following remains a separate limitation.
- Platform limit: macOS on Apple Silicon. Pinned-Bun embedded turns stalled before provider HTTP; setup discovery passed there, and successful embedded turns used the supported Node selector. No operator Gateway/state was touched. Existing-config preservation is covered at the production setup boundary; no latest-stable-to-head Azure upgrade campaign was run.
- Diff: production +149/-37 (net +112), tests +438/-12, docs +23/-1, and two verified stale max-lines entries removed. The setup handoff and selection require production growth; nearby duplicate verification-error formatting was removed, and transport/catalog ownership stays unchanged.

## External validation status

The repaired head is published and independently reviewed, but external gates remain pending: CI run [38782320894](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38782320894) has 35 completed jobs, 23 unassigned Blacksmith jobs, and no failures; `openclaw/ci-gate` has not passed. The requested ClawSweeper re-review was dispatched successfully, but no review for this head was published within the 15-minute observation window. The prior-head Azure finding is repaired and covered by the failing-before/passing-after regression above.
