prs.title: fix: resume interrupted tasks in their original session
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a task interrupted by a Gateway restart can only continue in a replacement conversation after automatic recovery gives up.

## User Impact

WebChat's **Resume** continues the saved task in the same session, preserving its identity, workspace, participants, children, and automation bindings. The click supplies current operator authority; it does not restore old approvals or replay completed tool calls. Retry exhaustion leaves the same actionable Resume path.

**Resume in new session** remains available when a CLI runtime cannot enforce required restart-safe tool restrictions. An already-linked replacement opens that existing session. Pending final delivery must settle first; a missing transcript requires repair.

## Why This Change Was Made

The original replacement flow in #122644 (`bb5ef9872a70`) avoided resuming a native provider thread with a changed dynamic-tool catalog. The current native runtime can rotate an incompatible provider thread while preserving the OpenClaw session (`extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle-run.ts:519`). The recovery service's unconditional successor allocation is now limited to the replacement path (`src/gateway/session-recovery-service.ts:427`).

The recovery owner validates the session ID and recovery cycle, then uses ordinary chat admission. The existing input actor accepts the continuation and clears the tombstone in one SQLite transaction (`src/config/sessions/session-pending-input-store.ts:282`). No new schema, scheduler, or durable store is introduced. WebChat requests in-place recovery; omitting the new mode preserves the existing public API replacement contract. Existing unknown-outcome guidance and restart-safe tool policy follow the turn through dispatch and queues.

The pre-admission recovery-row guard ends after its own successful commit; current operator/source authority and normal admitted-input access checks remain (`src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-recover.ts:60`). Otherwise, clearing the tombstone invalidated the new turn before dispatch.

Related work reviewed: #172234 (presentation, merged), #165957 (session-controller draft), #166340 and #170336 (restart continuation). This is an adapter at today's recovery/chat owners, with no competing controller.

## Evidence

The Team Gateway journal contains six delegated-sender-authority failures at lines 607774, 750589, 798599, 846511, 879013, and 916035. These are sanitized locations only; no message content or session identifiers are included.

Before:

![Before: restart banner offers only Resume in new session](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cfc3e7bf-0bc1-4c51-b73d-d71cd3f919f8)

After:

![After: restart banner offers Resume in the same session](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c9e7a4a7-3ace-4fdf-bc43-2ca3dac7886b)

Both captures use inspected synthetic sessions in the Control UI mock harness. The mock E2E also verifies the explicit second-click CLI fallback.

Real-process proof passed **4/4**: ordinary permission-change control, managed restart, raw SIGTERM, and SIGKILL with a second restart during the resumed turn. Every restart case reaches final completion in the original session, clears the tombstone, preserves a durably cancelled task, blocks revoked/restricted effects, and checks that completed tool effects occur exactly once. The initial full matrix took 119.539 seconds of test time (605.22 seconds including build). After preserving the stored restriction ceiling, the managed and SIGTERM cases passed again (27.635 and 59.396 seconds); the synthetic provider now deliberately issues a stale execution call when tools are hidden and verifies its rejection. SIGKILL plus the second restart and ordinary permission-control cases also passed in the subsequent CI run. No test timeout was increased.

The probe exposed an existing live-permission bug on clean main (`c3b63ff4c0ec5338d56a4109d2162889db49d653`): an ordinary operator turn failed with “Permission change was not authorized by the current operator request.” `run/attempt.ts` awaited tool reconstruction before recording the authorized change, after its synchronous authorization scope ended. Recording the change before the await fixes the owner without extending authorization lifetime (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts:423`); successful acknowledgement still waits for reconstruction.

<details>
<summary>Focused validation</summary>

- `pnpm test test/gateway-session-resume-restart.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 4 passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.sessions.recover-in-place.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 10 cases passed in the final focused run. Existing `server.sessions.recover.test.ts`: 23 passed.
- Touched session/runtime/recovery suites: 237 passed. Recovery-state suite: 32 passed. Auto-reply suites: 72 passed. After merging main, the complete `queue.authority.test.ts` file passed all 17 cases, including cancellation handoff and both new restart-tool-restriction cases.
- Focused UI suites: 25 passed. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/chat-restart-resume.e2e.test.ts`: 2 passed.
- Core/UI production, Gateway/messaging, UI-other and banner E2E test typechecks passed after the merge. The UI-chat graph has the clean-main failure recorded below. Typed lint, formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
- The final actionable-notice assertion passed in the delivery suite; both changed test files passed targeted lint, formatting, and the root-test typecheck.
- CI repair: extracted the shared authority input type to remove a type-only import cycle; `check-madge-import-cycles` reports zero cycles. Updated restart-message assertions and the remaining channel-feedback notice. Authority suites passed, sharing-state tests 9/9, model-lock session cases 3/3, delegated shutdown case 1/1, channel-notice suite 8/8. No timeout or safety assertion was weakened. The final Gateway suite passed all 10 cases, including persisted tool restrictions after a successful tool-result tail: restrictions reach native/embedded dispatch and block unsupported CLI continuation. A committed review found this missing retained restriction; the fix matches automatic recovery’s existing safety ceiling. PR review also identified omitted delivery constraints in the full-access exemption; the same automatic-recovery checks now keep media, disabled-message, and suppressed-text restrictions effective, with Gateway rejection proof for all three.
- `pnpm prompt:snapshots:gen`, UI English/i18n verification, and `pnpm docs:check-links`: passed; 15,539 links checked, none broken.
- Committed-branch Codex autoreview: scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings (including unchanged authority, input-actor, runtime-classification, and recovery-policy context).

</details>

Merged main `bd18e16d7de2c4ffd8a2bdaf1b15533dcf094197`, including its cancellation-handoff repair. The automatic merge preserves main’s aggregate cancellation owner and disposal unchanged; the only `queue/drain.ts` difference from main is propagation of `forceRestartSafeTools` and `forceCodeModeTools`. No manual conflict resolution or new production semantics were introduced.

Post-merge validation: queue authority 17/17, Gateway in-place admission 10/10, focused UI 25/25, banner E2E 2/2. Core/UI production and targeted Gateway/messaging, UI-other and banner E2E test typechecks passed; typed lint and formatting passed. The UI-chat graph fails at `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-model-catalog.test.ts:167` with `TS2304: Cannot find name render`. Running the same canonical graph on clean main `bd18e16d7de2c4ffd8a2bdaf1b15533dcf094197` reproduces that exact failure; the file is unchanged by this PR. The compiler-inventory test also reproduces on clean main: `test/scripts/tsgo-core-test-shards.test.ts` still expects `ui/src/components/agent-avatar-face.test.ts` after its rename to `.tsx`, yielding `expected [] to deeply equal [ui-components]`. Neither failing file is changed by this PR. Final-head CI [run 38837406620](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38837406620) completed on `c25ebe8a0b86270bf0b8e9a6482d7a51056176ea`. Its only failing test is the compiler-inventory assertion above (`checks-node-compact-small-1`); the aggregate gate is consequently red. The queue-authority failure did not recur, and there are no other failing jobs beyond the aggregate gate. No workflow was rerun.

Production: +851 / −389 lines (net +462); tests: +1452 / −42 (net +1410); docs: +25 / −8 (net +17). Most test growth is the real-process restart fixture and Gateway admission regression. Production growth adds the in-place recovery branch and carries existing tool restrictions through normal turn/queue owners. Existing source tracking and error presentation were split by responsibility to keep owner modules within their length limits.

prs.title: fix(cli): stop mangling version-suffixed invocations in command hints
prs.body:
Closes #173308

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: command hints OpenClaw prints (recovery, update, status, wizard suggestions) get mangled when `OPENCLAW_CONTAINER_HINT` or `OPENCLAW_PROFILE` is set and the command invokes the binary with a version suffix — e.g. `npx openclaw@latest ...` or the `openclaw-update` launcher — producing a copy-paste command that fails when run.

## User Impact

User impact: operators using a container hint or a named profile (container deployments, multi-profile setups) get correct, runnable command hints again. Version-suffixed invocations such as `npx openclaw@latest` are left untouched instead of being rewritten into a broken `openclaw --container <hint>@latest ...`. Plain invocations (`openclaw <cmd>`, `pnpm openclaw <cmd>`, `npx openclaw <cmd>`) keep the injected flag exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

`formatCliCommand` (src/cli/command-format.ts) detects the CLI invocation prefix with `CLI_PREFIX_RE = /^(?:pnpm|npm|bunx|npx)\s+openclaw\b|^openclaw\b/`. The `\b` word boundary is satisfied by any transition to a non-word character, including `@`, `-`, and `.`, so the injection `command.replace(CLI_PREFIX_RE, (m) => `${m} ${addition}`)` inserts `--container <hint>` / `--profile <name>` *before* the suffix and glues the suffix onto the flag value:

- `npx openclaw@latest gateway status --deep` → `npx openclaw --container demo@latest gateway status --deep`
- `openclaw-update` → `openclaw --container demo-update`

Requiring whitespace or end-of-string after the binary name (`(?=\s|$)`) matches only genuine binary invocations and leaves version-suffixed forms unchanged — the safe result, since the flag cannot be reliably placed inside a versioned specifier.

## Evidence

Environment: Windows 11, Node v24.16.0, pnpm 12.10.1, source checkout. Two kinds of real terminal evidence:

### 1. Shipped CLI entry point with an active container selector

Running the built OpenClaw CLI (`node dist/entry.js status`) with `OPENCLAW_CONTAINER_HINT=demo` and a config that produces diagnostics. Every hint the real command emits carries the correctly injected `--container demo`:

```
$ OPENCLAW_CONTAINER_HINT=demo node dist/entry.js status
Config diagnostics:
- Config file is invalid: <isolated state>/openclaw-config.json
- gateway: Unrecognized key: "bogusKey"
- Fix: openclaw --container demo doctor --fix
...
Security audit
Skipped in fast status. Full report: openclaw --container demo security audit
Deep check: openclaw --container demo status --deep
...
Next steps:
  Need to share?      openclaw --container demo status --all
  Need to debug live? openclaw --container demo logs --follow
  Fix reachability first: openclaw --container demo gateway probe
```

### 2. The regression itself, before vs after, in the real runtime

`formatCliCommand` is shipped to plugins as a public SDK export (`src/plugin-sdk/cli-runtime.ts`, `setup-tools.ts`, `setup.ts`, `provider-web-search.ts`). Captured through the same runtime the CLI uses (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs`), under an active container selector (`OPENCLAW_CONTAINER_HINT=demo`) and an active profile selector (`OPENCLAW_PROFILE=myapp`):

Before (`92e62263a2e`):

```
== OPENCLAW_CONTAINER_HINT=demo ==
npx openclaw@latest gateway status --deep              -> npx openclaw --container demo@latest gateway status --deep
openclaw@2026.9.9 connect https://gw.example/j/abc --service --session-host
                                                       -> openclaw --container demo@2026.9.9 connect https://gw.example/j/abc --service --session-host
openclaw-update --help                                 -> openclaw --container demo-update --help
pnpm openclaw@latest doctor --fix                      -> pnpm openclaw --container demo@latest doctor --fix

== OPENCLAW_PROFILE=myapp ==
npx openclaw@latest gateway status --deep              -> npx openclaw --profile myapp@latest gateway status --deep
openclaw-update --help                                 -> openclaw --profile myapp-update --help
```

After (this branch, `a17e1db544e`):

```
== OPENCLAW_CONTAINER_HINT=demo ==
npx openclaw@latest gateway status --deep              -> npx openclaw@latest gateway status --deep      (unchanged)
openclaw@2026.9.9 connect https://gw.example/j/abc --service --session-host
                                                       -> openclaw@2026.9.9 connect https://gw.example/j/abc --service --session-host   (unchanged)
openclaw-update --help                                 -> openclaw-update --help                        (unchanged)
pnpm openclaw@latest doctor --fix                      -> pnpm openclaw@latest doctor --fix             (unchanged)
openclaw doctor --fix                                  -> openclaw --container demo doctor --fix        (plain invocation still injected)
npx openclaw doctor --fix                              -> npx openclaw --container demo doctor --fix    (plain invocation still injected)

== OPENCLAW_PROFILE=myapp ==
openclaw doctor --fix                                  -> openclaw --profile myapp doctor --fix         (plain invocation still injected)
```

Focused tests: `pnpm test src/cli/command-format.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → 3/3 pass. `pnpm tsgo:core` typecheck passes; oxlint and oxfmt are clean on the touched files.

## Root Cause

`CLI_PREFIX_RE` used `\b` (a word boundary) after the `openclaw` token. A word boundary also matches before `@`, `-`, and `.`, so the prefix match consumed just the binary name and the injection inserted the flag before the version/launcher suffix, corrupting the resulting command.

## Regression Test Plan

Coverage level: unit + real-runtime captures above. New `src/cli/command-format.test.ts` pins:

1. plain invocations still get the injected container flag (`openclaw doctor --fix` → `openclaw --container demo doctor --fix`, `npx openclaw doctor --fix` → `npx openclaw --container demo doctor --fix`),
2. version-suffixed invocations are left unchanged (`npx openclaw@latest ...`, `openclaw@latest ...`, `openclaw-update`),
3. non-CLI commands are left unchanged.

Plain-profile insertion is covered by the existing `src/cli/profile.test.ts` (which also checks profile trimming), so it is not duplicated here.

## Scope Boundary

This change only tightens the invocation-prefix match in `src/cli/command-format.ts` and adds a focused unit test. It does not change flag placement for plain invocations, nor does it touch root-update handling, completion, config, or any other CLI surface.

## AI-Assisted Contribution

Authored with AI assistance; all verification was run locally as described in Evidence.

prs.title: fix(storage): defer WAL timers during owned offline maintenance
prs.body:
Related: #166413, #170022

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated lock-refusal warnings when a background SQLite checkpoint runs while the same process is doing offline maintenance.

## User Impact

Background maintenance waits until the offline work finishes, or stops waiting if canceled. Repeated reader/busy warnings are compact; real storage errors are still reported. The WAL change does not alter database contents, schemas, permissions, retention or durability settings and requires no migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The background timer should wait for its own maintenance operation instead of repeatedly attempting work that is expected to be refused. After release it resumes the existing schedule. Repeated reader/busy warnings are grouped by cause, while detailed WAL health remains available separately. The documentation now explains this in three sentences.

## Evidence

- **65 focused tests passed** on runtime head `42ef154`: WAL acquisition, worker scheduling, checkpoint diagnostics, scheduled-message actions and the complete admission-process file. Core types, focused test types, scoped lint and formatting passed. Fresh official P0–P2 review found no actionable findings in the selected diff.
- [CI on runtime head 42ef154](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38796748726) completed successfully: **105 jobs passed, 23 skipped, zero failed/pending**. The later changes are only the environment-budget correction and documentation simplification; runtime and test files are unchanged. New-head CI is being qualified separately, not claimed green from that earlier run.
- The exact environment-budget reduction **453 → 452** fixes the recorded ratchet failure without weakening the guard. The owning combined check passes: **527 existing max-lines suppressions and 452/452 environment names**. The source inventory is unchanged. The edited documentation passes scoped formatting, MDX validation and whitespace checks. Both corrections used normal commit hooks and preserve published history.
- **Proof limitation:** the tests exercise native SQLite and scheduling owners, not timer deferral through an installed CLI/Gateway. The historical malformed-ownership CI failure no longer reproduces on the composed candidate; its exact cause remains unproven. A passing replay is not presented as a causal fix.
- The latest durable ClawSweeper review is for `16cf632`, with **no code findings** and a historical conflict hold; it is not a fresh-head review. Inline review threads are empty. The PR remains open/non-draft with auto-merge off. Final RFR requires the actual published head's CI and mergeability qualification. No merge or auto-merge is requested.

<details>
<summary>Prior repair and validation details</summary>

Pinned main `2f228582` was merged normally into `a4bce384` to produce `42ef154`. Main's shared-worker suspension, engine selection, idle checkpoint parking and clean-close admission were preserved. The remaining WAL change is local release-driven deferral, queued admission revalidation and compact grouped diagnostics; cross-thread Doctor drainage in #166413 remains separate.

The prior failed [CI run 38669394622](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38669394622) was classified unknown, not proven inherited. The complete runtime and fixture fix from [#172794](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/172794) addresses its nine scheduled-message failures. The malformed-ownership case passed alone and in its complete file using the current pinned Bun fork, but that does not establish why the older CI run failed.

The 52 WAL/cron cases took 87.37 s wrapper wall; the 13 admission cases took 73.93 s, including 28.40 s worker preparation. Earlier 130-test and 67-test/27-type-graph results remain historical. The original failing timer regression and host-revalidation negative control remain provenance, not installed-runtime or held broker FIFO-queue proof. Review was diff-scoped and did not execute unchanged source.

</details>

prs.title: refactor(daemon): move runtime pins to a daemon-owned local store
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Runtime pins describe local service intent, but storing them in shared `config_machine_state` and reading them with Swift SQL made native recovery depend on the shared database. Pins now live in daemon-owned, SQLite-only `<state-root>/control/services.sqlite` on every engine. Swift consumes the typed CLI projection; malformed or stale values remain visible intent.

The local schema v1 includes a migration receipt. The Doctor `config-machine-state` step copies exact keys, JSON bytes, and timestamps with phase `copied` in one local transaction, retires source rows under exclusive custody, then records `complete`. Exact duplicates resume interrupted copies; conflicts retain both stores. A completed receipt for the same source skips shared writes. Runtime readers never read legacy values.

Includes R1 (`6b3617207ac1`), refreshed onto main `644ce068bc2` after a generated-inventory conflict. Production files merged automatically; the inventory was regenerated. No release stored runtime pins in PostgreSQL shared state, so no PG migration source exists. Under R1's boot-owned PG selection, the pin owner completes a local receipt with source `none/unshipped` once per process/root, without opening shared state or acquiring maintenance custody. The native fast projection also accepts that completed receipt without initializing the shared engine. SQLite keeps the exact copy/retire migration. A PostgreSQL conformance case exercises local status/install/update pin operations and asserts zero PG statements during those operations.

The PG maintenance-custody gap (`gateway-owner-lease.ts:150`, `gateway-owner-lease.worker.ts:44`) is an R14 follow-up; runtime pins do not enter that path under PG.

## Admission by path

| Path | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Install/start/repair/uninstall and Doctor service restoration | Existing service lock first, then SQLite migration under exclusive state custody or PG local receipt completion, then local pin read. |
| Read-only status and Swift projection | Typed `migrationPending`, with `run openclaw doctor`; never unpinned. |
| Update pre-stop inspection | Preserve the runtime/path from the original service definition and record the pending-migration warning. |
| Active update | Existing stopped-Gateway Doctor path completes SQLite migration; PG intent is local immediately. |
| Paused update/resume | Preserve runtime while pending; existing Doctor or CLI start/repair fence completes migration on resume. |

Exact updater capture/restore includes the local store and schema. Released callers retain their shared/agent schema response while capturing the complete local store; modern callers explicitly request local schema facts. The approved credential-writer guard entry only registers the migration caller, with no credential behavior change. Generated worker inventory is regenerated from source.

## Update behavior

- **First update:** pending migration preserves the original service definition, runtime, and path. The result warns: “runtime pins not yet migrated; preserved the current runtime; the post-update Doctor step migrates them”. Active updates run Doctor after stopping the Gateway.
- **Paused update:** migration may stay pending. Resume preserves runtime and completes migration through its existing Doctor or CLI fence. Accepted edge case: app-hosted resume invoking neither path keeps runtime preserved until the next CLI start/repair or `openclaw doctor`.
- **Mixed versions:** new readers use only local intent. Old binaries must not edit runtime pins after cutover; completed migration does not follow later legacy writes. New schema facts are opt-in for released updater compatibility.
- **Interrupted migration/rollback:** phase `copied` resumes retirement using exact duplicates; conflicts stop with both stores retained. Exact updater recovery includes the local store. No runtime compatibility reader was introduced.

Custody evidence: native active updates stop/drain the child and await service stop before Doctor (`GatewayProcessManager.swift:651`, `GatewayProcessManager+HostingChange.swift:286`, `GatewayProcessManager+HostingChange.swift:192`, `CLIInstaller+BundledPreparation.swift:52`). This covers both app-hosted and LaunchAgent paths. CLI updates park the foreground Gateway and stop the managed service before invoking package Doctor (`update-command-execution.ts:494`, `:513`, `:593`; `update-command-package.ts:170`). Doctor owns the existing exclusive state lock. Service admission covers paths before ordinary Doctor migration.

## Evidence

Net production change against rebased main: **+586 lines** (TypeScript +513, Swift +53, tooling +20), excluding tests, test-only helpers, and generated docs.

Focused proof covers receipt phases, exact malformed values/timestamps, conflict retention, interrupted copy/resume, service admission, pending status, update preservation/completion, paused/resume, released-worker schema compatibility, and exact capture/restore. The PG local-intent case passed (746 ms; suite 2/2). It uses the real selected engine in-process, verifies zero PG/config-machine-state statements during pin operations, and verifies native projection readback after engine selection is cleared. Native/AppKit tests never run on the operator Mac; CI provides native proof.

Local production Knip reports three unused exports, reproduced on pinned main `6b3617207ac1`: `prepareWorkerGitHubBindingGrant`, `DropdownMenuController`, and `scrollState`. None is changed by this PR. Main-only fixture setup also reports an unused `eslint` tooling dependency; the branch does not. Format, Kysely guardrails, and rebased SwiftFormat/SwiftLint pass. Independent Codex review is complete. Its full-delta P2 finding was assessed as described below; subsequent test-only repairs completed scoped-clean through P2. The max-lines checker reports two stale entries outside this PR (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/model.test.ts`, `src/channels/plugins/setup-wizard-helpers.test.ts`); no baseline was broadened. Line-cap, assertion-safety, database dialect, timeout-race, and environment-count ratchets pass. The regenerated worker inventory and worker ratchet pass: T1 calls 223 → 223; compatibility calls 12 → 12. Full local core lint exceeded 900 seconds; final-head core lint passed in CI. Fresh local proof covers the changed PG branch, all eight SQLite migration cases, and the corrected wizard fixture. The attempted broader local replay was stopped after inherited split-root timeouts; the final-head CI results below provide daemon/service and Swift proof.

Two Doctor orchestration timeouts are also inherited, reproduced with the same command on main at `f68299b62e9883006c5ac2921c88715f690d33e8`: `executes and receipts Doctor-owned exec and TUI migrations from the same mode` and `relocates the legacy state root before running Doctor-owned migrations`. Both keep their existing 120-second limits.

## Prior CI failure classification

The [prior full run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38715659365) had 12 failed leaf jobs plus its aggregate gate. Rebase precedes this attribution. “Inherited/disjoint” means the failure's executing path does not consume runtime-pin behavior; it does not claim a main reproduction.

| Prior failure | Attribution against rebased main |
| --- | --- |
| Swedish translation memory | Inherited/disjoint: UI catalog validation, no pin inputs. |
| Real-Gateway cron fixtures | Inherited/disjoint cron-add fixture path; main now seeds a synthetic inference profile before startup. New CI verifies the result; prior logs omitted the failing command stderr. |
| Swift `numericNestedEnable` | Inherited/disjoint catalog policy; main replaced it with `numericCatalogEnable`. |
| Real-Gateway privacy guards / Workboard locator | Inherited/disjoint DOM fixture/visibility paths after successful startup; no pin projection. |
| Duplicate “Copy path” locator | Inherited; main scopes the locator to the menu item. |
| Mocked UI reasoning count | Inherited/disjoint mocked event rendering. |
| Mocked UI live preferences | Inherited/disjoint `sessions.patch`/rendering; test revised on main. |
| Knip exports/type/MCP fixture | Inherited; the named exports and fixture helper are now private/removed on main. |
| Session visibility | Inherited/disjoint direct `sessions.search` fixture with `startServer=false`; no boot/daemon migration. |
| Cron inference account / continuity | Inherited/disjoint executor rejects missing recorded inference binding before callbacks. |
| Fast-mode and Telegram Doctor | Inherited/disjoint policy and selected conversation repair; main corrected fast-mode expectation. Telegram does not run the migration step. |
| Concurrent agent ownership claims | Inherited/disjoint direct child schema-open race; no daemon migration call. |
| Aggregate CI gate | Consequence of failed leaf jobs. |

The prior shard 39 cancellation at its approximately 60-minute limit had no failed assertion; unfinished cases were not proven. Final-head results are recorded below.

## Pre-landing-rebase head and CI

Head: `4f699d92e5c33c3665075334b3e3796e53862afe`, rebased onto `644ce068bc2`. The PR is ready and unmerged.

[Exact-head PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38812046596) completed successfully: **77 passed, 24 skipped**. [Main-tier native CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38812044013) completed with **134 passed, 14 failed, 14 skipped**. The failures comprise 13 leaf jobs plus the aggregate gate; all jobs are terminal. Automatic PR CI skips executed macOS tests by repository policy; the main-tier run supplies that proof.

| Required proof | Final-head result |
| --- | --- |
| PostgreSQL conformance | Passed; local runtime-pin case passed in 96 ms, including zero PostgreSQL pin access. |
| Swift app tests / Swift package tests | Both passed on CI; no native/AppKit tests ran on the operator Mac. |
| macOS Node | All three jobs passed. |
| Architecture / import cycles | Passed; exact Madge gate reports zero cycles. |
| Pin migration / update | All eight migration cases and 49 original-service update cases passed. |
| Status / updater local schema and retained imports | Their CI groups passed. |
| Gates and review | Focused tests, CI production/test types and core lint, local format and SwiftFormat/SwiftLint, inventory and worker ratchets passed. Knip is classified below. Independent reviews complete. |

The inventory conflict with newer main was generated-only and resolved with its generator. Main's added update cases exceeded the shared test helper's line limit; the unchanged pin-preservation case moved to a separate helper. CI caught a type-only cycle in that extraction, which was fixed by extracting the shared fixture type. The exact architecture gate now passes. No production behavior changed in those final test repairs. Net production remains **+586** (TypeScript +513, Swift +53, tooling +20).

### Pre-landing-rebase failure classification

These are causal classifications against this rebased head. “Disjoint” does not claim same-case reproduction on main. The Doctor cascade includes collateral failures in two touched rehearsal tests, so those cases are not claimed as passing proof.

| Run | Failed job | ID | Classification | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Main | control-ui-i18n | 116687823483 | Inherited/disjoint | `ui/src/i18n/.i18n/sv.tm.jsonl does not contain sv translations`; catalog is unchanged by this PR. |
| Main | checks-node-compact-small-19 | 116687828633 | Inherited/disjoint | Two `pr-baseline-incoming.test.ts` cases fail `Missing required command(s): rg`; unchanged release/PR tooling prerequisite. |
| Main | check-dependencies | 116687825452 | Inherited/disjoint | Knip production and full-tree unused export: `extensions/memory-wiki/src/markdown.ts: WikiPageNotUtf8Error`. This file/export/consumers are outside the runtime-pin delta. |
| Main | checks-node-compact-small-24 | 116687828615 | Inherited/disjoint | `ci-workflow-guards.test.ts` private Control UI server ownership expects 64 entries, discovers 65: missing inventory entry `ui/src/pages/agents-home/claws-catalog.e2e.test.ts`. UI fixture/inventory paths are outside this PR. |
| Main | ios-build (tests) | 116687824628 | Inherited/disjoint CI harness | Python cannot open `.ci-harness/scripts/swift-build-cache-metadata.py`; `restore ios` exits 2 before tests. Same missing cache-harness script failure as the previous head. |
| Main | checks-node-compact-large-18 | 116687828866 | Inherited/disjoint session fixture | `server.sessions.create-worktree-spawn.test.ts > required parent rejects external github project before binding or allocation with global sandbox off` fails fixture drain (`server-sessions-resources.test-helpers.ts:55`), one active Gateway root remains instead of zero. This is direct-handler session/worktree teardown: `create-worktree-spawn.test.ts:52` uses `setupGatewaySessionsHandlerTestHarness`, which passes `startServer=false` at `test/server-sessions.test-helpers.ts:298–301`, so no Gateway boot/Doctor/pin migration runs. No same-case main reproduction is claimed. |
| Main | checks-node-worker-e2e-2 | 116687828508 | Disjoint worker/skill execution; underlying error opaque | `skill-library-worker-wire.e2e.test.ts` reaches `bob-worker-first`, then `agent.wait` returns `status:error` instead of `ok` at `finishTurn:201`. The test passed `localFirst`, then failed `finishTurn(remoteKey, "bob-worker-first")` at line 341 after node readiness. `skill-library-node-process.ts:79–89` launches foreground `node run --ephemeral`, with no daemon install/start path; this is collaborator/remote skill execution. Job log contains only the generic reply failure, no pin-store error or underlying stack; no same-case main reproduction claimed. |
| Main | checks-node-compact-large-34 | 116687828954 | Inherited/disjoint heartbeat execution | Direct heartbeat fixtures: `model-override` admitted-work-timeout case never invokes reply spy; `tool-response` isolated-instructions case returns `failed` instead of `ran`. Both run through `heartbeat-runner.test-utils.ts:203`, not daemon lifecycle/pin reads; same class of existing heartbeat fixture failures. No same-case main reproduction claimed. |
| Main | checks-windows-node-test-3 | 116687824221 | Inherited/disjoint worker packaging | Three relocated worker archive tests time out: exec environment/authorization at 180 s, lazy plugin facades at 120 s, image/file operations at 120 s. Same unrelated worker-build fixture class observed on prior heads; no runtime-pin call or error. |
| Main | checks-node-compact-large-25 | 116687828878 | Disjoint Gateway close terminal expectations | `server.agent-execution-shutdown.test.ts` stop/graceful cases unexpectedly call `markRestartAbortedMainSessions`; `server.agent-late-admission.test.ts` receives restart/queue terminal instead of expected rpc terminal. The shutdown fixture awaits the harness then holds mocked dispatch/finalizer; late-admission explicitly calls `harness.server.close({reason:"gateway stopping",restartExpectedMs:null})` after held work admission at line 153. These are kernel-close/admission contracts with no daemon service operation or pin read after startup. No pin error or same-case main reproduction claimed. |

Failure is in subagent registry cleanup, not retained-import or runtime-pin behavior. |
| Main | checks-node-compact-large-10 | 116687828680 | Inherited/disjoint maintenance-release cascade | First failure: `doctor-update-schema-guard.test.ts:440` revalidates retired update authority after integrity work; shared state remains under offline maintenance at `gateway-state-owner.ts:709`, followed by 86 failing cases and teardown errors. The first test directly uses `migrateOpenClawAgentDatabaseForMaintenance` at lines 440–480; helper 147–163 calls `beginDoctorMaintenance` then `release()`. The release path (672–684) does not call `finish()`, service restoration, Doctor, or config-machine-state/pin migration. Includes two collateral failures in touched `doctor-rehearsal-capture.test.ts`, both refused on that same old shared path before assertions. Separate timer residual and retired-model successor warning also appear. |
| Main | checks-node-compact-large-12 | 116687828774 | Inherited/disjoint placement authority | `placement-turn-claims.worker.test.ts:804`: previous authority remains current when old release reply is held. The fixture directly opens shared state and creates its placement store in `beforeAll`; no Gateway boot, Doctor, or daemon pin path. No same-case main reproduction claimed. |

Monitoring completed at 22:30 UTC after every job settled, within the two-hour watch window. No CI reruns or remote cancellations were used.

The full rebased review raised a possible SQLite-to-PG switch bypass. That finding was declined after checking the existing admission contract: PostgreSQL shared state currently supports fresh roots only; `database-engine/open.ts:121-126` rejects existing SQLite data. Non-Gateway CLI preflight does not install PG selection (`startup-config-preflight.ts:112-119`), so the pin fence keeps the SQLite migration path. Gateway admission precedes migration. Shared-state porting remains outside this PR.

The split-root timeout is inherited at the shared fixture: main `94223e13e96` reproduces `keeps B facts and current data through split-root failure: same-version` at the unchanged 120-second limit (123.129 s reported; branch 124.997 s). The new `pin-migration-pending` variant also times out (134.361 s); it does not exist on main, uses the same fixture, mocks pending and skips pin reads, and enters no migration/service-lock wait. Main used its own frozen dependency install in a temporary detached internal-disk worktree, removed after the baseline wrapper exited. No timeout was increased.

## Real macOS proof

The coordinator has **satisfied the real-Mac landing gate for the CLI/LaunchAgent cells** on this exact head. A real Parallels Tahoe guest upgraded from published `2026.10.3` to the candidate by direct install followed by `openclaw doctor`: pinned **PASS**, unpinned **PASS**, and malformed-pin migration **lossless** (exact JSON bytes and timestamp retained, local receipt complete, legacy rows retired). Pinned and unpinned cells started successfully and passed required RPC checks with the expected stored runtime intent.

The app's exact `gateway status --runtime-intent-only --json` invocation reported `migrationPending` with `run openclaw doctor` before Doctor in all three cells. The malformed cell preserved a visible parse error; its missing recovery next step reproduces on the published baseline, and post-start plist normalization retained runtime arguments. Those inherited limitations are not claimed as a full malformed-cell pass.

Update-path cells could not run because of an **inherited published-updater capture failure on macOS**, reproduced with main as the target; that failure is out of scope for this PR. App-hosted signed-app cells are **deferred to R10 PR1/PR3**. No broader app-hosted or update-path proof is claimed here.

Evidence: `.artifacts/parallels/r10-runtime-pin-direct-20261015/REPORT.md` (final approved continuation). The coordinator approved landing with these results and deferrals.

## Landing rebase

Current head: `42699a82502e8a0d5cfaa820ad7e41ff3e1e25d3`, rebased onto `56c315156f4` because GitHub reported CONFLICTING. The only conflict was the generated worker inventory, resolved with `pnpm db:worker-inventory:gen`. A tree comparison against the automatic merge preview confirmed no other manual delta. Final regeneration and `git diff --check` passed. The earlier successful CI and real macOS proof above apply to the pre-rebase head; current-head CI results follow. prs.title: test(ui): finish native chat transcript fixtures
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The remaining transcript regression fixtures still enter through Lit adapters, and two virtualizer fixtures use Lit lifecycle hooks. They need to exercise the native renderer as the transcript completes its Solid migration.

## User Impact

Recovery, reader position, row identity, search, keyboard, media, and voice contracts are exercised through native Solid rendering. This final diff changes tests, test support, and the protected test inventory only. Product rendering, layout, and startup imports are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Moves the remaining transcript, message, composer, question, and activity fixtures onto native Solid renderers and the production virtual-core lifecycle. Obsolete Lit test hosts and mount helpers are removed. Controller and media retirement remain synchronous; only the outer test root waits one microtask before disposal so a same-task move retains its root.

Markdown and streaming tests mount native components with retained props. Disclosure parking checks the same card before, during, and after presentation changes. Search reads the existing transcript state, and opaque media callbacks use the existing native-content boundary. The protected inventory follows renamed files, including seven already-renamed chat entries. Coupled test callers use the same native fixtures, and four obsolete Lit support modules are removed.

The first full PR run exposed two fixture conversion defects, repaired without weakening assertions: end-follow reapplied unchanged bound heights over intrinsic DOM growth, while the keyboard fixture mixed a native listener with Solid's delegated render root and observed the wrong `currentTarget`. Height bindings now commit only when the fixture value changes; keyboard history intent uses the same JSX event boundary as the production thread. The repair also supplies required return annotations, keyed row rendering, a bound update callback, and correct JSX attribute casing.

After the repaired head passed full CI, main advanced into three conflicts. The merge takes main's complete native clipboard fixture and Solid avatar implementation unchanged. The message fixture uses a native `TestAvatar` mock and removes its retired Lit-content import. No assertions were removed. Clipboard and avatar files therefore disappear from this PR's final diff.

## Evidence

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| UI typecheck and exact chat test type graph | Both passed on the merged candidate committed as `bc3e83889f9e0fd7b45225d2c00f866dbfac7219` |
| Message fixture after avatar conflict resolution | 92/92 passed, one run with `--maxWorkers=1`, 11.02 s Vitest duration |
| Transcript row identity | 6/6 passed on the retained predecessor; one file run, 18.19 s wall |
| Transcript recovery | 12/12 passed on the retained predecessor; one file run, 22.91 s wall |
| Voice reconciliation | 4/4 passed on the retained predecessor; one file run, 20.49 s wall |

| Scoped lint | Repair candidate passed; only two existing self-closing warnings |
| Independent Codex review | Original and caller deltas, seven-file CI repair, and final conflict-only delta scoped-clean at P0–P2, followed by lead source verification |
| Production Knip | Passed on exact committed head `bc3e83889f9e0fd7b45225d2c00f866dbfac7219` |
| Full PR CI | Run 38835565326 on exact head `bc3e83889f9e0fd7b45225d2c00f866dbfac7219` failed only the two jobs attributed below; `ci:full` retained. Predecessor run 38832519669 passed |

The original 17-source codemod review was retrospective: its dry-run reported 50 templates and 146 manual diagnostics, reviewed against the draft. This does not claim the dry-run preceded those conversions. The two later coupled Markdown/streaming files had a pre-edit dry-run, with one template and 23 diagnostics. The subsequent direct-caller conversions had individual pre-edit codemod dry-runs.

Review scope is explicit: the original review received unchanged context only for supplied thread, search, and Solid-render files; the ten-test delta received six supplied datasets and two review passes. The earlier clipboard review received its diff without unchanged helper context; main's complete fixture now supersedes that delta. Reviewers did not execute project tests. The lead inspected final source, and the CI repair and conflict resolution each received fresh isolated reviews.

The first failed run (38829710841 on `00215d069793186934c8e935924ce47b3fe654a6`) also had an unrelated real-Gateway service-child cleanup timeout in the quota recovery case. Its runtime and test inputs were byte-identical to the base, but the compared scheduled-main run passed; this was not claimed as inherited or repaired. The subsequent repaired head's full CI run passed. The first head's security workflow also completed with dependency and sensitive-code review success. New-head checks must be evaluated independently.

The final full CI run (38835565326, attempt 1) has two source-proven main-side failures. `check-test-types-core-3` reports TS2304 at `chat-pane-model-catalog.test.ts:167`; `checks-ui (2/3)` fails `chat pane composer controls > revalidates the warm restricted configured model catalog when the picker opens` and `chat pane composer controls > revalidates the cold configured model catalog when the picker opens` with `ReferenceError: render is not defined` at the same line. prs.title: fix(memory-wiki): reject malformed UTF-8 source imports
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Memory Wiki source imports silently replace malformed UTF-8 bytes and mark the damaged content synchronized.

## User Impact

User impact: a malformed source refresh now fails with the source path and a recovery instruction, preserving that source's existing imported page and synchronization metadata. Restore the source as valid UTF-8 and retry the import. Valid Unicode, including a literal replacement character (`�`), continues to import normally.

## Why This Change Was Made

Validate the exact source buffer at the existing shared writer for bridge artifacts and unsafe-local imports, before rendering, page replacement or synchronization-state updates. The unchanged-source fast path stays intact. There is no charset conversion, new option, dependency or separate importer.

Alix-007's implementation and regression tests are retained. The additional documentation explains how to recover from rejected input. Coordination with the ChatGPT import fix confirmed that Node's `isUtf8` is already the common primitive; each importer keeps its own recovery message instead of introducing a forwarding helper.

## Evidence

Built once per version in isolated Linux containers with Node 24.16.0. Current-main baseline: `56c315156f4542f197a2b7f727681ba3f41c21b5`. Candidate production tree: `7bac65cdac5a5c94f439bf08ea61d3325c6176a1`; head `ff2e236f58c00ccc6e99ab11fdb93670cb1d995c` adds documentation only.

The same shipped entry point ran against isolated local vaults and real SQLite state:

```sh
node openclaw.mjs --profile <isolated-profile> wiki unsafe-local import --json
```

Each scenario first imported `Café 🤖 � original`, then replaced the source bytes with `ff 41 42` and advanced that file's modification time.

| Scenario | Current main (two independent vaults) | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Valid source seed | Exit 0, one imported source | Exit 0, one imported source |
| Malformed source refresh | Exit 0, one updated source; page contains `�AB`, synchronization metadata advances | Exit 1; page bytes and persisted source-sync rows remain identical |
| Valid source repair | Exit 0, one updated source | Exit 0, one updated source containing `Café 🤖 � repaired` |
| Unchanged valid source | Exit 0, one skipped source, no index refresh | Exit 0, one skipped source, no index refresh |

Captured candidate error:

```text
Imported source file must be valid UTF-8: <source.md>. Restore the source as valid UTF-8 and retry the sync.
```

The harness compared every vault Markdown file byte-for-byte and read the actual `plugin_state_entries` source-sync rows before and after rejection. It also verified that the malformed input bytes themselves were untouched. Both baseline runs observed the corruption; candidate preservation and valid-update controls passed.

Focused validation: 3 files / 25 tests passed (`source-page-shared`, `unsafe-local`, `bridge`); targeted type-aware lint reported zero warnings and errors; formatting passed for all three changed files. A separate shipped local-agent smoke with `openai/gpt-5-mini` returned `OK` (not required for this source-import-only fix). Full suites and cross-platform checks belong to CI. Real bridge artifact transport was not exercised; the shared writer's bridge regression is covered by the focused tests. This preserves one rejected source, not whole-batch atomicity.

Simplification retained one existing validation owner and no new abstraction. Whole PR: production +8/-1, tests +49/-0, documentation +6/-0.

Merge danger: two-way door; reverting restores the prior import behavior and does not require a schema or configuration rollback. Blast radius is bridge/unsafe-local source imports containing malformed UTF-8; valid imports and unchanged-source polling retain their existing behavior.

prs.title: fix(slack): requireMention threads go silent after a workspace-scoped bot reply
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Slack `requireMention` channel follow-ups are silently dropped after the bot has already replied, when outbound send recorded participation under a workspace id and the next inbound event has no enterprise `eventScope`.

## User Impact

User impact: operators with `requireMention: true` and default `implicitMentions.threadParticipation` now get the rest of a thread after the first bot reply, including relay and other inbound paths that do not attach an enterprise event scope. Direct mentions, unscoped (non-workspace) participation records, and cross-workspace isolation are unchanged. A follow-up that names a different enterprise workspace still does not inherit the earlier record.

## Why This Change Was Made

`send.ts` records thread participation with `delivery.teamId`. Inbound mention gating only looked up `eventScope.teamId`. Those keys diverge as soon as send has a workspace id and the next event does not �� the follow-up is treated as a stranger and dropped, with no error.

The participation owner now has one inbound lookup: a named enterprise event scope stays exclusive; when that scope is absent, the monitor workspace id is also accepted so it matches the send record. Inbound dispatch records through the same resolver. Existing unscoped store keys remain readable after upgrade.

## Evidence

### Production-boundary harness (inbound receive �� reply dispatch)

The inbound owner `createSlackMessageHandler` runs production `prepareSlackMessage`. The reply effect is `dispatchPreparedSlackMessage` �� the call that sends the Slack reply. A different enterprise workspace is rejected before that call.

Command:

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/slack/src/sent-thread-cache.test.ts extensions/slack/src/monitor/message-handler.thread-participation-workspace.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

After, on this PR head `96fae696f1f` (rebased onto current main):

```
dispatches an unmentioned follow-up when send recorded the monitor workspace
  dispatchPreparedSlackMessage called 1 time
  MentionSource=implicit_thread
  ImplicitMentionKinds=["bot_thread_participant"]

does not dispatch a different enterprise workspace before Slack reply I/O
  dispatchPreparedSlackMessage not called

dispatches after upgrade when only a pre-change unscoped store record exists
  persisted key default:C123:1700000000.000000
  memory cache cleared
  dispatchPreparedSlackMessage called 1 time
  MentionSource=implicit_thread

reads a pre-upgrade unscoped store record after restart with a monitor workspace id
  persisted key A1:C123:1700000000.000006
  inbound workspace T1=true
  inbound event T2=false

Test Files  2 passed (2)
     Tests  20 passed (20)
Duration  175.51s (transform 68%, tests 25%)
```

Before this change, the same inbound receive with a workspace-scoped send record and no event scope never reached dispatch (`old inbound lookup=false`). A follow-up that names enterprise workspace T2 still does not reach dispatch after the fix.

### Existing-store upgrade

A participation record written before this change uses the unscoped key `accountId:channelId:threadTs`. After upgrade, inbound lookup with a monitor workspace id still finds that SQLite row; a named other-workspace event does not.

### Mention-policy owner (same production function `prepareSlackMessage` uses)

```
recorded=send.ts delivery.teamId=T1
old inbound lookup (eventScope.teamId absent)=false
new inbound lookup (workspaceTeamId=T1)=true
other enterprise workspace T2=false
old mention policy requireMention=true implicit=[]
new mention policy requireMention=true implicit=["bot_thread_participant"]
```

### Static checks

- `oxfmt --write` on the changed files �� clean
- `git diff --check` �� clean

### Scope notes

Owner boundary only: Slack thread-participation cache and its inbound mention/dispatch callers. No change to send's enterprise key, no change to mention policy when `threadParticipation` is disabled, no new config option.

prs.title: fix(test): reduce serial tails in local full-suite runs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Untargeted local `pnpm test` spends hours in large serial cohorts while the scheduler's worker budget sits idle during exclusive Gateway runs.

## User Impact

Local full-suite runs can use the existing bounded worker budget inside exclusive Gateway invocations and retire large extension database cohorts sooner. Test coverage, exclusive barriers, explicit worker overrides, and CI scheduling stay intact. The full-suite target of less than one hour has not been measured; the scoped result below is the verified performance claim.

## Why This Change Was Made

The current local plan has 612 invocations, with automatic shard concurrency capped at ten (the earlier census explicitly selected four). Hundreds of invocations are intentional process-lifetime bounds; eliminating them would reintroduce retained module growth and starvation. At an assumed 3–10 seconds per invocation, fixed overhead contributes 1,836–6,120 aggregate process-seconds, while the census's infra and extension database tails alone accounted for 22,172 of 44,917 aggregate process-seconds.

Two tooling defects drive this change (bucket 1 in the Bun campaign):

- The scheduler assigned one Vitest worker even to exclusive Gateway invocations, despite running no other shards alongside them. Give those invocations the existing concurrency budget, preserving config-owned serial phases and explicit overrides.
- Extension database process cohorts included 243-file and 81-file groups. Apply the existing twenty-file job bound within each cohort, preserving Telegram singleton lifetimes and smaller existing limits. Respect suite-wide Vitest flags such as `--shard`; a regression caught unintended multiplication from one invocation to 48 before this guard was added.

Local invocation count becomes 629, including 105 extension database invocations instead of 88. The extra 17 invocations trade a small startup cost for bounded lifetimes and schedulable work. Remove redundant local-policy helpers and document the actual twelve-aggregate/leaf-expansion behavior.

## Evidence

The same sixteen files / 278 tests across three exclusive Gateway configs passed on the pinned Bun fork (`1.4.3-canary.1+65d94e715`) in **182.82s before → 101.72s after**: **81.10s / 44.4% less wall time**. Both runs reused compiler outputs on the same 32-core macOS host. Sampled peak process-tree RSS rose from **3.78 GiB → 6.26 GiB**, the intended tradeoff for using three workers instead of one. This measures the Gateway allocation change; the extension cohort bound is covered by exact inventory and planner tests. No full-suite wall-time claim is made.

- Effective inventory comparison against the original branch base: **18,915 files, each exactly once**, identical before/after SHA-256 `620110cfb550019b12b8b8957cd54533ef59e0ab513737360e15f02b9bbd2abe`; zero additions, omissions, or duplicates. Default CI, GitHub Actions, explicit CI parallelism, explicit CI leaves, and remote Testbox plans are byte-identical.
- Planner and scheduler files: **428 tests pass on Bun and Node**. After adding the suite-wide flag guard, the final focused selection passes **21 tests on each runtime**. This includes the new flag regression and the real scheduler's exclusive barrier, join, and disposal behavior. Full-file wall times were 288.87s on Bun and 355.40s on Node; these existing tooling files exercise subprocesses, complete inventories, and scheduler lifecycle contracts. Final focused wall times were 50.83s on Bun and 39.82s on Node.
- Scoped script/test typechecks, lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Independent Codex review is scoped-clean through P2.
- Application production code: unchanged. Tooling: **+24 / -25 (net -1)**. Tests: **+43 / -3 (net +40)**. Docs: **+7 / -5**. No fork-bug workaround or runtime-only skip.

<details>
<summary>Proof commands</summary>

Use the requested Bun fork, short temporary directory, and explicit runtime selection:

```sh
export PATH=/private/tmp/oc-bun-fork/bin:$PATH
export TMPDIR=/private/tmp/oc-fullsuite
export OPENCLAW_BUN_PATH=/private/tmp/oc-bun-fork/bin/bun
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun OPENCLAW_VITEST_FS_MODULE_CACHE_PATH=$TMPDIR/regression-bun /usr/bin/time -l pnpm test test/scripts/test-projects.test.ts test/scripts/test-projects-build-admission.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node OPENCLAW_VITEST_FS_MODULE_CACHE_PATH=$TMPDIR/regression-node /usr/bin/time -l pnpm test test/scripts/test-projects.test.ts test/scripts/test-projects-build-admission.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
# Final flag-guard selection, repeated with each runtime:
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun /usr/bin/time -l pnpm test test/scripts/test-projects.test.ts test/scripts/test-projects-build-admission.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'full-suite|real Gateway plan barrier|suite-wide sharding'
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node OPENCLAW_VITEST_FS_MODULE_CACHE_PATH=$TMPDIR/regression-node /usr/bin/time -l pnpm test test/scripts/test-projects.test.ts test/scripts/test-projects-build-admission.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'full-suite|real Gateway plan barrier|suite-wide sharding'
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.scripts.json scripts/test-projects-run.mts scripts/test-projects.test-support.mts
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.json test/scripts/test-projects.test.ts test/scripts/test-projects-build-admission.test.ts
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.scripts.json --incremental
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.scripts.json --incremental
pnpm exec oxfmt --check scripts/test-projects-run.mts scripts/test-projects.test-support.mts test/scripts/test-projects.test.ts test/scripts/test-projects-build-admission.test.ts docs/help/testing/suites.md
git diff --check
```

The warm benchmark runs these three configs with the same sixteen-file include inventory, `OPENCLAW_TEST_PROJECTS_PARALLEL=4` (clamped to three plans), and `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun`. The baseline adds `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1`, reproducing the old allocation; the final run unsets that override and `OPENCLAW_TEST_WORKERS`:

```sh
/usr/bin/time -l pnpm test test/vitest/vitest.gateway-core.config.ts test/vitest/vitest.gateway-database-workers.config.ts test/vitest/vitest.gateway-server.config.ts
```

Save the following inventory as `benchmark-includes.json` and set `OPENCLAW_VITEST_INCLUDE_FILE` to its absolute path. It contains four Gateway core files, six native database-owner files, and six Gateway HTTP/server files:

```json
["src/gateway/active-sessions-shutdown-tracker.test.ts", "src/gateway/agent-list.test.ts", "src/gateway/agent-prompt.test.ts", "src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-admission-controller.test.ts", "src/gateway/agent-runtime-identity-token.test.ts", "src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-run-execution-phase.owner.test.ts", "src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-run-media.test.ts", "src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-run-settle-continuation.native.test.ts", "src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-session-preparation.worker.test.ts", "src/gateway/approval-fixture.test.ts", "src/gateway/embeddings-http.test.ts", "src/gateway/gateway-codex-harness.app-server-args.test.ts", "src/gateway/models-http.test.ts", "src/gateway/openai-compatible-archived-session.server.test.ts", "src/gateway/openai-compatible-http.server.usage.test.ts", "src/gateway/openai-http.test.ts"]
```

prs.title: refactor: deslop agent harnesses, channel plugins and packages (wave-6 bundle A)
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agent harnesses, channel plugins, and internal packages repeat inspections of facts already prepared by their owning boundary and retain duplicate adapters or bookkeeping.

## User Impact

No intended change to supported user flows, public SDK/config/protocol shapes, stored data, permissions, or write settlement. External input validation and live authority at effects remain. This is an explicitly requested maintainer cleanup bundle; Phase E memory mechanisms and tests are retained, and there is no changelog change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three independently prepared wave-6 lanes are assembled on current main:

- **z08 — harnesses:** consume parsed config and projected native facts, consolidate MCP pagination and Computer Use artifact ownership, remove duplicate transcript and adapter work across Codex, Copilot, ACPX, migrations, Agents API, and Muse. Main's newer catalog/receipt/projection implementations win over conflicting older hunks; the existing client method remains the identity owner.
- **z10 — channels:** use SDK/transport/producer owners across channel group B, including Teams reference clients, Nextcloud signed requests, Tlon pokes, SMS pre-persistence media admission, current-host contracts, and native request deadlines. No message-content logging is added. The lane's separately landed LINE privacy and ClickClack activity fixes are already in main, not duplicated here.
- **z13 — packages (deferred under rule 8):** assembled and reviewed with the bundle, then restored completely to main after the Synology cleanup failure remained unsettled. The failed test reaches the shared package graph; source, related tests, and retired files were restored together rather than retaining an unproved partial cutover. These package simplifications are not part of the final diff.

Combined whole-diff reduction against integrated main `e4a0517cc2f`: **762 lines removed net** (+1,608 / -2,370 across 266 files). The artifact module relocates an existing owner rather than adding state. Hunks already absorbed or rewritten on main and the rule-8-restored package changes are not counted again.

Codex-backed adapters were personally checked against the native source contracts cited in the lane evidence, including thread/page/status and MCP schemas, dynamic-tool output, initialize identity, and completion envelopes. Native authority and receiver/envelope checks remain.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Typed internal handoffs are borrowed read-only. Malformed untyped internal callers may fail instead of being silently normalized; external network/config/file/persisted input remains validated. Internal consumers must not mutate handed-off declarations, tags, buffers, identity, or action facts. Teams pending-upload storage retains main's point-read fallback and buffer ownership.
- A malformed newly supplied Codex plugin snapshot may fail otherwise config-independent non-help commands until corrected/reloaded; help, empty-picker, policy, and usage exits stay early. Unsupported parallel initialization on one physical client may show older diagnostics, without changing native execution. Computer Use discovery inherits the existing repeated-cursor/100-page bound rather than paging forever.
- Invalid process clocks can produce best-effort cache or fallback-timestamp behavior until restart. Real TTLs, external timestamps, quota/refill, account authority, and capacity remain protected.
- Concurrent ClickClack discussion metadata edits may briefly show the earlier label before normal reconciliation; binding commit still checks current session/account authority. Failed Feishu Bitable batch cleanup leaves placeholders and reports a truthful zero cleanup count instead of replaying deletions. Tlon installs raw settings and derived policy together rather than partially updating before an injected throwing logger.
- LINE sends use the existing target parser: documented prefixes and case-sensitive real-ID checks remain; malformed multiply nested prefixes no longer have a separate send-only meaning. Native timeout error text/type may differ while exact budgets, accepted/rejected/indeterminate handling, and pre-connect-only retry policy remain.

## Evidence

**Final exact-head PR CI is green:** run **38838042570** on `78cca0a27e1df93491f20ca9f1666ebd49b726bc` completed all **93 jobs** with no failures. The previously failing Codex changed-extension shard and UI test-type stripe both passed. The exact-head watcher returned GREEN; older same-lane failed runs are superseded evidence, not current failures. No CI rerun or inherited-failure exception is used. Final correction types, format, focused lint, whitespace, and fresh independent Keychain review passed. Its bounded local runtime attempt was stopped after 334 seconds of worker preparation and subsequent setup without a case result; the hosted shard supplies runtime proof instead. Historical failures and deferred scope below remain disclosed, not relabeled green.

Exact-head run **38835804345** on `083b93d7e58` completed with two non-aggregate failures. `check-test-types-core-3` reported an undeclared `render` in the UI model-catalog test, outside this bundle; main's `56c315156f4` removes precisely that stale Lit cleanup. `checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-2-1` failed the Codex one-shot host-tool ownership case before `thread/start`: its five-second polling bound and attempt clock included cold startup. The correction freezes that unrelated clock (as the neighboring cleanup case already does), observes thread creation directly, and uses the existing harness turn-acceptance receipt before completion. Exact host-tool/config/terminal assertions remain. Independent Keychain-route review caught dispatch-versus-acceptance ordering in the initial correction; the final correction fixes it and returned scoped-clean P0–P2. This is a test-only repair, not a timeout increase, production deadline change, or CI rerun. New exact-head CI is still required; the old run is not green.

Latest reconciliation `083b93d7e58` integrates main `e4a0517cc2f` after GitHub reported a real new conflict. Main replaced the old Codex schema materializer with TypeBox's shared-context compiler; the **complete validator file remains byte-identical to main**, and the obsolete bundle hunks are dropped. Overlapping model/config/artifact/mock changes were personally inspected, and main's one-shot cleanup guard and model admission remain intact. A fresh full-bundle Keychain-route review against this main base returned scoped-clean (P0–P2), and the full extension test-type graph, six-file format/focused lint, whitespace and exact-main-input checks passed. The focused validator/model runtime attempt was stopped in compiled-subprocess preparation without cases before checkout identity changed. New exact-head PR CI is required; the older CI table below is historical evidence only until refreshed for this head.

Rule-8 follow-through in `47777f82f97`: exact-head PR run 38828635628 failed only `checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-5`, with a 180-second global `afterAll` cleanup timeout in the Synology outbound-media file (not an assertion failure). The bounded serial replay attempt remained in compiled-subprocess preparation without cases, and the isolated baseline checkout did not finish; both were stopped, with no passing or inherited claim. The Synology outbound-media source and all package changes reachable through its test/setup graph were therefore restored byte-identically to main, including associated tests and the retired event-listener file. The separate wider validation exposed an unused private Codex status-type export after the catalog cutover; that export is removed while the local type and wire shape remain. Fresh Keychain-route correction review returned scoped-clean (P0–P2), the full extension test-type graph, focused syntax lint/format and whitespace checks passed, and exact source restoration was verified against main.

Prior-head PR CI run **38832005632**, attempt 1 on `47777f82f97`, completed with one non-aggregate failure; all other jobs passed or were intentionally skipped. Production/test type graphs, extension lint, architectural guards, import cycles, boundaries, and independent `security-fast` passed. This historical red is retained transparently, not described as current-head proof or green. Any native exception must be requalified against the new exact failed head/run/actual checkout:

| Failed check | Observed failure and attribution |
| --- | --- |
| `checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-3-1` — job 116753580905 | The same Synology outbound-media global cleanup hook exceeded 180 seconds at `test/setup.extensions.ts:82`. CI's automatic table says **unknown**, because scheduled main run 38823827091 has no same-named job. Independent source qualification uses the **actual CI checkout** `4b5ff6d9743`, whose ordered parents are baseline `86118fa4f87` and this exact PR head. Its complete `src`, `packages`, and `test` trees, manifests/lock, and all local Synology outbound-media dependencies are byte-identical to baseline. The remaining Synology account-normalization hunk is not imported by this test, which constructs account literals and supplies its own runtime. The reachable bundle deltas were fully restored before this unchanged-input timeout recurred. This is an inherited cleanup failure, not a demonstrated teardown fix or passing replay. |
| `openclaw/ci-gate` — job 116756534725 | Aggregate failure caused solely by the above job. `security-fast` passed independently. |

Hosted SDK API job 116744788059 in run 38829426223 passed against exact base `012bb1ccaf0` and head `c742b8ecfb4`. Its uploaded declaration report contains no added/removed entrypoints or changed exported signatures; 157 reachable-closure entries trace to one additive internal compaction constant, which the package restoration removes. Other failures in that wider manual run are not green or inherited claims: missing Swedish translation memory, untouched UI/file-transfer dead-code reports, missing `rg` in native-Git fixtures, and a session-reader physical-owner mismatch. The final PR run must be evaluated independently.

Main advanced after exact-head CI run 38824730471 passed on `1cae53944ce`. Conflict repair `c742b8ecfb4` integrates main `012bb1ccaf0`. The one conflict was the Computer Use artifact relocation: main's shared candidate resolver remains authoritative, the obsolete relocated duplicate is removed, and main's desktop fingerprint and explicit-refresh inputs are forwarded unchanged. The existing entry-point cache test now asserts both inputs. A fresh independent Keychain-route reconciliation review returned scoped-clean (no P0–P2 findings); full extension test types, formatting, focused syntax lint, and whitespace checks passed. Local conflict-owner tests were interrupted in preparation without case results. The obsolete pre-repair SDK report dispatch 38827284204 was cancelled and confirmed completed/cancelled; it supplies no current-head API evidence.

Frozen-lockfile/prefer-offline install completed once. All touched production type graphs, the corrected full extension test-type graph, syntax lint/format, lint-suppressions (3/3), and diff whitespace checks passed. Independent Keychain-route review completed both full-bundle passes and found one actionable issue: an optional Teams bulk-read method had become required. The complete affected file was restored byte-identically to main, preserving its point-read fallback and buffer ownership, together with legacy-read test coverage. Two focused reconciliation reviews then returned scoped-clean, including the final correction batch. Exact-head PR CI is the broad proof; no CI reruns for green.

Initial exact-head CI run 38819202790 completed with 88 successful jobs and 11 failed non-aggregate jobs. The failures exposed catalog/Teams fixture contract drift, stale undefined-versus-parsed-config spy expectations, literal-widened test configs, incomplete module mocks, and two unused suppressions. The corrections preserve behavioral assertions, supply the real client/SDK contracts, strictly shrink obsolete mock/max-lines baseline entries, and remove the unused directives. An unchanged catalog projection fixture also exceeded main's existing 8 MiB admission cap; it now remains multi-megabyte (5,448,810 bytes), retaining all projection/ordinary-response assertions and the separate oversized-frame rejection case. The cap itself is unchanged. Run 38822368576 exposed two further nested mock omissions, one remaining stale expectation, and two stale max-lines entries; these are corrected and independently reviewed in head 1cae53944ce. New-head CI supplies broad proof, not reruns of failed heads.

Disclosed lane gaps are not passing claims: Copilot's 120-second timed-out-compaction reuse case reproduced on the lane's pinned clean base and head; earlier Agents API binding-before-deletion persistence failures were unresolved. The bundle's Copilot attempt hit the native no-output preparation watchdog before cases; conflict-owner, Mattermost, and local corrected-runtime batches were interrupted without case results on an overloaded host. The Mattermost loopback alias was independently confirmed unavailable (EADDRNOTAVAIL); its unchanged backfill authorization deadline gap remains disclosed. Local runtime cycles were interrupted without a result, so Madge did not execute. Full local type-aware extension lint previously timed out in declaration preparation. The local SDK API comparison was interrupted after prolonged rendering; its pre-reconciliation head is not exact-final-head proof. An immediately granted Blacksmith Testbox attempt stalled in local source preparation before payload execution; the lease was stopped and independently confirmed completed, with no remote test result claimed. Incomplete checks are not reported green; hosted failures follow changed-path repair/one serial replay/complete reachable-file restoration, or the native inherited-only failure-table exception.

Credit: wave-6 lanes **z08**, **z10**, and **z13**, with source commits `9b3fc5f8687`, `009c558937f`, and `d12022b40ca` respectively. This bundle preserves their coherent owner cutovers and accepted tradeoffs while dropping hunks already rewritten on main.
