prs.title: refactor(auto-reply): simplify runtime bookkeeping
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Reply admission had accumulated a second ownership system around the actual session, database and delivery owners: transitive rotation histories, per-database barrier source maps, physical-file capture handoffs, and an in-memory generation-fenced compatibility proxy. These mechanisms mainly reconstructed transient interleavings; they were not the owners of security policy or durable writes.

## Changes

Use an ordered walk over captured predecessor operations plus the authoritative session row for compaction continuation, including consecutive observed compactions. Keep ordinary settlement promises, but remove the lineage snapshots, source merging and alias-source updates around them. Let the existing session facts owner select the event destination rather than maintaining an additional physical-source capture protocol. Use one backing session-entry store instead of generation/timestamp arbitration and a Proxy. Combine aggregate source cancellation with AbortSignal.any rather than transferring controller/listener ownership at adoption.

Keep current tool/send policy at security effects, physical database admission, durable input and output, FIFO, ordinary shutdown settlement and the standalone session-memory backend unchanged. The finalization watchdog stays: human report #106112 documents repeated Slack production wedges. Human-backed stale drain recovery (#130810) and durable ingress dedupe recovery (#139341) also stay.

Production delta against base 164e243f909b8456f56918ba68dfcc927f7e520d: 109 added, 732 deleted, **623 net lines removed**. Test/support reductions are separate and remove only pins for the retired interleavings; normal compaction, wrong-store rejection, policy downgrade, cancellation, durable alias settlement and restart tests remain.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- A turn that enters, compacts and exits entirely during an unobserved admission await can now produce the existing retry error instead of reconstructing its transitive lineage. #152958/#156858 document controlled races and a CI failure, not a human incident; ordinary captured-predecessor compaction still works.
- A recovery-runtime object replacement during an await may finish through the captured runtime. The extra identity fence came from architectural coordination work (#138451 and follow-ups), with no human report for runtime replacement; ordinary restart cancellation still owns shutdown.
- Placement is sampled once after the preparatory row read, without reread loops or a service hot-replacement protocol. #172458 explicitly describes task-only scheduling checkpoints, not a historical deployment incident; preparation and the authoritative session/owner check remain once, and execution owns its actual claim.
- Physical event storage appearing or being replaced between initial capture and canonical preparation is no longer rejected merely for differing from that capture. #167113/#167629 describe design and synthetic capture handoffs, with no human incident; the canonical facts owner still validates its selected source and live effect policy.
- Config store remapping or a process event-generation rotation alone does not revoke accepted background bookkeeping. #167113 cites design/synthetic evidence for these fences. Normal restart already cancels and joins producers (including supervised exec) before reboot; a bare epoch rotation without shutdown is synthetic. Captured destinations remain fixed, ordinary cancellation still stops work, and final tool/delivery policy still refuses revoked authority.
- In-memory session replacement or timestamp races no longer arbitrate competing cache generations or abort compaction notices. #117145 describes consolidation and synthetic differential transitions, not a human incident. Explicit compaction publications update the single backing store; notices still read current send policy at their effects.
- An older aggregate source signal remains connected after adoption and can cancel the whole batch. #100123 added the two-phase cancellation handoff without a human report of that handoff failure; all sources retain cancellation before durable input writes and normal cancellation identities are still retired.
- A completed operation's delayed callback reports its own session, not a later operation's rotated session through per-store lineage metadata. #138451 introduced that transfer with architectural/synthetic proof, not a cited human incident; actual delivery and owner settlement still finish before the callback.
- Explicitly rebinding the same operation to another store during a held preparation read no longer drives a second observation/re-admission protocol. #155982's forced rebind keeps the original physical claim current; actual claim retirement and security effect checks remain.
- Completing an observed predecessor after a recovery claim commits no longer cancels otherwise-valid ownership solely because registry observation changed. #155982's held-return fixture is synthetic; the admitted claim remains owned and normally released.
- A failed preparatory reader reports its own error, without rerunning a lifecycle assertion to replace its classification. #172458 documents task-only scheduling checkpoints, not a human incident; refusal still publishes no entry and changes no durable row.

## Evidence

- Initial published cut passed core typecheck, scoped lint, formatting, diff whitespace, runtime import cycles (0), madge cycles (0), and isolated review through P2. The final five-file CI repair separately passed fresh isolated P2 review (scoped-clean), targeted core typecheck, supported source-backed scoped lint, and formatting/whitespace.
- Executed lint-suppression guard: baseline failure for the unchanged `src/infra/sqlite-worker-store.test-support.ts|typescript/unbound-method|1` entry introduced by #173239. Both that file and the expected allowlist are unchanged from the base; no suppression or allowlist entry was added here.
- Executed changed-file checks: conflict markers, line-cap growth, max-lines suppressions and assertion safety passed. The environment-name budget fails at 452 against 453; the exact baseline-index owner replay reproduces it. This diff changes no environment variable name. No full changed-check success is claimed.
- The first test command stopped at that tooling guard before reaching auto-reply. Its separate earlier 16-file replay had passing session-event permission/background-completion cases but was superseded by the repair. The final frozen seven-file replay passed all seven Gateway compaction-handoff cases, including consecutive observed compactions. After hosted CI passed, the optional remaining local infra stage was stopped and its task-owned children joined; it reported no assertions and is not claimed passing. No load-only delay is classified as a product failure.

Exact-head hosted CI run [38806369139](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38806369139) is GREEN for repaired head 310724cecfab3828ce9f48f890f5d904ef1b99c7, including openclaw/ci-gate. No inherited-red exception is used. Local load-only delays are not product failures. No timeouts, retries, skips, suppressions, schemas, dependencies, config keys or public protocol shapes were added or weakened.

### First-head CI attribution

Run 38801516200 on 7a56590b035d76b95fc1a28514a408fe471aec12 completed with six failing test jobs. `checks-node-changed-compact-small-7` exposed storeless successor selection; `checks-node-changed-compact-large-20` exposed the observed consecutive-compaction chain. Both are repaired in production, with their tests unchanged. `small-20`, `large-4`, `small-22`, and `large-12` exposed the retired store-rebind observation, cross-operation callback lineage, reader-error rewrapping and held recovery-claim observation pins described above; only those pins were retired or updated, preserving refusal/no-write, physical authority and settlement coverage. `openclaw/ci-gate` reported these failures; none is classified inherited. The separate PR-context failure required authored section headings, now corrected. No CI job was rerun.

prs.body:
Closes #108216

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users selecting Bedrock Mantle GPT-5.4, GPT-5.5, or GPT-5.6 models would send requests to the generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint instead of Mantle's required Responses endpoint.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Bedrock Mantle plugin now gives the documented GPT-5.4/5.5/5.6 model IDs explicit `openai-responses` routing and the `/openai/v1` base path. Other discovered OpenAI models retain the plugin's existing default route.

AWS documents this Responses-only compatibility and endpoint shape in:

- https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/models-api-compatibility.html
- https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-card-openai-gpt-54.html
- https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-card-openai-gpt-55.html
- https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-card-openai-gpt-56-sol.html
- https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/get-started-with-openai-gpt-5-6-sol-terra-and-luna-on-amazon-bedrock/

## User Impact

Users can configure the supported Bedrock Mantle GPT-5.4/5.5/5.6 models without the endpoint mismatch that previously prevented the intended request flow.

## Evidence

- Added focused discovery assertions for all five documented IDs and a generic OpenAI control model.
- Rebased onto current `main`; the PR is mergeable without conflicts.

prs.title: refactor(gateway): remove reload debt and startup claims
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway startup and config reload carry overlapping reservation, proxy-owner, and restart-debt state for unsupported internal interleavings.

## User Impact

Normal startup, reload, credential checks, active-work draining, and shutdown remain. Failed restart delivery still reports recovery guidance and an explicit reapply uses the current config and secrets; an unrelated later edit no longer automatically rearms a rejected restart. No config keys, protocol fields, database shapes, dependencies, or protected standalone session-memory behavior change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing Gateway/plugin service owners directly. Remove startup reservation claims and discovery claim replay, the duplicate startup service proxy, restart-generation bookkeeping, accepted-target custody, and paused/conservative restart-debt transfer. Keep one selected restart operation with checks at policy publication and signal emission. Keep public applied-config revision reporting, discovery FIFO, service cleanup, current-secret preparation, authorization boundaries, and ordinary write-capable shutdown settlement.

The real Discord cleanup outage recorded in #150953 remains covered by the separate failed-drain recovery/readiness path; this PR does not remove it.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Forced plugin reload during deferred startup can publish startup state late. Introducing #126627 explicitly says public operator startup admission prevents this window; its regression forces the internal interleaving. A restart recovers the unsupported case.
- Stopping/replacing startup exactly during the lazy service import no longer uses a proxy handle and second deadline wrapper. #124309 introduced it from synthetic lifecycle/scanner findings, not a human actual-use report. Startup producers still join shutdown, and the actual service owner publishes its cleanup handle before starting services.
- Rejected restart work is not transferred/rearmed across later unrelated config edits. Debt originated in #107577 while implementing applied-config revision reporting (#107216); no cited human incident supports debt transfer. Errors remain visible; correct the failure and reapply config or restart manually.
- A superseded reload tail failure warns instead of acquiring an accepted successor target and carrying conservative restart debt. #105289's linked #103736 demonstrates a forced handler window with stubbed channels, not an actual-use debt-transfer incident. Coherent config/secrets/subsystem publication and shutdown joining remain.
- Replaced request counters are unnecessary: the selected operation itself is checked immediately before publishing restart policy and emitting the signal. No credential or approval effect check is removed.

## Evidence

Candidate base: `62d5fd5092fbf212bbc7608f3eac418980690f43`.

Production delta after CI repairs: 175 added / 756 deleted, **581 net lines removed** across 16 production files, excluding tests/support/generated/declarations. Removed tests pin only the retired claims/proxy/debt mechanisms; ordinary startup, secret/policy checks, actual cleanup/recovery, and shutdown coverage remain.

Passed: core TSGo (356.86 s); runtime cycles 0; Madge cycles 0 (581.45 s); changed Gateway format (25 files); targeted corrected lint (318.70 s); independent review through P2 scoped-clean; lint-suppressions and gateway-bench-runtime tests (2 files/15 tests); exact env budget shrink (452/452).

Assertion baseline shrink also passed (2666 files, 6165 grandfathered assertions; 613.00 s). Changed test-graph types passed (1931.46 s). Repair-only independent review through P2 is scoped-clean; repair lint passed (482.46 s). Focused repair proof passed all 3 lint-suppression tests and 24 Gateway cases before a supervised-child test timeout and subsequent model-refresh hook timeouts. The command was intentionally interrupted after 3435.91 s, ended exit 2, and is not a completed pass. Its retained resource namespace was preserved. No timeout attribution or inherited-failure claim is made from that run. Remaining composite check-changed gates are running. The composite saw old env/assertion allowances before their shrink fixes; both corrected gates passed independently, and the composite has not been represented as green.

The earlier local supervised-child/lazy-cron replay was incomplete; it is not a passing or inherited-failure result. Exact published-head CI subsequently passed that named regression in 8845 ms. prs.title: fix(agents): preserve whitespace in node-host exec workdir paths
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Running a `system.run` command on a node host with a `workdir` whose name legitimately ends in whitespace (e.g. `/srv/data `) silently executed the command in a different directory (`/srv/data`). On Unix, leading/trailing whitespace is a valid part of a directory name, so the agent accepted the value but the execution host trimmed it before spawning, producing a silent-success in the wrong directory.

- **Problem:** The node-host workdir flowed through `normalizeXxxString` calls that trim leading/trailing whitespace. The shared plan normalizer, approval binding, and approval context resolvers also trimmed cwd, so a preserved-whitespace value from `resolveExecWorkdir` was re-trimmed before reaching `child_process.spawn`'s `options.cwd`, and the plan-match check broke for whitespace-bearing paths. Two downstream sites also re-trimmed: `resolveExecutablePathCandidate` (relative executable and PATH lookup) and `collectAllowAlwaysPatterns` (reusable shell-script grant hashing).
- **Solution:** Switch all cwd read sites on the node-execution path to `readNonBlankString`, which preserves original whitespace while still rejecting blank values. Extend the same fix to `resolveExecutablePathCandidate`/`resolveExecutableFromPathEnv` and `collectAllowAlwaysPatterns` so the prepare→approve→run chain is consistent end to end.
- **What changed:**
  - `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-workdir.ts` — node branch reads `params.workdir` / `params.nodeCwd` via `readNonBlankString`.
  - `src/node-host/invoke-system-run-plan.ts` — `buildSystemRunApprovalPlan` reads `params.cwd` via `readNonBlankString`.
  - `src/node-host/invoke-system-run.ts` — `parseSystemRunPhase` reads `opts.params.cwd` via `readNonBlankString`; plan-match compares `approvalPlan.cwd === cwd` directly.
  - `src/infra/system-run-approval-plan.ts` — `normalizeSystemRunApprovalPlan` reads `candidate.cwd` via `readNonBlankString`.
  - `src/infra/system-run-approval-binding.ts` — `buildSystemRunApprovalBinding` reads `params.cwd` via `readNonBlankString`.
  - `src/infra/system-run-approval-context.ts` — approval context resolvers read cwd via `readNonBlankString`.
  - `src/infra/system-run-normalize.ts` — re-exports `readNonBlankString`.
  - `src/infra/executable-path.ts` — `resolveExecutablePathCandidate` and `resolveExecutableFromPathEnv` use the original cwd value (not trimmed) when non-blank.
  - `src/infra/exec-approvals-allowlist.ts` — `collectAllowAlwaysPatterns` uses the original cwd value (not trimmed) for grant hashing.

## Why This Change Was Made

Fixing only the cwd read sites was cancelled out by downstream trimming. The relative executable lookup trimmed cwd before pinning `./tool`, mixing the sibling's executable with the requested directory. The reusable shell-script grant hash trimmed cwd, scoping persisted authorization to the wrong directory — a security concern where approval for `/srv/data` could authorize execution in `/srv/data ` or vice versa.

## User Impact

Agents and operators can now run commands on a node host whose working directory name contains leading or trailing whitespace, and the command executes in the intended directory. Relative executables resolve from the correct directory. Approval bindings and reusable script grants distinguish whitespace-distinct paths, preventing cross-directory approval reuse. Non-whitespace paths are unaffected.

## Evidence

### Gateway-level proof (running Gateway kernel + real `child_process.spawn`)

REAL Gateway kernel (`createGatewayKernel`) + REAL `NodeRegistry` + `nodeRegistry.invoke()` → `handleInvoke` → `handleSystemRunInvoke` → `runCommand` (real `child_process.spawn`). Two sibling dirs `data ` and `data`, each containing a `marker` file. All scenarios exercise the **production launch owner**.

Config: `security: "allowlist"`, `ask: "off"`. Grants created via production `resolveAllowAlwaysPatternEntries` + `saveExecApprovals`.

| Scenario | Before (main) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Authorized spawn in `data ` (grant for `data `) | `allowlist miss` ❌ (grant trimmed) | `ok: true`, stdout: `from-space-dir` ✅ |
| 2. Sibling grant rejected (grant for `data`, launch in `data `) | `ok: true` ❌ (cross-dir reuse) | `allowlist miss` ✅ (rejected) |
| 3. Revocation prevents spawn (grant → ok → revoke → denied) | always `miss` ❌ | `ok: true` → `ok: false` ✅ |
| 4. Plan-match rejects mismatched cwd (plan for `data `, cwd `data`) | `ok: true` ❌ (both trimmed) | `explicit approval requires matching systemRunPlan` ✅ |
| 5. Gateway record→replay→launch (`system.run.prepare` → serialize → `system.run`) | plan cwd trimmed ❌ | plan cwd preserved, spawn ok ✅ |

RED on main: all 5 fail. GREEN after fix: all 5 pass. Scenario 5 exercises the full Gateway flow: `system.run.prepare` creates a plan via `handleInvoke`, the plan is JSON-serialized (simulating WS transport), then replayed through `system.run` via `normalizeSystemRunApprovalPlan` inside `parseSystemRunPhase`.

### Data-model compatibility + upgrade proof (v2026.10.3 → candidate)

| Scenario | Before (main) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| Plan cwd after creation | `"data"` ❌ (trimmed) | `"data "` ✅ (preserved) |
| Plan cwd after serialize→replay | `"data"` ❌ (trimmed) | `"data "` ✅ (preserved) |
| Pre-upgrade grant for `data` still works | `true` ✅ | `true` ✅ |
| Pre-upgrade grant for `data` not cross-reusable with `data ` | `false` ❌ (identical hash) | `true` ✅ (distinct hash) |
| v2026.10.3 grants survive `normalizeExecApprovals` upgrade | — | hash unchanged ✅ |
| Ws-distinct cwd grant hash distinct after upgrade | — | distinct ✅ |

Non-ws cwd grants produce identical hashes before and after fix (`.trim()` is a no-op for non-ws paths), so existing stored grants remain valid.

### Regression tests

```
src/infra/exec-approvals-allow-always.test.ts: 44 passed
src/infra/executable-path.test.ts: 34 passed | 2 skipped
src/node-host/invoke-system-run-plan.test.ts: 25 passed
src/infra/system-run-approval-binding.test.ts: 33 passed
```

prs.title: fix(anthropic-vertex): bound googleAuthFetch requests with AbortController timeout
prs.body:
### What Problem This Solves

`googleAuthFetch` is used by `google-auth-library` as the HTTP transport for OAuth token requests (`https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token`). The old implementation had no AbortController, no timeout, and no `connectTimeout` on `EnvHttpProxyAgent` — a hung or unresponsive OAuth endpoint would block the request indefinitely, stalling the entire Vertex AI stream.

### Why This Change Was Made

Without timeout protection, any transient network issue between the OpenClaw process and Google's OAuth infrastructure can permanently block the stream. The `googleAuthFetch` wrapper is the single entry point for all Google Auth HTTP calls in the Anthropic Vertex provider, so adding timeout there covers the widest surface with the smallest change.

### User Impact

- Hung OAuth token requests now abort after 30s instead of hanging forever
- TCP connect timeouts after 10s when the proxy is unreachable
- Callers can cancel pending auth requests via `AbortSignal`

### Evidence

**Real terminal proof — both automatic timeout paths (redacted live output):**

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/anthropic-vertex/proof-timeout-paths.test.ts --reporter=verbose

  [PROOF-10s] EnvHttpProxyAgent({ connectTimeout: 10_000 }) (direct)
  [PROOF-10s] Proxy: http://198.51.100.1:3128 (silent-drop SYN)
  [PROOF-10s] Request started at 2026-07-20T07:09:35.365Z
  [PROOF-10s] Waiting for proxy connect timeout...
  [PROOF-10s] ✓ Rejected in 10527ms
  [PROOF-10s] ✓ Error: fetch failed
  [PROOF-10s] ✓ Cause: Connect Timeout Error
                  (attempted address: 198.51.100.1:3128, timeout: 10000ms)

  [PROOF-30s] Hanging server at 127.0.0.1:40029
  [PROOF-30s] GOOGLE_AUTH_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000
  [PROOF-30s] Request started at  2026-07-20T07:09:46.027Z
  [PROOF-30s] Waiting for automatic 30s timeout...
  [PROOF-30s] ✓ Rejected in 30008ms
  [PROOF-30s] ✓ Error: This operation was aborted

  [PROOF-cleanup] Request 1: HTTP 200 in 16ms
  [PROOF-cleanup] Request 2: HTTP 200 in 7ms
  [PROOF-cleanup] Request 3: HTTP 200 in 3ms
  [PROOF-cleanup] Request 4: HTTP 200 in 4ms
  [PROOF-cleanup] Request 5: HTTP 200 in 3ms
  [PROOF-cleanup] Shared signal not aborted: true

 ✓ googleAuthFetch real timeout proof > 10s proxy connect timeout 10661ms
 ✓ googleAuthFetch real timeout proof > 30s automatic request timeout 30018ms
 ✓ googleAuthFetch real timeout proof > Listener cleanup 40ms
```

**Listener lifecycle fix (ClawSweeper P2).**  The original code used an anonymous `() => controller.abort()` listener — no reference, so it could never be removed.  A long-lived shared caller signal would accumulate one listener per completed request, preventing GC of old controller/signal pairs.

Fix: name the listener as `onAbort`, register with `addEventListener("abort", onAbort, { once: true })`, and remove in `finally` via `init?.signal?.removeEventListener("abort", onAbort)`.  The regression test (above, 5 rapid requests on one shared signal) proves no listener leak.

**CI fix (checks-node-changed).**  The earlier proxy test stubs `HTTP_PROXY` and creates the `EnvHttpProxyAgent` singleton with a proxy.  After unstubbing, the singleton still routes through the now-dead proxy for any host not in `NO_PROXY`.  Set `NO_PROXY=127.0.0.1` before the timeout/abort tests so local test servers are reached directly regardless of CI environment.

**Full suite**: 7 test files, 68 tests — all passed.
```
 Test Files  7 passed (7)
      Tests  68 passed (68)
```

**Code quality**:
- `oxlint`: 0 issues
- `tsgo` (ext tsconfig): 0 errors
- File diff: +56/-4 lines across 2 files

**Files**:
- `extensions/anthropic-vertex/stream-runtime.ts` — `googleAuthFetch` with AbortController, connectTimeout, and named listener cleanup
- `extensions/anthropic-vertex/stream-runtime.test.ts` — 4 tests in `googleAuthFetch timeout and abort` describe block (pre-abort, mid-request abort, normal success, shared-signal regression)

prs.title: fix(cli): cron show crashes when a job row omits its state
prs.body:
Closes #173631

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw cron show <id>` crashes with a `TypeError` when a cron job row omits its `state` object, while `openclaw cron list` already renders the same row without crashing.

## User Impact

User impact: operators can now inspect any job with `cron show`, including version-skewed or malformed rows that lack a `state` object, instead of the command dying with `Cannot read properties of undefined` (matching `cron list` tolerance). No changes to stored data or job behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

`printCronShow` (`src/cli/cron-cli/shared.ts`) dereferences `job.state.nextRunAtMs`, `job.state.lastError`, `job.state.streamStatus`, etc. directly. Its sibling `printCronList` guards the same access with `const state = job.state ?? {}` and has an explicit "tolerates malformed rows in human-readable output" test that passes `state: undefined`. `show` was the only renderer in the file without the guard, so a single malformed row made the whole command crash. This change applies the same `job.state ?? {}` guard and additionally uses optional chaining on `job.payload` (matching `printCronList`), so `show` renders what it can instead of throwing.

## Evidence

**Before** — direct call to the shared renderer with a state-less row (job row shape mirrors the existing malformed-row test):

```
LIST OK
SHOW CRASHED: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'triggerEvalCount')
```

**After** — same row renders without crashing:

```
LIST OK
SHOW OK
```

**Regression test** — extended the existing `tolerates malformed rows in human-readable output` test to also run `printCronShow` and assert it renders the row id:

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  56 passed (56)
```

**Lint/format/typecheck** — `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` pass on both changed files; `tsgo:core` reports no new errors for these files (the only failure, `src/tui/tui-session-actions-test-support.ts` `setProgramStatus`, reproduces identically on pristine upstream HEAD with these changes stashed and is an unrelated inherited base-branch error).

prs.title: fix(auth): configured primary account blocks CLI fallback
prs.body:
Closes #158421. Thanks to @HerbertHuerto for the corrected report and @aoclaw-glitch for the per-agent reproduction.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a configured default primary account is treated as an explicit conversation account pin when a fallback uses another CLI provider. A valid destination CLI account is then rejected as belonging to the wrong provider.

## User Impact

Configured Chat and event-triggered fallback attempts select the destination runtime's supported account. Explicit conversation and person-linked account pins remain strict, including changes while a run waits for preparation or placement. Ordinary scheduled jobs retain main's recorded-inference-account and native-account restrictions; this PR does not allow an unbound schedule to acquire an account through fallback.

The public V1 preparation/context types stay source-compatible. The V2 transport context requires the host's current-owner assertion and asynchronous account admission. The bundled Anthropic transport uses V2 for cold startup, initial/warm prompts and injected input. No removal deadline, public option, wire protocol, database schema, permission or dependency change is introduced. SDK/security owner acceptance and exact-head security/fixture approvals remain upstream merge decisions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing auth selection producer records configuration provenance as a runtime-only fact. Provider scoping may drop that configured account when a fallback changes auth scope; it cannot discard a genuine user or user-link pin. Queue/account edits and live model switches retire the earlier configuration fact.

The existing CLI preparation/execution owners re-read current account intent after their waits. Process and paired-node paths use main's existing preparation/current-source operations. Plugin transports receive the same run-bound host operation. Account refusals stop model fallback. Incognito reads use main's captured exact memory actor; durable reads remain worker-owned. Retired SQL-incognito sharing/authority/facts paths and duplicate relay/Node dispatch owners are not restored.

## Evidence

Current maintenance source: f22d9efb43720ffec2f4986f23bfe5049243655d, normal merge of 9e1af72388809b06d9d721b603168eada82ed8dc with exact CI base 679c7b6e4cf8adaca84449419e00f42a6c93fc21. The complete pre-correction tree equals actual tested merge e69489808c78b9396d96657023eb5ce0cdae6fd7 from run 38829410711. The only differences from that CI tree are two test fixtures; production/runtime/config/package inputs are unchanged.

- The current-head CI identified two TS2741 diagnostics in the unchanged Windows transport-close fixture, which had not supplied the newly required current-owner assertion. The complete affected Anthropic test-consumer closure reproduces both errors on 9e in 79.783 seconds. The fixture now explicitly implements ClaudeCliProcessContext with its positively active assertion; production assertion/admission capabilities remain required.
- The other CI failure was main's stale queue-authority expectation: main a5787464af4 / #173452 deliberately connects all collected cancellations through AbortSignal.any. Own 9e still contained the old handoff, so directly applying the new expectation to that older runtime correctly produced a local failure (14 passes / one failure). That attempt is retained and excluded from passing proof. The actual CI base is now integrated, rather than reverting the new owner or masking the failure.
- On that exact integrated runtime, 25 selected regressions pass in 204.553 seconds wrapper: nine actual local Node protocol-process account controls, all 15 queue-authority cases and the mocked Windows close-ordering case. Two existing stored-account orchestration cases also pass in 91.66 seconds, covering both scheduled and event-triggered CLI refusal with zero CLI/embedded dispatch. No new test-only production hook was added.
- The full Anthropic test-consumer graph plus queue authority passes types after integration in 89.936 seconds. Targeted type-aware lint, format, diff and staged line-cap results: both changed fixtures pass type-aware lint (305.598 seconds with SDK boundary preparation, then 24.933 seconds for the queue file); all candidate format/diff/line-cap checks pass.

prs.title: fix(cli,agents,matrix): explain read cursor semantics and add Matrix cursor recovery guidance
prs.body:
Closes #173252

## What Problem This Solves

A Matrix read that passes a message id to `--before`/`--after` fails with a bare homeserver error, and nothing the caller reads tells them those options want a pagination cursor. Now the CLI help, the tool schema, the docs, and the Matrix error all say so.

- Problem: `openclaw message read --help` described `--before <id>`/`--after <id>` as ids, the shared `message` tool schema exposed `before`/`after` as undescribed strings, and the Matrix reader forwards them verbatim as the homeserver `from` pagination token. A caller who follows the help gets `MatrixError: [400] 'from' parameter is invalid` with no hint that the previous read's `nextBatch`/`prevBatch` is the expected value.
- Solution: document channel cursor semantics where callers read them, and translate only that specific Matrix failure into an actionable error that names the rejected cursor and points at `nextBatch`/`prevBatch`.
- What changed: the `read` help text and the shared tool-schema `before`/`after` descriptions, a note in `docs/cli/message.md`, and a narrow Matrix error rewrite in `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/errors.ts` + `actions/messages.ts`.
- What did NOT change: token handling. Cursors are still forwarded verbatim, other channels keep their id/timestamp semantics, and `--around` / `--message-id` are untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

The homeserver is behaving correctly and the Matrix spec defines `from` as a pagination token, so the fix is guidance rather than id-to-cursor conversion. Only a 400 whose message is the homeserver's from-parameter complaint is rewritten; every other Matrix failure propagates unchanged, with the original error preserved as `cause`.

- Best fix: reuse the existing `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/errors.ts` helpers and keep the rewrite at the single point where a caller value becomes `from`.
- Alternative: accept event ids and resolve them to cursors. Rejected: relations/room-history pagination has no defined mapping from an arbitrary event id, and it would change behaviour for other channels.
- Risk / non-goals: the predicate matches Synapse's `'from' parameter is invalid` wording. A homeserver with different phrasing still surfaces its raw error rather than a misleading hint.

## User Impact

Callers who follow the help text are now told what to pass instead of guessing, and the Matrix read error names the rejected cursor. The failed read stays debuggable through the original error on `cause`.

## Evidence

Observed result first: the same cursor is rejected before the fix with a bare homeserver error and after the fix with recovery guidance, while a valid cursor read is unchanged.

| Caller input (real HTTP to a local Matrix-shaped server) | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `after: "t42"` (cursor from a previous read) | page returned, `{"nextBatch":"t999","prevBatch":"t0","messages":1}` | unchanged |
| `after: "$event-id-used-as-a-cursor"` | `MatrixError: [400] 'from' parameter is invalid`, `cause: undefined` | actionable error naming the cursor and `nextBatch`/`prevBatch`, original error on `cause` |
| `before: "$event-id"` on a thread (relations endpoint) | raw 400 | same guidance |
| unrelated 400 / `M_FORBIDDEN` | passthrough | passthrough (unchanged) |

A temporary harness (run with `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs proof-173252.mts`) serves the Synapse 400 payload from a local HTTP server, calls the real `readMatrixMessages`, and builds the thrown error with the real `matrix-js-sdk` `parseErrorResponse`.

```text
# Before the fix
[proof] valid cursor request: GET /_matrix/client/v3/rooms/!proof%3Aexample.org/messages?dir=f&limit=25&from=t42
[proof] valid cursor result: {"nextBatch":"t999","prevBatch":"t0","messages":1}
[proof] invalid cursor request: GET /_matrix/client/v3/rooms/!proof%3Aexample.org/messages?dir=f&limit=25&from=%24event-id-used-as-a-cursor
[proof] invalid cursor error name: M_INVALID_PARAM
[proof] invalid cursor error message: MatrixError: [400] 'from' parameter is invalid
[proof] invalid cursor error cause: undefined

# After the fix
[proof] invalid cursor error name: Error
[proof] invalid cursor error message: Matrix rejected the read cursor "$event-id-used-as-a-cursor" with HTTP 400 ("'from' parameter is invalid"). The before/after options take an opaque pagination token returned by a previous read (nextBatch or prevBatch), not a message or event id. Retry with the nextBatch or prevBatch value from the previous read response.
[proof] invalid cursor error cause: MatrixError: [400] 'from' parameter is invalid
```

```text
pnpm test extensions/matrix/src/matrix/actions/messages.test.ts --maxWorkers=1   # 25 passed
pnpm test extensions/matrix/src/tool-actions.test.ts --maxWorkers=1              # passed
pnpm test src/agents/tools/message-tool-schema.test.ts --maxWorkers=1            # passed
pnpm test src/cli/program/message/register.read-edit-delete.test.ts --maxWorkers=1  # passed
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json                                  # clean
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p <changed tsconfigs>                                 # clean (core, core.test.commands, core.test.agents-tools, extensions.test)
```

What was not tested: no live Matrix homeserver was contacted (the 400 comes from a local server using the exact Synapse payload), and no prebuilt Control UI bundle exists here, so the schema description was verified from the built schema rather than a browser session.

## AI Assistance 🤖

This PR is AI-assisted. Used `grep`, `git diff`, `node --import tsx`, and `vitest` to trace issue #173252 from the CLI help through the tool schema to the Matrix `from` token, then implemented the guidance plus a runtime harness that proves the before/after difference. The implementer understands the code: `before`/`after` become the homeserver `from` pagination token verbatim, so the fix is documentation and a narrowly matched 400 rewrite, not id-to-cursor conversion.

CI keeps all nine release screenshots and their XCTest evidence while using one native capture job. The evidence collector accounts for every image, result bundle, and capture ledger entry before publishing three family manifests in one artifact. The reducer preserves exact source/toolchain provenance, digest checks, complete coverage, and reducer-only retry reuse. It rejects families mixed across capture attempts.

The capture selection, pinned runner tier, Xcode 27.0 build 27A266a, screenshot identities, and final release evidence artifact remain unchanged. Successful runs retain hardware and phase diagnostics. Hosted-row accounting and the CI lane documentation follow the new job.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169493. That PR changes capture selection; this change retains selection and removes duplicated builds.

## Evidence

- Frozen candidate: `48c4fefc6557c081c215affbc39a882a3bdca62c`, integrating main `a9e86934eb289bd0e90bd15834f8a337826bb704` to resolve actual workflow conflicts while preserving its action pins.

The remaining workflow guards passed locally. The final commit changes only the reducer documentation row.

Direct real collector/reducer fixture execution produced nine PNGs and eight XCTest results and passed strict negative controls.
- The single-artifact extraction mismatch found during independent review is fixed: download the exact artifact name into the explicit container path expected by the strict reducer. A receiver-layout regression exercises this path through the real collector and reducer.
- Native capture passed at prior head `d00417658a6a752714fa9ba8af6f9df4aaf115d5`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38830853409. Its capture job completed in 16m21s on Xcode 27.0 build 27A266a. All nine PNG identities and dimensions were verified, and all eight XCTest captures succeeded on their first attempt. Diagnostics record one 266.79s simulator build. Release/upload jobs were skipped.
- That native run remains prior-head evidence. Main integration changed native app and dependency inputs; it does not qualify this candidate or CI's changed artifact download/reducer path.
- The earlier focused Linux run stopped at formatting before running tests: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38835329111. Its three formatting issues were corrected at `31ad`; it is not passing test evidence.

## Review Follow-through

The previous ClawSweeper review's documentation and merge-conflict findings are fixed. Its native-pipeline rank-up move is covered by the pending exact-head CI proof above. The optional workflow-shape test is retained because it guards removal of per-family environment overrides and the capture matrix, plus retention of phase diagnostics; functional evidence comes from the receiver-layout regression, collector/reducer tests, and native CI.

Production changes add 40 net lines relative to the integrated main base, chiefly to give combined capture evidence one complete ownership and validation boundary. Tests add 90 net lines; documentation is line-neutral.

prs.body:
Related: #162675

## What Problem This Solves

The existing auth owner reads reference names before service-env cleanup without activating credentials or modifying source artifacts. Row decoding contains unreadable rows; lifecycle failures propagate with their causes. prs.title: feat(macos): launch the compiled OpenClaw runtime
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The macOS app cannot use the compiled OpenClaw runtime while it packages and launches a loose Bun installation. This cutover makes the compiled executable and its loose resource sidecar the sole packaged runtime.

Builds on merged #172384. **Draft: blocked on native hook-relay #173473 and signed qualification. Standalone invocation/Doctor #173154 and minimal-sidecar builder #172802 have merged.** Separately owned fixes used in the historical signed proof were local only and were not pushed as this PR’s commits. Related: #171489 and #171755.

## User Impact

The app-hosted Gateway, Doctor, terminal CLI, services, and embedded helpers launch the compiled executable. Packaging defaults to JIT; `OPENCLAW_MAC_RUNTIME_MODE=bytecode` selects bytecode. Packaging invokes the builder or accepts `OPENCLAW_MAC_RUNTIME_PREBUILT` only after checking the exact source commit, mode, architecture, production compiler identity, and payload hashes. The canonical signer derives the executable entitlements from the manifest, signs sidecar natives, refreshes hashes, and seals the app.

The builder owns the single `runtime/lib/libsqlite3.dylib`. App staging requires it and no longer builds another SQLite copy. Fresh standalone launches omit `OPENCLAW_SQLITE_LIBRARY`; retained rollback commands preserve their recorded overrides. The packaged verifier denies Homebrew/MacPorts SQLite access and includes selected-library and native vector-store checks; the historical signed campaign did not complete those checks. The verifier now permits the isolated Unix-domain IPC needed by Doctor; signed qualification has not been rerun.

### Update and rollback

Sparkle replaces the app bundle. A fresh or updated app starts its hosted Gateway, Doctor, and setup commands from the signed bundle until this build has a warmed profile copy. After Gateway health, low-priority background work clones the payload, validates manifest identity, contained paths, sizes and executable checksum, and runs `--version` without a short timeout. Only successful warm-up publishes `runtime/current` and the managed terminal wrapper. Service and explicit terminal installation wait for that durable runtime; the running app child keeps its executable until a natural restart.

Quitting cancels and drains warm-up. Failed or interrupted preparation preserves the previous selection and retries next launch, with a visible diagnostic warning on failure. App moves are re-resolved at the next child start. Current, previous, and live-process seeds remain retained; collection cannot remove an unpublished warming generation. Loose-layout seeds and old service commands remain upgrade/rollback inputs. This runtime retention does not roll back databases or user state.

Service installation recognizes the adjacent standalone manifest, probes `<executable> --version`, and writes `<executable> gateway ...` without a script entry. Fresh implicit installation selects the running standalone executable before host Node discovery; explicit runtime selections and saved pins retain precedence. Reinstalling an app-owned service replaces an old Bun-plus-script pin; an older app can reinstall its Bun-plus-script command. Paused-service resume also accepts the validated standalone command and reinstalls it with `--runtime bun --runtime-path <executable>`. Captured commands remain available for recovery. Runtime retention does not roll back database migrations or user state.

### Per-architecture release handoff

Ship separate ARM64 and Intel apps. `BUILD_ARCHS=arm64` or `BUILD_ARCHS=x86_64` selects one architecture and the matching builder manifest; universal/multi-architecture requests fail before building. ARM64 is the target for this campaign. Intel qualification awaits the builder's `--target darwin-x64` support.

The private release workflow must publish separately named arm64/x86_64 ZIPs, DMGs, symbols, and matching Sparkle enclosures. The distribution helper retains its intermediate filenames; the publishing wrapper owns final architecture suffixes. No private workflow is edited here.

Existing universal installs use the shared appcast, so adding two feeds alone does not migrate them. The shared feed must offer the ARM64 item first with `<sparkle:hardwareRequirements>arm64</sparkle:hardwareRequirements>`, then the Intel fallback at the same version. Pinned Sparkle 2.10.0 filters that requirement, recognizes Rosetta as ARM-compatible, and selects the first supported tied-version item ([hardware selection](https://github.com/sparkle-project/Sparkle/blob/eef1a539a373c1f1a320624b1130fc5de7b2e100/Sparkle/SPUAppcastItemStateResolver.m#L127), [item selection](https://github.com/sparkle-project/Sparkle/blob/eef1a539a373c1f1a320624b1130fc5de7b2e100/Sparkle/SUAppcastDriver.m#L525)). The release owner must verify universal-client updates on both architectures, including Rosetta, with correct enclosure URLs, sizes, signatures, and monotonic build numbers. Each architecture-specific feed must then continue delivering its matching artifact.

## Why This Change Was Made

The executable, resource sidecar, service pin, CLI installation, and profile seed now have one runtime contract. The loose Bun layout and its app-specific materialization/verification code are removed; compatibility remains only for existing service/seed upgrade and rollback. The sidecar stays loose because APFS clone seeding avoids archive extraction cost.

## Evidence — qualification remains NO-GO

Rebased on current main at `3971bf53e7b09905ca24c28c10719bd767c303ef`, including the invocation/Doctor fixes in #173154 and the fresh-profile lifecycle fix in #173246. No builder-owner or proof-only commits are published as this lane’s changes. The app retains both retry-aware readiness and background runtime warming.

The packaged verifier now allows only Unix socket bind/connect inside its canonical isolated root, after the existing network denial. IP networking, outside-root sockets, operator home, Keychain, launchctl, and host SQLite remain denied. A short temporary-directory prefix and a pre-copy 103-byte endpoint check prevent the broker’s long-path fallback from escaping the isolated root. This addresses the actual shared SQLite broker dependency; loose and standalone Doctor use that same IPC path.

Current focused proof: **67 script tests / 18.12 s wall**, including real native in-root bind/connect, outside-root socket and IP denial, and overlong-root rejection. Both new cases failed on the old verifier for the intended reasons (14.13 s wall). The previously blocked service-pin suite now passes **20 tests / 62.76 s wall** with `cli-invocation.mjs` on main. **35 Swift tests / six suites pass in 8.98 s wall** (2.523 s test time), after a pinned-Xcode/SDK test build taking 177.05 s wall. Formatting, lint, line-cap, assertion-safety, and timeout-race checks pass; independent P0–P2 review is scoped-clean. The repair adds 7/removes 1 production lines and adds 120/removes 17 test lines, plus removal of a dangling CI entry for the deleted loose-runtime verifier test. A 14-minute disk hold ended only after the host recovered above 20 GiB; stale lane payloads were removed and proof records retained. No app packaging/signing or live campaign ran this round.

Current lane head: `1c1a71aa255ede7625e956bbc184355cc1798686`. Historical signed proof head: `c305e2e92d40094b33acefcd2a1a9d09ddaba802`, incorporating the separately owned builder/Doctor fixes and Gateway lifecycle fix `959f3bfdb7a1d48b5a2e31501f1088ec71c54178` locally only. Those commits were not pushed as this PR's changes.

The historical release-config JIT ARM64 cohort reached the mandatory performance stop condition. Its timings are confounded by shared-host load; NO-GO remains in force until the remaining runtime blockers land and a quiet-host comparison passes. Three fresh copies/profiles per runtime, interleaved on a busy shared host:

| Measurement | Loose baseline | Standalone candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Fresh open → main median | 11.43 s | 9.34 s |
| Repeat open → main median | 0.158 s | 0.143 s |
| Fresh open → Gateway ready, individual runs | 57.22 / 38.90 / 36.36 s | 49.23 / 49.13 / 54.38 s |
| Fresh open → Gateway ready median | 38.90 s | 49.23 s |
| Automatic setup card | 2/3 | 1/3 |
| Bundle logical bytes | 1,209,004,552 | 1,929,559,168 |
| Profile logical bytes, median | 892,311,190 | 1,617,058,587 |

Candidate Gateway readiness regressed **26.6%**. Qualification stopped; the baseline-to-candidate upgrade cell was not run. One-minute startup load samples ranged approximately 25.56–78.26 for baseline and 34.75–52.16 for candidate. These are shared-host measurements, not unloaded-machine claims.

Candidate warm completed at 68.37 / 70.94 / 77.10 s from open. One full second launch of the same candidate copy/profile used the warmed seed and reached Gateway ready in 42.39 s; no baseline repeat Gateway comparison was collected. Dashboard observations were missing / 65.75 / 53.40 s for baseline and missing / 91.86 / missing for candidate. Positive values are observation upper bounds, not precise paint times; there is no valid three-run dashboard median. Missing cases showed native onboarding/recovery/model setup. Successful cells logged `openclaw.setup.auto`; candidate round 2 reused the existing Codex login. Early failures reported persisted-device-identity offline maintenance during Gateway startup; the missing lifecycle-table error did not recur.

### Functional results and blockers

- Selected-library logs confirmed bundled SQLite 3.53.4 in every candidate cell, from the app or warmed seed. This used the approved log-verification method; Homebrew/MacPorts permissions were not changed.
- The real chat turn failed with `Cannot resolve OpenClaw CLI executable path for native hook relay`. `resolveNativeHookRelayExecutable()` in `src/agents/harness/native-hook-relay-command.ts` requires a loose entry before reaching the shared invocation resolver. The builder/core owner needs to recognize the current standalone executable through `cli-invocation.mjs`, retain explicit overrides, and invoke `hooks relay ...` directly. No app environment workaround was added.
- Doctor ran once outside the sandbox, with a 120 s cap: exit 0, “Doctor complete.”, 82.59 s. Before the scoped IPC allowance, the sandbox packaging verifier exited 1 with `SpawnBrokerError` opening `/private/tmp/oc-zc2-macfat/tmp/openclaw-runtime-proof-rEopnq/oc-br-cuNqoH/resource.sock`. The current kernel-log query did not capture the matching denial; the prior network-bind denial is historical evidence only. That historical package did not qualify or publish its canonical destination. The new native socket regression passes with the corrected policy; real signed Doctor qualification remains pending.
- A separate owned Gateway restart switched from bundle to warmed seed and reached ready in 40.22 s. Warm receipt, `runtime/current`, terminal wrapper, and `macos-app` ownership marker were verified. All trial quits left zero observed children.

### Source proof and review

33 focused Swift tests passed: 2.202 s test time / 4.62 s wall. Warm/restart subset: 17 tests / 0.340 s; changed service-preparation case: four variants / 0.489 s. Initial native fixture build: 131.91 s. SwiftFormat, targeted SwiftLint, diff check, protocol, plugin inventory, native i18n, config docs, assertion safety, line-cap, timeout-race, and mock-export checks passed. Broader preparation failures (captured-updater verification and named-profile/default-port expectations) remain **unresolved, not proven inherited**. The environment-name ratchet remains 455/454; the warm follow-up added no name.

Local and committed warm-up follow-up autoreviews at `78bd83eb76c949704af386c3ff54820306b749e8` were P0–P2 scoped-clean; this is not a claim of a new full-branch review. Full PR production LOC: +1051/-2607; tests +1711/-649; docs +132/-143. Warm follow-up alone: production +225/-41, tests +562/-95. The added lifecycle code separates immediate app hosting from durable service/CLI publication.

Exact published-head CI has no commit status contexts or `openclaw/ci-gate` result; the rollup contains administrative successes/skips, not broad runtime qualification. The PR remains draft for hook-relay #173473 and failed historical qualification; the next comparison requires a quiet host selected by the lead. The fresh-profile Gateway lifecycle fix landed in #173246 (`1ed40a1aaaf9653f10eb46115c16f7154e11ccd4`) and is now part of the main base; it is not a remaining dependency. The ready-state ClawSweeper loop was not started. Nothing landed or submitted to Apple.

### Historical build provenance

Production-pinned Bun, JIT ARM64, shared mac build lock; minimum 20 GiB free before builds. Core build: 178.99 s; standalone builder: 799.91 s. Canonical packaging replay: 35m 30.6s JavaScript, 543.74 s release app compilation, 35.32 s CLI, 237.34 s MLX helper. MLX was not skipped. A stale interrupted packaging lock/snapshot was recovered through the canonical cleanup owner; no source or verifier bypass was used. Native disk holds resumed only after the 20 GiB threshold.

prs.title: feat(identity): support configurable Enterprise GitHub coauthor credit
prs.body:
Closes #173512

## What Problem This Solves

Enterprise GitHub users need Git coauthor credit tied to their verified enterprise account and commit address.

## User Impact

Operators configure the enterprise hostname through the existing `gateway.github.host` setting. Users retain their saved coauthor preference through consecutive profile merges and refreshed sign-in; eligible commits use the broker-verified enterprise address, and the Profile page explains that this address becomes visible in commit history. Missing addresses and stale principal bindings withhold credit until refreshed sign-in. Enterprise accounts do not match public-GitHub role rules.

## Why This Change Was Made

Trusted Enterprise GitHub metadata flows through the existing canonical profile worker and attribution owner. Identity keys include the host, and publication selects contributors for its selected GitHub host, preventing equal numeric IDs on different hosts from sharing credit. No tenant hostname is hardcoded, no enterprise noreply address is synthesized, and verified addresses stay out of profile responses and sign-in aliases.

The smallest coherent scope includes sign-in, persisted identity, attribution, publication, and profile disclosure together. It reuses the existing host configuration, profile consent and authority invalidation; one additive nullable identity field retains the verified binding. Simplification retained one principal parser and one attribution path. Enterprise GitHub writes settle in the existing profile worker transaction, independently of the identity reader; the credit disclosure covers both host-selected address forms even when the displayed primary account is public GitHub.

## Evidence

- Rebased onto `a9e86934eb289bd0e90bd15834f8a337826bb704` (main). Feature naming, internal types/operations and filenames now use Enterprise GitHub. Existing `x-factory-*` proxy headers remain unchanged. Enterprise identity projection also follows main's resident profile catalog; the retired full-profile reader was not restored.

- Rebased-source validation: 66 selected backend tests pass across Gateway identity and profile/multi-account suites, including two enterprise hosts, public-ID collisions, missing addresses, opt-out, consecutive merges without intervening sign-in, and host-selected credit after linking public and enterprise profiles. The 6-test Enterprise GitHub suite includes a new `users.list` catalog regression that fails before the rebase integration and passes afterward.
- Prior repair evidence (`fcf942776e4`): 3 focused Profile browser scenarios and the UI typecheck pass, including public and enterprise identity disclosures. The rendered UI code is unchanged by this naming/rebase update. Before/after screenshots below are from the actual mocked-Gateway UI and were inspected.
- Rebased-source core typecheck, touched lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Prior UI/i18n proof is retained for unchanged UI source. Both import-cycle checks report zero cycles; the database-worker ratchet reports no T1 growth (222 → 222).
- Independent source review and the publication Codex autoreview found no actionable P0/P1 findings in the repair.
- Backend proof ran on an isolated, credential-free AWS lease. The rebased backend invocation took 55 seconds wall time including compilation/worker setup. The prior browser invocation took 27 seconds. These tests exercise the durable profile/merge/attribution boundary and real UI controls; they do not validate a live Enterprise GitHub broker or deployment. Broad CI for the pushed head is separate evidence.

**Before — public primary described only noreply credit**

![Before: Profile credit disclosure with a public primary account](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6b6b1b77-194d-424a-b4d3-588d494c6589)

**After — disclosure covers the address selected for publication**

![After: Profile credit disclosure covers public and enterprise publication](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dde49183-dcde-46f9-9dfe-d7b94e702290)

Fixes #173206

## What Problem This Solves

The Memory settings page embeds Dreaming field policy in the Control UI host even though Memory Core owns that configuration.

## User Impact

No intended visual or runtime behavior change. Existing custom memory engines, same-ID overrides, unknown or unavailable schemas, read-only access, explicit zero/false overrides and clearing optional values remain supported. No migration or plugin publication is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the complete curated Dreaming presentation into Memory Core public metadata and consume it with the existing Solid settings controls. Remove the replaced host-specific panel and defaults helpers. The bundled presentation is a host-placement template; writes still target the currently configured Dreaming owner through the existing serialized config capability. Display defaults remain separate from runtime schema defaults.

Artifact-only changes also select UI CI so future plugin-owned presentation edits exercise their consumer.

## Evidence

- Integrated-baseline production-artifact, renderer and Memory page integration tests: 34 passed across three files, including the inherited model provider icon.
- Actual shared config-owner test preserves the Off sentinel and structured SecretRef while saving sibling edits, zero, false and a cleared override without writing display defaults.
- Prior unchanged Memory defaults Chromium E2E with mocked Gateway: 2 passed, including config.set omission after clearing and preserved sibling configuration. These were not repeated after the picker API reconciliation.
- Artifact-only CI planning assertion: passed.
- UI typecheck, formatter checks and production UI build: passed; startup bundle limits passed.
- Independent source review and fresh scoped autoreview: no actionable P0-P2 findings; the baseline refresh and current Solid picker API reconciliation were reviewed.

The browser E2E uses a mocked Gateway; no live Gateway or plugin registry publication was exercised.

The branch integrates the captured main baseline and carries its Solid provider icon API migration into the extracted renderer while preserving deletion of the replaced Dreaming panel.

Exact-head CI https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38835794899 attempt 1 completed 77 jobs: 50 successful, 24 skipped, two root failures and their downstream aggregate. The actual CI base reproduces both signatures with matching dependency inputs. prs.title: fix(active-memory): recall sub-agent receives huge prompt envelopes; bound recall context to 25K chars
prs.body:
Fixes #88077
Related: #92013

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Active Memory users on channel sessions with large runtime envelopes would see the blocking recall sub-agent ingest the full assembled `event.prompt` — observed in production at 29K-30K chars on ordinary Telegram group-topic turns (#88077) and at **609K-693K chars** with 30-second pre-prompt hook timeouts on long direct sessions (#92013) — even though the separate `memory_search` query was already clamped to ~480 chars. Every affected turn wasted tokens and added timeout/circuit-breaker risk inside a blocking hook.

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildQuery` forwarded `latestUserMessage` (the raw `event.prompt`) unbounded into the recall sub-agent's conversation context in every `queryMode`. Two earlier attempts didn't land: #88078 strips the envelope down to a ~2K latest message (recall loses all conversation context), and #92099 was closed with a P1 for sourcing the current request from historical `event.messages` (stale current turn) plus adding a new config surface.

This fix keeps `event.prompt` as the only current-turn source and instead bounds the complete model-facing recall context to **25,000 UTF-16 chars** inside `buildQuery`, structure-aware:

- A generated context-engine envelope (`<conversation_context>…</conversation_context>` + `Current user request:`, the shape emitted by `extensions/codex/src/app-server/context-engine-projection.ts`) is split: the **actual current user request is always preserved** (verbatim unless itself over budget), and only a **sanitized newest tail** of the context block fills the remaining budget — tool-call/tool-result traces, omitted-part placeholders, truncation markers, and envelope boilerplate are dropped.
- A channel inbound envelope keeps the whole `Current message:` section (including `[Replying to: …]` quoted-reply context) and a sanitized tail of the preceding metadata.
- A native reply-target block (`Reply target of current user message (untrusted, for context):`, producer `src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-meta.ts`) ahead of the projection envelope is preserved as bounded current-turn quote context.
- Unstructured oversized text is head-truncated UTF-16-safely with an explicit marker.
- The envelope split anchors on the projection's exact joint `\n</conversation_context>\n\nCurrent user request:\n` emission, so a request that QUOTES either marker (pasted transcript, hostile channel content) can never redirect the split and drop the real request — regression-tested.
- `queryMode: "recent"`/`"full"` use the extracted request as the latest message (recent turns already carry conversation context under their existing explicit budgets — no duplicated envelope), and the assembled output gets a final cap that keeps `Latest user message:` intact and drops the oldest turns first.
- The `memory_search` query is now seeded from the bounded request instead of the raw envelope head, and its 480-char clamp stays as defense in depth.
- Ordinary short prompts are character-for-character unchanged (beyond the pre-existing `.trim()`); no new config key — the 25K default matches the requested production behavior.
- Recall start logs gain ` queryCharsRaw=<n> queryBounded=true` when bounding engages (existing key=value logging convention; unbounded turns keep the existing compact line).

Explicitly **not** claimed fixed: the separate `memory_search` backend timeout — this PR only bounds what reaches the recall model and the search-query seed.

## User Impact

Active Memory users on Telegram/long direct sessions stop paying 600K-char recall prompts and their timeout/cost/latency risk in a blocking pre-prompt hook; recall keeps useful bounded recent context instead of losing it (the #88078 approach) or going stale (the #92099 approach). Operators see raw-vs-effective query sizes in the existing start log line when bounding occurs.

## Evidence

Real production observations (redacted; from the live gateway that motivated #92013 — `queryMode: "message"`, Telegram direct session):

```
[plugins] active-memory: ... start timeoutMs=30000 queryChars=609847 searchQueryChars=480
[plugins] active-memory: ... done status=timeout elapsedMs=30004 summaryChars=0
[plugins] active-memory: ... start timeoutMs=30000 queryChars=693210 searchQueryChars=480
[plugins] active-memory: ... done status=timeout elapsedMs=30011 summaryChars=0
```

**After-fix run from a real Active Memory gateway** (source gateway built from this branch, `openclaw gateway run` with an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, a replica of the reporting operator's auth/state, memory-core slot with `text-embedding-3-large`; the same 620,391-char projection-envelope shape submitted as a real turn through the gateway's `/v1/responses` endpoint, which routes as a `webchat` session — redacted log lines, timestamps preserved):

```
2026-07-18T16:48:42.639-04:00 [plugins] active-memory: agent=main session=agent:main:openresponses:e1fde2cb-… activeProvider=openai activeModel=gpt-5.4-mini thinking=off fast=inherit start timeoutMs=30000 queryChars=24680 queryCharsRaw=620391 queryBounded=true searchQueryChars=66
2026-07-18T16:49:01.938-04:00 [plugins] active-memory: agent=main session=agent:main:openresponses:e1fde2cb-… done status=ok elapsedMs=19298 summaryChars=211
```

The 620,391-char raw prompt reaches the recall sub-agent as a 24,680-char bounded context (cap 25,000), the memory-tool query is the 66-char actual user request instead of the head of the envelope, and the recall **completes with a real memory summary** (`status=ok`, `summaryChars=211`) inside the 30s hook budget that production turns previously exhausted (`status=timeout elapsedMs=3000x` in the before logs above). The HTTP turn itself completed in ~52s end-to-end with the main model answering from the recalled facts.

Setup notes for reviewers: the run used the operator's real auth/state replica; their production 9,648-chunk memory index could not be reused directly because its index schema predates current main and memory-core correctly fails closed pending reindex (`OpenClaw version/index mismatch`), so recall-content proof used a freshly indexed memory file in the isolated workspace. Nothing on the operator's running installation was modified; the dev gateway ran on a separate port/state dir and was stopped after the runs.

Hook-level regression test mirrors the same shape (builds a >600K projection envelope and asserts the embedded recall prompt is <30K, contains the request, has no tool traces, and the start log carries `queryCharsRaw=6xxxxx queryBounded=true`).

Commands run locally (Linux source checkout, deps via `pnpm install`; remote proof backend unavailable in this environment, so trusted-source local fallback per AGENTS.md):

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/active-memory/   # 4 files, 215 tests passed
pnpm tsgo:extensions                                        # clean
pnpm tsgo:extensions:test                                   # clean
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/active-memory/*.ts   # clean
pnpm format extensions/active-memory/... docs/...           # applied
git diff --check                                            # clean
```

New focused tests (`extensions/active-memory/query.test.ts`, 13 tests + 1 hook-level in `index.test.ts`): >600K generated conversation block bounded to the cap with the request preserved verbatim at the end; newest-tail retention with oldest content omitted; tool-call/tool-result/boilerplate removal; long pasted-document request bounded head-first; quoted-reply channel envelope preservation; UTF-16 surrogate-pair safety on giant emoji envelopes (lone-surrogate regex, works pre-ES2024 lib); recent-mode staleness guard (request comes from `event.prompt`, envelope not duplicated next to recent turns); full-mode overflow keeping `Latest user message:` intact; short-prompt no-op; under-cap full-mode byte-compat; reply-target block preservation; marker-injection (envelope markers quoted inside the request).

prs.title: feat(msteams): allow account-specific inbound tenant restrictions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Teams operators need to restrict inbound activities to selected Microsoft Entra tenants independently of the bot's credential tenant.

## User Impact

Optional `allowedInboundTenantIds` accepts 1–32 tenant UUIDs per account. Unset accounts retain existing behavior. Root configuration applies to the default account; named accounts must set their own restriction. Configuration changes use the existing Teams channel restart lifecycle.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native processor checks the authenticated activity before SDK routes, including SSO, and the same check runs before durable queued delivery. Every supplied `channelData.tenant.id` and `conversation.tenantId` must be valid, agree after case normalization, and belong to the configured set. Missing, malformed, conflicting or foreign tenant metadata is acknowledged without dispatch. Queued activities are rechecked against the restarted account's policy.

This extends the Teams plugin's existing processor and ingress owners. The channel type, schema, UI hints and generated channel metadata declare the option; no new core/SDK hook or transport is introduced.

## Evidence

Current source: `edd1c5d4d9d610256cbce7e6619e86606b8050e7`, preserving the published feature history with an ordinary merge of upstream `c47f8037cc4bdb4ae64d552626123a84c1c7fe0b`.

- Locked Vitest 5.0.3: **69/69 passed**, four focused files, **6.78s** wall time after the upstream merge. Covers default/named account isolation, runtime/emitted JSON Schema parity for lowercase and uppercase UUIDs, ordinary callbacks, pre-SSO token exchange, unchanged unset behavior and queued replay.
- Restoring the pre-change registered production paths produces four expected failures: schema acceptance, named-account isolation, ordinary-message denial and token-exchange denial. The feature patch was restored before final validation.
- Changed-file repository-config oxlint with warnings denied, formatting, generated metadata freshness and `git diff --check`: passed. Independent complete-diff review passed. The follow-up three-file schema correction also passed independent review and the repository-required isolated AutoReview at P0–P2.
- Extension production/test type wrappers, assertion-safety, config-doc publication checks, targeted lint, format and diff checks pass. The final three-file CI correction passed the required isolated AutoReview at P0–P2. Generated baseline publication adds exactly four channel paths and leaves core/plugin counts unchanged. The feature changes no dependency declaration. The ordinary upstream merge includes upstream lockfile changes; dependencies were not restored on the constrained connection. Focused tests used the existing dependency workspace. A fresh isolated complete-feature review against c47f8037 passed at P0–P2. Current-head CI remains required.

<details>
<summary>Local validation commands and environment</summary>

The checkout used temporary native bindings at the exact lockfile versions. Local binding paths are represented by placeholders below.

```bash
env NAPI_RS_NATIVE_LIBRARY_PATH="<locked-rolldown-binding>" pnpm vitest run \
  extensions/msteams/src/channel.config-schema.test.ts \

  --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-msteams.config.ts

env NAPI_RS_NATIVE_LIBRARY_PATH="<locked-oxlint-binding>" \
  pnpm exec oxlint --config .oxlintrc.json --threads=8 --deny-warnings <changed-ts-files>
```

prs.title: fix(auto-reply): steer compatible inputs into admitted direct runs
prs.body:
Related: #163058, #163064

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes compatible ordinary input being queued instead of steering an admitted direct embedded run that has no ReplyOperation.

## User Impact

Compatible input can reach the existing run. Changed authority, replaced owners, incompatible delivery contracts and definite refusals retain follow-up behavior. No new configuration, public API or persisted format is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing guarded direct target, its actual source identity and its authority projection across asynchronous preparation. The caller now supplies the existing inbound authority overlay when there is no ReplyOperation, so the target can perform its own canonical projection rather than comparing an unprojected inbound fingerprint. Existing comparators, source/lifecycle assertions and final native acceptance checks remain intact. Embedded dispatch carries its already-owned execution level; absent profile selection does not acquire fabricated automatic-selection provenance.

## Evidence

### Behavior addressed

Ordinary input could fail to steer a valid direct owner even when the target's canonical authority projection matched. The direct-owner permission-removal boundary also needed real final-effect proof rather than only mocked acceptance or a test using a ReplyOperation-owned run.

### Real setup tested

An isolated source checkout ran the real profile, admission, direct embedded execution, native queue and canonical transcript paths. Only inference responses were synthetic, served over local loopback. Both users and their profile/session state were fictitious and disposable. The admitted target had no ReplyOperation. Observers called the actual preparation and queue methods without forcing permission decisions or acceptance results. No production Gateway or deployed service was exercised.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

Admit the direct owner through the normal runtime with a normally initialized session row. Hold its first model response. Submit a compatible message from a separately linked, equally authorized user, then hold the actual returned native preparation before acceptance. Run an unchanged control and a matched case that removes only the original owner's profile role through the existing profile writer. In both cases, inspect the original registration, streaming state, native acceptance, subsequent model requests, retained follow-up and persisted canonical transcript.

The isolated integration harness has no public CLI. Repository-owned focused regression commands are:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts --maxWorkers=1 --no-file-parallelism src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-steer-adoption.worker.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply.binding-route-owner.test.ts
```

### Evidence after fix

- Before the final caller-overlay wiring, the same valid direct-owner setup failed: projected authority matched, but native acceptance was false and the native queue was not entered. This is an expected failing baseline, not a passing test.
- Unchanged control: native acceptance occurred once; the original run's next model request contained the input marker; the persisted canonical transcript contained exactly one matching user message; no successor model request was created.
- Original-owner role removal: the incoming user remained valid, and the original registration was unchanged and still streaming at the post-removal observation. Native acceptance was refused, model requests and the persisted transcript contained no marker, and exactly one follow-up remained. The original owner subsequently failed legitimately after losing its permission.
- Both matched integration cases passed. Source identity and test-owned process/resource cleanup were independently checked, with no production-path or network tripwire violation.
- The two affected regression files passed 21/21 after the final wiring change. Earlier unchanged dispatch-owner and execution-level suites retain another 21 passing scenarios: 42 distinct focused scenarios across separate invocations, not one combined run. Formatting and focused syntax lint passed for the final caller change.

### Observed result after fix

Compatible ordinary input reaches the original admitted direct run without a ReplyOperation. Removing only that original owner's role at the held preparation boundary refuses the input before native acceptance, model consumption and canonical transcript commit, while retaining a follow-up. No authority comparator or lifecycle guard was relaxed.

### What was not tested

The isolated source candidate is based on upstream `b833d16d4ef49749b3caaf8910d917e67f21b694`. A later read of main `40d01813a80a28d6c9bb48ca7581363ecb008a0b` found no changes to the nine contributed paths and a conflict-free test merge; behavior was not rerun on that merged tree. This is not installed-package, Gateway, end-to-end channel or production proof. It establishes one original-owner role-removal boundary, not every revocation timing or every caller.

Broad core type-aware lint reached its 600-second limit; production core compilation reached its 500-second watchdog without a type diagnostic. Both remain inconclusive, not passes, and were run before the final caller wiring. The existing local max-lines finding in `agent-runner-run.ts` remains reported. Final-head compiler results, broad PR CI and exact-head maintainer security approval remain required; this evidence does not mark the PR ready or authorize merge.

### Related public context

#161046 concerns preflight for an existing ReplyOperation; #165957 is the broader session-controller draft; merged #158699 restores existing queued/active-turn steering guards. #168830 addresses transcript-writer nested-read deadlock, #160275 steers an already queued Gateway input, and #145820 withdraws canceled steering. This PR addresses ordinary admission into a direct embedded owner without a ReplyOperation; these adjacent changes do not establish that this caller gap is already fixed.

AI-assisted implementation and testing. The contributed patch remains nine files; no deployment/configuration migration or independent review completion is claimed.
