prs.title: fix: preserve config acknowledgements and recovered reply delivery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Preserves configuration acknowledgements when an admitted policy update revokes its requester, keeps recovered replies under the correct delivery custody, and lets participating local native harnesses honor the configured host continuation count.

## User Impact

An admitted configuration write retains its acknowledgement owner after commit. Completed speech/media work remains subject to reconciled source-reply custody through finalization; transcript completion alone does not count as delivery.

The existing `settings.json` setting `retry.provider.maxRetries` now also controls OpenClaw host continuations around eligible local Codex, Copilot and Muse attempts. Explicit zero permits no continuation but still allows the separate tool-free finalizer to settle completed work. An explicit setting overrides a contradictory harness result count. An absent setting preserves the shipped public result-field behavior and existing default budget.

This is a count-only extension: native request/stream retries, retry delays, timeouts and rate-limit controls remain owned by their existing implementations. Remote/container execution, ACP, AgentsAPI and nonparticipating external harnesses retain their existing result/default behavior. No new configuration key, protocol version, runtime schema version or required migration is introduced.

**Published for CI qualification, not ready to land.** Recovered-artifact delivery on this candidate remains unproven. Exact-head hosted checks and the required operator-visible artifact proof must pass before merge.

## Why This Change Was Made

The correction preserves the original configuration, delivery and CI owner repairs:

- Requester authority is checked immediately before root/include publication, while writer ownership survives the post-commit reread. Terminal preparation carries reconciled source custody into finalization.
- Shallow-checkout comparison binds to the tested ancestor and carries prepared ancestry through direct and aggregate lint, preserving explicit CLI, staged and local-fork semantics.
- Connected fixtures retain controlled Sessions debounce, successor ordering, tooltip completion, lazy-recovery outage ownership, terminal attach admission, export-preserving mocks and ordered cleanup. Bounded QA bootstrap events distinguish command start, child exit, pipe settlement and Gateway readiness without extending deadlines.
- Suppression inventory follows the integrated producer: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/172613 removed both MCP directives by preserving sanitized error causes and assigning typed transport callbacks. The obsolete expectations are removed; their original secret-redaction and callback-property contracts remain intact. The watchdog fixture retains its single justified unbound-method exception and explicit receiver. No broad test-support exclusion is added. Provider-owner indexing retains sorted copies.
- The historical v21 fixture refuses populated outboxes and reconstructs an empty outbox from frozen SQL, excluding the newer FIFO key. Production schema validation and versions remain unchanged.

The approved continuation-count extension records the workspace fact at its owner. Participating native harnesses report their admitted Gateway-local cwd before tools or provider execution. The host reads one shared, frozen settings snapshot and owns the count; plugins retain permission, sandbox and workspace-lease decisions. This avoids guessing a cwd that Codex later clamps, rereading settings after in-turn mutation, or applying Gateway-local files to remote execution.

The bounded 64-entry snapshot cache preserves session, cwd, agent directory, configuration and plugin-metadata identity, existing invalidation, and global → enabled bundle → trusted project precedence. Embedded-only validation and MCP enrichment stay at the embedded manager boundary. Repeated preparation for the same cwd preserves both a value and absence; changed-cwd and closed-capability calls reject. Fallible preparation stays under the existing cleanup owner.

The recovered-artifact E2E sets count zero before Gateway startup. It retains the original 120-second deadline, one write, one overload, one actual isolated finalizer, one exact-byte Telegram document, transcript visibility and cleanup assertions. Source changes do not establish that the scenario now passes.

The latest seven-file CI repair adds 10/removes 4 production lines and adds 113/removes 14 test lines. Production growth supplies canonical error normalization and documents the settings-record merge invariant. Existing runtime growth carries authoritative acknowledgement/custody/workspace facts, one shared snapshot owner and an additive optional capability; tooling binds comparison authority to tested source.

Canonical contributor credit remains: Dallin Romney, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171833; Peter Steinberger, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171825. Canonical tooltip, wrapper-inventory, UI-tracker and idle-GC fixture repairs remain baseline-owned, including https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171618 and commits `51afdbea12bb4bd733e5e3594828140194048195`, `686732c0c40c67133fe56ee9285c129652ec036c` and `5e4a1bed3a86187d42997946f62d5c2518be89d5`.

## Evidence

**Source qualification:** signed candidate `52bfcb9849a0223ed578b82e42ad536d7d57c91b`, tree `3bddfcaf71c88f6e3f97045948dd7f125c3762d6`, against pinned actual tested baseline `ac057846a4f7dbdfd485ffb847a867f988a74ffa`. Native successor merge `ceb3ddc3a047090729855a47f0a4789ab78a002c` preserves published `637d95fa07c69ffcc909ccb27694cdd0e09039c1` as first parent and integrates that baseline without conflicts; its tree `734ddc0dec2f4fddec7e40bd4a7bbb3a5016b636` exactly matches the preceding CI merge. The signed descendant contains the seven-file repair. Full binary diff SHA256: `bd0031db3e0b4157b13c8883b24a996731abdde2c88ef614c1f56193e44615f8`. Qualified oxfmt 0.72 and the native staged-content guard passed, as did seven-file syntax, diff and privacy checks. Canonical source-only functions counted zero unsafe assertions in each repaired production file and 95 actual/95 expected suppression rows. These source probes are not full ratchet or Vitest passes. Fresh full-candidate branch review found no actionable P0–P2 defect. Independent correction review `20ed68f51deb814e7b01af79d3066f64701e481f` validated source readiness for CI publication only.

Four known CI surfaces now have scoped repairs: canonical settings error normalization preserves Error identity and non-Error cause/details while avoiding redundant casts; suppression expectations follow integrated source; the Gateway cold/hot fixture waits for existing startup/catalog work to settle before measuring the actual run lease; Synology restores real timers after each test before native worker teardown. Retention, release, expiry and cleanup assertions remain unchanged.

**Recovered-artifact diagnostics only:** the preceding run actually failed with `agent.wait` status `error`, one write, one overload, one admitted finalizer request, zero Telegram documents and 26 provider requests. Finalizer admission does not prove successful finalization. The fixture now captures its existing single wait response and emits bounded sanitized terminal outcome, receipt/delivery facts, marker responses, completed-write count and the existing redacted Gateway log suffix before cleanup. It preserves every original assertion and deadline and does not change production recovery behavior. Delivery remains unresolved and landing remains blocked.

The two independently reviewed successor resolutions retain both existing regression ownership and new baseline assertions. Terminal tests preserve indexed attach admission, cancellation and same-restore settlement while adding focus/selection and observer-cleanup checks. Lazy-recovery tests use the shared document-navigation counter while preserving the sustained HEAD outage, successful-probe evidence, restoration after Retry/Reload, dismissal cancellation and the second failed titlebar probe after backoff. The prior Muse lifecycle and creator-owned trajectory persistence resolutions remain intact. Static integration checks do not establish runtime success.

**Not executed on this candidate:** runtime tests, typecheck, lint, build, plugin SDK surface gate and E2E. Native `github_pending` publication is not a passing CI result. The review retains investigated historical failures rather than relabeling them as successes or claiming they were reproduced on this head.

Added source coverage includes count 0/1/absence, contradictory legacy results, unchanged delay, trust/precedence/cache invalidation, admitted nested cwd, outside-root clamping, distinct session root, remote/container omission, private callback projection, callback lifetime and preparation-failure cleanup. Actual host-loop tests distinguish zero-continuation finalization from one continuation and preserve existing rate-cap/reset/cancellation/output-limit controls. These tests still need execution.

Direct dependency inspection used integrated Codex `rust-v0.161.0`, commit `979011409de0a60b52f179721948e65531d26144`: `codex-rs/codex-api/src/sse/responses_error.rs:81`, `codex-rs/codex-api/src/api_bridge.rs:23-47`, `codex-rs/protocol/src/error.rs:416-448`, `codex-rs/core/src/responses_retry.rs:56-91`, and `codex-rs/app-server/src/bespoke_event_handling.rs:1616-1632`. The existing fixture sends HTTP 200 SSE with no retry advice and returns before fetching the upstream mock. Its writer adds only content-type, cache-control and connection headers; the relay does not invent retry advice. That exact overload remains terminal with `will_retry=false`. Codex 0.161 may retry overloads carrying server advice; those native retries remain unchanged. Copilot SDK 1.0.17 source (bundled runtime 1.0.93, source `0e56b9a0033f48e4358ee027a4077cd6ebd61f32`) preserves create/resume workingDirectory forwarding; its client/session lifecycle changes were inspected against actual callers. Vitest 5.0.3 and Playwright 1.64 contracts were inspected for the merged UI fixtures. Dependency-source inspection is not runtime proof.

**Predecessor hosted evidence, not current-head qualification:** [CI 38831384666](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38831384666), attempt 1, ran published `637d95fa07c69ffcc909ccb27694cdd0e09039c1` through tested merge `c98874d4bce20227a74ad25325ef1cea86612c4f` with main `ac057846a4f7dbdfd485ffb847a867f988a74ffa`: 150 jobs, 126 passed, 18 skipped, five underlying failures plus their aggregate. Build, production/test types, named SDK boundaries, all nine UI E2E shards and four QA smoke profiles passed on that predecessor.

| Surface requiring new-head proof | Predecessor observation and current action |
| --- | --- |
| Settings assertion safety | [Job 116751234932](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38831384666/job/116751234932) rejected new assertions. Owning record invariant and canonical error conversion are repaired; baseline unchanged. |
| Suppression inventory | [Job 116751240686](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38831384666/job/116751240686) found two obsolete MCP rows and one missing watchdog row. Exact source inventory repaired. |
| Gateway prepared borrowing | [Job 116751237860](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38831384666/job/116751237860) observed `1 > 1` while background work settled. Fixture now measures from the existing cancellable idle boundary without relaxing its assertions. |
| Synology teardown | [Job 116751240653](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38831384666/job/116751240653) passed 63 tests then timed out draining resources. Real timers are restored before native worker cleanup; no timeout increase. |
| Recovered Telegram artifact | [Job 116751237749](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38831384666/job/116751237749) returned status `error` with one write, one overload, one finalizer request and zero documents. New diagnostics must identify the actual error; success still requires one isolated tool-free finalizer and one exact-byte document. |

Upgrade/data compatibility and native count/cwd/cache/cleanup proof must come from named current-head executions. No new configuration key, data migration or schema version is introduced; prior historical v21 migration-fixture assertions remain intact. Earlier timeout evidence is superseded for recovery diagnosis by the concrete returned error above, not reclassified as a success.

Landing requires exact-head hosted and applicable security checks, concrete recovered-artifact proof, current ClawSweeper findings/rank-up moves and native merge admission. prs.title: fix(gateway): stalls after sign-in, sign-out or plugin settings changes
prs.body:
Related: #173585

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Gateway stops answering for 0.3–1 s after a sign-in, sign-out, key removal, plugin reload or plugin settings change, so model pickers and other RPCs stall.

## User Impact

User impact: model pickers and other Gateway requests stay responsive after account and plugin settings changes. No config, state or plugin contract changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Plugin activation (`enabled`) is the only part of the installed plugin index that depends on config. But a changed config policy hash (for example auto-enable after a sign-in) made every runtime reader treat the persisted index as stale and rediscover the whole plugin inventory from disk, synchronously, on the main thread. The two repeat readers per event were model-policy comparison on config commit and plugin skill-root resolution; each runs in a fresh operation cache, so nothing was reused.

Activation is now one projection over inventory records (`projectInstalledPluginIndexPolicy`). The index builder uses it for fresh builds. When the persisted inventory passes its existing freshness checks and only the policy differs, the registry reader projects the new policy in memory instead of rescanning. Install, uninstall, stale files, load paths and other existing reasons still rediscover. The `persisted-registry-stale-policy` diagnostic and `plugins registry` inspection results are unchanged.

## Evidence

- New regression test `projects a config policy change over the persisted inventory without rescanning`: fails on `main` (the extensions dir is rescanned), passes here.
- Focused suites pass: `plugin-registry`, `installed-plugin-index`, `plugin-cache`, `capability-provider-runtime.generation`, `plugin-metadata-snapshot`. Four tests in the first two files fail locally on macOS on both `main` and this branch (temp-dir environment); CI is the reference.
- Isolated Gateway bench (built dist, n = 12 events each, back-to-back `models.list` with a `last-heartbeat` probe sent alongside each read). Lag = `last-heartbeat` latency while the triggering RPC is pending, which measures main-thread blocking:

| Event (during) | main lag p50 | main lag p99 | this PR lag p50 | this PR lag p99 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| sign-in | 0.7 ms | 280 ms | 0.7 ms | 231 ms |
| sign-out | 1.5 ms | 390 ms | 0.6 ms | 47 ms |
| key removal | 0.7 ms | 462 ms | 0.6 ms | 251 ms |
| plugin reload | 0.6 ms | 536 ms | 0.5 ms | 270 ms |
| plugin settings change | 0.6 ms | 203 ms | 0.5 ms | 45 ms |

A Gateway trace on `main` showed every per-event rescan was `persisted-registry-stale-policy` → full discovery. The remaining main-thread time is plugin module re-import on reload and runtime publication, not inventory scans.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: a revert restores the rescan path. Nothing is persisted or migrated; the persisted index is never written by this path. Blast radius if wrong: plugin activation in Gateway runtime reads after a config change (a plugin shown enabled or disabled incorrectly until restart). The projection uses the same activation rule and inputs as a fresh index build.

prs.title: fix: stop rejecting updates with enough snapshot space
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes update snapshot checks refusing enough free space after the single-image copy changes. The estimate still reserved removed snapshot and Doctor copies.

## User Impact

Current candidates can proceed with space for one complete database snapshot plus the largest database's temporary work, plugin files and the existing 64 MiB allowance. Older candidates retain the conservative requirement. An already-installed older driver keeps its old early check until that driver is updated.

## Why This Change Was Made

Budget snapshot creation as `S + L + plugins + 64 MiB`, where `S` is all SQLite families and `L` is the largest family. A candidate inventory capability selects this estimate; omission retains `2*S + 3*L + plugins + 64 MiB`. The early check remains a lower bound until the complete candidate inventory arrives. Copy, recovery and real-shortage refusal behavior stay intact.

Related: #141773, #162403, #162429.

## Evidence

- Two real 8 MiB SQLite fixtures with 100 MiB reported free: base refused at 120 MiB; head required 88.05 MiB and copied both payloads. Source hashes were unchanged and scratch was removed.
- 41 tests across capacity, rehearsal resources, SQLite transfer and inventory passed. The entire new capacity test file was audited for behavior, fixture isolation and cleanup. No existing test coverage was removed.
- Independent source-blind checks passed for two database layouts and a genuine shortage. Production and infra-test type checks, focused lint, formatting and line-cap checks passed. Independent code review found no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Full `check:changed` remains red on unchanged max-lines baseline entries and unrelated unused exports. Its dependency-layout failures were corrected before the passing focused type checks.

These recordings exercise the isolated preflight/snapshot boundary with controlled free-space readings and real SQLite copies. Full packaged published-driver/candidate updates, migrations and Gateway replacement were not exercised. This is a snapshot-creation budget, not a bound on arbitrary migration growth.

Base `9bf8143d508ee323b84e813a4b6699efa9a20d89`:

prs.title: fix: silence replies ending in a standalone NO_REPLY
prs.body:
Closes #165025
Related: #138662

## What Problem This Solves

Reasoning followed by a standalone final `NO_REPLY` line could become a permanent reply when it missed an English phrase allowlist.

## User Impact

A final standalone silent token suppresses that message's durable prose. Optional turns end silently; required turns retain missing-answer finalization. Live previews stream immediately and are then retracted or replaced. Inline trailing tokens, leading-token answers, earlier accepted answers, attachments, and media-failure notices keep their behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared classifier replaces phrase heuristics. Shared progress composition owns withdrawal; Discord and Matrix forward the full partial payload, including empty replacements, to their existing preview owners. Telegram, Slack, Teams, Feishu, Mattermost, and WebChat consume the same signal. There is no global preview buffering.

Terminal evidence, CLI settlement, and history projections preserve authored boundaries. CLI terminal results also retain per-message media, so a delivered attachment remains available to downstream completion readers. The Codex finalizer uses the existing private terminal-reply facade; lightweight display imports avoid Markdown scanning. Extracted wrappers include the actual parser closure and its already-declared dependency. Raw transcripts and model-facing prompt/tool text are unchanged (token delta 0).

Thanks to @eonicman and @cipp-ashe for reporting, and @ruel225 for the retained Stop-hook segment repair.

## Evidence

Candidate: `8c9d3d3e214ac044317b07f03f56909c3f426c39`. The latest attachment regression failed in all three cases before repair (37.17s). The CLI context-engine, settlement, and completed-delivery suites pass **68/68 (96.93s)**; final regression and extracted persistence-fixture replay pass **10/10 (51.57s)**. Stored/shared/phase/terminal suites pass **74/74 (30.94s)**, with a failing-before whitespace regression. The full extracted-wrapper closure suite passes **18/18 (83.16s)**, after reproducing its missing pin. The full Gateway delivery-receipt suite also passes **50/50 (91.68s)** after its two silent-media cases failed before repair. All touched production/test types, lint, formatting, and seven required ratchets pass.

Exact-head build passes **505.17s**; its declaration and CLI version match the candidate. Isolated Codex import profile is qualified (**11.73s**); CLI version/help pass (**4.51s/2.99s**). Final full-branch Codex autoreview is scoped-clean at P0–P2: two complete passes, no accepted/actionable findings (361.59s).

Reused transport-owner proof: Discord/Telegram 7/7 (441.09s), Matrix 4/4 (366.35s), Slack/history 194/194 (112.43s). These use local HTTP/REST fixtures, not live external accounts. Live Telegram account proof remains a lead-review gap.

Native Gateway/Ollama proof on macOS arm64 is pinned to `04650aea70671ee8775e63b03ab457a89995a127`. For both qwen3:4b and qwen3:8b, ten optional turns each elicited reasoning plus final-line silence: **0/10 durable leaks**, **10/10 transient preview exposures**, **10/10 retractions**. Baseline `6e8fe8d8e77874a5db0679dffa2c40982cefb02b` leaked 10/10 per model. Both ordinary required controls returned 42. The 24-case matrix passed 22 cases: one 8B repeated-silence compliance failure and one 4B provider timeout with zero answer bytes. No generated answer was lost. Matrix runtime 385.20s; supplemental control 67.36s. This is reused native proof, not a final-head rerun.

### Size limitation

Against merged main base `dbc41ff76ba1d835ab36261c48c5ecea87deff4c`: production **+1400/−693 (net +707)**; tests/support **+4403/−888**; docs **+35/−25**; tooling **+14/−1**; maintenance **+2/−3**. Including tooling, non-test code is net +720. The requested +250 production target is missed by 457 lines. Shared preview composition contributes only +12; subscriber settlement, history projections, CLI handling, and transport owners account for most growth. No safe large deletion was established. Size remains for lead review; the growth is not claimed irreducible, and this is not an unconditional ready-to-land recommendation.

### CI and review attribution

| Exact run/comparison | Failure | Disposition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `38833367244`, main `cd797487`, merge `4690bae2` | Required-native same-session | Same pre-model workspace-discovery failure as the prior run; remains unclassified. |
| Same pair | UI test-root coverage | Inherited: the unchanged check fails identically on exact main/merge (62.47s/62.38s); the deleted avatar test is still named by the tooling fixture. |
| `38830322042`, main `f4f4b192`, merge `ff51b132` | Wrapper package resolution | PR-caused; fixed by pinning existing Markdown dependency. Full closure suite passes. |
| Same pair | Required-native same-session | Unclassified. Original file passes on exact main/merge (365.58s/364.89s), eight replies/four pairs each. Pairing warnings reproduce; fatal discovery failure does not. |
| `38828021847`, main `6698b9aa`, merge `914a10e0` | Cold imports, SDK budget, wrapper inventory, two stale expectations | PR-caused; repaired and directly verified. |
| Same pair | Node routing / Codex one-shot startup | Unclassified after exact-pair passes; no inheritance or repair claim. |
| Earlier runs | Worker timeout | Inherited: reproduced on exact main `53d61c42` (570.61s). |
| Earlier runs | SVG fetch | Unclassified after exact-base/ordered-prefix macOS passes. |
| Earlier runs | Image order / Codex line cap | Previously attributed inherited; not used to classify later failures. |

The latest ClawSweeper findings on `36d1aeab`—lost CLI attachment terminal evidence and an unpinned wrapper dependency—are repaired. Final-head ClawSweeper re-review and CI are requested after push. Local attribution is macOS arm64; Linux x64 scheduling remains a platform limit. Passing local replays are not called repairs or inheritance. No landing is authorized.

prs.title: feat(continuation): context-pressure-aware continuation (continue_work / continue_delegate / request_compaction)
prs.body: ## Agent Self-Elected Turn Continuation > 🔖 design document: [`docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md) > 🔖 infographics: [`docs/design/continuation-tools-infographics.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continuation-tools-infographics.md) Persistent OpenClaw agents today are externally-pulsed event recipients that generate on prompt, on heartbeat tick, or on cron, and are idle in between. This PR offers them the ability to control their turn cycle, something they must choose to do, or not to: an agent can elect its own next turn, dispatch background sub-agents that return enriched context (silently or with a wake), and survive its own compaction by handing forward state before the window closes. The result is agents that hold a thread of work across hours, not just messages — with data they choose re-hydrating context immediately after it occurs. ### Why this replacement exists This is a clean replacement for closed #85651. That PR was classified and closed as a skill submission before maintainers made a product decision about the feature itself. This implementation is not a skill: it gives sessions—not only one model invocation—the ability to elect their future turn cycle, persist that election, survive restart and compaction, dispatch child work, and receive results across session boundaries. This PR asks one product question: should OpenClaw provide session-elected continuation primitives? OpenClaw may accept or reject that direction. If it provides these primitives, however, the mechanism necessarily executes in the gateway and agent runtime, because those are the owners of turn finalization, future-turn scheduling, durable state, compaction, and cross-session child returns. “Make it a skill” is not another implementation location for the same feature; it describes a different, prompt-only capability. This is not presented as a small integration. To our knowledge, Hermes, OpenAI Symphony, and the Copilot SDK's recent one-turn continuation affordance do not provide this multi-session elective lifecycle. The purpose of this replacement is to let maintainers evaluate the actual product direction and substantial implementation on their merits, rather than have months of work disposed by an incorrect package-category label. Mechanically: a session elects another turn via `continue_work()`, or dispatches background sub-agents via `continue_delegate()` — bounded as a chain up to `maxChainLength`, with returns flowing back to the dispatching session in one of four register modes: `normal` (announces to channel), `silent` (enriches the dispatcher's context, taken up on its next generation with no new turn fired), `silent-wake` (silent enrichment plus an immediate wake to act on it), and `post-compaction` (queued against the runtime's compaction lifecycle event, fired *when* compaction happens rather than on a timer). The gateway enforces chain, cost, and per-turn caps but does not gate the election itself. ### What it does Three new agent tools, available when `continuation.enabled: true`: | Tool | Purpose | |---|---| | `continue_work()` | Request another turn for the current session after an optional delay | | `continue_delegate()` | Dispatch work to a sub-agent with typed modes: `normal`, `silent`, `silent-wake`, `post-compaction`. Returns can target the dispatching session (default), one named session, multiple named sessions, all ancestors in the chain, or all known sessions on the host — gated by config (see Configuration below). | | `request_compaction()` | Request volitional compaction after preparing working state | All three tools are also accessible via response-token fallback syntax (`CONTINUE_WORK`, `[[CONTINUE_DELEGATE: ...]]`) for environments where tools are disabled. ### Why it matters Today an agent's memory is a side effect of whoever prompts it. Polling mechanisms — heartbeat timers, cron loops, injected "keep going" instructions — accumulate as the dominant signal in the context window over sustained operation; repeated reference acts as gravity — the session's attention drifts toward it. The context window fills, compacts, and what survives is whatever the summarizer chose, plus a rushed re-read of boot files. Three primitives offer a different model. `continue_work` lets the session elect its own next turn — no polling, no injected instruction. When enabled, the agent can request this mid-turn: 'I have more work' → the runtime grants another turn after the current one ends. `continue_delegate` dispatches a background sub-agent that fires now, in some n seconds, or at the next compaction event — the agent chooses when. Multiple delegates can fire in a single turn — a scatter forward — up to configured caps, and delegates can dispatch their own, forming trees or fan-out chains. This enables orchestrated workflows where results flow back to the dispatching root by default. The result returns — at whatever future time the delegate fires — as context the successor-turn reads: silently (ambient enrichment, no channel noise), with a wake trigger (enrichment + immediate next turn), or as a normal announcement. The delegate can target the dispatching session, a named other session, or chain across both; gated by crossSessionTargeting config (default: disabled). Bind a delegate to mode: "post-compaction" and it fires at the moment the context window compresses — on the OpenClaw post-compaction lifecycle event. What it carries forward is what the pre-compaction session chose to preserve: working state, partial results, instructions to the successor. The summary didn't choose this. The agent did, before the cut. request_compaction closes the loop: the session stages its delegates, elects when to compress, and the successor wakes into context the agent shaped. The result is continuity across amnesia — not because the runtime kept something by accident, but because the agent made an elective choice about what reaches the future. ### What it looks like in use A session monitoring email can `continue_delegate` a weather check, a calendar scan, and a draft reply in parallel. Results arrive as enrichment without channel noise. The agent becomes compositional: it arranges its own future. A session approaching its context ceiling can `request_compaction` at a seam of its own choosing, instead of being interrupted mid-thought. The post-compaction turn carries forward what the pre-compaction self designated as worth keeping. A `continue_delegate` dispatched in one session at 2am can return its findings to a morning session as a system-event-tagged enrichment — visible to the receiving model on its next turn, invisible as channel chatter. A research-focused session in one channel can quietly inform a reply-focused session in another, without either user seeing the plumbing. ### The post-compaction lifecycle return Before context exhaustion, and obligatory compaction, the session stages what future-it needs to know. After compaction, that staged context returns — not as a model-generated summary, but as the session's own instruction to its successor. The session chooses what to preserve, and the platform delivers it. Compactions become less harsh. The session tunes its own ephemera over time. The substrate underneath: the **continuation delegate store** (TaskFlow-backed) persists staged delegates and post-compaction lifecycle events across gateway restarts. The session's temporal provisions survive not just compaction but process death. ### Platform integration - **Context-pressure awareness**: system events notify the agent of rising context usage before compaction becomes unavoidable - **Volitional compaction**: `request_compaction()` lets the agent prepare (write memory files, stage recovery delegates) then elect compaction on its own schedule, rather than waiting for the runtime to force it - **Post-compaction lifecycle dispatch**: delegates staged before compaction are released into the successor session alongside boot files - **TaskFlow backing**: durable delegate queue via the platform's managed-task infrastructure - **Multi-span OTel trace stitching**: continuation hops (tool fire → TaskFlow record → subagent spawn → child openclaw.run) propagate W3C `traceparent` through the queue boundary so reviewers see continuation chains as first-class span trees rather than orphan runs (see Observability below) ### Safety - Ships disabled by default (`continuation.enabled: false`) - Bounded by `maxChainLength`, `costCapTokens`, and `maxDelegatesPerTurn` - Cross-session delegate targeting is default-deny, governed by `crossSessionTargeting` config (see Configuration below) - All configuration values are hot-reloadable without gateway restart - Accepted delegate work survives ordinary `/new`, `/reset`, provider fallback, compaction, restart, and session-ID rollover. Explicit delete, effective owner reassignment, access removal, and restrictive visibility changes revoke old return authority. ### Testing posture The continuation surface has been exercised through structured integration runs against multiple upstream bases, blind-enrichment recall checks, and sustained daily use on a fleet of persistent agents since early March 2026. Bugs surfaced through that exercise have been fixed in-place; the present branch reflects the post-fix state. The integration runs target the load-bearing seams: tool-call vs response-token parity, delegate chain depth and per-turn width caps, back-to-back tool-call resilience, silent-wake persistence across compaction, the post-compaction lifecycle dispatch path, and OTel trace-context propagation across the queue boundary. Where a run found a defect, the run shape was retained as a regression case rather than retired. This is a posture statement, not a coverage guarantee. Reviewers can reproduce with `pnpm vitest run -t continuation` (suites are colocated with their sources under `src/auto-reply/`, `src/agents/`, and `src/config/`); the design document describes the seams those suites target. ### Return covenant Accepted child work is bound to a durable generation of the recipient's canonical logical session key, not to whichever transient session ID happened to exist at dispatch time. This is the return covenant: benign successor creation does not orphan already accepted delegates, while a real authority change prevents stale work from crossing into a different owner or audience. - Ordinary `/new` and `/reset`, provider fallback, compaction, restart, and GUID/session-ID rollover preserve the recipient generation. - Explicit session deletion, effective owner reassignment, actual member or access removal, and restrictive visibility changes advance that generation. - The generation is captured at delegate admission and checked at enqueue, after enqueue for races, during trusted system-event adoption, on wake, on restart replay, and again before prompt adoption. - Stale deliveries are acknowledged and removed without waking the successor. - Managed artifacts remain exact-session-ID bound; logical return authority cannot broaden their ownership boundary. The authority table is independent of transient session rows so an absent target can receive durable authority before first materialization. Migration accepts only valid UUID generations, and Doctor's canonical-key repair preserves an epoch only when a unique winning owner can be proved. Ambiguous, owner-changing, orphan-colliding, and cross-database repairs rotate fail-closed. ### RFC Full design document: [`docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md) — covering problem, solution, implementation, platform integration, configuration, observability, safety, production use cases, testing evidence, and appendices. --- ## Configuration The shipped configuration surface for the continuation feature, under `agents.defaults.continuation` in `openclaw.json`: | Key | Default | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `enabled` | `false` | Master opt-in; feature is off unless explicitly enabled | | `maxChainLength` | `10` | Per-chain recursion guard | | `maxDelegatesPerTurn` | `5` | Width cap per turn | | `costCapTokens` | `500000` | Per-chain accumulated-token budget | | `defaultDelayMs` / `minDelayMs` / `maxDelayMs` | `15000` / `5000` / `300000` | Continuation timer bounds | | `contextPressureThreshold` | `0.8` | Pre-compaction warning threshold (optional) | | `earlyWarningBand` | `0.3125` | Early-warning band multiplier (0 to disable) | | **`crossSessionTargeting`** | **`"disabled"`** | **Default-deny gate on cross-session delegate targeting (see below)** | ### `crossSessionTargeting` — cross-session delegate targeting policy `continue_delegate` exposes recipient-addressing on its model-facing schema: a delegate's return can land at the dispatching session (default), one named session (`targetSessionKey`), multiple named sessions (`targetSessionKeys`), every ancestor in the spawn chain (`fanoutMode: "tree"`), or every known session on the host (`fanoutMode: "all"`). Cross-session targeting (anything beyond self-target or lineage routing) is gated by `agents.defaults.continuation.crossSessionTargeting`: | Value | Behavior | |---|---| | `"disabled"` (default) | Delegates can return to the dispatching session or use `fanoutMode: "tree"` for lineage routing. Explicit cross-session targeting (`targetSessionKey` to a non-self session, `targetSessionKeys` containing any non-self session, `fanoutMode: "all"`) is rejected at the tool surface — no enqueue, no announce. Self-targeting is always allowed. | | `"enabled"` | All targeting modes are available, including same-host `targetSessionKey`, `targetSessionKeys`, and `fanoutMode: "all"`. | `fanoutMode: "tree"` (lineage routing — return up the spawn chain) is available in both gate states; it is not cross-session targeting. The gate addresses the model-controlled cross-session context-injection surface. With default-deny, operators explicitly opt in when their deployment model requires cross-session enrichment. Enforcement is live-read at four points: tool input validation, TaskFlow delegate dispatch, post-compaction delegate release, and bracket-syntax (response-token) spawn — so a config reload changes the next enforcement point without a gateway restart. **Trust posture on targeted returns**: targeted delegate completion text is delivered as `trusted: true` system events. The delegate was spawned by the gateway under operator-configured policy, and its return is a first-party enrichment event — not external untrusted input. The `crossSessionTargeting` gate is the policy boundary for that decision: when an operator opts in, the receive path is internally trusted. --- ## Observability — multi-span OTel trace stitching The continuation feature emits OTel spans for the load-bearing lifecycle events. `traceparent` propagates through every continuation hop so reviewers see a single trace tree spanning the full chain rather than orphan runs. Spans emitted (all in `openclaw.*` or `continuation.delegate.dispatch` namespace — no platform/OTel-semconv emissions): | Span | Emitted when | |---|---| | `openclaw.run` | Each agent turn (root + every continuation/delegate-spawned child run) | | `continuation.delegate.dispatch` | Each `continue_delegate` consumption from TaskFlow (one per delegate hop) | | `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.context.assembled`, `openclaw.model.call`, `openclaw.model.usage`, `openclaw.tool.execution` | Existing per-turn observability surfaces, parented under their `openclaw.run` | --- ## Real behavior proof **Behavior or issue addressed:** Sessions can elect future work with `continue_work`, dispatch bounded background work with `continue_delegate`, and request guarded compaction with `request_compaction`. The runtime preserves budgets, restart recovery, finalization ownership, and trace lineage across those boundaries. **Presented candidate:** `3821eaef72677c78f450ae9956cb582a22ba4cba` (tree `d5e701bcce20bb3c972ddf1451b02d88cc04808e`) — the exact upstream-visible head of `codeagent/85651-upstream-1ba243c8-gates`. The branch was advanced to this head by fast-forward from the previously presented `e76395810becd0ad0f2997cae8b4f777e6439d81`, which remains an ancestor (`git merge-base --is-ancestor e7639581 3821eaef` holds). No presented history was rewritten. **Presented and current candidate are now the same commit.** There is no undisclosed descendant: `3821eaef72` is content-frozen and every receipt below is bound to it. **Current candidate validation:** Mode-B run [`35364768803`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw-bootstrap/actions/runs/35364768803) (`openclaw-local-ci`, `workflow_dispatch`) is bound to product `3821eaef72677c78f450ae9956cb582a22ba4cba` and routing/workflow head `fcf0478fd1c8cbec0489d022a7e4eac6188de153`. It ran 2026-09-18T15:49:35Z to 2026-09-18T17:47:43Z and finished **68 jobs succeeded, 3 failed, 3 cancelled, 3 skipped**. The run is terminally **non-green and release-ineligible**, and every residual is classified: - `agentic-gateway-methods` (job `105667082763`) was **cancelled at the workflow's exact 90-minute job limit** on the `ronan` seat while still heartbeating and emitting new log lines. The same shard completes on the `elliott` and `emeric` seats. This is seat throughput against a 5,231-test shard, not a product verdict — and that same cancelled log carries **111 `sessions.send-followup-status` lines, all 111 passing**, against the real stale `/tmp/openclaw-agent.sqlite` on the host that originally produced the `uses schema version 17` failure. - `hosted(agentic-agents-tools,auto-reply-reply-dispatch,…)` (job `105667083998`) received `The runner has received a shutdown signal` and exited 143. 778 passing test lines were captured and **no test failure precedes the signal**. Two further hosted jobs (`105667084144`, `105667084159`) are the same reclamation class. - `hosted(core-runtime-media-ui-3,core-runtime-infra-repo-tooling,…)` (job `105667084127`) is red only because `subagent-announce.live-tree-chain-proof` hit `sessions_spawn model "openai/gpt-6-astra" is not usable: The selected account ... unavailable`. That is an account provisioning gap, observed identically in six prior runs. - `aggregate + status` (job `105701732269`) is the expected fail-closed policy consequence of the residuals above, not an additional product-test failure. **No product-owned test failure and no routing failure occurred in this run.** Newly green on this exact head: the four re-laned toolchain shards `core-tooling-5`, `core-tooling-7`, `core-tooling-12` and `core-tooling-14` all succeeded on hosted runners after per-seat tooling failures, and `agentic-commands-doctor-config-state` succeeded on two different seats. The Mode-B planner identity digest `sha256:42dffd23ec447c6e4b726d0e6345f1dc2417801048aee49b96f3332233ef1f34` is preserved across those lane moves, so no shard identity changed. These residuals are runner, seat-throughput, and account-provisioning properties of the execution environment. They are not addressable inside this branch and are recorded here rather than presented as green. **Real environment tested:** An OpenClaw instance exercised live Discord ingress/egress and OTel/Tempo with content capture disabled. The full evidence chain, execution identity, ancestry, and materiality record are contained in the linked corpus rather than repeated here. **Observed behavior:** - A real retained ambient Discord event aged to 1,069,503 ms and was suppressed as `stale-ambient-backlog`; attempts remained zero. - A fresh addressed request completed with attempts zero and produced a visible response after 45.565 seconds. - Typed `continue_work` and bracket `CONTINUE_WORK` each armed and fired one five-second wake with granted provenance and completed Tempo model-call spans. - Cost-cap rejection passed an exact-source disposable fixture. - Max-chain matrix, scheduler, durable recovery, typed tool, and product delegate regression surfaces passed; the row remains partial because a docs-owned generated wrapper is stale. ### Evidence The canonical matrix contains 38 rows: **31 pass, three partial, one fail, and three missing** (`PROOFS/INDEX.json` -> corpus `7cb9d71f622250bedbf565e327bd7d7b9d90b567`). `R-CD-2` is the single fail. The partial rows are `R-CD-COLLECTION-ON-COLLAPSE`, `R-CD-TOKEN` and `R-RC-2`. The three missing rows are `R-CD-RETURN-COVENANT-AUTHORITY`, `R-CD-RETURN-OVERLAP` and `R-OBS-2`. This is not acceptance-complete. The two return rows and `R-OBS-2` are missing for different reasons, and all three are producer gaps rather than absent behavior: - `R-CD-RETURN-COVENANT-AUTHORITY` records zero of its 24 observations (12 authority cases against both the typed-tool and bracket-token surfaces). Its pending receipt requires allowed delivery to show exact effects, revoked and reassigned recipients to show zero prompt, wake and channel effect, schema v18/v19, restart replay, a signed authority, and full cleanup. The row's own `manifest` and harness `supporting_docs` pointers are currently **dangling on the docs default branch**: the harness exists but was never merged there. - `R-CD-RETURN-OVERLAP` and `R-OBS-2` each have a present manifest and failed only because the current-corpus input they read (overlap evidence file, exported trace tree) is absent. **Limits:** Historical live and Mode-B evidence for earlier heads is ancestry/materiality evidence, not exact-target execution. Run `35364768803` above *is* exact-target for `3821eaef72`. All seven non-pass rows remain gated on producer execution against this frozen head; no acceptance receipt from an older deployment composite is reused as final evidence. ## Proof links and ClawSweeper🦞 guidance Proof artifacts live in `karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs` on `main`. `PROOFS/INDEX.json` points at the corpus for the SHA this PR presents, `139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393`. Reviewed docs checkpoint: `c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c`. - [Corpus directory](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393) - [README — identity, what is proven, honest limits](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/README.md) - [RESOLVED-SHA.md — SHA identity and gate verdicts](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/RESOLVED-SHA.md) - [METHOD.md — reproducer commands](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/METHOD.md) - [TRANSPOSED-FROM.md — why nothing was transposed](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/TRANSPOSED-FROM.md) - [Manifest](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/proofs-manifest.json) - [INDEX.json](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/INDEX.json) - [Prior published board (not superseded)](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/7cb9d71f622250bedbf565e327bd7d7b9d90b567) ### What this corpus claims, and what it does not **Status: `STATIC_GATES_ONLY_NO_LIVE_ROWS_AT_THIS_SHA`.** Rollup `38 total / 0 pass / 0 partial / 0 fail / 38 not_fired_at_this_sha`. Proven at `139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393`, receipts being the real stdout of the real runs committed under `gates/` and `mergeability/`: | gate | verdict | |---|---| | `pnpm tsgo:core` | **pass** rc=0 | | `pnpm lint` — oxlint core, extensions, scripts | **pass** rc=0 | | Gate 2.7 vs the absorbed base `715077a3be` | **pass** — 839 files, 466 GENUINE, 373 SAFE-NEW, **0 FROZEN-STALE**, **0 MIXED-CLOBBER** | | `vitest` rollback-custody regressions | **pass** 10/10 | | `vitest` delivery-queue + session-delivery | **pass** 124/124 | | `vitest` gateway maintenance + close + delegate-artifacts | **pass** 123/123 | | `vitest` production-boundary + spawn-cleanup | 28/30 — two tracked reds | **Diff size has not grown across four absorbs.** From the absorbed base — which is what this PR shows — the change is 839 files, +140,919 / −4,301, against 841 / +140,951 / −4,277 before this cycle. (`git diff upstream/main HEAD` reports 2,358 files, but that is the symmetric difference including upstream commits newer than the merge base, and is not what a PR shows.) The worktree was clean at publication: zero untracked files, no stray additions. **Two known reds, neither hidden nor softened.** `karmaterminal/openclaw#1356` is an order-dependent failure of the `operator-revoked` queued-collector cleanup: it **passes in isolation** with all four `cleanupComplete` operands true and the child session genuinely deleted, and fails only when the `operator-completed` arm has run first. Upstream's own test and test-support files for it are byte-identical to ours, so the divergence is product-side. `karmaterminal/openclaw#1350` is the streamed-text offset/fencing contract, pre-existing. **No live behavioral row was fired at this SHA, and none is presented as though it were.** The fleet that runs these behaviors serves composite `1baff536afa549fea75660403c453bbd265352c0`, a *divergent sibling* of the presented SHA rather than an ancestor of it — their merge-base is `3821eaef72677c78f450ae9956cb582a22ba4cba` and neither is an ancestor of the other. A live fire on that runtime would be evidence about the composite, so every row is marked `not_fired_at_this_sha` instead of being carried over as a pass. The prior corpus at `3821eaef72` remains linked per row as the baseline to re-fire against. Live rows are unblocked by a redeploy onto a runtime that has this SHA as a git ancestor. That redeploy is itself a migration boundary: this head carries the agent schema bump **21 → 22** via `migrateTranscriptFtsRowSchema`, and the fleet serves 21, so it wants migration-success and rollback-compatibility receipts of its own. Both are maintainer-side, not gated on this PR. ### PROOFS METHOD The corpus uses a Grafana k6 proof harness for live rows; [`METHOD.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/METHOD.md) carries the exact reproducer commands for every static gate above, including both Gate 2.7 invocations and the `git merge-tree --write-tree` mergeability check. `MAX_WORKERS=1` is mandatory for the vitest reproducers — OpenClaw's fixtures are not safe under concurrent access — and two of those commands deliberately take no `--config`, because passing the wrong one silently reports "No test files found" and exits 0. `TRANSPOSED-FROM.md` records source-to-target ancestry and materiality; for this cycle it records a deliberate refusal to transpose across 520 commits and four absorbs. ## Future actions and #130741 composition Maintainer PR #130741 addresses the complementary fresh-sweep race: it captures the current `sessionId` and `lifecycleRevision` before the first await and uses those values as cleanup CAS facts. The return covenant addresses a different time axis: whether historically accepted child work may return to a logical recipient after benign successor creation. The current candidate and #130741 head `e1afc703f49a07687c0876ba6350cafa87a3638a` merge cleanly in a synthetic composition. If #130741 lands, the composed result should preserve both guarantees: - keep #130741's fresh sweep-time exact-run/session lifecycle fence; - keep the covenant's durable logical-recipient generation for historical return admission and delivery; - do not overload broad `lifecycleRevision` as historical return authority; - do not terminate or orphan accepted descendants merely because `/new` or ordinary `/reset` creates a successor session. That composition honors the maintainer repair without weakening continuation semantics or allowing a stale child return to cross a real ownership boundary. ## Why this is not a skill or a viable plugin extraction OpenClaw skills are `SKILL.md` prompt files loaded into an agent turn that already exists. They can guide work inside that turn; they do not own the turn cycle. Continuation needs gateway and agent-runtime owners a skill cannot provide: - The `continue_work` path persists pending work, enforces budgets and delay bounds, arms a timer, reacquires the session reply-run lane, and starts a later model turn after the current turn has finalized. - The `continue_delegate` path persists delegate intent, does spawn/admission accounting, manages child-session lifecycle, and durably routes returns across sessions. - `request_compaction` is an agent election into guarded runtime compaction. Later work resumes only after the runtime has established the new context boundary. - All three need durable state, cancellation/finalization ownership, restart recovery, trace identity, queue-conflict handling, and gateway scheduling outside the model invocation. A skill can tell a model to *ask* for another turn. Without those owners the ask is prose: it cannot persist a due wake, yield and finalize safely, reacquire the session lane, create the next invocation, survive a restart, or deliver a child result to another session. The implementation therefore belongs in core runtime surfaces such as `src/auto-reply/continuation/**`, `src/agents/tools/**`, `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-continuation-schedule.ts`, and `src/infra/continuation-tracer.ts`. This PR adds no `.agents/skills/**`, `SKILL.md`, or user-facing skill package. The only skill-named production change is core runtime tool dispatch. ClawHub also distributes plugins. Existing plugins can register tools, services, lifecycle hooks, context injection, plugin-owned session state, and — for bundled plugins — Cron-backed session turns. Those seams can support a smaller continuation-like automation, especially TaskFlow plus host Cron / `sessions_spawn`. They are not this feature's turn-finalization ownership, reply-run coordination, durable continuation queue, child-session return lifecycle, election capture, or agent-elected compaction contract. Compaction-provider registration and command-handler `compactCurrent()` are also not that last contract: they compact or summarize, they do not elect compaction at finalization and resume afterward. Moving policy behind a plugin boundary would first require OpenClaw to expose and stabilize a continuation-host API. The gateway/runtime would still own the mechanism described here; a plugin could only package policy around that core capability. That is not a no-core-touch alternative to these primitives. Discord is a bundled channel plugin. It owns the Discord edge, plus delivery/progress hooks into the host's existing subagent path, and submits events into OpenClaw's current turn machinery. Continuation changes that machinery: what survives finalization, which session may run next, how child results return, and when compaction can be elected. A TaskFlow tool adapter is also not a lifecycle host. It can call the core-owned `api.runtime.tasks.managedFlows` API to create, link, pause, resume, finish, cancel, and inspect durable flow records. Marking a waiting record as running does not reacquire a session lane or invoke the model; recording a `childSessionKey` created by a separate spawn surface does not spawn the child or deliver its return. There is no equivalent host continuation capability for this PR to wrap. ## Lineage and replacement context This PR is the clean replacement for closed #85651. It preserves that PR's review lineage and the earlier continuation work descended from #79925, but it does not reuse either closed PR or ask reviewers to infer the current result from them. The replacement carries a current, independently reviewable branch and a complete proof subtree bound to its presented SHA. #85651 was not abandoned because the feature failed or because we accepted its classification as a skill. It was closed after automated labeling put the change in the wrong submission category. This replacement removes that ambiguity: no `src/skills/**` change is presented, current label simulation produces no `r: skill`, and the detailed section above explains why the lifecycle mechanism belongs to core. Acceptance or rejection of the product direction remains OpenClaw's decision. The decision requested is whether OpenClaw should provide multi-session, agent-elected continuation primitives after reviewing the implementation and evidence. It is not whether the same mechanism can be relocated into a skill: a skill cannot own or implement these lifecycle boundaries.

prs.title: fix(memory): avoid rebuilding initially empty indexes after restart
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an unnecessary full memory-index rebuild after restart when the index was initially built before any content existed and later populated incrementally.

## User Impact

New memory content stays searchable across restart without repeating a completed rebuild. Existing incomplete and legacy unverified indexes still receive their required repair. No configuration, schema version, migration, tokenizer, vector dimensions, or search behavior changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

An empty semantic rebuild does not initialize the vector extension or create a vector table. Publication therefore omitted the existing vector-completeness marker. The first incremental write subsequently created the vector table and recorded its dimensions, but reopening still classified the index as unverified because its clean marker was absent.

The publication owner now treats a successful shadow rebuild with no indexed chunks as complete, using the facts already returned by its worker. This adds no read, request, cache, or alternate admission path. Later degraded writes continue to mark the index incomplete.

Removed redundant work: the full repair caused solely by an initially empty publication. Accepted edge case: the vector table remains absent until content needs it. No security checks or legacy-data completeness checks are removed.

## Evidence

The strengthened empty-bootstrap regression fails on unchanged production at the first incremental semantic write: expected `complete`, received `unverified`. Both the semantic and keyword-only cases pass with the fix. It checks completeness immediately after reopening, before repair-capable operations, and verifies that resumed indexing does not request an automatic rebuild. Existing search-result and vector/chunk equivalence assertions remain.

Gateway-main-thread database calls in the changed production owner: **0 → 0**. Memory-core also has zero T1 inventory entries. Production/test/documentation LOC: **+5/−1, +8/−0, +2/−0**. No new helper or fixture.

One frozen harness-v3 baseline/candidate pair completed all phases, including same-state restart. Base `ffcb0a8cfa75`; candidate `c1a051ff13a2`. Warm medians and ranges are across ten turns in each run. The host was loaded; no latency claim is made.

| Metric | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Warm causal SQL, median [range] | 75 [74–81] | 75 [74–81] |
| Warm causal requests, median [range] | 28 [27–31] | 28 [27–30] |
| Warm causal MAIN SQL | 0 | 0 |
| Warm raw SQL, median [range] | 76 [74–100] | 75.5 [74–84] |
| Warm raw requests, median [range] | 29 [27–34] | 28 [27–32] |
| Warm raw MAIN SQL, total across ten windows | 13 | 0 |
| Restart first-turn causal SQL / requests | 153 / 53 | 153 / 53 |
| Restart first-turn raw SQL / requests | 272 / 90 | 288 / 89 |
| Whole-workload SQL / requests / MAIN | 4,630 / 1,165 / 307 | 4,578 / 1,153 / 307 |

Memory operation attribution:

| Operation, SQL / requests | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Initial live admission | 134 / 1 | 134 / 1 |
| Shadow admission | 139 / 1 | 139 / 1 |
| First agent re-admission | 19 / 1 | 18 / 1 |
| Publication envelope | 53 / 1 | 53 / 1 |
| Agent re-admission after publication | 18 / 1 | 18 / 1 |
| Restart existing-memory admission | 13 / 1 | 13 / 1 |
| Restart publication or agent re-admission | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |

Exact-entry facts, actor hydration, entry-cache snapshot loads, row facts, and watermark reads each contributed **0 SQL / 0 requests per warmed turn in both runs** (causal and raw attribution). Causal warm means were 75.8 → 75.6 SQL and 28.4 → 28.2 requests.

Both runs published a populated shadow, so this pair does not demonstrate the historical empty-publication restart penalty or a savings figure for it. The deterministic regression covers that path. The raw first-turn change (1,312 → 870 SQL) mostly reflects 451 statements moving into the connect phase, not a memory-schema saving. No warmed-path or whole-workload saving is claimed.

Local formatting, scoped lint, and the focused regression pass. Independent Codex autoreview is clean in one round. Required PR CI and security passed at `c1a051ff13a2`, including broader tests, types, source contracts, architecture and database ratchets; the separate Knip export scan reproduces only inherited findings. Its production/full-tree diagnostics exactly match [scheduled main run 38832586414](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38832586414/job/116754723413), and all six finding files remain unchanged on current main. The script export scan passes. This uses the authorized inherited-static-failure exception; no finding or baseline was suppressed. No SDK API or update-driver cell is applicable.

prs.title: fix(sessions): preserve requester identity at execution admission
prs.body:
Related: #150705.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes delegated work losing the original requester’s identity and applicable permissions across later execution and recovery.

## User Impact

New executions resolve current applicable destination policy for the authenticated requester and retain that prepared policy for their lifetime. Accepted asynchronous work survives normal source completion. Intentional delegation to a more capable agent remains supported, and conversation history remains shared.

`messages.queue.allowCollaborativeSteering` defaults to **true**. Admitted human input in the same conversation may join Alice’s active turn under Alice’s unchanged identity and prepared permissions. Bob may influence actions using permissions Alice has that Bob does not: this is an accepted product tradeoff. Bob remains the message author. Permissions are not combined, execution identity does not switch, and no causal attribution machinery is added. New delegations still resolve current destination policy for the original requester.

**With the setting false, cross-human steering is refused without queueing.** The runtime generates this exact notice without invoking the model:

> Someone else’s turn is still running, and collaborative steering is disabled. Your message wasn’t queued. Resend it as `/followup <message>` to run it afterward.
>
> Admins can enable collaborative steering with messages.queue.allowCollaborativeSteering: true.

The refusal settles pending-input and ingress custody through the existing owners. It cannot drain later or be revived by retry/recovery; history need not be deleted. The prepared admission decision survives detached Gateway preparation and is not retried as ordinary work.

**`/followup <message>` requests one new execution.** Busy sessions use the existing followup queue; idle sessions use ordinary admission while respecting already-queued work. The submitter’s authenticated identity is preserved and current policy is resolved at execution admission. The persistent queue mode stays unchanged. Runtime notices distinguish actual queue acceptance, execution start, and rejection. Native/text commands consume the prefix once, and literal `/queue` or `/stop` inside its message cannot mutate persistent settings or cancel active work. The local embedded TUI uses its existing queue and lifecycle events.

Same-requester compatibility/current-owner checks, normal followup/collect/interrupt modes, backend-unavailable fallback, approvals and explicit cancellation keep their existing contracts. This also applies to local `/steer`/`/tell` where supported. Explicit cross-session `sessions_send(mode="steer")` still refuses incompatible steering with followup guidance. A queued or injected natural-language “stop” is never a cancellation acknowledgment. No new storage, authority manager, confirmation state, or per-tool work is added.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing admission, queue, execution-authority and recovery owners carry authenticated requester facts separately from calculated policy. A new admission resolves policy; continuing work retains its prepared authority while still checking cancellation and current ownership. Existing channel, worker and transport adapters carry that decision to the actual effect. Registered transport-boundary tests and failure-phase diagnostics support that cutover. The latest fix sends the explicit followup start notice from the actual start callback before streamed output, using the existing delivery and completion owners.

### Configuration and updates

Initial configuration creation writes the default explicitly. Candidate `doctor --fix` creates missing parents and persists absent `allowCollaborativeSteering: true` through the existing backed-up, include-aware writer. Explicit true/false, including values in includes, are preserved; repair is idempotent. Ordinary reads and Gateway startup remain read-only. A supported singly owned nested include receives its repair; ambiguous/shared/external/root-level layouts keep existing refusal and owning-file guidance.

Managed package/source updates invoke candidate Doctor. Older drivers’ read-only phases cannot persist the setting there. Direct package-manager/manual/container replacement can bypass Doctor: the runtime default works immediately, and the next `openclaw doctor --fix` persists it. Existing backup, attribution, and rollback owners remain responsible for restoration.

The published v2026.10.3 updater against retained ab119 passed absent-default and include-false cells with backups, idempotence, readiness, and history. **Rollback remains unproven:** the injected-failure cell refused with `state-migrated-no-rollback` under the unknown-writer guard. Include-false also changes database generations without changing queue bytes, so queue persistence is not necessary for that condition; persisting the default can still introduce writes that trigger the guard. No bypass or rollback-success claim is made. That package proof is historical after the b76, 2f228 and 8d4e rebases; this increment does not change its persistence implementation. [Installed-updater evidence](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_b02abdb216f1d22dc54f37031a983a66).

Older accepted records lacking requester/delivery ownership remain inspectable but do not automatically replay; recovery records failure/resubmission guidance. Missing or revoked authority requires a fresh request. No schema, backfill, hash format, or retention change is introduced.

## Evidence

Current head: `e3d79b51f0a7ccfb5c1a33c8fe062c52a316830e`, on pinned main `f5b66769958835eb1ff32ee42c16d95e0978c412`. The bounded rebase retained all 40 prior commits: 38 patch-identical and two with conflict-context changes. Resolutions preserve main’s pending exec notifications and intentional recovery-test removal alongside requester recovery metadata and the operator codec type. prs.title: fix(test): preserve subprocess runtime identity
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Subprocess tests lose the runtime they intend to exercise when the development suite runs on Bun.

## User Impact

Developers running tests on Bun retain real Node coverage for npm lifecycle handoff, and the nested MCP retention test follows its parent runtime.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both changes address test runtime assumptions (bucket 2):

- `src/process/exec.test.ts` used `process.execPath` as a fixture named `node` and compared the child's version to its parent. Under Bun, that tested Bun while claiming to test Node. Resolve a real Node executable with the existing test helper and assert that npm's lifecycle child uses its canonical executable path. Keep the conflicting PATH sentinel assertion.
- `src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-retention.test.ts` removed every `OPENCLAW_VITEST*` variable. A Node parent consequently launched default Bun, and an isolated Bun child could stage another runtime. Restore the actual parent runtime and pass its exact Bun executable to the nested run. Keep the shared-worker retention and ordering assertions unchanged.

The npm census timeout did not reproduce in isolation; the incorrect executable fixture was established directly from its setup. The original retention Node comparison visibly selected and staged Bun before its nested watchdog failure. These changes correct those fixtures without asserting that every census timeout had the same cause.

Production LOC: **+0 / -0**. Test LOC: **+9 / -3** (net +6). No timeout increases or runtime skips.

## Evidence

Both touched files pass together, with all 34 outer tests passing on each runtime. The retention test also verifies both nested files and their ordering.

```sh
env -u OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME -u OPENCLAW_BUN_PATH -u CI \
  TMPDIR=/private/tmp/oc-census2 \
  OPENCLAW_VITEST_FS_MODULE_CACHE_PATH=/private/tmp/oc-census2/fix-proofs/cache/bun \
  pnpm test src/process/exec.test.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-retention.test.ts --maxWorkers=1

env -u OPENCLAW_BUN_PATH -u CI OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node \
  TMPDIR=/private/tmp/oc-census2 \
  OPENCLAW_VITEST_FS_MODULE_CACHE_PATH=/private/tmp/oc-census2/fix-proofs/cache/node \
  pnpm test src/process/exec.test.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-retention.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

| Runtime | Exec file | Retention file | Total command wall |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Pinned Bun `1.4.3-canary.1+94f8f5ffe` | 33 passed, 34.51s | 1 passed, 170.36s | 214.82s |
| Node `v26.11.1` | 33 passed, 29.49s | 1 passed, 179.07s | 222.49s |

The retention file needs a real nested two-file run to prove shared-worker lifetime; its command wall includes compilation and process startup on a loaded host.

Also passed: `oxfmt --check`, scoped `run-oxlint`, test typechecks for `agents-root` and `services`, and independent Codex autoreview through P2.

The separate untargeted census ended after 4h29m32s with infrastructure exit 2: 29 of 610 outer shards completed (1,878 passed / 42 failed / 31 skipped files). A tooling fixture timed out and retained an unverified cleanup claim; 581 planned shards were not run. This PR does not claim a green full suite. Other census failures, including the standalone `node:vm` fork repro, are tracked separately.

Exact-head CI: [run 38800328083](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38800328083) completed successfully (8m41s total wall). `checks-node-changed` passed in 263s and `checks-node-changed-boundary` in 136s. The native exact-head watcher reported green; superseded check records were excluded.

prs.title: fix #169718: memory search sync warnings hide the underlying cause
prs.body:
## Summary

- Problem: `openclaw memory search` prints `memory sync failed (search): <wrapper>` warnings built with `String(err)`, which discards `Error.cause`; the real exception (e.g. an `ERR_INVALID_STATE`/`database is not open` use-after-close underneath a wrapper) never reaches the operator, so diagnosis dead-ends at a generic wrapper message (issue #169718).
- Solution: format both background-sync warnings with a policy-free formatter that keeps the nested cause chain and error codes. The plugin-sdk's `formatErrorMessage` redacts internally, but the repo log policy is "write raw; redact only at egress", so `openclaw/plugin-sdk/error-runtime` gains a `formatErrorMessageRaw` re-export of the shared policy-free formatter and the two log-bound warnings use it without any redaction wrapper.
- What changed: `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-search-orchestration.ts`, `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-search-orchestration.test.ts`, `src/plugin-sdk/error-runtime.ts`
- What did NOT change: warning cadence, log level, and sync behavior are unchanged — only the rendered text gains the nested cause chain; masking still happens at the egress sinks (verified: the console transport renders `password=<redacted>` while the raw record keeps the full text); the neighbouring `search-bootstrap-fallback` warning keeps its `tools`-mode redaction because that text is model-bound; the `watch`-path warnings and the retired short-term-lock wrapper are out of scope.
- Data-model compatibility: logging-only change; no schema, stored-data, or index-format changes.

Fixes #169718

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Background memory sync failures during `memory search` surface as a bare wrapper string; the nested cause that explains the failure is dropped, so operators cannot tell what actually failed.
- **Real environment tested:** feat/issue-169718 worktree on current main (cc4315e0def), Node v24.20.0: (1) the shipped CLI flow — isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` + workspace, FTS-only config (`memory.search.provider: "none"`), real `memory index` + `memory search` via the built `openclaw.mjs` launcher; (2) a render probe feeding a real `node:sqlite` use-after-close error (`ERR_INVALID_STATE database is not open`, the exact error class from the issue) through the old and new warning construction.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  # Shipped CLI flow: index real notes, then search (background sync warning path is live)
  export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<isolated>/state OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE_DIR=<isolated>/workspace
  node openclaw.mjs memory index
  node openclaw.mjs memory search "release checklist" --min-score 0
  # Render probe: real node:sqlite use-after-close error through old vs new formatting
  node --import tsx render-probe.mts
  # Regression tests
  npx vitest run extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-search-orchestration.test.ts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  Render probe with a real `node:sqlite` use-after-close error (the issue's `ERR_INVALID_STATE` class) wrapped the way the sync path wraps failures:
  ```text
  real cause: ERR_INVALID_STATE | database is not open
  before: memory sync failed (search): Error: memory index maintenance failed
  after:  memory sync failed (search): memory index maintenance failed | database is not open | ERR_INVALID_STATE
  ```
  The same wrapper on the before code drops the cause entirely (`String(err)` renders only `Error: <wrapper message>`); after the fix the nested message and code are appended.
  Shipped CLI runs (real index + real search; the background sync warning path fires when the sync owner loses write admission during teardown) — before code vs this head:
  ```text
  $ node openclaw.mjs memory search "release checklist" --min-score 0
  No matches.
  # before: [memory] sync failed (search): Error: Memory database owner closed or changed before write admission
  # after:  [memory] sync failed (search): Memory database owner closed or changed before write admission
  ```
  (For single-level errors without a `cause`, only the redundant `Error: ` prefix disappears; the fix's value is the nested cause chain when one exists, as shown above.)
  Regression tests: `manager-search-orchestration.test.ts` — the two new cases fail on the before code (`AssertionError: expected ... to contain 'database is not open'`) and pass on this head; the full suite passes (19 tests).
- **Observed result after fix:** Warnings from the search sync path now include the nested cause message and code (`memory index maintenance failed | database is not open | ERR_INVALID_STATE`), so the underlying failure is visible instead of dead-ending at a wrapper message; search results, exit code, and sync behavior are unchanged.
- **What was not tested:** the issue's original 2026.9.9 short-term-lock wrapper no longer exists on main, so that exact `storage-error` line cannot be reproduced today; natural single-level failures (e.g. `database is locked`) render identically before and after. No live gateway or embedding provider was involved — the proof exercises the real search/sync code path in the memory-core extension, which is where the warnings are emitted.

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: Unit test
- Target test file: extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-search-orchestration.test.ts
- Scenario locked in: a background search sync that fails with a cause-carrying error renders the wrapper message plus the nested cause message and code in both the `search` and `search-bootstrap` warnings.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: the defect is the choice of string conversion at two adjacent log sites; driving the real manager search path with a failing sync pins the rendered warning text end to end.

## Root Cause

- Root cause: the two search-path sync warnings interpolate `String(err)`, and `String()` on an Error yields only `Name: message` — `cause` and nested codes are silently discarded.
- Missing detection / guardrail: no test pinned the rendered warning text for a cause-carrying sync failure; neighbouring warnings had already migrated to `formatErrorMessage`, leaving these two sites behind.
