prs.title: fix(ui): clarify imported insights cluster tabs
prs.body:
Fixes #80301.

## Summary

- Turns the Imported Insights cluster chips into a labeled, more prominent horizontal tab bar.
- Adds cluster counts directly to each tab so users can scan chats, sensitive clusters, and candidate signals before switching.
- Adds ARIA tab semantics with roving focus and keyboard navigation, plus focused Dreaming view regressions.

## Problem summary

Dreaming -> Diary -> Imported Insights already exposed cluster navigation, but the controls were small label-only chips. The useful counts were only visible after selecting a cluster, which made the row easy to miss and hard to scan in large imports.

## Root cause

`renderDiaryImportsSection` reused the generic diary day-chip style and rendered only `cluster.label` in each control. The memory-wiki import insight payload already carries the relevant counts, but the view did not surface them in the navigation row or provide stronger selected/focus semantics for this cluster-switching control.

## Architectural reasoning

This stays entirely in the Control UI presentation layer. The memory-wiki plugin remains the source of cluster data and ordering, the Dreaming controller contract is unchanged, and the view only formats the existing `WikiImportInsightCluster` fields. The patch does not alter runtime behavior outside the Dreaming UI, gateway/session flows, concurrency, cleanup logic, API behavior, or plugin contracts. Sort controls are intentionally not included because the issue discussion calls the exact sort dimensions a product/UX choice; preserving backend order keeps this PR narrow and reviewable.

## Testing performed

Local proof on refreshed head `ab1d6b0f92865eac250049059de1364a459b6480`:

- `pnpm test ui/src/ui/views/dreaming.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` passed: 16/16.
- `pnpm format:check -- ui/src/ui/views/dreaming.ts ui/src/ui/views/dreaming.test.ts ui/src/styles/dreams.css`
- `pnpm check:changed`
- `pnpm ui:build`
- `git diff --check upstream/main..HEAD`

GitHub Actions on `ab1d6b0f92865eac250049059de1364a459b6480`:

- Workflow Sanity #201587: success
- CI #207301: success

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Imported Insights cluster navigation is now visually prominent, labeled as `Filter by cluster`, shows useful counts in each control, and exposes correct tab selection/focus semantics.

Real environment tested: Local Windows checkout on branch `Hemant/improve-imported-insights-tabs`, Node `v22.15.0` with pnpm running under the repository install and the repo's existing engine warning. The branch was rebased onto upstream/main `11d7499db107f7669d89ead56bf2c5f5187bfe73`, and GitHub reported the PR mergeable after push.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Ran the Dreaming view Vitest file after the rebase with `pnpm test ui/src/ui/views/dreaming.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose`, then ran formatting, changed checks, diff whitespace checks, and the Control UI production build with `pnpm ui:build`. The refreshed GitHub PR checks then passed on the current head SHA.

Evidence after fix: The Dreaming view test asserts the Imported Insights cluster tab label, count-rich tab text, `role="tablist"`/`role="tab"`, `aria-selected`, `aria-controls`, roving `tabIndex`, `role="tabpanel"`, and ArrowRight keyboard navigation from Travel to Health. The production Control UI build also completed successfully, and GitHub Actions passed on the pushed head.

Observed result after fix: The focused Dreaming view test passed with 16 tests, including the keyboard navigation regression. Formatting, changed checks, whitespace checks, Control UI Vite production build, Workflow Sanity, and CI all passed.

What was not tested: I did not attach a live browser screenshot or recording from a real imported ChatGPT dataset. The visual behavior was verified through the jsdom view test harness and production Control UI build; a maintainer or contributor with screenshot upload access should attach redacted UI proof if required by review automation.

## Risk analysis

- Runtime behavior: Limited to Control UI rendering for Dreaming -> Diary -> Imported Insights.
- Concurrency/session/gateway flows: No changes.
- Cleanup/lifecycle handling: No changes.
- API behavior: No public API, gateway protocol, plugin manifest, or controller payload changes.
- Tests: Adds focused coverage for the new tab label/count semantics and keyboard navigation.
- Backward compatibility: Existing memory-wiki data contracts and backend cluster ordering are preserved.
- Developer ergonomics: The count formatter is typed against `WikiImportInsightCluster` and keeps the display logic local to the view.

## Backward compatibility

Backward compatible. Existing Imported Insights data renders through the same `wikiImportInsights.clusters` payload; this only changes presentation and accessibility semantics for the cluster selector.

prs.title: fix(trajectory): session.ended timestamp matches model.completed before cleanup
prs.body:
Closes #102014

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where trajectory exports showed `session.ended` with the same timestamp as `model.completed`, so cleanup duration looked like zero even when teardown took real wall-clock time.

## Why This Change Was Made

`session.ended` was recorded at finalize time, right after model completion, so its timestamp preceded session teardown. This PR captures the terminal payload at finalize and records `session.ended` only after attempt cleanup completes, on both the embedded runner and the Codex app-server. No new event types or exporter knobs; payload fields are unchanged, only emit timing moves from finalize into post-cleanup.

Rebased note (2026-08-26): the original branch predated the embedded-attempt lifecycle rewrite, so this was re-implemented onto current `main` (`attempt-finalize.ts` / `attempt-session-settle.ts` / `attempt-settle.ts` on the embedded side, `run-attempt-finalize.ts` / `run-attempt-cleanup.ts` / `run-attempt-turn-start.ts` for Codex). Review findings from the previous round are addressed:

- P1 "Guarantee terminal recording when Codex cleanup throws": `cleanupCodexAttempt` now records `session.ended` (captured payload, or the derived fallback) inside its `finally` block as the `codex-trajectory-terminal` step, followed by a terminal flush, so a teardown failure can no longer skip terminal recording.
- P2 "Finish startup-failure teardown before ending the session": the Codex turn-start failure path now captures the payload and records it only after binding clear, thread unsubscribe, route release, sandbox release, and shared-client lease release all finish.

## User Impact

Operators reading trajectory traces can measure real session end time versus model compute time, including cleanup latency.

## Evidence

Verified at head `0d46a743604` (current `origin/main` `636e21b1985` plus these two commits), Windows 11, Node v24.15.0.

Embedded runner tests:

```
npx vitest run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-session-cleanup.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-execution-settle.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-execution-phase.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-stream-finalize.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-result.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-finalize.media.test.ts

Test Files  16 passed (16)
     Tests  141 passed (141)
```

Codex app-server tests (new ordering coverage: `session.ended` recorded after `thread/unsubscribe` and after the one-shot client `closeAndWait`, on both the success path and the startup-failure path):

```
npx vitest run extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts -t "session.ended"

Tests  2 passed | 146 skipped (148)
```

Full `run-attempt.test.ts` A/B on this machine: 13 failures are `EBUSY: resource busy or locked, unlink *.sqlite` temp-dir cleanup flakes that reproduce identically on unmodified `origin/main` (13 failed / 133 passed baseline vs 13 failed / 172 passed with this PR's files in the same run); the failure set is identical test-for-test, so they are pre-existing Windows-only flakes, not regressions.

Revert-red check: with only the production hunks stashed, the new Codex ordering tests fail (2 failed) and the new/updated embedded cleanup tests fail (12 failed); all pass with the hunks restored.

Repo checks: `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` all clean. `oxfmt --check` clean on touched files. `pnpm check` guards pass, including the assertion SAFETY comment ratchet (the one new field uses a typed spread instead of an `as` assertion).

### Live embedded trajectory artifact (2026-08-26, this head)

Ran on this PR head (`0d46a743604`), Windows 11, Node v24.15.0, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, embedded `openclaw agent --local --json`, model `mistral/mistral-small-latest` (no Telegram / Vertex / gateway secrets).

Runtime event order from `trajectory_runtime_events`:

```
seq=0 session.started      2026-08-26T10:52:02.672Z
seq=1 trace.metadata       2026-08-26T10:52:02.680Z
seq=2 context.compiled     2026-08-26T10:52:02.741Z
seq=3 prompt.submitted     2026-08-26T10:52:02.746Z
seq=4 model.completed      2026-08-26T10:52:05.364Z
seq=5 trace.artifacts      2026-08-26T10:52:05.364Z
seq=6 session.ended        2026-08-26T10:52:05.371Z
```

`session.ended` is recorded after `model.completed` and after `trace.artifacts` (7ms delta on this short no-tool turn), matching the fixed ordering: the terminal event now carries the post-cleanup wall-clock time instead of sharing the `model.completed` timestamp.

### What was not tested

- `pnpm test` full suite and `pnpm build` artifacts beyond the local build used for the live run above (targeted suites only, per above).
- Codex app-server live run (its ordering is covered by the new harness tests instead).

## AI-assisted

Yes. Authored with Cursor/Grok assistance. Human: Stan Shih (stantheman0128). Rebase onto current main, review-finding follow-up, and live proof also Cursor.

prs.title: fix(gateway): share GitHub options preparation during reconnects
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Concurrent `sessions.github.options` calls after reconnect independently prepare the same session, then shared-receipt lookup prepares it again. These ordered metadata reads queue behind session discovery and cause options timeouts. Related: #173534.

## Change and Ownership

Share only pending durable-session preparation, keyed by published configuration identity/revision, requested agent, and session key. Each caller keeps independent cancellation, live permissions, and disposal; the last waiter releases the existing retained predicate. Incognito actors keep their caller-owned path. Settlement removes the pending entry: there is no completed cache, TTL, retry, schema change, or new configuration.

Carry that prepared read into receipt lookup instead of acquiring the session again. Both options and publication actions reuse their held owner. Standalone receipt/status reads still acquire their own owner; shared-state observation remains on readers. Identity, workspace, and disclosure checks still run around asynchronous observation. Identical durable observations share only their pending worker result. Publication, worktree-registry, repository-workspace, and database lifecycle owners clear pending entries on change; settlement evicts the entry. Private actors and maintenance contexts retain separate reads.

Production delta against the task base: +120 lines; tests: +158 lines. Growth preserves independent cancellation/release and coalesces two distinct pending operations without keeping completed snapshots. The 150-reader regression demonstrates why removing repeated acquisition also requires coalescing the resulting observation fanout. Removing ordered acquisition would lose the snapshot/invalidation boundary. The simplification removes repeated acquisition rather than layering another snapshot cache beside the existing owner.

## Reproduction and Measurement

The exact #173534 parent (`086fc5ca52d2`) and merge (`6574349e132d`) each use freshly generated synthetic state: 5,000 sessions, 6,000 retained runs, 200 approvals, 100 cron jobs, 12 projects, and 1,500 MiB logical transcript text (4.64 GB agent database). The existing restart driver pairs 150 clients, interrupts 30 held model requests, and measures five minutes of reconnect polling. Same fixture shape and command for every variant; authorized isolated Linux sandbox with CPU/memory/I/O limits and loopback ports. No production state is used.

| Version | Options requests | Timeouts | Successful p99 | All-attempt p99 | Publication writer requests |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Exact parent | 8,047 | 138 | 236.90 ms | 5,005.06 ms | 23,908 |
| #173534 merge | 8,055 | 126 | 257.03 ms | 5,004.07 ms | 1 |
| This fix (`3403dc4d8fa8`) | 8,100 | **0** | 1,772.35 ms | **1,772.35 ms** | **1** |

All baseline timeouts occur during the initial burst. This matched pair does **not** reproduce the earlier 2→55 count; the earlier report used a different baseline. It does reproduce duplicate ordered session preparation. Correlating request trace IDs with slow agent reservations finds 173 slow ordered reads for the merge run: 989,289 ms cumulative queue wait versus 39 ms execution (maximum 7,796 ms queue versus 3 ms execution). This identifies preparation queuing, not execution in the shared-state reader pool. An intermediate sharing-only run still had 111 timeouts; tracing it exposed the redundant receipt preparation removed in the final change.

The final burst has zero timeouts and zero capacity failures. All 150 clients connect. All-attempt p99 improves 2.82× versus the merge; successful-only p99 includes formerly failing slow startup requests and must not be interpreted without the timeout count. Options-attributed slow ordered reservations fall from 173 to 3, with cumulative queue wait 989,289 → 5,656 ms. A borrowed-session-only intermediate run exposed reader fanout (54 timeouts plus 34 capacity failures); it is not the final candidate. The 150-reader regression reproduced 150 observation submissions before coalescing, then one afterward, with new reads after publication and workspace-owner changes.

## Secondary Latency Control

The original driver sleeps after each response. Shared completion therefore clusters later polls: median in-flight `sessions.list` calls at arrival rise from 5 on the merge to 21 with the fix; requests per occupied 10 ms bin rise 7.01 → 31.19. Other RPCs have zero errors, but their original-run p99 rises: list 76.51 → 283.33 ms; catalog 81.27 → 289.31 ms; projects 81.81 → 289.76 ms. Warm main-thread CPU falls 605.49 → 485.68 ms per approximately five-second sample (~20%).

An additional two-minute fixed-cadence control compared the exact parent and fix using their already-recovered synthetic fixtures. It staggers 150 clients evenly over the existing five-second poll interval and samples the final minute. This isolates per-request latency from response-driven cohort synchronization; it is separate from the original five-minute reconnect result above. Each method completed 1,799 requests in the sampled minute, with zero errors on both versions:

| Method | Parent p50 / p99 | Fix p50 / p99 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| sessions.list | 0.75 / 4.32 ms | 0.68 / 4.28 ms |
| sessions.catalog.list | 3.04 / 7.25 ms | 2.31 / 6.79 ms |
| projects.list | 3.74 / 8.17 ms | 3.37 / 8.28 ms |
| sessions.github.options | 39.32 / 56.35 ms | 39.76 / 49.23 ms |

This control finds no meaningful per-request regression; the 0.11 ms projects p99 difference and 0.44 ms options median difference are noise-scale in a single paired run. The original driver remains the reconnect proof. Its higher sibling latency is consistent with the measured response-driven synchronization, not additional CPU work. These are single paired samples, not statistical confidence intervals.

## Proof and Review

Focused regression coverage proves one preparation for overlapping readers, independent cancellation/disposal, archive invalidation, fresh subsequent reads, and config revision separation even when the same config object is republished. The original sharing and revision tests failed before their respective fixes. A real retained-session regression fails when borrowed custody is ignored and passes when released custody is rejected.

Focused checks: authorization 8 passed; shared receipt reads 35 passed, plus the expanded workspace-invalidation regression passed after review; RPC/actions 47 passed; session lookup 14 passed. CI caught a stale three-argument mock expectation after adding the prepared-read argument; the failing file passes after repair. Changed-file oxfmt, core lint, and diff checks passed. An initial test import loaded production code before harness mocks; moving the import inside the test corrected all six fixture failures. One intermediate test invocation rejected source formatting changes during its compiled-worker run; final verification uses stable source.

PR CI owns broad validation; no Testbox/Crabbox was allocated and no broad local suite/typecheck/build was invoked. Focused test commands perform their normal worker-artifact preparation. Earlier authorization-only head CI passed; the borrowed-read head exposed the alias-routing mock expectation above. Exact-head [CI run 38833983805](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38833983805) passed on `3403dc4d8fa80ab24910d22453217f6542faa4be`, including broad tests, types, and lint. The required CI gate is checked before merge.

prs.body:
<!--
Optional linked context:
Add a visible `Closes #<issue-number>` or `Related: #<issue-number>` line
below this comment.

Required PR title:
type: user-facing description
Use a parenthesized scope only when it adds clarity:

Types: feat, fix, improve, refactor, docs, chore.

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.
-->

Related receiver (consolidated Windows PR): https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/pull/1692

## What Problem This Solves

<!--
Describe the concrete user, product, or operational problem.
Use one short, plain-language sentence. For fixes, prefer:
"Fixes: <what goes wrong> when <trigger or condition>."
For other changes, describe the need without inventing a bug.
Name the affected workflow, not the code-level cause.
-->

Windows Gateway compatibility monitoring currently waits for nightly reconciliation to discover newly published npm packages.

## User Impact

<!--
"User impact: <what users, operators, or developers can now do or expect>."
Lead with the concrete outcome in plain language, usually one sentence.
For internal-only changes, say there is no user-visible change; do not invent a benefit.
Keep important risks, breaking changes, migrations, and required user actions visible here.
-->

After activation, successful `openclaw` and `@openclaw/gateway-protocol` npm writes can promptly notify Windows monitoring without adding downstream validation or AI to upstream release checks. Nightly reconciliation and runtime npm-latest policy are unchanged.

**Activation is not included:** install a dedicated GitHub App only on `openclaw/openclaw-windows-node`, grant Contents write plus implicit Metadata read, and configure upstream `GATEWAY_PROTOCOL_NOTIFY_APP_ID` and `GATEWAY_PROTOCOL_NOTIFY_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`. Do not reuse Windows `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`. The receiver workflow must land on its default branch; no sender credentials or live cross-repository dispatch are proven here.

**Source assurance remains partial:** `source_commit` is sender-declared release checkout, not independently verified package source. Registry SLSA may identify the publisher tooling checkout instead. The receiver keeps that `workflowSha` separate, omits released-source inventory/diffs, and blocks automated implementation publication/handoff until independent candidate-to-exact-artifact verification exists. Dispatch acceptance does not activate remediation.

## Why This Change Was Made

<!--
Briefly explain how the change addresses the problem without repeating the impact.
Keep the body short. Leave file lists, internal acronyms, and root-cause walkthroughs
in the diff or optional <details>; include technical detail only when it explains
behavior or a material tradeoff. Do not hide risks or required actions in <details>.
-->

Capture each successfully published tarball's own version, SHA512 integrity, and release checkout. A separate optional job verifies exact-version registry metadata and sends `gateway-protocol-published` only to the Windows repository, using the agreed six-key v1 payload.

Receipt/summary failures cannot stop later npm publications; a successful protocol write remains eligible if the later core write fails. Delivery is attempted independently for each package, without automatic POST retries or npm rollback. Extended-stable readback recovery exempts only the specifically named optional notification job and still rejects other failed jobs.

## Evidence

<!--
Show the most useful proof that this change works. Screenshots, screencasts,
terminal output, focused tests, CI results, live observations, redacted logs,
and artifact links are all useful. For user-visible UI changes, follow the root
AGENTS.md "Product and validation" screenshot completion/landing gate; these other
forms of evidence do not replace the required screenshots in chat AND the PR.

Reviewers will inspect the code, tests, and CI. Use this section to make the
validation easy to understand, not to restate the diff.
Summarize what was checked and the result; note meaningful gaps. Link long output
or put it in optional <details>, keeping the useful evidence summary visible.
-->

Local proof used checksum-verified Node 24.21.0, repository-pinned pnpm 12.7.0, and isolated tooling on Windows ARM64. No published package, live Gateway, or receiver state was modified.

- `pnpm test test\scripts\gateway-publication-notify.test.ts test\scripts\openclaw-npm-resume-run.test.ts test\scripts\openclaw-npm-extended-stable-workflow.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **106 passed, 1 failed**; 43.62 seconds Vitest / 54.70 seconds wrapper wall time. All 28 sender cases passed, including actual Publish-shell sequencing with receipt/summary failures and npm failures. New summary regressions failed twice before the fix. CI seconds are not measured.
- The remaining unchanged test, `prints an executable resume command that preserves all inputs without shell expansion`, changes a newline into literal `n` on this host. `node scripts\run-vitest.mjs --config .local\gateway-tooling\baseline\vitest.config.mjs --maxWorkers=1 -t 'prints an executable resume command'`: **same failure against isolated exact HEAD sources**, 1 failed / 32 skipped. No assertion or unrelated shell owner was changed.
- `node --check scripts\gateway-publication-notify.mjs`, `git diff --check`, and formatting of all six changed files: **passed**.
- `pnpm tsgo:scripts`: **passed**.
- `pnpm lint:scripts`: **passed**, including Docker boundary and raw HTTP2 guards.
- `pnpm tsgo:test:root`: **passed all four root graphs**. `node scripts\run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.json test/scripts/gateway-publication-notify.test.ts test/scripts/openclaw-npm-resume-run.test.ts`: **passed**.
- Final `pnpm test test\scripts\gateway-publication-notify.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **28 passed**, 19.58 seconds Vitest / 30.48 seconds wrapper wall time. CI seconds are not measured.
- `node scripts\check-docs-mdx.mjs docs\reference\RELEASING.md`: **passed**. `node scripts\docs-link-audit.mjs`: **14,943 internal links checked, zero broken links**.
- `pnpm check:workflows`: pinned actionlint **passed**; pinned zizmor ran but **failed on 339 existing `ref-version-mismatch` warnings**. The touched workflow's only findings are its two unchanged `actions/download-artifact` version comments, present in baseline HEAD; none target the new job. Later checks in that wrapper did not run.
- `pnpm check:changed`: conflict-marker and line-cap checks **passed**, then the SQLite worker ratchet **failed**. `pnpm check:database-worker-ratchet --base HEAD` reproduces `Main-thread SQLite T1 total grew: 707 -> 1851` while relevant runtime sources are unchanged; Windows path classification remains a baseline limitation. Remaining changed checks were not reached.
- `pnpm check`: **not green**; an earlier run found unchanged changelog attribution errors (for example `CHANGELOG\2026.9.6.md:559`, `:643`, `:1228`, and `:4499`, `uses Thanks @steipete`) and missing ripgrep, then was stopped. Verified portable ripgrep was subsequently installed and affected targeted checks rerun; unrelated changelog entries were not edited.
- Canonical autoreview: **blocked by reviewer authentication**, not passed. The final coherent six-file run completed source verification and launched Codex, which returned HTTP 401 Unauthorized. The helper recorded `reviewer_unavailable`, `engine_failed`, `report_produced: false`. No safety controls or credentials were changed. On October 15, the author explicitly approved committing and opening this draft without completed canonical review, with this limitation documented. This exception does not waive required checks or approvals before merging.

Live registry evidence for both exact `2026.9.9` packages distinguishes publisher tooling `2b988ee83444f08ccaf37aa5e98f370726c75f6e` from signed release checkout `bcfc88812a35243893585dbeca87ca41b48272ca`; neither registry metadata nor inspected SLSA dependencies independently binds that candidate tree to the tarball. Upstream preflight receipts remain the candidate/artifact evidence, without inventing a receiver receipt verifier. prs.title: fix(config): keep deep config loading stack-safe past include resolution
prs.body:
Closes #153430

Related: #152847 (include resolution itself, already stack-safe in #152889) — this PR extends the same stack-safe contract to the loading stages that run after the resolver.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: loading a config whose deeply nested value passes `$include` resolution still crashes with an opaque `RangeError` when the resolved value reaches value merging, env substitution, or the legacy migration probes. The first iteration of this PR also reversed object key order on every substituted config (leaves were resolved in a reverse loop, and object slots record first-write order); that regression is fixed here, with a unit test pinning document key order.

## User Impact

User impact: a machine-generated config that nests deeply now fails with the normal actionable schema error instead of a stack-overflow crash from a stage after the one that already promises stack safety; nothing that was previously accepted is rejected, and persisted config key order matches the authored document.

## Why This Change Was Made

The include resolver walks documents on an explicit work stack, but every later stage still recursed. Each remaining walk now runs on an explicit work stack so document depth costs heap instead of call frames:

- `src/infra/deep-merge.ts`: `mergeDeep` and its plain-object sanitizer clone walk iteratively; prototype-key filtering is preserved.
- `src/config/env-substitution.ts`: `substituteAny` allocates object slots in source order (key order follows the document) and schedules child tasks depth-first, so `onMissing` warnings keep their original order.
- Legacy migration probes: the load-time `structuredClone(root)` calls (Node's built-in clone recurses too) are replaced by a shared iterative `deepCloneForMigrationProbe` in `legacy-config-record-shared.ts` across the models/providers/retired/config-tranche probes.

Net production growth is the shared clone helper plus the iterative walkers; no new configuration surface is added.

Competition/fix-surface note: #129403 overlaps on the env-substitution walk but does not touch the deep-merge or migration-probe clone crash points; this PR covers all three stages with tests.

## Evidence

All commands run from the PR checkout (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs` over the real CLI sources — the installed CLI runs dist and predates any local change).

**1. Full CLI chain, normal config through `$include` to merge, env substitution, migration probes, and schema (fresh config behavior).** `settings.json` is a minimal gateway block; `main.json` includes it and defines a provider whose `baseUrl` is `${PROOF_BASE_URL}/v1`:

```
$ PROOF_BASE_URL=https://proof.example.local OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/proof-153431/main.json \
    node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts config get models.providers.proof-provider.baseUrl
https://proof.example.local/v1
(exit 0)
```

**2. Full CLI chain, 600-level nested value.** `nested600.json` nests a scalar 600 levels deep under a top-level key. The chain runs to completion and the value is rejected by schema validation with the actionable error, not by a RangeError:

```
$ OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/proof-153431/nested600.json \
    node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts config get agents.defaults.timeout
OpenClaw config is invalid: /tmp/proof-153431/nested600.json
- nested600.json:1 — agents.defaults: Unrecognized key: "timeout"
- <root>: Unrecognized key: "deep"
(exit 0; the CLI reports the schema error and the next step instead of crashing)
```

**3. Depth matrix over the changed walkers** (module-level probe: build an n-level nested object, call `mergeDeep(v, v)` and `resolveConfigEnvVars(v, {})`):

| depth | recursive implementation (base 8ebc8cd021e) | this PR (iterative) |
|---|---|---|
| 4000 | mergeDeep RangeError; envSub RangeError | both OK |
| 8000 | both RangeError | both OK |
| 20000 | both RangeError | both OK |

The same matrix over the legacy migration probe clone (`findLegacyConfigIssues` -> `LEGACY_CONFIG_MIGRATION_RULES[].match` -> `deepCloneForMigrationProbe`, the load-time doctor detection path): recursive baseline RangeError at 5,000 levels; this PR completes the probe at 100,000 levels.

**4. Boundary note on depth.** At 4,000+ levels the still-recursive include resolver aborts the load before the stages this PR owns (Include resolution failed: RangeError); stack-safe include resolution is #152847's contract, delivered by #152889. See items 6-7 for the full real-loader crash-point chain and the 2,000-level end-to-end window measured after the include-resolver fix.

**5. Tests.** `src/config/env-substitution.test.ts` (19 cases: the 4,000-level no-overflow case, plus a key-order case that fails on the reversed-write implementation) and `src/infra/deep-merge.test.ts` (6 cases incl. the 4,000-level merge) are green on this head.

**6. Real-loader crash-point chain (post-Rev3 update).** Walking the real CLI load chain depth-by-depth with an isolated config (`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` / `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, synthetic values) maps every recursive crash point between the loader and the stages this PR owns, observed through a load-path probe on the real sources:

| Load stage | Observed crash depth | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| `$include` resolution (`resolveConfigIncludes`) | ~600 (2,000+ RangeError) | #152889 (stack-safe) |
| Read-path `$include` pre-scan (`containsConfigIncludeDirective`, `io.read-helpers.ts`) | 2,000 OK / 2,300+ RangeError | newly located; fixed by #153711 |
| Deep merge / env substitution / legacy migration probes | >2,300 — masked upstream on recursive baselines; isolated matrix in item 3 | **this PR** |
| `stableConfigStringify` (`runtime-snapshot.ts`) | 2,200 OK / 2,400+ RangeError | not yet fixed (family follow-up) |

**7. Full-chain proof at the new window.** On a checkout combining #152889 (include resolution) with this PR's three stages, a 2,000-level document under `agents.defaults.params` loads **end-to-end through the real CLI**:

```
$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/proof-153431/state OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/proof-153431/config/openclaw.json \
    node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/index.ts config get agents.defaults.model
test-model
(exit 0)
```

With this PR's three-stage fix removed from the same tree (recursive merge/env restored), the identical document also loads — because on a real load the recursive merge crash point sits deeper than the two masked stages above, the merge stages can only be observed through the isolated matrix in item 3. The depth-4,000 end-to-end claim therefore remains blocked by `stableConfigStringify` (item 6, last row), a recursive walker outside this PR's surface; recording it here so the family follow-up (#153708's chain) has the measured map.

**8. Doctor CLI chain over a legal deep config (real `openclaw doctor` on both baselines).** A config with an 800-level value under the schema-legal `tts.providers` catchall, run through the real CLI sources against the recursive base (origin/main `e63393bddc3a`) and this PR head, with isolated state dirs (`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` / `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`): both runs complete the full doctor flow (health checks, legacy-state detection, migration preview) with no RangeError, and the probe/merge/env stages this PR changes process the same config. At 1,300+ levels both runs abort with `Maximum call stack size exceeded` before the doctor flow completes. On the recursive baseline that abort is consistent with the merge/env/probe crash points this PR owns (item 3 matrix); on this PR head those stages are iterative, so the remaining abort sits in the still-recursive post-probe clones (the candidate `structuredClone` in `doctor-config-flow.ts`, `cloneConfigWithResolutionFacts` in `resolution-facts.ts`). The full-chain before/after delta is therefore masked by those family stages; the measured window is recorded here for the follow-up.

`tsgo` core (`tsconfig.core.json`) and the core-test shards exit 0; `oxlint` and `oxfmt` are clean on the touched files; the line-cap and assertion-safety ratchets report no violations for the touched files.

prs.title: perf(control-ui): make composer model pickers open faster
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Composer model choices take several frames to appear on first activation after a signed-in dashboard deep-link reload. The campaign recorded a 14-state reload, and its earlier interaction evidence measured 58.8 ms model-option readiness and 22.3 ms Details readiness.

**Ready for lead review.** Exact-head PR CI is green. Full UI e2e completed with 3,509 passing cases, one environment failure reproduced on baseline and current main, and one existing skipped desktop-carrier case. The lead reviews and lands this campaign PR.

## Change and User Impact

The shared composer owner presents accepted summary activation synchronously, instead of waiting for the queued native toggle. Composer surfaces declare their same-root relationship and use CSS anchors without opening a second spatial proxy. Generic live cross-root reanchoring retains its existing contract. Model selection closes through the existing overlay registry, preserving the upstream microphone migration's deletion of legacy dropdown dismissal machinery.

Catalog projection was already memoized; this adds no second projection cache. Unranked providers initially expose nine choices through the existing list/disclosure structure, keeping current/default choices first. **All models** and full catalog search retain access to every choice. Configured recommendations retain their behavior. Search assigns IDs to active descendants and updates the previous highlight and numbered shortcuts, removing list-wide DOM writes. Scoped pane bindings apply each accepted catalog result once, avoiding a warm-open pane render. Menus remain mounted at boot.

The model picker owns search focus; Effort preserves pointer typing focus. Unavailable Effort remains hidden, inert, and explicitly disabled, with the mounted control required by its private return type. The entry animation ends before closing inspects pending presentation, preserving rapid reopen/Escape behavior in WebKit. New Session fixtures use their document-owned mount helper. Details already meets the two-frame target and retains its positioning implementation.

Production source delta: **+46 lines**, 135 insertions / 89 deletions across nine modules, excluding both test extensions and test support. Growth supplies the accepted-activation/notification and same-root contracts while preserving keyboard, programmatic, and cross-root behavior. Duplicate trigger handlers, pane updates, catalog application, and list-wide writes are removed. There is no maintained benchmark diff, Gateway/schema/configuration/dependency change, or changelog edit.

## Evidence

Baseline production code `8d4e374169beb205e70986e02caa9da4d6f144b8`; candidate `2111eb5bc9278920d25599c03f7726678a79edc8`. One AWS Crabbox **cbx_843259ee1526**, **c7a.4xlarge**, run **run_ec50aff2056f7f7e56a0d5a1944acebf**. The standard catalog has **14 interleaved baseline/candidate pairs**, balanced seven AB/seven BA; the 300-model catalog has **seven interleaved pairs**, alternating AB/BA. All 42 reload samples are included. Interrupted comparisons are excluded. Both bundles are built in the pinned candidate checkout; baseline reverses the scoped production patch to the base, so the benchmark Git/build identifier is shared.

Repo Playwright Chromium, the maintained Team-scale bench (300 sessions, 30 pins, 120 people, 240 messages, 12 widgets), and campaign LoAF/mutation plus WS/RPC probes. Pre-measure one-second samples show 100% idle CPU, no swap activity, and no competing workload. Each target starts from a fresh document and real pointerdown with no held press. The posted task after the first ready rAF measures a **rendering-opportunity upper bound**, not an exact compositor timestamp.

All values are milliseconds, **median (IQR width)**.

| Interaction | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Standard model: first option ready | 58.05 (1.50) | **14.10 (0.10)** |
| Standard model: rendering opportunity | 66.60 (1.55) | **21.05 (0.50)** |
| 300 models: first option ready | 129.20 (5.35) | **19.20 (0.85)** |

prs.title: fix: finish compile-cache cleanup after short CLI commands exit
prs.body:
Fixes #173568

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Node's compile cache can grow far beyond its 512 MiB target when short-lived CLI commands exit before cleanup finishes.

## User Impact

Explicitly cached CLI commands and release prewarming can finish promptly while detached cleanup continues. Maintenance prunes the combined release cache toward 512 MiB and 4,096 files, with seven-day expiry. A large backlog needs multiple bounded passes; concurrent writers can temporarily exceed these targets. Node permission mode continues to skip maintenance.

## Why This Change Was Made

The old unreferenced worker died with the CLI after advancing the hourly timestamp, before the full directory walk and sort had reached any deletion. Cleanup now survives that exit, streams and prunes incrementally, and advances the timestamp only after a completed pass. A filesystem lock serializes cleanup; abandoned locks become recoverable after five minutes. Each invocation examines at most 16,384 entries and stops scheduling scan/prune work after 30 seconds. The retained-file bound prevents tiny entries from consuming unbounded metadata or starving later entries on subsequent passes. Eviction prefers the oldest files observed so far; it does not require a complete inventory first.

Captured facts in detached work: the build-qualified path is immutable cache identity and its namespace/type boundaries are checked by the child; permission mode is checked before launch; application preloads are stripped and child caching is disabled; the child reads the current completion timestamp and lock before pruning, and file metadata during traversal; retention limits are fixed policy owned by the same module. No Gateway configuration, session binding, or credentials are used.

Simplification removes the old worker and its completion-Promise tracking. Production code grows to provide process lifetime, serialization, and bounded incremental pruning rather than leaving any of those responsibilities in callers. Exact numstat versus the merge base: production +125/-43 (net +82), tests +276/-114 (net +162), docs +17/-13 (net +4). This uses the campaign LOC escape hatch: the extra production code owns detached lifetime, serialization, and bounded incremental eviction; no unrelated deletion offsets are included.

## Evidence

PR CI is the test gate per maintainer policy. It covers the changed cache owner, its regression tests, launcher integration, type checks, and repository checks. Regression tests added or updated:

- `leaves failed pruning eligible for the next invocation` — an injected unlink failure leaves the completion timestamp unchanged, and the next invocation removes the oversized file.
- `makes bounded progress through tiny entries without claiming an incomplete pass` — a synthetic 20,000-entry inventory shrinks across two bounded passes without creating thousands of files.
- `prunes an oversized cache after the packaged command exits` — a deterministic IPC barrier holds cleanup until the launching CLI exits, then verifies deletion of a sparse 600 MiB entry.
- `remains synchronously importable from CommonJS bundles` — bundles and imports the real helper to protect the build boundary exposed by the first CI run.
- Existing combined-release size/age retention, neighboring-cache preservation, symlink boundaries, Node permissions, and preload isolation remain covered.

Changed-file `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json node-compile-cache.mjs src/infra/node-compile-cache.test.ts test/openclaw-launcher.e2e.test.ts`, `oxfmt`, and `git diff --check` pass. Precommit and prescribed branch Codex autoreviews are both scoped-clean at P0–P2 with no actionable findings. The repository-local review executable is absent, so both used the installed canonical autoreview helper with the requested private temporary directory and review flags. Tests, typechecks, production negative controls, and live Gateway/Crabbox/Testbox proof were intentionally not run locally under the maintainer proof override. No leases were allocated. Local test wall time is therefore not measured; CI owns execution evidence.

The initial CI run ([38831336877, UI shard 7/7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38831336877/job/116751039521)) found a PR-caused CommonJS build failure from top-level await. The follow-up removes top-level await, guards the direct-entry path before evaluating `import.meta.url`, and adds the CommonJS regression. On corrected head `1b54e5760119454cc6a688769b5e74d9a3c93492`, [CI run 38832426683](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38832426683) has passed the formerly failing UI shard. The [cache test job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38832426683/job/116754334960) passed all 13 cache tests (3.26 s Vitest duration, 5.59 s wrapper wall time). The [launcher job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38832426683/job/116754334504) passed all 135 launcher tests (28.323 s test time, 30.40 s Vitest duration); the new cleanup-after-CLI-exit case took 100 ms. The full exact-head CI run completed successfully: 43 jobs passed, 26 skipped, and no failures, including production/test type checks and lint. ClawSweeper has acknowledged the PR; no P0–P2 code findings were posted as of this verification.

prs.title: fix: preserve standalone CLI profiles and settle Doctor shutdown
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Standalone CLI re-execution passed the loose runtime's `runtime/openclaw.mjs` operand back into the compiled executable, which parsed it as a command. `cli-invocation.mjs` now owns both executable identity and argument shape: loose `<runtime> <entry> <args>` versus standalone `<exe> <args>`. It uses the embedded builder fact for the current executable and the adjacent manifest for another executable, without hashing. CLI respawns and runtime CLI children consume this owner; registered embedded child programs keep their own dispatch protocol. Compile-cache workers and the bootstrap module are included in the appropriate embedded/package inventories.

Doctor had two further defects. A snapshot failure could be swallowed by optional inspections, yielding a false completion, and the compiled process could remain stuck behind a native cleanup barrier after SIGTERM. Execution completion and physical resource closure are now settled independently. Confirmed broker startup refusal releases undispatched resource claims only after the broker process and pipes close; operation errors retain the transport needed for cleanup. Doctor reports snapshot failures, exits nonzero, and stops admitting inspections after cancellation while preserving maintenance restoration.

## Sandbox contract

The reported allocation error occurred before SQLite snapshot allocation: the sandbox denied the spawn broker's AF_UNIX bind at `$TMPDIR/oc-br-*/resource.sock`. **Both loose and standalone Doctor use this broker**, through `sqlite-snapshot-staging-owner` and `worker-native-lifecycle`. A same-source loose Doctor control reproduced the denial. The earlier passing loose verifier exercised version/help and a direct SQLite import, not that Doctor path.

After `(deny network*)`, allow only local IPC under the isolated temporary root:

```scheme
(allow network-bind
  (local unix-socket (subpath (param "ISOLATED_ROOT"))))
(allow network-outbound
  (remote unix-socket (subpath (param "ISOLATED_ROOT"))))
```

IP networking, operator home, Keychain, launchctl, and host SQLite remain denied. Use a short canonical temporary root for Darwin's Unix-socket path limit. `docs/install/standalone.md` documents the requirement.

## Evidence

Signed production-pinned builds at `4aa64f9ddc294` passed both JIT and bytecode qualification. These are exact artifact identities, not claims that later source-only repairs were rebuilt.

| Proof | JIT | Bytecode |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Direct explicit-profile Doctor | exit 0, 32.092 s | exit 0, 4.433 s |
| Relocated sandbox, private IPC allowed | exit 0, 31.580 s | exit 0, 5.404 s |
| Same sandbox, private IPC denied | exit 1, 22.252 s | exit 1, 2.610 s |
| SIGTERM after failure, full process-tree settlement | exit 143, 364 ms | exit 143, 375 ms |

The original 60-second command limits are unchanged. Original loose Doctor printed false completion and stayed alive for 90 seconds, but SIGTERM already worked there; the original compiled process required SIGKILL. The fix does not claim an OS-level signal or Atomics defect.

The paired explicit-profile campaign passed config, Doctor, two Gateway generations, agent turns, restart, and stop: strict proof 402.053 s, 181/179 observed JIT/bytecode workers, zero disk-JavaScript execution; functional proof 4/4 rounds per mode in 1088.723 s. Delayed audit covered 453 owned PIDs with no owned or uncertain crashes. Builds and per-run state were retired after proof under the shared-disk policy; logs, JSON, and manifests remain.

Focused owner regressions cover invocation, embedding, broker startup refusal, resource settlement, snapshot propagation, cancellation, and maintenance restoration. Eighteen files passed with `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`; full build passed in 426.232 s. Independent Codex review is clean through P2. Later repairs also passed negative controls, focused tests, types, lint, format, and independent review: native-exit shutdown classification (19 transport/stderr tests, 35.654 s; exact CI Node 24.19 auth pair, 36.246 s), and the complete `doctor` readiness-command receipt (7 tests, 28.207 s). The source execution argv is unchanged by the receipt repair.

Reproduce either signed production-pinned mode:

```sh
node scripts/verify-standalone-doctor.mjs /path/to/standalone-output
node scripts/verify-standalone-doctor.mjs /path/to/standalone-output --deny-local-ipc
node scripts/verify-standalone-doctor.mjs /path/to/standalone-output --interrupt-on-snapshot-failure
```

The script APFS-clones the artifact, uses isolated state and an explicit profile, and preserves normal startup respawn. The interrupt case requires exit 143 and process-tree cleanup within two seconds. There is no Doctor skip, timeout increase, or interpreter fallback.

## CI and integration

Head `9617855492767` integrates main `172aae503c51c`. Exact-head CI [38833042547](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38833042547) passed: 172 successful jobs, 19 skipped, zero failures, including the aggregate gate. The tested merge `58c3b87a8594` has the prepared main/head parents and the same tree as the PR head. No CI exception or rerun was used. Previous head `4ba5b010dcc62` completed with 168 successful jobs, 19 skipped, and three failed extension bundles plus the gate. Scheduled main had no matching jobs, so no automatic inheritance classification or admin exception was used.

The browser, voice-call, and Synology failures reproduced on the actual main parent `44998b0afc07`. Main `172aae503c51c` fixes lifecycle cleanup lost behind an activity-cancelled browser sweep, scopes the voice fixture's worker-retirement assertions to its own workers, and restores Synology's fake timers before native shutdown. Telegram's relevant cases passed normal local replays; a controlled 1.25-second initialization delay exposed the one-second readiness assumption, and the repaired registration barrier passed all three delayed cases without changing deadlines or shutdown assertions.

That repair passed 53 focused cases, extension production/test types, lint, format, and independent Codex review through P2. Negative controls prove the browser regression catches a lost close and the voice assertion catches omitted database retirement. After integrating main's GC changes, voice and Synology passed again in 48.817 s and 44.409 s. The final rebases preserve the reviewed patch byte-for-byte. Historical investigated local failures remain in native review evidence, including a Node wire timeout whose original cause was not established; later exact-head CI passed that case.

The builder parent #172802 has merged, so this PR targets main. Desktop packaging #172569 consumes the shared invocation API and owns daemon migration. Stacked #173473 owns remaining standalone entry-discovery consumers and their separate live qualification.

prs.title: fix(ui): sidebar stays half-open during mobile swipes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: swiping right on mobile web can leave a clipped, non-interactive slice of the sidebar over the conversation while your finger is still down.

## User Impact

A deliberate right-swipe opens the full navigation drawer without waiting for finger release. Short drags and vertical scrolling leave the chat clear; tapping outside still closes navigation. This intentionally replaces continuous finger-tracking with the existing snap-open animation. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The gesture owner now commits the existing full-drawer opening once the existing horizontal-distance threshold is crossed, rather than painting an inert partial reveal. The obsolete drag-only styling is removed; modal/input/overflow guards and shell-owned focus behavior remain in place.

Worked on by:
- @vincentkoc

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/5c2c399d-74ff-45b6-b97e-42d083b9441b)

## Evidence

- **Before-fix reproduction:** held-swipe regression fails on the parent revision because navigation remains closed with a partial drawer visible before touchend.
- **Browser E2E:** 6 cases pass, including portrait (393 × 852), landscape (852 × 393), short/vertical gestures, full opening before touchend, scrim closing, focus/search, and safe-area/viewport coverage. `pnpm test ui/src/e2e/native-nav-responsive-layout.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 62.42 s wall, 8.54 s test execution; hosted CI seconds not yet available.
- **Unit tests:** 4 existing modal/focus cases pass. `pnpm test ui/src/app/nav-drawer-swipe.runtime.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 12.35 s wall.
- **Trusted browser touch input:** Chromium CDP touch replay passes short-drag, vertical-scroll, held-right-swipe, and tap-outside scenarios; all recorded touch events are trusted browser input.
- **Checks:** UI typecheck, targeted type-aware lint/stylelint/format, docs MDX sanity, and `git diff --check` pass.
- **Independent review:** Codex autoreview completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- **Limits:** mocked Gateway data, not a physical iPhone/Safari capture. No live Gateway restart or deployment. Hosted CI remains separate from these local results.

### Before — held swipe

prs.title: refactor(ui): simplify page rendering and derivations
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Several migrated pages still route Solid-only callers through custom-element bridges, while repeated derivations and expanded JSX obscure the rendering path.

## Solution

Render Search, Skills, dashboard previews, and plugin install actions directly in Solid. Search uses the existing native model picker. The install action keeps its imperative dismissal method because the plugin page uses it for keyboard dismissal.

Memoize schema fields, capabilities, selected portals, artwork, and library text. Simplify board loading branches, duplicate Systems menu items, redundant plugin fragments, and static prop spreads. Compatibility-notice link labels remain reactive when the locale changes; the existing locale-switch test now also checks the translated link label.

No user-visible layout change. Host tags, classes, routes, controls, keyboard behavior, lazy boundaries, and iframe/sidebar lifetimes are preserved. Domain owners remain plain TypeScript. Live bridges still serving imperative or raw-element callers remain.

## Scope and size

This PR changes **20 paths, including 17 production paths: 6,155 → 6,106 lines (−49)** against integrated main `49193738769d6cbbb57e310821997a649c1ddeca`.

Current head: `2f5c5ed28eaa6b54e696e50bb018989a1cafbece`. Main was integrated with ordinary merges. That integration was conflict-free, had no overlaps in the 20 authored paths, and includes main's stale mock-baseline repair `6a066e906845b89daf00c4edc68f860ad1fae43d`. No authored dependency, stylesheet, or startup-module changes.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Source and review | Fresh isolated review of all 20 authored paths and Claws/plugin dismissal callers: no actionable P0–P2 findings. Reviewed tree `70a7ad56245cf7662088428f79c3bb00182a7a00` matches this head. Root inspection and whitespace checks passed. |
| UI types | Fresh `pnpm tsgo:ui` passed once on this exact tree. |
| Focused browser proof | **26 Chromium cases passed** once: 17 primary Search cases and 9 configuration lifecycle cases, 2.21 s, `--maxWorkers=1`. |
| Repaired baseline ratchet | `pnpm check:test-mock-exports --base 49193738769d6c` passed: 9,524 grandfathered factories. |
| Production Knip | Prior integration passed with no new ignores. Latest main updates package scripts only, with no dependency or lockfile changes; Knip was not repeated for the main-only merge. |
| Full CI | Exact-head `ci:full` [run 38825188351](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38825188351) passed: **39 successful jobs, 26 skipped, zero failed**. |
| Startup | Current-head paired CI performance check passed: **349,506 B startup JS gzip / 8 requests**, **45,871 B startup CSS gzip / 1 request**. Chat boot JS −102 B, New Session boot JS −100 B, CSS and request counts unchanged. Tested merge `ac1881d73accee3335bc81f3476069c0116af74d` over main `885bd760863bd582fb17f22cae53ac690bd68d2b`. The log does not print paired-base startup JS bytes. |
| Visual proof | No visible markup/layout change, so no new screenshots under the polish-wave rule. |

The previous head's CI run 38821518774 failed only because its merged main tree had removed a Codex protocol-validator mock before pruning the baseline entry. Main's repair above deletes precisely that stale entry; the current ratchet and full CI pass. No UI test failed in that run. Historical setup-only Overview/Details/cron attempts are not claimed as passing tests.

## Native landing blocker

Both coordinator-authorized push → immediate preparation → auto-recovery sequences have completed without a merge request being dispatched. The first was refused because the now-repaired baseline ratchet made the required CI gate red. The second entered admission with a pending gate and passed merge verification, but GitHub's mergeability settled outside the qualified auto-admission states before dispatch. Native recovery stopped at 2026-10-15 23:59 UTC with:

> stale admin head retirement requires MERGEABLE/BLOCKED or MERGEABLE/BEHIND auto admission

After the API reset the head was **OPEN / MERGEABLE / CLEAN** (later `UNSTABLE`), with no auto-merge request and the green full CI above. The native Git ancestry message that the branch is behind main is separate from GitHub's required `BEHIND` projection.

The final read at 2026-10-16 00:46 UTC reports **OPEN / CONFLICTING / DIRTY**, still with no auto request. A read-only merge-tree against fetched `origin/main` confirms one content conflict: `ui/src/pages/search/search-page.tsx`. The CI results above apply to the recorded head and tested merge, before this later main movement. Both explicitly authorized push/admission sequences have been used; no third push was made.

Original outcome `10179a8605814a5514c76f23fd456f0a7eff635e` and its capture remain unchanged. No policy, tooling guard, check, or receipt was altered to manufacture admission. Native operation locks are released, all child processes drained, and the source/recovery checkouts remain in place as instructed. Landing now requires resolving the new Search conflict and a supported stale-intent retirement/admission route. The original outcome and captures have not been modified.

prs.title: fix(gateway): restore show_widget canvas previews through Tool Search history
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`show_widget` invoked through Tool Search (a `tool_call` run) renders its inline canvas live, but after a chat history reload the preview is gone: `augmentChatHistoryWithCanvasBlocks` restores nothing for these runs, while direct `show_widget` calls restore fine (#168625).

## Root cause

Two result shapes reach history that `extractChatToolResultCanvasPreview` never unwraps:

1. **Tool Search envelope row** — the outer `toolResult` row (toolName `tool_search`) carries a `{tool, result}` envelope (src/agents/tool-search.ts). The sanitizer deletes the row's `details` (no envelope key survives `projectToolResultDetails` whitelisting), so after reload the envelope survives only as the row's JSON text. The extractor read only `details.mcpAppPreview` and row-level text — the envelope JSON itself has no `kind: "canvas"`, so nothing matched.
2. **Nested tool record** — the `openclaw.nested-tool.v1` row projects a `toolResult` block whose canvas JSON sits in the block's own `content` text; the extractor never scanned nested blocks.

## Fix

In `src/gateway/chat-display-projection.canvas.ts`, add a fallback tail to `extractChatToolResultCanvasPreview` (direct-call behavior and `rawText` semantics unchanged):

- `extractCanvasPreviewFromResultRecord` — reads a target result record `{content, details}` via the existing `extractCanvasFromDetails` / `extractCanvasFromText`
- `extractToolSearchEnvelopePreview` — unwraps the envelope from `entry.details.result` while present (live path), else parses the sanitized envelope JSON text
- `extractNestedToolResultBlockPreview` — scans `entry.content` for `toolResult` blocks and applies the record reader

Everything reuses the existing extraction/dedupe machinery (`appendChatCanvasBlocks` still dedupes by viewId/url), so a preview already forwarded as content is not doubled.

## Evidence

- New focused tests in `src/gateway/chat-display-projection.test.ts` drive `sanitizeChatHistoryMessages` → `augmentChatHistoryWithCanvasBlocks` end-to-end for both shapes (envelope row post-sanitize with `details` deleted, nested toolResult block, live `details.result` unwrap). They fail on current `main` and pass with this change; no mocking of the code under fix.
- The existing placement suite ("preserves first-accepted previews") is untouched and still covers the direct `mcpAppPreview` path.
- Module-level verification of the three scenarios (red on the base commit, green on this branch, direct-call regression green) is reproduced by the committed tests.
- **Runtime proof — real Gateway, real Tool Search dispatcher, real chat-client history reload (2026-10-16):** drove a live Gateway instance (loopback; scripted local OpenAI-Responses provider so the agent loop, Tool Search dispatcher, and show_widget all run for real — nothing in the fixed path is mocked) through a full turn where the model's tool list contained only the Tool Search controls (`tool_search` / `tool_describe` / `tool_call`, plus `exec`/`process`) and the model invoked `tool_call {id: "show_widget", args: {title, widget_code}}`. The runtime executed show_widget as a nested tool activity and returned the `{tool, result}` envelope. A **fresh chat client** then reloaded the conversation through `chat.history`:
  - history rows returned: `user` → `assistant[toolCall]` → `custom[toolCall, toolResult]` (the nested show_widget activity) → `toolResult[text]` (sanitized envelope JSON) → `assistant[text, **canvas**]`
  - restored canvas block on the assistant reply: `{kind: "canvas", surface: "assistant_message", render: "url", title: "Tool Search reload chart", sandbox: "scripts", url: "/__openclaw__/canvas/documents/cv_9e55a68b9da5494eba6710078a7cbd46/index.html", viewId: "cv_9e55a68b9da5494eba6710078a7cbd46"}`
  - after a **Gateway process replacement** (SIGKILL + relaunch), another fresh client's `chat.history` reload returned the same canvas block attached to the assistant reply
  - the restored canvas document itself was still served: `GET /__openclaw__/canvas/documents/cv_9e55a68b9da5494eba6710078a7cbd46/index.html` → HTTP 200 containing the widget HTML
  - everything above ran on loopback (127.0.0.1) with synthetic content — no IPs, API keys, phone numbers, or non-public endpoints appear in the captured output; the scripted e2e harness that produced this (modeled on `test/gateway-widget-restart.e2e.test.ts`) is available as a patch on request.

- [x] Concise Evidence section included
- [x] I understand what the code does
- [x] `autoreview` skill — not available here; in its place: every new branch was reachability-checked against the real sanitizer/envelope/block bodies, the full placement regression suite still passes, and the new tests were verified red on the base commit and green on this branch
- [x] Will follow the pull request review flow after Barnacle/ClawSweeper/maintainer feedback

Fixes #168625

prs.title: feat: route additional manual Linux CI workflows through Crabbox
prs.body:
Stack order: #172670 → #173581 → #173582. Merge bottom to top; each PR targets the previous branch.

Related: #172670

## What Problem This Solves

The release-specific runner controller cannot yet dispatch standalone CI workflows or route their remaining eligible Linux jobs to Crabbox.

## User Impact

Operators can use `--workflow <file.yml> --ref <trusted-branch-or-tag> -- -f key=value` or supervise an existing manual run with `--run <id>`. Adds optional routing for 32 Linux job definitions across 12 additional workflows. Ordinary push, PR, schedule, and empty-label routing stays unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Stack 3/3, based on the Full Release Validation support PR. Reuses its provisioner and generic YAML runner anchors. GitHub API 2026-03-10 supplies the exact dispatch receipt, retained before identity verification; recovery never guesses an uncertain run. Ownership includes the exact root and positively label-identified same-ref/SHA children. Shutdown cancels newly identified children on later polls and leaves unrelated runs alone.

Native platforms, publication, short coordinators, and Telegram credentialed execution/attestation stay hosted. Linux App stays hosted because Crabbox lacks its required Ubuntu 22.04 image. CodeQL placement requires SecOps owner review. The runner-admin credential requirement from the parent still applies; no live campaign success is claimed.

## Evidence

- The initial three-layer split matched the previous reviewed PR. Follow-up review fixes are recorded below.
- Standalone receipt/adoption and routing tests passed 17 cases (4.63 seconds Vitest, 15.55 seconds wrapper); admission tests passed seven cases (10.64-second wrapper). CI seconds have not been observed.
- Actual CLI with fixture external services verified preflight precedes dispatch, JSON stdin/exact API receipt, terminal cleanup debt, cancellation of a child first labeled during shutdown polling, and preserving an unrelated active same-SHA run.
- Fresh P0/P1 review identified the late-child shutdown race; fixed and verified before the original combined push. This split preserves the fix unchanged.
- Workflow validation, targeted lint, formatting, line-cap check, diff whitespace, and docs links passed. No new release campaign dispatched.

## Review follow-up

- Applied campaign-scoped capacity labels to the additional manual workflows, matching the parent controller’s isolation contract.
- Fixed explicit manual OpenGrep base selection on merge commits; an older-base regression proves both branch changes are scanned while PR shallow-fetch recovery remains intact. The scanner already gates first-parent substitution behind an opt-in flag, which this workflow does not set.
- Updated manual concurrency fixtures and fixed standalone dispatcher argument typing. Combined focused proof: 77 cases passed in 11.01 seconds via the repository test wrapper. Root scripts typecheck, targeted lint, and workflow validation passed; CI seconds are pending the new head. Independent P0–P2 review cleared the manual scan correction.
- The parent’s runner-admin HTTP 403 still prevents live registration/campaign proof. CodeQL self-hosted placement still requires SecOps owner review.

### Fresh ClawSweeper disposition

Exact-head review confirms the manual scan defect is fixed and reports no new actionable code defect. Before merge it still requires real registration/cancellation/exclusion proof (blocked by runner-admin HTTP 403) and SecOps acceptance of optional CodeQL AWS execution. The requested SecOps team review remains pending.

### Descriptive anchor names

Replaced numbered Linux runner anchors with routing/capacity names (`linux_runner_ubuntu`, `linux_runner_hybrid_small`, `linux_runner_small`, `linux_runner_medium`, `linux_runner_large`, `linux_runner_xlarge`, and explicit Ubuntu-latest variants). Updated definitions and aliases throughout the stack. All 115 resolved workflow documents are unchanged at each layer; final routing proof passes five cases (3.73-second wrapper), workflow validation and whitespace checks pass. Previous-head review/CI evidence above remains previous-head evidence; the new changes rename anchors only.

### Latest feedback investigation

- Rechecked the real GitHub permission boundary: the active account has repository `maintain: true`, `admin: false`; listing repository runners returns HTTP 403. GitHub documents repository admin access for classic-token registration, or repository Administration (write) for fine-grained/App tokens. No credential values were printed or retained.
- Inspected Crabbox’s registration owner: `--labels` appends labels; it also retains configured/generic labels and GitHub defaults. The installed command does not expose a restricted runner-group or exclusive-label mode. The controller’s capacity labels preserve routing but do not establish workflow authorization. Live access qualification cannot be claimed from the fixture proofs.
- CodeQL is outside the Full Release Validation dispatch graph. Its optional routing belongs only to this standalone-expansion layer; the maintainer’s hosted-versus-SecOps decision remains pending.

Permission reference: [GitHub repository runner registration requirements](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/self-hosted-runners#create-a-registration-token-for-a-repository).

prs.title: fix #173199: Updates page shows status unavailable for healthy manual installs
prs.body:
## Summary

- Problem: For a healthy npm install with manual updates (auto-update schedule never enabled, nothing pending), Control UI Settings → Updates shows "Update status unavailable" while `openclaw update status` correctly reports the install as current. The `update.status` RPC omitted the discovered install identity, so the UI's `install.kind === "package"` branch never matched and the status fell through to the unavailable fallback (issue #173199).
- Solution: `getGatewayUpdateSchedule` now attaches the discovered install facts whenever the install identity is actually known (`package`, `git`, `immutable`, or a probe error), instead of only for immutable checkouts and probe timeouts.
- What changed: `src/infra/update-status-schedule.ts`, `src/gateway/server-methods/update-status-schedule.test.ts`
- What did NOT change: `unknown` install identities still publish no install facts (the status honestly reads as unavailable), and host-owned installs keep their existing projection (no install target, policy-driven `autoEnabled`). The schedule cache population, the update check flow, and the CLI `openclaw update status` path are untouched; no protocol field was removed or renamed — the RPC only stops omitting a field that was already part of the schedule shape.
- Data-model compatibility: read-side projection only; nothing is persisted differently.

Fixes #173199

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Healthy manual-update npm installs were mislabeled "Update status unavailable" in the Control UI because the `update.status` RPC dropped the install identity for exactly that healthy state.
- **Real environment tested:** feat/issue-173199 worktree on current main (5a70f529fac), Node v24.20.0, exercising the real `update.status` gateway RPC handler (`updateStatusHandlers["update.status"]`) end to end against the real update-check lifecycle with a discovered npm package install identity; no browser, no network.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  # Real RPC path: lifecycle initialized with a discovered npm package install, then the shipped handler
  npx vitest run src/gateway/server-methods/update-status-schedule.test.ts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  ✓ publishes discovered package install facts so healthy manual installs read as up to date
    → update.status result.schedule.install = { kind: "package" }
  ✓ keeps undiscovered and host-owned installs off the status schedule
    → unknown installKind: schedule.install stays absent; host-owned: unchanged projection
  Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 33 passed (33)
  ```
  On the before code, the same RPC flow returns `schedule: { channel: "stable", autoEnabled: false }` with no `install` field — the new test fails there (`expected undefined to equal { kind: 'package' }`), which is exactly the payload the issue captured. The UI mapping for this payload (`install.kind === "package"` → "Up to date") is already pinned by the existing `updates.test.ts` case at `ui/src/pages/config/updates.test.ts`.
- **Observed result after fix:** `update.status` now returns `schedule.install.kind = "package"` for a healthy npm install with no pending update, so the Updates page renders "Up to date" — matching `openclaw update status`.
- **What was not tested:** no live browser render of the Control UI (the label mapping for `install.kind: "package"` is already covered by the existing UI unit tests); git-checkout and immutable install shapes are exercised through the same projection and covered by existing tests.

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: Unit test
- Target test file: src/gateway/server-methods/update-status-schedule.test.ts
- Scenario locked in: the real `update.status` handler publishes `install: { kind: "package" }` once startup discovery has identified a package install; unknown identities stay unpublished; host-owned installs keep their existing projection.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: the defect is the producer-side gate in `getGatewayUpdateSchedule`; driving the shipped RPC handler pins exactly the payload the Control UI consumes.

## Root Cause

- Root cause: `getGatewayUpdateSchedule` attached install facts only for probe-timeout errors and immutable checkouts, so a healthy `package` install identity — the ordinary case for manual npm installs — never reached the `update.status` response.
- Missing detection / guardrail: no test covered the RPC payload for a healthy manual package install; existing UI tests only covered the already-correct rendering branch.

prs.title: fix(release): Linux channel promotion fails after a withdrawn Windows companion
prs.body:
## Problem

2026.10.4's Linux companion publication failed ([Linux App Release 38831609369](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38831609369), request 38831593145):

```
Release publication incomplete; reconcile before retry: Published Linux asset changed: OpenClaw-2026.10.3-windows-x86_64.exe
```

Before promoting a new release, `scripts/linux-app-channel.mjs` re-verifies the `linux-stable` channel's current publication (`canonical()` → `publishedManifest()`), requiring every asset in its `linuxPublication.assets` proof to still exist with the recorded ID. The current channel is 2026.10.3, whose proof lists 4 assets including `OpenClaw-2026.10.3-windows-x86_64.exe` (asset 637280297). 2026.10.3 withdrew that unplanned Windows companion by deleting it (RRI-133), so the channel can never advance. #171428 made stable closeout tolerate a withdrawn non-Linux companion (`linux-updater-manifest.mjs`), but the channel publisher kept the strict check.

## Solution

Apply #171428's rule in `publishedManifest`: Linux updater assets (AppImage, deb, `SHA256SUMS.linux-app.txt`) must remain and match; a non-Linux companion recorded in the proof may be absent (withdrawn), but if present it must still match its recorded identity. Canonical bytes, release identity and source checks are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Live data: `linux-stable/latest.json` is version 2026.10.3 with proof assets AppImage 637278755, deb 637279694, Windows exe 637280297, SHA256SUMS 637280766; `v2026.10.3` now has only the AppImage, deb and SHA256SUMS assets.
- New test `advances past a previous publication whose Windows companion was %s` in `test/scripts/linux-app-channel.test.ts`: `withdrawn` fails on the old code ("Published Linux asset changed") and passes with the fix (channel advances to 2026.9.4); `replaced` (present with new ID) and `linux-missing` (deb deleted) still refuse and leave the channel manifest unchanged.
- `pnpm test test/scripts/linux-app-channel.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 61 passed, ~12 s wall; no new processes or timers.

Blocks 2026.10.4 Linux companion publication (release tooling only; published bytes unchanged). After merge, recover with `Linux App Release Request` from `main` for `v2026.10.4`, which reuses the verified uploaded assets.

prs.title: refactor(ui): render shared avatars and session decorations with Solid
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Shared avatar callers still relied on Lit rendering during the Solid migration.

## User Impact

Avatars retain their images, fallbacks, theme artwork, geometry and lazy loading; choosing a background from None updates the retained view. No migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Native Solid avatar components now serve Solid consumers directly. Remaining Lit callers share that implementation through thin adapters. Authenticated images remain owned by the existing resource loader and DOM binding; generated faces, backgrounds and plugin artwork retain their lazy boundaries. The background slot subscribes to the existing theme owner, so choosing a background from None activates the lazy renderer without replacing application context. Coupled chat typing and forwarded avatars retain their geometry.

The completed cutover also removes the now-unused theme-icon facade and artwork mount helper. Three existing side-effect imports reach the same Solid registration directly, at the same eager or lazy locations. The avatar adapter remains because one chat renderer still uses it. An unused browser-test import exposed when the ports combined is removed without changing assertions.

Against actual landed parent `a9e86934eb289bd0e90bd15834f8a337826bb704`, the change spans 57 logical files: production **13,231 → 13,038 (−193)**, tests **6,355 → 6,584 (+229)**, CI inventory **2,231 → 2,231**. Total **21,817 → 21,853 (+36)**. Test growth includes native avatar assertions and targeted failure diagnostics.

## Evidence

Final reviewed head: `6ed1f20bca65ad0666c0e1a33ca8df6c5f8fb174`.

| Focused avatar proof | Retained unchanged-input evidence: avatars **37 passed**, welcome image browser **1 passed**, backgrounds **19 passed**, artwork browser **3 passed**. No tests were repeated for the final import/dead-code cleanup. |
| Same-machine startup pair | Main `c509d3da` → final integrated tree: **347,363 → 347,294 B JS gzip (−69 B)**, eight JS requests; **45,321 B CSS / one request** on both sides. Both `pnpm ui:build` runs and strict performance checks passed without warnings or violations. Builds took 18.09 and 17.43 seconds. |
| Final production Knip | `pnpm deadcode:knip` **passed in 141.42 seconds with no findings** on the final tree. This package command checks production files and dependencies. No new ignores were added. |
