Previous head `31913178` failed only for the unused browser-test import and aggregate gate; the final cleanup removes that import. |
| Codemod | Original pre-port logs are unavailable. Retrospective immutable-source dry runs covered nine files, 42 templates and 69 manual diagnostics. The welcome correction had a pre-edit dry run. No unresolved migration markers remain in the replacements. |

Main independently adopted native reply lines, model pickers and the lazy-error view. Ordinary merges preserve those native components together with this PR’s avatar and background renderers. The final conflicts were confined to import lists. Removing the last two `LitContent` imports completes those combined render paths; the reviewed avatar bodies remain unchanged.

Earlier full CI exposed a held-favicon teardown error. Integrated canonical fix `8e850d06` (#173491) releases and joins active callbacks before removing interception and lets late requests fall through. Its regression covers those cases. The local alternative was discarded; the helper files match canonical main. No duplicate local helper test was run.

That earlier CI also found both managed images absent from the live order after successful decode/capture checks. The runtime cause remains unresolved. Failure-only node-identity/count diagnostics preserve the exact assertion and deadline; no image-rendering fix is claimed. Later passing CI does not establish the cause.

Historical Update failures were corrected by canonical main `59d3a4a3`: the warning owner deduplicates equal strings, and the fixture now supplies distinct details. The original welcome-browser watchdog exit 143 remains an unexplained tooling gap; later focused proof passed the assertion. Prior export-aware Knip findings (`WikiPageNotUtf8Error`, `renderKbd`, `presentedProperty`) remain recorded with their original revisions and are not represented as results from the final files/dependencies scan.

prs.title: fix(update): wait for native Gateway ownership before restarting
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #173570: a systemd npm-global update from 2026.8.35 can report `restart-unhealthy` even though the updated Gateway subsequently becomes healthy.

## User Impact

Restart preparation waits for a newly activated native service to publish its Gateway ownership instead of immediately rejecting the startup gap. The fix is in the **new installation's restart preparation**, which the published 2026.8.35 updater already invokes after replacing the package, so it reaches existing 2026.8.35 users on their next update.

## Why This Change Was Made

The 2026.8.35 lock is not missing identity fields: the captured `ownerId`, `startTime`, state/config paths and native PID match. The updater stops that Gateway, installs the new package, then starts the new native service before asking it to restart. Activation precedes ownership publication. During this interval, ownership may be absent or may still describe a dead predecessor.

Only after verifying the installation root and stable live native PID, preparation waits within the existing startup allowance (45 seconds on Linux/macOS). It then uses normal lock/lease verification unchanged. A live or unknown unrelated owner is not treated as absent, and an unpublished PID never authorizes signaling. Timeouts, foreign locks and unrelated service processes still refuse.

Related diagnostic-only work: #162121 by @Bartok9 names hostname drift but does not fix this startup window; no contributor commits were replaced. Thanks to @obviyus for reporting and supplying the real-systemd upgrade reproduction. No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

## Evidence

- Frozen main `670017f9124cb27352e9806b19b3c6437b42c029`: 3 refusals / 4 real-systemd 2026.8.35 update cells. These include a 200 ms sidecar measurement and one I/O trace; they are observations, not a statistical acceptance test.
- The first cell's old Gateway lock recorded PID 1173 and start time 18276292, matching `/proc/1173/stat`. After replacement, the snapshot at `00:15:26.436Z` has `MainPID=4453`, no lock and no owner row; the lease first appears at `00:15:29.999Z`.
- At the fourth cell's outer refusal emission, the trace records:

  ```text
  2026-10-16T00:39:10.998Z  GATEWAY_RESTART_PREPARATION_REFUSED
  native service: MainPID=2216
  gateway.state.lock: pid=2046, startTime=18438825
  SQLite gateway-owner: pid=2046, mode=supervised
  ps: 2216 ... node .../openclaw/dist/index.js gateway --port 18888
  ps: no PID 2046
  ```

  This is the parent's buffered error report, not a timestamp of the original child decision. It proves the stale-predecessor shape at reporting time; the exact child-throw instant remains uninstrumented. The fix and regression cover both missing and dead ownership rather than relying on that timing inference.
- Deterministic regression holds a live native process at the selected root before ownership publication, starting with either absent ownership or a dead predecessor's lock and lease. All six cases fail on main (`settled` before `waiting`). With the fix, fresh publication permits the normally verified restart; foreign publication and timeout still refuse without signaling. Existing wrong-process, wrong-root, state/config mismatch, missing/mismatched start-time and unknown-owner refusals remain passing.
- Focused tests: **45 passed** across `restart-intent.test.ts`, `lifecycle.restart-intent.test.ts`, and `lifecycle.restart-intent-legacy.test.ts`; final changed-file rerun **18 passed**. Changed TypeScript formatting and lint pass.
- Real-systemd confirmation: published **2026.8.35 → frozen fixed package**, update **exit 0**, JSON **status `ok`**, no restart-preparation refusal, authenticated health **`ok: true`**, and the server reports build `2026.10.3-f6556c0cbb59-2026-10-16T00-44-27.902Z`. The pre-update session sentinel survives, and a post-update message is successfully injected and read back. The final review correction changes only the platform-specific test fixture; production source is identical to this frozen package.
- Addressed the review's macOS fixture finding: supervised success fixtures now use the platform's actual launchd/systemd kind and resolved service name.

Simplification: reused native installation/process verification and the existing startup budget; no new owner, fallback authorization or configuration. Production delta: +31/-4; tests: +71/-6; docs: +9/-0.

Merge danger: two-way door; reverting restores immediate refusal during startup. No schema or stored-data changes. Blast radius is native Gateway restart preparation on Linux/macOS before fresh ownership is published; malformed, unknown or unrelated ownership is still rejected.

prs.title: fix: keep task recovery working across shared Gateway updates
prs.body:
Do not merge this combined PR. It remains a draft preserving the original branch and source-bound evidence while focused replacements land.

The replacement update design is stop-first: refuse replacement while another Gateway uses the installation and tell the operator to stop it first. Automatic sibling updates are no longer part of that design. Session-identity work is being split into smaller storage, Doctor, runtime, and wire-boundary changes; the current direction uses qualified logical identities while retaining existing physical addresses and explicit adapters for published clients and durable data.

The historical landed checkpoint contains **53 named focused PRs**. It originally reported **1,824 fewer application lines**, **105 additional production-tooling lines**, and **1,719 fewer application-plus-tooling lines**. A subsequent reconstruction resolved all 53 canonical landings unambiguously and remeasured each actual first-parent diff using the same explicit classifier as the later accounting: **1,813 fewer application lines**, **103 additional tooling lines**, and **1,710 fewer application-plus-tooling lines**. Tests/support add 8,837 lines and docs add 91 under that classifier. The original per-file accounting is unavailable, so the nine-line application/tooling discrepancy remains unattributed; both figures are preserved rather than silently combined.

This historical subtotal is not the current replacement-series total, and the **overall net-negative goal is not yet established for the surviving series**. The broader campaign merge count is not this umbrella’s replacement set. A separate actual-parent measurement of 16 subsequently named landings records +5,677 application, +1,376 production-tooling, +22,006 test/support and +228 documentation lines. Another bounded measurement of #160203, #160472, #160663, #160718 and #161110 records +3,648 application, +718 tooling, +6,720 test/support, +78 docs and one explicit unclassified configuration line. Those two later sets add 7,053 and 4,366 application/tooling lines respectively. They are partial named sets, not a complete series or overall repository LOC claim.

Recent verified landings are updater runtime (#153764), chat identity cleanup (#155664), selected-session queue protection (#155714), failed-steer UI ownership (#155746), registry fixture migration (#155727), TUI/CLI session ownership (#155872), registry dependency retirement (#155796), stored-session address preservation (#155886), prepared lookup-key reuse (#156035), explicit Doctor migration policy (#156034), native restart ownership (#155355), and session-method policy consolidation (#156071). The updater-runtime landing has source-bound build, compiled-worker, binding, sealed-smoke, and published-driver qualification. Its original failed outer proof and unattributed timeout remain recorded; recovered inner evidence and diagnostic CI reruns do not relabel those failures.

Registry retirement #155796 removed 121 application lines and 13 test/support lines while preserving the existing runtime owners. Its original profile-merge test failure remains unattributed. The authorized exact-head rerun passed the target and all 152 cases in its state group on different GitHub-hosted hardware; no production fix or unrelated-flake verdict is claimed. Native merge, main ancestry, and cleanup are verified.

Stored-session address preservation #155886 landed after exact-head CI, independent review, the exact candidate package, and both actual published `2026.9.4` updater cells passed. The proof preserves session IDs, lifecycle revisions, lineage, projected history-window ownership, and transcript bytes; repeated Doctor leaves the entire captured agent state identical. The legacy `session.mainKey` field remains accepted but ignored. Its conflict case preserves canonical main while the existing repair quarantines the divergent retired-main claim. The Testbox hosting run was intentionally cancelled after successful proof and lease cleanup; it is not relabeled as green CI. The actual landed delta is +83 application, +553 test/support, and +19 documentation lines, byte-identical to the qualified candidate. Native receipt, main ancestry, and cleanup are verified.

Prepared lookup-key reuse #156035 removes 12 application lines by carrying one ordered key plan through store reads and returned targets. Its 31 focused cases passed. Initial CI timed out in two existing Doctor/config fixtures and reported a subsequent cleanup-order failure; the cause remains unattributed. One unchanged-source rerun of the original five groups passed 3,280 cases with eight skips, followed by verified native landing and cleanup. No product fix or flaky-test verdict is claimed.

Doctor migration policy #156034 makes the existing removed-default-agent choice explicit at the Doctor boundary. The landed patch adds 15 application and 49 test lines, with 19 focused cases, green exact-head CI, and both actual published `2026.9.4` updater cells passing against the exact candidate package. Repeated Doctor preserves the captured agent state. Retired-agent sibling placement is proved at the canonical-repair boundary; whole-update migration can move or quarantine retired-main claims, and whole-config byte idempotence is not claimed. The hosting run was intentionally cancelled after successful proof and verified cleanup; it remains separate from green CI.

Native restart ownership #155355 removes 752 application lines and one tooling line by using the installed Gateway CLI and verifying every attempted restart. Known-empty native metadata and retained PATH ordering now preserve eligible service rebinds without weakening authority or definition checks. Its 354 selected tests, retained 76-case owner proof, exact-head CI, exact candidate package, native candidate-to-same-candidate rebind, and genuine published `2026.9.2` upgrade are qualified. The retained recovery cases use real orchestration with simulated native manager, HTTP, and package transport; no native failed-activation recovery is claimed. Original failed acceptance, the optional continuation-row diagnostic, and cleanup warnings remain recorded. Actual-parent delta, receipt, main ancestry, and cleanup are verified.

Session-method policy consolidation #156071 removes 79 application lines from one file. One per-method map supplies the existing targeting, profile, approval, and run-start predicates with their conditional rules intact. All 31 selected existing tests passed before and after; 7,452 equivalence assertions, selected changed checks, independent review, and exact-head CI passed. The landed patch is byte-identical to the qualified delta. Native receipt, main ancestry, and cleanup are verified.

Requirement disposition (bounded updates through September 29):

- **Managed service discovery and source-build protection are landed.** [#151608](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/151608), merge `244d4419`, owns the registered-service inventory and strict Windows reader. #151463 was closed as superseded with its unique contracts and failed platform history explicitly transferred. [#152875](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/152875), merge `d09ffd22`, owns the live physical-dist build fence and selected-service failed-build recovery. Its final conflict composition passed 456 receiving cases, one existing skip, full changed checks and independent review. The maintained administrative route recorded its independently reproduced pre-existing CI planner overflow; skipped jobs were not called passing. Existing real Linux published-source-shell and Windows restoration/reassignment/disabled-start receipts retain their exact source/package identities. These establish the bounded build/recovery behavior, not whole shared-install admission.
- **Startup-only Windows discovery landed in [#151674](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/151674) (`733ceac1`).** Its exact CMD/VBS binding, private profile provenance, aggregate inventory deadline and bounded Startup state read preserve diagnostic-only discovery and never confer Scheduled Task control authority. Its landed source exactly matches the reviewed candidate and carries the landed Upper prerequisite. Native recovery and cleanup completed, preserving the original base-modified refusal. Fresh-install, explicit-start and authority component receipts remain source-bound; none is relabeled as a whole published-driver campaign pass.
- **TUI, saved-pane and bounded client identity requirements are qualified.** [#158240](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/158240) (`df5e316a`) keeps the selected agent/session owner consistent; [#158639](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/158639) (`3bdec389`) preserves saved-pane identity and leaves an ownerless raw-global pane unbound until explicit choice. [#158845](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/158845) (`bc84e282`) closes the old remembered-session/pointer-clear SQLite gap through awaited worker reads/writes/scan/CAS and joined normal shutdown, including awaited Doctor cleanup. Forced exit is not a persistence guarantee. [#159166](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159166) (`ccf4edde`) qualifies exact existing-row precedence, shipped Home fallback, immediate-send readiness and physical history/send/reply/persistence. It preserves the public alias contract; the obsolete #152895 unconditional exact-main dialect is not being revived. [#154069](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/154069) (`e0d80000`) supplies the landed projection/readiness owner work. None of these is a whole-product async-completion claim.
- **Wire and media evidence have precise boundaries.** Retained real browser→real Gateway evidence proves delayed/expired ACK handling, reconnect, successor ACK, retained selection and row update; the existing 18-case protocol/session-capability boundary additionally proves observer-versus-operation error ownership and clearing. Generic authenticated request/result/targeted-event payload preservation is separately proved. The stronger exact-event-label refinement failed amid a sessions.list/model-catalog readiness fault; that failure, unobserved label assertion and lost additional private diagnostic remain disclosed and separately routed. No observer-error banner or all-specialized-formatter claim is made. Source-bound before/after pairs for the TUI and saved-pane replacements were delivered and rendered in both destinations. All six attention images for landed #151412 were recovered, inspected and delivered in the originating task and verified rendered in the PR; historical first-delivery/capture-location uncertainty is not misrepresented as a new UI run.
- **Runtime, cancellation and exactly-once work is partly landed and partly active.** [#159632](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159632) (`0269af6f`) owns worker reply admission/FIFO/generation custody and joined release. [#159807](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159807) (`15bb24e3`) fixes mutable SessionManager rollback/view parity. [#159943](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159943) (`1fea5ee1`) preserves correlated completion custody and marker→await-onSettled→terminal ordering; [#160238](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160238) (`da51d9ed`) moves durable archive discovery/preflight to existing workers. [#160035](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160035) (`1ac31be0`) retains the shipped conditional ACP cancellation contract. [Native Stop #160203](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160203) has now landed as `fd1467d4`, qualifying the file-backed registered Stop path, source/session replacement and unknown-write custody through the existing worker. [Requester wake #160472](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160472) landed as `10e951e8`, retaining known-commit reconciliation without replay, surviving-sibling retry, restore fencing and marker→await-onSettled→terminal ordering. Both have verified complete native receipts and cleanup. [Initial requester transfer #160778](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160778) has also landed as `437572e2`, with matched merge parent/tree, all 92 reviewed postimages and complete native cleanup. Its independently attributed fixture failures and cancelled CI coverage remain explicit; this does not close ordinary announcement or Incognito work. Ordinary announcement bookkeeping, native/Incognito-only branches, prepared deletion/reset discovery, unqualified ACP/reset/conditional SDK cleanup, synchronous atomic replacement, and full retained/Incognito/session-storage execution still have named active owners and outstanding proof. The intentionally retired Tasks/TaskFlow domain is not restored. Partial worker proofs do not close remaining caller SQL, pending-input, Cron-descendant or compatibility obligations.
- **Atomic recovery remains with its dedicated owner.** Landed #158491 does not fully supersede originals [#144005](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/144005) and [#145169](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/145169). Complete config/includes, database, Workshop/plugin-resource recovery and recovered-generation publication preserving later writes/configuration/history remain under that owner’s current work. Its retained proof-loss disclosure is not erased. The separate stale-release follow-up [#160288](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160288) landed as `95414356`, with its official 2026.9.6 installed-update cell and complete native receipt; that bounded repair does not close the broader rollback requirements. This umbrella does not duplicate that implementation or close those originals.
- **Observed shared-install publication protection landed in [#160663](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160663) (`e694fa75`).** It checks known managed consumers before stopping the selected Gateway and again at publication, preserves package `--no-restart`, and grants no sibling controls. Known untouched preparation refusals retire safely so a later update can proceed; retained runtimes exclude activation control journals; common finalization adopts a recorded delegated Doctor stop. Exact-head [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36536818555), receiving tests, independent review, native merge and cleanup passed. Linux proof covers early live-sibling refusal, successful publication to an exact healthy target, untouched disjoint peers, and a published 2026.9.6 manual lifecycle upgrade. The strict native Doctor-adoption cell remains unqualified because a watcher-owned restart left that branch unexercised; controlled producer/finalizer proof is separate. macOS GUI proof preserves actual loaded-job observation across plist changes without granting selected-service authority; positive live System-domain proof remains absent. This is bounded observed physical overlap, not exhaustive discovery of every consumer. **The reference source-update script repair landed in [#161110](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/161110) (`8953498f`).** Its existing Git runtime transaction prepares privately before stopping and publishing source/dependencies/output; the last observed-consumer check follows private Git import. Exact candidate `cfe94b1e` passed 200 receiving cases, full changed checks and independent review. [Native run 36547729748](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36547729748) qualified stop refusal with the original installation intact, restoration before restart after a controlled publication fault, and ordinary success at the exact resulting target. All 80 command receipts joined and the task-owned service/account/lease were cleaned. The native administrative merge preserved three independently proved pre-existing workflow-fixture failures, the failed gate and all 67 cancelled jobs; canonical repair `c7e89bc6` is separate from product qualification. Genuine [released 2026.9.6 source proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36564324421) now establishes the exact old-script limitation and supported manual path. Actual `eb377` main/non-fast-forward and detached/locale-conflict refusals preserved PID 9387, native snapshots, all 141,282 runtime/dependency entries, and the seeded state. Neither old invocation reached dependency install or the three-argument adapter. The separate manual recovery stopped the installed-old service before selecting/building exact `cfe`; the manual build stayed stopped, Doctor restored the service, and explicit start confirmed already-running PID 14546. Real RPC build identity moved from `eb377` to `cfe`, the selected unit/environment/root/database identities stayed fixed, and the authored disabled automation, scratch and workspace were unchanged while shared schema migrated 18→19 with integrity passing. All 131 receipts joined normally and owned cleanup/provider completion passed. This closes the genuine source-installation follow-through for those exact refusals and manual recovery; it is not automatic old-script success, a published npm-tarball cell or all-state migration proof. Immediate pre-refusal source files were checked by the bound fixture but not separately exported; retained initial/post inventories and native snapshots support independent comparison. The [original setup attempt](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36557495387) remains failed; the corrected preparation used ordinary complete history and unchanged bounds. Required one-worker follow-through also passed all seven full changed test files (194 cases), with [exact costs and limits](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/161110#issuecomment-5887919665) recorded separately from earlier sharded measurements. These changes cannot patch already-running shipped scripts, and the whole stop-first umbrella requirement is not closed. Positive-live macOS System-domain proof also remains unavailable: two isolated task-owned guest attempts were cleaned, with the final attempt unable to obtain maintained guest execution because Parallels Tools were unavailable; GUI component evidence retains its narrower scope.
- **Published Windows completion and series accounting remain open, with explicit recovery continuity now proved.** The old 2026.9.3 parent still failed the unchanged command settlement bound; the loaded-addon/residual observation does not identify its active syscall or transfer backup authority. The separate [actual 2026.9.4 recovery run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36436325852), tooling `5388562f` and candidate `a68299da`, completed public repair → disabled-task public start → selected/peer continuity. This closes the post-disabled-start continuity gap only: the original automatic update still exited 1, and no whole-driver or full-matrix pass is claimed. A later bounded [native diagnostic](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36464960676), tooling `a5f20aad` against the same `a68299da` candidate, source-binds a newer-content rejection in the shipped 9.4 `getUpdateRun` callback during Windows recovery handoff, after the capability check and before normal finalizer launch. Its per-command/fixture cleanup passed, while outer Vitest descendant cleanup remained unverified. All original red campaigns remain red. Its [closure disposition](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/153643#issuecomment-5822012122) records the exact owner/caller removal and preserved restart-outcome suite; it explicitly does not claim new native Windows qualification. That resolves the historical helper disposition, not the remaining platform or whole-update contracts above.

The combined branch stays unmerged and must not be used as the next implementation base. The historical 53-PR subtotal and original source-bound evidence below remain retained; no new full-series LOC or completion claim is made. The twelve recent landings above join these 41 earlier verified replacements:

#151416, #151430, #151450, #151607, #151447, #151432, #151435, #151840, #151842, #151836, #151892, #151652, #152107, #152116, #152195, #152795, #153387, #153596, #151412, #152466, #153637, #153749, #153838, #153947, #153868, #154219, #154669, #154790, #153814, #154863, #154867, #154972, #154776, #155058, #155125, #154985, #155157, #155098, #155307, #155291, #155120.

<summary>Historical description and evidence for the original combined branch</summary>

The following describes the original branch only. Its automatic multi-Gateway behavior, LOC figures, and proof do not describe the replacement candidates or clear their remaining gates.

Related: #92241

## What Problem This Solves

Tasks can fail on missing runtime modules, remain waiting after interruption, or show another conversation's pending question or approval when Gateways share an installation or recover across updates.

## User Impact

One updater coordinates the Gateways sharing an installation while preserving each profile's service, configuration, runtime intent, verification, and decision to remain stopped. Interrupted work resumes from its latest execution transcript, equivalent completion delivery stays idempotent, and questions and approvals stay with their originating conversation. Foreground replacement survives slow startup and releases agent database leases before candidate repair.

Published 2026.9.3/2026.9.4 updaters retain their first-hop limitations: let active work finish, stop sibling Gateways sharing the installation before that initial upgrade, then restart and verify them afterward. Their original shutdown path can cancel work still active when its drain expires. Same-install system services require their deployment owner to coordinate replacement. Out-of-band package replacement while Gateways run remains outside this repair.

## Why This Change Was Made

Shared runtime publication and rollback have one owner; service policy and task state remain profile-specific. Only the origin publishes the final update result. The audit removes superseded update/Doctor paths, duplicate finalization decisions, session adapters, plist parsers, and private forwarding exports. Published-driver contracts and settlement of write-capable processes remain intact. Rotated runtime credentials reach the correct service refresh, explicit Responses strict-mode compatibility settings reach the provider, and recoverable plugin-path warnings remain in durable update history and JSON output.

Service discovery now includes macOS system/global consumers and binary plists, using one native decoder over captured bytes. External definitions retain their exact identity without granting native-service authority. Loaded or unverifiable external consumers remain protected. Malformed unrelated LaunchAgent plists no longer block updates; selected or recognizable Gateway definitions and captured OpenClaw/Clawdbot branding still require inspection when decoding fails. Positive system ownership blocks code replacement at update admission; Doctor retains its existing authority for state-only repair.

At `5dc7317102c8`, product source is reduced by **33 lines**. Including production tooling, the net reduction is **12 lines** against main `1e6ca9fe6e39`: 6,295 additions and 6,307 deletions. Tests, test support, documentation, and generated inventory are counted separately. Application deadlines and size limits are unchanged. Live ownership and write-settlement checks remain enforced. This change introduces no SQL schema migration. Published-driver upgrade evidence below covers the existing migration path. Changelog generation remains release-owned.

## Evidence

The candidate passed the native discovery/publication, Doctor ownership, systemd target, and caller-cutover regressions. The main integrations passed 216, 122, and 227 focused cases, respectively. The malformed-plist regression failed before the fix; 108 discovery, native decoder, and service-ownership cases pass afterward, with nine existing platform skips. Two complete independent P0–P2 reviews passed before the final mechanical merge; the merge resolutions and automatic overlaps were independently checked. A further focused P0–P2 review passed for the plist fix. The `5552fbe1acec` package build, tarball integrity/import graph, and exact-tarball macOS CLI/config/Gateway smoke passed with owned-process cleanup. The refreshed Linux shared-install live proof passed at `5552fbe1acec`. Full changed checks passed there; the final focused changed checks also passed at `b14038c40620` in a checkout with physical dependencies. Current-head [CI run 35292975843](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35292975843) passed at `5dc7317102c8`, including the corrected Node and UI E2E scenarios.

Retained real-provider evidence proves held-child recovery during shared-install updates, tool-result preservation across two cold restarts without command replay, duplicate-completion delivery, stale-replay refusal, and foreground replacement with all profiles preserved. Each result retains its original source and package identity; these are not described as fresh runs of the final candidate.

<summary>Live and integration evidence, including original failures</summary>

- The subsequent UI E2E failure came from a lifecycle waiting hint without a registered approval. The fixture now follows the Gateway registration order and retains every original assertion. Main independently landed the same repair plus a deferred-snapshot race check; the merge keeps that exact test. Browser-free ACK/approval controls passed 26 cases, and focused review was clean. The unchanged browser assertions passed in current-head hosted CI.
- CI at `b14038c40620` exposed four stale test expectations in one Node shard: an eager-loader forwarding name and an optional refusal argument. `57ffca32627d` repairs only those two tests; all 15 direct cases, targeted lint/formatting, and focused P0–P2 review pass. The wrapper exited 0, its 70-file evidence export verified, native cleanup reported zero errors, and the lease is completed. This retains its original source identity; the later main merge and macOS-only plist repair have separate focused proof.
- Installed-driver update at `6654812bf6af`: real provider replies, both running profiles replaced, held child resumed, one parent final, stopped profile and channel policies preserved. Published 2026.9.4 upgrade to that candidate verified removal of the old ACP chunk. Earlier published 2026.9.3 and system-service ownership cells also passed.
- The native active-child test exposed ordinary stop cancelling waiting work after drain expiry. The repair writes the existing profile- and PID-bound restart intent before the authorized stop and clears it if stopping fails. Regression failed before the fix and passed afterward; ordinary stop behavior is unchanged.
- Foreground Git update at `d96f72612042` failed with durable `doctor-failed` because the closed Gateway retained an agent database lease. Four real-server regressions failed before the final-owner retirement repair and passed afterward, including sibling ownership, pending resources, incognito handles, and fatal close failures. prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Decision credentials and tool results need regression coverage across OpenClaw and Codex when the primary model uses an API key or ChatGPT OAuth.

## User Impact

The documented setup separates primary-model authentication from the Platform API key required by Decisions. It explains both harnesses without implying that a Codex login authorizes Decision requests. Tool availability remains subject to normal tool policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

The tests exercise the real OpenAI auth policy and credential selection before the leaf credential resolver: incompatible OAuth and Sign in with ChatGPT profiles are skipped without refresh, while an explicit incompatible binding remains terminal.

Codex bridge tests assemble the real shared Decision tool schema, exercise direct and searchable tool surfaces, preserve typed success/unavailable payloads and the bridge's error classification, and propagate the caller's abort signal. The tool execution boundary is synthetic; this is not a model-driven native Codex round-trip. A test expectation was corrected to match the existing shared contract: an unavailable tool outcome maps to Codex `success: false`.

Follow-up to merged https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/172748. No production runtime changes or new config/default surfaces.

## Evidence

Feature-proof head: `4e393bb616f63a2e9d77458b33df393970ce022b` (original stack). The validation bullets below refer to that head. The current signed restack is `01093432209e18d983c2db4a290f4f63aba99623`, with the exact same three-file upper patch (stable patch ID `f08055b2551787cad90fbbab533ec1649a20b209`).

- Six focused files / 191 tests passed: OpenAI119, agent/auth17 and Codex bridge55. Includes the final explicit-Error cancellation fixture. AWS run: `run_7c91d05cca94d0b251e7b0b5ada7bb02`.
- Canonical extension test types passed on the final head using8 CPUs/~15.25 GiB RAM (2m12.6s). This resolves the earlier exit137 on the smaller box. AWS run: `run_aed0a59283e400fa024451385d1821f0`.
- Scoped Codex lint passed with0 warnings/errors and both changed test files passed formatting. AWS run: `run_de68d2d08cfc050362f0eefb5ef5dcc4`. Core test types and auth-test lint passed earlier with patch-identical source. `git diff --check` passed; independent review and scoped autoreview found no remaining actionable findings.
- Registered live test `src/decisions/openai.live.test.ts` passed through the real shared tool and OpenAI provider on the final head. Technical and billing evidence returned the correct predicate/choice/score outcomes from `gpt-6-luna`, with427/431 input tokens and0 output tokens. Only the selected Platform API key was forwarded through native secret transport; no hydration or credential files. AWS run: `run_b513116f62e3e10c8b5c335f1f58c37b`.
- Lower PR's exact-head [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38672931646) passed build artifacts, docs, production types, test types and all five core test-type shards. Overall CI is red in UI/E2E, dependency, boundary-invariant and heartbeat lanes outside these changes; no blanket green claim.
- Personally checked Codex source at `414782450952a196bbb64b1605a458c2531c47b6`: `codex-rs/model-provider-info/src/lib.rs:53–57,237–254` and `codex-rs/codex-api/src/endpoint/responses.rs:100–102,140–155`. Native inference uses Responses; Decisions remain an OpenClaw-owned shared tool capability.
- The two-auth/two-harness matrix is covered at credential policy and shared-tool bridge boundaries. Native model-driven Codex execution and remote OAuth entitlement remain unproven. Local OAuth rejection proves the supported adapter policy, not a universal remote entitlement claim.

## Landing baseline

prs.title: improve(ci): reduce macOS setup and real-time fixture cost
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Hourly CI repeats an expensive macOS dependency setup and spends five real minutes waiting for a mocked startup failure.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible product change. All 26 macOS Node files and all three Swift diagnostic outcomes remain covered. Runner labels, worker limits, deadlines, signing, and production startup tolerance are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing package-script planner now emits two balanced macOS Node rows. Historical targets retain their three-part or combined commands. The Swift diagnostic fixture uses the existing manual clock, waiting for the actual first retry registration before advancing the unchanged 300-second readiness budget. That fixture holds TestIsolation, so its real wait also delayed unrelated suites.

In [hourly 38802524013](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38802524013), the three Node jobs took 274/222/423 seconds, including 101/68/118 seconds of setup and roughly 42/42/48 seconds of checkout. Tests took 127/109/250 seconds. Two rows remove one complete checkout/setup repetition. The Swift diagnostic declaration took 306.842 seconds; avoiding its real readiness wait should save about 300 seconds. These are projected savings; the next natural hourly supplies hosted after-times. Cache policy remains unchanged because the local hardlink experiment did not establish a net setup benefit.

## Evidence

The focused routing contract passed for two-part, historical three-part, and combined targets; an exact inventory comparison preserved all 26 files once. Targeted root-tooling typecheck, lint, workflow sanity, docs links/format, and diff checks passed. Swift build-tests passed in 431.31 seconds; parse and formatting passed, and forced lint matched the existing baseline. P2 autoreview was scoped-clean.

PR CI exposed one additional package-script guard that still required three parts. Its expected width now requires exactly two; every aggregate-command, absent-extra-part, file-presence and disjointness assertion remains. The full file failed before this correction and passes all 21 tests afterward; targeted types/lint/format and a separate P2 review passed.

Native runtime execution remains for disposable macOS CI because the fixture uses AppDefaults/TestIsolation. Broad local Node row and workflow replays were intentionally interrupted when the shared host became overloaded; they are not claimed as passes. No assertions, scenarios, timeouts, or retry policies changed. No CI dispatch or rerun was used. Two direct-main pushes raced advancing main, so this uses the authorized ready-PR auto-merge fallback.

prs.title: refactor(providers): consolidate stream and catalog owners
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Provider implementations still have parallel stream settlement/framing paths,
catalog borrower protocols, and a private OpenCode Go watchdog competing with
the runner's existing liveness owner. Codex also materializes schema references
and defaults that the schema dependency and actual consumers already own.

## User Impact

Internal cleanup with existing provider features, cancellation, FIFO, security,
resource bounds and shutdown settlement retained. Ollama now reports a progress
callback failure instead of swallowing it as malformed JSON. Radius accepts
standard mixed SSE line endings. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use one owner for payload-hook settlement, sync/promise stream mapping, raw SSE
framing and bounded Ollama NDJSON. Keep vendor payload rules, EOF behavior,
reader lifetimes and transport validation local. Vertex uses existing Anthropic
thinking/output-budget policy, including authoritative listed capability overrides.

Read-only catalog loads become bounded, auth-keyed shared promises rather than
consumer-counted controllers and removable waiters. Native TypeBox reference
resolution replaces Codex's recursive schema closure/default injection; consumed
modality defaults live at the model owner. Owned finalization projections no
longer need recursive freezing; source/model/auth detachment stays.

The OpenCode Go provider uses the existing runner watchdog instead of a second
queue, pump, timer and terminal-event synthesizer. The registered-provider
integration test retains human-reported issue #93610's missing-EOF protection.
Actual cloud/cron/explicit bounds, transport first-SSE timeout and failover remain.

Net production: **609 lines removed**, excluding tests, support, fixtures,
generated files, declarations and documentation. No dependency, persisted schema,
protocol, permission or public SDK contract change. Phase E is untouched.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Read-only metadata can finish and warm the cache after all observers cancel.
  #157191/#157189 concern source review and synthetic cancellation, not a human
  actual-use failure. Each observer still cancels independently; loader deadlines,
  scoped keys, refresh, eviction and bounded cache size remain.
- A canceled observer's promise reactions can remain until the metadata load
  settles. #162516 explicitly lacked established production incidence; its
  amplified marker-retention harness does not justify a second waiter protocol.
- Unconsumed schema default annotations no longer invent response fields.
  #86639/#117382/#157080 describe compiler/materialization ownership, not a human incident
  requiring this allocation. Consumed defaults remain at their semantic owners;
  native schema validation still rejects malformed wire input.
- Private direct OpenCode Go stream invocation outside the runner has no second
  idle pump or synthesized terminal event. Real registered inference uses the
  shared watchdog; #93610 remains protected. #96518's synthetic harness does not
  require two owners. Transport timeout and native terminal/error handling remain.
- Synchronous payload hooks need not acquire an extra microtask solely from a
  forwarding adapter. Async hooks still settle before outgoing provider policy.
  #131294/#86461/#152399 provide implementation provenance, not timing incidents.
- Same-turn already-completed OAuth/realtime work follows the existing abort-race
  owner's precedence rather than another local race protocol. Real cancellation,
  startup errors, unref timers and the final credential-return abort check remain.
- A detached finalization projection is not recursively frozen for speculative
  internal mutation. Source detachment, captured auth/model facts and human
  #172837's durable completion restoration remain unchanged.

## Evidence

Targeted production and changed extension-test types passed. Runtime and Madge
cycles are both zero. SDK exports/surface checks, syntax lint, changed line caps,
formatting and diff checks passed. Fresh complete independent review found no
actionable P0–P2 findings. The moved assertion retains its explanatory invariant.

The first two focused provider/owner shards passed174 tests across15 files; the remaining
selection was stopped before repair edits. The pre-push lint-suppression
suite passed3/3. Full build remains pending; public SDK API comparison is running
against frozen refs. The isolated root-script test type graph reports an unchanged Vitest
performance-plugin type mismatch; the one changed inventory row only removes a
deleted test filename. Exact-head hosted CI is the broad proof, not a claim that
unfinished local preparation passed. The existing environment-count mismatch
(452 versus 453) was reproduced on the untouched base previously.

The assertion ratchet identified five stale allowances after the implementation
removed their casts; those exact rows are shrunk, never expanded. The broad
changed-check invocation was stopped after its unrelated SQLite ratchet made no
progress for over thirty minutes; scoped provider gates and hosted CI own the
remaining proof. No database code is changed.

Release-note context: provider-internal consolidation and visible Ollama progress
failure reporting; no live-provider, billing or general performance result claimed.

## Owned CI repairs

The first exact-head run exposed four owned jobs, not inherited failures:
`checks-node-compact-small-1-2` caught two newly eager imports outside the protected
tooling extraction; `check-test-types` caught a reader import lost by the clean

prs.title: fix(ci): macOS readiness test hangs and Node rows repeat preparation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the macOS Swift CI hang introduced by #173519 and removes duplicated worker preparation from its two-row macOS Node split. The lead reverted only the hanging Swift hunk in e24d626d775d; this correction follows that revert.

## User Impact

No product behavior, signing, cancellation, readiness budget, coverage, runner class, or worker limit changes. The exact readiness case completes instead of freezing a virtual clock, and the same 26 Node test files remain selected exactly once across two jobs.

## Why This Change Was Made

The previous fixture waited for an assumed 300 ms retry before advancing time, but initial attachment could first await a 1.5-second probe timeout. That retry gate could therefore remain unreachable with the virtual clock frozen. Initial attachment must expire before mocked service inspection starts the separate launchd startup budget; the healthy and responsive-error variants did not drive initial attachment either. The corrected test waits for an actual pending sleep, drives initial attachment, joins that inspection, and then drives the unresolved startup phase. It retains every assertion and all three outcomes. The clock helper continues to support existing exact-deadline callers.

Hourly 38823827091 also showed the two Node jobs preparing the same subprocess graph independently (64.230 and 90.077 seconds). Co-locating all runtime consumers within the invocation that already prepares the graph removes that duplicate work. The two jobs measured 416/663 seconds, including 247/465 seconds of tests. Cache extraction and unchanged fixtures also slowed, so the entire increase cannot be attributed to partitioning. Holding those other costs fixed projects about 90 seconds less aggregate work and 155 seconds less longest-job time. Actual hosted savings await the next natural hourly; no CI was dispatched or rerun. Routing documentation records the evidence and limitation.

Two direct-main pushes were rejected because main advanced; neither mutated main. This PR is the authorized fallback for those push races.

## Evidence

- Actual macOS execution of the exact GatewayProcessManagerTests case: **20 invocations, 60 parameter outcomes, 20 completed event streams, zero issues or watchdogs**. Median three-outcome body 0.999 seconds (range 0.603–2.434); the earlier real-clock case spent 306.842 seconds.
- Execution used audited temporary fixtures and the CI default profile, under an OS sandbox denying real launchctl/security execution, operator Gateway state, Keychain access and outbound networking. No app or real service was launched and signing was untouched.
- Existing exact-deadline sibling passed (0.038 seconds); native build-tests passed (112.67 seconds).
- All 21 package-script contracts and the existing current/historical macOS routing contract passed. Inventory is unchanged: 26 files exactly once, now 10/16.
- Swift formatting, package formatting, canonical docs formatting, 15,538 docs links and diff check passed. Forced SwiftLint retains the same 29 inherited findings by file/rule; it is not reported as a clean strict-lint run.
- Fresh isolated P2 review: scoped-clean, no actionable findings (confidence 0.87).

Related: #173519. This is test/helper, package-script selection and CI documentation only. The full native suite was not rerun locally; the exact previously hanging case was executed repeatedly, and the next natural hourly owns the hosted before/after measurement.


## Native inherited-red exception

CI run [38830461190](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38830461190), attempt 1, completed on exact head `19dec9cc631b2bbe79022bb8ddcefb840bbca5d3`: 159 jobs succeeded, three extension jobs failed, and their aggregate gate failed. Security passed independently. The native inherited-only admin exception is requested for these jobs; CI remains recorded as failed.

- [extensions-bundle-16-1, job116748348087](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38830461190/job/116748348087): Synology outbound-media assertions pass, then `test/setup.extensions.ts` teardown exceeds its existing 180-second hook deadline.
- [extensions-bundle-11, job116748351513](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38830461190/job/116748351513): Codex strict one-shot test expects `thread/start`, but observes only initialize/initialized/skills/list/config/read/account/read. This case passes locally on both revisions; its timing cause is unresolved and is not claimed fixed.
- [extensions-bundle-32, job116748351536](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38830461190/job/116748351536): browser transport cleanup assertions fail (0 versus1, empty close list,2versus3), and voice fixture cleanup leaves a database resource.

The inspected CI checkout is `c5ccb2ef996aef7ff095996c13657df074010b85`, with ordered parents main `f4f4b192c43fecf333dcaa299b1fdf1622903f77` and this exact PR head. Its delta from main is exactly the four reviewed files. Entire `src`, `extensions`, `scripts`, `test`, lockfile and runtime-config trees are byte-identical to main; package.json differs only in the two macOS selection strings, which these Linux extension tests do not invoke. Local selection of all four failing files reproduced the Synology, browser and voice failures on both candidate (317.90seconds) and the physical unpatched main baseline (277.95seconds), with identical totals:3failedfiles,1passedfile,2failedcases,40passed. prs.title: fix(talk): voice consults end with no reply when the primary model cannot run
prs.body:
Related: #161885

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: realtime Talk ends every turn with no reply when the agent's primary model can't run on the consult path (for example `anthropic/*` routed through `claude-cli` with no direct Anthropic API key), even though a working fallback model is configured.

## User Impact

User impact: voice consults now fall back through the agent's configured `model.fallbacks` the same way normal turns do, so Talk answers instead of going silent. Setups whose primary model works are unchanged.

This does not route consults through the CLI runtime itself; that half of #161885 is a separate change and stays open.

## Why This Change Was Made

`consultRealtimeVoiceAgent` called `runEmbeddedAgent` with a single model, so an auth `FailoverError` from the primary was never acted on. The consult now runs inside `runWithModelFallback`:

- The primary attempt passes the caller's original `provider`/`model` (often unset), so how the primary resolves is unchanged.
- Fallback candidates are tried only while no tool has run in the consult (`onAgentToolResult` sets a flag checked by `canFallbackAfterError`), so a consult that may already have acted is never replayed on another model. Aborts never fall back.
- Consults skip candidates that can only run through a subscription CLI runtime. The consult path is embedded and never dispatches to a CLI backend, so those candidates failed auth on every voice question. If no candidate can run, the configured chain is kept so the real error still surfaces.
- Each attempt defers its terminal lifecycle and the consult emits one terminal event, as chat replies already do, so a failed candidate no longer records "This turn ended before a reply".
- `createTalkClientAgentRuntime` reuses one operational run instance per `runId`. The fallback attempt re-enters the Talk runtime under the same `runId`; without this the completion claim rejects it with "The active Talk consult admission is no longer current".
- **Voice run binding across attempts (review P1).** Each attempt emits its own `run.completed`. For runs without a gateway root-work owner, the voice-session subscriber retired the run binding on the first one, before the fallback model ran. The consult now holds the run's voice completion (`client-voice-run-hold.ts`) for the whole fallback chain and releases it when the consult settles; a `run.completed` seen during the hold is deferred until then. Root-backed runs keep main's behaviour (they already ignore diagnostic completion). Since #159697, voice requests use ordinary permissions rather than a voice-specific confirmation gate, so the risk is now losing the binding that run ownership and effect capture use, not a confirmation bypass. The hold covers both.
- **Fallback attempt options (review P2).** The `run` callback now forwards `allowTransientCooldownProbe` to each embedded attempt. `isFinalFallbackAttempt` and `modelRoutingProvenance` are not part of `RunEmbeddedAgentParams` (the public runtime runs its own candidate loop and derives them there), so there is nothing to forward for those.

Rebased onto current `main` as a single commit; the earlier four commits conflicted with the move of the Talk client runtime into `client-agent-runtime.ts` and with the voice-session settlement rework.

## Evidence

- Regression tests that fail on `main` and pass here:
  - `walks the agent model fallback chain when the primary cannot run (#161885)` (consult runtime).
  - `keeps one owned run instance when a consult retries on a fallback model` (gateway Talk). On `main` it fails with "The active Talk consult admission is no longer current", the same error seen live.
  - `keeps the voice run binding when a failed attempt completes before the fallback` (consult runtime). Fails with the hold removed. The hold is not yet proven on a live call.
  - Companion tests: no replay after a tool ran; one terminal lifecycle event when a fallback answers; a subscription-CLI-only primary is skipped.
- `pnpm test src/talk src/gateway/talk src/meeting-bot extensions/voice-call extensions/facetime`: all pass except `extensions/voice-call/src/manager.test-harness.test.ts` (`PLUGIN_STATE_OPEN_FAILED`), which fails identically on unmodified `main`.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` clean.
- Live, on a macOS gateway with the fallback, admission, notice and skip changes as local patches (iOS Talk on iPhone and iPad, plus the macOS app; primary `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5` via `claude-cli`, fallback `openai/gpt-5.6-sol`): voice consults fall back and answer, with no admission refusals, no "ended before a reply" notice, and no anthropic auth attempt per question:

  ```
  model_fallback_decision decision=candidate_failed    lane=talk requestedProvider=anthropic ...
  model_fallback_decision decision=candidate_succeeded lane=talk requestedProvider=anthropic ...
  ```

- Original failure, from a 2026.9.7 gateway:

  ```
  lane task error: lane=talk durationMs=39 error="Couldn't sign in to anthropic. ... (No API key found for provider "anthropic". ...)" errorName=FailoverError runId=talk-realtime-consult-<uuid>
  OpenAI GPT-Live delegation consult failed: Couldn't sign in to anthropic ...
  ```

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw channels login` and `openclaw channels logout` could persist the entire global plugin auto-enable result while resolving a channel. An unrelated model-derived Codex activation could therefore be written to `openclaw.json` even though the user only requested channel authentication.

Closes #144972.

## Why This Change Was Made

Channel auth now gives plugin resolution the validated authored source config and commits only genuine install-on-demand config changes. Omitted-channel discovery still uses the active runtime's auto-enabled view, but that view is no longer treated as authored config.

## User Impact

Logging a channel in or out no longer enables unrelated bundled plugins or rewrites configuration solely because global auto-enable found a candidate. Channel inference, runtime-resolved account values, and install-on-demand writes continue to work.

## Evidence

Current-head update (2026-10-14, `10e57219faaeaf1895c5d53a3ac6b801205e9c55`):

- Integrated main and resolved the test conflict while preserving newer async account preparation and Gateway restart coverage. The effective contribution remains two CLI files; main movement through `5930f05a68b` does not change this scope and merges cleanly.
- The isolated channel-auth owner suite passed **19/19**, including a final committed-head run (41.41 s). Restoring main's original production logic makes the four config-preservation regressions fail for the expected reasons.
- Formatting, lint, core production typecheck, all six selected test-type graphs, and the remaining relevant source guards passed. Fresh scoped autoreview and independent committed-head review found no actionable findings.
- **Full changed validation is not entirely green:** the environment-name budget reports 455 versus 454, reproduced on an unchanged-main snapshot; unused-export scans report unrelated exports in byte-identical main files. This patch adds/removes no imports or exports. No baseline or guard was modified, and required GitHub CI remains authoritative before merge.

### Original published-revision proof

- The revised regression failed in four expected assertions on the original production code: explicit auth invoked global auto-enable, omitted-channel auth invoked it twice, and the Codex-bearing view reached the write/runtime path.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/channel-auth.test.ts` — 45 passed on the committed head.
- `pnpm test:changed` — 45 passed.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` — passed changed formatting, lint, production/test typechecks, dead-export analysis, and repository guards.
- Fresh Claude autoreview and independent exact-head Claude review found no actionable issue.
- Real built CLI proof used isolated synthetic config with an OpenAI model and configured WhatsApp channel. `openclaw channels logout --channel whatsapp` completed through the Gateway-fallback/local-cleanup path with exit 0; the config's SHA-256 was identical before and after, and no `codex` or `enabled` entry appeared.
- The same 45-test command-owner suite covers fresh catalog-backed channel installation and pending-install-record persistence; no external registry package was installed for this unrelated-write defect.

prs.title: refactor: simplify internal error handling and redundant recovery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Internal error transports and overlapping recovery owners obscure the actual failure boundary.

## User Impact

Normal supported flows retain their public results, diagnostics, security checks, crash recovery and write settlement. Previously silent cleanup/storage failures become visible through existing diagnostics. Exceptional best-effort concessions are listed below; no config, protocol, schema, dependency or permission change is intended.

## Why This Change Was Made

This maintainer-requested cleanup removes private Result-to-Error plumbing, ineffective fallback paths, duplicate catches, and synchronous verification of successful Storage writes.

The main cuts are the detached-spawn fallback, private Zalouser and setup error carriers, outbox readbacks, and managed-npm preparation envelopes. Smaller cuts remove duplicate bookkeeping retries and error shells. Previously silent storage/cleanup failures now reach existing diagnostics rather than disappearing.

Net production LOC: **506 removed** (672 added / 1,178 deleted), excluding tests, harnesses, fixtures, generated files, declarations, and separately published snapshot/CLI fixes.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Detached-only EBADF retry: human reports #2532 and #77750 show retry fails with the same inherited descriptors. Native spawn failure now surfaces once; actual Windows Job fallback, security authority and child settlement remain.
- MCP Events persistence-only retry timers: #165399 documents synthetic bookkeeping-failure proof, not a human incident requiring another retry owner. After storage repair, save the automation again or restart; the warning names those actions. Remote subscription retries remain.
- Tlon nested authentication retries: #21208 imported the feature without a cited auth-retry incident. Gateway startup and SSE reconnect already retry the operation. Invalid credentials are no longer repeated five or ten times inside those owners.
- Outbox Storage reentry guard: #162428 introduced synthetic recursive Storage fixtures, not native sessionStorage behavior or a human report. Monkey-patched recursive Storage is best effort; durable transfer staging remains.
- Outbox repeated full destination recapture: the same synchronous invocation now carries admitted destination facts. Account/Gateway/client/epoch and privacy authority still check at effects; synthetic arbitrary input replacement inside Storage no longer forces recapture.
- Outbox whole-store CAS rereads: native synchronous Storage does not run another writer during one invocation. The beforeCommit live-authority check stays; trusted own state is not repeatedly reloaded.
- Outbox successful-write readbacks: #162428's no-op/resurrection fixtures are synthetic. Successful native mutations are trusted; throwing and commit-then-throw recovery remains tested.
- Outbox repeated payload-admission checks: input is admitted once in the synchronous flow. History/account/client authority still checks at the effect.
- Update-report false-result retries: #139704 introduced outer loops; #167572 moved actual lock recovery and accepted-write reconciliation to the receipt owner. Domain refusals stay pending/retryable for a later action instead of being polled repeatedly.
- Bookkeeping catch shells: #168290 and #147379 added timing diagnostics, not evidence that typed Map/string/decoder operations need another failure boundary. Unsupported monkey-patched builtins now fail normally; external callbacks and logger isolation remain.
- Busy-spin fallback after Atomics.wait: the supported Node/Bun runtimes provide this builtin. Missing/monkey-patched Atomics now reaches the existing cleanup error owner instead of burning CPU. Signal authority and waits are unchanged.
- Duplicate synchronous Git metadata read: #39712 added the preferred live read before baked fallbacks but left the old final read. Spontaneous recovery between synchronous reads is no longer attempted; optional commit metadata remains unknown for its normal cache lifetime.
- Mattermost private fetch-hook normalization: #104594 is a retry-owner migration with synthetic proof, not an incident. Production/native Error identity remains; an injected private fetch hook throwing a non-Error is no longer normalized by this wrapper.
- OpenAI realtime same-stack Promise/void branching: #137636/#137574 describe injected failures, not actual outage evidence. Void retirement yields one microtask; shared closes, synchronous admission removal, awaited remote disposal, capacity and bounded retries remain.
- Hook adapter blanket catch: the real hook runner already logs and fail-opens ordinary handler faults. Framework or explicitly fail-closed runner errors now propagate instead of being silently hidden; security decisions are not converted to ordinary success.
- Npm archive success envelope: #138267 introduced a synthetic getter-after-cleanup assertion, not a production accessor contract. The sole internal installer returns plain data. Construct that final result inside the existing workspace callback; caller-visible success still waits for cleanup, and cleanup rejection still rejects. A hypothetical success getter now runs before workspace cleanup.
- Native audio nested normalization: #106495/#164679 introduced/refactored a private Error-to-string hop inside an existing catch, not a human non-Error native-runner incident. The native command owner produces Errors; a hypothetical replaced runner rejecting a non-Error no longer receives separate normalization here. Public transcode Outcome, reason/detail strings, timeout and workspace cleanup stay.
- Other private Result/catch cuts introduce no new recovery concession: public results and diagnostic text remain at their actual owner. Image unavailable errors retain identity; Ollama HTTP redaction remains at its transport producer; Zalouser preserves accepted receipts and credential persistence; setup preserves public unavailable/cancelled outcomes.

## Evidence

- Fresh independent P0-P2 review of the complete accumulated diff, including late npm/audio changes and all spawn test-callsite migrations: terminal scoped-clean, confidence0.84; final source verification passed. Author simplification retains existing operation owners and removes retired paths rather than adding compatibility aliases.
- Outbox owner+sibling suites: 80/80 pass. Loaded-host wrapper218.05s, Vitest171.52s; test bodies1percent.
- Current runtime import-cycle check: zero value cycles. Full static/madge proof remains pending, not claimed.
- Formatting:94 changed existing files pass; whitespace check clean. New/later files need the final format pass.
- Existing child-adapter24-case proof retained. Remaining process, plugin, provider, setup, hook, and diagnostic focused proof is PENDING.
- No new suppressions, timeouts, retries or skips. Existing suppression-inventory drift is recorded separately; no allowlist expansion.
- Late npm/audio/three-test caller delta: targeted graph types pass. Two local focused process selections expanded into cold compiled-subprocess builds and were stopped/joined before assertions; they are not passing proof. A configured Testbox attempt could not finish local source-capsule preparation in roughly16minutes, never reached allocation or payload, and was terminated. No remote proof or provider fallback is claimed. Remaining focused owners, broader types/lint, static SCC and bundled/public-SDK graph checks are exact-head hosted-CI requirements, not local passes.
- Exact-head hosted CI will be the broad gate. No live provider/Gateway proof or production-state mutation is claimed.

prs.title: fix(telegram): isolate private DM topic inbound buffers by thread id
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Messages in distinct private Telegram topics share one inbound debounce identity. Work waiting in one topic blocks another topic, and a text `/stop` in one topic discards buffered input from another.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared conversation serializer intentionally has no `scope: "dm"` case, so private bot topics fall back to the bare chat id. That same id is what session bindings look up. Changing it would stop existing private-chat bindings from matching, and a new delivery-target marker would not be honored by outbound thread selection.

Enqueue and cancellation both take their identity from the inbound debounce key. This change leaves shared peer ids and delivery targets alone, and adds a positive DM thread id only when building that key. A non-topic private DM (`scope: "dm"` with no positive thread id) still uses the bare chat id, so those messages stay one buffer.

## User Impact

Distinct private DM topics no longer block or cancel each other's buffered text. Ordinary private DMs without a topic keep the previous single-buffer behavior. Existing private-chat session bindings and outbound targets are unchanged.

## Evidence

Live run of `createTelegramInboundProcessing` (the real inbound debounce path) at `5d6eb9ad436030aac2eca7a7cb21bb93f5cbd0c4`. The debounce clock is advanced with Vitest fake timers, not a wall-clock sleep.

Two private DM topics in chat 7 were buffered separately and flushed as their own batches. Two messages in the same topic coalesced. A non-topic DM in the same chat still coalesced onto the bare chat id and did not mix with either topic.

```
HEAD 5d6eb9ad436030aac2eca7a7cb21bb93f5cbd0c4

DM_TOPIC_DEBOUNCE_PROOF {
  "keys": {
    "topic100": "7:dm-topic:100",
    "topic200": "7:dm-topic:200",
    "nonTopicDm": "7"
  },
  "dispositions": [
    { "kind": "buffered", "buffer": "debounce" },
    { "kind": "buffered", "buffer": "debounce" },
    { "kind": "buffered", "buffer": "debounce" },
    { "kind": "buffered", "buffer": "debounce" },
    { "kind": "buffered", "buffer": "debounce" }
  ],
  "flushed": [
    { "text": "beta", "thread": { "id": 200, "scope": "dm" } },
    { "text": "alpha-1\nalpha-2", "thread": { "id": 100, "scope": "dm" } },
    { "text": "plain-1\nplain-2", "thread": { "scope": "dm" } }
  ]
}

Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  1 passed (1)
```

Fixes #142107

prs.title: fix(imessage): advertise edit for the macOS 26 translation selector
prs.body:
Closes #173599

## What Problem This Solves

The iMessage message-tool discovery gated the `edit` action on the legacy `editMessage` / `editMessageItem` selectors only. A macOS 26 bridge reports `editMessageItemTranslation` instead and no legacy selector, so OpenClaw advertised no `edit` capability even though the bridge could edit.

## User Impact

`edit` is advertised again for macOS 26 iMessage bridges that report only the translation selector, so agents (and the Control UI action list) can use editing on those installs. A bridge that reports no edit selector at all still hides the action, and every other action gate is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reported `imsg status --json` payload advertises `editMessageItemTranslation: true` with both legacy flags false; the selector map is an open `Record<string, boolean>`, so this is a one-condition gap in the discovery gate rather than a contract change. The send path does not re-gate `edit` on selectors (only the poll actions do), so discovery is the single owner of this decision.

## Evidence

- Regression in `extensions/imessage/src/message-tool-api.test.ts` ("advertises edit for the macOS 26 translation edit selector"): a status with only `editMessageItemTranslation` advertises `edit`, while a status with no edit selector still omits it. Red before the change (`expected [...] to include 'edit'`), green after.
- `pnpm test extensions/imessage/src/message-tool-api.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → 7 passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` reports no new errors from these files (only the pre-existing `src/tui/tui-session-actions-test-support.ts` and `scripts/lib/runtime-import-closure.mts` drift, both untouched here); `oxlint --deny-warnings` and `oxfmt --check` clean; `git diff --check` clean.

prs.title: fix(control-ui): retain cached conversation titles on warm reload
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A warm reload could paint a cached conversation under “New session” until its live descriptor arrived, especially for a pinned conversation outside the saved sidebar page. The campaign’s seed evidence counted fourteen intermediate states for a signed-in dashboard deep-link reload; the maintained synthetic warm-reload fixture still exposed this generic-header phase.

The transcript snapshot now retains its existing label, display name, and derived title fields. The header consumes them through the pane’s existing scoped display-projection owner. Current rows retain title precedence and remain the source for session actions. The benchmark explicitly persists the selected transcript before reload and records the warm storyboard, row retention, LoAF, mutations, and RPC census.

## Evidence

Final source: `bc4193bef2ca1049e29da79e601bce7e3d15a564`. One quiet AWS `c7a.4xlarge` (16 CPUs, approximately 31 GiB), repository Playwright Chromium 153, seven interleaved AB/BA pairs, 35 ms inbound delay / 4 ms delivery spacing. Both production bundles share build identity; baseline changes only the three runtime files to merge base `dbc41ff76ba1`. Comparisons disable CDP tracing/CPU sampling; separate diagnostics supply screenshots. Values are median (IQR), milliseconds unless indicated.

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| FCP | 584.0 (16.0) | 600.0 (24.0) |
| First cached transcript row, DOM visibility | 489.8 (20.5) | 513.8 (28.7) |
| Live hello | 231.3 (14.3) | 253.1 (23.6) |
| Correct conversation header, DOM observation | 1057.0 (140.6) | 513.9 (28.7) |
| Live catch-up applied | 1588.0 (135.4) | 1634.1 (84.2) |
| Last layout shift | 3258.1 (58.0) | 3275.9 (96.9) |
| Last DOM mutation burst | 3400.9 (66.7) | 3433.5 (107.8) |
| Enabled input, DOM observation | 489.9 (20.4) | 513.8 (28.8) |
| Semantic phases | 6.0 (0.0) | 5.0 (0.0) |
| LoAF blocking | 723.0 (53.0) | 701.0 (74.5) |
| LoAF total duration | 2038.0 (96.5) | 2024.0 (124.0) |
| DOM mutation records | 5574.0 (308.0) | 5587.0 (25.0) |
| RPC count | 87.0 (0.0) | 87.0 (0.0) |

The correct header arrives with cached rows in all seven candidate runs, earlier in every matched pair (paired median gain 560.3 ms; difference of group medians 543.1 ms). All fourteen runs retain all ten cached row elements at catch-up, with zero removals. **Observed tradeoff:** FCP median is 16 ms later (584 → 600 ms), with IQR 16 → 24 ms. Cached-row/input DOM observations are about 24 ms later; five pairs delay early milestones and two improve them. Last layout-shift and mutation-burst medians are slightly later. CLS is approximately 0.00175 → 0.00143. This is a consistent title-state improvement, not a general startup, CPU, or network speedup; a small startup cost is not ruled out.

The six-to-five count uses the predeclared semantic vector: shell, sidebar, header, visible rows, enabled input, and board. It removes the generic-title phase. DOM milestones can precede paint; FCP and the inspected filmstrip are separate evidence. Large-pixel transition groups are six before and five after in this final traced pair; prior pairs had five/six and six/six. They vary with profiling/coalescing and do not establish uniformly fewer painted changes. This renderer fixture does not measure production authentication, redirects, real plugin cost, or service-worker behavior.

The largest IDBTransaction completion script in each untraced run has median duration 62 → 64 ms; its containing frame starts after cached rows are detected in the DOM in all fourteen runs. Those frames overlap FCP in 2/7 baseline and 4/7 candidate runs, so they can still delay paint. DOM readiness is not painted readiness. This does not assign the entire frame to initial transcript disk restore; native IDB/structured-clone and callback-induced UI work remain unseparated.

Proof:

- [Exact-head CI is green](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38823053106). Isolated review is clean through P2.
- Cache unit tests (31), terminal pane tests (9), native reload E2E (3), valid old-code negative control, script lint, and script types pass on this head. Native runner wall for `pnpm test ui/src/e2e/chat-cold-load-anchor.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 28.27 s. Old code fails with expected “Synthetic cold-load conversation,” received “New session.”
- Complete final-head normal-mode UI E2E: **807 files: 805 passed, 1 failed, 1 skipped; 3,510 cases passed, 1 failed, 1 skipped.** Wall time: 4485.04s (tests 94%, import 5%, transform 1%). No cases excluded. Native reload, both video-gallery variants, and update-run pass. The sole failure is QA automation setup: “Private mutation boundary is writable by another POSIX principal,” reproduced on main `631b5e86299` before product execution. Any cleanup stack belongs to that same failed case.
- Prior source `d45d77beda0f` completed 806 files: 804 passed, one failed, one skipped; 3,506 cases passed, one failed, one skipped. Its only failure is QA private-mutation-boundary setup before product execution, reproduced on main `631b5e86299`. Corrected update-run, native reload and both video-gallery variants pass. Main’s streaming benchmark #173264 landed during that long proof, requiring this rebase; both init/result paths and validators are retained, and the streaming benchmark with an extra init-script ordering assertion passes. Runtime/UI regression/fixture/docs remain byte-identical.
- Released AWS lease `cbx_fa79085e4acb`, measurement/full-suite run: https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_ee8a15969b5cfbb9263f0b2c6fb055e8 . Current-main control (released lease `cbx_1704bb181dca`): https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_0a02ed1e93d00351c456ff3beebae727 .

All seven lane leases are released with cleanup complete. No host Gateway was started.

Runtime LOC: **+17 / -1, net +16**. Requested production-stat command: **+307 / -18, net +289**, including +290 / -17 (net +273) lines of opt-in measurement tooling and guide. The growth carries missing display facts through the existing bounded cache and adds the requested scenario. Live descriptors remain necessary for current metadata/actions; genuine new or uncached conversations keep their existing title resolution. No server schema/config/protocol change or CHANGELOG edit. Release-note context: preserve a cached conversation’s header title during warm reloads, including off-page pinned sessions.
