prs.title: fix(config): retain source updates with unchanged runtime values
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes explicitly enabled plugins being rejected when a newer authored configuration resolves to unchanged runtime values.

## User Impact

Authored policy updates now reach consumers even when runtime values remain equal. Existing captured reads retain their original source; fresh reads see the replacement. Equal publications and version-only restamps remain no-ops. Display preferences and agent identities keep their narrow refresh scopes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The publication shortcut compared only runtime values and discarded meaningful source updates. Publication now compares runtime and authored policy against their recorded values and resolution provenance. The existing session-change owner combines their effects, preserving full invalidation for model-policy and in-place changes without rebuilding every session for presentation-only edits. Config hashes remain with the existing value-fact owner.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the original disabled-by-default plugin facade failure. Seven source publication/cache/capture assertions fail on the original producer while two version-only no-op controls pass.
- Five scope assertions fail on the previous PR revision; the correction passes all 71 publication/value-fact cases, including the moved and extended presentation/profile table.
- All 11 plugin-facade cases and two selected source-only secret-runtime cases passed. The remaining 38 secret-runtime cases were outside the selected scope.
- Targeted config/CLI test types, scoped lint, formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent scope review found no actionable P0–P2 findings. The subsequent hash-helper relocation was independently verified to preserve its exact body, imports and two callers.

The [exact-head hosted run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38784423856) failed in two jobs: pinned Bun setup exhausted downloads with HTTP 504 responses before tests started, and the cron registry-owner shard failed its selected/fallback provider and recurring startup-plugin cases. The aggregate CI gate failed downstream. The automated failure report marks these unknown because its scheduled-main comparison has no matching shard; preflight checkout receipts establish the exact tested merge, and direct source inspection attributes both failures to unchanged setup/account-admission owners. Landing uses the authorized inherited-failure exception, subject to native authority and review/security checks. These results are not green CI.

The cron fixtures and account-admission owners predate this change. The selected providers supply deferred runtime auth without a stored account; the recurring fixture uses a provider-config key. Later main [PR #173509](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173509) admits the latter route, while deferred runtime credentials remain subject to account admission. Those repairs stay separate from this configuration publication fix.

prs.title: refactor(search): engine-owned full-text and vector capabilities
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Search callers currently construct SQLite-specific FTS5 and vec0 operations, which prevents the admitted database adapter from owning search primitives.

## User Impact

SQLite search behavior is unchanged. This adds experimental SDK search capabilities through existing entrypoints; it does not enable PostgreSQL search, change a schema/version, or affect LanceDB.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move FTS schema/maintenance, native expressions, sqlite-vec loading, and the killable KNN child into `src/infra/database-engine`. Memory-core retains body/path retrieval, hybrid scoring, and exact fallback; standing intents retain chronology and token verification; transcript search retains branch/role visibility before LIMIT.

The [documented design summary](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5a950a8e80a5b60cd54caa7209051b5e97d14a3c/docs/plugins/sdk-overview/infrastructure.md#database-engine-adapters-experimental) describes the experimental contract. Optional `DatabaseEngineAdapter.search` binds `FullTextCapability`, `VectorCapability`, and `TextIndex`/`VectorIndex` handles at admission. Existing `fullText`/`vector` labels remain diagnostic metadata. Bundled callers migrate together; no SDK subpath is added.

P3-5b will supply PostgreSQL native `simple` + unaccent text search with `ts_rank_cd` normalization 2 and explicitly engine-local ranking, plus exact pgvector cosine. PostgreSQL capabilities remain `null` with an admission diagnostic here. ANN remains deferred; SQLite keeps its L2-candidate/cosine-rerank strategy and missing-vec exact fallback.

Carries forward #171402: clean vectors use exact encoded-embedding comparison before writes; complete replacements use scalar deletes through 32 stale IDs and one source/path-filtered scan above that threshold; session deltas retain scalar deletes across 128-row batches. Savepoint rollback, transaction-local rebuild debt, outer rollback, and repeated-ID last-write-wins stay in memory-core. Its kernel tests are unchanged from main. The added vector primitives are a prepared scalar existence lookup, `VectorCapability.prepareExists`, and a bounded ID-set expression, `idSet`. The latter reuses the canonical string-set expansion with the original JSON bytes; source/path filtering stays in memory-core. R2’s adapter schema admission changes are retained.

## Upstream integration and CI repair

Rebased onto `1bd533dfc7e40ea1e9f669203c81a359c19d333f`. Carries #173426's vector writer change into the engine owner exactly: prepare one scalar DELETE before the loop and propagate DELETE preparation/execution failures before INSERT. Deduplication and last-write-wins remain unchanged. Main's `manager-source-index-kernel.test.ts` is unchanged; `manager-vector-write.test.ts` differs only in its moved test-support import.

The two PR-caused failures from run 38823374132 are repaired: Kysely now declares the concrete native engine owners and annotates native expressions; the path-query observer uses a typed Proxy preserving SQLite iterator overloads, completion type, and lazy observation. No check is suppressed. The earlier lander repairs remain: native SQLite library transport testing at the engine owner, type-only imports to avoid cycles, observation of native `iterate()`, the moved worker entrypoint fixture, and SDK surface accounting. The old compact-test job failed during Bun download before tests; the fresh local owner suites below passed.

## Evidence

Validated commit: `5a950a8e80a5b60cd54caa7209051b5e97d14a3c`. Baseline: `1bd533dfc7e40ea1e9f669203c81a359c19d333f`. The final committed tree is the same tree captured and tested locally.

- **Byte identity:** 12,957 executions match exactly: SQL text, execution order, bindings, outputs, and errors. Includes all four FTS indexes; body/path/trigram, standing intents, transcript relevance/recent/snippets; writes, triggers, rebuilds; vec0 query/write paths, missing-vec exact fallback, dense truncation, and session deltas. Added DELETE preparation/step errors, INSERT failure, retries, and empty writes. 70 output phases and 56 coverage checks passed; native child response bytes also match.
- **Owner suites:** 374 tests across 29 files passed with `--maxWorkers=1`: memory search/standing intents (171), transcript search/index/rebuild (42), engine search/vec/loader, memory schema, KNN subprocess, vector writer, and unchanged source kernel (161). No owner skips. Wrapper inventory/closure passed another 4 selected tests across 2 files.
- **Gates:** full Kysely guardrails, both import-cycle checks, exact extension and core-infra test-type graphs, scoped formatting and four lint groups, core/extension/script production typechecks, and dialect/worker/assertion-safety/max-lines/line-cap ratchets passed. Wrapper inventory regenerated and closure verified. Canonical package-boundary preparation passed under its unchanged timeout. Full `pnpm build` passed.
- **SDK:** canonical API diff, acknowledgement and export registration checks passed; 41 → 57 exports, 16 additions plus optional `DatabaseEngineAdapter.search`, no removals or new subpaths. Existing diagnostic labels remain. API acknowledgement is `687ac9d3`; declaration-closure audit verified reusable canonical artifacts. The experimental capabilities note is in the linked SDK documentation.
- **Review:** one Codex autoreview of the complete task-owned delta from `0f4b45e1951ad579ae78c57b3ec9cb2f3e6e319e`, including staged repairs and upstream integration, completed scoped-clean at P0–P2.

Net production growth is **+387 lines** (1,703 additions / 1,316 deletions across 51 paths), excluding tests, fixtures, docs and wrapper metadata. This is 39 lines over the accepted +348, within the approved integration allowance. FTS schema, native loading and the KNN subprocess now have one engine owner; feature search policy stays with existing callers. No schema/version bump or PostgreSQL implementation is included.

## What Problem This Solves

Agent row chips still use a custom-element bridge even though all five rendering callers are Solid.

## User Impact

Render `AgentRowChip` directly inside the existing host tag, preserving its inner span, classes, owner projection, and memo. All five imports remain inside their existing lazy pages. The lazy plugin avatar factory now imports its implementation directly; its imperative bridge remains for the SDK contract. prs.title: fix(ui): hide realtime Talk tail block while session is idle
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In a session mixing typed messages and realtime Talk (voice), typed messages sent after a Talk session ends rendered above the earlier voice turns in the Control UI transcript. The render order did not match actual chronology.

## Why This Change Was Made

Finalized voice turns are persisted into session history with real chronological positions. The live Talk block is a tail row. Once a caption's saved history id arrives, that caption must leave the tail so history owns its slot and it is not pinned below newer typed messages.

An earlier revision hid the entire tail whenever Talk reported idle. A normal gateway-relay close reports idle without clearing the conversation or waiting for saved rows to reach `props.messages`. That gate deleted unmatched captions (for example `transcriptId` `voice:call:1` absent from loaded history) even though they were the only rendered copy. Live-caption retirement, introduced so a caption disappears only when its matching saved row arrives, is restored: idle is not a persistence receipt. Unmatched captions, including ones with no transcript id, stay visible across idle closure and retire only on history replacement.

## User Impact

- Saved voice turns stay in history order and are not duplicated at the transcript tail after Talk goes idle, so later typed messages no longer render above those saved turns.
- Unmatched voice captions remain visible after Talk becomes idle until their saved history rows arrive. Closing Talk does not erase the only record of what was said.
- During an active Talk session, live and not-yet-saved captions still stream at the tail. Already-saved captions still leave the tail as soon as their history ids arrive.

## Evidence

Head `cebc660b683da1a7e6d452e1fc97aa5caff52d48` on `upstream/main` (`2c7872bdad12ebef2a87e42566aa69cd405a543d`).

`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ui/src/pages/chat/chat-view.realtime-talk.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-transcript-voice-reconciliation.test.ts --reporter=verbose`

prs.title: fix(gateway): cancel disconnected hook admission
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Authenticated hook requests that disconnect while admission is still queued stay eligible to start. A client retry, including a watcher that times out before admission, can then run the same work twice.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pending bounded admission now follows the HTTP request lifetime. When the last connected caller disconnects before lane placement or runner entry, that admission is canceled and its replay identity is retired so the retry can start once. Acceptance detaches cancellation, so work already handed to the runner continues. Background fan-out keeps its documented replay contract and is not canceled by disconnect. Authentication still runs before admission.

## User Impact

A disconnected hook client no longer starts an agent run it already abandoned. Retries of that request execute once. Runs that already passed admission keep going. Gmail fan-out batches still finish in the background and replay instead of duplicating.

## Evidence

Rebased onto current `upstream/main`. Head `80acac776684bba94a01b3dc3935cc80dee506e9`.

Previous CI on `ca9f24ca5d0`:

- `check-lint-core-1` failed on `src/gateway/server-http.hooks-request-lifetime.test.ts:162:36` and `:203:36`: `This is the default value for this type parameter, so it can be omitted. (typescript(no-unnecessary-type-arguments))`.
- `checks-node-changed-compact-large-24` failed in `src/gateway/server-http.control-ui.test.ts` (`expected "prepareIdentityFile" to not be called at all, but actually been called 2 times`). That test is not in this diff and is not on current main. This branch does not change Control UI identity.

The lifetime suite now waits on request-close and dispatch-arrival signals instead of `setTimeout` or `vi.waitFor`.

- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/gateway/server-http.hooks-request-lifetime.test.ts` (0 errors)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-http.hooks-request-lifetime.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (5 passed)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server/hooks.agent-trust.test.ts src/gateway/server/hooks-request-handler.fanout.test.ts src/gateway/server-http.hooks-delivery.test.ts src/gateway/server/hooks.early-failure.test.ts src/gateway/server/hooks.wake-admission.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (89 passed)

Live proof was captured at `3b2b5ed1541c8f325a68458ee3d59b1173b5d95f`. `80acac77668` only annotates the test gate as `Deferred`; production hook admission is unchanged. A real Gateway HTTP server accepted `POST /hooks/agent`, the client destroyed the socket after auth and body parsing while the request was queued behind a same-session run, and the agent runner did not start for the abandoned request. The same idempotency key then ran once. The isolated runner was instrumented only to hold the queue and count starts. Token redacted.


prs.title: fix(sessions): persist explicit toolOverrides.webSearch true
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sessions.patch` silently drops `toolOverrides.webSearch: true` while normalizing the session overlay. A lone `{ "webSearch": true }` becomes an empty overlay and is deleted on write. `webSearch: false` already persists, and the sibling boolean maps (`skills`, `mcpServers`) already keep `true`.

Schema already allows either boolean (`SessionToolOverridesSchema.webSearch`). Callers that send an explicit enable, including a session patch of `{ "webSearch": true }`, get a successful patch whose stored entry omits `webSearch`.

Persisting that `true` also made a native composer display bug reachable: with `tools.web.search.enabled` false, a retained session `webSearch: true` showed the composer as On even though execution still disables search.

## Why This Change Was Made

`normalizeSessionToolOverrides` kept `webSearch` only for the strict check `raw.webSearch === false`. That owner is what `sessions.patch` uses before it stores or deletes the overlay. The normalizer now keeps `typeof raw.webSearch === "boolean"`, so an explicit `true` is stored the same way as an explicit `false`. Non-booleans are still dropped.

The native effective-state predicate now requires the global baseline before a session override, matching `resolveWebSearchToolOverrideState` in `ui/src/lib/sessions/tool-overrides.ts`. `composerWebSearchEnabled` stays false when web search is unavailable or `webSearchBaseEnabled` is false, including when the stored override is `true`.

This does not loosen other fail-closed tool gates. Runtime checks that treat `webSearch !== false` as "not session-disabled", and the global `tools.web.search.enabled` kill switch, are unchanged. `intersectSessionToolOverrides` still only retains a web-search deny. Persistence and the native display predicate are the contracts changed.

The earlier implementation candidate, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/121378, was closed unmerged.

## User Impact

`sessions.patch` with `toolOverrides.webSearch: true` now keeps that value on the stored session entry, including when it is the only override and when it sits beside other overlay fields such as `skills`. `webSearch: false` still persists. Replacing the overlay and `toolOverrides: null` still replace or clear it. The stored value survives a Gateway restart.

A persisted `true` does not re-enable web search while the global kill switch is off, and the native composer no longer shows that state as On.

## Evidence

Head `cdb6300983c780be6e1b7cc63a35bbc90f501f6d`, rebased onto current `upstream/main`.

Isolated loopback Gateway (throwaway state directory, not the operator Gateway). Redacted `sessions.patch` / `sessions.list` readback for `agent:main:websearch-proof`:

```text
patch {webSearch:true}        -> list {webSearch:true}
patch {webSearch:false}       -> list {webSearch:false}          # replacement
patch {skills:{docs:true}, webSearch:true}
                              -> list {skills:{docs:true}, webSearch:true}
patch toolOverrides:null      -> list toolOverrides absent       # clear
patch {webSearch:true}
stop Gateway, start again on the same state
                              -> list {webSearch:true}            # reopen
```

Focused regression on that head:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts -t "persists explicit toolOverrides|normalizes tool overrides"
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  2 passed | 125 skipped (127)
```

The existing native global-disable regression now loads a retained `webSearch: true` override and expects `composerWebSearchEnabled == false` before and after toggle, with no settings patch. This host has no Swift toolchain, so that test was not executed locally.

`git diff --check` was clean.

prs.title: fix(code-mode): retire idle workers after persistent GC storms
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Idle Code Mode workers can continue a sustained major-GC storm far below their heap limit. The near-limit watchdog does not retire them, so they remain in the Gateway process until ordinary idle expiry.

## User Impact

A persistently storming warm worker is retired with reason `gc-storm`, and the next cell acquires a healthy worker on demand. Active cells and parked continuations retain their worker until completion, cancellation, timeout, or existing continuation expiry. No configuration or schema changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing detector now sends a small control signal after two consecutive windows above 600 major collections/minute, each at least 10 seconds. Warning/profile cadence stays unchanged. The existing Code Mode pool lifecycle owns the decision: retire completed warm workers, mark other workers draining, and never return a draining worker to the warm pool. At most one worker enters draining per minute across the executor; later detector windows retry other candidates. Deferred exits can coincide when continuations settle.

This is containment, independent of the GC-observer feedback-loop repair in #173574; `gc-observer.ts` is unchanged. The two PRs have no overlapping files, and the replacement sampler preserves the GC sample contract consumed here. It does not establish or fix the underlying native V8 crash cause.

## Evidence

- Synthetic detector/transport measurement: one storm window sends no retirement signal; the second signals at 20,000 ms. A quiet window resets persistence. Existing warning/profile behavior is preserved.
- Before/after regression: the two focused test files on the original production code produce 4 expected failures and 19 passes; with this change all 23 pass. Warm workers now close with `gc-storm`, replacement is lazy, and active/parked work survives until completion or disposal.
- Focused local command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/code-mode-node.lifecycle.test.ts src/agents/code-mode-node.gc.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 23 passed, 22.40 s wrapper wall time (19.25 s Vitest, mostly transformation; test bodies below one second).
- Changed-file formatting, changed-file repository lint, and `git diff --check`. Broad validation belongs to PR CI; no Testbox/Crabbox lease, production access, or load benchmark.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): clean at P0/P1/P2. Autoreview preflight refused the requested route because it differs from operator configuration; configuration was not changed.
- Simplification review: reused the detector, memory port, and pool cleanup owner; no additional timer, queue, manager, or compatibility path. Production LOC delta: +43. Growth implements the explicitly requested containment and work-preserving drain contract; there was no superseded retirement implementation to delete.

Related: #172945, #173306, #173382.

## CI Attribution and Landing Evidence

The exact-head CI run [38827361061](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38827361061) has one substantive failed shard: [checks-node-changed-19](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38827361061/job/116738426919). Its only file, `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/required-native-same-session.e2e.test.ts`, failed with `implicit-main after-agent-wait run failed before settlement`; the terminal error was `WorkspaceAccessUnavailableError: Remote workspace skill discovery failed`, before the first native inference request. The aggregate CI gate remains red; it is not represented as passing.

The failing path is workspace skill discovery/admission. This PR changes neither that owner nor the native-workspace fixture. The test uses plain-text responses without Code Mode cells, and the failed run has no Code Mode storm signal or retirement. The new diagnostic control branch handles only that absent signal. Independent source review found no connection from the changed retirement path to this failure.

Under the operator-authorized unrelated-flake rule, ran the single failing file five times on each revision in an isolated Linux sandbox, with Node 24.19.0 matching CI, an unprivileged user, synthetic state, private loopback networking, and one Vitest worker:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/required-native-same-session.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

| Revision | Results | Wrapper seconds, runs 1–5 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CI main parent `012bb1ccaf0b63696b2608599b1cf4ea869a4245` | 5/5 passed; exit 0 each | 76.32, 79.05, 77.57, 77.74, 79.27 |
| Exact PR head `5a423e8cfb9026037517bbe895140af4a4dae65b` | 5/5 passed; exit 0 each | 95.80, 79.36, 82.92, 84.68, 75.87 |

CI tested merge `26853b2c6be18f35da1effc99c272645d1cecb9c`, whose ordered parents are the baseline and PR head above. Each replay reported `Test Files 1 passed (1)` and `Tests 1 passed (1)`. These are validation durations, not performance measurements. The matching `qaRuntime` build preparation passed on both revisions. Initial root-user attempts hit the fixture's explicit root-quiescence refusal and are excluded from attribution; an initial full build also exceeded an unrelated declaration-size budget by 1,272 bytes, while the required QA build profile passed.

prs.title: fix(slack): keep thread typing across queued follow-up turns
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Slack thread status is per thread, but each inbound dispatch owned its own typing lifecycle. A mid-turn mention that cannot be steered (claude-cli) is parked and later runs as a queued follow-up. That follow-up reused the predecessor dispatch's typing controller. Core cleanup seals that controller, and the channel callbacks close with it, so the queued turn never publishes `processing`. A stop from the parked or finished dispatch can also publish `active` while another turn on the same thread is still the one that should look busy.

## Why This Change Was Made

Admitted follow-ups now get a successor typing controller. The predecessor stays sealed. The successor reopens channel typing as a new generation, so a late stop from the sealed lifecycle cannot clear the new indicator. Slack session status uses the same generation: a parked pipeline that never published `processing` does not publish `active`, and a queued turn can publish `processing` again before its own visible output, then return to `active` when it finishes. Status writes are serialized, so a predecessor `active` request cannot take effect after the successor's `processing` request. A finished successor is not started again when that older request resolves. The existing visible-output gate still suppresses status once this turn itself has output.

## User Impact

In a Slack thread, a message sent while the agent is already working no longer drops the native working indicator just because that message was parked. When that message later runs as its own turn, Slack shows the working status again until the turn finishes.

## Evidence

Head: `d4ba62ab06df9b544c5eacf7bd8d1d5a2cac75c1`

Previous CI on `0573de80c75bfb19616c2d8ddc1c7bb13333262c` failed in two jobs:

- `check-lint-core-3`: `src/channels/typing.ts:103:7: error: Function 'stopIfCurrent' expected no return value. (typescript(consistent-return))`
- `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets`: `First-party mock factories must preserve real exports or explain isolation` for the new follow-up lifecycle test. The same job also warned `1073 -> 1074 counted lines (cap 700)` on `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply.ts`.

Those are fixed without new suppressions. `stopIfCurrent` now always returns a promise. The lifecycle test spreads `importOriginal`. `get-reply.ts` no longer passes the silent-token default explicitly, so its counted lines move `1076 -> 1075` against current main. Local `check:test-mock-exports` and `check:line-cap-ratchet` against `upstream/main` passed. oxlint on the touched files is clean, including the extension tsconfig rule that rejected unbound test helpers.

Local publisher stub, no Slack Socket Mode and no user token. `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/followup-runner.typing-lifecycle.test.ts extensions/slack/src/monitor/message-handler/thread-status.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed. The follow-up runner drove the stub and printed:

`FOLLOWUP_EVENTS ["processing#0","active#0","processing#1","followup-started","active#1"]`

A later stop and start on that sealed predecessor did not append another event. With the predecessor `active` write held until after the successor had started, settlement was `["processing","active","processing"]`. When the successor also finished before that write resolved, settlement was `["processing","active","processing","active"]`, and a further stop published nothing.

The ordering regression fails on the previous cycle: while the delayed `active` write is still pending, the successor `processing` write is already in flight (`expected 2 to be 1`).

Maintainer decision still open: whether `beginNextLifecycle` should become a supported optional `TypingCallbacks` contract. Issue #158350 does not pin that public-API choice.

Fixes openclaw/openclaw#158350

prs.title: perf(runtime): stop GC telemetry from waking idle workers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Prevents GC telemetry from scheduling event-loop work after every collection in idle Code Mode workers, other instrumented workers, and the main isolate. Related: #173306.

## User Impact

Collection counts, kinds, elapsed durations, worker attribution, storm warnings, and the near-limit Code Mode thrash guard remain available. Native GC samples now use `reason="other"` because the native profiler does not expose callback flags; SDK-provided bounded reason labels remain supported. No configuration, schema, or deployment change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace per-GC `PerformanceObserver` instances with one shared `v8.GCProfiler` per isolate, drained by an unreferenced one-second timer. Code Mode protection and exporter demand subscribe to the same sampler. The last subscriber drains and stops it; new subscribers do not receive earlier collections. Worker metrics retain their existing memory-port batching.

This removes the per-collection native/JavaScript immediate queue and duplicate Code Mode observers. Production delta: **+7 lines**; sharing sampler ownership and its stop/drain lifecycle is necessary to preserve continuous actual GC counts and durations. Heap size and ELU alone cannot supply those counters. Native profiling does record heap statistics internally, and Node releases stopped native profiler callbacks on subsequent GC rather than immediately; workload measurements below cover that tradeoff.

## Evidence

Isolated Linux, Node 26.8.2, synthetic real Code Mode worker with 16 completed cells and metrics enabled; no production mutation. Before/after:

| Measurement | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Idle major collections over 60 seconds | 2 | 2 |
| Idle GC time | 10.72 ms | 10.14 ms |
| Idle worker CPU | 21.37 ms | 29.32 ms |
| GC-triggered Immediate allocations in seeded 60-second regression | 5 | 0 |
| Major collections in seeded regression, including one deliberate GC | 3 | 3 |
| Median wall time, 200 allocating cells (five rounds after warmup) | 171.00 ms | 156.09 ms |
| Median process CPU for those rounds | 350.03 ms | 295.22 ms |

**Gap:** the reported ~100 majors/second production storm did not reproduce in this sandbox. Idle collection frequency is neutral; this proves removal of the event-loop feedback mechanism, not a measured production storm reduction. The regression fails on the original observer because it schedules Immediate work, passes after replacement, and also enforces fewer than 10 majors over a real minute. That one-minute test is intentional: fake timers cannot exercise native idle GC scheduling.

Node's stock platform disables V8 idle tasks; `schedule_idle` is a callback flag, not evidence that worker idle deadlines execute immediately. Source inspection: [Node platform](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/v26.8.2/src/node_platform.h), [GC observer delivery](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/v26.8.2/src/node_perf.cc), [native GC profiler](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/v26.8.2/src/node_v8.cc).

Focused local proof only (one worker): `diagnostic-gc.test.ts` 6 passed / 7.82 s; `code-mode-node.gc.test.ts` 1 passed / 3.30 s; Node `code-mode-node.test.ts` 15 passed / 16.44 s, including zero-duration near-limit retirement/recovery; Node `code-mode-node.watchdog.test.ts` 3 passed, 1 Linux-only test skipped / 84.90 s including compiler-cache preparation and the real 60-second idle interval. Changed-file oxfmt, scoped repository oxlint, and `git diff --check` pass. Broad build/typecheck/suites belong to PR CI; no Testbox/Crabbox lease used.

Simplification pass completed. **Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable):** clean, no actionable P0/P1/P2 findings. The configured autoreview provider selector was refused before launch; operator configuration was not changed.

## CI and inherited failure attribution

Exact head `f9fb71bc659d32452ac711fc387ad56bf6dbee2c`, [CI attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38827144148): all selected checks passed except `checks-node-changed-14` and its downstream `openclaw/ci-gate`. The sole failed file was `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/required-native-same-session.e2e.test.ts`, case `settles required native empty workspaces and same-session follow-ups through public RPC`. Security, production/test types, scoped lint, docs, other Node shards, and UI checks passed. No CI rerun.

Replayed only that file using Node 24.19.0, private-QA runtime build preparation, unprivileged processes, two CPU cores per run, synthetic state, and isolated loopback network namespaces. Exact CI main parent: `012bb1ccaf0b63696b2608599b1cf4ea869a4245`. Exact tested merge: `0dde71949ebe75efd257f2596943394f63d42943`; verified ordered parents and merge tree.

| Same failure signature | PR CI | Tested merge replay | Main-parent replay |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Assertion | `implicit-main after-agent-wait run failed before settlement` | same | same |
| `agent.wait` error for `REQUIRED-NATIVE-0-A` | `WorkspaceAccessUnavailableError: Remote workspace skill discovery failed` | same | same |
| First native HTTP request reached | No | No | No |
| File duration | 84.78 s | 60.30 s | 67.20 s |

The tested merge passed once and reproduced the exact failure on its second run. The unchanged main parent passed runs 1, 3, and 4; run 2 exposed a separate live-dispatch-owner failure; run 5 reproduced the exact CI failure above. These are inherited failures, not five clean replays. Earlier root-owned sandbox attempts were invalid for this fixture because workspace quiescence rejects root-owned worker sessions; they are excluded from attribution.

Command: `OPENCLAW_E2E_USE_PREBUILT_DIST=1 OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/required-native-same-session.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Required build preparation: `OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1 node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts qaRuntime` (both pinned revisions passed).

The failing test, remote-workspace adapter, pairing checks, and skill-discovery owner are unchanged between the main parent and tested merge. Its fixture has no GC exporter subscription, and the failure precedes native inference/Code Mode execution. Landing under the explicitly authorized inherited-failure exception; the failed CI run remains red. Follow-up: stabilize native workspace skill discovery during startup; the separate baseline dispatch-owner failure also needs attention.

The automated review's test-cost finding was considered and declined with a recorded reply: the requested real 60-second idle regression intentionally remains in PR coverage because fake clocks cannot exercise native V8 idle GC scheduling.

prs.title: perf(subagents): release settled run text from memory
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Settled subagent runs retained full task and result strings in the live registry, persisted-row cache, and session-list indexes for the lifetime of retained history. Aggregate-only heap analysis identified 7,080 registry task holders (25.16 MiB), 6,635 completion result holders (33.70 MiB), and 704 pending-delivery task holders (2.93 MiB). Retainer paths overlap; these are not additive retained-size claims. No snapshot or user text was exported.

## User Impact

Completed runs release large task/result payloads after cleanup and requester obligations settle. Full selected reads, later metadata writes, and restart recovery preserve durable text. Pending/suspended delivery, requester settlement, yielded work, and cancellation retain their payloads.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing registry keeps a detached 160-character task preview and hydrates selected payloads through its worker reader. FIFO mutations hydrate before planning, preventing later metadata writes from replacing durable text with a preview. Session-list indexes retain compact facts with the original runtime identity, preserving executor/reservation liveness. They compare ownership and displayed facts so progress-only publications do not invalidate projections.

No schema, stored format, durable-retention, or configuration change. Production delta: +159 lines net (+212/-53). The growth implements the required hydration boundary while preserving durable text and lifecycle ownership.

Scope: compact identity/status records remain resident for topology and authorization; this does not cap record count or total registry memory. Structured collector results, schemas, and diagnostic strings remain unchanged. Collector schemas also participate in synchronous request authorization. Visible terminal-reply evidence retains its existing 4,096-character bound.

## Evidence

### Measurement

Isolated Linux fixture uses the real registry writer, resident caches, session-list index, and forced GC: 6,000 completed runs across 5,000 child-session keys, in batches of 64. Each has independent 4,096-character task and 6,144-character result strings plus a retained 4,096-character visible reply. This is subsystem memory proof, not a whole-Gateway load test.

| At 6,000 completed runs | Parent | Final production code |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Retained heap | 103.16 MiB | 53.42 MiB |
| Retained heap per 1,000 runs | 17.19 MiB | 8.90 MiB |
| RSS after GC | 1,073.29 MiB | 1,042.95 MiB |
| Peak RSS | 1,095.84 MiB | 1,044.54 MiB |
| Whole-process elapsed time | 14.10 s | 14.29 s |
| Resident full result characters | 36,864,000 | 0 |
| Resident task characters | 24,576,000 | 960,000 |

Retained heap falls **48.2%**. RSS/time include the source loader, workers, and initialization; elapsed time is effectively neutral in this single paired run, with no throughput gain claimed. Earlier heap baselines varied by about 4.45 MiB; the table uses the conservative final paired result. A fixture without visible replies retained 79.13 → 23.79 MiB (13.19 → 3.97 MiB/1,000).

Representative observed retainers: `Object.runs -> SubagentRunMap.table -> array -> Object.task`, `SubagentRunIndex.latest -> Map.table -> array -> Object.task`, session-list `inMemoryRuns` / `inMemoryDisplayByChildSessionKey`, and `Object.completion -> Object.resultText`.

### Validation

- Forced-GC worker regression: 64 completed runs with 16 MiB of independent task/result text retain less than 6 MiB, including sliced visible replies. Both catalog policies pass; durable reads, later writes, and compact restart restoration preserve payloads.
- Focused memory, worker, scoped-read, async-state, and executor/reservation-liveness tests pass.
- CI-driven focused repairs pass: lifecycle 227, completion store 13, requester wake 35, registry seam 103, task replacement 15, cancellation publication 7, announcement cancellation 13, sessions.send 4, replay harness 16, projection 5, affected cron/restart cases 2, sessions-reset cleanup 18, swarm integration 1, historical cancellation 22, owner counts 3, and real Gateway startup/recovery WebChat 1.
- Fixtures persist acknowledged payloads, assert full text through durable readers, and publish immutable replacements. Existing behavior assertions remain intact. A readiness fix separates payload hydration from catalog preparation in the existing catalog-disabled test mode.
- Export-name guard, two script-closure files (21 tests), changed-file formatting/lint, and diff checks pass. Mock-baseline generation removes two obsolete exceptions and adds none.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): all actionable findings addressed; final P0/P1/P2 review clean.
- Final exact-head [PR CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38828541060) passed on `8dda2ed52038a9849597869c1644638d74b13687`, including PostgreSQL conformance, changed tests, typechecks, lint, and the combined CI/security gate. The last review repair replaces a broad partial mock with an explicit isolated factory; all seven scoped-read cases and the mock-export ratchet pass. Earlier runs exposed the repaired fixture/readiness issues and one GitHub download timeout during setup; none are described as passing evidence. No Testbox/Crabbox lease was allocated under this lane's validation policy.

prs.body:
Fixes #172222

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Doctor's missing embedding-key warning makes stopped memory indexing sound like reduced semantic recall, leaving operators unaware that new and changed notes are not indexed.

## User Impact

Doctor explains when memory sync stops, identifies the provider's environment key or credential setup, offers deliberate keyword-only recall followed by an agent-scoped rebuild, and tells the operator to rerun `openclaw doctor`.

This is Doctor diagnostic output only. Provider selection, search, indexing, fallback behavior, configuration, and persisted data are unchanged; no migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Memory Core already stops sync when an explicit provider is unavailable or an existing vector index would otherwise be replaced with keyword-only data. The warning now states those conditions and accounts for working fallback embeddings without duplicating runtime policy in Doctor. The first warning line stays unchanged for structured consumers.

Original fix by @serg0x; maintainer cleanup removes the config-path resolver and its imports, replaces the disable-only suggestion with keyword-only recovery that explicitly mentions agent overrides, and reduces the added tests to two focused cases. The earlier ClawSweeper agent-scoping finding remains addressed: the guidance applies to this agent's effective setting, and the rebuild uses its agent ID. The latest full review on the contributor head had no open findings.

## Evidence

- Source and history confirm the defect on main: the old warning mentions only semantic recall; `assertFtsOnlySyncAllowed` and the provider requirement owner explain the stopped-index conditions. Existing memory configuration documentation already describes these runtime contracts.
- Regression cases: `explains stopped indexing and recovery with fallback none` and `explains stopped indexing and recovery with fallback ollama`, in `src/commands/doctor-memory-search.test.ts`. They exercise the existing Doctor note owner and verify the consequence, key, agent-aware keyword-only rebuild guidance, rerun instruction, and single-note output. The new wording assertions fail against the pre-fix source by inspection; no negative-control execution was performed.
- Local formatting: `oxfmt 0.72.0 --check` passed on both changed files. Static oxlint 1.87.0 passed using the repository's core rules; the temporary config omitted only the unrelated UI-only override because the shared install lacks its Solid lint plugin. All rules applying to the changed files were retained. The standard wrapper could not resolve this nested checkout's dependencies; no install was performed.
- Autoreview: committed-branch Codex review through P2 on `59772cd6c5fa57674c01fc6a80a45375b55ba640` is **scoped-clean**, with no accepted/actionable findings; the reviewer executed no project code or tests.
- Exact-head [PR CI run 38827424602](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38827424602) **passed** for `59772cd6c5fa57674c01fc6a80a45375b55ba640`: 35 successful jobs, no failures. This includes production/test typechecks, lint, and the Doctor regressions. [Changed-tests job 116738556649](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38827424602/job/116738556649) passed all **40 Doctor memory-search tests** plus **8 Doctor memory-output tests**, including both new cases. No failure attribution or rerun was needed. PR CI is the proof per maintainer policy. Local unit tests and typechecks were intentionally not run; live Gateway proof, remote leases, and negative controls were intentionally skipped per maintainer policy.

prs.title: fix(wizard): honor session cancellation during hosted setup
prs.body:
## Update 2026-10-16 — rebased onto current `main`

Recreated as a single commit on `main` (`73bb9054970`); the branch previously carried a divergent fork history, which is why GitHub reported it as conflicting. `src/gateway/server-methods/wizard.ts` was the only hand-resolved hunk — `main` restructured `wizard.start` (`wizardRequestScopes.set(...)`, block-bodied arrow) — and the resolution keeps that structure while threading the session `signal` into the setup runner call. Re-verified on this head on the test host: base (`main` plus these tests) `Tests 2 failed | 50 passed (52)`, candidate `Tests 52 passed (52)`.

---

## What Problem This Solves

Closes #127374.

Classic hosted setup (`wizard.start` with flow `setup`) never hands the wizard session's `AbortSignal` to the setup runner.

`WizardSession` owns the controller and passes the signal to its runner (`src/wizard/session.ts`), but the gateway built the setup session as `new WizardSession((prompter) => …)` and `SetupWizardRunner` had no signal parameter, so the signal was dropped at that hop. Downstream, `runSetupWizard` → `runSetupModelAuthStep` → `prepareAuthChoice` could not receive one either, even though the provider-auth owner already accepts `signal` and forwards it to device-code polling and token exchange.

Effect: `wizard.cancel` during provider authentication does not abort that provider work. The cancelled session keeps setup admission until the provider eventually settles (device-code expiry can be 15 minutes), so an immediate replacement setup attempt is rejected as busy.

## Fix

Carry the session signal that already exists down the setup path:

- `SetupWizardRunner` gains an optional `signal`, and `wizard.start` passes the session's signal to it. `GatewayKernelContext.wizardRunner` now reuses that contract instead of restating it.
- `runSetupWizard` / `runSetupWizardOnce` accept and forward it.
- `runSetupModelAuthStep` forwards it, and `ApplyAuthChoiceParams` accepts `signal`.
- `prepareAuthChoice` and the provider-auth owner (`provider-auth-choice.ts`) already forward the signal end to end, so no new cancellation mechanism is added.

Scope correction (thanks @clawsweeper): the earlier body overstated durable-write protection. `beforePersistentEffect` is supplied only to the channels runner (`channelWizardRunner`); classic setup never receives that hook, before or after this change. This patch changes no durable-write behavior on either flow.

## Evidence

### Rebase note (2026-10-11)

This revision's head is `1f7bb369d31e1e508cbe87806257a4344ea603f6`, rebased onto `main` @ `b6fa7b58004` because the previous base (`e62f5f37442f152d238d5e838b52a48b2102f682`) predated a material amount of merged work. The rebase replayed the same commits with no conflicts and the patch is unchanged: `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD` still reports +69/-3 across 6 files. The proof receipts below were captured on the pre-rebase head and were not re-run on this base; CI re-runs on this head.


**Real behavior proof — full production chain, no mocks, no injected runner.**

- Real gateway process: `node dist/index.js gateway run --port 19777 --auth token` (production bundle built from the tested commit), fresh state dir.
- Real WS client driving `wizard.start` → `wizard.next` → `wizard.cancel` over the gateway protocol (token auth, signed device identity).
- Real provider authentication: the bundled github-copilot plugin's device flow, redirected through the provider's supported `COPILOT_GITHUB_DOMAIN` seam to a live local HTTPS stub: `proof-x.ghe.com` resolves via /etc/hosts to a public IP bound to loopback (so the SSRF guard's hostname allowlist + resolved-address checks pass), TLS via a local CA in `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`. The stub issues a real device code (interval 1s), answers `authorization_pending`, and withholds poll #3's response for 5s so cancellation lands mid-request.

Environment: Linux x86_64 (kernel 4.19), Node v24.18.0, 2026-10-02 (UTC).

**After fix (head `0e7a28c6c2f8`):** cancellation aborts the in-flight poll and frees setup admission.

```
+ 61858ms stub: device-code requested -> issuing code PROOF-CODE
+ 62890ms stub: token poll #1 received
+ 63905ms stub: token poll #2 received
+ 64920ms stub: token poll #3 received        <- response withheld 5s
+ 65003ms stub: poll #3 connection CLOSED BEFORE RESPONSE (in-flight abort)
+ 65004ms wizard.cancel -> {"status":"cancelled","error":"cancelled"}
+ 65012ms replacement wizard.start attempt 1: REJECTED (setup already in progress)
+ 65525ms replacement wizard.start attempt 2: ACCEPTED sessionId=0d61e25e-... status=running
+ 73526ms observation: polls at cancel=3, polls now=3 (delta=0 in 8s after cancel)
```

`wizard.cancel` lands while token poll #3 is in flight; the abort terminates the live HTTPS request (the stub sees the connection close before it can respond), the runner settles, and the replacement wizard is admitted ~0.5s later. No further provider polls occur. (Attempt 1 being rejected ~8ms after cancel is the intended settlement barrier: admission releases only after the runner finishes unwinding.)

**Before fix (base `64406536043`, identical harness and stub):** provider work survives cancellation and holds admission.

```
+ 33654ms stub: token poll #3 received
+ 33732ms wizard.cancel -> {"status":"cancelled","error":"cancelled"}
+ 33734ms replacement wizard.start attempt 1: REJECTED (setup already in progress)
+ 38654ms stub: poll #3 answered authorization_pending after 5000ms delay   <- NOT aborted
+ 39671ms stub: token poll #4 received   <- provider work continues after cancel
+ 45305ms replacement wizard.start attempt 24: REJECTED (setup already in progress)
+ 45685ms stub: token poll #5 received
+ 45805ms replacement wizard.start: still REJECTED after 12s of retries (setup admission held)
+ 51701ms stub: token poll #6 received
```

Verdict: `replacementAdmitted: false`, `pollingContinuedAfterCancel: true` — polling runs on past cancellation (until device-code expiry) and the replacement setup never gets in.

**Unit/integration evidence (unchanged):** red → green at the real handler boundary (`wizardHandlers["wizard.start"]`):

- Before: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/server-methods/wizard.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → `AssertionError: wizard.start must hand the setup runner the session cancellation signal: expected undefined to be defined` (`1 failed | 22 skipped`).
- After: `23 passed`. The new case takes 12 ms and reuses the existing suite-level wizard harness, so no new gateway boot is added.

Downstream forwarding is pinned at the setup entry: `src/wizard/setup.test.ts > runSetupWizard > forwards wizard cancellation to provider authentication` asserts `prepareAuthChoice` receives the exact signal object.

Suite comparison against clean `main` (`64406536043`) on this host:

- `src/wizard/setup.test.ts`: fix `8 failed | 27 passed (35)` vs clean `8 failed | 26 passed (34)`. The same 8 tests fail in both runs (migration picker/import flows, plugin compatibility notices, fleet workspace moves) — inherited on this host and unchanged by this patch.
- `src/wizard/setup.model-auth.test.ts`: `1 failed | 13 passed` in both runs (`runSetupModelAuthStep > re-prompts after a provider setup error instead of aborting`) — inherited, unchanged.

`oxfmt --check` is clean on all seven touched files.

## Test cost

- `src/gateway/server-methods/wizard.test.ts`: existing heavy unit suite, ~114 s wall on this host; this change adds one case of 12 ms.
- `src/wizard/setup.test.ts`: ~62 s wall; the new case is a single `runWizard` invocation using the file's existing mocks.

## Known gaps

- The verification-retry path (`offerLiveModelVerification` in `src/wizard/setup.inference-verification.ts`) re-invokes `runSetupModelAuthStep` without a signal; it is a separate entry point and is not limited to the migration-import flow. Not threaded here.
- `channelWizardRunner` (channels setup flow) still exposes no signal.
- The inherited failures listed above were not touched.

prs.title: fix(zai): preserve quota reset times and weekly periods
prs.body:
Fixes #172230

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: successful z.ai quota reports omit numeric reset countdowns and label weekly token quotas as an unspecified limit.

## User Impact

Usage reports retain the provider's millisecond reset timestamps, identify weekly token windows, and distinguish months from minutes. Missing or unsupported reset values leave the quota visible without a countdown. No configuration changes or migration are needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The [vendor quota contract](https://github.com/zai-org/ZCode/blob/aac4755666d09fdcd70272fcf063c077a639015f/docs/bigmodel-coding-plan-usage-quota.md) defines numeric epoch **milliseconds**, unit 6 as weeks, and unit 5 as months. Reuse the shared Date-range validator and existing date-string reset parser; retain the provider's unit table and shared percentage normalization. No seconds heuristic or duplicate parser is introduced. Remove redundant percent, unit, and reset intermediates from the fetcher.

Original fix by @fhgffy; maintainer cleanup simplifies normalization, covers unsupported reset shapes, and documents usage behavior. The original contributor commit is preserved.

This corrects successful response parsing. Authentication and the request header are unchanged; live-account authentication is not verified. There are no new deferred/background effects or captured authority facts.

## Evidence

- Confirmed from source/history on current main: string-only reset normalization drops numeric milliseconds; unit 6 is absent and unit 5 is mapped to minutes. Collision checks found no competing fix.
- Regression tests in `src/infra/provider-usage.fetch.zai.test.ts`: `preserves the documented quota reset timestamps in usage reports` (vendor five-hour/monthly payloads and a fixed-clock one-hour countdown); `identifies weekly token quotas even when their optional reset is absent`; `keeps quota visible without a reset for unsupported timestamps: %j` (out-of-Date-range number, unsupported numeric string, boolean, object). Existing mixed-limit coverage retains ISO resets, malformed siblings, unknown periods, and percentage bounds; its synthetic month expectation now uses `mo`.
- Local static oxlint 1.85.0: 2 changed TypeScript files, 231 rules, zero diagnostics. The nested wrapper lacks its own dependencies; direct oxlint used the repository's core rules with only the unrelated UI/Solid-plugin override omitted. `oxfmt 0.71.0 --check` on all 3 changed files and `git diff --check` pass.
- Independent Codex autoreview: both the pre-commit candidate and committed-branch review are scoped-clean at P0–P2, with no actionable findings. The canonical installed helper was used because the repository entrypoint delegates to it.
- Exact-head [CI run 38827348008](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38827348008) passed for `55024cb7e6bebcf0b7c384f02f8fb8c402e5a837`: 30 successful jobs, 30 scope skips, zero failures. `openclaw/ci-gate`, selected tests, production/test typechecks, lint, docs, boundary checks, and security-fast passed. No retries or inherited-failure exception were needed.
- Local tests/typechecks, negative-control execution, Gateway/Telegram live proof, and Crabbox/Testbox leases were intentionally skipped per maintainer policy (2026-10-13: trust PR CI, local lint only). No local runtime or live-account success is claimed. The [changed-test job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38827348008/job/116738333719) ran `node --import tsx scripts/ci-run-node-test-shard.mts`, selecting the quota suite on Bun: **11 passed**, Vitest duration **844 ms**, runner wall time **3.28 s**. Its full CI job took **159 s**, including setup and other selected tests. Fixtures use injected transport and a fixed clock, with no new sleep, polling, or Gateway process.
- ClawSweeper's [full review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/172231#issuecomment-6171283116) identified no P0–P2 code findings and classified the fix as complete. Its live-behavior-only request is superseded by the maintainer's CI proof policy. No human code findings were present.

prs.title: fix: OpenAI usage double-counts audio and omits cache writes
prs.body:
Fixes #172200

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes inflated OpenAI Admin usage totals and missing cache writes when organization responses contain audio or cache-write tokens.

## User Impact

Daily and per-model reports count each token once and separate uncached input, cache reads, and cache writes. Provider-reported dollar amounts stay unchanged. No configuration, migration, or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The [current OpenAI Completions Usage API](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/admin/subresources/organization/subresources/usage/methods/completions) defines input and output as inclusive totals across text, audio, and images. Input also includes cached and cache-write tokens. The existing shared provider-usage model receives:

| API field | Shared usage field |
| --- | --- |
| `input_tokens` minus cache reads and both cache-write counters | `inputTokens` (uncached input, clamped at zero) |
| `input_cached_tokens` | `cacheReadTokens` |
| `input_cache_write_tokens` (30-minute) + `input_cache_write_12h_tokens` (12-hour) | `cacheWriteTokens` |
| `output_tokens` | `outputTokens` |
| `input_tokens` + `output_tokens` | `totalTokens` |

Modality breakdowns are already included and are never added again. Missing optional counters default to zero; existing text-only behavior remains covered. The current contract has no reliable version discriminator for older text-only interpretations, so no payload-shape heuristic is introduced.

Original fix by @fhgffy; maintainer cleanup removes duplicate daily sorting before the shared history builder, simplifies regression HTTP fixtures, and documents the accounting rules. No new totals, state owners, SDK surfaces, or deferred side effects.

## Evidence

Current main at `012bb1ccaf0b63696b2608599b1cf4ea869a4245` still adds audio breakdowns to inclusive totals and records zero cache writes. Source history traces that arithmetic to `827402243d7fb307ea7ee4aa0cd398815ff00d23`. For the documented mixed payload, old arithmetic produces 1,600 total / 650 uncached / 0 cache-write tokens; corrected arithmetic produces 1,500 / 500 / 100.

PR CI is the test gate per maintainer policy. It covers the regression cases, existing provider tests, typechecks, and repository checks selected for this diff. No local tests or typechecks, negative-control execution, live Gateway proof, or Crabbox/Testbox leases were run in this maintainer pass; live proof was intentionally skipped per maintainer policy.

Regression cases in `extensions/openai/usage.test.ts`:

- `counts each token once for the documented mixed-modality and cache-write response`: asserts daily/model categories and `5 requests · 1,500 tokens`.
- `counts each token once for audio totals without optional text or cache breakdowns`: asserts daily/model categories and `5 requests · 500 tokens`.

Both exercise `resolveOpenAIUsageAuth` and `fetchOpenAIUsage` with synthetic HTTP responses and independent expected values. No new timers, polling, processes, or test-only production seams. The contributor reported both failing before the fix and all eight tests passing afterward; that prior report is not claimed as current-head CI proof. Local test wall time: not measured under this policy. Exact-head CI ran all eight tests in the usage file successfully: **3.89 seconds** for the file, **2 ms each** for the two new regressions.

Changed-file oxlint and oxfmt pass; `git diff --check` passes. The nested worktree lacks local dependency links, so lint used an existing pinned oxlint 1.87 installation and a temporary core configuration preserving all applicable rules, excluding only the unrelated UI Solid-plugin override (its dependency is absent). It checked two files with 231 rules and zero diagnostics in 0.88 seconds. Pinned oxfmt 0.72 checked all three files. Precommit Codex autoreview: scoped-clean, no P0–P2 findings. Committed-branch Codex autoreview after merging main: **scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings**. Exact-head [CI run 38827385009](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38827385009) for `3b0b806dc59e0382dc981dd0c0a17977c56994fb`: **passed**, including production/test types, lint, selected Node shards, and `openclaw/ci-gate`. The [changed-extension test job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38827385009/job/116738440886) reports `Test Files 1 passed` and `Tests 8 passed`. No CI retries or inherited failures were needed.

[ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/172201#issuecomment-6170611071): no actionable code findings. Its sole live-proof request is superseded by the maintainer policy above; PR CI is the proof. No human review findings were present.

Diff against the merge base: production **+11/-9 (net +2)**, tests **+71/-0**, docs **+6/-0**. The two net production lines are necessary to parse and propagate both cache-write counters; unrelated code was not removed to meet a line quota. Daily sorting remains owned by the shared history builder.

Agents and Search settings still route three model pickers through Lit even though the pages and picker implementations already use Solid. Those adapters also keep two unused wrapper modules alive.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

Page lazy boundaries, host tags, and CSS classes are preserved. The separate avatar adapter remains with its assigned port; main’s native fallback `MultiSelect` remains intact.

Two narrowly scoped browser-fixture corrections arose from CI investigation. Synthetic touch moves now sample their rendered scroll offset on the next animation frame. Neither changes production behavior or relaxes a threshold, duration, animation requirement, or cleanup assertion. The limits of their evidence are recorded below.

The historical build/capture pair predates wrapper retirement, a type-only import redirect, and test migration, which did not alter the rendered graph. Later integration preserved the production picker changes; the final conflict resolution adopts both exact main picker fixtures and retains all other automatically merged main changes. Captures use synthetic data at 1440 × 960, light theme, fixed time, and reduced motion. In Agents, Decision Model opens upward over the primary trigger; the primary picker was opened and dismissed earlier in the same flow. ## Screenshots

![Agents — before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4b24576d-ced6-4608-a941-f590505af546)

![Agents — after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0451889a-3dd5-449b-81cd-d14e2a007a93)

## CI investigation and remaining uncertainty

Replacement head `d9c4b101` and both previous heads `35c68e72` and `7e877cdd` passed, including both real-Gateway shards. The added snapshot diagnostics change only failure reporting; this passing run does not explain the earlier quota timeout or establish a runtime fix.

Prior published head `7ce7c462` failed only `Running Gateway quota status: saved-clear > serves the same account and shows ready status after recovery without restarting` in `quota-reset-status.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts`. The provider badge remained “Checking models…” instead of “Ready” after the 60-second poll. Public failure diagnostics show a connected browser, successful route, healthy authentication, and no observed `models.list` response. A connect snapshot can populate the catalog without that RPC, so the missing response is not itself a diagnosis.

The exact tested merge is `b4c181d8549a4c19c559f5319596c9969145f32f`, with main parent `748a6fd98f3f5cd38be7f91a9f31b1ae99138963`. This is a tooling failure, not a reproduced or passing quota case. No watchdog override, speculative production refresh, or threshold change was added.

The authenticated connect producer sends its `models.list` result as `models.snapshot.payload.catalog`. The failure catch now passes the latest already-recorded snapshot to the sanitizer. Its separate `models.snapshot` summary contains only presence, model/availability/pending-provider counts, and fixed outcome-category counts. Existing `listSeen`, `listOk`, and list counts keep their RPC-only meaning. The existing sanitizer file passed **22/22** cases once (**25.39 s** Vitest duration; **57.121 s** command wall time), including snapshot-only and missing-catalog reports and checks that private values never reach public output. The new evidence may distinguish a pending snapshot from missing RPC data; it does not explain the prior timeouts.

The prior `817b0434` run failed only WebKit’s `keeps descendant-only native overlap leased through closing and releases after settlement` in `menu-native-contract.browser.test.tsx`: one branch had zero closing animations. The actual tested merge was `712e9b7562262856b8772d5eeb2f6d31a8f49dbd`, with main parent `275c611ead7a010e544ce5337e0588ec593e8087`. Eighteen determining source/configuration inputs match between that merge, its main parent, and the author head. This establishes the reproduction target; it does not establish inheritance or cause. The latest completed scheduled-main comparison, [38761419261](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38761419261) at `ce7439db`, passed all three UI unit shards.

The fixture previously asserted logical/native openness without asserting the computed visible starting state. The correction waits for both menus’ opacity to reach `1` before close. It retains the requirement that each branch have closing animations, the 60-second hold, closing phase, native popover visibility, occlusion states, settlement, and cleanup. One corrected WebKit case passed locally; the original CI failure was not reproduced, so this result does not establish causality. All three UI unit shards passed in the replacement run; this does not by itself establish why the historical failure disappeared.

The earlier run [38744495449](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38744495449) at `5112ce3d` failed the WebKit modal registry fixture and the mobile touch-scroll case. Canonical modal correction #173183 is integrated through main `c35dcdd80693e99277eec0fb6752d1aa93076d83`; both modal disconnect cases pass in the later `817b0434` unit log. prs.title: perf(state): keep plugin and GitHub reads off the writer queue
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Uncached plugin-state reads and GitHub publication status queries occupy the shared SQLite writer queue during startup and UI reconnects, delaying unrelated writes and attachment metadata.

## User Impact

Plugin-state and GitHub discovery reads stop delaying unrelated SQLite writes during reconnects. The measured GitHub-options cold-start timeout regression remains an explicit limitation below; this PR does not claim all RPCs are faster. No configuration or schema migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the five pure plugin-state reads (`lookup`, `lookupMany`, `entries`, key-range entries, `count`) and the GitHub publication read registry to the existing shared-state reader pool. Remove their writer registrations and dispatch branches. Plugin reads still observe preceding namespace mutations; mutations retain FIFO ordering. Overlapping reads do not reserve writer positions. Comparison observations and actual mutations remain with the writer, including their authority checks.

The runtime delta is **+69 lines**: the GitHub portion removes 11 lines; the plugin cutover adds 80 because typed error envelopes, missing-store behavior, and namespace-cache publication must cross the reader transport. The retired writer read path is deleted. No schema, configuration, cache, or timer is added.

## Attribution

- `execute` includes the generic GitHub publication read operations used by status discovery and reconciliation. Reconciliation starts immediately and repeats every minute; UI discovery also invokes those reads per session.
- `plugin_state` included uncached keyed reads and catalog snapshots as well as real persistence. This change removes the pure reads from that class; actual catalog persistence and compound/compare operations remain writes.
- `githubRepository` included the `personalPending` read called by `sessions.github.options`. That old writer command is removed; the existing publication read registry now owns it.

Coarse production request-class metrics and logs cannot assign exact operation counts to individual callers. The comparison below isolates these paths through real Gateway RPCs with synthetic state.

## Measurement

Baseline source: `2aca37525ff0804790c29d9ab6fea1bb9e5f700e`. Measured reader-cutover source: `735f802912798910e01a1eaff00a214d87ac33dc`. The subsequent repair narrows the writer type contract and migrates one missed test caller; the measured reader path is unchanged. Both use the same final benchmark driver. Each run starts from independently generated state: 5,000 sessions, 6,000 retained runs, 200 approvals, 100 cron jobs, 12 projects with real worktrees, and a 4,641,595,392-byte agent database. All accounts, tokens, sessions, and model responses are synthetic.

The driver pairs 150 devices in batches before the measured crash, holds 30 real agent requests, kills its own Gateway, then starts all 150 reconnect clients concurrently. It polls session/sidebar, catalog, project, and GitHub-option RPCs for five minutes from restart spawn. Connection refusals/retries and RPC errors stay in the results. The synthetic catalog exercises real plugin-state lookup and session metadata without provider scans or external network latency.

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/team-shape-fixture.ts --state-dir "$STATE_DIR" --transcript-mib 1500
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/post-restart-burst-measure.ts --state-dir "$STATE_DIR" --clients 150 --runs 30 --seconds 300 --writer-reads --port 42340 --mock-port 42341
```

Five-minute target-class writer queue results:

| Request class | Before requests | After requests | Before queue wait | After queue wait |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `execute` | 7,988 | 1 | 110.966 s | 0.000012 s |
| `plugin_state` | 7,710 | 0 | 202.102 s | 0 s |
| `githubRepository` | 7,987 | 0 | 191.606 s | 0 s |
| **Total** | **23,685** | **1** | **504.674 s** | **0.000012 s** |

All 150 clients connected in both runs. Readiness was effectively unchanged (20.491 → 20.577 s). Successful RPCs increased from 31,953 to 32,095; total RPC errors fell from 151 to 55. HTTP 503 connection refusals before successful retries were 165 → 41. An unchanged-baseline repeat produced 470.019 s of target writer wait and 23,553 target requests.

| RPC | Before p50 / p99 | After p50 / p99 | Before → after errors |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `sessions.list` | 11.6 / 195.9 ms | 18.3 / 124.2 ms | 0 → 0 |
| `sessions.catalog.list` | 19.8 / 438.1 ms | 24.3 / 131.0 ms | 149 → 0 |
| `projects.list` | 17.0 / 203.3 ms | 25.2 / 131.7 ms | 0 → 0 |
| `sessions.github.options` | 70.0 / 1324.9 ms | 86.0 / 2879.5 ms | 2 → 55 |

**Adverse result and follow-up:** GitHub-options cold-start latency/timeouts worsened in the final run. All 55 timed-out calls started before 25 seconds from restart; none timed out after the initial burst. Clients also began polling earlier (first-150 polling-start median 29.50 → 26.91 s). The repeated baseline had one GitHub timeout, so this is not dismissed as proven noise. The catalog errors were initially empty metadata results.

A separate, temporary stage trace on final code using the reused synthetic fixture located its observed timeout in session preparation (6,227 ms), before publication reads began. Other traced slow calls spent about 1,850 ms in session preparation; personal-pending reads took at most 6 ms, shared-publication reads 273 ms, and identity discovery 52 ms. This identifies a remaining cold-session readiness bottleneck, but the different diagnostic run does not conclusively attribute all 55 original timeouts. No diagnostic instrumentation is included in this PR. The change removes target writer contention; it does not claim a universal RPC latency improvement. Medians increased in this run even where p99 improved.

The scrape occurs at five minutes from restart spawn. Counters cover events observed after exporter initialization; work still waiting at the cutoff is counted only when it starts. This is a cold-start comparison, not a statistical latency study or a production deployment claim.

## Evidence

Focused local files passed with one worker: plugin-state-worker (20 tests), plugin-state-publication (15), plugin-state-store (23), shared-state summary (5), shared-state imports (6), GitHub pending-publication (6), and persisted session-list worker (3). Changed-file formatting/lint and diff checks passed. Broad validation belongs to PR CI.

The plugin regression fails on old routing with five writer requests, then passes with five reader requests and zero writer requests while preserving prior-write visibility. The GitHub regression fails on old routing when writer dispatch is unavailable, then passes after the reader cutover. Existing quarantine, corruption, cache invalidation, and authority tests remain in force.

CI and review caught and drove repairs for stale cache-dispatch assertions, a contract import cycle, quarantine error classification, the worker-entry boundary, and one remaining test caller of the retired writer read. That session-list test failed before its caller migration and passes afterward. The shared writer type now excludes all five read operations. The final dispatcher lives in the existing worker module; no guard allowance was added.

Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable) found no actionable P0/P1/P2 findings, including the CI repairs and final writer-contract/caller repair. Operator configuration was not changed. No Testbox/Crabbox lease was used. Runtime benchmark builds ran only in the isolated Linux sandbox. Local validation used focused test files and changed-file lint/format. An initial lint invocation entered dependency-artifact preparation and was stopped; the corrected core-only lint passed. No local test suite or standalone repository-wide typecheck/build was run.

## Final CI

[CI run 38826388682](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38826388682) **passed** on final head `df6ff99bf4a107f472a127a20b060cb1471a7bd7`, including the test shards, architecture checks, production/test types, lint, builds, PostgreSQL conformance, and SQL ratchet. The final contract/caller repair independently passed the persisted session-list worker file (3 tests) and plugin-state worker file (20 tests), changed-file lint/format, and independent review.

The PR-description check initially rejected the nonstandard “Proof” heading. The body was corrected to the required “Evidence” heading, and its [replacement check passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38826974291) on the same head. Earlier-head CI caught the source repairs documented above and had two pre-checkout action-download failures; final CI has no failed shards. No CI rerun or branch update was requested to chase green.

The benchmark sandbox has been removed after verifying all task processes stopped. Cold-session GitHub-options readiness remains the explicit performance gap described above; the separate diagnostic does not conclusively explain the final measured timeout increase. No user-profile code or production state was changed.

prs.title: fix(agents): keep deepseek v4 reasoning replay when the transport requires it
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`resolveTranscriptPolicy` decides whether historical reasoning must be kept for an OpenAI-completions route that no plugin owns. Its `REASONING_CONTENT_REPLAY_MODEL_IDS` copy (`src/agents/transcript-policy.ts:109`) is missing `deepseek-v4-flash` and `deepseek-v4-pro`, while the transport owner (`packages/ai/src/transports/openai-completions-replay.ts:131`) lists both and replays their reasoning content. For those two ids the policy therefore drops reasoning from history at the same time the transport decides it must be replayed — the two halves of one contract disagree.

## User Impact

A session on an OpenAI-compatible route (custom proxy, vLLM/LM Studio-style endpoint, or any model entry without `reasoning: true`) whose model id is `deepseek-v4-flash` or `deepseek-v4-pro` keeps its historical reasoning again, instead of the agent silently stripping it and the follow-up request losing the context the transport expected. No other model id changes behavior: the set is only consulted for ids already in the owner list plus the two added here.

## Why This Change Was Made

Classification: **behavior-completing**. The owner list documents the DeepSeek-style `reasoning_content` replay contract (#87575) and grew to the v4 ids; this hand-maintained copy did not follow. The bundled DeepSeek plugin itself also declares `dropReasoningFromHistory: false` (`extensions/deepseek/index.ts:37`), so the copy contradicted both the transport and the plugin. The fix is the two missing ids — no option, config key, or new file.

## Evidence

Remote test host, tree from `git archive` of `upstream/main` (`3dba0514d30`) with the package-manager overlay; base and candidate differ only in `src/agents/transcript-policy.ts` (both trees carry the same extended test file). Command: `node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config vitest.config.ts src/agents/transcript-policy.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.

| Run | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Base (upstream/main + the new cases) | `Test Files 1 failed (1)`, `Tests 2 failed \| 42 passed (44)`, 10.14s |
| Candidate | `Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `Tests 44 passed (44)`, 10.14s |

Both new `it.each` cases fail on the base at `expect(policy.dropReasoningFromHistory).toBe(false)` (`src/agents/transcript-policy.test.ts:293`) and pass with the two ids added. Set diff against the owner: `only_owner = ["deepseek-v4-flash", "deepseek-v4-pro"]`, `only_copy = []`.

## Merge Danger

Only `resolveTranscriptPolicy`'s replay-id set changes; the transport, the plugin declarations, and every other policy branch are untouched. Model-id normalization (vendor prefix, `:cloud`/`:free` suffixes) already applies to both sides, so no new matching rules are introduced. Open PR #139979 also edits `src/agents/transcript-policy.ts` (its hunks remove the policy cache, not this list), so a trivial rebase may be needed depending on merge order.
