prs.title: fix(codex): backport terminal child release retries to October
prs.body:
Related: #173547

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes completed Codex subagent subscriptions staying claimed on October after both idle retention and fallback unsubscribe fail, even after the transport recovers.

## User Impact

Failed terminal cleanup retries through the existing per-thread queue every 30 seconds. Active follow-ups retain their subscription; successful cleanup adds no retry work. No new configuration or dependencies are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Backports #173547 (merged as fadcbe5870ccc54092646edab28324d288ca6e94, reviewed source head 08aed4fdcf9b5f2fd6941202d03fa3b16a121374) onto `kimiyu_openclaw_2026-10-01-beta1-reviewed` at 8a3081e9c4d78e0c8b21b30e964cf52ee1eaa006.

The monitor repair and nine regression cases are unchanged. October also needs main's read-only `isCodexAppServerLiveThreadProtected` helper; its existing ownership/protection state is reused. The existing protection-release no-op guards are combined to keep the file within its lint limit. October's cancellation interfaces remain intact. No separate registry, startup scan, reconnect mechanism, or runtime-version change is introduced.

## Evidence

- On unmodified October production code, three cleanup-retry regressions fail and 21 other cases pass. With the backport, all 24 cases pass: nine retry regressions plus 15 October custody cases.
- The tests exercise real monitor and client ownership paths with synthetic notifications, fake timers, and injected unsubscribe failures. They cover repeated failure, at most one release in flight, protected/admitted follow-ups, client/thread closure, and successful retention/release.
- Focused native wrapper run: 16.03 seconds wall, 14.31 seconds Vitest duration, under one second test execution. This is local proof, not measured hosted CI cost.
- All 43 client-runtime tests also pass after the equivalent no-op guard consolidation.
- Codex package types, all extension-test types, changed-file lint/format, and whitespace checks pass.
- Independent AutoReview raised one suggestion to permit only one retry. After checking the upstream contract and unsubscribe wrapper, it is non-actionable: repeated failures intentionally retry at 30-second intervals with one outstanding timer; successful already-unsubscribed responses end cleanup. Limiting the total attempt count would leave subscriptions stranded after longer outages. The raw review is not claimed clean.
- No live native-server recovery or production acceptance is claimed. No deployment, pin change, or dependency upgrade.

prs.title: ci(ui): give the real-Gateway UI shards 30 minutes on 16-class runners
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Real-Gateway UI shards exhausted the former 20-minute whole-job limit on 16-class runners while tests were still passing. Peter approved this on October 14, 2026: “Gateway shard limit: raise it to 30 minutes -> ok”.

## User Impact

Give every normal Blacksmith real-Gateway shard 30 minutes. Preserve the existing 40-minute hosted/retry fallback, runner size, worker count, shard split, individual test deadlines, and every other job's limit. The invoked runner/config chain has no inner 20-minute aggregate deadline to adjust. Update the existing timeout guards and CI documentation.

## Why This Change Was Made

After #170607 moved this workload from eight visible CPUs / 31 GiB to four CPUs / 15 GiB, successful jobs reached 17–19 minutes (maximum 19:04). The reported 1.39× slower-runner factor puts that maximum near 26:30; this is a headroom estimate, not a measured post-change runtime. First attempts of [#171744](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38558653729/attempts/1) and [#172245](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38585248708/attempts/1) hit the 20-minute limit without a failed assertion. Their later coordinator-authorized attempts passed both shards.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Repository workflow validation after final main integration | Passed: actionlint, zizmor, CI-owner, composite-input, and conflict-marker checks |
| Targeted timeout/routing guards after final main integration | 14 passed, one file, one worker |
| Final scoped whitespace check | Passed |
| Independent review through P2 | No actionable findings; added/removed lines remain identical to the reviewed patch |
| Earlier full CI | [38634242374](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38634242374) passed at `3bb2a6c440e5642bdd814cab04acfa281e9d867a`; Gateway shards completed in 20:27 / 14:21 |
| Coordinator-authorized retry | [38648992031, attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38648992031/attempts/2) passed at `012642df1a6431d52e2cabeb3484fca9e8c8c0b2`, including config-safe-write; Gateway shards completed in 17:31 / 16:17 |
| Earlier head CI | [38702630189](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38702630189), head `082629aee9b864d21f6aad952be35ec0a52700f7`: seven root jobs failed; attribution below |
| Earlier PR context and evidence | Passed in run 38703190882 on head `082629ae` |

Refreshed head `82a1289c47cf9ab785dcc1513fb51b0a2ba5fd29` merges `2439bd90525da3770727168559aaab7208f4641b` from main without rebasing. The 14 targeted guard tests and workflow validation were each rerun once and passed; the authored added/removed lines are byte-identical to the independently reviewed patch. Fresh PR CI run [38763317738](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38763317738) completed on this head. Its only failed test exactly matches scheduled main, as documented below; the older runs remain historical evidence. Its PR diff remains exactly five files, +23/−19 lines; combined LOC is 17,049 → 17,053. There is no production UI/startup change, so screenshots, startup builds, and production Knip are not applicable. One targeted Testbox baseline attempt was cancelled during source staging; no test ran and the lease was released. No local E2E or broad local suite was run. CODEOWNERS had no matching rule for these files; enforced review/security gates remain required.

## Refreshed-head CI attribution

Run [38763317738](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38763317738), attempt 2, tested head `82a1289c47cf9ab785dcc1513fb51b0a2ba5fd29`. Its only failed root job is [checks-ui-e2e (5/9)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38763317738/job/116587228801): `command palette background creation > aligns settings and preserves keyboard focus in light at 390`, with `Missing settings control: .agent-select__label`. The same exact case and error failed on the latest inspected completed scheduled-main run [38761419261](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38761419261/job/116514092024). All other current-head jobs passed or were intentionally unselected. The two real-Gateway jobs passed in 15:06 and 22:56, demonstrating the headroom needed beyond the former 20-minute budget.

Both logs are retained for native admin evidence; the CI checkout is `c857135b6333fc160b5d1045e03ec463eb6fa3c7`, merging this PR head into main parent `c8260d933e58a84ded513f929391b7bb990665c4`. The admin route is authorized for the matching failure; security and enforced review checks remain required.

## Historical-head failure attribution

In the earlier head run, both real-Gateway shards completed well below the new whole-job limit (12:17 and 14:35). They failed assertions, not timeout cancellation. Six of the seven root jobs have exact matching failures on scheduled main [38699948035](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38699948035). The command-palette case passed on that main run and is plainly unrelated to this timeout-only change under Peter’s October 15 landing rule; no matching inherited signature is claimed for it.

| PR job | Matching main job | Exact failure |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Real-Gateway 2/2, 116314770539 | 116305820846 | Logs lifecycle: changed source/reconnect recovery |
| Real-Gateway 1/2, 116314770617 | 116305820928 | Session PR readers: current workspace and reader |
| Real-Gateway 1/2, 116314770617 | Plainly unrelated; passed on both inspected main runs | Command-palette grouped spawned conversation: RPC settlement assertion at line 466, called from line 521 |
| UI 1/9, 116314771362 | 116305821390 | Both spawned-session nesting cases |
| UI 2/9, 116314771513 | 116305821502 | Native-pointer nested-conversation promotion |
| Node small 2-2, 116314772364 | 116305824024 | Windows CI partitions: extra shared config |
| Node small 9-1, 116314772439 | 116305823997 | Selected Gateway/embedded-agent runner-capacity planner |
| Extension lint 2, 116316223968 | 116305822505 | LINE send test: no-shadow at line 159, outer declaration at line 143 |

The actual earlier-head CI checkout was merge `3c73125a9c8035afbd73708ca8a1c8f16b573590`, with ordered parents `281fe9ffda60881138a090b12a105dd431bf2447` (main) and `082629aee9b864d21f6aad952be35ec0a52700f7` (PR). Only the five reviewed files differ from that main parent. The UI, runtime, package, planner, Windows partition and LINE source inputs match the main parent exactly. This source comparison does not replace the missing baseline attribution for the command-palette case.

## Admin landing evidence

Peter’s October 15 rule authorizes landing pre-existing or plainly unrelated CI failures. The coordinator explicitly directed this PR to use the native admin route after verifying hosted/retry/fork rows stay at 40 minutes and every other real-Gateway row is 30 minutes.

The command-palette RPC-settlement assertion is plainly unrelated: this diff changes only the whole-job timeout, the guard test and CI documentation. Its UI, runtime, invoked runner and per-test deadlines are unchanged and byte-identical to the actual CI main parent. The failure occurred long before either whole-job deadline. The exact case passed on scheduled-main runs 38699948035 and [38707273563](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38707273563), in 20.951 seconds in the latter. Its original pending RPC remains unidentified; failed CI is not represented as green.

The remaining six root jobs have exact test or diagnostic matches recorded above. For the earlier head, all seven roots, the aggregate gate, actual checkout parents, source-object equality and raw logs were bound in native admin evidence. Any admin admission of the refreshed head must bind its own current run and failures. Independent security checks and enforced owner reviews remain required. A targeted Testbox baseline attempt was cancelled during source staging; no test ran, the lease was released, and its temporary checkout was removed.

## Native landing status

The refreshed head is reviewed (`READY FOR /prepare-pr`, zero findings) and prepared without another push. The coordinator-authorized second CI attempt completed with the same exact main-matching E2E failure. Fresh protected Security Review publisher [38784841370](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38784841370), triggered by that completion, successfully reviewed this exact PR head on October 15 at 18:21 UTC. Native admin evidence now binds CI attempt 2, its actual checkout, the one failed root job and downstream gate. Security and enforced review gates remain required.

Wizard channel selection and sensitive inputs already had native Solid implementations, but the shared Wizard renderer reached them through `LitContent` and Lit facades. Render both components directly so their lifetime and reactive props stay inside the Wizard Solid tree.

Delete the two facades after moving their last runtime caller. Cron now imports its channel option type from the native component; the sensitive-input props type becomes private. Existing input drafts, labels, classes, selection values, validation, and submission behavior are preserved. No lazy import boundary changes.

## Evidence

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Codemod dry-run | Zero templates/diagnostics in the Wizard renderer and both retired facades; matching converter source, qualified donor parser |
| Independent autoreview | Original port and failure-only diagnostic both complete, no actionable P0–P2 findings |

| Full PR CI | Current [run 38821128409](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38821128409): 37 successful jobs, 26 skipped; all nine UI E2E shards, three UI-unit shards, both real-Gateway shards, security, and performance passed. Only the inherited mock-export baseline check and its aggregate failed; exact-base proof below. `ci:full` selected. |

The retained tests cover confirmation, busy state, input draft preservation, sensitive reveal and submission, cancellation, manual sign-in, and multiselect ownership. The new case verifies that channel selection submits its channel ID through the native picker. No local broad E2E or parity runs. Unit-file wall time: 8.92 s Vitest / 12.40 s wrapper shard; assertions 291 ms. Current full CI wall time: 14 min 14 s.

The four inspected, synthetic before/after screenshots below use the real components served by Vite at 1040×700. Both capture runs passed reveal/selection and page-error assertions; each before/after PNG pair is byte-identical. prs.title: fix(codex): stop failing successful one-shot commands at cleanup
prs.body:
Closes #161576

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes completed Codex `agent exec` commands being reported as failed, with their final response discarded, because native process cleanup cannot be certified.

## User Impact

Successful one-shot commands finish normally. If cleanup genuinely fails, the command still exits `1`, retains state for inspection, and preserves the completed answer, payloads, usage, and model metadata with `error.kind: "cleanup"`.

Strict one-shots now use OpenClaw's shell and filesystem tools instead of Codex-native execution. Codex remains the model runtime; ordinary Gateway-backed Codex sessions retain their native tools. No configuration migration or operator action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Native terminal completion, an empty terminal inventory, and app-server exit cannot establish settlement of descendants whose native handles already retired. This selects the existing host-owned execution path before the one-shot tool catalog and prompt are built. The existing native cleanup-uncertainty guard is unchanged; this does not suppress cleanup errors or claim to add a missing native descendant-shutdown primitive.

The CLI now annotates the completed result on cleanup failure instead of replacing it with an empty error envelope. Existing task-error/timeout precedence and state-lock retention remain unchanged. No new process manager, dependency, protocol, or configuration surface is introduced; production changes total eight net lines.

## Evidence

Live macOS proof used the real Codex app-server **0.162.1**, OpenAI API-key authentication, and the same finite shell command that writes a synthetic artifact. Each invocation used separate state, config, native home, and workspace; no live Gateway or shared state was changed.

| Live case | Exit | Artifact | Completed final response |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Current main `e19d0174124e` | `1` | Saved | Discarded (`final: ""`, `payloads: []`) |
| Patched normal cleanup | `0` | Saved | Preserved |
| Patched, test-owned launcher refusing graceful EOF | `1` | Saved | Preserved, `error.kind: "cleanup"`; model and usage retained |

The forced-cleanup case used real inference and a deliberately non-settling transport launcher, exercising the production cleanup failure. No sampled task-owned process survived either patched invocation. This is not an arbitrary-daemon containment claim. The original ChatGPT OAuth route was not live-tested.

Focused tests (repository runner wall time):

| `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` | Result | Wall time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-one-shot-cleanup.test.ts` | 10 passed | 29.19 s |
| `src/commands/agent-exec.state-lock.test.ts` | 6 passed | 22.39 s |
| `src/commands/agent-exec.test.ts` | 20 passed | 29.62 s |

The existing attempt suite also passed before the new regression was moved into the focused one-shot suite. Runtime build, core/extension production and test typechecks, targeted typed lint, formatting, whitespace, and the line-cap ratchet passed. AutoReview completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings. CI seconds are pending PR CI.

The broader `check:changed` run is **not green**: the untouched base independently reproduces an environment budget mismatch (`452` names versus budget `453`). Its dead-export scans also report `readCodexTurnCompletedNotification`, `WikiPageNotUtf8Error`, `renderKbd`, `syncDropdownItemRadio`, and `presentedProperty` in untouched modules; this change does not alter their production import/export graph. These findings are not masked or repaired in this PR.

Scope/simplification: production `+9/-1` lines; tests `+71/-1` lines. The fix reuses the existing execution and cleanup owners rather than introducing another shutdown mechanism.

prs.title: fix: exclude generated sandbox skills from Git changes
prs.body:
Closes #173546

## What Problem This Solves

Sandboxed Git workflows discover runtime-provided skill packages as untracked project changes. The files are already excluded from workspace reconciliation and publication, but ordinary Git discovery still includes them. A small development task can therefore capture substantial generated content during review.

## User Impact

Generated sandbox skill copies stay out of ordinary Git status and untracked-file discovery after initial preparation, cached reuse, and refresh. Tracked changes, original source skills, and unrelated project files remain visible, including siblings under `.openclaw`. Existing read-only skill mounts continue to apply.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing materializer now writes a self-ignoring `.gitignore` inside the generated skills root before its cache-return path, and retains that file during pruning. Keeping this with the producer covers existing cached directories and new copies through the same owner, without changing repository Git configuration or adding review-specific filtering. The file is readable by the sandbox user through the existing mounts.

## Evidence

The actual-Git regression fails on the original owner because discovery includes the generated manifest and skill file. It passes after this correction through first sync, repair of a cached directory missing the ignore file, and a source refresh; tracked changes and ordinary untracked siblings remain visible throughout.

Remote validation passed changed-file formatting/lint, the selected production and test type checks, all 19 owner tests, and 46 tests across eight related custody, sandbox-context, and read-only bridge files. `pnpm test src/skills/loading/workspace-skill-sync.runtime.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` took 30.17 seconds wall time, including 27.10 seconds in the native test run with compiler preparation. The related batch took 380.91 seconds including its 296.3-second E2E runtime build. The same owner file passed all 19 tests in hosted CI in 5.45 seconds. [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38824998882) passed all 39 selected jobs on this head, and independent review is clean.


The actual guest-session check also passed using a combined test build containing this PR's exact materializer bytes (`0458dfeca06d7646957c488f192cd9871f317293`). After normal development continuation, read-only inspection inside the running sandbox returned:

```text
$ git status --short
 M README.md
?? shipping-fee.js
?? shipping-fee.test.js
$ git check-ignore .openclaw/sandbox-skills/skills/.openclaw-sync.json
.openclaw/sandbox-skills/skills/.openclaw-sync.json
```

The generated ignore file contained `*` followed by a newline and had mode `644`. Previously, 74 generated skill files appeared among 76 untracked files and inflated capture to 2,152,306 bytes across five passes. Capture now uses one pass containing only the task change; the guest's 24 existing tests and diff check passed. This proves live Git discovery and capture. Completion of the separate host reviewer command remains outside this repair.

prs.title: refactor(agents): trust admitted facts and simplify metadata bookkeeping
prs.body:
<!-- Exact-head CI remains the landing gate; local proof gaps are explicit below. -->

Current CI status: submitted head `e449a9cabd0ec1750ebbb0b32474a8ee15d3ab3a` has failing run `38825468464`; this PR is not ready to land. Failed-job logs are being attributed individually. Local repairs restore real raw-source/plugin/error guards and sparse terminal delivery, correct invalid diagnostic/lifecycle fixtures, and remove only tests of the explicitly retired observer/reselection/in-place-mutation mechanisms. Focused failed-file proof and fresh independent repair review are running. The local candidate removes 900 net production lines; it is not yet committed or pushed. The submitted-head 912-line measurement below remains historical until that repair is published. Queue-authority and first-sign-in lifecycle failures remain unresolved attribution, not claimed inherited or green.

## What Problem This Solves

Agent preparation repeats validation and copying of already-admitted facts, duplicates small responsibilities, and carries speculative metadata-reload bookkeeping alongside the real execution and durability boundaries.

## User Impact

The cleanup preserves existing features and public contracts. Two adjacent failure-handling repairs stop synthetic auth fallback from hiding unavailable credentials/OAuth refresh failures and stop failed history inspection from producing an empty compaction boundary.

No config, CLI, SDK, Gateway protocol, persisted-data, dependency, SQLite schema/durability/retention/permission changes or operator action. The standalone session-memory backend and its factory, registry, expiry, federation and tests are untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing parser/producer as the owner of a fact, carry that fact through consumers, and keep current authorization at effects. This removes redundant internal scalar/record/array checks, copies, private-container freezes and no-op coalesces. LF counting, process-failure projection, Claude CLI identity and transcript-header lookup now use their existing owners. Shared borrowed-fact freezes, actual external-input boundaries, bounded caches, ordinary parallel sessions/tool calls, FIFO and accepted write settlement remain.

The structural cuts remove a private full-payload catalog mismatch protocol, speculative registry-lender observation/recovery, repeated published-owner reselection, passive suspension generations/compensating writes, obsolete append forwarders and scheduler fallback bookkeeping. Deprecated SDK append methods remain inherited with unchanged signatures; native persistence still owns rollback.

### Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Private catalog worker envelope guards and generation/request/reconstruction digests: the typed host is the sole producer and the maintained transport already correlates task IDs. Pooling #134935 and consolidation #167816 did not identify malformed private inputs in real use; #127712 injects a drifted fingerprint in a harness. Arbitrary in-process corruption now fails naturally rather than using a special mismatch protocol. The real stall repair in #157459/#157107, plugin-context reuse identity, request-local credentials and effect authority remain.
- Registry-lender retirement graph/callbacks: #161267 traces sibling-Gateway recovery to hosted CI, not a human deployment incident. A sibling registry retiring while passive catalog facts are cached may leave metadata stale until explicit reload/republication/restart. Minimal cache-retirement release, active leases, real shutdown settlement and live plugin invocation authority remain.
- Published-owner successor reselection: #169478 demonstrates a controlled Gateway/Telegram-mock replacement interleaving and a zero-retry assertion, not a cited actual-use report. A second overlapping replacement can now fail the read visibly; the next request selects the replacement. One pending wait, exact config/lifetime checks and the distinct real-incident auth retry from #156561/#156178 remain.
- Passive quota-suspension generation/rollback: #103211's evidence schedules a 250ms suspension across teardown; linked #101720 describes source-level hypothetical effects, not an observed teardown crash. #121278 subsequently removed global auto-resume timers. A committed diagnostic marker crossing same-process shutdown/start may remain until its existing TTL/recovery owner handles it. FIFO, closed-admission checks, error warnings and normal durability stay.
- MCP scheduler fallback: #162079 covers controlled multiple-host interleavings, not a cited deployment with competing schedulers. The latest explicit binding owns the manager and awaits predecessor shutdown; closing it does not resurrect an older host. Explicit rebinding/restart recovers.
- Passive advertised MCP catalog owner/membership checks: #131793's loopback reload interleaving is accepted best effort. A same-config reload crossing metadata installation may leave older advertised tools until reset/reconciliation. Config fingerprints and actual invocation authority stay; metadata is not an authorization grant.
- Internal capture/getter/cache copies: callers do not mutate the producer-owned nested facts. #164566's immediate caller mutation, #79882 isolation and #95506 cardinality proofs are synthetic; measured caches from #131442/#168655 remain. Unsupported internal mutation may affect another borrower until refresh/restart. External update admission, writer invalidation, cache bounds and public mutable-input isolation remain.
- Private WeakMap wrapper freezes: containers from #130579/#133324 cannot be borrowed by consumers. Removing their freezes accepts only unsupported internal mutation; issuer/executable/name/auth equality, returned shared frozen facts and the real TTS delivery behavior remain.
- Hydration revision: #153325 introduced synthetic worker consistency proof, not an actual same-manager concurrent-read incident. Merely starting a second read no longer invalidates the first; retained full-view/target/version comparisons reject a genuinely changed view, and navigation/write authority stays.
- Own-append reread: #156095 introduced worker receipt reconstruction for synthetic responsiveness proof. An unchanged local view now uses its durable append receipt position directly. Superseded views, unanchored legacy cases, pending-tool reconciliation and commit-before-ack remain; no new integrity assumption is made for those paths.
- Repeated typed facts: malformed data fabricated after its canonical parser/producer is not repaired again by every consumer. Representative owner histories include #126492, #143664 and #170257. Unknown network/plugin/model/file payloads remain admitted once; actual optional source fields, nullable seams and real union discriminators remain handled. In particular generic Gateway list/search response guards were retained after tracing their unparsed network path.
- Internal probe/media timestamps: typed process-owned clocks are not re-admitted by every reader. Existing TTL pruning, bounded probe/cache storage, duplicate prevention, delivery behavior and security scopes remain. No clock-skew recovery guarantee is added.

### Scope and delta

Production delta is **912 net lines removed** across 224 production files (+1,010/-1,922), excluding tests, fixtures, support/helpers, generated files and declarations. Whole-scope scan: 10,322 original occurrences have decisions, including 100 later identified as test-only; 43 repeated-name families plus semantic-owner clusters were reviewed. Cross-tree families and genuine unknown/public seams remain with their owners. Two zero-LOC edits were dropped entirely rather than add exceptions for existing file-length violations.

This uses the campaign's explicit 500–999-line exception after a whole-scope pass; no feature or boundary was removed to manufacture 1,000 lines. Required baseline updates only shrink allowances for removed code.

## Evidence

Current head: `e449a9cabd0ec1750ebbb0b32474a8ee15d3ab3a`, conflict-only rebase onto `a5832a9b38666c2be563a39e6003e294cd6732e3`. GitHub reported CONFLICTING before integration. Three resolutions retain main's removed diagnostic progress path and parameterized cron-list coverage, while keeping this cut's type import and removal of the retirement callback. Range-diff confirms no additional production cleanup. Local receipts below predate that rebase unless explicitly noted; fresh affected types, runtime/static cycles, focused tests and lint are running. Exact-head hosted CI is required before landing.

- Pre-fix owning-boundary regressions failed for both auth failure classes and both history-inspection stages; the moved unavailable-secret fixture independently failed by returning synthetic credentials instead of rejecting.
- Frozen-candidate runtime cycles: zero. Static import cycles: zero. SDK export synchronization passed.
- SDK surface API check passed: no forbidden exported subpaths, no public wildcard reexports and no unauthorized removals against the checked-in shipped inventory. The check reports the existing inventory-version warning (v2026.10.2 versus local stable v2026.10.3); release-owned inventory regeneration is outside this cut.
- Independent P2 review completed with two findings, both investigated and declined: passive mid-reload metadata staleness is the explicit accepted tradeoff above; the reasoning-ID warning overlooks the retained earlier non-string rejection and attributes an unchanged neighboring helper to this diff. This is not a scoped-clean review claim.
- Core types passed on the frozen pre-rebase production inputs. Formatting passed on 259 changed existing TS/MTS/MJS files; post-rebase formatting also passes all three conflict files. Repaired line-cap, max-lines and assertion-safety ratchets passed. Main already contains the two earlier stale max-lines removals, so they are no longer part of this PR; its remaining assertion baseline edits remove 23 allowances, with no increases.
- Supported `pnpm build:ci-artifacts` passed (exit 0), including runtime bundles, SDK declarations, all 155 public SDK subpaths, UI assets and startup metadata. Its phase time was 1h46m on the heavily loaded local host. This receipt precedes the two exact zero-LOC restorations; all remaining changed production inputs are unchanged. The earlier full `pnpm build` was deliberately stopped during global declaration emission and is not claimed as passing; no build-tool edits or manual skip flags were introduced.
- Local focused selection included all 31 changed/new test files and retained owner, sibling, rollback, SDK and lint-suppression coverage: 278 existing paths. Completed configurations: unit-fast 58 files/527 tests passed (1720s, 85% transform); unit-fast-isolated one file/four tests passed (1023s, 93% transform); tooling two files passed and one failed (18 passed/six failed assertions). Lint-suppressions passed all three assertions. The broad run was deliberately stopped (143) during gateway-database-workers initialization with no assertions in that configuration; later configurations are unrun locally. Host load exceeded 400. The history-failure regression was moved assertion-identically into the existing degraded-fallback suite. Direct final auth/compaction proof is pending below; exact-head CI owns broad remaining coverage.
- Investigated local tooling failures remain failures, not passing or proven inherited evidence: unchanged eager-import-closure's PR inventory case exceeded 120s at 165957ms; extracted dependencies at 268482ms; old anchor/empty dependencies at 148603ms; old anchor/legacy dependencies at 180244ms; migrated-finalization imports at 228424ms. Its wrapper-bootstrap fixture reported null child status instead of 0 (121807ms, no signal/error details surfaced by the assertion). The packaged-scripts closure case and 11 other cases passed. None of the 19 changed files in the wrapper inventory adds a runtime import; their only import-edge change removes an unused normalization helper. No timeout, assertion, inventory or retry policy was changed. No serial base replay or main-red attribution is claimed. Exact-head hosted CI remains required, with attribution if it fails.
- The original 276-path selection included one unchanged process E2E sibling and was stopped during its mandatory global declaration prerequisite (exit 143; no assertions executed). Existing process delivery/activity/retention suites replace it in the local selection; delivery exercises the unchanged failure projection through the actual process/Code Mode boundary. No test, assertion, skip, timeout or baseline was weakened. That E2E suite remains an explicit unrun gap, not a claimed CI pass.
- Actual changed-file checks passed all pre-type stages, production types and agents-root test types (388s), then were deliberately stopped (143) during broader test graphs. This is not a full check-changed pass; remaining test graphs are a local gap. Source-backed lint inspected all 257 original TS/MTS paths; its only findings were file-length violations in the two files subsequently restored to zero diff. The unchanged remaining 255 paths had no diagnostics; this reuses an inspected subset, not a claimed exit-zero invocation. No timeout, retry, skip or suppression was added.

prs.title: fix(usage): Usage tab double-counts prompts that older Codex runs mirrored twice
prs.body: Closes #140464 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: the Usage tab counts one prompt as two user messages when the transcript holds a prompt that an older Codex app-server run mirrored a second time. ## User Impact User impact: Usage message counts and the session message list show each prompt once, including sessions recorded before upgrading. Token and cost totals were already correct and do not change. ## Why This Change Was Made Codex app-server turns on releases such as 2026.9.2 annotated the admitted prompt with `mirrorIdentity` and `mirrorSourceFingerprint`, then mirrored a second user row with the same pair. Main no longer writes that row, but retained transcripts keep it and the Usage reader counts every user row. The rollup now skips a user row whose mirror identity and fingerprint match the previous counted user row, and `loadSessionLogs` applies the same rule. The key is kept next to `lastUserTimestamp` in the rollup and in the partitioned checkpoint, so a pair split across incremental refreshes still counts once. `USAGE_COST_ROLLUP_VERSION` goes from 8 to 9, so every cached count is rebuilt. Prompts with the same text but different identities still count separately. ## Evidence - Upgrade from v2026.10.2 on a real Gateway, with the Codex app-server against QA Lab's mock OpenAI provider. One isolated cron agent turn on v2026.9.2 wrote the reported pair, and a control session sent the same text as two turns. v2026.10.2 then ran `openclaw doctor --fix` (agent database v19 to v24) and its Gateway on that state, followed by this branch's doctor (v24 to v26) and Gateway on the same state. On v2026.10.2 the cron session's `sessions.usage` showed user 2 and total 3, and its session logs listed user, user, assistant. On this branch it showed user 1 and total 2, and the logs listed user, assistant. The control session stayed at user 2 and total 4, `usage.cost` stayed at 264 tokens, and the Usage rows cached at version 6 were rebuilt. - On that upgrade, `chat.history` for both sessions matched what v2026.10.2 read, and this branch's doctor left the config byte-identical. One more prompt sent to the control session through this branch's Gateway took it to user 3 on the next incremental refresh, and the cron session stayed at user 1. That turn's model call failed outside the QA harness, so it has no reply. - New tests in the worker refresh file (full scan, pair split across a cached refresh) and the reporting file (logs) fail on main and pass here, and a same-text control passes on both. Keying on the fingerprint alone fails the control. The split refresh test restores the checkpoint and partitions through `partitionUsageCostRollup` the way the worker does, and leaving `lastUserMirrorKey` out of the partitioned checkpoint fails it with a count of 2 instead of 1. - The 33 Usage-related test files pass, 309 tests. `--maxWorkers=1` wall time is 3.4s for the worker refresh file and 34.3s for the reporting file. The new tests take 0 to 4 ms. - Rows cached at version 7 or 8, including the ones current main writes, decode to nothing and are rebuilt, and a version 9 row is reused. - `pnpm check:changed` passes apart from two steps that fail the same way on unmodified main. The dead export scan lists unused exports in files this PR doesn't touch, and the max-lines ratchet reports the env var count of 452 below its budget of 453. Usage tab cron session from an earlier run of the same setup on main `e380a256`, before and after. Maintainer edits are enabled. GitHub offers that here as edits and access to secrets, and the fork has no Actions secrets, variables or environments.

prs.title: fix(update): recover stopped gateways after unverified service activation
prs.body:
Refs #171435. This fixes the stopped-Gateway outcome; the initiating native installer failure remains undetermined.

## What Problem This Solves

An update can leave a runnable Gateway stopped after unverified service-definition recovery. Final recovery originally only observed the stopped service and told the operator to keep it stopped without a named data risk.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing lifecycle owner supplies the recovery restart for an owned service stopped by this update. It never repeats an explicit restart attempt. An unverified installer receipt can permit the first explicit restart. Native restart-health timeout continuation is scoped to final recovery and uses the existing update readiness budget; other restart callers retain their behavior.

Migration, rollback and Doctor producers record their known data risk on the recovery verdict. Consumers read that typed fact. Resolved forward admission settles the risk before authorizing restart; unresolved risks remain unsafe. The private in-memory field is persisted through the already-shipped step failure-fact channel and decoded at one boundary, keeping strict v2026.10.2/v2026.10.3 run readers compatible. Settled success returns from its owner before an update exception is constructed.

The latest CI repair corrects a test double, with no production changes. The real native command records the attempt immediately before child dispatch; the recovery matrix's replacement omitted that notification. Linux reports a stopped service while macOS can report an unknown runtime, masking the missing event. The matrix now explicitly observes stopped service and emits the real command's callback. All existing one-start/zero-start, health, migration and persistence assertions remain intact.

## User Impact

Verified recovery of an unverified definition succeeds with a warning and `openclaw update repair` guidance. Failed startup retains its failure and gives concrete repair/deep-status commands. Only a recorded named data risk can require keeping the Gateway stopped. Unverified definition recovery retains both package generations.

## Evidence

Head: d3278efd1dc36fdf17473742e8354be3b0299179. Rebased without conflicts onto pinned current main `5431f5cd8e7c1b717b1de14917ed0fee965ee314`.

- All four requested files were run through `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <four paths> --maxWorkers=2` with `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node`, then `bun`. Bun is the CI-pinned fork revision `1.4.3-canary.1+94f8f5ffe`. Every test process starts with an explicit isolated HOME and OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR under this worktree's `.artifacts`.
- Rebased branch before the fixture correction: recovery 42/42 and Doctor 31/31 under each runtime (73 each). Plain pinned main: recovery 34/34 and Doctor 31/31 under each runtime (65 each). Node orchestration wall times were 412.30 s / 443.78 s respectively; Bun 253.89 s / 221.60 s. Runtime/compiler preparation is included in these orchestration times.
- Portable reproduction: setting only the service fixture to stopped, while retaining the old missing-callback mock, fails exactly the four CI cases (`settled`, `migration-required`, `current-core-parked`, `current-core-rollback-refused`) with two restart calls instead of one. Ten other matrix cases pass.
- Guard negative control: after correcting the callback, temporarily removing both production attempt guards still fails those exact four count assertions (ten others pass). The production source was restored byte-for-byte before final proof. These failures demonstrate that the preserved assertions still detect repeated starts.
- Final corrected fixture: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/update-cli/update-command-post-update-repair.test.ts src/cli/update-cli/update-command-service-command.test.ts --maxWorkers=2` passes under Node and Bun: recovery 42/42 and native dispatch 7/7 (49 each). Orchestration wall time: Node 191.70 s, Bun 60.51 s. The real native-dispatch child requires the attempt callback to have run before it starts. The unchanged Doctor proof above is reused; the repair changes only the separately isolated recovery fixture.
- CLI-update test typechecking (`node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.cli-update.json --noEmit`), changed-file type-aware Oxlint, formatting and `git diff --check` pass. Independent Codex review of this repair and its unchanged native/lifecycle owners is scoped-clean at P0/P1. The simplification pass leaves one existing test file changed: +4/-1 (net +3), production +0.

The Linux Bun offline-maintenance cascade was not reproduced on either revision; it is not claimed fixed or proven inherited by a failing-main control. CI's first failure is the schema-guard authority-retirement case, followed by repeated errors naming that original database and failed state-lifecycle teardown. The stack reaches the broker's access guard without captured maintenance scope or cleanup access. Those authority/capture/cleanup owners and all three Doctor test files are unchanged by this PR; the private recovery-fact branches are dormant for these fixtures. The remaining unknown is which Linux worker opener first loses custody during that case. No lease-admission check, assertion, timeout, retry, skip or baseline was changed to hide it. Local evidence is macOS; new Linux CI remains necessary.

Existing native activation timing is also present on main: Node's cold-source activation test took 53.961 s on the branch and 46.741 s on main; the related custody-revocation test took 43.327 s / 46.052 s. These pre-existing costs were recorded without increasing timeouts.

The complete PR against pinned main is production +316/-148 (net +168), tests +849/-248 (net +601), documentation +10. This latest repair adds no production architecture or restart policy. Earlier growth includes lifecycle ownership, compatible persistence projection and producer-owned risk settlement. The generic live harness was not rerun; no operator Gateway or default state was used.

<details>
<summary>Retained earlier proof and known failures (published safety-repair head 348dadb58aab)</summary>

These are prior-head results, not a claim of a fresh full replay after this rebase. Requested local replay (all files, original selection order):


- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/update-cli --maxWorkers=4`: 182 files, 2,499 passing tests; four owned test failures were then corrected and the complete affected files replayed below. The post-update repair matrix was not edited in this safety repair. Two pre-existing skipped files / 21 skipped tests remain.
- The literal `src/cli/update-cli.` argument selected no files, so all 21 root `update-cli*.test.ts` paths were passed explicitly in their original order: 290 passing tests; one inherited macOS failure, `handles changed service owner before already-current convergence`, previously reproduced on untouched `e106d1fa`. The Git restart stopped/throws cases and already-current stop-convergence cases pass.
- All 184 `src/infra/update-*.test.ts` files: 179 passing files / 2,421 passing tests; five pre-existing skipped files / 78 skipped tests, exit 0.
- Direct and one-barrel consumers outside those directories: 32 files, 1,127 passing tests. The sole host failure is `package-acceptance-workflow.test.ts > keeps every tracked repository skill visible to Git-aware syncs`: the shared `.git/info/exclude:47` rule `.agents/` matches tracked skill files under `git check-ignore --no-index`. The test and `.gitignore` are unchanged from `e106d1fa`; shared Git metadata was not edited.
- `node --experimental-vm-modules --test scripts/tests/update-restart-module-outcome.mjs`: 19/19 pass, including physical backup-retention assertions.

Final focused proof:

- Reporting: `update-recovery-guidance.test.ts` 28/28 pass, including the verified previous-generation rollback regression. Both additional direct consumers pass: `update-command-rollback.test.ts` 46/46 and `update-command-package.test.ts` 19/19.
- Physical database replay: 9/13 pass; four 120 s timeouts in `verification` (120.348 s), `convergence` (120.272 s), `started` (120.410 s), and `intervening` (125.317 s). The earlier full-directory run on the same production logic passed the first three; `intervening` reached the old reason assertion (15.646 s). Final post-migration-write (114.802 s), schema-neutral-write (94.540 s), and config-refused (67.671 s) pass with the stronger safety assertions. The four reported failures in this focused database replay are timeouts; no assertion failure was reported. The four timeouts remain failures, not passing evidence.
- During that replay, host load measured 76–80 on 32 CPUs, about 20,000 disk operations/s, and 70% system CPU. The fixture performs serial physical-database scenarios with fresh native executor/inspection/Doctor processes. Host contention is the supported timing diagnosis; it is not presented as a production fix. This lane's full-tree checker was paused during the remaining database cases, then resumed. No other lane's process was signaled, no timeout was raised, and the failures were not rerun to chase green.
- `update-command-post-update-repair.test.ts`: 42/42 pass, including all unchanged matrix expectations and the new invariant. Final isolated run: 139.83 s wall time in Vitest (77% tests), invariant 4.088 s; runtime preparation was 7m 56s, separately recorded. The earlier combined replay also passed the same 42 tests; these are counted once.

The four post-replay test corrections were fixture/contract fixes: the invariant now mocks the native stopped runtime and owns a real executor; three physical-database cases expect the resolved maintenance classification only after the forward-admission owner verifies the installed candidate. They still reject with `UpdateCommandFailure`, retain snapshots and later writes, and keep all physical row/schema/start-count assertions. Stronger assertions require an unsafe typed fact before admission and verified healthy recovery without the private risk afterward. All production bytes used in the broad replay are unchanged except the subsequently reviewed four-line guidance restriction for verified package rollbacks; that restriction is separately tested.

Every new proof command was invoked after exporting an isolated `HOME` and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` under this worktree's `.artifacts`. The generic live harness was not rerun. There is no new live Linux systemd proof.

The single new migration-safety invariant exercises migration inspection, inspection failure and rollback-blocked finalization through the real executor and finalizer with an explicitly stopped managed service. The mocked native start would make it healthy if incorrectly allowed. It requires no restart, an unsafe typed verdict and the persisted step fact. On `2778a790`, the negative control actually issues a native restart and marks recovery safe while `state-migrated-no-rollback` remains unresolved. The earlier macOS fixture returned an unknown runtime, which masked this start path; the invariant now supplies an explicitly stopped runtime. The earlier original stopped-Gateway regression fails all three selected cases on untouched `e106d1fa`; strict-reader/public-wire negative controls remain applicable to unchanged persistence projection.

`check:changed` passes the owned lint, production and test typechecks, line-cap growth, SQLite, loader and cycle checks. Its inherited failures are the environment budget (455 names against 454) and eight untouched Knip findings: `AuthProfileAuthorizationError`, `configuredOrFalseAsync`, `WorkerPreparationArtifactsSchema`, `PostgresSchemaDefinition`, `readPairedDevicePairingRecordsFromDatabase`, `webhookHeaders`, `renderCopyButton`, and `getChatRunOwnerSessionKey`. No ratchet/baseline was edited. The changed-file lint run reuses the immediately preceding qualified runtime build with the existing `OPENCLAW_OXLINT_SKIP_PREPARE=1` tooling switch; lint and typechecks remain enabled.

The final complete `check:changed` run on published head `348dadb58aab` finished with only those two inherited failing steps. Every owned guard passed, including core typechecking, all 28 test type graphs, changed-file lint, both line-cap checks, SQLite/storage, loader/cycle, and pairing guards. The focused CLI update test graph and final formatting checks also pass.

Independent Codex reviews found two issues, both corrected: clear the temporary configuration-risk marker after verified restoration, and exclude verified previous-package rollbacks from migrated-candidate guidance. The latter has a focused reporting regression. No accepted finding remains unresolved. No existing recovery assertion was weakened, timeout/retry raised, skip added, or baseline edited. No new CLI/config option, dependency or SQLite schema change.

This safety repair adds 65 and removes 37 production lines (net +28), with tests +143/-4 (net +139). The complete PR against `e106d1fa` is production +316/-148 (net +168), tests +845/-247 (net +598), and documentation +10. The repair stays within +40 production lines; the larger accumulated PR includes lifecycle restart ownership, compatible persistence projection, and explicit risk settlement rather than formatter inference.

Timing: the complete CLI directory took 2,129.33 s in Vitest (92% tests); the root CLI infra shard took 1,289.20 s (97% tests). The infra replay took 2,548.78 s wall time, with its main test shard 514.31 s and the E2E file 48.15 s. SDK preparation in the full replay recorded 30m 8.9s, including a 25m 29.3s package build and an additional 85.9s declaration build. An existing workflow consumer shard took 936.35 s (100% tests), dominated by repeated planner evaluations and subprocess cases. The additional direct guidance-consumer replay took 336.73 s across its two shards; the existing rollback file took 287.83 s (86% tests), with serial native rollback fixtures. These pre-existing costs were recorded without timeout increases or retries; the focused safety invariant does not perform a real install.

Thanks @rvelasquez for the incident evidence.

</details>

prs.title: docs+tests: clarify agents.list visibility scope across CLI and Gateway
prs.body:
## Summary
- document the visibility-scope difference between `openclaw agents list` (config-scoped) and Gateway `agents.list` (runtime-scoped)
- describe both supported explicit roster shapes: canonical `agents.entries` and compatibility `agents.list`
- add focused regression coverage for implicit discovery and both explicit roster shapes
- keep runtime behavior unchanged (no visibility-surface expansion)

## Root cause
Chat/UI surfaces (iOS/Android/TUI) call Gateway `agents.list` through `listAgentsForGateway`, while `openclaw agents list` uses `buildAgentSummaries` from configuration.

When no explicit roster is configured, Gateway may include disk-discovered agent state directories. When an explicit roster exists through either `agents.entries` or `agents.list`, Gateway intentionally restricts visibility to that configured scope. The CLI remains configuration-scoped.

## Changes
- Updated `docs/cli/agents.md` to use the shared “explicit roster” concept.
- Documented `agents.entries` as the canonical shape and `agents.list` as a supported compatibility shape.
- Added regression coverage proving both explicit shapes exclude disk-only agents from Gateway and CLI output.
- Retained the existing test proving Gateway/CLI divergence when no explicit roster exists.

## Verification
Automated checks are running for current head `527b3dc072a621d18935cb887293f77d8e53980f`.

Targeted commands:
```bash
pnpm test src/gateway/session-utils.test.ts -t "gateway agents.list and CLI agents list intentionally diverge"
pnpm test src/gateway/agent-list-explicit-roster.test.ts
pnpm build
```

## Real behavior proof
A redacted current-head CLI/Gateway RPC transcript is still required before final merge approval. This PR description will be updated with that evidence after running the current head in a real local setup.

## Notes
- no plugin diagnostic changes
- no security/routing-filter bypass
- no changes to agent eligibility or authentication policy

prs.title: fix(infra): keep quoted shell separators literal in approval binding
prs.body:
Closes #173240

## What Problem This Solves

`exec host=node` builds a POSIX shell carrier, then asks the approval binder whether the payload can be bound to a stable script operand. That check scanned the raw command text for `;[;&|<>]` before any quoting was parsed, so a *quoted literal* separator was treated as shell syntax and the request was refused before an approval could even be created:

```text
SYSTEM_RUN_DENIED: approval cannot safely bind this interpreter/runtime command
```

That blocked the documented two-step `gog auth add --remote` flow, where the callback URL legitimately contains `&` (`...?state=…&code=…`). Single quotes, double quotes and escaping all reproduced the refusal.

- Root cause: `shellPayloadNeedsStableBinding()` in `src/infra/system-run-mutable-file-operand.ts` started with `/[;&|<>]/u.test(shellCommand)` — a raw-text match that runs before `splitShellArgs()` and therefore cannot tell a quoted literal `&` from an active `&`.
- Fix: decide that question with a quote-aware scan. Separators inside single quotes (or inside double quotes with no command substitution) are literal argument data; separators outside quoting stay active syntax and keep the existing refusal.
- What did NOT change: the refusal itself, the approval flow, allowlist evaluation, operand binding, and every other check in the binder. Substitutions, redirections, pipelines, `&&`/`;` chains and mutable script operands are still refused.

## Why This Change Was Made

The guard is correct about *unquoted* operators; it was simply reading text before the shell grammar. Fixing the read keeps the existing security contract instead of weakening it.

- Best fix: distinguish literal from active characters at the same site, before `splitShellArgs()`. The binder already owns the "can this payload be bound?" decision, so no new owner or option is needed.
- Deliberately not done: removing the guard (would accept real operator chains) and reusing only the top-level control-operator helper (does not cover redirections or substitutions).
- Fails closed where quoting cannot be proven: a payload with an unbalanced quote still keeps the previous refusal, and a substitution inside double quotes (`"$(…;…)"`) is still refused because the substituted text is evaluated as real shell.
- Non-goals: no change to `splitShellArgs`, to `resolveMutableFileOperandIndex`, or to Windows command analysis.

## User Impact

Operators on a connected node can complete the quoted-callback-URL step of `gog auth add --remote` with approvals enabled. Commands whose separators are genuinely active are still refused, so the approval and file-binding guarantees are unchanged.

## Evidence

Real local runs on this branch (Node 24.22.0), exercising the exported production entry point the node host calls (`resolveSystemRunMutableFileOperandTarget`, planned as `["/bin/sh", "-c", text]` with `shellCommand: text`).

New regression test before the fix — red, reproducing the report:

```text
 × ... > shell payload literal metacharacter handling > accepts a quoted callback URL instead of refusing the payload 156ms
   → expected { ok: false, …(2) } to deeply equal { ok: true, argvIndex: null }
```

After the fix — green:

```text
 ✓ ... > accepts a quoted callback URL instead of refusing the payload
 ✓ ... > accepts double-quoted and escaped literal separators
 ✓ ... > still refuses active shell syntax
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  38 passed (38)
```

The negative case in the same file covers `&&` chains, `;` chains, `>` redirection, `"$(…;…)"`, `"$(…|…)"`, an unquoted backtick substitution containing `;`, and an unterminated quote — all still return `unsupported-command-shape` with the original message.

Adjacent suites exercising the same binder (11 files: `src/infra/system-run-*`, `src/node-host/invoke-system-run-plan`, `invoke-system-run-allowlist`, `bash-tools.exec.script-preflight`, `bash-tools.exec-host-node-phases`) pass with 0 failures (174 passed, 4 skipped). `npm run tsgo:core` passes; `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` are clean on both changed files. Not tested: a live agent-to-node round trip with real Google credentials — the reported refusal is reproduced and fixed at the planner seam.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used `rg`, `git diff` and `vitest` to locate `shellPayloadNeedsStableBinding()`, confirm the raw-text match runs before `splitShellArgs()`, and prove the before/after behaviour at the exported planner entry point. The implementer understands the code: the binder answers "can this payload be bound to a stable script operand", and the change only teaches it to read quoting before calling a quoted separator shell syntax.

prs.title: refactor(providers): simplify request and runtime ownership
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Provider runtimes still repeat auth/request construction and maintain machinery
for synthetic freshness and reentrant lifecycle scenarios. Those mechanisms add
work and competing ownership without improving normal provider operations.

## User Impact

Internal provider cleanup; no intended user-visible feature change or migration.
Rare recoverable freshness and reentrancy scenarios are accepted below.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Compose current runtime-key resolution with the existing HTTP request-policy
  owner once for ten Bearer media contexts. Keep specialized vendor auth local.
  Xiaomi now uses the existing API-key setup owner and retains its prefix validator.
- Observe managed Codex desktop replacement with bundle/executable metadata and
  one stable parent watch, not recursive content hashes and watcher rearming.
  Unified wrapper publication borrows that fingerprint; explicit install forces
  refresh. Signed-source verification and live execution authority are unchanged.
- Simplify lazy realtime connection/input ownership and reuse admitted queued tool
  results. Keep byte bounds, FIFO, normal reconnect, async adoption and shutdown.
- Charge Anthropic discovery budgets for actual reads, not imaginary cache-hit
  reads; drop inode-only same-size/same-mtime detection. Trust Foundry's internal
  process clock while still validating external token expiry. Use a plain fixed
  LM Studio preload cooldown instead of escalating failure history.

Net production: **520 lines removed** (+304 / -824 across 28 production files),
excluding tests, support, fixtures, generated files, declarations and documentation.
No dependency, config key, persisted schema, protocol or permission changes.
Phase E standalone session memory and its tests are untouched.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Config mutation while auth awaits uses the request's initially prepared route;
  the next request picks up the change. This removes rereads, not live credential
  checks. Prior duplicated contexts trace to #126053/#167205/#160080/#169111;
  no human mid-auth config-mutation incident was identified.
- Manual nested edits to a sealed desktop app that preserve bundle/executable
  identity may remain stale until explicit Computer Use install or restart.
  #127778's nested-byte fixtures were synthetic; actual-use report
  [#126080 comment5336833505](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/126080#issuecomment-5336833505)
  concerns normal signed desktop replacement, which remains supported.
- A failed desktop root watcher reports degraded health and refreshes metadata on
  acquisition; restart restores event watching. There is no extra rearm scheduler.
  No human watcher-rearm incident was identified in #127778/#168813.
- Native subagent monitor registration no longer handles simultaneous internal
  register/unregister/state-replacement calls. Actual callers await registration
  serially; #155800's forced replacement test is synthetic. Abort, host, connection,
  submission-store and live-thread authority remain checked at registration.
- Lazy xAI transcription uses a single in-flight promise rather than connection
  generations and duplicate-close tracking. Close clears that promise so normal
  reconnect can start; an older finalizer cannot clear its replacement.
  #138483/#138443 describe cold-import proof, not a human generation-fence incident.
- A synchronous realtime observer closing/replacing itself may receive remaining
  facts from its already-admitted frame; the next event checks its owner normally.
  The mid-callback scenarios in #149865/#133157 were synthetic. Real transcript
  finality, barge-in and tool-ownership repairs remain.
- Anthropic catalogs beyond the actual-read budget can reveal more rows in a warm
  refresh, shifting best-effort offset pagination. #109309 explicitly intended
  cache hits to consume no read budget; no human equal-frontier incident was found.
- External transcript replacement deliberately preserving both byte size and
  mtime can retain catalog metadata until another edit/restart. The inode-only
  regression fixture used artificial utimes; no human incident was cited.
- Monkey-patched/out-of-range Date.now is no longer repaired to a synthetic epoch.
  f13a6150361 only introduced an impossible-clock test. Real external expiry,
  account/scope separation, single-flight and cache bounds remain.
- LM Studio preload retries after a fixed60s rather than escalating5/10/20s to
  five minutes. A repaired setup can wait up to60s; sustained failures remain
  rate-bounded. #67401 describes preload rejection, but linked human issues
  #54938/#62971 do not establish a need for escalating failure history.
- The transcription startup audio tail uses a plain bounded FIFO, not cursor
  tombstones/compaction. #138483 provides no measured cursor-performance win;
  the same2MiB bound, drop-oldest policy and owned microphone copy remain.

Passed: targeted production and changed-test types; focused syntax lint and
core typed lint; runtime cycles (0) and Madge cycles (0); SDK export and surface
checks; changed-source line caps; formatting and diff checks. The shared auth
owner passed four boundary tests. Fresh independent review after the reconnect
repair found no actionable P0–P2 findings.

The required lint-suppression suite passed all three tests. The broader focused
plugin command reached its unchanged 900000ms no-output deadline while preparing
plugins, without a product assertion verdict. Extension typed lint and the remote
build attempt did not complete; the latter never allocated a lease. These are

The changed-check environment-name budget mismatch (452 versus 453) reproduced

Full public SDK API comparison is rendering frozen base/head inputs; the

Exact-head CI on0cd1427 identified three owned failures, repaired in test/support

The exact required PR-template headings are also corrected. The removed mock
baseline row is shrink-only. Targeted repair types and extension boundary checks
passed; fresh independent repair review is scoped-clean throughP2. Suppression
tests passed3/3. Local SDK auth tests reached their unchanged120s lazy-import
deadlines; that is an unresolved local proof gap, not the hosted failure signature.
That local invocation ended with four timeout failures before reaching the media
selection. A separate two-file failed-media selection is running without timeout
changes. The repaired mock-export ratchet and focused syntax lint both pass.

Fresh scope census covers61 provider roots:103 copy/guard matches,1484 admission
