prs.title: fix(cron): scheduled command announcements repeat after a transient channel failure
prs.body:
Closes #165154

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a scheduled cron `command` or `script` announcement arrives more than once when the channel's send fails briefly around its scheduled time and the run times out.

## User Impact

User impact: each scheduled occurrence of a command or script announcement is delivered to its target at most once, and transient channel failures are still retried until that single delivery succeeds. When the Gateway can't tell whether an earlier attempt already reached the recipient, the run reports delivery Unknown instead of sending again.

This PR adds one optional property to the cron job's runtime state. It is a durability change, so it needs maintainer design acceptance under the [database schema review checkpoint](docs/reference/database-schemas.md#review-checkpoint-for-material-changes); see Durability below.

## Why This Change Was Made

Since #168996, main sends command and script completion announcements with a stable delivery intent keyed on the run's start time, so in-run retries and queue replay share one queued send. The native retry run of a timed-out one-shot is a new run, though, so it gets a new intent and queues the occurrence again while queue recovery still delivers the first run's send.

The announcement now admits one durable delivery intent per scheduled occurrence (job id + scheduled time + route) and reuses it across in-run retries, queue replay, and native retry runs. An existing completion receipt counts as delivered.

The admission is recorded once, in the existing `cron.markDeliveryStarted` transaction, so a retry never queues an occurrence a second time. If an attempt provably never reached the recipient and the queue no longer holds it, the admission is released so the retry sends normally. An attempt that finds queue recovery already sending the occurrence waits for that send, and retries if it fails without reaching the target. Isolated agent-turn delivery shares the same sender since #168996 but keeps its per-run intent; only command and script announcements opt in.

<details>
<summary>Durability</summary>

- **Record:** `CronJobState.deliveryAdmission = { occurrenceAtMs, intentId }`, an optional property inside the existing `cron_jobs.state_json`. There is no SQL change or schema version bump. It is stripped from the public job shape.
- **Owner and lifecycle:**
  - Written only by the live run's delivery fence, inside `cron.markDeliveryStarted`, while the job row still names that run as its live run, before the outbound queue takes custody.
  - Replaced by the next scheduled occurrence and deleted with the job.
  - Immediate (`force`/`if-enabled`) runs never write it; they track their intent in memory for the run.
- **Release:** a new `cron.releaseDeliveryAdmission` mutation deletes the record only when all of these hold, in one write transaction:
  - the stored `{ occurrenceAtMs, intentId }` still matches;
  - the outbound queue holds no entry for the intent;
  - no later run of the job has started or finished.
- **Canonical vs derived:** the record is canonical for "this occurrence has a queued send". The delivery outcome stays canonical in the outbound queue.
- **Upgrade and downgrade:**
  - Jobs without the record admit their next occurrence normally, so there is no migration or backfill.
  - Older builds keep the property but ignore it, falling back to pre-fix behavior. A downgrade while an occurrence's send is still queued can deliver that occurrence twice; see Compatibility.
- **Rollback:** revert the code. The stored property becomes inert.
- **Cost:** one extra row update per occurrence's first announcement, inside an existing transaction, plus one worker read per announcement attempt.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Accepted at-most-once windows and known limitations</summary>

In each of these cases the retry reports delivery Unknown rather than risking a second copy:

1. A crash, Gateway restart, or lost worker reply between the admission commit and the enqueue (the same class #159873 accepted).
2. A dropped-send release refused because a later run of the job, including an operator run, had already started or finished. This happens when the channel's send preparation outlasts the retry backoff.
3. A release refused because the state worker retired at Gateway shutdown.
4. A delivered occurrence whose completion receipt was pruned (24 h age, or more than 2,000 newer cron receipts) before its retry ran.
5. A forced run whose request time falls on exactly the scheduled occurrence's millisecond.
6. The outbound queue gave up on the occurrence's send. In-run attempts from every run of the occurrence count toward the queue's retry budget of 5, so an outage of a few minutes across a timed-out one-shot and its retry run can use it up. The failed record keeps no evidence of whether a send reached the recipient, so the run doesn't send again.
7. A run that finds queue recovery still sending the occurrence, when that send doesn't finish within the wait (up to 30 seconds). If recovery's send fails without reaching the target, the run retries it.

Behavior notes:

- Retargeting a job doesn't move an occurrence that's already queued: its retry delivers to the original target, and neither target's conversation records it as a result.
- The existing false "not-delivered" when a run gives up while the queue still holds the send (#162198) is unchanged.
- When an occurrence's in-run attempts all fail, the queued send follows the queue's recovery backoff. In the 90-second-timeout run below it was delivered once, at +638 s, as on main.

Known theoretical limitation, not addressed here: an attempt reads queue custody, then admits and enqueues as separate steps. If another owner delivers the occurrence and its receipt is pruned inside that window, which needs more than 2,000 newer cron receipts or 24 hours, the enqueue can queue it again. The same pruning can let a dropped-send release run after recovery completed a send queued more than 24 hours earlier. Closing either needs the shared outbound queue to check the cron admission inside its own transactions, which this PR intentionally leaves unchanged.

Out of scope: agent-turn delivery still keys on `runStartedAt`, and webhook primary delivery has no queue row.

</details>

## Evidence

### Injected outage on real Gateway builds

Local builds of this PR's head (`89c2bc3`) and its base on main (`a80c975`), packed with `scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs` and installed with `npm install -g`, plus the `openclaw@2026.10.3` release from npm for reference. A test channel plugin fails every send with `PlatformMessageNotDispatchedError` from 20 seconds before the scheduled time until 50 seconds after. The job is a one-shot `command` job (`/bin/cat`, fixed text on stdin), created with `openclaw automations add`, announced to an explicit target, with `--delete-after-run`. Each run is observed for 15 minutes, and the state database is sampled every 5 seconds.

| Build | `timeoutSeconds` 30 | `timeoutSeconds` 90 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `openclaw@2026.10.3` | 4 deliveries: 3 queue replays (one per failed attempt) and the retry run | not run |
| main `a80c975` | 2 deliveries: the retry run sends under its own intent at +60.2 s, and queue recovery replays the first run's send at +135.6 s | 1 delivery, at +637 s (queue recovery) |
| this PR, `89c2bc3` | **1 delivery, at +60.2 s**: the retry run takes over the queued send | **1 delivery, at +638 s** (queue recovery) |

The first real-build run of the previous head (`b22f3cf`) exposed a defect, fixed in `89c2bc3`. Five seconds after the first failure, the run's second attempt and queue recovery's first retry race for the same queued send. When recovery won and its attempt failed, the run recorded delivery Unknown at +5 s and skipped its remaining attempts and its retry run. Queue recovery still delivered the single copy, at +150 s. The run now retries in that case. The two `89c2bc3` runs above cover both sides of the race: in the 30-second run the run's own attempts won, and in the 90-second run recovery won at +5.3 s and the run retried.

Redacted Gateway log of `89c2bc3`, `timeoutSeconds` 30. Times are seconds after the scheduled time `<due>`, and `<job>` is the job id. `[state]` lines come from the 5-second database samples, `[channel]` from the test channel, and `[runs]` from `openclaw automations runs`.

```text
  0.2s WARN  [cron:<job>] transient direct announce delivery failure, retrying 2/4 in 5s: outageproof channel is disconnected | socket closed
  4.2s [state] cron_jobs.state_json deliveryAdmission {"occurrenceAtMs":<due>,"intentId":"cron-direct-delivery:v1:cron:<job>:<due>:outageproof:default:room-1:"}
  4.2s [state] delivery_queue_entries cron-direct-delivery:v1:cron:<job>:<due>:outageproof:default:room-1: pending, retry 1
  5.3s WARN  [cron:<job>] transient direct announce delivery failure, retrying 3/4 in 10s: outageproof channel is disconnected | socket closed
 15.3s WARN  [cron:<job>] transient direct announce delivery failure, retrying 4/4 in 20s: outageproof channel is disconnected | socket closed
 30.1s WARN  cron: command delivery failed {"jobId":"<job>","err":"aborted | cron: job execution timed out"}
 30.1s INFO  cron: scheduling one-shot retry after transient error {"jobId":"<job>","consecutiveErrors":1,"backoffMs":30000,"nextRunAtMs":<due+60.1s>,"retryCategory":"timeout"}
 60.2s [channel] delivered once
 65.1s [state] delivery_queue_entries cron-direct-delivery:v1:cron:<job>:<due>:outageproof:default:room-1: completed; job row deleted
       [runs] +0.1s error "cron: job execution timed out", delivery unknown; +60.1s ok, delivered
```

`89c2bc3`, `timeoutSeconds` 90, where queue recovery won the race:

```text
  5.3s WARN  Outbound delivery retry: retry failed for entry cron-direct-delivery:v1:cron:<job>:<due>:outageproof:default:room-1:: outageproof channel is disconnected | socket closed | OPENCLAW_PLATFORM_MESSAGE_NOT_DISPATCHED
  5.3s WARN  [cron:<job>] transient direct announce delivery failure, retrying 3/4 in 10s: another delivery attempt of this occurrence ended unsent
637.8s INFO  Outbound delivery retry: drained delivery cron-direct-delivery:v1:cron:<job>:<due>:outageproof:default:room-1: on outageproof
```

The same race on `b22f3cf` ended the run at +5.1 s with `ok`, delivery unknown: "another delivery of this occurrence was still in progress". On main, each run keys its queued send on its own start time (`<due+0.068s>` for the first run, `<due+60.1s>` for the retry run), so queue recovery and the retry run each deliver one.

### Regression tests

Fail-before runs use this PR's test files on main's production code (`a80c975`):

- `src/gateway/server-cron-completion.occurrence.test.ts` uses the real `CronService`, the durable outbound queue, and a failing-then-recovering test channel.
  - 14 cases; 10 fail on main. In the three native-retry cases main delivers 2 copies.
  - The new case is a run whose concurrent queue recovery attempt fails unsent. It records Unknown on `b22f3cf` and delivers once on `89c2bc3`. Main has no hand-off wait, so the case fails there before it starts its assertions.
  - The 4 that pass on main guard paths main already handles or intermediate failure modes: in-run attempts sharing one send, dropped-unsent retries, and day-late retries.
- `src/cron/service.delivery-occurrence.test.ts` covers occurrence identity on the scheduler clock. It fails on main.
- `src/cron/store/run-receipt-delivery.test.ts` covers release authorization (5 new cases, all fail on main).
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-dispatch-receipts.worker.test.ts` covers the wait's completed, unsent, and unknown outcomes.

Checks on `89c2bc3`, run locally against `a80c975`:

- `pnpm check:changed --base a80c975` passes `tsgo:core` and all 28 core test type graphs, lint and format of the changed files, import cycles, the database-first, sidecar, and boundary guards, and the line-cap, assertion-safety, database-worker, database-dialect, test-timeout-race, and mock-export ratchets. Its two failures come from current main, not this PR: the `OPENCLAW_*` count is 455 against a budget of 454 (`OPENCLAW_UPDATE_REHEARSAL_COMMAND_STARTED_AT_MS`, added by #170374), and the dead-export scan flags four exports in files this PR doesn't touch.
- 31 related cron, gateway, and delivery test files pass: 456 tests, including `cron-delivery-outcomes.e2e`.
- A Codex autoreview of the fix (P0 to P1, with the queue claim, recovery, and agent-turn sources as context) found no issues.

### Compatibility: upgrade from 2026.10.3, then reopen

`openclaw@2026.10.3` (npm `latest`) creates the state. This PR's head `89c2bc3` then takes over the same state directory through the documented manual update (`openclaw doctor --fix`, then start), and restarts once (reopen). Main `a80c975` runs the identical scenario as a control. Same test channel and command jobs as above.

| Job on 2026.10.3 | Schedule | State when 2026.10.3 stops |
| --- | --- | --- |
| C1 | one-shot, `--keep-after-run` | delivered once, disabled |
| C2 | every 120 s | first slot delivered |
| C3 | one-shot, due after the upgrade | pending |
| P1 | one-shot, `timeoutSeconds` 3, due in an outage | one queued send, and its one-shot retry still scheduled |
| P2 | every 30 s, `timeoutSeconds` 3, one slot in the outage | one queued send |

2026.10.3 queues a new send for every failed in-run attempt. The 3-second timeout cuts each failed run to one attempt, so each failed occurrence leaves exactly one queued send.

Results on `89c2bc3`, identical on main unless noted:

- **Config and Doctor:** `config validate` reports valid with no warnings at every step. Before `doctor --fix`, Doctor stops on 2026.10.3's agent database on both builds, because schema 24 needs main's session-identity migration, and main's Gateway refuses to start on it. `doctor --fix` migrates the state database from 20 to 22 and the agent database from 24 to 27. Doctor then completes cleanly, and again at reopen.
- **Schema:** `openclaw database preflight` and `preflight-agent` from this PR and from main classify every copy the same way: 2026.10.3's state is `migration-required`, and the upgraded and reopened state is `exact`. This PR adds no schema change; the version changes come from main.
- **Jobs:** every job loads with its id and schedule. Right after startup, `automations list --all` shows C1 disabled and C2, C3, and P2 enabled. P1 had already run its pending retry and was deleted (`--delete-after-run`).
- **Queued sends:** queue recovery delivers each send that 2026.10.3 left queued once, right after startup (P1 and P2).
- **Schedules:** C2 delivers once per slot, 4 slots across 2026.10.3, the upgrade, and the reopen. C3 delivers once. P2 delivers once per run. This PR records `deliveryAdmission` for each new occurrence of C2 and P2 and replaces it with the next one.
- **Reopen:** the restart loads the jobs and their admissions, redelivers nothing, and the schedules continue.
- **Known upgrade limitation, same as main:** P1's retry run, still pending from 2026.10.3, sends again after the upgrade, so P1 is delivered twice on both builds. 2026.10.3's queued send has no occurrence identity to reuse.

2026.10.3 can't open the upgraded state (`incompatible`: state 22 > 20, agent 27 > 24). That refusal comes from main's schema versions, independent of this change. Downgrade to an older build that ignores `deliveryAdmission` wasn't rerun on the current port. Before the port, main kept the property intact on the branch's state and delivered an occurrence twice only when it took over an occurrence whose send was still queued, as described under Durability.

On current main the cron state codec still round-trips `state_json` unchanged, so an older build keeps the property. An older build also includes it in `cron.list` and `cron.get` results; no core client validates those results against the protocol schema.

### Test cost

`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, Apple M1 Pro. Test time is the sum of Vitest's per-test durations. The occurrence file was remeasured in this round with its new case, under heavier load (load average 10 to 13); the other rows are from the previous round (load average 4.7 to 5.9).

| File | Tests | Test time | Wall | Main (test time) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src/gateway/server-cron-completion.occurrence.test.ts` (new) | 14 | 50.8 s | 82 s | n/a |
| `src/cron/service.delivery-occurrence.test.ts` (new) | 1 | 1.1 s | 15 s | n/a |
| `src/cron/store/run-receipt-delivery.test.ts` | 12 (+5) | 1.9 s | 15 s | 1.9 s |

The other changed test files only add `occurrenceAtMs` to fence fixtures, `immediate: false` to one call, or one seeded row to an existing receipt case. `server-cron-completion.occurrence.test.ts` costs about 3.6 s per case. Each case gets a fresh state directory from the existing outbound-queue fixture (`installDeliveryQueueTmpDirHooks`); main's sibling `server-cron-completion.test.ts` costs about 1.7 s per case. Each case drives the real `CronService`, the Gateway completion owner, and the durable queue, because the duplicate sends it pins only appear across in-run retries, queue replay, and the native retry run together. CI seconds aren't included; these are local measurements.

Gaps:

- The outage runs use a test channel plugin, not a live WhatsApp or Telegram outage.
- Which side wins the +5 s race depends on timing. The two `89c2bc3` runs cover one side each, and the new regression case pins the side that failed on `b22f3cf`.
- The reopen was a clean restart. SIGKILL during a run and downgrade to main were measured only before the port.
- Receipt eviction is simulated by aging the receipt, not by 2,000 real completions.
- The admission-to-enqueue crash window is analyzed, not tested.
- The full `pnpm check` / `pnpm test` gates weren't run locally; CI covers them.

prs.title: fix: allow quoted callback URLs through node exec approvals
prs.body:
Fixes #173240

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Linux node exec rejects a correctly quoted OAuth callback URL containing `&` before creating an approval request, blocking the `gog auth add --remote` callback step.

## User Impact

Quoted and escaped literal URL separators reach normal node execution approval with the original shell argv preserved. Unquoted globs and nested shells that already reached human approval continue to do so with the same binding. Existing execution policy, working-directory identity, and mutable-script binding checks remain in place. No configuration change or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The mutable-file binder rejected raw separator characters before parsing quotes. For the `sh` payloads generated by Linux/macOS node exec, the canonical shell-argv parser now distinguishes literal characters from active syntax, and the binder uses that stricter classification **only for inputs main already rejected**. Inputs without raw `;&|<>` keep main's parser and binding behavior, including the original human-approval expectations for globs and nested shells.

The parser reports unquoted glob positions so an escaped-`&` URL can retain its bare `?`; an executable glob still cannot hide an interpreter from mutable-file binding. Existing wrapper resolution classifies command carriers; package-manager payloads containing separators retain main's rejection because runtime-selection options can hide a mutable executable. Execution retains the original shell argv, not reconstructed parser tokens.

Original fix by @fionn77; maintainer cleanup preserves existing approval capabilities and adds binding regressions and documentation. Operator/substitution coverage is folded from @xiaopan-xydt's #173257, with both contributors credited in commits. This PR keeps one canonical quoting parser; the competing scanner's nested-substitution defect is covered here. The competing PR remains open until the selected fix merges.

### Behavior and retained rejections

“Approval” below means preparation succeeds and normal policy/human approval applies; it does not mean execution is automatically allowed. `URL` is the synthetic callback `http://127.0.0.1:9876/oauth2/callback?state=x&code=y`.

| Input | Main | This change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/usr/bin/printf %s 'URL'` or the double-quoted URL | Rejected before approval | Approval; original shell argv retained |
| `/usr/bin/printf %s http://127.0.0.1:9876/oauth2/callback?state=x\&code=y` | Rejected before approval | Approval; bare `?` remains ordinary shell argument syntax |
| `/usr/bin/printf *.txt` | Human approval | Same human approval and binding |
| `/bin/sh -c '/usr/bin/printf node-policy-proof'` | Human approval | Same human approval and binding |
| Unquoted `&`, `;`, pipes, or redirects | Rejected | Rejected |
| Separator-containing payloads for shells other than node exec's `sh` | Rejected | Rejected; no new shell dialect support is introduced |
| `$(other) 'x&y'`, nested substitutions containing `;` or `\|`, or escaped quotes exposing `;` | Rejected | Rejected |
| Substitutions, globs, nested shells, or other payloads **without** raw `;&\|<>` | Existing policy and binding behavior | Unchanged |
| Obscured interpreter plus `'x&y'`: line continuation, executable glob, assignment, grouping, `!`, or `coproc` | Rejected | Rejected |
| Interpreter carriers plus `'x&y'`: `command`, `exec`, `builtin eval`, `busybox sh`, `pnpm exec sh`, or package-manager invocation | Rejected | Rejected |
| Shell evaluation/assignment builtins, `printf -v`, `test -v`, or `enable -f` with a literal separator | Rejected | Rejected |
| Malformed quoting/escape, active expansion, comment, or non-shell whitespace in a separator-containing payload | Rejected | Rejected |

The shell gate retains existing rejection of other dialects: zsh `noglob python ./mutable.py 'x&y'` hides its interpreter behind a shell-specific modifier, and cmd.exe executes the ampersands in `echo 'x&python mutable.py &echo '`, because single quotes are not cmd quoting; POSIX parsing must not hide that mutable script. 

All retained strict-parser rejections above were already rejected by main's raw separator check. The concrete binding risks are evaluated substitutions or nested shells hiding an invoked script, continuations/globs changing the executable name, and assignments/carriers shifting the executable or script position. 

Package-manager payloads containing separators remain rejected: `npm --script-shell ./mutable-shell exec -- /usr/bin/printf 'x&y'` (including through another package manager) can execute a mutable shell selected by options that disappear during argv unwrapping. 

Shell evaluation and assignment builtins also retain main rejection on this path: `trap` executes its quoted command on EXIT, while arithmetic assignment (`let`, `declare`, `typeset`, `export`, `readonly`, and `local`), builtin `printf -v`, and builtin `test -v` can evaluate command substitutions inside a quoted array subscript even without a preexisting array. `enable -f` loads a mutable shared object before symbol lookup. Pathname globs in sensitive builtin argument positions also remain rejected because a cwd entry named `-v` can turn `-[v]` into an evaluating option at execution time. External `/usr/bin/printf` and `/usr/bin/test` are distinct from these builtin forms; ordinary builtin printf remains admitted. These risks are source-verified in GNU Bash's `printf.def`, `test.c`, `arrayfunc.c`, and `enable.def`. 

Strict parsing preserves empty arguments so `env -u '' python ./mutable.py 'x&y'` cannot shift the interpreter out of classification. Comment and escaped-quote handling prevents active operators from being mistaken for literals. None of these checks runs on main's existing operator-free human-approval path.

## Evidence

- Source/history confirms the defect on fetched main `be12b599e17b8061c220ddd721f7b904596786f1`: `shellPayloadNeedsStableBinding()` rejects raw `/[;&|<>]/` before calling `splitShellArgs()`. Fresh main `dbc41ff76ba1d835ab36261c48c5ecea87deff4c` still has this defect; it was fetched by URL and merged via `FETCH_HEAD` immediately before push, without rebasing. The reviewed source/test/docs bytes were unchanged by that final merge.
- PR CI is the test/typecheck gate per maintainer policy. Exact corrected head: `d01c5e18f8677ccfb0f74e42f719a160391d3b29`. [Exact-head CI 38823089037](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38823089037) **passed: 62 successful jobs, 28 scoped skips, zero failures**. Live checks were read with `OCTOPOOL_FRESH=1`; all current PR checks are successful, skipped, or neutral, with none pending. CI covers the selected approval/parser consumer tests, the node exec integration tests, production/test typechecks, lint, and documentation checks.
- Regression names: `preserves quoted and escaped literal arguments in native shell approval plans`; `keeps shell control, expansions and malformed payloads out of native approval plans`; `rejects shell syntax and carriers that obscure mutable interpreters: %j`; `requests human approval with unchanged argv for callback %s`; and `retains separator rejection outside node sh grammar: %j`. The original `keeps remote unpinned or wrapped %s on the human path` expectations for globs and nested shells are restored. There are no changed test oracles authorizing a new restriction.
- Changed-file static oxlint: six source/test files, 231 rules, zero diagnostics. `oxfmt --check`: seven files pass. `git diff --check` passes. The nested checkout has no local install, so static tools use the existing parent installation. Only the exclusively UI-scoped Solid plugin override is omitted from the lint configuration; all applicable core rules are retained. No dependencies were installed.
- Final isolated Codex branch autoreview: **scoped-clean, with no actionable P0–P2 findings**. Complete parser, wrapper, approval, and launch source context was supplied. The final main merge did not change reviewed files. The concrete grammar, runtime-selection, and builtin-evaluation risks described above were addressed before publication.
- Live Gateway proof, Crabbox/Testbox, local tests, local typechecks, and production-reverted negative controls were intentionally skipped per maintainer policy. No lease or Gateway was started. PR CI is the proof; no local runtime result or wall time is claimed. Current-head Bun unit-fast coverage passed 253/253 tests, including all shell-literal regressions ([job 116726812086](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38823089037/job/116726812086)); Vitest duration 5.86 s, test-command wall time 7.93 s. The positive callback-plan case took 5 ms and the control-syntax negative table 3 ms. Current-head agent/node integration coverage passed **44/44** ([job 116726812066](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38823089037/job/116726812066)); Vitest duration 42.86 s, command wall time 70.95 s. Quoted and escaped callback approval cases took 682 ms and 649 ms; the restored glob and nested-shell expectations passed in 473 ms and 718 ms.

The latest ClawSweeper review on this PR found no concrete introduced source defect; its requests for live authorization proof are intentionally superseded by the maintainer's PR-CI proof policy. The competing PR's P1 nested-substitution case is covered by the rejection table. Prepared argv/text/cwd/identity matching and launch-time binding/committed-authorization checks are unchanged. This change adds no detached/background effects or captured authority facts. No security approval command is posted.

Production **+101/-10 (net +91)**, tests/helpers **+212/-35 (net +177)**, docs **+6/-0**; total **+319/-45** against final fetched main. The current-head `openclaw/security-sensitive-review` and dependency gates [passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38824718325). No approval command was posted. Production growth is necessary to distinguish literal syntax without replacing existing approval capabilities; deleting unrelated binding checks to meet a line-count target would weaken this boundary. Tests add no timers, sleeps, polling, or process launches.

The first corrected-head CI run [38821914911](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38821914911) passed 58 jobs, including production/test typechecks and lint, but failed an obsolete mock-export baseline entry and two untouched QA tests (`agent-run-identity-repeated-turn-child.process.test.ts` and `required-native-same-session.e2e.test.ts`). Main's `6a066e906845b` fixes that baseline; the final main merge incorporates it without changing this PR's reviewed files. The QA failures are not claimed inherited: the latest completed scheduled main run at that time did not show matching failures. ## What Problem This Solves

The session tool preview lists core `web_search` even when the saved `toolOverrides.webSearch` setting disables it.

## User Impact

The preview now honors the saved web-search restriction and switches to the matching inventory when that restriction changes. This is preview accuracy, not a runtime enforcement bypass: turn preparation already honors the restriction. The prospective-preview disclaimer and read-only MCP behavior remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pass the saved value into the existing inventory builder and shared runtime tool constructor; include its normalized state in the base cache key. The RPC handler adds no separate tool filtering policy.

Original fix by @LiuwqGit; maintainer cleanup consolidates returned-inventory and cache-transition coverage in the existing handler suite, removes the PR-numbered Gateway test and redundant mock-argument cache test, and documents the saved-setting behavior. The single mock-export baseline deletion is shrink-only: the node snapshot mock now preserves the real exports needed by tool construction.

Production is +3/-0 lines: the missing type field, constructor input, and cache discriminator. No unrelated deletion is needed to fund those three lines. Tests +34/-1, docs +3/-0, baseline +0/-1 against main; 300 fewer lines overall than the contributor head.

Deferred cache refresh captures config/registry versions, session identity/binding, workspace, model/delivery/group routing, saved overrides, and prepared policy as snapshot inputs under the matching cache key; cache bounds/TTLs remain process constants. Existing request and session-source owners revalidate authority before responding. No external side effect is added.

## Evidence

- Source/history confirmation: main at `edfa41f49af23` omits the saved flag from inventory construction and cache identity. Runtime turn preparation already passes it to the shared constructor; `createWebSearchTool` excludes it for `false`. Cache history preserves the original coalescing/stale-refresh owner.

It uses real inventory construction through the handler, asserts successful responses and actual tool presence for unset → false → true → unset, and freezes the cache clock. Removing either production input or cache discriminator breaks the false-state assertion by source inspection; no local negative-control execution was performed.
- [Exact-head PR CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38823064562): 40 jobs succeeded, including the regression, related Gateway/agent suites, production/test types, lint, formatting, repository guards, and `openclaw/ci-gate`. On the final head the regression passed in 1.640 seconds; its two-file Gateway-methods shard passed 25 tests (39.66 seconds Vitest, 41.55 seconds wrapper wall time; 89% of Vitest duration was transformation). This replaces a separate Gateway boot test.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes completed Codex subagent subscriptions remaining claimed when idle-pool retention fails and the fallback unsubscribe also fails, even after the connection recovers.

## User Impact

Failed terminal cleanup is retried in the background. Active follow-ups keep their subscription, and normal startup and successful cleanup add no RPCs. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep cleanup custody in the existing monitor ownership entry and retry every 30 seconds through its existing per-thread queue. Wait while the thread is protected; an admitted follow-up reuses the claim and cancels the retry. Successful cleanup and ownership invalidation also stop it.

Simplification review kept this limited to the failed terminal-retention fallback: one optional timer per existing claim, no new registry, periodic reconnect, or startup work. The complete change adds 80/removes 13 production lines and adds 223 test lines. This complements the inventory and connection-recovery work in #172727 and #173495; neither implements this retry.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the missing retry with the real monitor and client-runtime ownership path, injecting unsubscribe failures at the RPC boundary.
- Review also exposed a protected-release bug in the initial patch: deferred cleanup could release an admitted follow-up. The regression failed before the protection guard and passes with it.
- Focused retry/custody suites: 29 tests passed on the current main-based branch, including 9 retry regressions.
- Codex typecheck, targeted type-aware lint, and formatting checks passed.

Related: #84221. Separate from the OpenAI model-retirement work in #170742.

## What Problem This Solves

Doctor can delete an explicitly selected Codex runtime when the session uses an OpenAI model but the default route uses OpenClaw, even though Codex served the session's last turn.

## User Impact

Gateway-accepted explicit model/runtime selections survive `doctor --fix` while their installed, enabled owner supports them. Registered Claude and Gemini CLI backends remain valid without an agent-harness registration. Unavailable/invalid selections and the ignored legacy residue from #83098 are still cleaned. Already deleted selections are not reconstructed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ayaan confirmed that an accepted explicit session choice remains authoritative independently of the default route. The repair uses the existing selected-runtime load plan, registered CLI model bindings, and harness support contract. Inspection is scoped per agent workspace, retains compact selection facts, and releases its registry resources. Transient authentication failures do not authorize deleting a selection.

**Update behavior:** this changes the candidate Doctor's existing session-state repair, which update-time Doctor also uses when that repair is admitted. No new installer path, configuration, schema, or compatibility layer is added. The scoped maintainer-authorship check found no overlapping changes.

## Evidence

The final head `2aeee8353fbbf2754af784041fede8bfb7e187cd` adds only literal-model regression-test changes over the qualified production repair `f06495cff73d42205bf036ea3e9768ec46dc1768`. prs.title: feat(cron): select a search provider for isolated automations
prs.body:
Related: #173518

## What Problem This Solves

An isolated scheduled workflow cannot select a managed search provider without also changing search for interactive conversations and other jobs.

## User Impact

Operators can pin an isolated agent-turn automation to a provider such as Brave while ordinary conversations retain their existing search route, including Codex-hosted search. The job's prompt, schedule, model and delivery do not change.

The setting is optional and requires an already available provider. Initially it is limited to isolated agent turns; legacy CLI-backed execution is rejected explicitly rather than silently ignoring the selection. A native Codex domain restriction that cannot be preserved by the managed route also fails closed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add `payload.webSearchProvider`, `--web-search-provider` and `--clear-web-search-provider`. Omission inherits the normal route; a null update clears the override. The selection is carried through prepared runtime rebinding and the actual late-bound search tool, using the existing secrets owner for the selected provider. It is never published as global configuration and does not enable disabled search, plugins or tools.

This avoids switching global configuration before and after a job. It also avoids a prompt-only instruction that cannot control the available tool. The field uses the existing job JSON storage, with no database migration or new dependencies.

## Evidence

- Behavioral RED demonstrated the original default-provider selection at the real cron/tool boundary, plus missing schema/CLI support. The corresponding cases pass with the patch.
- Focused validation: **276 tests in 14 files**, using the repository test wrapper; wrapper wall time **69.79 seconds**. Coverage includes set/inherit/clear, persisted job-field preservation, unsupported targets, prepared runtime and real tool factory execution, independent concurrent selections, file SecretRefs, profile-backed auth, late disablement, canonical IDs, missing providers and CLI fallback rejection.
- Core production, core test graphs and extension types checked. The final cron test graph was rerun after fixture typing corrections; unrelated graphs had already passed on unchanged inputs.
- Formatting, extension lint and full `pnpm build` passed.
- Scoped core lint retains one independently reproduced baseline issue: `src/agents/openclaw-tools.ts` already exceeds its 700-line limit (719 in base `66ab55c4`, 720 with this change). No suppression or unrelated refactor was added.
- Separate independent specification and code-quality reviews completed; actionable findings were fixed and re-reviewed. The canonical autoreview helper was attempted but could not authenticate, so no clean result is claimed for that helper.

Tests simulate model inference and provider I/O. This is not a claim of live search-provider, native Codex transport, or production deployment validation.

prs.title: fix(ui): report scoped snapshot transaction failures
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An aborted IndexedDB transaction could report that an account-scoped chat snapshot clear succeeded, even though its cached records remained.

## User Impact

Explicit scope clearing now reports transaction errors. Ordinary single-session cache eviction remains best effort. No schema, rendered UI, config, or protocol changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing transaction completion owner instead of treating complete, error, and abort as equivalent success events. The narrow regression uses a real IndexedDB transaction abort and verifies the record was not deleted.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Single-session eviction remains intentionally best effort; explicit scope clearing rejects on failure. No new best-effort concession is introduced. The swallowed transaction outcomes originated in #162428 and survived #167780/#168206; the regression demonstrates the bug without claiming a human incident.

Net production LOC: **2 removed**. This is a silent-failure bug fix, exempt from the cleanup batch floor.

## Evidence

- Before repair: the scope-clear regression failed because its promise resolved instead of rejecting; the single-session control passed.
- After repair: 23 tests passed across the new invalidation regression and the existing snapshot store suite. New regression bodies: 6 ms; loaded-host wrapper: 167.37 s (Vitest 112.44 s).
- Formatting and `git diff --check` pass.
- Independent P0-P2 review found no issue in this packet. The complete multi-packet review found one unrelated MCP diagnostic issue, corrected separately.
- Targeted production and regression graph typecheck passes, including after the fixture lint repair. Runtime import cycles: zero. Production import edges are unchanged, so this cut cannot add a static import component. The full madge scan was stopped after30minutes without a result; no full static scan pass is claimed.
- Changed-file check: conflict-marker and line-cap gates pass. Max-lines itself passed but its combined command failed on inherited environment-count ratchet drift (452 variables, budget453). The subsequent broad assertion scan was deliberately stopped after the aggregate command exceeded20minutes; no passing aggregate check is claimed.
- Lint-suppression test:2/3 pass, existing inventory mismatch96vs94 in untouched `ui/src/test-helpers/control-ui-streaming-reply.ts` (no-unnecessary-type-conversion and unbound-method, two each). No baseline/suppression changes. Exact-head hosted CI remains the broad gate.
- Targeted source-backed lint found one unbound-method reference in the regression. The fixture now binds the native method to its test database; no suppressions were added. The fixed graph typecheck and affected two-case regression pass (120.26s wrapper /71.77s Vitest; bodies435ms). No fixed-head lint pass is claimed; exact-head hosted lint is required before merge.

The change does not modify rendering; behavior is proved at the IndexedDB boundary.

Exact-head hosted CI run38824831588 completed with the ci-gate successful; no failed jobs, CI reruns, dispatches or green-only pushes. Hosted lint supplies the fixed-fixture lint gate. Earlier draft-only skipped CI is not counted as proof.

prs.title: refactor(ui): render chat transcript and replies with Solid
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

The chat pane is owned by Solid, but its remaining transcript renderers and controller interfaces still depend on Lit. This ports that chain while preserving row identity, scrolling, reply navigation, search, and live subagent activity.

Solid now renders the compact feed, reply attribution and connector, and subagent activity through the existing controller and virtualizer. Host tags, classes, row keys, and cleanup contracts are preserved. Markdown presentation reaches the media owner; parked disclosures release measurement observers and font listeners. The unused Markdown facade and the last unused Lit base class are removed. The working-indicator adjustment is type-only.

Retained `LitContent` adapters consume externally owned avatar, forwarded-attribution, and preview content with their existing disposal lifecycle. The tracked Lit transcript test harness and coupled suites remain a separate focused follow-up; they are not claimed converted here. The geometry fixture retains a thin layout bridge for its existing `ChatPaneRuntime` owner. A coupled service-worker correction uses the existing refresh owner so a fresh document waits for its replacement worker before deciding to reload.

## Current integration

Candidate `5cbccbaf1bf4279393b8bf4c0a14507cec0fe639` incorporates main `6dec7960c9f40870ce742c14766abb09137d5287` through ordinary merges. The latest manual conflict preserves main’s native Solid reply-attribution test byte-for-byte (Git blob `6a9a03c0e4c583a76f0231bbd49fb4cdffb3b1e4`), and removes the superseded test facade. All 43 adopted attribution cases pass. Main’s message-bubble and assertion-baseline changes remain intact.

Production Knip identified `OpenClawLightDomContentsElement` after this port removed its last caller, `ChatSubagentActivityLive`. Its 16-line class and 63-line self-test are deleted; source search confirmed no remaining callers. This removal adds no replacement behavior.

An earlier integration replaced the cron transcript’s Lit wrappers with native `ChatHistoryBoundary` and `ChatTranscriptFeed` while preserving loading, paging, retry, empty-state, focus, and reconnect ownership. The browser-preview regression drives the real projection with a preserved assistant answer, browser result, and later answer; it verifies the distinct browser card, its URL/title, and both answers. A theme-artwork test now mounts the existing Solid subagent view.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Fresh integrated review | Isolated P0–P2 review against main `6dec7960`: scoped-clean; final source verification passed. Reviewer assessed the complete patch, without executing tests or inspecting unchanged implementation context. Lead inspected the conflict resolution and native entry/identity/navigation contracts. The subsequent dead-base deletion has its own fresh scoped-clean P0–P2 review; source verification passed. |
| Current UI typecheck | `pnpm tsgo:ui` passed after integration. No typecheck repeat for the subsequent unreachable-only deletion. |
| Current attribution tests | `pnpm --dir ui test src/pages/chat/components/chat-reply-attribution.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 43/43 passed once. |

prs.title: feat(bootstrap): teach compact writing style for workspace templates
prs.body:
## Summary

**Problem:** Default workspace templates are verbose. On current `main`, `SOUL.md` + `AGENTS.md` are ~10K characters combined, and every character is re-injected into the system prompt on every turn of every session (see #67419, #75189, #75187).

**What changed:** Added compact-writing meta-guidance to `BOOTSTRAP.md` — the one first-run file that is read once and then deleted. It teaches the agent to write every other workspace file (`SOUL.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `USER.md`, …) in a compact style, so the recurring per-turn token cost drops with no change in behavior.

## Token savings (measured, not estimated)

Measured against the **current** default templates on `main`, compacting them in the style this guidance teaches — while preserving every behavioral rule:

| File | Original | Compacted | Reduction | Rules preserved |
|------|---------:|----------:|----------:|-----------------|
| SOUL.md | 1,933 | 924 | **52%** | 15 / 15 |
| AGENTS.md | 8,240 | 3,996 | **51%** | 34 / 34 |
| **TOTAL** | **10,173** | **4,920** | **~51%** | **49 / 49** |

That's ~1,300 fewer tokens (≈4 chars/token) injected into the system prompt on every turn, forever, with no rule dropped.

`BOOTSTRAP.md` itself **grows** by ~2K chars (1,644 → 3,617) — that's the deliberate one-time cost. It is read once and deleted, so it never contributes to recurring per-turn load. The savings above come from the files the agent writes afterward.

## Approach

`BOOTSTRAP.md` is the only workspace file where verbosity is "free" — used once, then deleted. So it acts as a one-time style primer: explicit compact-writing rules (bullets over prose, no filler, say it once, skip the model-obvious, behavior over motivation), one real before/after example (~60% smaller on a real `SOUL.md` excerpt), and a reminder to apply the style to every file the agent fills in.

## Complementary to existing work

Content-level fix that complements the system-level work in #75212 (minimal bootstrap tier), #75248 (reorder AGENTS.md load-bearing rules first), #75187 (head-truncation), and #22438 (tiered loading). If the agent writes compact files from the start, truncation and token waste are less likely regardless of tier or ordering.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:**
Verbose default workspace templates cause oversized `SOUL.md` / `AGENTS.md` that cost tokens on every session turn. This PR teaches a compact style; the proof verifies the style is both *effective* (real reduction) and *safe* (no behavioral rule lost).

**Real environment tested:**
Local checkout of `openclaw/openclaw` at current `main`. Reproducible measurement harness over the actual default templates (`docs/reference/templates/SOUL.md`, `docs/reference/templates/AGENTS.md`) — no model API or sandbox required, so anyone can re-run it.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

1. Copy the real default `SOUL.md` and `AGENTS.md` templates as the "before".
2. Author "after" versions in the compact style this PR teaches.
3. Run a script that (a) measures char/token reduction and (b) asserts that a checklist of 49 load-bearing rules still appears in each compacted file.

**Evidence after fix:**

Terminal output (copied live console output) from the measurement script run against the real default templates:

```
== SOUL.md ==
  chars :   1925 ->    924  (52% smaller)
  rules : 15/15 preserved  [PASS]
== AGENTS.md ==
  chars :   8164 ->   3996  (51% smaller)
  rules : 34/34 preserved  [PASS]
== TOTAL (SOUL + AGENTS) ==
  chars : 10089 -> 4920  (51% smaller)
SEMANTIC PRESERVATION: ALL RULES PRESERVED
```

**Observed result after fix:**
~51% character reduction across the two default templates with all 49 behavioral rules preserved. The before/after example embedded in `BOOTSTRAP.md` is itself a real ~60% reduction on a `SOUL.md` excerpt.

**What was not tested:**
Live multi-turn agent sessions; whether a given model fully obeys the guidance in practice (model-dependent); other providers; non-English workspace setups.

---

### Note on revisions

The original version of this PR claimed ~83% reduction and per-example reductions of 75% / 85%. Re-measuring against current `main` showed those figures were overstated and conflated *hypothetical* agent output with what the diff ships (the "Compacted BOOTSTRAP.md" row in the old table was wrong — `BOOTSTRAP.md` grows, it does not shrink). The numbers above are the verified, reproducible measurements: ~51% with all rules preserved. The `CHANGELOG.md` entry was also dropped, since contributor PRs must not edit `CHANGELOG.md` (it is release-owned, per `CONTRIBUTING.md` and the repo `AGENTS.md`); this also clears the merge conflict.

---

_AI-assisted PR. Drafted with an AI coding agent; numbers re-measured and verified by hand against current `main` before posting._

prs.title: fix(browser): preserve network settings during allowed navigation
prs.body:
Related: #173453

## What Problem This Solves

Chrome relay clients can receive `tab <id> access was revoked` when an allowed navigation commits while a network configuration command is in flight, even though tab permission remains granted.

## User Impact

Cache disabling, extra HTTP headers, and service-worker bypass now complete across allowed navigation in both All tabs and Selected tabs modes. Actual permission removal and debugger detach still reject command results. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Classify the three exact methods in the existing command-scope owner. The CDP contract describes [`setCacheDisabled`](https://chromedevtools.github.io/devtools-protocol/tot/Network/#method-setCacheDisabled) and [`setBypassServiceWorker`](https://chromedevtools.github.io/devtools-protocol/tot/Network/#method-setBypassServiceWorker) as per-request toggles, and [`setExtraHTTPHeaders`](https://chromedevtools.github.io/devtools-protocol/tot/Network/#method-setExtraHTTPHeaders) as headers to always send with requests. Their configuration receipts have tab/session lifetime rather than document lifetime.

The bounded sibling audit also checked Fetch: `enable`/`disable` and request continuations already have tab scope; `getResponseBody` and `takeResponseBodyAsStream` access document/request content and keep document-sensitive checks ([CDP Fetch](https://chromedevtools.github.io/devtools-protocol/tot/Fetch/)). There is no blanket Network or Fetch exemption. Current tab access, group authority, connection, and debugger attachment are still checked around dispatch and result delivery; this change adds no detached or deferred side effect and captures no new facts.

Original fix by @LiuwqGit; maintainer cleanup extends the same classification to the two sibling settings, documents the behavior, and replaces the 195-line suite with 134 lines covering the affected boundary. Distinct error reasons for document invalidation versus actual permission revocation remain outside scope, so this PR uses a related reference rather than closing the whole issue.

## Evidence

- Source/history confirmation on main: unlisted methods capture `documentRevision`; allowed navigation advances it while retaining tab authority; the command handler rechecks the captured epoch after native completion. History `8d3e087f03526` and `b057266d78d0c` establish the existing tab-configuration/document-content distinction.
- PR CI is the test gate per maintainer policy. [CI run 38822735328](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38822735328) passed on exact head `8151070a614ccb9dc08132bbd35457e1cd982e96`, including production/test typechecks, lint, baseline ratchets, routed tests, and `openclaw/ci-gate`. The [browser job 116723595473](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38822735328/job/116723595473) passed all 11 new regressions and 229 tests across 12 selected browser files. CI ran `node --import tsx scripts/ci-run-node-test-shard.mts` with the planned `changed-extensions-config` scope and `test/vitest/vitest.extension-browser.config.ts`.
- `background.cache-configuration.test.ts` has 11 deterministic cases: `delivers $method after an allowed document commit during dispatch` for the three settings in both modes; `rejects a cache-setting receipt after genuine access revocation` in both modes; `rejects a cache-setting receipt after debugger detach`; and `rejects document-sensitive %s after an allowed document commit` for Network/Fetch response bodies. The real background handler, access policy, and navigation event wiring run with mocked native Chrome I/O. There are no new sleeps, polling loops, or unresolved deferred commands.
- Changed-file oxfmt 0.72.0 and oxlint 1.87.0 passed. The nested checkout has no local dependency directory and the parent install lacks the unrelated Solid UI plugin, so task-local, integrity-verified oxlint 1.87.0 used the unchanged core rules with only the `ui/**` JS-plugin override omitted: 2 files, 231 rules, zero diagnostics. `git diff --check` passed.
- Autoreview: precommit and final branch reviews through P2 both returned `scoped-clean`, with no actionable findings. The final branch review covered the merged candidate `0f47e9798f94965c4547bef51b386fdc036623af`; unchanged native event wiring was inspected separately by the maintainer. The subsequent merge of main into head `8151070a614ccb9dc08132bbd35457e1cd982e96` leaves the entire browser extension and changed docs byte-identical, so that review remains applicable.
- Local tests, typechecks, production-reverted negative controls, live Chrome/Gateway proof, and Crabbox/Testbox leases were intentionally skipped per maintainer policy. No contributor code executed locally. Local test wall time was not measured. Final-head CI reports 472 ms summed test time for the 11 regressions and 36.01 s total Vitest duration for the 12-file browser selection (including transform/setup); these are different measurements.
- ClawSweeper's latest review (comment 6202799774) reported no code findings. Its live-proof-only request is superseded by the maintainer policy that PR CI supplies proof. No human review findings were present.
- Exact diff versus main: production +3/-0, tests +134/-0, docs +3/-0. Production growth is the smallest correct fix: three exact-method set entries; deleting unrelated code to offset them would weaken scope. Relative to the contributor version, the test file is 61 lines smaller while covering both sibling settings and document-sensitive controls.

The first CI run failed `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` on a stale `turn-router.mcp-app.test.ts` / `protocol-validators.js` mock-export baseline row ([job 116720672491](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38821913969/job/116720672491)). Main independently removed that exact row in `6a066e906845b`; main was merged before the second push, and the final baseline-ratchet job passed. The latest scheduled main run at diagnosis, `38817599758`, predates this failure and passed that ratchet, so no matching inherited-CI exemption is claimed.

prs.title: fix(cron): record the planned account for legacy automations instead of failing every run
prs.body:
Related: #172590, #172792, #173411

## What Problem This Solves

After an update, an automation created before account binding keeps failing on every run when Doctor cannot choose an account for it:

- **Several eligible stored accounts** (for example an API key and a subscription login for one provider): Doctor only warns "More than one inference account is eligible", and every run then fails with "Automation has no recorded inference account" until someone edits the job by hand.
- **Creating a new job** whose route uses a key in env or provider config is refused ("requires a stored inference account"), although since #173411 an old job on the same key keeps running.

## Why This Change Was Made

Rule: a job with no recorded account gets the account its next unbound run would use. That is an explicit selection, or else the first account from the runtime's normal planner, the same account every unbound run used before #172590. Refuse only when no account fits, or when that account is another person's personal login. Keys in env or provider config, and credentialless routes, have no stored account to record: they keep the job unbound, for creation as well as for runs.

- **Doctor (`inference-binding-migration.ts`):**
  - computes the current route with the same `prepareAgentRuntimeAuth` call as a run, including the provider preferred-profile hook (`resolveProviderAuthProfileId`), which it did not pass before;
  - when several accounts are eligible, records the planner's first account instead of refusing;
  - names the other eligible accounts and the `automations edit … --model …@<profileId>` command in its change log;
  - leaves explicit selections, missing accounts, personal-account refusal, backup and commit unchanged.
- **Creation (`captureCronInferenceBinding`)** uses the run's predicate (`isConfiguredKeyAuthSource`): a configured-key route creates an unbound job instead of failing. Other direct sources are still refused.
- **Docs:** `cron-jobs/payloads.md` and `cron-jobs/troubleshooting.md`.

Not changed: AWS SDK and runtime credentials (they still need adoption; a separate follow-up can admit declared AWS SDK routes), bound jobs and their protection against later default or order changes, personal-account rules, native/CLI runtime ownership, the binding format and the stored data. A manual source upgrade still needs `openclaw doctor --fix`, as the docs already say. Managed updates and the container entrypoint run it. There is no new runtime write path: recording an account from a run would need the credential authority capture that Doctor's offline maintenance scope provides, and every supported update path already reaches Doctor.

## User Impact

After an update, an old automation with several eligible accounts keeps running on the same account it used before, and Doctor reports which account it recorded and how to change it. New automations can use a key in env or provider config, like old ones.

## Evidence

- **Doctor regression** (`inference-binding-migration.accounts.test.ts`): the `ambiguous` job (two eligible OpenAI accounts, one in cooldown) now records `openai:a`, the planner's first account, with "Also eligible: openai:b". On `main` the same test fails with "More than one inference account is eligible". A job whose session holds an earlier automatic fallback to another provider records the default provider's account, not the fallback's.
- **Creation** (`cron.inference-binding.test.ts`): `cron.add` on an env key and on a provider-config key creates an unbound job. On `main` both are refused.
- **Personal accounts** (new Doctor test): with a personal account first in `auth.order`, the unattended planner never selects it, so Doctor records the shared account a run would use and never the personal one. The existing Gateway test "requires the personal owner for explicit creation and account adoption" covers explicit adoption.
- **Focused suites pass:** Doctor migration (both files), Gateway cron binding, inference-binding executor, auth-profile propagation.
- **Fleet census** (read-only Doctor previews on four real installs): see the comment on #172590.
- **Live differential** (real Gateway and CLI; a mock OpenAI provider that logs each request's `Authorization` header; two stored OpenAI profiles added through the CLI, `openai:alpha` then `openai:beta`, with `auth.order.openai = [beta, alpha]`; synthetic keys; a credentialless `local` fallback):

  | Step | Build | Result | Provider request |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | `v2026.10.3` | `cron run` → `ok`; the job row has no `inferenceBinding` | `Bearer sk-synthetic-beta-…` |
  | 2 | `main` (`19752be`) | Doctor: "More than one inference account is eligible: openai:beta, openai:alpha". `cron run` → `error` "Automation has no recorded inference account…" | none, not even the fallback |
  | 3 | this head | Doctor: "retain openai:beta for openai/gpt-6-mock … Also eligible: openai:alpha"; row `inferenceBinding.profileId = "openai:beta"`. `cron run` → `ok` | `Bearer sk-synthetic-beta-…`, the same as step 1 |
  | 4 | this head | `auth.order` reversed to [alpha, beta], Gateway restarted, `cron run` → `ok` | `Bearer sk-synthetic-beta-…`: the binding holds |
  | 5 | this head vs `main` | fresh state with only `models.providers.openai.apiKey`: `cron add` succeeds with no binding and the run uses that key. `main` refuses `cron add` with "requires a stored inference account" | `Bearer sk-synthetic-config-…` |

  The account recorded in step 3 is not the alphabetical or first-added profile. It is the one the stable build actually sent.
- **Live boundary cases** on the candidate, from the differential state (Doctor recorded `openai:beta`):
  - the `openai:beta` key is replaced through `models auth paste-api-key`: `cron run` → `error` "Automation inference account was replaced. Explicitly select an authorized account again."; 0 provider requests, no fallback;
  - `openai:beta` is removed through `models auth logout`: `cron run` → `error`; 0 provider requests; `openai:alpha` is not used and no fallback runs. The error text is "MCP authorization was disconnected or replaced" (`MCP_AUTHORIZATION_RETIRED`), a misleading message from the existing authorization owner, not from this PR (follow-up).
  - A live personal-account case is not possible from a synthetic CLI: `users.authConnect` needs a signed-in person. Instead, `isolated-agent.auth-continuity.integration.test.ts` > "records the shared account a run plans, never a personal one listed first" connects a real personal account (`ensureProfileForEmail` + `connectUserModelAccountAsync`), puts it first in `auth.order` next to a shared API key, runs the real Doctor migration and then the real embedded cron runner with only provider HTTP stubbed. Doctor records the shared account. The run returns `ok`, and the only provider request carries the shared key (`Bearer synthetic-platform-key`): the personal key is never sent, and no fallback runs.

prs.title: perf(gateway): reuse prewarmed bytecode without main-thread flushes
prs.body:
**Outcome: withdrawn after measurement; do not merge.** The native read-only cache improves bootstrap but increases CPU and memory without improving end-to-end readiness.

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway startup cannot reuse prewarmed main-thread bytecode because writable Node compile caches were disabled to prevent synchronous startup/shutdown flush stalls.

## User Impact

On Node 26.8+, a warm build-scoped cache can accelerate Gateway imports without making the main thread serialize or persist bytecode. Cold/missing caches remain best-effort; older supported Node versions and Bun retain the uncached main-thread behavior. No configuration or schema changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use Node's native read-only compile-cache mode at the existing cache owner. Workers continue populating the same cache. Record successful read-only activation with that owner so the launcher and direct entrypoint do not respawn an already-safe process. Inherited writable caches retain the existing respawn policy.

Production delta: +19/-2 lines (+17 net). The growth preserves the existing no-main-thread-flush contract across supported runtimes and the repeated launcher/entrypoint boundary; there is no second loader, custom bytecode cache, or new configuration. Post-bind plugin registration stays ordered.

## Evidence

- Regression fails on the original code (`false !== true`: warmed cache remains disabled) and passes with the change. It checks native Node cache activation, repeated-entry respawn avoidance, warm/cold module loading, and unchanged cache contents after an explicit flush.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/node-compile-cache.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 11 passed; 2.68 s command wall time (1.46 s Vitest).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/entry.compile-cache.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 25 passed; 3.34 s command wall time (1.39 s Vitest).
- `OPENCLAW_E2E_SKIP_BUILD=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/openclaw-launcher.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'shares the Gateway cache base'`: all 9 focused launcher modes passed (126 unrelated tests skipped), 4.90 s wall time. Reproduced and corrected the two inherited-cache launcher assertions identified in review; the maintenance worker can create the cache before the repeated entrypoint enables read-only reuse.
- Changed-file formatting, targeted repository lint, and `git diff --check` passed. The first lint invocation automatically prepared shared declarations; subsequent lint skipped preparation. No full local build, test suite, typecheck, or Testbox/Crabbox lease. Broad gates run in PR CI.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): no actionable P0–P2 findings. The autoreview helper refused the configured provider selector before inference; no operator configuration changed.
- The reported compile-cache warning was emitted by pre-cutover activation work, before the serving Gateway started. It is not proof that Gateway workers lacked caching. The source history deliberately disabled writable main-thread caching to avoid lifecycle stalls; this change preserves that boundary.
- Local synthetic source startup profile: 5,000 sessions, 6,000 retained runs, 19 bundled plugins. Source transformation/import work dominates; activation preparation is only 0.7 ms. This saturated-host profile is attribution evidence, not a release timing claim.

## Measurement and decision

Four alternating baseline/candidate pairs used complete built release graphs, Node 26.8.2, the same final release path and prewarmed cache namespace, and the same already-started synthetic fixture: 5,000 sessions, 6,000 retained runs, 18 loaded bundled plugins. All eight runs started successfully and exited cleanly. A separate diagnostic confirmed one launcher respawn for each version, an uncached baseline main thread, and persistent read-only activation in the candidate. Normalizing emitted import hashes showed only the compile-cache owner differed semantically between the two built graphs.

| Median | Baseline | Candidate | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `process.bootstrap` | 2,126.9 ms | 1,871.5 ms | -12.0% |
| `plugins.runtime-post-bind` | 525.7 ms | 544.1 ms | +3.5% |
| Spawn to `/readyz` | 7,231.0 ms | 7,401.6 ms | +2.4% |
| Child CPU, startup through clean shutdown | 19,380.8 ms | 20,260.0 ms | +4.5% |
| `memory.ready.rssMb` | 1,262.8 MiB | 1,401.2 MiB | +138.4 MiB |
| `memory.ready.heapUsedMb` | 514.6 MiB | 618.3 MiB | +103.7 MiB |

Bootstrap improved in all four pairs, but CPU increased in all four too. The phase gain is offset elsewhere (`sessions.materialize` median 1,078.8 → 1,312.4 ms), and memory grows materially. The measurements establish neither reduced overall startup time nor a deployment downtime saving. Expected proven offline reduction: **0 seconds**; production was not modified or restarted.

The preliminary root-helper-only comparison was discarded: an old bundled owner in the entrypoint disabled caching again. Only the complete-build comparisons above inform this decision. The source profile is attribution evidence only; no cold-cache deployment gain is claimed.

The original implementation head passed CI run 38823796273. The subsequent launcher-test correction has focused local proof and independent review; its current-head CI was still running without reported failures when the performance result ruled out landing. No broad local test suite was run.

This adds 17 production lines and demonstrably increases resource use, so it does not meet the lane's no-regression requirement. Closing without merge rather than trading users' CPU and memory for a faster intermediate phase. The existing main-thread cache policy and ordered plugin registry remain unchanged.

## User Impact

Generated skill packages now stay out of ordinary untracked-file discovery. Source skills, unrelated project files and tracked changes remain visible. The existing workspace reconciliation/publication exclusion is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The synchronization owner writes a local `.gitignore` containing `*` in its generated skills directory, through the existing custody-checked root. It establishes the rule before cached reuse and retains the file when pruning generated children on refresh. No project-wide or user-global Git configuration is modified.

## Evidence

Baseline: `80f6c150ec764a7c83821460f768d0eaf0ead3b2`, Node 26.1.0, pnpm 12.10.1, locked workspace dependencies.

- New `workspace-skill-sync.git.test.ts` invokes actual `syncWorkspaceSkills` and real Git subprocesses in an isolated repository. The unchanged source fails because generated paths appear in ordinary untracked discovery; fixed source passes.
- The test covers initial materialization, repeated snapshot reuse, and refreshed discovery/pruning. It checks a source skill and unrelated untracked file stay visible, an indexed file's working-tree modification remains visible, and generated skill bytes remain readable.
- Focused Git, synchronization and custody files: **20 passed**. Vitest 21.45s; wrapper 24.63s including cold compilation. New Git test: 327ms. CI timing pending.
- Targeted Oxlint, formatting, line-cap ratchet and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Canonical autoreview P0–P2: scoped-clean, no actionable findings.

The Git commands and skill synchronization run for real; Git, filesystem and the synchronization owner are not mocked. No Docker/container allocation, full Gateway session, external service, paid model call or full workspace suite was run. AI assistance: Codex was used for investigation, implementation, tests and review.

`pnpm tsgo:core` and `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.services.json --incremental` passed, as did the final `pnpm format:check` for the three changed files.
