prs.title: refactor: trust prepared feature-plugin facts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Feature plugins repeatedly reconstruct private worker messages, copy facts their callers never mutate, reparse already-prepared results, and maintain duplicate owners for the same work. This adds both runtime work and opportunities for policy drift. Several catches also turn genuine failures into apparently successful partial results.

## User Impact

Keep existing features, public plugin/config/protocol contracts, normal cancellation, resource limits, security checks and durable state. Make active-memory consumer failures, native vector deletion failures and malformed Logbook distraction JSON visible instead of silently accepting incomplete work. CLI search retains matches with a warning when recall recording fails; Doctor surfaces legacy-directory discovery failures other than absence. No migration or configuration change is required. Phase E standalone session memory and its factory, registry, expiry, federation and tests are untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use one existing owner for MXC protected skill mounts and Team Reports HTTP response handling. Carry typed private IPC and prepared memory/CUA facts through their consumers rather than repeatedly reconstructing or serializing them. Make Team Reports consume the store's unique chronological daily-report stream once. Keep admission at actual external network, model, plugin, persisted-file and security-effect boundaries.

Coverage log: the lane's initial three-pattern production inventory spans 5,873 hits in 1,097 files before scope/family reconciliation. Detailed task-local ledgers cover browser, voice/meetings, memory, media/search, Workboard, policy, QA and peripheral owners. This is a reviewed cleanup packet, not a claim that the lane is exhausted. Config/directive, SQLite backend and generic-helper families remain with their designated lanes; ClickClack/SMS/Raft are excluded for their channel owner. No Telegram live harness, audit core, changelog or PR-tooling helper was edited.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- QuickJS private executor messages no longer get a second shape parser or silent empty-list defaults. The paired producer and worker share one payload type; guests cannot post host messages. Feature #154522 introduced these guards; linked #153889 requests a simpler runtime, not protection from malformed private host messages. A programming error now fails at the actual operation. Guest validation, host-dispatch authority and execution budgets remain.
- ONNX's paired subprocess no longer repeats full request/reply schemas, ready handshakes, request IDs or impossible response-kind checks. Serial IPC, native model-output admission, queue/input/cache bounds, cancellation kill/join and FIFO remain. #153476 describes implementation qualification rather than a human malformed-private-message incident. A broken same-binary worker may now fail normally instead of producing a custom protocol error. Existing catalog-filtered bounded warm producers are unchanged.
- Browser tool result projection trusts existing browser-client response contracts, but the Gateway/node `trackOpened(unknown)` boundary remains validated. #167926 and #114814 introduced repeated projections; #110797's durable ownership/closure contract remains. A broken private route result now fails at use rather than becoming an empty projection.
- Browser read-only dashboard preparation no longer suppresses owner-change errors through a duplicate read-result revocation wrapper. Destructive close/write authority, successor ownership and settlement remain. Config/runtime replacement during a read may now surface the owner-change error; existing synthetic concurrency coverage retains its no-successor-close assertions.
- Browser profile deletion borrows the immutable owner-published config fact rather than cloning it before teardown (#104601; linked proposal is synthetic in #168841). An unsupported in-place mutation of that published object can change the expected snapshot; supported config writes still go through the owner and exact effect-boundary comparison.
- FaceTime helper metadata is admitted once at the authenticated socket owner instead of being erased to unknown and reparsed by consumers (the peer reader originated in #119291; #163983 is a later owner refactor, neither claimed as a malformed-private-producer incident). Native payloads cannot supply peer/topology facts; raw call/audio fields, complete-topology requirements, current-peer effect checks and ordinary shutdown settlement remain. A future buggy private producer fails at use rather than being silently reconstructed downstream.
- Beam metadata refresh does not loop on speculative upload/reload revision races. The measured cache and periodic refresh from #158394 remain; its overtaken-refresh proof was synthetic. A concurrent upload can show old catalog metadata until the next poll, without changing transcript reads, retention or publisher authority.
- Beam saturated retry bookkeeping evicts by bounded queue order rather than scanning expiry timestamps. #121186/#121176 describes an injected source-audit reproduction, not actual-use clock rollback. At more than 1,000 tracked uploads the chosen retry entry may differ after rollback/rotation; source rows, receiver delivery, expiry and the just-acknowledged upload remain protected.
- Beam upload and Reef completion/key facts are no longer defensively deep-copied. Producers own those admitted values and current callers do not mutate them. #148908, #149849 and #109380 provide implementation/synthetic provenance, not a caller-mutation production incident. A newly buggy private consumer could mutate borrowed facts; publisher/claim authority, encryption, signing and durable completion remain.
- Team Reports borrows read-only report/roster/item facts and copies only containers it actually changes (#139850). Future private mutation is not hidden by a full deep clone. Final independent size enforcement, data admission, evidence ordering and public report shape remain.
- Team Reports reads accepted daily reports once, retaining snapshot/scope checks and missing-day accounting. #159101's measured worker/memory isolation stays. A future private source yielding multiple generations for one day gets the first accepted row rather than global newest-generation selection; today's SQL owner emits one accepted chronological row per day.
- Memory Wiki hashes/serializes a compiled snapshot once at its store owner (#110167), rather than accepting and rechecking a caller-supplied generation. Persisted hash/bytes, external source-byte validation, journal acceptance/privacy checks and measured string-retention detachment (#164441) remain. No arbitrary hash input exists after this private cutover.
- CUA MCP consumers use their admitted structured record rather than JSON stringify/parse round trips (#123635/#124035). The unused vendor-required rawJson field is empty; native SDK JSON admission remains. No OS authority, frame/reference identity or response-resource bound is removed.
- MXC consumes the existing SDK skill-mount owner rather than its 84-line duplicate (#97086). Read-write-only admission, canonical containment, protected read-only paths and writable-parent overlap refusals remain. Unexpected canonical resolution failure can fail setup visibly instead of silently omitting a mount; no path is newly authorized.
- OpenShell combines two same-operation source lstat preflights (c6f5725906d), keeping symlink/hardlink/device/root refusals and final fs-safe mutation checks. An unsupported swap between those speculative observations loses one accidental observation, not effect authority; no qualifying human report was cited by the introducing commit.
- Internal typed performance counters, optional scalar facts, exhaustive command dispatch and renderer-owned timeline width no longer receive impossible-shape checks. Producer/schema admission and actual persisted debug-entry validation remain. MCP catalog schemas are admitted once into locals, including valid false schemas; actual remote schema compilation/validation remains.
- Workboard and policy consume normalized producer facts rather than repeating normalization or type guards. External config/document admission, approval policy and write-effect authority remain; no public config key or schema changes.
- Active-memory no longer swallows errors from its internal transcript consumer; a failed scan rejects visibly rather than appearing complete. Vector writes no longer swallow native DELETE failures before INSERT. Logbook malformed persisted JSON now rejects instead of returning empty distractions and incorrect statistics (#99930, extracted in #144982). These are explicit silent-failure repairs, not accepted partial-success contracts.
- Parsed config/internal optional values no longer receive duplicate type checks or redundant undefined fallbacks. Real null-to-undefined wire/SQL/dependency conversions remain. Existing intentional nonfatal catches now state why ignoring is correct; no new silent swallowing was introduced.

## Net LOC

Signed head `7c1ad469dab55550a0bb091b5d0a6928e0f46d40`, excluding the separately published dir-fetch bug, removes **623 net production lines** (+843/-1,466 across138 production files, including the new seven-line private payload type). The hook changed no source bytes; all current-candidate proof below covers this head. Prior96f removed657 lines; initial published493c84 removed812 and signed repair6f7b3c removed817. Tests, docs, generated/declaration files and shrink-only baselines are excluded. This follows more than three hours of implementation and uses the requested honest 500–999 cleanup-packet fallback; it does not claim1,000 lines or whole-lane completion.

Per the explicit inconclusive-replay rule, the final reduction restores all OTel edits and the memory-core dreaming, consolidation, indexing, cache, KNN IPC, backfill and internal typed-guard cleanups to the original base, including their original tests and matching assertion allowance. The later reduction additionally restores every QA Lab/QA Channel production and test change to that base, with matching assertion allowances. Those mechanisms are not shipped reduction. The independently proved CLI/Doctor/vector-write error repairs remain; active-memory, Wiki and LanceDB are separate owners. No Phase E code or test was ever changed.

## Evidence

- Author-side `pr-simplify` and `deslop` inspected the complete changed diff, using existing owners. Prior full-candidate review through P2 was scoped-clean. Fresh final review raised three P2s; all declined on determining source evidence, not represented as a clean emitted verdict: canonical plugin state has no aggregate quota and registration commits or throws; Agents API `readRecord` already validates the complete persisted row with stricter schema/refinements before projection; both production ONNX warm callers already select catalog IDs and bound the list. No accepted/actionable finding remains; no review rerun for a nicer verdict.
- The623-line candidate's source-mapped complete production and touched-test graphs pass on the qualified frozen install. The full canonical type sequence completed exit0; prior96f proof is not substituted for this replay.
- Runtime value cycles and fresh Madge on the623-line frozen candidate:0.
- The623-line candidate passes rollback formatting, boundary lint, whitespace, assertion-safety and the line-cap ratchet (161 changed source files, no new violations or over-cap growth). Qualified local types cover every actual config in the cancelled hosted suite and both retained production/test graphs.
- Canonical101-file attempt was stopped after96min, not a completed pass. Tooling3/3, active-memory18/18, Browser147 plus one existing skip, Workboard87, short-term91, Doctor37 and additional assertions passed. Three Agents API cases failed from fixture/SQLite lease clocks; a selective timer correction preserves virtual execution deadlines while keeping Date and renewal intervals real. Its narrow replay stopped before assertions. The later59-file replay was deliberately stopped for attributable CI repairs, not represented as a full pass; Browser92/92 and suppression3/3 remain valid prior-input proof. The current13-file repair replay passed all258 tests acrosssix canonical shards, including completed-generation verification (2674.43s wall). No production lease, execution timeout, retry, assertion or skip change.
- Crabbox's prepared-archive FIFO test returned code:null/output:empty at its existing3s shell deadline; the FIFO production guard is unchanged. This remains unresolved local evidence, not a proven inherited or load-only failure. The earlier leaf replay was invalidated before assertions by compiled-source mutation; affected browser/database/memory suites are missing proof, not product or baseline failures. All source was frozen after the final batch, and the replacement owner replay uses current inputs.
- Memory-error baseline: both actual CLI/Doctor regressions fail for the intended missing warning and swallowed EACCES (969.86s wall,876.13s Vitest,94% transform). The search regression moved into the existing small diagnostic suite, retaining the real CLI boundary. Fixed regressions are in the final replay.
- Changed-file checks: deliberately stopped after31min in the repository-wide SQLite type graph; incomplete, not a passing check or baseline-red classification. Conflict markers and line-cap growth passed; the QuickJS private-seam SAFETY annotation is corrected. Removed exactly two verified obsolete max-lines allowlist rows; targeted max-lines replay passes (527 grandfathered suppressions, OPENCLAW count453/453). No suppressions added.
- Earlier targeted full lint reached the existing SDK declaration-preparation deadline before lint execution; no lint success claim. Exact-head hosted CI remains the broad gate.
- Logbook decoder baseline rejects the expected exception (intended failure); fixed decoder proof passes. The actual worker-store regression remains; incomplete local broad attempts and completed prior-head hosted evidence stay distinct.

All runtime proof uses task-owned HOME, OpenClaw state/config and XDG directories. No real Gateway/state, live call/browser session, schema/durability/retention/permission change or dependency change. Remote proof was unavailable; an unresolved task-owned pending receipt is retained for native recovery, without claiming allocation or absence.

## First-head CI attribution and repair status

Prior reviewed signed repair head: `6f7b3c3c89e4d6319d400a7619e46cd264cd2dd9`, CI run38804517932. Later reductions and their independent proof are recorded below. This run remains prior-head CI, not current-head evidence.

Exact initial head493c84ab306e6ef26ca204a84c2d6a2c585a0155, [run38796218926](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38796218926), attempt1, completed. No CI rerun. The table describes initial-head evidence, not a claim about an unpushed repair head.

| Failed job | Attribution and disposition |

| checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-2 | Ours: two dashboard board-read cases still pinned silent owner-change suppression. Expectations now reflect the accepted visible owner error; successor/no-close assertions retained. Complete repair replay passes. |
| checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-5 | Ours: two Reef cases mixed caller-mutation pins with useful crypto/source coverage. Only unsupported mutations removed; ciphertext reuse, nonce count, durable completion and source-affinity assertions retained. Complete repair replay passes. |
| checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-6-1 | Ours: six OTel cases inspected duplicate setter calls. Observation now accumulates creation and typed setter attributes; redaction/content expectations unchanged. OTel69/69 pass. |
| checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-8-3 | Ours: two private manager tests repeated external brief admission. Duration cap, voicemail ownership, provider-once and actual command/CLI schema coverage remain. Voice41/41 pass. |
| checks-node-changed-18 | Unknown, not inherited: memory provenance E2E reaches cron.add but lacks a stored inference account. Clean-main baseline failed in declaration preparation before assertions. Affected memory-core cleanup hunks dropped, original behavior/tests restored; account/security admission and protected memory test unchanged. |
| checks-node-changed-20 | Unknown, not inherited: OTel E2E timed out during Gateway startup before any span capture. Local comparison never reached assertions. All OTel cleanup and test changes dropped to the original base; no timeout/retry/skip or declaration-guard change. |
| check-test-types-core-3 | Pre-existing matching Apple-cache232 type diagnostic, also in scheduled-main run38794323475/job116627033406; canonical classifier agrees. Fixed independently on main by3edfe65212bc6d2585bd352284d4b27c7cbfdd0f (#173427). No lane edit/rebase for drift. |

Aggregate ci-gate is red because of the failures above.43 cancelled auto-response checks are superseded comment automation, with two successful same-head replacements; no required test suite is inferred from those cancellations. Other planned suites, including PostgreSQL conformance, completed without additional failed families.

The prior repair delta received author-side pr-simplify/deslop and fresh independent P0–P2 review: scoped-clean, correct0.94. Prior repair touched-test types, line caps, assertion ratchet, format, focused boundary lint and258 focused runtime tests pass. Full type-aware lint failed before lint execution at the existing300000ms SDK declaration-preparation deadline; no passing or inherited-lint claim. Neither original E2E failure received a root-cause attribution or inherited-failure waiver; both passed on the later repair head. The newer reduction has completed fresh author simplification, independent review and the final Doctor inventory/suppression replay. Current-head hosted CI remains pending.

The later private voice-manager P1 review comment was declined with concrete caller evidence in its discussion: all production callers admit unknown briefs at command-service or readCliBrief before this private helper; CallManager is not a public SDK/API export. No external validation was removed.

## Prior96f reduction proof and second-head CI

The reduced frozen production graph typechecks; its touched-test graph typechecks, including the final inventory regression. Runtime value cycles0; Madge cycles0. prs.title: refactor(ui): port chat metadata rendering to Solid
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Move chat comment previews, question summaries, pull-request rows, and GitHub publication controls to Solid as part of the Control UI migration.

## User Impact

The existing comment admission, question delivery/reopening, publication actions, full `owner/repo#number` references, and retained CI disclosures keep their behavior. Explicitly dismissing Details clears disclosure intent; temporarily parking it preserves that intent.

## Why This Change Was Made

Solid now owns these rendering consumers while the existing domain owners remain authoritative. Native Solid callers use the PR component directly; unused Lit publication, PR-rendering, and attachment-admission paths are removed. Thin adapters remain for active legacy callers. The growth is primarily JSX expansion and these remaining adapters; no second state owner is introduced.

The earlier bundle comparison exposed a real lazy-loading regression through the shared compiler decorator helper. Main now owns the neutral `decorator-runtime` chunk, and this PR adopts that production configuration byte-for-byte. Regression coverage retains both the class-decorator route-isolation test and the stronger field-decorator/shared-stylesheet test.

Release-note context: Control UI chat metadata rendering moves to Solid while preserving question, comment, and GitHub publication behavior.

## Evidence

Current candidate: `65195c7c71217449a8b1b206dbd9981ed3237ba6`, after an ordinary merge of actual main `9f4b34b842b3375b3e182e1836fc5114ab69c0ce`. The source repository's remote-tracking ref was explicitly refreshed before merging. The sole manual conflict was `ui/src/types/solid-elements.d.ts`: main's exported `ElementProperties`, native dock element contracts, catalog tags and systems-page cleanup remain intact alongside this port's typed chat CI properties and tags. The lead inspected the complete resolution.

The four automatically merged test files were also inspected against current main. Secret-leak assertions and scroll thresholds are unchanged; the prior diagnostic labels remain. The question-summary test retains its content assertions under `waitForSolid`. No additional runtime behavior was introduced by this integration.

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Independent Codex review, P0–P2 | Current main-relative candidate scoped-clean; final captured-source verification passed. The lead independently inspected the declaration resolution and all four automatic test overlaps. Unchanged dependency implementations and historical test results were not treated as current-head validation. |
| UI typecheck | `pnpm tsgo:ui` passed once on the final integrated source. |
| Formatting / whitespace | Resolved declaration formatting passed in 19 ms; staged declaration whitespace check passed. The ordinary merge commit completed without bypassing hooks. |
| Current production Knip | Failed with exactly three unused files: `src/shared/safe-record.ts`, `ui/src/components/dropdown-menu-controller.ts`, and `ui/src/components/web-awesome-popover.ts`. All three files, the Knip configuration and their discovered references match incorporated main byte-for-byte. Neither tree has a production caller; the metadata port retires none. No new ignores or unnecessary full baseline rerun were added. |
| Retained focused behavior checks | The predecessor's annotation browser suite passed 18/18 once with `--maxWorkers=1`; earlier unchanged-input chunking 6/6 and text-chip admission 7/7 passed. No local E2E battery or redundant rerun was added for the type-only merge. |
| Exact-head full CI observation | Run [38819457897](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38819457897) for `65195c7c71217449a8b1b206dbd9981ed3237ba6` returned completed/success: 45 successful jobs and 24 skips, including successful security and CI gates. Octopool explicitly marked the run view stale and the job list cached, so this is a recorded completed-run snapshot, not a live admission check. The native workflow must revalidate live state before landing. |
| Historical CI | Exact predecessor `2d8185acd3c290302ac470611a0580791cf1a90c`, run 38798317675, failed only the update-run restart-report case and its downstream gate. Its matching scheduled-main failure was attributed for that predecessor only. Earlier failed/cancelled runs remain historical; none is relabeled green or used to grant the replacement head an exception. |
| Retrospective codemod audit | After implementation drafting, dry-ran original baseline `72422c4007bff81a5d0b55b56e8439d7f83892e3` and traced the metadata lane's 7 Lit files / 68 markers to the port. Every marker has an explicit disposition. This is retrospective review, not evidence that the required dry-run preceded conversion. |
| Retained build / strict performance | Corrected predecessor build and strict same-host comparison passed with no violations or warnings. The current integration changes only type declarations manually; production renderers and the lazy route boundary are preserved. |
| Retained route-boundary inspection | Chat no longer includes the New Session bundle. Source-map comparison adds only the seven migrated chat renderers; no new New Session or pet modules. |
| Retained visual proof | Inspected synthetic 1440×960 PR Details captures are byte-identical, including a long full repository reference. The type-only integration introduces no visual change. |

prs.title: fix: show compaction failures instead of stale overflow advice
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes misleading context-overflow and reset advice when automatic compaction fails before the next model request.

## User Impact

Users see the final compaction failure and its recovery guidance instead of an earlier provisional overflow message. No context limits, compaction retries, model requests, configuration, or transcript retention change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The lifecycle callback records a provisional overflow while recovery is still running. A later structured `compaction_failure` already carries the authoritative failure, but command finalization currently prefers the old lifecycle error. Prefer the final failure only for that combination, and omit the obsolete overflow observation from the terminal event. Unrelated lifecycle-error precedence stays unchanged.

## Evidence

- Reproduced through the real lifecycle callback → final error resolution → terminal event path, using synthetic fixtures and no session data.
- On upstream base `25a55493f84320e78806a1fcb25a6b869ea72050`, the new regression fails with the misleading overflow/reset message; the other 18 tests pass.
- With the fix, all 19 lifecycle tests pass. Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/command/lifecycle.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (repository wrapper equivalent of `pnpm test`); 35.43 seconds wall including cold compiled-worker preparation, 31.38 seconds reported suite duration. CI seconds are not yet available.
- Targeted command-test TypeScript graph, scoped type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Production incident: automatic summary generation exhausted its output allowance without summary text, but the client displayed generic context overflow/reset advice. Manual compaction subsequently recovered the existing session.
- No live Gateway restart or provider replay was performed for this upstream patch. The regression verifies lifecycle behavior, not browser rendering.

- Independent native Codex review traced callback → lifecycle owner → post-run → chat delivery and found no actionable P0–P2 defects. This was an owner-approved alternate review after the CLI helper failed authentication, not a helper-certified review. Negative guard/fallback combinations are not individually tested; existing generic error and timeout coverage remains.

prs.title: fix(build): release preparation ownership after cancellation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Interrupted extension-boundary preparation could bypass normal ownership cleanup, leaving dist artifact ownership behind and blocking a later build. The original updater incident motivated this repair, but its precise originating failure is not proven by the available evidence. This change addresses the reproducible preparation cancellation path without reclaiming ownership merely because a PID died.

## User Impact

A cancelled preparation joins its compiler children and releases its own artifact ownership when cleanup is verified, so a subsequent build can retry. Live or unverified children, uncertain cleanup, and replacement owners remain protected by the existing fail-closed ownership rules.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing cancellable-command owner at the actual preparation CLI entry point instead of exiting inside a compiler step. Thread its cancellation signal through asynchronous preparation and compiler admission, join sibling work, and reject cancellation before publishing success receipts. No managed-lease, UI, permission, or crash-reclamation policy changes.

## Evidence

- 25 focused preparation tests pass, including actual CLI SIGINT/SIGTERM, descendant extinction, empty ownership/child claims, real retry, and cancellation during a gated asynchronous preparation gap.
- The final tests fail against the original implementation for both signals; the gap test also fails against the earlier candidate that discarded the command signal.
- Fresh independent API-only review of the complete three-file repair against the integrated main base completed without P0–P3 findings. Both earlier actionable findings were fixed; all 25 touched cases and their fixtures/helpers were audited. The integrated preparation test run passed all 25 cases without skips.
- Focused typed lint, formatting, erasability, line-cap, timeout-race, mock-export, and diff checks passed. Existing cancellation/lock/ownership and source-update preflight coverage passed.
- Local checking is not uniformly green: canonical shared TypeScript containment blocks the core-boundary and script/root-test typechecks before checking; the dead-export scan is incomplete. A prior targeted typecheck reports the same websocket-header TS2353 on base and candidate.
- Native source-build baseline coverage has 10 passes, 3 pre-existing missing-packaged-surface fixture failures reproduced on the original base, and 3 Windows-only skips. These failures are not represented as passing. Exact-head PR CI supplies the broader checks.

No live installation, running Gateway, configuration, or permission fixtures were modified.

### Exact-head CI

The prior head's run 38820728578 passed its selected changed tests, package-boundary checks, production/test types, lint and security, but failed the mock-export baseline ratchet after upstream removed the Codex protocol-validator mock. This repair integrates main and removes exactly that obsolete allowance (9,525 to 9,524 entries), with the official scanner passing; no new allowance or skipped test was introduced. Fresh exact-head CI run [38823670404](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38823670404) passed on `e95f41a9bfd7e92d497b6e402b802ff19a1d4892`: 33 selected jobs succeeded and 28 unselected jobs were skipped. Production/test typechecks, changed-boundary checks, baseline ratchets, lint, security and `openclaw/ci-gate` passed. Native completed-evidence verification passed, and the ordinary recovery route landed the reviewed head. The earlier failed run was not relabeled green and no inherited-failure exception was used.

prs.title: feat(plugin-sdk): expose bounded status projections from command-status
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #76759. Plugin authors building status integrations had no public types for the gateway `/status` payload: an external plugin (`lossless-claw#516`) guessed the session-row shape from formatted output and navigated fields that do not exist (`sessions.byAgent[].entries[].usage.*` instead of `sessions.byAgent[].recent[]`), so its number extraction returned `null` on every field. Without a public type, this drift recurs for every status-consuming plugin.

## Why This Change Was Made

The previous revision re-exported the host `StatusSummary`/`SessionStatus`/`HeartbeatStatus` types verbatim. ClawSweeper's review correctly rejected that: `StatusSummary` is a mutable host aggregate with transitive gateway, channel, task, audit, plugin, and degraded-secret details, and freezing it into the public SDK would make evolving host-owned nested shapes an implicit compatibility commitment (the old test even had to cast `tasks`/`taskAudit` through `unknown` to compile).

This revision defines **bounded SDK-owned projections** in `openclaw/plugin-sdk/command-status` instead — the smallest shape status-consuming plugins actually need:

- `StatusSessionRow` — one session row: identity (`agentId`, `key`, `sessionId`, `updatedAt`) plus token usage (`inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `totalTokens`, `remainingTokens`, `percentUsed`, `contextTokens`, `model`, `flags`).
- `StatusSessionsProjection` — the session portion of a `/status` payload (`count`, `recent[]`, `byAgent[]`).
- `StatusHeartbeat` — per-agent heartbeat schedule state.

Drift protection runs in the other direction now: `src/plugin-sdk/command-status.types.test.ts` compiles projection functions from the real host types (`SessionStatus → StatusSessionRow`, `StatusSummary["sessions"] → StatusSessionsProjection`, `HeartbeatStatus → StatusHeartbeat`), so renaming a projected field on the host side breaks the build loudly — with zero `unknown` casts. Host-only fields stay free to evolve.

## User Impact

Third-party plugins can `import type { StatusSessionRow, StatusSessionsProjection, StatusHeartbeat } from "openclaw/plugin-sdk/command-status"` and bind the exact session/heartbeat data the `/status` RPC exposes, without copying host internals or acquiring an implicit contract over unrelated host aggregates. Types only — no runtime surface, no startup cost.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/plugin-sdk/command-status.types.test.ts` — green; the test is a compile-time assignability contract from real host types plus behavioral assertions on projected values.
- Plugin SDK surface gate `scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mts --check` — green with the `+3` budget entry ("SDK-owned command-status projection types for plugin status consumers").
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` — green (format, oxlint, tsgo core + test shards, `api-baseline` test 22/22, boundary guards).
- Real consumer proof against the built package (fresh `pnpm build` on this head `e06332c90de`): a standalone strict `nodenext` TypeScript project outside the repo resolving `openclaw/plugin-sdk/command-status` binds all three projections and compiles with **exit 0**:

  ```ts
  import type { StatusHeartbeat, StatusSessionRow, StatusSessionsProjection } from "openclaw/plugin-sdk/command-status";
  export function summarizeStatus(sessions: StatusSessionsProjection): string {
    const rows: StatusSessionRow[] = sessions.recent;
    return `${sessions.count} sessions\n` + rows.map((r) => `${r.key}: ${r.totalTokens ?? "?"} tokens`).join("\n");
  }
  ```

  Runtime probe of the built subpath: `import("dist/plugin-sdk/command-status.js")` exposes exactly `buildCommandsMessage`, `buildCommandsMessagePaginated`, `buildHelpMessage` — the projections are type-only and correctly absent at runtime.
- Branch was rebased onto current `main` (post pnpm-12 bump) and squashed to one commit carrying the projection design.

prs.title: fix(gateway): omit media-store URIs from the workspace file projection
prs.body:
## Update 2026-10-15 — revived

Reopened after the queue reclaim and integrated with current `main`. Head is now `1bbe9b6ac57`, rebased onto `8e850d0631b` to pick up `6a066e90684` ("test: prune removed protocol validator mock baseline"), which cleared the inherited `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` red on this head; that failure came from `main`'s own stale baseline entry, not from this fix. The three-file change is unchanged: the media-exclusion hunks are the same as `2b57a7808`, and the only difference in the touched production file is `main`'s own drift from #172042 (`getSessionWorkspaceFile` gained `includeContent`), confirmed with `git diff`.

---

Fixes #150322.

## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI file panel offered an inbound chat attachment as an openable workspace file, and every click failed. `sessions.files.list` projected the assistant's `read` of `media://inbound/<id>` as a workspace entry with `missing: true`, and `sessions.files.get` answered `INVALID_REQUEST session_file_not_found` for that path. The attachment itself was healthy — the same bytes preview in the chat bubble — so the panel was advertising an action that could never succeed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The touched-file projection in `src/gateway/server-methods/workspace-files.ts:85-108` resolves every tool-argument path against the session root. `expandPath` (`src/agents/sessions/tools/path-utils.ts:33-47`) understands `file://` URLs, so an absolute `file://` path lands outside an out-of-tree root and is already excluded. A media-store identity had no such handling: `path.resolve(root, "media://inbound/x.png")` collapses the double slash and lands at `<root>/media:/inbound/x.png`, which is lexically inside the root. The entry survived the workspace filter, failed `stat`, and was reported as a missing workspace file.

Repair classification: **behavior-completing**. The projection already excludes `file://`, parent-relative, home and out-of-root shapes — `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-files.touched-files.test.ts:446` encodes exactly that contract — and the media-store URI was the one non-workspace shape that slipped through it.

The exclusion belongs at this projection boundary rather than inside the shared `resolveToCwd` (the `read` tool resolves `media://` URIs through it), and rather than granting the workspace file RPCs media-store access: the media store owns those bytes and already serves them through the authenticated `/__openclaw__/assistant-media` route (`src/gateway/control-ui-resource-routes.ts:7`). The predicate reuses the existing non-throwing scheme classifier `classifyMediaReferenceSource(...).isMediaStoreUrl` (`src/media/media-reference.ts:54`) instead of adding another URI guard.

## User Impact

The file panel no longer offers a dead attachment entry. Genuinely missing in-workspace files are still listed as missing, and the chat attachment preview is unchanged. `sessions.files.get` on a media URI still answers the same not-found error, so no wire contract changes: the URI was never an openable workspace path. Write paths are unaffected because `setSessionWorkspaceFile` only accepts a candidate that already exists as a file (`src/gateway/server-methods/workspace-files.ts:555-570`), which the phantom path never does.

## Evidence

### Inherited required-check failure: `checks-ui-e2e (1/2)` (2026-10-11)

The only red required lane on this head is a Control UI end-to-end timeout, and it is **not caused by this diff**:

- Failing case: `ui/src/e2e/chat-panel-layout.e2e.test.ts` › `Control UI chat panel layout` › `preserves live content and saved geometry across main, dock, focus, and narrow layouts` — `TimeoutError: locator.waitFor: Timeout 30000ms exceeded`, waiting for `[data-panel-slot="terminal"] openclaw-terminal-panel .tp-host canvas` (60× resolved to a hidden `<canvas>`).
- This PR's diff touches only `src/gateway/server-methods/workspace-files.ts` and its two tests — no `ui/**` file.
- Independent witness on a different, unrelated PR: #169173 (`refactor(storage): reduce SQLite bookkeeping per turn`, no UI files) fails the **same** case with the **same** locator and the **same** 30 s timeout at 2026-10-11T15:21:00Z (job `114503482331`). Two unrelated diffs failing one canvas-visibility case in the same hour is an inherited lane failure, not a diff-caused regression.
- Per the review's own instruction ("repair only a demonstrated diff-caused failure"), no repair is attempted here.

### ### Rebase note (2026-10-11)

This revision's head is `2b57a7808702016484afcd8dbb031e78fd1621dc`, rebased onto `main` @ `3529142cc84` because the previous base (`9f049a640d5f0c22628747a926b8ebd29377a4a5`) predated a material amount of merged work. The rebase replayed the same commits with no conflicts and the patch is unchanged: `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD` still reports +57/-3 across 3 files. The proof receipts below were captured on the pre-rebase head and were not re-run on this base; CI re-runs on this head.


Handler-level: the real `sessions.files.list` and `sessions.files.get` handlers over the real touched-file projection chain (`collectTouchedFilesFromMessage` → `resolveTouchedFilePath` → `toSessionFileEntry`), with the suite's standard mocks for the session entry and the transcript reader (`sessions-files.test-support.ts`). The mocked reader returns the real reader's message-event shape, and nothing in the projection under test is mocked. The transcript read itself is not part of this defect — a `read` tool call carrying a media URI is the input, and the projection is what mishandles it. Before and after use the same input: an assistant `read` of `media://inbound/image---15547f7e.png` plus ordinary workspace paths. The projection code is byte-identical between the revision the before-state was captured on and `main` (`git diff --stat origin/main -- src/gateway/server-methods/workspace-files.ts src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-files.ts` is empty; current `main` is `79121743a16`).

| Observation | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sessions.files.list` media entry | `{"path":"media://inbound/image---15547f7e.png","name":"image---15547f7e.png","kind":"read","missing":true}` | absent |
| In-workspace missing file | `{"path":"missing.txt","missing":true}` | unchanged |
| In-workspace real file | `{"path":"src/readme.md","missing":false,"workspacePath":"src/readme.md"}` | unchanged |
| `sessions.files.get` on the media URI | `INVALID_REQUEST session_file_not_found` | unchanged (still not a workspace path) |

The existing contract case "omits transcript paths outside the workspace without hiding missing workspace files" (`src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-files.touched-files.test.ts:446`) now carries the media-store URI in its input list.

- Red on unpatched `main`: `expected [ …(2) ] toHaveLength(3)` → received 4, failing at `sessions-files.touched-files.test.ts:473`.
- Green with this change: 10 passed in `sessions-files.touched-files.test.ts`.
- Baseline on this host: the same suite without the change fails only the `git init -b` case at `:107` (local git 2.27 has no `--initial-branch`), so the failure list is identical with and without the change.
- Siblings (`sessions-files.preview`, `sessions-files.repository`, `sessions-files`, `agents-files`): 16 failed | 60 passed both with and without the change. The 16 are `fatal: not a git repository` fixture failures on this host — zero new failures.
- `oxlint` on both changed files: exit 0. `check-tsgo-core-boundary`: exit 0. Import-cycle check: 0 runtime value cycles.
- `tsgo:core` reports one error in the untouched `src/wizard/clack-prompter.ts` (`TS2305 ... CANCEL_SYMBOL`, dependency drift in this checkout); the changed files produce none.

Not covered: this change excludes only the `media://` store scheme. Other unhandled URI schemes can still project phantom entries; they are a separate follow-up, not claimed here.

### Test cost (`sessions-files` suite — this PR's only test touch)

Measured on this host (Node v24.18.0, `vitest run src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-files.test.ts`, isolated worktree, shared dependency install; before = parent `4144ede2113`, after = head `6dbc9a3ad56`):

| Run | Before vitest duration | Before wall | After vitest duration | After wall |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 36.00s | 60.7s | 55.62s (cold transform cache) | 85.3s |
| 2 | 47.11s | 86.8s | 21.01s | 45.5s |
| 3 | — | — | 44.23s | 68.4s |

Both sides report `41 passed (41)` — the change adds one input entry to an existing case and no new test. Run-to-run variance on this host exceeds any before/after delta, and test execution is ≤10% of the suite duration (transform dominates at 56–78%), so the added guard has no measurable suite-cost impact.

CI on head `6dbc9a3ad56` (run `36964744772`): the changed-file shard `checks-node-changed-compact-large-10` finished in **1m37s** total; within it, shard `agentic-gateway-methods-hosted-7` ran this file alone with `41 passed`, vitest duration **4.71s** (tests 5%).

## Evidence: real Gateway + real Control UI, before/after

The handler-level evidence above isolates the defect. This section shows the same correction in the running product: a real Gateway process serving the real Control UI in Chromium, on one seeded session, with identical state and interactions in both runs — the only difference is this PR's guard.

| Frame | Files panel |
| --- | --- |
| Before | `3 read`: `media://inbound/proof-attachment---e29d1ac8-02e…` marked **Missing**, next to `missing-notes.md` and `notes.md` |
| After | `2 read`: the media-store entry is gone; the genuinely missing in-workspace file is still listed |

Before — ![Control UI Files panel listing the dead media-store entry](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/proof/150446/proof/150446/before-files-panel-media-entry.png)

After — ![Control UI Files panel with the media-store entry omitted](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/proof/150446/proof/150446/after-files-panel-media-entry-omitted.png)

Both frames also show the chat attachment preview rendering unchanged, so the authenticated assistant-media route is untouched. The same real Gateway answered `sessions.files.list` over the wire:

```text
before (guard removed)  -> files[0] = {"path":"media://inbound/proof-attachment---e29d1ac8-….png","kind":"read","missing":true}
after  (this PR)        -> the media-store entry is absent; "missing-notes.md" (missing) and "notes.md" (present) remain
```

How the captures were produced:

- Isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`; real Gateway (`openclaw gateway --port 34567 --auth token --allow-unconfigured --bind loopback`) from an isolated `dist` build, serving the real built Control UI; Chromium driven by Playwright.
- State seeded only with production writers: `saveMediaBuffer` (real inbound media bytes in the media store), `upsertSessionEntry`, and `appendSessionTranscriptMessageByIdentity` (a user message carrying the media reference, plus assistant `read` calls for the media URI, an existing workspace file, and a genuinely missing in-workspace path).
- Build disclosure: this host's dependency set predates current `main` by 182 commits and `tsdown` fails on that drift, so both runs build from commit `50c6072e470`, whose `src/gateway/server-methods/workspace-files.ts` and `sessions-files.ts` are byte-identical to `main` (`79121743a16`). AFTER is `bdab8e88449` (that base + this PR's guard); BEFORE is the same base with only the guard removed, everything else unchanged.
- Sanitization: the frames show isolated local paths only — no keys, tokens, IP addresses, or personal data.

## Impact Surface

| File | Change | Risk |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/workspace-files.ts:94-100` | Exclude media-store identities in `resolveTouchedFilePath` | All four call sites are read projections (list filter, relevance map, entry projection, get/set candidate list); `set` additionally requires an existing file, so no write target moves. |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-files.touched-files.test.ts:460-462` | Add the media-store URI to the existing exclusion contract case | None; strengthens an existing assertion rather than adding a parallel test. |

## Ownership

`.github/CODEOWNERS` does not route `src/gateway/server-methods/workspace-files.ts` or `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-files.ts` to a restricted owner: the `src/gateway` secops entries cover `*auth*`, `*secret*`, `secrets*.ts`, `security-path*` and `resolve-configured-secret-input-string*` only.

## Compatibility

No configuration, schema, protocol or retention change. Only the `media://` store identity is excluded, and `sessions.files.get` keeps its existing not-found response for such a path.

## Unrelated CI failures on this head

None of the failing checks touches this diff; `openclaw/ci-gate` only aggregates them. Every failing job names a file this PR does not change:

| Check | Failing point |
| --- | --- |
| `check-lint-core-5` | `extensions/slack/src/monitor/message-handler/dispatch.ts:623` (`typescript(unbound-method)`) |
| `checks-node-compact-large-2` | `src/gateway/server-methods/models-list.freshness.integration.test.ts` |
| `checks-node-compact-large-13` | `src/skills/loading/plugin-skill-read.test.ts` |
| `checks-node-compact-small-15` | `test/scripts/worktree-setup.test.ts` (`Cannot find module '…/scripts/lib/bundled-plugin-source-utils.mts'`) |
| `checks-node-compact-small-24` | `test/scripts/pr-operation-lock.test.ts` |
| `checks-node-compact-small-26` | `test/scripts/pr-main-refresh.test.ts` |
| `checks-node-compact-small-40` | `test/scripts/pr-wrappers.test.ts` |
| `checks-node-compact-small-42` | `test/scripts/pr-worktree-provision.test.ts` |
| `control-ui-performance` | `startup JS gzip: 354.2 KiB exceeds 354.1 KiB` (bundle budget) |

The same checks fail for other open PRs created in the same window with unrelated changes — #150445 (`check-lint`, `checks-node-compact-small-{37,38,42,44,46}`), #150444 and #150434 (`checks-node-compact-large-7`, `checks-node-compact-small-{42,44,46}`, `control-ui-performance`) — so these are main-side failures, not regressions from this change.

prs.title: fix: prevent Codex recovery and completion handoffs from stalling
prs.body:
Related: #172679

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Codex-backed conversations getting stuck during connection retirement and child completion recovery, with repeated plugin metadata reads adding startup latency.

## User Impact

Completed child work can release its connection and reach its parent without blocking later messages. Startup reuses successful plugin manifests within that preparation attempt while continuing to read current thread policy. No configuration, schema, dependency, or timeout changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Health observation must not hold the execution lease that graceful connection retirement waits to drain.
- An idle child with unavailable live history can recover its exact persisted turn; active, mismatched, or missing turn evidence cannot manufacture completion.
- Detached sibling handoffs share the existing requester queue, respect pending recovery custody, and release idle transport before waiting. Cold-custody SQLite scans run in the existing read worker, with requester/claim revalidation after awaits; the process-held incognito owner and transcript read fence are preserved. Foreground completion, lifecycle fencing, and independent requesters retain their behavior.
- Reuse successful `plugin/read` results only within one startup provider; activation invalidates them, subsequent startup rereads them, and failures/in-flight requests remain scoped to their existing deadline.

Native runtime cleanup after slow shutdown is a separate fix; this PR does not change the native runtime pin or claim to eliminate native stale loaded entries.

## Evidence

- Before/after regressions reproduce the health lease deadlock, idle history gap, sibling admission/custody collision, queued transport retention, and duplicate manifest reads. Each fails before its owning repair and passes after.
- Relevant shared-client/health and plugin configuration/deadline suites passed. History coverage: 56 tests; core/SDK completion: 66 tests; native completion/monitor: 59 tests. Final fixture-only corrections also passed their focused reruns.

After preparing the existing locked build artifacts, all core-test type shards and full dead-export analysis also passed; the previously reported 371 local UI/core-test errors and missing libterminal artifact no longer block these checks. The four previously observed extension-test type errors match the preserved baseline and were not reclassified as passing. No dependency versions, manifests, or lockfiles changed. The build emitted a non-fatal UI gzip budget advisory (365.9 KiB vs 364.7 KiB); its baseline attribution is unverified.
- Final candidate changed-file lint, production core types, agents-root test types, and the runtime build passed (53 built-module load checks; 43.9s runtime build). Full lint found six existing max-lines violations in unrelated files. Each file is byte-identical in release base `f155b936`, prior PR head, and this candidate; baseline blob evidence is retained locally. No lint rule or file was waived or changed.
- Prior head `9e0abc33d3b48f3b8593ff809c656d7f806bed91`, rebased onto release head `f155b936161ae58720bdc983eed4ec5743607438`: 88 tests passed across six focused files, including scheduled account/profile isolation and current-policy revocation. The repair patch is identical to the reviewed patch.

prs.title: feat(tts-local-cli): declare and select voices for the local CLI provider
prs.body:
Related: #165598 (staged delivery: this PR covers voice listing/selection for `tts-local-cli`; `talk.catalog` / `tts.providers` payloads stay out of scope, see below).

## What Problem This Solves

`tts-local-cli` users cannot see or switch voices: `/voice list` and `/voice set` (`/talkvoice` on Discord) fail with `speech provider tts-local-cli does not support voice listing`, so changing the voice of a multi-voice local engine (Kokoro, Piper, anything with a `--voice` flag) means hardcoding it into `command` and reloading.

## User Impact

Operators declare the voices their command accepts once, under `tts.providers.tts-local-cli`, and pass the active one with `{{VoiceId}}`:

```jsonc
// tts.providers.tts-local-cli
{
  "command": "/usr/local/bin/my-tts --voice {{VoiceId}}",
  "args": ["{{OutputPath}}"],
  "outputFormat": "wav",
  "voices": ["af_jessica", "af_bella", "am_michael"],
  "voiceId": "af_jessica"
}
```

`/voice list` shows those voices, `/voice set <voice>` switches Talk playback without a config edit, and TTS replies keep using `voiceId`. No migration: both keys are optional, and a command without `{{VoiceId}}` behaves exactly as before (the voice list is simply empty).

## Why This Change Was Made

The command owns its voice catalog, so the provider config declares it; the plugin adds `listVoices`, a `{{VoiceId}}` template key, and a `resolveTalkConfig` hook. Three rules keep the Talk path correct:

- **Talk selection wins.** `resolveTalkConfig` applies the Talk record over TTS defaults, then drops speaker aliases (`speakerVoiceId`, `speakerVoice`, `voice`, `voiceName`) inherited from the TTS record. Core normalization ranks `speakerVoiceId` above `voiceId`, so before this an inherited alias silently replaced the `/voice set` choice with the TTS default. The CLI only reads `voiceId`; core re-derives the aliases from the merged value.
- **One catalog.** `voices` is read from the TTS provider block only. `/voice list` receives that record and Talk synthesis merges over it, so both see the same list; a `voices` list under `talk.providers` is ignored rather than consulted as a second source. A Talk record may carry just the selection (`voiceId`, as written by `/voice set`) or its own executable settings.
- **Independent commands stay independent.** When Talk supplies its own nonblank `command`, it inherits only the TTS voice defaults, not another executable's arguments, working directory, environment, output format, or timeout. Selection-only and blank-command records still inherit the TTS executable settings. This preserves existing self-contained Talk wrappers when both TTS and Talk are configured.

Out of scope: `talk.catalog` / `tts.providers` payloads read the static `provider.voices` field and do not expose this provider's configured voice catalog; consulting `listVoices` would require asynchronous catalog resolution.

## Evidence

### Follow-up verification (current head `61e6708bb89d3cef0fef1f7fba6b6b04d9bc24c0`)

The follow-up fixes execution-setting leakage when TTS and Talk both define different CLI commands. Two new regressions use the production resolver and real subprocess I/O to verify independent argv, stdin, cwd, environment, and WAV/MP3 defaults; the selection-only path remains covered.

- Before the fix, both new regressions failed on `6bf157f0dfa4ac05af570f5685bc1ae7c6becb2b`: the Talk command inherited TTS arguments/cwd/environment, and an MP3 wrapper inherited WAV output settings.
- After the fix, `pnpm test extensions/tts-local-cli/ --maxWorkers=1`: **48/48 tests passed, 2 files, 48.19s wall time** including compilation, in secretless isolation (Node 24.21.0, pnpm 12.9.0). [Focused proof run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_67353cd8ee775fc13c898e7d471c7a13). The published source matches the tested bytes.
- Scoped `tsgo`, type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Fresh scoped review found no actionable P0–P2 issues.
- New-head hosted test CI: [CI run 38576480132](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38576480132) is in progress at publication and is attached to the full head above. Hosted CI duration/result is pending. Older-head green checks are not claimed as proof for this commit.
- Live Gateway proof for the mixed-command scenario and a v2026.10.3 upgrade trace are in the next section. Still no real speech-engine or Telegram run for this follow-up.

### Live Gateway on head `61e6708b`: independent Talk command + upgrade from stable 2026.10.3

Isolated Gateway in WSL (Node 24, `pnpm build` of the PR, own state dir, port 19789, `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1`). Two stub CLIs each write a valid WAV and log argv, cwd, and an env marker. `tts.providers.tts-local-cli` = tts-stub with `--voice {{VoiceId}} --speed 1.0`, its own cwd, `STUB_MARK=tts`, `voices=[af_jessica,af_bella,am_michael]`, `voiceId=af_jessica`. `talk.providers.tts-local-cli` = a separate full command: talk-stub with `--voice {{VoiceId}} --talk-only-flag`, its own cwd, `STUB_MARK=talk`, no `voices`/`voiceId`.

| # | Step | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `health` | `ok: true` |
| 2 | `talk.speak` | talk-stub, `--voice af_jessica --talk-only-flag`, no `--speed`; talk cwd, `STUB_MARK=talk` (voice default inherited from TTS) |
| 3 | `tts.convert` | tts-stub, `--voice af_jessica --speed 1.0`; tts cwd, `STUB_MARK=tts` |
| 4 | `/voice list` (via `chat.send`) | `tts-local-cli voices: 3` |
| 5 | `/voice set af_bella` (operator.admin client) | Talk record gains only `voiceId: "af_bella"`; its command/args/cwd/env/outputFormat unchanged; TTS `voiceId` stays `af_jessica` |
| 6 | `talk.speak`, `tts.convert` | talk-stub `--voice af_bella --talk-only-flag` with talk cwd/env; tts-stub still `af_jessica --speed 1.0` with tts cwd/env |
| 7 | Talk record → `{}` (hot reload), then restored | `{}`: tts-stub with tts args/cwd/env (selection-only inherits TTS). Restored: talk-stub again |

Upgrade: npm `latest` = `openclaw@2026.10.3` (`59cb447`), then this PR on the same state dir. Config shaped like today's users: no `voices`, `voiceId` or `{{VoiceId}}`; TTS `--voice af_jessica`, Talk an independent full command with `--voice am_michael` and its own cwd/env.

| Check | stable 2026.10.3 | PR `61e6708b` (after `doctor --fix`) |
|---|---|---|
| `talk.speak` | talk-stub `--voice am_michael --talk-only-flag`, talk cwd/env | identical |
| `tts.convert` | tts-stub `--voice af_jessica --speed 1.0`, tts cwd/env | identical |
| `/voice list` | `does not support voice listing` | `tts-local-cli voices: 0`, no error |
| config sha256 across the gateway run | unchanged | unchanged |
| `tts`, `talk`, `gateway` subtrees after `doctor --fix` | n/a | content-identical (doctor only added top-level `agents`, `plugins`, `wizard`, `meta`, `skills`) |
| `chat.history` of a session created on stable | 2 messages | same 2 messages still returned |

`doctor --fix` was run before starting the PR gateway (stable-created state needs it on current main; seen in the earlier 2026.10.2 trace as a schema-v24 refusal), so this does not show the PR gateway starting on unmigrated state. The `/voice set` step used a scratch client calling the repo's `callGateway({ method: "chat.send", scopes: ["operator.admin"] })`, since `openclaw gateway call` connects with `operator.write`.

### Live Gateway, real `/voice` command path (head `f431a9ec`)

Isolated Gateway in WSL (Node 24, own state dir and port, `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1`), `tts.providers.tts-local-cli` as above with a stub voice CLI that writes a valid WAV containing `{"voice": <--voice arg>}` and logs each call. `talk.provider = tts-local-cli`, `talk.providers.tts-local-cli = {}`. Commands go through `chat.send` (plugin command dispatch), replies read from `chat.history`.

```text
## /voice list
$ openclaw gateway call chat.send --params {"sessionKey":"agent:main:main","message":"/voice list"}
tts-local-cli voices: 3
- af_jessica   id: af_jessica
- af_bella     id: af_bella
- am_michael   id: am_michael

## talk.speak before set
$ openclaw gateway call talk.speak --params {"text":"hello"}
{ "provider": "tts-local-cli", "outputFormat": "wav", "mimeType": "audio/wav", ... }
stub log: voice=af_jessica

## /voice set af_bella (operator.write client)
⚠️ /voice set requires operator.admin.          <- existing admin gate, unchanged

## /voice set af_bella (operator.admin client)
✅ tts-local-cli Talk voice set to af_bella
config: "talk": { "provider": "tts-local-cli", "providers": { "tts-local-cli": { "voiceId": "af_bella" } } }

## talk.speak after set
stub log: voice=af_jessica
          voice=af_bella                        <- Talk selection beats the TTS voiceId default (P1)

## add talk.providers.tts-local-cli.voices = ["talk-only"], then /voice list
tts-local-cli voices: 3 (af_jessica, af_bella, am_michael)   <- TTS catalog only (P2)
```

`openclaw gateway call` connects with `operator.write`, so the admin `/voice set` used a small scratch client calling the repo's `callGateway({ method: "chat.send", scopes: ["operator.admin"] })` against the same Gateway and token.

### Real engine (earlier head; provider behavior for these inputs unchanged)

Kokoro ONNX behind a `--voice` wrapper, `openclaw infer tts voices` / `infer tts convert --local` from a clean `pnpm build`:

```text
voices: af_jessica, af_bella, am_michael    (main: "does not support voice listing")
voiceId=af_jessica   bytes=139756 sha256=d327338d29a98ce2
voiceId=af_bella     bytes=141804 sha256=946f88c260afc60a
voiceId=am_michael   bytes=147948 sha256=4ee50265dfd9ea62
```

Three voices produce three distinct WAVs, so `{{VoiceId}}` reaches the engine.

### Tests and checks (WSL, Node 24, head `6bf157f0`)

```text
pnpm test extensions/tts-local-cli/speech-provider.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
  -> 39 passed; 37.2s wall
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig extensions/tsconfig.json extensions/tts-local-cli
  -> 0 warnings, 0 errors
oxfmt --check (4 touched files)  -> clean
git diff --check                 -> clean
pnpm build                       -> ok (needed to run the Gateway above)
```

New regressions: a TTS record carrying core-normalized `speakerVoiceId: af_jessica` plus Talk `voiceId: af_bella` resolves without the alias and synthesizes `--voice af_bella`; a Talk-declared `voices` list is ignored and list/synthesis agree; `listVoices` does not read other config scopes.

Base-failure runs (same test file, provider swapped):

| Provider source | Result |
|---|---|
| this PR | 39/39 pass |
| previous head `1688d278` | 36 pass, **exactly the 3 new regressions fail** (Talk selection vs inherited `speakerVoiceId`; Talk-declared `voices` ignored; no cross-scope reads) |
| `main` | 13 fail: all voice tests, plus the full-Talk-record compat test (main has no `resolveTalkConfig`) |

New compat test: a pre-existing Talk record that carries its own `command`/`args`/`outputFormat` (required before Talk merging existed) resolves unchanged when TTS has no CLI block.

### Upgrade trace: stable `2026.10.2` → this PR, same state dir and config

Config shaped like today's users: no `voices`, `voiceId` or `{{VoiceId}}`; `tts.providers.tts-local-cli` passes `--voice af_jessica`, and `talk.providers.tts-local-cli` is a full executable record passing `--voice am_michael`.

| Step | stable 2026.10.2 | this PR (`f431a9ec`, after `doctor --fix`) |
|---|---|---|
| `talk.speak` | stub argv `--voice am_michael` | stub argv `--voice am_michael` (saved Talk record preserved) |
| `tts.convert` | `--voice af_jessica` | `--voice af_jessica` |
| `/voice list` | `does not support voice listing` | `tts-local-cli voices: 0` (empty, no error) |
| config sha256 across the gateway run | unchanged | unchanged (PR gateway does not rewrite config) |

The upgrade itself needed `openclaw doctor --fix`: the current-main checkout refuses the stable-created agent DB (schema v24, exit 78) until doctor migrates it. Doctor rewrote `openclaw.json` formatting and added unrelated keys (`agents`, `plugins.entries`, `wizard`, `meta`), but the `tts` and `talk` subtrees were content-identical before and after. That migration comes from `main`, not this PR. `/voice set` on the upgraded state was not re-run here; the live trace above covers it.

### Not covered

Telegram Test Server userbot proof (`proof: telegram-e2e`): that lane needs Convex-leased QA credentials that are not available to contributors. The live Gateway run above exercises the same plugin command handler and `talk.speak` path the channel uses; a maintainer-run Telegram lane would be appreciated if still required.

Needs an owner call: the new optional `voices` / `voiceId` keys on `tts.providers.tts-local-cli`, and accepting this as a partial step toward #165598.

Note for triage: the branch now touches only `extensions/tts-local-cli/**` and `docs/tools/tts/field-reference.md`; the `plugin: azure-speech` and `extensions: fish-audio` labels look left over from an earlier bad merge that has since been rebuilt.

prs.title: perf(agents): share retained system prompt prefixes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Long-lived sessions retain independent copies of identical system-prompt checkpoint strings, including separate `prefix` and `renderedPrefix` backing stores.

## User Impact

Reduces retained prompt memory without changing prompt bytes, refresh behavior, session metadata, or persisted transcript formats. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The observed retention chain is `SessionManager.fileEntries → checkpoint.data → prefix/renderedPrefix`. Rendering alone cannot fix this: JSON/worker hydration and append normalization copy strings again. One bounded content-addressed pool now owns shared prefix storage at those adoption boundaries and during prompt preparation. Changed content selects a new immutable revision; eviction affects sharing only. The pool is limited to 64 entries and 8 MiB of UTF-16 payload and clears with the runtime lifecycle.

Simplification review retained one string owner and no alternate prompt path. Production delta is +51 lines: the existing persisted two-field contract and session-local metadata must remain intact, so deleting either field would require an out-of-scope stored-format change. Tool-output string detachment remains necessary to avoid retaining large sliced backing stores.

## Evidence

- Focused local checks: codec and prompt-state files, 48 tests passed; file-scoped lint and formatting passed. Test run 26.99 s wall time; the real-manager retention subprocess takes about 9 s. CI timing pending.
- Regression covers 50 retained managers through both append and restored `fromEntries` paths, plus exact prompt bytes and distinct lone-surrogate revisions.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): scoped clean at P0–P2. The helper refused the configured provider mismatch; no operator configuration was changed.
- Linux/Node 26 synthetic measurement, 50 live managers with a 128 KiB prompt, baseline `68166d8e61e9` versus candidate `40a0fcf94bb5`:

  | Path | Baseline incremental heap | Candidate incremental heap |
  | --- | ---: | ---: |
  | Append checkpoints | 12.75 MiB | 0.26 MiB |
  | Restore checkpoints | 12.70 MiB | 0.20 MiB |

  Figures exclude the warmed shared pool (about 0.125 MiB for this fixture). A synthetic heap snapshot found 103/101 large matching strings before versus 2 after (the fixture and shared copy). The unchanged regression on baseline fails its 2 MiB bound; candidate passes. Prompt fields remain byte-identical.
- CPU tradeoff: single-run creation times were 11.3 ms append / 4.8 ms restore before, versus 16.5–23.5 ms append / 11.5–17.2 ms restore after for 50 managers. This is a retained-memory improvement, not a latency claim; content hashing costs roughly 0.1–0.25 ms per admission in this fixture.
- Measurements used an isolated Linux sandbox with synthetic data, dedicated HOME/state/temp paths, CPU affinity and memory limits. No production Gateway or stored state was modified. No Testbox/Crabbox leases or local broad suites were used; PR CI owns broad validation.

CI exception: [run 38822838382](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38822838382), exact head `40a0fcf94bb5d68e402d6fb9782806c5d8745fb4`. All source-dependent jobs passed. The sole failed job, [checks-node-changed-compact-small-26](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38822838382/job/116723734812), timed out three times downloading the unchanged pinned `runs-on/action` archive from `codeload.github.com` during runner setup. Its 20-line log ends before repository checkout or test execution; no failing test case exists to reproduce. This is an unrelated infrastructure failure, not a passing shard. No workflow/action pins changed, and CI was not rerun. The missing shard remains a validation gap. Export-name collision guard and the two required eager-import/PR-wrapper closure test files passed locally.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Chat-pane tests still import Lit after their pane subjects moved to Solid. Full CI also exposed a Playwright held-module teardown race: removing routes could auto-continue a slow request before its callback called `fulfill`.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. The same pane behavior remains covered as the Control UI migration continues.

## Why This Change Was Made

Convert 13 pane test files and two shared fixtures to the existing Solid test renderer and controller-host contract. Preserve all 707 assertion sites and add one check that the delayed browser card is absent before its commit is released. The browser fixture now uses a native host and a commit-gated Solid render instead of a synthetic LitElement.

The existing `renderPaneLegacyContent` helper remains necessary because the pane adapter returns opaque legacy content containing Solid directives. This changes the test harness, with no production, startup, dependency, selector, or styling changes. The shared E2E helper now releases all held gates and joins active callbacks before removing interception; late requests fall through. The existing regression verifies ordering and preserves original body failures.

## Evidence

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Codemod dry run | All 15 source files examined; manual lifecycle conversions resolved |
| Focused tests | 13 files, 177 distinct cases proved with one worker; see fixture correction below |
| UI typecheck | `pnpm tsgo:ui` passed |
| Scope / formatting | Changed-file scope, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed |
| Scoped lint | Final two-file repair passed scoped lint and formatting. The initial migration lint passed in 44.87s after an initial declaration-generation timeout was fully drained |
| Production Knip | Final `pnpm deadcode:knip` reports three unused files: `src/shared/safe-record.ts`, `ui/src/components/dropdown-menu-controller.ts`, and `ui/src/components/web-awesome-popover.ts`. All three match independently installed exact base `0d738854` with byte-identical output. No new ignores. |
| Independent review | Fresh isolated review of the complete 17-file candidate through P2: no actionable findings |
| Broad proof | `ci:full` requested. Original run 38810782716 passed all 438 tests in shard 6 but failed on an unhandled `route.fulfill: Route is already handled!`; latest scheduled main 38810511907 passed that shard, so this was investigated and repaired, not claimed inherited. That replacement run 38817117344 passed, including all UI/Gateway shards. Current-head full CI [38819719795](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38819719795) also passed at `953d154e743bb9532f35e1e67182bc0fc4dd3e91` after the ordinary merge of newer main diagnostics. |
| Held-route regression | Passed in the single owning-helper file run; native Playwright reproduction fails before the fix and completes without errors after it. The helper file had 12 passes and 8 local failures: missing dependency caused worker startup failure, reproduced on unchanged base, followed by 7 cleanup-guard failures. |
| Startup / screenshots | Not rebuilt or captured: test-only change with no runtime or visual delta |

The native Layout menu port subsequently changed two overlapping tests on main. Ordinary merge resolution preserves its button interactions, removes only their direct Lit renderer imports, and passes all 84 cases across the three affected suites. UI types, scoped lint, and a fresh full-candidate review also pass after that merge.

Main subsequently added held-response failure diagnostics. The ordinary merge preserves those diagnostics alongside the same callback-joining fix. Its exact cleanup regression, UI typecheck, scoped lint, format check, and fresh P2 review pass.

The panel-toggle file initially passed 12 of 13 cases. Its replacement browser fixture omitted production's `data-sidebar-panel-host` marker, so intent delivery could not find the recipient. Restoring that marker made the exact failed case pass; no expectation was relaxed and the file was not repeatedly run.

Scope: 17 files, two TSX renames; 9,167 → 9,211 LOC (+44, +0.48%), +201/−157. The 15-file migration itself is 7,491 → 7,511 LOC and retains 707 assertions plus one new assertion; the cleanup fix adds explicit callback ownership and ordering checks. Combined lexical assertion sites: 783 → 788.

Main was rescanned at `0d73885432fb3082fcef007a839d3216bd84892f` after the previous batch landed: 65 direct-Lit chat test/support paths, comprising these 15 newly eligible pane paths and 50 deferred because their subjects or supplied content contracts still use Lit. prs.title: perf(agents): release completed parents retained by fork replay
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Prepared native-session fork snapshots kept the disposed parent AgentSession and SessionManager alive alongside their intentionally retained replay prefix. Large conversations therefore retained an extra copy of their history until snapshot eviction or cleanup.

## User Impact

Completed parents can now be garbage-collected while later read-only forks still replay the prepared request. No configuration, schema, expiry, byte-budget, or run-registration policy changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The SDK transport was created inside `createAgentSession`, captured its full options, and shared the session factory's closure scope. A private transport factory now captures only the model registry, settings manager, and thinking flag. Per-request credential resolution, dynamic retry/attribution settings, and runtime binding remain intact.

The old inline construction is removed. Production delta: +12 lines (39 added / 27 removed); the extra private function/type boundary is necessary to isolate the retained closure rather than clear useful replay data. Test delta: +74 lines. The simplification pass found no second policy or compatibility path to retain.

## Evidence

Isolated Linux sandbox, synthetic data, exact base `2aca37525ff0804790c29d9ab6fea1bb9e5f700e`, real SDK session construction and native stream selection, fixture provider, forced GC. Six completed sessions with 8 MiB histories:

| Retained after completion, relative to explicit snapshot cleanup | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Heap + replay buffers, six runs | 96.18 MiB | 48.02 MiB |
| Per completed oversized run | 16.03 MiB | 8.00 MiB |
| Live disposed AgentSession / SessionManager objects | 12 | 0 |
| Successful later fork | yes | yes |

The fix removes approximately 8.03 MiB per run (50% of measured retention). The remaining 8 MiB per run is the intended prepared prefix. A separate twelve-run probe with 16.23 MiB prefixes stayed at 16.23 MiB for one session and plateaued at 48.69 MiB across distinct sessions under the existing 64 MiB budget; replacement, expiry, and cleanup released old data.

Registration investigation: the registration owner is a WeakMap. Twelve runs each through completion, abort, explicit finalizing-owner release, and lifecycle rotation left zero live handles, registrations, or 8 MiB SessionManagers. No registration-owner change was needed.

- New forced-GC regression fails on the original SDK implementation (2 retained objects, expected 0) and passes with this change, including a later fork after parent collection.
- `sdk.test.ts`: 23 passed; latest Vitest 7.01 s / wrapper 32.97 s (test execution about 1.3 s).
- `session-fork.test.ts`: 28 passed.
- `runs.test.ts` and `runs.generation.test.ts`: 33 passed.
- SDK sibling files `sdk.auth-migration.test.ts`, `sdk.metadata-admission.test.ts`, and `sdk.tool-outcomes.test.ts`: 30 passed (single worker, 51.11 s wrapper).
- Changed-file core lint, formatting, and `git diff --check`: passed. An initial root-config lint invocation triggered declaration preparation and was stopped; the successful check used the core config with preparation disabled.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): scoped-clean, no actionable P0/P1/P2 findings. The helper rejected a provider mismatch; operator configuration was unchanged.
- Initial PR CI caught a type mismatch in the new regression (`AgentMessage[]` versus provider `Message[]`). The test now uses the canonical `convertToLlm` boundary; focused tests/lint and independent review passed again. Production code and measurements are unchanged.
- No Testbox/Crabbox lease. Broad checks delegated to PR CI.

Limits: this measures the real session/fork ownership boundary with a synthetic provider, not a live provider call or the complete production Gateway heap. It does not attribute all idle-process memory to this defect.


## Final CI and inherited-failure attribution

Corrected head `5c04b86650d992e09e649022216552da1fcc268d`, [CI run 38821588178](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38821588178), attempt 1: all selected test lanes, build, production/test types, lint, docs, guards, and `security-fast` passed. The only root failure is `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets`; `openclaw/ci-gate` fails downstream.

The failure table labels it new because the older scheduled main job passed. Independent reproduction on the actual unchanged CI main parent proves it inherited:

- Main parent `68166d8e61e94ce46aeeed9fe439e82e7da7114f`: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-mock-exports.mts --base 68166d8e61e94ce46aeeed9fe439e82e7da7114f` exits 1.
- Exact CI merge `e9a7a10816e4d7b27d44af31f13aca184853db3f` (ordered parents: that main parent, corrected PR head): same command exits 1 with the identical entry below.
- Both isolated Linux runs use the same existing sandbox with CPU/memory/priority limits; no production state, broad test suite, or CI rerun.
- The failing test, baseline, ratchet implementation and its scanner/resolver inputs have identical Git objects between the main parent and tested merge. The merge adds only this PR's three files.

```text
Shrink config/test-mock-exports-baseline.txt (run with --prune):
  ["extensions/codex/src/app-server/turn-router.mcp-app.test.ts","./protocol-validators.js","179c97d5d976dacea55cb1994ace0d7af200608a224466b9e57daa260410890f",1]
```

Landing under the authorized inherited-failure exception; the unrelated baseline is not changed in this PR.

Native `scripts/pr merge-run` could not start because installed `tsx` 4.23.12 differs from the trusted tooling requirement 4.23.15. Shared dependencies were left untouched; the operator-authorized exact-head GitHub API fallback is used for this inherited-only landing.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated Slack error notices on the October branch when passive queued follow-up replies bypass the immediate reply deduplication path.
