It preserves October's existing execution path and shares the same Slack policy for immediate and queued replies. Record a notice only after its matching error is confirmed delivered; suppress a collected batch only when every participating source policy agrees.

## Evidence

prs.title: fix(cli): local terminal chat sends model requests without the configured proxy
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/173529 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: with `proxy.proxyUrl` configured, `openclaw chat`, `openclaw terminal`, `openclaw tui --local`, and bare `openclaw` without a reachable Gateway send their in-process model requests directly instead of through the proxy, and bare `openclaw` opens onboarding without the managed proxy, while `openclaw agent --local` uses it. ## User Impact User impact: the local terminal chat, and onboarding opened by bare `openclaw`, now route egress through the configured proxy, the same as `openclaw agent --local` and `openclaw onboard`. These commands now also follow the proxy's destination policy and `proxy.loopbackMode`, as `openclaw agent --local` does. A Gateway-connected `openclaw tui` still connects to its Gateway directly. ## Why This Change Was Made The CLI starts the configured proxy from each command's startup policy. `chat`, `terminal`, and `tui` were set to bypass it, although `chat` and `terminal` always run the embedded agent in the CLI process and `tui --local` does too. They now follow the `agent` rule: `chat` and `terminal` always route, `tui` routes only with `--local`. Bare `openclaw` has no command, so no startup policy applies. It picks onboarding, the local TUI, or a Gateway-bound TUI only after probing for a Gateway. The proxy now starts at that point, right before onboarding or the local TUI opens, and the existing CLI cleanup stops it. Gateway-bound targets are unchanged. prs.title: fix: wake sessions when background processes are lost on restart
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes idle sessions waiting forever when a Gateway restart loses their background exec process and the automatic completion turn that would have woken them.

## User Impact

Eligible owning sessions wake once with an explicit unknown-outcome notice and instructions to inspect side effects or saved state before retrying. Commands are never replayed. Processes still end with the Gateway; physical process survival belongs to a separate process host.

## Why This Change Was Made

The process registry and its captured completion target are memory-only (`src/agents/bash-process-registry.ts:126`, `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-notify.ts:351`). Persist a compact pending-notification fact in the existing private session-row JSON when exec becomes backgrounded, then reuse the same exec completion owner after admitted stores are ready. No new table, scheduler, process host, foreground recovery path, or output persistence.

The registry's unique process-instance ID keys both the fact and source-turn receipt; the display process slug is reusable. Normal adoption and explicit cancellation/removal clear the fact. Recovery retains the original route and tool restrictions, revalidates current session authority, and respects reset/archive, incognito, and notification opt-out. Subagents and ended cron runs retain their existing owners and receive no new wake. An older binary ignores the additive field; a subsequent upgrade can reconcile it. A crash before durable background registration remains outside this guarantee; the tool only returns its background handle after that write.

Shared physical stores retain their database path for storage, while recovery resolves the logical agent from each session key for target capture and all notification policy checks. Cleanup also supplies that logical identity to the canonical session mutation owner. A shared-store regression reproduces the missing secondary-agent handoff, then proves independent main/secondary opt-out, effect-boundary revocation, and cleanup. The other agent-ID uses introduced by this PR were audited; worker database IDs remain physical storage identities.

Startup uses the same candidate-discovery shape as #172894: the existing session reader worker filters pending exec facts in SQLite, selects at most 64 matching keys, then reads only their listing projections. Unrelated entry payloads and saved prompt snapshots stay in SQLite. This adds no schema or index; it uses the existing session-key ordering and JSON field. A real worker regression crosses the page boundary with 70 pending owners plus 70 unrelated sessions and an empty record.

Startup discovery can finish while an agent database is still under background admission. The earlier implementation silently omitted that store and never revisited it, leaving its notifications saved but undelivered. Recovery now captures pending agent IDs before discovery, joins the existing admission owner, and rescans admitted agents. It follows the main-session recovery pattern without a polling timer, new scheduler, or new storage. Failed admission stays excluded. A deterministic owner regression proves zero handoffs before admission and exactly one afterward.

Related overlap reviewed: #165957 changes session admission ownership but does not replace this exec notification owner. This change adds no competing turn controller. Main commit `7ee9c27cd427b455ae39e3a81644bb406b7a0755` (#173342) is integrated: every process shutdown now retains unfinished-turn custody. That complements this PR's background-exec notification obligation and lets an adopted recovery turn survive another raw shutdown.

## Evidence

Team's 72-hour journal contains 41 drain episodes, 24 with a positive background-exec count and 11 still reporting background work at the deadline. These are episode/snapshot counts, not a count of distinct lost commands. Sanitized evidence from the October 15 shutdown:

```text
L976005 06:57:03.684  drain begins; backgroundExecSessions=1
L976200 06:57:23.683  drain timeout; backgroundExecSessions=4
L976381/L976384      exec finalization: child cleanup unconfirmed
L976432 06:58:28.408  shutdown deadline; last backgroundExecSessions=4
L976437 06:58:30      systemd main process exited, status=9/KILL
```

This establishes background work overlapping shutdown; source inspection and the tests establish the missing wake.

Validation:

- Focused exec registry/runtime/cleanup/follow-up and session-event handoff suites: 108 tests passed. After the review-driven policy serialization fix, the owner suite passed all 17 tests.
- Core typecheck, focused agent test types, root test types, scoped type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check`: passed. Prompt snapshot generation passed with no tracked snapshot changes.
- The production E2E runtime build passed, including plugin assets, CLI import guard, and native-load checks.
- Current follow-up: the candidate reader and notification owner suites passed all 20 tests. Core typecheck, session test types, agent tool test types, scoped type-aware lint, formatting and diff checks passed.
- The final admission-race fix passed the full restart E2E file locally, then four additional focused SIGKILL runs. The prior intermittent SIGKILL timeout is now localized: discovery could finish before database admission and never rescan. The deterministic regression failed before the fix and passed afterward. No timeouts or behavior assertions changed.

| Restart mode | Runs passed | Case durations | Wake + unknown outcome, cancellation, revoked authority, no replay, later restart without duplicate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Managed | 1/1 | 36.556s | Pass |
| Raw SIGTERM | 1/1 | 91.243s | Pass |
| SIGKILL, including crash during recovery | 5/5 | 48.313s, 40.237s, 35.186s, 36.355s, 32.069s | Pass |

The fresh production build passed in 6m32s; repetitions reused those artifacts. The SIGKILL case makes a second provider call to resume the already-adopted turn after crashing during recovery; each request contains one lost-process notice, and the later managed restart adds no call. The owning session's turn runs without another user message.

- Committed-branch Codex autoreview is scoped-clean through P2 on final head `3f3e6db784edad5ac613a4e44dc28473c6982c1b`. Both follow-up repairs also passed their scoped reviews.
- Initial PR CI exposed regressions in process-output eviction, completion context keys, request Stop, and egress lifetime. The repair preserves queued live completion receipts during output eviction and retains their existing queue context keys; the durable process-instance source identity remains independent. The owner/process-poll suites (32 tests), routing/acknowledgment/Stop suites (18 tests), and egress-lifetime suite (2 tests) all passed locally with the original behavior assertions unchanged. No full-suite rerun or rerun-for-green was used.

Previous shared-store head `c0d99eeebe0144072c1a2e7e4a3cd00865befa4a` passed exact-head CI: [run 38816217205](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38816217205). Final admission-race head `3f3e6db784edad5ac613a4e44dc28473c6982c1b` passed exact-head CI: [run 38819842093](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38819842093). This PR remains unmerged.

Size against integrated main `26da73bf2aa83c89f2f806bb84ff9134b033549c`: production **+446 / -37** (net +409), tests **+1021 / -1**, docs **+39 / -11**. The initial follow-up CI run rejected the inline SQLite JSON extraction under the database-dialect ratchet. The query now uses the existing engine-owned `jsonExtractText` helper; the guard, candidate-reader tests, core typecheck, lint and formatting pass. No guard or baseline changed, and the repair has a scoped-clean P2 review.

The shared-store repair passed all 20 notification-owner tests; the admission repair expands this to 21 passing tests (39.52s Vitest wall time, approximately 4.5s test execution including real SQLite workers). Core and focused agent-tool test typechecks, type-aware lint, formatting, and diff checks passed. Codex autoreview is scoped-clean through P2 for both repairs. The shared-store repair is **+7 / -5 production lines**, **+90 / -9 test lines**; the admission repair is **+35 / -0 production lines**, **+47 / -0 test lines**. Neither introduces a schema or index change.

The author simplification pass retained one notification owner, one private field, and the existing admission/receipt contracts; the follow-up removes all-session materialization in favor of bounded candidate pages.

<details>
<summary>Focused proof commands</summary>

```sh
pnpm test src/agents/bash-tools.exec-notify.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-runtime.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-runtime.cleanup.test.ts src/agents/bash-process-registry.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-background-followup.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-handoff.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm test src/config/sessions/session-entry-recovery.worker.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-notify.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm check:database-dialect-ratchet --base 26da73bf2aa83c89f2f806bb84ff9134b033549c
pnpm tsgo:core
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-sessions.json --incremental
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-tools.json --incremental
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.other.json --incremental
pnpm prompt:snapshots:gen
pnpm test:e2e:gateway test/gateway-background-process-restart.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
OPENCLAW_E2E_USE_PREBUILT_DIST=1 pnpm test:e2e:gateway test/gateway-background-process-restart.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t SIGKILL
```

</details>

prs.title: fix(slack): deduplicate failures from queued follow-up replies
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated Slack error notices when passive messages queue behind a failing run and their follow-up replies are routed directly to the originating conversation.

## User Impact

Repeated passive failures share the existing per-thread/channel deduplication policy. Explicit requests still receive errors, and startup timeouts remain enabled.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry the originating Slack message's failure policy through queued delivery, including every source in a collected batch. Record a notice only after its matching error is confirmed delivered, and reset outage state after a healthy completed turn rather than cancellation or pending transport. Immediate and queued replies use the same policy and cache.

## Evidence

- The new origin-delivery boundary regression fails on the unpatched implementation: the outbound adapter is called once when the reply should be suppressed. It passes with the fix.
- 100 focused tests passed across delivery, runner, Slack monitor, and failure-policy coverage. Coverage includes explicit/passive batches, confirmed versus failed/held/ambiguous delivery, healthy reset, cancellation, and thread/team isolation.
- Focused production and test typechecks, native targeted lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed.
- Independent autoreview completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- `pnpm test:contracts:channels` passed all four groups: 49 files, 225 tests.
- Full PR CI is skipped while this PR remains a draft.
- Live Slack delivery has not been exercised by this change.

prs.title: fix(gateway): defer superseded startup model runtime publication
prs.body:
Fixes #173357.

## What Problem This Solves

During Gateway startup, a newer model-runtime publication that superseded the in-progress `sidecars.model-runtime` build propagated `PreparedModelRuntimePublicationSupersededError` out of the publication promise. The sidecar phase treated it as fatal ("gateway sidecars failed to start"), the process exited with `startup_failed`, and repeated boots tripped the crash-loop breaker, suppressing channels for the breaker window.

This is a different caller than the admission recovery in #172632: that fix teaches per-agent startup admission to retry on supersession, but the startup publication path itself still converted supersession into a process exit.

## Why This Change Was Made

The hot-reload path already treats supersession as cancellation and defers to the newer publication, in two parts: `refreshModelRuntimeAfterHotReload` passes `joinSupersedingPublication: true`, and `server-reload-hot.ts` classifies the residual error as a reload cancellation. The startup publication now does the first part: the Gateway startup publication joins the superseding publication instead of failing, so the newer generation owns startup and the Gateway stays up. Genuine successor failures still propagate unchanged.

Joining previously bypassed the bounded degraded startup wait (a joined refresh could wait on an unbounded successor chain). `PreparedModelRuntimePublicationQueue.complete` now keeps `PreparedModelRuntimeStartup.wait` around a joined publication, so a slow successor chain still degrades at the build timeout and acquisition continues in the background, exactly like an unjoined startup publication.

## Evidence

- Deterministic regression in `src/gateway/server-startup-model-runtime.supersession.test.ts`: holds the static-catalog preparation of a `publishConfiguredModelRuntimeSnapshots` startup build, starts a newer publication mid-build, and asserts the startup publication resolves (does not reject with supersession) and the newer config's snapshot is published. Before the fix it rejects with the production stack from the issue (`assertPreparedModelRuntimeInputCurrent` → `assertBuildCurrent` → `buildSnapshotBatch`); after the fix it passes.
- `src/gateway/server-startup.test.ts` updated for the new option threading; all 8 tests in the file pass.
- `prepared-model-runtime.owner-supersession.test.ts` (9 tests incl. join boundaries: lost claim, invalidation, close) passes unchanged.
- `prepared-model-runtime.cancelled-admission`, `published-replacement`, `reload-auth`, `registry-borrow`, `plugin-drain` suites pass.
- `oxfmt --check` clean; `run-tsgo` core/ui/extensions graphs, `run-tsgo-core-test-shards`, `test:root`, and both test tsconfig graphs pass; timeout-race ratchet passes; no new type assertions. The assertion-safety ratchet flags three files untouched by this PR that fail identically on main.
- Windows-local noise, verified identical on clean main via targeted control runs: `/tmp`-path assertions and 120s/180s fleet-timeout tests (`batch`, `startup-static`, `config-stamp`, `catalog-owner`, `owner-selection`, `hot-reload-dispatch`, `inbound-registry`). PR CI on Linux is authoritative for these.

prs.title: perf(gateway): avoid profile writer queues on reconnect
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The cold-load campaign recorded 14 visible states during a signed-in reload of a dashboard deep link. Such reloads can queue behind unrelated state writes because acquiring an existing user profile and listing the roster both reserve the shared SQLite writer.

## User Impact

Existing email-authenticated users reconnect faster once the Gateway's committed profile catalog is ready. The measured 150-client reconnect storm removes two profile writer admissions per client and reduces median attach p90 by 39%.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing write-through profile catalog for email acquisition and roster snapshots. Remove the runtime `userProfiles.list` writer operation and native snapshot reader; the native snapshot survives only in test support. Preserve roster ordering, creation timestamps, email bindings, primary GitHub identity, and selected numeric GitHub associations. New identities and verified GitHub/OIDC conflict checks still use canonical writes. Role authority, revocation, acquisition-current checks, and physical-store invalidation remain with their existing owners.

Runtime delta: **+29 lines** (124 added, 95 removed across 10 files), using `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD -- ':!*.test.ts' ':!*test-support*' ':!docs/*'`. Preserving the existing roster response requires creation time and the public GitHub projection in the catalog. No schema, durable shape, config, or protocol changes.

## Evidence

Measurement head: `6f41a9dc49188b396b6ecd4bd7ff4ee7eca67415`. Quiet AWS **c7a.4xlarge**, 16 vCPU, Node 24.19.0, lease `cbx_30d045fc637c`. Seven interleaved baseline/candidate pairs on the same instance, alternating pair order. Each run boots a real Gateway with 1,000 synthetic profiles, 1,000 devices, and 5,000 sessions, waits for startup, and performs three warmup handshakes before the 150-client simultaneous cohort. Clients use existing trusted-proxy email profiles, signed WebSocket handshakes, and one startup `users.list` each. The original runtime is restored between variants while regression tests stay fixed.

Values are median **[Q1, Q3]** across the seven cohort measurements; latency and queue wait are milliseconds.

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Profile writer admissions/client | 2 [2, 2] | 0 [0, 0] |
| Attach p50 | 951.99 [946.09, 959.01] | 661.87 [635.02, 674.56] |
| Attach p90 | 1,381.38 [1,377.05, 1,383.52] | 848.56 [825.14, 871.54] |
| Attach max | 1,493.46 [1,475.36, 1,498.55] | 905.23 [874.83, 935.60] |
| Profile ensure p50 | 9.840 [9.780, 10.106] | 0.041 [0.041, 0.046] |
| Profile ensure p90 | 15.934 [15.780, 16.644] | 0.050 [0.049, 0.058] |
| Aggregate profile queue wait/storm | 2,566.62 [2,563.13, 2,574.60] | 0 [0, 0] |

All **2,100 measured burst connects and roster requests** succeeded. Granted scopes and stored device approvals passed the same assertions in every run. The exact census is 150 `userProfiles.ensureEmail` plus 150 `userProfiles.list` admissions per baseline storm; both are absent from every candidate storm. Device metadata writer operations remain 150 per storm. More asynchronous transcript backfill completes during candidate storms, so total writer counts are not treated as a conserved workload. Aggregate writer queue wait is 3,518.03 → 5.62 ms; the profile-class figure above isolates the removed work.

Roster DTO projection now uses main-thread catalog facts. Median event-loop p90 is 12.74 → 13.08 ms and median maximum delay 95.55 → 75.56 ms in this fixture. The real Gateway fixture measures attachment and roster behavior; the Control UI Team-scale browser bench mocks the Gateway and cannot exercise this storage path. No browser cold-paint timing claim or visual change is included.

AWS proof on the measurement head: **119 focused tests / 7 files**, exact-file lint, formatting, import cycles, and production/state/Gateway-method type graphs passed. The strengthened owner regression passes through the public acquisition/list APIs, observes both writer dispatch entry points, checks committed role/identity/merge updates, and rejects revoked caller authority. Restoring the old runtime makes it fail on the expected writer-admission assertion. `pnpm test src/state/user-profile-writes.owner.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 5 tests, **40.24 s wall time** on AWS. The other changed focused test files took 35.90–47.21 s each. The preceding candidate passed 321 profile/auth/handshake tests across 21 files on `cbx_fc4e47c18370`, including configured-role, OIDC conflict, identity-scope, and trusted-proxy cases. Autoreview is clean through P2, including authority-owner context and the final snapshot simplification.

Final reviewed head: `5c46eedb95cf7d6993b47172761295eeca0c911b`. All ten runtime files in this change are byte-for-byte identical to the measurement head. On AWS `cbx_37ccd47a50c2`, the owner regression passed again (5 tests, 41.22 s wall), and the effective-role/selected-GitHub policy test passed on Node (2 tests, 48.20 s wall) and pinned Bun (2 tests, 43.91 s wall). Exact-file lint and formatting passed. The policy test mocks the current catalog owner; its role assertions are unchanged. Enumeration (3 tests, 48.22 s wall) and the line-cap ratchet also passed on the measurement lease.

Exact-head CI [38818986548](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38818986548) has passed the role-list and chat shards. Its only test failure is [the shutdown shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38818986548/job/116711261172): the stop and graceful cases in `server.agent-execution-shutdown.test.ts` expect no `markRestartAbortedMainSessions` call and observe one. Both failures reproduce exactly in a clean current-main checkout at [`6cace69448ae`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6cace69448ae7c6637c52becbc13210bcdde0d96) on AWS `cbx_7507e8eedd86` (2 failed / 1 passed, 79.93 s wall). All 77 tests in the separate chat-retry file pass on that main checkout; that shard also passes on the final PR head. PostgreSQL conformance and all other executed proof checks passed. CI is red only for these two inherited shutdown assertions and their aggregate gate. No CI reruns were requested. All lane leases are released.

<details>
<summary>Writer attribution and remaining scope</summary>

The campaign observed 978–1,046 `userProfiles` writer operations and 349–530 seconds of aggregate queue wait in five-minute restart windows. This metric counts dispatched operations, including reads, rather than SQL mutations; it cannot establish seven fixed operations per handshake.

| Path | Attribution / treatment |
| --- | --- |
| Email acquisition | Existing native ensure already avoids SQL mutation, but formerly reserved the writer; reuse current resident binding and canonical row. Authenticated HTTP requests share this path and can multiply reconnect-window admissions. |
| Tailscale email | Reuse the same resident row when display-name adoption is unnecessary. Provider aliases and actual adoption retain canonical writes. |
| Local owner | Existing resident shortcut retained. |
| GitHub/OIDC | Verified provider resolution, exact binding/conflict checks, and conditional metadata refresh retain existing canonical owners. No external verified-identity cache is introduced. |
| Roster | Remove observational writer-list operation and project committed catalog facts. The separate bounded human-mention directory is outside this reconnect path. |
| Authority / avatars / bookkeeping | Authority and revision fences remain unchanged. Avatar adoption is already detached. There is no profile last-seen/presence write in the handshake to coalesce. Device bookkeeping belongs to its separate owner. |
| `execute` / usage rollups | Neither appears in the measured storm census. `execute` is a coarse diagnostics fallback; `usageCache.writeRollup` comes from usage refresh rather than a direct handshake call. Usage coalescing belongs to its separate refresh lane. |

</details>

Release-note context: faster reconnects and roster loading for existing email-authenticated users without changing role or identity authorization.

prs.title: fix(memory): avoid repeated scans of shared memory folders
prs.body:
Related: #173445

## What Problem This Solves

Idle Gateways with several agents watching the same memory folders repeatedly reconcile identical trees, multiplying guarded filesystem work and delaying the event loop.

## User Impact

Agents in the same process share filesystem subscriptions for common admitted roots while keeping their own path patterns, multimodal exclusions, debounce, and indexing lifecycle. Native notifications remain prompt; the missed-event recovery scan runs every five minutes. Polling retains its 30-second default and explicit `CHOKIDAR_INTERVAL` overrides. A missed native event can consequently take up to five minutes to recover. No configuration or migration is required.

This addresses duplicate watcher subscriptions and their recovery frequency. The filesystem library's per-entry scan cost and separate per-agent indexes remain; this does not claim a measured CPU/stall reduction on the reporter's host.

## Why This Change Was Made

The memory watcher owner pools subscriptions by admitted root identity and observation mode, unions scopes and live exclusion policies, and fans invalidations through each agent's existing selection and settling logic. The last member closes and joins the underlying subscription. Scope updates are serialized and coalesced; unions above fs-safe's 128-scope bound use additional subscriptions. A failed shared observation retries with independent subscriptions, preventing a bad added scope from repeatedly disabling healthy peers. Detailed structural events refresh only interested agents, while ancestor and pathless hints preserve rediscovery.

Original fix by @ericcaiwx-star; maintainer cleanup adds subscription sharing and focused lifecycle regressions, removes the unrelated environment-budget edit and unnecessary SDK export, and keeps the recovery policy in the memory owner.

Deferred-work facts: shared membership is read again immediately before scope updates, exclusions, and delivery; each callback enters its current member's background context. Removed members cannot receive callbacks. Exact device/inode identity is captured once through the pinned Root at admission and separates replacement directories; member-specific reads still use that member's Root. Failed shared roots are marked isolated before callbacks retire memberships; isolation lasts for that member's pinned-root lifetime, and later watch-limit failures keep the existing capacity degradation. Settings, path selections, mode, and limits belong to the watcher lifetime; structural changes refresh selections, and the registry distinguishes observation-mode/polling overrides. Final release removes the record before joined close.

## Evidence

- Source and history confirm both defects on current main: per-watcher subscriptions and omitted native `intervalMs`. The pinned fs-safe 0.26.5 watch contract confirms independent native/polling cadence, bounded scopes, initial invalidation, and joined close.
- PR CI is the test gate per maintainer policy. It covers the memory watcher lifecycle/filter/filesystem tests and selected build, typecheck, lint, and repository checks for this head.
- New regressions: `shares roots across agents, fans out selected events, and joins the last release`; `unions shared scopes and exclusions without widening an agent's selections`; `does not share a replaced root with an agent admitted to the new directory`. The `isolates shared %s failures so a failing scope cannot disable healthy peers` matrix covers scan and watch-limit failures plus healthy-peer recovery; `refreshes only selected structural changes while retaining ancestor discovery` covers filtering and ancestor rediscovery; the existing recovery-budget regression now rejects unrelated peer events. The existing `honors background polling defaults and overrides with polling=%s interval=%s` matrix also checks the five-minute native cadence. Tests use fake timers and deferred joins. No new sleep or live service.
- Local changed-file `oxfmt` and type-aware `oxlint`: passed (3 TypeScript files, 264 rules, zero diagnostics). Lint used trusted main's rules with the unrelated UI-only Solid override omitted because that plugin is absent from the supplied dependency install; all rules applying to these memory files were retained.
- Autoreview P0–P2: scoped-clean, including a fresh pass after the two GitHub review fixes; the first pass's pathname-versus-root-identity finding was also fixed. The reviewed files are byte-identical after merging current main.
- Candidate head: `a9ba4b4e3ff03a0535358e12de65814741cd2836`, including a normal merge of main `40d01813a80a2`. Exact-head CI: [38815424427](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38815424427) — **passed**, including `openclaw/ci-gate`: 27 successful jobs, 30 intentionally skipped, zero failures/cancellations. Production and test types, lint, memory test bundles, package boundaries, docs, and repository checks passed.
- Live proof, leases, local tests/typechecks, and a production-revert negative control were intentionally skipped per maintainer policy. Local test wall time is therefore not measured. On this exact head, [memory test job 116699441639](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38815424427/job/116699441639) ran `node --import tsx scripts/ci-run-node-test-shard.mts` and passed all 26 lifecycle cases (518 ms summed reported test time). Sharing, replaced-root, per-agent filtering, scan isolation, watch-limit isolation, and structural filtering took 18/18/25/19/24/13 ms respectively. The containing shard passed 78 tests across 8 files in 212.98 s. Existing filesystem cases also covered edits/deletion, root replacement, and large-tree observation.
- First CI run [38811104072](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38811104072) found TS7030 and type-aware lint errors in the refresh completion callback; those change-caused errors are fixed by keeping `finally` synchronous and joining follow-up work in `then`. No inherited failure is claimed.
- Diff versus main: production +233/-70 (net +163), tests +217/-5 (net +212), docs +10/-2 (net +8). Necessary production growth owns shared membership, bounded scope updates, independent failure recovery, and final-member cleanup; the per-agent subscription creation path is removed.

ClawSweeper comment 6202155966 reviewed the earlier empty reservation head and reported no code findings. The implementation and cadence direction now match this work order. Its proof-only requests are superseded by the maintainer's PR-CI proof policy. GitHub review 5540495413 raised two P2 code findings (4288746257 and 4288746269): repeated shared-failure propagation and unfiltered structural refresh. Both are addressed with independent recovery and selection-before-refresh, with focused regressions; both threads are resolved. The current-head GitHub code review completed with no findings or unresolved findings. No human review findings were present.

prs.title: feat(openshell): run brokered inference on sandboxed nodes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Run native worker inference behind OpenShell's credential broker without requiring OCE or Kubernetes, with optional canonical agent files shared across its sessions.

## User Impact

Opt-in `openclaw openshell worker create/run/configure` commands provision a dedicated broker-attached sandbox through OpenShell, enroll its ordinary OpenClaw node, and configure the existing paired-device worker-inference profile. Docker and Podman use the same OpenShell gateway/CLI contract; neither engine is managed directly by this plugin. Existing sandbox-only behavior stays unchanged.

Optional `worker.agentWorkspace: { agentId, remoteRoot }` now binds one configured agent to an existing private directory on the paired node through File Transfer. Both Gateway and worker sessions use that canonical document owner; ordinary coding tools still use each session's task workspace. Setup never seeds or synchronizes documents, copies private Gateway state, widens node-command approvals, or overrides an existing File Transfer policy. Prepare the directory/files and review the existing grants before applying the binding.

**Scope and important limits:** one configured model, a qualified operator-supplied Node/OpenClaw image, and a foreground node host. OpenShell v0.1.3+ provider profiles, executable/endpoint policy, egress enforcement, and real provider credentials remain operator-owned. `worker run` owns a **dedicated sandbox** and stops the entire sandbox on exit/cancellation; cleanup failures explicitly report that the remote node may remain active. `configure --required --apply` affects all Gateway sessions and blocks turns when its worker is unavailable. No production deployment, real provider credentials, releases, or production configuration were changed during development or qualification.

**Historical standalone Docker E2E passed on October 10**, including broker authorization, revocation, and confirmed remote cancellation. It uses a synthetic OpenAI-compatible HTTPS upstream, not a paid model account. Full Podman, real-provider API, and latest-stable upgrade qualification remain separate gaps.

### Compatibility and operator actions

No breaking change was found in the existing sandbox-only `mirror`/`remote` flow when `worker` is absent: its schema fields/defaults, backend and SSH/mirror paths are preserved; CLI registration launches nothing. This PR adds no core/SDK API, database migration, dependency, or worker-protocol change. **The new worker mode is not a drop-in plugin upgrade for older Gateway/node builds.**

- Released OpenClaw **v2026.10.1** lacks the native-inference stack and `cloudWorkers.requiredProfile`; its strict OpenShell plugin schema also rejects the new `worker` block. Installing this plugin alone does not backport core capabilities. Use matching qualified Gateway/node builds and their supported Node version; generic plugin host/API metadata is not worker-mode qualification.
- For downgrade, finish/stop turns, reconcile pending browser inputs and reclaim native placements on the compatible build first; then remove required/native profiles and `plugins.entries.openshell.config.worker`. Older Gateways do not interpret `settings.inference` as a local-inference requirement. No complete stable upgrade or cross-version data-downgrade qualification is claimed.
- **OpenShell v0.1.3+ applies to the new mode only.** Upgrading an older OpenShell deployment has its own breaking migration away from managed inference routes and requires recreating pre-upgrade sandboxes per upstream. This PR does not automatically upgrade OpenShell or migrate those records.
- The workload needs Linux/OpenShell kernel enforcement (including Landlock), a qualified non-root Node/OpenClaw image with Git and POSIX process tools, and an imported provider profile authorizing the actual Node binary and HTTPS endpoint. Native Windows worker inference is unsupported; Docker/Podman selection alone does not establish host capability.
- Initial support is one model using `openai-completions`, `openai-responses`, or `anthropic-messages`, with broker environment placeholders and correct CA trust—not every provider/auth adapter. The runner is foreground and stops the entire dedicated sandbox on exit. `--required --apply` affects all Gateway sessions; unavailable workers block turns. Rotation requires a new node process, and model/state changes are not silently overwritten.

Full Podman E2E, real-provider behavior, and latest-stable upgrade qualification remain gaps, not inferred failures. [Setup and rollback guidance](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/openshell-workers#compatibility-and-rollback) records these boundaries; the source-bound historical Docker evidence below remains unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use existing owners instead of adding another provider or inference protocol:

- OpenShell creates/retains the sandbox with named existing providers and `--no-auto-providers`, then owns attachment readiness through `sandbox provider attach --wait`.
- The remote bootstrap refuses missing/raw model credentials, accepts only OpenShell's injected opaque placeholder, and writes canonical node model config containing an environment reference—not a key. It maps OpenShell's CA file to Node's supported trust setting without disabling certificate verification.
- Pairing uses `connect --target-file` with a private stdin handoff; reconnect uses `node run`. The Gateway profile derives the exact device ID from read-only `node identity --json` inside the selected sandbox, optionally checks an expected ID, preserves unrelated config, and refuses conflicting bindings.
- Core remains the owner of live pairing, admission, device availability, worker-local inference selection, recorded placement snapshots, and rejection of Gateway fallback. No core/SDK runtime changes, new credentials store, or OCE API dependency.

Current OpenShell calls the real provider endpoint, not the retired workspace inference route. API/CLI contracts were inspected at released NVIDIA/OpenShell v0.1.3 (`e1f3c82caa3ed3b65de22889ae7ef32a774878ef`). Placeholder-format checks and provider readiness are not cryptographic custody attestation or upstream model probes; the deployment trust contract remains explicit.

The original default-off worker option adds 15 plugin config fields; the optional agent-workspace binding adds 3 more (18 total over the pinned main base). Canonical config-baseline outputs were regenerated; this growth is intentional, not an unrelated baseline waiver.

## Evidence

### Requested final rebase and blocker check — October 15 (16:58 request)

Rebased the existing single commit from `10f275f9aa8dd0947205acc52a7f930fe37cece0` onto pinned main `7285b93504a9453c4fbd03ff2281f8da33e9a40d`. Published head **`9131246f6309a2d9aae682f86c55b0e3b340a91b`**, tree `27e5f60f6489e6b34b58cb7d0110e41eee73094a`. GitHub readback: one commit, OPEN, non-draft, mergeable. No merge/auto-merge/readiness transition.

- Only `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` conflicted. Both configuration baseline outputs were regenerated canonically; the intended +18 plugin paths remain unchanged.
- Production and documentation blobs are unchanged. Main's existing `index.test.ts` migration from polling to the authoritative plugin-retirement promise was retained automatically. The complete base-relative range comparison contains no new feature behavior or permission change. The single squashed commit, trimmed tests, Sally co-author and publication marker remain intact.
- Fresh proof: **123/123 tests across eight sandbox/default/mirror/worker files**, **65.63s wrapper wall**; extension production/test types, canonical baseline, formatting and whitespace passed. Typed lint of the affected registration test passed with zero warnings/errors. The idle private checkout was reconciled with main's pinned pnpm 12.10.1 frozen install; no dependency source files were changed.
- No fresh full build, VM or migration experiment was started for this mechanical refresh. Previous build, live broker and upgrade receipts remain bound to their actual earlier heads. No new implementation finding was identified in the resolved delta.

**Merge-gate distinction:** the effective rules returned by GitHub require `openclaw/ci-gate`; the new head's checks and automatic review are running. The current rules require zero general approving reviews and code-owner review where applicable; none of these 18 paths matches the current CODEOWNERS entries. GitHub reports no formal latest reviews, requested reviewers or review decision. This does not waive any enforced check or later owner/security requirement.

The older ClawSweeper comment `6098113740` still says “blocked before merge” for upgrade/preservation qualification, but was last updated October 13 for `c89bc66069cd` and lists **no findings**. Treat it as an unresolved qualification/review hold for maintainer disposition—not an identified old-record incompatibility or proof that a database migration is broken. It is distinct from the live required CI gate.

**Recovered historical upgrade evidence (not new-head proof):** the separately isolated v2026.10.3 installed updater did successfully activate `10f275f9aa8d`, with managed restart, exact serving build, readiness and durable `finished/succeeded` status (run `ae1791af-6bbf-4c2e-bfd4-c0d63ac87254`, **383.139s**). [Attempt 2 receipt](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_a838e2534adf606a3717163cfd112a8b). The task fixture then falsely matched “lease” inside “releases”; full preservation comparisons, candidate-plugin replacement and optional setup were not reached. Attempt 3's controller ended 143 without recoverable terminal proof; its lease expired and live recovery inspection confirmed no host or remaining provisioning resource. **Neither attempt is a complete preservation pass.** Existing sandbox-only fields/defaults remain preserved by source review; older-host/native-placement prerequisites and post-opt-in downgrade cleanup remain documented.

Pre-rebase head `6003d3d131598de28d887f401d88220ab5b73a57` adds only the image-tool prerequisites documentation; runtime source is identical. No protocol, dependency, or core/SDK change.

**Environment:** configured direct AWS Crabbox, small `c7a.2xlarge` VM; Ubuntu 26.04.1, Linux `7.0.0-1014-aws`, Docker 29.8.2, host Node 24.19.0, workload Node 26.8.2, released OpenShell v0.1.3 (`e1f3c82caa3ed3b65de22889ae7ef32a774878ef`). Pairing succeeded; configuration read back the selected sandbox node identity; the recorded required placement was active with `inference: worker`.

The native `write` tool produced the expected worker file and the completed assistant marker appeared in canonical Gateway history; the turn completed `ok`. A separate approved-executable control request also authenticated correctly.
- The sandbox launch environment contained only the opaque broker placeholder and its canonical model config retained the environment reference. The real synthetic upstream key was absent from Gateway configuration/environment inputs. This is not a claim to have dumped the inference child’s private credential pipe.
- A copied executable at an unapproved path and an unlisted endpoint both failed with **EACCES**, not timeout or certificate failure; **zero forbidden requests reached upstream**. An approved executable/endpoint control succeeded with certificate verification enabled.

- After acknowledged `sandbox provider detach --wait`, a new native turn using the retained placeholder reached terminal **error** with **no additional upstream request** and **zero Gateway chat-inference fallback requests**. Only the exact pinned Gateway endpoint uses TLS passthrough; model-provider TLS inspection and credential substitution remain enabled.

### Defect found and repaired by live testing

The original `configure --profile` collided with OpenClaw’s global configuration-profile option and was consumed before the plugin. The actual installed command failed its required-option check. It now uses **`--worker-profile`** consistently in code, tests, and documentation, without a competing root-parser exception or a legacy alias for the unreleased broken interface.

- Updated regression first failed on the old implementation; **25/25 focused tests then passed**, 8.10s Vitest / **9.48s** wrapper wall.

prs.title: perf(build): reduce ownership walks and overlap UI compression
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Runtime builds repeat shared dependency-ownership graph walks and compress Control UI assets serially. Across four deployment builds, compilation took 32.3–45.2 seconds and the UI took 17.4–26.1 seconds, the two largest build phases.

## User Impact

Reduce preparation work before deployment. Generated runtime ownership, Brotli/gzip bytes, build checks, and release publication ordering remain unchanged. No controller adoption, production restart, schema, or configuration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the ownership producer's existing `(chunk, owner)` map instead of allocating a visited set and traversing the same closure for every entry. Compress up to four UI assets concurrently with the existing Brotli quality and canonical gzip settings; join every started writer before failure cleanup. All compressor callers now await completion.

Production delta: +14 lines across three files. The ownership change deletes a redundant traversal set; the remaining growth bounds native compression memory and settles concurrent writers. No new cache or scheduler.

## Evidence

- Historical phase attribution: tsdown 32.3–45.2s; UI 17.4–26.1s, including precompression 5.558–5.875s; CLI bootstrap guard 9.93–10.3s; plugin builds 6.74–9.15s; runtime postbuild 8.43–8.81s; startup metadata 3.36–3.45s. Total build 88.2–107.2s. Separate staging interval 12.66–14.07s includes copying, sealing, validation, and publication, not filesystem checks alone. Postbuild logs identify compatibility generation at 5.60–5.77s; they do not separately time the other 13 phases.
- Isolated Linux measurements (Node 26.8.2, 64-CPU affinity, 64 GiB cap): actual emitted ownership topology with synthetic chunk bodies, 9,438 chunks / 1,213 entries / 78,094 edges, seven alternating measured pairs after warmup: **1.193s → 0.200s (5.97×)**, identical metadata. Actual UI corpus, 547 assets / 1,094 sidecars, five alternating measured pairs after warmup: **6.204s → 5.102s (17.8% less time)**, every sidecar byte identical. Combined owner work saved: **2.095s per fresh build**; this is not yet an end-to-end deployment claim. Four complete runtime builds, before/after/after/before: build-all **83.0s / 77.9s / 76.6s / 75.0s**; enclosing CLI **86.10s / 80.92s / 79.65s / 78.06s**. Whole-build timing is neutral/noisy: unrelated plugin time ranged 3.90–8.06s and compilation 30.9–34.5s. Do not attribute the aggregate difference to this patch. Peak RSS: baseline 7,549,388–7,577,208 KiB; candidate 7,592,036–7,597,816 KiB (under 0.5% difference). No live deployment was performed, so end-to-end seconds saved per deploy remain unproven.
- Focused local tests: five touched UI/build-check files passed (52 tests; 4.58s tooling + 16.54s UI wall time). Ownership compiler-to-installed-verifier contract: 4 passed, 190ms test time (28.89s wrapper, including existing worker preparation). Covers cycles, repeated roots, distinct plugin owners, and root ownership.
- Changed-file formatter, syntax lint, and `git diff --check` passed. PR CI owns broad validation; no local full suite, build, or typecheck. No Testbox/Crabbox lease allocated. Exact-head PR CI passed: run 38819494006, 884s wall time; aggregate CI and security/dependency gates green. No rerun or inherited-failure exception. Per-file CI timing was not separately collected.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings. Autoreview rejected the requested provider because it did not match operator configuration; configuration was preserved.

<details>
<summary>Isolated baseline postbuild breakdown (all 14 phases)</summary>

Compatibility chunks 5.835s; built plugin control-plane load checks 1.504s; stable root import rewrites 0.283s; plugin runtime overlay 0.164s; plugin metadata 0.140s; stable aliases 0.038s; export HTML 0.026s; static extension assets 0.013s; channel catalog 0.005s; provenance 0.002s. Hook metadata, private diagnostic companions, legacy root aliases, and legacy CLI aliases each rounded to 0ms. Historical logs only expose the slowest phase; these individual measurements come from the isolated instrumented build.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Historical phase ranking across four successful deployments (seconds)</summary>

| Phase | A | B | C | D |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| tsdown | 32.3 | 45.2 | 32.5 | 43.8 |
| UI | 17.4 | 18.8 | 17.5 | 26.1 |
| Build preparation before first phase | 17.06 | 17.46 | 16.94 | 16.55 |
| Staging interval | 12.93 | 13.52 | 12.66 | 14.07 |
| CLI bootstrap guard | 9.93 | 10.1 | 10.2 | 10.3 |
| External plugin local dist | 8.95 | 9.15 | 8.04 | 6.74 |
| Runtime postbuild | 8.49 | 8.58 | 8.43 | 8.81 |
| Plugin assets build | 3.59 | 3.57 | 3.57 | 3.70 |
| Startup metadata | 3.39 | 3.45 | 3.36 | 3.43 |
| Plugin assets copy | 2.73 | 2.56 | 2.60 | 2.69 |
| Build stamp | 1.54 | 1.50 | 1.49 | 0.99 |

The main tsdown invocation accounts for 28.1–39.7s; AI invocation 0.4–3.9s. Plugin input caching already exists, and its `built 97 plugins` message includes cache hits. UI compression counts were 541/543/543/547 assets, rather than 542 in all samples. UI/stamp overlap is negligible in these journals. No invented individual timings for unlogged stage substeps.

The isolated compiler trace identifies sealed SQLite worker (12.04s), sealed main worker (11.02s), unified runtime (8.11s), node-host launcher (6.99s), and code-mode worker (4.49s) as the largest configs. These run concurrently; their durations are not additive. The retained optimization removes repeated graph work within unified runtime without changing compiler concurrency or standalone-bundle contracts.

</details>

prs.title: fix(cron): scheduled reports leave sessions marked read
prs.body:
Closes #142002. Reported by @lakemike; @DarkJuanFra supplied the fresh scheduled-session reproduction.

## What Problem This Solves

A scheduled agent report can be saved to a persistent conversation after its last read acknowledgment while the Control UI still shows that conversation as read.

## User Impact

Visible scheduled reports restore the conversation's unread indicator, including with delivery mode `none`. Assistant-written blocker reports count without implying scheduler execution failure; empty results, text-only silent replies and heartbeat acknowledgments preserve read state. Detached runs with no source delivery preserve their source conversation’s read state; source delivery keeps its existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Record the completed output's visibility on the original live run claim before its existing terminal event is emitted. The existing lifecycle owner remains the activity writer; execution timing, transcript identity, delivery and access checks stay with their owners. Shared reply/payload classifiers preserve silent and structured-output semantics. Gateway test doubles now use the real Cron function contract and preserve the facade's exports, so the regression reaches actual execution. The canonical mock-export prune removes one obsolete closed-factory entry from the ratchet; it adds no exception.

## Evidence

<!-- exact-head-complete-gateway-proof-f9dd -->
Natural broad [CI run 38812626406](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38812626406) on exact head `f9ddf58f4d004e87eb616af8236dc8bf379723bd` completed **successfully**. Its [Gateway job 116690071869](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38812626406/job/116690071869) tests merge `7a3b49a1c60be46e77127e6eae02074969493f98` against official base `b4fb60242fef5a39ba2db40225072762e6a08200`. The complete `server.cron.unread-activity.test.ts` case passes in **62.240 seconds**.

This is the actual isolated Gateway flow with a synthetic loopback model: stored-account admission, model response, chat/cron history equivalence and visible-report unread; ordinary blocker report with status `ok`, persisted text and unread; all three `NO_REPLY`/empty/`HEARTBEAT_OK` quiet controls; and detached session identity/history with the source staying read. The unconditional test body reaches its final detached assertions. This resolves the earlier account and obsolete text-protocol fixture failures; it does not claim provider/runtime-error reports, installed production services, power-loss or real vendor proof. No local Gateway operation or CI rerun was used.

Current head: `f9ddf58f4d004e87eb616af8236dc8bf379723bd`. The latest one-file correction migrates the retained Gateway fixture to official main's accepted blocker-report contract; product code and persisted-account setup remain unchanged from `412cd9cff58245156d507c47c606df80622d4975`.

Current-parent natural [CI run 38808499872, job 116676475840](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38808499872/job/116676475840) tested merge `50040983d8acf35b33fbec89f4618c0ff4bf180a` against base `d9fa5ac1303a1fc85e82363d5aad6d2f8f573923`. The stored-profile correction passes `cron.add`, the first actual model request, both public histories, last-activity advancement and the unread assertion. It then fails at the old `status: "error"` expectation for an HTTP-200 assistant report; subsequent blocker history, quiet and detached checks were not reached. This is a recorded failing job, not an overall passing Gateway flow.

Official [#170267](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/170267), commit `0ae42f07a6537dab50cb6788d66e1c92aaef91d5`, intentionally removed the `AUTOMATION_FAILED` prose protocol. The current unattended-run docs and canonical `cron-blocked-outcome` QA require ordinary task-blocker prose to finish with status `ok`; runtime/provider failures remain structured errors. This fixture now uses `OWNED_BLOCKER_REPORT`, names its variables accordingly, and expects `ok` while preserving actual model execution, public report history, lastActivityAt and unread-positive assertions, along with every quiet and detached control. It does not change production error classification or replace a visible assistant report with a synthesized provider error. It is **not Gateway runtime-error proof**.

- Two existing real Cron outcome-owner controls, distinguishing ordinary output from structured errors while keeping delivery-target failure separate, pass: **2 passed / 7 unselected**, **95.987 seconds wrapper / 87.42 seconds Vitest**. They use the existing isolated orchestration harness and do not boot a Gateway; they are not execution of the corrected Gateway fixture.
- Final relevant test-consumer types pass in **22.947 seconds**, type-aware core lint in **26.585 seconds**; formatting, diff and the one-file native staged line-cap check pass. No new tests, sleeps, timeout changes, skips, mocks, permissions, schema or dependency changes are introduced.
- Fresh independent P0–P2 review of the one-file correction plus its full fixture and accepted contract is scoped-clean; the committed fixture hash matches reviewed bytes. Node 24.19.0 / pnpm 12.10.1 satisfy the integrated branch requirements. Earlier unchanged product and stored-account-owner checks remain qualified below.

**Local execution limit:** the complete natural CI result above now covers those Gateway assertions. It has not been rerun locally; the old Gateway approval was for `2e7e990`, not this head. Current-parent partial actual Gateway proof is labeled with its exact merge above. No failed check is waived, and no existing Gateway, production data, external provider, paid allocation or CI rerun was used.

<details>
<summary>Prior stored-account correction, integration and historical Gateway proof</summary>



Current head: `412cd9cff58245156d507c47c606df80622d4975`. This follow-up changes only the retained Gateway fixture; the unread activity implementation and previously reviewed product inputs remain identical to `b80fa3b5ed1c54a633cc3db5016ae2e79b586a45`.

<details>
<summary>Prior integration proof and historical Gateway evidence</summary>

The import conflict retains both the existing terminal-output classification and main's dedicated model-response diagnostic owner. Admission, scope, claim currentness, usage, continuation sealing and cleanup remain with main's owners.

- Corrected exact-main negative control: the actual Cron orchestration entry emits its terminal event without a visibility fact in all six selected report/silent/empty/media/error cases. **6 intended assertion failures / 4 filtered cases**, **97.59 s Vitest / 105.40 s wrapper**. Candidate `run.ts` is restored exactly afterward.

The new table uses the real payload classifier and run registry, reads visibility synchronously at lifecycle end, and checks opt-in diagnostic capture separately. `NO_REPLY` remains a genuine captured model response while it does not become unread activity; structured media remains visible.
- Existing siblings separately produced **6 diagnostic-model-response, 49 lifecycle-projection and 6 payload-classification passing cases**. The corrected 10-case file is independently green.

The first fixture version subscribed to the two-argument ordinary diagnostic API but attempted to read private content as a third argument. It now uses the existing trusted private-data subscription, with the same expectations and no casts, added production seam, privacy change or relaxed assertion. Failed runs remain recorded.

Current verification uses synthetic model results and the existing in-process Cron orchestration, classification, registry and lifecycle owners. **No real Gateway, public RPC, real CLI, vendor API or external message was executed for this maintenance head.** The actual Gateway/Cron/history/unread/acknowledgment proof below belongs to historical `2e7e9903`; it is not reclassified as current-head runtime evidence. The planned repair uses the real stored-profile owner and explicit `model@profile` binding, preserving production admission and all history/unread controls. That Gateway fixture is not currently passing; no local Gateway was started.

## Prior-head evidence (`2e7e9903` and predecessors)

<details>
<summary>Historical public Gateway proof and retained earlier failures</summary>



- On the unchanged production baseline, authenticated `cron.run` reached the owned model HTTP endpoint, saved the matching report, and returned identical `chat.history`/`cron.history` content. The public session list then returned `unread: false`, with no `lastActivityAt`; the regression failed there (62.70s wrapper wall time).

After strengthening the public assertion order, all 73 related cases across five files passed in 121.88s, including existing media classification, lifecycle, registry and authority controls. prs.title: fix(logging): drop malformed redaction entries instead of throwing
prs.body:
Fixes #173461

## What Problem This Solves

Directory inspection and Doctor can throw a secondary TypeError and lose the config-rejection warning when a rejected config also contains malformed `logging.redactPatterns`, such as `[1]` or `[null]`.

## User Impact

Malformed redaction settings no longer stop the recovery warning. Valid custom patterns keep masking, and malformed policies retain built-in credential protection. A single diagnostic asks the operator to correct the patterns without printing their values. No migration or new setting is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared redaction resolver admits only callable programmatic matchers, skips rejected entries, and composes usable patterns with defaults whenever the policy is malformed. Valid custom-only policies keep their existing behavior. Warning failures cannot interrupt masking. The resolver now uses one insertion-ordered Set instead of parallel array/Set bookkeeping; no caller-side catch was added.

Original fix by @skyzhao1223; maintainer cleanup fixes the null regression, preserves default and custom redaction, adds recovery-path coverage, and documents the fallback.

## Evidence

Current-main source and history confirm the defect: `readCurrentConfigForResolution` formats its load error through implicit logging redaction, while the logging reader can return unvalidated patterns and the old resolver accepts them as matchers. The warning detail was added in `634ca9ee00f`; the shared matcher contract predates it in `103bdf8d147c`.

PR CI is the test gate per maintainer policy. CI invoked `node --import tsx scripts/ci-run-node-test-shard.mts` for the changed-test shards. It covers the changed config/logging tests, typechecking, and the repository's planned checks. Regression cases:

- `emits the directory-resolution warning with a malformed redaction entry %j` covers `[1]` and `[null]` through `readCurrentConfigForResolution`.
- `keeps valid and default redaction with malformed patterns and warns only once` checks exact masking, mixed policies, malformed containers, and a failed diagnostic sink.
- `redactSensitiveLines keeps registered and default protection when custom regexes are rejected` preserves registered-secret masking while checking the restored defaults.

Changed-file oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` passed. The nested install cannot load the lint wrapper or the UI-only Solid plugin, so static lint used the existing shared binary and a temporary config preserving all core rules while omitting only the unrelated UI override. Prescribed isolated Codex branch autoreview returned `scoped-clean`, with no actionable P0–P2 findings; contributor code was not executed on the maintainer host. The subsequent `git merge origin/main` was conflict-free and changed none of these five files. Tests, typechecks, negative controls, and live Gateway proof were intentionally not run locally; live proof was intentionally skipped per maintainer policy. No remote leases were created. Exact-head CI passed all 78 tests in the three changed files: `redact.test.ts` 50/50 in 2.19 s ([job 116704425377](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38816880964/job/116704425377)); `redact-patterns.test.ts` 18/18 in 1.05 s ([job 116704425312](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38816880964/job/116704425312)); `io.best-effort.test.ts` 10/10 in 18.27 s ([job 116704425456](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38816880964/job/116704425456)). These are whole-file CI durations including setup/transform. The added warning cases took 14 ms and 8 ms, the mixed-policy case 2 ms, and the corrected rejected-regex case 3 ms. No measured local test times are claimed. Added cases use no timers, polling, or Gateway startup.

The first [CI attempt, job 116699018354](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38815304311/job/116699018354), found one incorrect expected string in the updated rejected-regex test (49 other tests passed in that file). Both built-in assignment rules mask `TOKEN`, so the shortened hint is fully masked as `***`; the source-verified oracle now expects `TOKEN=*** opaque…7890`. This one-line test correction passed lint/format and an additional isolated autoreview. No production change or rerun-only retry was used.

ClawSweeper's P2 null-entry finding is addressed. Its live-proof request is superseded by the maintainer's explicit PR-CI proof policy. No human review findings were present at preparation.

Against `origin/main` (`9f4b34b842b33`): production **+35/-14 (net +21)**; tests **+55/-3 (net +52)**; docs **+5/-0**. The source-growth exception is needed for malformed-policy fallback and a guarded once-only diagnostic; duplicate collection bookkeeping was removed. Exact-head [CI run 38816880964](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38816880964) completed successfully for `e2da53f51930cabb43ed07a55de13d4fd8aa036d`: **49 successful jobs, 28 intentionally skipped, no failures**. Production types, test types, lint, all Node shards, and UI E2E passed; `openclaw/ci-gate` and `openclaw/security-sensitive-review` are green. No inherited-failure exception was needed. No deferred or background effect was added, so there are no captured lifetime or authority facts requiring revalidation.

prs.title: perf(gateway): avoid pairing queues during reconnect storms
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Paired-device reconnects wait for worker reads and access-metadata writes before the Gateway can send hello. During a signed-in dashboard deep-link reload storm, campaign evidence reported attach p50/p90 of 5.4/12.4 seconds, device lookup p50 of 1.1 seconds, and metadata p50 of 2.0 seconds. The broader reload capture recorded 14 visible states. Those observations motivate this fix; they are separate from the synthetic baseline below.

## User Impact

The existing pairing publication retains complete paired-device records, loads them before connection admission, and updates them from committed writer receipts. Normal Gateway lookups use that process-owned publication. Fresh CLI readers and invalidated publications retain the worker path. Public-key, token, role/scope, revocation, and approval-generation authority checks remain in place.

Hello no longer awaits access metadata. The existing detached-connect owner tracks the work, and pairing coalesces simultaneous tabs per device. A worker-side public-key/approval-time guard refuses bookkeeping for a replacement approval. Recent last-seen time/reason changes skip writes and receipt publication for one minute; changed client metadata still records after hello. The previous critical-path writes and redundant outer metadata lock are removed. There are no config, durable schema, or durable record-shape changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reconnect storms after each Team deploy left connect attach waiting seconds on the shared state writer (Team r127-r129: deviceLookupMs p50 1.1-3.3 s, deviceMetadataMs p50 0.9-4.1 s). Auth-relevant device lookups now come from the committed process-owned pairing publication, and last-seen/metadata bookkeeping is coalesced after hello.

## Evidence

### Measured Before / After

Final candidate: `6eb5385ecd583bd2e5f24650572a3c27bbd00807`; baseline runtime: `a612ff0f07e2ea8c34d7ab07506116aaf7282ed8`, with identical diagnostics in both modes. Quiet AWS **c7a.4xlarge**, Node 24.19.0, one fixed lease **`cbx_ab925003e115`** for the entire comparison. Seven alternating baseline/candidate pairs per shape: **28 measured trials**, all **160/160 successful** with the expected scopes. Warmup and smoke trials are excluded. Cells show median of seven run-level statistics **[Q1, Q3]**, in milliseconds.

| Attach statistic (ms) | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Unique devices, run p50 | 579.4 [575.9, 589.1] | 51.7 [31.8, 87.3] |
| Unique devices, run p90 | 709.2 [705.9, 753.0] | 112.9 [90.5, 138.2] |
| Unique devices, run max | 774.4 [763.5, 828.6] | 139.2 [100.3, 152.0] |
| Multi-tab/node, run p50 | 593.1 [568.3, 602.9] | 6.1 [5.8, 6.3] |
| Multi-tab/node, run p90 | 754.2 [700.1, 757.8] | 50.1 [39.7, 57.2] |
| Multi-tab/node, run max | 1398.6 [1394.2, 1425.1] | 523.8 [510.6, 554.7] |

Worst observed attach across all seven runs: unique devices **839.5 → 160.7 ms**; multi-tab/node **1,467.0 → 558.4 ms**.

Both shapes seed 1,000 paired devices, 1,000 profiles, and 5,000 sessions with fresh timestamps. The first uses 160 unique operator devices. The second uses 144 browser connections (four tabs per device), 16 node clients, 128-character metadata padding, 42 concurrent public history requests with 200 roughly 1 KiB messages each, restart recovery, and 80 session reads through normal worker admission. Every multi-tab/node trial verifies all 42 history responses contain 200 messages and recovery marks 140 interrupted sessions. Warmup primes real health inspection via the public `health` RPC, equally in both modes, and records that cost separately.

In the multi-tab/node variant, browser-only attach p50/p90 is **572.8/703.0 → 5.6/16.1 ms**; node p50/p90 is **1,197.9/1,208.0 → 462.9/519.5 ms**. Required token/node preparation remains on the connect path.

### Queue Attribution

These fixture results identify pairing admission and superseded-read retries as the expensive waits, rather than worker execution or receipt publication. Pairing mutations share the canonical state writer/database with user profiles, Gateway boot/recovery records, node/bootstrap work, delivery state, and worker environments. Pairing reads use the shared state-read pool. Session transcript repair/recovery also runs concurrently through the agent-database owners.

| Operation statistic (ms) | Unique baseline → candidate | Multi-tab/node baseline → candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Device lookup p50 | 161.441 [159.862, 169.966] → 0.042 [0.040, 0.042] | 224.250 [208.294, 228.746] → 0.051 [0.050, 0.053] |
| Device lookup p90 | 545.654 [544.673, 584.996] → 0.150 [0.147, 0.155] | 316.454 [310.781, 387.541] → 0.158 [0.157, 0.165] |
| Awaited metadata p50 | 380.5 [370.8, 399.0] → After hello | 330.6 [318.6, 340.3] → After hello |
| Pairing admission wait p50 | 309.728 [305.459, 315.922] → 257.013 [248.564, 268.050] | 273.604 [251.233, 276.674] → 0.037 [0.036, 0.038] |
| Receipt publication p50 | 0.004 [0.004, 0.004] → 0.021 [0.021, 0.021] | 0.004 [0.004, 0.004] → 0.019 [0.019, 0.019] |
| Metadata worker execution p50 | 2.681 [2.646, 2.734] → 4.988 [4.741, 5.058] | 2.768 [2.727, 2.804] → 4.087 [3.760, 4.162] |
| Metadata broker queue p50 | 0.374 [0.370, 0.414] → 5.477 [5.341, 5.685] | 0.351 [0.349, 0.357] → 0.020 [0.019, 0.021] |
| Metadata worker receive → execute p50 | 0.024 [0.024, 0.024] → 0.032 [0.030, 0.036] | 0.025 [0.024, 0.025] → 0.035 [0.034, 0.037] |

Baseline worker lookup completions have median counts **278/366** per 160-client storm because publication changes force retries. Candidate completes **zero** pairing lookup worker requests in either storm. The unique-device bookkeeping queue still exists after hello: its observed lock-wait p50 is **257.0 ms**, but attachment no longer awaits it. Multi-tab candidate lock-wait p50 is **0.037 ms**, with a 237.9 ms p90 as required token work and detached writes settle. Counts and operation distributions cover the connect window; fewer completions in a shorter window do not imply that all deferred writes disappear. Across the observed storm and following sequential connects, the largest receipt-publication cost is **0.089 ms**.

### Proof and Limits

**84 focused behavior tests passed** on AWS `cbx_1769533ed982`: startup hydration, pairing cache/write-through and mutable-callers, reader failures, revocation/publication ordering, metadata coalescing and stale-approval refusal, handshake/hello ordering, auth-none/device-token/mobile bootstrap, connect metrics, and node authorization. That proof is on `722dc78`; the final follow-up removes only an erased default type argument and rebases over changes outside these owners. Final-head targeted format and lint pass on `cbx_ab925003e115`; final-head CI production/test types and lint also pass. Controlled old-code cache and recent-last-seen regressions failed as expected, then passed on candidate. Detached branch review is clean through P2.

Final-head [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38813741186) is **red**, with four test failures across three jobs. Production/test types, lint, and seven selected UI e2e shards pass. The two `server.agent-execution-shutdown` failures and the `server.agent-late-admission` stop-reason failure also occur on main ([shutdown job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38810511907/job/116682662447), [admission job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38810511907/job/116682662526)). AWS `cbx_459ff3dde0bc`, using CI's Node 24.21.0, reproduces those failures on clean base `a612ff0` and on candidate `6eb5385`.

The remaining [session-reader schema-probe failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38813741186/job/116694098423) is `database is locked`. Its unchanged 14-test file passes alone on both clean base and candidate. The original four-file CI shard also passes **37/37** on both base and candidate with CI's two-worker setting on AWS `cbx_f1ab1ab76ae0` (48.82/44.85 s wall time). Its trigger remains **unattributed**, so this report does not claim all remaining reds are inherited or that a passing replay fixes the CI failure. The native CI gate remains unresolved for the lead. No CI reruns, expected-failure masks, or unrelated shutdown changes were made.

The canonical Team-scale renderer benchmark ran seven settled captures on the same final AWS lease using repository Playwright Chromium and both rig probes. Each cold-load capture has zero pending/queued requests and 87 RPCs. The bench mocks the Gateway, so this is a renderer control, not an end-to-end reload speed claim. Long-frame/mutation probes were captured; the rig WebSocket census is empty under its mock transport. No UI source changed; all seven UI e2e shards selected by CI pass.

An earlier unprimed-source comparison exposed two candidate tail regressions around 6.7 seconds. A separate CPU capture on `cbx_063284d4a862` attributes about 6.2 seconds to synchronous source loading of health account inspectors through Jiti/esbuild. The built-JS companion has a native loading path. The final fixture explicitly warms this owner in both modes; that warmup is approximately 7.3–7.5 seconds and is excluded from attachment measurements. This PR does not fix cold source health-inspector loading, and no live deployment was modified or measured. The original unprimed result is retained as a limitation rather than presented as a pairing improvement.

<details>
<summary>Focused test wall times and runtime size</summary>

AWS wall time for `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, including the repository runner, on `cbx_1769533ed982`:

| File | Tests | Wall time |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `src/gateway/server-kernel.startup.test.ts` | 3 | 69.94 s |
| `src/infra/device-pairing-worker.test.ts` | 13 | 37.40 s |
| `src/infra/device-pairing-publication.test.ts` | 25 | 34.30 s |
| `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/connect-device-pairing.test.ts` | 11 | 98.12 s |
| `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/connect-hello.setup-completion.test.ts` | 6 | 39.87 s |
| `src/gateway/server.auth.connect-metrics.test.ts` | 1 | 45.09 s |
| `src/infra/node-pairing-authz.test.ts` | 5 | 2.81 s |
| `src/gateway/server.node-pairing-authz.test.ts` | 17 | 55.70 s |
| `src/gateway/server-kernel.test.ts` (startup phase) | 1 | 50.10 s |
| `src/gateway/server.auth.test.ts` (device-token/mobile targets) | 2 | 47.31 s |

Prescribed production stat: `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD -- ':!*.test.ts' ':!*test-support*' ':!docs/*'` gives **18 files, +240/-26, net +214**; it includes two `.suite.ts` test files. Excluding those gives **16 runtime files, +217/-20, net +197**. Of that growth, 39 lines provide the requested queue/operation diagnostics. The rest supplies committed full-record publication, one tracked coalescer per device, and stale-approval protection while preserving mutable public getter results. It extends the existing owners and removes the awaited metadata path; no second state owner or durable compatibility path is added.

</details>
