prs.title: fix(telegram): stop DM topics inheriting the plain DM's model pin
prs.body:
Closes #131355

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a new Telegram DM topic silently uses the model pinned with `/model` in the plain DM (or, under the default `dmScope`, in the agent's main session) when the topic has no pin of its own.

## User Impact

User impact: each Telegram DM topic keeps its own `/model` choice. A topic without one uses the configured default. Replies, `/status`, and the native `/think`, `/fast`, and `/login` menus agree on that model. Forks and spawned sessions with a persisted parent still inherit from it, and Discord, Slack, and other channels' threads, plus Telegram forum (group) topics, still inherit from their parent conversation as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

A DM topic's session key is the DM's base key plus `:thread:<chat>:<topic>`. With no pin on the topic, the stored-model resolver derived a parent from that suffix and returned the base session's pin as `source: "parent"`. The base follows `dmScope` and bindings (`agent:main:main`, `agent:main:direct:<chat>`, `agent:main:telegram:direct:<chat>`, `agent:main:telegram:<account>:direct:<chat>`, or a bound key), so the key shape alone cannot identify a DM topic.

So the fix uses Telegram's own topic identity instead of key matching. `resolveTelegramTargetSession`, the one place that builds the topic key, now also returns `modelParentSessionKey: null`. The resolver treats an explicit `null` as "no model parent" instead of deriving one. The five inline `entry.parentSessionKey ?? ModelParentSessionKey ?? ParentSessionKey` chains in core move to one helper, `resolveModelParentSessionKey`, so the `null` is not lost to the `??` fallback. Telegram's native menu resolvers take the same value. When a DM topic has no pin and no persisted parent, the native menus resolve the model its next reply will use: the `channels.modelByChannel` match for the chat, else the agent default.

Things a reviewer should know:
- `MsgContext.ModelParentSessionKey`, `RouteFacts.modelParentSessionKey`, and the resolver's `parentSessionKey` widen from `string` to `string | null`. Existing producers are unaffected. A third-party plugin that reads the field into a `string | undefined` slot sees a new possible `null`.
- A persisted `entry.parentSessionKey` still wins over the channel's `null`. Telegram never sets `ParentSessionKey`, so DM topics have no such row unless something explicitly parented them.
- Native menus now honor a topic's persisted parent. Before, they only used the key-derived parent, so they could disagree with replies for a forked topic.
- A topic that already replied under the leaked pin still stores that model as `entry.model`. Native menus no longer read it for an unpinned DM topic, so they show the model the next reply uses, not the old pin.
- Out of scope: the Gateway session list (`src/gateway/session-utils-model-selection.ts`) has no Telegram topic identity and can still show the parent's model on an unpinned DM topic row.

This takes over the approach of #131387, which was closed for inactivity, without its file moves.

## Evidence

- Test commit first, fix on top. On the test commit, 7 new cases fail:
  - `src/sessions/stored-model-overrides.test.ts` "does not derive a parent when the channel declares the session has none": `expected { provider: 'anthropic', … } to be null` (1 of 9 fail).
  - `extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-context.dm-session.test.ts` drives the registered Telegram handler through `getReplyFromConfig` for each `dmScope` key shape. With `explicitParent=false`, the real `/status` reports `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6` (the DM pin) instead of the default `openai/gpt-5.4` (4 of 16 fail). The explicit-parent case passes on both commits.
  - `extensions/telegram/src/bot-native-command-dispatch.delivery.test.ts`: the native `/think` keyboard for an unpinned topic lists the DM model's 8 levels instead of `['default', 'off', 'ultra']`, and an explicitly parented topic's keyboard lacks the parent model's `max` (2 of 15 fail).
- With the fix: 9/9, 16/16, 15/15.
- Follow-up for the ClawSweeper finding on native menus (test b6cc9fa1ee8, fix 637f6027ed6). Two new `/think` keyboard cases in `bot-native-command-dispatch.delivery.test.ts` fail on 695676718a7: a topic row whose last-run model is the old DM pin lists that model's 8 levels instead of `['default', 'off', 'ultra']`, and a topic under `modelByChannel.telegram['*']` set to the reasoner model lacks `max`. Both pass with the fix (17/17, 20.7 s for the file). The Telegram native-command and DM-session test files pass 114/114. `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` pass, and `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` are clean.
- Touched area: 15 core test files (stored-model-overrides, model-selection*, get-reply*, dispatch-from-config*, native slash fast path, inbound-event context) 258/258 pass. 15 Telegram test files (dm-session, session routing, conversation route, native command dispatch, model callback, login) 236/236 pass.
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` are clean on the changed files, and `git diff --check` is clean. `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, and `pnpm tsgo:test:src` (21/21 shards) pass.

prs.title: fix(control-ui): saved reasoning stays hidden when reasoning comes from reasoningDefault
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/79469

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Control UI chat hides saved reasoning when reasoning is enabled through `agents.defaults.reasoningDefault` or `agents.entries.<id>.reasoningDefault` instead of a per-session `/reasoning` override, even with View > Reasoning on. This is the remaining case in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/79469.

## User Impact

User impact: operators who turn reasoning on with a configured default now see each completed answer's saved reasoning in the Control UI, live and after reload. An explicit session `/reasoning off` or `stream` still wins, and View > Reasoning still hides it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The transcript gate read only the session's stored `reasoningLevel`. A session that inherits the configured default has no stored value, so the gate treated it as off. The Gateway row now carries `reasoningDefault` beside the stored `reasoningLevel`, resolved per agent the same way `/status` resolves it (agent entry, then `agents.defaults`). Unlike the catalog-backed `thinkingDefault`, which `sessions.changed` snapshots drop, `reasoningDefault` depends only on config, so the snapshot carries it too. The UI uses `reasoningLevel ?? reasoningDefault`. Because the UI resolves the override first, a local `/reasoning` change applies immediately.

Reply-time resolution and its authorization check are unchanged. The UI only decides whether to render reasoning that the transcript already stores for the operator, as it does today for an explicit session override. The protocol schema is unchanged; the field is additive on Gateway session rows, like `effectiveFastMode`.

## Evidence

Tested at `f5ba4773645` (base `upstream/main` `b53ba16c63a`). The browser proof ran at `699f5adbfba`. Later commits only move and type the Gateway regression test (now in `src/gateway/session-utils-row.materialize.test.ts`); production code is identical.

Real Gateway (`openclaw gateway run`, loopback, isolated HOME and state directory) serving a Control UI built from the same commit, driven by headless Chromium. Config: `agents.defaults.reasoningDefault: "on"`. The model is a keyless OpenAI-compatible stub on loopback that streams `reasoning_content` and then the answer. Steps: open `/chat`, send `hi`, wait for the answer, reload, then send `/reasoning off` and reload again.

Before (base `b53ba16c63a`):

```text
{"answerShown":true,"reasoningShownAfterAnswer":false,"answerShownAfterReload":true,"reasoningShownAfterReload":false,"answerShownWithSessionOff":true,"reasoningShownWithSessionOff":false}
```

`chat.history` shows that the reasoning is saved: the assistant message holds `{"type":"thinking","thinking":"STUB-REASONING thinking about it"}` before `{"type":"text","text":"STUB-ANSWER"}`. The session row carries no inherited level.

After (this PR):

```text
{"answerShown":true,"reasoningShownAfterAnswer":true,"answerShownAfterReload":true,"reasoningShownAfterReload":true,"answerShownWithSessionOff":true,"reasoningShownWithSessionOff":false}
```

`sessions.list` after `/reasoning off`, with the session override and the inherited default side by side:

```text
      "key": "agent:main:main",
      "reasoningLevel": "off",
      "reasoningDefault": "on",
```

Observed result: the inherited reasoning shows after the answer and after reload. An explicit session `/reasoning off` still hides it.

| Before (after reload) | After (after reload) | After, session `/reasoning off` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![Before: answer only](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261015-issue-79469/before.png) | ![After: Reasoning block above the answer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261015-issue-79469/after.png) | ![After: explicit off hides reasoning](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261015-issue-79469/after-session-off.png) |

Regression tests fail on the base and pass on this branch:
- `projectChatReasoning`: inherited `on` shows, inherited `stream` hides completed reasoning, an explicit override wins in both directions.
- Gateway row and snapshot: the per-agent default wins over `agents.defaults`.

The existing browser suite for explicit levels still passes: `pnpm test:ui:e2e ui/src/e2e/chat-reasoning-visibility.e2e.test.ts`, 6 of 6 (`on`/`off`/`stream`, with and without tools).

Simplification pass against the merge base: production +10/−2 in 4 files, tests +42 in 2. Nothing was removed; the growth is one session-row field and its use in the UI gate. Explicit overrides, View > Reasoning and reply-time authorization keep their existing behavior and tests.

Checks: the touched tests (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`) pass. `pnpm check:changed` scoped to the changed files passes typecheck (core, core tests, UI), format and the ratchets. Three lanes failed locally without naming a changed file: the max-lines ledger (stale entries already removed on `main`), the dead-export scan (unrelated exports) and core lint, which could not load its config because the local install lacks `eslint-plugin-solid`. Lint and the broad suites run in this PR's CI.

| Test file | `--maxWorkers=1` wall |
| --- | --- |
| `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-reasoning.test.ts` | 5.1 s (new test 1 ms) |
| `src/gateway/session-utils-row.materialize.test.ts` | 16.3 s (new test 0.6 s) |

Not covered: the per-agent default is proven by the Gateway test, not in the browser run. A session with no configured default, where reply time may still enable reasoning from the model's capability, keeps today's behavior: model-capability defaults need the model catalog, which is where earlier attempts (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/118682, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/128249) stalled. Native apps are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(cron): restore inherited native job authoring on October
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Restores the old pinned release's inherited-tool authoring contract for ordinary jobs created or edited from native Codex conversations. This prevents a task-content edit from introducing a finite `toolsAllow` list that removes the native tools the job relies on.

## User Impact

Ordinary scheduled agent turns authored from native Codex conversations preserve inherited tools. A newly authored finite selection is intentionally rejected before saving, with instructions to retry a content-only edit without changing tool policy. Existing saved restrictions are not migrated by this patch; restoring inherited tools remains an explicit owner-authorized operation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The requested compatibility baseline is old pin [06b999fa4fcb](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/06b999fa4fcb3d6cc1d5c3836420ca7532845cca). It contains [5b33b1f0c3c](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/5b33b1f0c3c7ae8fafd1b17caae530d3f485dcea), which rejects newly authored per-job tool restrictions at both add and update. Its description states that scheduled work uses the agent's current tools. The October base accepts those writes and recommends finite caps again.

This intentionally restores rejection for ordinary native-conversation authoring. It does not claim that finite-list jobs are inherently unexecutable: the existing policy-filtered OpenClaw fallback can execute deliberate restrictions. That execution path and stored restrictions remain unchanged. Script payloads, condition triggers, non-native creators, and CLI/Gateway restrictions keep their current behavior and authorization checks. This is a scoped release compatibility repair, not a complete backport of the old scheduler or a removal of restricted-job support from main.

Targets `kimiyu_openclaw_2026-10-01-beta1-reviewed`, based on `f155b936161ae58720bdc983eed4ec5743607438`.

## Evidence

- Boundary regression tests exercise the real Codex capture and cron tool entry with a mocked Gateway transport. They cover add/update with native names, canonical names, and empty selections; rejected writes do not mutate state, content-only retries preserve policy, and script/trigger selections remain supported. Three initial regression cases failed against the unchanged base because the cap writes succeeded.
- Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/cron-tool.test.ts src/agents/tools/cron-tool.management.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/codex-mcp-projection.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed 91 tests on Node 24.16.0. Final warm wall time: 13.74s across two shards; hosted CI time is not yet available.

Command: `node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs --changed-paths-json '["src/agents/tools/cron-tool.test.ts"]' --concurrency 1` passed the agents-tools test graph.
- Focused `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` over the five changed TypeScript files, `oxfmt --check` over all six changed files, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Command: `pnpm build` exited 0 in 11m 9.9s. It also reported a UI startup JS budget overage (365.9 KiB versus 364.7 KiB); baseline attribution for that report is unverified. No UI files changed.
- Independent autoreview found no P0-P2 issues in the production patch. Subsequent edits only corrected test assertions. No deployed-candidate end-to-end run or full repository test suite was performed.
- Wording-only follow-up `9207458b163fe7e2d093a97572605cfb3e01aa49`: the same 91 cron/capture tests passed in 32.65s wall. The existing finite-list shell fallback regression also passed (1 selected test, 115 unselected; 29.99s wall), confirming the restricted runtime remains available. Focused lint/format and diff sanity passed. No executor or permission logic changed in this follow-up.
- [Hosted re-review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173503#issuecomment-6203573915) completed on `9207458b163fe7e2d093a97572605cfb3e01aa49` with no actionable findings. The prior authoring-capability finding was withdrawn after verifying the accepted October compatibility scope. This is review clearance, not passing CI or deployed end-to-end proof.


### Current CI blocker

At current head `9207458b163fe7e2d093a97572605cfb3e01aa49`, `security-fast` failed in [Audit production dependencies](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38817999354/job/116707757168) on the same three advisory IDs below; `openclaw/ci-gate` consequently failed and other jobs were cancelled. prs.title: fix: queued messages show no typing indicator while they wait behind a live run
prs.body:
Closes #162547

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a direct message that queues behind a live run shows no typing indicator for the whole wait, even though `docs/concepts/queue.md` says typing still fires on enqueue.

## User Impact

User impact: on Telegram and other channels whose turns carry an adoption lifecycle, a message queued behind a busy session keeps showing "typing…" until its own run starts and replies. Typing stops when the queued item finishes, is cancelled, or is dropped from the queue. Messages that do not queue are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The enqueue path already signals typing when a follow-up queues behind a live run, and the follow-up runner keeps the same typing controller. But the buffered dispatcher that handled the inbound message then returns. Its dispatcher idle callback and its `finally` (`markRunComplete` and `markDispatchIdle` in `src/auto-reply/dispatch.ts`) seal that controller and call the channel's `onIdle`, which closes the channel typing loop for good. So typing starts and stops within the same ~360 ms dispatch the issue's log shows (`message dispatch completed ... duration=363ms`).

Related: #92287 starts typing when a queued turn begins to execute (#92267). This change covers the wait before that, and keeps the controller that run would use from being sealed when the inbound dispatch returns.

This follows the direction in the ClawSweeper review: the queued item owns typing from enqueue to settlement.

- `createReplyDispatcherWithTyping` returns a new internal `onTypingHandoff` reply option. It lives in `InternalReplySessionOptions` next to `onReplyOperationOwned`, not in the public `GetReplyOptions`, and `publicReplyOptions` strips it from plugin-supplied options. Core builds these reply options itself in `dispatchReplyWithBufferedBlockDispatcher`, so Telegram still gets the handoff. After it is called, the dispatcher no longer completes the typing controller. When typing comes only from `typingCallbacks`, their `onIdle` (typing teardown) is deferred, and the queued item's typing cleanup runs `onCleanup` and then that `onIdle` once. The handoff state lives in `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-dispatcher-typing-handoff.ts`.
- A channel that passes its own `onIdle` gets no `onTypingHandoff`, so its whole typing lifecycle is unchanged. That `onIdle` can do more than stop typing: Feishu's (`extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.ts:1232`, `queueIdleSideEffects`) finalizes streaming delivery and closes the card preview. Deferring it made finalization wait on itself (ClawSweeper revision 3). Running it while the handed-off controller kept ticking let the next tick's `onReplyStart` reopen the closed preview (revision 5). So Feishu does not get typing through the queued wait. Channels that pass only `typingCallbacks`, such as Telegram, do.
- `runReplyAgent`, on the enqueue-behind-a-live-run path, closes typing from the queued item's `turnAdoptionLifecycle.onSettled`. Queue completion calls that for a run that finished, a cancelled item, a cleared queue, and the sources of a collected batch.
- The handoff happens only when the follow-up has an adoption lifecycle and queued typing actually started (`typing.isActive()` after `signalToolStart`). Without a lifecycle nothing would settle the typing. In `message` typing mode typing does not start before text, so the controller's `cleanup` never calls `onCleanup` and a deferred `onIdle` would never run. Both cases keep today's behavior. That keeps a dropped item from leaving a typing loop running forever.
- The dispatcher exposes `onTypingHandoff` only when the channel supplied a cleanup callback, because the deferred `onIdle` runs from that callback.
- Each queued `FollowupRun` now carries the typing controller of the dispatch that queued it (`typing`), and the follow-up runner completes that one (`queued.typing ?? defaults.typing`). The queue keeps only the latest runner per key, so before this an earlier queued message, when it finished, completed the later message's controller and sealed it before that message's own turn (ClawSweeper revision 6).

`waitForReplyDispatcherIdle` moved to `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-dispatcher-idle.ts` with main's current body (including its `abortSignal` handling), the queued item's `onSettled` wrap lives in `bindQueuedFollowupTyping` in `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-run-typing.ts`, and the two queued-typing cases moved to `agent-runner.runreplyagent.queued-typing.cases.ts`, so the line-cap ratchet holds for `reply-dispatcher.ts`, `agent-runner-run.ts`, and the runner e2e file.

## Evidence

- New `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-utils.test.ts` case drives a real `createReplyDispatcherWithTyping`, `createTypingController`, and `createTypingCallbacks` (channel TTL off, as on Telegram) through handoff, dispatcher idle, `markRunComplete`, and `markDispatchIdle`. On the test commit the channel `start` runs 0 times in the next 60 s. On the fix it runs 30 times, `stop` is not called during the wait, and `stop` runs once after the queued run settles.
- New `agent-runner.runreplyagent.queued-typing.cases.ts` case: a follow-up with a lifecycle queued behind a live run calls `onTypingHandoff` once and keeps typing open, and `completeFollowupRunLifecycle` on the queued item cleans typing up once. On the test commit `onTypingHandoff` is called 0 times.
- Channel with its own idle (ClawSweeper revisions 3 and 5, fixed in 0f720c428ae). The `reply-utils.test.ts` case with distinct `onReplyStart`, `onIdle`, and `onCleanup` callbacks uses fake timers: it calls the handoff option if offered, completes the run and the dispatcher, then advances 5 s. On 4f0fc716970 it fails: the controller never cleans up (`["idle"]` instead of `["cleanup", "idle"]`) and keeps calling `onReplyStart`, which is the call that reopens a Feishu preview. On 0f720c428ae it passes: cleanup and `onIdle` run once at dispatcher idle, and `onReplyStart` is not called again. It replaces the case that raced finalization against a real 50 ms timer.
- Message typing mode. New `queued-typing.cases.ts` case: a follow-up queued behind a live run in `message` mode never starts typing, so it must not take over idle. On 10d05599818 `onTypingHandoff` is called once. On a0ebdb83961 it is called 0 times. The existing handoff case now marks the mock controller active when its typing loop starts, as the real controller does.
- Two messages queued behind one live run (ClawSweeper revision 6, fixed in 2c7c47c9acd). New `followup-runner.test.ts` case runs a queued item that carries its own controller through a runner whose default controller belongs to a later message. On 0f720c428ae it fails: the item's own `markRunComplete` runs 0 times and the later message's controller is completed instead. On 2c7c47c9acd it passes: the item's own controller is completed once and the later one is untouched. The queued-typing handoff case now also checks that the enqueued run carries the dispatch's controller.
- On 2c7c47c9acd: `followup-runner` 30/30, `src/auto-reply/reply/queue` 75/75, `agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts` 226/226 with the e2e config, `dispatch-from-config.delivery.test.ts` 294/294, `extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts` 79/79, `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` pass.
- On 0f720c428ae: `reply-utils` and `reply-flow` 74/74, `extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts` 79/79, `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` exit 0, `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` on the changed files clean. `agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts` (226/226 on 4f0fc716970) was not rerun: this commit does not touch the runner, and its queued-typing cases pass a mock `onTypingHandoff`.
- CI on 0f720c428ae: `checks-node-changed-1` failed in `src/agents/model-fallback.reply-entry.e2e.test.ts` and `checks-node-changed-5` in `dispatch-from-config.delivery.test.ts` ("delivers deferred Telegram text when generation fails after a block"). Both assert the old error copy ("API rate limit reached", "Authentication failed", "Something went wrong") that main changed in d0b48d63efb (#163381) after this branch's base. CI's merge ref picked up the new copy. Main updated the delivery test in 08eb496e2c6. The model-fallback e2e on main still expects the old strings. On this branch's base the delivery file passes locally (294/294) and the model-fallback e2e passed 10/10 in an earlier pass. This PR does not touch the error copy.
- Earlier, on a0ebdb83961: rebased onto upstream/main 836087a89a4 (green CI); `src/agents/model-fallback.reply-entry.e2e.test.ts`, red in an earlier CI run and on main at that time, passed 10/10 locally.
- 2026-10-05: rebased onto upstream/main e7edee1790d to clear a conflict (main added an import next to this PR's import in `agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts`; both kept, no code change). On 8afd852ac2d: `followup-runner`, `reply-flow`, and `reply-utils` 103/103, `agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts` 226/226 with the e2e config, `pnpm tsgo:core` exit 0. The other suites listed above were not rerun after the rebase.
- 2026-10-06: rebased onto upstream/main d8a62a83f37 after main's #166085 deleted `reply-dispatcher-observers.ts` and made `invokeReplyDispatcherObserver` local to `reply-dispatcher.ts`. 242a714b8d8 resolves it: `createReplyDispatcherWithTyping` wraps the channel idle in that observer guard once and passes it to `createTypingHandoff`, which no longer imports anything. Commit ids in the bullets above name the head they were measured on; the 2026-10-09 line below gives the current ones. On 242a714b8d8: `followup-runner`, `reply-flow`, `reply-utils`, and `src/auto-reply/reply/queue` 179/179, `dispatch-from-config.delivery.test.ts` and `extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts` 373/373, `pnpm tsgo:core` exit 0, `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` clean. `agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts` was not usable locally: most cases fail with "Session database target changed outside captured discovery custody", and three of them fail the same way on d8a62a83f37 with no PR changes.

## What Problem This Solves

Real-Gateway UI row 1 is the last substantive job in 10 of 20 recent completed same-repository PR CI runs. It finishes after row 2 in all ten paired observations.

## User Impact

There is no product behavior change. The same selected tests and desktop proof run once across the existing two jobs, with unchanged worker limits, runners, previews and deadlines.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove an old six-file balancing override. Required serial and desktop fixtures stay on row 1; already-audited parallel fixtures use row 2's existing bounded worker pool. This deletes a separate parallel phase from the busy serial row without introducing another scheduler.

The observed cohort has an 18.84-minute median wall and 19.35-minute p75, versus an earlier four-run median of 25.7 minutes; the scope mix differs. Two paired logs show 104–119 seconds in the extra phase. Measured-file replay projects a 17.59-minute median and 19.04-minute p75, but two already-balanced samples could be 93 and 30 seconds slower. These are projections; natural CI must establish the actual result.

- Sample runs include 38815238931 and 38814691623; both job pages were checked for all 20 exact run/head pairs. Assignment waits are mostly 1–2 seconds.

prs.title: fix(update): honor drain deadline before status RPC dispatch
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes deployment deferral when a graceful drain deadline expires while preparing its next status poll, before the CLI starts.

## User Impact

An authorized bounded drain reaches its existing deadline policy instead of aborting the prepared update. Defer-only updates still defer. Fresh status, lease, process-generation, and write-custody checks still gate interruption. Controller adoption remains a separate operator action; this PR does not deploy or restart a Gateway.

## Why This Change Was Made

The outer poll loop can observe remaining time, then request preparation consumes that time. The RPC subprocess owner returned generic exit 1 without dispatching anything, which the transient-poll classifier correctly treated as fatal. Return the existing timeout exit 124 for pre-dispatch drain expiry, just as for an exhausted subprocess budget. This reuses the existing bounded retry/deadline owner; no new retry loop, admission bypass, configuration, or schema change.

## Evidence

The observed failure occurred at the 30-second drain boundary without a status RPC subprocess launch; the lease had approximately 90 seconds remaining. That strongly supports local deadline exhaustion rather than lease expiry or an RPC admission refusal. No raw failure payload was retained, so this is a source-backed diagnosis, reproduced deterministically through the controller's existing virtual-clock shell harness.

Before: all three new regression cases failed, showing exit 1 and premature deferral. After: all 32 tests in `drain-deadline.test.mjs` passed (51.24 seconds on a busy Mac). The regression proves zero expired-budget dispatches, fresh status plus generation proof before authorized interruption, refusal of pending terminal persistence, and defer-only behavior. Existing tests cover typed transport retries, fatal protocol/authentication failures, and original-budget exhaustion.

Command: `node --import ./.agents/skills/update-team-server/controller/test-environment.mjs --test .agents/skills/update-team-server/controller/drain-deadline.test.mjs`.

This is a correctness repair; no throughput or memory improvement is claimed, and no benchmark or live deployment was run. No Testbox/Crabbox allocated. PR CI passed on `cea551476071b7f4fc0bc9dc4e390a8903c587f9`: [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38818854783), with both required `openclaw/ci-gate` checks successful. No CI retries were needed. The privileged full controller cutover suite and live deployment were not exercised. The production change is one return code plus one explanatory comment (net +1 line); tests add 23 net lines. A smaller fix cannot preserve the reason for this otherwise non-obvious exit code.

Shell syntax, Node syntax, changed-file formatting, and single-file syntax lint passed. The ordinary lint wrapper began package-artifact preparation despite an explicit file target; it was stopped to respect the local compute limit, and the supported focused-config mode passed. Existing brace-style violations in the touched test were fixed mechanically.

Review: independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable), clean through P2.

prs.title: fix(tests): keep shutdown and stale recovery checks reliable
prs.body:
Related: #173342

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Gateway shutdown/admission and auto-reply recovery test failures seen in main CI run 38810511907.

## User Impact

Test-only repair. Process stops continue preserving unfinished turns for the next start; completed graceful work remains successful.

## Why This Change Was Made

#173342 deliberately made ordinary process stop use typed restart interruption so terminal cleanup cannot discard recovery custody. Two older Gateway fixtures still expected no recovery marking and an RPC cancellation. The shutdown fixture now verifies the durable marker, entry fence, cancellation ordering, original command/finalizer settlement, and foreign-Gateway isolation for both stop and restart. Graceful completion explicitly requires no recovery marker, no aborted signal, and no terminal stop reason. Late admission still proves the provider never starts.

The stale pre-backend recovery case passes alone but reproduces the hourly `null` versus `run_stalled` failure in its 49-file CI selection. Its one-second polling wait raced asynchronous dispatch preparation. Waiting for the existing operation abort event makes the test advance the unchanged terminal-settlement clock at actual expiry. The replay also reproduced the same polling race in the two adjacent delivery-settlement cases. Those cases now await explicit fixture-owned delivery and follow-up milestones. All result, retained-owner, resolver, final-delivery, and ordering assertions remain. No retries, timeout increases, skips, or shared test-helper changes.

## Evidence

Before: Gateway shutdown 2 failed / 1 passed; late admission 1 failed, both matching the hourly signatures on current main. Auto-reply passes alone (22/22), then reproduces the identical failure in the CI shard selection at `--maxWorkers=1`.

After focused `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`: shutdown 3/3 (54.73s Vitest / 64.64s wrapper), late admission 1/1 (48.57s / 58.86s), terminal recovery 22/22 (92.65s / 118.44s). These Gateway files exercise a real isolated server and lifecycle ownership, so they cannot be replaced by a cheaper pure-helper test.

Adjacent delivery-settlement file: 13/13 (166.83s Vitest; 196.12s wrapper). Reply lifecycle siblings: 83/83 (14 recovery-admission + 69 registry cases). Gateway lifecycle siblings: 87/87 across server-close, server-run-shutdown.recovery, and session-lifecycle-state.recovery (164.81s Vitest; 186.46s wrapper). Gateway-server and messaging typecheck graphs passed; changed-file type-aware lint, boundary lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed. Isolated P2 review is scoped-clean with no accepted/actionable findings. The separate P2 review of the adjacent delivery-settlement repair is also scoped-clean. The completed 49-file Mac reply replay ran 630 cases: 627 passed and 3 failed (859.04s). Two failures are the adjacent settlement cases subsequently repaired and proven 13/13; the third is an untouched directive-acknowledgement wait in active-command, recorded as a local proof gap. Both complete 26-file Gateway selections also ran: shard 4 had 271 passed / 1 untouched RPC failure (1324.01s), and shard 2 had 184 passed / 1 untouched subprocess timeout (1219.76s). All reported target cases passed in shard order. Mac replay gaps: untouched `chat.send fences the admitted session settings` exceeded its RPC deadline in the broad replay, then passed the exact focused command (1 case; 127.76s Vitest including cold setup; 146.47s wrapper). The untouched fixture-lifecycle child process exceeded its existing 90s managed-command deadline; it passed the cited hourly job in 46.82s. These remain recorded local failures, not repaired by this patch. Their deadlines are unchanged; PR CI supplies broad proof.

prs.title: fix(cron): let CLI-runtime automations run under their own login
prs.body:
Related: #172590

## What Problem This Solves

CLI-runtime automations must use their CLI's own login, without adopting an OpenClaw inference account or inheriting host API credentials.

## User Impact

CLI-runtime agent-turn automations can run without an inference binding. Embedded automations retain recorded-account ownership, explicit legacy adoption, and explicit failures for lost, revoked, or incompatible accounts; environment-only and provider-config keys still cannot establish ownership.

## Why This Change Was Made

Peter's decision (2026-10-14): a CLI runtime authenticates with its own login; OpenClaw passes it no host inference credentials. Admission and creation support already landed in #172717 and #172794. This focused follow-up closes the remaining execution-boundary gap: live-test preserve-env and configured/prepared environment overlays could restore host credentials.

Native-only execution now enforces the backend's environment exclusions and removes known provider-auth environment variables after local overlays, including credentials for other providers. Paired-node execution also receives the provider exclusions. Prepared non-auth runtime settings remain available, and interactive profile selection keeps its existing behavior. Stored profile forwarding is already disabled by native-only preparation. Since no host inference credentials cross into the CLI runtime on this path, changing OpenClaw's interactive account or billing defaults cannot silently switch the automation's host-managed account. The CLI's own login and native authorization remain authoritative.

Native-only exclusions match environment names case-insensitively so Windows casing cannot bypass the boundary.

@fuller-stack-dev, please review the credential boundary and preserved embedded ownership guarantees as the owner of #172590. Per Peter's instruction, this PR will wait for your review, or 24 hours without a response, before landing; normal CI and enforced review gates still apply.

## Evidence

- Original S3 census: **15/15 cases pass** on the main-based branch, with no missing cases.
- Selected cron/Gateway/CLI account-ownership proof: **166 tests across 15 files passed** before the final casing refinement, including embedded auth continuity, revoked/incompatible binding behavior, CLI admission/preparation, and lint-suppression checks. Unchanged cron/Gateway proof is reused.
- Earlier CLI execution proof: **47 tests across 3 files passed**, including all 40 existing spawn cases, installation-target siblings, and four native-auth cases. This preceded environment-owner extraction and the final prepared-OAuth refinement; it is not exact-final-source proof. The new file had about 3.1 seconds of test time; the shared two-config wrapper took 212.61 seconds on the loaded local host, mostly compilation/import. Final-source and hosted CI timing are pending.
- Negative controls: the original credential regressions failed against unfixed execution; adding unrelated-provider keys produced three intended failures, and the alternate-casing expansion produced four intended failures before normalization.
- Prepared-OAuth negative control at the real environment owner failed before the fix (credential leaked, non-auth setting retained); the exact-source positive probe passes (credential absent, alternate-cased host-managed marker absent, non-auth setting retained). Only synthetic inputs and absence booleans were recorded.
- Fresh independent review of the exact four-file patch: scoped-clean, no actionable findings through P2. Review caught the prepared-OAuth gap, which was fixed before this final pass.
- Exact-source formatting and staged whitespace checks pass. Earlier runtime/import cycle checks found zero cycles; post-extraction cycles and final lint/types/changed-file proof remain pending. Local broad checks were interrupted under extreme host load rather than represented as passing. The final targeted lint attempt was interrupted in package-boundary artifact preparation (exit 130), before lint assertions. The supported Blacksmith Testbox wrapper also stalled during local source-capsule preparation and was interrupted at the no-progress limit; its test payload did not execute. Exact-head PR CI must supply the outstanding proof before landing.
- Earlier changed-file checking passed production/core-test type graphs but found inherited environment-inventory and unused-export failures; it also caught a new file-size violation, resolved by extracting the environment owner, and a capture-env optionality error, fixed before final review. No assertions, retries, timeouts, or suppressions were weakened.

All local OpenClaw execution uses task-owned HOME/state/config/XDG directories; no real Gateway or user state is used. Tests inspect only credential-absence booleans and synthetic fixture values, never print or serialize process environment.

prs.title: fix: automation details retain old locale after language changes
prs.body:
Related: #172212

## What Problem This Solves

Retained automation details keep the previous language after a locale change. Hovercard source paths also miss the existing WebKit interaction suite. Existing Settings and plugin-theme timeouts lack enough failure-only evidence to distinguish the state present when their waits fail.

## User Impact

Labels, schedules, accessible captions, and disconnected status update without reloading jobs or replacing the focused trigger. Existing cron loading, cancellation, reconnect, link behavior, tags, classes, markup, CSS, and lazy boundaries remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing reactive translation projection, track its revision when formatting schedules, derive status once, and share the identical open links. One additive owner glob selects hovercard renderers, browser fixtures, and styles in the existing first UI shard, preserving its three-row matrix and the disjoint presentation-owner entry in #171664.

On failure of the existing Settings `system.info` wait, a new bounded diagnostic collects document visibility/focus, host DOM attachment, host-system section presence/busy state, and `system.info`/`last-heartbeat` request counts. These sanitized scalar facts are collected within a new five-second diagnostic bound, then the original error is preserved. Assertions and the successful/reconnect flow stay unchanged. This is a diagnostic improvement, with no claimed Settings repair or inheritance finding.

| Production file | Before | After | Delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Automation renderer | 297 | 295 | −2 |
| CI manifest | 2,080 | 2,081 | +1 |
| Total | 2,377 | 2,376 | **−1** |

The plugin-theme test now also captures the theme owner mode, resolved mode, document mode, toggle label/role, and menu visibility/expanded/focus state only when its original next-label wait fails. The snapshot has a five-second bound and excludes identity text. The original click, wait, assertions, successful path, and thrown error are preserved. This supplies evidence for the unexplained CI timeout below; it does not claim a causal repair.

## Evidence

Current head `14b83f2ce8241757e952af94616984ce212d3a0b` normally merges published main `5fdd725db9ae4221bd735a879c3409a78feeb50b` to align the Security Review workflow source and pick up the published dependency graph. The complete authored effect remains six files, **227 additions / 50 deletions**: all added and removed text is unchanged after accounting for Git index and hunk addresses. The maintainer inspected the changed main manifest blocks and connection-test setup; the existing failure-only diagnostics remain intact. Production is **2,377 → 2,376 LOC (−1)** against this incoming base.

| Current-head check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Review | Retained isolated Codex review applies to the unchanged authored effect. The maintainer personally inspected the complete prospective patch and relevant changed main inputs before the normal merge. |
| Dependencies | `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` passed in this checkout’s separate dependency directory using the external pnpm store. |
| UI types | Fresh `pnpm tsgo:ui` passed on the integrated tree; the committed tree was verified identical. Production config excludes test files. |
| Scoped validation | Authored diff check passed. The normal merge had no conflicts. |
| Production Knip | One final-head run failed solely on unused `src/shared/safe-record.ts`. The same command failed identically once on exact incoming main `5fdd725d`, with a separate frozen install. Relevant config, dependency, helper, and former-caller blobs match. Both runs remain failed; no new ignore or core cleanup. |
| Focused proof | Locale 1/1 and selector 16/16 proof retained for unchanged inputs, with no repeat runs. |
| Full CI | Exact-head [run 38813416822](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38813416822), attempt 1, completed with `ci:full`: **77 jobs terminal — 52 successful, 23 skipped, 2 failed**. Sole failed leaf is browser shard 4 below; aggregate CI gate also failed. All UI unit, both real-Gateway, eight browser, independent security, and performance jobs passed. Previous-head results remain historical evidence. |
| Strict paired performance | Passed for this head: startup JS **350,740 B gzip**, 8 requests; CSS **45,894 B gzip**, **1 CSS request**. Same-runner Chat boot JS −13 B, New Session boot JS −10 B, CSS +0 B; request counts unchanged. Initial base startup-JS integer is not printed, so no initial-JS delta claim. |
| Native admission | Fresh review initialization, baseline/head checkouts, identity, guard, validation, and GitHub preparation passed at this exact head. Preparation is `github_pending`; CI and Knip remain failed as recorded. Final exception inspection and selected-head replacement recovery are pending. The original auto request remains confirmed cancelled and will not be re-armed. |

The current browser failure is one unhandled rejection: `route.fulfill: Route is already handled!` at `ui/src/e2e/control-ui-e2e-suite.test-support.ts:140:19`, attributed to `ui/src/e2e/chat-native-turn-activity.e2e.test.ts`. Its last case was `keeps roster activity until terminal delivery while chat foreground activity resumes on tools and retries`; the assertion itself passed in 2,964 ms. All **95 files / 421 cases** passed, but the unhandled error correctly kept the job failed. The capture-time most recent completed scheduled-main run `38810511907` ran this exact case in **browser shard 6**, where it passed in **3,456 ms** with no route error. That is a nonreproduction, with no causal repair or matching-failure claim. The published table calls browser shard 4 **new** because its same-number main job passed without comparing selected scope. Manual attribution reuses the retained real-browser baseline reproduction of the unchanged shared held-response helper from #173470. All 15 selected fixture/dependency inputs, actual E2E config and selected direct runner inputs match actual CI base `07f22451` and tested merge `6f84e06d`. Prior-reproduction differences are inspected failure-capture code and one unrelated private-suite inventory entry. The reproduction used two registrations; the original test has one registration that can receive multiple callbacks, and neither CI run recorded the exact callback interleaving. Locked Playwright/Vitest contracts match, while identical OS, hardware or timing is not claimed. The maintainer personally inspected and accepted this source-equivalent inherited-fixture attribution. The failed result remains failed; fresh exact-head native validation and GitHub preparation have now passed; final exception inspection still gates recovery. No CI rerun, assertion change, or failure suppression was used.

A fresh pre-admission scheduled-main observation found newer [run 38817599758](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38817599758), head `ed4bb8ca`, **queued** at observation. It has no completed named-case result to compare yet. Run `38810511907` above is the capture-time completed comparison. Attribution remains based on pinned actual CI base/tested merge and the retained baseline fixture reproduction, with the stated limits.

## Historical CI and recovery evidence

The following results apply to the earlier `6823` and `a5` heads. They are preserved to distinguish observed failures, later nonreproductions, and current-head proof.

<details>
<summary>Earlier heads: complete CI, source attribution, performance, and recovery history</summary>


Head `6823c0a00a7f37fdc71a3bab5f6f32d17c6bb38b` adds only that failure diagnostic to the prior reviewed head. The complete authored scope is six files, 227 additions / 50 deletions, with production still **−1 LOC**. The diagnostic accounts for 44 additions / 6 deletions in one E2E file.

| Earlier `6823` check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Independent review | Fresh isolated Codex review through P2 completed with no actionable findings; final source verification passed. Prior full-patch review remains applicable to unchanged inputs. |
| UI types | `pnpm tsgo:ui` passed; production config excludes test files. |
| Scoped formatting/lint | Passed for the diagnostic after correcting a shadowed local variable; `git diff --check` passed. |
| Production Knip | Final-head `pnpm deadcode:knip` passed once with no findings or new ignores. |
| Focused proof | Existing locale 1/1 and selector 16/16 proof retained on unchanged inputs; no local E2E or repeat runs. The diagnostic preserves the test's assertions and success path. |
| Full CI | Exact-head [run 38798789840](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38798789840), attempt 1, completed with `ci:full`: **77 jobs terminal — 52 successful, 23 skipped, 2 failed**. The sole failed leaf is the update-run case below; the other failure is its aggregate CI gate. All three UI unit shards, both real-Gateway shards, eight browser shards, `security-fast`, and performance passed. |
| Current plugin-theme case | `forwards an explicit host theme and live switches without reloading the plugin frame` passed in **5,710 ms**; all **6/6** plugin-tab-slugs cases passed. No failure-only diagnostic was emitted. This pass does not explain or repair the older a5 timeout. |
| Source binding and native admission | Source qualification complete: actual CI merge `9b669543` has ordered parents actual base `488bfb5f` and this head; independent merge-tree reconstruction matches, and all 23 selected update-run inputs are identical. Actual CI base is an ancestor of captured protected main `04adf167`. Exact `6823` native review, guard, validation, and GitHub preparation completed with `github_pending`. Replacement recovery stopped before new intent or dispatch because the branch retained the older `actions/setup-node` pin in the Security Review workflow. The retained confirmed-cancellation outcome stayed unchanged. This named owner-source mismatch prompted the normal main integration above. |
| Strict paired performance | Passed for this head: startup JS **350,435 B gzip**, CSS **45,894 B gzip**, **1 startup CSS request**. Same-runner CSS +0 B; Chat boot JS −23 B and New Session boot JS −14 B, with request counts unchanged at 31 and 29. Initial base JS integer is not printed; no initial-JS delta claim. |

The current failed test is `ui/src/e2e/update-run.e2e.test.ts > Control UI update run E2E > resumes the same update after restart and keeps its successful report visible`: the successful report headline timed out after 30 seconds at `225:68`. The full test name, headline locator, timeout, and fixture stack matched the capture-time scheduled-main [run 38794323475](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38794323475), job `116627031569`. The published failure table classifies the job as pre-existing by **job name only**; the exact case and assertion were compared manually. Selected-head tested-merge/source qualification is complete; the `6823` native preparation completed and its recovery later stopped on the workflow-owner source mismatch. That CI result remains failed. GitHub’s 220-file listing exactly matches its retained historical base range; the actual fork-to-head effect is six files, 227 additions / 50 deletions. All seven main integrations are ordinary two-parent merges, the five authored commits are unique, and the other 214 listed paths are historical-only. No main replay or branch rebuild was found.

The later completed scheduled-main [run 38802524013](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38802524013), head `6a38d58970dc86332a5835bdc6e2e31ae4ca60fe`, passed the exact update-run case in **6,720 ms** in job `116655529755`. This is a later nonreproduction, with no causal-repair claim. The `38794323475` comparison above is capture-time matching-failure evidence, not a claim that the latest main run fails. Between that capture-time baseline and the actual `6823` CI base, 22 of the original 23 broad source inputs are identical; the sole difference adds an unrelated Ollama integration test to the isolated-tooling inventory. Ten additional update-page, fixture, and runtime inputs were also checked and are identical across that baseline, actual CI base, and tested merge. These historical bindings do not admit the new integrated head.

## Prior-head evidence and unresolved failure

Head `a5f684253970d689f66d51c3ac95684daa66ee3e` integrates published main `ace190874ae363df1d3dd70af959811783ed714a` by a normal merge after GitHub mergeability remained `UNKNOWN`. Its authored patch is byte-identical: five files, 183 additions / 44 deletions, production −1 line. The integration adds no authored runtime or dependency/version change.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Review | Completed isolated Codex review retained for the byte-identical patch; scoped-clean, zero findings. Maintainer personally inspected the full prospective patch and all four changed main inputs. |
| Prior production UI types | `pnpm tsgo:ui` passed on the exact integrated tree; production config excludes test files |
| Prior production Knip | Knip 6.40.0 passed once on the exact integrated tree in 11m 26.84s; no findings or new ignores |
| Focused local regressions | Retained unchanged-input locale 1/1 and selector 16/16 proof, one worker each; no repeats |
| Prior full CI | Exact-head run [38745857592](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38745857592), attempt 1, completed failed: all 77 jobs terminal. All three UI unit shards, both real-Gateway shards, eight browser shards, independent security and performance passed. Browser shard 7 has one unresolved plugin-theme failure; no inherited-only qualification. |
| Prior strict performance | Passed: startup JS 350,304 B gzip, CSS 45,955 B gzip, one CSS request. Same-runner CSS +0 B, Chat boot +2 B, New Session boot +5 B. Base initial-JS integer is not printed; no initial-JS delta claim. |
| Prior WebKit | Nested hovercard checks passed: one job 424 ms, two jobs 476 ms, including keyboard focus, Escape/flyout dismissal and disconnected definitions. |
| Actual tested merge | Merge `5053e0a7a0cd4f414767faba168c31603be3ca7f` has ordered parents actual base `3f9822434aa62b044883dc5f8212dea8e359623b` and a5 head. Its derived tree matches, and its actual base-to-merge effect is byte-identical to the five reviewed paths. |

The unresolved test is `Control UI plugin tab slugs > forwards an explicit host theme and live switches without reloading the plugin frame`: the System color-mode click completed, then the next `Color mode: Light` menu label timed out after 30 seconds at `plugin-tab-slugs.e2e.test.ts:197`. **The a5 CI failure remains unknown.** The uploaded failure diagnostic shows a responsive, connected plugin page but does not record the theme/menu state needed to identify the cause; the runner's private DOM and screenshot were not uploaded.

| Additional attribution evidence | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Unchanged case on actual CI base | [Blacksmith run 38792289325](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38792289325): the exact plugin-theme case passed in **3,205 ms**, with one test passed and five excluded by the name filter. The collected command result is **exit 0**. |
| Latest scheduled main | [Run 38787185097](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38787185097), head `486f5b5181fb4d8220456602d0dba01b5bd8955b`: the same case passed in **2,679 ms** in browser job 116602330598. |
| Remote cleanup | The passing command and source/resource artifacts were collected. The wrapper exited 1 on a GitHub settlement-read deadline after the test; a supported native stop retry exited 0 after canonical settlement completed. The retained lease record is completed, has no host, and is not ready. No active lease remains. |

The remote source receiver verified actual CI base `3f9822434aa62b044883dc5f8212dea8e359623b`, tree `128ff681156204d0a13abce8c04acb553492a919`, and the payload verified all 27 bound source hashes after frozen installation. The unchanged single-case command used `--project ui-e2e-bundled --testNamePattern "forwards an explicit host theme and live switches without reloading the plugin frame$" --maxWorkers=1`. Measured capacity was four available CPUs and 16,555,134,976 bytes RAM; the default workflow's runner label says 16 vCPU, which is not the measured capacity. An earlier attempt was prematurely stopped during already-granted hydration before any payload or assertion; that lease was also fully settled. No provider/profile escalation, timeout, guard, fixture, or assertion change was used.

The exact-base and newer-main passes are **nonreproductions, not inherited-failure or causal-repair evidence**. Shared menu inputs changed on main after the actual CI base. Neither pass changes the failed a5 check result or qualifies its admission.

At reconciliation, GitHub's retained older `9e3514ae` base explained its 219-file range. The actual CI merge and prospective merge into captured protected main `e7a155a8ae860d71b1ab5eed45fa4af338011db9` each had exactly the reviewed five-file effect. Ordered parents are normal published-main merges; no main commits were replayed. Historical-head CI and admin artifacts do not qualify the new diagnostic head. Earlier Settings/palette timeouts remain unexplained; passing replays are not repair claims.

The a5 native review artifacts recorded `NEEDS WORK`, `tests.result: fail`, and no inherited-CI attribution. The diagnostic head requires fresh native review/preparation and its own CI; the historical failure remains unexplained. The original auto request remains confirmed retired and will not be re-armed; any replacement admission must use the documented selected-head recovery and bind the current reviewed head and actual gates.

</details>

Related to #165961

## What Problem This Solves

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes cancelled Doctor schema inspection poisoning unrelated database cleanup and Doctor operations in the same process.

## User Impact

Doctor on an independent state root remains usable. This does not grant another owner access to the retained original state.

## Why This Change Was Made

The regression began with #173225. Native lease cleanup already belongs to the active maintenance scope; registering the same cleanup with process-wide canonical close allowed a later close outside that scope to revisit it. Keep the existing maintenance owner authoritative while preserving canonical-close retention for ordinary native leases.

The node-hosting discovery stacks in hourly run 38810511907 were downstream symptoms: the first failure was the update-schema-guard owner-retirement case, and subsequent tests inherited that fixture's failed teardown. The five initially reported files pass alone on the original main; the first-failure case fails alone and passes when only #173225's production delta is removed. #173213's maintenance-contention retry addresses a separate failure class.

## Evidence

- Original main: the first schema-owner-retirement case fails alone with `StateDatabaseAccessError`. Removing only #173225's production delta passes that same case.
- Final focused regression: original refusal and byte preservation plus real Doctor maintenance/preflight on an independent root, 1 passed / 25 filtered; `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test src/commands/doctor-update-schema-guard.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'revalidates the update owner after integrity work'`, 58.62 seconds command wall (43.26 seconds Vitest; 10.873 seconds case).

- Core production and Doctor test types; scoped and boundary lint; formatting; docs MDX sanity; whitespace checks passed.
- Fresh isolated Codex review through P2: scoped-clean, no accepted/actionable findings.

The strengthened case uses real SQLite and maintenance admission to distinguish preserved original custody from an independent Doctor operation. Full Doctor sibling/shard coverage comes from PR CI. prs.title: perf(workspaces): skip dependency prewarm for disabled sandboxes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agents with sandboxing disabled still prepare dependency templates after Gateway startup. The default Docker backend passed the prewarm selection even when resolved sandbox mode was `off`, causing unnecessary Git discovery, checkout, container installation, and potentially recursive cleanup/recheckout after an install failure. This work can contend with foreground workspace preparation and chat turns.

## User Impact

Disabled agents skip background dependency preparation, including per-agent `off` overrides. Enabled `all`/`non-main` agents retain prewarming. Creator-role-required sandboxes still prepare dependencies on first use; this changes no sandbox enforcement, schema, configuration option, or on-demand preparation contract.

## Why This Change Was Made

Check the resolved mode before repository discovery in the existing prewarm owner. No new cache, worker, or alternate preparation path. Production LOC grows by 3 only to express the missing selection predicate while preserving preparation for enabled agents; the expensive work itself disappears for disabled agents.

## Evidence

- Regression cases for default-off and per-agent-off fail before the fix because a template directory is created. Existing integration coverage retains template reuse, source-only fallback, on-demand preparation, and cancellation.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): clean through P2. The configured review route was refused before inference; operator configuration was unchanged.
- Synthetic source-mode macOS Gateway: 5,000 sessions, 6,000 retained runs, 1,500 MiB logical transcripts, 12 projects, isolated 30,003-file Git workspace with a local-only origin, ten subscribed clients, 20 measured turns, eight streamed chunks. The baseline reproduced the unwanted install attempt and source-only fallback (pnpm exit 127).
- Both captures completed all 20 turns, with complete current-cohort final transcripts on all ten clients (200 deliveries/revision), including the separate CPU-only turn. Both produced three parent/utility requests. The after Gateway created no dependency-template directory and made no template install attempt.

| Metric | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Whole-turn p50 | 473.647 ms | 416.744 ms |
| Whole-turn p99 (N=20; observed maximum) | 1,680.461 ms | 643.615 ms |
| Last model chunk → final transcript receipt p50 | 38.227 ms | 36.411 ms |
| Last model chunk → final transcript receipt p99 (N=200) | 157.065 ms | 55.419 ms |
| Main-isolate allocation/turn | 126.926 MiB | 126.804 MiB |
| Main-isolate GC/turn | 16.634 ms | 14.265 ms |
| Process warm RSS | 3,509.604 MiB | 3,748.919 MiB |

Steady-state allocation is neutral; warm RSS increased in this single observation, so this PR makes no memory-reduction claim. The direct improvement is eliminated startup work for disabled agents. The baseline template fallback finished before the measured rounds, so the observed tail improvement cannot be attributed solely to removing that work.
- The original 14.049-second whole-turn outlier was not reproduced; concurrent parent replies were present in both completed captures. That metric includes parent reply preparation and is not enqueue-to-client broadcast latency; no claim of a 14-second main-thread block. This contended-host A/B is descriptive, not a controlled production capacity estimate.
- Focused local proof: `local-workspace-template.test.ts` (10 tests) and `server-startup-handler-prewarm.test.ts` (14 tests), all passed with `--maxWorkers=1`. Changed-file formatting, syntax lint through the repository wrapper, and `git diff --check` passed. The default lint invocation was stopped when it expanded to unrelated package-declaration preparation; its task-owned processes and lock were cleaned up. PR CI owns broad and type-aware validation; no Testbox/Crabbox lease or local full suite/typecheck.

prs.title: fix(agents): keep the process poll wait on the monotonic clock
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `process` tool's poll wait measures its relative `timeout` budget on the wall clock. A system-clock step (NTP correction, container/host time sync, suspend-resume) is then read as elapsed work:

- forward step: `Date.now() < deadline` fails immediately, so the poll returns "(no new output)" without waiting for output the caller asked for;
- backward step: `deadline - Date.now()` grows, so the poll keeps sleeping past the requested timeout.

## User Impact

An agent that polls a backgrounded shell with `timeout: 30000` can miss output that arrives milliseconds later, or block its turn well past 30s, after any clock adjustment on the host. The wait budget is elapsed time, so it must be measured on a clock that does not step.

## Why This Change Was Made

`pollWaitMs` is a relative duration capped at 30s (`MAX_POLL_WAIT_MS`); nothing about this wait is persisted or compared against another owner's epoch, so `performance.now()` is the correct accessor and is already the established monotonic clock in this tree. Three lines in `src/agents/bash-tools.process.ts` move the seed and both comparisons off `Date.now()`; the elapsed-time arithmetic, the 250 ms slice, abort handling, and delivered-output bookkeeping are unchanged. Classification: behavior-preserving.

Precedent: #172780 (`fix(native-session): keep binding lease wait deadline on the monotonic clock`, merged 2026-10-15) fixed the same shape for a 70 s binding-lease budget.

Impact surface:

| Location | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `src/agents/bash-tools.process.ts:438` | seed the poll wait budget on `performance.now()` |
| `src/agents/bash-tools.process.ts:445,447` | compare and size the sleep slice on the same monotonic clock |
| `src/agents/bash-tools.process.delivery.test.ts:390` | regression case for a mid-wait forward clock step |

## Evidence

### Shipped Gateway dispatcher agent-turn trace

The scenario runs through the real Gateway dispatcher started in-process by a probe (`startGatewayServer` + an authenticated Gateway client, not the CLI bootstrap), as a real agent turn (`chat.send` → `agent.wait`) whose scripted local OpenAI-compatible provider calls the real `exec` and `process` agent tools over a real backgrounded shell child. Only `Date.now` is patched — a +60 s step armed 400 ms after the scripted poll call; `performance.now()` and timers stay real. The child prints `late-output` ~0.9 s after the poll call, gated on a file the driver touches once the poll is in flight, so the ordering does not depend on host speed. Base and candidate trees are byte-identical apart from the three poll-deadline lines (`diff -rq` reports only `src/agents/bash-tools.process.ts`).

```console
BASE (upstream/main 92e62263a2e, Date.now)
shipped Gateway dispatcher ready on port 42459 (boot 134214ms)
authenticated Gateway client connected
exec tool output: Command still running (session quick-bloom, pid 431).
wall-clock step armed: Date.now += 60000ms (observed 1792083236207)
child printed late-output 1069ms after the scripted poll call
agent.wait settled: successfulToolNames ["exec","process"]
POLL_ELAPSED_MS: 666
POLL_TOOL_TEXT: "(no new output)\n\nProcess still running."

CANDIDATE (same tree + the three poll-deadline lines)
shipped Gateway dispatcher ready on port 39808 (boot 140872ms)
authenticated Gateway client connected
exec tool output: Command still running (session glow-willow, pid 431).
wall-clock step armed: Date.now += 60000ms (observed 1792083248842)
child printed late-output 908ms after the scripted poll call
agent.wait settled: successfulToolNames ["exec","process"]
POLL_ELAPSED_MS: 1674
POLL_TOOL_TEXT: "late-output\n\nProcess still running."
```

### Direct producer-chain probe

The real `createExecTool()` starts a real backgrounded child (`sh -c 'sleep 1; echo late-output; sleep 15'`), then the real `createProcessTool()` polls it with `timeout: 5000`. Only `Date.now` is patched — armed 300 ms after the poll starts — injecting a +60 s step; `performance.now()` and `setTimeout` run genuinely. Same script, only the three deadline lines differ:

```console
BASE (Date.now)
SESSION: tidal-atlas
ELAPSED_MS: 504
POLL_TEXT: "(no new output)\n\nProcess still running."

CANDIDATE (performance.now)
SESSION: fast-daisy
ELAPSED_MS: 1269
POLL_TEXT: "late-output\n\nProcess still running."
```

### Regression case and controls

Regression case in the existing fake-timer suite (`vi.useFakeTimers({ toFake: [...] })` + `vi.setSystemTime(now + 60_000)` mid-wait, output appended one fake second later):

```console
pnpm test src/agents/bash-tools.process.delivery.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
BASE + new case   1 failed | 12 skipped   (poll returned "(no new output)" instead of the late output)
CANDIDATE         13 passed               (160s)
```

Controls: the neighbouring poll cases (retained delivery through failed persistence, retry replay, parallel-poll de-duplication, blocked-output replay) all still pass. `oxlint` reports 0 warnings and 0 errors on both files; `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` exits 0.

The earlier "no shipped Gateway agent turn" gap is closed by the trace above. The backward-step direction is covered by the same deadline arithmetic rather than a separate case.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: reverting restores the wall-clock reads. Only the poll wait budget changes; output delivery, retention, abort handling, and the 30 s cap are untouched.
