prs.title: fix: usage undercounts Claude CLI turns that make several model calls
prs.body:
Related: #148603 (this PR fixes the whole-turn accounting; the issue's final per-call output count is listed under Not in scope below)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: session usage, `usage.cost`, and the Usage page count only the last model call (with its stream-start output count) for Claude CLI turns. Turns that make several model calls, such as tool-using turns, are therefore heavily undercounted.

## User Impact

User impact: Claude CLI turns now record the whole turn's tokens in the session transcript, so usage reports and anything built on them (cost estimates, budget alerts) match what Claude Code reports.

- Context-window sizing, preflight compaction, and memory-flush gating keep using the latest model call.
- Chat context displays (Control UI message footer, iOS/macOS chat) keep showing the latest call's context size.
- Turns recorded before this change keep their existing counts.
- No config, schema, or migration change (see compatibility below).

## Why This Change Was Made

Claude Code's terminal `result` event already carries whole-turn usage, and the stream parser keeps it as `diagnosticUsage` (#120100). Both CLI transcript writers still persisted the last call.

- **Both writers:** they now persist the turn total as the usage counters. `contextUsage` is derived from the last call through one shared helper (`resolveCliTranscriptUsage`), so every context reader still sizes the window from the latest call.
- **Reply-path writer:** it adds that context marker only when the backend reports a turn total separately. Other CLI backends keep their unmarked records, which context readers already refuse to treat as a fresh context size (#120497).
- **Memory flush and preflight:** their transcript snapshot now takes the last completion's output from the context marker instead of the turn counters.

- **Chat context displays:** chat history now forwards an available, coherent `contextUsage` marker with assistant usage. The Control UI message footer and the native context control and footer size context from it. Rows without an available marker keep sizing from the counters, as before.
- **Tiered pricing:** summed tokens cannot recover each request's tier. `usage.cost` now leaves a turn unpriced when its counters exceed the marker's prompt and their sum reaches past the lowest tier.
  - A sum inside the lowest tier keeps every call there, so it is still estimated. Flat pricing is unchanged.
  - The rule reads the usage shape, so it also applies to Codex harness rows whose summed prompt crosses a tier boundary.
  - `USAGE_COST_ROLLUP_VERSION` moves to 8 so cached usage summaries rebuild with the new rule. `main` is at 7 since #169660, which also carries version-6 summaries forward; both were priced under the old rule, so this PR accepts only version 8. The schema cutover still moves version-6 rows, and readers rebuild them.

Live `agentMeta.usage` / `lastCallUsage` and the context-engine hook message are unchanged.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof (after the fix, live OpenClaw)

Setup:
- A production OpenClaw 2026.9.2 gateway with Claude Code 2.1.263 on a Claude subscription.
- This PR's three production edits applied as a local backport, with identical logic, because the host runs the published build.
- Output is redacted to usage counters; the session id is replaced.

Two non-delivering `openclaw agent` turns ran on one dedicated session:
- Turn 1 makes two model calls: a Read tool call, then the reply.
- Turn 2 reuses the existing session.

```text
$ openclaw agent --agent main --session-key agent:main:<proof> --json \
    --message "Use the Read tool to read IDENTITY.md in your workspace, then reply with only the number of lines in that file."

# live run metadata (unchanged by this PR)
turn 1  lastCallUsage    {input 2, output 1, cacheRead 74593, cacheWrite 325}
        diagnosticUsage  {input 4, output 89, cacheRead 74593, cacheWrite 74918}
turn 2  lastCallUsage    {input 2, output 1, cacheRead 74918, cacheWrite 102}
        diagnosticUsage  {input 2, output 3, cacheRead 74918, cacheWrite 102}

# persisted assistant transcript records, read back from the session's SQLite transcript
turn 1  usage {input 4, output 89, cacheRead 74593, cacheWrite 74918, totalTokens 149604,
               contextUsage {state available, promptTokens 74920, totalTokens 74921}}
turn 2  usage {input 2, output 3, cacheRead 74918, cacheWrite 102, totalTokens 75025,
               contextUsage {state available, promptTokens 75022, totalTokens 75023}}

# Claude Code's own transcript for the bound CLI session (deduplicated by message id)
turn 1  model calls 2  sum input 4 / output 89 / cacheRead 74593 / cacheWrite 74918  last-call prompt 74920
turn 2  model calls 1  sum input 2 / output 3  / cacheRead 74918 / cacheWrite 102    last-call prompt 75022

# usage.cost for the agent's day, read back before and after the two proof turns (rollup refresh)
before  totalTokens 404634  output 13   cacheWrite 45337   totalCost 0.3800  missingCostEntries 0
after   totalTokens 629263  output 105  cacheWrite 120357  totalCost 0.8764  missingCostEntries 0
delta   totalTokens +224629 (= 149604 + 75025)  output +92 (= 89 + 3)  cacheWrite +75020 (= 74918 + 102)
```

What this shows:
- The persisted counters equal Claude Code's per-turn totals exactly.
- The usage report's delta equals the two persisted records. The dollar figure comes from a locally configured `claude-cli` price entry; this PR does not change pricing.
- `contextUsage.promptTokens` equals the last call's prompt.
- Without this change, turn 1 would have been persisted as output 1 / cacheWrite 325.
- A scheduled heartbeat turn on the same gateway also persisted its final output count (9) and not the stream-start value (1): `usage {input 2, output 9, cacheRead 69062, cacheWrite 10885, totalTokens 79958, contextUsage {state available, promptTokens 79949, totalTokens 79950}}`.

### Real behavior proof for the chat display and pricing follow-ups

Setup:
- OpenClaw built from this branch at 4f6d8a833ce, run as an isolated local gateway (own state directory, loopback only, channels off).
- Both turns ran with `openclaw agent` through the real `claude-cli` backend. The `claude` binary on `PATH` was a stand-in that emits the usage of the live turns above as Claude Code stream records: one `assistant` record per model call and the terminal `result`. No model call was made.
  - The first call's record is derived: turn total minus the last call.
  - `qa/scenarios/channels/telegram-claude-cli-compaction-final-priority.yaml` uses the same stand-in technique.
- The runner, transcript writer, chat history, `usage.cost` and the Control UI are the built product with no proof-only changes. The only stand-in is the `claude` binary.
- **Before** is this branch with the source changes of fa8ed7c9688 and db6439b5fd3 reverted and rebuilt. That is the state reviewed at 9366812645d: whole-turn counters stored, displays and pricing not yet following the marker. **After** is the head.
- The turns ran once, on the before build. The after build read the same session from the same state directory. The transcript writer is identical in both builds.
- Proof configuration: a 200,000-token context window, and a `claude-cli/claude-sonnet-4-5` price entry with a tier boundary at 100,000 prompt tokens (`$3 / $15 / $0.30 / $3.75` per million tokens below it, `$6 / $22.50 / $0.60 / $7.50` above). Each call of turn 1 stays below the boundary (74,595 and 74,920 prompt tokens). Their sum (149,515) crosses it.

```text
$ openclaw agent --agent main --session-key agent:main:proof --json \
    --message "Use the Read tool to read IDENTITY.md in your workspace, then reply with only the number of lines in that file."
$ openclaw agent --agent main --session-key agent:main:proof --json --message "Reply with only the word ok."

# run metadata from the stand-in, equal to the live run above
turn 1  lastCallUsage    {input 2, output 1, cacheRead 74593, cacheWrite 325}
        diagnosticUsage  {input 4, output 89, cacheRead 74593, cacheWrite 74918}
turn 2  lastCallUsage    {input 2, output 1, cacheRead 74918, cacheWrite 102}
        diagnosticUsage  {input 2, output 3, cacheRead 74918, cacheWrite 102}

# openclaw gateway call chat.history: assistant usage as the Control UI and the apps receive it
before  turn 1  {input 4, output 89, cacheRead 74593, cacheWrite 74918, totalTokens 149604}
        turn 2  {input 2, output 3, cacheRead 74918, cacheWrite 102, totalTokens 75025}
after   turn 1  {input 4, output 89, cacheRead 74593, cacheWrite 74918, totalTokens 149604,
                 contextUsage {state available, promptTokens 74920, totalTokens 74921}}
        turn 2  {input 2, output 3, cacheRead 74918, cacheWrite 102, totalTokens 75025,
                 contextUsage {state available, promptTokens 75022, totalTokens 75023}}

# openclaw gateway call usage.cost --params '{"days":1}': totals
before  totalTokens 224629  totalCost 0.6315762  missingCostEntries 0
after   totalTokens 224629  totalCost 0.0229089  missingCostEntries 1
        missingCostByModel {"claude-cli/claude-sonnet-4-5": 1}
```

What this shows:
- **`usage.cost`, before:** turn 1 is priced from its summed prompt at the upper tier. That is `$0.6086673` of the total; the rest is turn 2. Both of its calls sit in the lower tier, where the same tokens cost about `$0.3047`.
- **`usage.cost`, after:** turn 1 is left unpriced and counted in `missingCostEntries`. Turn 2 is a single call and keeps its estimate, `$0.0229089`.
- Token totals are the same in both builds (224,629 = 149,604 + 75,025).
- The before build stored its usage rollup under version 6. On the head, the first `usage.cost` read reported it stale and refreshing. The next read, 3 s later, was fresh with the new totals, and the stored rollup carries version 7. No manual step was needed.

**Control UI** (web): the usage details of turn 1's reply in the chat view. They show when the message footer is hovered.

Before: `75% ctx`

![Control UI message footer before: 75% ctx](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mcaldas/openclaw/3dfa8d6f0e5f2621859385790d6ed887ea566fbd/web-before.png)

After: `37% ctx`

![Control UI message footer after: 37% ctx](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mcaldas/openclaw/3dfa8d6f0e5f2621859385790d6ed887ea566fbd/web-after.png)

**Native** (iOS): the message footer (top) and the context control's menu (bottom).

Before: `75% ctx` with a warning, and "149.6k of 200.0k tokens used"

![iOS chat before: 75% ctx, 149.6k of 200.0k tokens used](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mcaldas/openclaw/3dfa8d6f0e5f2621859385790d6ed887ea566fbd/native-before.png)

After: `37% ctx`, and "74.9k of 200.0k tokens used"

![iOS chat after: 37% ctx, 74.9k of 200.0k tokens used](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mcaldas/openclaw/3dfa8d6f0e5f2621859385790d6ed887ea566fbd/native-after.png)

- The iOS app target is a Debug build of `apps/ios` on an iPhone 17 simulator (iOS 26.4.1), from a reduced project without the watch app, in the app's screenshot fixture mode (`--openclaw-screenshot-mode`).
- A local, uncommitted patch to the fixture transport seeds the chat history with turn 1's usage row and a 200,000-token window. The chat text and the model label (`claude-sonnet-4-6`) are the fixture's own.
- Both runs receive the same history payload, marker included. Before reverts the Swift changes of fa8ed7c9688, so only the app code differs.
- The macOS app renders the same shared `OpenClawChatUI` views from `apps/shared/OpenClawKit`. It was not captured separately.
- The screenshots hold proof-session and fixture content only: no endpoints, addresses, keys or personal data.

### Tests and checks

Regression tests. Each one fails on `main` and passes with this change:
- `cli-runner.turn-usage.test.ts` › "persists the terminal Claude turn usage for a multi-call turn"
  - Runs a turn whose parsed output carries the last call and a separate turn total through `runPreparedCliAgent`, then reads the persisted transcript back.
  - Before: input 2 / output 1 / cacheRead 27,376.
  - After: 6 / 77 / 54,631, with `contextUsage` at the last call's 27,378 prompt tokens.
- `transcript-persistence.test.ts` › "persists the terminal CLI turn usage while keeping last-call context"
- `session-transcript-readers.test.ts` › "sizes CLI output from the context marker when counters cover the whole turn"
  - Before: 30,000 output tokens.
  - After: 2,000 output tokens.

- `chat-display-projection.test.ts` › "forwards an available context marker with assistant usage"
- `chat-message-timestamp.test.ts` (new file) › "sizes context from the marker when usage counters cover a whole turn"
  - Before: 75% ctx for a two-call turn in a 200k window.
  - After: 37% ctx.
- `ChatContextUsageTests.swift` › "whole-turn counters report the latest call's context marker" and "usage footer sizes context from the marker and keeps whole-turn counters"
  - Before: 149,000 tokens and "98% ctx".
  - After: 75,000 tokens and "49% ctx".
- `session-cost-usage-pricing.test.ts` (new file) › "leaves a multi-call turn unpriced when its sum crosses a tier" and "prices a multi-call turn whose sum stays in the lowest tier"

Guard test:
- `cli-run-transcript.test.ts` › "keeps CLI usage unmarked when the backend reports no separate turn total"

Suites and checks (branch merged with `main` at 035bf890344):
- Merge history: the merge at efa6458a090 had three conflicts, all code `main` had moved: the transcript accounting reader now lives in `session-transcript-accounting-policy.ts`, and the chat footer's `extractGroupMeta` in the Solid `chat-message-timestamp-view.tsx`; this PR's two edits were re-applied there unchanged. The merge at 432d890350b was clean. The merge at 035bf890344 had one import conflict in `chat-message-timestamp-view.tsx`; both helpers are kept.
- #120008 (usage reports marked unavailable) landed in three files this PR also changes: the chat history projection, the usage pricing estimate and the Control UI footer. Both changes are kept side by side: an unavailable usage report is skipped before this PR's context marker and tier guard are read.
- On the merged head, `pnpm test <files> --maxWorkers=4` passed 2,239 tests across 171 files:
  - every test file in `src/agents/cli-runner/` and `src/agents/command/` (live and e2e files excluded);
  - the `cli-runner.*`, `cli-output*`, `usage*`, `agent-runner-memory*`, `session-transcript-readers*`, `chat-display-projection*`, `session-cost-usage*` and `usage-format*` suites;
  - the Control UI `chat-message*` suites, including the six chat browser tests;
  - the usage cache suites (`session-cost-usage-cache.*`), `doctor-usage-cost-cache.test.ts` and the schema cutover test `openclaw-agent-db.storage-migration.test.ts`.
- The version 8 move updates two cutover tests from #169660: a migrated version-6 report is still moved (the cache test checks it arrives byte for byte), but no longer decodes as current (`session-cost-usage-cache.sqlite.test.ts`, `openclaw-agent-db.storage-migration.test.ts`). Our earlier fixture change in the cutover test (4f6d8a833ce) is replaced by `main`'s stored version 6.
- CI on the first merge failed two of this PR's new tests and one existing e2e test:
  - `cli-runner.turn-usage.test.ts` and the guard test in `cli-run-transcript.test.ts` relied on runtime config being loaded on demand, which #169714 removed. Without config the persistence wrapper wrote no row, so both saw an empty transcript. Both now pass `config: {}`, as #169714 did for the neighbouring tests. Both fail on the new merge without that change and pass with it.
  - `cli-runner.fault-sequences.e2e.test.ts` › "dispatches bridge mode through one fresh CLI child and bypasses the native run budget" fails with "Runtime config is not prepared" on this head, and identically with all of this PR's source changes reverted (tests kept). It comes from `main`, not from this PR.
  - Left out of the local run: `session-cost-usage-cache.creation-race.test.ts`, new on `main`, fails on this Mac with "state … is undergoing offline maintenance", identically with this PR's source changes reverted.
- Test cost of the four added tests, from `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` on an M-series laptop:
  - `cli-runner.turn-usage.test.ts` (new file): 2.2 s for the test, 11 s for the file. It runs the real runner and transcript store, because that is the only layer that proves the turn total is wired from the runner into the writer.
  - `transcript-persistence.test.ts`: 63 ms for the added test.
  - `session-transcript-readers.test.ts`: 144 ms for the added test.
  - `cli-run-transcript.test.ts`: 201 ms for the added test.
- Gates re-run on the merged head: `oxfmt --check` and oxlint on the changed files, `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:ui`, `tsgo:core:test`, and the line-cap, assertion-safety and mock-export ratchets. `git diff --check` is clean.
- Gates last run before the merge of `main`: import cycles (0 runtime, 0 madge), dead-code exports, deprecated API usage, `lint:ui:i18n`, stylelint on the changed UI files, and the max-lines and test-timeout-race ratchets. The SQLite-worker ratchet last ran before the chat-display and pricing commits, which add no database code.
- The three regression tests moved out of `cli-runner.reliability.test.ts`, `attempt-execution.cli.test.ts` and `agent-runner-memory.test.ts`, which are over the line cap and may not grow.
- Chat display and pricing follow-up:
  - `swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --filter ChatContextUsageTests` passed 14 tests on the merged head; SwiftFormat and SwiftLint at the pinned versions report nothing on the changed files.
  - The added TypeScript tests take 0 to 2 ms each. Each new regression test fails with its source change reverted.
  - The iOS app target was built (Debug, simulator, reduced project without the watch app) for the screenshots above. Not run locally: the full OpenClawKit suite, the full iOS project and the macOS app build.

Live Claude Code semantics (stream-json, `--include-partial-messages`):
- A tool-using turn's `result` reported 77 output tokens, while its two `assistant` events carried 15 and 1.
- In one warm stdio process, each turn's `result.usage` covered only that turn (78 output tokens each time). Only `total_cost_usd` accumulates, so persisting `result` usage does not double count warm sessions.
  - Rechecked on Claude Code 2.1.293: two turns in one process reported cache writes of 28,094 and then 5,619, while `total_cost_usd` rose from 0.0057 to 0.0072.

## Upgrade and data compatibility

- **No schema, migration, or config change.** The persisted assistant `usage` keeps its existing shape. `contextUsage` is an existing optional field that the agent-command writer has persisted since #120497.
- **Existing records are untouched.** Older unmarked CLI records still hit the existing provenance barrier, so readers treat them exactly as before.
- **Old and new records mix safely in one session.** Accounting sums the counters, and context readers use the newest record's marker (proof turn 2 above ran in an existing session).
- **Upgrade.** Only turns recorded after the update carry turn totals, and nothing needs to run. Rolling back leaves new records readable, because their counters are ordinary usage fields.

## Related

- #148676 targets the same issue. Its current revision uses the same projection for both writers and the same reader change.
  - It also switches live `agentMeta.usage` to the turn total in `cli-run-settlement.ts`.
  - This PR leaves live `agentMeta.usage` on the last call.

Not in scope (possible follow-ups):
- `lastCallUsage` still takes its output count from the stream-start `assistant` event, because `readCliUsage` does not read `message_delta`. This only affects the small output side of the context marker.
- A run with several interim `result` events persists the last segment's total. That undercounts rather than double counts, and the behavior predates this change.
- Live `agentMeta.usage` for CLI runs (reply footer, session store counters, cron run records) still reflects the last call.
- Subscription dollar pricing (#102771).
- Turns whose reply goes out through the message tool, and room-event turns, write no CLI assistant row, so they still add nothing to `usage.cost`.
- Rows whose marker is `unavailable` (for example an aborted Codex turn) keep sizing context and choosing a tier from their counters, as on `main`.

AI-assisted (Claude Code).

## Maintainer simplification

Reviewed the complete diff and the contributing commits at `443a1722ce` before executing the branch. The changes stay within usage accounting, its existing consumers, and regression tests: no new network calls, credential/environment reads, package or lockfile changes, install hooks, or build-configuration changes.

The smallest complete fix is to persist the terminal whole-turn counters, preserve the latest call in `contextUsage`, and keep every context consumer on that marker. The pass preserves mcaldas's commits and implementation:

- Reused the shared `CliTranscriptUsage` contract instead of maintaining an identical local type in the command writer.
- Removed the new Control UI no-marker fallback test: the existing rendered-chat test, “uses the largest prompt for context and aggregates usage, cache, and nested cost,” already exercises that behavior more thoroughly. The distinct whole-turn marker regression remains.
- Kept chat-history forwarding and both web/native consumers: without them, the accounting correction inflates the displayed context size.
- Kept the tiered-pricing guard: a summed prompt cannot reconstruct each request's tier, and applying a higher tier to a sum would introduce incorrect dollar estimates. Flat pricing and sums below the first boundary remain estimated. The same shape-based protection applies to existing Codex rows; no separate backend policy was added.
- Kept rollup version 8 and the adjusted storage-cutover tests: cached versions 6/7 were priced under the old rule and must rebuild. The existing migration still preserves the old cache bytes; the reader correctly declines to treat them as current.
- Kept the small shared `cli-transcript-usage.ts` leaf: both transcript writers need the same projection; importing it from the command writer previously pulled its runtime dependency graph into the runner. There is no competing usage owner to remove.

No additional feature or split-out is needed for these retained pieces; all prevent regressions introduced by persisting totals. The existing “Not in scope” items above remain out of scope.

Line deltas against merge base `035bf8903442` (production includes the native and web consumers):

| | Before pass | After pass |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Production | +164 / −44 (net +120) | +165 / −51 (net +114) |
| Tests | +375 / −4 (net +371) | +371 / −4 (net +367) |
| Total | +539 / −48 (net +491) | +536 / −55 (net +481) |

The pass removes 6 net production lines and 4 test lines without removing any distinct regression boundary. GitHub reported the branch mergeable, so no extra merge or rebase was performed.

## Maintainer real-CLI verification

Verified the simplified code at `c8a5bb223bb0130863f2159640faa2adf674ecd6` using a full production build (pueue task 7067), real Claude Code **2.1.300**, and an isolated loopback Gateway launched in the GUI session so the CLI could use its existing login keychain. No stand-in binary was used. The setup and prompts match the main-branch reproduction: one Read-tool turn followed by a plain reply on the same fresh session. The test Gateway was stopped afterward.

These are separate live runs, so model token counts vary between main and PR. The invariant is equality between the CLI's own per-turn sum and the canonical persisted counters within each run.

| Revision / turn | Claude transcript output | Persisted output | Claude transcript cache write | Persisted cache write |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Main `3f1011275f`, Read (2 calls) | 104 | 1 | 61,090 | 216 |
| Main `3f1011275f`, plain reply (1 call) | 4 | 1 | 425 | 425 |
| PR simplified head, Read (2 calls) | 106 | **106** | 60,587 | **60,587** |
| PR simplified head, plain reply (1 call) | 4 | **4** | 427 | **427** |

PR-head details (Claude transcript assistant records deduplicated by `message.id`):

| Turn | Source | Input | Output | Cache read | Cache write | Total |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Read | CLI sum = live diagnosticUsage = SQLite usage = usage.cost delta | 4 | 106 | 60,369 | 60,587 | 121,066 |
| Read | Live lastCallUsage | 1 | 1 | 60,369 | 218 | — |
| Plain reply | CLI sum = live diagnosticUsage = SQLite usage = usage.cost delta | 3 | 4 | 60,587 | 427 | 61,021 |
| Plain reply | Live lastCallUsage | 3 | 1 | 60,587 | 427 | — |

- `contextUsage` persisted and returned by **chat.history** is `{state: available, promptTokens: 60588, totalTokens: 60589}` for the Read turn and `{state: available, promptTokens: 61017, totalTokens: 61018}` for the reply. Both prompts equal the native transcript's last-call prompt exactly.

prs.title: fix(imessage): keep one-to-one chat ID sends in direct sessions
prs.body:
Fixes #173367

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes duplicate group sessions when an iMessage one-to-one reply or explicit send uses `chat_id:<n>` instead of a handle.

## User Impact

Direct chat selectors now use the same normalized-handle session as inbound turns, while delivery keeps the original chat address. Native groups and explicitly configured group chats retain group routing; GUID and identifier aliases resolve to the numeric group session.

Existing incorrectly classified rows and their history are preserved. Doctor cannot safely replace the live direct session with a duplicate or merge its transcript through the current session-store repair operations. Selectors absent from the existing bounded chat lookup do not create a guessed session.

## Why This Change Was Made

The iMessage plugin treated every non-handle selector as a group. Target resolution and outbound session routing now share the plugin's existing account-scoped Messages chat lookup. The returned GUID carries the same direct/group fact that imsg uses to produce `is_group`; direct GUIDs supply the canonical handle. Explicit `channels.imessage.groups.<chat_id>` configuration still takes precedence.

The simplification removes the selector-based group branch and the separate target-kind decision, and reuses the action lookup rather than adding a second cache. Production changes are +141/-82 (net +59); resolving actual chat facts and sharing that result requires more code than the deleted prefix assumption. Tests are +119/-7; docs +2/-0. No SDK or schema change, new setting, or detached/background effect.

## Evidence

- Confirmed by source and history on `origin/main`: inbound direct routing uses the sender handle but replies to `chat_id:<n>`; the old outbound route created a group peer for that selector.
- Regression cases in `session-route.test.ts`: “keeps a direct reply on the direct session”, explicit chat ID/GUID/identifier sends, native/configured groups, named-default account group/direct routing, and “does not invent a session for an unresolved chat ID”. `targets.test.ts` no longer locks opaque chat IDs to group classification. Approval regressions in `approval-native.test.ts` require explicit approvers for selector origins and retain local fallback prompts. Existing action-runtime lookup regressions continue to cover transport-cache isolation and strict ID parsing.
- Changed-file oxlint using `config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json`: passed. Oxfmt on all nine changed files: passed; `git diff --check`: passed.
- Codex autoreview: `scoped-clean`, no actionable P0–P2 findings. All three review passes were scoped-clean; the later passes include both GitHub review corrections. Subsequent main merges changed no iMessage files.
- Addressed the GitHub review P1: ambiguous selectors must not enable implicit same-chat approval authorization. Approval routing now requires a handle target or configured approvers; local-prompt suppression follows the same rule.
- Addressed the second GitHub review P1: carry the resolved default account into group policy and account-scoped session construction.
- [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38813333760) passed on `77785552d6bd7caff8ac108b45f41a6d4ec2af06`, including `openclaw/ci-gate`, production/test types, lint, and repository checks. The [iMessage test shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38813333760/job/116693000072) passed 150 tests across 11 files in 47.16 seconds; direct-reply and explicit chat-ID regressions each took 8 ms. Current-head GitHub code review also completed with no findings. PR CI is the test gate. Local unit suites, negative controls, typechecks, and live Gateway/Crabbox/Testbox proof were intentionally skipped per maintainer policy. The lint wrapper's declaration-preparation subprocess was stopped; lint was rerun directly with the allowed core config. No leases or Gateway processes were created. Local test wall times are unavailable because tests were not run locally.

prs.title: fix: verify the installed Windows desktop release before signing
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Windows desktop release checks that it built an NSIS installer, but does not verify that it installs the expected desktop and runtime. The existing prefix comparison also accepts `2026.10.30` when `2026.10.3` is expected. Tauri writes a full string ProductVersion distinct from its numeric version field.

## User Impact

Selected PRs and new releases spend additional time qualifying the installer. Successfully qualified artifacts proceed to release signing without a rebuild. Already-published releases are not retroactively rebuilt or qualified.

## Why This Change Was Made

The pull-request workflow keeps its existing trigger paths and job count. Changes to the installer, packaging, runtime, or signing workflow add an installation step inside the Windows build already running; they add no PR runner, build, or blanket main push.

A new release runs a required, secret-free qualification job on clean hosted Windows, capped at 25 minutes. It silently installs the uploaded artifact and checks exact version, manifest bytes and embedding, file set and hashes, Bun’s timestamped Foundation signature, and revision and source-commit probes. The approved artifact ID and digests flow into both signing paths.

## Evidence

[Final-head hosted Windows qualification](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38813223499/job/116691370638) installed `OpenClaw_0.1.0_x64-setup.exe`, verified version `0.1.0`, and qualified SHA-256 `1e43d0c3b0b99e3ee6a47ac8b7039d07c979eb26f842480949f4e5ef71fef133`. Path decision: **within GitHub’s one-second timestamp resolution**; pre-existing installer build: **39m 24s**; new installation and verification: **49s**. The [preceding hosted run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38805549228/job/116665640240) measured 1s, 45m 30s and 47s respectively. These are step times, not billing estimates. No production release or signing was attempted.

[ClawSweeper](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173450#issuecomment-6201816035) resolved the earlier guard finding and reports no findings or before-merge actions on `40b52fa1`. [Required CI and applicable security checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38814444961) passed.

The signing guard now evaluates qualification success, failure, skip, and cancellation. Evaluating the actual signing conditions on base and head with a successful build: base permits both signing paths without qualification; head blocks both on failed, skipped, or cancelled qualification and still permits both on success. The corrected guard and focused Tauri workflow tests passed 14/14; the matching type-aware CI lint command passed.

A separate digest-verified prior artifact exercised all 32,304 payload entries; negative controls rejected a missing file, extra file, modified byte, and wrong manifest digest.

## Separate Linux companion failure

The [Linux onboarding test](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38813223499/job/116691371047) expected “Local model setup” but displayed “Connection Settings.” Its fixture recorded the correct `/fixture/settings/model-setup` request; we do not know why the document did not finish loading. The full Linux build job and implicated navigation/test code are unchanged by this PR. This exact failure [predates the PR on a documentation-only change](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171114); [another maintainer is investigating the same transition](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173421). We have not rerun the job or changed its test, timeout, or landing policy.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Speech providers repeated directive alias/policy dispatch, and Voice Call rebuilt defaults already owned by its schema.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible change, migration, or required action. Provider aliases, policy gates, validators, warning text, independent mutable defaults, and external-input validation remain protected. No config keys, schemas, protocols, dependencies, security effect checks, or durability behavior change. The standalone session memory backend is untouched.

## What changed

One lightweight speech directive dispatcher serves all bundled parsers and the compatible-provider factory. Providers retain their value contracts; the TTS host retains patch accumulation. Voice Call's existing schema owns defaulting and external validation once, while typed consumers use its parsed result. A browser helper also drops redundant undefined coalescing.

The coordinator-directed CI cut restores every changed source file reachable from either failing Gateway test to origin/main. Dropped: all channel secret-assignment consolidation, shared record omission and its provider-normalization callers, reply/CLI cleanup, TTS layered/status cleanup, video duration consolidation, and meeting-config consolidation with its registrations/tests/docs. These changes are preserved separately on `deslop/z15-parked-cron-auth-20261015` with the failing-test note; no PR is proposed for that branch.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Providers return directive patches without copying unrelated accumulated overrides; the TTS host already owns accumulation. The original parser split (#138483) and helper sharing (#167205) do not establish a separate accumulation contract or human-reported incident requiring those copies. ElevenLabs still merges nested voice settings; host-boundary coverage protects accumulation.
- Voice Call trusts already-parsed internal config instead of cloning and reconstructing schema defaults at each consumer. Previous normalization work (#165276 and commit3087893ef96) is code provenance, not a human incident requiring repeated parsing. Malformed raw input still fails at the canonical schema boundary; typed internal callers supply its parsed result.
- No concurrency/recovery/security guard was removed. Browser undefined coalescing is a redundant absence conversion, not a fallback contract.

## Size

**155 net production lines removed**, counting registration metadata and excluding tests, docs, fixtures, generated files, and the exact assertion-baseline shrink. The coordinator waived the size floor for this reduced branch. All other inventoried family candidates are retained for named distinct contracts or parked by the CI drop rule; no additional sound unattempted cut remains.

## Evidence

Reduced-cut local proof: extension production type graph passes, covering the core speech consumers; static SCC/madge reports zero cycles. Runtime-cycle proof reports zero cycles and remains input-valid after the sole subsequent runtime import change removed Microsoft's now-unused speech SDK edge. prs.title: fix(litellm): image generation fails when the backend returns image URLs
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/173507

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: image generation through LiteLLM fails with `LiteLLM image generation response malformed` when the backend answers with `data[].url` instead of `b64_json` (for example `dall-e-3`).

## User Impact

User impact: LiteLLM image generation and edits now save the image when the backend returns URLs, the same way custom OpenAI endpoints already do. The download uses the provider's existing network policy and the `agents.defaults.mediaMaxMb` cap, and does not send the LiteLLM key to the image host.

## Why This Change Was Made

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/170278 added URL downloads to the OpenAI plugin only. LiteLLM goes through the shared OpenAI-compatible image provider, which still parsed only `b64_json`.

This change moves that download, unchanged, from the OpenAI plugin into `src/image-generation` as `inlineOpenAiCompatibleImageUrls` (exported from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/image-generation`). The shared provider and the OpenAI plugin both call it, so there is one implementation of the download policy: SSRF checks, image `Content-Type`, the byte cap, the download count limit, and keeping provider TLS identity on the provider origin. Error messages keep the provider label, so the OpenAI messages do not change. A second copy inside the shared provider was the smaller diff, but would leave two download policies to drift. Against the merge base, production code is +153/−94 lines (most of the added lines are the download moved out of the OpenAI plugin), tests +28, docs +4.

Downloads use the provider's resolved private-network setting; the mechanism is the same as in the OpenAI plugin, but the LiteLLM default differs. LiteLLM turns that setting on for a loopback base URL (its default `http://localhost:4000`), so with the default config a backend-returned URL on a LAN or link-local address is now fetched too. This assumes the operator trusts the LiteLLM proxy they run, which already receives the API key; downloads still need an image `Content-Type` and stay under the size cap. When a request timeout is set, each download is bounded by what is left of it; otherwise each download gets 60 s. Providers that request `b64_json` (DeepInfra, xAI) are unaffected: entries with inline data are passed through.

The LiteLLM request is left as is rather than forcing `response_format: "b64_json"`: LiteLLM forwards to arbitrary image backends, and OpenClaw already avoids forcing that legacy parameter on custom OpenAI endpoints (as the image generation docs state), handling both response shapes instead.

## Evidence

Tested at `5b6a5216809` (base `upstream/main` `b53ba16c63a`).

The real CLI built from source, isolated HOME and profile, a dummy `LITELLM_API_KEY`, no config file (LiteLLM's default `http://localhost:4000`). A loopback stand-in for the LiteLLM proxy answers `POST /images/generations` with `{"data":[{"url":"http://127.0.0.1:4001/generated/a.png","revised_prompt":"stub"}]}`; a second loopback origin serves a 1x1 PNG at that URL and logs whether an `Authorization` header arrives.

Before (base `b53ba16c63a`):

```text
$ openclaw --profile p193 infer image generate --model litellm/dall-e-3 --prompt 'a red square' --json
[image-generation] candidate failed: litellm/dall-e-3: LiteLLM image generation response malformed
{"ok":false,"error":{"type":"cli_error","message":"LiteLLM image generation response malformed"}}
exit=1

# stand-in log
litellm POST /images/generations authorization=present body={"model":"dall-e-3","prompt":"a red square","n":1,"size":"1024x1024"}
litellm answered {"created":1,"data":[{"url":"http://127.0.0.1:4001/generated/a.png","revised_prompt":"stub"}]}
```

After (this PR):

```text
$ openclaw --profile p193 infer image generate --model litellm/dall-e-3 --prompt 'a red square' --json
{"ok":true,"capability":"image.generate","transport":"local","provider":"litellm","model":"dall-e-3","attempts":[],
 "outputs":[{"path":"<state-dir>/media/generated/image-1---<uuid>.png","mimeType":"image/png","size":69,"width":1,"height":1,"revisedPrompt":"stub"}],
 "ignoredOverrides":[]}
exit=0

# stand-in log
litellm POST /images/generations authorization=present body={"model":"dall-e-3","prompt":"a red square","n":1,"size":"1024x1024"}
litellm answered {"created":1,"data":[{"url":"http://127.0.0.1:4001/generated/a.png","revised_prompt":"stub"}]}
image-host GET /generated/a.png authorization=absent
```

Observed result: before, the URL is never fetched and the command fails; after, the image host gets one GET without the LiteLLM key, and the saved file's sha256 matches the served PNG.

Checks: the touched tests (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, wall time per file in the table below), the unchanged OpenAI URL and TLS download tests (`extensions/openai/image-generation-provider.url.test.ts`, `extensions/openai/image-generation-provider.tls.test.ts`), `extensions/litellm/image-generation-provider.test.ts`, and `pnpm check:changed` on the changed files (core and core-test typecheck, format, Plugin SDK export and surface budget); lint and the broad suites run in this PR's CI.

| Test file | `--maxWorkers=1` wall |
| --- | --- |
| `src/image-generation/openai-compatible-image-provider.test.ts` | 6.6 s |

The new test "downloads data[].url results without forwarding provider credentials" fails on the base with `Sample image generation response malformed` and passes on this branch.

Not covered: a real LiteLLM proxy and a real `dall-e-3` backend (the stand-in reproduces their response shape); image edits with URL results go through the same shared code path but had no separate CLI run; no test times a download against the remaining request budget (it uses the existing deadline helpers).

prs.title: fix: address MCP and source-map dependency advisories on October
prs.body:
> Maintainer hold: dependency merge is deferred for separate compatibility acceptance. This PR is not a functional prerequisite for the independent cron regression repair. No merge or deployment is being requested at this checkpoint.

## What Problem This Solves

The October release branch fails the production dependency audit on MCP OAuth destination validation ([GHSA-6qxp-vccf-f47h](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6qxp-vccf-f47h)) and indexed source-map denial of service ([GHSA-68fv-2mgg-jv7q](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-68fv-2mgg-jv7q)).

The SDK update also needs its integration guard: after a normal refresh, a resource challenge naming another issuer could make SDK 1.31.0 register and persist a replacement client before OpenClaw refused background authorization. That overwrote the original registration while retaining the original refresh token.

## User Impact

Updates the affected dependencies to their first patched versions and preserves the original registration and tokens when background refresh encounters another issuer. Normal same-issuer refresh remains available, including credentials saved by SDK 1.30.1. Explicit login can still register with the new issuer. Issuer changes require explicit authorization; this does not promise compatibility with every external OAuth provider.

## Changes

- MCP SDK 1.31.0 in the three direct consumers; Control UI MCP client/core 2.2.0; source-map-js 1.2.2 using the workspace override. No other package version changes.
- Backport only the clientInformation issuer guard and DCR retention coverage from [#166217](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/166217), commit c39d9b0692dbaafa5b1bfe02514c9f6411ab5546. Reuse the existing token eligibility predicate without changing it. Preserve the October branch's existing credential mutation and login-lifecycle fencing.
- Keep the SDK's issuer fields through SQLite callback persistence/reopen. No schema migration, credential reset, scheduler change, or deployment.

## Evidence

Candidate source and SDK 1.31.0 were exercised with a real loopback HTTP server, canonical guarded HTTP transport, real OAuth leases, and isolated SQLite state:

| Path | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Original PR without the guard | One unwanted replacement registration POST; original client overwritten; regression test failed |
| Same-issuer refresh after the guard | Refresh succeeds and authenticated resource returns 200 |
| Replacement issuer advertising working DCR | Zero registration/token POSTs; original client, tokens, and token issuer retained |
| Explicit login after rejection | One replacement registration; SDK returns REDIRECT; no token POST before authorization |
| SDK 1.30.1 saved credentials, database close/reopen, then SDK 1.31.0 | Existing issuer-less credential records load and refresh successfully; new issuer fields persist |
| Lease revoked while HTTP discovery is in flight | Zero token/registration POSTs; credentials retained; lease released |

The SDK 1.30.1 compatibility cell uses the real older SDK with the unchanged storage owner; it is not a full published-binary updater or external-provider login test. Explicit-login proof reaches authorization redirect, not a completed browser callback. The temporary HTTP proof adds no CI files.

Validation results and exact candidate binding are recorded in the follow-up review comment. Earlier unchanged dependency validation covered UI bridge/cursor, browser MCP, QA-lab helpers, dependency pin/patch guards, root release-lock mirror, and UI/extension types. Production audit returned no high-or-higher npm bulk advisories for this lockfile.

The Control UI startup-JS overage was previously reproduced with exact October base dependencies: 374730 B gzip on base versus 374721–374722 B on the dependency candidate, limit 373454 B. No budget or check is waived. Remote CI/review must complete on the updated head.

Credit: the upstream registration repair is from #166217 (Patrick Erichsen, with Vincent Koc and Dallin Romney).

### Subsequent review and CI

ClawSweeper's exact-head re-review of `a977f084655833f72751cca52adaa351ad55c2b2` found no actionable defects and accepted the supplied boundary/compatibility evidence. The explicit branch-inclusion hold remains.

[CI extensions shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38816914167/job/116704258626) fails 16 provider-review cases because its fixture lacks `connection.pluginConfig`, read before the expected provider-review behavior. The same 16 failures reproduce with SDK 1.30.1 in the separate cron candidate (`9207458b163`) using the unchanged production/test files from release base `f155b936161`. Both affected files are byte-identical between this dependency candidate and that release base. This establishes an inherited fixture failure, not passing CI. No tests, checks, or execution policy were altered to hide it.

prs.title: fix(gateway): honor session webSearch override in tools.effective preview
prs.body:
Closes #173403.

## What Problem This Solves

`tools.effective` included core `web_search` in the preview even when the session's saved `SessionToolOverrides.webSearch` was `false`, contradicting the documented behavior that the preview is a projection from saved settings (see issue #173403).

## Fix

- Thread `webSearchEnabled` through `ResolveEffectiveToolInventoryParams` → `createOpenClawCodingToolsInternalAsync` → `createWebSearchTool` (which already returns `null` when `enabled === false`).
- The handler passes `false` only when the session override is explicitly `false`; `undefined` otherwise (no behavior change).
- Include the override in the inventory cache key so override changes are not masked by stale entries.

## Evidence

- Added two handler tests in `src/gateway/server-methods/tools-effective.test.ts`:
  - Session with `toolOverrides: { webSearch: false }` → `webSearchEnabled: false` is passed to the inventory resolver.
  - Session without the override → `webSearchEnabled` is `undefined` (unchanged behavior).
- The `createWebSearchTool({ enabled: false })` → `null` path is pre-existing and covered by the tool's own contract.

prs.title: feat(control-ui): show plugin steering notes in chat
prs.body:
Stacked on #173460 (private model-prompt display isolation).

## What Problem This Solves

Plugin steering was invisible in Control UI chat, while next-turn fallback guidance could leak to display clients inside private prompt metadata.

## User Impact

Control UI users can expand a timestamped **Advisor guidance** notice to inspect guidance without creating another user turn. Other plugins use the same presentation with their own display name. Channels, native apps, and the TUI do not receive these notices.

Private `modelPromptProjection` metadata is now omitted from all display reads and message events; the user's visible message and the model's recorded input remain unchanged. No protocol schema, migration, or channel-delivery change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The notice says **Plugin name guidance**, not that steering succeeded. Canonical persistence can precede native submission, and no durable row field proves acceptance: `extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-active-turn.ts:443-452` persists before `attempt-steering.ts:292-378` can reject dispatch. Attribution remains useful without making an unsupported delivery claim. No new persistence field was added.

- Keep persisted steering rows `display: false`. Only the exact authenticated Control UI client ID enables an internal display projection in history/startup, incremental reads, exact-message hydration, and live delivery. Live recipient filtering precedes shared serialization caches.
- Reuse the native collapsed, non-turn-starting notice. The host records plugin attribution; optional SDK `displayText` separates operator-facing guidance from model-only instructions. Advisor supplies the finding without its delivery prefix. Existing notes without display text retain their original text rather than guessing at plugin-specific prose.
- Strip `modelPromptProjection` at the shared display sanitizer. It is private replay state, and the consumer audit found no UI, native-app, TUI, SDK, or extension reader of that field. Canonical persistence and runtime replay are untouched.
- Next-turn guidance is intentionally not rendered as another notice in this change; only its accidental metadata exposure is fixed.
- Expanded notices switch from **Show content** to **Hide content** and center their body with the native notice header. Steering notices preserve the existing mid-run notice grouping contract: like injected CLI context and background-task notices, they separate visible tool groups without starting another semantic turn.

## Evidence

Current-session authority is exercised through the real `chat.history` handler and live transcript broadcaster: revoking a shared-session viewer after asynchronous history/transcript preparation prevents the response or event from exposing guidance, while the authorized owner still receives the live event.

| Real Gateway path | Before revocation | Revoked after awaited preparation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`chat.history`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/6402a9d8627c75d6075f759d89bf663db01c8880/src/gateway/server-methods/chat-plugin-steering-authority.test.ts#L17) | Non-admin Control UI viewer receives the guidance. | Response is `INVALID_REQUEST` with no message payload or guidance text. |
| [`session.message`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/6402a9d8627c75d6075f759d89bf663db01c8880/src/gateway/server-broadcast.serialization.test.ts#L169) | Owner and non-admin Control UI viewer receive guidance. | Viewer socket receives nothing; the still-authorized owner receives the guidance. |

- Focused Gateway/plugin/Advisor/UI suites: **223 passed** across 11 files.
- Final display/privacy regression sweep: **119 passed** across 5 files (overlaps the focused suites).
- Native notice browser component: **4 passed**; production-bundle mock-Gateway E2E: **4 passed** across light/dark and desktop/mobile.
- UI polish regression suite: **18 unit tests**, **4 browser component cases**, and **4 production-bundle E2E cases** cover disclosure labels, body alignment, and all three mid-run notice kinds.
- Latest review-focused run: **16 Gateway tests passed**, including both real-path post-await revocation cases; **18 UI unit tests**, **4 browser component cases**, and **4 production-bundle E2E cases passed** with neutral guidance wording.
- The three next-turn privacy regressions **fail on origin/main `5678421c7571bf76502a6a645cb6d60e39ed85ab`** because history, live events, and deltas expose the captured prompt; they pass with this change.
- Changed-file Oxfmt/Oxlint, scoped core/UI/Advisor tsgo, i18n verification, and Madge import-cycle check exercised. One existing Solid reactivity warning remains in the unchanged run-failure branch of `chat-divider.tsx`.
- Consumer audit covered Android chat/voice/wear, shared iOS/macOS chat history/event codecs, the TUI, MCP relay/plugin readers, and public session sharing. Non-Control-UI history and live notice exclusion are also tested with equally authorized recipients.

The affected Gateway server test-type project and 15 live/broadcast tests also passed locally after completing the fixture’s profile type.

prs.title: fix: keep gateway responsive during external plugin preparation
prs.body:
Related: #160959

## What Problem This Solves

Keeps the Gateway responsive while preparing large non-bundled plugins.

## User Impact

External plugin source capture runs in a retained worker. The Gateway continues serving health requests during preparation, while plugin admission, registration, reload, and synchronous CLI behavior remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each captured external plugin has its own preparation worker. Existing plugin-instance caching reuses loaded instances, and recovery retains the original capture and worker. Capture can finish without an arbitrary two-minute deadline.

Workers return new native admission receipts and independently retained root leases to the original cache owner. Repeated private inspections reuse unchanged native captures, and cache retirement releases their custody.

The extracted PR wrapper includes the native-root lease module. The Copilot integration fixture implements the callable loader's preparation contract. Concurrent publication tests use independent admission owners, and the deferred-publication fixture explicitly closes its secondary database.

Recovery preserves the missing-capture behavior established in #155065: replacement can continue with its warning when the old temporary source is unavailable. The worker restores the owned recovery-error type. Copied source-path resolvers are recreated locally so consecutive rollbacks continue working after their producer worker retires.

Ordinary worker request/reply graphs now have message-scoped identities. Persistent handles are reserved for callable and native-resource owners, preserving cycles, aliases, and shared arguments while allowing temporary results to be collected.

## Evidence

### Transport lifetime — `7d738aa5aa95c83b2479e9919368a4a34e4de471`

- The garbage-collection regression failed before the correction: its control was collected while the original and decoded payload objects stayed retained. All temporary payload objects are collected after the fix, and retained callbacks remain callable.
- A real-worker test verifies collection of 100 module-preparation reply arrays while the artifact continues resolving its source.
- All 34 tests passed across codec, worker, async loader, native admission, gateway recovery, and installed-package suites.
- Production and plugin-test TypeScript, type-aware lint, formatting, whitespace, and the assertion-safety ratchet passed.
- Full `pnpm build` passed in 4m 57.3s.
- Fresh independent review found no actionable P0–P2 findings.


### Recovery corrections — `de532beba6065e3c414694c66de32d653dbcfeb8`

- The worker-backed missing-capture regression failed before the error-identity correction and now verifies the warning, unavailable recovery marker, and successful replacement registration.
- Both installed-package cases verify consecutive rollback after syntax and activation failures. They pass with the copied resolver lifetime correction.
- All 14 tests passed across `plugin-generation-worker.test.ts`, `server-plugin-reload-recovery.test.ts`, and `server-plugin-reload.installed-package.test.ts`, using `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <files> --maxWorkers=1`.
- The worker lifetime test verifies source resolution after final disposal and rejects paths outside the captured package.
- Production TypeScript, gateway and plugin test TypeScript, type-aware lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed.
- Full `pnpm build` passed in 5m 19.6s.
- Fresh independent review of both recovery corrections found no actionable P0–P2 findings.

### Preparation and reuse validation — `cdf47905`

- Native reuse regression reproduced a second physical capture before the correction and verifies the same captured files, namespace, hashes, and bytes afterward.
- 32 focused worker, async-loader, native-reference, and native-admission tests passed. The final affected two-file rerun passed all 19 tests.
- Wrapper import-closure suite: 13 passed; 5 POSIX-only checks skipped on Windows.
- Exact core2 TypeScript selection passed: six graphs and root-tooling stripe 1/4. Plugin test TypeScript, type-aware lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed.
- Full `pnpm build` passed, exit 0, in 7m 49s.
- Fresh independent review of the corrections found no actionable P0/P1 findings.
- The real-worker timeout regression verifies successful resolution and disposal after advancing the host task clock by 120,001 ms while publication is held.

### Built Gateway Measurement — `cdf47905`

Windows, Node 24.21.0, actual `openclaw.mjs` entry points, temporary state and loopback ports. The external fixture registers `proof.echo` and contains 4,000 generated JavaScript payload files totaling 16,384,000 bytes. Both captured trees were checked for all 4,000 files.

The baseline was the integrity-verified official npm 2026.10.3 package (`59cb447`). Its exact published AI and Koffi dependencies were installed in the temporary package; other missing dependencies were linked read-only from the checkout.

Independent HTTP `/healthz` and WebSocket `health` probes ran during the accepted `plugins.reload` call with a 15-second deadline. The final run required no startup-busy retries.

| Measured during reload | Published stable | PR candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Captured payload files | 4,000 | 4,000 |
| Reload duration | 22,515 ms | 21,717 ms |
| HTTP probes / failures | 6 / 1 timeout | 169 / 0 |
| WebSocket probes / failures | 4 / 1 timeout | 160 / 0 |

| Maximum WebSocket latency | 15,004.1 ms, timed out | 2,427.5 ms |
| Newly registered revision | 2 | 3 |
| Restart required | false | false |

The candidate opened the same stable-created state and preserved the synthetic plugin settings, agent workspace settings, and project marker. Plugin registration, completed reload receipts, and revision changes were verified. The candidate's runtime module path confirmed preparation-worker capture.

These are measurements from one synthetic workload; stable timeout latency is bounded by the probe deadline.

<details>
<summary>Build provenance</summary>

Source: `cdf47905a870ca77ad909c2a49724da91038c937`.

The build started with the native-reuse correction present before it was committed, so build-info records parent `8b42910723963650fcf145b792ef274fe48c0944`. The compiled production source matches the correction committed as `cdf47905`; subsequent edits were test fixtures.

`068AA53F615BCC5CB89CCAC2C3C7574998DE93BBA60E3D102983DA0EFF0E6F48`.

</details>

The source owner marks recovery capture, retained source custody, and recovery forks by callable identity; the codec and preparation-worker wrappers preserve that classification. prs.title: fix(reply): let stranded message-tool retries pass queued admission
prs.body:
## Problem

The existing stranded message-tool retry is rejected as a duplicate of its completed parent by queued admission. Once admitted, its first send is also rejected as already delivered because the parent's source tombstone takes precedence over the retry's active claim.

## Fix

Give the existing marked retry one deterministic internal admission identity while retaining the original source correlation. Use that identity for the exact active retry's terminal-delivery check and cleanup, reusing the existing terminal-run ledger. Parent redeliveries, duplicate retries, pending sends, and completed sends remain fenced. No persisted field or schema change is added.

## User impact

A substantive answer that was never sent can reach the existing restricted message-tool recovery turn and be delivered once. Ordinary source-redelivery protection is unchanged; this does not change same-run steering behavior.

## Proof

- Real queued-admission regression: one retry reaches model execution; retry and parent replay do not execute again or add a second user transcript row.
- Real admission through message-tool/channel dispatch: the first retry send reaches transport once; duplicate and replayed sends are refused. Admission and delivery claims are not mocked; transport is a test adapter, not a live external channel.
- Focused run before the base update: all 4 selected files executed, 297 tests passed. The updated fixtures use the typed session status, Gateway identity, and transcript reader contracts.
- Two unrelated tooling failures required the landed main fixes in d09442030ed (Windows partition ownership) and 372d648e448 (capacity proof independent of live inventory). The PR's two test-type failures were repaired.

The small shared-owner change adds no new manager or storage. Reverting restores the prior retry behavior.

prs.title: fix(release): plugin asset hooks inherit release tooling's tsconfig
prs.body:
## Problem

Publishing 2026.10.4 failed before anything was published ([Release Publish 38814521097](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38814521097) → [plugin-npm-release 38815531612](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38815531612)). `preview_plugin_pack` for `discord` and `slack` failed in "Prepare immutable npm preflight artifact":

```
[plugin-npm-runtime-build] build assets slack: cd ../.. && node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-plugin-control-ui.mts extensions/slack
packages/terminal-core/src/ansi.ts:1
import { containingSegment } from "@openclaw/normalization-core/grapheme";
SyntaxError: The requested module '@openclaw/normalization-core/grapheme' does not provide an export named 'containingSegment'
```

#173259 set `TSX_TSCONFIG_PATH` to `.release-tooling/tsconfig.json` on that step so trusted tooling resolves its own workspace packages. The step also runs each plugin's `openclaw.assetScripts.build` hook, which builds the **packed candidate tree** (its own `scripts/tsx.mjs`, its own `packages/*`). `runPluginAssetCommand` passed `process.env` through unchanged, so the hook inherited the tooling tsconfig and mapped the candidate's `@openclaw/normalization-core` imports onto main's packages. The 2026.10.4 candidate (`383c124cc32`) exports `containingSegment`; current main no longer does. Any candidate whose workspace packages differ from main's breaks the same way — this is the mirror image of #173259.

## Solution

`runPluginAssetCommand` strips `TSX_TSCONFIG_PATH` from the hook environment. An asset hook builds the package's own source tree, so it must resolve that tree's tsconfig; the candidate's `scripts/tsx.mjs` shim reselects a tsconfig itself when needed. Tooling steps keep the pinned tsconfig.

## Evidence

- Real reproduction in a clean 2026.10.4 candidate checkout (`383c124cc32`): `TSX_TSCONFIG_PATH=<main>/tsconfig.json node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-plugin-control-ui.mts extensions/slack` → exit 1 with the same `containingSegment` SyntaxError; without the variable → exit 0.
- Regression test `builds package assets against the packed tree's tsconfig, not release tooling's` in `test/scripts/plugin-npm-runtime-assets.test.ts` fails on the old code and passes with the fix.
- `pnpm test test/scripts/plugin-npm-runtime-assets.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 10 passed, ~4.9 s wall; no real processes or timers added.

Blocks 2026.10.4 publication (release tooling only; candidate unchanged).

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: copying a modal-dialog recovery hint after a browser action on a non-default profile can accept a different profile's dialog instead. Dialog IDs are page-local, so both profiles can have a pending `d1`.

## User Impact

User impact: the printed recovery command keeps the selected browser profile. No new options, configuration, permissions, or browser state are introduced. Default-profile and JSON output behavior are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry the existing browser profile into the recovery hint, normalized like request routing. Use `--browser-profile=<name>` so configured leading-hyphen names remain unambiguous. The regression replays the printed command through registered click/dialog commands rather than checking a string alone.

## Evidence

- **Actual CLI and Gateway, without a transport mock:** [baseline](https://github.com/ly85206559/openclaw/actions/runs/38814279212) on pristine `a166c4931a4015935b710070f1a4a1c585b32fb1` genuinely failed the two wrong-profile assertions; [current-head candidate](https://github.com/ly85206559/openclaw/actions/runs/38815127875) on `a9f8fa35372173e60d8fafd3e9ee17bc900f3dd2` succeeded. Both used the same [proof driver](https://github.com/ly85206559/openclaw/blob/87302d58ef59934ad8eae3447f912d2c4162c00e/.proof/browser-dialog-profile/cli-dialog-profile.mjs) after pristine canonical `qaRuntime` builds: a real supported Gateway process plus six separate supported browser CLI processes, authenticated Gateway RPC, and two real Chromium profiles each holding `d1`. The driver substituted only the accept/ID choices in the printed hint, never repaired its routing. All six browser commands exited 0 with empty stderr; source/build custody, page/fixture/error arrays, owned-process shutdown, both browser contexts, port rebinds, and isolated-state cleanup were checked. Raw artifacts were downloaded and inspected. An earlier proof-fixture attempt was canceled before product execution after source inspection found an unsupported fixture-only config field; it is not passing evidence.

Sanitized excerpts from the actual process output and page receipts (synthetic endpoints and token omitted):

```text
Baseline work action stdout:
Action blocked by a modal dialog ("d1"). Use openclaw browser dialog --accept or --dismiss --dialog-id <id> to continue.
Literal replay: pnpm --silent openclaw browser dialog --accept --dialog-id d1
Page receipts: openclaw accepted=true; work still pending, then explicit dismiss=false.

Current-head work action stdout:
Action blocked by a modal dialog ("d1"). Use openclaw browser dialog --browser-profile=work --accept or --dismiss --dialog-id <id> to continue.
Literal replay: pnpm --silent openclaw browser dialog --browser-profile=work --accept --dialog-id d1
stdout: dialog armed
Page receipts: work accepted=true; openclaw still pending, then explicit dismiss=false.
Final DOM: work=accepted; openclaw=dismissed.
behaviorFailures=[]; errors=[]; pageErrors=[]; fixtureErrors=[]
```

- [Real Chromium baseline](https://github.com/ly85206559/openclaw/actions/runs/38799928224) on pristine `a166c4931a4015935b710070f1a4a1c585b32fb1`: two isolated profiles each opened a real confirm dialog with ID `d1`. Replaying the work-profile hint accepted the default profile; work remained pending until an explicit-profile dismiss. The final DOM and loopback confirmation receipts agreed. Exactly one test failed the intended wrong-profile assertion, with no skipped tests or page/fixture/harness/cleanup errors.
- [Candidate Chromium job](https://github.com/ly85206559/openclaw/actions/runs/38801469587/job/116651307650) passed: replaying the actual hint accepted only work, and the untouched default dialog remained available for explicit dismissal. All six registered CLI invocations completed without runtime stderr or exit calls; raw receipts and source custody were inspected. This ran at `6e2e4d48638baf56c866d2021c3b06b8bca306c9`; current `a9f8fa35372173e60d8fafd3e9ee17bc900f3dd2` changes only the native test fixture, with identical production/browser runtime inputs.
- The first native runs failed before their target assertions because the test mocked a helper export instead of the dialog's Gateway boundary; they are not counted as regression evidence or passing checks. The corrected fixture uses the existing Gateway test helper. prs.title: fix(feishu): accept the documented markdown table mode
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes gateway startup rejecting Feishu's documented `markdown.tables` option and applies the selected table mode across sends, replies, presentations, and previews.

## User Impact

Channel and account table settings are accepted, including the delivering/default account. Ordinary `off` table messages settle as authored rich-text posts. In `off`, presentations keep controls and show literal rows in card text and live previews. When idle close reuses a posted answer, missing reasoning follows it without duplicating it.

Accepted-prefix failures keep their receipts and do not replay accepted content. The unchanged post renderer still draws authored Markdown tables as grids.

## Why This Change Was Made

Feishu's strict schema gains the shared table option and keeps the legacy `markdown.mode` and `markdown.tableMode`. Formatting-aware delivery converts whole logical tables before chunking. Presentations and reasoning degrade undrawable block-mode tables to readable lists. For `off`, display-only delimiter escaping leaves authored fallback and deduplication text alone. The PR also declares `block` as Feishu's table default (see Table default).

The generated channel baseline rises from 4031 to 4033 for `channels.feishu.markdown.tables` and `channels.feishu.accounts.*.markdown.tables`. Core and plugin counts stay unchanged. [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f659a3576b1/AGENTS.md#L96) permits narrow source-verified exceptions with a reason. This exception is not maintainer approval.

## Evidence

### Upgrade proof

Published stable `2026.10.2` (`b8952d477f0c`) seeded channel `markdown.mode: native` and `markdown.tableMode: ascii`, an account's `mode: escape` and `tableMode: simple`, and two accounts without Markdown settings. The proof head (`effbf8c7a8ab`) used that state, main (`29fc232d40be`) a copy. Both used fresh detached worktrees and separately packed Feishu plugins.

| Check | Stable | Proof head | Upstream main |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Legacy config validates, keys and overrides read back unchanged | Yes | Yes, before and after migration | Yes, before and after migration |
| Feishu config object on disk | Seed | Byte-identical | Byte-identical |
| Stored session loads with the same key and ID, and a label update survives restart | Created and patched here | Yes | Yes |
| Documented `markdown.tables` at channel and account scope | Rejected, exit 1 | Accepted, all four values | Rejected, exit 1 |
| Account override wins, unset accounts inherit the channel value | Key rejected | Yes | Key rejected |

Both builds refuse the schema 24 agent database (Gateway exit 78) until `openclaw doctor --fix` migrates it to 26. Repair and shutdown then exit 1 with `ERR_SPAWN_BROKER_UNAVAILABLE`. The cause is undiagnosed and both databases stay readable. This is compatibility evidence, not a clean upgrade. Replacement was manual, not the published updater. Credentials were synthetic and Feishu accounts and transports disabled. Only the Feishu config object is byte-identical. Maintenance changed other config. The diff has no `src/state` change or database migration.

### Table default

Upgrade proof resolves `code` on stable and main and `block` on the proof head for unconfigured or legacy-only accounts. Legacy keys do not select the mode. In `auto`, stable and main route ordinary pipe-bordered tables to raw cards (`markdown.ts:25-27`, `outbound.ts:253-262`, `reply-dispatcher.ts:1289-1293` at main `29fc232d40be`, same logic at stable). Before captures show native grids. `block` retains them. Other modes convert before routing (`outbound-text-plan.ts:48-49`). Head lines use `948b2088919`.

Against main, standalone pipe-less and one-sided-pipe tables now get cards on `auto` sends and non-streamed replies. In chat text, blockquoted and list-opened tables take posts, but forced-card sends bypass that guard. Main sent these shapes to cards in streams or beside a fence or pipe table. Table messages needing multiple static cards also take posts. These posts use `code` unless fences cannot survive the cut. The five-table limit excludes streams. Direct post sends and edits still resolve `code`. Comments now convert raw rows to `code`. Explicit modes and size/fence safeguards apply.

A `code` default would fence those grids in cards (`outbound.markdown-tables.test.ts:662`). `block` also drops "Avoid Markdown tables." from Feishu group prompts, even with account `code` or `bullets`, because `src/auto-reply/reply/groups.ts:129-131` reads the plugin default. Telegram and Matrix already declare `block`. Maintainers decide the default.

### Current repair verification

CI tested `cf49e1d3c83` merged with main `0858cc64613`. On that head 88 checks passed, none failed, 49 were skipped and CodeQL was neutral. In `checks-node-changed-1`, `telegram-ingress-coalescing.e2e.test.ts` passed 20 tests, and the shard's seven other targets, six contract tests and a gateway e2e test, passed 115. Locally at `cf49e1d3c83`, `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions` and `tsgo:extensions:test`, four ratchets and five generated-file check scripts passed, and `extension-feishu` passed 1256 tests.

### Fresh Lark before/after rendering

[Comparison and limits](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147886#issuecomment-6093982920) cover four byte-identical synthetic fixture pairs through the production send, reply and streaming components with the real SDK. Captures compare plugin source `e7f29073f4dc` with rendering files published at `34f132a1bb49`, not whole deployments, and were not retaken at `effbf8c7a8ab`. Merges after `34f132a1bb49` left `presentation-card.ts`, `card-table-shapes.ts`, `markdown.ts` and `outbound.ts` unchanged, kept the off-mode projection in `streaming-update.ts`, and moved the reasoning formatter and close route into `reasoning-structure.ts` and `table-routing.ts` intact, so the three off-mode rows render through the same code. The idle row's settlement bookkeeping took upstream's latest-settlement shape, so that row rests on the proof head's regression tests, not the captures.

| State | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Off-mode presentation | ![Native table despite off mode](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ff00b807-a9e6-465b-9f63-5829ea331710) | ![Literal rows and retained button](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/96bf5ced-1f4e-4375-985f-cf0a9ab4132f) |
| Off-mode answer preview | ![Native answer-preview table](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e54aec3f-9a7c-41a7-886d-145522b8feed) | ![Literal answer-preview rows](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/02c9e642-b5dd-4203-a3cf-87be4de7f7aa) |
| Off-mode reasoning preview | ![Reasoning-table rows missing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/325f6680-67b2-4de6-99f7-a93a0eb9afb1) | ![Reasoning-table rows visible](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c07ea2c4-df53-4628-9793-8e1946bbf661) |
| Idle reuse of accepted answer | ![Reasoning disappears after idle](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4087a562-8abe-4253-8517-ac947981a16c) | ![One answer and separate reasoning](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/430c18ca-2774-45cc-9055-44da9e169007) |

Both runs exited 0. Idle settlement adds exactly one reasoning-only post and keeps two actual receipts without replaying the accepted answer. All three dispatcher cases keep byte-identical authored final-post payloads. The button is retained, not clicked. All eight images were verified in the saved comment. The captures used no Gateway, model or mainland Feishu client. Lark still joins adjacent quoted paragraphs in the reasoning preview, not addressed here.

### Historical evidence

Pinned to the commits named, not current-head proof.

- CLI at `dbb422c85a5` (before) and `08c0c469de4` (after). Before, `config validate` rejected `tables` at channel and account scope (exit 1) and `gateway run` refused to start (exit 78). After, validation passed, the Gateway reached ready and shut down with child exit 0, and `doctor --fix --non-interactive` removed no `markdown` key.
- Gateway send RPC at `314ddb95`, HTTPS Feishu stub, real SDK, `renderMode` unset. Accounts resolved `code`, `bullets` and `off` as configured across full, reply and default-account sends, all exit 0.
- Authority proof at `c311d8a5d53` ([comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147886#issuecomment-5707888042)), registered sender, production components, real SDK. Allowed sent four of four with every receipt. Revoked after one of four was accepted, kept its receipt and exact content in the partial-delivery envelope, and the claim guard refused the pending terminal rather than replay it.
- Lark client round at `9d52663f11b` and `d0f6e3a3ba0` ([comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147886#issuecomment-5689525610)), real SDK, 62 captures. Blockquote and list-opened tables became readable fenced posts, and a mixed message kept both tables.
- Regression tests for schema acceptance, account selection, off-mode finals, comment delivery, block posts, preview dedupe and presentation cards each failed before the fix and passed after.

Native plugin turns and side questions keep the configured `on-request` policy, so managed accounts can use their existing approval flow. No account-policy change is required.
