prs.title: fix(mac): preserve companion exec timeouts
prs.body:
Closes #139706

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running long commands through the macOS companion would hit an unexplained failure after about 20 seconds, even when the requested command timeout was much longer. The Gateway reported the companion as unavailable and could not return the command's real result.

## Why This Change Was Made

The companion request already carries the caller's command timeout, so the socket response deadline now follows it with a 5-second grace period. The transport also distinguishes pre-send unavailability, post-send response loss, and response timeout; submitted commands remain fail-closed and are never replayed locally. A zero command timeout disables the transport deadline as well.

## User Impact

Long-running macOS companion commands can now wait for their requested lifetime and return their actual result. A late response is reported as `TIMEOUT`, while a lost response is reported as an unknown outcome instead of being mislabeled as an unreachable companion. Safe fallback remains available only when the request was never submitted.

## Evidence

- Before fix, base `9e5bb4a3ecd`: the real UDS regression suite passed while its `timeout` case observed `null` after a signed request had started a child; the direct probe returned: `{"result":null}`
- After fix, commit `eb8b824922a`: the same 50 ms transport probe with a 30 s command timeout returned: `{"result":{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"TIMEOUT","reason":"timeout","message":"TIMEOUT: macOS app exec host response timed out; execution outcome is unknown"}}}`
- Response-loss probe changed from `{"result":null}` before the fix to typed `UNKNOWN / response-lost` after the fix.
- Real UDS transport tests: **21 passed**, including child-started timeout, response-loss, malformed-response, zero-timeout, signing, and cancellation cases.
- Node-host system-run tests: **87 passed**; enforced response-loss path confirms `runCommand` was not called (no local replay).
- `pnpm test:changed`: passed.
- `pnpm check`: passed.
- `pnpm check:changed`: passed.
- `pnpm build`: passed.
- Autoreview: `scoped-clean`, no accepted/actionable P0/P1 findings.
- No screenshot is applicable; this is a transport/runtime behavior change with no UI surface.

## Rebase onto `main` (`e8684576989`)

Main still uses a fixed 20 s socket deadline (`exec-host.ts`, `params.timeoutMs ?? 20_000`) and maps every transport failure to `COMPANION_APP_UNAVAILABLE`. Conflicts were re-expressed on main's current node-host code:

- `src/node-host/invoke.ts`: main removed `runViaMacAppExecHost` and moved the macOS app dispatch into `invoke-system-run.ts`. Main's version is kept; the response deadline is now derived inside `requestExecHostViaSocket` from `request.timeoutMs` (+5 s grace, `0` disables it), so no call-site timeout is needed. The previously exported `resolveExecHostResponseTimeoutMs` is inlined (it would otherwise be a test-only export); `exec-host.test.ts` covers the same three cases through the real call.
- `src/node-host/invoke-system-run.ts`: `sendSystemRunDenied` now takes `(opts, execution, message, reason)`; `timeout` → `TIMEOUT` and `response-lost` → `UNKNOWN` are mapped there.
- `invoke-system-run.test.ts` / `invoke-system-run.socket.test.ts`: the two new cases are rewritten on main's `runMac` / `invokeResult` / `expectExecDeniedEvent` helpers; the socket test asserts the exact `UNKNOWN` result and the `response-lost` denial reason.
- `src/infra/exec-host.native.test-support.ts`: the macOS native transport proof expected `null` after a dropped response; it now expects the typed `UNKNOWN` / `response-lost` result.

The numbers above are from the previous base; CI on this head is the gate for the re-run. The native proof runs on macOS only.

prs.title: perf(doctor): avoid repeating integrity checks after agent migrations
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a repeated full SQLite integrity scan during Doctor after an agent database schema migration, extending update downtime for large stores.

## User Impact

Schema-crossing updates reuse the integrity admission they just established when Doctor next opens that agent database. The initial integrity check, WAL-aware backups, original migration witness, forward recovery, and restart seal requirements remain unchanged. No schema, stored format, or configuration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The migration schema owner already publishes current validation facts. Registering the database afterward without its admitted connection invalidated those facts, so a later open scanned the whole file again. Let the existing schema owner register through its admitted-handle contract; retain explicit registration for branches that skip that owner. The schema owner uses the open SQLite handle's native path so symlink/.. locators still identify the correct physical file.

Production delta is +6/-3 lines (+3 net, including two ownership comments): the two bypass branches must retain registration, and the schema owner must preserve the opened file's physical identity. There is no new cache, seal, wrapper, or parallel admission mechanism. Existing backups already request reflinks where supported.

## Evidence

- The changed focused test file passed all 17 tests with one worker. The regression runs a real historical-schema migration and verifies one initial worker integrity check and zero integrity scans on the subsequent ordinary same-process reopen.
- Initial PR CI exposed a symlink/.. registration regression in `state-migrations.media-persistence-targets.test.ts`. Reproduced locally and fixed at the schema owner by using the already-open handle's native path. The complete targets file (8 tests) and admission-reuse file (11 tests) pass; the original 17-test migration file also passes again.
- Scoped lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Broad validation is delegated to PR CI; no Testbox/Crabbox lease was used.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): no actionable P2-or-higher findings, including a fresh review of the locator repair. Autoreview refused the configured provider route; no operator configuration was changed.
- An observed large-database crossing spent 56.454 seconds on this duplicate scan within roughly 509 seconds of stopped-to-ready time. Removing that scan projects about 453 seconds (8m29s → 7m33s), assuming other phases are unchanged. This is a historical projection, not an end-to-end deployment measurement.
- Isolated Linux benchmark: 5,000 sessions, 6,000 retained runs, 10,495 transcript events, 200 approvals, 100 cron jobs, an empty outbox, and a 232,706,048-byte agent database. Independently regenerated identical fixtures exercised the real v26 → v27 update migration and ordinary reopen. Actual full integrity checks: **2 → 1**. Same-process reopen: **609.393 ms → 6.729 ms** (90.6×; 98.9% lower). The retained migration check was 591.39 ms → 610.29 ms. Single-run timings, with the deterministic scan-count reduction as the primary evidence; total migration timings include source/worker startup variance and are not claimed as a separate speedup. Timings were captured at `3363dfba6d21`, before the native-path correction; final-head focused tests reverify the scan-count contract.
- Fresh-process reopen remained neutral: 647.067 ms → 647.832 ms, with a full integrity scan in both cases. This change preserves same-process admission; it does not publish a new restart seal.
- The state-only crossing, initial pre-migration scan, backup hashing, and other Doctor phase delays remain outside this reduction. A predecessor's seal is not reused across changed schema identity. No production deployment or end-to-end outage measurement was performed.

prs.title: fix(mac): long exec commands through the macOS app node fail after 20 seconds
prs.body:
Fixes #139706

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: macOS companion commands fail after about 20 seconds despite a longer requested timeout, and report a slow or lost response as an unavailable app.

## User Impact

Long commands can return their real result within their requested timeout. A submitted request whose reply times out reports `TIMEOUT`; a lost or oversized reply reports `UNKNOWN`. Neither is replayed locally. Unreachable companions remain `COMPANION_APP_UNAVAILABLE`, and caller cancellation still closes the request.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing exec-host requester now derives its response deadline from the command timeout plus the companion's 15-second approval window and 5 seconds of transport grace. Missing timeouts retain the 20-second default; zero disables the deadline while preserving cancellation. The shared socket owner distinguishes submission from response loss, and the existing node result owner maps those outcomes.

Original fix by @holgergruenhagen, building on @ylcn91's #140067; maintainer cleanup simplifies deadline/error mapping, handles oversized replies consistently, removes duplicate mocked coverage, converts existing fault deadlines to fake clocks, and documents the behavior. Compared draft #163978; its separate connection deadline does not address error classification or the full approval window, so no code from that draft was folded. Keep this PR; the alternatives remain open pending the coordinator's landing decision.

Deferred callbacks retain only this invocation's immutable timeout budget and socket/request identity; the socket owner tracks submission, checks current cancellation before sending, and destroys the reader on abort. Native approval, command, config, path, and session ownership are unchanged; these callbacks only settle the originating request.

## Evidence

- Source/history confirmation: main `04adf1677dec04cd3fc076b27c346e46e007002d` still uses `params.timeoutMs ?? 20_000` while the production caller supplies the budget only inside `request`. Timeout, close, and oversized-response paths return `null`, which the node host labels unavailable.
- Exact-head [CI run 38805647953](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38805647953) **passed** for `076a9cfdd46c3c2d38858d6d35d9ab0f2a6f203f` (20:53:57–21:11:51 UTC; 17m54s total workflow time). All selected node test shards, production/test typechecks, lint, docs, and guards passed. Overall PR checks: 75 passed, 54 skipped, zero failing or pending; `openclaw/ci-gate` passed. No retries, CI repairs, or inherited failures. PR CI is the test gate per maintainer policy. Native Swift transport proof and the separate build-artifacts job were skipped by CI selection and are not claimed for this head.
- Regressions include `receives a late reply within command budget %s plus approval and grace` (30 s and 1 s command budgets), `classifies an oversized reply as response loss after submission`, `returns the caller's typed timeout result after the request is submitted`, `can wait without a transport deadline when timeoutMs is zero`, `classifies a companion response deadline as a timeout`, and `does not replay locally when a completed execution loses its socket response`. Existing signing, unreachable-host, cancellation, malformed-response, and native-support assertions remain.
- Changed-file `oxfmt --check` passed (10 files). Static oxlint passed (9 TypeScript files, 231 rules, zero diagnostics), using the repository's applicable core rules with only the nonmatching UI-only Solid override omitted because the supplied parent install lacks its Solid plugin. The normal wrapper also cannot resolve this nested checkout's absent local `node_modules`; no install was performed. `git diff --check` passed.
- Autoreview: `scoped-clean`, no accepted/actionable P0–P2 findings on `076a9cfdd46c3c2d38858d6d35d9ab0f2a6f203f`. The precommit review independently identified the oversized-reply defect in the original index and confirmed the working-tree fix; the final branch review is clean. Used the canonical installed autoreview helper because the repository entrypoint no longer contains a script.
- Live Gateway/Crabbox/Testbox proof, local tests, local typechecks, and negative controls were intentionally skipped per maintainer policy. No leases or Gateway processes were started. New deadline regressions advance fake clocks. Per-file test wall times were not published as CI artifacts; the total workflow time above is not the cost of these regressions.
- Contributor-reported historical app evidence at `3273803f88e89a22141d0cb979bfcc3272c55e76`: 25 s and 40 s commands returned normally after failing at 20 s on the base; a 5 s process timeout remained effective. This was not rerun for the current head.
- Latest full ClawSweeper review (comment 6168325229, head `789d6e70ecaf0420e8c466188b199dcd0669515b`) has no findings; no human reviews or inline findings were present.

Change size against main: production +58/-13 (net +45), tests/support +264/-30 (net +234), docs +9/-0. Maintainer cleanup removes 9 production lines from the contributor head. Remaining production growth is the necessary deadline calculation and explicit transport-outcome classification; no unrelated deletion was added to meet a LOC quota.

prs.title: fix: prevent stale leases after brief offline maintenance
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A state lease can remain held until expiry when brief offline maintenance interrupts its release. A later operation then waits for a lease whose operation callback has already finished.

## User Impact

Lease cleanup now recovers when typed maintenance contention clears within the existing two-second retry budget. The existing ownership checks, database identity checks, timeout, and handling of other failures stay intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

Release already retries SQLite lock contention. This adds the existing typed maintenance-contention classifier to that retry condition, including nonempty aggregates whose errors all qualify. Only release is retried; the operation callback is not replayed. There is no new retry loop or schema change.

The investigation began with the model-picker catalog-replacement failure in [CI run 38745029040](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38745029040) for #171652. Its log showed operation/cleanup failure followed by reload waiting for the same five-minute lease, but did not expose the underlying error class. The controlled release-owner regression proves this typed retry defect; it does not reproduce the entire Gateway/UI incident. Retention of failed native cleanup for a later canonical close landed separately in #173225.

## Evidence

The original implementation failed the four intended maintenance regression cases while passing both refusal controls. The fixed implementation passes all six cases.

Scoped validation completed successfully:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/state/openclaw-state-lease-maintenance-retry.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: six cases passed; Vitest reported 382.19 seconds, dominated by cold prerequisite compilation.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`: passed, 74.44 seconds.
- Scoped type-aware lint on both files: passed, 157.26 seconds including the artifact-lock wait.
- Scoped formatting and whitespace checks: passed.
- Fresh isolated Codex review through P2 of the merged candidate: no actionable findings; final source verification passed.

Current head `f6b20e0c2d37eb51193ca4c5352f130593b7f535` incorporates main `5fdd725db9ae4221bd735a879c3409a78feeb50b` with a conflict-free ordinary merge. Both authored files, their maintenance and SQLite classifiers, retry backoff, package manifest, lockfile, and Vitest configuration remain byte-identical to the validated implementation, so scoped execution proof is reused.

The main refresh brings in the landed Raw editor retention repair from [#173483](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173483). The previous lease head failed the guarded-config E2E when a config publication replaced its textarea before input. That repair preserves textarea identity, focus, and selection, and passed its full exact-head CI. Fresh CI is required for this new lease head; no previous-head exception is applied.

Two authored files, +78/-1: production code grows by four lines and the focused regression adds 73 lines. No UI rendering or dependency pins are changed by the authored patch. No live Gateway incident reproduction is claimed.

prs.title: fix: preserve restricted Codex session continuation
prs.body:
Related: #144917. Builds on #156651 (mywondvision).

Related to #148329, but does **not** resolve it: authority/client-dependent tool descriptions, schemas, and catalog membership can still change the durable fingerprint. This PR addresses compatible restricted continuation and temporary-grant isolation.

## What Problem This Solves

A persistent tool restriction can make an ordinary Codex follow-up start a new native thread and resend assembled history. The host must distinguish a conversation-owned restriction from a temporary run-owned restriction or additive grant.

## User Impact

Compatible persistent restrictions retain the native conversation across warm turns and Gateway restarts. Temporary restrictions and additive grants use isolated owners and return to the durable conversation afterward. No-op wildcard and scheduled policies retain ordinary continuation.

When a persistent creation policy changes, the existing guarded replacement operation prepares a successor using already-assembled history. Failed startup preserves the previous binding and protected owners retain their refusal behavior. In the covered configured-MCP ownership transition, predecessor cleanup follows replacement commit; independent rotation reasons retain their existing behavior. Automatic guarded recovery remains a **maintainer product decision**, not an approved policy assumption.

## Why This Change Was Made

The restricted-resume and creation-policy fingerprint foundation adapts mywondvision's #156651 at `7e56f0b802b8fe9deb3d5ed95b469fb50aa69278`, with attribution retained. This contribution adds host-produced policy lifetime, guarded recovery, prepared-history replay, and regression coverage. If merged, maintainers or the original author can close #156651 as superseded; no prior agreement is claimed.

The optional persisted fingerprint needs no schema migration. Legacy unattested owners transition once through existing guards. No compaction implementation, retry subsystem, replacement database, or separate bootstrap-acceptance PR #172450 is included.

The follow-up commit `27e2843f8901d45174b19bf0cd90503e86d107b2` fixes a static import cycle, aligns ordinary-run test fixtures without weakening assertions or shared defaults, preserves temporary grant lifetime across the private-state boundary, and orders restricted replacement checks after configured-MCP ownership classification. The follow-up is 13 files, +59/-21; the full PR is 31 files, +1252/-95, including its adapted foundation and tests.

## Evidence

Current source: `27e2843f8901d45174b19bf0cd90503e86d107b2`; tree `1480084c7962f6afa41959a9f37da43e9d03a46f`. Follow-up patch from reviewed head `604bc2738a19ec85085801a72451bf41b681d536`: SHA-256 `b8ecd1aac3d0cb68904fa85018484be58da59e57daf597a29e424ecea5899c32`.

- Focused source verification passed: 35 tests for the first failed CI bundle; 129 tests covering the second failed bundle and affected restricted lifecycle; 108 tests for the grant handoff regression. These runs overlap and are **not** an additive unique-test count. The grant regression first failed before its correction. All 29 failures from the second original CI bundle are present in the passing run. Scoped types, lint, formatting, and the import-cycle check pass.
- Canonical `qaRuntime` build passed on Node 24.19.0 / pnpm 12.10.1. Linux smoke and all 22,247 built-file hashes match the admitted manifest before and after the effect proof. Generated build metadata embeds the pre-commit base; the full source/patch/runtime manifest establishes exact equivalence to the published commit.
- Real isolated Gateway and native Codex 0.160.1, with a deterministic local Responses provider: **12 completed turns, 24 requests, six actual permitted receipt-file writes and six rejected calls** in one physical OpenClaw session. Temporary grant withdrawal returns to the original native owner; cold restart retains it. Policy narrowing and broadening create and then reuse the appropriate successor. Native accepted/completed IDs match terminal Gateway receipts; all owned processes stopped.
- Sender isolation passed through real QA channel ingress: Alice -> Bob -> Alice, one physical session, native A-B-A, six provider requests; Alice writes succeed, the forced Bob call is rejected, and channel processing acknowledgments plus final replies complete.
- Genuine archived stable v2026.10.3 saved-state replay passed on the fixed runtime: Doctor succeeds; the original three transcript rows, saved settings/tool denial and original accepted-turn ledger row remain exact. Two continuations reuse one attested successor (transcript 3 -> 7, ledger 1 -> 3), retaining old native rollout bytes. This is archived stable state, not a fresh stable run; the legacy unattested binding transitions once instead of resuming its old native thread. Native Codex 0.160.0 matches that archived state.
- **Current-head hosted CI passed:** [run 38802766048](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38802766048). All three previously failing jobs pass. CI tested merge `1383e0296ac2b8dac9543796d7a3e1ab4c17cade` (source head27e2843f into basecfbbe0c2); runtime proofs above bind the published source tree separately.
- Independent review and canonical Codex autoreview found no confirmed P0-P2 findings within the supplied changed scopes and contracts. Reviews did not execute the tests themselves.

The new provider intentionally forces tool calls; this is final-effect and ownership evidence, **not real-model recall or reasoning evidence**. The first packet's four actual ContextPilot requests remain historical evidence for `604bc2738a19ec85085801a72451bf41b681d536`, not a new-head model run. No production deployment or live baseline performance claim is made.

First packet: [published archive](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33508499/restricted-continuation-upstream-packet-ready.zip). Second packet: `restricted-continuation-second-packet.zip`, attached with the follow-up response. It includes the completed hosted CI receipt and an offline integrity/selected-evidence consistency verifier.

Second packet archive SHA-256: `e623ac588250c8e710c4e413d545caf1fcdd1d5130ce65c2967239c5b1e8ac98`.

prs.title: fix(imap): continue after malformed messages
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the IMAP watcher stops advancing to later messages when one message contains MIME content that the email parser rejects.

## User Impact

User impact: later valid email continues through the IMAP automation flow even when an earlier mailbox message cannot be parsed. The rejected message remains in the mailbox and is recorded as skipped.

## Why This Change Was Made

Parser rejection is deterministic for the same message bytes, so retrying it cannot recover. The watcher now records `message-parse-failed`, advances its cursor, and continues without dispatching the malformed message. The IMAP runtime documentation now describes this behavior.

## Evidence

- Exact head: `e840132113cdfd2d2183ff19666d1d2821007c9f`.
- Negative scenario: a 10,002-part MIME message is rejected by `mailparser`, is not dispatched, and records one `message-parse-failed` skip.
- Positive control: the valid message immediately after it advances the cursor and is the only message dispatched to the hook sink.
- `pnpm test extensions/imap/src/watcher.test.ts` — 22 tests passed through the local IMAP protocol-boundary harness.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` — passed.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --openclaw-focused-config extensions/imap/src/watcher.ts extensions/imap/src/watcher.test.ts` — passed.
- `pnpm format:docs:check` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

Environment: Linux x86_64 with Node v24.20.0 and pnpm 12.9.0. No external IMAP provider was exercised; the focused test uses the plugin's real local IMAP connection boundary.

prs.title: perf(control-ui): avoid reparsing completed code while replies stream
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Streaming replies containing ordinary code comparisons repeatedly parse and sanitize completed Markdown as later blocks arrive.

## User Impact

Less JavaScript work and long-frame blocking while an answer streams, with identical rendered output. Total renderer CPU remains nearly unchanged because style recalculation dominates; this does not eliminate all streaming jank.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cold-load campaign originally measured 14 visual states over roughly 15 seconds for a signed-in dashboard deep-link reload. This lane measures subsequent streaming use.

The renderer already cached completed Markdown, but its HTML guard treated `<` inside code as possible HTML. Once a comparison arrived, later completed blocks could re-render the entire prefix. The existing streaming owner now uses the shared Markdown code-ownership parser on newly completed text and retains its HTML classification in the existing bounded cache. Actual HTML retains its conservative fallback. The DOM owner also skips unchanged non-media fragments while preserving media lifecycle updates.

The benchmark adds a 15,468-character answer with prose, code comparisons, and tables, delivered cumulatively in 645 deltas at a nominal 30 per second. It measures untraced streaming CPU by message-length quartile, parsing work, LoAF, frame gaps, and trusted composer input latency, and accepts the campaign's generic LoAF/mutation and WebSocket census probes. Native HTML hooks retain string conversion for TrustedHTML inputs omitted by lib.dom's types; the benchmark rejects non-finite character counts.

## Evidence

**Final-head comparison:** seven interleaved baseline/candidate pairs on one quiet AWS Crabbox **c7a.4xlarge**, lease **cbx_70beb3ceff7f**: 16 CPUs, AMD EPYC 9R14, about 30.6 GiB RAM, startup load 1.04. Baseline runtime source: `e8633bd8930438e3ee165ad934d60e8a1ff9bd63`; candidate: `97cda729f353094dfb950a657e52129979b3f9f0`. Both production bundles use identical fixture/probes and the repository's Playwright Chromium. Boot profiling ends before the streaming segment; no validation jobs run during the comparison.

Values are median (IQR) across seven runs:

| Streaming measurement | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Last-quarter JavaScript CPU, ms/delta | 10.495 (0.086) | **8.385 (0.056)** |
| LoAF blocking, ms/stream | 5,230.6 (228.2) | **4,307.0 (77.4)** |
| Run-level p95 input → next rAF, ms | 92.9 (9.6) | 91.3 (11.9) |
| DOMParser/template input, characters | 4,322,231 (115,469) | **1,312,078 (75,717.5)** |
| Estimated missed 60 Hz frames | 774 (12.5) | 733 (14) |
| LoAF count | 207 (3.5) | 214 (8) |
| Last-quarter total renderer CPU, ms/delta | 33.34 (0.50) | 33.28 (0.56) |
| Last-quarter style recalculation, ms/delta | 19.20 (0.32) | 21.06 (0.37) |
| Geometry reads per stream | 2,693 (82) | 2,897 (52) |
| Computed-style reads per stream | 1,017 (37) | 1,110 (21.5) |

JavaScript CPU falls **20.1%**, LoAF blocking falls **17.7%**, and parsed input falls **69.6%**. Input latency has overlapping IQRs: this is not a clear input-latency win. LoAF count increases while total blocking decreases. Geometry/style work also increases, and total CPU stays flat. Frame loss is estimated from rAF gaps; input-to-rAF is not a presentation timestamp. CPU counters include the benchmark/probes and native input. The first CPU quartile also includes fixture scheduling overhead.

JavaScript CPU across the four message-length quartiles is 12.44/11.59/10.76/10.50 ms per delta before and 11.83/10.74/9.34/8.38 afterward. Total CPU is 31.01/31.01/32.24/33.34 before and 30.12/31.07/32.22/33.28 afterward. Style work remains the dominant remaining cost. These counters do not prove a strict constant-time total renderer path.

All 14 captures have valid parsing counters, 645 delivered deltas, 24 headings, 24 code blocks, and 24 tables. Rendered HTML is identical across every capture after removing reconciler comments (SHA-256 `5ecca9b6c7c28a6469d221875934598ef42efe24534f37fbe7a51140a35b9291`). The focused regression separately checks byte-identical streamed/full renderer output at each completed section.

### Validation

- The strengthened existing regression failed before the parser fix: 4,042,462 sanitizer-input characters for a 16,630-character reply exceeded its 332,600-character budget. Afterward, all 18 streaming tests pass, including actual HTML, reference definitions, containers, locale/options/source changes, and truncation. `pnpm test ui/src/components/markdown-streaming.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **18 passed**, final-head AWS wall time **10.58 s**.
- `pnpm test ui/src/components/markdown-dom-ref.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **4 passed**, final-head AWS wall time **4.92 s**, covering DOM retention and media cleanup.
- Independent Codex review is clean through P2, with full owner modules supplied as context. The final rebase changed none of the reviewed owner context.
- Final-head scoped UI/scripts lint and `pnpm tsgo:ui` / `pnpm tsgo:scripts` passed. **Full UI e2e passed on the final head: 803 files / 3,500 tests passed, one existing file/test skipped, zero failures.** Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --maxWorkers=6`; AWS wall time **3,978.19 s**. The skipped file is `ui/src/e2e/desktop-resize.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` (existing platform-specific skip). All eight archived check exit codes are zero. The full pass/skip list is retained in the lane proof artifacts.
- Native preflight and the full suite both passed all three previously affected files (preflight: **11 tests**): automation-management, cron-duration-save, and quota-reset-status. Main's pending-catalog discovery fix and obsolete cron-dismissal removal were integrated before this proof. Chromium/WebKit tooltip activation and native Workboard coverage both passed; task-owned checkout ancestors are non-group-writable and artifacts stay inside the repository, satisfying the existing fixture contracts.
- Exact-head [PR CI run 38800144117](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38800144117): **green** for `97cda729f353`.

### Scope and size

Runtime: **+27 lines** (31 added, 4 removed) across the three existing Markdown owners. The additional classification preserves the actual-HTML invalidation contract while allowing literal code to stay cached. No persistent state, server schema, configuration, dependency, or transport changes.

Benchmark/probe tooling: +369 net lines. The requested `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD -- ':!*.test.ts' ':!*test-support*' ':!docs/*'` includes that tooling: 402 added, 6 removed, **+396 net lines**. Six files total, including the one-line regression edit.

Release-note context: Control UI keeps completed Markdown cached when streamed code contains comparisons, reducing repeated rendering work without changing the answer.

### Synthetic before / after

The captures below show the completed baseline and candidate reply on the final-head comparison. Both were inspected in full and contain only the synthetic benchmark fixture.

![before-streaming](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b0acb0cd-c373-4c1f-9504-bdcefda528b2)

![after-streaming](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e75ac86a-971a-4176-b694-209adf91bcb6)

prs.title: feat(discord): AI auto-naming for threads via channels.discord.thread.autoName
prs.body:
Related: #160865

## What Problem This Solves

New Discord threads can retain generic names after their conversations develop. This adds optional AI naming after an admitted conversation reaches a configured message threshold.

## User Impact

`channels.discord.thread.autoName` defaults to `false`; `true` uses five messages, a positive integer chooses the threshold, and `0` disables it. Account settings override the channel-wide value. The thread's bound or routed agent uses its utility model, or primary model as fallback, to process a bounded recent transcript in an isolated title run. Other bots and webhooks do not contribute. Generated identifiers such as `snake_case_parser` retain their underscores.

Changing `autoName` or `enabled` uses the existing Discord channel restart. Before downgrading to a release without this setting, remove the `autoName` key at the global and every account scope; setting it to `false` still fails that release's strict schema.

Naming applies to threads observed at creation and their first 24 hours. Each threshold crossing consumes one attempt, including when permissions, exhausted budget, or later configuration changes prevent naming. Every persisted claim has a 24-hour TTL, survives Gateway restarts, and is deleted with its thread. An account/parent pair permits two attempts in ten minutes. Both protection stores reject new entries at 10,000 rows. Transcripts are not persisted.

**Maintainer decision remains open:** acceptance of the new setting, model processing, and persisted lifecycle is required before landing. Neither this PR nor #160865 records that acceptance. The existing change request has not been dismissed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discord owns collection, admission, and rename decisions; existing label, binding, state-worker, and REST owners provide execution. Naming follows current binding/routing authority through model dispatch, fallback, and queued rename retries. Ordinary in-flight messages preserve the existing restart behavior for naming, enablement, and action-setting edits; actual access-policy revocation still rejects them.

The latest review follow-up separates route preparation from final rename authorization and PATCH dispatch. A missing binding inspection now has an explicit failure, and the title timeout and per-window rename limit have names. The claim-before-permission/budget ordering is documented as intentional. The PR description reflects only the current expiring-claim lifecycle; the removed non-expiring-claim repair is not retained.

Any effective config replacement abandons an active naming attempt without refunding its claim or reserved budget. Role routing uses the retained most recently admitted human, so naming and another author's reply may select different agents. Binding runtime loading remains lazy.

## Evidence

Published head: `79c8f2a0a682549c3dfb5f1190dcfcfe243bfacb`. Validated source tree: `40ce8a9fa93acf0ec4ffe54b6158ee7809d84b6f`.

- Rebased onto main `4f5bdeb0dfe8ff8d4d7862b5ffa4608256cb8c20`, which includes [upstream CI fix eccc1bdf](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/eccc1bdfeb88c2fa38b4202be602f6f21d45da3e). That fix removes stale Actions compiler-cache restores and saves after a same-checkout benchmark showed older state could cost more than a cold check. All compiler commands, graph coverage, resource limits, and deadlines are preserved. Local incremental compilation remains available.
- All nine feature commits are patch-equivalent across the rebase. Of the 27 feature source/docs/test paths, 26 have identical blobs to the previously reviewed head; `provider.startup.ts` incorporates upstream gateway ownership simplifications while retaining naming listener registration and cancellation.
- Canonical channel-metadata/configuration-baseline generation and checks, MDX, and `git diff --check` pass; the generators require no artifact changes. All 151 affected Discord tests across eight files pass (106.11 seconds wall time), including startup, lifecycle/cleanup, listeners, in-flight preflight, naming/runtime, and persisted state. Both extension production and test typechecks pass.
- An independent subagent reviewed the startup, lifecycle, cleanup, AbortSignal, binding, and CI integration and found no actionable P0–P3 findings. The earlier substantive naming repair's P0–P3 subagent review and P0–P2 canonical `autoreview` also found no actionable issues; its feature patches are unchanged by this rebase. Reviews were static; runtime validation is recorded separately.
- [Current-head CI run 38814381864](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38814381864) completed successfully. The formerly cancelled [core typecheck stripe 3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38814381864/job/116696368324) passed in 6m36s against the unchanged 15-minute limit, with no compiler-cache restore step. Both required gates passed: [CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38814381864/job/116700267277) and [combined CI/security gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38815894031). GitHub confirms this head merges cleanly. Maintainer product acceptance remains open.

<details>
<summary>Previous-head CI diagnosis, timings, and retained proof</summary>

The previous head `879785713a9b8866a71c3764ba637f477ef9f28b` had a cancelled [CI run 38808622666](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38808622666). Its `check-test-types-core-3` job restored stale compiler state, ran for 15m20s against its 15-minute limit, and caused both CI gates to fail. All seven compiler groups completed with exit code 0 and empty diagnostics, including both completion records and the final step receipt. The compiler step took 14m24s. The same stripe had taken 6m11s on the previous head and 6m30s on preceding main; no TypeScript error was reported.

A targeted retry was attempted after diagnosis, but GitHub denied it with HTTP 403 because the PR author lacks upstream Actions permission. This new head incorporates an actual upstream CI repair through the normal PR update path. The old cancelled run remains historical evidence and is not relabeled successful. The upstream cache-removal benchmark showed 295.27s with one-hour-old state versus 157.81s cold; its commit explicitly makes no promise of equal savings on every source change.

Current-rebase validation: metadata generation/checks 4.68s/4.57s, baseline generation/checks 5.46s/5.05s, MDX 11.08s, affected tests 106.11s, extension production types 47.13s, extension test types 75.68s. Commands used repository wrappers and the pinned OpenClaw Bun fork in secretless, network-disabled Node 24.19.0 Docker. Current-head core-type stripe 3 took 6m36s overall (22:05:46–22:12:22 UTC); both required CI gates passed. CI completed all 79 jobs with no failures; unselected jobs are skipped. The job summary does not isolate the changed test file’s CI time.

The prior substantive repair at `879785713a9b8866a71c3764ba637f477ef9f28b` passed all 57 focused naming/runtime/state/title cases, both extension typecheck lanes, typed lint, formatting, and staged-content checks. Its new production-path regression first reproduced Discord receiving `snakecaseparser` instead of `snake_case_parser`, then passed after the repair. Independent subagent and canonical autoreview found no actionable issues. The changed test file took 38.79 seconds wall time (31 cases); its new underscore case took 0.559 seconds. Full [CI run 38793049547](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38793049547) passed at the earlier `a647bb349850b505641341a1389569871c123391` head; that is previous-head evidence.

The latest substantive repair adds 28 net production lines and nine test lines relative to `a647bb349850b505641341a1389569871c123391`. The complete proposal against merge base `4f5bdeb0dfe8ff8d4d7862b5ffa4608256cb8c20` adds 912/deletes four production lines and adds 1,588 test lines, excluding documentation and generated output.

Earlier repair `05f1675058ebcca0f3d75f14cce092b1991f1816` passed 177 focused Discord cases, both Gateway policy/reload integration cases, both extension typecheck lanes, typed lint, and `pnpm build`. Its qualified Discord cold-import snapshot measured peak RSS 104.9 MiB and baseline 44.0 MiB; this was not a full Gateway startup benchmark and has not been repeated on this head. Its full documentation anchor audit had three failures reproduced identically on its pinned main: `cli/index.md`, `gateway/config-tools.md`, and `releases/2026.10.1.md`. Neither edited document had a finding. These measurements describe that earlier commit only.

</details>

### Historical live Discord demonstration

On October 13, 2026, an isolated ordinary compiled Gateway at `f2b5c61988be2af10c7f6a5880790ba2f6b61c6f` connected to real Discord and a real model service. With `autoName: 2`, the title stayed `Untitled` after the first plain human message and changed automatically after the second. This demonstration predates later routing and policy repairs and has not been repeated on this head; current regressions cover those changes.

<details>
<summary>Redacted historical observations (UTC)</summary>

```text
source_sha=f2b5c61988be2af10c7f6a5880790ba2f6b61c6f
foreground_cli=node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway run
```

</details>

prs.title: fix(backup): Git backup restore leaves a staging directory when the SQLite open fails
prs.body:
Closes #171959

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `restoreGitBackupDirectory` leaves a `.git-backup-restore-*` directory behind when creating or opening the staged SQLite file fails.

## User Impact

Failed Git backup restores no longer leave private staging directories next to the target.

## Why This Change Was Made

Staging setup now runs inside the existing try/finally, so cleanup covers every failure path.

## Evidence

Shipped CLI, isolated state, restore target on a tmpfs with a tiny inode quota (user namespace), so the staging dir fits but the staged SQLite file does not:

```
$ openclaw backup git restore --repository <repo> --global --target <full-tmpfs>/openclaw.sqlite
# main
ENOSPC: no space left on device, open '<full-tmpfs>/.git-backup-restore-3p6WSs/database.sqlite'
exit=1
$ ls -A <full-tmpfs>
.git-backup-restore-3p6WSs

# this PR
ENOSPC: no space left on device, open '<full-tmpfs>/.git-backup-restore-EnGjmS/database.sqlite'
exit=1
$ ls -A <full-tmpfs>
(empty)
```

New `staging-open` case in `git-backup-failure.test.ts` fails before the fix (staging directory left) and passes after. Git backup tests and `tsgo:core` pass.

Closed shadow roots remain opaque; current modal callers do not use positive tabindex values.

All four header menus build rows only when first opened. Test fixtures open their real triggers and wait for the native popover before reading rows. The scrollbar census includes native menus alongside remaining Web Awesome surfaces.

The latest main integration preserves its pending-title placeholder, direct Details renderer, and native external-panel links. prs.title: fix(cron): keep replies to delivered questions in the same idle session
prs.body:
Fixes #128797

## What Problem This Solves

A reply to a cron-delivered question can cross an idle reset and lose the question, even when the operator answers within minutes of delivery.

## User Impact

A visible automation result newly appended to its destination conversation starts a fresh idle window. Silent runs, failed or uncertain deliveries, and retries of the same result do not refresh it. Recurring visible results can keep a destination idle-fresh; daily resets still use the session start time. No configuration or schema migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Current main removed direct transcript mirrors in #168996 and now commits destination results through the canonical background-result writer. That writer still updates `updatedAt`, while idle expiry reads `lastInteractionAt`. Pass the message timestamp through its existing lifecycle patch so the guarded worker transaction commits the message and freshness together, only on a new append. This adds no parallel freshness writer or main-thread database access.

Original fix by @Thinkr1; maintainer cleanup moves the repair to the current owner and removes the obsolete six-file opt-in plumbing and QA scenario. The new regression uses a bare `ok` follow-up, addressing ClawSweeper's P2 finding that the old scenario repeated the question marker and could falsely report retained context. Main's current delivery, restart, and writer guards are preserved.

The background commit retains the admitted config-derived store path, agent/session identity, confirmed payload, and occurrence key. Existing producer/abort checks and session ID/lifecycle checks revalidate authority at the commit; the timestamp is captured after waiting for active work and preparing display content. No new deferred work or captured limits are introduced.

## Evidence

[Exact-head CI run 38812272070](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38812272070) **passed: 37 successful jobs, 28 skipped, zero failures**, on `c247a03bd5eeb96df8d417e643ceb9cd32f07b00`. This includes production/test typechecks, lint, build, UI checks, and the selected test shards.

- Source/history confirmation on main `f6c0408505eb32d25d794557df153bdc4738a85d`: the background-result commit omitted `lastInteractionAt`, and `evaluateSessionFreshness` uses that field for idle expiry.
- Regression: `keeps the destination session for a reply to a delivered cron question` in `src/cron/isolated-agent/destination-completion.test.ts`. It exercises cron dispatch, durable destination persistence, replay without a second freshness touch, and the next operator reply under a 180-minute idle policy. The previous human interaction is already 185 minutes old at delivery. The stored row is seeded as stale; no clock overrides, real timers, or sleeps are added.
- Initial [CI run 38805509290](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38805509290/job/116666076825) caught a fixture bug: pinning only the test-thread clock to May made it disagree with the real SQLite delivery worker, so dispatch timed out before the freshness assertion. Removed the clock override and retained the production-path assertions. The next run passed delivery, freshness, and replay assertions, then exposed a missing inbound-finalization step in the reply fixture; it now uses the production `finalizeInboundContext` owner. The third run passed the runtime regression and all destination/background-result tests; its test typecheck caught the missing required `commandAuthorized` argument, now explicitly `false` for this ordinary reply. These were new fixture errors, not inherited failures; no CI reruns were requested.
- Existing destination regressions cover `NO_REPLY`, failed/uncertain sends, session resets, and duplicate results. PR CI ran these tests through `node --import tsx scripts/ci-run-node-test-shard.mts` and supplied the typecheck gate. On head `c247a03bd5eeb96df8d417e643ceb9cd32f07b00`, [changed-test job 116689168044](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38812272070/job/116689168044) passed all **16 destination tests** and **9 background-result tests**. The new regression passed in **5.322 seconds**. File wrapper wall times were **75.01 seconds** and **25.74 seconds**, respectively (including transforms/imports and worker setup). The destination integration uses real delivery/storage/reply-admission owners; no Gateway process or local test execution was used.
- Changed-file `oxfmt`, core `oxlint`, and `git diff --check` passed. The borrowed install lacks the UI-only Solid lint dependency, so the static lint config omits only UI overrides; all applicable core rules are retained. No dependency installation or shared-install changes.
- Codex autoreview, including the CI fixture correction: **scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings**. Review covered the diff and current writer/kernel/delivery owners; no project code was executed.
- ClawSweeper revision 15 (reviewed head `bc5b35fad377`) reports **no actionable code findings** and confirms the earlier false-positive test was addressed. Its sole remaining request is live Gateway/Telegram proof; that proof-only request is intentionally not followed under the maintainer policy below. The final required-boolean fixture correction is covered by fresh autoreview and green exact-head CI.
- Live Gateway/Telegram proof, leases, local typechecks, local test suites, and production-revert negative controls were intentionally skipped per maintainer policy. PR CI is the proof; earlier contributor live claims are not carried forward as evidence for this head.
- Delta against main: production **+1/-0**, tests **+89/-0**, docs **+4/-2**. The one production line uses the existing lifecycle contract; unrelated deletion would not make this fix safer.

prs.title: perf(control-ui): remove chat reload padding jump and cut overlay style work
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Removes a 20 px padding jump during a signed-in reload of a dashboard deep link, then reduces overlay-selector matching across the page. The campaign's original reload showed 14 visual states over roughly 15 seconds; its later layout investigation isolated a roughly 0.0095 CLS jump from this padding transition.

## User Impact

Chat and dashboard routes reserve their final workbench geometry before the pane mounts. New Session, Systems, pending creation, failed/unknown routes, and successful missing/ambiguous/error notices retain their existing layouts. Settled appearance is unchanged. No configuration, Gateway protocol, or stored-data changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The pane's settled callback reported workbench layout too late. The shell now derives it from the rendered route state. The existing route-state owner distinguishes resolved notices from session content, including those returned successfully by the loader. This removes the pane/pending-create reporting path, the workbench reporter trait, and its obsolete pane test.

Equivalent explicit overlay ancestors replace grouped universal-descendant selectors, preserving matching sets and specificity while allowing cheap ancestor rejection. Earlier diagnostic traces of this same selector patch reduced matching time for the two expensive groups from 154.025 to 7.193 ms. No other grouped-ancestor/universal-descendant pattern appeared in the selector statistics.

## Evidence

prs.title: perf(sessions): skip unused physical row aliases
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Large idle Gateways retain a physical-store lookup alias for every session even though ordinary sessions never use that lookup path.

## User Impact

Reduce resident session-index memory without changing session lookup, parent inheritance, federation, or authorization. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only raw `global` and `unknown` parent keys resolve through physical-store references. Ordinary keys resolve through the existing logical index. Retain physical aliases for those two sentinel keys and stop allocating the otherwise-unused strings and singleton sets. The existing physical-parent inheritance test now covers both sentinels, including invalidation and ownership replacement.

Production LOC delta is +3: the condition preserves the required sentinel contract while removing the per-session allocations. No new cache, module, export, or test file is introduced.

## Evidence

An isolated Linux sandbox ran a synthetic Gateway with 13,400 sessions, 6,000 retained runs, 200 approval recovery records, 100 disabled cron jobs, 12 projects, and 1,500 MiB logical transcript text (4.37 GiB agent database). Node v26.8.2; base `6dec7960c9f40870ce742c14766abb09137d5287`. Ten `sessions.list` warmups preceded five idle minutes and a main-isolate heap snapshot. No operator data or credentials were used.

Matched before/after capture: post-GC JS heap **423.29 → 418.02 MiB** (−5.27 MiB, 1.25%); strong-edge retained graph **434.10 → 428.83 MiB** (−5.27 MiB). The lookup-index dominator drops **15.36 → 12.39 MiB**; the total saving also includes strings shared elsewhere in the graph. Set count drops by 13,404, consistent with removing one unused singleton set per ordinary session. This is one matched retained-memory comparison, not a throughput claim.

A one-session reference retains 225.04 MiB JS heap; default plugin activation adds about 21 MiB. Constructor retained totals overlap and are not summed. Baseline constructor aggregates include objects 187.37 MiB, arrays 181.15 MiB, maps 135.12 MiB, strings 123.05 MiB, contexts 68.33 MiB, and sets 22.16 MiB. Strong-edge graph totals include native allocations represented in the snapshot and therefore differ from JS heap counters.

Largest distinct baseline owners: session rows 68.48 MiB (required resident metadata/presentation), Node module loader 16.18 MiB (runtime-owned), session lookup index 15.36 MiB (includes the unused physical aliases removed here), membership facts 12.81 MiB (required authorization/category/participant facts), plugin-cache generation 7.02 MiB (lifecycle-owned discovery/runtime artifacts).

- `pnpm test src/gateway/session-row-projection.test.ts src/gateway/session-row-projection.topology.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 33 tests passed; 57.00 s Vitest wall time, 61.28 s wrapper time.
- Changed-file `oxfmt`, repository lint, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Runtime builds for measurement run only in the isolated Linux sandbox. No Testbox lease; PR CI owns broad gates.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): no actionable P0–P2 findings. The configured autoreview provider did not match operator configuration; no configuration was changed.

An additional head-only probe seeded one 8 MiB synthetic conversation, completed a real agent turn against a loopback mock provider, then idled five minutes. Post-GC JS heap was 466.63 MiB (494.45 MiB retained graph). The fork-replay snapshot map retained 16.23 MiB, with the path `timer → clearEmbeddedSessionForkSnapshot → snapshots`; a `SessionManager` retained 8.08 MiB through the embedded-run registration graph. The actor-replica pool itself retained 0.57 MiB. Fork replay has an existing 64 MiB payload budget and 90-minute expiry; changing its retention would change a supported feature. The probe does not establish that the retained run registration is unnecessary; its lifecycle is a follow-up investigation.

The prepared-runtime object and model-catalog object in this probe exclusively dominate only 2,208 and 1,024 bytes respectively; their shared dependencies are accounted elsewhere, so these are not total reachable sizes. The fixture does not enable Prometheus; source inspection shows its metric store has a 2,048-series cap, but production-shaped metric cardinality remains unmeasured.

The synthetic fixture and single-turn probe do not reproduce a 1.2 GiB idle JS heap. This is an attributed index reduction, not a claim to explain all long-lived workload retention. Full plugin composition, repeated real workload history, and retained run-registration ownership remain gaps. No production snapshot or database was used.

prs.title: fix(logging): drop unusable redaction patterns at the logging config boundary (#173461)
prs.body:
Closes #173461

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw doctor --fix` dies with `TypeError: pattern.exec is not a function` and prints no diagnostic at all when the active config carries a non-string entry in `logging.redactPatterns` (for example `[1]`). Doctor is the documented recovery path for a config it cannot load, so the crash lands on the command meant to repair it, and every other redacted write on that config is exposed to the same throw.

## User Impact

User impact: an operator whose `logging.redactPatterns` is malformed now gets the normal Doctor report, the named config rejection and the instruction to fix that value, instead of a stack trace. Redaction keeps working from the built-in patterns while the unusable operator list is ignored. No configuration, migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

`readLoggingConfig()` parses the config file with `parseJsonWithJson5Fallback` and no schema validation, then casts the result to `LoggingConfig` (`src/logging/config.ts:146-149` before this change), so the declared `string[]` could hold any JSON. `parsePattern` treats anything that is not a string and not a `RegExp` as an already-resolved matcher (`src/logging/redact.ts:156-158`), so `1` reached the matcher loop and `visitRedactMatches` called `.exec` on a number. The console sink redacts every formatted write (`writeFormattedConsoleOutput`), so the throw escaped from inside `console.error` and killed the process.

The repair normalizes once in the canonical read, which is the boundary where that untrusted file becomes typed config. That choice is deliberate:

- The sibling diagnostic path in the same owner, `resolvePartialDiagnosticLoggingConfig`, already refuses a `redactPatterns` list that is not all strings, so the canonical path accepting one was the outlier.
- Fixing it in one consumer would leave the others crashing. `resolveConfigRedaction`, `resolveToolPayloadRedaction`, `resolveLogTailRedactOptions` and `src/agents/embedded-agent-error-observation.ts` all read the same list, and two of them already filter string entries defensively - a sign the producer was the wrong shape.
- The hot matcher loop stays untouched, so trusted internal matchers from `LINEAR_MATCHER_SOURCES` and `DEFAULT_REDACT_PATTERNS` keep their fast path, per root `AGENTS.md` ("validate/inspect untrusted input once at its trust boundary; trust internal data after that").

A value that is not a list is dropped outright, because the resolver would otherwise read a string's own length and iterate its characters as patterns. Within a list, unusable entries are dropped individually rather than discarding the whole list: with `["customer-secret-[0-9]+", 1]` the valid rule must keep masking, because dropping it would expose exactly the values the operator configured. If nothing usable remains, the empty list makes `usesBuiltInRedactPatterns` apply `DEFAULT_REDACT_PATTERNS`, so redaction is never silently disabled, and config validation still reports the invalid value to the operator.

## Evidence

Real behavior, built CLI, isolated config and state directory. Both runs use the same config and `node dist/index.js doctor --fix`:

```json
{
  "logging": { "redactPatterns": [1] },
  "skills": { "workshop": { "approvalPolicy": "pending", "maxPending": 3 } }
}
```

Before, on a build of `d01e78ce4c9` (current `main`) - exit 7, no diagnostic:

```
┌  OpenClaw doctor
TypeError: pattern.exec is not a function or its return value is not iterable
    at visitRedactMatches (dist/redact-DPX-Km1I.mjs:752:31)
    at replaceRedactPattern (dist/redact-DPX-Km1I.mjs:795:2)
    at redactText (dist/redact-DPX-Km1I.mjs:2749:195)
    at redactSensitiveTextWithOptions (dist/redact-DPX-Km1I.mjs:2786:9)
    at redactSensitiveText (dist/redact-DPX-Km1I.mjs:2781:9)
    at writeFormattedConsoleOutput (dist/console-BYEp9nom.mjs:113:8)
    at console.forwardedConsoleCall [as error] (dist/console-BYEp9nom.mjs:179:4)
```

After, on a build of this branch - the run completes and explains itself:

```
┌  OpenClaw doctor
Config warnings: /tmp/oc-173461/openclaw.json: Config unavailable; using environment and default agent directory settings. (Invalid config at /tmp/oc-173461/openclaw.json:\n- logging.redactPatterns[0]: Invalid input: expected string, received number\n- skills.workshop: Unrecognized keys: "approvalPolicy", "maxPending")
...
│  - logging.redactPatterns[0]: Invalid input: expected string, received  │
│    number                                                               │
│  No config changes were written. Fix the value(s) above in              │
│  /tmp/oc-173461/openclaw.json by hand, then rerun "openclaw doctor      │
│  --fix".                                                                │
└  Doctor finished, but config fixes were not applied.
```

The after-run exits 1 because Doctor could not apply config fixes, which is its documented outcome for a config needing manual repair: a recorded non-outcome with a next step, not a crash.

Supporting checks:

- Red-first: the new regression in `src/config/io.best-effort.test.ts` fails on `d01e78ce4c9` with `TypeError: pattern.exec is not a function. (In 'pattern.exec(text)', 'pattern.exec' is undefined)` while the two existing `readCurrentConfigForResolution` tests in that block pass (1 failed | 8 passed).
- With the fix: `pnpm test src/logging/config.test.ts src/config/io.best-effort.test.ts` - 15 and 9 passed. The owner tests pin each shape: a mixed list keeps its usable rule, a non-list value and blank sources are dropped, a list with nothing usable becomes empty, an all-strings list is returned unchanged, and an applied snapshot is normalized too.
- No regressions in the sibling redaction paths: `pnpm test src/logging/redact.test.ts src/logging/redact-patterns.test.ts src/logging/log-tail-redaction.test.ts src/logging/logger-redaction-behavior.test.ts src/logging/diagnostic-support-redaction.test.ts` - 152 passed across 5 files.
- `pnpm tsgo` - passed. `pnpm build` - passed. `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1` - clean on the changed files.
- `codex review --base upstream/main` - `findings: []`, "patch is correct". Earlier iterations of this patch were revised in response to its review: dropping the whole list was replaced by per-entry filtering so valid operator rules keep masking, non-list values and blank sources are now dropped, and the applied-snapshot producer normalizes as well.

Risk:

- `availability`: this removes a throw from the console redaction path, which every command shares. It cannot add one, because the boundary check is a type test over already-parsed JSON.
- `security-boundary`: redaction is never weakened. A non-list value is dropped so the built-in patterns apply (pinned), a mixed list keeps every usable operator rule (pinned by a test with `["customer-secret-[0-9]+", 1]`), a list with nothing usable becomes empty so `DEFAULT_REDACT_PATTERNS` apply rather than no redaction (pinned), and a valid all-strings list is returned unchanged (pinned). Programmatic callers that pass explicit options, including `RegExp` matchers, never reach this path.
- Out of scope: `logging.redactPatterns` is still reported as an invalid value by config validation and Doctor; this change only stops it from crashing the process first.

- Changelog: none. `CHANGELOG` is release-owned per root `AGENTS.md` and generated from `docs/releases/*`.
- AI-assisted: yes. Testing degree: fully tested - red-first regressions plus the built-CLI before/after above.

prs.title: fix(advisor): cancel stale guidance after abort or new turn
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Advisor guidance arriving after an aborted run, or remaining queued from a stale review after a new user turn starts.

## User Impact

Aborting work also cancels its in-flight Advisor review and verification. Starting a new user turn drops unfinished advice based on the preceding turn instead of delivering it later. A duplicate steering outcome never creates fallback guidance. Normal run-end fallback remains supported.

## Why This Change Was Made

The lifecycle subscription treated aborted terminal events like ordinary completion, ignoring their `aborted` flag. The controller also retained in-flight reviews when a new user run replaced the previous one. These transitions now cancel the stale review at the owning controller, preventing both active delivery and fallback queueing.

Duplicate keys are terminal no-ops rather than unavailable steering, so the fallback path now leaves them alone.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on `5678421c757`: aborted `end` and `error` events left the review signal active; regression assertions failed with `expected false to be true`.
- Reproduced active delivery followed by another pending review spanning a new user turn; its cancellation assertion failed on the baseline.
- A duplicate-result regression also demonstrated an unwanted fallback queue entry before its repair.
- All 51 Advisor tests passed, including cancellation, duplicate handling, normal run-end fallback, tool settlement, verification, and interval accounting. Combined owner checks covered 127 distinct tests; changed-file oxfmt/oxlint, scoped tsgo, Madge (0 cycles), and diff checks passed.
- Final raw-evidence campaign combined this head `1fac8ffa671`, core head `5677912be70` (#173458), and display fix `07c940c6959` (#173460); tested integration `04a5747760d1e9655b73fac511ddb81fad7a3c97`.
- Executable invariants: **before 80 PASS / 5 FAIL; after 86 PASS / 0 FAIL / 0 UNPROVED**. Shared case/invariant pairs improved **59 PASS / 5 FAIL → 64 PASS / 0 FAIL**; totals include different commissioning/channel coverage and the new successor-run case.
- The accepted abort left zero queued notes. The overlapping user turn retained one active correction and zero queued copies. Built-in minutes review completed verification and delivered once. Provider requests, SQLite rows, and events independently establish these outcomes.
- A/B behavior stayed unchanged: Advisor-on 4 tool calls / 2 repeated actions, solved; off 8 / 7, unresolved. Actual Codex tool/minutes and late-snapshot Telegram persistence/display/recipient checks passed. No active-session compaction occurred; that RPC remained refused.
- The fork slice from the tested core revision is now isolated in #173489; #173458 retains steering deduplication and the later native rejected-guidance producer repair.

prs.title: fix: deduplicate steering without replaying rejected guidance
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated plugin steering reaching the model twice, and rejected native guidance being retained as if it had been delivered.

## User Impact

Plugins can retry steering without injecting the same guidance twice, including after a successor run starts. A native steer rejected before dispatch leaves no guidance in subsequent model context and can be retried after plugin reload. No configuration, schema, or stored-row shape change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Transcript idempotency alone did not protect the active-run input queue. The existing run registration now joins pending/accepted admissions after authority validation, and the plugin host checks the durable session/key owner before dispatch. Stored steering receipts replay the original run ID, matching `src/gateway/server-methods/inflight.ts:38-51`; older rows without a receipt return terminal `duplicate`. Rejected queue reservations are released.

Codex previously appended internal guidance before the final physical-send authority check. It now retains preceding tool-result mirroring and inbound user persistence, but appends internal plugin guidance only after native acceptance or accepted-unconfirmed delivery. Accepted history can still be recorded if the plugin is subsequently disposed; session/storage identity guards remain. This prevents rejected guidance from poisoning both replay and same-key retry without adding stored fields.

The independent fork snapshot repair moved to #173489. Advisor cancellation and duplicate-fallback handling are in #173459.

## Evidence

- Baseline `5678421c757`: sequential/concurrent duplicate-key regressions persisted one row but admitted two model-input messages.
- Successor-run regression: before the durable check, the same key was accepted by a later run rather than deduplicated.
- Native regression: before the producer fix, pre-wire disposal left a hidden transcript row, included it in `SessionManager` model context, and caused a reloaded plugin's retry to return `duplicate`. Afterward, rejected guidance is absent from both transcript and context; retry reaches native `turn/steer` once. Accepted-then-disposed guidance still persists once.
- Focused steering, native admission/authority/settlement, recorder, and recorder-persistence tests passed. Changed-file oxfmt/oxlint, scoped tsgo, Madge (0 cycles), and diff checks passed.
- The pre-review-fix combined raw-evidence campaign tested integration `04a5747760d1e9655b73fac511ddb81fad7a3c97`: **80 PASS / 5 FAIL → 86 PASS / 0 FAIL / 0 UNPROVED**. Shared case/invariant pairs: **59 PASS / 5 FAIL → 64 PASS / 0 FAIL**. Totals include added successor/channel coverage rather than an identical inventory.
- That campaign proves same-run and successor-run idempotency, abort/overlap handling, display isolation, and built-in/native minutes verification. The later rejected-guidance producer fix is separately covered by the focused native regression above, not claimed as part of that campaign.
- Focused native follow-up tested `0903019c1131cfa29a81b4e192c3353fb65a3def` (integration `998ff42a15f` plus the display fix): **36 PASS / 0 FAIL / 0 UNPROVED**. Live Codex tool-call, minutes, abort, overlap, and same-key within/across runs passed; every accepted steer row preceded its first provider request. A controlled native-transport probe separately proved pre-wire rejection leaves no row or wire request, then same-key retry delivers exactly once. The controlled rejection probe is not claimed as live-daemon fault injection.

prs.title: fix: preserve session forks during parent request preparation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes background session-fork verification failing while the parent prepares its next model request.

## User Impact

Advisor can finish a review and its verification across a parent-request preparation boundary instead of failing with a missing prepared-parent error. No configuration or storage migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

New runs/transports still retire the previous snapshot; reset/delete revocation and existing TTL, count, and byte bounds remain intact. Ordinary run-end disposal already preserves provider resources, so no attempt-stream-settle change is needed.

This independent fork slice was extracted from #173458; steering idempotency and rejected-guidance delivery remain there.

## What Problem This Solves

When a plugin's next-turn injection is consumed into a prompt (for example Advisor's fallback when the run already ended), the exact model-facing prompt is recorded on the next user message as private `__openclaw.modelPromptProjection` metadata. The shared display sanitizer did not remove that field, so `chat.history`, live `session.message` events and transcript deltas sent the full hidden injection text to every display client. That includes guidance that is deliberately `display: false`.

Found by a raw-evidence proof of Advisor steering: the fallback note's complete text appeared in `__openclaw.modelPromptProjection.text` in both history and live display output.

## Fix

The shared display sanitizer (`src/gateway/chat-display-projection.sanitize.ts`) now drops `__openclaw.modelPromptProjection` from display copies for every client. The field is private model-replay state (see `docs/reference/database-schemas/layout.md`), not display data. Canonical persistence and runtime replay are unchanged.

## User Impact

Hidden plugin or system prompt context no longer appears in the metadata of chat history or live events. A search found no client that reads this field (Control UI, Android, iOS/macOS codecs, TUI, MCP relay, public sharing), so nothing visible changes.

## Evidence

- Three regressions (history, live `session.message`, transcript delta) fail on `main` with the full injected text present, and pass with the fix.
- Focused privacy sweep: 119 tests passed.
- Split out of #173456 as a standalone repair; the commit is identical.

prs.title: perf(usage): batch durable rollup publications
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Startup usage backfills send one shared SQLite writer request per stale transcript, competing with foreground writes on large session inventories.

## User Impact

Usage backfills use fewer writer admissions while preserving committed rollup values, monthly partitions, and fresh-checkpoint skipping. No schema, stored-format, configuration, or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing refresh worker now publishes bounded cohorts in one transaction: 50 transcripts, 1 MiB of prepared payload, or one elapsed second, checked between complete transcripts. Every completed/yielded refresh flushes its tail. A single large transcript can exceed the byte/time threshold; failed or canceled scans leave uncommitted derived totals for the next refresh.

The single-row internal request is replaced throughout by an array request. Explicit post-write body/partition deep copies disappear: the worker retains bounded originals, and message transport clones only changed partitions sent to the host. Committed metadata and bodies remain in the existing receipt-invalidated read cache. Production delta is +36 lines: the bounded buffer and mandatory completion flush preserve atomicity and completed-refresh visibility while replacing per-transcript writer dispatch. No new timer, global cache, or shutdown owner.

## Evidence

Focused local worker integration, SQLite cache, admission, and worker snapshot files passed. Proof covers exact totals, append/rewrite and monthly partition behavior, unchanged refreshes, cancellation/authority revocation, failure health, reads during a blocked write, batch rollback, and deterministic batching/yielding. Latest admission + snapshot run: 25 tests, 53.96 s wall including worker preparation; initial worker integration: 59.35 s; SQLite + snapshot: 63.47 s. Broad tests/typecheck/build are delegated to PR CI. No Testbox/Crabbox leases.

Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): clean after correcting a wall-clock-sensitive test assertion; exact batching now uses a controlled clock. GitHub review then found that failure health must record every row of a rolled-back batch. The extended real-worker regression failed with one health record instead of two before the fix, then the complete worker file passed (10 tests, 41.08 s wall). A fresh independent review of that repair was clean. CI then caught a regression in post-write cache reuse. The repair retains committed metadata and bodies without explicit full-partition copying; the unchanged worker-I/O file now passes all 10 tests (54.41 s wall), and independent review of this repair is clean. A second health finding covered a scan failure before publication: the host now tracks started transcripts until their batch commits. Its regression failed with only the latest health fact before the repair; admission + worker files then passed all 31 tests (62.63 s wall), and independent review was clean. This host-boundary test deterministically supplies two scan notifications before failing; it does not simulate a parser error. No operator configuration changed.

Five-minute synthetic Linux backfill comparison, baseline `732a6e611fcb` versus `13cebc12a330` (including restored bounded cache reuse):

| Metric | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Rollup writer operations in 5 minutes | 5,000 | 100 |
| Rollup writer operations/minute | 1,000 | 20 |
| Cumulative rollup queue wait | 35.513 ms | 2.613 ms |
| Cumulative native rollup execution | 2,484.089 ms | 559.327 ms |
| Refresh completion | 19.434 s | 16.561 s |

The fixture uses `scripts/perf/team-shape-fixture.ts`: 5,000 sessions, 6,000 retained runs, 200 approvals, 100 disabled cron jobs, 12 projects, and 64 MiB logical transcript text (about 236 MB agent DB before usage seeding). One deterministic assistant usage event was appended per session through the existing writer. The real background `requestCostUsageCacheRefresh` owner ran with its normal 50-file scheduling; trusted `worker.request` diagnostics counted queued/started/completed requests and durations. Fresh independent fixtures were generated with identical seed and reference time. Both full 300-second windows had no additional rollup writes after refresh completion.

All 5,000 reports are fresh with zero pending/stale files. Final totals are exactly equal: 17,497,500 tokens and the same floating-point $5 aggregate. A harness-only report-range error initially caused bounded replay; correcting the inclusive quarter-hour end recovered the existing baseline cache without changing measured counters.

This is **98% fewer rollup writer requests**. It isolates the usage startup-backfill workload, not a full Gateway or production reconnect contention: maximum writer queue depth was one. The measured fixture is much smaller than a large production store, and this single pair does not establish production tail latency or RSS improvements. The AFTER window was repeated after restoring bounded cache reuse; the table uses that repeat. The later host failure-bookkeeping repair replaces the active-file markers with a set of uncommitted keys and was not separately benchmarked; batching, transport, and cache retention are unchanged. Broad validation and CI timing remain with PR CI.

Changed-file formatting and `git diff --check` pass. Targeted lint has one inherited file-length finding: `src/infra/session-cost-usage-worker-io.test.ts` is 1,020 counted lines (limit 1,000) on both the unchanged base and candidate; the baseline file was run through the same targeted lint command. No lint suppression was added.
