prs.title: fix(cron): record designed heartbeat skips as successful no-ops
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An agent whose heartbeat file is intentionally empty (or comments-only) skips every interval by design, but each skip was recorded as a `skipped` cron run, which `resolveCronCompletionStatus` maps to `failed`. `openclaw tasks list --status failed` accrued one row per interval (~48/day) for the heartbeat cron and failure alerts fired, even though `consecutiveErrors` stayed 0 (#144959).

Designed no-op skips now settle as `ok` runs whose summary carries the skip reason (`heartbeat skipped: empty-heartbeat-file`), matching the busy-deferral handoff path that already returned `ok`. The heartbeat runner's own state (`system heartbeat last`, `consecutiveSkipped`) keeps reporting the precise skipped status, so no signal is lost.

## Evidence

- **Real-behavior proof (updated in f8c3fa97 and 6fb6ec66 per review):** `src/cron/service.heartbeat-real-preflight.test.ts` wires the **real heartbeat runner** (real preflight, no injected heartbeat results), a **real comments-only scratch row** in the sqlite state store (stock "keep this file empty" content), and the **real cron service**. The two review findings are addressed:
  - **Same-partition fixture:** the sandbox is now selected as the cron partition the preflight actually reads — `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` points the default partition (`<state>/cron/jobs.json`) at the seeded `cronStorePath`, so `resolveHeartbeatPreflight` genuinely consumes the seeded comments-only scratch instead of a different store.
  - **Required dependency supplied:** the `CronServiceDeps.requestHeartbeat` member is provided (non-waiting) alongside `requestHeartbeatAndWait`, matching the production contract.
  - **Safeguard restoration:** commit ffb0026a accidentally dropped the fixture safeguards; 6fb6ec66 restores them (partition stub, `requestHeartbeat` dependency, skip-summary + spy assertions), so the test again cannot pass through ordinary heartbeat execution.
  - **Skip assertions, not just success:** the finished event must carry `summary: "heartbeat skipped: empty-heartbeat-file"`, and the reply/telegram spies must stay unused — so an ordinary successful agent turn can no longer satisfy the test. Paused-reminder recovery stays covered: the operator `disabled` skip keeps its `skipped`/`failed` outcome in the unit matrix.

Runtime output (local vitest run at 6fb6ec66, cron config, redacted):

```
✓ src/cron/service.heartbeat-real-preflight.test.ts > real heartbeat preflight task accounting > settles a real empty-scratch preflight as a successful no-op task 1155ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```

Full local cron-suite run at 6fb6ec66 (`service.heartbeat-payload.test.ts` + `service.heartbeat-real-preflight.test.ts` + `service.test.ts`):

```
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  10 passed (10)
```

- The test also asserts the ledger that feeds `tasks list --status failed` contains zero failed cron rows after the designed skip.
- Unit-level matrix in `service.heartbeat-payload.test.ts` (10/10): designed skips settle `ok`/`succeeded` with `consecutiveErrors: 0`; the operator `disabled` skip keeps its `skipped` outcome for visibility.
- Matches the existing intentional-silence precedent in `resolveCronCompletionStatus`, and the busy-deferral handoff path in `timer-execution.ts` that already returned `ok`. The runner's own state (`system heartbeat last`, `consecutiveSkipped`) continues to report the precise skipped status.

prs.title: fix(talk): keep slow audio appends from ending calls
prs.body:
Fixes #173388

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Control UI Talk ends when one microphone audio append takes longer than eight seconds, even if the Gateway recovers shortly afterward.

## User Impact

Talk stays connected through a ten-second relay stall. The existing three-second input budget still drops excess audio with persistent guidance to repeat the last part. If outstanding audio receives no acknowledgment for 30 seconds, Talk ends with an explanation and guidance to reconnect; explicit Gateway errors and connection failures remain terminal.

## Why This Change Was Made

The earlier input-budget fix (#155839) deliberately retained dead-relay detection, but an individual append deadline could not distinguish slowness from lost progress. The relay transport now owns one progress watchdog instead of independent append deadlines: successful appends renew it while any audio remains outstanding, and shutdown clears it and aborts pending requests. Audio is neither retried nor replayed.

The deferred callbacks retain only this transport's fixed client/session binding and original abort signal. Reply settlement checks that signal before changing state; shutdown clears the watchdog, and its failure path checks the current closed state before detaching. No config, identity, paths, or limits are resampled from another session.

The simplification pass removed the old unconditional settlement path and extended existing tests rather than adding a parallel suite. Production changes are +33/-6 (net +27), tests +78/-30 (net +48), docs +7/-0. The production growth is the outstanding-request count, shared watchdog, lifecycle cleanup, and explanatory UI copy; unrelated deletions would not make this fix smaller.

## Evidence

- Source and history confirm the eight-second failure on main; the intent of #155839 is preserved.
- [Exact-head CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38810804370) on `6e713714470ef69745a00436ee646e6081dfe50c`: 30 successful jobs, no failures or retries, including all three UI unit shards, UI E2E, selected Node tests, production/test typechecks, lint, docs, security, and architecture gates. PR CI is the test/typecheck gate. The fake-timer regressions exercise the real Gateway request-deadline owner in `gateway-relay.test.ts`: `recovers from a 10-second append stall with bounded audio and repeat guidance`, `detaches with a clear error after 30 seconds without an audio acknowledgment`, and `renews liveness on audio acknowledgments while an older append is still pending`. They also cover idle/stop timer cleanup; existing rejection, relay-close, ordering, and detach tests remain.
- Local changed-file oxlint passed (`node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json` on the three changed TypeScript files); the first run caught an unbound-method fixture callback, corrected before the clean run. Oxfmt, `git diff --check`, and keyless `pnpm ui:i18n:baseline` passed; no generated baseline change was needed.
- Independent Codex autoreview through P2: scoped-clean, no accepted/actionable findings; review-only, no tests run. The hosted code review also completed on this head with no findings.
- [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173490#issuecomment-6203016316): no findings, complete fix scope, ready for maintainer review. Its live-proof/negative-control observation does not change the maintainer policy: PR CI is the proof for this change.
- Live Gateway/Crabbox/Testbox proof, local tests/typechecks, and a production-reverted negative control were intentionally skipped per maintainer policy. No leases were created. CI UI shard 2/3 reports 1.25 seconds of test execution for the relay file (6.63 seconds from queued to completed); the three regressions took 33 ms, 42 ms, and 12 ms respectively. No standalone local wall time is claimed. This behavior-only change does not require screenshots.

prs.title: fix(ui): align native UI consumers and browser fixtures
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Settings agent selection still listened for Web Awesome’s `wa-show` after its selector moved to the owned overlay, so opening it missed the existing lazy identity refresh. Follow `overlay-show`, cover the three Settings presentations, and align directly coupled fixtures, parity selectors, and diagnostics with native controls.

The fixture changes preserve behavioral assertions: real Cron/Usage rows exercise check alignment, the synthetic HTTPS proxy allows one supported retry for an observed asset-fetch connection reset, and the existing connection fixture is retained from main. The redundant intermediate Stop screenshot is removed; the settled capture and physical cleanup, cancellation, output, and subsequent-instruction assertions remain.

The tooltip fixture now holds external clipboard completion until the real click finishes and its exact-path write assertion passes. Only then does it check transient feedback; no production timer or flow assertion changes.

Normal integration of official main `5a70f529` retains main’s complete native-menu contract and delayed connection-route fixtures. It drops this branch’s duplicate native-menu hunk and superseded connection-readiness move. Main’s connection owner fix and held-module regression now cover the timing failure at its source. Main also supplies the independent Workboard, theme-pointer, and menu-retention fixes. No unlanded lane branch, authored CSS, startup import, registered tag, or dependency change is included.

Further normal integration of official main `3150853d` preserves main’s complete TSX picker test after its rename, including `SettingsRow` and every assertion. The sole resolution deletes the same obsolete vendor stylesheet import as this PR already did. Native landing confirmed its earlier attempt stopped before dispatch; no merge request was sent. The merged candidate passed a fresh UI typecheck and independent P0/P1 review.

Normal integration of official main `f6c04085` includes update-run fixture repair [#173438](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173438), giving each warning distinct text. The merge is conflict-free; all ten reviewed file blobs and the complete authored patch are byte-identical to the independently reviewed candidate. Review is reused with recorded blob/delta evidence; a frozen install, UI typecheck, and whitespace check passed.

Normal integration of official main `0a32b78` adopts the Solid Settings port [#171691](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171691) and its bootstrap diagnostics. The port still listened to `wa-show`, so the existing fix now uses `onOverlay-show` in the Solid component. The old Lit file stays deleted, the same identity-refresh assertion stays in the converted three-presentation real-click test, and all new asset diagnostics remain alongside the original one-retry option. The coordinator inspected this resolution; a new full-scope independent P0/P1 review found no actionable issues.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Current head | `7e64da9d8f2082101264cb063bf9e5b16ba7a491`; full `ci:full` run [38810041869](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38810041869) passed: **48 successful jobs, 23 skipped, zero failures**. All UI shards, nine ordinary E2E shards, and both real-Gateway shards passed. |
| Prior full CI | `f6e6f9bf`, run [38805291697](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38805291697): **48 successful jobs, 23 skipped, zero failures**. All UI, nine ordinary E2E, and both real-Gateway shards passed. Prior-head evidence only. |
| Preceding full CI | `9731a09d`, run [38798771024](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38798771024): 45 successful jobs, 23 skipped, two failed test jobs plus the aggregate. Update-run headline failure exactly matches scheduled main `d0d0f865`; dictation phase layout failure remains unattributed. |
| Dictation investigation | One replay on actual CI main parent `488bfb5f`: 1 passed, 12 skipped, exit 0; 93.19 s total. The same scheduled-main case passed. Eight relevant blobs are unchanged, but source equality and baseline success do not prove inheritance or a fix. Assertions and production remain unchanged. |
| Prior full CI | `6dc41006`, run [38787321161](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38787321161): **48 successful jobs, 23 skipped, zero failures**. All three UI shards including WebKit, all nine ordinary UI E2E shards, and both real-Gateway shards passed. Prior-head evidence only. |
| Tooltip fixture | Exact CI main parent `868ceb34`: 13/13 passed, 36.30 s. Controlled-clipboard candidate: 13/13 passed, 64.66 s. One single-file run per side, one worker. A passing baseline does not reproduce or attribute the prior CI failure. |
| Historical preceding CI | `c291ae97`, run 38779437036: 44 successful jobs, 23 skipped, three failed test jobs plus aggregate. All nine ordinary UI E2E shards and real-Gateway shard 1 passed. |
| Exact failure attribution | Cron timeout-clearing and quota saved-clear failure blocks match scheduled main run 38777890355 (`d33195ff`) exactly. WebKit palette phase failure remains unreproduced: exact-parent one-case replay passed (34.45 s) after installing the missing pinned browser; no inherited or fixed claim. Tooltip status assertion is addressed by the fixture ordering change above; precise original cause remains unproved. |
| Independent review | New canonical full ten-file P0/P1 review after the Solid Settings conflict repair: exit 0, scoped-clean, no findings; final source verification passed. |
| UI typecheck | `pnpm tsgo:ui`: exit 0 after a frozen install of main’s declared dependencies. |
| Focused Settings proof | `settings-sidebar.test.tsx`: **24/24 passed**, one worker, 26.01 s wrapper, exit 0. Includes lazy identity refresh through the real selector click in all three presentations. No separate new-port baseline replay. |
| Focused historical proof | Three alignment assertions passed in Chromium, followed by a teardown hang; not a clean command pass. Historical local Settings and Stop commands produced no assertion result. These gaps remain in native review. |
| Startup | Prior matching replay: **351,931 B gzip JavaScript, one CSS request, 45,983 B gzip CSS**. No authored startup changes; final Web Awesome retirement owns final build, Knip, and media proof. |

Historical full CI [38753268531](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38753268531) on `bb737e8` completed with 44 successful jobs, 23 skipped, three failed test jobs plus the aggregate. Its ten failures were independently attributed: three skill-library EventTarget-receiver failures reproduced on baseline `669f`; six menu-retention cases reproduced on the actual CI main parent `fc5d7817`; the palette settings case exactly matched scheduled main `824fde2b`. Main now includes the menu-retention repair. These results do not establish current-head success or authorize a new-head inherited-failure exception.

The earlier `8c` WebKit phase, touch-fling distance, and dashboard probe-count failures, and the `15c` terminal-docking failure, remain unexplained. Baseline passes and green shards do not establish fixes or exact-test passes. Native review preserves these historical uncertainties and the interrupted local commands separately from current-head proof.

LOC against integrated main: **10 files, 4,301 → 4,336 (+129/−94)**. Growth is in alignment coverage of real Cron/Usage renderers; the sole production change replaces one event name.

The chat microphone menu still uses Web Awesome, and migrated chat pickers retain obsolete adapters and duplicate dismissal handlers.

prs.title: fix(release): waive provider outages without changing frozen candidates
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Release operators cannot excuse a known third-party credential outage against an existing Full Release Validation (FRV) without changing the frozen candidate or starting new validation.

## User Impact

Operators can declare an exact failed live-provider or Telegram lane at trusted-P verification/publication time. Every waived lane stays **waived — not a pass**, with its reason and approving maintainer; all other required checks remain blocking. The candidate-side `telegram_waiver` input is removed.

Frozen release branches remain readable when their recorded legacy value is empty, without changing the original digest. Non-empty old grants are rejected with migration guidance because they omitted coverage rather than identifying an authenticated failed execution. The direct protected publisher is supported; the prepared Release Button rejects waivers because its existing handoff does not authenticate the initiating human.

## Why This Change Was Made

One P-owned declaration parser and exact job/suite allowlist replace the version-wide candidate skip mechanism. The declaration binds version, candidate SHA, parent/child runs and attempts, role, exact job/suite, reason, and the authenticated maintainer.

When candidate aggregates failed and no success manifest exists, P authenticates the original execution-plan upload/witness, source admission, terminal decision/drain, complete GitHub job/attempt records, and sealed candidate. It recovers the normal manifest writer's inputs through the existing successful runner-header reader; unchanged npm/Docker/plugin consumers authenticate actual producer identities and qualified bytes. Known aggregates can fail only for independently proven waived causes. The result is explicitly a P-side projection—not a forged candidate success seal—and each publication consumer authenticates it again. CI, install/upgrade, artifact, soak, performance, plugin-prerelease, and integrity gates cannot be waived.

Final registry writes refresh both the qualification operators and the distinct waiver approver. Stable closeout binds its declaration to the original trusted publisher input/operator and re-runs strict authentication, rather than treating a serialized projection as authority.

This is one atomic replacement: candidate grant removal and P verification/transport must land together. Necessary growth is the strict failed-parent evidence reconstruction; no separate approval receipt/store, projection artifact/cache, standalone preflight reconstruction, or candidate workaround is introduced. The old version-specific live-file omissions are also removed.

## Evidence

- Strict production-boundary fixtures cover the 2026.10.4 failed-parent shape, exact waiver acceptance, no-waiver rejection, frozen empty input, carried jobs, mismatched identities/attempts, cancelled/missing lanes, extra hard failures, and second aggregate causes.
- Read-only real-run proof targets [FRV 38774938703](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38774938703). **Live failed-parent waiver acceptance is not claimed.** At the original observation, parent attempt 1 lacked the required terminal drain and had extra orchestration failures; the independently rerun Z.AI leaf was already successful and could not be waived. The latest read-only refresh now finds parent **attempt 2 completed/success** and independent child [38775999936 attempt 4 completed/success](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38775999936). Those external successes supersede the old pending observations, but do not supply eligible failed-parent waiver-acceptance or protected final-effect/recovery authority proof. No FRV mutation was performed by this task.
- Reduced P head `ad2dc30a99f3619e3349e3a6b6d18c224f7c3ed5` was run against the real GitHub records at the earlier failed-attempt observation: without a waiver it rejects the failed parent (`not completed/success`, 1.14s); with the exact current-attempt Z.AI declaration it rejects absent terminal drain evidence (`no drain artifact exists at or before the current parent attempt`, 9.79s). That collector/evidence-integrity failure is not waivable. These are live rejection proofs, **not** live failed-parent acceptance; independently, the now-successful Z.AI leaf is not eligible for a grant.
- The reduced reader was also exercised read-only against parent summary job 116638318194/1: the successful artifact-qualification step header reproduced the npm descriptor and Docker run/attempt/name/digest exactly equal to the retained receipts, with the complete plugin descriptor. This proves the replacement input-recovery boundary, not waiver acceptance.
- Real final-effect integration with controlled GitHub/registry I/O permits the distinct waiver approver and rejects revocation during channel reads or between writes. Both revocation cases failed before the callback repair and pass after it.
- Real closeout/strict-reader integration accepts the frozen empty-input failed-parent fixture while preserving its failed conclusion. It reads the original successful P runner header (including pretty JSON), rejects a forged published declaration, and rejects revoked approver authority. The old actual workflow and log reader reproduced their respective failure-only and multiline-input defects before repair.
- No candidate/release-branch changes, FRV reruns/cancellation/dispatch, publication, or merge were performed.
- Original Codex AutoReview was scoped-clean at P0–P2 after fixing both findings; the reduced staged snapshot and scalar-role follow-up are both independently scoped-clean at P0–P2. Scripts/root-test types, scoped script/test lint, formatting, workflow checks, docs MDX, and the line-cap ratchet pass. The previous head failed a stale 25-input dispatch-fixture assertion after removing the candidate input and CodeQL flagged dynamic regex construction. Both repairs are pushed at the reduced head. The authority/closeout correction at `33317becb0e792a6d93a5b91ebf3125f173d0aed` passed fresh staged P0–P2 AutoReview with no actionable findings; scripts/root-test types, scoped lint, formatting, workflow validation, docs MDX and the line-cap ratchet pass. The prior reduced head finished hosted CI green. ClawSweeper completed on `33317becb0e792a6d93a5b91ebf3125f173d0aed` with no code findings, but retained a needs-human security/proof hold (readiness/proof 2/6, patch quality 3/6) for missing real acceptance/final-effect evidence. Its hosted CI found a stale inline closeout assertion and an unrelated Control UI inventory failure. The additive test-only correction at `941150616da77e54f05835c17862a8a4e67f639d` replaces obsolete inline snapshots with the workflow's authenticated-owner run/attempt handoff checks; the focused case fails before and passes after, and root-test types, lint/format, pinned-base ratchet and fresh P0–P2 AutoReview pass. Hosted CI on `941150616da7` completed with the closeout correction and all type lanes passing; only the independently reproduced Control UI inventory failure and its aggregate gate failed. Its durable ClawSweeper review raised a late original-versus-rerunner identity defect. That defect is reproduced and repaired in signed additive `373f99ae1863edf034fc68fce940addb1eca8b9f`: bot children select the original authenticated publisher actor, matching direct GITHUB_ACTOR and closeout, rather than a later rerunner. The exact parent/run/attempt checks and final-effect revocation checks remain unchanged. The existing distinct-actor regression fails before and passes after; identity69 + strict-waiver22 + closeout82 cases pass (173 total,16.20s), with scripts/root-test types, lint/format, pinned-base ratchet and fresh staged P0–P2 AutoReview clean. The current-head terminal results are recorded below; prior-head green checks are not current-head clearance.
- Naturally triggered [CI 38810163662](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38810163662) is terminal failure on `373f99ae1863edf034fc68fce940addb1eca8b9f`: **36 successful, 2 failed, 31 skipped, 1 cancelled** jobs (70 total). Failures are the reproduced inherited Control UI inventory mismatch and its aggregate gate. `check-test-types-core-2` was cancelled at the configured 15-minute job limit and is **not passing type coverage**; its emitted graph receipts contain no type diagnostics before cancellation. No CI rerun or timeout increase was performed.
- [Durable exact-head ClawSweeper verdict](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173437#issuecomment-6201494340) confirms the original-actor repair and reports **0 code findings**, but remains **needs-human, security/proof hold** (readiness/proof 2/6; patch quality 3/6). Actual protected-publication acceptance of eligible terminal failed evidence, unauthorized-approver rejection, and revocation during delayed/recovered publication before registry I/O remain unproven. Controlled integration and a successful FRV are not live waiver acceptance. This PR is not merge-ready and remains unmerged, with auto-merge off.

<details>
<summary>Operator interface and compatibility</summary>

Publisher input: `validation_waivers_json`; helper flag: `--validation-waivers-json '<JSON>'`, always with an existing `--full-release-run`.

```json
{
  "schema": "openclaw.release-validation-waivers/v1",
  "targetVersion": "2026.10.4",
  "candidateSha": "383c124cc32ffee3f8e56f549b88da94d269a4af",
  "parentRunId": "38774938703",
  "parentRunAttempt": 1,
  "waivers": [{
    "childRole": "releaseChecksIndependent",
    "childRunId": "38775999936",
    "childRunAttempt": 2,
    "jobName": "Run repo/live E2E validation / Native live suites (Native live Z.AI Coding Plan)",
    "suiteId": "native-live-src-agents-zai-coding",
    "reason": "Third-party credential outage: shared key rejected by Z.AI (auth).",
    "approvedBy": "maintainer-login"
  }]
}
```

This is a historical shape example, not a valid approval of the now-green Z.AI leaf. Bind attempts to the actual terminal composite and replace the approver with the authenticated maintainer. A changed attempt requires a freshly bound declaration, not a new FRV.

```bash
pnpm release:candidate -- \
  --tag v2026.10.4 \
  --target-sha 383c124cc32ffee3f8e56f549b88da94d269a4af \
  --workflow-sha <trusted-P-sha> \
  --full-release-run 38774938703 --skip-dispatch \
  --validation-waivers-json "$(cat zai-waiver.json)"
```

This helper emits a handoff; it does not publish. [The evidence guide](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/fix/release-publication-waivers/docs/reference/full-release-validation/evidence.md#publication-waivers) documents authentication, owner execution contexts, hard gates, and the legacy removal path. Current October `release/*` lines and active `extended-stable/2026.9.33` retain the frozen empty input. Remove compatibility only when the last eligible pre-cutover line and its supported recovery evidence retire.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Independent review repairs</summary>

The first P2 AutoReview found two real issues. The standalone strict CLI no longer accepts an approver override or trusts an ambient actor name; it derives the operator from GitHub authentication. Only protected internal consumers pass a verified workflow/publication-parent actor. Telegram waiver reuse is now limited to the exact FRV package Telegram proof with the same bytes/provider mode; source QA waivers, different packages, and different provider modes cannot suppress independent verification. Both boundaries have regressions.

The ClawSweeper authority and closeout findings were verified against the reduced head and repaired in their existing owners. The closeout reader reuses the retained-header parser; no second parser, approval receipt, or projection artifact was added.

The Control UI ownership-inventory failure in [checks-node-compact-small-9](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38810163662/job/116681804477) reproduces on untouched main `e5b5a35a3ba68dd5d857dc9fe2042f579fc5abfd`: 65 discovered private-server files versus 64 registered, missing `ui/src/pages/agents-home/claws-catalog.e2e.test.ts`. The current hosted checkout is merge `4bf56fc215da7d253e9e1ee3ffbaaf70f7109bae` of base `6dec7960c9f40870ce742c14766abb09137d5287` and this exact PR head. No relevant UI/configuration/parser/dependency inputs change between that tested base and merge. Refreshed current main `5fdd725db9ae4221bd735a879c3409a78feeb50b` retains identical ownership helper, inventory, paths, offending file, parser, plan owner, and lockfile blobs; the missing registration is not independently fixed there. Other UI files have evolved, so no fresh full-main replay is claimed. The original focused baseline used macOS Node 24.16.0 versus hosted Linux Node 24.19.0: source/configuration proof, not matched-runtime full-shard qualification. No unrelated UI repair is mixed into this release PR.

[check-test-types-core-2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38810163662/job/116682315944) has a GitHub failure annotation stating “The job has exceeded the maximum execution time of 15m0s.” Five core graph receipts passed before cancellation; the overall stripe did not finish. This is an execution-time/coverage blocker, not a passing check or a diagnosed feature type error. The prior head and scoped local checks do not replace this hosted result.

The reduction removes the parallel npm/Docker/plugin receipt-recovery implementation, projection artifact upload/download lifecycle, standalone preflight reconstruction/factory, duplicate projection metadata, and redundant parser/fixture cases. It reuses `readRecoveryStepInputs`, `manifestContextFromEnvironment`, and existing authenticated helper context. Publication consumers retain their exact artifact/producer checks. The lazy failed-parent import keeps Docker/recovery machinery out of ordinary candidate paths.

Against the pinned main base, the corrected reduced patch is +2,768/-914 (net +1,854), compared with +3,053/-928 initially. Remaining footprint: production/workflows +1,310/-435; tests +1,197/-436; allowlist data +65; docs/skills +196/-43. The net production/workflow growth is 875 lines, principally strict failed-parent authentication and the authenticated closeout consumer—not moving the old candidate skip. This is an atomic cutover; removal and the replacement cannot land separately without breaking the release path.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Focused test commands and wall times</summary>

All rows use `pnpm test test/scripts/<file> --maxWorkers=1`; `-t` is noted for focused follow-ups. Times are observed wall clock, not Vitest-only duration.

| File (`.test.ts`) | Result | Wall |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| release-validation-waivers | 20 passed (distinct reduced boundaries, including scalar/own role keys) | 1.60s |
| release-ci-summary-waivers | 22 passed (including distinct-approver final effects and authenticated closeout) | 1.60s |
| release-ci-summary | 136 passed | 17.58s |

| full-release-validation-state.qualification | 9 passed | 2.24s |
| full-release-validation-at-sha | 91 passed | 163.71s |
| full-release-validation-at-sha.candidate (CI input-count repair) | 18 passed | 67.20s |
| verify-stable-main-closeout (workflow routing/shared recovery reader) | 82 passed | 9.35s |

| Same file, full final-head run (Bash 5.3.15) | 107 passed / 2 existing skips | 229.01s |

The admission run's three Bash-3 failures are the unchanged empty `admission_args[@]` expansion in a Linux-only workflow step, not failed waiver coverage. All three reproduce identically on clean main at `6dcc186d070b9993d29f5696b8550cb553cb22e7` (3 selected failures, 3.37s). The fourth was a 30-second bootstrap-fixture timeout: isolated replay passed without a source change, so its cause is not claimed fixed. The full final-head Bash-5 run passed all 107 enabled cases (229.01s); hosted results remain in the Checks tab. The original package suite's isolated-bundle dependency failure was repaired; the full 553-case run passed, followed by the final reduced-tooling-bundle regression.

`pnpm tsgo:scripts`: 3.12s; `pnpm tsgo:test:root`: 27.96s (including checkout-lock wait); both passed. Workflow checks used supported Python 3.14 rather than the host's Python 3.9.6.

</details>

prs.title: fix(config): name the rejection behind an unavailable config warning (#167314)
prs.body:
Closes #167314

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw doctor --fix` reports `Config unavailable; using environment and default agent directory settings.` for a config file that exists and is usable, and never says what was refused, when that file still holds settings the same run is about to migrate (for example the retired `skills.workshop.approvalPolicy` and `maxPending` keys). Operators are told their config could not be read while the same command reads, repairs and rewrites it, with no hint about the real rejection.

## User Impact

User impact: operators now see why directory resolution refused the config, for example `Config unavailable (skills.workshop: Unrecognized keys: "approvalPolicy", "maxPending"); using environment and default agent directory settings.`, so a misleading "unavailable" claim becomes an actionable one. No configuration, migration or user action is required, and the message for a genuinely missing config file is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`readCurrentConfigForResolution` (`src/config/io.runtime.ts`) loads the config with `skipSuspiciousRecovery: true` for directory resolution. A present-but-rejected config throws, the empty `catch {}` discarded the error, and because `config` stayed `undefined` one generic message covered two different states: file missing and file refused. The rejection reason was already built and already terminal-safe, so the fix carries it into the existing diagnostic instead of inventing a new one.

ClawSweeper's recommendation on the issue was to "retain strict inspection and fallback semantics, but preserve the rejection reason in the existing sanitized diagnostic rather than accepting invalid config". That is what this does: strict inspection, the `config ?? {}` fallback and the returned `configDiagnostics` shape are untouched; only the message gains the reason.

<details>
<summary>Root cause and code path</summary>

- Owner: `src/config/io.runtime.ts` - `readCurrentConfigForResolution`, with the warning emitted through `logConfigWarningsOnce` (`src/config/io.warnings.ts:12`).
- Path on the reported command: `doctor --fix` -> `src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.ts` -> `assertDoctorRetiredStateAdmission` (`src/commands/doctor-retired-state-admission.ts:14`) -> `readCurrentConfigForResolution()`.
- Reason source: `throwInvalidConfig` builds the error from `formatInvalidConfigDetails` (`src/config/io.invalid-config.ts:29`, `:79`), whose lines already pass through `sanitizeTerminalText` (`src/config/issue-format.ts:85`).
- Change: capture the failure and derive the reason from the owners that already format it, `isInvalidConfigError(error) ? redactSensitiveText(error.details) : formatErrorMessage(error)`, collapsed to one line and capped at 300 characters with `truncateWithMarker`. With no captured reason, the original message is emitted unchanged.
- Files: `src/config/io.runtime.ts` (+36/-3) and the new `src/config/io.runtime-resolution.test.ts`.

</details>

## Evidence

Real behavior, built CLI, isolated config and state directory. Both runs use the retired-key config from the issue, `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` pointing into a temporary directory, and `node dist/index.js doctor --fix` from `pnpm build`.

```json
{ "skills": { "workshop": { "approvalPolicy": "pending", "maxPending": 3 } } }
```

Before, on an unpatched build of `cffb3d91698`:

```
┌  OpenClaw doctor
Config warnings: /tmp/oc-167314/openclaw.json: Config unavailable; using environment and default agent directory settings.
...
│  Migrated legacy config keys in the active openclaw.json:             │
│  - Removed skills.workshop.approvalPolicy; Skill Workshop proposals   │
│    were removed.                                                      │
│  - Removed skills.workshop.maxPending; Skill Workshop proposals were  │
│    removed.                                                           │
```

After, on a build of this branch:

```
┌  OpenClaw doctor
Config warnings: /tmp/oc-167314/openclaw.json: Config unavailable (skills.workshop: Unrecognized keys: "approvalPolicy", "maxPending"); using environment and default agent directory settings.
...
│  - Removed skills.workshop.approvalPolicy; Skill Workshop proposals   │
│    were removed.                                                      │
│  - Removed skills.workshop.maxPending; Skill Workshop proposals were  │
│    removed.                                                           │
```

Both runs print the same repair output and both leave the retired keys removed from the config on disk, which is exactly why the generic wording was wrong. The user-visible delta:

- before: `Config unavailable; using environment and default agent directory settings.`
- after: `Config unavailable (skills.workshop: Unrecognized keys: "approvalPolicy", "maxPending"); using environment and default agent directory settings.`

Supporting checks:

- Red-first: with the production change reverted, the new regression fails as `AssertionError: expected 'Config warnings: /private/var/folders…' to contain 'skills.workshop'` (1 failed | 1 passed). The missing-file case passes before and after, so that branch is pinned as unchanged.
- `pnpm test src/config/io.runtime-resolution.test.ts` - 2 passed.
- `pnpm test src/config/io.state.test.ts` - 12 passed; `pnpm test src/infra/state-migrations.caller-mode.storage.test.ts` - 3 passed (the warning sink and a resolution caller).
- `pnpm tsgo` - passed. `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1` - clean on both files. Re-run after merging current `main`.
- `codex review --base upstream/main` - scoped-clean, `findings: []`, "patch is correct".

Risk and gaps:

- `compatibility`: the only behavior change is the warning text on the refused-config branch. The missing-file message is byte-identical and pinned by a test, and the returned `config`, `env` and `configDiagnostics` shapes are unchanged, so agent-directory and state-directory resolution are unaffected.
- Secrets and terminal safety: the reason is either `error.details`, already built through `sanitizeTerminalText`, or `formatErrorMessage`; both paths run through `redactSensitiveText`, and `logConfigWarningsOnce` sanitizes again at the sink. It is collapsed to one line and bounded to 300 characters, so the existing "emits each config warning record on one physical line" contract in `src/config/io.state.test.ts` still holds.
- Local-only caveats, both reproduced independently of this change: `pnpm build` completed every bundling stage but its final `write-cli-startup-metadata` stage hit the 120 s render budget while other jobs were running, and the `doctor --fix` process stayed alive after printing its full report. The second one reproduces with a valid config on the same build, where this patch's branch never executes, so neither is attributable to this change.
- Changelog: none. `CHANGELOG` is release-owned per root `AGENTS.md` and generated from `docs/releases/*`; release-note context is in this body.
- AI-assisted: yes. Testing degree: fully tested - red-first unit regression plus the built-CLI before/after above on the issue's own reproduction.
- Base: branched from `cffb3d91698`, where the proof was captured, then merged current `main` (`27721b8fec4`); the only conflict was import ordering from #171623 and the production hunk is unchanged.

prs.title: perf(build): hash warm cache inputs once
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Warm release builds calculate a complete static-input hash that they immediately discard before calculating the compiler-owned input hash for the same cache lookup.

## User Impact

Builds do less filesystem I/O and hashing when reusing plugin, package, and UI artifacts. Artifact bytes, cache invalidation, output validation, and deployment behavior remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing cache owner now tries the recorded compiler inputs first and computes the static-only fallback only for cold or missing-input cases. This removes a redundant hashing pass without adding a cache, flag, or alternate build path. Production LOC delta: 0 (two lines moved/adjusted); test LOC: +47.

## Evidence

- Regression fails before the change: five static bytes are read twice (10 bytes instead of 5). Passes after the change, including invalidation when a consumed input changes or disappears.
- Focused `test/scripts/build-all.test.ts`: 61 passed, single worker. Changed-file formatting, lint, and `git diff --check` passed. The lint wrapper also performed SDK declaration preparation unexpectedly; broad validation belongs to PR CI.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): clean through P2. The configured autoreview helper refused the requested provider route; operator configuration was left untouched.
- Isolated Linux sandbox, Node 26.8.2, 97 real plugin caches, seven interleaved before/after pairs after one cold build: median stage time **1,007.1 → 950.3 ms**. Every run produced the same output hash. Filesystem reads **69,018 → 61,588** (7,430 fewer); bytes read **634,472,158 → 579,520,548** (54,951,610 fewer). The benchmark ran the actual plugin build/cache owner with before/after cache modules and identical warmed artifacts.
- Timing was noisy (after samples ranged 870–1,405 ms); this is a small I/O reduction, not a large release-build speedup. Expected saving for a deployment with these warm plugin inputs is about **0.06 seconds**; full end-to-end build timing was not measured. Other cache consumers also avoid the discarded hash but are not included in the estimate. No meaningful full-build or memory improvement is claimed.
- No Testbox/Crabbox allocation; no local full test suite or repository-wide typecheck. Broad gates run in PR CI.

prs.title: perf: reduce redundant cold transcript work
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cold history preparation can append model metadata outside the resident transcript actor, invalidating already-loaded state. Reading a reset or compaction boundary also makes a separate query for the first retained message position.

## User Impact and Design

History preparation now uses the attempt's existing owned transcript context, as prompting already does. Metadata writes publish through the resident actor. Boundary metadata and the first post-boundary message position are read in one statement; the separate read is deleted. The size-limiting JSON projection stays in SQL. Transcript contents, ordering, reset/compaction behavior, and public APIs are unchanged.

The metadata fix applies to initial history preparation or a model change. A same-model restart does not append another model snapshot, so this part is not claimed as a restart saving. No authority or security checks were removed. Folding the position read into the same statement introduces no accepted stale-read edge case.

## Measurements

Shared harness v3, three alternating pairs (M,C,M,C,M,C), exact base `2592babcd45a` versus candidate `22f3977ba329`; candidate patch verified identical to the squash merge. Each cell is median [min–max]. Warmed values first average the ten turns in each run, then take the median/range across runs. SQL counts successful all-thread executions; requests count dispatches, including zero-SQL requests. Requests and their SQL can cross phase boundaries. Turn-attributed counts use propagated turn context. Every run, including both memory-recovery runs, is retained. No wall-time claim is made on the busy host.

| Phase | Base SQL | Candidate SQL | Base requests | Candidate requests | Base MAIN | Candidate MAIN |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Restart boot | 441 [438–442] | 441 [439–444] | 113 [111–114] | 113 [111–114] | 83 [83–83] | 84 [83–84] |
| Restart connect | 40 [22–65] | 60 [51–76] | 16 [15–40] | 35 [25–45] | 0 [0–0] | 0 [0–0] |
| Restart first turn, raw | 314 [271–358] | 709 [293–776] | 111 [89–112] | 112 [92–126] | 0 [0–0] | 0 [0–0] |
| Restart first turn, turn-attributed | 156 [156–156] | 294 [154–295] | 54 [54–54] | 54 [54–55] | 0 [0–0] | 0 [0–0] |
| Warmed turn, raw | 81 [79.2–82.1] | 78.1 [77.6–79.8] | 29 [28.8–29.8] | 29 [28.5–29.1] | 1.3 [0.4–1.3] | 0.4 [0–1.3] |
| Warmed turn, turn-attributed | 76.7 [76.7–76.7] | 75.2 [75.2–75.8] | 28.5 [28.5–28.5] | 28.2 [28.2–28.4] | 0 [0–0] | 0 [0–0] |
| Initial first turn, turn-attributed | 266 [251–270] | 226 [224–228] | 73 [73–74] | 66 [65–69] | 0 [0–0] | 0 [0–0] |
| Whole workload, raw | 4803 [4781–4829] | 5074 [4626–5106] | 1195 [1195–1199] | 1188 [1171–1195] | 307 [307–307] | 308 [307–308] |

The direct restart saving is two SQL statements, with unchanged request count. Initial metadata append switches from a 16-SQL standalone request to a 7-SQL actor append, and avoids downstream rehydration/reads. The larger initial-turn saving must not be confused with the same-model restart saving.

| Owner operation | Base SQL / requests | Candidate SQL / requests |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Restart bounded-hydration request | 13 / 1 | 12 / 1 |
| Restart readonly-accounting request | 9 / 1 | 8 / 1 |
| Initial bounded-hydration requests | 19 / 2 | 9 / 1 |
| Initial model metadata append | 16 / 1 standalone | 7 / 1 resident actor |

The aggregate restart result is worse, and the target is not claimed as achieved. Candidate runs 2 and 3 initially published an empty memory index, then rebuilt it on restart. Turn-attributed SQL is **295 = 154 + 140 schema readmission + 1 actor rehydration** in run 2, and **294 = 154 + 140 + 1 - 1 auth read** in run 3. Each trace shows memory DDL publication, retained-writer schema readmission, then actor hydration. The 140 statements include 116 expected-schema statements, 12 schema-fact statements, and 12 other admission/metadata statements. This is actual extra work, not merely phase redistribution; both runs remain in the table.

Initial empty-index publication precedes session hydration and the changed history/metadata code in both runs (about 18.7 and 14.1 seconds before metadata append, respectively), and neither run performs an initial session-memory export. Neither run executes the changed boundary-facts query before restart; even their first unchanged reset-window query occurs after empty-index publication. The initial corpus-discovery divergence therefore occurs upstream of both changed paths. The exact reason the corpus was empty is not logged. This follow-up is recorded for the memory/schema owners; this PR does not change their recovery or admission semantics.

Raw restart totals also include asynchronous memory export, cache/admission, and delivery work. These vary across phase boundaries. The altered reset-window operations consistently save two statements; the metadata wrapper does not run an extra model-snapshot append on same-model restart.

### Shared-read-family attribution

Cells are SQL / requests, median with range when variable. Warm and whole-workload columns include all contexts; restart column is turn-attributed. Family request counts follow dispatch phase and include requests that execute that family's SQL anywhere in the workload. Families overlap and must not be summed. The extra restart actor hydration in candidate runs 2 and 3 belongs to the documented memory/schema readmission; whole-workload actor hydration still decreases from ten to six statements.

| Family | Warm base → candidate | Restart turn base → candidate | Whole workload base → candidate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Exact-entry facts | 0 / 0 → 0 / 0 | 2 / 2 → 2 / 2 | 33 / 33 → 30 [29–35] / 30 [29–32] |
| Actor hydration | 0 / 0 → 0 / 0 | 1 / 1 → 2 [1–2] / 2 [1–2] | 10 / 10 → 6 / 6 |
| Entry-cache snapshots | 0 / 0 → 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 → 0 / 0 | 24 [23–27] / 14 [13–15] → 24 [22–25] / 14 [13–14] |
| Row facts | 0 / 0 → 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 → 0 / 0 | 10 [10–12] / 4 [4–5] → 10 [10–12] / 4 [4–5] |
| Watermark reads | 0 / 0 → 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 → 0 / 0 | 4 / 3 → 4 / 3 |

### Permitted sensitivity pair

One additional alternating base/candidate pair was run because of the restart discrepancy. It is reported separately and does not replace or filter the prescribed three pairs above.

| Phase | Base SQL / requests / MAIN | Candidate SQL / requests / MAIN |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Restart boot | 439 / 110 / 83 | 432 / 110 / 83 |
| Restart connect | 62 / 40 / 0 | 51 / 24 / 0 |
| Restart first turn, raw | 339 / 90 / 0 | 305 / 104 / 0 |
| Restart first turn, turn-attributed | 154 / 53 / 0 | 154 / 54 / 0 |
| Warmed turn, raw | 74.9 / 26.5 / 0.4 | 78.1 / 28.5 / 0.4 |
| Warmed turn, turn-attributed | 72.6 / 26.4 / 0 | 75.7 / 28.3 / 0 |
| Whole workload, raw | 4796 / 1169 / 307 | 4615 / 1164 / 307 |

Both extra-pair runs initially populated memory, and neither repeated the 140-statement restart schema refresh. Restart turn-attributed SQL is unchanged: the two saved reset-window statements are offset by one active-transcript identity read and one auth-row read. Whole-workload SQL/requests decrease from 4796/1169 to 4615/1164. This sensitivity result does not erase the worse original-three restart aggregate or establish aggregate restart non-regression.

The extra pair's warm increase is +32 SQL/+20 requests across ten turns: +30/+10 entry patches, +10/+10 auth-row reads, -9/-1 transcript hydration, and +1/+1 background upstream-link read. Provider-purpose records show only five Activity recap completions in this baseline, versus seventeen in its candidate and in every original run. The added auth reads originate in isolated-completion model authorization; each extra warm patch is the existing three-statement session-entry operation. `session-activity-summaries.ts` connects recap completion to that persistence operation. The patch caller is truncated from the trace, so recap-persistence attribution combines source and workload correlation. Why this baseline skipped recaps remains unproven. There is no extra model-metadata append on warm turns, and no changed reset-window query before compaction. All eight runs passed workload, restart, and shutdown assertions.

## T1 and Scope Limits

The mixed reset-window module's static T1 call sites decrease **10 → 9**. Synchronous plugin-facing SessionManager APIs retain their supported contract through 2026-12-31; deleting those calls requires the public API migration. The module is not relabeled worker-only. Restart connect/turn MAIN stays zero. Boot admission, locks, connection setup, and migration bookkeeping remain unchanged; expected-schema scratch contributes zero in the ordinary same-state restart boot. The separately observed memory-triggered schema refresh is described above.

The target of 80 fewer restart statements was not reached. Cold actor hydration is already one statement. Remaining opportunities include pairing snapshot invalidation and work owned by auth, catalog/workspace, activity/usage, startup maintenance, and memory/schema admission.

## Proof

- 56/56 focused tests passed across execution-phase, bounded-context, and active-events suites. The new regression uses a real writer/actor, checks residency after metadata append, and verifies persisted metadata/message ancestry after reopening. Existing tests cover reset/compaction, empty tails, cached reads followed by append, and reopening.
- Type-aware core lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. An earlier lint command timed out during unrelated plugin declaration preparation before lint ran. Madge passed with zero cycles. Independent Codex review and completed automated PR reviews found no actionable correctness/security defects.
- [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38804150682) passed production/test types, lint, source contracts, changed tests, architecture, and database-worker/T1/dialect ratchets. Full local Knip export scans found seven unchanged findings: `classifyAttachedCiRun`, `normalizePersistedBinding`, `PackageInstallerDeps`, `openUrl`, `expireDueOperatorApprovals`, `expectInvalidSlug`, and `mountLoginGate`. Every same-rule/same-file finding appears in [scheduled main CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38802524013/job/116655534125); the inherited-static-failure exception was used and the red-main owner notified.

Production delta **+25/-18**; test delta **+78/-0**. No SDK surface, schema, update, Doctor, plugin-loading, or service-lifecycle changes; no update cell required. Landed through the authorized head-pinned REST squash fallback; all required remote checks were green.

prs.title: fix(claude-cli): stop cache-prefix churn after child completion
prs.body:
Related: #146902

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Claude CLI prompt-cache rebuilds on managed local `claude-cli` sessions, because ordinary turns and verified child completions expose different tool/settings surfaces.

## User Impact

Managed local `claude-cli` turns now use one OpenClaw-mediated tool surface for ordinary turns and completions, so a completion no longer flips the session between Claude's native tools and the restricted MCP surface.

**Behavior change:** on `main`, ordinary managed turns ran with `--setting-sources user` and Claude's native tools; only completion/restricted turns were isolated. All managed local turns now use the isolated path: OpenClaw's policy-filtered MCP tools, and no Claude user settings, `CLAUDE.md`/rules, auto-memory, user hooks/plugins, Chrome or extra native MCP servers. OpenClaw supplies instructions, selected skills and tools. Explicit native-tool selections, node execution, side questions and isolated utility completions are unchanged. Existing sessions take one cache miss on the first turn after upgrade.

**Known remaining gap:** a completion turn still drops caller-gated tools (observed: `transcripts`, which requires an operator/channel caller), so the completion turn itself still misses cache. See Evidence.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ordinary local bundled Claude turns now reuse the existing exact mediated projection that verified completions already required (`prepare-tool-policy.ts`). Bootstrap routing runs after the final tool projection, so mediated read/write count as file access, and the native skill plugin is skipped on exact runs so selected skills stay in the prompt (`prepare.ts`). Docs updated.

Maintainer direction (@VACInc): keep native isolation on the managed path, with OpenClaw-owned instructions, skills and memory.

## Evidence

- Focused tests pass: `prepare-tool-policy.delegation`, `prepare.completion-tools`, `prepare.existing-session`, `prepare`, `mcp-http.exec-completion`.
- **Live Anthropic, built Gateway plus real Claude Code 2.1.300** (Blacksmith Testbox, `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6` via `claude-cli`). Flow: ordinary → `sessions_spawn` child completion → ordinary. Cache hit = cacheRead / (input + cacheRead + cacheWrite):

| turn | `main` 7b7db6fc | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| ordinary after completion (unbound CLI session) | 0%, 60.2k rewritten | **97%** |
| ordinary after completion (WebChat `chat.send`) | 0% | 96% (one run); 0% (two runs) |
| child completion turn | 73–74% | 0% (`transcripts` tool absent on completion) |
| user `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` sentinel | loaded | **excluded** |

- Per-launch `--allowedTools` capture: parent ordinary turns 49 tools; completion relaunch 48 tools (missing `mcp__openclaw__transcripts`); next ordinary 49.
- The `gateway-cli-backend.live` cache probe now also asserts cache reuse on the completion turn and the following ordinary turn. Currently, on Testbox, both `main` and this branch stop before any turn with the known live-harness native-owner error (`native owner closed without kernel descendant extinction`), so the built-Gateway run above is the live proof.

AI-assisted implementation by @Marvinthebored, with follow-up work co-authored by @VACInc.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @VACInc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/13bde8a4-8871-483d-810e-9f67f6fd8bfc)
- [Scope reduction, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/d0a61139-e2e3-46b9-ba68-6536a886cb28)

prs.title: fix(ui): preserve Raw editor focus during config refreshes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the Raw config editor losing focus and dropping an edit when a background config publication refreshes Settings. The failure was observed in [the guarded-config CI scenario](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38804334058/job/116661744336).

## User Impact

The Raw editor keeps its focused textarea and selection across equivalent config refreshes. Save and Discard continue to dispatch to the current callbacks.

## Why This Change Was Made

Read the Save and Discard callback props when clicked. Reading them while constructing the SettingsPage children made the Raw subtree depend on config-prop publications, which could replace the textarea before an input event arrived. The repair changes two handler bindings and adds one focused browser regression.

## Evidence

- The new regression fails on main at 26da73bf2aa83c because an equivalent config publication replaces the textarea; it passes after the two-line repair and preserves focus and selection.
- All 15 Raw-view browser tests pass. The original guarded set/patch/reload/apply E2E passes with its assertions and timeouts unchanged.

prs.title: feat: run sandbox Auto Review with a restricted host reviewer
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Sandboxed development needs the canonical Auto Review checkpoint to review the repository the session is actually editing. That repository can have different Git state from its host worktree, while the sandbox intentionally has neither provider credentials nor an installed OpenClaw CLI. The required review therefore needs a bounded way to execute its reviewer without moving repository capture onto the host.

## User Impact

The optional `autoreview` plugin tool runs the installed helper inside the calling sandbox, executes the explicitly selected reviewer through restricted host `openclaw agent exec`, and returns the helper-validated result. Operators enable the plugin and grant this tool through the existing agent and sandbox policies. It requires the updated canonical helper from openclaw/agent-skills#326 and a selected managed or library installation protected by enforced read-only mounts inside the sandbox. SSH file uploads and package-replacing mounts do not qualify.

The reviewer uses an empty private workspace and home, an explicit single-model provider projection, and no tools, skills, workspace context, or bundled plugins. Credentials stay on the host. Failed, interrupted, mismatched, or oversized executions fail visibly; the operation never changes engines. Review plans are capped at eight passes and 600 seconds per pass, with a bounded total deadline. Complete final results are capped below the default Code Mode inbox limit. Direct calls that would exceed their existing model output budget fail explicitly and direct the caller to Code Mode or a smaller review.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin context previously carried a sandbox Boolean and host workspace information, which cannot identify a copied or remote execution repository. The existing harness and sandbox owners now supply closure-bound execution and model authorization to version 2 plugin factories. They retain the original invocation, selected sandbox, installed skill provenance, current model policy, and cancellation lifecycle. Docker and Podman explicitly admit piped input when requested; backends that still declare closed stdin are refused for that operation.

The generated config baseline adds the 21 standard entry fields for this optional plugin. The plugin defines no custom settings.

The plugin coordinates the existing helper exchange. Capture, source revalidation, exclusive response submission, and report validation remain in the helper. Only the fixed reviewer command runs on the host; the complete raw CLI envelope returns to the same helper. Concurrent calls have separate exchanges and process custody, with no new service, reviewer profile, or persistent job store.

## Evidence

Remote fast checks and selected compiler families passed. Earlier related-file evidence covers 1,348 passing cases and two platform skips. The correction and caller batch passed 84 cases with four platform skips across seven files in 45.44 seconds. The final focused correction passed 52 cases with four platform skips across five files in 31.79 seconds, including writable-alias rejection and preserved read-only access. The temporary-directory, mock-export, and config-docs guards passed. The required runtime build took 293.5 seconds; a clean activation build is pending. Hosted CI remains the broad exact-head baseline.

A synthetic near-limit reviewer response passed through the actual canonical helper, tool, catalog value call, and Code Mode inbox: with the real plugin lifecycle wrapper, all 283 findings were preserved from a 1,989,609-byte encoded exchange. The same flow rejected an oversized direct result, accepted a small direct report, preserved source state, and removed each exchange.

Independent review, a clean activation build, and the ordinary guest checkpoint proof remain in progress. The guest proof covers findings and clean results, source changes, Stop, denied substitutions, and separate concurrent sessions.

prs.title: fix(plugins): fence enqueueNextTurnInjection by plugin generation and global side effects
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where a Plugin SDK generation can retain `api.session.workflow.enqueueNextTurnInjection` (or deprecated `api.enqueueNextTurnInjection`) after `register()` returns, allowing retired generations to recreate durable next-turn injections. After disable cleanup removes the generation's state, the stale API can still enqueue model-visible text under a replacement generation's identity. Sibling late-callable mutators (`emitAgentEvent`, run context, attachment delivery, schedule/unschedule) are already generation-fenced via `shouldCommitWorkflowSideEffect()` and `activateGlobalSideEffects`; the enqueue handler was the only gap.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repair adds the same two guards the sibling handlers use:

- When `activateGlobalSideEffects` is `false`, return the existing nonthrowing `{ enqueued: false, id: "", sessionKey }` shape so global opt-out still applies.
- When `shouldCommitWorkflowSideEffect()` is `false` (registry retired or generation not active), return the same inert shape so a retired generation cannot recreate durable state.
- Valid activation-time calls remain aligned with `emitAgentEvent` and pass through to the durable enqueuer.

The fence is checked before policy diagnostics, config reads, and state writes, so the retired generation can no longer commit new workflow side effects. The check uses the workflow-side-effect guard rather than the stricter live-registry helper so valid activation-time calls remain aligned with `emitAgentEvent`.

## User Impact

Trusted in-process plugin code can no longer accidentally or asynchronously mutate durable session state after disable. Re-enabling a plugin no longer lets a new generation consume retired-generation text as model-visible prompt context, and a stale idempotency key can no longer occupy the replacement generation's queue. The repair is a Plugin SDK lifecycle and model-input integrity fix; it is not a plugin sandbox or privilege-escalation change.

## Evidence

Files changed:
- `src/plugins/registry-api.ts` — `enqueueNextTurnInjection` handler now checks `activateGlobalSideEffects === false` and `shouldCommitWorkflowSideEffect()` before policy diagnostics, config reads, and state writes; returns the same inert shape the existing `allowPromptInjection === false` path uses (+14 / -0 production LOC).

Reproduction from issue #127396: a temporary session store, real plugin registries/APIs, real registry retirement, real disable cleanup, a stale retained enqueue API call, and the production next-turn drain. The production proof showed `pendingAfterDisableCleanup: null`, `staleEmit: { emitted: false, reason: "plugin is not loaded" }`, and `staleEnqueue: { enqueued: true, id: "retired-proof", sessionKey: "agent:main:main" }`. After this fix, the `shouldCommitWorkflowSideEffect()` check returns false for the retired generation so the handler returns the inert shape and `staleEnqueue.enqueued` becomes `false` while `staleEmit` continues to be correctly rejected.

CI must validate: full vitest lane + lint + typecheck on the PR head SHA.

## Why This Change Was Made

The text is built from the real admission rules: ACP ids go through the ACP resolver and `acp.allowedAgents`, and `requireAgentId` is honored. Callers pass the requester's already-resolved subagent status, so building the tool reads no session store. One helper resolves `allowAgents` and `requireAgentId` for all four callers.

Native and ACP lists share one renderer (`describeTargetIdList`, built on `summarizeStringEntries`). It lists the first 20 sorted ids, then `(+N). Only the first 20 ids are listed.` Agent ids are at most 64 chars, so the count cap also bounds bytes (about 1.4 KB per list). The overflow text does not assume `agents_list` exists.

It lives in the tool description, not the `agentId` schema property. Codex drops every schema description once a tool schema passes 5,000 bytes (first pass of `compact_large_tool_schema`), and `sessions_spawn` is already at 5,045 on `main`. The schema is unchanged; the tool description is kept.

Tests: the metadata-only suite that imported the full spawn runtime is deleted. Policy and cap cases live in the target-policy and ACP target tests. One registration assertion and the prepared-requester regression (never a store read) sit in the existing `sessions-spawn-tool.test.ts`.

## Evidence

Shipped entry point: `pnpm openclaw agent --local --agent main --message hi` against an isolated state dir and a local OpenAI-compatible mock that records the model request. Agents `main` and `planner`, `tools.toolSearch: false`. `sessions_spawn.description` in the captured request:

| Config | `main` (base) | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No allowlist | no `agentId` text | `` `agentId` targets: Only the requester agent is allowed as a target; no other agentId is configured. Omit to keep the requester agent ("main"). `` |
| `agents.entries.main.subagents.allowAgents: ["planner"]` | no `agentId` text | `` `agentId` targets: Configured agent to target: planner. Omit to keep the requester agent ("main"). `` |

The schema `agentId` stays `{"type":"string"}` in both.

ACP, through the Gateway with a backend enabled: an isolated `pnpm openclaw gateway run` (own state dir, loopback port) with `acp.enabled`, `acp.backend: "acpx"`, `acp.defaultAgent: "codex"`, `acp.allowedAgents: ["codex","claude"]`, agents `main` and `planner`, and `main.subagents.allowAgents: ["planner"]`. The Gateway logs `embedded acpx runtime backend registered lazily`. `pnpm openclaw agent --agent main --message hi` then sent this `sessions_spawn.description` fragment (head `02c4032`) to the local OpenAI-compatible mock (full text, nothing truncated, no secrets):

```
`agentId` targets: With runtime="subagent" (default): Configured agent to target: planner. Omit to keep the requester agent ("main"). With runtime="acp": ACP harness id from: claude, codex. Omit to use the configured ACP default ("codex").
```

The captured `agentId` schema is still `{"type":"string"}`.

Real output, config with `main`, `planner`, `acp.defaultAgent: codex`:

```
description: `agentId` targets a configured agent; ... `sandbox` inherit|require. `agentId` targets: With runtime="subagent" (default): Only the requester agent is allowed as a target; no other agentId is configured. Omit to keep the requester agent ("main"). With runtime="acp": ACP harness id, for exam...
schema agentId: {"type":"string"}
acp agentId=codex:     accepted
acp agentId=main:      rejected: agentId "main" is an OpenClaw config agent, not an ACP harness
acp agentId=(omitted): accepted
requireAgentId=true:   ... agentId is required; the requester agent is "main".
```

Codex fixture, `sessions_spawn`: schema 5,045 bytes on both `main` and this branch (byte-identical); tool description 2,805 to 2,884. Checked against `openai/codex` at `064c6b8c`, `codex-rs/tools/src/json_schema/compaction.rs`. A local Codex checkout was not available, and Codex's own normalized byte count was not measured.

The existing `agents_list` rewrite of `configured agent;` still applies (`agent-tools.deferred-followup-guidance.test.ts`).

Cap regressions: exactly 20 ids has no overflow text, 21 ids does, and 5,000 allowed ids render under 1,000 chars (native); 25 ACP ids are capped for both the allowlist and example forms.

Main merged; prompt snapshots regenerated with `pnpm prompt:snapshots:gen`. Focused tests, `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, `tsgo:core`, changed `tsgo:core:test` graphs and `prompt:snapshots:check` pass.

Test wall (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, measured on this head):

| File | Wall |
| --- | --- |
| `subagent-target-policy.test.ts` (16 tests) | 3.4s |
| `acp-spawn-target.test.ts` (22 tests) | 20s |
| `sessions-spawn-tool.test.ts` (74 tests, existing suite) | 31s warm; the 2 added cases take 5ms and 51ms |
| removed `sessions-spawn-tool.agent-target-description.test.ts` | was ~74s cold |

CI on `02c4032` (main at `12a91e0919` when it ran), all in files this PR does not touch:

| Red | Same on base? |
| --- | --- |
| `test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts` (wrapper inventory) | Yes. Fails on pure `main` `12a91e0919` and `08005517c4` locally, and on unrelated PRs in the same window. |
| `src/gateway/server.visible-spawn-fallback.product-proof.test.ts` (session storage) | Yes. Fails 2 cases on pure `main` `12a91e0919` locally (`Session patch failed unexpectedly`). |
| `ui/src/e2e/chat-mention-search.e2e.test.ts` (UI) | Not reproduced locally (no browser here). No UI file is touched; unrelated PRs fail other UI e2e cases in the same window. |

Touched tests, `tsgo:core` and `prompt:snapshots:check` pass on this head.

prs.title: fix(gateway): IPv6 Gateway hosts fail in SSH targets and discovery URLs
prs.body:
Closes #127454

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: IPv6 Gateway hosts produce SSH targets and discovery URLs that OpenSSH and `new URL` reject.

## User Impact

IPv6-only remote Gateways work with inferred SSH routing, `gateway probe --ssh`, and discovery output. DNS names and IPv4 are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`parseSshTarget` now reads `[IPv6]` and `[IPv6]:port` as the raw host. Discovery and status bracket IPv6 through one `formatUrlHost` helper, which replaces six inline copies.

## Evidence

- New tests fail before the fix and pass after (the direct formatter table is dropped). Touched and sibling suites, `tsgo:core`, oxlint, and oxfmt pass.
- `openclaw gateway probe --ssh 'me@[2001:db8::10]:2222'`, before: `ssh: Could not resolve hostname [2001:db8::10]`. After: the raw address reaches SSH and times out (unreachable documentation address).
- Real `parseSshTarget` and `buildGatewayDiscoveryTarget` on Linux, node 24, before then after:
  ```
  parseSshTarget('me@[2001:db8::10]:2222') = {"host":"[2001:db8::10]","port":2222}  ->  {"host":"2001:db8::10","port":2222}
  parseSshTarget('me@[2001:db8::10]')      = null                                   ->  {"host":"2001:db8::10","port":22}
  discovery JSON = {"wsUrl":"ws://2001:db8::10:18789","sshTarget":"me@2001:db8::10:2222"}
               -> {"wsUrl":"ws://[2001:db8::10]:18789","sshTarget":"me@[2001:db8::10]:2222"}
  ```
- Not covered: the macOS app's Swift SSH parser.
