## SDK / caller upgrade contract

- **Permitted callers (unchanged):** Unsandboxed sessions (`sandbox.mode: "off"` without `sessionEntry.sandbox === "required"`, and `non-main` main-session turns) continue to run CLI backends (`claude-cli`, `google-gemini-cli`, `codex-cli`) through `runCliAgent`. Sandboxed sessions configured with API-backed models (or recovered via per-agent `agents.entries.<id>.subagents.model` or payload `model`) continue to dispatch through `runEmbeddedAgent`.
- **Fail-closed callers:** Sandboxed sessions (`sandbox.mode: "all"`, `non-main` non-main sessions, or `sessionEntry.sandbox === "required"`) that resolve a CLI execution provider via inherited `agents.defaults.subagents.model`, fallback candidates, `models.<ref>.agentRuntime` overrides, or payload `model` fail closed with `AgentHarnessPreflightError` before any CLI subprocess is spawned.
- **Stored-data compatibility:** This change touches no SQLite table, session-store writer, or migration step; pre-existing sessions from `v2026.10.3` (schema 24) migrate to schema 27 and preserve `sandbox: "required"` and `sandboxMode: "off"` fields verbatim.

## Boundary decisions requested from maintainers

1. **Fail-closed candidate rejection vs. silent model fallback:** Confirm that failing closed with `AgentHarnessPreflightError` (naming `agents.entries.<id>.subagents.model`, `agents.defaults.subagents.model`, and payload `model`) is preferred over silently altering the documented subagent model precedence order (`#58823`).

The plain TypeScript controller stays authoritative through `projectOwner`; value memos preserve pending desktop setup writes across equal route refreshes. ## What Problem This Solves

Matrix's bounded exhausted-decryption retry map retired old entries without retiring their notification-deduplication markers. Long-running clients could retain those markers indefinitely and suppress a later failure for a retired event.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing `clearDecryptRetry` owner for TTL and capacity eviction, and clear the in-memory notification set at stop. No retry budget, timeout, map cap, TTL, persisted format, schema, retention policy, credential authority, or crypto shutdown contract changes.

Production delta: 8 additions / 2 deletions (+6 net). Tests/support: 113 additions / 32 deletions (+81 net), including a coherent extraction that keeps the existing SDK suite below its pre-change line count. This is a concrete bounded-resource bug fix, not a deletion-quota cleanup.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

None. This joins existing related in-memory state under its existing cleanup owner; no timing or authority guard is removed.

## Evidence

- Baseline regression failed at the intended final notification assertions for both capacity and expiry; not setup or timeout failures.
- Fixed full SDK suite: 98/98 passed; lint-suppression contracts: 3/3 passed. Full command 1248.11 seconds on the loaded host; SDK file 1058.98 seconds (72% transform). The capacity regression drives 513 real SDK event-bridge entries through the existing eight-attempt retry lifecycle with fake time; no sleeps, skips, retries, or timeout changes.
- After extraction, the three retry-cap/capacity/expiry cases passed again, plus three lint-suppression contracts (two-shard command 1152.26 seconds; SDK file 967.00 seconds, 96% transform). Other SDK cases were outside that focused selection; their earlier full-suite result is not relabeled a second full run. All cases, hooks, and assertions are preserved.
- Production extension typecheck, runtime cycles and full Madge passed, both cycle counts zero. Fresh independent P2 review of the complete fix and extraction completed scoped-clean. Final line-cap ratchet passed for all three changed files. One final type-only import annotation/formatting correction does not change runtime behavior.
- Required changed-file checking was invoked and identified the SDK test's over-cap growth; the coherent extraction repairs it without weakening coverage or limits. Two unrelated stale max-lines entries and the incomplete aggregate remain recorded rather than called passing. Local SDK declaration lint preparation reached its existing 300-second limit before diagnostics; exact-head hosted CI is the broad gate. No public SDK surface changed.
- All runtime proof uses task-owned HOME/OpenClaw/XDG state. No live Gateway, channel credentials, or message-content logging.

## Hosted CI repair

The first published extraction head failed `check-test-types` (job 116646065703): the SDK fixture's unspecialized Vitest function type admitted a constructor rather than promising the callback the extracted cases actually consume. This is owned by this PR. The repair specializes that fixture at its producer and shares its exact fake-event decrypt callback type; it adds no cast, runtime behavior, suppression, or assertion change. The actual full extension test type graph now passes. Fresh independent P2 review is scoped-clean, formatting passes, and the final lint-suppression run passes 3/3. prs.title: fix(gateway): reject ambiguous QR login accounts and preserve sibling listeners
prs.body:
Related: #135142

## What Problem This Solves

Starting QR login without an account ID on a multi-account channel can pair the wrong account and stop every other account's listener.

## User Impact

Multi-account requests must name an `accountId`; an omitted or blank ID returns an actionable error listing valid IDs before login or listener effects. Single-account requests retain their existing default/profile behavior. Pairing account B stops and restores only B, while A continues running.

A configuration reload, plugin replacement, or Gateway shutdown invalidates pending credential writes; start a new QR login afterward. This does not repair credentials already written to the wrong directory or add an account selector to the Control UI. The issue remains linked rather than automatically closed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway now uses the plugin's canonical account inventory/default resolver for lifecycle scope and rejects ambiguous requests. It preserves omitted single-account plugin input because account IDs and credential profiles can differ.

A narrow, additive `assertCredentialPersistenceCurrent` option on the existing QR-start adapter carries the Gateway's account binding to the plugin's credential-writing owner. WhatsApp and Zalo compose it with their active-login guards. No protocol version, configuration option, schema, new SDK export, or package dependency is added. The existing SDK export inventory is unchanged; CI checks the affected public type surface.

Deferred facts: configuration and plugin-registry identity are checked against the live Gateway owner immediately before credential persistence; reload/close state is also checked. The requested account and plugin-selected credential path stay bound to that immutable configuration, while the plugin owns active-login identity and expiry. The RPC may finish while QR pairing continues. Timeouts and socket settings remain operation inputs. Cached WhatsApp QR flows retain their original guard, and stale or unguarded flows are replaced.

Original fix by @Yigtwxx; maintainer cleanup adds ambiguous-account rejection, current-target validation, RPC/SDK documentation, and smaller lifecycle coverage. The lifecycle fixture shrinks from 206 to 127 lines, removing its transition manager and type-laundering casts. Production delta versus main is +99/-43 (net +56): the ambiguity check and deferred credential guard require growth; unrelated deletions were avoided. Tests: +278/-5 (net +273). Docs: +11/-2 (net +9).

## Evidence

- Current-main source/history confirms that an omitted ID reaches `stopChannel`/`startChannel`, whose owner widens omission to all channel accounts. The relevant prior handler refactor is `83b060d2349d0`; the existing WhatsApp operation-lifetime guard comes from `bb8c04d53778d`.
- PR CI is the test gate per maintainer policy. It covers Gateway handler/lifecycle tests, affected WhatsApp/Zalo tests, types, lint, and SDK/package-boundary checks. The first head passed all executed runtime/unit test shards and production types. Its two fixture-only failures (`no-unnecessary-type-arguments` and TS2352 on the partial Gateway context cast) were fixed by using the shared typed context factory and default deferred type. Final head `1e96c3abb60f9e2e093a8f58e0d84a4f44b533cb` passed [CI run 38800397522](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38800397522): 41 successful jobs, 28 intentionally skipped, no failures. This includes the repaired Gateway test types and core lint. The aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate`, dependency review, and security-sensitive review also passed in [run 38802306109](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38802306109); no approval command was posted. [Initial run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38798077372).
- Regressions: `%s rejects an ambiguous account before plugin or listener effects` (start and wait); `keeps an omitted account omitted for the plugin so environment-selected profiles survive`; `keeps account A running while account B pairs (connected=%s)` (success and timeout); `revokes deferred credential writes when the account configuration changes`; `transfers credential writes to the exact active login instance`; `handles a %s cached QR account binding` (unguarded, stale, current).
- Final-head Gateway regressions passed in [job 116648301602](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38800397522/job/116648301602): listener continuity for successful/timeout pairing took 247/5 ms, ambiguous start/wait rejection took 1/2 ms, current-target credential rejection took 2 ms, and single-account compatibility took 1 ms. prs.title: fix(nostr): filter literal-allowlist authors before admission
prs.body:
## Summary

Keep denied authors from consuming durable-admission capacity for Nostr accounts configured with a literal-key allowlist. The Gateway derives a normalized local rejection hint; the bus drops nonmembers before durable ingress while preserving both existing rate guards and canonical authorization. This builds on the durable-ingress ownership in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/110653 and retains the signature-before-policy ordering in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/58236.

## What Problem This Solves

1. In `extensions/nostr/src/nostr-bus.ts`, arrivals previously entered shared durable admission before sender policy ran. For literal-key allowlist accounts, traffic from denied authors could consume the allowance needed for approved DMs.
2. Moving only the admission counter would leave the separate dispatch-global limiter unchanged. Instead, `extensions/nostr/src/gateway.ts` supplies an internal local key hint, and the live relay handler discards nonmembers before either counter is reached.

The result is scoped availability hardening for explicit literal-key allowlists, not a new authorization grant.

## Why this design

- Enable the optimization only for explicit allowlist policy with a nonempty list of entirely valid literal pubkeys; reuse existing hex/npub/nostr-prefix normalization and deduplicate once per account lifecycle.
- Retain the ordinary admission path for wildcards, access groups, invalid/non-string entries, pairing, open, disabled, and default policies.
- Keep the peer list local rather than including it in relay subscription filters.
- Preserve canonical sender-policy checks, signature verification, durable recovery, and existing 200-event/60-second and per-sender limits.
- Intentionally stop storing/deduplicating newly denied arrivals in this narrow mode. Previously queued rows keep their existing recovery path. No configuration, schema, dependency, public SDK, or migration change is introduced.

## Composition with existing ingress work

| Related change | Governed layer | Composition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/110653 | Durable Nostr ingress and recovery | Already in the base; admitted events retain the same queue, cursor, retry and terminal lifecycle. |
| https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/58236 | Signature verification before policy/pairing effects | Already in the base; real transport verification and dispatch verification remain in place. |

The new check sits before durable admission; it neither moves the existing guards nor bypasses dispatch authorization.

## Evidence of Fix

| Path / mode | Command or observation | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Literal allowlist, 200 signed denied arrivals then approved DM | `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/test-projects.mts extensions/nostr/src/nostr-bus.outbound.test.ts -t "delivers approved DM"`, controlled subtraction/restoration of only the membership check | Clean control passed; saturation case failed with durable-admission-rate rejection (exit 1). | Real local WebSocket + pinned SimplePool + NIP-04 + real durable queue: only approved event enqueued and onMessage called. |
| Forged approved author, relay privacy, and canonical denial | `pnpm test extensions/nostr/src/nostr-bus.outbound.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` | Existing sender and transport contracts retained. | Forgery rejected before callback; matching author still blocked by authorization; wire filters contain no peer list. Full owner file: 14 passed. |

prs.title: fix(security): warn when toolsBySender uses mutable name or username keys
prs.body:
## Summary

Operators configuring `toolsBySender` with `name:` or `username:` prefixes received no security audit warning or documentation guidance that those prefixes match self-service mutable sender attributes and replace the enclosing scope's `tools` policy on match. Emit a `channels.<id>.toolsBySender.mutable_entries` security audit and doctor warning whenever channel or account `toolsBySender` policies use `name:` or `username:` keys—covering both `.config`-wrapped channel accounts and flat resolved account shapes such as WhatsApp, as well as channel entries named `accounts`—and document in the group, Slack, and tool-policy references that stable `id:` keys should be preferred when granting extra tools or overriding group `deny` rules, complementing the typed sender-key contract from #24907 and #162427 and the channel-policy binding guidance in #171829.

## What Problem This Solves

1. **Unwarned mutable sender keys in channel `toolsBySender` scopes (`src/security/audit-channel.ts`, `src/config/tools-by-sender.ts`, `src/config/group-scope-tree.ts`, `extensions/whatsapp/src/accounts.ts`)**: `resolveScopeToolsPolicy` (`src/config/group-scope-tree.ts:130`) returns `resolveToolsBySender(...) ?? node.tools`, so a matching per-sender entry replaces the group or channel `tools` policy for that turn. While `collectChannelSecurityFindingsCore` (`src/security/audit-channel.ts`) audited `allowFrom` lists for mutable name entries, it did not inspect `toolsBySender` maps for `name:` or `username:` keys across either `.config`-wrapped accounts (such as Slack and Discord) or flat resolved account records (such as `resolveWhatsAppAccount` in `extensions/whatsapp/src/accounts.ts:133`), leaving operators without a warning when a display-name or handle key could be selected by a group member renaming themselves.
2. **Documentation omitted mutable-key risk and Slack sender-key constraints on tool grants (`docs/channels/groups.md`, `docs/channels/slack/access-control.md`, `docs/gateway/config-tools/tool-policy.md`, `extensions/slack/src/group-policy.ts`)**: the `toolsBySender` documentation listed typed prefixes without noting that `username:` and `name:` match mutable sender attributes and should not be used to grant extra tools over a group `deny`, and `extensions/slack/src/group-policy.ts:111` intentionally omits `messageProvider`, so Slack per-channel `toolsBySender` supports `id:`, `e164:`, `username:`, `name:`, and `"*"` (not `channel:` keys).

Net effect: operators who used `name:` or `username:` in `toolsBySender` to grant tool exceptions in a restricted group had no audit diagnostic or documentation warning that another member could rename their display name or handle to match that key.

### What this Problem Solves

See the numbered defect paths above (`src/security/audit-channel.ts`, `src/config/tools-by-sender.ts`, `src/config/group-scope-tree.ts`, `extensions/whatsapp/src/accounts.ts`, `docs/channels/groups.md`, `docs/channels/slack/access-control.md`, `docs/gateway/config-tools/tool-policy.md`).

## Why this design

- Preserve the explicit typed-key runtime contract (`id:`, `channel:`, `e164:`, `username:`, `name:`) with zero breaking runtime or config schema changes.
- Emit `channels.<id>.toolsBySender.mutable_entries` (`severity: "warn"`) in `collectChannelSecurityFindingsCore` (`src/security/audit-channel.ts`) across both `audit` (`runSecurityAuditCore`) and `doctor` (`collectSecurityWarnings`) modes whenever `toolsBySender` contains `name:` or `username:` keys, recommending `id:` keys.
- Inspect `account.config ?? account` and skip `accounts` only at the account-root level (`isAccountRoot = true`) so flat resolved accounts (such as WhatsApp) and channels literally named `accounts` (such as `channels.slack.channels.accounts.toolsBySender`) are both audited without duplicating per-account findings.
- Report only the count and config scope path (for example `channels.whatsapp.accounts.default.groups.120363123456789@g.us.toolsBySender` or `channels.slack.channels.accounts.toolsBySender`) without echoing raw configured usernames or display names into audit output.
- Document in `docs/channels/groups.md`, `docs/channels/slack/access-control.md`, and `docs/gateway/config-tools/tool-policy.md` that `id:` keys should be preferred when granting extra tools or overriding group `deny` rules, and list only supported prefixes (`id:`, `e164:`, `username:`, `name:`, `"*"`) in the Slack channel `toolsBySender` reference.

## Why this does not conflict with #24907, #162427, and #171829

| PR | Governed layer | Relation to this PR |
|---|---|---|
| #24907 (`cfa44ea6b4f`) | Unprefixed channel `allowFrom` matching and `dangerouslyAllowNameMatching` audit checks in `src/security/audit-channel.ts` | This PR extends `src/security/audit-channel.ts` to also warn on explicit `name:` and `username:` entries inside channel `toolsBySender` maps while leaving `allowFrom` checks untouched. |
| #162427 (`d6a09202b14`) | Doctor migration of bare `toolsBySender` keys to `id:` and typed key parsing via `parseToolsBySenderTypedKey` | This PR reuses `parseToolsBySenderTypedKey` from `src/config/types.tools.ts` to classify `name:` and `username:` keys without altering Doctor migration or runtime matching. |
| #171829 (`68c3f3fb660`) | Discord channel-policy binding and documentation recommending stable IDs when granting extra tools | This PR applies the same stable-ID guidance to `toolsBySender` sender keys in `docs/channels/groups.md`, `docs/channels/slack/access-control.md`, and `docs/gateway/config-tools/tool-policy.md`. |

All three PRs are already in this branch's `upstream/main` base (`512cc70c54f`), and no runtime resolver files overlap.

## Evidence

### Evidence of Fix

| Path | Mode | Command | Before Fix | After Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Shipped CLI `security audit` and `security audit --json` with WhatsApp `default` (`toolsBySender["name:ops-lead-name"]`) and `work` (`toolsBySender["username:bob-handle"]`) accounts (`src/cli/security-cli.ts` -> `src/security/audit.ts` -> `src/security/audit-channel.ts`) | Shipped CLI (`src/entry.ts security audit` & `--json`) | `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$TMP_STATE" OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="$TMP_STATE/openclaw.json" node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts security audit` | 0 `toolsBySender.mutable_entries` findings rendered in CLI output or `--json` report | Renders `channels.whatsapp.toolsBySender.mutable_entries WhatsApp toolsBySender uses mutable sender keys (account: default)` and `(account: work)` with `1 toolsBySender entry in channels.whatsapp.accounts.<id>.groups.<jid>.toolsBySender match mutable username:/name: sender attributes... Fix: Prefer stable id: keys in toolsBySender...` while redacting `ops-lead-name` and `bob-handle` |
| Shipped CLI `doctor --non-interactive` security box (`src/commands/doctor-security.ts` -> `src/security/audit-channel.ts`) | Shipped CLI (`src/entry.ts doctor --non-interactive`) | `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$TMP_STATE" OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="$TMP_STATE/openclaw.json" node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts doctor --non-interactive` | No `toolsBySender` warning in the `◇ Security` summary box | Renders `- WhatsApp toolsBySender uses mutable sender keys (account: default): 1 toolsBySender entry in channels.whatsapp.accounts.default.groups.120363123456789@g.us.toolsBySender match mutable username:/name: sender attributes...` and `(account: work)` in the `◇ Security` box |
| Real `whatsappSetupPlugin` flat resolved accounts and real `slackPlugin` with a channel named `accounts` (`channels.slack.channels.accounts.toolsBySender["username:alice-handle"]`) (`src/security/audit-channel.ts`) | `runSecurityAuditCore` (`audit`) and `collectSecurityWarnings` (`doctor`) | `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/test-projects.mts src/security/audit-channel-entry-authentication.test.ts` | `account.config` is `undefined` on `ResolvedWhatsAppAccount` and unconditional `key === "accounts"` skips `channels.slack.channels.accounts`; 0 warnings | Emits `channels.whatsapp.toolsBySender.mutable_entries` for `default` and `work` and `channels.slack.toolsBySender.mutable_entries` for `channels.slack.channels.accounts.toolsBySender` while redacting `ops-lead-name`, `bob-handle`, and `alice-handle` |
| Channel `toolsBySender` with stable `id:` keys only (`src/security/audit-channel.ts`) | `collectChannelSecurityFindingsCore` (`audit` and `doctor` modes) | `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/test-projects.mts src/security/audit-channel-entry-authentication.test.ts src/security/audit-channel-account-metadata.test.ts` | 0 `toolsBySender.mutable_entries` warnings | 0 `toolsBySender.mutable_entries` warnings; all 10 tests across 2 files pass |
| Core typecheck, lint, assertion-safety, and docs glossary gates | Static verification | `pnpm tsgo:core && pnpm exec oxlint src/security/audit-channel.ts src/security/audit-channel-entry-authentication.test.ts && pnpm run docs:check-i18n-glossary --base upstream/main && pnpm check:assertion-safety --base upstream/main` | N/A | All gates exit `0` (`0 warnings and 0 errors`, assertion SAFETY ratchet OK) |

Observed shipped CLI output at head `a52e67e091e41a5c20b4ef64afa15d0aa7875974` (`src/entry.ts security audit` and `src/entry.ts doctor --non-interactive`) and sink-level assertions in `src/security/audit-channel-entry-authentication.test.ts` confirm both the rendered warnings and identifier redaction.

```text
$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$TMP_STATE" OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="$TMP_STATE/openclaw.json" node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts security audit

  Fix: Prefer stable id: keys in toolsBySender, especially for entries that grant extra tools or override group deny rules.
```

## What Problem This Solves

The quota-recovery E2E case released an old held catalog response as soon as the provider began its successful response. Clearing the persisted quota block does not prove that the replacement catalog has been published, so the old request could succeed before supersession and fail the intended assertion.

Keep the old response held while polling `models.list` with `preparedOnly: true` until the published catalog reports OpenAI no longer pending and the recovered model available. Then release the response and retain the existing structured superseded-generation rejection and explicit-release assertions. prs.title: fix(exec): expand file: URI sqlite targets before variable expansion in live-state guard
prs.body:
## Summary

The gateway-host exec preflight that keeps external `sqlite3` off OpenClaw's live state database failed to recognize `$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`$HOME` variable spellings hidden behind a `file:` URI prefix, so an agent running `sqlite3 "file:$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/state/openclaw.sqlite?mode=ro" …` skipped the refusal while the real shell expansion still delivered the live database path to sqlite3. This fix normalizes the `file:` scheme before variable expansion inside `expandSqliteDatabaseToken` (src/infra/exec-control-command-guard.ts), so every recognized variable spelling is now refused equally, bare, `file:`-prefixed, or with an empty or `localhost` authority.

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway-host exec runs a preflight guard that refuses to start external `sqlite3` when its database target resolves inside the active OpenClaw state directory — external SQLite clients join the live WAL outside the embedded runtime's version/ownership guard and risk state corruption (src/agents/bash-tools.exec-run.ts rejects via `rejectUnsafeExecLiveStateSqliteShellCommand`). The guard expanded recognized variables only when they started the token and stripped the `file:` scheme afterwards, so `sqlite3 "file:$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/state/openclaw.sqlite?mode=ro"` slipped past: `fileURLToPath` turned the unexpanded token into the literal path `/$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/state/openclaw.sqlite`, which never matches the state root, while the shell expanded the variable inside the double-quoted token and sqlite3 received the real live-database URI. The bare `"$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/…"` spelling and literal absolute `file:/…` URLs were already refused; the variable-bearing URI spelling alone escaped. After this change, the guard strips the scheme (and `?`/`#` suffix, percent-decoding) before running the existing `$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`${…}`/`$HOME`/`~` expansions, so the URI spellings are refused exactly like their bare equivalents, and private database copies outside the state directory remain fully inspectable.

## Why this design

- Normalize before expanding: scheme handling happens first, then the existing variable expansions run on the resulting path — this keeps one expansion code path instead of adding a second URI-specific expansion inside the URI.
- Absolute `file:/…` URLs keep `fileURLToPath` semantics (host/percent handling) unchanged; only non-absolute (variable-bearing or opaque) `file:` bodies take the strip-and-decode path, because `fileURLToPath` on `file:$VAR/…` invents a bogus root-absolute path that hides the variable — the exact defect.
- Fail-closed breadth is deliberately not extended: tokens with unrecognized residual variables keep the guard's existing recognition families. Widening to "refuse any token containing `$`" is a behavioral policy change left to maintainer decision, not smuggled into this normalization fix.
- No config surface, no default change, no exported signature change: `expandSqliteDatabaseToken` is module-private.

## Evidence of Fix

| Path | Mode | Before fix | After fix | How verified |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sqlite3 "$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/state/openclaw.sqlite"` | bare variable (control) | refused | refused (no regression) | existing suite case; new suite run 6/6 green |
| `sqlite3 "file:/abs/state/openclaw.sqlite?mode=ro"` | literal absolute URL (control) | refused | refused (no regression) | existing + new test; absolute branch keeps `fileURLToPath` |
| `sqlite3 "file:$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/state/openclaw.sqlite?mode=ro"` | reported gap | **guard missed** — preflight returned null; shell argv demo confirmed bash delivers the expanded live-DB URI to sqlite3 | refused with "external sqlite3 cannot open databases under the active OpenClaw state directory" | direct probe of the exact function before/after (scratch, no DB opened) + new regression test |
| `sqlite3 "file:${OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR}/state/openclaw.sqlite"` | reported gap, braced form | **missed** (expanded to literal `/${OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR}/…`) | refused | probe + new regression test |
| `sqlite3 "file:$HOME/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite?mode=ro"` (state under HOME) | HOME form | **missed** (expanded to literal `/$HOME/…`) | refused | probe (os.homedir mocked per repo test pattern) + new regression test |
| `sqlite3 -cmd '.open "file:$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/…"' :memory:` | carrier-wrapped reopen | **missed** | refused | new regression test (`.open` tokens share the same expansion path) |
| `sqlite3 "file:~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite"` | tilde URI | not normalized (parity only; shell does not expand mid-string `~`) | normalized like bare `~/…` and refused when under state dir | new regression test |
| `sqlite3 "file:/tmp/snapshot-outside-state/openclaw.sqlite?mode=ro"` | private copy (negative control) | allowed | allowed (still) | new negative-control test asserts null |
| `sqlite3 "/tmp/snapshot/openclaw.sqlite"` | bare private copy | allowed | allowed | existing suite case green |
| `sqlite3 "file:$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/…"` via real gateway exec tool | end-to-end spawn proof | refused before spawn (stand-in binary marker stays `ENOENT`) | same, verified end to end | new e2e test: tool.execute rejects with the guard message |
| `sqlite3 "file:/…/snapshot/openclaw.sqlite?mode=ro"` via real gateway exec tool | end-to-end private-copy proof | executes | executes (marker written) | new e2e test: tool.execute completes |
| full suite (7 tests incl. the spawn regression) | recorded base-versus-head run | **base (pre-fix) 3 failed / 4 passed** — both URI-detection tests and the e2e spawn proof fail, i.e. the preflight misses the variable-bearing URI live target | **head 7/7 passed** — same suite, same commands, green | `git worktree` at merge-base ca0a172d29 with the new test file vs branch head 37db2fd; both runs recorded in the worklog |
| `sqlite3 "file:$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/…"` through the shipped `createExecTool` gateway exec path, standalone (no test mocks) | recorded production-path observation | (pre-fix) guard returned null and the command reached execution | **REFUSED before spawn**: `external sqlite3 cannot open databases under the active OpenClaw state directory. Use OpenClaw commands for live state, or inspect a private backup copy outside OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR.` (literal captured output) | captured via the repo's own `scripts/tsx.mjs` runner calling the production tool; runId-scoped, no secrets in output |
| private-copy `file:` URI + full guard behavior | recorded test-runner observation | (pre-fix, same suite run) 3 failed / 4 passed at merge-base | verbose run: all 7 tests `✓` incl. `rejects a variable-bearing file: URI live target before spawn and runs a private-copy URI` (spawn-proof: live-URI marker `ENOENT`, private-copy marker written) | `pnpm vitest run --reporter=verbose`; a bare-node standalone private-copy run hits a pre-existing process-supervisor cleanup race unrelated to this change (the same command completes under the shipped test harness) |

| `/bash sqlite3 "file:$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/…?mode=ro"` as a real chat turn on a running Gateway (released 2026.10.3, test VM) | live Gateway session, before the fix | **RAN, Exit 0, printed `7`** — the live decoy database was opened | n/a | `chat.send` + `chat.history` against a throwaway Gateway on loopback; decoy DB `user_version=7` placed inside the state dir |
| same turn on this branch (head `d1b0378`) with `file:$VAR`, `file:${VAR}`, `file://$VAR`, `file://localhost$VAR` | live Gateway session, after the fix | n/a | **all REFUSED**: `external sqlite3 cannot open databases under the active OpenClaw state directory. Use OpenClaw commands for live state, or inspect a private backup copy outside OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR.` | same harness; bare `$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` control also refused |
| private copy `file:/tmp/t/snap/copy.sqlite?mode=ro` and `file:///tmp/t/snap/copy.sqlite?mode=ro` as real chat turns (head `d1b0378`) | live Gateway session, private-copy execution | n/a | **RAN, Exit 0, printed `42`** for both | copy outside the state dir with `user_version=42` |

Sink-level observations: the guard's refusal fires **before process spawn** — the new end-to-end test drives the real gateway exec tool with a stand-in `sqlite3` binary and asserts (a) the variable-bearing URI live target throws the refusal while the marker file stays `ENOENT` (process never started), and (b) a private-copy `file:` URI command executes end to end (marker file written). Both halves of the chain — guard miss before the fix, refusal after — are additionally covered by direct probe observation, the shell-expansion argv demo, and the live Gateway-session chat turns above (the spellings `file://$VAR` and `file://localhost$VAR`, which the shell expands to `file:///<state>/…`, are refused too).

## Testing

- New cases in `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-live-state-sqlite-guard.test.ts`: variable-bearing `file:` URI spellings (`$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` plain/braced, `-cmd .open` carrier, literal state-dir URL), `$HOME` URI forms incl. bare-form regression, private-copy URI negative control, a `cd` regression control with the exec workdir inside the state directory (relative URI stays allowed, variable-bearing URI still refused), and an end-to-end gateway exec test proving the variable-URI live target is rejected before spawn while a private-copy URI command runs. Suite: 9/9 passed (includes the `file://` and `file://localhost` authority spellings and a `file:///` private-copy control).
- Adjacent guard suite `src/infra/exec-control-command-guard.test.ts`: 2/2 passed.
- `pnpm oxfmt --check` clean on both changed files; `pnpm tsgo:core` exit 0.

releases.body:
## 2026.10.10-beta.1

### Highlights

- **Faster, steadier Gateway:** chat turns, session lists, startup, and idle Gateways do far less SQLite and main-thread work, with more database work moved onto worker threads, so busy hosts and large agent fleets stay responsive. (#167965, #168002, #168093, #169005, #169164, #171685, #170151, #169871, #168649, #170612, #171371, #171805, #168992, #169543) Thanks @obviyus, @609NFT, @Leon-SK668, @chelsealong, @RomneyDa, and @joshavant.
- **Updates that finish:** upgrades from 2026.10.1 and earlier betas complete, busy Gateways and slow Doctor steps no longer refuse or roll back a good update, failed updates no longer leave a half-installed version, and macOS, Windows, and Bun installs recover from their platform-specific failures. (#168849, #172249, #172196, #172151, #172247, #171101, #170519, #172640, #171936, #170940, #171077, #172494) Thanks @RomneyDa, @homeworld520, @Yolo521-bot, @giulianoaccorsi, @AntaresGG, @stop-time, @davidcittadini, and @SBC2016.
- **Restart-safe replies:** interrupted and unfinished replies resume after a Gateway restart, and watched child results, queued turns, accepted agent updates, and operator tasks survive restarts instead of disappearing. (#172234, #172412, #169489, #171717, #170697, #170858, #170384, #172356, #172023) Thanks @jeanmonet.
- **Cloud sessions:** move sessions between local and cloud from the session menu, organize cloud environments by repository with environment recipes and verified Node toolchains, and see snapshot progress while sessions start before the first snapshot finishes uploading. (#171690, #170892, #170862, #170796, #170875, #170895, #171729)
- **Local Gateway in the desktop apps:** the Windows desktop app and fresh Tauri installs can run a local Gateway, fresh macOS installs start in guided dashboard setup, and first-run setup chooses inference automatically. (#169522, #169512, #169568, #169628)
- **New models:** Gemini 4 Argon becomes the default Gemini model alongside Gemini 3.8 Flash, Nemotron 3.5 Super VL and xAI Imagine Image 2.0 arrive, Meta models run through Muse Code, and pickers stop offering retired models. (#171852, #172339, #172449, #172445, #170487, #171526, #171879) Thanks @nv-kasikritc, @jacobtomlinson, @JFLeonM, and @obviyus.
- **Newer Apple platforms required:** OpenClaw now requires macOS 26.2, iOS 26.2, and Safari 26.2 or newer. (#168595)

### Changes

- **Apple platform requirement:** require macOS, iOS, and Safari 26.2 or newer for the native apps and Control UI. (#168595)
- **Cloud sessions:** move sessions between local and cloud from session menus, organize cloud environments by repository, support repository environment recipes with verified Node toolchains, save suggested cloud profiles on first use, show snapshot startup progress, start sessions while the first snapshot uploads, ready workers for empty-workspace sessions, report slow dispatch phases, and keep cloud setup secrets behind scoped egress grants. (#171690, #170892, #170862, #170796, #170875, #170895, #171729, #170929, #171749, #171073, #170810) Thanks @VACInc.
- **Desktop apps and first run:** support local Gateways in the Windows desktop app, start fresh Tauri installs with a local Gateway, start fresh macOS installs in guided dashboard setup, guide missing native permissions in chat, and choose inference automatically during first-run setup. (#169522, #169512, #169568, #169635, #169628)
- **Local setup:** offer optional memory embedding setup, add managed llama.cpp OCR and vision setup, and allow non-interactive llama.cpp embedding-only setup. (#163693, #148193, #170153) Thanks @PollyBot13, @duyufansh2008, and @dh-js.
- **Bun runtime:** build standalone OpenClaw executables with Bun, add an opt-in pinned Bun runtime that rejects unpinnable paths before changing anything, and start the Gateway faster on Bun. (#172384, #168832, #168982, #169543) Thanks @vincentkoc.
- **Experimental PostgreSQL:** add an experimental PostgreSQL engine for the Workboard store, select the shared-state engine at its owner, generate PostgreSQL DDL from canonical SQLite schemas, add PostgreSQL migrations with capability admission and exact schema-drift checks, preserve PostgreSQL stores in backups and updates, and add verified offline database port tooling. (#169214, #171962, #168219, #169933, #172265, #170828, #170518, #171368, #171265, #170037, #170055, #170059, #171350, #171484, #171518, #171795, #172046, #171545) Thanks @vincentkoc and @joshavant.
- **Conversations:** organize and archive nested conversations explicitly, choose when sessions can send and receive messages, opt in to `sessions_send` thread targets, run sessions in existing folders on paired devices, and snooze sessions until a custom time. (#168076, #162316, #168846, #169722, #171255) Thanks @VACInc, @obviyus, and @jacobtomlinson.
- **Session personalization:** personalize session backgrounds, add per-session speech bubbles and prompt reactions, show session-specific previews for public links, and match public conversation pages to the chat design with copy buttons. (#168301, #168861, #169527, #168156) Thanks @vyctorbrzezowski and @VACInc.
- **Control UI navigation:** organize personal navigation in a compact sidebar rail with real shortcut icons, filter sidebar users by online status, keep New conversation visible across sidebar modes, show session details beside wide conversations, make colored sessions easier to scan, inspect attached automations from session hovercards, put everyday session actions first, and make release updates discoverable from the account menu. (#168325, #168997, #172243, #170771, #170707, #170382, #172240, #168616, #172544, #100024) Thanks @fuller-stack-dev, @shakkernerd, and @VACInc.
- **Control UI chat:** group session context and task progress in Details, clarify the session details inspector, render assistant directives and an embed tag, show readable tweet preview cards, load older history in larger pages, shrink the composer in existing sessions, search emoji by name in the reaction picker, add manual code folding to session diffs, and show or hide values in secure entry prompts. (#161674, #172436, #64104, #168213, #170481, #171637, #172577, #172350, #169925, #172549) Thanks @vyctorbrzezowski, @obviyus, @Takhoffman, @Patrick-Erichsen, and @jacobtomlinson.
- **Languages:** add Swedish to the Control UI and docs, and include plugin catalogs in locale refresh. (#62063, #171496) Thanks @yeager and @vincentkoc.
- **Agents API:** choose Agents API hosted workspaces when starting sessions, isolate Agents API sessions from Gateway tools and MCP, and allow shared compaction tuning in hosted sessions. (#168259, #170728, #171813)
- **MCP apps and automations:** use MCP plugin apps across conversations and workspace files, trigger automations from MCP events, connect MCP apps through a principal-bound relay plugin, and support principal-bound remote Control UI for trusted plugins. (#161747, #165399, #168233, #170540)
- **Plugins and SDK:** allow per-run model fallback overrides, fork a session's live context for background side questions, let plugins steer a session's active run, support Solid Control UI views, add worker-owned keyed state and conversation binding APIs, join service and account scheduling at retirement, complete awaited SQLite compatibility migration paths, and show calm notices for deprecated SDK usage. (#168893, #170146, #170152, #168408, #168478, #168483, #162669, #171443, #171752) Thanks @obviyus, @dwty11, and @joshavant.
- **ClawHub:** expose published ClawHub packages to the Gateway and accept portable manifest categories. (#171622, #171532) Thanks @Patrick-Erichsen.
- **Models and providers:** add Gemini 4 Argon as the default Gemini model with Gemini 3.8 Flash, replace Nemotron 3 Super with Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, add xAI Imagine Image 2.0 without silent image-model fallback, accept the Fish Audio Drama 3 preview, support endpoint-resolved custom model aliases, prefer a newer installed Codex for ChatGPT discovery, and prioritize shared private vLLM requests. (#171852, #172339, #172449, #172445, #170473, #170009, #168228, #129434) Thanks @nv-kasikritc, @jacobtomlinson, @JFLeonM, @xyrolle, @obviyus, @m888m, and @joshavant.
- **Muse Code:** run Meta models through the Muse Code CLI agent runtime, sign in to Muse Code from Model Setup and Provider Access, and run consented turns under a conversation tool policy. (#170487, #171526, #171790, #172361) Thanks @obviyus.
- **Usage and accounts:** show active auth subscription blocks, show Ollama cloud balance in status usage, add a ClawRouter sidebar dashboard for subscription pool headroom, show local provider processing with estimated wait time, and show every matched session in a paged usage overview. (#133087, #167474, #169514, #170041, #170369, #169660) Thanks @Leon-SK668, @vincentkoc, and @usimic.
- **Model recovery:** use model fallbacks after context-overflow recovery, compact ChatGPT sign-in sessions server-side, end runs after confirmed final source replies, and support typed OpenAI Decisions API evaluations. (#170141, #168401, #170653, #166320) Thanks @amirarenco-create, @obviyus, @RomneyDa, @sunlit-deng, @jjjhenriksen, and @Kimiyu-186.
- **Labs Advisor:** add an experimental Advisor that steers agents away from avoidable work. (#169564) Thanks @obviyus.
- **CLI progress:** show progress while tool input is generated. (#167789) Thanks @ZengWen-DT, @obviyus, and @umeranjum17.
- **Skills:** show a Learned notice row with one-press Undo, make background review channel notices opt-in, and save only repeatable procedures from background reviews. (#167996, #170025, #170277) Thanks @obviyus.
- **Clearer messages:** simplify wording across Settings, Gateway and security diagnostics, CLI and Doctor, agent and command execution, browser and approval help, provider, messaging, workspace, and memory plugins, and the macOS, iOS, Android, and Linux apps. (#168703, #168704, #168705, #168706, #168707, #168709, #168710, #168711, #168713, #168714, #168715, #168716) Thanks @RomneyDa, @synthalorian, and @obviyus.
- **Mobile and devices:** add Android system, photos, contacts, calendar, and motion capabilities, add an authenticated iOS background presence beacon, and support multiple Microsoft Teams bot accounts. (#29398, #73330, #112811) Thanks @obviyus and @jimmypuckett.
- **Worker placement:** require configured worker placement for sessions and allow keyless Gateway selection for worker-local inference. (#158903, #170132) Thanks @sallyom, @RomneyDa, and @obviyus.
- **Diagnostics:** export turn prompts and final answers on message and run spans, attribute GC metrics by kind and worker, measure allocated bytes per RPC and turn, attribute native CPU samples to JavaScript callers, capture main-thread stall stacks, and expose SQLite worker delay phases. (#156603, #171923, #172486, #171686, #170904, #169535, #170932, #171082, #171062) Thanks @ryan-dyer-sp, @vincentkoc, and @joshavant.
- **More:** expose wrapped browser observations to Code Mode, allow pausing automatic team-report collection, and add scoped startup migration backups. (#164833, #171840, #171764) Thanks @alkor2000, @potterdigital, and @vincentkoc.

### Fixes

- **Content boundaries:** keep internal runtime context, serialized tool-call XML, split tool-call markers, raw background command notices, runtime prompts, and legacy requester guidance out of replies and chat history, and stop models that print tool-call text from reporting false success. (#163471, #138204, #169172, #171898, #168236, #166080, #163521, #168943, #168928, #170799, #137273) Thanks @RomneyDa, @obviyus, @consoleaf, @JacquesLFR8, @ericcaiwx-star, @ruiling-smartbear, @JasonBuildAI, @Marvinthebored, @Peetiegonzalez, @rogeriochaves, @llmsommelier, @alkor2000, @Oldrich333, and @LiuwqGit.
- **Reply text:** keep trailing reply text after quoted closing tags, suppress punctuated and truncated silent placeholders, prevent thinking-only utility replies, and keep Ollama reasoning out of replies for manually configured models. (#149775, #168571, #170190, #169920, #169851, #171573) Thanks @bodapatisaikrishna, @liwenjie200543, @maliv2, @jacobtomlinson, @boeingchoco, and @vincentkoc.
- **Security and authority:** stop setup diagnostics repairing state without approval, reject project cache symlinks, bind Discord and Slack channel tool policy to resolved channel IDs, resolve Matrix room policy by room ID, never treat Tlon group DM authors as the owner, enforce exclusive Matrix crypto store ownership, separate exec approval ownership from node policy, isolate managed local provider auth, and align pairing setup with administrator scope. (#171960, #172079, #171829, #171828, #171645, #165801, #160707, #148612, #158108, #170988, #160982) Thanks @vincentkoc, @yetval, @eleqtrizit, @joshavant, @beenhero, and @ysumatta.
- **Private data:** stop logging inbound message content and spoken text, wait for explicit actions before reading Chrome data on macOS, honor ordinary permissions for voice requests, reject unknown WhatsApp login actions, disable unresolved hook ingress without blocking the Gateway, and reject oversized workspace document saves. (#170815, #170999, #171177, #159697, #158719, #165019, #171938) Thanks @brokemac79, @Alix-007, @mcaxtr, and @eleqtrizit.
- **State ownership:** keep secret, catalog, config, agent, plugin, backup, device, Memory, Matrix, and Workboard writes with the running Gateway, protect provider and MCP credentials from concurrent CLI writes, keep channel setup credentials out of config, and refuse local Claws, migration, and proxy writes while a Gateway owns the state. (#168108, #168135, #169732, #168417, #168757, #168466, #168471, #168457, #168586, #168419, #168459) Thanks @obviyus.
- **Restart recovery:** resume interrupted replies, aborted main turns, and requester-settle work after Gateway restarts, keep streamed answers when a restart aborts the run, settle replaced subagents and permanently rejected restart events, and resume sessions whose aborted run finished before recovery. (#172234, #172412, #170697, #170858, #170699, #171158, #170513, #172322, #171717, #169489, #170384, #172356, #172023, #170781) Thanks @jeanmonet.
- **Interrupted and queued input:** keep interrupted turns when new messages arrive, continue interrupted requests when asked, preserve queued work and inbound messages when preparation is cancelled or fails, let sends right after Stop succeed, stop Stop errors when a turn completes, and keep stopped Codex conversations ready. (#170647, #168279, #171718, #172080, #172421, #170542, #171656, #168906, #170652) Thanks @bitfroest.
- **Reply delivery:** preserve streamed answers across tools and reasoning, completed replies after invalidated reads, pending reply custody, follow-up errors and attachments, and committed CLI replies, stop outbound recovery from replaying sent replies, and avoid duplicate deferred tool results and false failure warnings after retries. (#169020, #169987, #170937, #170916, #170757, #99600, #169537, #170675, #170925, #172458, #151921, #165291, #101024, #169503, #169843) Thanks @VACInc, @elikampf, @zhangguiping-xydt, @TUARAN, @obviyus, @kseczhouyb, @Kimiyu-186, @shakkernerd, @amittell, @SunnyShu0925, @tiffanychum, @TheAngryPit, @CassieMei, @joshavant, and @vincentkoc.
- **Chat history:** keep delivered slash commands and Discord, Slack, and Mattermost native commands in history, return one history entry per user turn, keep channel messages when preflight compaction fails, show fallback and recovery in history, and keep visible failures out of later model requests. (#169026, #169200, #169236, #169255, #169434, #160462, #169773, #171327, #169369) Thanks @obviyus, @RomneyDa, @masatohoshino, @jacobtomlinson, and @joshavant.
- **ACP and CLI replies:** keep complete ACP answers after tool commentary, stop bound and long ACP turns losing replies, keep ACP follow-ups after a stopped turn, preserve the first acpx conversation after restart, keep rejected Claude CLI drafts out of final replies, and credit WebChat internal-sink sends as the source reply. (#168201, #168989, #171447, #170880, #170883, #166368, #168764, #167736, #168345, #168247) Thanks @ericcaiwx-star, @potterdigital, @fanmeng-felix, @alkor2000, @obviyus, @jhgaylor, @ruel225, @Oliver4Spot, and @Oldrich333.
- **Subagents:** wake parents when registry writes overlap, keep completion retries and recovered final replies, return visible child results to yielded guests, stop large completion batches overflowing the requester, keep stopped yielded tasks from restarting, and count and show waiting subagents accurately. (#163195, #169015, #171929, #171657, #171796, #172068, #169453, #167672, #168186, #169984, #169848, #155019, #164175, #171021, #150209, #172286, #171580) Thanks @ruel225, @Yolo521-bot, @fuller-stack-dev, @shakkernerd, @freeqaz-openai, @xydigitLybnnnn, @obviyus, @Oldrich333, @linhongyu510, @jerryliang122, @etzelm, @johan-eilertsen, @chelsealong, and @residentb2b.
- **Background work:** deliver background results to WebChat-only sessions, warn about dead-lettered deliveries, honor subagent concurrency for dreaming, cancel native descendants on session stop, release worker capacity after forced cleanup, keep child task custody for browser follow-ups, and stop agent deletion hanging on embedded runs. (#158067, #169932, #170273, #169700, #168746, #172017, #172511, #168199, #167368, #170855) Thanks @vincentkoc, @huyengiang101086-spec, @Yolo521-bot, @aniruddhaadak80, @obviyus, @jalehman, and @VACInc.
- **Shared and guest sessions:** let guest children start after parents yield, expose session publication in default sandboxes, let guests choose managed project worktrees and saved project choices, keep guest commands working during checkpoints, let guest readers open attachments, select an available checkout for new project sessions, and make saved web fetch output readable in sandboxes. (#171668, #171803, #171811, #171842, #172114, #172137, #172195, #172202, #172542, #172499, #168085) Thanks @shakkernerd.
- **Public conversations:** show complete public conversations with shared images and stop public-session chat reloads bouncing after deployment. (#169644, #171244) Thanks @VACInc.
- **Telegram replies:** redeliver saved final text after ambiguous network failures, avoid duplicate history replies, keep messages queued after handler timeouts, keep follow-up text behind photo albums, keep final replies linked after progress cards, honor first reply mode for message tools, prevent dropped replies on IPv4-first hosts, and stop retrying archived root-DM commands. (#168738, #169019, #169202, #170690, #171127, #171123, #171564, #171810, #169663, #166869) Thanks @obviyus, @diregoblin, @ooiuuii, @SanderHelgesen, @Dat1GUI, @dankarization, @VACInc, and @vincentkoc.
- **Telegram content:** keep dice rolls, shared contacts, voice durations, group voice mentions, tap timestamps, bare URLs, captions, and progress notes intact, and show native portraits in Home. (#137112, #144602, #142552, #163746, #170210, #171216, #171180, #171877, #171178, #168723, #168225, #168281, #168464, #170677, #171417, #166248) Thanks @adeepn, @obviyus, @JamesY023, @szafranski, @jewseppi, @maliv2, @zori7, @Irish-Joseph, @SanderHelgesen, @ruel225, @boeingchoco, and @vincentkoc.
- **Microsoft Teams:** paginate channel thread replies, include users in reactions, fix reactions on thread replies, keep DM progress rows separate, receive pasted DM images, and show fetched text in reads and searches. (#120824, #151128, #166582, #157704, #170437, #171153) Thanks @Linux2010, @obviyus, @qingminglong, @Leon-SK668, @ericcurtin, @yetval, @rdbartram, @RomneyDa, @EbulenConsult, and @ly85206559.
- **Discord, Slack, and Mattermost:** retry Discord edits, deletes, and pins after a lost response, keep consults and pending replies across voice changes, honor Slack silence for implicit thread follow-ups, render Slack control-sigil links and progress mentions safely, show Slack pinned messages, and render Mattermost agent buttons. (#169806, #171029, #172380, #164877, #168438, #169760, #171042, #168368) Thanks @ericcurtin, @obviyus, @ericcaiwx-star, @brainmonger, @shannon0430, @KhanCold, @yetval, @Takhoffman, @ooiuuii, @hannnnn-l, and @vincentkoc.
- **Other channels:** fix Feishu forwarded-message attribution, CardKit streaming fallback, monitor registration, and nested code fences; render Google Chat Markdown and deliver after truncated 404s; report LINE partial delivery; ignore IRC CTCP queries and report reconnecting accounts; fix Tlon reconnects, CRLF events, and nested code; stop Zalo polls; isolate Synology Chat accounts; and contain Matrix sync outages and stale room sends. (#150214, #152086, #169226, #171222, #141752, #168107, #100996, #168113, #171053, #169267, #170125, #171584, #169270, #144991, #62779, #163012) Thanks @chelsealong, @obviyus, @peach980, @kqtxmaster-boop, @Simon2256928, @ruel225, @junniar, @rudycelekli, @ericcaiwx-star, @pbreault, @ly85206559, @masatohoshino, @yetval, @ooiuuii, @zhangguiping-xydt, @Abhishek-B-R, @gumadeiras, @janstenpickle, and @vincentkoc.
- **Channel runtime:** keep hot restart working with disabled account credentials, report ingress claim refresh failures, keep progress titles within their line budget, keep ClickClack omissions on retries, stop thread replies misreading the current message, and fix WhatsApp audio actions. (#171734, #171365, #168312, #169509, #169817, #170889, #170500) Thanks @davidcittadini, @ynaamane, @obviyus, @Yolo521-bot, @yousan, and @SunnyShu0925.
- **X and A2A:** preserve X reply guidance and recover allowed mentions after authorization changes, recover mention profiles and background refresh, and stop A2A retried messages, task references, push errors, and queued host notices from stranding tasks or looping replies. (#169747, #171384, #170507, #170896, #167594, #167596, #170469, #172064) Thanks @obviyus, @clawSean, @rh7, and @Oldrich333.
- **Talk and speech:** keep macOS Talk replies from slow runs, fix iOS realtime Talk crashes and speaker output, preserve Anthropic Talk consult updates and custom Azure speech endpoints, honor configured speech in Control UI, keep speech-only and delayed speech replies, keep browser Gemini Live turns in history, and stop push-to-talk capture when the hold ends. (#164485, #168416, #171267, #151253, #170343, #170357, #171090, #171506, #143064, #137329, #171377, #167066, #170386, #166211) Thanks @PollyBot13, @rsaeks, @masatohoshino, @Takhoffman, @LiuwqGit, @marleyman5000-boop, @Leon-SK668, @obviyus, @mcfex, @mike-nott, @ericcurtin, @Twilight-Networks, @vincentkoc, @wangyan2026, @eiriktorheim, @jonathanlindsay, @hugenshen, @cursoragent, and @VACInc.
- **Media and attachments:** pass Whisper language hints, keep Windows-1252 accents, stop silent audio counting as a failure, avoid false busy-chat delivery warnings, stage WebChat images for file tools, let sandboxed agents reuse generated media, restore SSH sandbox reply attachments, and keep attachments through uncertain admission and steering. (#164841, #165771, #171514, #172637, #168537, #171058, #171079, #169710, #167369, #165105) Thanks @ooiuuii, @obviyus, @yetval, @masatohoshino, @Patrick-Erichsen, @synthalorian, @woohahahaaa, @adembektas, @valkyriweb, @vincentkoc, and @joshavant.
- **Claude CLI:** use Claude Code native models and names, keep context across account switches and model switches, restore thinking Off, keep utility work on Haiku, recover native login without a restart, stop sessions when the Gateway is killed, steer mid-turn messages into the running turn, and distinguish slow auth checks from logout. (#168728, #168781, #168726, #168965, #169657, #168603, #172471, #171016, #171969, #159816, #170604, #169670, #157766, #170627, #171723) Thanks @obviyus, @eliavb43, @RomneyDa, @kiranvk-2011, @Shagrat2, @VACInc, @potterdigital, @veritasaiflows-cell, @deepujain, @von8794, @chughtapan, @vincentkoc, and @joshavant.
- **Codex and ChatGPT:** run ChatGPT-listed models on the default Codex runtime, use ChatGPT routes for isolated completions, deliver plugin next-turn context on Codex, compact ChatGPT sessions before large context jumps, raise the GPT-6.1 Sol context default, renew expired ChatGPT sign-in before fallback, explain unavailable Codex sessions on paired devices, and unblock sessions after native child interruption. ### Highlights

## 2026.10.4

### Highlights

- The Gateway keeps running after the computer sleeps or the system clock jumps, instead of restarting itself because its ownership heartbeat looked stale. (#170790) Thanks @AnvinaLI, @sgh6688, @waynegault, and @RomneyDa.
- Gateway shutdown and restart no longer hang on a stalled transcript worker or in-flight session lifecycle events. (#170493, #170555) Thanks @Oldrich333.
- Tlon group DMs no longer treat other participants as the owner, closing an owner-impersonation path. (#165801) Thanks @eleqtrizit.
- Headless browser pages keep responding to clicks while a site waits for a passkey. (#170857) Thanks @trukhinyuri.
- Manual `/compact` settles the active run before compacting instead of aborting it and dropping the pending request. (#166163) Thanks @holny and @alexph-dev.

### Changes

- Stability patch for 2026.10.3 with no new features or configuration changes. Thanks @RomneyDa.

### Fixes

- Gateway: stays responsive during long reply-tagged streams, and long replies that quote tool-call XML no longer re-parse Markdown on every token. (#166782, #171573) Thanks @boeingchoco.
- Gateway: blocked durable context-engine turns are logged once instead of on every run. (#167595) Thanks @jalehman.
- Control UI: delayed application heartbeats no longer force a reconnect. (#171253)
- Gateway: recover state ownership after sleep and wall-clock changes, and allow `openclaw gateway restart` from verified external macOS terminals. (#170790, #170354) Thanks @AnvinaLI, @sgh6688, @waynegault, and @RomneyDa.
- Gateway: bound transcript-worker shutdown waits and wait for session lifecycle publication during shutdown. (#170493, #170555) Thanks @Oldrich333.
- Gateway: start enabled standalone plugin files with the Gateway, and keep worker heap limits enforced when the managed service sets a process-wide heap flag. (#171330, #166581) Thanks @holgergruenhagen, @valkyriweb, @xydigitLybnnnn, @goslingmanagment, @waynegault, and @obviyus.

- Updates: `openclaw update repair` turns no longer time out before running tools on slower hosts; nested authority checks reuse the current state snapshot instead of copying the database again. (#166847)

- Tailscale: an interrupted start stops its serve process, local access stays available when the tailnet denies Serve, and Doctor checks configured Tailscale startup prerequisites. (#167514, #171509, #166947) Thanks @pandysp and @RomneyDa.

releases.body:
This is a gateway-only `extended-stable` release, which is our current equivalent to LTS. This release is OpenClaw from the end of September 2026, plus critical security updates, reliability and performance fixes, and features like new model support. The latest version of OpenClaw at the time of this release is [2026.10.3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases#release-v2026.10.3)

## 2026.9.33

### Highlights

- **Safer September upgrades:** updates on the 2026.9 line keep state, plugin data, service ownership, and Windows state paths intact, and refuse automatic restore over unattributed Doctor writes. (#160167, #166755) Thanks @RomneyDa, @vyctorbrzezowski, @jalehman, @Alix-007, @jayzhou2309, @nitinjwadhawan, @SunnyShu0925, @obviyus, @vincentkoc, @taihartman, and @DonnieFi.
- **Updates that finish on pnpm, npm, and Windows:** pnpm 12 Gateway services and launchers survive native updates, retained updater runtimes no longer block npm recovery, and Windows updates no longer roll back after Doctor rechecks driver ancestry. (#170003, #170131, #170170, #169563) Thanks @xilopaint, @k-sekula, @Warhangel, @RomneyDa, @DonnieFi, @Takhoffman, @NianJiuZst, @masatohoshino, @obviyus, @ericcurtin, @jjjhenriksen, @sjf-oa, @ceckert, @jayzhou2309, @brokemac79, @Yolo521-bot, @mightyx, and @ajmtrz.
- **New model support:** run Meta Muse Wonder, use MiniMax M3.1 thinking effort levels, and stay signed in to MiniMax portal OAuth past token expiry. issues.title: CLI exits with UnicodeDecodeError at startup when the command line ends with a non-ASCII character (macOS; SPT_NOENV interaction with setproctitle)
issues.body:
## Summary

On macOS, every nanobot CLI invocation whose command line **ends with a non-ASCII character** (e.g. a CJK message passed to `nanobot agent -m "..."`) crashes at startup with `UnicodeDecodeError` before any model or network call. `--help` with a trailing CJK argument reproduces it. This hits Chinese/Japanese/Korean users on essentially every agent CLI call.

## Environment

- nanobot-ai 0.3.5 (current PyPI release), installed via `uv tool install nanobot-ai`
- setproctitle 1.3.8 (current release), Python 3.13, macOS 15 (arm64)

## Minimal reproduction

```bash
# crashes (isolated, unpatched environment):
uvx --isolated --from nanobot-ai nanobot --help 中文测试

# fine (ASCII-only argv):
uvx --isolated --from nanobot-ai nanobot --help
```

```text
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../nanobot/cli/process_identity.py", line 17, in _set_process_title
    from setproctitle import setproctitle
  File ".../setproctitle/__init__.py", line 57, in <module>
    getproctitle()
UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode bytes in position 153-154: unexpected end of data
```

## Root cause

1. `nanobot/cli/process_identity.py` unconditionally does `os.environ.setdefault("SPT_NOENV", "1")` before importing setproctitle. The intent (per the comment) is keeping titles out of `/proc/PID/environ` — a Linux-only concern.
2. On darwin, `SPT_NOENV=1` makes setproctitle use `PS_USE_CLOBBER_ARGV`, confining the title buffer exactly to the argv string area.
3. setproctitle ≤ 1.3.8 has an off-by-one there: `spt_strlcpy` writes the initial title (NUL-terminated) into a buffer of identical length and silently drops the **final byte** (dvarrazzo/py-setproctitle#167, fix PR dvarrazzo/py-setproctitle#169 still open).
4. If the command line ends with a multibyte UTF-8 character (CJK/emoji), the dropped byte truncates the sequence. On darwin only, setproctitle calls `getproctitle()` at import time (workaround for dvarrazzo/py-setproctitle#113), which decodes strictly → `UnicodeDecodeError` → the CLI never starts.

Verified experimentally on 0.3.5 / setproctitle 1.3.8 (macOS arm64):

| Scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| isolated unpatched install, ASCII-only argv | works |
| isolated unpatched install, argv ends with CJK | crashes at import |
| same, `SPT_NOENV` unset beforehand | works, title intact |
| argv with raw invalid UTF-8 bytes | crashes regardless of `SPT_NOENV` |
| Linux-equivalent truncation | last title byte silently lost (cosmetic; no crash — no import-time `getproctitle()`) |

## Proposed fix

`SPT_NOENV` is only meaningful on Linux; on macOS it provides no benefit and activates the truncation path. Limit it accordingly (keeps Linux behavior byte-for-byte identical):

```diff
--- a/nanobot/cli/process_identity.py
+++ b/nanobot/cli/process_identity.py
@@ -4,6 +4,7 @@
 
 import hashlib
 import os
+import sys
 from pathlib import Path
 from typing import Final
 
@@ -13,7 +14,15 @@
 def _set_process_title(title: str) -> None:
     # Process titles are short; do not trade Linux /proc environment visibility for
     # extra title storage. setproctitle reads this switch when it is imported.
-    os.environ.setdefault("SPT_NOENV", "1")
+    # SPT_NOENV only has an effect on Linux, where it keeps the title out of
+    # /proc/PID/environ. On macOS it confines the title buffer to the argv area,
+    # where setproctitle <= 1.3.8 drops the final byte of the title
+    # (dvarrazzo/py-setproctitle#167). A command line ending in a multibyte
+    # UTF-8 character (e.g. CJK) then contains a truncated sequence, and the
+    # darwin-only getproctitle() call at import time raises UnicodeDecodeError,
+    # crashing every CLI invocation.
+    if sys.platform == "linux":
+        os.environ.setdefault("SPT_NOENV", "1")
     from setproctitle import setproctitle
 
     setproctitle(title)
```

Optionally, hardening on top (process naming is cosmetic and should never be fatal):

```python
try:
    from setproctitle import setproctitle
    setproctitle(title)
except Exception:
    pass
```

## Workaround for affected users

Until fixed: launch with `SPT_NOENV=` set to an **empty** string (nanobot's `setdefault` preserves it, and setproctitle treats it as unset), or keep CLI arguments ASCII-only.

## Related

- dvarrazzo/py-setproctitle#167 — the upstream truncation bug
- dvarrazzo/py-setproctitle#169 — upstream fix PR (open; once released, `uv tool upgrade` picks it up automatically since nanobot doesn't pin the version)
- dvarrazzo/py-setproctitle#113 — why `getproctitle()` runs at import time on darwin

issues.title: Agnes AI (custom provider) double-encodes nested-object tool arguments as JSON strings
issues.body:
### Bug Description

When using Agnes AI (`apihub.agnes-ai.com/v1`, model `agnes-2.5-flash`, via `providers.custom`) as the model provider, any MCP tool call with a **nested-object parameter** fails with:

```
MCP error -32602: Input validation error: Invalid arguments for tool obsidian_get_note: Invalid input: expected object, received string at target
```

Root cause, confirmed by inspecting the raw session log (`workspace/sessions/*.jsonl`): Agnes emits the nested object as a **JSON-text string** instead of a real nested object. For example, calling `obsidian_get_note` (from `cyanheads/obsidian-mcp-server` via an MCP bridge), the actual `tool_calls[0].function.arguments` Agnes returned was:

```json
{"format": "content", "target": "{\"type\": \"path\", \"path\": \"Projects/nanobot.md\"}"}
```

`target` should be a real object (`{"type": "path", "path": "..."}`), but it arrives double-JSON-encoded as a string. The MCP server correctly rejects this per its schema.

This reproduces on **every** call to any tool with a nested-object parameter, 40+ consecutive attempts. Flat-parameter tools (e.g. `obsidian_list_notes`) succeed every time on the same connection — so this is isolated specifically to nested-object schema parameters, not a general MCP/transport failure.

**Isolated to Agnes, not a general nanobot bug:** I tested the identical call against two OpenRouter free-tier models to rule out nanobot's own tool-calling/dispatch layer:
- `openai/gpt-oss-20b:free` — different failure: the provider rejected the tool's schema outright (`"auto tool schema uses unsupported assertions or reserved metadata"`, likely the `oneOf` union on `target`).
- `nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free` — **worked correctly**. Raw log shows a genuine nested object: `{"target": {"type": "path", "path": "Projects/nanobot.md"}, "format": "content"}`, and the tool call succeeded with real content returned (verified against the file on disk).

This suggests nanobot correctly relays whatever the model emits — Agnes's function-calling output is what's malformed for nested-object schemas. Filing this as a bug against nanobot anyway since (a) it may be reproducible with other/related providers with similar function-calling limitations, and (b) a defensive repair on nanobot's side (similar to the fix already shipped for #1487's malformed-argument replay path) could make nanobot more robust against providers with this class of limitation, the same way #1487 already handles malformed `function.arguments` on history replay. Filing primarily as documentation for other Agnes AI users who hit the same wall, and to let the maintainers decide whether a defensive fix belongs here or is out of scope (upstream/Agnes-side only).

Related but distinct issues I checked first: #1487 (fixed a different code path — repairing malformed arguments on **history replay**, not the original construction) and #4864 (a different tool entirely — wrong tool name / XML-style call format confusion, unrelated to nested-object serialization).

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure nanobot with Agnes AI as the provider (`providers.custom` pointed at `apihub.agnes-ai.com/v1`, model `agnes-2.5-flash`) and any MCP server exposing a tool with a nested-object parameter (reproduced with `cyanheads/obsidian-mcp-server`'s `obsidian_get_note`, which takes `target: {type, path}` via a `oneOf` union).
2. Send a message forcing the model to call that tool, e.g.:
   ```
   nanobot agent -m "You MUST use ONLY the obsidian_get_note MCP tool to read the note at path 'some/note.md'. Do NOT use the file tool. If the tool call fails, report the EXACT error message verbatim and stop."
   ```
3. See error: `Invalid input: expected object, received string at target` on every attempt.

### Expected Behavior

The tool call should succeed with a genuine nested-object argument, as it does when using `nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free` via OpenRouter against the identical MCP server/tool/prompt.

### Relevant Logs

Malformed call (Agnes), from `workspace/sessions/<session>.jsonl`:
```json
{"role": "assistant", "content": "", "tool_calls": [{"id": "call_ed85de2e7e0b4008b8c28feb", "type": "function", "function": {"name": "mcp_obsidian_obsidian_get_note", "arguments": "{\"format\": \"content\", \"target\": \"{\\\"type\\\": \\\"path\\\", \\\"path\\\": \\\"Projects/nanobot.md\\\"}\"}"}}]}
```
```
MCP error -32602: Input validation error: Invalid arguments for tool obsidian_get_note: Invalid input: expected object, received string at target
```

Working call (OpenRouter/nemotron), same tool/prompt:
```json
{"role": "assistant", "content": "", "tool_calls": [{"id": "chatcmpl-tool-af190a63b0bff2d4", "type": "function", "function": {"name": "mcp_obsidian_obsidian_get_note", "arguments": "{\"target\": {\"type\": \"path\", \"path\": \"Projects/nanobot.md\"}, \"format\": \"content\"}"}}]}
```

### nanobot Version

0.3.0 (latest release, confirmed via `nanobot --version` and `pip index versions nanobot-ai`)

### Python Version

Other — 3.14.6 (`C:\Python314`) on PATH; nanobot itself installed as a standalone pipx-style binary, exact bundled interpreter version not independently confirmed.

### Operating System

Windows

### Channel / Platform

Other — reproduced via direct CLI (`nanobot agent -m "..."`), not through a chat channel.

### LLM Provider

Other — Agnes AI (`apihub.agnes-ai.com/v1`, model `agnes-2.5-flash`), configured via `providers.custom` (not a named provider preset).

### Configuration (Optional)

```json
{
  "providers": {
    "custom": {
      "apiBase": "https://apihub.agnes-ai.com/v1",
      "apiType": "auto"
    }
  },
  "modelPresets": {
    "agnes": {
      "provider": "custom",
      "model": "agnes-2.5-flash",
      "maxTokens": 4096,
      "contextWindowTokens": 65536,
      "temperature": 0.1
    }
  },
  "tools": {
    "mcpServers": {
      "obsidian": {
        "command": "jmunch-mcp",
        "args": ["--config", "obsidian.toml"]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Additional Context

Worked around locally by switching the default model preset to `nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free` via OpenRouter, with `agnes` kept as a `fallbackModels` entry rather than removed. This isn't a request to fix Agnes's own model behavior (out of nanobot's control) — filing so other Agnes users searching for this exact error message find it, and so maintainers can decide whether a defensive argument-repair (parallel to the #1487 fix, but for initial construction rather than history replay) is worth adding.

prs.title: fix(webui): preserve sidebar state after failed initial fetch
prs.body:
Fixes #6008.

## Summary

- Keep sidebar state read-only until a fetch or server push supplies saved state, instead of treating a failed fetch as an empty store.
- Retry failed reads every three seconds using the current token, cancelling retries on unmount and stopping further reads once a push supplies state.
- Ignore late initial-read success or failure after a server push so subsequent writes preserve the pushed state.
- Keep the sidebar list in its existing loading presentation until saved state is available.
- Leave the backend persistence format and successful-load behavior unchanged.

## Verification (initial fix)

- Reproduced the original hook sending a full-state write with empty saved collections after a rejected initial fetch.
- `NODE_OPTIONS=--no-experimental-webstorage npm test -- src/tests/useSidebarState.test.tsx src/tests/app-layout.test.tsx`: 87 passed on the final run. An earlier search-dialog timeout passed both individually and in the final full selection.
- `npm run lint` and `npm run build`: passed.
- Real isolated gateway and headless Chrome: blocked sidebar reads across retries left the state file byte-identical; restoring reads displayed the saved title. Toggling archived visibility then preserved pins, archived keys, title overrides, tags, and ordering in the actual state file. The browser harness stopped on an incorrect section-label locator after the click; the resulting file was checked separately and all five collections plus the changed view preference matched expectations.
- `git diff --check`: passed; reviewed the final four-file diff.

No live provider calls or existing user data were used. This does not change the broader concurrent-client/full-file-overwrite contract.

## CI follow-up (initial fix)

The initial WebUI CI run failed 13 temporary-chat navigation tests because their fetch fixture returned 404 for sidebar state when no grouped topics were configured. The fixture now returns a successfully loaded empty state in that case; the production read-only guard is unchanged.

- Serial targeted run covering temporary-chat navigation, sidebar state, and app layout: 112 passed.
- Lint and diff whitespace checks passed.
- The local full coverage run did not pass (2293 passed, 103 failed, including broad UI timeouts and rendering failures). This is not a claim of a green full suite; the updated commit needs CI verification.

## Push/initial-read race follow-up

- A server push now completes initialization. A late initial GET response or an already scheduled read retry cannot replace the pushed state.
- Added three regressions: push before a failed initial GET, push before a stale successful GET, and push before a scheduled retry. All three failed before this follow-up and pass afterward; the hook suite passes 5/5.
- `NODE_OPTIONS=--no-experimental-webstorage bun run test -- src/tests/useSidebarState.test.tsx src/tests/app-layout.test.tsx src/tests/temporary-chat-navigation.test.tsx --maxWorkers=1 --minWorkers=1`: 116 passed, 1 failed. The failure is `App layout enables task controls only when bootstrap advertises support: false` waiting for its initial textbox. The same test also failed before this change at `0b4e750ea7b5dc2104d8a99fd4b5dfdab55ef8cd` (113 passed, 1 failed); it is not included in a green-suite claim. The sidebar recovery integration test and all 25 temporary-chat navigation tests pass.
- `bun run lint`, `bun run build`, and `git diff --check`: passed. The build retains its existing chunk-size warning.
- Real isolated gateway and headless browser: a server push survives a delayed 503 and a delayed stale 200; pinning afterward preserves all saved sidebar fields through refresh. With no push, a failed first read leaves the list loading and sends no mutation; the automatic retry reads saved state, after which changing archived visibility persists without losing saved collections. Final API and on-disk state match, with no browser runtime errors.
- No live provider calls or existing user data were used. The isolated gateway and browser were cleaned up after verification.

This remains a focused initialization fix, not a change to the broader concurrent-client/full-file-overwrite contract. Final-head CI is reported separately from local verification.
