prs.title: fix(webui): resume queued prompts after turn completion
prs.body:
## Summary

Resume queued follow-ups when their waiting turn completes while the composer is unmounted or the browser is disconnected.

The composer previously relied on a mounted `isStreaming: true -> false` transition. Returning to a topic after background completion mounts it directly idle, so its persisted queue remains in **Waiting to send** even though the reply has finished.

- Persist the lifecycle turn each queued entry waits for, and require that turn's canonical completion before automatic submission.
- Send one entry at a time; remaining entries wait for the next actual lifecycle owner rather than reusing an earlier completion.
- Persist manual-only pauses after Stop or an observed send failure. The Stop button and slash palette share the pause path.
- Reuse ThreadShell's existing canonical completion normalization, including its constrained legacy-host handling.

## Dependency

**Stacked on #6211.** The base is `fix/webui-reconnect-reconciliation`, so this PR's diff contains only the queue fix. Merge #6211 first, then retarget this PR to `main`.

A controlled base/head comparison confirmed that the queue defect predates #6211: both snapshots leave the queued follow-up unsent. #6211 restores the completed reply and idle state after reconnect; this PR resumes the queue from that restored completion.

## Reproduction

1. Start a reply and queue two follow-ups.
2. Switch to another topic and disconnect the browser while the original turn completes.
3. Reconnect in the other topic, then return to the original topic.
4. The first follow-up should submit once; the second should wait for the next turn to complete. Repeat the disconnected-completion path for that next turn.
5. Stop a reply with a queued follow-up, navigate away, reconnect, and refresh. The stopped queue must remain manual until **Send now** is selected.

## Compatibility and scope

The existing localStorage array and key remain unchanged; waiting-turn and pause fields are optional. Identity-less legacy drafts do not auto-send merely because a topic mounts idle, and retain the existing live-completion behavior. No HTTP/WebSocket protocol or backend queue changes are included.

This does not change the pre-existing image-only automatic-drain behavior or asynchronous send-failure restoration after the composer has already unmounted.

## Verification

Checks cover the exact committed sources; source fingerprints were compared before commit.

- [x] `bun run test -- --maxWorkers=2 --minWorkers=2` — 2744 tests across 159 files.
- [x] Composer, ThreadShell, and reconnect focused tests — 271 tests across 3 files.
- [x] `bun run lint`, `bun run build`, `bun run check:imports`, `bun run test:imports`, and `git diff --check`.
- [x] Built WebUI through an isolated real gateway and Microsoft Edge, using an external OpenAI-compatible streaming fixture and byte-preserving network-outage relay.
- [x] Offline completion, topic isolation, two-entry FIFO, actual-owner handoff, Stop followed by navigation/reconnect/refresh, and manual retry.
- [x] Each queued submission generated exactly one model request; refresh did not duplicate sends. No uncaught browser errors or unexpected console errors beyond the intentional outages.
- [x] Verification gateway, browser, fixture, and relay cleaned up; owned processes and listening ports released.

prs.title: fix(webui): avoid blocking the gateway on skill loading
prs.body:
The WebUI fetches `/api/webui/skills` during startup. In an 81-skill workspace, generating this response rediscovered skills and fingerprinted the plugin package 163 times on the gateway event loop. Concurrent page and health requests stalled for about 25 seconds.

Build each skill list and detail payload within one `SkillsLoader.snapshot()`, and move payload construction to worker threads. Installation, enable/disable, and deletion responses use the same background list builder. Each request still verifies plugin packages and observes fresh metadata, while disabled-state updates stay on the gateway loop.

Validation:

- Python skill API, loader, plugin, and WebSocket HTTP suites: 173 passed, 2 skipped. New list/detail regressions fail before the fix and cover repeated package verification, metadata freshness, and concurrent HTTP responsiveness.
- Ruff on the four changed files; BasedPyright on both changed runtime modules; Python import boundaries; `git diff --check`.
- WebUI skill-marketplace and API tests: 77 passed; `bun run build` passed.
- Isolated real gateway with 81 skills, including 54 plugin skills: list requests completed in 156–172 ms while concurrent health requests completed in 1–26 ms. Playwright verified skill details, plugin instructions, disabling a skill across refresh, and re-enabling it, with no console errors. Verification runtime cleanup passed.

prs.title: fix(webui): don't persist sidebar state until initial load succeeds
prs.body:
Fixes #6008.

**Problem:** When the WebUI's initial `GET /api/webui/sidebar-state` request fails, `useSidebarState` silently falls back to `DEFAULT_SIDEBAR_STATE` and clears `loading`. Any sidebar mutation afterwards (pin, rename, archive, tag) — or the session-pruning effect — calls `update()` → `persist()`, which writes the degraded default back to the server. The backend write is a full-file overwrite with no field-level merge, so the user's previously saved sidebar state is wiped.

**Fix:**
- Accept sidebar mutations only after a successful state read or a server `onSidebarStateUpdate` push. Session pruning and workbench reconciliation also wait for known state.
- Show a localized error and **Retry** instead of editable defaults after a failed read. Manual Retry and WebSocket reconnect re-read the state, with one read in flight and no periodic retry loop. Normal editing and serialized persistence resume after recovery.
- Ignore late initial GET failures and older successful responses once a server push has supplied state.
- Use the backend's actual empty-state contract: missing saved state returns HTTP 200 with defaults. A failed read, including HTTP 404, does not authorize a full-state write.

**Verification:**
- 176 focused tests passed: sidebar hook/App (103), chat-list/sidebar behavior and focus (43), and localization (30).
- TypeScript/production WebUI build, focused ESLint on the five changed TS/TSX files, and WebUI import-boundary checks passed.
- Real isolated gateway and production-build browser checks passed for repeated read failure followed by manual Retry, and for recovery after an actual WebSocket disconnect/reconnect. Rename and Pin/Unpin persisted across refresh without losing saved pins, archives, titles, tags, order, or project overrides; API and on-disk state matched.
- Real server-push checks passed with a delayed initial 503 or stale 200, followed by Pin and refresh. The pushed state was preserved.

prs.title: fix(shell): separate wait, idle, and runtime limits
prs.body:
## Summary

Separate shell observation waits, output silence, and the hard execution budget so long-running work is not treated as stalled merely because a tool call stops waiting.

- Use one supervisor for inline and yielded commands. Enforce runtime/idle termination and owner cleanup without polling, and retain ownership while a worker still holds captured pipes after the root exits.
- Default to a one-hour hard runtime and a five-minute output-silence report. Silence is only a signal, not proof of stalled work; optional `idleAction: "terminate"` enforces a configured silence limit. Only received stdout/stderr bytes refresh the idle clock.
- Add canonical `maxRuntime`, `maxRuntimeLimit`, `idleTimeout`, and `idleAction` configuration. Align each tool instance's schema and runtime validation with its configured request limit (86400 seconds by default). This limit bounds explicit model requests, not trusted configuration defaults.
- Replace the raw Settings seconds input with localized duration presets, custom whole seconds, and an explicit **No time limit** choice. Show the configured maximum and reject over-limit input and paste without clamping; enforce the same bound on runtime edits in the backend while preserving longer trusted defaults when saving other settings.
- Preserve explicit legacy `timeout` as a hard-runtime alias, including trusted configuration `0` for unlimited runtime. Keep the existing Settings timeout control functional through canonical save/load, including legacy environment variables, while preserving configuration-source precedence and rejecting conflicting aliases within one source. Observation timeouts and cancelled observers do not stop or extend execution; creator/session cancellation still cleans up the owned process tree.
- At session capacity, evict the oldest completed result so cached output cannot block new `exec` or `rg` calls. Keep the existing total session limit and retain ownership of running or stopping executions.

No background-command panel, durable job system, or change to ordinary detached-service lifetime.

## Verification

- Current follow-up checks: **463 Python tests passed / 5 skipped**, plus **21 WebUI Settings tests passed**. Full Ruff and focused strict BasedPyright passed.
- Earlier follow-up regression checks: all nine added cases passed on WSL and native Windows. Related suites: WSL 558 passed / 6 skipped; native Windows 485 passed / 3 skipped. Full Ruff, focused strict BasedPyright, and import-boundary checks passed.
- **Earlier full-suite validation: 9604 Python tests passed locally**: 9384 in the Windows parallel partition, plus 220 serial CLI/process compatibility tests; 124 platform/optional skips.
- Earlier full Ruff, strict BasedPyright, and import-boundary checks passed.
- Real subprocess coverage includes unpolled silence, partial stdout/stderr bytes, fixed hard budgets despite output/repeated waits, owner isolation, creator versus observer cancellation, and early root exit with inherited pipes under both hard timeout and owner closure.
- Public tool-registry smoke passed with real PowerShell-launched processes.
- WebUI lint and production build passed. A real isolated browser check on the merged source verified over-limit rejection, the finite maximum, **No time limit** (`0`), and save/reload persistence, with no browser console warnings/errors. Verification runtimes and ports were cleaned up.

Three existing file-preview symlink cases could not run locally because this Windows account lacks symlink creation privileges (`WinError 1314`); full Linux/Windows CI remains required. Idle observation cannot see buffered or redirected file output. Shell sessions are not a service manager.

[NAN-245](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-245)

prs.title: fix(cli): reject misplaced gateway instance selectors
prs.body:
## Summary

Keep the documented gateway option scopes and reject misplaced instance selectors instead of silently ignoring them.

For gateway management, selectors belong after the subcommand:

```powershell
nanobot gateway stop --config C:\bots\custom\config.json
```

`nanobot gateway --config ... stop` now exits with a usage error (code 2), explains the required placement, and points to `nanobot gateway stop --help`. This prevents an incorrectly placed selector from silently targeting the default instance.

- Reject misplaced `--config` / `-c` and `--workspace` / `-w` before loading configuration or invoking a management action.
- Preserve foreground/background startup and the documented management syntax.
- Add no global selectors, parent-to-child inheritance, or new precedence rules.
- Clarify parameter placement in the CLI reference and cover both rejected placement and documented placement for `status`, `logs`, `stop`, `restart`, and `install-service`.

## Verification

Tested on Windows with Python 3.14.6:

- The five new misplaced-selector cases fail against the original implementation, which continues to the management action instead of reporting a usage error.
- `uv run --no-sync python -m pytest tests/cli tests/gateway tests/config tests/channels/test_channel_plugins.py tests/test_documentation_build.py -q -ra` — **973 passed, 32 platform-related skips**.
- `uv run --no-sync ruff check nanobot/cli/gateway.py tests/cli/test_gateway_commands.py` — passed.
- `uv run --no-sync basedpyright nanobot/cli/gateway.py` — 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- `uv run --no-sync python -m scripts.check_import_boundaries` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

Real CLI smoke verification used two isolated temporary gateways with fake provider credentials and no inference requests:

- Misplaced selectors on all five management commands returned exit 2 with placement guidance; both gateways retained their original PID and health.
- Equals-form config, attached short config, and workspace-only misplacement were also rejected.
- The suggested command-specific help listed the selectors; documented `status` and `logs` syntax selected the intended instance.
- Documented `stop --config ... --workspace ...` stopped only the selected gateway; the temporary default gateway remained healthy with the same PID.
- All temporary processes, ports, and runtime directories were cleaned up. No existing user gateway was stopped or restarted, and no OS service was installed.

prs.title: fix(providers): tighten tool calls and compatibility fallbacks
prs.body:
Assistant text containing `<tool_call>` markup could become an executable tool call, including quoted examples. Remove the plaintext extraction introduced in #4662 and require the API's structured tool-call fields, preserving the assistant text verbatim.

Responses and compaction errors also triggered compatibility fallbacks merely by mentioning a field name. For example, an invalid `max_output_tokens` value could switch protocols and eventually open the Responses circuit. Require an explicit unsupported-feature error, while honoring the API declarations from #5204. Apply the same classification to Codex HTTP and WebSocket compaction errors, and send `context_management` through SDK `extra_body` so older supported SDKs do not disable server compaction because of a missing Python keyword argument.

The existing image retry policy is retained, including switching to Chat with images when Responses explicitly rejects `input_image`. Required Codex compaction still fails the request if compaction cannot succeed. Provider and configuration docs describe these boundaries.

prs.title: refactor(session): centralize state ownership in SQLite
prs.body:
Session persistence currently shares mutable cached sessions across turn execution, metadata updates, and shutdown. This replaces JSONL as the authoritative store with SQLite transactions and routes runtime state operations through a bounded worker pool, keeping storage I/O off the event loop.

A title or goal update can commit while a turn is running without being overwritten by that turn. Reset and deletion revoke old drafts so late results cannot restore replaced state. Accepted writes settle before cancellation or shutdown returns.

## Changes

- Store messages, metadata, provider continuation state, checkpoints, and pending inputs in SQLite with WAL, foreign keys, and `synchronous=FULL`. Metadata and checkpoint updates do not rewrite message history.
- Return detached session views and use explicit operations for turn commits, recovery, imports, forks, delivery, and Dream cleanup. Query sidebar metadata directly instead of scanning JSONL files.
- Admit WebUI messages against the resolved execution session and its generation in separate and shared-session modes. Preserve temporary-session guards and roll back newly created admission sessions when dispatch fails.
- Check revisions before reusing owner-held history; submit changed message suffixes and keep metadata, checkpoint, and follow-up updates off the message table. Queue mutations through one FIFO writer; readers retain their own connections. Drain accepted operations and stop workers before closing their connections.
- Read detached headers for controls and task lists, and project a committed sidebar snapshot without waiting for every active turn. Discover display files once per query and reuse the metadata snapshot for visibility and workspace scope.
- Check idle-archive eligibility through the indexed message suffix before loading a transcript. Skip command and summary checkpoint messages; scanning already archived sessions does not load or copy their history.
- Serialize idle and explicit SDK compaction with turns through the same session lock. Preserve the admitted draft and its delivery route while resolving summaries.
- Bound prompt filesystem work, history snapshots, and local token estimation in background jobs. Reuse skill discovery within one prompt, preserve next-prompt updates, and skip unused run-hook history snapshots. Lifecycle snapshots run outside the prompt-preparation slot so cancellation does not wait for unfinished preparation. User hooks and runtime state changes remain on the owner loop.
- Drain the session worker on Windows Ctrl+Break and verify normal gateway exit before reopening its database in restart tests.
- When child-session admission is cancelled before its run starts, drain creation and remove the committed child before returning cancellation.
- Make SDK session operations asynchronous and remove deferred-save/flush behavior. Public interfaces intentionally change without compatibility wrappers; update SDK and CLI documentation accordingly.
- Import legacy JSONL once in a single transaction, reject malformed/conflicting sources, and commit completion with any pending workspace isolation. After commit, move workspace JSONL and checkpoints into private backups outside the workspace; external canonical originals and failed-import sources stay unchanged. Resume interrupted isolation before admitting conversations, without reimporting deleted sessions.
- Add ordered, transactional schema upgrades and explicit INSERT column lists. Preserve the v1 schema and reject newer databases before changing persistent settings.
- Keep JSONL support at the one-time import boundary and use SQLite backups for recovery. Remove the former `nanobot sessions restore-workspace` command; session-file export is deferred to a separate UI feature.

## Migration window

JSONL migration is introduced in **0.3.6**, supported through **0.4.x**, and removed in **0.5.0**. A version test requires removing the importer and startup hook at that boundary. Older installations must upgrade through the migration window.

This supersedes the persistence approach in #5580 and includes its event-loop fixes.

## Validation

Current head (`9d99a902f93867a97b244ea7ff4121f8412d8e81`, base `73c2441abc3a5806a6eeecb515a25639f8b09597`): candidate `771e4a1d3cb1` passed simplify, candidate review and fetched-head PR review. Fixed cancellation waiting behind unfinished token preparation, retaining detached hook data and callbacks on the owner loop. Local verification: 369 Python tests passed (3 skipped), 83 focused frontend tests passed, Ruff and import boundaries passed, BasedPyright reported no errors or warnings, and the production WebUI build passed. Public SDK checks covered atomic import validation, nested-data isolation, concurrent-reader durability, reset and restart. Built gateway + Chromium checks covered command replay, topic rename/refresh, and temporary-session isolation; runtime and browser cleanup passed. Exact-head CI: [Test Suite](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/38687901578).

Performance warning on this candidate: three controlled runs with 32 active conversations retaining 1,000 messages each, plus 500 archived conversations retaining 1,000 messages each, completed 960 turns without loss. Event-loop p99 was 44.43–56.02 ms (maximum 177.43 ms), command HTTP p99 was 6.99–9.54 ms, and full-turn p95 was 3.00–4.77 s. A separate 640-turn run with continuous 500-row sidebar and task-panel refreshes measured sidebar p95 48.61 ms and p99 115.56 ms, exceeding the 100 ms p99 target; task-panel p99 was 43.56 ms. The sidebar p99 has 210 samples and three tail observations. These runs used a simulated 200 ms model on this Windows host; concurrent browser frame rate and real provider/tool/network load were not measured. This is a current-candidate responsiveness check, not a new comparison against main.

## Earlier validation

Previous validation (`0b29f6243c1f6f7c31813b96c1f54f2f0808cd69`, based on `e8798ba6f`): autocompact and SDK coverage: 184 passed; combined session, WebUI admission, and subagent persistence selection: 189 passed. Ruff passed; BasedPyright over the 10 changed production modules reported 0 errors and 0 warnings. Import boundaries passed (10 rules, 158 files). Focused frontend tests: 99 passed; production build passed. Current-head CI: [run](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/38573993636).

Built gateway + Chromium verified ordinary message delivery in separate and shared-session modes against a localhost SSE provider stub, authenticated thread reads after refresh (HTTP 200), and shared history across two topics. All isolated gateway, browser, and provider-stub processes were cleaned up.

Previous head (`e8798ba6f`) is based on `4497f7ef2`. Idle scans check only messages at or beyond the persisted archive boundary using the existing `(session_key, position)` index, without adding fields or migrations. Regression coverage verifies that archived sessions and command/summary-only tails avoid full history reads, while subsequent ordinary messages still schedule archival. Focused session/autocompact/consolidator selection: 313 passed, 2 skipped; Ruff, BasedPyright (0 errors/0 warnings), import boundaries, and diff checks passed. All nine checks passed: [CI run](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/38537452357).

Idle-scan comparison against the preceding PR head `1d80fdc45`: three alternating paired processes per dataset, with TTL 15 minutes, three pure scans and three scans overlapping 32 active conversations (1,000 initial messages each, 10 turns each). Retain real AgentLoop, warmed token counting, provider retry/safety, SQLite usage recording, and 200 ms deterministic model waiting. Scans start every 5 seconds to exercise overlap (production default: 60 seconds). For 500 archived conversations ×1,000 messages, median pure scan: 3275.94 → 127.48 ms; overlapping scan: 7968.71 → 395.47 ms; complete-turn p95: 5513.83 → 2898.58 ms; event-loop p99: 138.40 → 42.26 ms. All three new processes met loop/command p95 ≤50 ms, p99 ≤100 ms, max ≤250 ms.

For 100 archived conversations ×10,000 messages, median pure scan: 3172.84 → 47.22 ms; complete-turn p95: 12644.80 → 4125.57 ms; event-loop p99: 469.90 → 63.97 ms. Every new process met loop/command p95/p99 limits, but one event-loop episode reached 260.97 ms, exceeding the 250 ms maximum. Across all 12 processes, 3,840 measured turns and usage records were checked; archived conversations retained their counts, archive boundaries, messages, and revisions, and no archive tasks were scheduled. The new implementation performed zero full archived-history reads or copies during measured scans, including command-only tails. These are previous-PR comparisons with idle scans enabled; they do not replace the earlier main comparison with compaction disabled or the separate 32 ×10,000 active-history stress results. Browser frames, sidebar refresh, and real model/tool/network load are excluded.

Previous head (`1d80fdc45`) is based on `4497f7ef2`. The latest commit removes the internal session-storage article and its references, keeps user upgrade/backup instructions in the CLI reference, and removes manual prose wrapping. Existing CI tests enforce storage compatibility, transactional upgrades, bounded admission, ordering, and shutdown drain. Focused storage/state/documentation-build selection: 69 passed; local links and diff checks passed. Production code and tests are unchanged from `34e72793e`, whose nine checks passed: [CI run](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/38505935250).

Earlier code verification (`414f707df`, based on `328e933d3`): Local regression selection: 4,651 passed, 21 skipped under the CI environment without external Langfuse tracing; Ruff, BasedPyright (0 errors/0 warnings), import boundaries, and diff checks passed. All nine current-head checks passed: [CI run](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/38393563059). Built gateway + Chromium verified `/help` delivery, refresh replay, stable sidebar handles, authenticated thread/task reads, and invalid-token rejection. The isolated gateway/browser were cleaned up.

Concurrency comparison against the previous PR head `f782b5485`: three alternating paired runs at 32 active conversations with 1,000 initial messages and 500 sidebar sessions. Keep real warmed token counting, provider retry/stream handling, SQLite usage recording, and 200 ms deterministic model waiting. Median complete-turn p95: 10,981.57 → 2,877.71 ms; throughput: 3.28 → 13.55 turns/s. Median event-loop p99: 3,724.95 → 32.50 ms; independent TCP command p99: 3,378.98 → 8.20 ms. Every measured turn and usage record was checked.

Three subsequent 30-turn-per-conversation runs (2,880 turns total) passed the predefined responsiveness limits: event-loop and command p95 ≤50 ms, p99 ≤100 ms, max ≤250 ms; sidebar/task-panel p95 ≤50 ms and p99 ≤100 ms. Command p99 ranged 7.26–7.98 ms, event-loop p99 43.56–48.41 ms, and sidebar p99 54.98–99.83 ms. The sidebar/task-panel p99 populations are sparse, and one short paired run had sidebar p95 80.88 ms; do not interpret this as a guarantee against every transient.

Stress boundary: 32 conversations retaining all 10,000 messages, with automatic compaction excluded, did **not** meet the same limits. Event-loop p99 was 166.51 ms; sidebar p99 391.79 ms and max 678.64 ms. This is a moderate remaining risk for large histories under continuous heavy concurrency. The verified envelope is 32 ×1,000 on this Windows / NTFS / 16 logical CPU host. Real model/network/tool load and concurrent browser frame rate are outside this controlled test. Earlier benchmark entries below retain their original identities.

Previous rebase (`f782b5485`): rebased onto `328e933d3`, migrated the asynchronous recovery coordinator to `nanobot/webui/recovery.py`, and kept main's generic session recovery and import boundaries. Removed `.agent/session-state-refactor.md`. The measured storage/cache/core execution files remain byte-for-byte identical to `1350196da`; performance evidence retains that original commit identity and excludes startup/import costs. Local verification: 390 focused architecture/config/session/SDK/agent/WebUI tests passed (2 skipped); 161 serial CLI and real gateway restart tests passed (1 skipped). Python import boundaries, Ruff, BasedPyright, and diff checks passed. All nine current-head CI checks passed: [CI run](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/38357212464).

Previous CI (`1350196da`): all nine checks passed on that head: [CI run](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/38344200639). Limit the Windows full suite to two pytest workers to bound concurrent storage work; preserve Linux auto concurrency and the existing serial CLI/native-process test routing. Windows full suite: 9,221 passed, 115 skipped in 434.90 seconds; serial CLI tests: 160 passed, 1 skipped. Workflow parsing/routing and diff checks passed.

Scope update (`7c8b83bbd`): removed JSONL file export and its CLI/API/documentation surface. Legacy child-session migration now uses independent JSONL input records. Local verification: 221 session, SDK, collision, and subagent tests passed (2 skipped); 160 serial CLI tests passed (1 skipped). Ruff, BasedPyright, and diff checks passed. These local results remain applicable because the subsequent change only adjusts CI concurrency. Earlier validation entries retain their original commit identities.

Local verification: 92 lifecycle/activity tests passed serially and with four xdist workers, and 57 Windows process/handoff tests passed; the two readiness regressions passed again after cleanup changes. prs.title: feat(update): integrate managed installs and recoverable in-app updates
prs.body:
## Summary

Connect managed installation, exact-version updates, recovery and the WebUI into one flow. This continues chengyongru's updater work in #5817 and the prepare-only candidate pipeline from #6154. Their commits and attribution remain intact. The maintainer closed #5817 as a duplicate; coordinate #6154 before merging.

Normal users receive prebuilt WebUI and native TUI packages. They do not need Bun to build the interface. This PR does not publish a release or enable daily publication.

## In-app installation-owner guidance (b87def6e5)

- Update entries name the detected owner. The existing dialog shows the gateway machine/environment, stop-and-backup steps, applicable copyable commands, original-launcher restart, and an authenticated **running gateway** version check. Documentation is secondary.
- Commands bind the uv/pipx root or exact interpreter, retain pipx suffixes and respect recorded constraints. Unrecorded-venv inspection uses Python's standard-library metadata, without requiring pip to be installed. Unknown extras, pins/locks/fixed sources, unconfirmed manager layouts and GitHub-only Preview targets do not receive guessed registry upgrades. Source/container/system deployments keep their own workflow and data volumes. Display/copy never executes an installer.
- A target already installed on disk but not running gets restart-only guidance. Copy failures, check-in-progress, version mismatches and reconnect failures have feedback; host/token changes discard stale verification. Reuses existing button, textarea, disclosure and dialog CSS; closes remain reachable on narrow screens. All 10 locales updated.
- Verification: **152 Python tests + 101 frontend tests pass**; focused basedpyright, Ruff, ESLint, import boundaries and production build pass. Real browser component-fixture checks cover light/dark, 390px viewport, disclosure, checking/mismatch feedback and focus return. This does not claim a new real package upgrade/native Windows E2E run. Current-head [GitHub CI](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/38781693199) is pending/in progress, not yet claimed green. Earlier green evidence below remains scoped to its recorded heads.
- No expansion of inline-install/recovery ownership, no changes to user configuration/chat data, no merge/publication. Protocol additions are optional; legacy check payload and older-host fallback remain supported.

## User flow and installation ownership

The sidebar update entry and Settings → About use one shared confirmation and saved-job view. The gateway selects an exact verified target, stages its files, obtains stop/install/restart consent, waits for idle reviewed gateways, installs offline and verifies the restarted runtime. Refresh, reconnect and duplicate requests read the same job; they do not authorize another installation. Completion requires the reconnected gateway to report the target version.

| Installation | Update and recovery route |
| --- | --- |
| Fresh official installer | Dedicated environment, explicit package-selection receipt and persistent gateway. Inline update with bounded automatic service recovery for eligible layouts. Interrupted first installs retain their owner for retry. |
| Verified POSIX uv 0.11.16 registry tool | Inline update preserves the uv receipt, extras, constraints and additional packages. Keeps its saved-job/original-launcher recovery route; it is not converted into a managed install. |
| Other uv, pipx, ordinary pip venv, Docker, service or Desktop | Version checks and owner-specific instructions. No silent adoption, pip replacement of another manager's files, or invented extras. |
| CLI/source | Existing `update`, `--check` and opt-in `--dev` remain available with their original restrictions. Source checkouts preserve their branch and refuse dirty/divergent states. Source is not the Preview channel. |

Only affected background gateways restart, not the user's computer. Stopped profiles are not started. Active tasks and other writers block shutdown. Remote mutations require the existing explicit package-install permission. Native Desktop installations retain the distributor's updater.

## Stable and Preview

**Receive preview updates** is visible, off by default, and installation-scoped. There is no separate update mode or hidden settings section. Saving the preference never grants installation consent.

- Stable → Preview offers a newer compatible candidate. Preview → next Preview or final also requires a newer compatible version. Installing a final does not unsubscribe from Preview.
- Turning Preview off never downgrades. If the final release is older, keep the installed Preview and wait. A verified newer final remains available if the Preview index is unavailable.
- Withdrawal remains visible when a replacement is missing, older or incompatible. Offline, partial and unsupported releases cannot produce false success.
- Revision checks reject stale tabs and invalidate reviewed plans after a channel change. Inactive staged work is settled through ownership checks; active/admitted work must finish or recover first.
- Stable discovery uses the complete PyPI wheel/sdist set. Preview uses the protected official catalogue and immutable manifests. Exact-target revalidation, approved HTTPS hosts, pinned DNS, hashes, size limits and catalogue history checks remain enforced.

Stable fixes can ship between monthly feature releases. The documented daily Preview policy publishes only eligible changed source after release checks; users may skip intermediate builds. The PR does not activate a cron or public feed.

## Failure recovery and compatibility

Eligible managed installs keep a verified copy of the original program and dependencies before mutation. An independent frozen supervisor can retry the same admitted target once. If it cannot complete before activation, it can restore the original program and restart the reviewed gateways **only when protected user data is unchanged**. Journaled renames handle an interrupted program switch. The UI reports **Previous version restored**, not update success.

Recovery never restores old configuration or chats over current data. Activated or data-changing candidates cannot be downgraded automatically. Missing base Python, corrupt backups, persistent storage/ownership failures or loss of both recovery processes can still require an operator. There is no OS boot-time recovery service or zero-failure guarantee. The frozen stdlib recovery launcher remains available outside a broken application environment.

Fresh official installs intentionally change to managed/persistent defaults. Existing installation owners, data locations, chat/config formats and core WebUI protocol 1 remain unchanged. Older saved jobs retain their frozen/manual recovery behavior. Optional capabilities and additive status fields do not authorize old clients to mutate unsupported hosts.

## Behavior-preserving simplification

This pass removes redundancy without reducing current product flows or uv support:

- Remove the unused, unreleased prototype WebUI updater: its unmounted component, separate in-memory task, routes/capability, translations and component-only tests. It was introduced within this PR, not on main. The current saved-job flow and CLI source updater remain. Correct documentation that still described the abandoned panel.
- Give job state one transition writer and worker mutation leases one acquisition helper. Keep every existing check at its original boundary, acquisition order, child-process lifetime and durable format.
- Share the reviewed-gateway restart predicate between eligibility and execution. Remove pass-through service methods, retaining distinct execute/retry authorization at the routes.
- Share bounded redirect traversal while keeping metadata and artifact host allowlists separate. Keep checksum, staging and partial-file cleanup behavior.

The second pass (`a02db53d3`) also reuses the existing cancellation-drain helper, gives `ProfileReceipt` one runtime/data-path projection for observation, backup and restart, and replaces the CLI updater's duplicate identity, marker path and second lock with the shared installation owner. The exact pending-marker/source locations, stored schemas and all lifecycle guards remain unchanged. Runtime-reader and competing-updater coverage is retained through the same installation-lease contract.

The two refactors remove **568 net lines** (521 then 53, plus six lines to make a deadline regression deterministic), without adding modules or dependencies. The PR changes 164 files versus 168 before simplification. This is not a claim that the remaining PR is small. The retained recovery, multi-process coordination and platform tests protect supported behavior. Independent installer bootstraps and frozen-worker boundaries are deliberately not collapsed. Removed code remains recoverable in Git history.

## Verification

- First-pass regression evidence: **191 backend tests** for worker/restart/stop/backup/channel/plan contracts; **170 backend tests** for CLI, uv, release feed, authorization, compatibility and update routes. These groups overlap and are not summed. The final annotation correction also passed all 26 feed tests.
- Second-pass local checks: **379 tests passed** across CLI updates/installation leases/backup/channels/plans/job routes (123), native worker/profile/restart/stop/uv behavior (125), prompt/skills and client/settings compatibility (111), and the merged shell-output filter/update maintenance (20). After merging the latest base, another **58-test run** passed for process identity, skills and actual gateway profiles (overlapping coverage, not added to 379). Ruff, strict changed-module Python types and import boundaries passed.
- **62 frontend tests** pass for the current update/recovery flow, notices, channels and About. Production TypeScript/Vite build, WebUI lint, Python/client import boundaries, Ruff and strict changed-file Python types pass.
- **Seven fresh private packaged macOS arm64 journeys passed after both refactors**: healthy update, candidate import failure, restart-module failure, backup refusal after shutdown, abrupt worker exit, missing package metadata and interrupted restoration reservation. Each verifies the actual running gateway, unchanged configuration/existing chat bytes, authenticated history read, a new WebSocket turn and a second normal start. Transport and fault points are controlled; installation, stop/restart, auth and stores are real. The wheel contains `a02db53d3`; subsequent base-only output-filter, skill-description and process-title environment changes do not alter updater/recovery logic. Their output/maintenance, identity and real gateway profile regressions passed separately.
- Windows full-suite CI on `d7988246a` exposed an artificial two-second retry deadline in a stop-protocol test (9662 passed, one failed). A delayed-write probe reproduced the same failure. `af985141e` reuses the existing controlled clock, expires only after an actual admission hold, and preserves abort/release/no-stop/retry assertions with real-time watchdogs. The delayed-write probe and **43 related tests** pass. Production timeouts and protocol are unchanged; no tests were disabled to obtain a passing result. Current-head [CI run 38771669823](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/38771669823) **passed all nine checks**, including both Windows Python jobs and both native package checks.
- Fresh Linux/Windows package reports identify test merge `3ce6dd248`, with API-verified parents `9d2762a4f` (main) and current head `af985141e`. Both installed native wheels, served 377 bundled assets, ran native TUI without downloads and started a ready gateway without frontend build tools. Linux shutdown was graceful; Windows probe cleanup terminated the process. This is native package/startup evidence, not all-platform interactive update E2E.

The daily installation, configuration and chats were not modified. The disposable acceptance gateways were stopped and their listeners checked closed. Detailed behavior and operator instructions are in [updating.md](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/af985141e/docs/updating.md), [cli-reference.md](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/af985141e/docs/cli-reference.md) and [releasing.md](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/af985141e/docs/releasing.md).

## Release gates — not performed by this PR

- [ ] Maintainer review/approval and merge; coordinate #6154.
- [ ] Select actual stable/Preview versions. Existing users install the first updater-enabled version through their existing owner.
- [ ] Confirm the distributor can honor the three-year corresponding-source/relinking offer in `tui/SOURCE_OFFER.md`; check pinned notices and sources.
- [ ] Build final candidates from reviewed source: five platform wheels, sdist, matching native archives, checksums and provenance. Complete packaged upgrade/recovery acceptance on supported platforms; distinguish native execution from cross-builds.
- [ ] Approve GitHub/PyPI publication and protected release-index ownership. Verify all referenced assets before advancing the catalogue, including final releases for Preview subscribers. Test clean public installation and updating before announcing availability.

No approval, merge, release, tag, PyPI upload, public Preview catalogue or daily schedule has been performed/enabled. **Verify Release Candidate** remains manual and prepare-only. Routine PR checks retain small reports; candidate retention is an explicit bounded storage option. No paid macOS runner is added.

prs.title: fix(webui): distinguish unreadable sidebar state from a fresh install so updates can't wipe real data
prs.body:
Follow-up to #6008, implementing the minimal fix sketched in [this analysis comment](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/issues/6008#issuecomment-5986203909): the client-side-only proposal leaves the hole open where the GET handler serves silent defaults for a corrupt/oversized/unreadable file, so this closes both sides.

## Server

`load_webui_sidebar_state()` returns `(None, "missing")` for an absent file and `(None, reason)` with a machine-readable reason (`"corrupt"` / `"oversized"` / `"unreadable"`) when the file exists but cannot be served, instead of collapsing every failure into defaults. The GET handler maps these to **404** and **409**. A corrupt file (invalid UTF-8 included) is quarantined as `sidebar-state.json.corrupt-<ts>` so the original bytes stay inspectable instead of being silently replaced by the next write. `read_webui_sidebar_state()` is unchanged for existing callers (gateway heartbeat keeps its current semantics).

## Client

`loadSidebarState()` maps the new responses. The hook renders defaults but **blocks `update`/prune persistence until a load succeeds**, retries on reconnect, and surfaces a banner in the sidebar (10 locales). A missing file (404) is treated as a fresh install and stays writable.

## Compatibility (per .agent/review-guide.md)

- **Current client / current host**: covered by new route- and unit-level tests.
- **Oldest client / current host**: treats 404/409 as a fetch failure and falls back to defaults exactly as before — no regression — and a quarantined file can no longer be destroyed by their default write (strictly better).
- **Current client / oldest host**: old hosts always return 200, so the client takes the loaded path, unchanged.
- No protocol/capability changes.

## Behavior notes

- While the banner is up, persistence stays blocked until the next reconnect triggers a successful reload (intentional fail-safe, not a transient warning).
- The WS `set_sidebar_state` write path does not quarantine; with the new client flow the GET has already quarantined before any write can happen.

## Docs

`docs/webui.md` sidebar section notes the new notice and the quarantine filename.

## Tests

- Backend: 5 new unit tests (four read outcomes + quarantine of non-UTF-8 bytes), 1 new route-level test (corrupt → 409 + quarantine assertion), and the existing route test updated to expect 404 for a fresh config dir (the behavior change itself). Full affected files: 129 passed.
- Frontend: 2 new tests — 404 keeps persistence enabled; 409 blocks `setSidebarState` until a reconnect reload succeeds, then persists exactly once. Full affected file: 3 passed.
- Known unrelated: `src/tests/remote-instances.test.tsx` has one failing test on clean `main` (verified by stashing this change); not touched here.

Fixes #6008

prs.title: feat(provider): langfuse tracing for codex
prs.body:
Summary

- Codex had no Langfuse tracing because its custom OAuth transport does not use the OpenAI-compatible SDK wrapper. Adds tracing through Langfuse's native SDK with model, input, output, usage, and error information.
- Traces main and native compaction requests separately over WebSocket or HTTP. Rejected compaction responses are recorded as errors, with validation shared by the Codex provider and Responses backend.
- Upgrades the optional Langfuse dependency to `>=4.7.0,<5.0.0` and uses `start_observation(as_type="generation")`. Enables real-time ingestion on Langfuse v4 without custom OTLP headers. Supports Langfuse Cloud and self-hosted Langfuse 3.63.0 or later.
- Keeps tracing failures from affecting Codex responses and closes each generation once when its request exits, including cancellation.
- Maps Codex usage to Langfuse's exclusive input, output, and cache buckets so cache reads/writes do not inflate totals and standard pricing can match the usage fields.

Testing

- 304 focused provider, Responses backend/state, context-pressure, and optional-dependency metadata regressions passed with Langfuse SDK 4.18.0.
- Real SDK WebSocket and HTTP fallback export tests verify completed generations, model/output, cache usage, and SDK identification headers. Both cases also passed with the minimum supported SDK 4.7.0.
- OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions and Responses APIs: 4 real SDK checks passed, covering streaming and non-streaming calls against local API and OTLP peers.
- Langfuse Cloud verification with SDK 4.18.0 and no custom OTLP headers passed: the Observations v2 API returned the generation with input/output and usage within 12 seconds.
- Ruff, focused BasedPyright, and import-boundary checks passed.
- Live deployment verification reported by the PR author.

prs.title: fix(cli): set SPT_NOENV only on Linux
prs.body:
Fixes #6231.

`_set_process_title` set `SPT_NOENV=1` on every platform before it imported setproctitle. The switch keeps the title out of `/proc/PID/environ`, which only matters on Linux. On macOS, the switch confines the title buffer to the argv area, where setproctitle (<= 1.3.8) drops the last byte. If the command line ends in a multibyte UTF-8 character, such as `nanobot agent -m "中文"`, the darwin-only `getproctitle()` call that setproctitle makes at import time then raises `UnicodeDecodeError`. The CLI crashes before doing anything.

`SPT_NOENV` is now set only when `sys.platform == "linux"`, so Linux behavior is unchanged. This is the fix proposed in the issue. I didn't add the optional `try/except` around the import that the issue also suggests: with this change the reported path no longer fails, and a blanket fallback would hide other errors.

Validation:

- `tests/cli/test_process_identity.py::test_process_title_keeps_environment_only_on_linux`: with setproctitle stubbed, `_set_process_title` sets `SPT_NOENV=1` on `linux` and leaves it unset on `darwin`. Both cases still set the title. The `darwin` case fails before this change.
- `python -m pytest tests/cli -q`: 650 passed, 28 skipped. This is on Windows, so the actual macOS crash isn't reproduced here. The test covers the environment switch that triggers it.
- Ruff check on both touched files, `python -m scripts.check_import_boundaries` and `git diff --check` passed. `ruff format` wasn't run, per `AGENTS.md`.

prs.title: fix(agent): route direct subagent results in-turn
prs.body:
## Summary

- route direct-mode subagent completions into the active turn's pending queue instead of relying on the global bus consumer
- preserve structured subagent result content for MapReduce-style reductions
- keep `long_task` scoped to sustained cross-turn work so current-turn spawn/review tasks do not get converted into a goal loop
- make MapReduce output guidance conditional in the subagent system prompt

## Why

Real CLI/direct-mode A/B runs showed that subagents could be spawned, but their completion messages did not reliably reach the parent turn. The parent then either waited, produced a status-only answer, or fell back to direct file reads. A later DS Flash run also showed the model could misuse `long_task` for a current-turn spawn review, causing a wait loop.

## Validation

- `python -m ruff check nanobot/agent/tools/long_task.py nanobot/agent/subagent.py nanobot/agent/loop.py tests/agent/tools/test_subagent_tools.py`
- `python -m pytest tests/agent/tools/test_subagent_tools.py -q` (`12 passed`)
- Real DS Flash A/B run `exp/runs/dsflash-r5` with `maxConcurrentSubagents=3`:
  - control exits: A/B/C all `0`, total `102.74s`, but B/C produced status-only waiting responses rather than final reductions
  - treatment exits: A/B/C all `0`, total `338.18s`, with final synthesis for A/B/C and structured subagent-result evidence preserved

## Notes

This remains a draft because the experiment is LLM-dependent and single-run evidence is not statistically significant. The treatment looks qualitatively stronger on merge quality, but slower.

prs.title: fix(webui): support WSL browser launch and clearer startup output
prs.body:
In WSL, opening WebUI could fall through to a Linux browser launcher that cannot reach the Windows desktop. The launcher now opens the Windows default browser through the inbox Windows PowerShell, while respecting an explicit `BROWSER` setting and `--no-open`. The existing authenticated launch URL travels through stdin and a private temporary redirect file, keeping credentials out of process arguments. The helper owns file cleanup independently of the calling CLI.

On Unix, browser selection retains the standard library's `BROWSER`-first order and continues with registered platform defaults when a selected launcher is missing or exits unsuccessfully. Generic launcher output remains suppressed.

Startup output now groups readiness, the complete copyable login link, model setup guidance, config, logs, and exit controls with blank lines and distinct colors. A fresh installation gets one setup confirmation and a direct **Settings → Models** next step without an unexplained default model error. Gateway warnings and errors remain visible; routine logs and the Vite banner no longer crowd the startup summary. Browser-launch failure points to the printed link. The launcher shares one lease and dev-server cleanup flow for new and existing gateways, preserving external gateway ownership.

This PR is limited to WSL browser opening and startup output. WebUI pages, authentication policy, password generation, network-access configuration, and TUI code match the PR base. No access toggle, password-setting flow, or password-policy change is included.

Related to [NAN-238](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-238).

Earlier validation (`ed4865ac5`; Windows handoff and gateway lifecycle source is unchanged by the follow-up):

- Python CLI, browser handoff, and dev-server checks: 250 passed; one native Windows Python ACL check skipped under Linux. The Windows PowerShell ACL, sharing, and cleanup checks ran through WSL. Existing gateway ownership is covered across ordinary/dev and open/no-open modes.
- Real isolated CLI runs covered ordinary, `--dev`, `--no-open`, and dev + no-open. Ordinary and dev opened the actual Windows default browser and reached the authenticated workbench; no-open modes created no browser tab. Startup output was checked at 48 columns for complete links, spacing, colors, and setup guidance.
- Real managed and external gateway reuse covered ordinary and dev modes. Closing the launcher left the existing gateway running, preserved its config, and released the dev port. Synthetic warning/error log entries remained visible with their detail and colors.
- A separate Windows headless Chrome session exercised the built WebUI through a real WSL gateway, opened settings, and restored the settings page after refresh without page errors. 96 existing WebUI bootstrap/layout tests passed.
- Ruff, full basedpyright, WebUI lint, production typecheck/build, and `git diff --check` passed. Test gateways, temporary configurations, browser sessions, and ports were cleaned up. [Current PR checks](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/pull/6150/checks).

Validation for the browser fallback fix (`ed84fc553`):

- 142 focused Python checks passed on native Windows. Under each of CPython 3.11 and 3.14 in WSL, 104 passed and the native Windows Python ACL check was skipped; that check passed on Windows. Cold-registration probes with real subprocesses covered missing/failing `BROWSER` commands and platform defaults, preserving the complete URL.
- 96 WebUI bootstrap/layout tests and the production typecheck/build passed. A real local gateway and Windows headless Chrome verified the workbench, **Settings → Models**, and refresh persistence with no page or console errors. Ruff, strict touched-file BasedPyright, and `git diff --check` passed; the verification gateway, browser session, and ports were cleaned up.

Windows desktop evidence is from WSL with the Windows default browser and a separate Windows headless Chrome session. Standalone Windows Python and macOS desktop launches were not rerun locally. The first dev-browser observation timed out at 20 seconds; the unchanged code passed a second run with a 40-second observation window.

prs.title: fix(webui): give media gallery components distinct examples
prs.body:
## Problem and change

The ImageGallery, ImageLightbox, ZoomableImage and AttachmentTile source entries all opened the same combined media preview, making distinct components appear duplicated. Give each source path its own interactive example and English/Chinese description and usage guidance:

- ImageGallery: large and compact thumbnail layouts, selection and overflow across six images.
- ImageLightbox: controlled opening/closing and three-image full-screen navigation.
- ZoomableImage: a standalone positioned viewport for existing zoom and pan gestures.
- AttachmentTile: image viewing, playable video, file download and unavailable image/video/file tiles, without assuming why an attachment is unavailable.

Reuse the production components and their existing composition unchanged. Numbered SVG data URLs, a text download fixture and a 34 KB local WebM avoid external media dependencies. The video is generated from FFmpeg's `testsrc2` (320×180, 12 fps, two seconds, VP9, no audio) and lives only in the developer gallery source tree.

## Validation

prs.title: fix(exec): filter terminal control sequences from shell output
prs.body:
Colorized CLI output currently sends terminal escape sequences directly to the model and counts them toward output limits. For example, `\x1b[38;5;190m+21\x1b[0m` now becomes `+21`, preserving the value and surrounding layout.

Add a small incremental `ShellOutputFilter` in the tool layer and apply it after UTF-8 decoding, before buffering or truncation, for both `exec` and `exec_session`. Each stdout/stderr stream owns its parser state, so sequences split across reads or polls are consumed correctly and `wait_for` matches plain text. Control-string payloads are discarded as they arrive, keeping parser memory bounded.

The filter removes 7-bit ESC sequences, including CSI formatting/cursor controls and OSC title/hyperlink metadata. Visible text, whitespace, stderr labels, and execution status remain intact. It preserves progress text rather than emulating terminal screen updates. The dedicated module and `feed()` entry point keep future filtering rules localized without introducing a registry, configuration, or dependency.

prs.title: fix(tools): decode JSON-string nested object/array tool args
prs.body:
Fixes #5311

Some OpenAI-compatible providers (Agnes AI was the reported one) send nested object/array tool arguments as JSON strings, e.g. `{"options": "{\"a\": 1}"}`. Schema validation then rejects them and the tool call fails.

This adds a small, schema-driven coercion step in `nanobot/agent/tools/base.py`: when a parameter's schema expects an object or array and the value is a string that parses as JSON of that type, it's decoded before validation. Everything else is left exactly as the provider sent it — real objects, string parameters, and strings that don't parse.

It also handles the schema shapes that show up in real tools:
- `oneOf` / `anyOf` (only decodes when no string branch accepts the value), plus a sibling `type: object|array` next to constraint-only branches
- `allOf`, treated as an intersection of container constraints
- local `#/...` `$ref`s, resolved against the tool schema

**Tests**
- New cases in `tests/tools/test_tool_registry.py`: nested objects/arrays, deep nesting, string params untouched, invalid JSON untouched, unions with a string branch, `allOf`, local `$ref`.
- Locally: `ruff` clean, basedpyright 0 errors, tool tests 266 passed, full suite 9444 passed. The few remaining failures (ssh/gateway smoke/inotify limits) reproduce the same way on a clean `main` checkout, so they're environment-related and not from this change.

prs.title: fix(agent): keep idle compaction from archiving a running direct turn
prs.body:
# Fix idle compaction archiving a turn that is still running (#6214)

## Problem

`AgentLoop._check_expired_sessions_if_due` reports
`self._pending_queues.keys()` as the set of sessions with an in-flight turn.
The only writer of `_pending_queues` is `_enqueue_session_message` — the bus
path. `process_direct` takes the session lock and never enqueues, so a turn
running through it is invisible to the idle-compaction guard:

- `nanobot/agent/loop.py:1324` (before: `active_session_keys=self._pending_queues.keys()`)
- `nanobot/agent/autocompact.py:73-79` — two predicates, both must hold to archive:
  `key in active_session_keys` (skip) and `_is_expired(updated_at)`
- `_pending_queues` writers: `loop.py:888/894/897/1380/1389/1446/1453/1497/1675` — all
  bus-path; `process_direct` (`loop.py:2498`) is not among them

The turn's own persistence does not rescue it: the user message is saved once at
turn start (`_persist_user_message_early` → `sessions.save`), and after that
mid-turn state goes to the sidecar via `save_runtime_checkpoint`
(`loop.py:1017` → `session/manager.py:1108`), so `updated_at` rests at turn start
for the whole turn. Both predicates therefore hold and an archive is scheduled
for a turn that is still running.

No messages are lost — the live turn's final `sessions.save()` overwrites the
summary checkpoint the archive wrote — but the compaction is wasted, and it
repeats on every direct turn that outlives `sessionTtlMinutes` (default 15 min).

`process_direct` is not an edge path. It is the entry point for the API server
(`api/server.py:350`, `:394`), the SDK, one-shot CLI (`cli/agent.py:246`),
gateway runtime (`cli/gateway_runtime.py:586`, `:655`), builtin commands
(`command/builtin.py:487`) and the top-level entry (`nanobot.py:197`, `:280`).

## Fix

Register direct turns so the guard can see them (the guard's view), rather than
refreshing `updated_at` mid-turn:

- `_direct_turn_sessions: set[str]` on `AgentLoop`
- `process_direct` adds its key before taking the session lock and discards it
  in the existing `finally`, so failures release it too
- `_check_expired_sessions_if_due` passes
  `self._active_session_keys()` = `set(self._pending_queues) | _direct_turn_sessions`

This keeps the meaning of `_pending_queues` ("this session has an inbound
queue") intact and adds no new concept — a running direct turn is what
`active_session_keys` already means.

Refreshing `updated_at` instead was considered and rejected: it does not fix the
case where the turn starts on an already-expired session, and it would make long
turns (cron, goals) never go idle, raising token cost. `updated_at` also drives
`prepare_session`'s reload decision, the summary's `last_active`, and session
list ordering.

Because several unit tests construct `AgentLoop` via `__new__` and attach only
the attributes the method under test needs (6 such tests), the new set is read
defensively rather than becoming a hard dependency of `process_direct()`.

## Verification

Repro script (blocked `chat_stream_with_retry`, real guard, real active set) —
four assertions, A/B against the unpatched tree via `git stash`:

| | unpatched | patched |
|---|---|---|
| direct turn visible to the guard | FAIL (`_pending_queues=[]`) | OK (`_direct_turn_sessions=['cli:direct']`) |
| `updated_at` frozen during the turn | OK (unchanged, issue premise) | OK |
| archive scheduled for a running direct turn | **FAIL** (`background_tasks=1`) | OK (`0`) |
| summary clobbered by the live turn's save | **FAIL** (`after_archive=set after_turn=None`) | OK (nothing archived) |

Three tests added to `tests/agent/test_auto_compact.py::TestProactiveAutoCompact`:

- `test_direct_turn_is_reported_as_active` — blocked direct turn is not
  archived, transcript unchanged
- `test_direct_turn_archives_after_it_completes` — registration is released, so
  the next idle tick archives normally
- `test_direct_turn_released_after_failure` — a failed turn must not leave the
  session registered for the life of the process

All three fail on the unpatched tree (`3 failed, 52 passed`) and pass after
(`55 passed` in that file).

Full suite: **8387 passed, 121 skipped, 4 deselected** in 678s. The 4 deselected
are this workspace's known environment failures. No pre-existing test changed
behavior.

One note worth flagging: the first full-suite run caught
`tests/test_openai_api.py::test_process_direct_accepts_media` failing with
`AttributeError` on the new attribute. That test builds `AgentLoop` via
`__new__` and attaches only the two attributes the method under test needs —
an existing pattern in this repo (6 sites), not a dirty test. Rather than
adjusting their test, the new set is read defensively so `process_direct()`
gains no new hard attribute dependency.

Full evidence chain, including two of my own assumptions that were wrong and
cost me a false repro: `repro/6214-idle-compact-direct/EVIDENCE.md`.

## Uncertainties

- I did not run the reporter's original repro verbatim; my script measures the
  same predicates with fewer variables. The code-line correspondence is
  verified, the exact script is not.
- The lock-ordering interaction (direct turn holding the session lock while
  `compact_idle_session` wants it) is analysed, not measured under interleaved
  turns.
- I have not confirmed with a maintainer that the fix belongs in the active set,
  as the issue itself flags ("only a suggestion").

Full evidence chain, including two of my own assumptions that were wrong and
cost me a false repro: `repro/6214-idle-compact-direct/EVIDENCE.md`.

prs.body:
## Summary

Adds FXMacroData as an optional MCP preset in Apps.

- connects to the hosted `https://mcp.fxmacrodata.com/mcp` endpoint over streamable HTTP
- read-only tools for official-source macro data: central-bank rates, CPI, jobs and GDP releases, release calendars and FX rates
- no API key needed for USD data (releases readable 15 minutes after publication, last 90 days); other currencies and FX rates need a key, which can go in an `Authorization: Bearer` header on a custom MCP server
- new `data` category, since none of the existing ones fit
- documented in `docs/webui.md` next to the other hosted keyless presets, attached with `@fxmacrodata`

## Why

Macro and FX questions ("what did US CPI print", "when is the next Fed decision") currently go through web search. The preset makes the official numbers one click away without touching the built-in providers or the agent loop. It stays opt-in.

prs.title: perf(agent): prepare prompts outside the event loop
prs.body:
Prompt file reads, transcript shaping, and local token estimation currently run on the gateway event loop. A slow read or large replay can delay status handling and cancellation before the next model request.

Capture read-only replay inputs from the live JSONL Session on the event loop, and apply prepared request/accepted-history state there. A cancelled caller can return while its physical worker retains the slot until completion. Preserve detached lifecycle hook snapshots, including nonempty cancellation snapshots, and protect the shared tool token cache across worker threads.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep theme text and selections readable
prs.body:
Dark themes could hide capability mention names that used near-black brand colors, while light themes made ANSI whites/yellows and orange inline tokens difficult to read. Code comments, diff line numbers, timestamps, and TUI hints also lost contrast on their actual backgrounds. Light TUI selections could render black text on a near-black background.

Use the theme foreground for capability names, shared CSS syntax tokens for code and diffs, and opaque secondary text. Darken the light-theme accent/error colors, select ANSI standard foregrounds for the current appearance, and clear foreground/background colors on SGR reset. Explicit ANSI color pairs and RGB values retain their encoded colors. Improve TUI hint/code colors on common terminal backgrounds and apply explicit selection pairs across TUI conversation text, the composer, and diffs, including when terminal theme detection is unavailable. A small adapter updates retained OpenTUI table selections because version 0.5.11 exposes their colors only at construction.

Diff statistics, line markers, and row backgrounds share added/deleted theme tokens defined in CSS; components select only the semantic roles.

Give the blank composer cursor cell the theme foreground. Hosts that draw the cursor by reversing the cell can then show a readable caret at the end of input instead of a white block on a light surface.

Preserve the inner syntax colors of nested JSX tokens when Prism also attaches their ancestor `tag` class. Ignore destroyed selection renderables during recoloring so automatic theme changes can rebuild an actively selected diff without raising `TextBufferView is destroyed` or opening the debug console.

Validation:

- WebUI: 2,708 tests passed across 157 files with `bun run test:coverage --maxWorkers=2 --minWorkers=1`; coverage thresholds passed (93.09% statements/lines, 87.40% branches, 90.61% functions). ESLint, import checks, and production build passed.
- TUI with Bun 1.3.13: 264 tests, TypeScript/import checks, Windows build, and ConPTY smoke test passed. The diff regression test drags a real selection and checks its rendered contrast without an OSC theme response. Composer regressions cover cursor movement, deletion, Unicode input, and wrapping in light, dark, and automatic themes.
- Rechecked 123 component groups in both appearances plus 676 state/overlay scenarios. Production-component probes cover bundled MCP brand colors, all 16 ANSI standard foregrounds, reset behavior, code, and diffs.
- Built WebUI through an isolated real gateway: 68 code/command text samples per appearance passed 4.5:1, with minimum ratios of 5.04:1 in light and 4.74:1 in dark. Theme selection survived reload; `/model` replay returned HTTP 200; browser console had no errors or warnings. Runtime and ports were cleaned up.
- Diff token follow-up: 62 focused tests, ESLint, import checks, and production build passed. The built UI through an isolated gateway retained identical light/dark computed colors and diff content; a live CSS token override updated both statistics and line markers. Expand/collapse, theme reload, browser console health, and runtime cleanup passed.
- TUI conversation selections: regressions cover user text, Markdown paragraphs, bold text, lists, code, tables, keyboard selection, and an active table selection through theme changes. Selected samples have minimum contrast of 11.99:1 (light), 8.91:1 (dark), and 9.82:1 (automatic). The real CLI through Windows ConPTY and an isolated WebSocket protocol fixture verifies explicit RGB output during active mouse drag for paragraph/code/table text in all three appearances, with terminal restoration and fixture-port cleanup.
- Selection/syntax follow-up: both regressions failed before the fixes and passed afterward. An isolated built gateway passed 42 light/dark computed-color checks across Markdown code, diffs, and file previews, with theme/transcript reload and a clean browser console. Real WezTerm verified dark → light → dark diff rebuilds with active mouse selections, continued file navigation, and subsequent input without buffer errors or console takeover. WezTerm did not supply native OS theme notifications; injected CSI997 input and real terminal OSC10/11 replies exercised the TUI's theme-detection path. All owned runtimes and fixture ports were cleaned up.
- Native execution was verified on Windows. Linux and macOS were not run locally.

prs.title: fix(memory): serialize manual and scheduled Dream runs
prs.body:
## Summary

Prevent overlapping Dream runs from overwriting newer memory and moving the processing cursor backward. Both manual and scheduled triggers use one shared Dream executor in the agent layer.

## Root cause

Manual and scheduled Dream runs share memory files and a processing cursor, but per-session execution locks do not serialize those updates. An older run can finish after a newer run, overwrite its memory updates, and replace its cursor with an earlier value.

## Changes

- Add a shared asynchronous Dream lock to MemoryStore.
- Centralize batch selection, model/tool execution, completion checks, cursor updates, Git commits, and cleanup in `nanobot/agent/dream.py`.
- Keep command feedback and cron logging in their respective entry points, using a structured execution result.
- Preserve manual cursor-only commits, scheduled content-only commits, and scheduled MCP preparation.
- Cover overlapping triggers, failure and cancellation recovery, partial edits, commit policies, and MCP preparation failure.

## Result

Dream runs sharing a MemoryStore execute sequentially. Waiting runs select fresh history after the preceding run finishes. Failed or cancelled runs retain pending history and release the lock for subsequent attempts; partial memory edits retain the existing Git audit behavior.

## Test

- Original serialization baseline: both overlap regressions fail, as expected.
- Previous production follow-up: 90 Dream and command tests plus 158 serial CLI tests passed (248 total).
- Test refinement: 194 tests passed across Dream concurrency, shared execution, command feedback, and CLI tests. The final cron assertion refinement also passed its focused rerun.
- Both broken-progress and missing-lock mutations were detected.
- Ruff on the three updated test files: passed.
- Ruff on the six files in the maintainer follow-up: passed.
- Strict BasedPyright on the three production modules in the maintainer follow-up: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

prs.title: Make `sendProgress` mean what it says: authorise the text it delivers
prs.body:
Fixes #6000

## What this changes

`channels.sendProgress` defaults to `true`, but on a default install it has nothing to
deliver and behaves exactly like `false`. The switch gates *delivery*; the text it is
supposed to deliver is never produced, because on the message that carries tool calls the
model is told not to write anything (`templates/agent/tool_contract.md:10`) while the
adjacent line (`:13`) tells it to outline its plan. Both rules land on the same field.

Two changes:

**(a) Authorise the text.** When `send_progress` resolves true for a channel, append a
short section to the system prompt (`templates/agent/progress_notes.md`) that asks for one
short progress line on the message carrying each stage's tool calls. Gate in
`AgentLoop._progress_notes_enabled()`; rendering in `ContextBuilder.build_system_prompt()`
behind a `progress_notes` parameter that defaults to `False`.

**(b) Default `send_progress` to `false`** (`config/schema.py:33`, `channels/base.py:31`).
Until (a) is in, the honest default is off. After (a), opting in produces a setting that
means what it says.

## Before / after

A turn that needs many tool calls, seen from the user's side. On a channel with
`sendToolHints=false` the tool calls and their output are hidden, so the only things that
reach the chat are progress lines and the final answer.

**Before** — factory default, `sendProgress=true`:

```
[15 tool calls happen, invisible]

                                     ← the user sees nothing at all for the whole turn
...
                                     ← then one long final answer
```

**After** — the behaviour this PR brings in-product:

```
📢 先读一下你加的 skill，同时探一下 HN 的可达性。

[several tool calls]

📢 HN 的 Algolia API 通，codeload 也通，可以真把仓库拉下来看。

[several tool calls]

📢 仓库拉下来了（27MB）。开始按 skill 的流程查。

    ...

                                     ← then the final answer
```

Same shape of turn, same hidden tool calls. Before: one long silence. After: three short
lines marking the stages the turn actually went through.

The silent case is not a corner case: across that deployment before the workaround, a
15-tool-call turn produced zero lines and a 17-tool-call turn produced one — at most a
single line at the very start, then nothing.

## Why this shape

**Generation follows delivery; no new switch.** A separate "should the model write
progress?" key would create a `sendProgress=true` + "no generation" combination — exactly
the state this issue reports, one level deeper. One switch, one meaning, honoured by both
halves.

**`tool_contract.md` is unchanged, byte for byte.** Line 10 is the brake added in #4945 for
the #705 / #825 class of interim text; touching it reads as a revert, and this PR does not
need to touch it. The new section refines line 13's "outline the plan briefly" by saying
*which* messages count and how long the line may be. The safety line ("This is not an
answer. Never put results, conclusions, or the final answer in a progress note") is kept
from the first draft so the new section cannot displace the existing guard.

> **Open design question, deliberately not decided here.** Line 13 says "outline the plan
> briefly **and then execute it**" — once — while this section asks for a line per stage.
> Those are in tension, and the tension lives in `tool_contract.md` itself. Reviewers may
> prefer to make the contract internally consistent (e.g. "outline each step briefly before
> executing it") instead of adding a second place that defines the same behaviour. That is a
> design call, so it is raised in the issue rather than folded into this PR.

## Wording: where it comes from

The wording is not invented. It is a language-neutral rendering of a rule that a real
deployment has been running in its `SOUL.md` for weeks — a workaround, which is the strongest
argument for fixing this upstream.

Three things in it are deliberate:

- **"in the same message as that stage's tool calls"** rather than "the message" — the target
  is one line per stage, not one opener. The progress hook only reads text from the message
  carrying the tool calls, so this is also the only place the line can go.
- **Stating the consequence** ("the user sees a long blank screen") — turns a formatting
  request into something with a cost, which matters because the behaviour being fought is
  "say nothing".
- **No "skip it when unnecessary" escape hatch.** An earlier draft had one; the deployment's
  rule does not. "Does this step need explaining" is a judgement a model will almost always
  resolve toward skipping.

**Kept from the first draft:** "This is not an answer. Never put results, conclusions, or the
final answer in a progress note" — that line is the brake for the #705 / #825 class of interim
text and must not be displaced by the new section.

**Kept short on purpose.** The deployment's rule also spells out the mechanism (which hook
publishes the line, that it only applies to non-streaming turns). That detail belongs in the
code, not in the prompt — a prompt that has to describe its own plumbing is a sign the
behaviour is not discoverable, which is part of what this issue is about.

## Scope

- No new configuration keys.
- `tool_contract.md` unchanged (see above).
- Tool-hint behaviour unchanged (`sendToolHints` unaffected).
- Does not address reasoning text spilling into the content channel — separate phenomenon.

**On the diff size.** Most of `channels/manager.py` is a refactor, not new behaviour:
`channels/config_bools.py` is a shared boolean-resolver extracted so the gate in
`AgentLoop` and the delivery check in `ChannelManager` read `sendProgress` the same way.
The gate depends on it (and so does `tests/agent/test_progress_prompt_gate.py`), so it
belongs here. What rides along is a `logger.debug` on the drop path in `manager.py` — the
same code path this PR touches, and the reason the issue could observe that a drop and
"nothing was produced" looked identical.


## Testing

Full suite: **7373 passed, 96 skipped, 4 deselected** (the 4 deselections are this
repository's known local-environment WebUI-build failures, excluded by `run-tests.sh`).

The area this PR touches, on its own:

```
pytest tests/agent/test_progress_prompt_gate.py tests/agent/test_loop_progress.py \
       tests/channels/test_channel_manager_delta_coalescing.py tests/channels/test_channel_plugins.py
```

201 passed, 1 skipped.

New tests live in `tests/agent/test_progress_prompt_gate.py` (20 tests) and the two channel
test files, covering:

- the gate: no section is injected when `send_progress` resolves false — for the global
  default, a per-channel override, an unknown channel, and a non-bool value;
- the prompt is otherwise unchanged — `tool_contract.md` is asserted intact, so a future
  edit that starts leaning on it fails here;
- the consumer invariant: every consumer of `context.response.content` during a
  tool-executing iteration gates on `send_progress`, which is the #705 / #878 bug class.

## Behaviour change

Default value changes for all users, and opting in changes model behaviour (the model is
told it may write a short line). Stated explicitly for review.
