issues.title: Steers/queued prompts carry no origin attribution; duplicate row persistence; compaction puts unverifiable text into context
issues.body:
# Steers / queued prompts carry no origin attribution; plus duplicate row persistence and compaction transcript contamination

**Environment**: Hermes Agent (desktop app, Windows 11), main + aux model `stepfun-ai/step-5-preview` via NVIDIA provider. Self-hosted local backend. All evidence below is from a single session on 2026-10-15 (session id `20261015_203742_d0e248`).

This started as a user-facing security concern: a message appeared in a live conversation that the user swears they never typed, arriving with **zero way to audit where it came from**. The audit below found no third-party writer — but found four real flaws that (a) make an inbound message unauditable, and (b) put unverifiable text into the model's context. Together they are indistinguishable from prompt injection from the user's perspective.

---

## 1. Desktop steers / queued prompts are persisted with no origin metadata (the core flaw)

A message that arrived mid-turn was recorded in `state.db` as:

- `role="assistant"`, content `[Request interrupted by user]\n<text>`, `platform_message_id=None` — no sender, no client id, no surface, nothing.

Measured timeline (from `agent.log`, same session):

```
21:48:15,736 INFO agent.conversation_loop: Turn ended: reason=text_response(...) ...
21:48:15,73  -> the ghost message row is written (same instant as turn end)
```

Mechanism, as traced in the code:

- The desktop composer keeps a **per-session persisted prompt queue** (`apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/hooks/use-composer-queue.ts`) that **auto-drains on the busy→idle settle edge**, on mount/reconnect, and after re-keying. A stale/abandoned queued entry therefore fires on its own the moment a turn ends — no human present.
- Server-side, `session.steer` / `session.redirect` (`tui_gateway/methods_session_interrupt.py`) and `_enqueue_prompt` / `_drain_queued_prompt` (`tui_gateway/session_auto_continue.py`) accept and dispatch text with **no origin fields at all**. The messaging-gateway path has `_steer_text_with_origin` (gateway/run_busy.py) that embeds a JSON origin block; the desktop/TUI RPC path has no equivalent.
- On successful drain the queue entry is **removed** (`removeQueuedPrompt`), and the persisted row carries no provenance — so after delivery there is **nothing left to audit**.

Impact: any of the surfaces feeding the local RPC backend (desktop windows, quick-entry, browser extension sessions, etc.) can deliver text that is then recorded as if it were the user, with no way to distinguish "user typed it" from "stale queue entry" from "another surface". For a single-user machine this is the difference between "software glitch" and "someone else is writing to my agent" — and the software currently cannot answer it.

Suggested fix: attach an origin block (surface/window id, client capabilities, transport id, enqueue timestamp) at `_apply_correction` / `_enqueue_prompt` / `prompt.submit` time, persist it on the message row (or a side table), and keep drained queue entries in an audit trail.

## 2. Duplicate message rows persisted with identical timestamp+content

Many messages are written **twice** to `state.db` with the exact same `timestamp` and `content`. Measured across sessions:

- 252 duplicate pairs in one 2026-09-29 session, 169 in a 2026-09-20 session, 100+ in several others.
- In the audited session: 406 rows, 368 unique (`SELECT ... GROUP BY timestamp, content HAVING COUNT(*)>1`).

Impact: doubles context growth, wastes prompt-cache (identical consecutive rows re-sent), accelerates compaction, and makes token accounting unreliable.

## 3. Compaction leaves non-matching rows and the rebuilt transcript contains text that exists nowhere in the DB

From `agent.log` during this session's compaction:

```
21:13:40 WARNING agent.conversation_compression_reply_anchor: Compression: engine folded away the
         just-delivered assistant reply and left a non-matching assistant row at its slot; not
         reinserting it to keep strict role alternation
21:13:40 INFO   agent.conversation_compression: Compaction rebuilt a drifted system prompt
         (52642 -> 53296 chars): builder output changed since the stored snapshot
```

Consequence observed: after compaction, the model's context contained fragments presented as user/assistant turns (short out-of-place sentences, e.g. an unrelated line about a TV-show character) that **return zero rows** in `messages`, zero hits in the memory stores, and zero hits anywhere on disk when searched afterwards. The model receives unverifiable content interleaved as conversation turns. For the user this is indistinguishable from a third party injecting messages — which is exactly how this investigation began.

Related aux-compaction errors seen in the same window:

```
Auxiliary compression: provider rejected the reasoning field; retrying without it:
  Error code: 400 - {'message': 'Validation: Unsupported parameter(s): `reasoning`', 'type': 'Bad Request'}
Auxiliary compression: structured provider error on nvidia (Service temporarily overloaded),
  trying fallback → falling back to main agent model
```

## 4. Runtime "system notes" persisted as assistant transcript rows

Rows like:

```
[System note: The user has ended the conversation. Do not start new tasks or make further
tool calls. Provide a brief closing message ...]
```

are stored with `role="assistant"` in the durable transcript (two such rows in this session). Runtime control text entering the persisted history can later be replayed/compacted as if the assistant produced it.

---

## Reproduction / verification performed

1. Dumped every `role="user"` row of the session from `state.db` and confirmed the ghost text exists only as an assistant-row interrupt marker with `platform_message_id=None`.
2. Searched all DB tables, all local memory stores and the whole Hermes home dir for the stray fragments seen in the reconstructed context: 0 hits (only echoes of this audit itself).
3. Correlated `agent.log` turn-end timestamps with the ghost row timestamp: delivery 0.01s after turn end.
4. Quantified duplicate rows across sessions (numbers above).
5. Ruled out external writers: no non-local inbound connections to the backend; all other sessions in the window belong to the same user's surfaces.

Happy to provide the full audit scripts/outputs if useful.

issues.title: [Bug]: hardline guard false-positives on $(grep/rg/sort ...) inside double quotes — benign commands blocked as 'malformed executable payload'

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/tools
labels.description: Tool registry, model_tools, toolsets

labels.name: tool/terminal
labels.description: Terminal execution and process management

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

issues.body:
### Summary

The hardline command guard's malformed-executable-payload check false-positives on well-formed benign commands whenever a read-only tool (`grep`, `rg`, `sort`, `man`) appears inside a `$(...)` command substitution within double quotes. The command is unconditionally blocked (not bypassable via `--yolo`, `/yolo`, or `approvals.mode=off`) with:

```
BLOCKED (hardline): command parser limit or malformed executable payload. ...
```

### Minimal reproduction

Any of these perfectly valid shell commands are hardline-blocked by the `terminal` tool:

```bash
echo "done=$(grep -c 'some pattern' file.txt)"
echo "n=$(rg -c foo file.txt)"
echo "n=$(sort -u file.txt | head -1)"
```

Programmatic repro against `tools/approval.py`:

```python
from tools.approval import detect_dangerous_command
print(detect_dangerous_command('echo "n=$(grep -c \'x y\' f)"'))
# (True, 'command parser limit or malformed executable payload', ...)
```

### Root cause

`_iter_shell_command_starts()` correctly registers a command start inside `$(...)`, but the span-preserving lexers that then tokenize from that start — `_shell_tokens_with_spans()` (grep-pattern span detection) and `_shell_segment_tokens()` (execution-flag detection for `rg`/`sort`/`man`) — read to the **end of the top-level segment**, crossing the substitution's closing `)"` into the enclosing command. The enclosing close-quote is then seen as a fresh unbalanced quote, the lexer returns `None`, and the caller fails closed as "malformed executable payload".

This matters in practice because agents naturally emit this shape (`echo "count=$(grep -c ...)"` in loops/status lines), each block costs a wasted round-trip, and the block message steers the model toward "run it outside the agent" instead of the trivial restructure.

### Fix

PR incoming: bound both lexers to the command region that actually runs at that command position — walk quote-aware from the region start and stop at the first unmatched `)` outside quotes (matched pairs, i.e. nested substitutions, stay inside). Genuinely unterminated payloads still fail closed, and dangerous commands inside/after substitutions still match their hardline patterns (regression tests included).

### Hermes version

Reproduced on current `main`.

Related (same false-positive class, different detectors): #20064 (closed/fixed), #22722, #32737 — independent.

issues.title: [Bug]: sessions archive --title silently skips open (never-ended) desktop sessions
issues.body:
### Summary

`hermes sessions archive` with explicit filters (`--title`, `--cwd`) prints "No sessions match" for sessions that are clearly visible in the desktop sidebar. The shared prune/archive selector is pinned to `ended_at IS NOT NULL` (see the comment in `hermes_cli/sessions_cmd.py`). Desktop sessions never set `ended_at`, so they can never match.

### Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.22.0 (2026.9.24), commit `e06df9c2eae`, macOS, desktop app

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a session in the desktop app and give it a title, for example "Review Hermes projects for duplicates".
2. Run `hermes sessions archive --title "Review Hermes projects for duplicates"`.

### Expected

The session is archived (archive is reversible), or the CLI says why it was skipped.

### Actual

"No sessions match". There is no hint that the session exists but is still open.

### Context

During a cleanup we needed to archive 58 desktop sessions. We had to call `SessionDB.set_session_archived(id, True)` directly from the Hermes venv. Pinning **prune** to ended sessions makes sense because it deletes. **Archive** is reversible, so the same restriction is less necessary there.

### Suggested change (either one)

1. When explicit filters match only open sessions, print: "N matching sessions are still open and were skipped (use --include-open to archive them)".
2. Add `--include-open` to `sessions archive` (not to `prune`).

issues.title: [Bug]: skills reset --restore reports success but restores nothing for a curator-archived bundled skill
issues.body:
### Summary

`hermes skills reset <name> --restore --yes` prints a success message but does not restore anything when the bundled skill was previously archived by the curator. Nothing appears in `hermes skills list` and no directory is created.

Related but different: #29856 (misleading success for `reset` **without** `--restore`).

### Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.22.0 (2026.9.24), commit `e06df9c2eae`, macOS 26.6.2 (Apple silicon)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have a bundled skill that the curator archived, so it lives at `~/.hermes/skills/.archive/<name>/` and has no active copy. (Ours: `weekly-review-planning`.)
2. Run `hermes skills reset weekly-review-planning --restore --yes`.
3. Run `hermes skills list | grep weekly`.

### Expected

Either the skill is active again, or the command fails with a pointer such as: `'weekly-review-planning' is archived by the curator. Run: hermes curator restore weekly-review-planning`.

### Actual

Step 2 reports a restore (the `restored` branch: "Restored '<name>' (no prior user copy, re-copied from bundled)."). Step 3 prints nothing. No directory exists under `~/.hermes/skills/productivity/`. We restored it by copying `~/.hermes/hermes-agent/skills/productivity/weekly-review-planning` by hand.

### Cause (from reading the source)

`reset_bundled_skill()` in `tools/skills_sync_bundled_ops.py` sets `action = "restored"` and a success message after the sync, but it does not check that the sync actually copied `<name>` (for example `name in synced["copied"]`, or that the active path now exists). The likely reason the sync copied nothing is that the name is present in `.archive/`, which the sync respects.

### Suggested fix

After the sync, verify the active copy exists. If it does not and `<name>` is in the curator archive, return `ok: False` with `action: "archived"` and the `hermes curator restore <name>` hint. A unit test: an archived bundled skill + `restore=True` → `ok` is False and the message names `hermes curator restore`.

I am happy to open a PR for this.

issues.title: Docker: one TUI launch makes every later container boot start the gateway
issues.body:
## What happens

In the s6 Docker image, the first time the TUI starts its gateway, `gateway-default` is recorded as "start at boot". From then on every container boot on that volume starts the gateway, including boots that never open the TUI (for example `docker run ... bash`).

This comes from #139511. That PR is right to start the s6 slot so the TUI can connect (it fixes #138945). The open question is only whether that client start should also become the boot intent.

## Why

- The s6 branch of [`start_existing_gateway_service`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/bd9ba771a5a160b2b9225a86adae78d9c8a2cd12/hermes_cli/gateway_runtime_service.py#L280-L288) calls [`S6ServiceManager.start`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/bd9ba771a5a160b2b9225a86adae78d9c8a2cd12/hermes_cli/service_manager.py#L548-L550), which writes `desired_state: running`, the same operator intent `hermes gateway start` records.
- [Boot reconciliation](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/bd9ba771a5a160b2b9225a86adae78d9c8a2cd12/hermes_cli/container_boot.py#L120-L133) starts `gateway-default` from that intent.
- The host backends only request a start and don't touch boot persistence ([systemd](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/bd9ba771a5a160b2b9225a86adae78d9c8a2cd12/hermes_cli/gateway_runtime_service.py#L145), [launchd](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/bd9ba771a5a160b2b9225a86adae78d9c8a2cd12/hermes_cli/gateway_runtime_service.py#L202), [Windows](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/bd9ba771a5a160b2b9225a86adae78d9c8a2cd12/hermes_cli/gateway_runtime_service.py#L245)), and unmanaged client starts use `idle_exit`.

## Reproduction

An image built from #139511 merged with `main`, using a fresh named volume. The container runs `sleep infinity` with `-t`, and `gateway_bootstrap.py --start` runs as `hermes`:

```text
boot1 before TUI: up=false state=no-state-file
bootstrap rc=0
boot1 after TUI:  up=true state={'desired_state': 'running', 'gateway_state': 'running'}
boot2 (plain shell CMD, same volume): up=true state={'desired_state': 'running', ...}
container-boot.log: profile=default prior_state=running action=started
```

## Why a one-line fix isn't enough

If the TUI start stopped writing `desired_state`, boot would still start the gateway. [`_read_desired_state`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/bd9ba771a5a160b2b9225a86adae78d9c8a2cd12/hermes_cli/container_boot.py#L240-L255) falls back to the gateway's own `gateway_state`, and that reads `running` after a stopped or killed container. So changing this means changing boot reconciliation too, and existing installs rely on that fallback.

## Decision needed

1. **Keep it.** Under #106742 the gateway is the local backend for the TUI and cron as well, so keeping it running once Hermes has been used is reasonable. Document it in `website/docs/user-guide/docker.md`.
2. **Client starts don't set boot intent.** Record a client-initiated start separately (or not at all), and have boot autostart only from an operator start or the legacy `gateway run` migration. This needs a decision on the `gateway_state` fallback and a two-boot Docker regression test.

Refs #134889 (GW-5), #139511, #138945

issues.title: [Bug]: `hermes update --help` is gramatically incomprehensible and have wrong confusing info - preventing correct channel updates
issues.body:
### OS

- Debian

### Issue

- Running `hermes update --help` spits out a bunch of humanly incomprehensible gibberish. 
- There is zero consistency and in particular how to enter and exit available distribution channels.
- Also no info how to combine the different options.  
- Statements like: *`Track CHANNEL for this run only (transient override; --set-channel persists). 'stable' and 'canary' select published releases, 'main' the branch tip. Source installs only.`* provide zero insight and clarity while being completely wrong. There is no command option or channel named `persists`.

### Acceptance Criteria

- Write each command option in STE-100 for comprehension.
- Test that the command option is actually doing what it says.
- Expand help with how the different options can interact and be combined. (if they are required, exclusive or inclusive.)
- Clearly separate the different distribution channels in the text. 
- What channels are available? 
- Provide example commands for each channel on how to enter and exit that channel, and if there are further steps required to complete the change. (E.g. `hermes update`, `npm install` etc.)
- Provide command for checking your current distribution channel.

As of today, several issues show options are ignored or do something different than what is written.

issues.title: [Feature]: durable plugin turn admission, automation provenance and writer-release receipts

labels.name: type/feature
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: comp/gateway
labels.description: Gateway runner, session dispatch, delivery

labels.name: comp/plugins
labels.description: Plugin system and bundled plugins

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low — cosmetic, nice to have

labels.name: needs-decision
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer decision before any implementation

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

labels.name: area/sessions
labels.description: Session lifecycle, resume, persistence, history

issues.body:
We need a supported way for a trusted plugin to deliver automated work to one exact Hermes session, recover a lost acknowledgement without starting it twice, and know when the attempt can no longer write to its transcript. Would you accept a native contract for this, building on the plugin-author work in #130622?

A concrete consumer is a collaboration plugin that delivers a question or task to an agent. Its local supervisor can journal requests and enforce owner consent. It cannot tell whether Hermes admitted input if the host crashes between enqueue and acknowledgement, or stop another native input path from competing for the same transcript.

### Existing work and evidence

#130622 covers plugin input being attributed to the human by memory providers. Its proposed `turn_author` path is a useful foundation. Please keep that repair independently shippable. #110031 proposes authorized same-session completion events; we would prefer extending suitable host-owned admission, typed-event and session-lease machinery from that work over creating another queue.

Our source review and no-model probe used v0.22.0, commit `e06df9c2eae6901f4c88f464e0ae6e753c0428b8`:

- [`inject_plugin_message`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/e06df9c2eae6901f4c88f464e0ae6e753c0428b8/hermes_cli/plugins_injection.py#L12-L62) returns a Boolean and converts a non-user role into a text prefix. In a probe using the real functions with disposable in-memory host collaborators, duplicate calls retained both copies. A deliberately injected exception after enqueue returned `False` while the input remained queued. This is a synthetic failure case, not a production incident or a native crash/restart test.
- [TUI/Desktop injection](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/e06df9c2eae6901f4c88f464e0ae6e753c0428b8/tui_gateway/plugin_inject.py#L24-L66) drops `plugin_id` and may start draining immediately. That route exposes no retained attempt-to-turn receipt.
- [Deferred active-session leases](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/e06df9c2eae6901f4c88f464e0ae6e753c0428b8/tui_gateway/session_lifecycle.py#L598-L668) include an age-based concurrency-slot reaper. That slot's release does not prove every writer has stopped. We are not claiming Hermes has no transcript locks.

These findings are pinned to that release and route. We have not run a complete native conformance suite or established the absence of an equivalent on every current surface.

### Requested contract

The operation names below describe semantics, not a required Python or RPC API. We call the complete bundle handshake v1; this is a proposed integration contract, not a claim that Hermes already defines it.

1. **Prepare without model input.** Resolve one exact native session lineage and incarnation, plus a stable transcript identity across reconnect and compaction. Preparation may bind a consented dormant child, but must not submit a prompt or start inference. Reject stale identities and unrelated forks; never silently substitute a new session or incarnation.
2. **Durable admission.** Accept a caller-retained admission key bound immutably to the request, event, attempt, destination and payload. Commit the admission before execution can start. Identical duplicate calls, including after queue drain or restart, return the same retained admission and native turn correlation. Changed input under the same key conflicts. Keep consumed and withdrawn records, or an equivalent durable fence, so cleanup cannot make an old key executable again.
3. **Inspect and withdraw.** Inspect that same key after reconnect or a lost acknowledgement. Distinguish admitted/queued/started from permanent never-admitted and Unknown. Missing data, `False` or a timeout cannot prove never-admitted. Withdrawal and queued start must have one durable winner at the native execution boundary. Successful withdrawal closes the key permanently, including against delayed submission; if start won, report that attempt instead of promising it cannot run.
4. **Trusted automation provenance.** Carry host-authenticated plugin identity and typed automation metadata separately from message text. For our consumer, preserve the meaning of `source=artifactbridge`, `actor_kind=automation`, request/wake ID, event ID, attempt ID and causal-root identity. A documented lossless native mapping is fine. Preserve it through transcript storage, context assembly, real compaction and every enabled memory provider. Automated instructions must not become facts about the human. External collaboration text stays untrusted data and cannot grant permissions or forge the envelope. A role prefix or `is_bot` alone cannot preserve exact attempt identity.
5. **Writer exclusion and release evidence.** Bind input ownership to the exact attempt and stable transcript, independent of the caller's room, workspace or machine. Competing supervisors, sibling incarnations and native human/plugin input paths must respect it. Human input can be held or explicitly arbitrate takeover, but cannot silently become part of the bound attempt. Expose inspectable evidence that all attempt-owned writers and relevant child processes have physically stopped or safely relinquished the ability to write. A model reply, turn-end notification, interrupt acknowledgement, supervisor death, discovered PID or elapsed lease is insufficient. Incomplete shutdown must retain uncertainty and exclusion.

We would enable this only for a documented runtime version, adapter, route and platform that passes the whole bundle. Individual primitives can ship separately; partial capability flags would not qualify a route for v1. One supported route is a useful starting point and would not imply support for every Hermes surface.

Our supervisor remains responsible for durable client journaling, owner consent, external authorization, deadlines, budgets and outcome handling. An uncertain attempt is never replayed through a fresh session or fallback. Once the caller commits a final Unknown outcome, late receipts may refine that attempt's result or prove release, but cannot authorize another execution. This asks for admission safety and evidence; it does not promise exactly-once arbitrary tool side effects.

### Tests a route must pass

- Dormant prepare makes zero model calls. Stale incarnation, unrelated fork and wrong-profile access refuse without admitting input.
- Duplicate admission before/after drain and restart produces one native turn. Lost acknowledgement and crashes around admission/receipt commits reconcile the same key without a second execution; changed payload conflicts.
- Start versus withdrawal has one durable winner. Successful withdrawal survives restart and delayed duplicates. Missing records remain Unknown unless a permanent rejection fence is proven.
- Two clients, scopes or incarnations targeting one transcript cannot own competing attempts. Genuine human input follows the documented arbitration rule. Compaction preserves the stable transcript binding.
- Automation identity survives actual transcript/context/compaction/memory paths. Forged payload text cannot change attribution, and human messages remain human. Honcho must not derive plugin instructions as human facts.
- Cancellation, result arrival, supervisor death and incomplete child shutdown cannot falsely certify release. A positive release receipt proves the exact attempt's writers lost custody. Final Unknown never creates a new execution, even when a late negative receipt arrives.

### What we can contribute

We can provide the small no-model reproducer and help turn these cases into native regression tests using isolated profile homes and disposable sessions. If the contract is accepted, we can contribute focused upstream changes and documentation using your existing queue, author and lifecycle boundaries, then verify a pinned route with real crash/restart, compaction, memory and writer-release tests. The external integration and its consent/journal policy would stay in a standalone plugin; no product-specific dependency belongs in core.

Which existing host boundary should own this contract? If another supported API already supplies it, a pointer to its guarantees and tests would let us target that instead.

issues.body:
## Bug

The `desktop_preview` and `drive_preview` tools (preview pane beside the chat) never work in the Hermes desktop app. `desktop_preview action=open` returns `{"success": true, ...}` but nothing opens. `drive_preview action=elements` always returns "No live page is open in the in-app browser."

## Root Cause

`tools/desktop_ui.py:set_emitter()` — the function that connects these tools to the app's renderer — is called from **exactly one place** in the entire codebase:

```
tui_gateway/session_notifications.py:822
```

That is the **TUI gateway** (terminal interface). The desktop app does not use `tui_gateway`, so for desktop sessions the emitter is **never wired**. `desktop_ui._emit` stays `None`, and `emit_or_error` returns the `desktop_only` error message — but `open_preview_tool` calls `emit_or_error` with a success result, so it returns fake success.

Additionally, `gateway/run.py:4269` calls `set_session_vars()` but **never passes `ui_session_id`**, so even if the emitter were wired, it would not know which window to route events to.

## Evidence

1. `tools/desktop_ui.py` — `_emit` is `None` unless `set_emitter` is called
2. `tui_gateway/session_notifications.py:822` — the only production call to `set_emitter`
3. `gateway/run.py:4269` — `set_session_vars()` call missing `ui_session_id` parameter
4. `tools/open_preview_tool.py:84` — calls `emit_or_error` with success result, so fake success is returned when emitter is `None`
5. `tools/drive_preview_tool.py:57` — returns "No GUI window answered" when callback is `None`
6. Preview pane code exists in renderer bundle: 42 references in `apps/desktop/dist/assets/index-C34RWtGu.js`
7. `HERMES_UI_SESSION_ID` is set in the session env (confirmed: `29952e9a`) but never used because emitter is `None`

## Impact

The preview pane feature is completely broken in the desktop app. Users cannot open URLs, files, or interact with web pages from the chat. The tools appear to work (return success) but silently do nothing.

## Expected Behavior

- `desktop_preview action=open` should open the URL in the preview pane
- `drive_preview action=elements` should return the page's interactive elements
- The emitter should be wired for desktop sessions, not just TUI

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.21.5+4908.g4767698 (2026.9.24)
- Windows 11
- Desktop app (Electron)
- Profile: echo

## Possible Fix

1. Wire `desktop_ui.set_emitter` in the desktop app's session setup (not just TUI)
2. Pass `ui_session_id` in `gateway/run.py:4269` when calling `set_session_vars`
3. The emitter should route events to the correct desktop window via the existing message bus

## Related

- The preview pane works on other devices/setups (user confirmed)
- The renderer code for the preview pane exists and is functional
- This is a backend wiring issue, not a renderer issue

issues.body:
### Bug Description

Clicking "restart gateway" in the desktop app fires /api/gateway/restart, which fails to spawn the replacement gateway. The old gateway then drains and is killed mid-drain, and nothing pulls it back up, so the desktop app stays unable to reach it until a manual scheduled-task pull-up. The restart failure is un-diagnosable: the action log has only a bare "=== gateway-restart started ===" line with no stderr or exit code.


### Steps to Reproduce

1. On Windows, with the gateway hosted by a scheduled task, click "restart gateway" in the desktop app.
2. The replacement gateway fails to spawn ("Failed to spawn gateway restart").
3. The old gateway drains and exits; no pull-up happens.
4. Desktop app repeatedly logs "Desktop boot failed: Gateway inaccessible (service_identity_unverified)".


### Expected Behavior

After a stop, the gateway is reliably pulled back up (two-phase stop + pull-up), and a failed restart records the spawned process's stderr / exit code in the action log.


### Actual Behavior

The restart action fails; the old gateway is killed mid-drain and nothing restarts it. The action log only contains "=== gateway-restart started ===" — no stderr, no exit code, no pull-up result.

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (CLI only)

### Debug Report

```shell
Not uploaded (privacy). Environment: Windows 11, hermes-agent v0.22.1, npm 12, gateway hosted by a scheduled task. Can provide a redacted `hermes debug share --local` excerpt on request.
```

### Operating System

Windows 11

### Python Version

3.14.7

### Hermes Version

V0.22.1

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

The restart path does not capture the spawned gateway's stderr/exit code on failure, and after a clean stop / mid-drain kill nothing re-pulls the gateway: the scheduled task only has a Logon trigger, and RestartOnFailure fires on non-zero exit only. Related upstream threads: #91097, #62531, #115163.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

1) Capture the spawn's stderr/exit code to the action log when a restart fails. 2) Make "stop success -> pull back up" a guaranteed two-phase step, or add an official pull-up helper that does not depend on schtasks.exe (which security software can block on Windows).


### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

prs.title: fix(kanban): a board-scoped dispatch fence (board.json "dispatch": false)
prs.body:
## What

A **board-scoped dispatch fence**: a board whose `board.json` carries `"dispatch": false`
is never served by the kanban dispatcher, and the flag fails closed at BOTH gates the
dispatcher has.

* **enumeration** — `kanban_db.list_dispatch_boards()` is the dispatcher's own board
  list. It drops the fenced board, so `tick_once_for_board` is never called for it.
  `list_boards()` is unchanged: a fenced board stays VISIBLE in
  `hermes kanban boards list` / the dashboard — it is simply never spawned from.
* **the per-tick spawn guard** — `kanban_db_dispatch.dispatch_once()` resolves the board
  it is actually against (the `board=` kwarg, else the board the OPEN CONNECTION belongs
  to) and returns `DispatchResult(skipped_board_disabled=True)` **before** the tick lock,
  the reclaim phase and every claim. So a caller that bypasses enumeration — the CLI
  `hermes kanban --board <estate> dispatch` — still cannot spawn a card from it. A
  refused pass leaves the card `ready` with 0 runs and prints
  `Refused: board is NOT dispatch-enabled (estate/scratch board)`.

`board.json` gains `"dispatch"`, default **true at read time** (absent / `None` /
unrecognised = admitted), so every board that predates the key is unchanged and an
unrelated write does not materialise it. Set it at birth with
`hermes kanban boards create <slug> --no-dispatch`, or later with
`hermes kanban boards set-dispatch <slug> on|off`.

Also closed here, measured on a live worker: **archiving is not durable while a worker's
env pins its store path.** The pinned worker's next `connect()` mints an empty
`kanban.db` back at the archived slug's directory, which used to read as
`archived=False` and re-enter the dispatch set. `kanban_db.board_is_archived_stub()`
refuses to admit a minted directory sitting beside an `_archived/<slug>-<epoch>` copy —
including the board's own `archived` tombstone once a store has been minted beside it —
so a mint can no longer undo an archive. An explicit
`hermes kanban boards create <slug>` is the sanctioned re-admission.

## Why

Measured 2026-09-29: a SEV1/failure card redirected to a "scratch" board was spawned by
the fleet dispatcher (`~/.hermes/logs/gateway.log` 18:12:16
`kanban dispatcher [failure-acceptance-t4ffa46e3]: spawned=1`) at the reserved-tranche
priority 999000, while the board held 13 ready phantom cards. A redirect to a normal
board is not isolation: the dispatcher serves every non-archived board. This is the
board-level admission flag that makes a rehearsal/estate board safe BY CONSTRUCTION.

## Test plan

`tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_estate_board_dispatch.py` (9 cases):

* a ready card on an estate board spawns NOTHING — `skipped_board_disabled is True`,
  `spawned == []`, the spy `spawn_fn` is NEVER called — with a negative control: the
  identical card shape on an unflagged board still spawns;
* the refusal holds when the tick names the board directly and when it is resolved off
  the connection (`HERMES_KANBAN_BOARD` pinned, no `board=` kwarg);
* `_KanbanDispatcher.tick_once()` visits the live board and never the estate one;
* `list_dispatch_boards()` drops it while `list_boards()` still shows it;
* the archived-slug resurrection guard (`board_is_archived_stub`) and the sanctioned
  re-create;
* the flag defaults on, round-trips both ways, is not materialised by an unrelated write,
  and the `set-dispatch` verb admits and excludes.

`scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_estate_board_dispatch.py` → 9 passed,
0 failed.

prs.title: fix(cli): a resumed session's model follows the profile config, not a stale cached pin
prs.body:
`sessions.model` is written at session creation from whatever `model.default` said at that instant, so it is a CACHE of the config default rather than a record of user intent. `_restore_session_model` (`hermes_cli/cli_model_switch_mixin.py`) restored that cached value unconditionally on every resume, so a settled change to a profile's `model.default` never reached sessions that had already cached the old value — with no warning and no repair. This PR makes the reconciliation the invariant and gives it the config knob to control it.

## Mechanism (current `main`)

- `hermes_cli/cli_model_switch_mixin.py::_restore_session_model` — on resume it calls `stored_session_route(...)` and assigns `self.model = stored_model` from the row whenever the row has a model and the CLI got no `-m`. Nothing there distinguishes a model a user picked from the config default of the day.
- The row's model is written at creation from the then-current `model.default`, and nothing re-derives it when config changes.
- Net effect: change a profile's `model.default` and every session that had already cached the old default keeps running the old model on resume.

## Change

A stored model is now honoured only when the row records a deliberate pick — and the reconciliation is operator-configurable.

1. **`session.model_policy`** (new knob; root or per-lane `config.yaml`, inheriting exactly like `model.default` because it is read from the same resolved config `load_cli_config()` produces):

   ```yaml
   session:
     model_policy: follow_config   # default
   ```

   - `follow_config` *(default)* — a stored model is a cache: honoured only for a row that records a deliberate pick (the route stamp below) **and** that came from an interactive source; everything else reconciles to the resolved config default.
   - `never_pin` — no stored model is ever restored; config always wins.

   An unknown value is a **config error**, never a silent fallback: `resolve_session_model_policy()` raises `SessionModelPolicyError`, and `validate_config_structure()` reports it as an `error` `ConfigIssue` (so `hermes doctor` and the startup check name it instead of a session that simply will not open). Only an absent/`null` value means "unset".

2. **The repair no longer restamps the route it just rejected.** A `provider` key beside the model IS pick-provenance, so writing the config's provider back onto the reconciled row turned it into a permanent "a user chose this" and handed the pin straight back at the next config change. The repaired row now records the model that actually ran and **deletes** the stale route keys (top-level and nested `gateway_runtime`), so it stays a cache and reconciles again next time.

3. **Non-interactive sources never pin** — `kanban`, `cron`, `oneshot`, `bot_peer_dm`, `peer`, `webhook`, `delegation`, `subagent`, `background_review`: no user was present to choose, so a stray route key cannot resurrect a stale pin. A resumed **one-shot** (`hermes_cli/oneshot.py::_apply_stored_session_runtime`) treats the stored route as a cache too, so `hermes -q --resume` cannot restore a pin either. A source this change does not know falls back to the conservative route check (honour the stored model), so an unknown surface is never silently clobbered.

4. **Pick-provenance is unchanged** (and already written by every deliberate switch): a `provider` at the top level of `model_config` or under its nested `gateway_runtime`, written by the CLI's `_persist_model_switch_to_session`, the messaging gateway's `SessionDB.update_session_model(provider=...)`, and the TUI/desktop's `_runtime_model_config`. That stamp is the only thing that authorises a stored model ≠ the config default.

5. **The RETENTION pin is not touched.** `sessions.pinned` (col 47, `set_session_pinned`, `hermes_state_sessions.py:992`) is a *different* thing that shares the name: `sessions.model` / `model_config` is ROUTING, `sessions.pinned` is RETENTION. Nothing here reads or writes it, so prune/archive exemption keeps working — "do not pin models implicitly" must not break it.

When the profile config names no default there is nothing to reconcile against, so the ordinary stored-route restore runs unchanged, preserving its credential re-resolution and its in-place `agent.switch_model` swap — except under `never_pin`, where a stored model is never restored at all.

## Relation to existing reports

This is the CLI resume seam. It shares the symptom with #101514 (a profile session is pinned to its stored model on resume) but fixes a **different root cause**: #101514 describes the gateway seam (`tui_gateway/server.py` `_stored_session_runtime_overrides` / `_sync_agent_model_with_config`), whereas this change is `hermes_cli/cli_model_switch_mixin.py::_restore_session_model`. The two are complementary. #89084 asks for the same "follow config on resume" property as a config option; this delivers it — plus the config option (`session.model_policy`) that asks for.

I searched for existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate (`gh search prs --repo NousResearch/hermes-agent "session model resume"`) and found none matching this file or seam.

## Verification

Red→green at the PR head (`2996c2bd69c9d2d28bf8d7a9ce7038a64e633cdb`; its code commit is `e141e5110c7fd6376211375a9966726b01bb4b70` — the tip adds one docs-only commit) with the repo's own runner:

- `tests/hermes_cli/test_session_model_follows_config.py` → **28 passed**. New cases: a stale cached pin is reconciled **and repaired in the store** so it cannot return (including on a *second* config change), a stamped deliberate pick survives, every non-interactive source is a cache even with a route key, `never_pin` ignores every stored model, and an unknown knob value is refused.
- Red-first, both ways: (a) with the base tree the file is a collection error, and (b) with only the pre-fix repair restored (route restamped instead of deleted) the two "the pin cannot return" tests fail — so they exercise real behaviour, not a mirror.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_resume_model_restore.py`, `test_oneshot_resume.py`, `test_model_persist_one_shape.py`, `test_model_switch_reasoning_flag.py`, `tests/tui_gateway/test_custom_provider_session_persistence.py` → unchanged failure sets against the same files on the base tree (the 8 failures are pre-existing in this sandbox, identical in both arms).
- Regression sweep, per-file isolated (each file its own process and `HERMES_HOME`, the runner's isolation model) over 146 files of the CLI/config surface — `tests/hermes_cli/test_config*.py`, `test_cli_init.py`, `test_oneshot*.py`, `test_resume*.py`, `test_model*.py`, `test_session*.py`: **identical failure sets on both arms** (214 ids at the head, 215 at the base). The only delta is a single id that fails in *both* arms and is merely labelled `ERROR` on one and `FAILED` on the other (`test_session_owner_backfill.py`, which trips the harness's real-home file-I/O guard in either tree).
- Live before/after against the live tree's own `_restore_session_model` (live install venv, real `SessionDB` row, config default `deepseek-flash`, stored `deepseek-v4-pro`): **before** → `deepseek-v4-pro` restored and the row left as-is; **after** → `deepseek-flash`, the row repaired to `deepseek-flash` with the stale route deleted, and the override warned on stderr. Under `never_pin` the same deliberate-pick row is ignored; an unknown policy value raises `SessionModelPolicyError`.

Authored with AI assistance (Hermes Agent); diff verified manually.

prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Keep the tool category visible inside provider pickers, and make checklist confirmation explicitly apply to the whole selection.

In `hermes tools` / `hermes setup tools`, a user can leave the global checklist cursor on **Vision / Image Analysis** and press Enter, then see a provider menu containing image-generation choices. The batch behavior is intentional: Enter confirms every checked toolset, and setup proceeds only for selected toolsets that still need configuration. However, `_configure_tool_category()` prints its category heading **before** curses opens, while the actual radiolist title is only `Choose a provider:` / `Select provider:`. Curses clears the heading, leaving no visible indication that the subsequent menu is for Image Generation rather than the focused checklist row.

This fixes the missing context without changing batch selection, readiness, provider routing, or configuration persistence.

## Related work / duplicate search

Searched open and closed issues/PRs using the global-config menu text, Vision/image-generation/menu symptoms, checklist/context terms, and provider-picker/title terms. No direct matching fix found.

Related merged #67230 (salvage of #54639) intentionally configures selected-but-unready tools in global/per-platform flows; this PR preserves that behavior. #93770's setup back/cancel navigation is also preserved. First-install duplicate-prompt work (#109445, #24077, #39092) addresses a different problem.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking UI/context fix)
- [x] Tests

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/tools_config_providers.py`: include the category name in the actual curses title for setup and reconfigure. Category-specific setup wording is retained. The shared path covers every provider category, not just image generation.
- `hermes_cli/curses_ui.py`: clarify `ENTER apply all selections` in checklists and the equivalent numbered fallback guidance. No input-handling changes.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_tools_config_menu_context.py`: two parameterized behavior contracts exercise real menu rendering/key handling against an in-memory screen: category identity survives the curses clear, and batch confirmation is explained without dropping selected toolsets. Provider metadata/key setup are isolated; interactive selectors are not stubbed.

Production change: four lines of displayed text, with no new dependencies or config keys.

## Reproduction / before and after

On upstream main `0eeba2d7a2632e11cc72d586ae61ca317664eb40`:

1. Have Vision available and Image Generation enabled but requiring provider setup.
2. Open `hermes setup tools` → `Configure all platforms (global)`.
3. Leave Vision and Image Generation checked, navigate the cursor to Vision, and press Enter.
4. Before: the subsequent curses menu says only `Choose a provider:` and contains image-generation choices.

prs.title: fix(cron): a profile with no model of its own inherits the host default
prs.body:
## What

A cron job created in a **named profile** whose `config.yaml` carries no `model:` block dies before
it can spawn. Two arms, one symptom:

**Arm 1 — the scheduler raises instead of falling back.** `_load_cron_job_config`
(`cron/scheduler.py`) resolves the run's model from the *active profile's* config only
(`load_user_config_effective` reads that one file — profiles are self-contained), then raises
`RuntimeError: … has no model configured (job.model=None, HERMES_MODEL='', config.yaml model.default
missing or empty)`.

**Arm 2 — `pinned=True` silently pins nothing.** `create_job` locks `_main_model_pin()`'s
`(None, None)` onto the job when the profile has no resolvable main model, so it returns `success`
while persisting a **dead, unpinned** job. Same silent-failure class.

## Fix

- `cron/jobs.py`
  - `host_default_model(active_home)` reads the **HOST root** config's `model.default` + provider
    (`get_default_hermes_root()`), consulted only when the active home names no model of its own.
  - `_main_model_pin()` inherits it, and passes the host provider as `requested` to
    `resolve_runtime_provider` (without it the provider resolve raises `AuthError` in a profile with
    no `model.provider`).
  - `create_job` and `_apply_pin_update` **refuse** (`ValueError`, naming the profile whose store it
    is) when a pin resolves no model at all, instead of persisting an inert job.
- `cron/scheduler.py` — `_load_cron_job_config` falls back to the host default (model **and**
  provider) so an unpinned one-shot runs; the raise now names the profile's store and fires only
  when **no** model resolves anywhere.
- `tools/cronjob_tools.py` — surface the pin refusal as a tool error.

## Why host fallback

The host root config is where the operator's default lives; a named profile with no `model:` of its
own has no default to run unpinned jobs on. Reading the host root is the same layer the root
profile's own jobs use, so an unpinned job in a profile behaves like an unpinned job in the root.
A profile that *does* set `model:` is untouched (a regression test pins that).

## Tests

`tests/cron/test_cron_model_host_fallback.py` — 7 regression tests (scheduler inherits host model;
profile model still wins; raise names the profile and only fires when nothing resolves; pin inherits
host model+provider; pin refuses instead of persisting a dead job; pinned create locks the host
model).

- new suite: **7 passed**
- `tests/cron/test_cron_pinned_job_fallback.py` + `tests/cron/test_cron_provider_pin.py`:
  **25 passed** (no regression)

prs.title: feat(desktop): configurable session-source exclusions for sidebar recents + search
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

The Desktop sidebar's "recent sessions" slice and the Cmd+Shift+F session search mix in A2A sessions (`source='a2a'`). The built-in `SIDEBAR_EXCLUDED_SOURCES` already drops `cron`, `kanban`, `subagent`, `tool` and the messaging platforms — A2A is the one machine source missing from that list, and there was no way to exclude it without editing the constant.

A2A conversations are machine-to-machine dispatches, not interactive chats: on a host that runs A2A peers they crowd out the recents page (measured on one always-on worker: A2A alone was 35% of the last 500 sessions, A2A + cron 66%). This adds a configurable exclusion list so the sidebar and session search stay shaped around interactive chats without forking the constant.

Design: one config key, read through the existing Desktop config record, merged **on top of** the built-in constant rather than replacing it. Additive, user-controllable, zero backend work.

## Related Issue

Fixes #108003

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py` — new `sessions.exclude_sources` (default `["a2a"]`; `[]` restores today's behavior, absent key → built-in list only).
- `apps/desktop/src/lib/session-source.ts` — `configuredExcludeSources()` reads + normalizes the key out of the raw config record; `mergeExcludedSources()` merges it on top of a built-in list (deduped; returns the built-in array identity when nothing is configured).
- `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-session-list-actions.ts` — the recents fetch passes the merged list as `recents_exclude` (was the constant).
- `apps/desktop/src/api/sessions.ts` — `searchSessions(query, profile?, excludeSources?)` sends `exclude_sources` (upstream has since added the profile argument); previously only `q` was sent, so session search ignored every exclusion.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/use-server-session-search.ts` — the debounced search hook reads `sessions.exclude_sources` out of the shared config record and passes it through, the same pattern the recents slice uses in `use-session-list-actions.ts`. `index.tsx` is deliberately untouched: code health caps the sidebar file at its `main` value and it is already over target.
- Tests: `session-source.test.ts`, `use-session-list-actions.test.tsx`, `api/sessions.test.ts` (9 new cases), plus a `QueryClientProvider` wrapper in the two sidebar tests that mount `ChatSidebar` (it now reads the config record).

**Zero backend changes** — `GET /api/profiles/sessions/sidebar` (`recents_exclude`, `hermes_cli/web_routers/profiles.py:419`) and `GET /api/sessions/search` (`exclude_sources`, `hermes_cli/web_routers/sessions.py:257`) already accept and honor both.

## How to Test

1. `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run --project ui src/lib/session-source.test.ts src/api/sessions.test.ts src/app/session/hooks/use-session-list-actions.test.tsx`
   → **Test Files 3 passed (3) · Tests 53 passed (53)** — 9 new cases: config read + normalization, malformed/absent fallback, merge + dedupe, built-in identity preserved, recents fetch carries the merged list (and falls back without the key / with `[]`), search sends `exclude_sources`, search omits it when empty.
2. `cd apps/desktop && npm run typecheck` → clean (`tsc -p .` / `tsconfig.electron` / `tsconfig.e2e`).
3. `cd apps/desktop && npx eslint src/lib/session-source.ts src/lib/session-source.test.ts src/api/sessions.ts src/api/sessions.test.ts src/app/session/hooks/use-session-list-actions.ts src/app/session/hooks/use-session-list-actions.test.tsx src/app/chat/sidebar/index.tsx src/app/chat/sidebar/chat-sidebar.integration.test.tsx src/app/chat/sidebar/gateway-groups.test.tsx` → clean.
4. `bash scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_config.py` → **171 passed, 4 skipped** (the new key is a config default; no existing assertion enumerates `sessions.*`).
5. Full UI suite: **785 of 786 files pass** — `src/store/voice-prefs.test.ts` fails 2 cases, and it reproduces identically on a pristine `origin/main` checkout (2 failed | 5 passed) without this branch, so it is a pre-existing upstream failure unrelated to this change.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide
- [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits (`feat(config):`, `feat(desktop):`)
- [x] I searched for existing PRs — this supersedes the closed #84322, which bundled unrelated agent / dashboard-auth / TUI changes; this PR carries only the sidebar + search feature
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this issue (no unrelated commits)
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` — not run in full: this change adds a config default only, so I ran `tests/hermes_cli/test_config.py` (121 passed, 4 skipped). Happy to run the full suite on request.
- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 26.5 — unit tests, typecheck and lint on this branch; the Desktop-app manual check is listed under Screenshots / Logs and is still to be attached.

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — `sessions.exclude_sources` is documented in `website/docs/user-guide/sessions.md` (Session Sources). Required, not optional: the docs-drift ratchet (`tests/ci/test_docs_drift.py`) fails any new config key that no docs page mentions.
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — N/A: that file has no `sessions:` section today
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — N/A
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the compatibility guide — N/A: renderer-side filtering only, no platform-specific code
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — N/A

## Screenshots / Logs

Command output for steps 1-5 above is the code-level evidence. Backend side, verified live against a real `state.db` (43 A2A sessions) through the same access path the two endpoints use (`_open_session_db_for_profile` → `list_sessions_rich` / `search_messages`):

```
sidebar recents (same call as /api/profiles/sessions/sidebar?recents_exclude=...)
  without exclusions: 20 rows {'tui': 5, 'cli': 3, 'cron': 12}
  with exclusions   : 20 rows {'tui': 12, 'cli': 6, 'todo-launch-84673e37': 1, 'todo-launch-55cee1b1': 1}
session search (same call as /api/sessions/search?q=A2A)
  without exclude_sources : 100 hits {'cli': 51, 'tui': 45, 'a2a': 2, 'cron': 2}
  with exclude_sources=a2a: 100 hits {'cli': 53, 'tui': 45, 'cron': 2}
```

So the exclusions really do change which rows surface: once the machine sources are dropped the page refills with interactive sessions. On this host the A2A rows are older than its cron/tui traffic, so its recents page is not A2A-dominated — the 35% / 66% figures in the description come from a busier always-on A2A worker.

The Desktop-app manual check is still to be attached: on a host with A2A traffic, the recents list before/after (with and without `[A2A]` rows) and a Cmd+Shift+F search for a term that only exists inside an A2A session (no result after the change, hit after setting `sessions.exclude_sources: []`).

## Follow-up

- A `Filter → Sources` submenu that edits `sessions.exclude_sources` from the UI is intentionally not in this PR (it adds a config write path + i18n); will open it separately.
- Related, not overlapping: #68123 fixes excluded rows re-entering local recents through the keep-semantics path in the same file; this PR only changes where the exclusion list comes from. Happy to rebase if #68123 lands first.

prs.title: fix(mcp): a shutdown-race scheduling error is teardown, not a server failure
prs.body:
## Problem

A gateway restart parks every managed MCP server:

```
WARNING tools.mcp_tool: MCP server 'virlo' failed after 5 reconnection attempts, parking; will self-probe
every 300s until it recovers (state: degraded → parked): RuntimeError: cannot schedule new futures after shutdown
```

Production observation (long-lived gateway, 7 remote MCP servers, 48h window of `errors.log`):

- 77 identical park WARNINGs, one per server per restart, all clustered inside gateway restarts (e.g. a restart at 13:06 produced the seven `virlo`/`cloudflare`/`x-docs`/`aixbt`/`blockscout`/`crypto-com`/`vfat` parks between 13:07 and 13:11).
- Each park cost 5 reconnect attempts plus backoff for a process that is already going away.
- The WARNING text says `degraded → parked`, so the error log reads as a real MCP outage on a machine whose servers were healthy.

## Reproduction

The error is a scheduling failure, so it needs no network: the code under test reaches the park on its own.

```python
from tools.mcp_tool import MCPServerTask
from tools.mcp_tool_server_run import _RetryBudget

task = MCPServerTask("t")
task._ever_connected = True
task._reconnect_retries = 0
await task._on_transport_error(
    RuntimeError("cannot schedule new futures after shutdown"), _RetryBudget())
```

Before this change: retries are charged and, with the budget exhausted, the server parks with the WARNING above (the first two tests in the new file fail on `main`, the third — the park with an exhausted budget — reproduces the exact production line).

## Fix

`tools/mcp_tool_server_run.py`:

- New `_is_shutdown_scheduling_error()` delegating to `tools.interpreter_shutdown.interpreter_shutting_down` — the shared predicate for this class (both CPython message variants: `cannot schedule new futures after shutdown` / `... after interpreter shutdown`, plus `sys.is_finalizing()`), already used by cron delivery, tool submission and the conversation retry (#55924/#58720).
- `_on_transport_error` checks it right after unwrapping the exception group, before classification: log DEBUG and `return False` (end the run loop), mirroring the existing `self._shutdown_event.is_set()` branch two lines below. Guarding the single entry point covers both the initial-connect and reconnect ladders and the park path.

Whole-bug-class, not one site: the MCP ladder is the sibling call path of the sites that already had this guard; the initial-connect ladder, the reinstated-stdio branch and both park sites all sit behind the same check.

## Validation

- `pytest tests/tools/test_mcp_shutdown_scheduling_error.py` — 4 passed (2 parametrized shutdown variants, the exhausted-budget park case, plus a control asserting a genuine `ConnectionError` still charges the ladder).
- Regression: `pytest tests/tools/test_mcp_reconnect_log_hygiene.py tests/tools/test_mcp_rapid_drop_budget.py tests/tools/test_mcp_parked_self_probe.py tests/tools/test_mcp_park_log_dedupe.py tests/tools/test_mcp_cancelled_error_propagation.py tests/tools/test_mcp_shutdown_scheduling_error.py` — 18 passed.

fixes #136957

prs.title: fix(bootstrap): only an entry point finishes a source update or re-execs
prs.body:
## What

`hermes_bootstrap` is imported by every entry-point module, so its module body also runs for a plain `import`. Two things in that body are only correct for a process that is *becoming* the CLI:

- finishing an armed source update (`prepare_launch`), and
- `os.execv`-ing the relaunched interpreter.

Measured 2026-10-01: a unit-test module imported the live CLI; the bootstrap completed a real source update against the live checkout and then `os.execv`-ed the pytest session away. Instrumentation saw three such routes from one test module (2026-10-04).

## Change

Both blocks are now gated on `_launched_as_entry_point()`, which reads the **importer's** frame. (`__name__` of `hermes_bootstrap` itself is `hermes_bootstrap` either way, so it cannot be used.)

A launch is one of:

- the module that imports us **is** the program — `python main.py`, `python -m hermes_cli.main`, `runpy` with `run_name="__main__"`; or
- the module that imports us was **itself imported directly by the program** — a console-script wrapper's `from hermes_cli.main import main`, and `python -c "import <launcher>"`.

The second clause is required by the product: `relaunch_command` reconstructs a relaunch for `argv[0] == "-c"` (`hermes_cli/venv_sync.py`), so that launch mode is first-class and must keep the tail.

Anything deeper is a library caller inside a longer-running process (a test module under pytest) and is withheld.

The withheld path is not silent: when armed completion state is present it prints exactly one line naming the command that finishes the update, suppressed under pytest. `recover_if_needed`, `activate_dependencies`, the Happy Eyeballs socket shim and the scratch TMPDIR keep running for **every** importer.

## Tests

New `tests/test_bootstrap_launch_tail_guard.py` — a fake tree with stub modules and a recording `venv_sync`, run in child processes with `-S` so the fake tree's modules win over the interpreter's editable finder:

- a module *inside another program* imports the CLI → the tail does **not** run (the incident route);
- `-m hermes_cli.main`, `-c "import hermes_cli.main"` (the launcher mode above) and a script keep the tail;
- with a relaunch armed, an import neither re-execs nor warns;
- armed completion state is announced once on the withheld path, and suppressed under pytest;
- **negative control:** with the guard forced open, the incident route *does* run the tail — the assertions bite.

Red before this change (4 failed / 3 passed on the pre-change bytes); green after (7 passed) on the checkout's own test environment (CPython 3.14.7, pytest 9.1.1).

- `tests/test_bootstrap_launch_tail_guard.py`: **7 passed**
- `tests/test_hermes_bootstrap.py`: **27 passed, 12 skipped** (identical to the pre-change baseline)
- `tests/pm/test_source_update_launch.py`: **16 passed** (the 5 tests that drive the real bootstrap — `test_real_bootstrap_reexecs_before_app_imports[script|module|command]`, `test_failed_launch_completion_degrades_to_a_warning[argv0|argv1]` — were 5 passed before the change as well)

## Scope / rollback

One file (`hermes_bootstrap.py`) plus one new test module. Rollback is a revert of this commit.

prs.title: Characters typed while the CLI starts up are kept in the composer instead of dropped (Copilot CLI 1.0.98 port)
prs.body:
Characters you type while the classic CLI is starting up now show up in the composer instead of vanishing.

**Inspired by Copilot CLI 1.0.98** ([changelog](https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/blob/main/changelog.md#1098---2026-10-14)): "Keep ordinary characters typed while the input box is still coming up at startup, instead of dropping them".

## Root cause
Before prompt_toolkit takes the tty, `cli.py` asks the terminal for its background color (OSC 11 query fenced with DA1) to choose light or dark mode. `tty.setcbreak()` defaults to `TCSAFLUSH`, and the restore used `TCSAFLUSH` too, so the kernel threw away whatever the user had typed in the first ~2 s. The 50 ms drain loop then read and discarded anything left over.

## Changes
- `hermes_cli/cli_render.py::_query_osc11_background`: switches modes with `TCSANOW`/`TCSADRAIN` (no flush), keeps every byte the probe reads, and hands them to `_keep_typeahead`. That strips terminal replies (OSC, CSI, a trailing partial escape) and keeps printable text only.
- Enter and other control bytes are **dropped**: a keystroke typed before the prompt appeared cannot submit anything. The text lands as a draft.
- `seed_startup_typeahead(buffer)` fills the composer when the input area is built. It assigns a `Document` because `insert_text()` schedules completion and no event loop is running yet; the paste-collapse heuristic baseline is seeded too.
- Late OSC 11 replies are still consumed the way #40250 needs: the same bytes are read, then filtered instead of flushed.

## Ours vs theirs
Copilot is an Ink/Node app whose input component mounts late. Hermes loses the keystrokes in one specific place (its own terminal probe flushing the tty), so the fix lives there. Nothing gets buffered globally.

## Validation
| | `origin/main` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Live tmux: type `typedearly` 0.4 s after `hermes chat`, check the composer after startup | placeholder only, text lost | `❯ typedearly` |
| Live: type more once the prompt is up | `❯ +late` | `❯ typedearly+late` |
| Live: type `hi there` + Enter during startup | — | `❯ hi there` as a draft, nothing submitted |
| Live, OSC 11 probe skipped (`HERMES_TUI_THEME=dark`) | `❯ typedearly` (proves the probe is the culprit) | `❯ typedearly` |
| `test_keystrokes_typed_during_startup_probe_reach_the_composer` (real PTY child, real OSC 11/DA1 reply) | **FAILED** | passed |
| `tests/hermes_cli/test_cli_light_mode.py` (incl. #40250 leak guards, DA1-fence PTY tests) | — | 27 passed |
| prompt-stash / rapid-enter-paste / input-area suites | — | 44 passed |

`scripts/check --only health` passes. The `cli_tui_mixin.py` facade stays at its line cap; the new behavior lives in `cli_render.py`.

prs.title: fix(kanban): a completion-time phantom scan must not flag a sibling board's card
prs.body:
## What

`_flag_phantom_prose_refs` — the advisory post-commit scan that flags unresolvable `t_<hex>` prose references in a completion handoff — resolved every reference against the **one board the completing connection was open on**.

A real card on a **sibling** board is a cross-board handoff, which is normal on a multi-board host, so a legitimate reference was durably recorded as `suspected_hallucinated_references`. Measured: a live ops-board child named in a defcon-board card's completion summary was written as a phantom.

## Change

The scan is now board-aware:

- `board_for_store_path()` / `board_for_connection()` — the connection's own board, read off the open file's path (the inverse of `kanban_db_path`). The ambient current board is deliberately not used: a `--board` override or a worker's injected `HERMES_KANBAN_DB` pin can disagree with it, and a pin can name a database no board claims.
- `_prose_ref_search_boards()` — the completing board first, then every other registered board, deterministically.
- `_missing_task_ids_everywhere()` — an id is a phantom only when **no** reachable board carries it; sibling stores are opened `mode=ro` and only when the store file already exists, so the scan can never mint a stray `<slug>.db`.
- The durable payload now names `boards_searched` (and `matched_elsewhere` when a phantom coexists), so an operator can tell a real cross-board card from an invented id without re-deriving the resolver.
- `_scan_prose_for_phantom_ids()`, whose only caller this replaces, is removed.

## Tests

`tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_phantom_refs_cross_board.py`:

- against the pre-change file: **2 failed, 1 passed**
- with the change: **3 passed**

It pins both directions — a reference to a card on a sibling board is *not* flagged; a genuinely nonexistent id *is* flagged and the payload names the boards searched — plus the existing `verified_cards` exemption.

A control run of the broader kanban files against pristine `main` shows the same single pre-existing failure as the patched tree (`tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_db.py::test_infrastructure_spawn_refusal_never_charges_the_card`), i.e. this change introduces no regression.

prs.title: fix(desktop): keep find-in-page off the DOM (CSS Custom Highlight API)
prs.body:
### What does this PR do?

Replaces the renderer-side find engine's painting path. `apps/desktop/src/lib/find-in-page-scope.ts`
painted each match by rewriting the DOM it searched — splitting matching text nodes, inserting
`<mark class="find-hit">`, and `normalize()`-ing on clear. This PR paints matches with the **CSS
Custom Highlight API** (`CSS.highlights` + `Range`s) and never writes to the DOM, and it takes editor
content out of the search scope.

Two reasons the node-wrapping engine has to go.

**1. It fights everything that owns the scope's DOM.** The scope is the active `[data-chat-surface]`:
a React-owned transcript that re-renders on every streamed delta, plus a live `contentEditable`
composer. Injecting nodes into a tree React re-allocates meant the walker had to re-walk and re-wrap
the *whole* scope on every mutation to keep highlights consistent, and splitting and replacing text
nodes under a live caret is exactly the external DOM write the editing machinery is not required to
survive — the mechanism behind #134070's composer direction/caret flip.

**2. The cost is unbounded in the thing the user does most.** Measured with the desktop's own
Electron build (40.10.2 / Chromium 142) on a deterministic fixture the size the DOM budget in
`thread/list.tsx` allows — 875,824 characters, 41,977 text nodes, 42,281 elements — three runs,
shipped engine vs. this PR:

| metric | shipped node-wrapping engine | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| query with no matches | 28–33 ms | 10–17 ms (first scan after page load: ~110 ms, V8 warm-up) |
| search `the` (8,011 matches) | 320–345 ms | 222–278 ms |
| search `e` (99,759 matches) | 1.20–1.36 s | **58–92 ms** |
| three more keystrokes, same query | 6.1–8.7 s | **263–400 ms** |
| 20 × Enter / Ctrl+G steps | 2.7–6.1 s (≈0.1–0.3 s per step) | **0.1–0.3 ms** |
| DOM elements after the search | 142,050 (**+99,769**) | 42,291 (**+10**) |
| streamed deltas served in 8 s while the bar is open | **2–4** (≈2–4 s per delta) | **68–267** |
| clearing the search | 0.57–1.13 s | 0.2 ms |

The last two rows are the user-visible failure: with the bar open on a long session the observer's
re-wrap runs synchronously on every streamed delta, so the renderer's main thread is saturated for as
long as the assistant keeps answering. `desktop.log` shows what that looks like from the outside —
the renderer is reported unresponsive and then killed/crashes:

```
[renderer:main] render-process-gone reason=killed exitCode=1073807364
[renderer:main] render-process-gone reason=crashed exitCode=-1073741205
[renderer:main] suppressing reload: 3 crashes within 60000ms (likely a crash loop)
[renderer:main] renderer terminated while live (reason=crashed, exit code -1073741205); surfacing recovery page
```

Ranges are inert: React never sees them, a re-render only detaches some of them, and one cheap
re-scan repairs the set. Stepping reuses the same `Range` objects, so `Enter`/`Ctrl+G` costs one range
instead of re-walking the page.

### Related Issue

Fixes #134070.

- **The composer half:** the walker no longer writes into the scope's DOM at all, so it cannot detach
  the text node a live caret points into — the reported direction flip and caret jump are removed
  outright, and pinned by a test that sets a caret inside the composer, searches, and asserts the
  selection and the draft are untouched.
- **The counting half:** editor content leaves the scope (`[contenteditable]`, `textarea`,
  `[role="textbox"]` join `script/style/noscript` and the find bar's own `[role="search"]` in
  `SKIPPED_SELECTOR`), so the match counter no longer counts the composer's own draft — the class of
  "matches reported that nothing on screen can show" the issue describes.
- **Not claimed:** rows outside the mounted transcript window are still neither counted nor
  highlightable (find searches the DOM that exists). That is the windowed-transcript limitation of
  `thread/list.tsx`, unchanged by this PR, and worth its own issue if it is not already filed.

Not this bug: #70206 ("renderer crash / webContents became unresponsive on large sessions") is a
different root cause — a React duplicate-`toolCallId` key tripping the root error boundary — fixed in
#92392. The log lines above are the *symptom* shape both issues share; this PR removes the find path's
contribution to it and does not claim #70206.

### Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

### Changes Made

- `apps/desktop/src/lib/find-in-page-scope.ts` — the engine. The public API is unchanged
  (`resolveCurrentFindScope`, `captureFindScope`, `currentFindScope`, `performScopedFind`,
  `releaseFindScope`, `ScopedFindResult`, `ScopedFindOptions`). Matches are collected with one
  `SHOW_TEXT` TreeWalker (no per-node `NodeFilter` callback; skip subtrees are collected once per
  scan) and published as `CSS.highlights` entries (`hermes-find`, `hermes-find-active`). The mutation
  watcher now only marks the scan dirty; the re-scan is throttled to one per 200 ms and no longer
  scrolls (a background re-render must not move the reader). `data-find-root` scope capture,
  keep-alive re-targeting, and the #81726 / #81778 behaviours are preserved.
- `apps/desktop/src/styles.css` — `::highlight(hermes-find)` and `::highlight(hermes-find-active)`.
  These are new: nothing in the tree ever styled `mark.find-hit`, so the browser's UA `<mark>` paint
  was the only highlight and the active match was **not** visually distinct. Highlights layer in
  registry-insertion order, so the module registers the active one last.
- `apps/desktop/src/test/jsdom.ts` + `vitest.setup.ts` — jsdom stand-in for the highlight registry
  (real Map/Set semantics) plus readers (`findHitTexts`, `findHitsWithin`, `activeFindHitText`). jsdom
  implements no highlight API; a test that needs the real paint belongs in a browser.
- `apps/desktop/src/lib/find-in-page-scope.test.ts` — assertions move from `mark.find-hit` to the
  registry, and the suite gains three contracts: *searching never modifies the transcript DOM*
  (byte-compare `innerHTML` before/after), *the composer and form fields are out of scope*, and *a
  caret inside the composer survives a search*.
- `apps/desktop/src/components/find-bar.test.tsx` — 30 `mark.find-hit` count assertions →
  `findHitsWithin(surface)`; the registry is process-wide, so `afterEach` now calls
  `releaseFindScope()` (a `document.body` wipe leaves stale ranges registered).

No dependency, config key, locale string or user-facing copy changes.

### How to Test

1. **Reproduction (before):** open a long session (the one in the log above is 9,261 messages /
   30 MB of text), press `Ctrl+F`, type a single letter such as `e`. The window stops responding while
   the assistant keeps streaming, and `logs/desktop.log` shows the `render-process-gone` / crash-loop
   lines above. On a long session, also type into the composer with the find bar open: the old engine
   could flip the composer's writing direction / move the caret (#134070).
2. **After:** the same search returns in tens of milliseconds, the DOM node count is unchanged, the
   composer keeps its caret and direction, and `Enter` / `Ctrl+G` step instantly through the matches.
3. **Tests** (from `apps/desktop/`):
   ```bash
   npx vitest run src/lib/find-in-page-scope.test.ts src/components/find-bar.test.tsx   # 83 passed
   node ../../node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit                 # exit 0
   node ../../node_modules/eslint/bin/eslint.js src/lib/find-in-page-scope.ts src/lib/find-in-page-scope.test.ts src/components/find-bar.test.tsx src/test/jsdom.ts vitest.setup.ts
   node ../../node_modules/prettier/bin/prettier.cjs --check <the five files>
   ```
   Do **not** use `npx tsc` here: the repo root is an npm workspace, so `npx` aborts with
   `ENOWORKSPACES` and tsc never runs (exit 0, zero diagnostics — reads as a clean pass and is not).
4. **Red on the base:** with `HEAD`'s engine in place, this assertion fails — the base inserts three
   `<mark class="find-hit">` elements into the searched DOM:

   ```js
   const before = surface.innerHTML
   performScopedFind(surface, 'needle', { forward: true, findNext: false })
   expect(surface.innerHTML).toBe(before)   // base: RED, this PR: green
   ```

   Same fixture, same assertion, both engines, real Electron 40.10.2:
   ```json
   {"base":  {"count": 3, "domUnchanged": false, "marks": 3, "registryRanges": 0},
    "fixed": {"count": 3, "domUnchanged": true,  "marks": 0, "registryRanges": 3}}
   ```

### Checklist

#### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits (`fix(desktop): …`)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) — no duplicate; the closest work, #94644 (unit tests for this lib), is complementary
- [x] My PR contains only changes related to this fix (the 6 files above; an unrelated `search-field.tsx` edit sitting in my working tree is **not** part of the commit)
- [ ] `pytest tests/ -q` — N/A for this diff: no Python file is touched (all six are `apps/desktop/**`). I ran the suite anyway on Windows 11 with a local Python 3.12 plus the pinned extras, from a copy of the checkout outside the Hermes home. The first pass was misleading and is superseded: that copy had carried a stale `.pytest_cache`, so the suite's home-isolation guard (`tests/home_io_guard.py`) refused reads of the copy's *old* absolute path and turned 41 files red (30 with test failures, 11 that never collected). With the caches excluded the guard never fires (0 hits), and the residue is 14 files — every one in a Python module this PR does not touch, with ordinary environment causes: missing optional modules (`snowballstemmer`, `nemo_relay`, `portalocker`), Windows temp-file locking (`WinError 32`), an LSP server binary exiting `0xC0000409`, timing/network flakiness, and one test-side `NameError` (`Path` undefined) in the repo's own test. No green Python run is claimed, and no CI run has started on this commit yet (0 check runs), so the suite has not been exercised by CI either.
- [x] `python scripts/check` — passes: `scripts/check: 12 checks, ok`, code-health ratchet `7 files vs main: 0 blocking, 0 advisory`. Note it wants a checkout free of stray profile-export archives: three `venv*` migration backups and `.cache/desktop-inputs/**` had to be moved out of my tree first — which is exactly what that guard asks for, and what a fresh CI checkout already satisfies.
