prs.title: fix(skills_sync): do not seed a category DESCRIPTION.md into a category the profile does not hold
prs.body:
On a profile opted out of bundled skills (`.no-bundled-skills`), only the
essential skills are considered, and the sole essential (`hermes-agent`) lives
under the `autonomous-ai-agents` category. When that skill is not materialised
locally — it is already in `.bundled_manifest` with no copy on disk, or it is
deferred to an external dir — the skill loop writes nothing for it, yet
`_seed_category_descriptions` still created the category dir unconditionally to
hold the bundled `DESCRIPTION.md`.

That leaves a stray top-level REAL directory in the lane's skills root —
`skills/autonomous-ai-agents/` containing nothing but `DESCRIPTION.md` — which
a lane drift/sync check reads as an extra real dir. Deleting it is not a fix:
the next sync (any lane session touching the profile) puts it straight back.

## Change

Gate the seed on the category dir already existing. The function runs *after*
the skill loop, so the parent dir exists iff the profile actually received a
member of that category:

```python
        if (only_dirs is not None and dest_desc.parent not in only_dirs) or dest_desc.exists():
            continue
        # Only seed into a category the profile actually holds. ...
        if not dest_desc.parent.is_dir():
            continue
        try:
            dest_desc.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
```

No member ⇒ no description ⇒ no stray dir. A category that *does* hold a
materialised skill still gets its `DESCRIPTION.md` re-seeded.

## Verification

- `py_compile` clean; `tests/tools/test_skills_sync.py` and
  `tests/tools/test_skills_runtime_cache.py`: 54 passed before and 54 passed
  after the change.
- On opted-out lanes (essential in the manifest with no copy on disk,
  `ABSENT → REALDIR['DESCRIPTION.md']` before), the patched writer leaves the
  category dir absent.
- Regression: a lane whose category dir *does* hold a materialised
  `hermes-agent` but whose `DESCRIPTION.md` was removed gets it re-seeded
  byte-identically to the bundled file.

Reproduced and diagnosed on macOS 26.5 (Hermes host install); no platform-
specific behaviour involved.

prs.title: fix(deps): bump dompurify 3.4.13 -> 3.4.16 (GHSA-6688-9rhm-gjv2, GHSA-p98j-92pf-mc4p)
prs.body:
## Problem

`dompurify` is pinned at `3.4.13` in **three** places, and that version is
vulnerable to two published advisories:

- [GHSA-6688-9rhm-gjv2](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6688-9rhm-gjv2)
  (2026-10-05) — `IN_PLACE` returns a force-removed rawtext root whose text can
  be re-parsed (XSS).
- [GHSA-p98j-92pf-mc4p](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-p98j-92pf-mc4p)
  (2026-09-30) — `IN_PLACE`: a node-removing `afterSanitize` hook leaves a
  detached subtree that is still returned.

Both are fixed in `3.4.16`.

`dompurify` is a **production** dependency of the desktop app
(`apps/desktop/package.json` → `src/` sanitizes assistant-rendered HTML), so
this is a runtime XSS surface, not just a build-time one.

Reproduction (root lockfile):

```
$ npm audit --json | jq '.vulnerabilities.dompurify'
{ "severity": "low", "range": "<3.4.16", ... }
```

The pin is duplicated so a single-location bump silently leaves the other
sites vulnerable:

| Site | File |
| --- | --- |
| direct dependency | `apps/desktop/package.json` |
| root override | `package.json` (`overrides.dompurify`) |
| website override | `website/package.json` (`overrides.dompurify`) |

The three copies are also why `npm audit fix --force` aborts with `EOVERRIDE`
today (npm refuses an override that does not textually match the direct
dependency it replaces — see #136475).

## Fix

Bump all three sites to `3.4.16` and refresh the resolved entries in the two
committed lockfiles (`package-lock.json`, `website/package-lock.json`). The
override and the direct dependency stay identical, so the `EOVERRIDE`
condition cannot be reintroduced.

Only the `dompurify` entries move; `3.4.16` has the same dependency metadata as
`3.4.13` (no `dependencies`, `optionalDependencies: {"@types/trusted-types": "^2.0.7"}`),
so no other node in either tree changes.

## Why not just bump the desktop dependency

Because the root/website overrides would keep resolving the vulnerable version
for the `^3.3.3` range (mermaid and friends pull it in transitively) — the same
bug class this repo has hit before with `js-yaml`/`aiohttp` (a fix that covers
one site only is rejected or lands half-applied).

## Validation

- Tarball integrity matches the registry:
  `sha512-sqo+pNp3qRhCIpbgRi1y8Tgk27Bo2Ry7w0dC1NBeNTdZChWjz9Xb/KOoZbRP/R6pQZ80Qw8YhXw13hWWBbMRnQ==`.
- Root tree: `npm ci --dry-run --ignore-scripts` → exit 0 (`added 1422 packages`).
- Website tree: `npm ci --dry-run --ignore-scripts` with the repo's required
  npm (`>=11.17.0`) → exit 0 (`added 1390 packages`).
- `npm audit --json` at the root no longer reports a `dompurify` entry.
- `grep -rn '3\.4\.13' package.json apps/desktop/package.json website/package.json package-lock.json website/package-lock.json` → no matches.

prs.title: fix(deps): bump concurrently 10.0.4 -> 10.0.6, clearing shell-quote 1.9.0 (GHSA-pqg4-j6r4-53mv)
prs.body:
## Problem

The root lockfile resolves `shell-quote@1.9.0` (via the desktop dev toolchain),
which is vulnerable to a **critical** advisory:

- [GHSA-pqg4-j6r4-53mv](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pqg4-j6r4-53mv) —
  `quote()` command injection via a line terminator (fixed in `1.11.0`).

`npm audit` also flags the carrier itself as critical, because `concurrently`
pins `shell-quote` **exactly** (`"shell-quote": "1.9.0"`), so no consumer range
can float it forward:

```
$ npm audit --json | jq '.vulnerabilities["shell-quote"]'
{ "severity": "critical",
  "range": "1.8.4 - 1.10.0",
  "fixAvailable": { "name": "concurrently", "version": "10.0.6", "isSemVerMajor": false },
  "effects": ["concurrently"] }
```

Adding an override would paper over a pin that upstream `concurrently` has
already fixed; the correct fix is to move the carrier.

## Fix

Bump the direct dev dependency `concurrently` `10.0.4` → `10.0.6` in
`apps/desktop/package.json` and refresh the two resolved lock entries. `10.0.6`
depends on `shell-quote@1.12.0`, so the vulnerable `1.9.0` node disappears from
the tree entirely (nothing else in the root lock requires `shell-quote`).

No other dependency of `concurrently` moves (`chalk 5.6.2`, `rxjs 7.8.2`,
`supports-color 10.2.2`, `tree-kill 1.2.2`, `yargs 18.0.0` are all unchanged).

## Validation

- Tarball integrity verified against the registry for both new versions:
  - `concurrently@10.0.6` → `sha512-qgICXXFp2/3nAebRLmxcINKEXM1mLK3ij/y31P02VTs/KIkddIeC05n73DxOXsXMB9LFSqNU1/na3lDlOhcbIw==`
  - `shell-quote@1.12.0` → `sha512-PcByqNyT/38F2kDNi006HAMRJaULuBzq/FOsw3qdZvX/GA9W/jamDaRskgHjubHiftXK5sIFxLNkvrXUwcof6Q==`
- `npm ci --dry-run --ignore-scripts` → exit 0 (`added 1422 packages`).
- `npm audit --json` → `vulnerabilities["concurrently"]` and
  `vulnerabilities["shell-quote"]` are both `null`; the reported `critical`
  count drops to 2 (from 4) with nothing new introduced.

---

prs.title: fix(install): activate the dependency generation when re-entering a caller
prs.body:
## What

The lazy-install handoff re-enters the caller's own `__main__` under the store interpreter. That interpreter boots cold — its own `site-packages` is the bare tool, and the committed dependency generation only reaches `sys.path` when the bootstrap activates it. `relaunch_command` prepended the project root and replayed the caller, but never activated the environment, so a handed-off caller that loads a dependency it declares before it can engage the runtime died at the handoff.

Measured with a caller run under the committed generation's interpreter, `import yaml` at module top, then the runtime import:

```
PROBE begin exe=.../environments/<gen>/venv/bin/python3.14 ver=3.14.7
PROBE yaml ok version=6.0.3
PROBE begin exe=.../tools/python-3.14.7-.../bin/python3 ver=3.14.7
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'yaml'
```

The same shape is why a missing parser could be mis-read as a corrupt config file by imports that shell through `hermes_constants`.

## Change

`relaunch_command` now activates the committed generation in the re-entry prefix, before the caller's code runs. A new `activate_relaunch_environment(project_root)` in `hermes_cli.venv_sync` performs the activation, so the re-entry keeps the environment the handoff would otherwise take away.

## Tests

`tests/pm/test_source_update_launch.py`:

- new `test_reexec_activates_generation_before_the_callers_own_imports` drives the emitted re-entry with a declared dependency loaded first — red on the previous code, green with the change;
- the existing re-entry tests (`test_real_bootstrap_reexecs_before_app_imports[script|module|command]`, `test_failed_launch_completion_degrades_to_a_warning`) still pass.

prs.title: feat(skills): deterministic tier ladder, and the flat skills index retired by default
prs.body:
## What this is

Two commits, stacked, each independently reviewable:

1. **The deterministic skill tier ladder** — profile-local > external/shared > project-local,
   replacing an ordering that let a repo checkout silently shadow fleet/user doctrine with a
   same-named skill.
2. **The flat skills index retired by default** — stacked on 1, because the ladder's tests assert on
   a rendered index and are pinned to the legacy renderer by the autouse fixture added here.

## Why the flat index goes

The per-call prompt built one `- name: description` line per visible skill under a `## Skills`
heading that told the agent to scan the list and load whatever looked relevant. That is a
keyword/search-shaped routing surface, and it:

- duplicates the curated hierarchical surface a profile already carries in its SOUL
  (`## Skills — your curated surface`, grouped by category, loaded by name),
- routes every lane to skills its own shelf does not carry,
- charges every API call of every lane for a list most lanes never searched.

Nothing is disabled:

- `skills_list()` still enumerates the same tree on demand — a tool call the lane chooses to pay
  for, instead of a per-call prompt tax;
- `skill_view(name)` still loads any skill by name;
- **a profile with no curated surface can restore the legacy index**: `skills.index: flat` in
  `config.yaml`, or `HERMES_SKILLS_INDEX=flat` (env wins).

So this is a product option, not a removal: `skills.index: flat | dark`, dark by default, with the
index-line renderer kept reachable through the hatch because it still has to work for an
opted-in profile. Each re-pointed suite pins the hatch ON for its own module for exactly that
reason; `tests/agent/test_skills_index_deprecated.py` guards the dark default and fails if an index
line is rendered again.

`SKILL_PROMPT_DESC_LIMIT` keeps its value and its consumers (`skills_list`, `skill_view`, the
create path, the linter); it is documented as no longer gating routing. `ONESHOT_SKILLS_LOAD_GUIDANCE`
no longer tells the model to scan a list.

## Tests

```
python -m pytest tests/agent/test_skills_index_deprecated.py tests/agent/test_prompt_builder.py \
```

prs.title: feat(slack): add opt-in thread_followup_silence for unaddressed thread replies
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

**Problem.** In a Slack channel thread the bot takes part in, people often talk to each other without @mentioning (e.g. replying to a colleague mid-thread). The Slack adapter admits those replies as a plain follow-up, and `_slack_reply_expected` returns `None` for them (#110952: a follow-up is usually meant for the bot). When the model correctly decides the message isn't for it and answers with a bare `[SILENT]`, `silence_allowed()` rejects the marker and the gateway posts `gateway.errors.unexpected_silence` into the thread:

> ⚠️ The model returned only a silence marker...

So every side conversation in an engaged thread gets a warning from the bot.

**Fix.** A new opt-in flag `thread_followup_silence` (`platforms.slack.extra` / `slack:` YAML key, env `SLACK_THREAD_FOLLOWUP_SILENCE`, default `false`). When on, an unaddressed reply in a non-DM Slack thread gets `reply_expected=False`, so a bare silence marker is allowed to stand. Unchanged:

- 1:1 DMs and group DMs (still `True` / `None`),
- messages that @mention the bot, commands, reaction triggers (`True`),
- flat `reply_in_thread: false` channel follow-ups (`None`),
- messages opening with someone else's mention (already `False`).

**Why opt-in / default off.** #110952 deliberately keeps the visible fallback for thread follow-ups so a question aimed at the bot is never silently dropped. That is the right default for most workspaces; the flag is for teams whose bot-engaged threads are mostly human-to-human chatter, where the warning is noise. Default behaviour is byte-for-byte the same.

## Related Issue

Follow-up to #110952 (no separate issue).

## Type of Change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `plugins/platforms/slack/adapter.py`: `_slack_thread_followup_silence` flag getter; `_slack_reply_expected` takes `channel_thread_followup` (`is_thread_reply and not is_dm`) and returns `False` for it when the flag is on; YAML→env bridge entry.
- `plugins/platforms/slack/adapter_config_readers.py`: the `_extra_or_env_*_getter` method factories moved here unchanged (re-imported by `adapter.py`) so `adapter.py` stays under its code-health line cap.
- `tests/gateway/test_slack_reply_expected.py`: cases for flag on/off in a thread, on + bot mention, on + DM, on + flat channel.
- Docs: `website/docs/user-guide/messaging/slack.md` (YAML example + silence-marker note), `website/docs/reference/environment-variables.md`.

## Note for reviewers: the deleted lines are a verbatim move

`adapter.py` is over the code-health `FILE_LINES` target (6940 lines on `main`), so the ratchet in `lint.yml` fails on any net growth, and this feature needs about +8 lines there. Following the ratchet's own guidance ("move an existing function or class into a topical sibling `<stem>_<topic>.py`"), the two `_extra_or_env_*_getter` factories were moved **unchanged** into `adapter_config_readers.py` and re-imported, so existing `from plugins.platforms.slack.adapter import ...` callers keep working. No behaviour changes come from the move. Use `git diff --color-moved=dimmed-zebra origin/main...` (or GitHub's moved-lines view) to see the moved block separately; the functional change is only the flag getter, the `_slack_reply_expected` branch, the call-site argument and the YAML bridge entry.

prs.title: fix(kanban): an unresolvable skill name is advisory, never fatal
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes a class of run that could never start: a skill name the worker's profile cannot resolve was
treated as fatal at preload time, so the run died at INIT with `Unknown skill(s): <name>` before a
line of substantive work. Two callers were affected, and both supply names no operator ever typed:

- **The kanban review dispatcher force-loaded `sdlc-review` onto every review run.** Where that name
  did not resolve for the assignee's profile, the worker's preload loader raised
  `Unknown skill(s): sdlc-review` with nothing loaded, so each review card died at INIT twice and was
  parked by the failure limit without any work done.
- **A name in a card's own `skills` column that the assignee's profile cannot resolve** reached the
  same loader unchecked and killed the run the same way.

The rule now: a harness-supplied (advisory) name warns and continues; a name an operator actually
requested still fails loudly. Injection is resolved for the target profile *before* spawn, so a name
that cannot load in the spawned worker is never handed to it.

## Related Issue

No issue filed — diagnosed from a live dispatch failure where every review card on a host was parked
at INIT.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `agent/skill_commands.py`: `preload_skill_resolvable()` — the preload path's own resolution
  (payload must load; an operator-disabled name counts as missing), callable by an injecting caller
  for the TARGET profile. `ADVISORY_SKILLS_ENV` + `harness_advisory_skills()` + `is_advisory_skill()`
  mark harness-supplied names so the preload path degrades them to a warning.
- `cli.py`, `hermes_cli/oneshot.py`: a missing name is fatal only when it was actually requested. An
  advisory name never is — not even when it is the only name requested, which is the case that killed
  every review run.
- `hermes_cli/kanban_db_dispatch.py`: resolve a card's own skill names and the injected review names
  for the assignee's profile before spawn; unresolvable ones are skipped and recorded on the card
  (event + comment), and the worker is told which names are advisory. Adds `kanban.review_skills`
  (default `["sdlc-review"]`, `[]` disables injection) and a once-per-process boot check that names
  every review-capable profile which cannot resolve an injected review skill.
- `website/docs/user-guide/features/kanban.md` and `kanban-worker-lanes.md`: document the resolution
  rule and the new config key.

## How to Test

1. Let the review dispatcher claim a card for a profile that does not carry the review skill.
   Before: the run dies at INIT with `Unknown skill(s): sdlc-review`. After: the run starts, the
   skipped injected name is recorded on the card, and the review proceeds.
2. Put a name the assignee's profile cannot resolve into a card's `skills` column and spawn it: the
   card records the skip and the worker continues. A genuinely requested-but-missing name still
   raises `Unknown skill(s)` — the loud path is intact.

Tests added, and proven RED on the parent commit:

- `tests/agent/test_skill_commands.py` — resolution and advisory-name behaviour.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_review_lifecycle.py` — injection resolved per assignee, skipped names
  recorded on the card, the boot check, and the warning-not-raise path.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_oneshot_skills.py` — the oneshot preload raise/no-raise split.

Run at the branch tip through the repo's own runner
(`.venv/bin/python scripts/run_tests_parallel.py -j 4 <those three files>`):
**70 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped** in 12.0s — the single skip is a `platform('linux')` case, which
runs on the Linux CI lane.

prs.title: fix(kanban): a block-loop escalation is for a human, not for the decomposer
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`block_task` parks a card that keeps blocking for the same cause in **triage** with a
`block_loop_detected` event — a hand-off that is waiting for a person. The auto-decompose tick read
that card as ordinary rough-input triage work, asked the aux LLM to break it up, and fanned it out:
the escalation was answered by a machine, and children were manufactured from a card nobody had
touched.

This PR makes the escalation mean "a human decides": no promotion out of triage for a card whose
newest block-routing event is `block_loop_detected`, decided inside the promotion transaction.

## Related Issue

Addresses the `block_loop_detected` condition in #79728; the same symptom is reported from production in #75444. (Neither is closed by this change: cards reach triage by other routes too, and those are separate conditions.)

## Root cause on current main (`68a9817`)

1. `hermes_cli/kanban_db.py:3335` — `_route_block` returns `("triage", "block_loop_detected", …)`
   once the same cause reaches `BLOCK_RECURRENCE_LIMIT`.
2. `gateway/kanban_watchers_dispatcher.py:261` — the auto-decompose tick takes every id from
   `list_triage_ids()` with no check of *how* the card entered triage, and calls `decompose_task`
   (`:281`).
3. Both promotion sinks accept any row still in `triage`: `specify_triage_task`
   (`hermes_cli/kanban_db.py:3827`, sets `status = 'todo'`) and `decompose_triage_task`
   (`hermes_cli/kanban_db_graph.py:90`). Neither consults the escalation event, so the parked card
   is re-promoted on the next tick and the recurring-block context that caused the escalation is
   discarded with it.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/kanban_db.py` — new `triage_escalation_refusal()`: the **newest** block-routing event
  decides, so a card escalated and then blocked again for another cause is judged by the later
  routing decision rather than a stale one. The guard runs **inside the write transaction** of
  `specify_triage_task`, atomic with the read that decided it — a preflight before the aux call
  cannot bind the write that follows it (the P1 on #78895). `block_loop_detected` gains
  `triage_round_trips`, because recurrences alone read as N consecutive honest blocks and a count
  that already spans a triage trip is not that.
- `hermes_cli/kanban_db_graph.py` — the same guard inside `decompose_triage_task`'s write.
- `hermes_cli/kanban_decompose.py`, `hermes_cli/kanban_specify.py` — refuse **before** the aux LLM
  request, so a parked card costs no inference; the falsy `TriageEscalationRefusal` names the trigger
  event, the cause and the round trips, so existing `if not specify_triage_task(...)` callers and the
  dashboard surfaces say why instead of showing an unexplained no-op.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_triage_escalation_guard.py` — new suite (15 tests).

## How to Test

1. On a board with `kanban.auto_decompose: true`, block one card `BLOCK_RECURRENCE_LIMIT` times for
   the same cause: `block_task` parks it in `triage` with a `block_loop_detected` event.
2. Watch the next auto-decompose tick. Before: the card leaves `triage` with children and no human
   acted. After: it stays in `triage`, the tick records the refusal, and `hermes kanban decompose
   <id>` / `hermes kanban specify <id>` report the escalation instead of promoting.
3. A triage card that arrived any other way still specifies and still fans out (covered by the new
   suite, and by the existing decompose/specify suites below).

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_triage_escalation_guard.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_decompose.py tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_decompose_db.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_specify.py tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_specify_db.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_block_kinds.py tests/gateway/test_kanban_auto_decompose_live.py -q
# 33 passed
```

`ruff check` clean on the four source files and the new test. One unrelated failure,
`tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_db.py::test_infrastructure_spawn_refusal_never_charges_the_card`,
reproduces with this commit's files swapped for their `68a9817` blobs, so it is not introduced here.

## Duplicate search / cross-links

Searched PRs and issues before opening. #78895 is the same symptom and is still open; its review's
P1 is exactly the atomicity requirement above, which this PR satisfies. #94232 was closed unmerged
by its author. This is not a competing preflight gate — the decision lives inside the two promotion
sinks themselves.

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)

- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [x] I ran the scoped suite covering every file this PR touches — `python -m pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_triage_escalation_guard.py tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_decompose.py tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_decompose_db.py tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_specify.py tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_specify_db.py tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_block_kinds.py tests/gateway/test_kanban_auto_decompose_live.py -q` → 33 passed. prs.title: fix(kanban): name the cause a timed_out notice actually records
prs.body:
## What

A `timed_out` kanban notice invented the cause it could not see: it reported a runtime cap the
worker never hit, so the recorded cause was invisible exactly when the operator needed to act on
it (raise the cap? raise the iteration budget? neither is what happened).

Three placed facts:

1. `agent/turn_finalizer.py:47` (`_record_kanban_budget_exhausted`) records an iteration-budget
   exhaustion as `event_payload_extra={"budget_used": N, "budget_max": M}` — and no
   `limit_seconds`, which only the runtime cap (`hermes_cli/kanban_db_dispatch.py:651`,
   `enforce_max_runtime`) ever sets.
2. `_record_task_failure`'s non-trip path (`hermes_cli/kanban_db_dispatch.py:1415`) dropped that
   extra, so the `timed_out` event it appended carried only the free-text cause:

   ```json
   {"error": "Iteration budget exhausted (200/200) — task could not complete within the allowed iterations",
    "failures": 1, "retry_status": "ready"}
   ```

   The run row was written from the same `detail`, so it lost the fields too.
3. Both notice formatters then read the absent `limit_seconds` as `0` and printed a cap that
   never existed — `tui_gateway/session_notifications.py:314` and
   `gateway/kanban_watchers_notifier.py:449`.

Before → after, rendering the payload above:

| surface | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| board | `⏱ Kanban t_… timed out (max_runtime=0s); will retry` | `⏱ Kanban t_… timed out (exhausted its turn budget (200/200)); will retry` |
| Telegram | `⏱ t_… ran past its time limit and was stopped; it will be retried automatically.` | `⏱ t_… exhausted its turn budget (200/200) and was stopped; it will be retried automatically.` |

Measured on one board in our deployment: 19 of 19 `timed_out` events in a 3-day window carried no
`limit_seconds`, so every one of them rendered `max_runtime=0s` (or "its time limit").

## How

- `_record_task_failure`: merge `event_payload_extra` into the event payload and into the run
  row's metadata — `detail` feeds both — matching what the trip path already does with the same
  argument.
- Board notice and Telegram notice: name `limit_seconds` when the payload carries one, name the
  budget when that is what it records, and say `cause not recorded` when it has neither. No
  invented cause in any branch.
- `timed_out` is still the only outcome value used, and the event still counts toward the
  consecutive-failure circuit breaker exactly as before: no metrics enum, retry-accounting or
  idempotence (`_end_run` CAS) change.

## Testing

`tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_timed_out_cause.py` (new) drives the production caller
(`_record_kanban_budget_exhausted`) into a temp board and renders the payload it actually
recorded through **both** formatters, so a regression that drops the cause, or a formatter that
invents one, fails here. It also pins the unchanged cases: a recorded runtime cap still renders
as the minute limit / `max_runtime=Ns`, and a payload with no cause fields at all says so.

- A/B on the same file: pre-fix tree 6 failed / 2 passed; with the fix 8 passed.
- Neighbouring suites (kanban, tui_gateway, gateway, turn-finalizer): 76 passed, 0 failed via
  `scripts/run_tests_parallel.py -j 8`; `ruff check .` clean.
- Platform: macOS 26.5.2, CPython 3.14.7.

prs.title: fix(kanban): report a fully held ready queue instead of an idle board
prs.body:
A ready lane whose every spawnable row is held by a respawn guard spawns nothing,
tick after tick, and no surface outside `gateway.log` says so. `describe_suppression()`
summarises the tick from skip buckets it only partially reads, and there is no
board-level read that separates "all of this work is held" from "there is no work".
This PR makes the hold visible, bounds the event it writes, and lets a deliberate
re-queue release it.

One concern: `0 spawned` must not be the only number available, and a board that is
fully held must not read as idle.

## Related Issue

Fixes #123963. The PRs that share this symptom are cross-linked under "Related work"
below; none of them carries the board-level read, and no covering issue existed, which
is the half that issue is filed against.

- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## What changes

`hermes_cli/kanban_db_dispatch.py`
- `active_pr` lifts on `status`, `promoted` or `unblocked` as well as on the handoff
  kinds (`assigned`, `changes_requested`, `review_reopened`). `reclaimed` is
  deliberately excluded, unlike guard 3: a crash or reclaim is not a decision, and
  the PR is still open and unattended.
- `_RESPAWN_GUARD_PR_WINDOW` is untouched at 86400, and a test asserts it.
- `respawn_guarded` is written once per hold episode: re-emitted when the reason
  changes, when a new episode starts, or after an hour.
- `describe_suppression()` counts `skipped_per_profile_capped`, `skipped_nonspawnable`
  and `skipped_unassigned` in addition to the buckets it already counted.
- `board_health()` returns `(ready_total, spawnable, suppressed_by_reason)` with a
  state verdict, and `observe_dispatch_tick()` files one routed card after six
  consecutive stalled ticks with repeat spacing.

`hermes_cli/kanban.py`, `hermes_cli/kanban_parser.py`
- `hermes kanban health` renders the verdict and the per-reason counts.

`plugins/kanban/dashboard/plugin_api.py`, `dist/index.js`, `dist/style.css`
- the board payload carries `dispatch_health`, and a strip renders it, so a starved
  board does not look like a quiet one.

No config key, no env override, no GitHub API call from the tick.

## Root cause

`check_respawn_guard` matches any GitHub PR URL in a card's thread
(`hermes_cli/kanban_db_dispatch.py:1784-1802`, regex at :85) inside a 24 hour window
(:83). The URL does not have to belong to this card and its state is never consulted:
a card naming a parent's PR, or a PR that has since merged, is held exactly like one
with its own open PR. The lift set at :1797 is stricter than the sibling guard's at
:1766-1776 over a window 24 times longer.

## Verification

Base is `d0288be5b3`, the same commit as `upstream/main` at branch time.

- Premise A/B, one test file, base-blob swap: base `d0288be5b3` = 21 failed / 4 passed
  (the 4 passing are the controls: handoff vocabulary, the `reclaimed` negative, the
  empty tick, the window assertion), tip = 25 passed.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh` over the nine kanban test files: 129 passed, 1 failed,
  1 skipped, with `test_kanban_dispatch_health.py` at 25 passed. The single failure
  (`test_kanban_db.py::test_infrastructure_spawn_refusal_never_charges_the_card`) is
  pre-existing: the same file, run the same way at `d0288be5b3`, fails identically.
- macOS, Python 3.11.16.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_dispatch_health.py` — 25 passed.
2. On a board with a ready row held by the respawn guard, `hermes kanban health`
   reports `state=starved` and names the guard in `suppressed_by_reason`; an empty
   board reports `state=idle`. The state line does not depend on how many rows are held.
3. To watch the lift: `hermes kanban unblock <id>` (or `promote`) on a held row, then
   run a dispatch tick — the row starts, and the guard event is not written again.

Searched for existing PRs before writing this one. Each of these is open and covers a
part of the same symptom:

- #122301, #105233: the guard's predicate and PR-state awareness.
- #105078, #104277, #104629, #106865, #121177, #107347: the requeue lift.

- #108518: surfacing the skip buckets in dispatch output.

The root cause here is complementary rather than the same: those change when a hold is
released or how the identical events are collapsed, while this one adds the board-level
read and the stalled-board escalation, so a fully held queue is reported as its own

prs.title: fix(hardware): keep nvidia-smi readings when one cell is N/A
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Follow-up to b9b1328b7d, which consolidated the statusbar, budget probe and vendor detection onto one cached `nvidia-smi` query (#120262).

That shared query parses the memory and utilization cells with bare `int()`. nvidia-smi answers a field the driver cannot report with `N/A`, `[N/A]` or `[Not Supported]` instead of a number, so a single such cell raises `ValueError`, the error is swallowed, and `None` is cached for the 4s TTL. Every reader then sees "no NVIDIA GPU":

- the GPU name disappears from the hardware endpoint and from `HardwareBudget.gpu_name`;
- `probe_budget()` drops the card and budgets from system RAM as unified memory, so the VRAM budget and catalog pricing describe the wrong device.

(Backend selection mostly survives on main because `_detect_gpu_vendor()` now falls back to `gpu_class()`; the visible damage is the lost name and VRAM budget.)

This PR parses each cell on its own, so an unanswered cell is `None` and the rest of the row stands. The healthy path is unchanged: one spawn per poll window, including on devices that report some cells as N/A. Only when the wide query is rejected outright (rc≠0 / empty output, e.g. a driver that does not know one of the fields) does it retry once with `name,memory.total,memory.free`; a timeout is not retried, so install/launch never stalls twice.

## Related Issue

Follow-up to b9b1328b7d (#120262). No separate issue.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/local_runtime/hardware.py`:
  - `_smi_query()` runs one `--query-gpu` field set and parses each cell independently (`_smi_int` / `_smi_mib`); unanswered cells are `None`, never 0.
  - Numeric columns are read from both ends of the row and the name is whatever lies between, since nvidia-smi does not quote the name and a comma in it would otherwise shift every later column.
  - `_cached_nvidia_gpu_query()` trusts an answered wide row as-is and retries once with `name,memory.total,memory.free` only when the wide query is rejected. Misses are still cached for the TTL.
  - `_nvidia_vram()` uses `total - used` when only free memory is N/A. With neither, discrete live budgets keep the capacity plan, `launch_budget()` returns `None` (callers keep the capacity plan, as for a failed query), and the unified-memory live budget adds nothing for the unknown carve-out (OS-available RAM only).
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_local_nvidia_smi_cells.py` (new): N/A cells keep the name and VRAM budget with exactly one spawn; unknown free keeps the capacity plan (discrete and unified memory); a rejected wide query retries once and the partial reading is cached; a comma in the name does not shift columns (wide and fallback); a timeout is not retried.
- `tests/test_windows_subprocess_no_window_flags.py`: the failure-is-cached test now pins `windows_hide_flags()` with `_patch_hide_flags`, so it asserts the hidden flag on both the wide query and the fallback spawn on the Linux lane too, and expects two spawns (wide + one retry) followed by a TTL hit.

## How to Test

1. Run the focused tests:
   ```bash
   scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_local_nvidia_smi_cells.py tests/test_windows_subprocess_no_window_flags.py
   ```
2. Run the neighbouring hardware / budget suites:
   ```bash
   scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_local_n1x_pci_identity.py tests/hermes_cli/test_unified_pool_quirk.py tests/hermes_cli/test_local_launch_budget.py tests/hermes_cli/test_local_runtime.py tests/hermes_cli/test_local_models_routes.py
   ```
3. Proof on main: with `hermes_cli/local_runtime/hardware.py` reverted to main, 6 of the 7 new tests fail (e.g. `test_na_cells_keep_name_and_vram_budget`: `budget.uma` is `True` and the name is empty because the row with `[N/A]` free memory was dropped); the timeout test passes on both, as it pins existing behaviour.
4. On a machine whose driver reports `[N/A]` / `[Not Supported]` for some fields (`nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.total,memory.free,name,pci.device_id,memory.used,utilization.gpu --format=csv,noheader,nounits`), the desktop statusbar keeps the GPU name and the local-models pane keeps the card's VRAM budget instead of showing system RAM.

```text
python scripts/check: 11 checks, ok
```

prs.title: kanban: never read an unreadable worker identity as death (boot-relative start time + tri-state liveness)
prs.body:
Fixes #123811.

### What goes wrong

A live worker is declared dead, killed, and de-owned. In one dispatch tick the reclaim path
declared six live workers dead; each recovery then spawned a duplicate beside the worker it had
just abandoned. A worker that has been "reclaimed" while still running cannot close its card:
`kanban_complete` is refused, its run is `crashed` in `task_runs`, `tasks.current_run_id` is NULL
and the card is `blocked` — bricked until a human clears it.

Liveness asked one question — "is this worker alive?" — and accepted only yes/no, so every failure
to *read* a process identity was answered "no". Three independent branches, each sufficient on its
own:

1. **The start-time reference steps.** The recorded fingerprint is an absolute start instant derived
   from the boot reference (plus psutil's `|INIT_BOOT_TIME - boot_time()|` shift on macOS), so the
   same live process reports a different value minutes apart:

   ```
   recorded at spawn   179030725877270          (ticks; Δ vs a re-read 9.27 s later: 927 cs)
   re-read later       179030725868000
   ```

2. **A failed probe is read as death.** `ps` exit status 1, or a `subprocess` failure, means "gone".
3. **An unreadable fingerprint is read as death.** A row whose fingerprint has an older shape (bare
   ticks, no boot component) cannot be compared at all — but it was compared, and the mismatch was
   read as "the PID was recycled".

### The change

* **`gateway/status.py`** — `host_boot_witness()` names the boot itself (`kern.bootsessionuuid` on
  macOS: fresh per boot, unaffected by clock or boottime adjustments; `boottime:<epoch>` as the
  fallback; never `''`). `get_process_uptime_start_time()` subtracts a boot reference read in the
  same call, so both halves of a comparison move together when the reference steps, and returns
  `None` — "cannot certify identity" — when it cannot read one. `start_time_fingerprints_match()` is
  the single comparator for the pair. `get_process_start_time()` keeps its absolute semantics.

* **`hermes_cli/kanban_db_dispatch.py`** — liveness is now a witness with three answers:
  `WORKER_ALIVE` / `WORKER_DEAD` / `WORKER_UNKNOWN`. `WORKER_UNKNOWN` is what an unreadable identity
  yields, never `WORKER_DEAD`; only `WORKER_DEAD` may release a claim, requeue a card or authorize a
  signal. Held rows are re-read next tick, bounded by the heartbeat/TTL backstops.

* **`hermes_cli/kanban_db.py`** — the run-ownership guard separates the two cases it used to
  conflate: SUPERSEDED (a newer run owns the card — still refused on every transition, because the
  write would land on the successor) and UN-OWNED (`current_run_id` is NULL and the caller's run is
  the card's newest — the write lands):

  ```sql
  AND (current_run_id = ? OR (current_run_id IS NULL
       AND ? = (SELECT MAX(id) FROM task_runs WHERE task_id = tasks.id)))
  ```

  A recovery through that branch is recorded honestly rather than written into the crashed row: the
  completion lands on a synthesized run carrying `recovered_from_run_id` + `infra_reclaimed: true`,
  the crashed row stands as history, and the failure counter the reclaim booked is cleared.

* **`tools/kanban_tools.py`** — a refusal is built from the live row (`kanban_db.live_row_refusal()`:
  the card's status, which run owns it, whether the caller's run is superseded or was closed by the
  infrastructure and how to record that recovery) instead of `tasks.last_failure_error`, which is
  durable and describes a run that is over. The crash text is still shown — labelled as history.

### Two deliberate consequences

* A legacy-shaped fingerprint is uncomparable, so such rows are **held**, not reclaimed — the safe
  direction, and observable in the test suite. It costs nothing for rows this code wrote; for older
  rows the heartbeat/TTL backstops still bound the wait.
* A witness that comes back in a **different form** (the boot-session probe failing, leaving the
  `boottime:` fallback) reads as *unknown*, not as *a different boot*. A probe changing the shape of
  its answer is not proof that the host rebooted, and reading it as one would declare every live row
  dead in a single tick — the failure being fixed here. Same-form witnesses are compared exactly.

### Tests

New: `tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_liveness_witness.py` (witness/liveness),
`tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_run_fence_recovery.py` (run fence, recovery, refusal text),
`tests/tools/test_kanban_complete_refusal_live_row.py` (the refusal at the tool surface).
Updated for the new contract: `test_kanban_worker_pid_fingerprint.py`,
`test_kanban_terminal_worker_reaper.py`.

A/B, each test in its own process so a test the base code kills is still recorded:

```
base   d0288be5    PASS 11   RED 19   SIGTERM 1
branch 06b83d22    PASS 31   RED  0   SIGTERM 0
```

The `SIGTERM rc=143` row is the point of the change:
`test_a_failed_secondary_probe_holds_the_claim`, on the base tree, is killed by the base reclaim
path signalling the live PID it wrongly believes is a stale worker — the test process itself. On
this branch it passes.

```
python -m pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_liveness_witness.py \
                 tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_run_fence_recovery.py \
                 tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_worker_pid_fingerprint.py \
                 tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_terminal_worker_reaper.py \
                 tests/tools/test_kanban_complete_refusal_live_row.py
```

### Related

#117505 — the same class of defect in cron's `_owner_is_live()` (an exact start-time compare
rejecting a live process).


## Related Issue

Related Issue: #123811

- [x] I ran the files this change touches, not the full suite — `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_liveness_witness.py tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_run_fence_recovery.py tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_worker_pid_fingerprint.py tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_terminal_worker_reaper.py tests/tools/test_kanban_complete_refusal_live_row.py` → **31 passed, 0 failed (base d0288be5: 11 passed, 19 failed, 1 SIGTERM)**. The full `pytest tests/ -q` was not run on this host.
- [ ] `python scripts/check` passes (the blocking lint and code-health checks CI runs)

prs.title: feat(kanban): ready-queue admission — defer instead of enqueue
prs.body:
## What

One gate between `todo` and `ready`. A ready lane deeper than the fleet can drain in an hour does not run more work — the enqueue is what fails (spawn cap → exit 78 / "kanban worker hit the cap"), and the case that loses is the one that arrived last. Over budget, a filing now parks in `todo` instead of joining the ready population, and is admitted when the board drains.

## Mechanism

- `hermes_cli/kanban_db_admission.py` (new): the ONE predicate (`decide`) and the ONE writer of `tasks.status='ready'` (`admit_to_ready`), so there is one place to answer "does this card get a slot, and why".
- Budget: trailing completion cohort in `kanban.admission_lookback_window_hours` (default 168) × `admission_cohort_multiplier` (0.55), floored at `admission_floor` (20), pinned by `admission_budget_pin`. Lane budget is a fraction (4%) of the lane's own number — the lane binds before the global check.
- Exemptions: P0 fault severity, explicit `admit_reason="consent"`, and re-entry (unblock / review round trip / reclaim / reopen / transfer) — the demand was already admitted once.
- `tasks.admit_state` / `tasks.ready_since`: `admitted`/`deferred` (NULL = pre-mechanism backlog, deliberately left NULL), and a wait clock written on every entry into `ready` and cleared on claim/archive. Existing rows get `ready_since` backfilled once from their newest ready-entry event.
- Every writer of the ready status routes through the helper: create, dependency promotion, operator promote, unblock, review reopen, `request_changes`, the reclaim/retry sweeps, board import.
- The decision rides the transition event that made it (`admit` payload); a deferred card is re-evaluated every tick and only the FIRST refusal is recorded (no event firehose); a completing parent reports `children_promoted` vs `children_deferred_ids` so a worker is never told its child is running when it is parked.
- Read surface `hermes kanban queue-state [--json]`: depth/budget/budget_source, per-lane depth/budget, deferred/admitted/fallback/bypass counts, pre-mechanism backlog, and the ready-ageing numbers (oldest + warn/escalate counts).
- Dedupe honesty: `deduped` is reported by both create surfaces, `idempotency_key` is readable on the detail surface.
- Config keys ship INERT: with `kanban.admission_enabled_at` unset the mechanism is off and every path behaves exactly as today — that single key is what turns it on.

## Testing

`tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_admission.py` — 12 tests: over-budget create parks with the reason on its own event; lane budget binds before global depth; budget derivation (cohort → floor → pin); re-entry exemption + wait-clock re-stamp; the promotion guard lands a deferred card when the board drains and does not re-log refusals; ageing numbers and the claim clearing them; mechanism-off parity (no `admit` payload, ready as before); the pre-mechanism backlog is reported and NOT mass-addressed; no filing is dropped silently (park + count, or comment on origin with no orphan card); both dedupe surfaces; and a source guard asserting no module writes the ready status without the helper.

`pytest tests/hermes_cli -k kanban`: 430 passed / 20 failed with this change vs 418 passed / 20 failed on the unmodified tree — identical pre-existing failure set (missing optional deps/order), zero regressions.

prs.title: feat(kanban): gate completion on landed evidence, route stranded cards to their owner
prs.body:
Fixes #123428, the two problems in that issue: a board that lets unlanded work read as done, and a stranded ready card that is only reported.

**A landing card cannot close without evidence of the landing.** Whether a card has to land is read from structured declarations only, and there are two: a landing CLAIM on the completion (the `landed` / `merged_commit` / `deploy_stamp` / `live_sha256` vocabulary), or a non-done child carrying a landing contract (the chain-head case — a parent must not close ahead of the leg that lands its deliverable). Nothing parses prose, so a `local-only` card and the ordinary review flow are untouched. A card's own `completion_contract` is deliberately NOT a third trigger: that vocabulary is publication-shaped (`OWNER/REPO` or a PR URL) and is already gated at the completion boundary by `kanban_pr_acceptance`, whose criterion is a PR published at the exact head with its required checks green; demanding a merge as well would refuse the completions that gate exists to allow, and a fork PR is a legitimate end of a deliverable. Blast radius: the gate bites completions; `--force`, a retry without the claim, and the dashboard's drag-to-done (which passes `force=True` as a human override) are all escapes.

The accepted forms are the merged commit, a deploy stamp naming it, and a live hash equal to the merged blob. Every form names a target, and the target is read rather than trusted: the commit comes out of the deploy stamp FILE itself, so a stamp line with no readable file behind it — like a stamp that names no commit — is not evidence; an artifact the live hash points at is hashed on disk; and a merged commit is resolved with read-only local git against the checkout it says it merged in (`merged_repo`, plus `merged_branch` when it is not that checkout's own HEAD) and must be an ancestor of that branch — so a sha only on an unpushed branch, on another branch, the head of an open unmerged PR, or in no repository is not a landing, and a bare sha with no checkout named is not evidence. A target that contradicts its own claim refuses the completion. A refusal names the missing evidence in one line, changes no state, and `--force` stays the operator override. Accepted evidence is recorded on the closing event.

**A stranded ready card gets a routed repair card instead of a log line.** At error severity the dispatcher files one card AND one audit event per stranded card, routed by a fixed cause table: an unknown assignee, a fleet at capacity, and a lane with no worker go to the ops head, and a lane whose own queue is deeper than its spawn budget goes to that lane's design authority. The cause is read from board state (profile resolution, queue depth, fleet cap) and never inferred from prose, so the same board always produces the same owner and the same card; the fleet-cap reading now matches the dispatcher (`resolve_max_in_progress`, and a running count over every `status='running'` row). Filing is idempotent per card and cause, capped per pass, and one generation deep, so a repair card is never routed again; past three cards of one cause a single card stands for the population. The pass runs outside the dispatch lock, and a router failure is logged rather than raised into the tick.

Relation to #89511: that PR recovers cards that are blocked or stranded in review. This change leaves the stranded card itself untouched and files a routed repair card for the starvation, which is a queue-shaping decision rather than a recovery.

Verification on this commit:

- `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_landing_gate.py tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_stranded_routing.py -q` gives 40 passed. The same two files against the pre-fix code at the parent `b5d65faa` give 9 failed, 31 passed — the new tests bite.
- `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban*.py tests/plugins/test_kanban*.py -q --tb=no` gives 576 passed, 33 failed, 11 skipped (620 collected); the same command on the base tree without these commits gives 569 passed, 33 failed, 11 skipped (613 collected). The FAILED set is byte-identical name-for-name between the two, so these commits add no new failure; the +7 passed is exactly the 7 new test functions, and both new test files are among them. The 33 are pre-existing at this base (real-root write guards and HTTP admission tests that want a host setup this checkout does not have).
- A direct probe of the reworked gate against a real checkout: a commit on the branch lands; a commit that exists but is not an ancestor of the named ref is refused; a sha in no repository is refused; a path that is not a checkout is refused; a named commit with no `merged_repo` is unsubstantiated; and a deploy-stamp line with no file behind it resolves to no commit.
- The dispatcher pass was timed against a copy of a live board of 378 ready cards: 0.08s per pass, so it does not need a throttle.

prs.title: feat(estop): keep an allowlisted identity working through a pause, and bound the pause itself
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`hermes pause` is all or nothing, and it never lifts on its own.

Two consequences. The operator cannot work through their own pause: `agent/estop.py::is_engaged()`
is the single predicate behind the gateway turn gate, the cron tick and the kanban dispatcher, so
an armed pause blocks the operator's new turns exactly like everyone else's, and the in-band
`/pause off` needs a turn the pause is blocking. And a pause outlives its reason when the job that
armed it dies: the sentinel records `engaged_at` and `reason` but no deadline, so a crashed
maintenance window parks every consumer until a human removes the file by hand.

This adds two fields to that one sentinel and one branch to the gate that reads it. Same sentinel,
same predicate, no second mechanism.

`allow.user_ids` / `allow.profiles` exempt an authenticated identity. `agent.estop.is_allowed()`
is consulted at the top of `gateway/run_inbound.py::_hm_estop_turn_allowed`, ahead of the command
check, so an allowlisted turn is served while everyone else still gets the pause notice. `user_id`
is the primary key because it survives a platform or profile change; `profile` is the secondary key
for naming a maintenance lane directly. Fail-closed: no allowlist, or a body that cannot be read,
admits nobody.

`expires_at` is a deadman. Past that instant `is_engaged()` reports not engaged, the lift is logged
once at WARNING, and the dead sentinel is retired. The unlink re-checks the engagement's identity
first, so a re-arm landing between the read and the unlink is never eaten. An empty, corrupt or
unparsable body stays engaged.

`hermes pause --allow-user <id> [--allow-profile <name>] [--ttl 45m]` arms it, and an unusable
`--ttl` is refused before the sentinel is written. `hermes status` renders the reason, the deadline
and the allowlist.

One disclosure up front: this is two behaviors on one sentinel, not one. They answer the same gap
(a pause that cannot be survived and cannot end), they touch the same two functions, and splitting
them means two PRs against the same predicate. Say the word and I will split them.

## Related Issue

Fixes #121053

## Type of Change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `agent/estop.py`: the sentinel gains `allow` and `expires_at`; `is_engaged()` is expiry-aware and
  retires a dead sentinel (`_parse_stamp`, `_is_expired`, `_retire_expired`, `_engagement_key`);
  new `is_allowed()` and `_normalize_allow()`; `engage()` takes `allow` / `ttl` / `expires_at`;
  `get_state()` reports the two new fields; `paused_reply()` and `check_paused()` name the
  auto-resume when there is one. New local `parse_duration()`.
- `gateway/run_inbound.py`: the allowlist branch at the top of `_hm_estop_turn_allowed` (line 264),
  plus its docstring.
- `hermes_cli/subcommands/pause.py`: `--allow-user`, `--allow-profile`, `--ttl`.
- `hermes_cli/status.py`: the pause line carries reason, deadline and allowlist.
- Tests: `tests/cron/test_estop.py`, `tests/gateway/test_control_socket_pause.py`, and new
  `tests/gateway/test_estop_allowlist.py`.

## How to Test

1. `hermes pause --reason window --allow-user <your-id> --ttl 45m`, then `hermes status` shows the
   reason, `auto-resumes <stamp> (deadman TTL)` and `allowed through: <your-id>`.
2. Send a turn as the allowlisted identity and it is served. Send one as any other identity and the
   pause notice still comes back.
3. `hermes resume` lifts it. Then re-arm with `--ttl`, and it lifts itself, with one WARNING line
   naming the sentinel.
4. `hermes pause --ttl banana` refuses with `NOT pausing` and leaves the sentinel untouched.
5. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/cron/test_estop.py tests/gateway/test_estop_allowlist.py
   tests/gateway/test_control_socket_pause.py` gives 51 passed, 0 failed.

For the red side of that last one: revert the four source files to the parent commit and keep the
tests, and the same run gives 18 failed, 26 passed with `tests/gateway/test_estop_allowlist.py`
failing to collect (it imports `is_allowed`). Revert only `gateway/run_inbound.py` and 4 of the 7
tests in that file fail, one of them on the operator turn that should have been served.

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`feat(estop):`; the `estop` scope is already in this repo's history, e.g. `fix(estop): honor canonical ~/.hermes/ESTOP from profile gateways`)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate

The full `pytest tests/ -q` was not run: fork PRs sit at `action_required` here until a maintainer approves the workflow run, so it has not had a chance to speak.

- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 26.5.2 (Darwin 25F84), Python 3.11 venv

- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — N/A, no config keys
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — N/A

- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — N/A, no tool schema changed

## For New Skills

## Screenshots / Logs

Green, at this commit, with the repo's own runner:

```
Discovered 3 test files (~41 tests) under ['tests/cron/test_estop.py', 'tests/gateway/test_estop_allowlist.py', 'tests/gateway/test_control_socket_pause.py']; running with -j 28
=== Summary: 3 files, 51 tests passed, 0 failed (100% complete) in 1.9s (28 workers) ===
run_tests rc=0
```

Red, the four source files reverted to the parent commit with the tests kept:

```
======================== 18 failed, 26 passed in 0.84s =========================
=== 1 file where no tests ran (collection/import error, timeout before collection, etc.) ===
  tests/gateway/test_estop_allowlist.py
```

Red, only `gateway/run_inbound.py` reverted:

```
collected 7 items
========================= 4 failed, 3 passed in 0.29s ==========================
```

The other two consumers were exercised directly, against a snapshot of a live board and a scratch
home, rather than through their dispatch wrappers. A due one-shot job reports `executed=0` with 0
`executions` rows while the pause holds, then `executed=1` with 1 row after the deadman expires,
leaving `next_run_at` unchanged across both ticks. The dispatcher writes `spawned=0` across two
ticks with 68 ready cards while the gate is held, then 16 spawned on the control tick after the
expiry. Both hold, and both lift.

Finally, one thing for you to weigh rather than something I am hiding: `parse_duration` lands in
`agent/estop.py` as the third copy in this tree (`cron/jobs.py` returns minutes and raises;
`hermes_cli/session_filters.py` is CLI-facing). Importing `cron` from `agent` would invert the
layering, so this one is local and returns seconds or None. Consolidating all three into one shared
helper is a clean follow-up if you would rather have it in this PR.

prs.title: fix(docker): make supervised TUI startup and terminal output work together
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

An interactive Docker TUI could fail before connecting because client startup treated the existing s6 supervisor as inaccessible. After a manual gateway start, supervised stdout and stderr could overwrite the TUI screen. This replacement fixes both paths together: client startup requests the registered s6 owner, and an interactive container gives the foreground command exclusive terminal output while retaining supervised logs.

Named profiles use the root multiplexer unless explicitly standalone. Discovery verifies the container's own HERMES_HOME instead of selecting gateway-default for an unrelated installation.

## Related Issue

Fixes #138945.

Replaces the now-closed logging-only #139490. This is the single combined repair PR. Salvages the startup change from #138957 by cherry-picking KoNit-K's commit cd2be758597c4b56e490acb4a6829b0406e6b0ba with its original authorship and a cherry-pick trailer, then adds container-home identity, multiplex ownership, and real Docker regression coverage.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] Security fix
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/gateway_runtime_service.py`: discover and start an existing s6 slot without installing or launching an unmanaged gateway. Verify the container home, route normal named profiles to their root owner, and retain independent standalone slots.
- `docker/entrypoint-dispatch.sh`: default interactive terminal launches to S6_LOGGING=2 and S6_CMD_USE_TERMINAL=1 before /init connects service descriptors. Preserve headless forwarding and explicit s6 settings.
- Docker regressions execute Ink's real gateway_bootstrap.py helper, verify its authenticated ticket and profile identity, check s6 owner selection, and prove supervised stdout and warnings are retained outside the foreground terminal.
- Document automatic TUI startup and the actual catch-all log path and lifetime.

## How to Test

1. Run `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/docker/test_tui_gateway_startup.py tests/docker/test_interactive_logging.py tests/docker/test_main_invocation.py tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_runtime_service.py -j 2 -q` with a built image through HERMES_TEST_IMAGE.
2. Default, normal named, and standalone named profile bootstrap must obtain a ticket from the correct supervised gateway. Normal named startup must leave its competing per-profile slot stopped. Another installation root must be refused.
3. Inject stdout and a warning through the production s6 service/log scripts. Interactive output must stay outside the CMD console and remain readable in the profile/catch-all logs. Headless and explicit console/tee modes must still forward output.

Focused local results: 40 passed and 18 native-host cases skipped across the four explicit files. Docker tests ran real Linux containers from Windows. Both startup and logging have red/green evidence. The original startup salvage also failed the multiplexed-profile and foreign-home regressions before the follow-up corrections.

Validation: all 12 blocking scripts/check gates pass. Ruff 0.15.10 formatting passes for both new Docker test files. ShellCheck 0.11.0 passes for the full CI Docker shell scope at error severity. Hadolint 2.12.0 passes both CI Dockerfiles with the repository configuration. Ty 0.0.82 reports no findings in the four changed Python files, while the full repository advisory report contains 32,825 findings.

Local containers used current clean Python source over a cached dependency/runtime image. A completely fresh Dockerfile build, both architectures/image variants, full Python suite, and native Linux/macOS cases remain CI work. No model prompt or paid provider call was made. This proves the bootstrap/owner/terminal paths, not a visual acceptance test of the Ink interface or reporter-confirmed recovery.

prs.body:
## Problem

A gateway that serves several profiles (multiplex) spawns children with the **launch** process's env: `HERMES_HOME` is the default root and `HERMES_PROFILE` is not exported at all. The served profile lives only in the per-session ContextVar.

So a child that has to *name* the profile it is acting for cannot:

```
# inside a gateway-served session for profile `ops-coder`
$ hermes kanban comment <card> "note"
# attributed to: default      <- the home-derived fallback
$ hermes peer dm ...           # X-Hermes-Sender-Profile: default
```

Measured on the pre-fix arm of this branch (a real child process spawned through the factory, session bound for `ops-coder`): the child's `HERMES_PROFILE` is unset, so `hermes_cli.profiles.current_profile_name()` resolves it as `default`.

## Change

- **`tools/environments/local.py` — `_export_served_profile_env()`** publishes the identity the turn is acting as as `HERMES_PROFILE`, beside the profile-scoped `HERMES_HOME` that `_apply_profile_home()` already pins, from `_finalize_child_env()` — the one place both child-env paths (`build_subprocess_env()`, `hermes_subprocess_env()`) pass through. A child process has no bound home override, so the parent is the only place its identity can come from. Authority order: the bound home override, then the bound session profile (ContextVar before its `os.environ` mirror). With neither bound the inherited value is left untouched, which preserves the kanban dispatcher's `HERMES_PROFILE` pin on the workers it spawns.
- **`tools/environments/local.py` — `served_profile_child_env()`** now DROPS a `HERMES_PROFILE` pin that names a profile other than the explicit target home it just pinned. `current_profile_name()` reads the env pin before the home in a child (there is no override there), so an identity exported for the spawning session would label a child that acts under a different profile — `hermes -p X`, a routed profile's gateway service, the host gateway on the default root. Removal only: the helper still never SETS `HERMES_PROFILE`.

## Rebase (2026-09-26, platform-stl)

Rebased onto `upstream/main` (`fbb06142ef`). Both conflicts were this PR overlapping upstream's own board-identity fix, which landed the same night:

- **`hermes_cli/profiles.py`** — upstream's `current_profile_name()` is taken as the one resolver (it honours the bound home override; the gap it cannot close is the child, which is what the export above closes). This PR's rival `resolve_acting_profile_name()` is dropped rather than kept as a second authority.
- **`hermes_cli/kanban.py`** — upstream's `_profile_author()` (delegating to that resolver) is kept; this hunk no longer differs from main.

Net diff after the rebase: `tools/environments/local.py` and its test file — the PR is the child-env half only.

## Tests

`tests/tools/test_build_subprocess_env.py` — 11 passed, 0 failed (hermetic env, isolated `HOME`, `TZ=UTC`), plus 59 passed across the neighbouring env/identity suites: `test_kanban_persisted_identity`, `test_served_profile_child_env`, `test_served_profile_child_env_authority`, `test_host_gateway_profile_env`, `test_subprocess_env_guard`, `test_cron_multiplex_served_profile_parity`, `test_bot_chat_delivery_child_env`, `test_profile_gate_env_isolation`, `test_profile_gate_env_shape`, `test_subprocess_home_isolation`, `test_check_profile_scope_patterns`. `ruff check` on the changed files: clean.

The same file with the export call disabled — the base arm, measured on this host:

```
4 failed, 7 passed
  test_session_profile_is_exported_as_hermes_profile
  test_profile_scoped_home_alone_still_names_the_profile
  test_e2e_child_cli_author_names_the_served_session_profile
  test_explicit_target_home_owns_the_identity
```

and the spawned child, which reports `current_profile_name()`, on each arm:

```
base  (export off): served-turn child -> 'default'    own-home child -> 'ops-coder'
fix   (export on) : served-turn child -> 'ops-coder'  own-home child -> 'ops-coder'
```

## Why not just `served_profile_child_env`

That helper scopes `HERMES_HOME` (and credentials) to the target, and deliberately never sets `HERMES_PROFILE` — so it is the right env for a child that acts *under* a home, and it is not a name. The two compose: this PR is the identity half, and it is why the helper now removes a pin that contradicts the home it hands over.

prs.title: fix(skills): restore a symlinked skill as a symlink on batch rollback
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Stops a failed multi-op `skill_manage` batch from converting a directory-symlink skill
entry into a real directory. `_restore_snapshot` now records whether the pre-state was a
symlink and re-creates the link instead of `copytree`-ing the snapshot over the link's
path.

## Related Issue

Fixes #118699

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `tools/skill_manager_batch.py`
  - `_snapshot_skills` records the pre-state shape alongside the copy: when `pre_dir` is a
    symlink it stores `os.readlink(pre_dir)` as `link_target` in the snapshot tuple.
  - `_restore_snapshot(pre_dir, snap, post_dir, link_target=None)` re-creates a symlinked
    pre-state with `os.symlink(link_target, pre_dir)` (after removing the current entry,
    whether link or directory) and returns, instead of `copytree` over the path. A
    real-directory pre-state keeps the existing `copytree` behaviour.
  - The symlinked aside is removed with `os.unlink` (a `shutil.rmtree` on a symlink is a
    swallowed no-op, which is what left the `.rollback-broken` link behind).
- `tests/tools/test_skill_manage_batch.py`
  - `test_failed_batch_preserves_symlinked_skill`: a batch whose second op fails asserts
    both symlinked entries survive as symlinks with their original targets and no
    `.rollback-broken` residue.

Relationship to #112321: same underlying defect, different mechanism. #112321 resolves the
entry to its link target and runs snapshot/restore there, which also restores the target's
content after a partial op landed. This PR restores the *farm entry itself* as a symlink
and does not write back into the link target — the narrower invariant that a pre-state
that was a symlink is restored as a symlink. Relationship to #118692: complementary — that
PR moves the park outside the skills root and removes the park with a symlink-aware
helper; this PR changes what the restore writes at the original path. No files touched
here overlap #118692, and the symlink-restore hunk is independent of #112321's
`_real_skill_dir`.

## How to Test

```
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_skill_manage_batch.py
```

The new test installs two skills as directory symlinks into a shared tree, runs a two-op
batch whose second op fails, and asserts both entries are still symlinks pointing at their
original targets with no `.rollback-broken` residue. The successful-batch control
(`test_cross_skill_batch_and_rollback` and the single-op path) is unchanged and still
passes.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix
- [x] I've run `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_skill_manage_batch.py tests/tools/test_skill_manager_tool.py` and all tests pass (79 passed)
- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS (Darwin 26.5, Python 3.11.15)

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation — docstrings on `_snapshot_skills` and
  `_restore_snapshot` describe the symlink invariant; no user-facing docs describe this
  path
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` — N/A (no config keys added or changed)
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` — N/A (no architecture or workflow
  change)

  directory symlinks, which the suite already exercises elsewhere; no platform-specific
  behaviour added
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas — N/A (behaviour matches the existing tool

prs.title: Shell hooks ask for consent on the CLI and follow config/allowlist changes without a gateway restart (CLI-5, #134889)
prs.body:
Shell hooks work again under the one-gateway runtime: the classic CLI asks for first-use consent on its terminal, `--accept-hooks` is honoured, and hooks added, approved, removed or revoked after the gateway started take effect at the next local session open instead of the next gateway restart. Fixes CLI-5 in #134889.

## What changed

- **Consent on the CLI terminal.** Before it opens its gateway session, the classic CLI asks the main-branch "Allow this hook to run? [y/N]" question for each configured hook not yet in the allowlist (`hermes_cli/cli_init_mixin.py::_record_shell_hook_consent`, `agent/shell_hooks.py::record_consent_from_config`). It skips remote gateways (`HERMES_TUI_GATEWAY_URL`) and `--safe-mode` / `--ignore-user-config` launches.
- **`--accept-hooks` on chat.** `_prepare_agent_startup` exports `HERMES_ACCEPT_HOOKS=1` for chat launches, so the flag reaches `session.create` (`env_launch_flags`) and the CLI's consent check. Before, only the Termux light-parser path did this.
- **Gateway re-sync on every local session create / resume.** `gateway/session_controls.py` calls `session_policy.refresh_profile_hooks` off the loop, and it calls the new `shell_hooks.sync_from_config` with the owner home's live config:
  - hooks configured and consented since start register; hooks removed from `config.yaml` or revoked are unregistered;
  - consent is the allowlist, or an opt-in in force (`hooks_auto_accept`, `HERMES_ACCEPT_HOOKS`), as on main;
  - add and remove happen under one lock hold;
  - it never prompts or writes, and a failure is logged without blocking the session open;
  - an empty (failed-open) config or an unreadable allowlist adds but never removes, so a `fail_closed` guard is never disarmed by a half-saved file or a failed allowlist write.
- **`register_from_config` stays add-only** for every other caller (startup, TUI agent build, plugin force-reload, managed workers). A shared `_hook_specs` guard covers safe worker, safe mode and non-dict config for all three entry points.
- **Text.** `hermes hooks revoke` (docstring, output, help) and `hooks.md` no longer say "until restart". `gateway/AGENTS.md` names the re-sync as the only path that removes hooks.

## Validation

| Check | origin/main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Live: real gateway + classic CLI in tmux, TTY consent prompt shown | no | yes |
| Live: hook fires after answering "y" | 0 | 1 |
| Live: hook added after gateway start, `chat -q --accept-hooks` | 0 fires | 1 |
| Live: revoked and removed hook on the next session | 0 | 0 (the other hook still fires) |
| Live: unguarded terminal commands that ran | 2 | 0 |
| `tests/gateway/test_shell_hook_resync.py` + `test_cli_startup_trim.py` | 4 fail | pass |
| 35 test files touching hooks / session policy / session controls | | 479 passed |
| `scripts/check` (12 lint checks, incl. code health) | | ok |

Mutation checks: dropping the opt-in, the empty-config guard, or the unreadable-allowlist guard each turns `test_shell_hook_resync.py` red.

## Root cause

46a5a627 (teknium1, Oct 12; cherry-picked from 4dbd7426, landed with #106742) moved hook registration out of the classic CLI process. After that, only the gateway registered hooks: once at startup, with no TTY, so nothing prompted, nothing re-read the allowlist, and nothing ever unregistered.

## Scope

- Leaves alone: the multi-profile re-scan when the allowlist changes for messaging-only gateways (#133067), and `hermes hooks accept` (#138419 / #138421).
- Outbound webhooks keep startup-only registration.

## Blast radius

The registry can only lose hooks through `sync_from_config`. Its remove step is skipped whenever the config is empty or the allowlist is unreadable, and every consent source main honoured still keeps a hook. Proof level 4: probes and tests call the real `sync_from_config` / `refresh_profile_hooks`, and the live E2E (level 5) covers the CLI paths.

prs.title: fix(skills): park a batch rollback outside the skills root
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

A failed multi-op `skill_manage` batch parks the half-applied skill **inside the skills
root** while it copies the snapshot back (`_restore_snapshot`, `tools/skill_manager_batch.py`:
`post_dir.with_name(post_dir.name + ".rollback-broken")`, removed with
`shutil.rmtree(aside, ignore_errors=True)`).

That park is itself a skill:

* `agent.skill_utils.iter_skill_index_files` walks a root with `os.walk(followlinks=True)`
  and prunes only `EXCLUDED_SKILL_DIRS`, so a parked directory holding `SKILL.md` is
  offered as a skill — with the live skill's frontmatter `name`, so the name resolves
  twice in one root. A process killed between the park and the copy-back (SIGKILL, host
  restart, power cut) leaves it there for good, because nothing sweeps it.
* `shutil.rmtree` refuses a symlink, so when the entry is a directory symlink the park
  cannot be removed at all — `ignore_errors=True` swallowed the refusal and the link
  survived even the successful path.

This PR moves the park outside every skills root, removes it with a symlink-aware helper,
and sweeps parks older than a day.

## Related Issue

Fixes #118691

Complementary to #112321 and #67748, not a duplicate of either: those fix which path
*discovery* returns and make snapshot/restore operate on the resolved link target. This
PR changes where the park *lives* — the two are independent, and they compose (with
either applied, the park becomes a real directory, but it is still parked inside the
skills root, so an interrupted restore still leaves a loadable shadow entry).
No files that #112321 touches are modified here.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `tools/skill_manager_batch.py`
  - `_restore_snapshot` parks via the new `_park_entry_aside` and cleans up with
    `_remove_path` (symlink-aware) instead of `shutil.rmtree`, which cannot delete a
    symlink.
  - `_park_entry_aside` renames the entry into `_asides_root()` — a hidden
    `.skill-rollback-asides` directory beside the skills root (same filesystem, so the
    rename stays atomic; `tempfile.gettempdir()` when `HERMES_HOME` is itself configured
    as a skills root, so the park is never inside a walked tree) — and stamps the park's
    own mtime so the stale check is about the *park*, not the entry.
  - `_sweep_stale_asides` drops parks older than `_ASIDE_STALE_SECONDS` (24h): a park
    exists only between the rename and the copy-back, so anything that old was abandoned
    by a process that died mid-restore.
- `tests/tools/test_skill_batch_rollback_park.py` (new, 5 tests) — assertions use the
  loader's own walker (`iter_skill_index_files`), so "nothing loadable was left behind"
  is checked the way the reader side sees it.

## How to Test

1. Base tree (change reverted): `python -m pytest -q tests/tools/test_skill_batch_rollback_park.py`
   → **4 failed, 1 passed**, and on the same base tree
   `python -m pytest -q tests/tools/test_skill_manage_batch.py` → **9 passed** (the delta
   is the new file). The one test that passes at base is the plain successful-rollback
   path; it is a regression guard.
2. This branch: `python -m pytest -q tests/tools/test_skill_batch_rollback_park.py tests/tools/test_skill_manage_batch.py`
   → **14 passed**.
3. The interruption test SIGKILLs a child process that is between the park and the
   copy-back, then asserts the loader walk yields nothing under the root and exactly one
   park exists outside it.
4. `scripts/run_tests_parallel.py -j 8 tests/*/test_skill*.py tests/*/test_skills*.py`
   → **55 files, 883 passed, 0 failed, 9 skipped** (macOS 26, Python 3.11). I ran this
   skill-related surface rather than the full suite.
5. `python -m ruff check tools/skill_manager_batch.py tests/tools/test_skill_batch_rollback_park.py`
   → clean.

- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) — #112321 and #67748 cover the discovery/resolve halves; this is the park-location half (see Related Issue)

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (docstrings) — docstrings on the new/changed
