prs.title: feat(web): honest, state-driven working indicator
prs.body:
## 📝 Description

Implements **part 1** of #3406: replace the Web UI's canned rotating "thinking" phrases with an honest, state-driven working indicator.

Today `components/chat/typing-indicator.tsx` shows bouncing dots + a shimmer bar + 4 rotating canned phrases (`chat.thinking.step1..4`) that never reflect what is actually happening. During a long reasoning turn (or a hung provider) the user cannot tell "working" from "dead", so they wait, reload, or resend.

This PR drives the indicator only from events the `pico` WebSocket **already reports** — no synthetic progress.

**What changed**

- `store/chat.ts` — the chat store now tracks the running turn: `turnPhase` (`idle | connecting | thinking | reasoning | tool | writing`), `turnPhaseDetail` (e.g. the tool name), `turnStartedAt`, and `turnActivityAt`. `updateChatStore` reconciles the phase with `isTyping` when a patch does not set the phase explicitly, so call sites that only flip `isTyping` (send / switch session / new chat / connection errors) can never leave a stale phase behind.
- `features/chat/turn-phase.ts` (new) — a small pure reducer that folds a stream event into the turn-phase state, plus a `firstToolCallName` helper. `now` is injected so it stays testable.
- `features/chat/protocol.ts` — derives the phase from the events it already handles: `typing.start` → connecting; `message.create` with `placeholder: true` → thinking; assistant `kind === "thought"` → reasoning; `kind === "tool_calls"` → tool (with the tool name); `message.update` → streaming progress; normal reply / `typing.stop` / `error` → idle.
- `components/chat/typing-indicator.tsx` — renders the concrete phase (e.g. *Running `exec`…*), a live elapsed timer, and after **20s** without any stream event escalates to a clearly different "still working — taking longer than usual" hint (dots switch from bounce to pulse). No fake progress bar.
- i18n — adds `chat.working.*` keys to all five locales (en, zh, pt-br, bn-in, cs).

Frontend-only; no backend or gateway changes.

prs.title: fix(pico/web): surface steering queue state so queued/dropped messages are no longer invisible
prs.body:
## 📝 Description

When a session is already running a turn, an inbound message on the `pico` (web UI) channel is routed to the steering queue. Previously the client got **no acknowledgement on success** and **no signal at all when the queue was full** (`MaxQueueSize=10`), so a message could be silently lost with no UI feedback.

This PR adds end-to-end feedback for that path:

**Backend (`pkg/agent`, `pkg/channels`)**
- Emit the existing `agent.interrupt.received` event with machine-readable attrs (`steering_result=queued|dropped`, `message_id`, `channel`, `chat_id`, `queue_depth`) on **both** the enqueue and the queue-full paths.
- Channels can opt in to observe these via the new `channels.RuntimeEventAware` interface, which the `Manager` injects at channel creation.
- Reuses the existing event kind, so no new event kinds or docs changes are required.

**Frontend (`web/frontend`)**
- Handle the new server frames: mark the matching local user message as **queued** and show its queue depth; on `steering_queue_full`, keep the bubble visible, mark it **failed** and toast the server error.
- Clear the queued state once the assistant starts producing a normal (non-placeholder) message.
- Add `queued`/`failed` fields to the chat store and translate the new badge strings in all five locales.

## 🗣️ Type of Change
- [x] 🐞 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] 📖 Documentation update
- [ ] ⚡ Code refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)

## 🤖 AI Code Generation
- [ ] 🤖 Fully AI-generated (100% AI, 0% Human)
- [ ] 🛠️ Mostly AI-generated (AI draft, Human verified/modified)
- [x] 👨‍💻 Mostly Human-written (Human lead, AI assisted or none)

## 🔗 Related Issue

Fixes #3408

## 📚 Technical Context (Skip for Docs)
- **Reference URL:** https://github.com/sipeed/picoclaw/issues/3408
- **Reasoning:** The steering queue (`pkg/agent/steering.go`) already had the `agent.interrupt.received` event kind and a bounded queue (`MaxQueueSize=10`), but the enqueue/queue-full paths never surfaced anything to the client, and the `pico` channel did not consume runtime events. The fix wires the existing event through a new opt-in `RuntimeEventAware` interface (no new event kinds, no protocol break) and renders the queued/failed state in the web UI.

prs.title: fix laggy interface
prs.body:
## 📝 Description

This fix allows the web UI to stop lagging when there's a lot of text in the chat area.
I have built and tested `picoclaw-launcher` and have no more lag either on the desktop and mobile browser (both Brave).
I am **no** TS / node developer, this has been analyzed and fixed by Qwen 3.8 27B harnessed on crush, here's what it has to say about it:

### Root cause

The chat input lives in `ChatPage` (`web/frontend/src/components/chat/chat-page.tsx:110`). Every keystroke calls `setInput`, re-rendering the whole page, which re-renders the message list and re-rendered every `AssistantMessage` – each one re-parsing its markdown via `react-markdown` + `remark-gfm` + `rehype-sanitize` + `rehype-highlight`. Cost is O(history length) per keystroke, hence the lag once history grows.

### Fix

Memoized both message components so unchanged messages are skipped:

- `web/frontend/src/components/chat/assistant-message.tsx:305` – `export const AssistantMessage = memo(AssistantMessageBase)`
- `web/frontend/src/components/chat/user-message.tsx:103` – `export const UserMessage = memo(UserMessageBase)`

This is safe because props are plain data (no inline callbacks), and the safe store's streaming updates (`features/chat/protocol.ts:163–179`) preserve object references for messages that didn't change, so during streaming only the actively-updating message re-renders. Named exports and imports are unchanged. Per your instruction, I did not build or launch – recommend running `pnpm build` / `lint` in `web/frontend` and typing in a long session to verify smoothness.

prs.title: fix(openai_compat): handle Gemini thought_signature (echo captured + sentinel for unsigned tool calls)
prs.body:
## 📝 Description

Fix the `400 INVALID_ARGUMENT` error returned by Gemini 3 when continuing a tool-calling conversation through the OpenAI-compatible endpoint:

```
Function call is missing a thought_signature in functionCall parts.
This is required for tools to work correctly, and missing thought_signature
may lead to degraded model performance. ... https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/thought-signatures
```

Gemini 3 requires the `thought_signature` to be **echoed back inside `extra_content.google.thought_signature`** on every `functionCall` part of the request history. PicoClaw's OpenAI-compatible provider only sent it under `function.thought_signature`, which Gemini rejects on the follow-up request.

Three distinct bugs are fixed:

1. **Serialization** (`pkg/providers/common/common.go`): resolve the signature from every known location (`Function.ThoughtSignature`, top-level `ThoughtSignature`, `ExtraContent.Google`) and emit it inside `extra_content.google.thought_signature`. A signature-less tool call no longer emits an empty `extra_content` block.

2. **Streaming capture** (`pkg/providers/openai_compat/provider.go`): `parseStreamResponse` did **not** read the `thought_signature` at all. Since `ChatStream` is the default chat path, any tool call produced in streaming mode lost the signature entirely, so the next request was rejected. The delta parser now captures the signature from both `function.thought_signature` and `extra_content.google.thought_signature`.

3. **Unsigned tool calls on Gemini hosts** (`pkg/providers/common/common.go` + `pkg/providers/openai_compat/provider.go`): fixes 1 and 2 only cover the case where the tool call was produced *by Gemini itself*, so a signature is available to echo. They do **not** cover the case that actually breaks the fallback chain: the tool call was produced by another provider (e.g. `deepseek-v4.1-flash`) and the turn later fell back to Gemini 3. There is no signature to echo, and Gemini rejects the request with the same `400`. Fix: a new `SerializeOptions{GeminiThoughtSignatureFallback}` injects the documented sentinel `skip_thought_signature_validator` into `extra_content.google.thought_signature` on every unsigned `functionCall` part. The option is enabled only for Gemini hosts (`isGeminiHost`), so every other endpoint keeps omitting `extra_content` exactly as before, and a real captured signature is never overridden.

## 🗣️ Type of Change
- [x] 🐞 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] 📖 Documentation update
- [ ] ⚡ Code refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)

## 🤖 AI Code Generation
- [ ] 🤖 Fully AI-generated (100% AI, 0% Human)
- [x] 🛠️ Mostly AI-generated (AI draft, Human verified/modified)
- [ ] 👨‍💻 Mostly Human-written (Human lead, AI assisted or none)

## 🔗 Related Issue

Refs #3230, Refs #3111 — same `400` on OpenAI-compat Gemini 3 tool loops.

## 📚 Technical Context (Skip for Docs)
- **Reference URL:** https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/thought-signatures
- **Reasoning:**
  - Gemini 3 (via both `generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/` and gateways such as Cloudflare AI Gateway) mandatory-signature contract. The signature must be resent on the assistant tool-call message of the following request, and Google specifically looks for `extra_content.google.thought_signature`.
  - `extra_content` is a Google-only extension. Providers that don't support it ignore unknown fields on the assistant tool-call object, so emitting it is additive; the `google` key is what only Gemini accepts. This mirrors upstream's existing `serializeToolCalls` behavior of preserving signatures, ordering the resolution so a top-level `ThoughtSignature` (set by the streaming path) still wins.

## 🧪 Test Environment
- **Hardware:** PC (linux/amd64)
- **OS:** Linux
- **Model/Provider:** `gemini-3.8-flash` via Google AI Studio OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/`)
- **Channels:** Telegram / web

## 📸 Evidence (Optional)
<details>
<summary>Click to view Logs/Screenshots</summary>

Reproduced failure mode (provider fallback from a DeepSeek primary to Gemini):

```
failover(format): provider=openai model=gemini-3.8-flash status=400
Function call is missing a thought_signature in functionCall parts...
```

Live reproduction against `generativelanguage.googleapis.com` (OpenAI-compat endpoint) confirms the fix for bug 3: an unsigned `functionCall` part fails with `400`, while the same part carrying the documented sentinel `skip_thought_signature_validator` is accepted; a real captured signature is preserved and never replaced.

Local verification:
```
$ go test ./pkg/providers/...
ok  github.com/sipeed/picoclaw/pkg/providers/common        0.032s
ok  github.com/sipeed/picoclaw/pkg/providers/openai_compat 0.121s
(... all pkg/providers packages pass)

$ golangci-lint run --build-tags goolm,stdjson ./pkg/providers/...
0 issues.
```

New tests cover: wire payload contains `"extra_content":{"google":{"thought_signature":"..."}}` when the signature is only on `Function`, only top-level, or only on `ExtraContent`; no `extra_content` when there is no signature; a streaming `ChatStream` round that captures the signature from the delta; the sentinel is injected for unsigned parts on Gemini hosts and omitted on non-Gemini hosts; and a real signature is never overridden by the sentinel.

</details>

- [x] My code/docs follow the style of this project.
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my own changes.
- [x] I have updated the documentation accordingly. (inline doc comments; no user-facing docs affected)

issues.title: install-signal-cli.sh pins signal-cli 0.14.3, which silently hangs forever establishing a session with a new contact — fixed upstream in 0.14.7

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something is not working as expected

issues.body:
## Summary

`setup/install-signal-cli.sh` pins `VERSION="0.14.3"` for the native Linux
build. That version has a bug where sending to (or receiving from) a
Signal contact it hasn't established a session with before **hangs
indefinitely** — no error, no timeout, on either side of the conversation.
Self-send (an account messaging itself) works fine on 0.14.3, which makes
this easy to mistake for an application-level or network problem rather
than the `signal-cli` binary itself.

Upgrading to the latest release (0.14.7 as of this writing) fixes it: the
exact same call against an unfamiliar/invalid recipient returns a proper
error (e.g. `UNREGISTERED_FAILURE`) immediately instead of hanging.

## Steps to reproduce (isolating it to signal-cli itself)

With the daemon already running, talk to its JSON-RPC socket directly to
rule out anything in NanoClaw's own channel/adapter code:

```bash
exec 3<>/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/7583
echo '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"send","params":{"account":"+1...","recipient":["+1...never-messaged-before..."],"message":"test"},"id":1}' >&3
timeout 30 cat <&3
exec 3<&-
```

On 0.14.3: no response at all, ever (tested up to 45s). Self-send to the
account's own number, by contrast, returns a `SUCCESS` result instantly.

After replacing the binary with 0.14.7 (same account, same data
directory, no other changes) and restarting the daemon: the identical call
against an unregistered number returns
`{"error":{"code":-1,"message":"Failed to send message", ... "type":"UNREGISTERED_FAILURE" ...}}`
immediately.

## Suggested fix

Bump `VERSION` in `install-signal-cli.sh` (and the equivalent Homebrew
formula pin, if any) past 0.14.3 — 0.14.7 is confirmed working. Worth
checking AsamK/signal-cli's changelog between those versions for the exact
fixing commit/release note, but the practical fix is just the version bump.

## Environment

- Ubuntu 24.04 on WSL2 (Windows 11), Node 22.23.2
- nanoclaw v2.3.0 (commit `f7376aa9`, 2026-08-25)
- Confirmed not an already-filed AsamK/signal-cli issue — nothing open
  there matches this symptom, and it's already fixed in the latest
  release, so filing upstream isn't useful; the actionable fix is on
  NanoClaw's side (the version pin).

issues.title: Service doesn't start at boot when linger is enabled on an encrypted home directory

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something is not working as expected

labels.name: priority/medium
labels.description: Maintainer-set

issues.body:
## What happens

On systems where the **home directory itself** is encrypted (ecryptfs, fscrypt, gocryptfs — i.e., per-user encryption decrypted at PAM login, **not** full-disk LUKS which is decrypted at boot), enabling linger causes the nanoclaw service to silently not start at boot. Every reboot reproduces it. The service only comes up after a manual `systemctl --user daemon-reload && systemctl --user restart nanoclaw` after logging in.

This matches a recurring report from the community: "Does anyone have problems with the systemd service not running because of linger combined with encrypted user dir? I seem to struggle with this again and again."

> **Scope note:** This issue is specifically about per-home encryption. LUKS / full-disk encryption is decrypted before userspace runs and is **not affected**.

## Why it happens

The setup wizard writes the systemd unit to `~/.config/systemd/user/nanoclaw.service` and runs `loginctl enable-linger` so the service survives reboots.

The problem: on per-home-encrypted systems, the home directory is only decrypted when you log in via PAM. At boot, systemd starts the user manager (via linger) before any login happens, so `~/.config/systemd/user/` is not readable. The user manager starts with an empty unit table and nanoclaw never launches.

When you later SSH in, PAM decrypts the home — but the user manager is already running with its stale state and won't pick up the unit file until you reload manually.

The setup wizard doesn't catch this because it probes `systemctl --user daemon-reload` from your interactive shell, where the home is already decrypted, so the check always passes.

## Repro

1. Set up a Linux system with a per-home-encrypted home directory (e.g. Ubuntu's classic "encrypt my home directory" ecryptfs option, or fscrypt-managed home).
2. Run `bash nanoclaw.sh` — setup completes successfully.
3. Reboot.
4. The nanoclaw service is not running.
5. SSH in, then run `systemctl --user daemon-reload && systemctl --user restart nanoclaw` — service comes up fine.
6. Repeat from step 3.

## Why the obvious fixes don't actually work

It's tempting to "just move the unit file outside the encrypted home" (e.g., to `/etc/systemd/system/` with `User=$USER`, or `/etc/systemd/user/`). This doesn't fix the bug: the unit's `ExecStart=${nodePath} ${projectRoot}/dist/index.js` and `WorkingDirectory=${projectRoot}` both still reference paths inside the encrypted home. The user manager would be able to read the unit at boot but the exec would fail because the binary and working directory aren't decrypted yet. You'd just get a fast-failing service in a restart loop instead of an empty unit table.

Making it actually work at boot would require relocating the entire install (node binary, project root, logs) outside the encrypted home — a substantially bigger architectural change, and arguably the wrong tradeoff for users who specifically chose per-home encryption.

## Suggested fix

Accept that this can't work at boot on per-home-encrypted systems, and make the degraded behavior honest and self-healing:

1. **Detect per-home encryption specifically.** Check for ecryptfs / fscrypt / gocryptfs on `$HOME` — e.g., `findmnt -T "$HOME" -o FSTYPE` matching `ecryptfs`, the presence of `~/.ecryptfs` / `~/.Private`, or fscrypt policy markers. Do **not** treat LUKS or other block-level encryption as a trigger.
   - **fscrypt is the fiddly one to detect.** It's per-directory encryption layered on top of ext4 / f2fs / etc., so there's no separate mount entry and no universal marker file. The reliable signal is `fscrypt status "$HOME"` (when the `fscrypt` CLI is installed) or querying the kernel directly via `ioctl FS_IOC_GET_ENCRYPTION_POLICY`. Marker-file heuristics will miss legitimate setups, so whatever detection lands here should be validated against a real fscrypt-protected home before shipping.
2. **Skip `loginctl enable-linger`** silently when detected, and install the user unit as today.
3. **Warn the user clearly** at setup time: linger was disabled because the home directory is per-home-encrypted; the service will start on first login after each reboot rather than at boot itself.
4. **Optional: add a login hook** (PAM `pam_exec`, `~/.bash_profile`, or similar) that runs `systemctl --user start nanoclaw` on first login so the service self-heals after each reboot without manual intervention.

## Related

Similar in spirit to #2482 — both are cases where setup checks pass in the interactive shell but boot-time / non-interactive behavior differs silently.

prs.title: fix(setup): wait for docker before starting the systemd unit
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Makes the generated systemd unit wait for Docker before starting the host.

- **Problem**: the unit only had `After=network.target`. On a Pi reboot the host started before dockerd was ready and hit `FATAL: Container runtime failed to start`. `Restart=always` recovered from that one, but it adds a crash-loop to every boot. Adding `After=docker.service` alone doesn't help the default install, which is a user unit: a user unit can't order itself against system units.
- **Fix**: an `ExecStartPre` loops on `docker info` every 2s, capped by `TimeoutStartSec=300`. It also adds `After=network-online.target docker.service` + `Wants=network-online.target`, which take effect for root/system installs.
- **Out of scope**: rewriting units that are already installed. Existing installs pick this up the next time setup's service step runs.

## Related work

No issue. The change is confined to the `renderSystemdUnit` template, plus a test.

prs.title: fix(signal): stage inbound attachments via the session inbox
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

<!-- Please give this PR a conventional-commit title (`fix:`, `feat:`, `docs:`,
     `refactor:`, `chore:`, `ci:`, `test:`, `build:`, `style:`, `perf:`) —
     a request, not a requirement; it helps labeling when no kind box is checked.

     Plain English, short sentences, no filler. Write for a reviewer with 60
     seconds — technical terms fine, decoration not. If a sentence adds no
     reviewable fact, delete it.

     Keep Summary, Change kind, Validation, Security, and AI assistance in
     every PR ("None." beats deletion); Related work, User and release
     impact, and Skill delivery may go when they don't apply. -->

## Summary

Lets Signal users send files to their agent — today every inbound attachment is either dropped or unreachable.

* Problem: inbound attachments are filtered to image/* and audio/*, so a PDF sent alongside text arrives as text alone, and a PDF sent by itself returns early and the agent never wakes.
* Problem: "Note to Self" is the primary DM path on a device-linked install, since the agent shares the operator's own Signal account. It  never read attachments at all, and dropped caption-less files before the agent woke
* Problem: images don't work either. The adapter emits a host path under SIGNAL_DATA_DIR, but signal-cli's attachments directory isn't mounted into agent containers, and extractAttachmentFiles only stages entries carrying inline data  so the agent gets a dead reference.
* Fix: read every attachment into base64 data, the contract the host already implements. The host writes the bytes to inbox/<messageId>/ and rewrites each entry to a container-readable localPath.
* Precedent: fc64137a applied exactly this fix to the iMessage adapter, which had the identical defect.
*  Also: an attachment that can't be read now produces a visible [report.pdf could not be read] note instead of vanishing silently.
* Also: a 20MB inline cap (SIGNAL_MAX_INLINE_ATTACHMENT_BYTES) bounds what travels base64-inline through the session DB, matching the iMessage adapter's default.
* Behavior change: image-only messages now carry empty text - the attachment renders through the formatter's suffix rather than an [Image: <path>] line. [Voice Message - file not found] is replaced by the shared failure note.
* Base branch: channels, since signal.ts exists only there. CONTRIBUTING says to branch from main, but that guidance covers contributing a new channel skill; happy to retarget if you'd rather take it differently.
* Out of scope: outbound attachments, which already work (b672e827), and the base64-inline transport itself.
* Testing: 10 new unit tests, 53 pass in signal.test.ts; verified end-to-end on a live device-linked install — an 8-page PDF sent to Note to Self now stages into the session inbox and the agent reads it.


## Change kind

<!-- Check exactly one. -->
- [X] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

<!-- A bullet per piece of evidence: command -> result. Add the manual path
     for behavior CI cannot cover. New or changed behavior needs a new or
     changed test — or one line saying why not (docs-only, config-only,
     unreachable in CI). -->

- [X] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

<!-- Maintainers own CHANGELOG.md — do not edit it in this PR. -->
- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [X] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
Optional: one user-facing line for the changelog. Skip it and a maintainer will write one.
```
Add inbound attachment support for Signal channel

## Security and trust boundaries
* Untrusted input: attachment filenames come from the sender. The adapter passes filename through as name unmodified and does not build paths from it. Containment stays with the host's existing guards — isSafeAttachmentName rejects traversal sentinels, path separators and NUL, ensureContainedInboxDir refuses a symlinked inbox, and staging writes with wx so an existing file is never overwritten. This  change adds no new path-construction sink.
*  Filesystem: reads are confined to join(config.signalDataDir, 'attachments', att.id) for ids signal-cli itself reported. The adapter writes nothing to disk; it previously handed out host paths and now hands out bytes, which strictly reduces what the container is told about the host layout.
* Resource bound: attachment bytes are read into memory and base64-encoded into the session DB. The 20MB cap is checked against statSync before the read, so an oversized file is never loaded. Signal permits ~100MB, so this is a deliberate ceiling rather than a theoretical one.
* No change to permissions, credentials, approval flows, CI workflows, container configuration, or mounts. No new dependency.

prs.title: fix(scheduling): honor task-script shebangs instead of forcing bash
prs.body:
## Summary

Pre-task scripts that declare their interpreter via a shebang stop failing with bash syntax errors.
- **Problem**: `runScript` writes the script to `/tmp/task-script-<id>.sh` and always `execFile('bash', [file])`. Bash treats the `#!` line as a comment and the body as shell — a `#!/usr/bin/env node` script fails with `line 5: syntax error near unexpected token '('` before running a line. The language contract is also undocumented: `ncl tasks create --help` advertises gate scripts without stating one.
- **Fix**: scripts starting with `#!` are exec'd directly under an extensionless temp name (the kernel resolves the interpreter — runtimes that sniff extensions re-route `.sh` files to their own shell); everything else keeps the historical `bash <file>` call.
- **Out of scope**: script timeout policy (30s stays) and the `--help` language line if maintainers prefer that separately.

## Related work

No open issue — safe to review directly. #3662 recently touched this function (timeout error message); orthogonal, composes cleanly, either rebases trivially.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`

## Validation

- New test: shebang'd script executes under its declared interpreter (failed under bash before) — `bun test --isolate src/scheduling/task-script.test.ts` → 7 passed, 0 failed
- Existing pinned bash behavior unchanged — same suite green
- Manual: daily-scrape task with a `#!/usr/bin/env node` pre-task script ran end-to-end on a live install (scrape+build+publish, `wakeAgent` JSON, agent woken)

## User and release impact

- [x] User-visible change — release note below

```release-note
Pre-task scripts that start with a shebang now run under their declared interpreter (e.g. `#!/usr/bin/env node`) instead of always bash.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

None. Pre-task scripts already execute arbitrary task-author code under the container identity; this changes only which interpreter parses the file.

- [x] A human has reviewed this PR and stands behind every change

prs.title: fix: stage inbound attachments that expose only a url (Discord)
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Makes Discord attachments (images, and pasted text Discord turns into `message.txt`) readable by the agent.
- **Problem**: the chat-sdk bridge only downloads bytes via `att.fetchData()`. The Discord adapter exposes a CDN `url` instead, and the bridge drops `url` when serializing. The entry reaches the host with no `data`, `extractAttachmentFiles` skips it, and the agent sees a path-less `[file: message.txt]` it can never open.
- **Fix**: move enrichment into `enrichAttachments()`. Always keep `url` on the entry. When there is no `fetchData` but there is a `url`, download from the url so the bytes stage to the inbox like any `fetchData` attachment.
- **Cap**: both download paths bound inlined bytes by `MAX_INBOUND_ATTACHMENT_BYTES` (default 10 MB). Checks run cheapest first: declared `att.size`, then `Content-Length` (url path only), then actual byte length. Oversized attachments keep `url` as a reference and carry no bytes.
- **Out of scope**: rate-limiting repeated uploads. That belongs at the session/rate layer.

## Related work

Closes #2426. Supersedes #2427, which preserved `url` but never fetched the bytes, so url-only adapters still produced no readable file.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/channels/chat-sdk-bridge.test.ts` → new `enrichAttachments` suite passes: url-only download, `fetchData` preferred over `url`, url kept and no `data` on download failure, metadata-only when neither is present, and the cap on both paths (declared size, oversized body without size metadata, within-cap still staged).
- `pnpm exec vitest run` on this branch merged with current `main` → 213 files / 2532 tests pass.
- `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` → clean.
- Manual: running in production on a Discord install since June; pasted text and images reach the agent as files in the inbox.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
Discord attachments (images and pasted text) now reach the agent as readable files instead of a bare placeholder. Inbound attachment downloads on every chat-sdk channel are capped at 10 MB, overridable with MAX_INBOUND_ATTACHMENT_BYTES.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

Untrusted input: anyone who can message the bot controls attachment contents and size. The host now fetches the adapter-supplied attachment `url` (the Discord CDN link from the platform payload, not user message text). Bytes are inlined only within the cap, so a large upload cannot inflate the POST body or prompt context. The same cap now also applies to the existing `fetchData` path (Slack et al.), which previously had none.

prs.title: fix(cross-session-context): the agent's own replies from other threads read as "you"
prs.body:
## What and why In a DM or channel where each thread has its own session, the agent's reply in one thread is copied into its other live threads as context. The copy was signed with the agent group's name, so in thread B the agent saw `sender="Pixel"` and took its own earlier reply for a second agent's. History rows already show the agent's own posts as `sender="you"`, through a `self` flag that backfill writes. The copies now carry the same flag. ## How it works ```mermaid --- config: look: neo --- flowchart LR subgraph before["Before"] direction TB b1["Thread A
Pixel replies to Alex"] b2["fanOutbound
copy: sender Pixel"] b3["formatEchoMessage
sender=#quot;Pixel#quot;"] b4["Pixel in thread B
another agent said this"] b1 -->|delivered| b2 -->|"writes to thread B"| b3 -->|renders| b4 end subgraph after["After"] direction TB a1["Thread A
Pixel replies to Alex"] a2["fanOutbound
copy: sender Pixel
+ self: true"] a3["formatEchoMessage
self → sender=#quot;you#quot;"] a4["Pixel in thread B
I said this in another thread"] a1 -->|delivered| a2 -->|"writes to thread B"| a3 -->|renders| a4 end before ~~~ after classDef req fill:#ddf4ff,stroke:#54aeff,color:#0a3069 classDef step fill:#f6f8fa,stroke:#8c959f,color:#24292f classDef bad fill:#ffebe9,stroke:#ff8182,color:#82071e classDef good fill:#dafbe1,stroke:#4ac26b,color:#116329 classDef new fill:#fff8c5,stroke:#d4a72c,color:#4d2d00 class b1,a1 req class b2,b3 step class b4 bad class a2,a3 new class a4 good style before fill:none,stroke:#8c959f,stroke-dasharray:4 4,color:#57606a style after fill:none,stroke:#8c959f,stroke-dasharray:4 4,color:#57606a linkStyle default stroke:#8c959f ``` - `fanOutbound` copies the agent's own delivered messages, and now passes `self: true`. `fanEcho` writes the flag into the copy. Copies of people's messages never carry it. - `formatEchoMessage` uses one rule for history rows and copies: a row with `self` renders `sender="you"`. The history branch's own copy of that rule is removed. - The system prompt said a copy's `from` tells the agent which kind it is. For a reply from a sibling thread it doesn't (`from="another conversation in #pixel-room room"`), so the sentence now says `sender="you"` marks the agent's own. - Copies the agent posts into a conversation from a scheduled task, or from another conversation, get `sender="you"` too. Their labels already say "posted by your scheduled task" and "posted by you from another conversation". ## Tested - Real host and runner code against the same mailbox file, locally: `fanInboundMessage` and `fanOutboundMessage` wrote into thread B's `inbound.db` for a channel with two thread sessions, and the runner's `formatMessages` read that file. - On `main`: `Here is the summary: launch moved to Tuesday.`. - On this branch: the same line with `sender="you"`. The person's message keeps `sender="Alex"`. - `fan.test.ts`: the agent's outbound copy carries `self: true` and a person's copy does not. - `cross-session-echo.test.ts`: a copy from a sibling thread with `self` renders `sender="you"`, and a history row with `self` still does. - `destinations.test.ts`: the reading section names `sender="you"`. - Each test fails when its change is reverted. Dropping the moved rule fails both formatter tests. Writing `self` on every copy fails the person's-copy test. - `pnpm run format:check`, `tsc` for host and runner, and `bun run test` (603 pass) all pass. `vitest run`: 3544 pass. 5 tests in `scripts/update/` timed out at 5 s in the parallel run; on their own they pass (45/45), and they touch none of these files. - Reviewed by a second agent. ## Not done - Not run in a live Slack workspace. ## AI assistance - [x] AI tools or agents helped produce this change - [x] A human has reviewed this PR and stands behind every change

prs.title: feat(skills): add /add-lean-tasks for minimal-context scheduled task runs
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Adds `/add-lean-tasks`, so a scheduled task can run cheaply on a small or local model without the agent's full context.

- **Problem**: every task fire carries the Claude Code preset, composed instructions, skills, memory, all MCP servers and the resumed session. A small model spends most of the turn reading that and often cannot drive the tools anyway.
- **Feature**: `ncl tasks create/update --lean true` runs each fire with a slim plain system prompt (name, destinations, output format), no filesystem settings, no resume, no MCP servers and no built-in tools.
- **Delivery**: the lean turn has no tools, so it writes `<message to="NAME">` and `<card to="NAME" title="...">` blocks in its final text; each block is delivered and recorded in the run log as one line (`[sent → family] ...`).
- **Render**: optional `--render "<command>"` pipes the final text through a command (stdin → stdout) before the blocks are parsed, so the model can return plain data and a script writes the message. A failing or silent command falls back to the model text.
- **Skill payload** (on `main`, like `/add-opencode`): host module registers the two task fields; agent-runner module registers a turn hook that marks lean task batches and a Claude provider wrapper that sends marked queries to a second, minimal-context instance and delivers the blocks before the poll loop sees the result. One barrel line per tree.
- **Core commit** `refactor(agent-runner): add a minimalContext provider option`: `settingSources` and the built-in tool list were not reachable through `ProviderOptions`/`QueryInput`. `minimalContext: true` makes the Claude provider load no settings and disallow its built-ins; omitted (every existing caller) the SDK options are unchanged. prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Lets an install add its own per-task fields to scheduled tasks without editing `tasks.ts`, the scheduling module, or the mailbox.

- **Problem**: every extra task field (a per-task timeout, a label, and so on) means editing the tasks CLI flags, the create path's content JSON, `TaskUpdate`, the SQLite update merge, and the `get` output. That is five upstream files per field, and each one conflicts on the next update.
- **Fix**: `registerTaskField({ flag, contentKey, type?, description, parse? })` in `src/modules/scheduling/task-fields.ts`. A registered field becomes a `ncl tasks create` / `update` flag. The CLI coerces it by `type` and validates it with `parse`, and the result is stored as `content[contentKey]`. On update it is merged into the envelope, leaving other keys alone. `ncl tasks get` returns it under the flag name.
- **Default unchanged**: with nothing registered, the create/update flag lists, the stored content JSON, the `get` output and the strict `unknown flag` rejection are all the same as before.
- **Guard rails**: flags and content keys that core already uses (`prompt`, `script`, `originSessionId`, `--group`, ...) are refused at registration, and so are duplicates.
- **Lazy flag lists**: `crud.ts` now reads a custom verb's `args` on each call, not once at registration. The tasks verbs expose `args` as a getter, so a field registered after `tasks.ts` loads is still accepted.
- **Container side**: no change needed. The agent-runner already gets the whole `messages_in.content` envelope and `JSON.parse`s it (see `container/agent-runner/src/scheduling/task-script.ts`). Recurrence clones and `ncl tasks run` copy the content verbatim. A consumer reads `content[contentKey]` there.
- **Out of scope**: registering any concrete field; changing what the container does with the envelope.

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Makes Slack show `send_card` collapsible sections as real collapsible blocks, starting collapsed, so long logs and stack traces don't flood the channel.

> **Merge order: after #3926 and #3927.** Depends on #3926 and #3927. It compiles and is harmless without them, but it does nothing until both are merged.

- **Problem**: once #3927 is in, a collapsible section still renders expanded on Slack, because the shared `Card` model has no collapsible element.
- **Fix**: the Slack adapter passes the bridge a `postCard` override (#3926). If the card has a collapsible child, it posts Block Kit through the adapter's `webClient`: title as header, then description and plain children as sections, then one `container` block per collapsible section (`is_collapsible`, `default_collapsed`), then link actions as buttons. It returns the message `ts`.
- **Default card still used**: a card with no collapsible child, one over Slack's 50-block message limit, or any Slack API error (for example `invalid_blocks`) returns `undefined`, so the bridge posts its default card the way it does today.
- **Limits**: the container title is trimmed to 150 characters, with `Details` when it is empty. Section text is split at newlines into at most 10 child blocks under the 3000-character section cap. Text past that is cut off and ends with `…`.
- **Same look as today**: title, sections and buttons go through `cardToBlockKit`, so apart from the containers the card looks the same as the default one.
- **Works with an older bridge**: `postCard` is typed locally and passed through a typed config variable, so this branch also compiles against a core without #3926, where the bridge ignores the extra field.

## Related work

Reviewed as a set with #3926, #3927 (maintainer grouping on #3899).

prs.title: docs: document the fork-local code folder convention
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Documents a folder convention that keeps a fork's in-tree code from conflicting on upgrade.

- **Problem**: the docs say "every change is a skill", but they don't say where a fork's own code should sit in the tree before it becomes a skill, or where a skill's copied-in files should go. Edits inside upstream files are what make upgrades expensive.
- **Evidence**: in one real fork upgrade across ~420 upstream commits, 124 fork-only new files produced 0 conflicts. 208 edits inside upstream files produced 91 conflicted files (~200 hunks).
- **Convention**: fork-only code goes in one folder that mirrors the upstream layout (`src/local/`, `container/agent-runner/src/local/`). It is wired in with one barrel line per upstream file, each guarded by a registration test. Upstream behavior is extended by wrapping (a decorator), and upstream helpers are imported, never copied. When a fork needs an upstream decision to change, it proposes a behavior-neutral seam upstream.
- **Where**: a fuller section in `docs/customizing.md`, plus a short section (under 12 lines) in `CLAUDE.md` that links to it. The Docs Index entry for `customizing.md` is updated to match.
- **Out of scope**: no code, no new doc file. The registration-test details are left to `skill-guidelines.md`, which the new section links to.

prs.title: refactor: add an operational error sink seam for host plumbing failures
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Adds a behavior-neutral seam so a skill can observe the host's own plumbing failures, which today only reach the host log.

- **Problem**: a startup crash loop, a task script that keeps failing and backing off (or gets auto-paused), and a message given up on after its final attempt are logged and nothing else. From the chat side that is indistinguishable from "nothing to report".
- **Seam**: `src/operational-errors.ts` — `registerOperationalErrorSink(sink)` (returns an unregister function) and `reportOperationalError({ kind, message, key, details })`.
- **Call sites**: `enforceStartupBackoff` (when it delays startup, before the sleep), `handleRecurrence` (script-failing re-arm and auto-pause), `drainSession` (permanent delivery failure). One call each, next to the existing log line.
- **Default**: no sink registered → `reportOperationalError` returns immediately. Behavior is unchanged.
- **Guardrails**: sinks run on a microtask and are never awaited; a throwing or rejecting sink is logged at warn and dropped, so a sink can never block or break startup, the sweep, or delivery.
- **Out of scope**: any destination. The companion `/add-error-reports` skill (separate PR) is one consumer.

## Related work

Reviewed as a set with #3935 (maintainer grouping on #3899).

Related: #2492 and #2498 describe the same silent-failure gap; #2498 hard-wires Discord alerts into core. This PR only adds the observation point, so any channel can consume it from a skill.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [x] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/operational-errors.test.ts src/circuit-breaker.test.ts src/modules/scheduling/recurrence.test.ts src/delivery.test.ts` -> 53 passed
  - `operational-errors.test.ts`: no sink is a no-op; every sink gets the event with a timestamp; a slow, throwing, or rejecting sink never blocks or throws into the caller; unregister works.

prs.title: refactor(agent-runner): turn-lifecycle hook registry for the poll loop
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Adds a turn-lifecycle hook registry so installs can attach per-turn behavior without editing `poll-loop.ts`. Nothing changes unless a hook is registered.

- **Problem**: anything that has to act on a turn has to be written into the loop body itself. That includes enriching inbound rows before formatting, picking a model per batch, observing provider events for progress or tracing, and reacting to a failed query. Every such edit conflicts with upstream changes to the poll loop.
- **Fix**: new `container/agent-runner/src/turn-hooks.ts` with `registerTurnHook({ name, beforeTurn?, prepareQuery?, onProviderEvent?, onError? })`. It follows the same pattern as `registerProvider` / `registerTools`: register at module scope, get loaded through the `modules/index.ts` barrel.
- **Hook points**:
  - `beforeTurn(ctx)`: runs after pre-task scripts and before formatting, for the opening batch and for follow-ups (`ctx.followUp`). Rows in `ctx.messages` may be rewritten in place.
  - `prepareQuery(input, ctx)`: opening batch only, just before `provider.query()`. It may return a replacement `QueryInput`.
  - `onProviderEvent(event, routing)`: runs on every event after `handleEvent`. It is fire-and-forget and never awaited, so it cannot stall the stream.
  - `onError(err, ctx)`: runs when the query throws, before continuation recovery.
- **Isolation**: hooks run in registration order. A hook that throws or rejects is logged as `[turn-hooks] <name>.<point> failed` and skipped. It never breaks the turn or the hooks after it.
- **Behavior-neutral**: with no hooks registered, `beforeTurn` and `onError` do nothing and `prepareQuery` returns the same input object. The only structural edit is that `processQuery` now gets `input.prompt` / `input.continuation`, which are the same values when no hook runs.
- **Out of scope**: runner commands, result-text transforms and delivery changes. Those are separate seams.

## Related work

Reviewed as a set with #3921, #3925, #3932, #3939 (maintainer grouping on #3899).

prs.body:
## Summary

Keeps each agent session's container stderr after the container exits, through a new log sink hook and a skill that uses it.

- **Problem**: containers run with `--rm`. The agent-runner's stderr is lost on exit. The host log has it at debug level only, plus a 10-line tail after a non-zero exit. A session that hangs, or exits 0 having done nothing, leaves no trace.
- **Hook**: `registerSessionLogSink()` in `src/drivers/session-log-sink.ts`. The docker driver opens it where it already reads the container's stderr: `src/drivers/docker-driver.ts:500`. With no sink registered, nothing changes.
- **Consumer**: new skill `/add-session-logs`. It registers a sink at `.claude/skills/add-session-logs/payload/src/drivers/session-file-log.ts:79` that appends each line to `logs/sessions/<session-id>.log`, with a per-file size cap (5 MiB default). Files are never rotated or deleted.
- **Who needs this**: anyone debugging a session whose container is already gone. The hook and the skill are one PR because a hook with no code on `main` that uses it does not land.
- **Out of scope**: log retention, other drivers, log shipping.

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Adds `/add-error-reports`, a skill that tells a chat of your choice when NanoClaw itself breaks, instead of leaving you to infer it from silence.

- **Problem**: a host crash-looping on startup, or a scheduled task whose pre-task script keeps failing and backing off, only writes to the host log. No message arriving looks exactly like "nothing to report".
- **What it does**: registers a sink on the operational error seam (`registerOperationalErrorSink`) and posts one short message per failure — startup backoff, failing or auto-paused task scripts, permanently failed deliveries — to one configured messaging group.
- **Channel-agnostic**: delivers through the host's channel delivery adapter (`onDeliveryAdapterReady` → `deliver`), destination resolved with `getMessagingGroup`. Any installed channel works; no webhook, no new credential.
- **Startup timing**: the crash-loop report is raised before channels exist, so it is queued (bounded to 20) and sent once the adapter is ready.
- **Rate limit**: per failure key; repeats inside the quiet window (default 60 min) are counted, and the next report says how many were suppressed.
- **Config** (`.env`): `ERROR_REPORTS_MESSAGING_GROUP` (required, from `ncl messaging-groups list`), optional `ERROR_REPORTS_THREAD_ID`, `ERROR_REPORTS_QUIET_MINUTES`. Unset → the module registers nothing.
- **Out of scope**: a host that dies before its channels start cannot report through a channel; SKILL.md Troubleshooting says so.

## Related work

Reviewed as a set with #3934 (maintainer grouping on #3899).

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Adds `/add-turn-traces`, so an operator can see what an agent did on each turn, with the data kept in the central DB and nothing sent to an external backend.

- **Problem**: finding out which tools an agent called on a turn, with what inputs, what they returned and how long it took means reading container stderr, which is gone once the container exits. The session DBs keep only the messages.
- **Feature**: one trace per answered batch in a `turn_traces` table. A trace holds message ids, provider, configured model, status (`ok` / `error` / `incomplete`), timings, inbound content, final output, provider error, and ordered steps (mid-turn text, tool calls with input, output, error flag and duration). Text fields are capped and each turn keeps at most 200 steps.
- **Read**: `ncl traces list [--agent-group-id] [--session-id] [--status] [--limit]` returns summaries with a one-line preview. `ncl traces get <id>` returns the full trace. Both are read-only and `hostOnly`.
- **Opt-in**: installing the skill records nothing. A group is traced only while `groups/<folder>/turn-traces.enabled` exists. The check runs every turn, so it needs no respawn.
- **Retention**: `TURN_TRACE_RETENTION_DAYS`, default 3. The first trace a host process records prunes and starts an hourly prune. Every `ncl traces` read prunes first, so an expired trace is never shown.
- **Footprint**: two self-registering modules and one barrel line per tree. The host module (`src/modules/turn-traces/`) registers a `registerMigration` module migration, an unguarded `turn_trace` delivery action and the CLI resource. The container module (`container/agent-runner/src/modules/turn-traces/`) registers a turn hook.
- **Code edit**: the only edit to existing code is `hooks: withTurnTraceHooks({...})` in `providers/claude.ts`. It appends tool-hook matchers after the provider's own, so the existing PreToolUse guard still runs first.
- **Out of scope**: tool steps for non-Claude providers (they get turn-level traces), retry turns after a wrap nudge (not recorded), and exporting to OTLP (#3796 covers that). An agent-to-operator notification tool is a separate follow-up.

## Related work

Reviewed as a set with #3904 (maintainer grouping on #3899).

Depends on #3904. This branch contains #3904's commit (merged in unchanged); only the last commit is this PR.

- #3904 turn-lifecycle hooks: the recorder attaches through `beforeTurn` / `onProviderEvent` / `onError` instead of editing `poll-loop.ts`.
- #3796 `/add-telemetry` exports OpenTelemetry spans to an external collector. This skill is the local, zero-infrastructure counterpart: a central-DB table plus `ncl`, with no collector or new dependency. The two can be installed side by side.
- #2012 `/add-usage-logging` records token and cost usage per query in `outbound.db`. It covers different data and does not overlap.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [x] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

These runs used the skill applied by hand from SKILL.md. It was then removed by hand following REMOVE.md steps 1–3, and `git status` showed only the skill folder.

- `pnpm run typecheck` -> clean
- `pnpm exec tsc -p container/agent-runner/tsconfig.json --noEmit` -> clean
- `pnpm run lint` -> 0 errors, no new warnings
- `pnpm run format:check` -> clean; container payload checked with prettier directly -> clean
- `pnpm exec tsx scripts/skill-directives.ts .claude/skills/add-turn-traces/SKILL.md` -> no problems
- `pnpm exec vitest run src/modules/turn-traces/` -> 6/6 pass. It covers the real modules barrel with real migrations: store, list, get, filters, unknown-status drop, container caller refused, expired trace hidden, and prune on first trace. With the host barrel line removed -> 4 fail.
- `bun test src/modules/turn-traces/` -> 8/8 pass. It covers the real turn-hook dispatch plus outbound row: one trace per batch, follow-up gets its own trace, retry not recorded, error, incomplete, step cap, nothing without the marker. With the container barrel line removed -> `turn-traces.test.ts` 0 pass. With the `claude.ts` wrap removed -> `claude-hooks.test.ts` 2 fail.
- `bun test` (full agent-runner suite, skill applied) -> 495 pass, 0 fail. The opt-in marker is what keeps existing poll-loop tests, which count outbound rows, unaffected.
- `pnpm test` (skill applied) -> 2936 pass. 3 failed with 5s timeouts on a loaded machine: `scripts/update/transaction.e2e.test.ts` and `src/templates/plugin-dir.test.ts`. Rerun alone -> 238/238 pass. Unrelated to this diff.
- `src/modules/community-portal/registration.test.ts` -> passes with the skill applied. The module registers no host-lifecycle callback, because that test assumes the portal's callback is the last one.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
New /add-turn-traces skill: opt-in per-turn agent traces (tool calls, inputs/outputs, timings, model) stored in the central DB with 3-day default retention and read with `ncl traces list/get`.
```

- **Privacy**: traces contain prompt content, tool inputs and tool outputs. Tracing is off until the skill is installed and a group is opted in by marker file. Default retention is 3 days, and REMOVE.md drops the table.

- **Untrusted input**: the `turn_trace` payload comes from inside the sandbox. The host re-validates every field, rejects unknown statuses, caps text, steps and total step JSON, and takes `session_id` / `agent_group_id` from the delivering session, never from the payload. The action is registered `unguarded(...)` because it writes only a host-only row for the sending session.
- **Not a control**: the marker sits in the agent's writable workspace, so an agent can turn its own tracing off. SKILL.md says traces are for debugging, not auditing.

prs.title: refactor(agent-runner): add a provider-wrapper seam with per-query model and retryable failures
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Lets an install wrap a provider (for example, retry a failed attempt on a backup model or credentials) without editing the provider module.

- **Problem**: adding attempt-level fallback today means editing `providers/claude.ts` itself. There is no hook at construction time, no per-query model, and a failed result does not say whether retrying is safe.
- **Fix, wrapper seam**: `registerProviderWrapper(name, (inner, ctx) => AgentProvider)` in `provider-registry.ts`. `createProvider` applies registered wrappers to the bare provider, and then attaches the contract hooks (`beforeQuery`, `afterExchange`, input binding) to the provider the runner actually holds. `ctx.create(options)` builds more unwrapped instances of the same provider, for example one per credential env. Registration can happen before or after `registerProvider`. Multiple wrappers compose in registration order.
- **Fix, per-query model**: optional `QueryInput.model`. The Claude provider sends `input.model ?? configured model`. Providers without per-query model selection ignore it.
- **Fix, retry-safety signal**: a failed `result` event gets an optional `retryable` field. Claude sets it to `true` when the failed attempt ran no tool call and emitted no assistant text, so a retry cannot repeat side effects or visible output. The poll-loop ignores the field.
- **Default unchanged**: with no wrapper registered and no `model` set, construction, SDK options and delivery are the same as before. `retryable` only appears on failed results, and nothing in core reads it.
- **Out of scope**: any fallback policy. Which models or credentials to try, in what order, and how to label the result belong to the wrapper, which ships as a skill or local module.

<details><summary>Sketch of a wrapper (not part of this PR)</summary>

```ts
import { registerProviderWrapper } from './provider-registry.js';
import type { AgentProvider, AgentQuery, ProviderEvent, QueryInput } from './types.js';

const BACKUP_MODELS = ['model-b', 'model-c'];

registerProviderWrapper('claude', (inner) => {
  const wrapped: AgentProvider = {
    registerMemorySessionHook: (hook, memory) => inner.registerMemorySessionHook(hook, memory),
    isSessionInvalid: (err) => inner.isSessionInvalid(err),
    maybeRotateContinuation: inner.maybeRotateContinuation?.bind(inner),
    query(input: QueryInput): AgentQuery {
      let active = inner.query(input);
      const pushed: string[] = [];
      let aborted = false;
      async function* events(): AsyncGenerator<ProviderEvent> {
        for (const model of [undefined, ...BACKUP_MODELS]) {
          if (model) {
            active = inner.query({ ...input, model });
            for (const msg of pushed) active.push(msg);
          }
          let retry = false;
          for await (const event of active.events) {
            if (aborted) return;
            if (event.type === 'result' && event.isError && event.retryable && model !== BACKUP_MODELS.at(-1)) {
              retry = true; // hold the failure back and try the next model
              break;
            }
            yield event;
            if (event.type === 'result') return;
          }
          if (!retry) return;
        }
      }
      return {
        push: (msg) => { pushed.push(msg); active.push(msg); },
        end: () => active.end(),
        abort: () => { aborted = true; active.abort(); },
        events: events(),
      };
    },
  };
  return wrapped;
});
```

To rotate credentials instead of models, a wrapper calls `ctx.create({ ...ctx.options, env: otherEnv })` for each alternative. It forwards `registerMemorySessionHook(hook, memory)` to every instance it creates.

</details>

## Related work

Reviewed as a set with #3921, #3904, #3932 (maintainer grouping on #3899).

No issue. #3069, #3057 and #2666 each build a specific fallback policy into core. This PR adds only the extension point, so a policy like theirs can ship as a skill without core edits. It is behavior-neutral and safe to review directly.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [x] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `bun test src/providers/provider-wrapper.test.ts` -> pass. Covers: no wrapper means an unwrapped provider; a registered wrapper is applied; `ctx.create` builds unwrapped instances with the given options; wrappers compose in order and can register before their provider; contract `beforeQuery` runs once per wrapped query.
- `bun test src/providers/claude.attempt.test.ts` -> pass. Covers: the configured model is used without an override; `QueryInput.model` reaches the SDK; a failure with no tool or text is `retryable: true`; a failure after a tool call or after text is `retryable: false`; a success result is unchanged.
- `cd container/agent-runner && bun test` -> 490 pass, 0 fail
- `pnpm exec tsc -p container/agent-runner/tsconfig.json --noEmit` -> clean
- `pnpm run typecheck` -> clean; `pnpm run lint` -> 0 errors (warnings only, all pre-existing); `pnpm run format:check` -> clean
- `pnpm test` -> 2921 pass, 12 fail, all under `scripts/` or `src/templates/` (vitest excludes the agent-runner tree). Rerun alone: `skill-conformance`, `update-skills` and `plugin-dir` pass. `update/transaction.e2e` still has 1 test timing out at 5s on a loaded machine. These are load timeouts, not related to this change.

<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Ports `/add-dial-tool` to OneCLI agent grants so Dial keeps working after the 1.45 pin move in https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4094. Merge right after it.

- **Problem**: on 1.44+ the project policy API and secret lists the skill used answer `410`, so it stops at its 1.42 gate and `/add-dial`'s tool offer aborts setup. The gateway's upgrade also deletes `Dial: blocked agents` and gives Dial to every agent.
- **Fix**: `dial-secret.ts` updates the Dial key in place (its id and grants stay), then the skill detaches it from this install's unchosen groups and attaches it to the chosen ones, which also re-narrows an upgraded install. It gates on 1.45.x, no agent still in `all` mode, and a CLI with `agents grants`. `dial-policy.ts` is gone.
- **Behavior change**: new groups never get Dial until the skill runs again. With no agents yet, `/add-dial` installs the tool with nobody holding the key.

## Related work

Stacked on https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4094 (base is its branch; retarget to `main` after it merges, which also starts CI). Replaces the policy path from https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4052 (and #4036's guard). Related: https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/issues/3532, https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4082.

<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Moves NanoClaw to OneCLI gateway 1.45.0 and CLI 2.11.0, the required stop before 2.x, and decides what a new agent group may use now that 1.44+ starts every agent with no grants. Supersedes #4082 and keeps chiptoe-svg's commits.

- **Problem**: on 1.44+ a new group's OneCLI agent holds nothing, so it cannot reach its model. Working out a group's secrets from other agents' grants widens or narrows access depending on history nobody can see.
- **Fix**: NanoClaw records the id of each model credential its provider logins save, per install, and on every spawn attaches the ones for the provider the group runs (older installs are matched once by the names NanoClaw writes). Tool secrets and app connections are opt-in; `/add-vercel` now asks which groups. A new `pre-upgrade-check.sh` runs before the pin is saved and stops on anything the conversion deletes or changes.
- **Out of scope**: `/add-dial-tool` (stacked PR on `feat/dial-tool-grants`, merges in the same sitting), per-group model keys (#3205), docs portal pages.

## Related work

Supersedes https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4082. Related: https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/issues/3532, https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/issues/3205, https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4052, https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4036.

<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Keeps the Linux signal-cli pin from going stale or wrong without anyone noticing.
- **Problem**: `setup/install-signal-cli.sh` pins `VERSION` and `SHA256` (https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4093), and upstream warns that releases older than three months may stop working. Dependabot has no ecosystem for a GitHub release tarball, signal-cli has no advisory feed, and Renovate has never run here (https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/3978). A fix, security or otherwise, only shows up as a new release.
- **Hash check**: a 9-line step in the `skill-pins` CI job fails when `SHA256` is not GitHub's `digest` for `signal-cli-${VERSION}-Linux-native.tar.gz`, and prints the corrected `SHA256="…"` line. One API call, no download.
- **Weekly issue**: `signal-cli-release.yml` (Mondays, or run by hand) opens one issue per newer stable release once the release and its Linux asset are 3+ days old, with the two lines to paste. Actions cannot open PRs here, so an issue is the reminder. It finds earlier issues by exact title, open or closed, so it never opens a duplicate.

## Related work

Follow-up to https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4093. No issue: CI and a scheduled job only, no runtime change.

prs.title: fix(add-onecli): use OneCLI agent grants and move the gateway pin to 1.45.0
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Lets OneCLI installs move off the 1.42.0 stopgap. The skills use OneCLI's agent grants API, and the gateway pin moves to 1.45.0.

- **Problem**: OneCLI 1.43+ answers `410 Gone` on `onecli agents set-secrets`, `agents secrets` and `agents set-secret-mode`, which `/add-onecli`, `/add-vercel` and `/debug` use. From 1.44 an agent gets only the secrets attached to it, and a new agent starts with none. On 1.45, every agent group created after the upgrade would have no credentials, not even the model key.
- **Fix**:
  - `/add-vercel`, `/add-onecli` and `/debug` use `onecli agents grants attach-secret|detach-secret|list`.
  - When the OneCLI adapter creates a group's agent, it attaches the secrets held by every agent that holds any secret. It does not count OneCLI's default agent or empty agents. If no other agent holds secrets, it uses the default agent's secrets (right after the 1.44 conversion that is every secret); on a fresh gateway, every stored secret.
  - Grant steps for new agents run one at a time across all groups, and same-group spawns share one setup.
  - On a gateway without the grants API (1.42's unknown-route 404), nothing is attached.
- **Pins**: `onecli-gateway` 1.42.0 → 1.45.0. `onecli-cli` 2.2.5 → 2.11.0, because `agents grants` arrived in 2.9.0. The approval-summary compatibility pin moves with the gateway; its vendored OneCLI files are byte-identical at 1.45.0.
- **Upgrade behavior to know about**: most skills store a credential and let agents use it. Some, like `/add-dial-tool`, also restrict who can use theirs: they write a OneCLI "block" rule, so only the agents you picked can text or call. The upgrade to OneCLI 1.44+ converts the old setup into grants, and during that one-time conversion it: 1. gives every agent that had `all` access a grant for every stored credential, 2. deletes all custom network rules, including those block rules, and 3. removes the policy API those skills use to write the rules, so after the upgrade they can't run at all. The upgrade guide now has a check to run before upgrading, and the safe options.
- **Out of scope**: OneCLI 2.x; app connections, which a new agent still does not get; group-scoped grants.

## Related work

Follows #4036. `/add-dial-tool` still needs OneCLI 1.42: it writes its block rule through the policy API that 1.44 removed, so installs using it should stay on 1.42 until it is ported to grants. Overlaps #2483. Refs #4068, #3205.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm run build`, `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` → clean. `pnpm test` → 3553 passed, 15 skipped, 0 failed.
- Payload tests (skill applied to a scratch worktree): `onecli.test.ts` 29 passed; the skill's validation list 118 passed. New `scripts/add-vercel-onecli.test.ts` 4 passed. Each new assertion was red-proofed against the old code or a mutation.
- Throwaway 1.42.0 and 1.45.0 gateways with fake secrets. Covered: the 410s, attach, detach and injection, the new-agent rule, concurrent spawns of one group and of different groups, the conversion, and rollback.
- Not run: a full NanoClaw container session on 1.45; ChatGPT OAuth refresh; the Iron image rebuild; a OneCLI cloud gateway.

<details><summary>Receipts</summary>

- **New agent (1.45.0)**: a1, a2 and a3 held X; only a1 held Y, a fake Dial key. A new group got `["X"]` and not Y, and its proxied request had X injected.
- **Different groups at once (1.45.0)**: the vault held Model, Vercel and Dial; n1 held Model and Vercel. p1 and p2 spawned concurrently, then n3 spawned. Results:
  - With the previous code, all three got `[]`.
  - With this PR, all three got `["Model","Vercel"]` and none got Dial.
  - A further group spawned with the three empty agents still present also got `["Model","Vercel"]`.
- **Base cases**: on a fresh gateway the first agent got Dial, Model and Vercel, and the default agent held nothing. After a 1.42.0 → 1.45.0 conversion the default agent held Echo and Model. The first new group got exactly those two, not a secret added after the upgrade.
- **Same group at once**: three concurrent spawns for one new group. Before the fix, two logged "gateway applied" 28–40 ms before the grants existed. After it, all three logged after.
- **Block rules lost (1.42.0 → 1.45.0)**: an agent blocked from `api.getdial.ai` and `postman-echo.com` got `403`. After the upgrade the log said `deleted: 2 network`, the agent held both secrets, and the same request returned `200` with the header injected. The guide's pre-upgrade check, run verbatim, printed the Dial block rule and the Dial secret.
- **Rollback without the backup**: the 1.42 gateway logged a startup error and the converted agent had an empty list. `set-secret-mode --mode all` restored injection.
- **Red-proofs** (each mutation turned its test red):
  - no process-wide queue (the cross-group test also fails on the previous commit);
  - empty agents counted;
  - no default-agent base case;
  - default agent counted alongside others;
  - no intersection;
  - grants not limited to the vault;
  - failed grants read treated as empty;
  - no same-group join;
  - any 404 treated as "no grants API";
  - first agent gets nothing;
  - old `/add-vercel` commands.

</details>

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [ ] User-visible change — release note below
- [x] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
[BREAKING] **The OneCLI gateway pin moves to 1.45.0 and the OneCLI CLI pin to 2.11.0.**
- Detect: `curl -s "$ONECLI_URL/api/health"` reports a version below 1.45.0, or `onecli version` reports below 2.11.0.
- Why: OneCLI 1.43+ removed the per-agent secret commands NanoClaw used, and their replacement (agent grants) needs 1.44+.
- Caution: the one-time upgrade conversion gives every `all`-mode agent every stored credential and deletes all custom network rules, including the block rules `/add-dial-tool` uses. `/add-dial-tool` also stops working on 1.44+. On a fresh gateway, the first NanoClaw agent gets every stored credential, including ones attached to no agent: attach a restricted credential to its chosen agents before the first spawn, or detach it afterwards.
- Fix: follow docs/onecli-upgrades.md. Run its pre-upgrade check, back up the gateway database, then upgrade the gateway and the CLI. Installs using `/add-dial-tool` should stay on 1.42 until it is ported to grants.
- Rollback: restore the database backup taken before the upgrade. Without a backup, run `onecli agents set-secret-mode --id <id> --mode all` for each agent on 1.42.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

- A new agent gets the secrets held by every agent that holds any secret. OneCLI's default agent and empty agents are not counted, so an empty agent no longer narrows anything.
- To restrict a credential, attach it only to chosen agents; new agents will not get it. If only one agent holds any secrets, new agents get that agent's whole set.
- On a fresh gateway, the first NanoClaw agent gets every stored credential, including ones attached to no agent. Attach a restricted credential to its chosen agents before the first spawn, or detach it afterwards.
- Existing agents' grants are never changed.
- Grant steps for new agents run one at a time across all groups in the host process, including different groups spawning at once. No spawn returns credentials before its grants exist. If a step fails, the new agent is deleted and the spawn fails. If that delete also fails, the error names the cleanup command. Until that cleanup runs, the leftover agent's partial set also narrows what later groups get.
- Serialization is per host process.

prs.body:
## Summary

Adds `/add-delivery-fallback`, an opt-in skill that retries a failed send on a second channel, together with the two host hooks it needs.

- **Who needs this**: anyone running more than one channel who wants approval requests and replies to still arrive when one channel (say a Slack workspace) is down.
- **Seam**: `registerDeliveryAdapterWrapper` / `wrapDeliveryAdapter` in `src/delivery.ts` decorate the delivery adapter; `registerApprovalDeliveryOrder` in `src/modules/approvals/primitive.ts` lets a module reorder or narrow the approver walk. With nothing registered both behave exactly as before.
- **Consumer**: the skill's module calls the wrapper hook at `.claude/skills/add-delivery-fallback/resources/delivery-fallback.ts:108` and the approver hook at `:109`. The entry point applies the wrapper at `src/index.ts:178`.
- **Behavior**: a send that throws on the preferred channel type is retried once, same content, on a named fallback destination. If that fails too, the original error surfaces and the normal retry path runs. After a failure, approvers on the preferred channel are tried last for a cooldown (default 60s).
- **Config**: `DELIVERY_FALLBACK_FROM`, `DELIVERY_FALLBACK_TO=<type>:<platform-id>`, optional `DELIVERY_FALLBACK_COOLDOWN_MS`. Unset means nothing registers.

prs.title: feat(scheduling): pluggable scheduler admission with a container-cap skill
prs.body:
## Summary

Lets an install cap how many agent containers the scheduler sweep keeps running, and adds the admission hook that makes it possible.

- **Problem**: when many scheduled tasks come due together, the reconcile sweep wakes every session at once. There is no way to bound concurrent containers.
- **Fix**: `registerSchedulerAdmission({ shouldWake, onSessionIdle? })` lets one policy decide whether a due session may wake and hear when a running session goes idle. The default admits every wake, so behavior is unchanged.
- **Consumer**: the `/add-scheduler-cap` skill registers a policy limited by `SCHEDULER_MAX_CONTAINERS`. It defers wakes at the cap and stops an idle container only when the cap is full and a session is waiting.
- **Who needs this**: operators running many scheduled tasks on one host with limited memory or CPU.
- **Seam call sites**: `src/reconcile-session.ts:139` (`admitWake`, which calls `shouldWake`) and `src/reconcile-session.ts:201` (`onSessionIdle`).
- **Consumer call site**: `.claude/skills/add-scheduler-cap/payload/src/modules/scheduler-cap/index.ts:24` calls `registerSchedulerAdmission`.
- **Out of scope**: gating wakes that come from chat messages; per-group limits.

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Adds a stale policy that only looks at items waiting on their author: `.github/workflows/stale.yml` (dry run) and `.github/workflows/triage-author-reply.yml`.

- **Population**: issues labelled `triage/needs-repro` or `triage/needs-author` (stale at 21 days, closed 14 days later) and PRs labelled `triage/needs-author` (stale at 21 days, closed 21 days later). Each label means a maintainer read the item and asked its author for something. An author answer (comment, push, or review reply) removes the triage label and `stale`, so an answered item leaves the population.
- **Dry run**: `debug-only: true`, so the stale job marks, comments and closes nothing until a later change flips it. The author-reply path is live from merge and only removes labels: `triage-author-reply.yml` for comments and pushes, and an `answered` job before each run for review replies (fork review events get a read-only token) and missed runs. The header holds the arming checklist and rollback.
- **Out of scope**: any general-inactivity sweep. Most idle items are waiting on us, so a bot must not close them. Backlog cleanup stays a human batch close under [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#core-or-your-fork).

<details>
<summary>Notes</summary>

- Exempt: `kind/security`, `kind/hardening`, `priority/critical`, `priority/high`, `good first issue`, `help wanted`, `core-team`, `triage/keep` (the manual freeze), plus anything with a milestone or an assignee, and draft PRs.
- Close messages point to a new PR or issue, because an outside author cannot reopen an item the bot closed. No response-time promise.
- Pins: `actions/stale@4391f3da… # v11.0.0`, `actions/github-script@3a2844b7… # v9.0.0` (both latest). Runner `ubuntu-26.04`.
- Known gap: a push or review reply in the seconds while the stale job processes a PR on its close day does not save it; `actions/stale` re-checks comments itself.

</details>

## Related work

No issue. Repository automation that ships in dry run, so it is safe to review directly.

A live run today would remove nothing and mark nothing.

prs.title: feat(cli): add `ncl health` — local, read-only operational health check
prs.body:
Closes #2504. Implements exactly what the issue asked for: a zero-dependency health check that reads local state directly (central DB opened read-only, the error log) and keeps working even when the main host process is down — unlike every other `ncl` command, which requires a live host to serve the Unix socket. It's special-cased in `client.ts` before a transport is ever picked, the same way `--help` already is.

Reports: host liveness + uptime per instance (from the host_instances lease table, migration 024), a session summary (status/container_status/last_active joined with the agent group name), recent warn/error/fatal log lines within a 1h window (ANSI-stripped, tailed rather than fully read since there's no log rotation), and pending approvals nearing expiry. `--json` for scripting, matching the issue's "can be piped or used in health check scripts" ask.

Two things worth flagging for review:

- `status` was already taken (`src/cli/commands/status.ts` — hidden, host-only, reads in-process live state, fundamentally socket-bound) with different semantics than what #2504 describes, so this lands as `health` instead. Happy to rename either one if maintainers would rather repurpose `status`.
- The issue's "token expiry warnings" is scoped down to pending approval requests nearing their own expiry (pending_approvals.expires_at) — there's no existing API, local or in the OneCLI SDK, to query actual vaulted credential/token expiry. Flagging as a real gap rather than a silent no-op; a follow-up once that API exists would close it properly.

I built a similar host-health tool for a personal fork exploring a Go trust-kernel for NanoClaw's privileged host decisions, and ported the idea back here as plain TypeScript with no new dependencies, since #2504 already asked for exactly this.

prs.title: fix(db): add busy_timeout to central DB to avoid contention-as-corruption
prs.body:
Fixes #3811.

## Summary

The central DB (task/schedule state, `container_configs`, `agent_groups`) is opened in WAL mode with no `busy_timeout`, so any momentary lock contention throws immediately instead of waiting briefly and retrying — indistinguishable from real corruption to a caller seeing `ncl tasks list`/`ncl tasks run` fail.

The session DBs (`inbound.db`/`outbound.db`) already carry this protection (`container/agent-runner/src/cli/ncl.ts`, `busy_timeout=5000` on both). The central DB never did.

## Fix

Sets the same `busy_timeout = 5000` on the central DB's read-write connection in `src/db/compose.ts`.

## Scope note

Does not address an ungraceful-shutdown-mid-write scenario (the other candidate cause of the intermittent task-DB failures this was observed alongside) — only the contention half. Distinct from #3708 (closed, unmerged) and #2640/#2750/#2196/#2188, all of which are about `outbound.db`'s readonly/journal handling, not the central DB.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` — clean
- [x] `pnpm exec vitest run src/db` — 10 files, 100 tests pass
