prs.title: feat(providers): add pi agent provider (/add-pi skill)
prs.body:
## Type of Change

- [x] **Feature skill** - adds a channel or integration (source code changes + SKILL.md)
- [ ] **Utility skill** - adds a standalone tool (code files in `.claude/skills/<name>/`, no source changes)
- [ ] **Operational/container skill** - adds a workflow or agent skill (SKILL.md only, no source changes)
- [ ] **Fix** - bug fix or security fix to source code
- [ ] **Simplification** - reduces or simplifies source code
- [ ] **Documentation** - docs, README, or CONTRIBUTING changes only

## Description

**What** — Adds [pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi) (Pi Coding Agent) as an agent provider, installable via the new `/add-pi` skill. Three commits: the container-side provider + MCP bridge + contract donor, the host-side container config + skill + tests, and skill hardening from a real end-to-end install.

**Why** — pi is a lightweight coding agent with server-side sessions and MCP support; this makes it a per-group provider choice alongside `claude` / `opencode` / `codex` (`ncl groups config update --provider pi`).

**How it works**

- `container/agent-runner/src/providers/pi.ts` — `AgentProvider` over the in-process pi SDK (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`, pinned 0.85.1). No serve process, no SSE: the whole server-lifecycle complexity class of the OpenCode provider does not exist here. Continuation = pi session file path; activity on every SDK event; fail-closed memory hook; one-shot empty-resume fallback.
- `container/agent-runner/src/providers/mcp-to-pi.ts` — bridges the core's MCP servers to pi `customTools` in-process (stdio + http, per-process lifecycle, lazy reconnect, `isError` → throw, `env:{}` omission so default environments survive).
- `src/providers/pi.ts` (host) — container config; seeds `auth.json` / `models.json` / `settings.json` from a host template agentDir into a per-session directory mounted at `/pi-agent` (pi reads no auth from env vars), passes `PI_AGENT_DIR`.
- `container/agent-runner/src/provider-contracts/pi.ts` — runtime contract donor (seamVersion 1), following the same donor-file pattern as the codex/opencode payloads.
- `.claude/skills/add-pi/SKILL.md` — copies the payload in from the `providers` ref, wires both barrels, installs the pinned SDK dep, rebuilds the image. Prose format, idempotent steps, same shape as `/add-opencode`.

**How it was tested**

- `bun test` on the standalone providers tree: 43 new tests pass (MCP bridge incl. InMemoryTransport e2e, factory/registration, empty-resume rotation, active-turn steering/interrupt). No new failures vs base — the 1 fail + 1 error present on both trees are pre-existing core-layout issues that the provider-contract workflow covers by testing payloads against real cores.
- Verified under bun 1.4.2 in addition to CI's 1.3.x; SDK parity with node, session resume continuity intact.
- End-to-end dogfood: full install on a main-based tree + this payload, live turns over a messaging channel, definitive check via `continuation:pi` in `session_state`. The third commit hardens the skill from that install (container.json propagation model, the two-table trap and its failure signature, the fresh-install path where the setup provider picker doesn't list pi).

**Usage** — On an installed system: run `/add-pi`, then `ncl groups config update --provider pi` and `ncl groups restart` for the chosen group. Prerequisite: a populated pi agentDir on the host (run `pi` once and `/login`, or set `PI_TEMPLATE_AGENT_DIR`).

Note for reviewers: the **Provider contract** workflow on this PR is sitting in `action_required` (first-time contributor) — it needs a maintainer approval click to run.

## For Skills

- [x] SKILL.md contains instructions, not inline code (code goes in separate files)
- [x] SKILL.md is under 500 lines (251)
- [x] I tested this skill on a fresh clone

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Makes `src/group-skills.test.ts` pass under any umask, so `/update-nanoclaw` can validate on hosts whose umask is `002`.

- **Problem**: "resolves the legacy shape to the same anchored result as the segments form" (added in #4063) asserts the copied `SKILL.md` is `…:body:644`. Under umask `002` it is `664`, so the test fails, and `validate` (which runs the full host suite) refuses cutover.
- **Cause**: the fixture helper `templateSkill` writes `SKILL.md` with `fs.writeFileSync`, whose mode is masked by the process umask. `AnchoredDir`'s copy correctly preserves the source mode, so the copy inherits it. Only the test's expectation depends on the environment.
- **Fix**: `templateSkill` pins the fixture to `0o644` with `fs.chmodSync`, the same way this file already pins `run.sh` to `0o755` and #3979 fixed the OneCLI files test.
- **Unchanged**: product code. Every other test that uses `templateSkill` gets a fixed `0644` fixture instead of an umask-dependent one; none asserts a different mode.

## Related work

Closes #4074 (reported 2026-10-11 on Raspberry Pi OS; same diagnosis, and this is the first fix it suggests). Same pattern as #3979.

prs.title: fix(service): skip linger on per-home-encrypted systems (#2680)
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Skips `loginctl enable-linger` on per-home-encrypted systems, where it makes the service silently fail to start at boot, and tells the operator how to start it.

- **Problem**: on systems where `$HOME` lives on per-user-encrypted storage (ecryptfs, fscrypt, gocryptfs), linger brings the user systemd manager up at boot before PAM has decrypted the home. `~/.config/systemd/user/` is unreadable at that point, so the unit table is empty and nanoclaw never launches at boot. The service only starts after a manual `systemctl --user daemon-reload` and start following login. LUKS / dm-crypt block-device encryption is decrypted before userspace and is unaffected.
- **Detection**: `detectEncryptedHome()` probes the three per-home types: `ecryptfs` via `findmnt -T "$HOME" -o FSTYPE` and the `~/.ecryptfs` / `~/.Private` marker directories; `fuse.gocryptfs` via `findmnt`; `fscrypt` via the `fscrypt` CLI when installed (no marker-file heuristic; the issue warns against rolling our own `FS_IOC_GET_ENCRYPTION_POLICY` ioctl). Without the `fscrypt` CLI, fscrypt detection is skipped silently; ecryptfs and gocryptfs are still caught via `findmnt`. LUKS and dm-crypt are intentionally not triggers. Probes use `execFileSync(file, args)`, never a shell.
- **Skip path**: linger management is an exported `manageUserLinger(unitName, detect, exec)` so the skip path is testable. On a positive detection it skips `loginctl enable-linger` and logs a warning that names the detected encryption type, explains why linger was skipped, prints the recovery sequence with the real per-install unit name (`systemctl --user daemon-reload && systemctl --user start nanoclaw-v2-<slug>`), and links back to #2680. `LINGER_ENABLED` in the status block now reflects the actual outcome, and a new `ENCRYPTED_HOME` field surfaces the detected type for the setup wizard.
- **Layout**: the linger / encrypted-home code lives in `setup/linger.ts`. `setupSystemd` dynamic-imports it, so the detection never evaluates on macOS or on the WSL nohup fallback path; `setupLinux` and `setupSystemd` became async for that. The module header notes that callers must gate on Linux.
- **Out of scope**: item 4 of the issue's suggested fix (a PAM / `pam_exec` / `~/.bash_profile` login hook that starts the service on first login so it self-heals after each reboot). A `TODO(#2680)` in `manageUserLinger` points back to the issue.

## Related work

Closes #2680.

Review fixes folded into 058cc4f4: the recovery command was hardcoded to `nanoclaw` (copy-paste hit `Unit nanoclaw.service not found`), and the probes used `execSync(string)` with a `JSON.stringify`-quoted home dir, which does not escape `$` or backticks. Rebased after #3768 (Linux fallback service, merged 2026-09-12), which touched the same `setupSystemd` region. https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/3798 also changes linger handling in setup; whichever lands second needs a rebase.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

Evidence from 2026-09-16 (before the 2026-09-17 merge of main, not re-run after it):

- `setup/service.test.ts` `manageUserLinger` block: ecryptfs detection skips `loginctl enable-linger` and warns with the encryption type, the recovery sequence using the real per-install unit name, and an `issues/2680` link; fscrypt and gocryptfs detections also skip linger; a negative detection runs `loginctl enable-linger` and returns `lingerEnabled: true`; a `loginctl` failure logs the existing warning and returns `lingerEnabled: false`.
- `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm test` pass (336/336).
- No live run on an encrypted-home machine is recorded; fscrypt token matching is pinned to CLI v0.3.4 in a code comment.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
**Setup now warns when your home directory is encrypted, because NanoClaw can't start at boot there.** It prints the exact command to start the service after you log in.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

Setup runs new local probes (`findmnt`, `fscrypt`, marker-dir checks) through `execFileSync` without a shell, closing a low-likelihood injection surface from a hostile home path. It now does less privileged setup (skips `enable-linger`) on encrypted homes. No credentials or network exposure change.

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Gives forks a place for their own coding-agent instructions so they stop editing `CLAUDE.md` and stop conflicting on it every update.

- **Problem**: a customized install that wants its coding agent to know about its changes has to edit the root `CLAUDE.md`, which upstream edits constantly — `/update-nanoclaw` conflicts on it every time.
- **Fix**: `CLAUDE.md` ends with a `Fork Instructions` section: an `@CLAUDE.fork.md` import plus one sentence telling any agent to read that file if it exists and is non-empty. Upstream never ships the file, so a fork owns it outright and commits it.
- **Why an explicit line, not `.claude/rules/`**: Claude Code auto-loads `.claude/rules/*.md`, but other harnesses read `AGENTS.md` (a symlink to `CLAUDE.md`) and only see what `CLAUDE.md` says. The plain sentence covers them; the import covers Claude Code.
- **Missing file is harmless**: Claude Code ignores an `@` import whose target does not exist (checked below), so fresh clones see no change in behavior.
- **Docs**: short paragraph in `docs/customizing.md` pointing forks at the file.
- **Out of scope**: per-group agent instructions (`groups/<folder>/…`) — unrelated, already composed per spawn.

prs.title: fix(discord): connect the Gateway through Node's env proxy
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Lets the Discord Gateway connect on hosts that reach the internet only through an HTTPS proxy.

- **Problem**: with `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1` / `--use-env-proxy`, `fetch` goes through the proxy, so Discord REST works. The Gateway doesn't: `@discordjs/ws` dials it with the `ws` package, which opens TLS itself and ignores the env proxy, so the connection gets reset. Discord looks connected but never receives messages.
- **Fix**: when a proxy is set (`HTTPS_PROXY`/`HTTP_PROXY`, either case) and Node's env proxy is on, `discord.ts` loads `@discordjs/ws` with `ws.WebSocket` briefly pointed at the native `WebSocket` (which does honor the env proxy), then puts it back straight away. `@discordjs/ws` reads `require('ws').WebSocket` once at load, so only the Gateway gets the native constructor.
- **Scoped to Discord**: the swap is synchronous and restored in a `finally`, so other `ws` users see the real package. That includes Slack Socket Mode, which passes an options object the native `WebSocket` would drop.
- **Why not an option**: neither `@discordjs/ws` 1.2.3 nor `@chat-adapter/discord` 4.29.0 lets callers pass a WebSocket implementation. The adapter builds its own `Client` without passing through `ws` options.
- **Load order**: `@chat-adapter/discord` moves from a static import to a dynamic `import()` inside the (already async-capable) factory, so the swap runs before discord.js loads. The type still comes from a type-only import.
- **Unchanged without a proxy**: no proxy or no env-proxy flag means nothing is patched and the adapter builds exactly as before.

## Related work

No issue. Pairs with #3901 (the host launcher side of running behind an HTTPS proxy). That PR gets the service's REST traffic through the proxy; this one covers the Discord Gateway WebSocket, which it can't reach.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/channels/discord.test.ts src/channels/discord-registration.test.ts` -> 16 passed
  - `isEnvProxyActive`: off with no proxy, off with a proxy but no env-proxy flag, on via `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1`, `--use-env-proxy`, and `NODE_OPTIONS`
  - `withNativeWebSocket`: the native constructor is visible only while the gateway loads, and gets restored even when loading throws
  - `resolveGatewayModules`: resolves the same `ws` copy `@discordjs/ws` loads, in the installed layout
- Manual smoke (tsx): loaded `@discordjs/ws` through the helper with a stand-in native class, then called `WebSocketShard.connect()` -> the shard built the stand-in (`native:wss://…?v=10&encoding=json`), and `ws.WebSocket` was restored to the real class afterwards
- `pnpm run typecheck` -> no errors in the changed files; 28 errors in untouched files on the base branch (local-web, canvas-actions, slack-onboarding, slack-room-membership)
- `pnpm exec eslint src/channels/discord.ts src/channels/discord.test.ts` -> 0 errors (2 existing `no-explicit-any` warnings)
- `pnpm run format:check` -> clean
- `pnpm test` -> the only failures are in untouched files on the base branch: registration tests for channels the barrel doesn't import on this branch (gchat, github, matrix, …), local-web suites, and `slack-raw-text`

prs.title: feat(skills): add /contribute-upstream operational skill for giving fork features back
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Adds `/contribute-upstream`, an operational skill that helps any customized NanoClaw fork give its local features back upstream safely, as seams and skills instead of long-lived edits.

- **Problem**: forks that edit upstream files directly pay for it on every `/update-nanoclaw`: each edit is a potential conflict. Giving features back by hand is slow and easy to get wrong (wrong route, leaked internal names, work identity on commits).
- **What it does**: four modes. `map` inventories local-only files vs files owned by installed skills (registry branches and gateway payloads filtered out) and upstream files edited by churn, classifies each feature as `bugfix` / `seam` / `skill` / `docs` / `local-only`, and records decisions in a numbered ledger. `contribute <slug>` builds one approved feature in its own worktree off `upstream/main` (or off a dependency's `contrib/<dep>` branch), verifies, scrubs, and opens the PR. `status` writes a numbered report per PR (links, review state, new feedback, conflicts; several PRs per feature supported). `reconcile` runs after `/update-nanoclaw` to move local code onto merged seams.
- **Why seams**: `references/seam-patterns.md` describes how to split a feature into a behavior-neutral upstream base plus a local override that registers into it, so the fork's upstream-file edits shrink to one line.
- **Safety**: two operator gates per feature through `AskUserQuestion` (may it be contributed; may this exact diff and body be pushed). A blocking scrub check (`scripts/scrub-check.ts`) scans the branch diff, commit messages, branch name, and PR body for private IPs, home paths, emails, internal hosts, credential shapes, and a per-install denylist. Commit authors are checked too: only the operator's personal email passed via `--allow-identity` is allowed. Internal systems of the operator's employer or organization are classified `local-only` and never contributed.
- **Configurable**: fork owner (`--owner` / `CONTRIB_FORK_OWNER` / `gh api user`), contribution remote (default `contrib`, created with `gh repo fork` when `origin` is private or not a fork), and ledger, status, denylist, and optional divergences paths (defaults under `.nanoclaw-contrib/`, chosen so they don't collide with `.nanoclaw-migrations/` used by `/migrate-nanoclaw`).
- **Footprint**: skill-owned files only. The skill edits no core file and no other skill. At runtime it writes only under `.nanoclaw-contrib/` in the operator's checkout.
- **Branch hygiene**: each invocation fast-forwards the contribution fork's `main` from `upstream/main` when it is behind, and stops on unexpected divergence. Before revising a PR, it merges the latest PR base into the branch without rewriting published history.

## Related work

No existing issue. This is a new, self-contained operational skill that touches only its own directory, so it can be reviewed directly. #1113 (`/contribute-skill`) covers authoring a new skill from scratch. This skill covers mapping an existing fork's features and routing them upstream.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [x] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm exec vitest run .claude/skills/contribute-upstream` -> 4 files, 31 tests passed (inventory parsing and area grouping, ledger with and without a `#` column, scrub rules / denylist / identity allowlist, PR-status next-action logic including merge-not-rebase guidance, multi-PR row labels, PR links, flag and owner resolution).
- `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit --strict --module nodenext --moduleResolution nodenext --skipLibCheck --types node .claude/skills/contribute-upstream/scripts/*.ts` -> clean.
- `pnpm exec prettier --check ".claude/skills/contribute-upstream/**/*.ts"` -> clean.
- `pnpm exec tsx scripts/skill-directives.ts .claude/skills/contribute-upstream/SKILL.md` -> no problems, no warnings.
- `pnpm run typecheck` -> clean. `pnpm run lint` -> 0 errors (warnings are pre-existing, none in the skill). `pnpm run format:check` -> clean.
- `pnpm test` -> all pass except `scripts/update/transaction.e2e.test.ts` and `scripts/update-skills.test.ts`, which timed out on a heavily loaded machine. Rerun alone: `transaction.e2e.test.ts` 14/14 pass, `update-skills.test.ts` and `skill-conformance.test.ts` pass (210/210 conformance). This diff cannot affect them.
- Manual: ran `inventory.ts` on a clean upstream checkout (empty inventory) and on a customized fork (local-only, skill-owned, and churn sections populated). Ran `pr-status.ts` against a real ledger with open PRs; the report rendered links, review and merge state.


## Security and trust boundaries

- The skill pushes to GitHub and opens PRs only after an explicit per-feature operator approval (Gate 2), and only to the contribution remote. It never pushes to `upstream` and never pushes a contribution branch to a private `origin`.
- The scrub check is a blocking gate against leaking internal names, hosts, personal data, and credential shapes. The denylist stays in the operator's checkout and never ships, because contribution worktrees branch from upstream.

prs.title: feat(skills): add /add-scheduled-update for unattended host-side updates
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Adds `/add-scheduled-update`, a utility skill that runs `/update-nanoclaw` unattended on a schedule from the host.

- **Problem**: a NanoClaw scheduled task cannot run the update. Cutover needs launchctl/systemctl and the Docker socket, and the container drain waits for every agent container of the install to exit, including the one doing the update.
- **Fix**: a host-side runner (`.claude/skills/add-scheduled-update/scripts/scheduled-update.ts`) started by a launchd job (macOS) or a systemd user timer (Linux). It runs a headless coding-agent CLI (`claude`, `codex`, or `opencode`) that follows `.claude/skills/update-nanoclaw/SKILL.md` and drives `scripts/update-nanoclaw.ts`. The runner does not reimplement the controller.
- **Configurable**: schedule, agent CLI, model (unset = the CLI's own default; no model is baked in), timeout, dirty-tree policy, and an optional reporter task. Settings live in git-ignored `.nanoclaw/scheduled-update.json`.
- **Lock**: exclusive pid lock in `logs/`; a concurrent run exits, a lock from a dead process is taken over.
- **Never races an operator**: stops with `blocked` while any earlier update transaction is still open.
- **Dirty tree**: default `refuse` (report the files, skip the run). Opt-in `commit` commits everything not ignored, then re-stamps `scripts/upgrade-state.ts set` so the host still starts.
- **No work, no tokens**: fetches upstream first and exits `up-to-date` when nothing is pending.
- **Timeout**: kills the agent's whole process group (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 30s).
- **Never force; the controller's rollback is the recovery path**: after the agent exits or is killed, a transaction this run left open is settled through the controller: `rollback` when cutover had already snapshotted the live install (including an interrupted cutover whose phase never advanced), `abandon` otherwise. Every run ends on the new version or the old one.
- **Reporting**: writes `logs/scheduled-update.last.json`, probes `bin/ncl groups list`, and optionally appends a one-line outcome to a task's run log (`ncl tasks append-log`) and fires it (`ncl tasks run`).
- **Out of scope**: no core source changes, no pruning of old transactions, no push.

## Related work

No existing issue or PR. This is an additive skill: the only in-tree files are under `.claude/skills/add-scheduled-update/`.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [x] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm exec vitest run .claude/skills/add-scheduled-update` -> 13 passed. Covers config parsing, per-CLI argv (model flag only when set), lock takeover, process-group timeout kill, settle decisions over state read through the real controller `loadState`, and end-to-end runs against real temp git repos: dirty refuse + reporter wake, dirty commit + re-stamp, up-to-date skip, open-transaction block, rollback of a transaction left after cutover, completed update, agent that never starts a transaction.
- `tsc --noEmit` over the two skill scripts (root tsconfig + node types) -> no errors. The repo `typecheck`, `lint`, and `format:check` scripts only cover `src/`; the scripts were formatted with the repo's prettier config.
- `pnpm run typecheck` -> pass. `pnpm run lint` -> 0 errors. `pnpm run format:check` -> pass.
- `pnpm test` (machine at load average ~20) -> 2916 passed, 30 failed, every one a `Test timed out` / `Hook timed out`. 25 are in files this PR does not touch (`transaction.e2e`, `templates/*`, `fan`, `delivery-poll`, `skill-conformance`, ...); rerun alone they all pass except `transaction.e2e` (2 timeouts), which passes 14/14 with `--testTimeout=30000`. The other 5 were this skill's git-driven cases, which now declare a 30s timeout and pass (13/13).
- Manual path (not reachable in CI): install per SKILL.md Phase 4, trigger once with `launchctl kickstart` / `systemctl --user start`, read `logs/scheduled-update.last.json`.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
New /add-scheduled-update skill: run /update-nanoclaw unattended on a launchd or systemd schedule, with a lock, timeout, dirty-tree policy, and automatic rollback of a run left half-done.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

- The scheduled coding agent runs with permission prompts bypassed (`--permission-mode bypassPermissions`, `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`, `--auto`), as the operator's user, on the host. SKILL.md makes the operator acknowledge this before install. It is equivalent to an interactive `/update-nanoclaw` session with every prompt approved.
- No credentials are handled. The CLI uses its own login/config; SKILL.md says not to put API keys in the plist or unit.
- The runner only runs git, the update controller, `scripts/upgrade-state.ts`, and `bin/ncl`. It never adds remotes, pushes, prunes, or resets the live checkout itself.

## Skill delivery

- [ ] Not a skill
- [x] Skill: apply/remove footprint and fresh-clone verification are described above

Apply writes `.nanoclaw/scheduled-update.json`, one launchd plist or a systemd service + timer, and runtime files under `logs/scheduled-update.*`. REMOVE.md reverses each. The runner runs in place from the skill folder; nothing is copied into `src/`.

## AI assistance

- [x] AI tools or agents helped produce this change

- [ ] A human has reviewed this PR and stands behind every change

prs.title: fix(opencode): resolve config, runtime key and server env from one environment
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Makes the OpenCode payload read one environment, `options.env ?? process.env`, for config resolution, the shared-runtime cache key, and the spawned `opencode serve` process, so config and credentials cannot disagree.

- **Use case**: #3925 adds `registerProviderWrapper`, whose `ctx.create(options)` builds extra provider instances with a different env (for example a second credential or base URL used as a fallback). Today the OpenCode payload resolves inference from `process.env`, keys the shared server on config + cwd only, and spawns `opencode serve` with `process.env`. Two instances with different envs can therefore share one server running the wrong config and credentials.
- **Fix, inference**: `createProvider` passes `opts.env ?? process.env` to `resolveRuntimeConfiguration`, so `resolveOpenCodeInference(input, environment)` sees the provider's own env. The payload's no-contract fallback in `buildOpenCodeConfig` and `query()` uses the same source.
- **Fix, cache key**: `ensureSharedRuntime` includes that environment in the key. A provider with a different env respawns the server instead of reusing it.
- **Fix, serve env**: `spawnOpencodeServer` takes the environment and uses it for `buildOpenCodeServerEnv` and for the auth-state init (`XDG_DATA_HOME`, `OPENCODE_AUTH_MODE`), so the auth file lands where the server reads it. `OpenCodeSharedRuntimeDeps.spawnServer` receives it too.
- **Fix, per-query model**: the payload ignored `QueryInput.model` from #3925. When it is set, inference is resolved as for a provider constructed with that model, so the server config declares it and the prompt names it. Without it, the core-resolved configuration is used unchanged.
- **Default unchanged**: the runner builds the provider with `env: { ...process.env }` and no per-query model, so resolved config, cache key, serve env and prompt model are the same as before. Claude's inference capability ignores its environment argument.
- **Tradeoff**: a query with a model override uses a different server config, so the single shared server restarts for it and again on the next normal query. That is the cost of keeping config and server in sync.
- **Out of scope**: the fallback policy itself (which env or model to try, and when). That belongs to a wrapper.

## Related work

Depends on #3925 (stacked on it; the first commit here is #3925's).

Follows up #3896, closed because OpenCode now ships as the `/add-opencode` payload on `main`. This PR targets that payload and makes the cache key and serve env follow the same source, as asked there.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm run typecheck` -> pass
- `pnpm run lint` -> 0 errors (warnings only, all in files this PR does not touch)
- `pnpm run format:check` -> pass
- `pnpm exec tsc -p container/agent-runner/tsconfig.json --noEmit` -> pass
- `cd container/agent-runner && bun test` -> 491 pass, 0 fail
- Payload applied to a scratch runner copy (the skill's copy + barrel steps), then `bun run typecheck` -> pass and `bun test --isolate src/providers/opencode*.test.ts src/providers/mcp-to-opencode.test.ts src/providers/factory.test.ts` -> 142 pass, 0 fail
- New tests in `opencode.shared-runtime.test.ts`: config and spawn env come from `options.env`; two providers with different envs get two servers; a per-query model is declared in the server config and sent on the prompt. All three fail against the unchanged payload.
- New test in `factory.test.ts`: contract capabilities see `options.env` when supplied and `process.env` otherwise.
- `pnpm test` -> all pass except `scripts/update/transaction.e2e.test.ts` (one 5s timeout under machine load; it does not load agent-runner code). Other files that timed out in the full run pass when run alone.
- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [x] No user-visible behavior change
- [ ] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

## Security and trust boundaries

Credentials: the spawned `opencode serve` now inherits the provider's env instead of always the process env. With the default runner these are the same object's contents. The env is included in an in-memory cache-key string only; it is not logged or persisted.

## Skill delivery

- [ ] Not a skill
- [x] Skill: apply/remove footprint and fresh-clone verification are described above

The payload file list, barrels and dependencies are unchanged, so apply/remove footprint is the same. Existing installs pick it up with a skill refresh.

## AI assistance

- [x] AI tools or agents helped produce this change

<!-- Required. -->
- [ ] A human has reviewed this PR and stands behind every change

issues.title: tracking: OpenClaw parity PRs for streaming, channel UX and provider reasoning (#1057-#1065)
issues.body:
## Context

I have opened several PRs in a short time while running nullclaw as a Slack and Telegram assistant against OpenAI-compatible gateways (DeepSeek, IFM K2). This issue collects them in one place so they can be reviewed, deferred or closed without triaging each one separately. Two of them overlap open maintainer PRs and need a decision from you (see below); the rest are ready for review.

Each item closes a gap where OpenClaw already has the behaviour; the OpenClaw reference is linked per item (permalinks at `fead50a`). Each PR is independent of the others unless noted and based on current `main`; all are green on linux/macos/windows CI, which runs `zig build test --summary all` with 0 failures and 0 leaks. I also trial-merged each onto `main` + #971 and ran the full suite there, so none of them conflicts with #971 landing first.

## Overlaps with existing PRs

Two of my PRs turned out to overlap with open maintainer PRs. I compared them in detail and propose the following, to avoid duplicate review:

- **#1057 duplicates #971** (native tool calls while streaming). Both use the same design. #971 goes further: it refuses to execute a tool call salvaged from a truncated stream, opts in the dedicated OpenAI provider, and keeps `SseLineResult` source-compatible. **#1057 is closed in favour of #971.** The only thing #1057 adds is a substring guard that skips the tool-call JSON parse on chunks that cannot contain tool calls; I can send that as a small follow-up to #971 if it is wanted.
- **#1059 overlaps #1050** on the config key (reasoning display default off/on/stream; `agent.reasoning_mode` vs top-level `reasoning_mode`, with different invalid-value handling, so only one shape should survive). #1050 also fixes reasoning-only turns being reported as an empty response, which #1059 does not. #1059's distinct part is restoring the configured default when `/restart` or `/debug reset` resets the session state (today that falls back to hard-coded off), plus a `config_mutator` restart entry and a save round-trip test. Happy to rebase it onto #1050's key, fold it into #1050, or close it, whichever you prefer.

## Remaining PRs

| PR | What it does | OpenClaw reference | Size |
|---|---|---|---|
| #1060 | `provider/model` routes to any configured provider entry, not only the primary or `reliability.fallback_providers`. | [model-selection-normalize.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/fead50a35107ed73cbb1f34b93c21716a0583f98/src/agents/model-selection-normalize.ts#L24-L46), [configured-provider-model.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/fead50a35107ed73cbb1f34b93c21716a0583f98/src/agents/configured-provider-model.ts#L16-L49) | small |
| #1062 | Telegram live drafts use the same Markdown to HTML rendering as the final message, falling back to plain text on `can't parse entities`. | [draft-stream-message.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/fead50a35107ed73cbb1f34b93c21716a0583f98/extensions/telegram/src/draft-stream-message.ts#L44-L108), [rich-plain-fallback.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/fead50a35107ed73cbb1f34b93c21716a0583f98/extensions/telegram/src/rich-plain-fallback.ts#L17-L40) | small, 1 file |
| #1064 | Resend assistant history with an empty `reasoning_content` when the endpoint rejects history without a thinking field (seen with IFM K2: every turn after the first failed until `/new`). Also keeps the provider's error text on the streaming path instead of a generic "An error occurred". | [provider-stream-shared.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/fead50a35107ed73cbb1f34b93c21716a0583f98/src/plugin-sdk/provider-stream-shared.ts#L436-L476) backfills `reasoning_content: ""`; `compat.requiresReasoningContentOnAssistantMessages` in [custom-providers.md](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/fead50a35107ed73cbb1f34b93c21716a0583f98/docs/gateway/config-tools/custom-providers.md#L129) | small, 3 files |
| #1065 | `/think` and config `reasoning_effort` actually reach OpenAI-compatible non-OpenAI models (they were dropped for anything outside `gpt-5*`/`o*`); adds `max`; lowers to `high` per model when an endpoint rejects `xhigh`/`max`. Stacked on #1064. | thinking ladder with `xhigh`/`max` in [thinking.shared.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/fead50a35107ed73cbb1f34b93c21716a0583f98/src/auto-reply/thinking.shared.ts#L14-L25); clamp to `high` in [openai-reasoning-effort.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/fead50a35107ed73cbb1f34b93c21716a0583f98/packages/ai/src/providers/openai-reasoning-effort.ts#L198-L226) | medium |
| #1058 | Slack replies stream while generated: native `chat.startStream`/`appendStream`/`stopStream` in threads, `chat.postMessage` + throttled `chat.update` elsewhere or when native streaming is refused. | [streaming.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/fead50a35107ed73cbb1f34b93c21716a0583f98/extensions/slack/src/streaming.ts#L138-L276), [messaging.md](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/fead50a35107ed73cbb1f34b93c21716a0583f98/docs/channels/slack/messaging.md#L62-L120) | large |
| #1061 | Slack task lifecycle as reactions on the inbound message (accepted, running, done, failed), removing the superseded reaction since Slack reactions accumulate. Opt-in per account. | [status-reactions.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/fead50a35107ed73cbb1f34b93c21716a0583f98/src/channels/status-reactions.ts#L16-L52), [dispatch-setup.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/fead50a35107ed73cbb1f34b93c21716a0583f98/extensions/slack/src/monitor/message-handler/dispatch-setup.ts#L123-L156) | medium |
| #1063 | Per-agent autonomy: `agents.list[].autonomy` gives a named agent (e.g. a guest bound to one peer) its own policy instead of inheriting the global one, and closes the paths that bypass it (spawn, schedule, delegate, MCP, slash commands, attachments, shell path arguments). | per-agent `sandbox` / `tools` in [multi-agent-sandbox-tools.md](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/fead50a35107ed73cbb1f34b93c21716a0583f98/docs/tools/multi-agent-sandbox-tools.md), [entries-and-multi-agent.md](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/fead50a35107ed73cbb1f34b93c21716a0583f98/docs/gateway/config-agents/entries-and-multi-agent.md#L147-L240) | large |

## Suggested review order

1. Small, self-contained fixes: #1060, #1062, #1064.
2. #1065 (after #1064).
3. Slack UX: #1058, #1061.
4. #1063 last. It is large because each bypass needed its own change; I can split it (config and dedicated runtime, withheld tools, slash commands and attachments, shell confinement) if that is easier to review.

If any of these are not a direction you want, say so here and I will close them rather than keep them in the queue. I will keep this issue updated as PRs are merged, closed or split.

prs.title: feat(config): add agent.reasoning_mode default
prs.body:
> Tracking: #1066. This overlaps maintainer PR #1050 on the config key; see the comment below for how the two could be combined.

# feat(config): add agent.reasoning_mode default

- Branch: `feat/configurable-reasoning-default`
- Scope: one concern, a configurable default for the `/reasoning` display mode
- Risk tier (AGENTS.md §5): high, config schema. Change is additive only, no security, runtime, or gateway boundary is touched.
- Breaking change: no

## Summary

Adds the optional `agent.reasoning_mode` key (`off` | `on` | `stream`, default `off`) to the `agent` config section. It sets the reasoning display mode applied to newly created sessions, and it becomes the value `/restart` and `/debug reset` restore instead of the hard-coded `off`.

Diffstat (8 files, 182 insertions, 14 deletions):

```text
 docs/en/configuration.md | 18 ++++++++++
 docs/zh/configuration.md | 18 ++++++++++
 src/agent/commands.zig   |  2 +-
 src/agent/root.zig       | 49 +++++++++++++++++++--------
 src/config.zig           | 72 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 src/config_mutator.zig   |  1 +
 src/config_parse.zig     |  5 +++
 src/config_types.zig     | 31 +++++++++++++++++
 8 files changed, 182 insertions(+), 14 deletions(-)
```

## What changed

### `src/config_types.zig` (+31)

- New `pub const ReasoningMode` enum with variants `off`, `on`, `stream`, plus `toSlice()` and a case-insensitive `fromSlice()`.
- New field `AgentConfig.reasoning_mode: ReasoningMode = .off`.
- The enum is declared in the config layer so a parsed value can be assigned to the runtime field with no conversion step.

### `src/config_parse.zig` (+5)

- `parseJson` reads `agent.reasoning_mode`. A non-string value or an unrecognized string returns `error.InvalidReasoningMode`, so a typo fails loudly instead of silently falling back to `off`.

### `src/config.zig` (+72)

- `Config.save()` emits `reasoning_mode` inside the pretty-printed `agent` section, so a saved config round-trips through `parseJson`.
- New tests: `parse agent.reasoning_mode`, `agent.reasoning_mode defaults to off`, `agent.reasoning_mode rejects invalid values`, `Config.save preserves agent.reasoning_mode`.

### `src/config_mutator.zig` (+1)

- `pathRequiresRestart` returns true for `agent.reasoning_mode`, alongside the existing `agent.default_queue_mode` entry. This matches the documented behavior that new sessions pick the value up after a restart.

### `src/agent/root.zig` (+36 / -13)

- Deletes the private `ReasoningMode` enum and aliases `config_types.ReasoningMode`, removing the conversion that would otherwise be needed when applying the configured value.
- New field `default_reasoning_mode: ReasoningMode = .off`, documented as the value restored by `/restart` and `/debug reset`.
- `Agent.fromConfig` sets both `reasoning_mode` and `default_reasoning_mode` from `cfg.agent.reasoning_mode`.
- New test `Agent.fromConfig applies agent.reasoning_mode and resets to it` covers the configured default, a per-session `/reasoning on` override, and the reset path, and carries a `Regression:` comment citing the idle-eviction problem.

### `src/agent/commands.zig` (+1 / -1)

- `resetRuntimeCommandState` sets `self.reasoning_mode = self.default_reasoning_mode` instead of `.off`. This is the shared code path behind `/restart` and `/debug reset`, so one change fixes both commands.

### `docs/en/configuration.md` (+18) and `docs/zh/configuration.md` (+18)

- New `agent.reasoning_mode` section in both languages, placed next to the other `agent.*` keys. CONTRIBUTING requires syncing English and Chinese pages when both audiences are affected, and this is a user-facing config key, so both pages are updated in this PR to satisfy that requirement.

## Why it changed

`reasoning_mode` always started at `off`, and `resetRuntimeCommandState` hard-coded `.off` for `/restart` and `/debug reset`. Sessions are evicted after `agent.session_idle_timeout_secs`, so anyone who wants reasoning visible had to re-run `/reasoning on` after every idle eviction.

The display mode is a preference, not per-session state, so it belongs in the `agent` config section. `agent.default_queue_mode` already solves the same class of problem for the queue mode, so this follows an existing pattern rather than introducing a new one. This also gives the new key a concrete caller in `Agent.fromConfig` and `resetRuntimeCommandState`, as required by AGENTS.md §3.2.

`/reasoning <mode>` still overrides the mode for the current session. The config key only changes what a new or reset session starts from.

## Validation

No local Zig toolchain was available when this patch was written. The commands below were not executed locally and no results are claimed here. CI is the source of truth for this PR.

Required for code changes (CONTRIBUTING, AGENTS.md §8), with Zig 0.16.0:

```bash
zig build test --summary all      # must be 0 failures and 0 leaks
zig fmt --check src/              # the same check .githooks/pre-commit runs
```

Optional release check, since the change touches config and agent paths:

```bash
zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseSmall
```

Test coverage added by this PR (AGENTS.md §8.1), 5 tests total:

- `src/config.zig`: `parse agent.reasoning_mode`, `agent.reasoning_mode defaults to off`, `agent.reasoning_mode rejects invalid values`, `Config.save preserves agent.reasoning_mode`
- `src/agent/root.zig`: `Agent.fromConfig applies agent.reasoning_mode and resets to it`

## Config surface

- Key: `agent.reasoning_mode`
- Type: string enum, one of `off`, `on`, `stream` (case-insensitive)
- Default: `off`
- Optional: yes. A config that does not set the key behaves exactly as it does today.

```json
{
  "agent": {
    "reasoning_mode": "stream"
  }
}
```

- `off` hides reasoning content, `on` prints a `Reasoning:` quote block above the final reply, `stream` prints reasoning live while the model produces it.
- `/reasoning <off|on|stream>` overrides the mode for the current session only.
- Changes apply to sessions created after a restart. `config_mutator.pathRequiresRestart` reports this for `nullclaw config set`.

## Risks and follow-up work

- Risk: a config typo now fails config loading instead of being ignored. This is intentional (AGENTS.md §3.4 fail fast) and matches how `agent.default_queue_mode` already behaves.
- Risk: `ReasoningMode` moves from `src/agent/root.zig` to `src/config_types.zig`. Both are internal to the module; no public API is exported and no caller outside these files references the type.
- Follow-up, deliberately not in this PR to keep it single-concern: `resetRuntimeCommandState` also resets `verbose_level` and `usage_mode` to fixed values, which could get the same configurable-default treatment.

## Breaking change

No. The key is optional and defaults to `off`, which is the pre-change behavior for both the initial mode and the reset path. No existing key changes meaning, no CLI flag is removed, and no config file needs editing.

## Rollback

- `git revert` the commit, or
- set `agent.reasoning_mode` back to `off` (or remove the key) and restart. Sessions then behave exactly as they did before this change.

## Notes

- The reset path and the config default now read the same field, so there is a single source of truth for "what mode does a new session start in".
- `/reasoning` command parsing is unchanged. Only the initial value and the reset value moved.
- No new dependency and no new allocation on the hot path. The addition to `Agent` is one small enum field next to the existing `reasoning_mode`.
- No secrets, tokens, or personal data are included in the code, tests, docs, or this description.

**Branch:** `feat/streaming-native-tool-calls`
**Commit subject:** `feat(providers): support native tool calls while streaming`
**Diffstat:** 6 files changed, 790 insertions(+), 92 deletions(-)
**Risk tier:** high per `AGENTS.md` section 5 (vtable interface change). The runtime effect is opt-in and default-off.

## Summary

### What changed

OpenAI-compatible streaming requests now carry `tools` / `tool_choice` when the provider serving the turn can emit native tool calls, and the SSE parser reassembles `delta.tool_calls` fragments per index into complete tool calls. Streaming results expose them in `StreamChatResult.tool_calls`, so the agent loop executes them exactly like the non-streaming path: history receives the assistant `tool_calls` message plus the tool results, instead of the provider markup being rendered as plain text.

| File | Change | +/− |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/providers/root.zig` | `StreamChatResult.tool_calls`; new `supports_streaming_native_tools` vtable slot defaulting to false; `emitChatResponseAsStream` hands tool calls to the caller | +34 / -1 |
| `src/providers/sse.zig` | `DeltaToolCall`, `ToolCallAccumulator`, `extractDeltaToolCalls`; `SseLineResult` becomes a struct | +385 / -85 |
| `src/providers/compatible.zig` | advertise the capability when `native_tools` is on and streaming is not disabled | +50 / -0 |
| `src/providers/reliable.zig` | forward the capability through a failover chain to the provider that actually serves the request | +121 / -0 |
| `src/providers/router.zig` | forward the capability through a router to the resolved provider | +41 / -0 |
| `src/agent/root.zig` | keep native tools enabled on streaming turns for capable providers and forward accumulated tool calls into the turn loop | +159 / -6 |

### File by file

**`src/providers/root.zig`**

- `StreamChatResult` gains `tool_calls: []const ToolCall = &.{}`, owned by the caller and freed the same way as `ChatResponse.tool_calls`. Empty when the provider did not stream tool calls.
- New optional vtable slot `supports_streaming_native_tools: ?*const fn (ptr: *anyopaque, model: []const u8) bool = null` plus the accessor `Provider.supportsStreamingNativeTools(model)`. The default is `false`, so every provider that does not opt in keeps the text tool protocol on streaming turns. The query takes the model because the answer can differ per model behind a wrapper.
- `emitChatResponseAsStream` now detaches `response.tool_calls` into the returned result instead of freeing them. Providers that fall back to a blocking `chat` mid-stream (large prompt, curl failure, responses API) must still surface native tool calls to the agent loop, so the calls are handed to the caller rather than dropped. The existing ownership test is extended to cover the transfer and asserts the result carries the call.

**`src/providers/sse.zig`**

- `DeltaToolCall` models one streaming fragment: a required `index` and optional `id` / `name` / `arguments`, because providers split those fields across chunks and some repeat `id` and `name` on every fragment. `freeDeltaToolCalls` frees a fragment slice.
- `ToolCallAccumulator` merges fragments keyed by `index`, so parallel tool calls and argument strings split anywhere in the stream both reassemble. `id` and `name` are recorded on first sight and later repeats are ignored; `arguments` fragments are always concatenated. `toOwnedSlice` transfers ownership of the finished calls field-by-field and leaves the accumulator empty but still deinitializable.
- `extractDeltaToolCalls` walks `choices[0].delta.tool_calls`. It guards on a `"tool_calls"` substring before paying for a JSON parse, falls back to the array position when a gateway omits `index`, and returns an empty slice rather than an error when the payload does not parse or does not have the expected shape.
- `SseLineResult` changes from a `union(enum)` (`delta` / `done` / `usage` / `skip`) to a struct with optional fields, a `deinit`, and an `isSkip` helper. A single chunk can carry content and tool-call fragments and usage together, which a union cannot express; some gateways do interleave a text delta with the first tool-call fragment.
- `curlStream` accumulates fragments into a `ToolCallAccumulator` and passes `tool_acc.toOwnedSlice(allocator)` into every `finalizeStreamResult` return path, including the partial-stream recovery paths that return accumulated output after a curl failure. `finalizeStreamResult` takes the tool calls as a parameter.
- `curlStreamAnthropic` passes an empty slice. Anthropic streaming is deliberately untouched and keeps the text tool protocol.

**`src/providers/compatible.zig`**

- `supportsStreamingNativeToolsImpl` returns `self.native_tools and supportsStreamingImpl(ptr)`: true when native tools are on and streaming is neither disabled nor routed to the responses API. Registered in the vtable.
- Note that `buildStreamingChatRequestBody` already serialized `tools` and `tool_choice` when `req.tools` was non-null. The missing piece was upstream: the agent passed `.tools = null` on streaming turns. The added request-body tests pin both directions of that plumbing.

**`src/providers/reliable.zig`**

- `supportsStreamingNativeToolsImpl` mirrors `supportsVisionForModelImpl`: an explicit `provider/model` ref is answered by the provider that will actually serve it. Without an explicit ref it returns true when the inner provider or any extra is capable. Wrapping a capable provider in a failover chain no longer hides the capability.

**`src/providers/router.zig`**

- The router resolves the model the same way `streamChatImpl` does and reports the capability of the provider that will serve the stream, so an alias routed to a capable provider is not reported as incapable.

**`src/agent/root.zig`**

- Both capability call sites now branch: on a streaming turn the agent asks `supportsStreamingNativeTools(turn_model_name)`, otherwise it keeps `supportsNativeTools()`. The same change is applied to the system-prompt path that decides whether tool specs are described in text.
- The streaming request sets `.tools = if (native_tools_enabled) turn_tool_specs else null`, on both the primary request and the retry request.
- The streaming branch builds its `ChatResponse` with `.tool_calls = stream_result.tool_calls` instead of `&.{}`. That single line is what makes the turn loop execute the calls and record the assistant `tool_calls` message plus the tool results in history.

### Why it changed

**User-visible bug.** With a streaming channel or alias, a model that supports native tools silently fell back to a text tool protocol, so tool-call markup could leak into the reply as literal text.

The cause was two-sided. The agent computed `native_tools_enabled = !is_streaming and self.provider.supportsNativeTools()` and passed `.tools = null` on every streaming request, so the streaming request never carried tool specs. There was also no way for a provider to say "I can emit native tool calls while streaming", so the agent had no correct condition to use even if it had wanted to send them. The result was that a provider which streams OpenAI-style `delta.tool_calls` had those calls displayed to the user as text and never executed, while the identical turn on the blocking path worked correctly.

This patch adds the missing capability query, asks the provider that will actually serve the model, sends the specs when it answers yes, reassembles the streamed fragments, and feeds the result into the same execution path the blocking case already uses.

## Validation

**I did not run the build or the test suite.** The environment where this patch was prepared has no Zig toolchain, so there is no local result to report and none is claimed. The validation signal for this change is CI plus the maintainer's own run, not the author's.

Checks to run, in the order the repository's own hooks run them:

```sh
zig version                          # must print 0.16.0 (upstream pin)
zig fmt --check src/                 # .githooks/pre-commit
zig build test --summary all         # .githooks/pre-push; expect 0 failures, 0 leaks
zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseSmall    # size check, see below
```

The `ReleaseSmall` build is worth running because `AGENTS.md` treats binary size as a hard product constraint (target under 1 MB). This patch adds a JSON walk plus an accumulator to the streaming path, so confirming the target still holds is part of validating the change rather than an optional extra.

Tests added by the patch (12 new test blocks plus one extended), all deterministic and network-free:

- `src/providers/sse.zig`: content-only chunks yield no fragments; a single fragment is extracted with `id`, `name`, and partial `arguments`; content and tool calls in the same chunk both survive; two parallel calls with argument strings split across chunks reassemble to the exact expected JSON; argument-only fragments stay keyed by index and produce empty `id` / `name`.
- `src/providers/compatible.zig`: the streaming body carries `"tools":` and `"tool_choice":"auto"` alongside `"stream":true`; the body omits both keys when no specs are supplied; the capability follows `native_tools` and `disable_streaming`.
- `src/providers/reliable.zig`: delegation to a capable inner, and resolution through an explicit prefix where the prefix wins over a capable primary.
- `src/providers/router.zig`: the capability follows the resolved provider, so an explicit ref to a capable provider reports true and a bare model resolving to an incapable default reports false.
- `src/agent/root.zig`: an end-to-end streaming turn. A two-turn streaming provider asserts that tools were advertised on both streaming requests, that the returned tool call was executed, that the final response text is correct, that the streamed text order is preserved, and that the observer recorded at least one tool call.

## Notes

### Review focus: memory ownership

The main correctness risk is ownership of tool calls, which now move `ChatResponse` -> `StreamChatResult` -> `ChatResponse`. The patch transfers rather than copies and clears the source in both places (`response.tool_calls = &.{}` in `emitChatResponseAsStream`, and `entry.id` / `entry.name` nulled in `ToolCallAccumulator.toOwnedSlice`), with callers freeing field-by-field. `AGENTS.md` requires zero leaks under the leak-detecting test allocator, so a leak or double free introduced here would surface in `zig build test`, but the transfer is the part of the diff worth reading closely.

### Scope

The commit subject says `providers`, and the patch also changes `src/agent/root.zig`. The agent change is the consumer side: without it the capability would be advertised and never used, and the bug would remain. Happy to split it into a providers-only PR plus an agent follow-up if you prefer a narrower first step.

### Naming

The vtable field is `supports_streaming_native_tools` (snake_case) to match the adjacent `supports_streaming` and `supports_vision` fields in the same vtable, while the accessor and implementations use camelCase (`supportsStreamingNativeTools`). `AGENTS.md` prefers camelCase for new vtable fields and notes the existing snake_case family, so this follows the local family. Flagging it so a reviewer can ask for the camelCase variant if that is preferred.

### Source-level API change

`SseLineResult` in `src/providers/sse.zig` is no longer a `union(enum)`. All in-tree call sites are updated in this patch. Any out-of-tree code that switches on `.delta` / `.done` / `.usage` / `.skip` needs the struct-field form plus `deinit`. The reason for the change is that one SSE chunk can carry content, tool-call fragments, and usage together, which the union could not represent.

### Config surface

No new config keys, CLI flags, or environment variables. The existing per-provider `native_tools` field now also gates the streaming path, which is a behavior change for users rather than a new surface:

- With `native_tools` on (the compatible-provider default) and streaming enabled, a streaming reply can now execute tool calls instead of showing markup as text. That is the point of the patch, and it is visible to anyone using a streaming channel or alias.
- Providers that do not implement the new vtable slot are unaffected and keep the text tool protocol while streaming.

### Rollback

`git revert <sha>` reverts the whole change. Two operational escape hatches avoid a revert entirely: set `native_tools = false` on the provider entry to force the previous text tool protocol, or set `disable_streaming = true` to force the blocking path, which already used native tools before this patch.

### Security impact

- **New permissions or capabilities:** No new permission surface. The streaming path now advertises the same tool specs the blocking path already advertises for the same turn, and tool execution still goes through the existing dispatcher and policy layer. The capability is default-off for every provider that does not opt in.
- **New external network calls:** No.
- **Secrets and credentials:** No change. The new parse path does not log payloads.
- **Untrusted input:** `extractDeltaToolCalls` parses provider-controlled JSON from the stream. It is defensive: a substring guard skips the parse on the common non-tool path, a parse failure returns an empty slice instead of propagating an error, and unexpected JSON shapes return empty. Tool arguments are model-controlled and remain untrusted; they reach the same dispatcher and validation as the blocking path, which is not weakened by this change.
- **Prompt injection:** No new model-visible text is introduced. The tool specs sent on streaming turns are the same specs already sent on blocking turns.
- **PII in the diff:** None. Test fixtures use neutral placeholders and generic provider aliases.

### Docs

`CONTRIBUTING.md` requires docs updated in the same PR for user-facing behavior changes, so this is called out explicitly rather than left implicit.

I checked the docs tree against `main`: no page documents the OpenAI-compatible fallback to a text tool protocol (`native_tools`, `text tool`, and `<tool_call>` produce no hits under `docs/en/` or `docs/zh/`), so no existing sentence is contradicted by this change and none is left stale. The one nearby sentence in `docs/en/configuration.md` and its `docs/zh/configuration.md` counterpart that mentions native tool calls on non-streaming requests is scoped to the native Anthropic provider, and Anthropic streaming is deliberately untouched here, so it stays accurate.

No docs change is included. If you want the new behavior documented, the natural home is the provider section of `docs/en/configuration.md` plus the `docs/zh` mirror, and I can add it to this PR.

### Formatting

Two hunks introduce consecutive blank lines (`src/agent/root.zig` before `test "slash /new clears history"`, and `src/providers/reliable.zig` before `test "multi-provider fallback: primary fails, extra succeeds"`). If `zig fmt` normalizes runs of blank lines, the `pre-commit` hook (`zig fmt --check src/`) will fail. I could not check this without a Zig toolchain, so run `zig fmt src/` before pushing.

## PR checklist

- [x] Scope is focused and does not mix unrelated refactors
- [x] Commands, config keys, and examples match the current codebase
- [ ] Docs are updated for any user-facing behavior change (see the Docs note: no contradicting page found, no docs change included, offer to add one)
- [ ] Validation was run and results are included in the PR description (not run locally, no Zig toolchain; CI runs `zig build test --summary all` on this head)
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or personal data were added
- [x] New code follows existing naming and module boundaries

prs.title: fix(providers): send /think levels to OpenAI-compatible models and add max
prs.body:
> Tracking: #1066

> Stacked on #1064 (it reuses that PR's retry path in `compatible.zig`). Only the last commit is new; I will rebase once #1064 is merged or dropped.

## Summary

`/think` and the config `reasoning_effort` only reach OpenAI reasoning models. `appendGenerationFields` drops the field for every model `isReasoningModel` does not recognise (`gpt-5*`, `o1`, `o3`, `o4-mini`, `codex-mini`). So on DeepSeek, Kimi, K2 and other OpenAI-compatible models behind the compatible provider, the chosen level is silently ignored. Those endpoints take the same top-level `reasoning_effort` field.

I confirmed this from the gateway side: none of the requests nullclaw sent carried `reasoning_effort`, whatever `/think` was set to.

Changes:

- **Send the level to OpenAI-compatible models.** The compatible provider now adds `reasoning_effort` for models outside `isReasoningModel`. `minimal` maps to `low`; `xhigh` and `max` pass through. Providers that already map reasoning_effort to their own field are unchanged and do not get the extra field:
  - GLM `thinking`
  - Qwen `enable_thinking`
  - MiniMax `reasoning_split`
  - vLLM `chat_template_kwargs`
- **Learn per-model limits from rejections.** Measured against the endpoints:
  - DeepSeek accepts `low`/`high`/`xhigh`/`max`.
  - IFM K2 rejects `xhigh`/`max` with `400 Invalid value for 'reasoning_effort'`.

  On that error the provider records a limit for that model and resends. A level above `high` is lowered to `high`. If `high` is rejected too, the field is dropped for that model. Limits are kept per model, because one provider entry often serves models with different ranges, so K2's rejection does not lower DeepSeek's level.
- **Add `max`.** `/think` and config `reasoning_effort` accept `max`. OpenAI reasoning models, Gemini and the Codex provider map it like `xhigh`. The Codex provider previously sent `xhigh` verbatim, which its backend rejects; it now normalizes the same way as the other OpenAI paths.

This matches how OpenClaw handles OpenAI-compatible reasoning effort: its thinking ladder includes `xhigh` and `max`, and it clamps to `high` for models that only support the standard levels.

## Validation

Zig 0.16.0, on this branch:

```text
$ zig fmt --check src/
$ zig build test --summary all
Build Summary: 13/13 steps succeeded; 7498/7512 tests passed (14 skipped)
```

New tests:
- the field is sent to non-OpenAI models with the right mapping
- it is absent without a level
- OpenAI models still get exactly one normalized field
- providers with a native thinking field get no extra field, on both the streaming and non-streaming builders
- per-model limit learning: lower to `high`, then drop; another model behind the same provider keeps its level; unrelated errors do not retry

Running against live endpoints through an OpenAI-style gateway, with `/think max`:
- DeepSeek received `reasoning_effort: "max"`.
- K2 logged `rejected reasoning_effort=max for k2; resending with high`, and the retry succeeded with `high`.

## Notes

- Only changes behaviour when a reasoning level is set. With no `/think` and no config `reasoning_effort`, request bodies are unchanged.
- Files: `src/providers/{compatible,helpers,openai_codex}.zig`, `src/agent/commands.zig`, `src/config_parse.zig`.

prs.title: fix(providers): resend assistant history with reasoning_content when required
prs.body:
> Tracking: #1066

## Summary

Some OpenAI-compatible endpoints require a thinking field on every assistant message of a multi-turn request. IFM's K2 models (reached here through an OpenAI-style gateway) answer with:

```text
400 Add a supported thinking field to each assistant message in the multi-turn conversation history.
```

nullclaw never sends one. As soon as a session has one assistant turn, every later request in it fails, and the only way out for the user is `/new`.

Two problems made this hard to see:

1. **No thinking field.** `ChatMessage` gets an optional `reasoning_content` that the compatible serializer emits on assistant messages. When the endpoint returns this specific error, the provider remembers it and resends the request once with an empty `reasoning_content` on every assistant message. Later requests include it directly, so existing sessions recover without `/new`. I checked against the endpoint: an empty string is accepted, and so is `reasoning`. Other endpoints are unaffected because the field is only added after this rejection.
2. **The error text was dropped on the streaming path.** `sse.curlStream` classified a JSON error body but never recorded it, so channels showed only `An error occurred. Try again or /new for a fresh session.` and the log only `error.ApiError`. It is now recorded with `setLastApiErrorDetail` like the non-streaming path, so the real reason reaches the user and the log.

## Validation

Zig 0.16.0, on this branch (based on current `main`):

```text
$ zig fmt --check src/
$ zig build test --summary all
Build Summary: 13/13 steps succeeded; 7495/7509 tests passed (14 skipped)
```

New tests:
- `reasoning_content` is serialized on an assistant message only when set.
- Only the missing-thinking-field `ApiError` triggers the resend. A rate-limit message or a different error does not. The resend happens once, and afterwards only assistant messages get the field.

## Notes

- Only `src/providers/{compatible,root,sse}.zig` change. No config change.
- The history does not keep reasoning text, so the resent field is empty. Endpoints that need the actual reasoning back (rather than the field's presence) would need history to store it. That is a larger change and out of scope here.

prs.title: feat(security): per-agent autonomy for named agents
prs.body:
> Tracking: #1066

## Summary

Every named agent currently runs under the global `autonomy` policy. `SessionManager` builds each agent runtime's tools from `config.autonomy` and shares one global `SecurityPolicy`, so a guest agent bound to a single chat peer through `bindings` gets exactly the same shell and file permissions as the main agent. With a `full` or `yolo` main agent, any bound peer can run arbitrary shell commands and read `config.json` (provider keys, channel tokens).

This adds an optional `autonomy` object to `agents.list[]` entries:

```json
{
  "agents": {
    "list": [
      { "id": "guest", "provider": "openrouter", "model": "...", "workspace_path": "agents/guest",
        "autonomy": { "level": "read_only" } }
    ]
  }
}
```

- It accepts the same keys as the top-level `autonomy` block and **replaces** the global one for that agent. Omitted keys fall back to the secure `AutonomyConfig` defaults instead of inheriting the global (possibly `yolo`) values. An unknown `level` is rejected at config load.
- An agent with its own autonomy always gets a dedicated runtime that owns its own `SecurityPolicy` and `RateTracker`, scoped to its own workspace. `makeAgentConfig` also carries the agent's autonomy, so `Agent.fromConfigWithProfile` derives `exec_security`, `allowed_paths` and `multimodal_unrestricted` from it.
- `nullclaw agent --agent <name>` applies the same policy.
- Agents without an `autonomy` block behave exactly as before.

### What is closed for an agent with its own autonomy

A stricter policy is only meaningful if the agent cannot reach the global policy or the host through another door, so these are closed too:

- **Tools that act under the global policy or outside the workspace are withheld:** `spawn` (subagents run under the global config), `schedule` (cron shell jobs use the scheduler's global policy), `delegate` (runs any configured agent's provider with the operator's key), MCP tools (child processes that never consult the policy), `git` (writes regardless of `read_only`), `screenshot`, `image_info` (opens any absolute path).
- **Global config surface:** `/config` and `/export` are refused, `/capabilities` and the `/model` menu no longer read the shared `config.json`, `/model` does not persist the global default, and Telegram `/bind` is refused for a peer routed to such an agent (otherwise `/bind clear` escapes back to the default agent).
- **Attachments:** legacy `[DOCUMENT:]`/`[FILE:]`/`[IMAGE:]` markers in the reply are filtered at the session boundary. A local target must resolve (realpath) inside the agent's workspace or its own `allowed_paths`. Previously any absolute path was uploaded, even under `read_only`, because this does not go through a tool call. Inbound `[IMAGE:/tmp/...]` reads of the platform temp dir are refused as well.
- **Shell confinement (`supervised`/`full`):** arguments that name a path outside the workspace (absolute, `..`, `~`) are rejected. Commands are restricted to a strict byte set (letters, digits, spaces, `;`, `|`, `&&`, `||`, `-_./,:=+@%^`), so quotes, redirections, escapes, `$` expansion and globs, which the shell would rewrite after the check, are refused. Package-manager run verbs and script-running git subcommands are refused, as are `find` exec/write predicates.

The shell confinement is a best-effort argument check, not a filesystem jail. The docs (en + zh) say so explicitly and recommend `"level": "read_only"` for untrusted guests, which disables all tool calls.

### Two latent fixes found while testing

- An unknown autonomy level is rejected before `parseJson` writes any field, so `Config.load` no longer keeps a half-parsed config.
- `Config.save` no longer double-frees the serialized agent `api_key` strings when the loop errors part-way.

## Validation

Zig 0.16.0, on this branch (rebased on current `main`):

```text
$ zig fmt --check src/
$ zig build test --summary all
Build Summary: 13/13 steps succeeded; 7517/7531 tests passed (14 skipped)
```

New tests cover the config parse/reject paths, the dedicated runtime and policy, withheld tools, `/config`, `/export` and `/bind` refusal, attachment filtering, the temp-dir image refusal, and the shell confinement (including `cat ''/etc/passwd`, `cat </etc/passwd`, `cat \/etc/passwd`, `cat $IFS/etc/passwd`, `find . -fprint x`).

Also running on a live gateway with a `yolo` main agent and a `read_only` guest bound to one peer: the main agent's shell is unrestricted, the guest's shell calls return `Action blocked: agent is in read-only mode`, and `nullclaw doctor` is clean.

## Notes

- This is large because each closed door needed its own change. Happy to split it (config + dedicated runtime first, then withheld tools, then attachments/slash commands, then shell confinement) if that is easier to review.
- No behaviour change for configs without `agents.list[].autonomy`.

prs.title: feat(telegram): render live drafts with HTML parse mode
prs.body:
> Tracking: #1066

## Summary

Telegram live drafts are sent through `sendMessageDraft` as plain text, while the finalized reply goes through `markdownToTelegramHtml` and is sent with `parse_mode: "HTML"`. Anything formatted in the streaming draft (quoted reasoning, bold, inline code, lists) therefore shows up as raw Markdown until the final message replaces the draft, and the formatting appears to "jump" at the end of every turn.

This change renders the draft the same way the final message is rendered:

- `sendDraft` converts the preview text with the existing `markdownToTelegramHtml` and sends it with `parse_mode: "HTML"`. `sendMessageDraft` accepts `parse_mode` like `sendMessage` does.
- The body construction moves into a small `postDraft` helper so the same request can be sent with or without `parse_mode`.
- A draft is the tail of a message that is still being generated, so it can end inside markup that Telegram rejects. When Telegram answers with `can't parse entities`, the same draft is resent as plain text, which is always accepted. Other errors keep going through the existing handling (rate limits, unsupported peer, message too long).
- If the conversion itself fails, the plain text is sent as before.

The 4096-character limit is unaffected in practice: `buildTransportText` caps the draft source at 3000 bytes, and the "message too long" handling still applies if an HTML expansion ever exceeds the limit.

## Validation

Run locally with Zig 0.16.0:

```text
$ zig fmt --check src/
$ zig build test --summary all
Build Summary: 13/13 steps succeeded; 7493/7507 tests passed (14 skipped)
```

Manually verified on a live Telegram bot: with `/reasoning stream`, the streamed reasoning renders as a quote block and formatting in the in-progress answer renders while streaming; the final message is unchanged.

## Notes

- Only `src/channels/telegram.zig` changes. No config, API, or behavior change outside draft rendering.
- No new tests: the change is in the network send path, which the existing draft tests stub out (`sendDraft` returns early under `builtin.is_test`). Happy to extract the fallback decision into a pure function with a unit test if maintainers prefer.
