> Tracking: #1066

# feat(slack): show the task lifecycle as reactions

**Branch:** `feat/slack-status-reactions`
**Base:** `main`
**Title:** `feat(slack): show the task lifecycle as reactions`

## What changed

Adds Slack status reactions: the message that triggers a turn gets a reaction that
follows the task through `accepted`, `running`, and `done` or `failed`.

```
 docs/en/configuration.md  |  25 ++++
 docs/zh/configuration.md  |  20 +++
 src/channels/root.zig     |  27 +++++
 src/channels/slack.zig    | 248 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 src/channels/telegram.zig |  10 +-
 src/config.zig            |  43 +++++++
 src/config_types.zig      |  16 +++
 src/daemon.zig            |  42 ++++++-
 8 files changed, 424 insertions(+), 7 deletions(-)
```

- `src/channels/root.zig`: new `Channel.TaskReaction` enum (`accepted`, `running`,
  `done`, `failed`), new `TaskReactionUpdate` payload, and a new vtable field
  `setTaskReaction` defaulting to `defaultSetTaskReaction`, which returns
  `error.NotSupported`. The default lets the daemon name a lifecycle state on any
  channel without every existing channel file changing.
- `src/channels/slack.zig`: `SlackChannel.setTaskReaction` plus the pure
  `planTaskReaction` transition table, the target parser `slackChannelIdOf`, the
  `reactions.add` / `reactions.remove` request builder, and the vtable wiring
  (`vtableSetTaskReaction`). The account latches `reactions_disabled` on an auth
  failure.
- `src/channels/telegram.zig`: `pub const TaskReaction` becomes an alias for
  `root.Channel.TaskReaction`. No other Telegram change.
- `src/config_types.zig`: `SlackReactionEmojisConfig` and the two new optional
  `SlackConfig` fields.
- `src/config.zig`: parsing tests for the defaults and for an explicit config.
- `src/daemon.zig`: `setInboundTaskReaction` helper, called from
  `processInboundMessage` on the accepted, running, and every terminal path.
- `docs/en/configuration.md`, `docs/zh/configuration.md`: the two new keys, a
  "Slack status reactions" section, and a config example, per the CONTRIBUTING
  rule that user-facing changes update docs in the same PR.

## Why it changed

`status_reactions` and `reaction_emojis` existed only under
`channels.telegram.accounts.<id>`, and the code that drives them is Telegram's
inherent `setTaskReaction`, which is called from the Telegram polling loop. Slack
does not run that loop: it receives events through its own socket/HTTP event
pipeline, so there was no place in the Slack path for the lifecycle to attach to,
and the same config keys would have been dead for Slack.

Copying the Telegram lifecycle into Slack would have forked the state machine into
a second implementation that can drift from the first. Instead the daemon names
the state and the channel keeps the mapping, which is the pattern AGENTS.md
prescribes: extension work implements vtable structs and registers them, it does
not add cross-cutting branches per channel.

## Design notes

### The vtable hook

`Channel.setTaskReaction(update: TaskReactionUpdate)` is a new function-pointer
field on `Channel.VTable`, following the same shape as the existing `setReaction`
and `markRead` hooks. The default implementation returns `error.NotSupported`, so:

- a channel that does not implement the hook is not a compile error and not a
  silent no-op either; the caller gets an explicit error it can ignore,
- the daemon can call the hook unconditionally and let the channel decide.

`setInboundTaskReaction` in `src/daemon.zig` swallows exactly `error.NotSupported`
and logs anything else at debug level. Telegram's vtable is not touched by this
change, so the hook is a no-op for Telegram and its polling-loop lifecycle keeps
running exactly as before.

`Channel.TaskReaction` is the shared vocabulary because the states themselves are
domain-neutral. `telegram.TaskReaction` becomes an alias for it rather than a
duplicate enum, so Telegram's existing call sites and tests keep compiling.

### Where the states are emitted

`processInboundMessage` emits the same sequence the Telegram loop uses, through
the `setInboundTaskReaction` helper:

| State | Emitted |
|---|---|
| `accepted` | after the routing decision returns something other than `.skip`, before the processing indicator |
| `running` | immediately before `processMessageStreaming` |
| `done` | on the draft-edit path and on the normal publish path, after the outbound event is published |
| `failed` | on the streaming error, the draft send failure, the publish failure, and the `makeOutbound` failure |

Every terminal path sets a final state, so a turn does not leave a stale
`accepted` or `running` reaction behind. The helper returns without calling the
channel when there is no message id to react to.

### Why the state to reaction mapping stays channel-local

The daemon passes a state name; each channel resolves it against its own config.
That split is deliberate:

- the value domain differs per channel. Telegram takes emoji characters
  (`TelegramReactionEmojisConfig` defaults to `👀 ⚡ 👍 💔`), Slack takes reaction
  short names (`eyes`, `hourglass_flowing_sand`, `white_check_mark`, `x`). The two
  are not interchangeable, which is why `SlackReactionEmojisConfig` is its own
  struct and only the enum is shared,
- the transport differs. Slack needs a remove-then-add plan, Telegram does not,
- the config type lives next to the channel config it parses, so a new channel
  adds a hook implementation without the daemon learning anything about reactions.

### Add, not replace

Slack reactions accumulate on a message. Adding `white_check_mark` after `eyes`
leaves both, so a transition has to remove the state it is leaving before adding
the state it is entering. `planTaskReaction` returns a `ReactionPlan` of up to two
removals and one add:

| New state | Supersedes | Default plan |
|---|---|---|
| `accepted` | none | add `eyes` |
| `running` | `accepted` | remove `eyes`, add `hourglass_flowing_sand` |
| `done` | `accepted`, `running` | remove `eyes`, remove `hourglass_flowing_sand`, add `white_check_mark` |
| `failed` | `accepted`, `running` | remove `eyes`, remove `hourglass_flowing_sand`, add `x` |

Two properties fall out of the same table:

- **Zero extra calls when two states share a name.** If the name being added
  equals a superseded state's name, that removal is skipped, so the reaction
  already on the message stays put. Setting `accepted` and `running` to
  `hourglass_flowing_sand` makes the `running` transition one add and zero
  removals.
- **An empty name withdraws the state.** `reactionEmoji` maps an empty string to
  null, which drops that state's add and still removes the superseded occurrence.
  With every name empty the plan is empty and no API call is made at all.

Duplicate removals are collapsed, so the plan never issues the same remove twice.

`planTaskReaction` is a pure function, which is what makes the transition table
testable without a network.

### Error handling

`already_reacted` and `no_reaction` are treated as success, so a retry or a
double transition is harmless. Any code matched by the existing
`SlackChannel.isAuthFailureCode` (which already covers `missing_scope`) latches
`reactions_disabled` and logs one warning per account; later turns skip the calls
entirely. Reaction failures never propagate: `setTaskReaction` is best-effort and
returns `void`, so a reaction problem cannot fail a turn.

## Config surface

Two optional keys on the Slack alias, mirroring Telegram's key names:

| Key | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `channels.slack.accounts.<alias>.status_reactions` | bool | `false` |
| `channels.slack.accounts.<alias>.reaction_emojis.accepted` | string | `eyes` |
| `channels.slack.accounts.<alias>.reaction_emojis.running` | string | `hourglass_flowing_sand` |
| `channels.slack.accounts.<alias>.reaction_emojis.done` | string | `white_check_mark` |
| `channels.slack.accounts.<alias>.reaction_emojis.failed` | string | `x` |

Values are Slack reaction short names, not the emoji themselves. An empty string
withdraws the reaction for that state.

```json
{
  "channels": {
    "slack": {
      "accounts": {
        "<alias>": {
          "bot_token": "YOUR_BOT_TOKEN",
          "status_reactions": true,
          "reaction_emojis": {
            "accepted": "hourglass_flowing_sand",
            "running": "hourglass_flowing_sand",
            "done": "",
            "failed": "warning"
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The app needs the `reactions:write` scope. Without it the API answers
`missing_scope`, which is logged once and then disabled for that account.

## Backward compatibility

- Both keys are optional and default to the pre-change behavior. With
  `status_reactions` false (the default), `setTaskReaction` returns before
  building a plan or touching the network, so existing Slack deployments are
  unaffected.
- The new vtable field carries a default (`&defaultSetTaskReaction`), so no
  existing channel implementation has to change.
- Telegram's vtable is untouched and `telegram.TaskReaction` still names the same
  enum, so Telegram behavior and its tests are unchanged.
- No config migration is needed.

## Rollback

The change is one commit. `git revert <sha>` restores the previous behavior;
because both keys are optional and default to off, nothing has to be undone in a
config file.

## Security impact

- The only new outbound requests are `reactions.add` and `reactions.remove` on
  the Slack Web API. Both require `reactions:write` and nothing else; no other
  scope, endpoint, file, or shell surface is added. The scope is only exercised
  when `status_reactions` is explicitly enabled.
- The request body is built with the existing `appendJsonStringW` escaper, so the
  channel id, timestamp, and reaction name are JSON-escaped rather than
  interpolated.
- No secret is logged. The failure path logs the endpoint name, the API error
  code, and the account alias. The bot token is not included.
- The reaction target comes from the inbound message's own channel and timestamp,
  so no new destination is derived from user input. `slackChannelIdOf` drops the
  thread suffix because Slack keys reactions by channel.

## Validation

Required by CONTRIBUTING.md and AGENTS.md for a code change:

```sh
zig build test --summary all   # 0 failures, 0 leaks
zig fmt --check src/           # .githooks/pre-commit
```

`zig build test --summary all` also runs from `.githooks/pre-push`. The pinned
toolchain is Zig 0.16.0 exactly.

No Zig 0.16.0 toolchain was available in the environment where this PR body was
prepared, so those two commands are reported here as the checks that gate the
change rather than as output. No test or format result is claimed that was not
observed; CI results will be added once they are available.

What the branch does cover without a network:

- `src/channels/slack.zig` adds 6 tests: the default transition table including
  the explicit removals, the shared-name case (0 removals on the `running`
  transition), the all-empty no-op case, the target parser, the inert path when
  `status_reactions` is off, and the vtable wiring. `callSlackApi` is stubbed
  under `builtin.is_test`, so none of these tests perform network I/O.
- `src/config.zig` adds 2 tests: defaults when the keys are absent, and an
  explicit config, both with the allocations freed.
- The existing `Channel message operations default to not supported` test in
  `src/channels/root.zig` gains an assertion that `setTaskReaction` returns
  `error.NotSupported` on the default vtable.

Manual check for a reviewer with a Slack app that has `reactions:write`: enable
`status_reactions`, send a message that triggers a turn, and watch the reaction
move through the configured names and disappear when `done` is set to an empty
string. That path is not covered by the automated tests.

## Notes

- Only the message that triggered the turn is reacted to. The agent's own reply is
  not, and no reaction is placed on a parent message.
- Reaction names are passed through to the API as configured. An unknown name
  comes back as an API error code, which `callSlackApi` logs; it does not affect
  the turn and does not disable reactions.
- Telegram still runs its own polling-loop lifecycle. A later change could point
  Telegram's vtable at the shared hook and delete the duplicate, but that is a
  separate concern and is not attempted here.

prs.title: fix(providers): route configured providers by explicit prefix
prs.body:
> Tracking: #1066

# PR title

fix(providers): route configured providers by explicit prefix

# Branch

fix/route-providers-by-prefix

# PR body

## What changed

An explicit `provider/model` model reference previously resolved only for the primary provider and for providers listed in `reliability.fallback_providers`. A provider that is configured under `models.providers` but is not a fallback target was never registered as a routing target, so `/model <provider-alias>/<model-id>` was unusable for it. This PR makes every configured provider reachable by its explicit prefix, without adding it to the failover chain.

Two files:

- `src/providers/reliable.zig`: new `routable` field on `ReliableProvider` (defaults to `&.{}`, so the struct stays backward compatible), a `withRoutable()` builder next to the existing `withExtras()` / `withModelFallbacks()`, and the explicit-prefix matching extracted into a shared `matchExplicitProviders()` helper that is applied to `extras` and to `routable` with the same longest-prefix accounting. The exact-provider-name branch of `resolveProviderTarget()` consults `routable` (lookup order: `extras`, then `routable`, then the primary provider). `deinit()` and `warmup()` now cover the new slice.
- `src/providers/runtime_bundle.zig`: new `collectRoutableProviderNames()` collects every provider configured under `models.providers` except the default provider (already the primary) and providers already covered by `reliability.fallback_providers` (name comparison via `provider_names.providerNamesMatch`, duplicates skipped). The extra-slot arrays are sized as `reliability.fallback_providers.len + rotating_key_count + routable.len`, and the single entry array is split back into two slices at wiring time: `entries[0..failover_entry_count]` goes to `withExtras()`, `entries[failover_entry_count..]` goes to `withRoutable()`. When the inner provider is the provider router, no routable entries are built, since the router already resolves explicit refs against the same provider set.

## Why it changed

Concrete failure, all names placeholders:

1. `models.providers` contains the default provider `<primary-provider>` and a second provider `<provider-alias>` whose `base_url` points at a gateway that serves `<model-id>`.
2. `reliability.fallback_providers` is empty, or lists a different provider. The user runs `/model <provider-alias>/<model-id>`.
3. `RuntimeProviderBundle.init()` registered only `reliability.fallback_providers` (plus rotated keys) as `ReliableProvider` extras, so `<provider-alias>` had no entry anywhere in the wrapper.
4. `resolveProviderTarget()` found no explicit-prefix match, fell through to the bare-model path, stripped the `<provider-alias>/` prefix, and sent `<model-id>` to the primary provider.
5. `<primary-provider>` does not serve `<model-id>` and rejects the request with `Model <model-id> is not allowed`.

The prefix was parsed correctly the whole time. The only defect was that the provider it named was never registered as a routable target, which also explains why the workaround was to add the provider to `reliability.fallback_providers` even when it was not wanted as a failover target.

## Routing and failover stay separate

This is the part worth reviewing closely. `routable` is not a second failover chain:

- `extras` still contains exactly `reliability.fallback_providers` plus rotated keys, in configured order. Nothing was added to it, and `withExtras()` receives the same bounds as before (`entries[0..failover_entry_count]`).
- `routable` entries are consulted only in the explicit-prefix paths: longest-prefix matching against both the configured entry name and the provider runtime name, plus the exact `provider/model` name lookup in `resolveProviderTarget()`. A bare model never consults them.
- A bare model (`<model-id>` with no prefix) therefore keeps its existing behavior: it goes to the primary provider, and on failure it fails over through the configured `fallback_providers` only. A configured-but-not-fallback provider is never used as a failover target.
- The regression test `ReliableProvider keeps failover limited to extras` pins this: the primary fails, the configured fallback serves the request, and the routable-only provider is asserted to have received zero calls.

## Validation

Not run locally: the authoring environment has no Zig 0.16.0 toolchain, so there is no local test output to paste. CI is expected to provide the pass/fail evidence. The checks this branch must pass, per `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `.githooks`:

- `zig build test --summary all` (required for code changes; 0 failures, 0 leaks)
- `zig fmt --check src/` (what `.githooks/pre-commit` runs)
- Optional, as this is not a release-sensitive change: `zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseSmall`

Tests added or updated here (4 new, 1 updated):

- `ReliableProvider routes an explicit prefix to a non-failover provider` (new, `reliable.zig`): the prefixed reference reaches the routable provider, that provider receives the bare model id, and the primary is not called.
- `ReliableProvider keeps failover limited to extras` (new, `reliable.zig`): bare-model failover behavior is unchanged.
- `ReliableProvider resolves supportsStreamingNativeTools through an explicit prefix` (updated, `reliable.zig`): now exercises a routable entry instead of an extra.
- `RuntimeProviderBundle makes non-fallback configured providers routable` (new, `runtime_bundle.zig`): for a config whose second provider is not a fallback target, `extras.len == 0` and `routable.len == 1`.
- `RuntimeProviderBundle keeps fallback providers in the failover chain` (new, `runtime_bundle.zig`): the fallback target stays in `extras` while the other configured provider lands in `routable`.

Each new test carries a comment naming the regression it guards, per `AGENTS.md` 8.1.

## Notes

- No config surface change: no new keys, no changed defaults, no new CLI flags. The only new state is internal (`routable`), derived from the existing `models.providers` and `reliability.fallback_providers`.
- Backward compatible: existing configurations keep identical behavior for bare models and for failover. The only behavior change is that an explicit `provider/model` reference to a configured provider now resolves instead of being stripped and rejected by the primary provider.
- Rollback: `git revert` of the squash commit. No migration, no persisted state, nothing written to disk.
- Docs: this restores behavior that `docs/en/commands.md` already documents (`/model <provider/model>` pins the session to that model). No config key or flag text changes, so no doc edit is strictly required; if maintainers want it explicit, the clarification belongs in that `/model` bullet.
- Ownership: routable entries are appended to the same `reliable_entries` / `extra_holders` arrays the bundle already owns and frees, so deinit stays in one place. The collected name slice borrows from `cfg.providers`, which outlives the bundle, and is freed by `init()` once the entries are built.
- Risk tier: medium per `AGENTS.md` 5 (`src/providers/**` behavior change, no boundary or security impact).
- Linked issue: <ISSUE-URL>

prs.title: feat(slack): stream outbound replies while they are generated
prs.body:
> Tracking: #1066

# feat(slack): stream outbound replies while they are generated

**Branch:** `feat/slack-outbound-streaming`
**Commit subject:** `feat(slack): stream outbound replies while they are generated`
**Commits:** 2. First: 12 files changed, 2044 insertions(+), 14 deletions(-). Second: 4 files changed, 264 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-).
**Risk tier:** high per `AGENTS.md` section 5 (config schema). The behavior itself is opt-in and default-off. The vtable slots implemented here already existed, so no interface changes.

## What changed

Slack was the only streaming-capable channel without an outbound stream sink. `Channel.VTable.sendEvent` with its `.chunk` / `.final` `OutboundStage`, and `supportsStreamingOutbound`, already existed in `src/channels/root.zig`, and Telegram already implemented both, but the Slack vtable registered neither. A Slack reply therefore appeared only once the model had finished, and an operator watching a long turn had no way to tell "still generating" from "stuck".

This change adds a per-account `streaming` key, implements the two vtable hooks on `SlackChannel`, and puts the turn-level state machine in a new transport-free module so it can be tested without HTTP.

### Files changed

| File | Change | +/- |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/channels/slack_stream_presenter.zig` | New. Transport-free logic for one streaming turn: transport selection, target parsing, the coalescing window, the late-chunk grace window, the four request bodies, failure classification, and length splitting. 28 tests. | +767 / -0 |
| `src/channels/slack.zig` | `streaming_enabled`, `native_stream_disabled`, `stream_states` and the mutex that guards them; `sendEvent` / `supportsStreamingOutbound`; the native and fallback transports; `streamFinal` reconciliation; `callSlackApi`; `appendPostMessageBody` takes `thread_ts` explicitly. 17 tests. | +733 / -3 |
| `src/config_types.zig` | `streaming: bool = false` on `SlackConfig`, with a doc comment naming the feature gate and the fallback. | +5 / -0 |
| `src/config.zig` | Four tests: the key defaults to false when absent, parses true when present, and appears in the saved config for both values. | +68 / -0 |
| `docs/en/configuration.md` | New `### Slack` section (the page had none) with the parameter list, `#### Slack streaming replies`, `#### Live reasoning in drafts`, the required Slack app settings, verification commands, and common issues. | +107 / -0 |
| `docs/zh/configuration.md` | The same section in Chinese, kept in sync with the English page. | +83 / -0 |
| `src/daemon.zig` | `channelShowsLiveReasoning`; `makeStreamingSinkForChannel` gains a `stream_reasoning` argument and builds the tag filter with the matching think mode; `processInboundMessage` decides it from the outbound channel and the session. 3 tests. | +59 / -5 |
| `src/streaming.zig` | `ThinkMode` (`strip` / `passthrough`), `TagFilter.initWithThinkMode`, and the `inside_think` filter state that forwards a reasoning body verbatim while still stripping tool-call markup. 5 tests. | +103 / -2 |
| `src/providers/helpers.zig` | `quoteThinkBlocks` renders `<think>` blocks as `>`-quoted lines for live drafts; the delivered reply still goes through `stripThinkBlocks`. 4 tests. | +77 / -0 |
| `src/channels/telegram_draft_presenter.zig` | `snapshotDraftText` uses `quoteThinkBlocks` instead of `stripThinkBlocks`. 2 tests. | +30 / -4 |
| `src/session.zig` | `SessionManager.streamsReasoning(session_key)`, a read-only query used to decide whether a draft may render reasoning. | +11 / -0 |
| `src/providers/root.zig` | Re-export `quoteThinkBlocks`. | +1 / -0 |

Two consequences of wiring that sink are worth calling out:

- The draft-side reasoning plumbing: `ThinkMode` in `src/streaming.zig`, `quoteThinkBlocks` in `src/providers/helpers.zig`, the daemon's channel gate, the `streamsReasoning` query, and the Telegram draft presenter. When a session streams reasoning (`/reasoning stream`) and the outbound channel renders it, the thinking is forwarded to the draft and rendered as a quote above the in-progress answer. The delivered reply is unchanged, because the provider still strips think blocks from the final content and `.off` / `.on` previews stay stripped as before. The Notes section below records two gaps in this half.
- A Slack turn that streamed reasoning rewrites the stopped message in place instead of posting the reply a second time, because that turn's draft contains text the final reply omits.

## Why it changed

The outbound staging the daemon needs already existed; only the channel side was missing. Filling it in for Slack is the smallest change that removes the last channel where a reply is delivered in one lump, and it reuses the interface every other streaming channel already goes through instead of adding a Slack-specific path in the agent loop.

Slack's own constraints are why one transport is not enough, and why the implementation carries an account-level degradation flag rather than a single happy path:

- `chat.startStream` is only accepted inside a thread, so a top-level reply can never use the native methods.
- The native methods are gated behind the app's Agents & AI Apps feature, which requires a paid plan, and behind the assistant scope Slack adds when an app is declared as an agent. An app without them cannot stream at all.
- The streaming methods are tiered per minute, so a naive implementation that forwards every model token as one API call would hit the rate limit and break replies that used to work.

## The two outbound paths

`vtableSendEvent` receives `.chunk` events while the model generates and one `.final` event with the authoritative reply. The transport is chosen once per turn and stored on the turn's `StreamState`:

| Reply target | Transport |
| --- | --- |
| Threaded target: `reply_to_mode = all`, an inbound thread reply, or an assistant thread | `chat.startStream` with the first snapshot, throttled `chat.appendStream` deltas, then `chat.stopStream` |
| Top-level target | `chat.postMessage` with the first snapshot, then throttled `chat.update` edits of that same message |
| Any target, once the account has hit a permanent native error | `chat.postMessage` plus `chat.update` |
| Any target, when a native call fails mid-turn | The turn stays on the native transport so the stream can still be closed with `chat.stopStream`; live updates stop and the final reply reconciles the message |

**Native path.** The first flush splits at the `markdown_text` cap and sends it through `chat.startStream`, which returns the streaming message `ts`. Later flushes send only the unsent suffix through `chat.appendStream`, computed from the last snapshot handed to the transport. On `.final`, `pendingFinalSuffix` checks whether the streamed snapshot is a prefix of the final reply. When it is, the remainder is appended and `chat.stopStream` closes the message, so the user sees one message and no duplicate. When it is not, the stream is closed and the reply is delivered separately, because the streamed message holds an intermediate prefix the model later abandoned (text emitted before a tool call, or a reply rewritten by redaction rehydration after the last delta). The one exception is a turn that rendered reasoning: that snapshot can never be a prefix of the final reply, so the stopped message is rewritten in place with `chat.update` instead of leaving the thinking behind and posting the reply a second time.

**Fallback path.** One `chat.postMessage` carries the first snapshot and returns its `ts`; every later flush edits that message with `chat.update`. On `.final`, the reply is split at the `chat.update` cap, the first slice replaces the message, and up to eight overflow slices are posted as follow-ups in the same thread with a warning logged if more are dropped.

`chat.stopStream` is sent with the channel and `ts` only. The content was already delivered through start and append, so passing `markdown_text` there would append it twice.

## Throttling

Slack's streaming Web API methods are tiered per minute, so a token stream must be coalesced before it becomes HTTP calls. The tier table is recorded next to the constants: `chat.startStream` and `chat.stopStream` at Tier 2 (20+ per minute), `chat.appendStream` at Tier 4 (100+ per minute), `chat.update` at Tier 3 (50+ per minute), and `chat.postMessage` at roughly one message per second per channel.

`appendStreamChunk` accumulates deltas in the turn buffer and emits a flush when either condition holds:

- the unsent buffer has reached `STREAM_FLUSH_MIN_DELTA_BYTES` (128 bytes), or
- `STREAM_FLUSH_MIN_INTERVAL_MS` (one second) has elapsed since the previous flush.

For a normal token stream every delta is far below 128 bytes, so the interval is the pace that applies and a turn costs about one API call per second, which keeps `chat.appendStream` and `chat.update` inside their tiers. The byte threshold exists so a burst that arrives between two ticks is not held back for the rest of the second. The window opens on the first delta rather than on the first flush, so a short reply that completes inside one second never opens a stream at all and never pays the Tier 2 start/stop pair. Whitespace-only snapshots are not sent.

Two further guards keep the call count bounded in a long-running bot. A finalized target keeps ignoring `.chunk` events for `STREAM_LATE_CHUNK_GRACE_MS` (five seconds), because the daemon publishes the final reply on the durable outbox worker while the outbound dispatcher may still be draining deltas of the same turn; without it those leftovers would open a second stream for a turn that already ended. Above `STREAM_MAX_TRACKED_TARGETS` (64) tracked targets, the channel sweeps finalized entries that are past the grace window, so a bot does not accumulate one entry per thread it has ever answered in.

`stream_mu` covers both the state map and the API calls made from it, since chunks arrive on the outbound dispatcher thread while the final reply may arrive on the outbox worker.

## Permanent errors degrade the account

`classifyStreamFailure` maps the Slack `error` string to a retry policy:

- **Permanent** (`disable_native`): `channel_type_not_supported`, `method_not_supported_for_channel_type`, `unknown_method`, `not_allowed`, `invalid_thread_ts`, `restricted_action_thread_only_channel`, `restricted_action_non_threadable_channel`, `restricted_action_thread_locked`, `missing_scope`, `not_allowed_token_type`, `no_permission`, `restricted_action`, `invalid_arguments`, `missing_recipient_user_id`, `missing_recipient_team_id`. These mean this app, workspace, or channel can never stream natively, so the account sets `native_stream_disabled` once and every later turn selects the fallback transport directly through `chooseTurnTransport`. The warning is logged once per account, not once per turn.
- **Transient** (everything else, including `ratelimited`, `internal_error`, `service_unavailable`, and `message_not_in_streaming_state`): the current turn abandons the native path and the API is retried on a later turn. Unknown codes are treated as transient, so a Slack error that did not exist when this was written can never permanently disable streaming for an account.

A rejection of the start call switches the current turn to the fallback transport. A failure of a later append or update sets `send_failed` for that turn, which stops live updates and leaves the final reply to reconcile the message. If the first `chat.postMessage` of a fallback turn fails, the same flag applies and the reply is sent complete through the existing `vtableSend` path. In every failure case the user still receives the reply; the only difference is whether it arrives progressively.

## Configuration

New key, `channels.slack.accounts.<alias>.streaming`, default `false`:

```json
{
  "channels": {
    "slack": {
      "accounts": {
        "<alias>": {
          "bot_token": "YOUR_BOT_TOKEN",
          "app_token": "YOUR_APP_TOKEN",
          "reply_to_mode": "all",
          "streaming": true
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The key is documented in `docs/en/configuration.md` and in `docs/zh/configuration.md`. Both pages state the app-side requirements for the native path: enable **Agents & AI Apps** under *Features* (the gate for `chat.startStream`, and a paid-plan feature), keep `chat:write` for outbound replies and `assistant:write` for the assistant scope, reinstall the app after changing scopes, and set `reply_to_mode` to `all` if replies in channels should stream, since Slack only streams inside a thread.

## Backward compatibility

- The key defaults to `false`. A configuration that does not mention it parses to `false`, and the saved configuration writes the effective value.
- With streaming off, `supportsStreamingOutbound` returns `false`, so the daemon never routes Slack through the outbound staging, and `sendEvent` forwards `.final` to the existing `vtableSend` while ignoring `.chunk`. Delivery is byte-for-byte what it is today.
- `appendPostMessageBody` now takes `thread_ts` as an argument instead of reading the mutable `self.thread_ts` field that `parseTarget` rewrites. The existing call site passes the same value the function read before, so the payload is unchanged.
- No state is persisted. Stream state lives in the channel instance, is released per turn by `finishTurn`, and is freed on `stop`.
- No new command, flag, or migration, and no change to the config file layout.

## Rollback

Set `streaming` to `false` (or remove the key) and restart the channel; replies go back to being delivered complete. `git revert <this-commit-sha>` also works, and no data migration or cleanup is needed because nothing is persisted.

## Security

- No new credentials. The streaming methods authenticate with the bot token the account already has, through the existing `Authorization: Bearer` header built in a fixed stack buffer.
- No new scope is required for the fallback path: `chat.postMessage` and `chat.update` are covered by `chat:write`, which outbound replies already need. The native methods are the same scope but are additionally gated on the app's Agents & AI Apps feature and the assistant scope, as both doc pages state. Enabling `streaming` without that entitlement cannot break replies, because the first `chat.startStream` is rejected and the account degrades to edited messages.
- No new endpoints. Requests go through the existing `root.http_util.curlPost` to the existing Slack Web API base over HTTPS.
- No new inbound surface. The change adds no webhook, listener, or event parser.
- No new file, filesystem, or subprocess access.
- No secrets in logs. Failure paths log the Slack error code, the endpoint name, and the Zig error name only; message bodies and tokens are not logged. The token never leaves the auth header.
- Under `builtin.is_test`, `sendMessage` returns before building a request and `callSlackApi` returns a canned `ts`, so the suite opens no sockets. Both guards carry a comment, per the `builtin.is_test` side-effect rule in `AGENTS.md` section 3.4.
- Tests and docs use synthetic values (`xoxb-test`, `xoxb-YOUR_BOT_TOKEN`, and example channel and user ids), not real credentials or workspace identifiers.

## Validation

Required checks for a code change, both run in CI on the pinned Zig 0.16.0 toolchain:

- `zig build test --summary all` (the `pre-push` hook in `.githooks`; must report 0 failures and 0 leaks)
- `zig fmt --check src/` (the `pre-commit` hook in `.githooks`)

No Zig toolchain was available in the environment where this description was written, so neither command was run here and no pass counts are claimed. Both must be confirmed by CI before merge. The commit message records an author-side container run; that result is not reproduced here.

Test coverage added by this change (63 test blocks):

| File | Tests | What they exercise |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/channels/slack_stream_presenter.zig` | 28 | Transport selection across the four target/state combinations; target parsing for a threaded, bare, empty-thread, and DM-style target; the coalescing window (buffered inside it, interval flush, byte-threshold flush, unsent-suffix delta); the late-chunk grace window and the fresh turn after it; prefix versus divergent finals; all four request bodies including JSON escaping and the stop body carrying no text; permanent versus transient classification; length splitting at newline boundaries and without cutting a multibyte character |
| `src/channels/slack.zig` | 17 | The vtable hooks and the full state machine, driven with `callSlackApi` stubbed: native start for a thread target, native kept across chunks, fallback for a top-level target, fallback after the account is degraded, prefix final, divergent final, in-place rewrite after streamed reasoning, late deltas dropped, streaming disabled, empty chunk, short reply inside the window, overflow splitting, and `stop` releasing buffers |
| `src/streaming.zig` | 5 | Strips think blocks by default, forwards them in passthrough mode, survives a tag split across chunks, keeps angle brackets inside reasoning, and still strips tool-call markup in passthrough mode |
| `src/providers/helpers.zig` | 4 | Quote rendering that keeps the answer, plain text untouched, an unterminated block, and a stray close tag |
| `src/config.zig` | 4 | The key defaults to false when absent, parses true when present, and appears in the saved configuration for both values |
| `src/daemon.zig` | 3 | The sink keeps reasoning only when the session streams it, strips it by default, and the channel gate enables only Telegram and Slack |
| `src/channels/telegram_draft_presenter.zig` | 2 | Streamed reasoning renders as a quote, and a draft without reasoning is unchanged |

The new Slack section in both doc pages also carries manual verification steps (`nullclaw channel start slack`, `nullclaw channel status`). Those require a live Slack app and were not run in the environment where this description was written.

## Notes

- Two commits. The first adds the Slack outbound stream and the shared draft-side plumbing for streamed reasoning, which belong together because both are served by the one outbound sink this PR adds: the same `.chunk` events feed the Slack stream and the draft renderers. The second fixes that plumbing on the channels with their own message loop and is a hard dependency of the first. Happy to narrow the scope however maintainers prefer.
- The second commit fixes the channels that are served by their own message loop. Telegram is served by `channel_loop.processTelegramMessage` rather than `daemon.processInboundMessage`, so the passthrough selection the daemon performs never ran for it and its drafts were always stripped; the draft think mode is now resolved from the outbound channel and the session, the same way the daemon already does it. That commit also teaches `TagFilter` the provider's text tool markup, which otherwise reaches drafts and delivered replies verbatim. It is in this branch rather than a PR of its own because it cannot compile without the first commit: the `ThinkMode` and `initWithThinkMode` symbols it consumes, and the daemon-side channel gate, are introduced here.
- Reasoning in a draft is presentation-only. The finalized message is still produced by `stripThinkBlocks`, so thinking never reaches a delivered reply in any mode.
- The native path needs the app's Agents & AI Apps feature, which requires a paid plan. On a workspace without it, `streaming = true` is harmless: the first start call is rejected, the warning is logged once per account, and replies use edited messages.
- Behavior worth knowing when reviewing the native path: a final reply that diverges from the streamed text is posted as its own message, so that turn produces two messages. This is deliberate, because the streamed message holds an intermediate prefix that the model abandoned, and the reply has to be complete. The one exception is a turn that rendered reasoning, which is rewritten in place.

issues.body:
# Daily ironclaw failure taxonomy — 2026-10-15

## Suites analyzed
- [officeqa (50 non-pass)](https://nearai.github.io/benchmarks/#/runs/ironclaw/officeqa/417ae5e9-500f-43f5-8a6b-91f739687305) — This run's 50 non-pass tasks are overwhelmingly genuine model-quality errors: DeepSeek-V4-Flash navigates the OCR-digitized Treasury Bulletins with healthy, self-recovering trajectories (read/grep/shell/result_read all succeed) but reads the wrong cell, picks the wrong year/row, or applies the wrong formula, so the final number falls outside the ±1% tolerance while nothing in ironclaw fails. The prior run's numeric-extraction category recurs and dominates. Every 'Hard' capability signature is incidental to a model-error trajectory — most are the model reaching out to live external APIs (BLS, FRED, api.stlouisfed.org) on a document-grounded benchmark, which variously succeed (UID0037), transiently fail (UID0122/UID0174 Network), or are denied (UID0089). The one genuine, confirmed-live harness defect recurs from the prior run: a network-egress POLICY denial is minted as the generic RuntimeHttpEgressError::Request and classified InputEncode ('fix your arguments and retry') instead of NetworkDenied/PolicyDenied ('refused, pivot'), which can misdirect model recovery but changed no verdict here since the model pivoted to the document anyway. Two tasks produced no usable answer at all (UID0028 empty, UID0029 a no-progress give-up after 81 self-inflicted script errors).

_ironclaw rev(s): b0b999d96781516ee05e6ba961d6f3ead900da96_

## 🔧 Harness fix candidates (ranked by blast radius)

| # | Category | Tasks | Suites | Confidence | Files |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | HTTP egress policy-denial misclassified as InputEncode | 2 | officeqa:2 | 0.70 | `crates/contracts/ironclaw_host_api/src/http.rs:551, crates/kernel/ironclaw_host_runtime/src/egress/host_port.rs:196, crates/kernel/ironclaw_host_runtime/src/first_party_tools/http.rs:492` |

### 1. HTTP egress policy-denial misclassified as InputEncode — 2 tasks
**Root cause:** The egress error taxonomy conflates two distinct failures under RuntimeHttpEgressError::Request → RuntimeHttpEgressReasonCode::RequestDenied → RuntimeDispatchErrorKind::InputEncode. One is genuine request malformation (sensitive_header_denied, manual_credentials_denied, body-over-limit — where InputEncode is correct); the other is a host network-egress POLICY denial, minted at crates/kernel/ironclaw_host_runtime/src/egress/host_port.rs:196 (map_err → RuntimeHttpEgressError::Request { reason: 'host network egress policy was not authorized: …' }), whose own unit test asserts stable_runtime_reason()=='request_denied'. A policy denial routed through this path never reaches the PolicyDenied reason-code arm (which only fires for Network { reason == "policy_denied" }, http.rs:557), so it is classified InputEncode and projected to CorrectArgumentsBeforeRetry (result_meta.rs:371) instead of ReviseApproach. The correct behavior is for an egress policy denial to classify as NetworkDenied/PolicyDenied (non-retryable, ReviseApproach).

**Fix:** Distinguish an egress policy denial from a malformed request so it no longer collapses to InputEncode. Minimal option: at host_port.rs:196 mint the denial through the existing policy-denied convention (RuntimeHttpEgressError::Network { reason: "policy_denied", .. }) so reason_code() returns PolicyDenied (http.rs in host_api) and http.rs:493 maps it to RuntimeDispatchErrorKind::PolicyDenied → ReviseApproach. Cleaner option: add a dedicated RuntimeHttpEgressError::PolicyDenied variant + RuntimeHttpEgressReasonCode::RequestPolicyDenied and map it to PolicyDenied/NetworkDenied at http.rs:492-493, reserving RequestDenied→InputEncode strictly for the sanitize.rs/credential.rs request-malformation cases. Update the host_port.rs policy-denial test to assert the policy-denied reason code, and add a first_party_tools regression test asserting a denied builtin.http dispatch surfaces PolicyDenied/ReviseApproach, not InputEncode.

_Files:_ `crates/contracts/ironclaw_host_api/src/http.rs:551`, `crates/kernel/ironclaw_host_runtime/src/egress/host_port.rs:196`, `crates/kernel/ironclaw_host_runtime/src/first_party_tools/http.rs:492`

prs.title: fix(skills): remove retired film and music search skills
prs.body:
## Summary
Remove `films-search` and `music-search` from the bundled skills. On startup after an app upgrade, remove their existing user-data copies, saved defaults, enabled state, and interrupted-upgrade backups so they cannot be restored by upgrade recovery.

## Related Issue
N/A

## Changes Made
- Remove both bundled definitions, default entries, and bundled display names.
- Clean up retired skills before bundled sync, including when bundled resources are missing; preserve unrelated skills and preferences.
- Skip retired skills in stale bundled directories and retry failed cleanup on later startups.
- Add six regression tests covering bundle contents, fresh installs, upgrades, repeated startup, legacy state, interrupted upgrades, malformed config, and cleanup retries.

## Type of Change
- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Other: remove two built-in skills

## Testing
- [x] Tested locally: 127 tests passed across bundled sync, skill manager, listing, installation, and localized skill names.
- [x] Added new tests
- [x] Changed-file ESLint passed with zero warnings.
- [x] `npm run compile:electron`
- [x] `git diff --check`
- [ ] Manual testing performed

## Screenshots
N/A: removes bundled skill entries without changing UI layout.

## Checklist
- [x] Follows project style guidelines
- [x] Self-reviewed the diff
- [x] Commented the upgrade cleanup and recovery behavior
- [x] Added regression coverage; relevant existing tests pass
- [x] No new lint warnings
- Documentation changes are not needed.

## Electron-Specific Changes
- [x] Main process: skill bootstrap deletes the two retired skill directories and `.upgrading` backups under `userData/SKILLs`, removes their defaults from `skills.config.json`, and clears their entries in SQLite-backed `skills_state`.
- No preload, IPC, or window-management changes.

## Additional Notes
Real packaged cross-version upgrade testing has not been performed. File-system migration behavior is covered using isolated temporary directories; Electron compilation passed.

prs.title: feat(mcp): add Lynxce Omni AI as a one-click MCP OAuth entry and bundled skill
prs.body:
## Summary

This PR adds **Lynxce Omni AI** (灵策全能AI) to the MCP marketplace as a one-click entry. It also lets local registry entries declare MCP OAuth in a generic way, so future OAuth entries need no extra code.

> **Depends on #2874** (remote MCP OAuth sign-in), and this branch is stacked on it. Until #2874 is merged the diff also shows its commits. The changes for this PR are the last two commits, `ec9c7b86` and `0017bce7`.

**Disclosure:** I work on Lynxce. The service is commercial: usage is billed to the signed-in user's Lynxce account credits. It is kept in a separate PR so #2874 can be reviewed on its own.

## Related Issue

None.

## Changes Made

- **Generic OAuth registry entries** (`types/mcp.ts`, `mcpRegistryPresentation.ts`)
  - `McpRegistryEntry` gets `auth?: 'oauth'`. For remote entries, `command` holds the URL, the same convention the Qichacha entry uses.
  - `mergeMarketplaceRegistry` keeps such entries as app-managed local entries, the same way it keeps `oauthProvider` entries. The server-provided marketplace list stays the single source for everything else.
- **One-click connect** (`McpManager.tsx`)
  - An OAuth entry has nothing to fill in, so **Connect** adds the remote server straight away.
  - The server is saved under the entry id, which keeps the OpenClaw server key ASCII and stable.
  - It is saved with `auth: 'oauth'` and `registryId`, and then the browser sign-in from #2874 starts.
  - While waiting for the browser, the button reads *Waiting for browser…*.
  - The marketplace card and the detail dialog share one label helper.
- **Entry** (`data/mcpRegistry.ts`)
  - Lynxce Omni AI, `https://web.lynxce.cn/api/mcp`, Streamable HTTP, in the Design category, at marketplace position 5 (Qichacha stays at 4).
  - A bundled SVG icon.
  - zh/en description.

- **Bundled skill** (`SKILLs/lynxce-omni/`, commit `0017bce7`)
  - A `lynxce-omni` skill that teaches the agent how to use the server's `lynxce_*` tools:
    - check the balance before videos or batches
    - pick the aspect ratio by use
    - map requests to edit-image operations
    - poll long video and music tasks instead of spinning
    - handle sign-in, credit and moderation errors honestly, never inventing result URLs
  - Registered in `skills.config.json` **disabled by default** and given a display name in `bundledSkillNames.ts`.
  - Registry entries get an optional `skillId`. Connecting the entry turns that skill on, so users who never connect Lynxce never load it.

## Expert kit (not in this PR)

The kit store is delivered by your kit-store config, so a kit cannot be added through the repo. We have prepared a ready-to-list **Lynxce Omni AI Studio** kit in the same format as the current catalog:

- 5 skills: poster and product images, photo retouching, short videos, songwriting, and Douyin script breakdown
- zip bundle
- 512px icon

If you're open to listing it, I can send the files, or host them wherever you prefer.

- text-to-image and image editing: upscaling, background replacement, cut-out, old photo restoration, in-image text translation
- text- and image-to-video

- extracting the voice-over script from a Douyin share link

The server implements the MCP authorization spec:

- protected-resource and authorization-server metadata

prs.title: feat(mcp): sign in to remote MCP servers with OAuth
prs.body:
## Summary

Remote MCP servers (Streamable HTTP / SSE) can now sign in with MCP OAuth 2.1, so users no longer have to create an API key in the provider's dashboard and paste it into a header.

OpenClaw v2026.8.1 already implements the whole flow: discovery, dynamic client registration, PKCE, the loopback callback on `127.0.0.1:8989`, token storage and refresh. This PR only:

1. writes `auth: "oauth"` into `openclaw.json`, and
2. drives `openclaw mcp login | logout | status` from the MCP page.

The gateway reads the stored token on every request, so signing in takes effect **without a gateway restart**.

## Related Issue

None.

## Changes Made

- **Config** (`src/shared/mcp/auth.ts`, `mcpStore.ts`)
  - New optional `auth?: 'oauth'` on remote servers.
  - Only `'oauth'` is persisted, and stdio servers never carry it, so existing data is unchanged.
- **openclaw.json and gateway sync** (`openclawConfigSync.ts`, `mcpRuntime.ts`)
  - OAuth servers get `auth: "oauth"`.
  - The `authorization` header is dropped, because OpenClaw ignores it on OAuth servers and logs a warning. Other headers are kept.
- **CLI driver** (`src/main/mcp/mcpOAuthCli.ts`, new)
  - Runs the OpenClaw CLI the same way the gateway is started: Electron with `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1`, the same state dir and config path, plus the secret env vars referenced as `${VAR}` in `openclaw.json`.
  - `login` streams stdout and opens the printed authorization URL once with `shell.openExternal`. Only a bare http(s) line counts as a URL.
  - If OpenClaw cannot bind the loopback port, it still exits 0 but saves no token. The driver detects this and returns `callback_unavailable` **before** opening the browser, so the user is not sent to a dead redirect.
  - Success requires "credentials saved" in stdout.
  - Only one sign-in can run per server at a time.
  - `status --json` is parsed defensively, tolerating log lines around the JSON.
- **IPC**
  - New channels `mcp:oauthLogin`, `mcp:oauthLogout` and `mcp:oauthStatus`.
  - Login syncs `openclaw.json` first, so the CLI sees the server that was just saved.
  - Server keys reuse `safeServerKey()` from the config sync.
- **UI**
  - The server form has a new **Authentication** choice: *None / headers* or *OAuth sign-in*.
  - Tool preview is skipped for OAuth servers, since they answer 401 until signed in.
  - Server cards show a *Signed in* or *Sign-in required* badge, a **Sign in** button (shown as *Waiting for browser…* while in progress), and a **Sign out** menu item.
  - `mcp status` runs only when at least one server uses OAuth.
- **Docs and i18n**
  - zh/en strings.
  - Design doc in `specs/features/mcp-remote-oauth/`.

## Type of Change

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Code refactoring
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Performance improvement
- [ ] Other (please describe):

## Testing

- [x] Tested locally
- [x] Added new tests
- [x] Updated existing tests
- [ ] Manual testing performed (in the Electron app; see notes below for what was run against the real OpenClaw CLI)

Commands run:

- `tsc` for the renderer and electron configs: clean.
- `npm run compile:electron`: clean.
- `eslint --max-warnings 0` on all changed files: clean.
- `vitest` for `src/main/mcp`, `src/main/ipcHandlers`, `openclawConfigSync.runtime.test.ts`, `src/renderer/components/mcp` and `src/renderer/services`: 903 passed, 5 skipped (the skips are baseline).

New tests:

- `mcpStore` round-trips `auth`.
- `openclawConfigSync` writes `auth: "oauth"` and drops the `authorization` header.
- `mcpOAuthCli` (9 tests, fake child process), covering:
  - URL extraction, including rejecting `file:` and `javascript:` URLs
  - status parsing
  - successful sign-in
  - still-valid stored credentials
  - busy callback port
  - non-zero exit
  - concurrent sign-in
  - missing runtime

Real CLI check: I ran the compiled `mcpOAuthCli` against an **OpenClaw 2026.8.1 runtime** with an isolated state dir and a production MCP server that implements MCP OAuth (discovery + DCR + PKCE).

- `mcp status --json` was parsed as `unauthenticated` before sign-in and `pending-authorization` after the authorize page opened.
- `login` completed discovery and dynamic registration. The authorization URL was extracted and "opened" exactly once (`…/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=…&code_challenge_method=S256&redirect_uri=http://127.0.0.1:8989/oauth/callback&…`). The run then hit the expected timeout because I did not finish the browser step.
- With another process listening on `127.0.0.1:8989`, `login` returned `callback_unavailable` in about 1s and opened nothing.

## Screenshots (if applicable)

Not included. I did not run the full Electron app for this PR.

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the project's style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my code
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

## Electron-Specific Changes

- [x] Changes to main process (src/main/)
- [x] Changes to preload script (src/main/preload.ts)
- [x] Changes to IPC communication
- [ ] Changes to window management
- [ ] None

## Additional Notes

- **Why the CLI and not the gateway RPC:** OpenClaw exposes MCP OAuth only through `openclaw mcp login|logout|status`. The login command prints the URL instead of opening a browser, which lets the app keep control of `shell.openExternal` and validate the URL first.
- **First turn after sign-in:** if the gateway already tried the server and got a 401, OpenClaw retries the tool catalog about 5 seconds later. A message sent right after signing in may still miss that server's tools. Later turns have them.
- **Token identity:** OpenClaw keys stored credentials by server name + URL. Renaming a server or changing its URL therefore requires signing in again, which seems like the right behavior.
- **Out of scope:**
  - The existing Qichacha integration (`oauthProvider: 'qichacha'`) is untouched.
  - Marketplace entries cannot declare `auth: 'oauth'` yet. That could build on this PR separately.

prs.title: feat(cowork): 增加临时会话功能，提高隐私
prs.body:
## 功能描述

新增「临时会话」功能——在侧边栏「新建任务」按钮右侧增加一个 ⚡ 按钮，点击后打开一次性轻量聊天会话。

**特性：**
- 临时会话不出现在侧边栏任务记录中
- 切换到其他任务时自动消失
- 不允许收藏（pin）
- 不加载历史上下文
- 聊天结束后不存档，随用随清
- 支持中英文双语（hint 文案：「临时会话，轻量聊天，随用随清，让对话随风而去」）

## 问题与修复

**问题1：** 临时会话在应用重启后仍出现在侧边栏任务记录中。

**修复：** 在 `cowork_sessions` 表新增 `is_temp` 字段，临时会话创建时标记为 `is_temp=1`，应用每次启动时自动清除所有残留的临时会话记录。

**问题2：** 临时会话在正常使用过程中偶发出现在任务列表中（竞态问题）。

issues.title: [Feature]: web_search built-in tavily provider has no API-key config surface — paid quota unusable (内置 tavily provider 无法配置自有 API key)

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

issues.body:
## Summary

The built-in `web_search` tool's tavily provider always uses keyless anonymous REST (request header `X-Tavily-Access-Mode: keyless`), and **there is no configuration surface to supply a user's own Tavily API key**. Users with a paid Tavily subscription can neither consume their own quota nor avoid the anonymous channel's rate limits.

中文：内置 `web_search` 的 tavily provider 固定走 keyless 匿名 REST（请求头 `X-Tavily-Access-Mode: keyless`），没有任何配置入口填入用户自己的 Tavily API key。持有订阅的用户既无法消耗自有额度，还随时受匿名通道限流。理解 keyless 是"开箱即用"的产品决策，本单无意要求改变默认；诉求只是**给有 key 的用户一扇门**。

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (agents/tools — `websearch` providers & factory)
- [x] Console (frontend web UI — provider dropdown has no key field)
- [ ] Channels
- [ ] Skills
- [x] CLI (`qwenpaw` config surfaces for `web_search.config`)

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.2.1
- **OS:** macOS 15 (arm64), Python 3.12, pip install
- Tavily account: Researcher plan (1000 credits/month)

## Problem Details / Reproduction

1. Inspect outbound requests from `web_search`: every call carries `X-Tavily-Access-Mode: keyless`; the account's own quota consumption stays at zero.
2. Look for a place to configure a key: `web_search.config` schema exposes only the provider choice (`tavily` / `anysearch`); the Console dropdown likewise. Neither has an `api_key`/credential field anywhere.
3. Result: a user holding a valid Tavily key has no supported way to make the built-in provider use it.
4. Keyless is not a theoretical risk: our logs contain a real **HTTP 432** (quota-class error) failure from the anonymous path.

This is a feature gap rather than a crash — the symptom is "I have a key but nowhere to put it", with no warning anywhere. It belongs to the same natural evolution as #8139 and #7711 (adding new web_search providers).

## Current Workaround & Its Cost

We patched venv site-packages directly (with the operator's explicit authorization): added an authed provider that reads the key reference from QwenPaw's **existing credential store**, POSTs to `api.tavily.com/search` authenticated, and on any 432/429/401/network error **automatically falls back to keyless** — plus wiring changes in `factory.py` default and the Console dropdown options. End-to-end verified: authed path genuinely used; fallback path PASS.

Costs we are paying, which upstream fixes would eliminate:

1. `qwenpaw update` overwrites the patch — explicit technical debt we must re-apply after every upgrade.
2. During rollout we hit a related papercut: AgentConfigWatcher hot-reloads JSON configs only; Python code changes do not take effect, and the running process kept reporting `Unknown web_search provider` with **no hint that a restart was required**.

## Suggested Implementation

1. Add an `api_key_ref` field to `web_search.config` pointing into the framework's existing credential store (we verified tool-layer code can read it; implementation cost is low and it avoids plaintext keys in `agent.json`); expose a key input in the Console form accordingly.
2. Implement **authed→keyless automatic fallback** officially: degrade with a log line when quota is exhausted/rate-limited. This is the most valuable part of our hand-rolled solution and we suggest adopting it as-is.
3. (Bonus) At startup or config change, if tool-layer module mtime is newer than process start time, emit `WARN: restart required` — prevents the "changed it but nothing happened and nobody knows why" class of confusion.

Severity: **feature-gap level**. All implementation details from our prototype are available on request. Thanks!

---

### 中文版全文

**问题**：内置 tavily provider 无 API key 配置入口，付费额度用不上，只能吃匿名通道的限流与低质量结果（日志有真实 HTTP 432 记录）。**复现**：任何位置尝试配置 key → 无处可填 → 出站请求仍为 keyless。**临时解决及代价**：直改 site-packages 实现 authed + keyless 自动回退（已端到端验证），但升级即被覆盖，属技术债；且暴露"改代码不重启不生效、框架无任何提示"的关联问题。**建议**：① `web_search.config.api_key_ref` 指向既有 credentials 库 + Console 表单露出密钥输入；② 官方吸收 authed→keyless 自动降级；③ 工具层模块 mtime 晚于进程启动时打 WARN "restart required"。原型实现细节可提供，欢迎评论区索取。谢谢！

issues.title: [Bug]: Windows压缩包在Qwenpaw乱码 。

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
根因分析
问题出在 QwenPaw 解压 ZIP 的核心代码。关键入口有两个：

Skill ZIP 导入（store.py 第 754-775 行）：
python

def _extract_and_validate_zip(data: bytes, tmp_dir: Path) -> None:
with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(data)) as zf: # ← 没传 encoding 参数
...
zf.extractall(tmp_dir)
2. Hub 下载（hub.py 第 1753、1699 行）同理，ZipFile(...) 都没传 encoding。

为什么 Windows 压缩的中文文件名会乱码
ZIP 规范规定文件名编码有两种方式：

不设 UTF-8 标志位 → 文件名用 CP437（原始 ZIP 规范）
设 UTF-8 标志位（bit 11） → 文件名用 UTF-8
问题在于：Windows 中文系统上很多压缩工具（尤其是系统自带的"发送到→压缩文件夹"）不会设置 UTF-8 bit，而是用 GBK/CP936 编码文件名。当这个 ZIP 上传到 Linux 服务器上，Python zipfile 模块默认按 CP437 解码文件名，GBK 的中文就变成乱码了。

好消息：文件内容不受影响
QwenPaw 已经为文件内容做了编码兼容——_FRONTMATTER_ENCODINGS 和 decode_text_bytes_with_encoding_fallback 里都包含了 gbk / cp936 的回退。所以即使 ZIP 文件名乱码，解压后 SKILL.md 的正文大概率能正确读取。但如果技能目录名本身是中文，路径会出问题。

规避方案
避免用 Windows 资源管理器自带压缩。改用 7-Zip、Bandizip 等——它们在创建 ZIP 时会设置 UTF-8 标志位。
用 QwenPaw 工作区里的 Python zipfile 打包（AGENTS.md 里也写了这条建议），Python 3 的 zipfile 默认写 UTF-8 标志。
技能市场 / Hub 下载不受影响——服务端返回的都是 UTF-8 编码的 ZIP。

问题在于：Windows 中文系统上很多压缩工具（尤其是系统自带的"发送到→压缩文件夹"）不会设置 UTF-8 bit，而是用 GBK/CP936 编码文件名。当这个 ZIP 上传到 Linux 服务器上，Python zipfile 模块默认按 CP437 解码文件名，GBK 的中文就变成乱码了。

好消息：文件内容不受影响
QwenPaw 已经为文件内容做了编码兼容——_FRONTMATTER_ENCODINGS 和 decode_text_bytes_with_encoding_fallback 里都包含了 gbk / cp936 的回退。所以即使 ZIP 文件名乱码，解压后 SKILL.md 的正文大概率能正确读取。但如果技能目录名本身是中文，路径会出问题。

规避方案
避免用 Windows 资源管理器自带压缩。改用 7-Zip、Bandizip 等——它们在创建 ZIP 时会设置 UTF-8 标志位。
用 QwenPaw 工作区里的 Python zipfile 打包（AGENTS.md 里也写了这条建议），Python 3 的 zipfile 默认写 UTF-8 标志。
技能市场 / Hub 下载不受影响——服务端返回的都是 UTF-8 编码的 ZIP。

issues.title: [Bug][Console] Message-navigation directory cannot locate accurately: positions are apportioned by item count, only the active anchor is measured

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.2.2b4 (QwenPaw Desktop, Windows 10 AMD64) - tested against the 2.2.2-beta.5 desktop bundle

## Description

Related to #8186 (message-navigation jump overrides manual wheel scrolling). PR #8214 fixed the "user cannot interrupt the auto-positioning" half, but the navigation directory itself still cannot locate accurately - and the two share the same cached state, so this looks like the other half of one mechanism.

### Repro (long session, 40+ messages)

1. Open a long conversation and open the **"导航 (N)" / "Navigation (N)"** panel on the right (`messageAnchors.title`).
2. Click any entry, or click the "scroll directory to active user message" button in the panel header.
3. Expected: the transcript scrolls to that user message, and the active item is scrolled into view inside the panel.
4. Actual: the jump lands at a **wrong position**, and/or the locate button appears **disabled / does nothing**. The mismatch grows with session length.

After using the panel once, a subsequent wheel gesture keeps snapping the transcript back to the list head - the same symptom as #8186. Without touching the panel, plain wheel scrolling is unaffected, so the trigger is the navigation action itself.

## Code evidence

From the installed console bundle `console/assets/chat-vendor-*.js` (2.2.2-beta.5 build):

**1. Anchor vertical positions are apportioned by item count, not by real height**

```js
// orderPercent = (index + 0.5) / total * 100
// when a real rect is unavailable, the estimate is used as-is as a coordinate:
var Ze = V.get(xe.id); if (!Ze) return Se[xe.id] = xe.orderPercent, Se;
```

One long answer and one short "ok" are treated as equal height, so the directory's coordinate system does not match the transcript's real scroll geometry.

**2. Only the active anchor gets a real element ref**

```js
ref: C ? l : void 0     // C = (g.id === n)  -> only the active item is measured
```

Everything else falls back to the estimate above.

**3. The locate button's availability depends solely on the active anchor**

```js
disabled={!n}           // n = activeAnchorId
```

Measurement is throttled behind `requestAnimationFrame` + `ResizeObserver` + `MutationObserver`; while a measurement pass has not produced an active id yet, the button is unusable.

**4. Shared cached-state path with #8186**

The directory caches the current anchor in a mutable ref (`C.current`) and re-runs its measurement on scroll / resize / mutation of the transcript. This is the same state that the jump-and-pin loop maintains (`Ue / RA / NA`, the ~1.6 s re-anchor described in #8186). Hence "positioning is inaccurate" and "wheel gets dragged back" are two faces of one mechanism rather than two independent defects.

## Suggested direction

1. Use the real DOM geometry for anchor positions - the rect map is already collected in the same pass, so the fallback to `orderPercent` should not be used as a coordinate (or should be recomputed on demand).
2. Do not gate the locate action on the active anchor only.
3. Clear the navigation's anchor/reset cache once a navigation completes, so later scroll interaction is not influenced by residual navigation state.

---
*Read-only inspection of the installed console bundle on QwenPaw Desktop 2.2.2-beta.5 (Windows 10 x64).*

issues.title: [Bug] Agent 间调用会话被静默取消（CancelledError）：同秒成对、产物归零，且取消不记录发起方与原因
issues.body:
## 环境
| 项 | 值 |
|---|---|
| 客户端 | QwenPaw Desktop（Windows 10 AMD64） |
| 版本 | **2.2.1**（`qwenpaw --version`） |
| 场景 | 多 agent 舰队（Orchestrator / Reasoner / Executor / Reviewer / Defender）+ 一个飞书通道入口；agent 之间通过 `ChatWithAgent` 互相调用 |
| 涉及代码位置 | `qwenpaw/hooks/error/error_hook.py:90`、`qwenpaw/runtime/runtime.py:297,379`、`qwenpaw/app/routers/tool_calls.py:91`、`qwenpaw/app/channels/base.py:589` |

## 现象（Actual）
1. **跨 agent 调用会话被静默取消**：日志落 `cancel_cleanup: cancelled (session=<A>:to:<B>:<epoch>:<hash>): CancelledError`，并伴随 `cancel-save: persisted interrupted turn` 与 `cancel-save: ... closed 1 dangling tool call(s)`。被取消的会话**没有 result、没有产物**。
2. **成对出现**：多为**同一秒**两条一起被取消（形如 `f-orchestrator:to:f-executor:*` + `f-reasoner:to:f-orchestrator:*`）。
3. **系统性**：本地主日志 3 天内共 **19 次**（10-12: 6 次、10-13: 7 次、10-14: 6 次）；**全部**为 `A:to:B` 跨 agent 会话，未见到单机/用户直连会话被同样取消。
4. **不可溯源**：日志**只**记录 `CancelledError`，**不记录取消的发起方与原因** ⇒ 使用者无法判断属于"框架回收 / 超时 / 上游断开 / 路由错配"中的哪一种。

### 单个实例（逐条可复核的原文形态）
| 时刻 | 日志原文（截断） |
|---|---|
| 11:52:23 | 本地派发台账行：`task_id=<任务号>, agent=f-executor` |
| 11:52:29 | `legion-guard: cb pass task=<任务号> agent=f-executor attempt=1`（本地插件，仅登记、无取消能力） |
| 11:52:29 / 11:52:30 | `Auto-registered new chat` → `builder: built agent for session=...85c3f2e3 agent=f-executor` |
| 11:52:32–35 | 一连串 `Read` / `Bash` 放行（**只读巡检，无写无删**） |
| **11:55:56** | **`cancel_cleanup: cancelled (session=f-orchestrator:to:f-executor:...85c3f2e3): CancelledError`** |
| 11:55:56 | `cancel-save: persisted interrupted turn` + `cancel-save: ... closed 1 dangling tool call(s)` |
| 11:55:56 | **同一秒**另一条：`cancel_cleanup: cancelled (session=f-reasoner:to:f-orchestrator:...ccd46635): CancelledError` |
| 之后 | **零 result、零产物**；该会话上下文仅 2 条（末条为 Executor 自述"我先读权威状态机"）⇒ **刚开工即被掐** |

## 已逐项排除的原因（本地只读取证）
1. **审批（approval）** — 取消时刻**无任何** `app/approvals` 行；对照：另一次取消伴随 `Cancelled 1 pending approval(s) for root session ...`，与本例形态不同。
2. **本地插件 / 自定义守卫** — 本地守卫插件源码中无 `cancel` / `interrupt` / `terminate` / `stop_session` 任何关键词（不具备取消能力）；取消时刻亦无任何插件日志行。
3. **危险命令触发** — 被取消的会话上无删除类或命令行写文件类命令（被取消的 Executor 会话刚进入只读阶段）。
4. **保存配置触发的"零停机热重载"**（即 #8225 所述机制）— 四次取消时刻（10-13 11:20:07 / 10-13 14:28:31 / 10-14 09:37:27 / 10-14 11:55:56）**均无** `config.json` 或任一 `agent.json` 的写入（mtime 逐一核对）；日志亦无 reload / restart / `feishu channel started` 标记。⇒ **与 #8225 不是同一机制**。

## 与 `session_id mismatch` 的时间相关（因果假设，未闭合）
- 10-13 `22:24:43` 落 `qwenpaw/app/routers/tool_calls.py:91` 的 `session_id mismatch`（`url=<调用方会话>` vs `backend=1791895062459-d82gki8`）；
- **10-13 `22:29:16`**：该 `backend` 会话被 `cancel_cleanup: cancelled`。
- 另见 `qwenpaw/app/channels/base.py:589 Message ignored (task already running)`（框架对"同一会话重复投递"的护栏）⇒ 佐证该**投递 / 回执通道确有重复与错配**。
- **保留**：因框架不记录取消发起方，因果链**未 100% 闭合**；本条的重点不只在错配，更在于**取消本身不可溯源**。

## 影响
单次取消 = 该子任务**会话死亡、零产物、需人工决策重派**；对多 agent 舰队属**可用性级**损失。并且，由于 `CancelledError` 与"agent 自身失败/超时"在日志上无法区分，本地只能靠人工逐条复核（本例即花了一轮人工取证才定性）。

## 期望
1. **让取消可溯源**：取消时至少落一条含 **发起方 / 原因 / 目标会话** 的日志（以区分：框架回收 / 超时 / 上游断开 / 路由错配）。
2. 确认上文「mismatch + 高频重投」路径**是否会导致会话级联取消**。
3. 若"同一秒成对取消"属**既定回收语义**（例如父会话结束回收子会话、收尾回收），请在文档或日志中明示。
4. 提供**可观测手段**（日志字段 / 接口 / 指标），以便本地自动区分"被取消"与"agent 失败"，无需人工复核。

## 最小复现建议
短时间内成批发起跨 agent 调用（同一调用方 → 多个被调方），观察数分钟后是否出现**同秒成对**的 `cancel_cleanup`；本地侧只读日志即可复核。可复跑聚合：以工具调用 id（`tc`）为主键，统计同一 `tc` 在 ≤120 秒窗口内的重复条数与 `session_id mismatch` 计数（正常段为 1，收尾段显著大于 1）。

## 相关 issue（可串联）
- **#8225**（保存 agent 配置触发的"零停机热重载"会取消正在运行的 cron 任务）— 机制不同，本条已显式排除配置保存。
- **#6608**（长命令绕过 `shell_command_timeout`、取消时留孤儿子进程、飞书会话被无限阻塞）
- **#7011**（Console 停止请求可取消活跃飞书会话；已 closed）
- **#8088**（图片路由卡死后被静默取消、用户无回复；已 closed）

---
*本报告按"不依赖私有环境、只读日志取证"整理；不含任何凭据、密钥或业务数据。*

issues.title: [Bug]: Plugin hot-install aborts when importlib.invalidate_caches() raises on distro-patched Python 3.11（我的插件被这个卡了））

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.2.2

## Description

The plugin loader calls `importlib.invalidate_caches()` unconditionally at three
sites (`loader.py:201`, `loader.py:465`, `loader.py:1094`). On Python builds where
this stdlib function itself raises (a real-world distro backport bug, see
Additional Notes), the exception propagates and aborts the entire plugin
install / hot-update.

Cache invalidation is best-effort by design — a failure here should not be fatal.

**Related PR(s):** N/A
**Security considerations:** None

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.2.2
- **OS:** Linux x86_64 (Lifsea 8 container, kernel 5.10.134-18.0.12.lifsea8)
- **Install method:** pip (venv)
- **Python version (if applicable):** 3.11.15 (`libpython3.11-minimal 3.11.2-6+deb12u9`)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On an affected Python build, verify the environment bug directly:

   ```bash
   python3 -c "import importlib; importlib.invalidate_caches()"
   ```

   → `TypeError: MetadataPathFinder.invalidate_caches() missing 1 required positional argument: 'cls'`

2. With QwenPaw running, install any plugin whose `requirements.txt` contains a
   not-yet-satisfied dependency (Console upload or `qwenpaw plugin install`).
3. The install aborts with the TypeError above; the plugin directory is copied
   into `plugins/` but the plugin never loads.

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** The entire plugin install fails with `TypeError: MetadataPathFinder.invalidate_caches() missing 1 required positional argument: 'cls'`.
- **Expected:** A cache-invalidation failure degrades to a warning and the install proceeds.

## Logs / Screenshots

```
File ".../qwenpaw/app/routers/plugins.py", line 847, in upload_plugin
  record = await _load_plugin_with_optional_force_reinstall(...)
File ".../qwenpaw/plugins/loader.py", line 1179, in load_plugin_from_path
  record = await self._load_plugin_from_path_unlocked(...)
File ".../qwenpaw/plugins/loader.py", line 1316, in _load_plugin_from_path_unlocked
  await asyncio.to_thread(...)
File ".../qwenpaw/plugins/loader.py", line 465, in _install_requirements_locked
  importlib.invalidate_caches()
File "/usr/lib/python3.11/importlib/__init__.py", line 70, in invalidate_caches
  finder.invalidate_caches()
File "<frozen importlib._bootstrap_external>", line 1409, in invalidate_caches
TypeError: MetadataPathFinder.invalidate_caches() missing 1 required positional argument: 'cls'
```

## Additional Notes

Root cause has two layers:

1. **Environment (not QwenPaw's fault):** this distro build backported the
   CPython 3.12 change "PathFinder.invalidate_caches also clears
   importlib.metadata caches" into 3.11's frozen bootstrap, but the backported
   `/usr/lib/python3.11/importlib/metadata/__init__.py` (line 918) lost its
   `@classmethod` decorator:

   ```python
   def invalidate_caches(cls):      # ← @classmethod missing in backport
       FastPath.__new__.cache_clear()
   ```

   So **every** `importlib.invalidate_caches()` call raises. Reproduced with a
   bare interpreter, including under `python3 -S`. The same environment bug
   also breaks `pip`, `pytest`, etc., so QwenPaw cannot rely on the
   environment being fixed — it should tolerate the failure.

2. **QwenPaw side:** `loader.py:201` / `:465` / `:1094` call it unguarded.

**Suggested fix** — wrap all three sites:

```python
try:
    importlib.invalidate_caches()
except Exception:
    logger.warning("importlib.invalidate_caches() failed; continuing", exc_info=True)
```

**Workaround for plugin authors:** ship the plugin without `requirements.txt`
when all deps are already QwenPaw host dependencies — `loader.py:392` returns
early when the file is absent, bypassing the failing path entirely. (Verified:
`pyyaml>=6.0` is already a direct `Requires-Dist` of the `qwenpaw` package.)

issues.title: [Feature]: Firecrawl as a web_search provider
issues.body:
Hey, I'm Juampi from the Firecrawl team.

## Summary

Add Firecrawl as a third `web_search` provider next to the two existing ones. I'd build and maintain it.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [x] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Problem / Motivation

The `SearchProvider` abstraction from #7081 makes a new backend small. Today users who want Firecrawl have to go through ClawHub skills or a custom MCP config. Firecrawl search also works without an API key on a keyless free tier that is capped per IP (https://docs.firecrawl.dev/billing), and a key raises the limits, so it fits the same optional-key shape as the provider added in #7081.

## Proposed Solution

Follow the layout from #7081: a `FirecrawlProvider` in `websearch/` that posts to `https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/search` through the existing `_post` helper, the provider option in the Console modal and router config, an optional `api_key` credential slot, and unit tests. No new dependency. The current default stays the default. Requests carry an `origin: "qwenpaw"` field so Firecrawl can tell where they come from.

A possible follow-up, only if you want it: an opt-in `web_fetch` fallback to Firecrawl for pages the direct fetch can't read. I'd keep that as a separate PR.

## Alternatives Considered

A Firecrawl MCP client template next to the existing one. The provider needs no MCP setup, so it is simpler for users.

## Additional Context

I have the change built and tested, and I'm opening the PR next to this issue. Happy to change anything from the layout in #7081. @rayrayraykk @cuiyuebing

issues.title: [Bug]: Hub restart leaves desired-running Local runtimes stopped and silently skips cron jobs
issues.body:
## Summary

Hub with the Local process provisioner does not restore desired-running user runtimes after the Hub process restarts. Enabled cron jobs inside those runtimes silently miss their scheduled executions until an authenticated request starts the runtime again.

The Hub can be healthy and reachable while the user runtime, its channel connections and its cron scheduler are not running.

## Environment and verification scope

- Observed on QwenPaw 2.2.0, Linux, Hub with Local runtimes.
- Also inspected v2.2.1, v2.2.2-beta.4, and main at 753cb6dc4f1b7440dcd2d3869360d2a5677bd168: no startup restoration of desired-running user runtimes was found. These newer versions were inspected statically, not reproduced in production.
- Runtime desired state is running; cron jobs are enabled with an explicit timezone.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start Hub and a user's Local runtime.
2. Create an enabled recurring cron job scheduled a few minutes ahead; confirm its next execution time.
3. Restart the Hub process before the scheduled time.
4. Do not open that user's chat or make an authenticated request through the personal runtime proxy.
5. Wait past the scheduled time.
6. Open the user's chat / access the personal runtime API.

## Actual behavior

- The Local runtime does not restart with Hub, so its cron scheduler never triggers the job.
- Accessing the user's personal runtime starts it later.
- The scheduler registers the next future execution; the missed recurring job is not automatically replayed.
- An enabled task and a healthy Hub do not indicate that its execution runtime is actually running.

In the affected deployment, all three enabled daily jobs missed execution after a Hub restart. They had triggered the previous day, and their schedule configurations had not changed.

## Expected behavior

On Hub startup, reconcile runtimes whose persisted desired_state is running and restore their execution processes without requiring user traffic. Explicitly stopped or administrator-disabled runtimes should remain stopped.

Recovery should use existing lifecycle locking, capacity checks and provisioner operations; leave healthy runtimes alone; and isolate failures so one tenant does not block recovery of other tenants. Failed recovery should remain visible to administrators.

Missed-job notification / replay policy would be a separate improvement. Increasing misfire_grace_seconds alone cannot help when the runtime itself is not running.

## Relevant code

- src/qwenpaw/hub/control_app.py: the application lifespan has no desired-running runtime restoration. ensure_personal_runtime() starts a stopped runtime on request.
- src/qwenpaw/hub/service.py: close() closes provisioners and records stopped observed states.
- src/qwenpaw/hub/local_provisioner.py: close() terminates the child processes it owns.
- src/qwenpaw/app/crons/manager.py: startup loads job specs and registers a fresh process-local scheduler.

Source inspected: https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/blob/753cb6dc4f1b7440dcd2d3869360d2a5677bd168/src/qwenpaw/hub/control_app.py

## Local mitigation tested

We added desired-running runtime restoration to the Hub lifespan using the existing lifecycle service. Local tests cover stopped vs. desired-running runtimes, healthy-runtime idempotency, an administrator stop during recovery, and one failed tenant not blocking another.

After deploying that mitigation and performing a controlled Hub restart, both desired-running Local runtimes started automatically before any personal-runtime API request. The affected agent's channels and all three enabled cron schedules were restored; the disabled job remained disabled and all job configurations were unchanged.
