issues.title: [Feature]: Make skill-pool download a cancellable background job (progress + explicit cancel)
issues.body:
Follow-up from the review of #8055.

`POST /pool/download` currently waits for the whole copy before responding.
#8055 removes the event-loop freeze by moving the copy to a worker thread,
but the request itself is still synchronous, so a large skill still trips
the client's 30 s timeout and the UI still reports a failure for a download
that is actually progressing.

The end state we want:

* The download runs as a server-side job; the request returns immediately
  with a job id.
* Progress is pollable (files copied / total, current skill).
* Explicit cancellation that **reaches the worker** — aborting the HTTP
  request does not stop an already-running copy, so cancel needs to be a
  real signal to the thread doing the work.
* The frontend stops treating 30 s as a failure and shows pending state
  until the job reports done or cancelled.

Scope note: this changes the API contract and the UX, which is why it was
not folded into #8055.

Related: #8013

issues.title: [Feature] Add built-in provider presets for CommandCode and Hugging Face

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

issues.body:
### Summary

Two OpenAI-compatible gateways are missing from the built-in provider catalog:
**CommandCode** and **Hugging Face Inference Providers**. Users can add them as
custom providers, but they get no preset entry and no official icon.

### Why these two

The built-in catalog already covers comparable aggregator / coding gateways such
as `opencode` and `kilo`. These two belong to the same category:

| Provider | Base URL | Compatibility |
|---|---|---|
| CommandCode | `https://api.commandcode.ai/provider/v1` | OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses, Anthropic Messages |
| Hugging Face Inference Providers | `https://router.huggingface.co/v1` | OpenAI-compatible |

- **CommandCode** — a multi-model gateway (Claude / GPT / Gemini / top open
  models) with subscription plans (Go / GOAT / Pro / Max) plus a pay-as-you-go
  Provider API tier. The same API key authenticates both the CLI and the
  endpoints. Docs: https://commandcode.ai/docs/provider
- **Hugging Face** — Inference Providers, an OpenAI-compatible router that
  aggregates multiple inference backends under one token.
  Docs: https://huggingface.co/docs/inference-providers

### Request

1. Add both to the built-in provider catalog so they can be configured without a
   custom provider entry.
2. Add their icons to the frontend `providerIcon` map (providers without a mapped
   icon fall back to the letter icon today). Both have publicly-available icon
   assets (verified reachable on 2026-10-14):

   | Provider | Icon source |
   |---|---|
   | CommandCode | `https://commandcode.ai/apple-touch-icon.png` (180×180 PNG) or `https://commandcode.ai/favicon.ico` |
   | Hugging Face | `https://huggingface.co/front/assets/huggingface_logo-noborder.svg` (SVG) or `https://huggingface.co/favicon.ico` |

   (This follows the existing `kilo` pattern, which references
   `https://kilo.ai/favicon/android-chrome-192x192.png` directly.)

### Current workaround

Custom providers work fine; the only gap is the missing preset entry and icon
(they render the default placeholder / letter icon).

Thanks!

issues.title: [Bug]:  保存 agent 配置（如心跳设置）触发的「零停机热重载」会取消正在运行的 cron 任务，任务被记为 `cancelled` 且无任何提示

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
# [Bug] 保存 agent 配置（如心跳设置）触发的「零停机热重载」会取消正在运行的 cron 任务，任务被记为 `cancelled` 且无任何提示（2.2.1）

## QwenPaw Version

2.2.1（`pip show qwenpaw` → Version: 2.2.1；`qwenpaw --version` → QwenPaw, version 2.2.1）

## Description

在 Console 里**保存一次心跳设置**（`PUT /api/config/heartbeat`），会把**当时正在运行的 cron 任务一起取消掉**，任务在运行历史里被记为 `status=cancelled / error="Job was cancelled"`；前端没有任何"这次保存将中断正在运行的任务"的提示，用户第一反应是"我并没有点取消，为什么显示 cancelled"。

**完整链路（实测，2.2.1 安装态）：**

```
PUT /api/config/heartbeat
  └─ app/routers/config.py:711   agent.config.heartbeat = hb
  └─ app/routers/config.py:712   save_agent_config(agent.agent_id, agent.config)   # 改写 agent.json
  └─ app/routers/config.py:718   await agent.cron_manager.reschedule_heartbeat()   # 异步

AgentConfigWatcher（poll=2.0s，监控 agent.json）
  └─ 指纹变化 → 重新加载并比对 _channels_hash / _heartbeat_hash（app/agent_config_watcher.py:35-63, 174+）
  └─ 判定 changed → app/agent_config_watcher.py:231  "config changed, triggering graceful reload"

MultiAgentManager.reload_agent()
  └─ :592  "Reloading agent (zero-downtime): <agent>"
  └─ :611  "Creating new workspace instance: <agent>"
  └─ :140  "New workspace instance started: <agent>"
  └─ :671  "Workspace instance replaced: <agent>"
  └─ :473  "Old workspace instance stopped: <agent>. Zero-downtime reload completed."

旧实例内正在执行的 agent 回合被硬切断
  └─ hooks/error/error_hook.py:90   cancel_cleanup: cancelled (session=<session>): CancelledError
  └─ runtime/runtime.py:297         cancel-save: persisted interrupted turn (session=<session>)
  └─ app/crons/executor.py:269-270  捕获 asyncio.CancelledError → "cron execute: job_id=… cancelled"
  └─ app/crons/manager.py:785-788   st.last_status = "cancelled"; st.last_error = "Job was cancelled"
```

**实际影响：** 本例被取消的是一天只跑一次、当天唯一的选股任务（19:15:56 启动，19:43:19 被杀，**已跑 27 分钟**）。由于 `cancel-save` 会把中断回合落盘、调度器随后在 19:43:47 自动重投递（`app/crons/manager.py:405`），最终 19:54:06 仍以 `success` 收尾，**业务结果没丢**；但：

1. 整个过程用户**完全无感**，只会在运行历史里看到一个 `cancelled`，无从判断原因（既不是自己点的取消，也不是任务报错）。
2. 重投递是**续做**而非回滚：中断前已执行的写操作（建监控/建分析/发消息等）不会被撤销，续做若重复执行会造成**重复实体**，需要调用方自己做"写入指纹核查"来兜底 —— 这个成本不该由上层业务承担。

**Related PR(s):** 无（reporter 未找到相关 PR）

**Security considerations:** 无。本例只涉及配置下发与运行时任务取消，未涉及凭据、鉴权、越权或数据泄露。

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
  - `app/routers/config.py`（`PUT /heartbeat`：写 config + 触发 reschedule）
  - `app/agent_config_watcher.py`（`AgentConfigWatcher._check`：文件变更判定 + 触发 reload）
  - `app/multi_agent_manager.py`（`reload_agent` 零停机替换实例，`:473` 停旧实例）
  - `app/crons/executor.py:269-270` ＋ `app/crons/manager.py:405,785-788`（`CancelledError` → 记 `cancelled` → 重投递）
- [x] Console (frontend web UI) —— 保存设置时未提示"将中断正在运行的任务"，也未在运行历史里区分 `cancelled` 的成因
- [x] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.) —— 仅间接：被取消的 cron 任务是投递到 console channel 的 agent 任务；若投递目标换成 IM channel，任务半途被切断同样会向该 channel 暴露不完整输出。**未验证**其他 channel 下是否有额外影响。
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website) —— 建议补充"修改 agent 配置会影响在跑任务"的说明
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.2.1（pip 安装态，`site-packages` 无 git 提交信息）
- **OS:** Linux (WSL2)，kernel `6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2`；userland `Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS`；host timezone `Asia/Shanghai`
- **Install method:** pip（venv `/home/pavino/.qwenvenv`）
- **Python version:** 3.12.3

补充环境：单机、单进程 `qwenpaw app`（PID 在故障前后未变，**排除了进程重启导致的取消**）；多 agent 工作区，本次受影响的 agent 有 1 条 `agent` 型每日 cron 任务。

## Steps to Reproduce

1. 给某个 agent 配置一条**运行时间较长**的 cron 任务（本例：每日 `19:15` 触发的全市场选股，实测典型耗时 25–40 分钟），并让它开始运行。
2. 任务运行期间，在 Console 打开该 agent 的**心跳设置**页（`GET /api/config/heartbeat`）。
3. 点击**保存**（`PUT /api/config/heartbeat`，返回 `200 OK`）。
4. 观察日志（**同一秒起**）：

```
19:43:14 | heartbeat rescheduled: every=1h                                              (crons/manager.py:298)
19:43:14 | AgentConfigWatcher (<agent>): config changed, triggering graceful reload
           (channels: <hash> -> <hash>, heartbeat: <hash> -> <hash>)                    (agent_config_watcher.py:229)
19:43:14 | Reloading agent (zero-downtime): <agent>                                     (multi_agent_manager.py:592)
19:43:14 | Creating new workspace instance: <agent>                                     (multi_agent_manager.py:611)
19:43:19 | New workspace instance started: <agent>                                      (multi_agent_manager.py:140)
19:43:19 | Workspace instance replaced: <agent>                                         (multi_agent_manager.py:671)
19:43:19 | Old workspace instance stopped: <agent>. Zero-downtime reload completed.      (multi_agent_manager.py:473)
19:43:19 | cancel_cleanup: cancelled (session=<session>): CancelledError                (hooks/error/error_hook.py:90)
19:43:19 | cancel-save: persisted interrupted turn (session=<session>)                  (runtime/runtime.py:297)
19:43:19 | cron execute: job_id=<job-id> cancelled                                      (crons/executor.py:270)
19:43:19 | cron _execute_once: job_id=<job-id> status=cancelled                          (crons/manager.py:787)
```

5. 任务运行历史（`jobs_history`）出现：`{"status": "cancelled", "error": "Job was cancelled"}`。

**可复现性：稳定复现**——本例的取消时间点（19:43:14）恰好落在任务运行窗口（19:15:56 启动、被杀时已跑 27 分钟）内，两者重叠即触发。因此只要"保存 agent 级配置"与"长任务在跑"两个条件同时满足，该问题即出现。

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:**
  1. 保存与任务无关的设置（心跳）会**取消正在运行的 cron 任务**，且是"硬切断"——被切在 27 分钟处，回合内的工具副作用已落盘不回滚。
  2. 用户侧无提示：Console 不告警，运行历史只留一个 `cancelled`；`cancelled`（被外部打断）与 `timeout`（跑超时，`crons/executor.py:251/266` → `status=timeout`）在 UI 上不易区分，导致需要翻日志才能定性。
  3. **触发条件是"写文件"这个动作，而不是"值发生变化"**：`save_agent_config()` **无条件重写** `agent.json`，`AgentConfigWatcher` 只比对文件指纹与 `channels`/`heartbeat` 哈希。本例保存前后心跳**间隔相同**（均为 `every=1h`，保存前日志中已有 `Heartbeat job scheduled for agent <agent>: every=1h`），而 watcher 打印的 heartbeat 哈希 `-5931758269779770202 -> 1725766300364508814` **确实变了** ⇒ 这次保存改动的是心跳的**其它**字段。至于"把完全相同的值再存一次"，我们未单独实测，但按上述代码路径应当同样触发 reload —— 请 dev 确认。
- **Expected:** 修改 agent 配置（心跳 / 渠道 / driver 等）不应以牺牲在跑回合为代价。希望至少做到其中一项：
  1. **延迟切换**：`save_agent_config` 后由 watcher 触发 reload 时，若该 agent 有**正在执行的 agent/cron 回合**，则等待其结束（或等到下一个安全点）再做实例替换；或
  2. **重新排队而非取消**：把被中断的回合显式标记为 `interrupted/requeued` 并**从头或从中断点安全续做**，而不是让在跑回合收到裸 `CancelledError`；或
  3. **前置提示**：Console 在保存前检查该 agent 是否有在跑任务，弹窗告知"保存将中断 N 个正在运行的任务（任务名/已运行时长）"，由用户选择"等任务结束"或"立即保存"。
  4. 附带：`cancelled` 的成因（配置重载 / 用户取消 / 进程退出）建议结构化落库，便于 UI 展示与检索。

## Logs / Screenshots

触发请求与取消（`journalctl -u qwenpaw`，已脱敏：主机名、客户端 IP、会话 ID、job ID 掩码）：

```
19:15:56 | INFO crons/executor.py:48    | cron execute: job_id=<job-id> channel=console task_type=agent
                                          target_user_id=default target_session_id=<session>
19:43:09 | INFO (uvicorn)               | 192.168.0.x - "GET /api/config/heartbeat HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
19:43:14 | INFO (uvicorn)               | 192.168.0.x - "PUT /api/config/heartbeat HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
19:43:14 | INFO crons/manager.py:298    | heartbeat rescheduled: every=1h
19:43:14 | INFO agent_config_watcher.py:229 | AgentConfigWatcher (<agent>): config changed, triggering
                                          graceful reload (channels: 2766186957541623328 -> 2766186957541623328,
                                          heartbeat: -5931758269779770202 -> 1725766300364508814)
19:43:14 | INFO multi_agent_manager.py:592  | Reloading agent (zero-downtime): <agent>
19:43:14 | INFO agent_config_watcher.py:114 | AgentConfigWatcher already disabled for agent <agent>, skipping cancel
19:43:14 | INFO multi_agent_manager.py:611  | Creating new workspace instance: <agent>
19:43:19 | INFO workspace/workspace.py:725  | Workspace started successfully: <agent>
19:43:19 | INFO agent_config_watcher.py:106 | AgentConfigWatcher started for agent <agent>
                                          (poll=2.0s, path=/home/pavino/.qwenpaw/workspaces/<agent>/agent.json)
19:43:19 | INFO multi_agent_manager.py:140  | New workspace instance started: <agent>
19:43:19 | INFO multi_agent_manager.py:671  | Workspace instance replaced: <agent>
19:43:19 | INFO hooks/error/error_hook.py:90 | cancel_cleanup: cancelled (session=<session>): CancelledError
19:43:19 | INFO runtime/runtime.py:297      | cancel-save: persisted interrupted turn (session=<session>)
19:43:19 | INFO crons/executor.py:270       | cron execute: job_id=<job-id> cancelled
19:43:19 | INFO crons/manager.py:787        | cron _execute_once: job_id=<job-id> status=cancelled
19:43:19 | INFO multi_agent_manager.py:473  | Old workspace instance stopped: <agent>. Zero-downtime reload
                                          completed.
19:43:47 | INFO crons/manager.py:405       | cron run_job (async): job_id=<job-id> channel=console
                                          task_type=agent target_session_id=<session>     ← 自动重投递
19:43:47 | INFO crons/executor.py:48       | cron execute: job_id=<job-id> channel=console …      ← 续做
```

运行历史落库（该任务当日两条记录）：

```json
{"run_at": "2026-10-13T19:43:19", "status": "cancelled", "error": "Job was cancelled", "trigger": "scheduled"}
{"run_at": "2026-10-13T19:54:06", "status": "success",   "trigger": "manual"}
```

关键旁证（排除其它成因）：

- 进程 PID **前后未变**（同日 `qwenpaw[1362054]`，服务自 10-12 21:29 起持续运行）⇒ 不是进程重启/关机导致的取消。
- 当日**仅此一次**配置变更事件（全天 `journalctl` 中 `AgentConfigWatcher … config changed` 只出现 1 次）⇒ 与本次取消一一对应。
- 该 agent 的 watcher 在 19:43:14 之前**没有**任何 reload 记录。

## Additional Notes

**Workaround（目前采用）：** 不要在长任务运行窗口内保存 agent 级配置。本例的安全窗口是"避开每日 19:15 起的 25–40 分钟"，即 20:30 之后或次日盘前再改。

**同族风险（未逐一验证）：** `AgentConfigWatcher._check` 同时比对 `_channels_hash`，并对**任何** `agent.json` 变化触发同一 reload 路径；另外还存在独立的 `DriverConfigWatcher`（`app/driver_config_watcher.py:49`，poll=2.0s，监控 `<workspace>/drivers`）。因此"渠道设置""driver 配置"的保存**很可能有同样效果**，建议一并纳入修复范围与回归测试。注意：直接编辑 `agent.json`（绕过 API）同样会触发（watcher 是按文件指纹轮询的），所以只在前端加提示并不能覆盖全部入口。

**区分 `cancelled` 与 `timeout` 的提示（对使用者很重要）：**

- `cancelled` = `app/crons/executor.py:269-270` 捕获 `asyncio.CancelledError` → `app/crons/manager.py:785-788` 落库 → **"被外部打断"**。
- `timeout`  = `app/crons/executor.py:251/266` → `status=timeout`、`error="timed out after <N>s"` → **"跑超时"**。

两者是完全不同的成因，但在运行历史里都表现为"没跑完"。本例排查耗时主要花在这里：`cancelled` 必须回日志里找同一秒的 `AgentConfigWatcher … config changed` / `Reloading agent` / `Old workspace instance stopped` 才能定位。若能在 UI 上直接给出成因标签，可显著降低排查成本。

**期望的回归用例（供参考）：**

1. 启动一个长时 agent cron 任务，期间保存心跳设置 → 断言该任务**不被取消**（或按预期被安全延迟/重新排队，而不是落 `cancelled`）。
2. 保存前后心跳配置完全相同 → 断言**不触发**全量 reload（当前是触发的）。
3. 保存 `drivers/` 或 channels 配置 → 断言不与在跑回合冲突。

issues.title: [Feature]: Optional host navigation policy shared by sidebar and settings

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

issues.body:
## Summary

Would QwenPaw accept an optional, host-owned navigation policy for curated deployments, evaluated before the first Console render and shared by every navigation consumer?

The plugin menu API is useful for adding, replacing, or removing entries after a plugin loads. A deployment-level navigation contract would cover a different lifecycle: the intended menu should remain consistent when that optional plugin is absent, delayed, disabled, or unloaded, and when a user resets navigation preferences.

Related context: #4904 discussed simplifying the sidebar for nontechnical users. This proposal is narrower: a documented extension boundary for deployments, while preserving the current navigation for ordinary upstream installations.

## Existing behavior and evidence

Reviewed stable `v2.2.1` and main commit `1dc281f7b1cf33f10858ce987cce6d22604cb07f`:

- [The public menu SDK](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/blob/1dc281f7b1cf33f10858ce987cce6d22604cb07f/console/src/plugins/registry/sdk.ts) supports plugin add/replace/remove operations. `MenuItem.visible` is attached to an individual registered item.
- [Menu hooks](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/blob/1dc281f7b1cf33f10858ce987cce6d22604cb07f/console/src/plugins/registry/hooks.ts) consume registry snapshots; they do not expose a deployment policy.
- [Settings Center](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/blob/1dc281f7b1cf33f10858ce987cce6d22604cb07f/console/src/pages/SettingsCenter/index.tsx) also declares built-in pages independently. A policy applied only to the primary sidebar would not cover every navigation surface. Main additionally has settings search, which needs the same decision.

In a local downstream `v2.2.1` desktop reproduction, filtering the registry alone hid primary sidebar entries while the corresponding Settings Center entries remained visible. A small local experiment sharing one predicate between these consumers corrected that mismatch. This is evidence for the missing contract, not a claim that a production-ready implementation has been tested against all main-branch shells.

## Proposed contract for discussion

1. The host accepts an optional navigation policy as part of deployment/bootstrap configuration. It is available before the initial menu is rendered; it does not wait for an optional plugin or a network request.
2. The policy identifies entries through documented stable IDs, with an explicit mapping for built-in settings pages and plugin entries. An allowlist can provide a curated default; omitted policy preserves current upstream behavior exactly.
3. The primary sidebar, Settings Center, navigation customization/reset, and settings search use the same policy decision. Empty groups are removed. User preferences can further hide allowed entries but cannot restore deployment-excluded entries.
4. Late plugin registration and plugin cleanup cannot accidentally restore an excluded entry. No polling, DOM removal, CSS selectors, or localStorage seeding is needed.
5. This is a presentation contract only. It must not be represented as authentication, authorization, or enforcement against direct API requests. No routes or backend permissions are removed by this proposal.

The exact configuration transport and identifier model are intentionally open for maintainer feedback. A bootstrap configuration and a build-time configuration are possible alternatives; publishing another runtime plugin API alone would not solve the plugin-absent case.

## Validation expected in a follow-up PR

- No configured policy: existing default navigation and plugin behavior remain unchanged.
- Configured policy with a fresh profile and no optional frontend plugin: the first menu respects the policy.
- Delayed plugin registration, plugin unload/reload, and repeated snapshots: excluded entries remain excluded; React subscriptions remain stable.
- Settings entry, settings search, navigation reset, and application restart: the same IDs remain excluded.
- Allowed plugin entries and ordinary user hide/show preferences continue to work.
- Component tests, public documentation, and a real Console/desktop demonstration accompany the implementation. Other shells must be explicitly included or documented as outside the initial scope after maintainer agreement.

## Scope

One generic optional navigation contract, without organization-specific menu lists, branding, private endpoints, authentication rules, installer changes, or model restrictions. Theme customization from #7741 and market provider extensions from #8128 are separate existing capabilities and are not part of this proposal.

Following the contribution guide, this issue seeks agreement on the extension point before a focused implementation PR. I can prepare the implementation and tests after the intended configuration boundary is agreed.

issues.title: [Bug]: qwenpaw acp never loads installed plugins; plugin tools missing in ACP sessions and cross-process task callbacks cannot wake them
issues.body:
## Summary

Two linked gaps make plugin-provided tools and inter-agent completion callbacks unavailable in ACP-hosted sessions:

1. The `qwenpaw acp` server never instantiates `PluginLoader`, so **installed plugins are not loaded at all in ACP sessions** — only built-in workspace tools get registered.
2. The background-task store behind `submit_to_agent` / `check_agent_task` (`POST/GET /console/chat/task`) is **process-local**, while ACP sessions run in a separate `qwenpaw acp` process, so a completion callback raised in the console process can never wake an ACP-hosted session.

The generic "no push callback" gap is already tracked in #7056 (see also #8059, #7580). This issue covers the ACP-channel-specific half those issues do not.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [x] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Environment

- QwenPaw **2.2.2b4** (pip/venv), Linux x86_64
- Source checkout at commit `9698475e` (2026-10-13); all line references below are from that commit
- Topology: console app (`qwenpaw app`, one process) + ACP server (`qwenpaw acp`, a second process); an IDE harness attaches to the ACP process

## Gap 1 — installed plugins are never loaded in the ACP process

`PluginLoader` is instantiated in exactly two places:

- `src/qwenpaw/app/_app.py:500` — the console/FastAPI app
- `src/qwenpaw/cli/channels_cmd.py:641` — the CLI channels command

The ACP server's workspace bootstrap (`src/qwenpaw/agents/acp/server.py:459`) calls `workspace.bootstrap_plugins(...)` (`src/qwenpaw/app/workspace/workspace.py:288`), which registers only **built-in** workspace tools via `WorkspacePlugins` (`src/qwenpaw/app/workspace/workspace_plugins.py:33`). It never touches `PluginLoader` or `~/.qwenpaw/plugins/`. A repo-wide `grep -rn "PluginLoader(" src/qwenpaw/` confirms there is no third instantiation site.

Observed: a plugin installed and enabled for the console (its tools visible to console sessions) is completely absent from the tool list of every session served by `qwenpaw acp`.

## Gap 2 — completion callbacks cannot cross the process boundary into ACP sessions

`submit_to_agent` posts to `POST /console/chat/task` on the console app and `check_agent_task` polls `GET /console/chat/task/{id}`; the task store is a process-local dict (one global dict in 2.2.x). A watcher living in the console process therefore cannot deliver a finished result into a session whose turn runs inside the `qwenpaw acp` process:

- `POST /console/chat/task` addressed at an ACP-hosted session never reaches that session — the ACP process owns its session loop, and the console's routing cannot inject a new user turn into it.
- The ACP server exposes no inbound push path (e.g. ACP `session/update`) for externally completed work, so nothing wakes the ACP turn.

Observed with a callback plugin (watcher thread + re-injection via `POST /console/chat/task`): delivery works for console-routed sessions; for ACP sessions the plugin must refuse registration outright, because watching there would poll pointlessly forever. The two processes also have disjoint task-id spaces, so a task submitted in one 404s in the other — the same family as the lost records in #8059.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install and enable any plugin that registers tools.
2. Start the console app (`qwenpaw app`) and an ACP server (`qwenpaw acp`) as two processes.
3. From an ACP-hosted session, list available tools: the plugin's tools are missing (Gap 1).
4. From a console session, `submit_to_agent` a background task and register a completion watcher whose target session is the ACP-hosted one: the result never arrives (Gap 2). The identical flow delivers correctly when the receiving session is console-routed.

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** plugin tools exist only in console sessions; completion callbacks only reach console-routed sessions.
- **Expected:** `qwenpaw acp` loads installed plugins the same way the console app does (PluginLoader in the ACP workspace bootstrap, or a shared plugin registry across entry points); and a finished background task is deliverable to its originating session regardless of which process hosts it — either by routing delivery through the ACP process or by making the task store cross-process/durable (the durability ask in #8059).

## Related

- #7056 — generic background-task callback/notification gap (console side)
- #8059 — task records lost (404) after completion; "no push; retrieval is polling-only"
- #7580 — blocking wait-tool request (polling trips doom-loop protection)

## Willing to Contribute

We run a working push-callback plugin (`agent-task-callback`, console side, watcher + re-injection) that can serve as a regression fixture for both gaps, together with the two-process repro setup. Happy to provide both.

issues.title: [Bug] Doom-loop gate kills legitimate task-authorized polling; cron records false success after termination
issues.body:
## Description

The doom-loop gate terminated a **legitimate, task-authorized polling pattern** while the awaited background task was genuinely progressing. The gate cannot distinguish "agent stuck repeating itself" from "agent waiting for a long-running background task exactly as its task instructions require".

Additionally, the cron scheduler recorded `last_status: "success"` for the killed run — the termination is invisible to operators.

## Reproduction (real production case, 2026-10-12 08:00 Asia/Shanghai)

A daily cron job (`6e7d12f7`, 08:00, agent-type) runs a ~12-minute report script in the background (`nohup ... &`), then polls for a completion marker (`---CHARTS---` in an output file) every 30 seconds, exactly as the job's task text instructs.

Observed sequence (from `history.db` of session `5ff775cf`, seq 33987–33994):

1. Agent issues, four times in a row, the **identical** tool call:
   `sleep 30 && (ps -p 18280 > /dev/null && echo "PID 18280 存活" || echo "PID 18280 已退出") && tail -c 300 /tmp/morning_output.txt`
2. Each result was byte-identical and showed **real external progress**: the background script advanced from "连接数据库..." to "腾讯新闻 AI 详摘 42 条" between polls.
3. After the 4th identical call the gate fired: `Doom loop: agent stuck after 4 consecutive repetitions` and killed the session at 08:02:38.
4. The background script (PID 18280) was completely healthy and finished on its own at ~08:12. Nothing was stuck — only the *waiting pattern* matched the repetition heuristic.
5. `qwenpaw cron state 6e7d12f7` afterwards: `{"last_run_at": "2026-10-12T08:02:38+08:00", "last_status": "success", "last_error": null}` — a killed run reported as success. The failure only became visible by manually inspecting session files.

## Root cause discussion

The repetition gate compares tool calls for similarity (and after PRs #7919/#7906, requires new evidence to escalate — good). What it still ignores:

1. **Intent context**: the repeated call is explicitly instructed by the task text ("poll every 30 seconds until marker X appears"). Within a cron/agent task, periodic `sleep + check` is a *waiting* idiom, not a stuck loop.
2. **External progress**: the awaited world state (log file content, process liveness) *was* changing between calls. A stuck loop has static observed state; a poll has evolving observed state.
3. **Inter-call spacing**: 30s between identical calls is not the tight-fire behavior the gate was designed for (sub-second or back-to-back regeneration).

The combined effect: any task instruction that says "wait for a background job by polling" is a guaranteed gate trip after N polls, and the operator gets a false success.

## Suggested fixes

1. **Recognize wait/poll morphology** (e.g. `sleep N && check-same-target`, or same tool+args with N-second spacing): exclude from repetition accounting, or place in a separate slower-escalation track, while the awaited condition (marker file / process) can still change.
2. **State-change awareness**: if the observed environment between identical calls changed (file grew, process still alive, log advanced), treat as polling-with-progress, not repetition.
3. **First-class wait primitive**: a `wait_for`-style tool (wait for file marker / process exit / condition, with timeout) removes the need for agents to hand-roll polling loops entirely.
4. **Cron truthfulness**: when a run is terminated by the doom-loop gate (or any loop gate), record it distinctly — e.g. `last_status: "terminated"` with `last_error` naming the gate — instead of `success`.

Longer term, a `script`-type cron task (see our feature request #4963 — direct shell execution without agent inference) would structurally eliminate this class: no agent in the loop means no polling loop to misclassify.

## Related

- #6116 — original doom-loop report (closed as wontfix; today's case is a *different* failure mode: authorized polling, not model repetition)
- #4963 — feature request: script-type cron tasks (structural avoidance)
- #7919 / #7906 — doom-loop gate accounting fixes (merged; today's case survives them)
- #7420 — different mechanism (runtime re-dispatch after `write_file`)

## Environment

- QwenPaw: 2.2.1 (Docker, Linux x86_64)
- Channel: Feishu; session `5ff775cf`; cron job `6e7d12f7` (daily 08:00 Asia/Shanghai, agent type, runtime timeout 1800s)
- Models routed via self-hosted gateway (free-pool small models on this job)
- We mitigated on our side by rewriting the task text to use a single blocking wait command instead of repeated polling; the gate/cron behaviors above remain unfixed framework-side.

---
*Tooling disclosure (per #4333): this report was prepared with AI assistance under human direction. All timestamps, commands, and state outputs come from a real live deployment.*

issues.title: Feature: Add i18n support for protected execution contract prompt

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

issues.body:
## Background

QwenPaw already has an i18n mechanism for the scroll context management prompt (`SCROLL_SYSTEM_PROMPT_TEMPLATES` dict with `"zh"` and `"en"` keys in `agents/context/scroll/prompt.py`, selected via the `language` field in agent config). This works well — when `language: zh` is set, the scroll system prompt (retrieval headline, recall_history, context map, etc.) is correctly rendered in Chinese.

## Problem

The **protected execution contract** (`runtime/protected_prompt.py` → `PROTECTED_EXECUTION_CONTRACT_PROMPT`) is hardcoded in English only. It's injected via `ProtectedExecutionContractContributor` in `runtime/prompt_contributors.py` without any language parameter.

This means even when `language: zh` is configured, the agent's system prompt contains a mix of:
- ✅ Chinese: scroll prompt (headline/recall/map/discipline), AGENTS.md/SOUL.md/PROFILE.md
- ❌ English: protected execution contract (Match the request / Clarify before acting / Stay within authorization / Untrusted content / Finishing the job / Tool-use enforcement)

Other sections like the framework info block (About/GitHub/OS/Working directory) and agent-skills description are also English-only, but the protected execution contract is the most impactful one since it defines core behavioral constraints.

## Proposal

Extend the existing i18n pattern to `protected_prompt.py`:

1. Add `PROTECTED_EXECUTION_CONTRACT_PROMPT_ZH` (and other languages as needed)
2. Add a `PROTECTED_EXECUTION_CONTRACT_TEMPLATES` dict similar to `SCROLL_SYSTEM_PROMPT_TEMPLATES`
3. Update `ProtectedExecutionContractContributor.contribute_sync()` to accept and use the `language` parameter from agent config

This would be a natural extension of the i18n infrastructure already in place for scroll prompts, and would give non-English users a fully localized system prompt experience.

## Environment

- QwenPaw deployed via platform.agentscope.io
- `language: zh` set in agent config
- Observed English protected execution contract in system prompt despite Chinese language setting

prs.title: feat(models): add TypeSafe decision model configuration
prs.body:
## Description

Add TypeSafe/JEV as a configurable decision-model provider, with separate global defaults for chat and decision models. Model type (`chat` or `decision`) is independent of image, audio, video, and tool capabilities and can be edited for any provider.

- Reuse provider credentials, discovery, and connection-test controls. TypeSafe discovers models through `/models` and tests them with a minimal native `/systemone` request.

- Keep the conversation picker focused on chat models. A collapsed Advanced options section contains a Use decision model switch. Its default follows the agent; a session can enable the agent's model or fall back to the global decision model. Missing decision configuration never prevents normal chat.

The conversation switch stores a preference only. Decision execution and automatic tool selection are outside this PR.

prs.title: fix(task_tracker): bound the run completion callback and always clean up
prs.body:
## Description

Fixes the **run-cleanup half** of #8173: a chat run whose completion callback hangs or is cancelled never releases its entry in `TaskTracker._runs`, so the run stays `running` forever.

### Root cause

`TaskTracker._producer` clears its `_runs` entry and pushes the end-of-stream sentinel at the end of a `finally` block, *after* awaiting the `on_finished` completion callback. Two paths meant that cleanup never completed:

1. **The callback hangs.** `on_finished` is `ChatManager.mark_chat_finished`, which persists a completion marker under a lock shared with ~24 other manager methods. Lock contention or a stalled repo suspends the producer task *inside its own `finally`*. The task is then not done **and** the entry is still registered, so every status reader reports `running` — workspace reload is blocked and inbound messages are dropped with HTTP 409.
2. **The producer is cancelled mid-callback.** `CancelledError` is a `BaseException`, so it escapes the `except Exception` guard and skips cleanup entirely, leaving subscriber streams without their sentinel.

### The fix

- Run the callback through `asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.shield(...))` bounded by `ON_FINISHED_TIMEOUT`, so a hung callback is logged and given up on rather than holding the run open.
- Move the cleanup into a nested `finally` so it always runs.

**Related Issue:** Relates to #8173

Deliberately *not* `Fixes` — see the scope note below.

### Scope — what this does **not** fix

This addresses the cleanup leak only. The other items from #8173 are **not** implemented here: the post-spawn connection health probe, the idle watchdog, `force` semantics on the reload/disable-enable paths, and in-channel hints for `/new` and `/stop` on backends that do not support them. Those are larger design questions and I would rather land the narrow fix first.

Note that the wedge is now **bounded** by `ON_FINISHED_TIMEOUT` rather than eliminated: the run stays `running` while the callback runs, because `test_attach_or_start_reports_completion_before_becoming_idle` pins that ordering deliberately (it asserts `get_status == "running"` from inside the callback). Reordering the pop ahead of the callback would break that contract.

### Tests

New `tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py` (6 tests) covers a hung callback, a callback that raises, a callback that raises `TimeoutError`, a producer cancelled mid-callback, and `request_stop` against a slow callback. Waits are event-based rather than fixed sleeps.

Against unmodified source these fail on behavioural assertions (`run entry survived a hung completion callback`, etc.), not on import or attribute errors; with the patch they pass.

- targeted file: **4 failed, 1 passed** on unmodified source → **23 passed** with the patch
- `tests/unit/app`: **3118 passed, 1 skipped**

### Security Considerations

Not applicable — no change to channel auth, credentials, or config handling.

prs.body:
PawApps can now expose durable work to Main Chat and their own UI through the same scoped Host contract. Small Apps register an `app.action` handler; external runtimes keep the adapter protocol. Host owns task identity, retries, permissions, setup, questions, results, artifacts, and continuation delivery.

The implementation adds generated Python/JSON Schema/TypeScript contracts, schema-checked structured results, scoped Python and frontend clients, and a managed execution journal with explicit restart policy. File Browser demonstrates the small-App integration. Data's legacy session routes enforce user/workspace ownership; artifacts remain reusable across sessions within their authorized user/workspace/App scope. Creator retains its public video workflow, approval/setup gates, and canonical final-film artifact checks.

Compatibility and migration:
- The exact published Engine revision is pinned in `tests/fixtures/pawapp-compatibility.json`; the Host requires `scoped_sessions` and fails closed against older Engines.
- Existing descriptor/event digests and Data origin identities remain compatible. Managed storage is additive.
- File Browser's new `browse-directory` action needs its own grant; the old action remains private for recovery.
- Cold App loads install Host hooks before rendering. Managed streams cannot miss a concurrent terminal event. Nested custom working directories retain stable paths across restart.

prs.title: fix(telegram): render every fenced code block as code in HTML
prs.body:
## Description `markdown_to_telegram_html` found fenced code blocks with ```` r"```(\w*)\n?(.*?)```" ````. That pattern mishandles common shapes of model output (details and a reproduction table in #8011): - **Info strings with symbols.** ```` ```c++ ```` rendered as `
++\n…`, and ```` ```objective-c ```` as `language-objective` with a stray `-c` line.
- **`~~~` fences weren't protected**, so their contents were formatted as prose: `# setup` became `setup`, and `__init__` became `init`.
- **A longer fence around a ``` example** closed at the inner ```, leaving an empty `
`, the example leaked as formatted text, and a stray backtick.

The fix adds a line scan, `_replace_fenced_blocks`, that runs before the existing regex:
- A block opens on ``` or `~~~` (a backtick fence's info string can't contain a backtick).
- The language is the info string's first word.
- The block closes on a line holding only a run of the same character that is at least as long.

One-line ```` ```code``` ```` and unclosed fences are left to the existing regex. I compared old and new output on plain fences, no-language fences, unclosed fences, one-line fences, consecutive blocks and a mixed-formatting sample: those six shapes are byte-identical.

Other fence shapes change too. Most are fixes, and each one that matters is now pinned by a test:
- **CRLF input:** `main` left a phantom empty first code line (`\r\nx = 1…`), and now the code starts at `x = 1`.
- **A closing run longer than the opener** no longer leaves a stray backtick.
- **An info string with attributes** (```` ```python {.highlight} ````) no longer leaks the attribute text into the first code line.
- Trailing whitespace on a closing fence is accepted, ```` ``` python ```` (leading space) gets a language class, and backticks or `~~~` inside a longer fence stay code.
- **An unclosed fence** now runs until a bare closing run, as in CommonMark. A later ```` ```bash ```` line is code, not a close, so one unclosed fence captures the rest of the message. On `main` it closed at ```` ```bash ```` and leaked the rest as prose.
- **Minor:** a fence indented under a list item now renders its `
` at column 0 instead of under the bullet. Telegram shows `
` as a block either way.

**Attribute escaping:** the language now comes from the info string's first word, which can contain quotes, so it is escaped as an attribute value (`_escape_attr`: `& < > " '`). ```` ```a"onmouseover="alert(1) ```` renders as `class="language-a"onmouseover="alert(1)"`. Real language names render as before.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8011

**Security Considerations:** None. Code content goes through the same `_escape_html` as before.

prs.body:
## Description

Hey, I'm Juampi from the Firecrawl team.

Adds Firecrawl as a third `web_search` provider next to the two existing ones.

1. `FirecrawlProvider` posts to `https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/search` through the existing `_post` helper and maps `data.web[]` to the same `title` / `url` / `snippet` / `content` shape the other providers return. The API key is optional and is read from the credential store at `tool/web_search/firecrawl`.
2. The provider is selectable in the Console modal and in the router options. The current default stays the default.
3. The existing quota hint now shows only for the provider it was written for.

No new dependency. No change to `web_fetch`, the MCP templates or the credential store.

**Related Issue:** Relates to #8199

**Security Considerations:** The key is read from the existing per-agent credential store and sent only as a Bearer header to `api.firecrawl.dev`. It is not logged. Tests use fake keys.

Tests  9 passed (9)

pytest tests/unit   (files that touch the OS keychain excluded)

```

The one failure, `tests/unit/security/tool_guard/test_safety_checks.py::TestIsCommandDestructive::test_b1_normalize_before_home_glob_match`, also fails on a clean `main`.

`pre-commit run --files` on the changed files: all hooks pass. A full `--all-files` run also reports two pylint `E1120` errors in `src/qwenpaw/sandbox/runtime_boundary.py`, which this PR doesn't touch.

New tests cover factory routing, the request body and headers with and without a key, reading the key from the credential store (including a changed key), response parsing, a missing `data.web`, `success: false`, HTTP errors such as 429, the router credential ref, and the Console modal not carrying one provider's key into another when the key fetch fails.

There is no providers list in the docs to extend, so I didn't change the docs.

## Evidence

Ran `qwenpaw app` on a clean working dir, set the web_search provider to `firecrawl` through the tool config endpoint, then called `web_search` for "what is Firecrawl web scraping API".

Without an API key:

[1] Firecrawl | Web Data API for AI Agents

    URL: https://github.com/firecrawl/firecrawl
```

prs.title: feat(tools): add structured human-in-the-loop questions
prs.body:
## Description

Add the built-in `ask_user_question` tool so an agent can pause its current invocation, collect structured answers from a person, and continue in the same turn. The implementation reuses AgentScope 2.0.10's `AskUserParams`, `AskUserAnswer`, and `AskUserMetadata`, with QwenPaw's existing ApprovalService providing the host-side wait and answer delivery.

The Console and desktop show one question at a time, retain answers during previous/next navigation, and submit one complete batch. The form supports single/multiple selections, option descriptions, question context, single-select previews, client-provided free text, and seven locales. Chat and Inbox share the form.

Recommendations follow the framework's existing convention: the model puts its recommended option first and appends `(Recommended)` to the label. The UI displays a localized recommendation badge and the option's explanation. It neither invents a recommendation nor preselects it; users may choose another option. Selection and structured answers preserve the full original label. No custom `recommended` schema field is introduced.

**Related Issue:** Relates to #6274. Related alternative implementation: #6384.

### Scope and framework integration

- Reuse the framework's question/answer contracts through the existing host approval bridge; no external-tool execution loop is introduced.
- Same-agent `spawn_subagent` questions surface in the root session. Cross-configuration/remote agents, unattended cron/heartbeat/mail runs, and ACP/TUI without a supported answer surface return before waiting.
- Inter-agent delegation carries an explicit origin marker, including matching agent IDs and nested workers, so it cannot be mistaken for a direct human conversation.
- Console submissions and IM `/approve` / `/approval approve` commands use the existing resolution path. SUCCESS, refusal (DENIED), stopping (INTERRUPTED), missing answers, delivery failure, timeout and stale/replayed calls remain distinguishable.

**Security Considerations:** AGENT identity policy and the existing approval API authentication/authorization remain in force. Asking for information requires no separate security approval. An answer does not create an Always Allow rule or authorize a later sensitive action. Ordinary user refusal does not trigger sandbox recovery.

Check a marked recommendation and an unmarked question, choose either the recommended option, an alternative or free text, review previous/next questions and submit the whole batch. prs.title: feat(plugins): add clean unload and rollback-safe hot reload
prs.body:
## Description

Add a clean plugin unload path and rollback-safe hot reload so plugin install / update / uninstall no longer rebuilds every live workspace, and a failed update does not leave users on a half-applied new version.

This PR introduces a two-layer teardown ledger (`PluginInstance`) and a `PluginLifecycle` facade (`load` / `unload` / `reload` / `update_config`):

- Official `register_*` entries record real teardowns (HTTP, provider, control command, middleware, prompt section, channel, tools, hooks). Workspace contributions are projected and revoked by name via `WorkspaceProjector` (`start_one` / `stop_one` for channels). Uninstall no longer calls `_schedule_all_agents_reload`.
- Unload modes (`shutdown` / `unload` / `uninstall`) share one ledger. Author shutdown / uninstall hooks run before table rows are dropped. `shutdown` only stops hosted resources (`custody` / `effect`) and does not clear tables or disk.
- Reload probes new code into `plugin_<id>__probe` first; import failure does not tear down the old instance. Hosted resources that do not go quiescent abort the swap. Rollback restores the previous directory / modules and does not run legacy uninstall hooks. Boot recovers interrupted “updating” / “migrating” markers.
- `update_config` rebuilds contributions without reimporting; a half-successful `register()` is torn down before the old config is restored. Disable is `config.plugins[<id>].enabled = false` (reserved framework key).
- Boot dependency policy is local-only: missing deps mark the plugin `FAILED` without installing. Explicit install / update / `POST /plugins/{id}/repair-dependencies` still go through `DependencyGate` (imported host-package blacklist → require restart). Console repair / status UI is intentionally not wired.
- CloudPaw no longer monkeypatches `PluginLoader.unload_plugin`; agent cleanup is an `api.provision` teardown (uninstall only).
- `LifecycleDelegate` is the single predicate at the reserved branch points (`owns_commit` / `owns_dependency_env` / `notify_unload`). Name collisions fail loudly and name the occupant.

Out of scope (documented as deferred): `SourceWatcher`, dry-run / interval-intersection gate enhancements, and Console repair / last-unload UI.

**Security Considerations:** Dependency installation stays gated: boot never networks when deps are already satisfied; colliding with an already-imported host package (e.g. `httpx`) refuses the install and does not write site-packages. Unload / reload only revoke registrations owned by the plugin id; user `agent.json` / provisioned files are not deleted on `mode=unload`. Provision / directory swap are skipped when `owns_commit` is false.

## Type of Change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [x] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Checklist

- [ ] I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and it passes
- [x] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks
- [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass
- [ ] Documentation updated (if needed)
- [ ] Ready for review

### For Channel Changes (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Console, etc.)

- [ ] I ran `./scripts/check-channels.sh` (or `./scripts/check-channels.sh --changed`) and it passes
- [ ] **Contract test** exists in `tests/contract/channels/test_<channel>_contract.py` (REQUIRED)
- [ ] Contract test implements `create_instance()` with proper channel initialization
- [ ] All 19 contract verification points pass (see `tests/contract/channels/__init__.py`)
- [ ] **Optional**: Unit tests in `tests/unit/channels/test_<channel>.py` for complex internal logic

## Testing

1. Unit: `pytest tests/unit/plugins/ -q` (lifecycle, reload rollback, workspace revoke, config update, ledger teardowns).
2. Unload a loaded plugin via `DELETE /plugins/{id}` (or unload without delete) while a conversation is in progress — tools / commands / channels contributed by that plugin disappear by name; the workspace is not rebuilt; `agent.json` is unchanged on `mode=unload`.
3. Force-update a plugin whose new entry has a syntax error or whose `register()` raises — the previous version stays loaded; user-edited provision files stay on disk.
4. Kill the process mid-update (directory swap) and restart — boot restores the backup from the “updating” marker.
5. Boot offline with a plugin whose `requirements.txt` is missing — that plugin is `FAILED`; others still load. `POST /plugins/{id}/repair-dependencies` installs when the user explicitly asks.
6. `PATCH /plugins/{id}/enabled` with `{"enabled": false}` unloads the instance without renaming the plugin directory.

## Additional Notes

- `update_config` is a separate path and does not add a fourth unload mode.
- `enabled` is a reserved framework key and is stripped before `plugin.register()`.
- Repair HTTP is `POST /plugins/{id}/repair-dependencies` only; do not add a second endpoint. Console does not expose a repair button or last-unload report in this PR.
- `unregister_plugin` remains a leftover safety sweep; ledger teardowns are the primary path.

## Description

Add a JSON-driven evaluation website with direction, benchmark and overall rankings, cost/performance charts, SDK history, filtering and downloadable records. The external runner submits raw per-task observations; all score aggregation belongs to this website.

The strict v3 contract accepts arbitrary benchmark IDs, dataset revisions, complete task identities, terminal statuses, raw scores, model budgets, judge metadata, provenance and original-currency costs. Final execution, infrastructure, timeout, scoring and artifact failures count as zero with a fixed task denominator. Missing benchmarks remain incomplete rather than zero; unknown costs remain unknown.

Versioned index definitions assign each benchmark to one direction. Benchmark weights are normalized within that direction, then fixed direction weights produce the overall score. The initial research, office, coding and general directions each weigh 25%. Adding a benchmark creates a new definition while preserving historical definitions. Compatible historical observations are reused by date and provenance; missing observations require backfill, never selection by highest score. CNY costs use the declared fixed rate of 7 CNY per USD, with original amounts retained.

Official and testing records remain separate. The real leaderboard starts empty; `/evaluation/demo/` uses explicitly labeled synthetic data. No private observations, credentials, internal snapshots or trajectories are committed. The contract accepts v3 only.

## Validation

- Full website build passes: JSON validation, TypeScript, search index, Vite and static routes.
- Eleven actual runner-produced smoke observations validate against v3; temporary inputs removed afterward.
- Integration verification covers failure-as-zero, fixed direction weights, missing benchmark coverage, historical definitions, later backfill and duplicate task rejection.
- Browser verification confirms office scores stay unchanged when research expands, incomplete new definitions remain unranked, and historical definition scores remain available.
- Runner lifecycle suite: 26 passing cases covering raw observations, terminal failures, exact-protocol reuse, billing and OSS recovery.
- Formatting and git diff checks pass. Existing plotting bundle size warning remains.

## Security Considerations

CI validation uses read-only permissions and no secrets. Public source links cannot contain credentials or query strings. Testing/official classification is not access control; only reviewed public observations belong in this repository.

- Hand admitted speech to the ordinary Chat execution path so history, tools, long-running work, queueing, persistence, and rendering remain shared.

- Add provider-neutral realtime contracts plus a DashScope adapter with recoverable idle-close handling and automatic reconnect.
- Persist Voice capability in the existing Chat metadata while keeping `source="chat"`, including migration of early development records for downgrade safety.

## Module Layout

Two-layer split — provider-neutral vendor layer vs. application orchestration:

- `providers/realtime_voice/` — vendor-neutral contracts (`RealtimeProviderSession`, `ProviderEvent`, `RealtimeSessionConfig`) plus the DashScope adapter. No application dependencies.
- `app/realtime_voice/` — orchestration: `VoiceCoordinator`, `VoiceTaskBridge`, `SpokenTurnCommitter`, `PresentationQueue`. Pure prompt building lives in `prompts.py`; user-facing text and ordinals in `labels.py`.
- `app/routers/realtime_voice.py` — HTTP/WS boundary only, no business logic.

Input vs. reply source of truth: `runtime/input_context.py` (`ChatInputContext`) owns committed input identity/order and admission status; `runtime/reply_cycle.py` (`ReplyCycleContext`) owns run and reply identity. `InputStateEvent` flows one-way from the reply cycle into the input context as a read-only projection.

prs.title: fix(chat): truncate oversized tool outputs when serving chat history
prs.body:
## Description

Chat history responses can exceed 10 MB because file and screenshot tool outputs are persisted as **base64 inside `tool_result`** blocks. Serving them verbatim makes the console's fixed 30 s request timeout fail reliably on slow links: on a 5 Mbps link a single 13.3 MB response (`send_file_to_user` + `view_image` in a 6-message chat, 96 % of the payload base64) already takes ≥21 s in the ideal case and exceeds 30 s under loss — the fetch is aborted (`retries = 0`), the transcript never renders and no error toast is shown. See the issue for the full reproduction (rate-limited proxy shows the abort at exactly 30.3 s).

This PR caps oversized `tool_result` outputs **when serving chat history** (not at storage time and not for other consumers): each output is truncated to 64 KB with an explicit marker, so a 13.3 MB response drops to ~3.4 MB; combined with the upstream response-compression middleware (#7917, already in main) it becomes ~2 MB and transfers in ~3.3 s at 5 Mbps — comfortably inside the 30 s timeout.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8228

**Security Considerations:** None — no credentials or private data involved; this only bounds the size of what is served to the console.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills

- [ ] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass
- [ ] Documentation updated (if needed)
- [x] Ready for review

> Notes on environment: this container has no `pytest` / dev toolchain installed (offline constraint). I verified the change with an equivalent standalone Python script against the real 13 MB session data (output below) and added pytest cases that will run on CI. `pre-commit` was not available locally; changes are small and follow the surrounding code style.

## Testing

Run the new and existing conversion tests:

```bash
pytest tests/unit/app/chats/test_msg_block_conversion.py -q
# (CI) will run the full unit suite
```

Local equivalent verification (standalone Python against the repo `src` + real session data):

```
[1] truncate=True  -> truncated, final len = 65601
[2] default False  -> unchanged, final len = 66560
[3] small + True   -> unchanged, final len = 100
[4] real 13MB session: full=13.24MB -> truncated=3.37MB (75% smaller)
[5] gzip(truncated response) = 2.06MB (at 5Mbps ~3.3s ideal)
ALL CHECKS PASSED
```

## Evidence

Standalone script output reproducing the fix against the real affected session (the 13.1 MB session JSON used in the issue):

```bash
$ python - <<'PY'
# (see Testing section; script uses agentscope_msg_to_message with the
#  new truncate_oversized_outputs flag on the real session file)
[1] truncate=True  -> truncated, final len = 65601
[2] default False  -> unchanged, final len = 66560
[3] small + True   -> unchanged, final len = 100
[4] real 13MB session: full=13.24MB -> truncated=3.37MB (75% smaller)
[5] gzip(truncated response) = 2.06MB (at 5Mbps ~3.3s ideal)
ALL CHECKS PASSED
```

New pytest cases (will run on CI):

```bash
tests/unit/app/chats/test_msg_block_conversion.py::test_tool_result_oversized_output_truncated_when_requested

tests/unit/app/chats/test_msg_block_conversion.py::test_tool_result_small_output_kept_when_truncation_requested
```

## Additional Notes

- The backend still returns the full history (no pagination) — #7361 covers that independently and is complementary, not required for this fix.
- Other callers of `agentscope_msg_to_message` (proactive-trigger inspection, PawApp context serialization) keep byte-for-byte behavior because the new flag defaults to False.
- The response-compression half of the fix already landed in main via #7917 (`ResponseCompressionMiddleware`, gzip for `application/json` full bodies, streams excluded).

prs.title: fix(console): echo the user's own message as the first frame of a new run stream
prs.body:
## Description

When a chat turn is started from the mobile app (or another console tab), the web console shows no user bubble until the turn finishes: the run stream only carries the assistant's frames, and the user's own message is persisted to history only at run completion (`append_turn`), so mid-run views are blind to it. Worse, before this PR the console could not even **attach** to a run it did not start — an opened chat simply waited for its next history reload.

The first commit of this PR added the server-side half: a `user_message` **echo frame** as the first frame of a new run stream (and therefore included in every reconnect replay). Its original docstring assumed *"the console chat SDK … ignores stream frames it does not recognize."* **That assumption is wrong**, and it was confirmed by a live deployment: the console chat SDK's response builder routes any frame without a recognized `object` field to its **error path**, which fails the entire stream — every chat in the console died with "Answers have stopped". The remaining three commits are the verified console-side design that makes the feature actually work.

### What this PR does

Four commits, two layers (all verified end-to-end against a live deployment):

**Server (`src/qwenpaw/app/routers/console.py`)** — commits 1–2

1. A `user_message` echo frame (no `object` field, same shape as `turn_usage` / `replay_end`) is emitted as the **first frame** of every new run stream, and sits in the per-run TaskTracker buffer, so every reconnect replay re-sends it.
2. The frame carries identity fields so a client without a local echo can key its pending user message:
   - `chat_id` — the backend chat UUID (the key the console's pending cache and history patching use);
   - `session_id` — echoed from the request;
   - `client_message_id` — echoed back from the sender's request metadata (`qwenpaw_client_message_id`) when present, letting the console confirm persistence by unique id instead of text.
3. The docstring states the contract explicitly: consumers must special-case the frame; the RN client is *expected* to ignore it (verification on the RN side still open — see below).

**Console (`console/src/pages/Chat/`)** — commits 2–4

*Commit 2 (`049a4319`) — own-turn safety.* The chat `responseParser` special-cases `user_message` frames **before** anything reaches the SDK builder: it extracts `text` / typed `content` (text, image_url, file_name, file, data), calls the existing `sessionApi.setLastUserMessage(chat_id, text, content, client_message_id)`, and returns `null` — a safe no-op for every SDK consumer. The existing `patchLastUserMessage` pass (run on every history load while `generating`) renders the user card from that cache and clears it once the persisted history contains the turn (matched by `client_message_id`, falling back to text). No new rendering path, no new cache.

*Commit 3 (`7506018d`) — live attach + live external bubble.* Two mechanisms:
- **Auto-attach.** The sidebar's 3s session-list poll already flips the opened chat's status to `"running"`. When the current tab holds no active run for that chat, the page calls `controller.resume({ sessionId })` — the existing reconnect path — joining the run's SSE stream, which replays the leading echo frame plus the assistant output so far. `resume()` is idempotent when a run lifecycle already exists.
- **External user projection.** A `user_message` frame whose text is **not** in the local pending cache (i.e. the turn started elsewhere) is projected inline as a `user_echo` message frame (`role: "user"`, `status: "completed"`) inside the in-flight response. A new `UserEchoBubble` component renders it through the response `render` slot: a user card while the response is in flight, replaced by the persisted history once the turn lands. `sessionApi` gains the read-only pending-entry peek used for the own/external decision.

*Commit 4 (`4dc22bb8`) — two live-verified fixes.*
- **Own-send bubble suppression.** The echo branch originally wrote the pending cache *before* peeking the pending entry, consuming the very message the send handler later looked up — the user's own bubble disappeared on own-send. Fixed by **peek-before-set**: the pending map is now read-only in the echo path, and a regression test asserts the bubble renders exactly once on both the send path and the echo path.
- **Auto-attach re-trigger.** The original guard (`getActiveRun(chatId)`) missed on the first poll tick — the run lifecycle is keyed by the frontend session id, not the backend chat id — and re-fired after the run settled while the status feed was still stale, opening a second stream and leaving an orphaned three-dot spinner. Replaced with a **triple guard**: (1) attach only on the rising edge of a bounded per-chat status map (`undefined → running`, map capped at 100 entries), (2) skip when a run lifecycle is already active for the chat, (3) skip when the active messages already contain a `generating` assistant message.

### Why this is safe (behavior matrix)

| View | Before this PR | After this PR |
|------|---------------|---------------|
| Console, turn started in **this** tab | local optimistic bubble (unchanged) | echo frame → idempotent rewrite of the **same** pending cache entry; peek-before-set guarantees the send path still finds its message → **exactly one bubble, no suppression, no duplicate** |
| Console, turn started **elsewhere**, opened/attached mid-run | assistant stream only after manual reload; no user bubble ever mid-run | auto-attach joins the stream (replay includes the echo) → `user_echo` card rendered **while the run is in flight**; replaced by persisted history at completion, no duplication |
| Console, stale `"running"` status ticks after run settle | n/a | rising-edge + active-run + generating guards → **no second stream, no orphaned spinner** |
| Console, attached after run finished | full history (already persisted) | unchanged — history contains the turn, cache is empty |
| SDK response builder | crashed on the frame-less echo ("Answers have stopped") | never sees the frame (parser consumes it first) |
| Mobile app | — | expected to ignore the unknown frame type (to be verified on the RN side; the console assumption was wrong once already, so the docstring says so explicitly) |

### Evidence

- **Server**: `PYTHONPATH=src pytest tests/unit/app` — **3109 passed, 2 skipped** (without `PYTHONPATH=src` the test process imports the installed baseline package, not the worktree — the reconnect test file must be run with it). The echo test asserts `chat_id` / `session_id` / `client_message_id` on the frame.
- **Console**: `vitest run src/pages/Chat` — **59 files / 823 passed** (includes the new `responseParser` cases, the auto-attach guard cases, and the peek-before-set regression/negative-control cases).
- **Build**: `npm run build` (tsc + vite + verify:monaco-css + precompress + verify:initial-bundle) — green; the built bundle is the one used for all live checks below.
- **Live dual-path curl** (deployed build, 10/10 assertions): originating stream's first frame is the echo with all three identity fields and exactly one echo per stream; a reconnect issued mid-run replays the echo before `replay_end` plus the full assistant stream.
- **Live browser E2E** (deployed build, final code):
  1. *Own-send*: single user bubble, reply completes, **0** "Answers have stopped", **0** residual spinners.
  2. *External turn* (run started by a separate client; console opens the chat mid-run): auto-attach streams the assistant output **in real time** (mid-run sampling shows partial output) and renders the external user bubble live; clean completion, 0 spinners, 0 interrupted alerts.
  3. *Negative controls*: guard-disabled build attaches exactly once per run (no double stream); guard-enabled build produces no orphaned spinner on stale status ticks.

### Open item

- **React Native client**: this repository does not contain the RN client source, so its handling of the unknown `user_message` frame type (expected: ignore) has not been verified. The server docstring and commit message flag this explicitly.

---

## Description

当一轮对话从移动端（或另一个 console tab）发起时，web console 在 turn 结束前看不到 user 气泡：run 流只带助手的帧，而用户自己的消息直到 run 结束才持久化进历史（`append_turn`），所以 run 进行中视图是"盲"的。更糟的是，本 PR 之前 console 甚至无法 **attach** 到它自己没有发起的 run——打开的 chat 只能等下一次历史刷新。

本 PR 的第一个 commit 加了服务端一半：`user_message` **echo 帧**作为新 run 流的首帧（因此也进入每次重连回放）。它最初的 docstring 假设*"console chat SDK……会忽略它不认识的流帧"*。**这个假设是错的**，并被一次真实部署证实：console chat SDK 的 response builder 把任何没有可识别 `object` 字段的帧路由到**错误路径**，导致整条流失败——console 里所有 chat 都死于 "Answers have stopped"。其余三个 commit 是让这个功能真正可用的、经过验证的 console 侧设计。

### 本 PR 做了什么

四个 commit，两层（全部对真实部署做过端到端验证）：

**服务端（`src/qwenpaw/app/routers/console.py`）** — commit 1–2

1. `user_message` echo 帧（无 `object` 字段，与 `turn_usage` / `replay_end` 同构）作为每个新 run 流的**首帧**发出，并驻留在 per-run TaskTracker buffer 中，因此每次重连回放都会重新发送它。
2. 帧携带身份字段，让没有本地 echo 的客户端能给 pending 用户消息建立索引：
   - `chat_id` — 后端 chat UUID（console 的 pending 缓存与历史 patch 用的 key）；
   - `session_id` — 从请求原样回带；
   - `client_message_id` — 发送方请求元数据（`qwenpaw_client_message_id`）存在时回带，让 console 用唯一 id 而非文本确认持久化。
3. docstring 明确写出契约：消费方必须特判该帧；RN 客户端*预期*忽略它（RN 侧验证仍未完成——见下）。

**Console（`console/src/pages/Chat/`）** — commit 2–4

*Commit 2（`049a4319`）— 本 tab turn 安全。* chat 的 `responseParser` 在**任何内容到达 SDK builder 之前**特判 `user_message` 帧：提取 `text` / 类型化 `content`（text、image_url、file_name、file、data），调用既有的 `sessionApi.setLastUserMessage(chat_id, text, content, client_message_id)`，然后返回 `null`——对所有 SDK 消费方都是安全 no-op。既有的 `patchLastUserMessage` 通道（`generating` 期间每次历史加载都跑）从该缓存渲染用户卡片，并在持久化历史包含该 turn 后清空（按 `client_message_id` 匹配，退化为文本匹配）。无新渲染路径，无新缓存。

*Commit 3（`7506018d`）— 实时 attach + 外部气泡实时投影。* 两个机制：
- **Auto-attach。** sidebar 的 3 秒会话列表轮询本来就会把打开的 chat 状态翻成 `"running"`。当当前 tab 对该 chat 没有活跃 run 时，页面调用 `controller.resume({ sessionId })`——既有的重连路径——加入该 run 的 SSE 流；流会回放首帧 echo 以及到目前为止的助手输出。已存在 run 生命周期时 `resume()` 是幂等的。
- **外部用户投影。** 文本**不在**本地 pending 缓存中的 `user_message` 帧（即 turn 在别处发起）被内联投影为一个 `user_echo` 消息帧（`role: "user"`、`status: "completed"`），位于 in-flight response 内。新的 `UserEchoBubble` 组件通过 response 的 `render` slot 渲染它：response 进行中显示用户卡片，turn 落盘后被持久化历史替换。`sessionApi` 新增只读的 pending 条目 peek，供本 tab/外部判定使用。

*Commit 4（`4dc22bb8`）— 两处实测修复。*
- **own-send 气泡被吞。** echo 分支原先在 *peek* pending 条目**之前**就写 pending 缓存，把 send handler 稍后要查的那条消息消费掉了——用户自己发的气泡在 own-send 时消失。修复为 **peek-before-set**：echo 路径对 pending map 只读，回归测试断言气泡在 send 路径与 echo 路径上各恰好渲染一次。
- **Auto-attach 重复触发。** 原守卫（`getActiveRun(chatId)`）在首个轮询 tick 必然 miss——run 生命周期按前端 session id 建键，不是后端 chat id——并且 run 结束后状态源还陈旧时再次触发，开出第二条流、留下孤儿三点 spinner。替换为**三重守卫**：(1) 仅在受限 per-chat 状态表的上升沿 attach（`undefined → running`，表上限 100 条）；(2) 该 chat 已有活跃 run 生命周期时跳过；(3) 活跃消息中已含 `generating` 助手消息时跳过。

### 为什么安全（行为矩阵）

| 视图 | 本 PR 之前 | 本 PR 之后 |
|------|-----------|-----------|
| Console，turn 在**本 tab** 发起 | 本地乐观气泡（不变） | echo 帧 → 对**同一条** pending 缓存条目做幂等重写；peek-before-set 保证 send 路径仍能找到它的消息 → **恰好一个气泡，不丢、不重** |
| Console，turn 在**别处**发起，run 中途打开/attach | 手动刷新后才有助手流；run 中永远没有用户气泡 | auto-attach 加入流（回放含 echo）→ run **进行中**渲染 `user_echo` 卡片；结束后被持久化历史替换，不重复 |
| Console，run 结束后陈旧的 `"running"` 状态 tick | n/a | 上升沿 + 活跃 run + generating 三重守卫 → **无第二条流、无孤儿 spinner** |
| Console，run 结束后才 attach | 完整历史（已持久化） | 不变——历史含该 turn，缓存为空 |
| SDK response builder | 遇到无帧型 echo 崩溃（"Answers have stopped"） | 永远看不到该帧（parser 先消费掉） |
| 移动端 app | — | 预期忽略未知帧类型（待 RN 侧验证；console 侧的假设已经错过一次，docstring 因此明确写出） |

### 证据（Evidence）

- **服务端**：`PYTHONPATH=src pytest tests/unit/app` — **3109 passed, 2 skipped**（不带 `PYTHONPATH=src` 时测试进程导入的是已安装的基线包而非 worktree——重连测试文件必须带着跑）。echo 测试断言帧上的 `chat_id` / `session_id` / `client_message_id`。
- **Console**：`vitest run src/pages/Chat` — **59 files / 823 passed**（含新增的 `responseParser` 用例、auto-attach 守卫用例、peek-before-set 回归/负向对应用例）。
- **构建**：`npm run build`（tsc + vite + verify:monaco-css + precompress + verify:initial-bundle）— 全绿；以下所有 live 检查用的就是这份构建产物。
- **Live 双路 curl**（部署版，10/10 断言）：源流首帧为带全部三个身份字段的 echo、每流恰好一个 echo；run 中途发起的重连在 `replay_end` 之前回放 echo 及完整助手流。
- **Live 浏览器 E2E**（部署版，最终代码）：
  1. *Own-send*：单个用户气泡、回复完整收尾、**0** "Answers have stopped"、**0** 残留 spinner。
  2. *外部 turn*（另一客户端发起 run；console 在 run 中途打开该 chat）：auto-attach **实时**流出助手输出（run 中途采样可见部分输出），并实时渲染外部用户气泡；干净收尾，0 spinner、0 interrupted 告警。
  3. *负向对照*：守卫关闭的构建每次 run 恰好 attach 一次（无双流）；守卫开启的构建在陈旧状态 tick 下不产生孤儿 spinner。

### 未完成项

- **React Native 客户端**：本仓库不含 RN 客户端源码，其对未知 `user_message` 帧类型的处理（预期：忽略）尚未验证。服务端 docstring 与 commit 说明中均已明确标注。

## Release Notes

- Fixed: the console chat page crashing ("Answers have stopped") on run streams carrying the `user_message` echo frame — the frame is now consumed by the chat UI before it can reach the SDK response builder.
- New: user messages from mobile-app / other-tab turns appear in the console **while the run is in flight** (auto-attach + live user-bubble projection), not only after the run finishes.
- Fixed: own-send user bubbles being suppressed by the echo path, and auto-attach re-triggering on stale status ticks (orphaned spinner).


---

- 修复：console 聊天页在携带 `user_message` echo 帧的 run 流上崩溃（"Answers have stopped"）——该帧现在在到达 SDK response builder 之前就被聊天 UI 消费掉。
- 新增：移动端/其他 tab 发起的对话，其用户消息在 **run 进行中**就出现在 console（auto-attach + 用户气泡实时投影），而不只是 run 结束后。
- 修复：own-send 用户气泡被 echo 路径吞掉的问题，以及 auto-attach 在陈旧状态 tick 上重复触发（孤儿 spinner）的问题。

prs.title: fix(creator): close project logging before directory delete
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On Windows, deleting a Creator project fails with `503 STORAGE_INTEGRITY_ERROR` / `WinError 5` once that project's `creator.log` has been opened. `delete_project` renamed the project directory via `atomic_replace_path` / `os.replace` **before** releasing the per-project log handler (`close_creator_project_logging`) and the poller. Windows refuses to rename a directory that contains an open file, and on failure the close never ran — so the project stayed undeletable for the life of the process.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8206

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (Creator plugin)
- [x] Tests

## Checklist

- [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` as relevant) and they pass
- [x] Ready for review

## What Changed

In `plugins/apps/qwenpaw-creator/backend/api/project_routes.py::delete_project`, close the poller and per-project logging **before** calling `services.projects.delete`, so the open `creator.log` handle is released ahead of the directory rename.

## Evidence

Portable regression test simulates the Windows denial: while the project log path is still in `_FILE_HANDLER._targets`, `atomic_replace_path` raises `PermissionError(5, "Access is denied")`.

**Before the fix** (test fails with 503):

```
AssertionError: ... STORAGE_INTEGRITY_ERROR ... Cannot delete Project: ...
assert 503 == 204
PermissionError: [Errno 5] Access is denied
```

**After the fix:**

```
tests/api/test_delete_closes_logging_before_rename.py + tests/api/test_projects.py
10 passed
```

## Testing

```bash
pytest tests/api/test_delete_closes_logging_before_rename.py tests/api/test_projects.py
```

Happy to adjust if maintainers prefer a different approach (e.g. relocating per-project logs outside the project tree).
