releases.body:
## What's Changed

## ✨ Added

**Console & Workspaces**

- Add six theme palettes and custom colors and corner radii, with live preview and saved preferences ([#7741](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7741))
- Add an authenticated, multi-tab terminal inside Chat, with a working directory for each conversation ([#7861](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7861))
- Allow Console font size to be adjusted from 12 to 20 pixels across chat and settings ([#8005](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8005))
- Save multi-folder workspaces as an Agent’s default for future tasks ([#7789](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7789))
- Show files delivered by the Agent directly below its reply for easier preview and download ([#7750](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7750))

**QwenPaw-Flash**

- Recommend QwenPaw-Flash 9B, 27B, and 35B-A3B locally: update the 9B recommendation and add 27B and 35B-A3B options ([#8155](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8155))

**PawPort**

- Add PawPort to import supported conversations, memory, Skills, plugins, MCP settings, projects, and scheduled tasks from Codex and Qoder, with compatibility checks and selective retries ([#6960](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/6960))

**QwenPaw Creator & Data**

- Upgrade Creator to 2.0.1: review scripts before media production, keep manual regenerations from triggering paid downstream steps, and recover stalled projects ([#8121](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8121))
- Upgrade QwenPaw Data to 0.3.0 with an integrated analysis workspace, interactive clarification, inline HTML reports, and `/data` and `/datasource` commands in chat channels ([#7637](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7637))

**Models & Memory**

- Unify model discovery, pricing, and selection, with a candidate model pool and per-conversation model and thinking controls ([#7899](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7899))
- Configure a custom provider’s name, endpoint, protocol, and API key in one dialog ([#7826](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7826))
- Configure ReMe search reranking in the Console, including the model, endpoint, candidate multiplier, and timeout ([#6399](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/6399))

**Hub**

- Add a Hub model gateway with centrally managed organization models, member token budgets, usage dashboards, and invitation-based registration ([#7779](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7779))
- Support initializing the first Hub administrator from the command line, including Local-only deployments without the Docker SDK ([#7696](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7696))

**Skills, Tools, Automation & Channels**

- Add a `view_audio` tool so Agents can understand audio files through the existing transcription pipeline ([#8083](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8083))
- Configure scheduled tasks with plain-text instructions and a chosen model, preserve history after interruptions, and inspect timeout results and sessions from the Inbox ([#7776](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7776))
- Distribute selected Skills from the Skill pool to workspaces in batches ([#7852](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7852))
- Allow Skills to be assigned to custom channels as well as built-in channels ([#7782](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7782))
- Install or remove Skill Market sources as plugins, including QwenPaw, ClawHub, ModelScope, and Aliyun ([#8128](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8128))
- Add collapsible thinking panels in Feishu, with optional automatic collapse after generation ([#7685](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7685))
- Render Markdown tables as native Telegram Rich Messages in replies and completed streams, with fallback when unsupported ([#7713](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7713))

## 🔄 Changed

- Improve model settings and selection interactions in the Console ([#8017](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8017))
- Improve Settings navigation and search, add clearer runtime configuration tabs, and smooth conversation switching ([#7956](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7956))
- Unify memory commands under `/reme <action> key=value`, replacing `/dream`, `/memorize`, and `/reme_status` ([#7444](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7444))
- Limit visual compaction to older conversation history, preserve the latest two user turns, and retrieve original passages with `recall_context` ([#7703](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7703))
- Reduce delays in long conversations by avoiding repeated full history-database checks on every request ([#7639](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7639))
- Redesign conversation history with time, source, or ungrouped views, more room on small screens, richer session details, and conversation ID copying ([#7665](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7665), [#7688](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7688), [#7788](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7788), [#7846](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7846))
- Use source grouping by default for the conversation list ([#7972](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7972))
- Move the chat file drawer to the right side ([#7704](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7704))
- Reduce initial Console downloads by loading chat dependencies and language resources on demand ([#7829](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7829))
- Stream background tool output only while its task panel is expanded, reducing idle connections ([#7831](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7831))
- Upgrade Make Skill to 2.1 with more reliable planning, argument validation, and evaluation guidance ([#7753](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7753))
- Report daily runtime activity when Agents execute, including scheduled tasks, while honoring existing telemetry consent and opt-out settings ([#7802](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7802))

## 🐛 Fixed

**PawPort**

- Show the exact asset and cause when a PawPort import fails so failed items can be retried ([#7953](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7953))

**Console, Chat & Files**

- Keep chat terminal tabs working on HTTP deployments that assign UUID session IDs ([#8144](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8144), [#8146](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8146))
- Keep chat input controls usable when the window is narrow ([#8145](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8145))
- Keep files sent by the Agent visible after a conversation is restored from history ([#7949](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7949))
- Allow users to interrupt navigation between conversations while messages are loading ([#8214](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8214))
- Ignore replayed QQ gateway events to prevent duplicate handling of messages ([#8006](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8006))
- Keep queued messages bound to their original Agent and conversation, and prevent delayed chat creation or history loading from disrupting navigation and cancellation ([#7382](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7382))
- Preserve unsent drafts when pasting long text into Chat ([#8119](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8119))
- Mark interrupted tool calls correctly after stopping a reply instead of leaving them stuck in a running state ([#7345](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7345))
- Restore assistant reply timestamps and the correct visibility of response actions ([#7851](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7851))
- Run `/compact` in the current conversation instead of opening a new session ([#7834](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7834))
- Refresh cached text and CSV tabs when reopened or activated while preserving unsaved edits ([#7902](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7902))
- Move Skill pool downloads off the request path and clear unfinished temporary files ([#8055](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8055))

milestone.title: v0.9.0
milestone.description:
Phase 3: The Gateway. Separate the web surface from the agent core so the gateway is optional and can restart independently.

Source of truth: [#7432 - v0.9.0 gateway](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432#v090-gateway), including existing issues/PRs, missing work, sequencing, and acceptance evidence.

Deliverables: agree the full core IPC contract first; finish the supported local IPC server; ship standalone zeroclaw-gw; migrate vendor webhook behavior into channel plugins; and have Tauri package and manage both processes.

Completion requires a core artifact without web assets or HTTP server code, a working IPC-connected gateway, core/channel operation when the gateway is absent, and demonstrated two-process desktop lifecycle. Existing OIDC, principal-isolation, and ZeroRelay work must integrate with this boundary. WATI is already retired. Feature acceptance and normal review/CI/release holds still apply.

issues.body:
## Purpose

This tracker is the source of truth for completing the remaining **Phase 2 runtime work in v0.8.6** and **Phase 3 gateway separation in v0.9.0** from [RFC #5574](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/5574).

It owns the deliverable map, remaining gaps, sequencing, and release-completion evidence. The [v0.8.6 milestone](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/milestone/31) and [v0.9.0 milestone](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/milestone/11) provide release assignment views. Existing implementation trackers, especially #8850, retain their detailed work lists; link them here instead of opening duplicate program trackers.

This revises the earlier fixes-only description of v0.8.6 to include the remaining Phase 2 work alongside compatible fixes. v0.9.0 is centered on separating the web surface from the agent core. Existing authentication, principal-isolation, security, and ZeroRelay work must integrate with that boundary.

## Evidence and scope

Audit date: 2026-09-18. Source baseline: [core master ecc0c30c6b](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/tree/ecc0c30c6b58c61914b665d51887870e008f34b0), live issue/PR states, and the official plugin repository.

“Landed” below means the named implementation was merged and/or is present in the inspected source. It does not certify the complete release acceptance scenario. No release-artifact or live-service acceptance test was run for this planning audit. All delivery checkboxes remain open until their acceptance evidence is attached.

Delivery-issue pass: 2026-09-20, checked against [core master a7dad4ae5c](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/tree/a7dad4ae5c0fa1b24996f6d94e07251edf11880b) and the live open-issue inventory. The uncovered work now has 12 focused sub-issues: seven assigned to v0.8.6 and five to v0.9.0. Each has acceptance criteria and links to the relevant existing work. `status:accepted` records the agreed delivery scope; it does not ratify an unresolved design or approve an implementation. Native blocking relationships record the explicit dependencies between these new issues.

The maintained [FND-001](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/master/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md), [ADR-006](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/master/docs/book/src/architecture/decisions/ADR-006-runtime-channel-plugins.md), [ADR-007](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/master/docs/book/src/architecture/decisions/ADR-007-gateway-extraction.md), and [ADR-009](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/master/docs/book/src/architecture/decisions/ADR-009-wit-wasmtime-plugin-execution.md) qualify the older RFC excerpts:

- The accepted plugin execution backend is direct Wasmtime with WIT components. Extism was superseded by ADR-009.
- WATI was retired by #9571 and removed from FND-001's migration target. It is not a remaining channel deliverable.
- A `zeroclaw-gateway` crate and local daemon RPC already exist. A standalone `zeroclaw-gw` process and its complete supported IPC boundary do not.
- The current IPC endpoint is `<data_dir>/daemon.sock` on Unix and a data-directory-derived named pipe on Windows. The future `zeroclaw-kernel`, `ipc` feature, and `kernel.sock` names in the old text need an explicit mapping to the current implementation; they are not existing components.
- This plan does not require deleting all of `zeroclaw-runtime` before the gateway can be separated.

## v0.8.6 runtime

Theme: formalize a clean agent runtime and let users install optional capabilities without rebuilding ZeroClaw.

| Deliverable | Existing work and verified state | Remaining work |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **D1: Clean runtime composition boundary** | #5559 landed the workspace split; #7430 landed `DaemonRegistry`. Current `daemon/registry.rs` registers subsystem starters. The old #5618 issue is closed as not planned, so its state alone is not delivery evidence. | Define and finish the public runtime/registry composition contract, or record the reviewed equivalent of the RFC sketch. Move concrete provider/tool/channel construction to the owning composition layer. Runtime still depends on `zeroclaw-tools` and constructs concrete tools. Prove independent runtime use and a thin executable entry point. **Delivery: #10993**, with existing channel dependency work in #6864. |
| **D2: WASM execution bridge** | #8368 landed the Wasmtime component host; #10146 activates logical channel instances; #9582 governs tool HTTP egress; #10750 governs channel HTTP egress. ADR-009 owns the accepted backend design. | Complete the supported release-artifact backend/permission/configuration path and its end-to-end proof. #8863 supplies the still-open WebSocket capability needed by Discord and declares #8923 as its prerequisite. The existence of a host adapter does not prove every channel's networking or lifecycle is supported. **Delivery: #10994** (supported artifact) and **#10999** (Discord acceptance). |
| **D3: Registry client and package lifecycle** | #8264 landed registry search and install-by-name. Current `src/plugin_registry.rs` reads the official JSON registry, resolves versions, downloads archives, and checks provided hashes. `PluginHost` applies the configured manifest signature policy. CLI list/search/install/remove/info/migrate exist. #7333 was closed unmerged; #8264 is the landed implementation. | `plugin update` is absent from the current command enum. Define update/rollback and trust/compatibility behavior. Existing open work: #9584 grant ceremony, #10746 install load-verification, #10752 info/list load verdicts (depends on #10746), #10162 incomplete install/config seeding, and #9624 host/registry WIT compatibility. **New delivery issues: #10995** (update/rollback) and **#10996** (channel-instance configuration/grants). |
| **D4: Plugin installation during onboarding** | #9009 owns the broader operator onboarding program. Current Quickstart configures agents and channels. | Add an explicit onboarding-to-registry install/configure/activate flow that works from a downloaded binary without Cargo. **Delivery: #10997**; no implementation PR for the complete flow was found in the audit. Reconcile the original `zeroclaw onboard` command wording with the maintained CLI/Quickstart interface. |
| **D5: Core tools only in the default runtime** | #8850 is the existing optional-channel/tool migration tracker. Historical #5617 was closed with a “requirements have shifted” comment; its associated #5566 PR was closed unmerged. | Reconfirm the core tool set and move optional capability construction out of the default runtime. Current `all_tools_with_runtime` still builds cron, scheduling, Pushover, calculator, weather, canvas, and other tools beyond the RFC list. **Delivery: #10998**, including the focused composition slice and binary-size proof under #8850. |

### Runtime implementation PRs

PR states below were checked on 2026-09-18. Each link identifies the slice it supplies; the phase acceptance criteria still require the complete user-facing outcome.

| Deliverable | PRs to follow | Coverage and missing PRs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **D1: Runtime composition** | Merged: [PR #5559: workspace split](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/5559); [PR #7430: daemon registry](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/7430). Open supporting extraction: [PR #10557: extract cron into its own crate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/10557). | Cron extraction reduces the holding crate, but does not complete the generic runtime composition contract. **No open PR completing the full D1 boundary was found.** |
| **D2: WASM execution and channel support** | Merged: [PR #8368: Wasmtime component host](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/8368); [PR #10146: activate channel instances](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/10146); [PR #9582: govern tool HTTP egress](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/9582); [PR #10750: govern channel HTTP egress](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/10750). Open drafts for the Discord transport path: [PR #9142: named TLS profiles](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/9142); [PR #8923: TCP and STARTTLS](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/8923); [PR #8863: channel WebSocket capability](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/8863). | The execution foundations are present. The transport drafts, release backend/configuration choices, compatible Discord package publication, and end-to-end artifact proof remain. |
| **D3: Registry and package lifecycle** | Merged: [PR #8264: registry search and install by name](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/8264). Open: [PR #9584: install/list egress-grant ceremony](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/9584); [PR #10746: load-verify installation](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/10746); [PR #10752: report info/list load verdicts](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/10752). Merged supporting fix: [PR #11107: escape apostrophes in egress remedy commands](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11107), preserving the complete grant list as one shell argument. | These cover install usability and verification. **No open PR implementing the missing plugin-update/rollback command was found.** Channel-only grant seeding is explicitly outside #9584's scope. |
| **D4: Install plugins during onboarding** | **No dedicated open implementation PR found.** Existing coordination: #9009 and #8850. | Link the eventual install/configure/activate onboarding PR here; general onboarding changes alone do not meet D4. |
| **D5: Minimal core tools** | **No open PR delivering the complete core-only runtime tool set was found.** Existing coordination: #8850; historical #5617. | A focused tool-composition/packaging PR and binary-size evidence are still required. |

**Declared prerequisite order:**

- [PR #10746: install verification](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/10746) precedes [PR #10752: load verdicts](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/10752).
- [PR #9142: named TLS profiles](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/9142) precedes [PR #8923: TCP/STARTTLS](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/8923), which precedes [PR #8863: WebSocket capability](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/8863).
- #9142 still cites [PR #8857: scoped secrets and encrypted state](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/8857), which is **closed unmerged**. Its [closure record](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/8857#issuecomment-5681552958) identifies merged [PR #9128: scoped tool secret service](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/9128) and [PR #9129: channel config services](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/9129) as the scoped-secrets replacement; the encrypted-state portion was deferred. Its other declared foundation, [PR #9137: shared egress policy](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/9137), is merged. Reconcile that stale prerequisite before treating the transport chain as ready.

These dependency links come from the current PR descriptions and the verified predecessor dispositions. They do not certify that each branch has already incorporated the latest predecessor revision.

### Runtime gaps to close

- [ ] **R1: Runtime API and ownership.** #10993; supporting channel dependency cleanup remains in #6864. Finish D1 with explicit injection boundaries, dependency checks, and an independently usable runtime; incorporate the landed `DaemonRegistry` instead of treating it as missing.
- [ ] **R2: Supported plugin distribution.** #10994. Select and verify the execution backend for each shipped target and record the loading, grants, signature, and compatibility decisions. The current Cargo default feature set omits the plugin host. #8135 is still an unaccepted RFC with older Extism assumptions; citing it does not approve a default-on policy change.
- [ ] **R3: Registry update and install completeness.** #10995 (update/rollback) and #10996 (channel-instance configuration/grants), alongside existing #10162 (install recovery) and #9624 (compatibility). Finish the relevant #8850 install/verification work and define the missing update/rollback command. Include channel-instance grant/config seeding; #9584 explicitly excludes channel-only grant seeding.
- [ ] **R4: Install-from-onboarding experience.** #10997, coordinated with #9009/#8850. Provide a focused implementation under the existing onboarding/plugin programs and prove the complete user flow without a Rust toolchain.
- [ ] **R5: Minimal core and size evidence.** #10998. Agree the retained core tools, implement the optional-tool boundary, and record binary size for named release targets/profiles in release notes. Reuse #8850; historical issue closure is not proof of this criterion.
- [ ] **R6: Discord acceptance.** #10999. The official plugin repository contains [Discord source](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw-plugins/tree/main/plugins/discord), but its README requires host WebSocket capability. #8863 is open, that host feature is absent from the inspected master, and the [official registry index](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw-plugins/blob/main/registry.json) has no Discord entry. Publish and verify the compatible package and demonstrate install, configuration, inbound delivery, and replies from the supported release binary. Reconcile the original `channel-discord` example with the actual package name `discord`.

The RFC core-tool baseline is `shell`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `file_edit`, `git_operations`, `glob_search`, `content_search`, `memory_recall`, `memory_store`, `memory_forget`, and `web_fetch`. Any revised set needs a recorded rationale before D5 is marked complete.

**Runtime acceptance:** an independently usable runtime with the agreed dependency boundary; a real Rust/WIT tool plugin executing under the shipped host; Discord plugin installation and operation without recompilation; onboarding that installs plugins without Cargo; and published size measurements for the supported runtime artifact. A component unit test or a source directory alone does not establish these product outcomes.

## v0.9.0 gateway

Theme: make the web surface a separate, optional process that can be omitted or restarted without interrupting healthy agent execution.

| Deliverable | Existing work and verified state | Remaining work |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **D1: Agreed kernel IPC contract** | [RPC socket documentation](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/master/docs/book/src/architecture/rpc-socket.md), `zeroclaw-api/src/jsonrpc.rs`, and the runtime RPC code define an existing NDJSON/JSON-RPC transport. The gateway also generates a partial OpenAPI 3.1 document in `openapi.rs`. #9133 recorded ADR-007; #8691 remains its decision-record home. | Agree the complete core-to-gateway contract for messages/streams, sessions, installed plugins, status, memory, and cron, including identity, permissions, version negotiation, cancellation, errors, reconnect, and lifecycle. Explicitly resolve how the requested OpenAPI 3.1 specification relates to existing non-HTTP JSON-RPC and the no-HTTP-server-in-core success criterion. **Design delivery: #11000**, with the review and decision linked through #8691/ADR-007 before dependent implementation. |
| **D2: Supported local IPC server** | `rpc/local.rs` already implements Unix sockets and Windows named pipes. Existing session/turn methods and protocol initialization are useful foundations. #8289/#7141 and open #10259 supply related principal/authentication work. | Complete the D1 method and lifecycle coverage for an external gateway; record the core owner/feature/endpoint mapping; prove isolation, authentication, version mismatch, cancellation, and reconnection on supported platforms. Existing local transport is partial delivery, not a reason to write a second server. **Delivery: #11001**, after #11000's contract review. |
| **D3: Standalone zeroclaw-gw** | `zeroclaw-gateway` already exists. ADR-007 describes the intended process boundary. Its current manifest still directly depends on `zeroclaw-runtime` and `zeroclaw-channels`; the daemon starts it through an in-process registry callback. WATI is excluded because it was removed. **Cross-process delivery: #11003**; #8850 retains vendor migration ownership. |

Current desktop code supervises the existing daemon/gateway product. | Package and supervise the separate core and `zeroclaw-gw` executables: startup ordering, readiness, authentication, compatible versions, gateway restart, coordinated shutdown, and upgrades. **Delivery: #11004**, after #11002; no implementation PR for the final two-process arrangement was found in the audit. |

issues.title: [Bug]: Regional OS locales (fr_FR, es_ES, ja_JP) fall back to English
issues.body:
### Affected component

runtime

### Severity

S2 - degraded behavior

### Current behavior

On Unix, `sys-locale` reports the OS locale with its region, e.g. `LANG=fr_FR.UTF-8`, `es_ES.UTF-8`, `es_AR.UTF-8` or `ja_JP.UTF-8`. `i18n::normalize_locale` turns these into `fr-FR`, `es-ES`, `es-AR` and `ja-JP`, but the catalogues are per language (`locales.toml`: `en`, `fr`, `ja`, `es`, `zh-CN`). Nothing then matches:

- `zeroclaw-runtime`: `builtin_cli_ftl_source` has arms only for `es`, `fr`, `ja` and `zh-CN`, and `load_ftl_from_disk` looks in `<ftl dir>/fr-FR/`.
- `zeroclaw-tools`: `load_ftl_from_disk` looks in `<ftl dir>/fr-FR/tools.ftl`.

The result is English everywhere: CLI strings, channel notices and tool descriptions. Only Simplified Chinese works from the OS locale, because its catalogue happens to be named with the region (`zh_CN` → `zh-CN`). A config `locale = "fr-FR"` fails the same way.

### Expected behavior

A regional tag without its own catalogue falls back to its language's catalogue: `fr_FR.UTF-8` → `fr`, `es_AR.UTF-8` → `es`, `ja_JP.UTF-8` → `ja`. A region with its own catalogue keeps it (`zh_CN` → `zh-CN`), and a language without a catalogue stays English as today (`de_DE`, `zh_TW`). POSIX modifiers such as `@euro` are ignored like the encoding.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
# master: the Telegram voice-drop notice is checked against English text
# (#11769), so it passing under French shows French was never selected.
LANGUAGE= LC_ALL= LC_MESSAGES= LANG=fr_FR.UTF-8 \
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib voice_drop_notices
# test telegram::tests::voice_drop_notices_name_the_reason_without_internals ... ok

LANGUAGE= LC_ALL= LC_MESSAGES= LANG=zh_CN.UTF-8 \
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib voice_drop_notices
# ... FAILED: the notice is in Chinese
```

### Impact

Every French, Spanish and Japanese user who relies on the OS locale gets English, although the translations ship in the binary. That is the default setup on most desktops and servers, since a locale in config is optional.

### Logs / stack traces

_None: the fallback to English is silent._

### ZeroClaw version

`master` at `329e66f76`; also v0.8.5.

### Rust version

1.99.0

### Operating system

Linux (Linux Lite 7.8, Ubuntu 24.04 base). Affects any OS where `sys-locale` returns a regional tag.

### Regression?

Unknown; the per-language catalogues and the normalization have not changed recently.

### Pre-flight checks

- [X] I reproduced this on the latest master branch or latest release.
- [X] I redacted secrets, tokens, and personal data from all submitted content.

---

I will open a PR: `normalize_locale` in `zeroclaw-runtime` maps a tag to the registry code it matches (case-insensitive), or else to its language when that is a registry code. `zeroclaw-tools`, which cannot see the runtime registry, tries `<ftl dir>/<tag>/tools.ftl` and then `<ftl dir>/<language>/tools.ftl`.

issues.title: Bootstrap file cap differs between gateway turns (20,000) and channel/agent-loop turns (6,000 with compact_context); doctor reports one
issues.body:
Follow-up split from #11710. The prompt contradiction from that issue is fixed separately; this tracks the cap mismatch it also reported.

### Current behavior

The same bootstrap file (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, …) is capped differently depending on which turn path builds the prompt:

- **Channel, agent-loop and turn paths** (`crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/agent/system_prompt.rs`): `COMPACT_BOOTSTRAP_MAX_CHARS` = 6,000 when the agent's `compact_context` is on (the default), otherwise `BOOTSTRAP_MAX_CHARS` = 20,000.
- **Agent / gateway path** (`agent/prompt.rs::IdentitySection` → `agent/personality.rs`): a fixed `MAX_FILE_CHARS` = 20,000, regardless of `compact_context`.

`zeroclaw doctor` (`doctor/mod.rs::check_agent_bootstrap_truncation`) computes only the first cap. With `compact_context` on, it reports 6,000 while gateway WebSocket turns on the same agent keep 20,000. The #11710 reporter measured this from system-prompt sizes before and after splitting their AGENTS.md.

### Expected behavior

One of:
1. The gateway/Agent path honors `compact_context` with the same limit selection, so every path and `doctor` agree. This is a behavior change: gateway turns would see less of an over-cap file.
2. The caps stay different on purpose, and `doctor` names the cap per turn path when they differ.

Needs a maintainer decision on which.

### Notes

- `personality.rs` also loads `HEARTBEAT.md`, which the `system_prompt.rs` path does not inject. That is worth checking while unifying.
- The runtime truncation WARN (`agent.bootstrap_file_truncated`) fires once per process per size, so on a long-running daemon the evidence leaves the rolling trace early. `doctor` is the durable signal, which is why it should be right.

issues.title: [Bug]: Voice-drop and model-fallback channel tests depend on the operator locale
issues.body:
### Affected component

channel

### Severity

S3 - minor issue

### Current behavior

Four `zeroclaw-channels` tests hard-code English notice text. Production translates that text, so the tests fail when the locale is any other supported one. This is the same failure #10303 fixed for the Telegram lifecycle tests, in tests added since:

- `telegram::tests::voice_drop_notices_name_the_reason_without_internals` expects `900s limit`, `smaller or shorter` and the `⚠️ Audio message skipped:` prefix.
- `telegram::tests::try_parse_voice_message_skips_when_duration_exceeds_limit` expects `5s limit`.
- `orchestrator::tests::model_fallback_notice_modes_preserve_existing_delivery_contracts` expects `fallback model`.
- `orchestrator::tests::process_channel_message_model_fallback_notices_are_live_and_delivery_only` expects `fallback model`.

All four fail with `locale = "fr"`, `"es"`, `"ja"` or `"zh-CN"`, and with `LANG=zh_CN.UTF-8` and no locale in config. They pass with English.

### Expected behavior

The channel test suite passes whatever the operator locale is. As #10342 did, the tests take the expected text from the same catalogue production uses, or check only what every translation shares. The English wording checks, such as advice that fits audio uploads and not only voice notes, run against the English catalogue directly.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
tmp_config="$(mktemp -d)"
printf 'locale = "fr"\n' > "$tmp_config/config.toml"
ZEROCLAW_CONFIG_DIR="$tmp_config" cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-channels --lib
# test result: FAILED. 1968 passed; 4 failed
```

### Impact

Runtime behavior is not affected. The documented channel test command gives misleading failures to contributors whose ZeroClaw or OS locale is not English.

### Logs / stack traces

```text
thread 'telegram::tests::try_parse_voice_message_skips_when_duration_exceeds_limit' panicked at crates/zeroclaw-channels/src/telegram.rs:17477:9:
notice names the limit: ⚠️ 已跳过音频消息：时长超过 5 秒的上限。请发送更短的录音，或分段发送。
thread 'orchestrator::tests::model_fallback_notice_modes_preserve_existing_delivery_contracts' panicked at crates/zeroclaw-channels/src/orchestrator/mod.rs:19527:13:
assertion failed: redacted.contains("fallback model")
```

### ZeroClaw version

`master` at `329e66f76`.

### Rust version

1.99.0

### Operating system

Linux (Linux Lite 7.8, Ubuntu 24.04 base); not platform-specific.

### Regression?

Yes. These tests came in after #10303 was fixed.

issues.title: Honor the HTTP Retry-After response header for provider 429s
issues.body:
Follow-up split from #10779. The quota-exhausted classifier slice is in #11767; this tracks the remaining Retry-After part.

### Current behavior

For a retryable 429, `ReliableModelProvider::compute_backoff` and the rate-limit cooldown use `parse_retry_after_ms` (`crates/zeroclaw-providers/src/reliable.rs`). That function only scans the **error message text** for `Retry-After:` / `retry_after:`. Provider errors reach the Reliable layer as plain text: `api_error` / `api_error_from_parts` in `crates/zeroclaw-providers/src/lib.rs` format `"{provider} API error ({status}): {body}"` and drop the response headers. So a standard HTTP `Retry-After` response header is never seen. The provider then falls back to its fixed backoff (500 ms, 1 s, …) even when the upstream said exactly how long to wait.

### Expected behavior

For transient 429s (and 503s where providers send it), honor the HTTP `Retry-After` header in both forms: delta-seconds and HTTP-date. Keep the existing 30 s cap and the existing text fallback.

### Notes on scope

- `api_error(model_provider, response)` still has the `reqwest::Response`, so it is the natural shared point to capture the header. One option is a typed error source carrying the parsed delay, which `parse_retry_after_ms` checks before the text scan, rather than appending more text.
- Several providers build their own error strings and would bypass that helper. Examples: `gemini.rs`, `ollama.rs`, `hailo_ollama.rs`, `telnyx.rs`, and the OpenAI Responses streaming path in `openai.rs`. Each needs either to route through the helper or to carry the header the same way.
- Channel-side precedent for honoring `Retry-After` headers: #7027.

### Acceptance

- A 429 response whose `Retry-After` header says N seconds produces a backoff of N s (capped), proven with a mock HTTP response rather than an error string.
- HTTP-date form parsed; a malformed header falls back to existing behavior.
- Non-retryable business 429s still fail fast (no wait).

prs.title: fix(providers): project JPEG admission without copying the input
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `projected_allocation` now routes `image::ImageFormat::Jpeg` to a new
    `projected_jpeg_allocation`, which projects the decode peak from the SOF
    (`jpeg_frame_header`) on the borrowed `&[u8]`.
  - `image` 0.25.10's `JpegDecoder::new` copies the whole encoded input and
    walks retained metadata before `Limits` apply, so the previous admission
    path allocated in proportion to the input before the 64 MiB per-image cap
    or the aggregate budget could refuse the image.
  - PNG / GIF / WebP keep the existing `into_decoder()` header-only path.
- **Scope boundary:** Admission projection only. The decode path, both caps,
  and aggregate-budget accounting are unchanged. The JPEG output term is now
  charged as 3 B/px for every JPEG (Rgb8), conservative for 1-component
  grayscale images — see Compatibility. No config, CLI, or dependency change.
- **Blast radius:** Multimodal image admission (`validate_within_budget` /
  `projected_allocation`) for image attachments across providers; the
  projection also charges the shared aggregate decode budget.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11654

### What this does, simply

Before decoding an image, ZeroClaw estimates how much memory the decode will
need so it can refuse one that would exceed the per-image or per-request caps.
For JPEG that estimate used the decoder's own header parse, which copies the
whole encoded file first — so an image that was about to be refused had
already paid for a copy of itself. This change reads the JPEG frame header
(SOF) straight from the bytes already in memory, so the estimate costs nothing
extra and the refusal decision precedes any proportional allocation.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A` — no interactive path; admission is
  covered by unit tests and CI.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `CI Required Gate`
  green on `9febc2d`, including `Format`, `Lint`, `Check *`, `Test`, and
  `Test (Landlock)`; the change is confined to `zeroclaw-providers`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No test asserts that the JPEG admission
  path avoids constructing `JpegDecoder` (see below).
- **Commands run and tail output:** `cargo test -p zeroclaw-providers --lib --
  jpeg` → `5 passed; 1957 filtered out` (`oversized_jpeg_coefficients_…`,
  `jpeg_projection_accounts_for_padded_sampling_…`,
  `unprefixed_jpeg_frame_header_…`, `jpeg_tem_marker_…`,
  `unsupported_jpeg_sof_marker_…`).
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The new path reads only the
  borrowed `&[u8]`: `projected_jpeg_allocation` and `jpeg_frame_header` walk
  marker lengths and the SOF, and `ImageReader::into_decoder()` is no longer
  reached for JPEG. That the copy is actually avoided is not yet asserted by a
  test; a focused allocation / `into_decoder`-counting check is the
  recommended follow-up.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A` — no user-visible interface.
- **Tested revision:** `9febc2d0a68589ab4c39cb422f0476d4f54ffa34`.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- Note: image bytes are untrusted input; the new SOF parser is bounds-checked
  and returns `CorruptImage` for any header it cannot project, so malformed
  input is refused before decode (fail-closed).

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? No — for 1-component grayscale JPEGs the output term
  rises from 1 B/px (the old `JpegDecoder::total_bytes` for L8) to 3 B/px, so
  a grayscale JPEG whose `w*h*1 + auxiliary` was under 64 MiB but whose
  `w*h*3 + auxiliary` is over is now refused (e.g. a 4000×4000 baseline
  grayscale image: ~50 MB before, ~82 MB after). Deriving the output term from
  `jpeg_frame_header(..).components.len()` (1 ⇒ 1 B/px, else 3 B/px) restores
  the previous value without `into_decoder()`.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- Exact upgrade steps for existing users: none for operators; the affected
  inputs are large grayscale JPEGs near the per-image cap.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert 9febc2d0a68589ab4c39cb422f0476d4f54ffa34`
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** New decode-memory refusals for JPEG
  attachments — `corrupt_image` / "decoded canvas … exceeds per-image limit"
  in provider logs for images previously accepted.

prs.title: feat(gateway): move plugin webhook admission and dedup into a core ingress
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (`a0f70b7925`). **Depends on #11318** (plugin webhook golden frames and CI leg) and **Depends on #11339** (the reservation store move). The branch merges #11339 at `59875788c1`; both show in the diff until they land.
- **Restacked onto #11339 (maintainer decision on this PR):** #11339 lands first and moves the reservation store into `zeroclaw-api` with no behavior change. This PR now uses that store, `WebhookReservationStore`, instead of a store of its own, and keeps the ingress (route lookup, queue admission, the deadline) in `zeroclaw-infra`. On top of #11339 it makes the dedup behavior change described under **Behavior change** below.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Channel-plugin webhook dispatch was split between the gateway handler (route lookup, queue admission, the 10 s deadline) and the gateway's idempotency store (message dedup), both reached through in-process handles. A gateway in another process could reach neither. This moves all four into one core-owned service with a single entry point, so the next PR can expose it over RPC unchanged.
  - `zeroclaw-infra`: new `plugin_webhook` module. `PluginWebhookIngress` owns the route registry, per-route queue admission, the deadline counted from enqueue, and message dedup in #11339's `WebhookReservationStore`, with the same owner, in-flight, rollback and generation-fencing semantics as before. `dispatch(request, cancel)` returns a typed outcome; dropping or cancelling it cancels the worker's copy of the request.
  - `zeroclaw-api`: shared limits and path grammar, the route owner (`PluginWebhookOwner`), a validating `PluginWebhookRequest` (redacting `Debug`; header names limited to what `http`'s `HeaderName` accepts, values to what `HeaderValue::to_str` yields), and `PluginWebhookOutcome`. Routes now carry their owner.
  - `zeroclaw-gateway`: the `/plugin/{path}` handler is an HTTP adapter over `dispatch` with a pure outcome-to-response mapping. The idempotency store keeps only the `/webhook` and `/sop/*` replay path.
  - The gateway's `/webhook` and `/sop/*` replay store keeps #11339's `WebhookReservationStore` backing, with a store of its own for each gateway run.
- **Behavior change (dedup, on top of #11339):**
  - **Lifetime:** plugin webhook dedup lasts for the daemon generation instead of one gateway run. A gateway restart inside the generation keeps it; a reload or daemon restart still clears it.
  - **Budget:** plugin deliveries get a committed-key budget of their own (`gateway.idempotency_max_keys`), no longer shared with `/webhook` and `/sop/*`. A burst of generic keys can no longer push out plugin keys, or the reverse. The worst case is twice that many committed keys across the two stores.
  - **Key:** dedup keys include the owning plugin and channel alias, so two instances never collide and a path that changes owner starts clean. #11339's pinned unscoped key no longer applies.
  - Tests that pinned the old behavior in #11339 (per-run lifetime, shared budget, unscoped key) are replaced by `plugin_webhook_dedup_state_outlives_a_gateway_router`, `plugin_and_generic_webhook_keys_have_separate_budgets` and `dedup_key_separates_every_identity_component`. #11339's store tests stay in `zeroclaw-api`.
- **Follow-up from the review, not in this PR:** a per-owner share of the dedup budget, #11565.
- **Scope boundary:** No other HTTP-visible change: the PR 1 plugin webhook golden frames replay byte-identical. No WIT, config schema, `zeroclaw-plugins`, or `zeroclaw-channels` change. No RPC surface (next PR).
- **Blast radius:** plugin webhook ingress in the supervised and standalone gateway; the gateway's `/webhook` and `/sop/*` replay store (same behavior, #11339's implementation, its own budget); route publication in `zeroclaw-runtime/src/plugin_runtime.rs` (mechanical: routes gain an owner, and the grammar and queue depth come from shared definitions; no new functionality, so no holding-crate exception row is needed for it).
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11003. Related #7432. Related #11000.
- **Labels:** `ci`, `docs`, `dependencies`, `core`, `gateway`, `runtime`, `tests`, `scripts`, `size:XL`, `cli` (applied by the labelers)

### What this does, simply

When a chat platform calls a channel plugin's webhook, several things have to happen before the plugin sees the request: find which plugin owns the URL, check its queue has room, start a deadline, and make sure a message the platform retries is not delivered twice. That work was spread across the web gateway. This PR puts it in one place in the core, so a gateway running as its own process can later ask the core to do it.

One thing changes on purpose. The core remembers delivered message IDs for as long as the daemon runs its current configuration, not just while one gateway process lives, so restarting the gateway no longer forgets them; reloading the config still does. Plugin messages also get their own memory, so a flood of other webhooks cannot make the core forget them, and each plugin channel's IDs are kept apart. This only suppresses platform retries; it is not a security check, which stays with each plugin's signature verification.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: the PR 1 golden frames replay the public HTTP contract byte-identical, and the root e2e test drives a real WASM guest through the ingress.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Check (plugins gateway ingress)` (gateway plugin webhook tests and golden frames), `Check (plugins cranelift runtime)` (`plugin_channel_runtime_e2e` with the real guest, runtime plugin admission tests), `Test` (infra and api units, gateway default-feature tests), `Lint`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** `cargo test -p zeroclaw-api` alone does not compile on master (its manifest lacks tokio's `time` feature, which `channel.rs` uses); the api tests run through workspace feature unification, as in CI.
- **Commands run and tail output:** (head `98e1666b31`: this PR on master `a0f70b7925` with #11339 `59875788c1` merged; macOS arm64, rustc 1.98.0)

```text
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-infra --lib
test result: ok. 292 passed ; test result: ok. 331 passed   (api includes #11339's store tests; infra includes plugin_webhook::*)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib ; cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --features plugins-wasm --lib
test result: ok. 636 passed ; test result: ok. 653 passed   (includes plugin_and_generic_webhook_keys_have_separate_budgets)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --features plugins-wasm --test golden_frames plugin_webhook   (x2)
test result: ok. 5 passed; 0 failed; fixtures unchanged
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --test golden_frames -- --include-ignored
test result: ok. 12 passed
$ cargo test --locked --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --test plugin_channel_runtime_e2e
test result: ok. 5 passed (includes a_repeated_message_id_is_delivered_once_through_the_core_ingress)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --lib plugin_runtime::
test result: ok. 17 passed
$ cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets ; RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-default-features
Finished ; Finished, no warnings
$ cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-infra -p zeroclaw-gateway [--features zeroclaw-gateway/plugins-wasm] --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings ; cargo clippy --locked --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --bin zeroclaw --test plugin_channel_runtime_e2e --no-deps -- -D warnings
Finished, no warnings (all three)
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check ; bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh ; bash scripts/ci/plugin_backend_change_filter.test.sh ; docs quality gate on the changed docs
clean ; passed ; pass ; 0 errors
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Mutation checks, each caught by the new tests: a longer or shorter deadline, the wrong log level, key or alias, dropping `"` from the allowed header-name bytes, removing the header-name length bound, and one eviction assertion. A 256-byte sweep compares the header-name rule with `http::HeaderName` byte by byte.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Workspace clippy with `ci-all` is left to CI.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No (plugin secrets stay in the guest; header values pass through as before)
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A. The ingress re-validates every request with bounds that are supersets of what the HTTP layer admits, so nothing new reaches the guest.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for HTTP clients and plugins. Intended behavior changes, relative to #11339 (which keeps today's behavior):
  - Dedup lives for the daemon generation instead of one gateway run, so it survives gateway supervisor restarts; it still starts empty after a daemon reload or restart. In plain terms: restarting the gateway no longer lets a platform's retry of an already-delivered message through.
  - Dedup keys include the owning plugin and alias, so a path that changes owner starts clean.
  - Plugin dedup has its own capacity (from `gateway.idempotency_max_keys`) instead of sharing the `/webhook` and `/sop/*` store; the worst case is twice that many committed keys across both stores. In plain terms: heavy traffic on one kind of webhook no longer makes the other kind forget recent message IDs.
  - Dedup remains best effort: a key can still be displaced inside its TTL once the plugin store is full, and it is not replay protection (the plugin docs now say so).
  - Outcome logs (`plugin_webhook_unauthorized`, `plugin_webhook_invalid`, `plugin_webhook_unavailable`) now come from `zeroclaw_infra::plugin_webhook` with plugin, channel alias and path. New WARN keys `plugin_webhook_route_closed` and `plugin_webhook_reply_dropped` replace two silent 503 paths. A request outside the ingress bounds gets 400 `invalid webhook` with `plugin_webhook_request_invalid` (the HTTP listener's own header and URI limits normally refuse such a request first).
  - Rust API: `PluginWebhookRegistry::get` returns a `PluginWebhookRoute`; `GatewaySupervision::new` takes `Arc<PluginWebhookIngress>` in place of #11339's registry and per-run store, so #11339's `zeroclaw_gateway::plugin_webhook_reservations` and `IdempotencyStore::shared` are removed; `zeroclaw_gateway::IDEMPOTENCY_MAX_KEYS_DEFAULT` moved to `zeroclaw_infra` (no workspace users). Experimental crates.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`. No persisted state, WIT, or config changes.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `plugins.enabled = false` or a build without `plugins-wasm` disables plugin webhook routes, as before.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `plugin_webhook_*` error keys from `zeroclaw_infra::plugin_webhook`; duplicate deliveries after a gateway restart would indicate dedup regressions; golden-frame drift in the plugin gateway CI leg.

Phase 3: The Gateway. Separate the web surface from the agent core so the gateway is optional and can restart independently.

Source of truth: [#7432 - v0.9.0 gateway](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432#v090-gateway), including existing issues/PRs, missing work, sequencing, and acceptance evidence.

Deliverables: agree the full core IPC contract first; finish the supported local IPC server; ship standalone zeroclaw-gw; migrate vendor webhook behavior into channel plugins; and have Tauri package and manage both processes.

Completion requires a core artifact without web assets or HTTP server code, a working IPC-connected gateway, core/channel operation when the gateway is absent, and demonstrated two-process desktop lifecycle. Existing OIDC, principal-isolation, and ZeroRelay work must integrate with this boundary. WATI is already retired. Feature acceptance and normal review/CI/release holds still apply.

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:** Stage the declared `sign_manifest` example and genuine `vendor/` path-patch inputs before dependency prefetch in the default, Debian and Alpine Dockerfiles. The original seven image jobs lacked the example; after that correction, the next run exposed the missing crossterm path patch. Both inputs are now present before Cargo parses the temporary tree.
- **Regression protection:** Four named architecture methods check signer target declaration/staging/replacement and canonical vendor path-patch staging. Internal refusal variants cover missing, late, wrong-stage, wrong-path, comment-only and removed inputs, including LF/CRLF forms.
- **Scope boundary:** Four files only. Existing build commands, features, profiles, cache policy, base images, generated zones, runtime images and size checks retain their bytes. This does not change the real signer example, Containerfile, ignore policy or dependencies.
- **Blast radius:** Source-image dependency staging and architecture tests. No product API, credential, permission or configuration change.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #7432; Related #11310; Related #11221. The shared Rustls repair in #11736 remains a separate change.

### What this does, simply

The plugin manifest names a signing example, so Cargo requires its file to exist even when building another target. These Dockerfiles first copy only manifests and create temporary targets to cache dependencies. The new example was missing from that temporary tree. The primer now seeds that minimal target and copies the genuine vendor tree required by the root manifest. Existing cleanup removes the dummy targets before real crate source arrives; the vendor implementation and build recipe are unchanged.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, through the existing hosted source-image matrix and architecture lane; use disposable image tags.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** N/A for user-facing UI. Build inputs and existing container CLI/gateway smokes only.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Current published source and the existing Docker workflow, with its normal platforms, cache policy and feature selections.
- **Steps to run:** Inspect all four named architecture results, the unchanged container-input gate and installer generator check, then all seven source-image results and any broader Containerfile selection from the existing workflow. Preserve raw failures and actual checkout/command receipts.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Cargo can parse the declared example in the dependency primer, followed by real-source replacement. All source builds and their existing smokes/size checks must independently pass.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The manifest-only tree lacks `examples/sign_manifest.rs`; the retained seven actual image logs fail at that Cargo parsing boundary. No baseline image success is inferred.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Pending on the published head. The prior seven raw failures identify the input omission; they supply no after-fix result.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** All four Rust methods, their internal obligations, official Format/compiler/generator checks and all corrected images are NOTRUN. A structural source guard is not a Docker/shell interpreter or image-execution proof. The shared Rustls Security gate remains a separate requirement.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Static Git/hash/inverse checks and extracted `bash -n` only: producer64 members verified, four owned paths, 2,269 outside objects and 12 generated zones exact, six primer syntax checks exit0. No Docker, Rust/Cargo, formatter or generator execution ran locally.

Root and independent source reviews approved the corrected candidate. The new caller normalizes only its owned input and checks both LF and controlled CRLF forms through the same predicates; this is source review, with actual methods/variants still NOTRUN.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A; no product UI or presentation state changes.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Current signed head `050df4e87d148703a69e739771639600d51177f3`, tree `4f54a1def68482be3ead7c2049c8031ce2638a1c`, parent `1d66868d7ef239410f47b62cbbf8daffa6bf36b5`. Current runtime evidence is pending; historical runs are identified below.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A for UI; current-source image/test logs remain pending.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Source preparation only; no corrected image ran.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Local project/Docker/Rust/Cargo/fmt/generator execution was excluded; hosted CI is the verification venue.

### Current official follow-through

**Current signed head:** `050df4e87d148703a69e739771639600d51177f3`, tree `4f54a1def68482be3ead7c2049c8031ce2638a1c`, normal forward parent `1d66868d7ef239410f47b62cbbf8daffa6bf36b5`. Root and independent reviews approved the four exact official Rustfmt postimages in the appended vendor tests. This successor changes formatting only; signer/vendor predicates, test names and controls, Docker inputs, vendor contents, lock, features, profiles, cache/base/runtime policy and generated zones retain their bytes.

[Current Quality Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38627932413), attempt 1, completed FAILURE: 32 successful jobs, 10 declared skips and only Security plus the correctly failing required gate. Current Format and Lint both passed. All four signer/vendor architecture methods have actual named PASS records in current Test116071767631, with reviewed source/tested-tree equality; internal LF/CRLF and negative variants are not separate named executions. [Current source-image run](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38627933152), attempt 1, is terminal SUCCESS: all10jobs succeeded, including all7source-image builds. The complete ten-log inventory now binds every checkout to the exact reviewed tree. All seven source rows ran genuine vendor staging, signer primer, prefetch, cleanup, real-source restoration/build and the two-binary floor guard as current DONE stages. The two loaded normal amd64 images (Default and Alpine) passed their configured nonroot/Compose smokes; Alpine also ran both CLI version checks. prs.title: feat(a2a): extract A2A protocol core into a dedicated zeroclaw-a2a crate
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Extract the A2A protocol core out of `zeroclaw-api` / `zeroclaw-tools` / `zeroclaw-gateway` into a single `zeroclaw-a2a` crate, so the wire model, outbound client, and inbound protocol handling have one ownership home instead of four, and the protocol layer doesn't depend on any host config module.
  - Follow the official `a2a-rs` layering: the crate defines `A2aExecutor` / `AgentCardProducer` / `A2aPeerSource` as host-implemented seams and keeps its own config types, letting hosts adapt + inject.
  - Wire moves from `zeroclaw_api::a2a_wire` to `zeroclaw_a2a::wire`; `api` stops re-exporting it.
  - Hosts adapt through `A2aPeerSourceHost` (implements the protocol-layer `A2aPeerSource` over the host's **live** config handle) and the standalone `a2a_router` defaults closed to task operations.
- **Scope boundary:** Organization-only extraction — no new A2A protocol capability, no config-field change. Streaming and inbound task management are explicitly out of scope. The extraction preserves the pre-existing live/lazy host behavior (see below); it does **not** intentionally change runtime behavior.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw-api` loses its `a2a_wire` module (import sites moved); consumers of `zeroclaw-tools` / `zeroclaw-gateway` / `zeroclaw-runtime` see no tool, route, or behavior change.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #3566; Implements (RFC) #11254

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw's A2A support previously lived in four crates, split by hosting crate rather than by protocol: the wire model in `zeroclaw-api`, the outbound client in `zeroclaw-tools`, and the inbound surface in `zeroclaw-gateway`. That made every A2A extension thread re-export paths across multiple manifests. This PR consolidates the A2A protocol core into one `zeroclaw-a2a` crate whose layout mirrors the official a2a-rs SDK, and keeps host-coupled glue (the 4 `a2a_*` tools, gateway card building + auth) in the host crates, adapted through `A2aExecutor` / `AgentCardProducer` / `A2aPeerSource`.

### Live configuration ownership (review follow-up)

The first revision of this PR snapshotted peers, decrypted tokens, and proxy policy at client-construction time. That regressed the behavior the pre-extraction client had via its live config handle: removing a peer, rotating a token, tightening private-host policy, or changing the proxy no longer took effect on a retained agent, and one peer with a corrupt credential disabled all four tools.

This revision restores live/lazy semantics through a single host-implemented seam, `A2aPeerSource`, consulted on **every** call:

- `peers()` returns the current peers with **raw** (undecrypted) token fields — no snapshot.
- `resolve_token()` decrypts **lazily**, for the resolved peer only — one broken credential can no longer disable the whole tool set.
- `proxy_policy()` is resolved per call, including the `tool.a2a` service-scope check, so a proxy scoped to another service (or disabled while its URL is configured) does not block A2A.
- `settings()` reads card-cache TTL / response cap / SSRF allowlists live.

The protocol crate depends on none of the host's config modules (it holds an `Arc<dyn A2aPeerSource>`), preserving the RFC's config boundary while keeping resolution host-owned and current-at-use.

## Testing (required)

### How I tested

- `cargo +1.98.0 clippy --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean, no warnings.
- `cargo +1.98.0 doc --no-deps --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop` (Rustdoc warnings gate) — clean.
- `cargo test -p zeroclaw-a2a` → `94 passed; 0 failed`
- `cargo test -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib a2a` → `34 passed; 0 failed`
- `cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib a2a_client` → `36 passed; 0 failed` (2 ignored = cross-harness external-peer tests)
- `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib a2a` → passed

The A2A conformance/security tests moved with the code. Tests that had been dropped during the extraction were restored, and new boundary tests were added for the host adapter: lazy token decryption (encrypted / missing-dir / literal), disabled and other-service proxy scopes, live config reload (a removed peer disappears, settings follow), and the standalone catalog's `catalog` interface marker.

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — organization-only extraction; behavior matches the pre-extraction client.
- **Commands run and tail output:**
  ```
  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-a2a --lib
  test result: ok. 94 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored
  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib a2a
  test result: ok. 34 passed; 0 failed
  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib a2a_client
  test result: ok. 36 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored
  ```
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The host source reads live config per call (verified by a reload test: publishing a config with a peer added/removed is reflected immediately); proxy policy honors the `tool.a2a` service scope; a standalone `a2a_router` rejects task injection without a configured admission check; the standalone catalog emits the `catalog` interface marker so a single published alias is not mistaken for a single agent by `select_interface`.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A (no user-visible interface change)

### CI note

All checks affected by this PR are green (Lint incl. the Rustdoc gate, Format, Clippy incl. Windows-targeted, MSRV, every `Check`, every `Test`). The `Security` job is red on `cargo deny`, reporting newly published rustls advisories — `RUSTSEC-2026-0346/0347/0348/0349` against `rustls 0.23.45`, the version `master` also pins. That is a repository-level dependency finding (an upstream rustls bump or a `deny.toml` ignore), independent of this change and reproducible on `master`; it is not introduced by or fixable within this PR.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No**
- New external network calls? **No**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No behavior change.** Peer-token decryption stays host-owned (`A2aPeerSourceHost`, via the canonical `SecretStore`) and is now performed lazily per resolved peer; the protocol layer only applies `${VAR}` interpolation to the plaintext it is handed.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No**

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes**
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No**
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No**

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

`git revert <sha>` is the plan. Organization-only extraction with no data/config surface; reverting the merge restores the prior layout.

## Supersede Attribution

N/A (no `Supersedes #` used).

prs.title: feat(plugins): replace an installed package through staged admission
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`. Depends on #11236; `84b583e4d1` merges its current head, `95a30deb27`. Earlier parent merges and update follow-ups are preserved in history. The reviewable update slice remains the host update/cache/admission implementation and its original corrections; the normal merge adds the tested recovery/dependency parent.
- **What changed and why:**
  - #10995 asks for `zeroclaw plugin update` with verified replacement and rollback. This PR is the host half; the stacked CLI PR, #11262, builds on it. The contract was posted on the issue for review: https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/10995#issuecomment-5894198515. It is built on the package protocol #11236 introduces, so every step that changes the plugins directory runs under the persistent hidden package lock, holds each moved directory generation in a leased hidden transaction, moves directories only by renames that refuse an existing destination, and deletes only through the transaction's own handle. Where the platform or filesystem has no such rename, the move is refused before anything is replaced; #11236's `1743b13959` removed the plain-rename fallback.
  - `PluginHost::admit_update(name, source)` is `admit_source` with the identity decided the other way round. `name` must be loaded, which is checked before the source is opened. The source's manifest must name it, which `admit_open_directory` checks after the shape check and before the signature check and the component read. Everything else is #11236's admission, unchanged.
  - `PluginHost::update_admitted(admitted)`, under the package lock:
    - stages the replacement in a leased `installing` transaction exactly as `install_admitted` does, then checks the staged skill bundle of a skill-capable package as discovery will: staging copies no symbolic links while admission follows links inside the package, so a bundle admission accepted can stage incomplete. It is refused, with the reason, before the installed package is touched;
    - claims the installed directory into a leased `replacing` transaction and checks that the claimed generation has the manifest text, which carries all the authority the caller compared, and the admitted component this host loaded. A package replaced since with a different manifest or component is published back untouched and the update refused with `NamespaceChanged`. Skill content is not compared; it was never admitted bytes;
    - publishes the replacement into the directory the package was discovered in, by #11236's publication helper, whose rename refuses an existing destination. Where no such rename exists, the claim above has already been refused, so the installed package never moved. If publishing fails, the claimed generation is published back; if even that fails, the new `PluginError::ReplacementInterrupted` names where it is preserved, and its lease is released on return. On every other error the installed package is exactly as it was;
    - gives the replaced generation the delete mark #11236's remove sets once it commits to a delete, then deletes it through its handle, so recovery only ever finishes that delete. One that cannot be deleted stays there, marked, and `ReplacedPackage::leftover` names it.
  - `update_admitted` does not compare authority. Its rustdoc now states the precondition: the caller compares what the replacement requests (permissions, capabilities, `provides` ids and publisher) with the loaded generation and has the operator accept any increase, as #11262's CLI does. What the method guarantees is that the generation it replaces is the one that comparison was made against. An `# Errors` section lists what it returns and what state each leaves. Moving the comparison into the host is #11561.
  - `PluginHost::recover_interrupted_update(name)` covers a process stopped mid-update. Under the lock it judges only `replacing` transactions of `name` whose lease it can take; a held lease is reported as `RecoveryRetained`, and a lookup error inside a claim refuses rather than counting as absence. Whether the package is installed is judged by discovering the plugins directory again under the lock, never from the host's earlier view, which can predate the update that left the claims, and an installed package of the name takes precedence over any claimed generation. When it is installed, every claimed generation is marked for deletion and deleted, and one that cannot be is reported in `UpdateRecovery::Swept.kept`. When it is not, the one restorable claim is published back to `<plugins_dir>/<name>`, so the restored package is admitted only if the configured policy accepts it. Several claims, or anything already at the name, are reported and left as found; a generation marked for deletion is never put back; a claim that holds neither is finished; an empty transaction a stopped process left without a lease is removed, and a non-empty one is reported. Abandoned stages of `name` are swept with #11236's `remove_stale_staging`, and a namespace change refuses. `displaced_packages()`, also under the lock and judging installation the same way, lists the names with an abandoned claim that holds a package.
  - Also: `write_package` writes the admitted component after the `skills/` copy, so a component under `skills/` holds the admitted bytes even if the source changed after admission. One fix of #11236's own scope is carried here because the update work found it: install now runs the same staged skill check, so it refuses a staged bundle discovery would reject instead of publishing a package discovery then skips. Configuration and durable state are untouched: `PluginInstanceId` excludes the version, so the package's `[[plugins.entries]]` rows and state carry over.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - No CLI, config, WIT, or on-disk format change beyond one more hidden transaction kind, `replacing`. The one operator-visible change is install's refusal above. The CLI, its Fluent strings, and the operator docs are in #11262.
  - `remove` and discovery behave as in #11236; install does too, except for the `write_package` order and the staged skill check above. `remove` leaves `replacing` transactions alone: the displaced generation of a removed package is put back only by a named update.
  - Renames are not followed by `fsync`, as #11236's install does not fsync either, and the replaced generation is deleted right after the replacement is published. A power loss right after an update may leave the new package partly unflushed with the previous one already gone; #11262's docs give the remedy.
  - Discovery still reads a package's manifest and its component by path at different moments, so a daemon that discovers during a swap can pair the previous manifest with the new component when no `wasm_sha256` binds them, until its next discovery. Admitting discovered packages through one directory handle, as admission already does, is #11562.
  - Between claiming the installed directory and publishing its replacement, no package is at the name. The package lock keeps install, remove and recovery out, but discovery does not take it, so a daemon that discovers in that moment loads no package of that name until its next discovery. This is separate from #11562's mixed pairing, and discovery through one handle would not close it; an exchanging rename (`RENAME_EXCHANGE` on Linux, `RENAME_SWAP` on Apple platforms) could.
  - Staging never follows symbolic links, so a bundle with real skills beside linked ones still installs and updates without the linked ones.
  - A process killed between publishing the replacement and marking the replaced generation for deletion leaves that generation claimed. Recovery deletes it while the package is installed; after a later `plugin remove`, a named update would put it back.
- **Blast radius:** The published `zeroclaw-plugins` API gains `admit_update`, `update_admitted`, `recover_interrupted_update`, `displaced_packages`, `ReplacedPackage`, `UpdateRecovery`, and `PluginError::ReplacementInterrupted`. #11236's exhaustive `is_structural_admission_failure` classifies the variant as non-structural here, since admission never returns it. `host/recovery.rs` gains `transaction_package`, and #11236's delete mark is now shared by remove and update; `LoadedPlugin` keeps its admitted manifest text. Update opens the plugins root on first use, as install and remove do.
  - #11232 has landed on `master`, and #11236 merges `master` after it, so the stack holds one revision of each. `claimed_is_loaded` relies on `admit_component_in`, which #11232 and #11236 moved onto the no-follow walk; the replacement and recovery tests pass on this head. Merge order: #11236, this PR, #11262.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10995 (closed by the stacked CLI PR, #11262). Depends on #11236; #11715 has landed. Related #7432, #11232. Follow-ups: #11561, #11562.
- **Labels:** `enhancement`, `docs`, `dependencies`, `core`, `runtime`, `distinguished contributor`, `release-gate`, `domain:security`, `risk:high`, `size:XL`, `cli`, `ci:windows`, `topic:plugins`, `release:v0.8.6`.

### Since the last reviews

tidux requested changes at `f817e5386e`, which JordanTheJet had approved. Each item:

- **Restack.** The commit is rebased onto #11236's fixes, `c5fbbe2313`, as `420969ea90`, and `89cd78102d` merges #11236's later merge of `master`. The rebase conflicted only in `host/recovery.rs` and `host/recovery_tests.rs`, as your simulated restack showed. The approvals at `f817e5386e` do not cover this head.
- **One delete mark.** `SUPERSEDED` and `Transaction::retire` are gone. Update gives the replaced generation the mark remove sets (`mark_deleting`) and deletes it with `finish_delete`, and recovery classifies a marked claim as one it only ever deletes. The mark's doc comment says what it means for both.
- **Bounded barrier.** #11236's version, which gives up after 30 seconds, is kept, and this commit no longer changes it.
- **One empty-entry rule.** `abandoned_claims` uses `Root::remove_empty_entry`.
- **Tests on the new walk.** The replacement and recovery tests pass on `369fb21334`; see the commands below. Since #11236 now opens the plugins root on first use, update, recovery and `displaced_packages` do too.
- **Authority in the host API.** Documented as a precondition, with an `# Errors` section, on `update_admitted`. Moving the check into the host is tracked in #11561.
- **Mixed manifest and component in discovery.** Tracked in #11562, linked from the scope boundary.
- **`plugin remove` retiring abandoned `replacing` claims.** Not done here. `remove` still leaves `replacing` transactions alone, as the scope boundary says. The window it would close, a stop between publishing and marking, is narrow, and it would make remove act on update's transactions, which I'd rather review on its own.

### What this does, simply

To update a plugin, ZeroClaw has to swap one package directory for another without leaving the operator with no working plugin when the swap fails or the process stops part-way. This PR adds that swap to the plugin host; the command that uses it is the next PR.

The new version is first checked exactly as a fresh install is checked, then written, complete, into a hidden folder. Only then does the host move the installed folder into a hidden folder of its own, check that it is still the version the update was prepared against, and move the new folder into its place. If that move fails, the old folder is moved back.

Every step that changes the plugins folder happens under the same lock install and remove use, so those steps never interleave across processes, and whatever ran before the lock is checked again under it. If the process dies part-way, the hidden folders say how far it got, and the lock on each ends with the process: the next update puts the old version back, or finishes cleaning up. An update and its recovery never delete a package by name.

### Completed-update cache correction

The signed follow-up 284d2820482d3b818e386ad5320654c3b3d49edd fixes a host that loaded a package before another host completed an update and could retain the old generation after all update claims were removed. Recovery now refreshes the installed view under the existing package lock even when no abandoned claims remain. This also removes stale cached packages that another host deleted, while preserving current and missing-package no-op behavior.

The one-file follow-up adds three deterministic host regressions for completed replacement followed by another replacement, external removal while preserving another package, and current/missing-package no-ops. Source and patch/whitespace checks pass. The follow-up was separately qualified on its earlier named heads; current combined execution is supplied by the f33 current-head run above. No duplicate local execution is claimed.

The f33 normal parent integration now adopts the corrected #11236 copy and atomic-only move implementation. The current combined run qualifies the named mutex/cache/recovery controls. #11561/#11562 and downstream CLI/configuration acceptance remain separately scoped; no broader closure is claimed.
