prs.title: fix(channels): parse flat inbound Lark post content
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Feishu delivers inbound rich-text (`post`) messages with a flat body (`{"title":…,"content":[…]}`); `parse_post_content_details` only accepted the locale-wrapped body used when *sending* (`{"zh_cn":{…}}`), so every inbound `post` message was dropped before any reply.
  - A formatted list typed in the Feishu client *is* that flat `post` body — the `1. `/`- ` marker is plain text in the first element — so list messages looked silently ignored while plain `text` messages kept working.
  - Accept the flat body (plus the `content_v2` alias the same payload carries) in addition to the locale-wrapped shape, with a regression test built from a captured inbound payload.
- **Scope boundary:** the inbound `post` content decoder (`parse_post_content_details`), two regression tests, and the CI selector that runs the full Lark test module. Outbound post construction, the `list` message-type branch, group-mention policy, and every other channel are untouched.
- **Blast radius:** all Lark channel users sending rich text, in direct and group chats. The function is shared by the websocket listener and by `parse_event_payload` (HTTP/webhook ingress), so both paths change. Locale-wrapped payloads keep their existing precedence and behavior.
- **Linked issue(s):** None.

### What this does, simply

When you type a line into the Feishu (Lark) client that starts with a list marker such as `- ` or `1. `, the client does not send a `text` message. It sends a rich-text `post` message whose body is a flat JSON object, `{"title":"","content":[[…]],"content_v2":[[…]]}`, with the list marker as ordinary text inside the first element.

ZeroClaw's Lark decoder only understood the *sending* shape of a post, where the body is wrapped in a language key, `{"zh_cn":{"title":…,"content":[…]}}`. Fed the flat inbound body, none of its lookup branches matched, the function returned `None`, and the message was discarded before the agent was ever asked — no reply, no reaction, and not even an INFO trace line (the drop is logged at DEBUG level). Plain `text` messages never hit that path, which is why only rich text looked broken.

This PR teaches the decoder to accept the flat inbound body as well, and prefers `content` with `content_v2` as a fallback. Rich text, including lists, now reaches the agent like any other message. Posts with no extractable text remain ignored; untitled posts with text are accepted. Nothing about how ZeroClaw *sends* rich text changed.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `Yes` — the fix is about the shape of a live inbound event, so live A/B is the most direct demonstration.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel: lark`
- **Setup / preconditions:** a Lark channel configured and reachable from a Feishu client (bot present in the chat).
- **Steps to run:** in the chat with the bot, send one line starting with `- ` or `1. ` (the client converts it into a rich-text/list message).
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the runtime trace shows `channel inbound` carrying the parsed text, followed by a model turn and `channel outbound` / `reply delivered`; the chat receives an answer.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** running the same step produces no reply and no `channel inbound` event at all — the message is dropped during decode.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the workspace Rust gates exercise the changed function through `zeroclaw-channels`; the added unit test is the focused gate for this behavior.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** none that CI would miss. For reviewers running the local `.githooks/pre-push` hook on macOS: its final full-workspace `cargo test` step fails on the unrelated, pre-existing `zeroclaw-config::policy::tests::unix_foreign_null_spellings_get_no_filesystem_exception`, which creates the symlinks `nul` and `NUL` in one directory while the default APFS volume is case-insensitive (the second `symlink` returns `EEXIST`). The `rust_quality_gate` (fmt + clippy, whole workspace) and firmware protocol stages of the same hook pass on this branch.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```sh
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
# (no output)

$ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-channels --features channel-lark --all-targets -- -D warnings
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 1m 14s

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --features channel-lark --lib lark_parse_post
test lark::tests::lark_parse_post_message_accepts_md_tag_text_content ... ok
test lark::tests::lark_parse_post_message_accepts_flat_inbound_content ... FAILED

# before the fix, with the captured inbound payload:
#   assertion `left == right` failed
#     left: 0
#    right: 1

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --features channel-lark --lib lark::
test result: ok. 125 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1975 filtered out
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** A live end-to-end run on a Lark-configured daemon: a formatted list message sent from the Feishu client produced `channel inbound` with the parsed text, a normal agent turn, and a delivered reply; the regression test uses the captured payload byte-for-byte. I did **not** verify group-chat rich text with an @-mention beyond the existing `lark_parse_post_message_preserves_at_mention_for_group_reply` test, and I did not test other message types.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A` — message decoding only; no layout, styling, or interaction change.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `channel: lark`, exercised live against a locally built daemon.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** sent a list-formatted rich-text message → agent turn ran → reply delivered to the chat.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `N/A`

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? (`No`)
- New external network calls? (`No`)
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? (`No`)
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, or docs? (`No`)
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? (`Yes`) — previously dropped post text now reaches the existing inbound path. Sender authorization and group-mention filtering remain in place, with the same trust boundary as other channel text.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: `N/A`

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? (`No`)
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? (`No`)
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: `N/A`

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low-risk PRs: `git revert <sha>` is the plan unless otherwise noted.

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Replace the Keenable oversized-response test's finite write-error proxy with a controlled, unterminated chunked response containing exactly cap + 1 body bytes.
  - Observe EOF or connection reset directly while the real HTTP Client remains alive. Retain the oversize/provider/no-body-echo checks and explicitly require the no-decoding diagnostic.
  - Bound fixture buffers and request owned-server cancellation on early failure, preserving the existing 15-second client and 20-second server-join limits.
- **Scope boundary:** One existing test and its adjacent comment in `crates/zeroclaw-tools/src/web_search_tool.rs`. Every hunk is inside the unchanged test-only boundary. Production code, the shared response reader, all other tests, all Cargo files, workflow selection, permissions, profiles and release settings are unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** The named test and its owned loopback server. This corrects a validation fixture; it does not claim a production HTTP/read-cap repair.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #7432 and #11715. No implementation or release acceptance issue is closed.

### What this does, simply

This test checks that Keenable rejects an oversized unfinished response without decoding it and abandons its connection. The old fixture tried to prove closure by writing until a socket error, but its finite write budget could end before an error appeared. The release merge-group Test job failed with `the client never closed the connection`.

The new fixture sends only the controlled overflow input, keeps the response unfinished, and waits for the peer's actual EOF/reset. A successful write is no longer treated as evidence about how much the application read. The production response cap and HTTP client behavior are untouched.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes: verify the named real loopback test and its closure/error assertions.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** Developer test harness and internal HTTP fixture; no production `web`, `tui`, `cli` or messaging interface changes.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Repository Rust/toolchain and existing dependencies; no real provider account or credentials.
- **Steps to run:**

```sh
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-tools --lib   web_search_tool::tests::test_keenable_oversized_chunked_response_is_rejected_before_decoding   -- --exact --nocapture
```

- **Expected on this branch (after):** The one named test passes after an oversize/no-decoding error and direct EOF/reset observation, before the Client is dropped. Missing closure, unexpected I/O and timeout still fail.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The unchanged fixture uses the finite write-error proxy. It failed in [merge-group Test job 115581365188](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38480423428/job/115581365188). It may pass on other runs; this PR does not assert a deterministic failing baseline or explain the old socket/scheduling outcome.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Current [Quality Gate 38488466987](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38488466987) is SUCCESS for signed 82e7bb8634fb7149815da5b3293c4531f5455e82; [Required Gate 115611402559](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38488466987/job/115611402559) passes. Exact named-test/source receipts are being sealed separately. The first c4ada748 run failed Format on two macro layouts; this successor applies exactly those official postimages without changing predicates or literals. Its workspace Nextest job exercises this named test with the ordinary unified feature set; Format, Clippy and compiler checks must independently pass. No predecessor result qualifies the new fixture.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Current required compiler/lint/format/workspace checks pass; the per-method source-bound receipt is being sealed. Greedy-reader, decoder-bypass and retained-stream counterfactuals, plus failure-cleanup controls with a parent runtime kept alive, have not executed. Ordinary test-process teardown is not failure-cleanup proof.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Static Git checks only:

```text
git diff --check          exit 0
git diff --cached --check exit 0
1 file changed, 84 insertions(+), 35 deletions(-)
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Reviewed finite framing/sends, direct closure matching, Client lifetime, original error assertions and cancellation wiring. Production prefix/suffix, the shared reader, three dependency files and all 2,198 outside Git objects/modes match the parent. The published parent b6bad4d41e3db803721fb9c274ce412e25a2a456 has the same complete source tree as the reviewed #11715 head. Normal completion and failure-path reaping remain unexecuted claims.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A; no user-visible interface or presentation state changes.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Static source 82e7bb8634fb7149815da5b3293c4531f5455e82; the linked original job supplies the historical failing test log. Current aggregate execution evidence comes from this PR's linked successful Quality Gate; named/source receipts are retained separately.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** The historical failure is `the client never closed the connection`; no new runtime PASS is claimed.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** The reviewed test-only correction and two exact official formatting postimages are published; all production/dependency source remains identical. New-head required CI is successful; explicit counterfactual and failure-cleanup proof remains unexecuted.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Compiler, formatter, lint, sockets, runtime and mutation execution use hosted CI. No duplicate local project execution is supplied.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

prs.title: docs(plugins): document the Discord plugin and its acceptance run
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Issue 10999 asks for the official Discord plugin to be documented under its real package name and proven end to end from a published binary. This adds the operator page and the maintainer runbook for that. It is a draft until the pieces it documents have merged (listed below).
  - `channels/discord.md` gains "Running Discord as a plugin (experimental)": what the host needs, install and bind (`zeroclaw plugin install discord --channel-alias main --egress declared`, or `plugin bind` for an installed package), why the grant is `discord.com` plus `*.discord.gg`, the instance key for the alias `main`, the token through the masked `config set` prompt, turning plugins on, routing `plugin.main` to an agent, a peer group that admits numeric user IDs, what to check once it runs, and a comparison with the built-in channel. A callout warns against giving one bot token to both.
  - `plugins/distributing-plugins.md` gains "Package names and Cargo features": the registry package is `discord`; `channel-discord` is the Cargo feature that compiles the built-in channel; FND-001 and FND-004 say `channel-discord` and `channel-discord.wasm` for what is now the `discord` package. It also tells publishers to keep a package's name, because every instance key derives from it.
  - New `maintainers/plugin-release-acceptance.md`: the acceptance runbook. It covers recording the environment, installing by name, binding, and exercising the plugin. A 14-row evidence template (inbound, outbound, built-in channel idle, negative control, reconnect, shutdown, denied destination and recovery, denied sender, missing platform permission, invalid token, trust policy) is followed by redaction, posting, and cleanup. The page is registered in `SUMMARY.md` and the maintainers index.
- **Scope boundary:** Docs only, English source only; translations follow the normal sync. No edits to FND-001 or FND-004, which are ratified; the distribution guide records the mapping instead. No edits to pages that say release binaries ship without the plugin host, which the #10994 work owns, or to the binding docs #11302 adds.
- **Blast radius:** four existing pages gain a section or a line; one new page.
- **Current prerequisites and merge hold** (the PR remains draft):
  - #11302 is merged; its binding commands, readiness report and linked `binding-a-channel-instance` heading are now in this receiving source.
  - #11303 and #11348 are merged; the documented polling, shutdown and guest-health lifecycle is in public master.
  - #11304's WebSocket-denial record remains a prerequisite. Its current `95dcb66` CI is green, but current review and landing remain separate. #11228's selected host baseline likewise still needs its protected Runtime-owner review and landing.
  - The original [Discord port #161](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw-plugins/pull/161) is merged as `a5fb8292511a11446fe591689dead3285a65fad5`. Its landed tree exactly matches [successful current validation](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw-plugins/actions/runs/38808378778): ten jobs pass, including 65 individually named Discord tests, both Clippy lanes and the Wasm build. Iftekhar’s authorship and the original PR/topic are preserved. It remains `registry = false` against `wit/next`; source landing does not establish package publication or final released-pair acceptance.
  - A compatible published host archive and a separately reviewed released-WIT/Discord registry promotion are required before install by name. Published v0.8.5 lacks the port's required WebSocket contract; current registry/release assets contain no Discord package.
  - The existing functional test of the original Discord port #161 worked and has screenshots, as confirmed during release review. Reuse that working test and visual evidence. The 14-row published-pair template remains blank in this documentation PR; that is not evidence that no Discord test occurred. Map the existing receipts to their tested host/package revisions and fill only genuine remaining published-pair gaps before making a release acceptance claim.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10999. Related #7432 (R6).

### Current source reconciliation

Signed `26b216a43451d1860191a6aff4300a685c210c51` normally merges public master `996355b83c403e8e9b8080dff5f9b75cea188459` into the original docs topic. The merge was clean, with no manual source changes: four whole author pages, the original SUMMARY insertion, all master entries and all 14 blank acceptance rows are preserved. The binding anchor comes from already-merged #11302. No #11228 or #11304 feature parent was added.

Root and independent static review checked all 15 added links and their headings against this receiving source. These are source checks, not a built-book or live-command result. #11310 subsequently landed as `266ce2e`; its public signer changes are reconciled as current-master context for the actual tested CI merge. [Automatic Quality Gate 38499975529](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38499975529) completed with its required gate successful on this head. The current native readback confirms that result; it does not turn static link checks into built-book or live-command evidence; older `25d38658` CI and author-local checks supply no successor execution credit. No local Rust, docs helper or live Discord command was run for this publication.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw can talk to Discord in two ways: the Discord support built into the program, or a Discord plugin installed separately that runs in a sandbox and can reach only the servers you allow. This PR explains how to set up the plugin, how it differs from the built-in support, and how maintainers prove the published plugin installs and runs on a released copy of ZeroClaw before telling people it works.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Optional: read the new section in `channels/discord.md` and the new runbook. The commands can only be run once the dependencies above merge.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** Documentation source review for this PR. The user-confirmed working #161 test and screenshots are credited above; this documentation change adds no new operator CLI or live Discord execution. Exact final released-pair acceptance remains separate.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Read the five changed pages. Live testing needs the exact compatible published host/package pair, dedicated test bot and explicit grants described in the runbook.

### Follow-up: invalid-token acceptance control

The invalid-token row now requires a syntactically valid invalid or revoked
token entered through the masked prompt. It distinguishes Discord's
authentication refusal from malformed-token rejection during local
configuration. The evidence cells remain blank; this change records no new
live acceptance result.

Validation for `25d38658`:

- Full-file `docs_quality_gate.sh` on the changed runbook: zero lint errors.
- `docs_links_gate.sh` against parent `7b4e389d`: all six collector controls
  passed; no added links.

  the same declared merge and publication prerequisites.

### How I tested

- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** the link gates strip `#fragments`, so anchors are unchecked in CI. I checked them separately (below).
- **Commands run and tail output:** Historical author-local report from before the `26b216a` receiving publication, on macOS 26 (aarch64). These commands were not repeated by Root and are not current receiving-head execution evidence.

```text
$ BASE_SHA=$(git merge-base origin/master HEAD) bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
No prose em-dashes in changed docs files.

Summary: 0 error(s)

No added HTTP(S) links detected in changed docs lines.

```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Historical author checks follow. Current static source/link preservation is recorded above; the older missing-anchor exception is resolved by the public-master import.
  - Every anchor link in the changed pages resolves against the source headings, except `plugins/index.md#binding-a-channel-instance`, which #11302 adds.
  - `git merge-tree` against the heads of #11302, #11262, #11310, #11311, #11284, #11303, #11304, and #11348: clean.
  - Each runtime claim was checked against `master` source:
    - plugin senders are matched exactly (`plugin_sender_allowed` in `plugin_runtime.rs`);
    - the `channel inbound message` and `reply delivered` records run inside a scope carrying `channel = plugin.<alias>`;
    - `/health` names the component `channel:plugin.<alias>`; on `master` it tracks only the listener, and with #11348 (head `de4f86dca6`) it reads `error` on a failed poll and otherwise follows the plugin's health check, which is what the page states;

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:** `Cargo.lock` moves `rustls` from 0.23.45 to 0.23.46, the output of `cargo update -p rustls` and nothing else. Security jobs auditing a lockfile that still contains 0.23.45 fail these advisory checks. An earlier green run does not qualify an unchanged lockfile against the current advisory database.
- **Scope boundary:** no source change, no feature change, no other dependency moves.
- **Blast radius:** TLS connections handled by Rustls now use 0.23.46, a patch release. Other TLS backends and application-specific exposure are outside this claim.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #7432. This addresses the shared Security blocker for the release queue; #11715 is the earlier separate dependency-security repair.

### What this does, simply

A library the project uses for encrypted connections had four security problems announced today, which makes the project's own security check fail for everyone. This updates that library to the version that fixes them. Nothing else changes.

prs.title: fix(mcp): relocate tool-result images to a user message (OpenAI-compatible 400)
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** #10448 added `tool_result_image_policy` with two modes — `image_url` (keep the image as an `image_url` part **inside the `role:"tool"` message**) and `omit` (drop the image, leave a notice). On OpenAI-compatible endpoints that reject image parts in a tool result (HTTP 400 — reproduced on opencode zen / mimo-v2.5; llama.cpp behaves the same), the `image_url` default still 400s, and `omit` avoids the 400 only by **discarding the image** so the model never sees it. There was no mode that both avoids the 400 **and** delivers the image. This PR adds a third mode, **`relocate`**, and makes it the **default**: after native-message conversion, each `image_url` part is moved out of its `role:"tool"` message into a following `role:"user"` message (merged into an adjacent user message when one is present); the tool message keeps its text. Each relocated image group is prefixed with a **bounded local ordinal** label (`[external tool output - image from tool result N]`). The producing tool message carries the same ordinal in a relocation marker, so image-to-call attribution survives the move — bare image bytes alone would let the model attribute an observation to the wrong tool across a parallel batch. The provider-returned (or reconstructed) `tool_call_id` is deliberately **not** echoed into this user-role text; the real id stays on the `role:"tool"` message for native pairing. The image reaches the model as a native image part — the same shape a bare user-message image request uses — without violating the tool-result schema, so an image-returning MCP tool works out of the box with no per-provider config.
- **Why default (not opt-in):** leaving `image_url` as the default means every image-returning MCP tool 400s on the most common OpenAI-compatible endpoints until the user discovers and sets a policy — unnecessary friction. `relocate` uses the user-message image shape supported by the affected endpoints. Providers that never receive image parts (system-merge families, `allow_user_image_parts = false`) are a no-op. This non-lossy path becomes the default; `image_url` and `omit` remain available for explicit opt-in.
- **Bounded label, not the tool_call_id (review fix):** an earlier revision prefixed each relocated group with `[image from tool_call_id <id>]`. The provider-returned id is untrusted, unconstrained text and a reconstruction fallback can even borrow a guessed id, so echoing it into a `role:"user"` message let an instruction-shaped id become model-visible free text and could assert a false producing-call. The label is now a bounded local ordinal computed at relocation; per-call attribution is preserved by stamping the same local ordinal into the producing tool result and its relocated image group, including mixed text-only/image batches. The label identifies the image as external tool output; it is not a guarantee against visual prompt injection. Nothing downstream parses the label back — native tool-call pairing uses the untouched `role:"tool"` `tool_call_id`.
- **Scope boundary:** `crates/zeroclaw-config/src/schema.rs` (new `ToolResultImagePolicy::Relocate` variant, now `#[default]`, + docs), `crates/zeroclaw-providers/src/compatible.rs` (the relocation post-pass, gated on the variant), the provider docs (`configuration.md`, `custom.md`), and the default-coupled test assertion in `crates/zeroclaw-providers/src/lib.rs`. The relocation runs under the `relocate` policy; `image_url` and `omit` are byte-for-byte unchanged when selected. Histories with no image-bearing tool message take a fast path and are left untouched. Parallel tool-call batches flush relocated images only once the run of tool messages ends, so a relocated user message never splits a tool result from its siblings. Only native OpenAI-compatible chat-completions providers are affected — direct user images and OpenAI Responses providers are untouched. No API or CLI surface change.
- **Blast radius:** OpenAI-compatible provider request assembly, only for turns where a tool result carries an image. With the new default, such turns now place the image in a following user message instead of inside the tool result — which is what makes them succeed on endpoints that previously 400'd. Turns with no image-bearing tool result, `omit` configs, and explicit `image_url` configs are unchanged.
- **Relationship to #10448:** builds directly on it — same config knob, same conversion surface — and fills the gap its two modes leave (`image_url` → 400 on strict endpoints; `omit` → image discarded). `relocate` is the non-lossy option, and making it the default fixes the 400 for image-returning MCP tools without requiring any configuration. `image_url` (the previous default) stays available for endpoints that accept in-tool images.
- **Refreshed onto current master.** Re-applied on top of master after the approvals: added the `thinking_blocks: None` field that landed with the native-message change, and moved all relocate fixtures from inline `[IMAGE:...]` markers in the result text to the declared `attachments` array, the only source of tool-result images master reads — without that switch the tests would no longer exercise relocation at all. The doc conflicts were resolved on top of master's attachments wording, keeping its statement that legacy tool results pass through unchanged. Added one conversion test that leaves `tool_result_image_policy` untouched, so the default itself is covered rather than only the explicitly-set policy.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #10501.

### What this does, simply

Some OpenAI-compatible servers refuse a request when an image sits inside a tool
result, and answer 400. Until now the only choices were to fail that way or to
throw the image away. This moves the image one message down, into a normal user
message the same servers accept, so the model actually sees what the tool
returned — with no setting to discover first.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — deterministic message-assembly transform, covered by the `compatible.rs` conversion tests.
- **A/B (before → after):** Call an MCP tool that returns an image on a custom OpenAI-compatible provider. **Before (`image_url`, the old default):** the request carries an `image_url` part inside the `role:"tool"` message and the endpoint returns 400. **With `omit`:** no 400, but the model receives only a notice, not the image. **After (`relocate`, the new default):** the image is moved to a `role:"user"` message and the turn succeeds with the image visible to the model — no config needed.

### How I tested

Author-reported local validation on the earlier revision: `cargo test -p zeroclaw-providers --lib compatible::tests::convert_messages_for_native` passed, and `rustfmt --check` was clean.

On c3948b5a927f7b8a6ef2b7d46cc27c847c60c050, the [hosted Test job](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/36081372054/job/107903858225) passed and explicitly reports PASS for the policy round-trip and all seven relocate/merge conversion tests, including the two repair regressions below. This checks the production message conversion and serialized image framing; no live provider request was run for this repair.

Conversion tests:

- `convert_messages_for_native_relocates_tool_result_image_to_user_message` — image moves out of the tool message into a following user message labeled `[external tool output - image from tool result 1]`; the tool message keeps its text and real `tool_call_id`, and gains the matching relocation marker.
- `convert_messages_for_native_merges_tool_image_into_following_user_message` — the image merges into an adjacent user message rather than emitting two consecutive `role:"user"` messages.
- `convert_messages_for_native_relocate_labels_each_parallel_call_group` — an assistant message issuing two calls with uneven image counts (call A one image, call B two) keeps the two groups distinct and contiguous, labeled `[external tool output - image from tool result 1]` / `[external tool output - image from tool result 2]`.
- `convert_messages_for_native_relocate_does_not_echo_tool_call_id_into_user_text` (new) — an instruction-shaped id with brackets/whitespace never appears in the relocated user text (the label is the bounded ordinal only).
- `convert_messages_for_native_relocate_labels_missing_id_groups_by_distinct_ordinal` (new) — two id-less groups (the fallback would otherwise borrow the first assistant id) get distinct ordinals, not a borrowed/guessed id.

- `convert_messages_for_native_relocate_links_image_to_its_producing_call_across_identical_text` — moving the sole image between two same-caption calls changes which source tool result carries the matching marker.
- `convert_messages_for_native_relocate_frames_tool_image_as_external_output` — the image is preceded by fixed external-output framing, without copying instruction-shaped tool text into the label.

#10448's default-coupled tests remain updated for the new default (schema round-trip expects `relocate`; `convert_messages_for_native_promotes_tool_result_image_markers` sets `image_url` explicitly; the `omit` tests are unchanged). Local full-workspace build is not possible on the author's box (OOM); hosted CI supplies broader validation. The initial `CI Required Gate` failed because the unrelated `Repository Structure` Apple-preflight test counted a subprocess reap sleep as a retry. #11101 fixes that test on master. [Run 36081372054, attempt 2](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/36081372054/attempts/2) passed on c3948b5a927f7b8a6ef2b7d46cc27c847c60c050 after rerunning the failed jobs.

On the refreshed head, the whole gate (fmt, `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`
with `-D warnings`, clippy, and the lib tests) runs green on Linux.

Negative check, as requested: with the `Relocate` arm in `convert_messages_for_native`
made unreachable and nothing else changed, exactly eight tests fail and nothing else
does — the seven relocate tests plus the new default-coverage one:

```
convert_messages_for_native_relocates_tool_result_image_to_user_message
convert_messages_for_native_relocates_tool_result_image_without_setting_the_policy
convert_messages_for_native_merges_tool_image_into_following_user_message
convert_messages_for_native_relocate_labels_each_parallel_call_group
convert_messages_for_native_relocate_does_not_echo_tool_call_id_into_user_text
convert_messages_for_native_relocate_labels_missing_id_groups_by_distinct_ordinal
convert_messages_for_native_relocate_links_image_to_its_producing_call_across_identical_text
convert_messages_for_native_relocate_frames_tool_image_as_external_output
```

So the fixtures reach relocation through the declared `attachments` array, rather
than passing for the wrong reason.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No**
- New external network calls? **No**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes:** the default moves tool-produced images into a user-role carrier. Fixed external-tool-output labels and matching local ordinals preserve their source association without copying provider IDs or tool-result text into the user label. Image bytes are unchanged. This framing does not guarantee immunity to visual prompt injection.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Behavior change to a default.** The default `tool_result_image_policy` changes from `image_url` to `relocate`; for an image-returning tool result this moves the image from the tool message into a following user message. This is a no-op on providers that never receive image parts, succeeds on endpoints that previously 400'd, and uses a user-message image shape rather than relying on tool-role image support. Anyone who specifically wants the old in-tool shape can set `tool_result_image_policy = "image_url"`. Serialized config still omits the field at its (new) default.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Additive value + default change** — one new accepted value (`"relocate"`) for the existing `tool_result_image_policy` key, now its default.
- Rust / MSRV / toolchain floor changed? **No**

## Rollback

- **Fast rollback:** revert the single squash commit; the default returns to `image_url`, the `relocate` variant disappears, and any config still naming it falls back to a parse error at that key (resolved by switching to `image_url`/`omit`). No data migration or companion changes.

- **Feature flags or config toggles:** Set `tool_result_image_policy = "image_url"` to retain the previous wire shape, or `"omit"` to drop tool-result images while retaining text.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** an image-returning tool still causes an upstream 400, the model receives no image, or a relocated image is associated with the wrong tool result.

prs.title: fix(zerocode): name Enter in the paused-queue hint
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - The paused-queue ghost text only named the `PauseResumeQueue` chord (`Alt+P`, shown as `⌥P` on macOS). With macOS Terminal's default profile, Option is a character modifier, so `⌥P` types `π` and the queue stays paused. Enter on an empty input bar (`InputBarAction::ResumeQueue`) already resumes the queue on every terminal, but the hint never mentioned it.
  - `zc-queue-paused-ghost` now names both keys: `Queue paused — press { $send } or { $key } to resume, or send a message`. `$send` comes from the default chord of the keymap's `InputBarAction::Submit` (`send_chord_label()`, same pattern as the existing `resume_queue_chord_label()`), so it renders as `Enter`.
  - `zc-queue-missing-completion-ghost` has to fit the default queue dock at 80 columns (54 cells, guarded by `missing_completion_hint_fits_default_queue_dock_in_all_locales`). `Completion unconfirmed. Enter, Option+p or send to resume.` does not fit, so this hint now names Enter instead of the Alt chord: `Completion unconfirmed. { $send } or send to resume.` The Alt chord is still listed in the queue help entries.
  - All five catalogues (en, es, fr, ja, zh-CN) are updated the same way.
- **Scope boundary:** No keybinding changes. `PauseResumeQueue` keeps its `Alt+P` default and Enter's resume behavior is unchanged. Only the two hint strings and the arguments passed to them change.
- **Blast radius:** ZeroCode TUI ghost text in the empty input bar while the queue is paused. Nothing else reads these two message ids.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11691

### What this does, simply

When ZeroCode's message queue is paused, the empty input box shows a hint telling you how to resume. It only mentioned `⌥P`, which on a default macOS Terminal types the character `π` instead of resuming. Pressing Enter on the empty box already resumes the queue everywhere, so the hint now says so: `Queue paused — press Enter or ⌥P to resume, or send a message`.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Optional. The steps from the issue on macOS Terminal.app (default profile) show the difference directly.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `tui`
- **Setup / preconditions:** ZeroCode connected to a daemon, with a paused, non-empty queue (for example a queued message after a prompt error, or a `SESSION_BUSY` requeue).
- **Steps to run:** Look at the empty input bar while the queue is paused.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** `Queue paused — press Enter or ⌥P to resume, or send a message` (`Alt+p` instead of `⌥P` off macOS). Enter on the empty bar resumes.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `Queue paused — press ⌥P or send a message to resume`; in macOS Terminal's default profile ⌥P types `π`.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The Rust test job runs the new `i18n` catalogue test and the new rendered-input-bar test in `zerocode`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The macOS `⌥P` → `π` behavior is a terminal setting and isn't reproducible in CI; the tests check that the hint names the Enter key.
- **Commands run and tail output** (Linux x86_64, rustc from `rust-toolchain`, at 1e82f3ed0):
  - New tests fail on `master`'s strings:
    - `cargo test --locked -p zerocode --bin zerocode queue_paused_hints_name_the_send_key` →
      ```
      panicked at apps/zerocode/src/i18n.rs:661:17:
      en: Queue paused — press Alt+p or send a message to resume
      test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed
      ```
    - `paused_queue_hint_names_enter_in_rendered_input_bar` with `en/zerocode.ftl` from `master` → `panicked at apps/zerocode/src/chat.rs: Queue paused — press Alt+p or send a message to resume`.
  - After the fix:
    - `cargo test --locked -p zerocode` → `test result: ok. 1461 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored` (bin unit tests) and all integration test binaries `ok`.
    - `cargo clippy --locked -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` → `Finished`, no warnings.
    - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` → clean.
    - `bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh` → `Comment hygiene gate passed.`
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The final renderer output below (ratatui `TestBackend` through `Chat::draw_with_dock`, English locale). I did not run ZeroCode in a real macOS Terminal.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Exact final-interface output (semantic-only text change; the hint lives in the same ghost-text slot and the 80-column fit is asserted by the existing dock test).
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** 1e82f3ed0, ZeroCode chat input bar via `Chat::draw_with_dock` into a `TestBackend`, English locale, Linux (so the chord shows as `Alt+p`).
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:**
  ```
  # paused_queue_hint_names_enter_in_rendered_input_bar, 120x24
  │Queue paused — press Enter or Alt+p to resume, or send a message                                                      │
  # prompt_completion_settles_turn_when_terminal_update_is_missing, 80x24 with the 24-column queue dock
  ```

- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Paused queue with one item → the ghost text names Enter and the Alt chord; the missing-completion pause names Enter and still fits the 80-column dock in every catalogue.

prs.title: feat(runtime): add capability-taking constructors for turn entry points
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`. Current signed head `85466e9cc3a0a9954baf07004b96a11903db40ce` is a normal merge with ordered parents `f1bf79986c236520795a7de9e34fc14ca1aeaf1a` and public master `329e66f76394b00af9d00b767e00ad298133961e`; tree `8a13cd30c1851f123bb5f9ab5984ad056718a32d`. The original fork, topic and history are preserved.
- **What changed and why:** This PR introduces capability-taking runtime entry points for supplied providers, memory, tools and the requesting principal. Existing public entry points remain config-backed adapters. The latest correction fixes both real CLI model-switch branches: a supplied turn now calls its switch source, propagating refusal rather than reusing startup construction.
- **Scope boundary:** This successor reconciles current public master and adds the two CLI call-site corrections with four real-entry-point regression controls. It does not complete the supplied-only construction boundary or migrate application callers; those remaining requirements are listed below.
- **Blast radius:** Runtime turn construction, model switching, child turns, registered manual cron, vision routing and source/principal propagation. This successor adds no dependency, config, CLI argument or permission change.
- **Linked issue(s):** Contract lineage #11090; Related #10993 and #7432. The application migration is #11187; independent construction/consumer proof is tracked separately in #11526. The existing #11092 holding exception is bounded and does not waive other placement requirements.

### What this does, simply

A caller can supply the sources used to construct a turn instead of relying only on runtime factories. Provider requests carry the resolved model and principal, memory requests are asynchronous, and child bindings carry the enclosing capability set. Existing adapters preserve the configured application route.

The latest CLI fix matters when a source distinguishes startup from a mid-turn switch. Both the one-shot and interactive paths previously called startup construction again. They now ask `switched_model_provider` with the same resolved target, alias, model and principal, and propagate its error. Config-backed behavior remains behind its existing adapter.

### Remaining construction and acceptance holds

This is still a partial construction migration. The current registry builds native tools before appending supplied tools. A supplied `execute_pipeline` can collide with the later native creator, and accepted supplied tools are not yet projected into the bounded delegate's already-captured parent handle. The reviewed supplied/native construction design is preparation, not implemented or compiled proof. These source requirements remain before merge; ordinary green CI would not close them.

Application-owned defaults, the remaining placement/Core decisions and the independent consumer/dependency/full R1 proof remain separate. No exception is inferred from path overlap. The existing `model_switch` catalog-listing factory path is also not changed by this bounded CLI-switch correction.

The original SOP-memory change remains: the engine requests memory through the supplied memory source with the agent provider's credential, matching the agent's embedding resolution. This successor introduces no additional credential flow.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes: review the current CLI correction and remaining construction requirements independently. Application caller migration remains #11187 work.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=cli`; actual `run_with_capabilities`, one-shot message and interactive stdin/EOF. The child is a real same-test-executable fixture, not a packaged CLI archive.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Rust 1.98 with locked dependencies and isolated synthetic config/data. Providers are supplied test implementations; the configured endpoint is a controlled loopback counter.
- **Steps to run:** `cargo +1.98.0 test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- agent::loop_::capability_entry_point_tests`. Each active parent explicitly executes the exact private ignored child with its selected case.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Serving and refusing switches in both CLI branches reach the switch source exactly once, retain alias/principal/model requests and balanced lifecycle events, and do not fall back to startup or a configured provider.
- **Prior behavior (before):** Restoring either old production call sends that branch to startup construction. The adversarial source rejects reuse after the successful real `model_switch` tool witness.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [Current Quality Gate 38784355225](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38784355225) completed with 33 successful jobs, 9 conditional skips and two failures: Security and the aggregate required gate. Security rejects the locked Rustls 0.23.45 for RUSTSEC-2026-0346 through 0349; shared fix #11755 remains subject to independent Core review and protected landing. Format, Lint, the declared-floor check, selected Windows compilation and the workspace test job pass. The workspace log reports 19,619 passed / 40 skipped; it does not print the new CLI controls individually. Their named execution and negative controls are the separate dev-box evidence below.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No current official full-gate, Core, platform or release result is transferred from an older head. The endpoint evidence proves counted accepted connections with an acknowledgment of each own probe, not a universal factory-entry claim. The source-window check reads request config; it does not independently observe outer-loop context rematerialization.
- **Commands run and tail output:** On the dedicated Linux dev-box, default features, Rust 1.98, jobs 8, incremental off, locked dependencies and an isolated target:

```text
cargo +1.98.0 fmt --all -- --check                         PASS
four exact CLI parent controls                           4 PASS
full capability_entry_point_tests module                 6 PASS / 1 private ignored
baseline: both switch calls restored                     4 intended semantic FAIL
one-shot call restored                                   2 intended FAIL / 2 PASS
interactive call restored                                2 PASS / 2 intended FAIL
restored fixed source                                    4 PASS
cargo +1.98.0 clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings
                                                         PASS
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Source review against both parents, actual source-tree/lock/workfile/binary bindings and exact test preservation. Every negative case reaches the native tool-completed witness and rejects startup-source reuse. No compiler/setup/deadline or zero-selection failure is counted as a negative control. The final rebuilt binary equals the initial fixed binary, SHA256 `4e53089590821cf2ef6789a8764de417a64aac238b13972b091c53bf63eff072`.
- **Visual interface evidence:** No renderer/layout change. The parent checks actual child stdout, native tool completion and source/refusal results; no screenshot or packaged CLI acceptance is claimed.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Exact tree `8a13cd30c1851f123bb5f9ab5984ad056718a32d`, now signed `85466e9cc3a0a9954baf07004b96a11903db40ce`. All five source variants were freshly compiled. Four parents verify their child's exact status, one-test summary and case-specific success marker; the ordinary ignored row earns no execution credit.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Current stdout/source outcomes are summarized above. The process fixture uses synthetic values and owned loopback connections only.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** The supplied switch source serves a distinct reply or refuses; the correct branch changes independently under each production-call counterfactual. All four fixed cases pass after restoration.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full workspace, current official CI, external application consumer, platform and live release suites are separate. Source invariants do not imply full construction acceptance.

**Historical evidence:** Official QG38143090708 at `f1bf799` passed its selected 27 capability/lifecycle controls. Earlier `af00b35` native area tests had three delegate timeouts reproduced on their own baseline; they are not a current failure or pass claim. No execution credit from either source is transferred to this head. Original registered-cron, vision, SOP, source/principal and policy controls remain in source.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No new grant in this successor.** Supplied native sources remain trusted in-process implementations; filtering and approval do not confine arbitrary native code. The remaining construction/captured-view requirements above are not waived.
- New external network calls? **No.** Development controls use a disposable loopback endpoint and synthetic sources.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **Yes in the original PR's retained SOP-memory path:** it uses the same agent provider credential already used for the agent's memory. This CLI correction adds no credential, disclosure or fallback.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No;** test principals and credentials are synthetic.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No new surface in this successor.**
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Keep the original effective-policy/source contract and existing credential boundaries. Source/namespace, placement and independent Core review remain required before merge.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes for existing callers:** public adapter signatures remain. Contract request changes from #11090 are unreleased. Supplied callers now get their declared switch-source behavior and refusal.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No product surface.** Only two known OPEN_SKILLS overrides are removed from the private test child's environment.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.** Current default development checks use 1.98; declared-floor qualification remains part of official CI.
- Exact upgrade steps: N/A; no serialized migration or user configuration is introduced by this successor.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the eventual landed squash through the normal PR workflow. The current topic retains its normal signed history.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None added.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** A supplied switch asks startup construction again, silently reaches a configured provider, loses principal/target metadata, or masks the supplied refusal. The new controls cover these bounded paths; broader construction remains held.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A. Original PR/fork/topic/history preserved; no replacement PR.

prs.title: feat(channels/signal): add media attachment support
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Inbound: Signal attachments are fetched from signal-cli (`getAttachment`), saved under the owning agent's workspace in `signal_files/`, and rendered as `[IMAGE|AUDIO|VIDEO|DOCUMENT:<path>]` markers with `MediaAttachment.marker` set, so the shared media pipeline treats Signal like the other media-capable channels instead of seeing `attachments: vec![]`.
  - Attachment-only messages now reach the agent when `ignore_attachments = false`; previously they produced no message.
  - Outbound: media markers in replies are resolved into signal-cli attachments (RFC 2397 data URIs, so delivery works when signal-cli does not share ZeroClaw's filesystem). Only regular files inside the workspace are accepted; URLs, other schemes, and paths that resolve outside the workspace are refused.
  - Unresolved markers are removed from the reply, logged with a reason (never the path), and summarized in a count-only Fluent notice.
  - signal-cli echoes a rejected attachment argument in its error text, which for a data URI is the whole file; `rpc_request` now redacts data URIs from signal-cli errors before they can reach logs.
  - Signal gets a `channel_delivery_instructions` block (same shape as WhatsApp Web's) so the model is told the marker syntax and the workspace/no-URL rules. Without it, the model has no way to know Signal accepts attachments and sends paths as plain text.
- **Scope boundary:** No changes to Signal auth/account lifecycle, SSE reconnect, typing indicators, health checks, other channels, shared helpers (`util.rs`, `zeroclaw-api` media types, media pipeline), or config schema. `[LOCATION:…]` markers stay text. Outbound URL fetching is intentionally not supported.
- **Blast radius:** Signal channel only: `signal.rs`, Signal construction sites and the Signal delivery-instructions block in `orchestrator/mod.rs`, the `channel-signal` feature (now enables the existing optional `mime_guess` dependency), two Fluent keys in each runtime locale, and the Signal docs page. `rpc_request` now moves params/results instead of cloning them and redacts data URIs from signal-cli error text (all Signal RPC calls go through it; wire format unchanged).
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #7891. Related #11013 (RFC #9488 implementation tracker), Related #9488, Related #5832 (earlier, unreviewed attempt closed by its author; see notes below).

### What this does, simply

Signal could only exchange text with the agent. Photos, voice notes, and files sent to the bot were silently dropped, and when the agent tried to send a file back, the literal `[IMAGE:/path]` tag showed up in the chat. With this change, files people send over Signal are saved into the agent's workspace and the agent can see them (images go to vision-capable models), and the agent can send files from its workspace back as real Signal attachments. Files outside the workspace, and links, are never sent; if the agent asks for one, it is dropped and the message gets a short "(note: I couldn't deliver N file.)" line instead of exposing the path. Text-only behavior and `ignore_attachments = true` are unchanged.

### Interim scope and RFC #9488 migration

This is the narrow interim implementation agreed on #7891: it uses today's channel media contract (`MediaAttachment`, `RenderedMarker`, `MarkerKind`, the `[KIND:path]` marker rendering, and provider-loadability classification) and keeps all Signal-specific work in the Signal adapter and its orchestrator wiring. No shared contract, no-new-marker check, `FileId`, or `ContentPart::File` exists on `master` at this head; if one lands first, this PR adapts to it rather than adding an exception.

Signal paths that RFC #9488 Phase 4 will migrate (tracked by #11013):

| Path | Today | Phase 4 |
|---|---|---|
| Inbound marker writer: `SignalChannel::attach_inbound_media`, `fetch_inbound_attachment`, `inbound_marker_kind`, `marker_label` (`signal.rs`) | Renders `[IMAGE\|AUDIO\|VIDEO\|DOCUMENT:<path>]` into `ChannelMessage.content` and sets `MediaAttachment.marker` | Emit a `ContentPart::File { file_id }` through the shared intake instead of a marker |
| Inbound storage: `save_inbound_attachment`, `SIGNAL_ATTACHMENT_SAVE_SUBDIR` | `<agent workspace>/signal_files/<uuid>_<basename>` | Managed file intake; existing `signal_files/` contents are legacy channel media (the RFC excludes automatic deletion) |
| Outbound marker reader: `prepare_outbound`, `resolve_outbound_marker`, `SIGNAL_OUTBOUND_MARKER_KINDS` (`signal.rs`) | Parses markers with the shared `util::parse_attachment_markers_of_kinds`, confines targets to the workspace, sends RFC 2397 data URIs | Runtime resolves and authorizes a `FileId`; the adapter only streams the resolved bytes |
| Model guidance: `"signal"` arm of `channel_delivery_instructions` (`orchestrator/mod.rs`) | Teaches the marker syntax and workspace/no-URL rules | Removed or replaced with `FileId` delivery guidance |
| Failure notice: `channel-signal-delivery-failure-note-{one,many}` | Count-only note for dropped markers | Replaced by the runtime's delivery outcome reporting |

Expected to carry over unchanged: the `getAttachment` download (after the sender checks), the `size`/decoded-length caps, and the signal-cli `send` `attachments` parameter with data URIs.

### Sending a received file back

An inbound attachment is saved at an absolute path inside the agent's workspace (`<workspace>/signal_files/<uuid>_<name>`), which is exactly what the outbound resolver accepts, so the agent can send it back by copying the inbound marker into its reply (`[DOCUMENT:/…/signal_files/<uuid>_report.pdf]`); `inbound_saved_attachment_can_be_sent_back_with_its_marker` covers this. The shared provider preparation keeps `[DOCUMENT:]`, `[FILE:]`, `[VIDEO:]`, and `[PHOTO:]` paths model-visible for exactly this delivery case. Two shared behaviors outside this PR apply: an `[IMAGE:]` marker is consumed by vision preparation, and `[AUDIO:]`/`[VOICE:]` markers are replaced by a placeholder (the audio is transcribed), so for those kinds the path is not in the model-visible text of that turn; the file remains in `signal_files/`.

### Known behavior outside this PR

- **Forwards arrive as two messages.** Signal sends a forwarded file and its added comment separately, so each becomes its own turn unless `[channels] debounce_ms` merges them. The debouncer measures arrival time, and the file arrives only after signal-cli downloads it, so large files can need a longer window. Tracked in #11553.
- **Earlier images are re-sent on later turns.** Signal image markers are file paths, which history keeps (as for Telegram and Discord), and with the default `[multimodal] max_image_turns = 0` they are reloaded on every turn; the model can then describe images that were never sent. Tracked in #11554.
- **Full-resolution 12 MP photos are dropped.** A 4000×3000 JPEG exceeds the 64 MiB per-image decode ceiling and is skipped with a "could not be loaded" note; see #9887.

Notes:
- Prior art: #5832 (closed by its author before review) sketched the same feature. No code was carried over; this implementation follows the current channel media contract (`RenderedMarker`, provider-loadability classification, per-agent workspaces, workspace confinement), so there is no `Co-authored-by` trailer.
- Source of truth for the workspace: `Config::channel_workspace_dir("signal.<alias>")` (owning agent's workspace), resolved when the channel is built, the same way Telegram, Slack, Discord, Matrix, and WhatsApp receive it. Per the channel runtime lifecycle, listeners adopt agent-binding changes on daemon reload.
- Docs: English source only; `.po` translation-cache churn is left for a dedicated translation pass.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel` = `signal`
- **Setup / preconditions:** A dedicated test Signal account linked in a `signal-cli` HTTP daemon; a `[channels.signal.<alias>]` entry bound to an agent via the agent's `channels` list; a vision-capable model if you want to check image understanding.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. From another Signal account, send the bot a photo with a caption, then a photo with no caption, then a PDF.
  2. Ask the agent to send back a file from its workspace (for example, have it write `report.txt` and reply with `[DOCUMENT:report.txt]`).
  3. Ask it to send `[IMAGE:https://example.com/a.png]` or a path outside its workspace.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** (1) The agent receives each file; it is saved in `<agent workspace>/signal_files/` and the agent can describe the image. The caption-less photo still reaches the agent. (2) The file arrives as a Signal attachment without the marker text. (3) Nothing is attached, the marker is gone, and the reply ends with the count-only note; logs show `signal: dropping unresolved outbound attachment marker` with `reason` `scheme` or `outside_workspace`.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** (1) The agent sees only the caption; caption-less photos produce no message. (2) and (3) The literal `[DOCUMENT:report.txt]` / `[IMAGE:…]` text is sent to the chat.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Required CI passes on `b9022fc7`. Lint checks the feature-enabled code through workspace clippy with `ci-all`; the default-feature workspace Test job covers shared code and the Signal delivery-instructions test, but does not enable `channel-signal` or run its `signal::` unit tests. The 87 focused Signal and delivery-instructions tests below are local validation reported by the author, not hosted Test-job coverage.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No automated system test drives a Signal envelope through runtime dispatch to an outbound reply; the new tests exercise the adapter against a mocked signal-cli JSON-RPC endpoint. Vendor-side behavior (real `getAttachment` payloads, data-URI acceptance, Signal's post-encryption size limit) is covered only by the manual run below.
- **Commands run and tail output:** (Rust 1.98.0 in a podman build container; Rust checks ran on this commit's code before two docs-only amends; markdownlint was re-run on the final docs page)
  ```text
  (Updated for b9022fc7, the review fix: fmt, channel clippy, and the Signal tests below were re-run on it; the workspace clippy, rustdoc, hygiene, and ci build lines are from f8b0bffb, with CI covering b9022fc7)

  $ cargo fmt --all -- --check
  (no output, exit 0)

  $ bash scripts/ci/run_clippy.sh --scope workspace ...   # cargo clippy --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets --features ci-all -- -D warnings
      Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 1m 56s   (exit 0, no warnings; CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1)

  $ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-channels --all-targets --features channel-signal --locked -- -D warnings
  (exit 0, no warnings)

  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --features channel-signal --locked --lib -- signal:: channel_delivery_instructions
  test result: ok. 87 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1966 filtered out

  $ cargo doc --no-deps --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop
      Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 3m 36s   (no warnings)

  $ bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
  Comment hygiene gate passed.

  $ cargo fluent check && cargo fluent scan
  (both exit 0; scan reports no Signal keys)

  $ cargo check --locked --features channel-signal
      Finished `dev` profile ... (no warnings)

  $ cargo build --locked --profile ci -p zeroclaw --features ci-all
      Finished `ci` profile [optimized] target(s) in 10m 41s   (no warnings)

  $ npx markdownlint-cli2 docs/book/src/channels/signal.md
  1 issue: MD001 at the existing `#### sh` tab heading in "Start and check" (present on master; not in changed lines)
  ```
  New unit tests (26): outbound data-URI attachment for direct and group recipients, count-only note with no target leakage, note-only reply when every marker fails, verbatim text when no markers (including `[LOCATION:…]`), refusal of URLs/`data:`/`file:`, missing workspace, absolute and `..` escapes, symlink escape, `not_found`/`not_a_file`/`too_large` failures; inbound image save with `RenderedMarker::Image`, attachment-only group document with traversal-style filename, `ignore_attachments` (no download), no workspace (bytes only), download failure (text kept, empty message dropped), oversized `size` skipped without download, DM `recipient` vs group `groupId` download params; Fluent note keys present and count-only; the Signal delivery-instructions block describes the marker contract, offers no `[LOCATION:]`, and reaches the channel system prompt; an inbound saved document sent back by copying its marker arrives as the same bytes; a signal-cli error that echoes a data URI is redacted (`data:<redacted>`) and ordinary text such as `metadata:` is left alone; and, from the review fix: an inbound batch stops calling `getAttachment` once the per-message budget is spent (including an attachment with no declared size), a declared size past the remaining budget skips the download, an oversized `getAttachment` response is refused even when the payload itself would fit, an outbound batch over budget sends what fits and counts the rest, saved-name sanitizing, and a `report]v2.pdf` attachment round-trips through its marker. Removing each of the four fixes makes its test fail.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Ran a `ci-all` build of this branch live for several hours in Signal DMs against signal-cli 0.14.7 on a dedicated test account. Outbound: the agent sent two different attachment types, and both arrived as real Signal attachments with the marker text removed. After the delivery-instructions change, a plain-language request that did not mention markers (asking the agent to tar and compress several screenshots from its workspace and send them) produced the archive and delivered it as a real Signal document attachment; when extracted, it contained the expected files. Inbound: a photo of a printed document in several languages was read and every language translated correctly; a photo of a handwritten note in cursive and print was transcribed correctly; text-only follow-ups were correctly told no new image was attached until the shared image-history behavior described above set in. The forward, re-sent image, and 12 MP findings are under "Known behavior outside this PR". Not verified live: inbound documents and voice notes, sending a received file back (covered by a unit test), group conversations, files near the 100 MiB limit, a signal-cli daemon on a separate host.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `ci-all` builds of this branch; the live daemon runs a build of this commit's code, made just before it was committed, so it reports `v0.8.5-432-g32f90e9ba-dirty`; later changes to the commit were docs only. `channel` = `signal` (DM); signal-cli 0.14.7
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Outbound: a plain-language request to archive several workspace files was delivered as a Signal document attachment, and the extracted archive held the expected files. Inbound: a photo of a multilingual printed document was read and translated in full, and a photo of a handwritten note in cursive and print was transcribed correctly.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full workspace `cargo nextest run` was not run locally; CI runs it. `scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh` was run up to its markdownlint step, which was then run directly (the container lacked Python).

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? `Yes`
- New external network calls? `No`
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? `No`
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? `No`
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? `Yes`
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation:
  - File system: inbound attachments are written to `<agent workspace>/signal_files/<uuid>_<basename>`; sender-supplied names are reduced to their final path component and UUID-prefixed. Outbound markers can read only regular files whose canonical path is inside the canonical workspace (absolute, `..`, and symlink escapes refused). Each file is capped at Signal's 100 MiB limit, and all attachments in one message at 100 MiB combined, in both directions. `getAttachment` responses are capped before they are buffered, and outbound reads are capped at the checked size. Saved names have `[`, `]`, and control characters replaced so their markers stay parseable. Downloads start only after the sender passes the allowlist/group checks and the message is not an approval reply.
  - Model-visible text / injection: outbound markers come from model output, which may be influenced by inbound content. Workspace confinement prevents exfiltrating host files outside the workspace; files inside the agent's workspace remain sendable, as on other channels. Failure logging records kind/outcome/reason only, never the target path; the user-visible note carries only a count. Attachment contents never reach logs: data URIs are redacted from signal-cli error text, and inbound failure logs carry signal-cli's error text as returned (with data URIs redacted and credentials scrubbed) and local I/O error causes, which do not include file paths.
  - Network: only additional JSON-RPC methods on the already-configured signal-cli daemon; outbound URL markers are refused rather than fetched.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? `Yes`. Replies without media markers are sent byte-for-byte as before. With `ignore_attachments = false` (the default), attachment-only messages now reach the agent instead of being dropped.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? `No`
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? `No`
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`; text-only Signal behavior is the fallback.

prs.title: fix(i18n): fall back from a regional locale to its language catalogue
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - The OS reports its locale with a region (`LANG=fr_FR.UTF-8`), but the catalogues are per language (`en`, `fr`, `ja`, `es`, `zh-CN`). `normalize_locale` produced `fr-FR`, which matches no built-in arm and no `<ftl dir>/fr-FR/` directory, so French, Spanish and Japanese users got English everywhere. Only `zh_CN` worked, because that catalogue carries the region in its name.
  - `zeroclaw-runtime`: `normalize_locale` now maps the normalized tag to the `available_locales()` code it matches, ignoring case (`zh_cn` → `zh-CN`). If nothing matches, it uses the language when that is a registry code (`fr_FR` → `fr`, `es_AR` → `es`). Otherwise the tag stays as before (`de_DE` → `de-DE`, `zh_TW` → `zh-TW`), which still means English. It also drops a POSIX `@modifier` (`fr_FR@euro`) the way it already dropped the encoding. Config `locale`, OS detection and `i18n::init` all go through `normalize_locale`, so all three get the fallback.
  - `zeroclaw-tools` cannot see the runtime registry (the dependency runs runtime → tools). Its `load_ftl_from_disk` now tries `<ftl dir>/<tag>/tools.ftl` and then `<ftl dir>/<language>/tools.ftl`. Its `normalize_locale` drops `@modifier` too.
- **Scope boundary:** no catalogue, registry or config schema change. No new locales. `zh-TW` and other languages without a catalogue keep falling back to English.
- **Blast radius:** processes whose locale comes from a regional tag of `fr`, `es` or `ja` now show those translations instead of English. That covers CLI strings, channel notices and tool descriptions.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11773

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw ships French, Spanish and Japanese translations, but a computer set to "French (France)" reports `fr_FR`, and ZeroClaw only looked for a catalogue named exactly `fr-FR`. It found none and used English. Now it falls back from the region to the language, so those users get their language without having to set `locale` in the config.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Optional:

```bash
LANGUAGE= LC_ALL= LC_MESSAGES= LANG=fr_FR.UTF-8 \
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib voice_drop_notices
```

On `master` this passes, because the notice is still English. On this head it fails on the English-only assertion that #11769 / #11770 fix, which shows the French catalogue is now selected.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the `Test` job runs the new unit tests below. They call `normalize_locale` and `catalogue_candidates` directly and do not depend on the environment.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** CI runs in English, so it does not exercise detection from a regional OS locale end to end. The manual run below does.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
(clean)

$ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings \
    -A clippy::needless_borrows_for_generic_args -A deprecated
(clean)

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib i18n::
test result: ok. 45 passed; 0 failed

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib i18n::
test result: ok. 6 passed; 0 failed
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - `normalize_locale_falls_back_from_region_to_language_catalogue`: `fr_FR.UTF-8`, `es_AR.UTF-8`, `ja_JP.eucJP`, `fr_FR@euro` and `es-MX` map to their language. `zh_cn.utf8` maps to `zh-CN`. `zh_TW` and `de_DE` are left as they are.
  - `catalogue_candidates_fall_back_from_region_to_language` (tools).
  - With `LANG=fr_FR.UTF-8`, the Telegram voice-drop notice comes out in French on this head. On `master` it stays English (see above).
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** clippy with `needless_borrows_for_generic_args` and `deprecated` allowed: my local stable 1.99 flags untouched code that CI's pinned 1.98.0 does not. The pre-push hook was skipped with `--no-verify`; I ran the touched crates' suites above.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No (the tools crate may read one more catalogue path, inside the same FTL directory)
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. An explicit `locale = "fr"` behaves as before. Only regional tags change, from English to their language.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert` the squash commit.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** set `locale = "en"` in config to keep English.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** strings in an unexpected language for users with a regional OS locale.
